1169111920.readme_excerpt:
# Super Mario Kart — Static Recompilation

Static recompilation of **Super Mario Kart** (SNES, 1992) from WDC 65C816 assembly to
native C, built on [snesrecomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/snesrecomp) and playable on
modern hardware via SDL2.

Follows the recomp house style shared with snesrecomp, lynxrecomp, xboxrecomp,
ps3recomp and pcrecomp: the toolkit lives in its own repo, generated code is
never committed, and every build runs headless.

## Status

**Alpha. Unversioned.** **Playable end-to-end.** A cold boot walks the authentic flow from controller input —
title → driver select → 50cc class / cup select → a live **Mode-7 race** — with a Dear
ImGui menu bar, save-states, configurable keyboard + gamepad controls for two players, and
**lockstep netplay**. The SNES hardware (PPU Modes 0–7, SPC700 + DSP audio, DMA/HDMA, DSP-1
coprocessor) is fully emulated by the LakeSnes backend.

Two execution paths share the same backend: **real-frame mode** (the default) runs the
genuine ROM through LakeSnes's cycle-accurate frame, so the whole game plays today; the
**recompiled-shell path** (`SMK_SHELLS=1`) runs hand-written `RECOMP_PATCH` functions and is
where the static-recompilation work grows incrementally. Recompiled functions are defined
with `RECOMP_PATCH(name, snes_addr) { ... }` and auto-register in snesrecomp's dispatch table
at static-init time — adding a translated function is a one-line change, no central list.

### What works
- **Full authentic flow from controller input** — title → driver select → 50cc class / cup
  select → Mode-7 race, all driven by the genuine ROM's state sequencer (`$81:E000`)
- **Mode-7 race** rendering + gameplay: perspective track, karts, HUD, lap timer, split-screen
- **Dear ImGui menu** overlaying the game — File / Graphics / Sound / Controller / Multiplayer / Help
- **Save-states** — File → Save/Load (and F5/F8), full machine state via LakeSnes; File → New resets
- **Configurable input** for **both players** — rebind keyboard *and* Xbox-style gamepad per button
- **Lockstep netplay** (TCP) with input-delay buffering — host/join, save-state sync on connect,
  deterministic in-sync emulation (verified by matching WRAM checksums)
- Full boot chain: reset vector → hardware init → WRAM 0x55 fill → PPU/APU/DSP-1 setup → Mode-7 tables
- Custom tile/tilemap decompressor (`$84:E09E`) — all 7 compression modes + E0+ extended counts
- Joypad/auto-joypad input with edge detection; real palettes ROM → CGRAM; per-scanline HDMA
- LakeSnes renders all PPU scanlines per frame; SDL2 window (3× scale by default), 60 fps, audio

What's next: [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).

## Screenshots

![Title Screen](docs/screenshots/newtitle.png)

The full menu flow runs from controller input — title → driver select → class/cup select:

![Driver Select](docs/screenshots/charselect.png)

![Class / Cup Select](docs/screenshots/class.png)

The Mode-7 race renders and plays — perspective track, karts, HUD, split-screen:

![Mode-7 Race](docs/screenshots/race.png)
![Mode-7 Race 2](docs/screenshots/race2.png)

**Lockstep netplay** — two machines run the same deterministic emulation in sync (host =
Player 1, client = Player 2), starting from a shared save-state:

![Multiplayer netplay](docs/screenshots/mp.png)

## Getting Started

A one-click `Setup.cmd` is not written yet ([ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md)). Step by step, on
Windows:

1. Install the prerequisites:
   - Visual Studio 2022 (or its Build Tools) with *Desktop development with C++*
   - CMake 3.16+ (bundled with Visual Studio; `cmake --version` in a Developer prompt)
   - Git
   - SDL2 through vcpkg: `vcpkg install sdl2:x64-windows`
   - Python 3.10+ only for the tools (`py --version`; if `python` opens the Microsoft
     Store, use `py`)
2. Clone with submodules (snesrecomp and LakeSnes are submodules; without
   `--recursive` CMake stops at `add_subdirectory(ext/snesrecomp)`):
   ```
   git clone --recursive https://github.com/sp00nznet/mk.git
   cd mk
   ```
3. Configure and build:
   ```
   cmake -B build -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64 -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=C:/vcpkg/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake
   cmake --build build --config Release
   ```
4. Copy `SDL2.dll` from `C:/vcpkg/installed/x64-windows/bin` next to
   `build/Release/smk_launcher.exe` (vcpkg usually does this for you).
5. Supply your own ROM: the US v1.0 cartridge dump, MD5 `7f25ce5a283d902694c52fb1152fa61a`.
   It is not included and never will be.
6. Run it:
   ```
   build/Release/smk_launcher.exe "Super Mario Kart (USA).sfc"
   ```
   The console prints `smk: REAL-FRAME mode (full LakeSnes execution)` and the title
   screen appears.

## Usage

```
smk_launcher.exe <rom.sfc>                              play (real-frame mode, the default)
smk_launcher.exe <rom.sfc> --headless --record out.mp4  no window; frames piped to ffmpeg
SMK_SHELLS=1 smk_launcher.exe <rom.sfc>                 the recompiled-shell path
```

By default the launcher runs in **real-frame mode**: the genuine ROM via LakeSnes's
cycle-accurate frame, so menus *and* the Mode-7 race play at full speed. The
recompiled per-frame shells (`SMK_SHELLS=1`) can't yet drive the race's multi-frame
setup; as gameplay functions are recompiled they take over.

Headless runs take snesrecomp's capture variables, for example
`SNESRECOMP_SHOT_FRAMES=600 SNESRECOMP_EXIT_FRAME=610` (screenshot at frame 600, then
exit). The full list is in snesrecomp's `docs/runtime.md`.

### Controls

Default Player 1 keyboard (rebindable in the menu):

| Key | SNES Button |
|-----|-------------|
| Arrow keys | D-pad |
| Z | B |
| X | Y |
| A | A |
| S | X |
| Q | L |
| W | R |
| Enter | Start |
| Right Shift | Select |
| F5 / F8 | Save / Load state |
| Escape | Quit |

**Gamepads** (Xbox-style, via SDL_GameController) work out of the box for both
players — A→B, B→A, X→Y, Y→X, shoulders→L/R, Back→Select, Start→Start, d-pad and
left stick steer. Rebind any of it in **Controller** (P1/P2 tabs).

### Menu

A Dear ImGui menu bar (modelled on [LinksAwakening](https://github.com/sp00nznet/LinksAwakening))
overlays the game:

- **File** — New (reset/restart), Save / Load state (`smk_state.sav`; also **F5 / F8**),
  Settings ▸ (save/load `smk_config.ini`), Quit
- **Graphics** — window scale, V-Sync, texture filter, scanlines, show FPS
- **Sound** — master volume, mute
- **Controller** — rebind keyboard **and** gamepad for **Player 1 and Player 2**
- **Multiplayer** — Host / Join (IP:port), input-delay, connection status — lockstep netplay
- **Help → About** — links back to this repository

The menu auto-disables in headless/scripted runs (`SMK_HEADLESS`/`SMK_SCRIPT`).

## Building from source

As in Getting Started. Optional: `src/recomp/smk_autogen.c`, the cycle-accurate
routines generated from your ROM by `tools/recomp/autogen.py`, is built in when present
(see [docs/autogen.md](docs/autogen.md)). The netlab farm cross-builds with mingw-w64
(`projects/mk.env` in recomp-netlab).

## Documentation

- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md): layers, project structure, the decompressor, ROM details, references.
- [docs/autogen.md](docs/autogen.md): generating `smk_autogen.c` locally.
- [docs/smk_flow_re.md](docs/smk_flow_re.md): reverse-engineering the menu → race flow.
- [docs/own_recompiler_design.md](docs/own_recompiler_design.md), [docs/recomp_frame_model_plan.md](docs/recomp_frame_model_plan.md), [docs/mode7_track_fix_plan.md](docs/mode7_track_fix_plan.md), [docs/mstan_recompiler_spike.md](docs/mstan_recompiler_spike.md): design notes.
- [docs/history.md](docs/history.md): milestones before the changelog.

## Contributors

See [CONTRIBUTORS.md](CONTRIBUTORS.md). Contributions: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Legal

This project contains no Nintendo copyrighted material. The ROM is not included and
must be legally obtained. Source generated from the ROM (`smk_autogen.c`) is never
distributed: you generate it on your own machine. BizHawk, snes9x and Mesen are run only
as separate black-box references to compare output against; none of their code is here.

## License

MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). snesrecomp, LakeSnes and Dear ImGui carry their own
licences (see `ext/snesrecomp/NOTICE`).

008f228a6fab54d310eca696d67dbcbb9be4aeaa.message:
Follow-up to #211: a clipped vertex sits exactly on its plane

After the lerp the new vertex is wherever the arithmetic lands. With w
from -168 to 415 (@apexJCL's numbers) or in the 1e4s, the rounding is
bigger than NV_CLIP_W and w can come out <= 0, which the divide turns
into inf/NaN. Plane 0 now sets w = NV_CLIP_W and the near plane sets
z = c[59].z * w.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

00e951847512d507a23afa029c481f558b2f5315.message:
fix(recomp): derive OF and PF for integer flag consumers

jo/jno after adc, sbb, neg and the shifts by one, and jp/jnp after adc,
sbb, neg and the shifts, had no rule and lifted to the never-taken
_flags. Worse, add's jl/jge/jle/jg read SF alone, wrong whenever the sum
overflowed, and 8/16-bit sub rebuilt its left operand at 32 bits, so
"sub al, bl; jl" with al = 0x80 did not branch.

_overflow_flag stays the one OF derivation and now covers adc/sbb (OF
captured into _fb before the write, as inc/dec do), neg, and shl, shr
and sar by one. PF is the parity of the snapshotted result. The signed
conditions after the result setters are SF != OF from those. neg's
jbe/ja are constants. A function whose jo or signed condition reads
shl's OF declares _cf.

(cherry picked from commit cd2c7f236d298707fe6dd6526dc918e527157c9e,
with shl's OF from 19a791b; imul's flags go with the product fix)

01064f3b57e58f40635af3904c12ecf928066b09.message:
lifter: lift FCMOVcc instead of leaving it as a comment

The eight x87 conditional moves fell through _lift_fpu to the
`/* FPU: ... */` catch-all, so the move never happened. MSVC compiles
float min/max to `fld a; fld b; fcom st(1); fnstsw ax; test ah, 1;
fcmove st(0), st(1); fxch st(1); fstp st(0)`, and without the move
min(x, 1.0) always returned 1.0 and max(x, 0.0) always 0.0. Jet Set
Radio Future clamps its screen-fade colors that way: the fade went back
to zero every frame and the boot never left its first logo.

In lift_basic_block each FCMOVcc now reads the tracked flags through the
jcc with the same condition code (fcmovb/jb, fcmove/je, fcmovbe/jbe,
fcmovu/jp and the negated forms) and emits `if (cond) st(0) = st(i);`.
Without a tracked setter it falls back to `_flags`, as cmovcc does.
tools/recomp/test_lifter_fcmov.py covers the MSVC min idiom, every form
with a non-st(1) source, the parity forms and the fallback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

01786c25be2195d119290ba9c30f74c16fd79b72.message:
disasm: a function packed straight after a switch table is a function

MSVC parks a function's jump table after its last ret, aligned with int3
or `mov edi, edi`, and the linker packs the next function straight after
the table. Nothing marks that start. The int3 boundary pass finds a table,
not a ret, in front of it; the gap-prologue pass looks only after a ret;
and a function whose address is only ever stored into a callback slot is
reached by no call or jmp. A frameless callback packed after a four-entry
table is that shape, and it needed a hand seed.

_pass_jump_table_followers starts a function at the first byte past a
measured table and anything packed after it: padding, further dword
tables (including ones under resync_jump_tables' 3-entry minimum that a
`jmp [reg*4 + disp]` still names), and byte index tables. The start must
be in a gap (a table in the middle of a function is followed by more of
that function), not a switch arm, not a byte below 0x0F (every index
table starts with small arm numbers, no function does), not inside an
instruction decoded from before the table unless it probes as a prologue,
and must probe as a body.

The engine now records byte tables read through an index (`movzx/movsx
r, byte ptr [r + disp]`, MSVC's two-level switch), and index_table_length
reads their length off the `cmp reg, N; ja` in front of the load. Without
that bound an index table is sized by walking bytes below the arm count,
which is safe for 16 arms or fewer; a larger walk also stops at a frame
setup or a known start, and is trusted only when padding or another table
follows it.

This leaves the inline jump-table arm lifting from #173 as it is, and the
`mov edi, edi`-before-a-table check in the gap-prologue pass from #182.

Tests: test_jump_table_follower.py (the follower; a two-level switch's
index table, with and without a bound; a switch arm after its table and a
table inside a function give no follower; the small-opcode guard; a decode
from before the table vetoes the follower; padding before a table is not
a

04107347a83b3e6583e8b9dd7d2c4fc3c2df2722.message:
nv2a: RECOMP_RASTER_THREADS splits raster rows on POSIX too

RECOMP_RASTER_THREADS existed and was documented but silently did nothing on POSIX

Measured on an Apple M4 with full-screen quads: 110 Mpx/s on one thread,

08e727f61fb2c53067747b392395404877e07707.message:
devices: decode trapped x86-64 MMIO on Linux, so OHCI and the APU work there

#191 added trapped MMIO on POSIX for arm64 only and left it out on x86-64:
both devopt hooks were compiled to "no decoder on this host", so the OHCI
aperture stayed plain memory and a title found no controller.

This is the x86-64 twin of mmio_decode_a64.h. The fault arrives the same
way, as SIGSEGV/SIGBUS with si_addr and a ucontext; the decoder reads the
instruction at RIP, works out direction, width and register, performs the
access through the callbacks and advances RIP past it. si_addr supplies the
address, so the ModRM/SIB work is there to get the instruction length right
(a wrong advance is an immediate crash loop). RIP-relative disp32 is decoded
for its length too.

Forms covered: MOV 88/89 8A/8B, moffs A0-A3, MOVZX 0F B6/B7, MOVSX 0F BE/BF,
MOV r/m,imm C6/C7, MOVD/MOVQ 0F 6E/7E, MOVUPS/MOVAPS 0F 10/11. Anything else
returns 0 and names the RIP and the first eight opcode bytes once per unique
opcode, rather than stepping an instruction it did not understand.

The Windows half of each file is untouched: both call sites still call
mmio_emulate() with a CONTEXT. Only the POSIX branch picks an arch decoder,
and the dispatcher in xbox_memory_layout.c (APU, AC'97, OHCI) now accepts
Linux x86-64 alongside Linux arm64.

tests/usb_ohci_posix was skipping on anything but arm64. It now runs its
assertions on x86-64 Linux: the aperture faults, the decoder answers, an
8-byte read is split into two register reads, and nothing falls through to
the crash path (0 undecoded accesses).

Tested with: tests/usb_ohci_posix on Linux x86-64 (all assertions pass);
full library build on Linux x86-64 and with mingw-w64 for Windows; a title

0bd4b297ffde5bd9dd457c777b115e6e6b2b6776.message:
kernel files: drop a directory search when its handle closes on POSIX

The Win32 backend has released a search on NtClose since a4e0f36; the
POSIX backend kept its own table and never did. Its handles are heap
objects, and the allocator hands a freed one straight back, so a search
abandoned after one result (FindFirstFile, then FindClose) resumed under
the next directory opened: its first answer came from the old directory.
Without reuse, abandoned searches filled the 64-slot table instead.

xbox_dir_context_drop now exists on POSIX too and NtClose calls it after
settling a pending overwrite and before CloseHandle, so the freed handle
value can't be handed out while its search is still in the table. The
handle is still closed once; closedir only closes the search's own stream.

kernel_fatx_overwrite runs 300 searches over 8 directories, each closed
after one result, before its overwrite and rename checks. On macOS it
was 100/300 fresh before (handle value reused 298 times), 300/300 after.

14dc2f461ccfd01d36cd98aa5565a1ccc4d7474a.message:
disasm: an immediate naming a body that tail-calls a known function is a function

Every C++ EH handler thunk is `mov eax, <FuncInfo>; jmp
__CxxFrameHandler`, and the function's SEH prologue pushes its address as
an immediate. The imm-ref pass takes a closed callback body, a vcall
thunk, or a target that is itself a jmp with a provable tail, and these
are none of those: the body has no ret, and its jmp is the second
instruction. Frameless `return f(...)` wrappers taken by address have the
same shape. Unfound, each became an unresolved stub.

The pass now also accepts a straight-line body whose walk ends in a
direct jmp to the exact start of a function already built. A stray jmp
decoded out of data almost never lands precisely on a function start, so
the destination is the corroboration the missing ret would have been. A
jump that lands anywhere else is still refused, and so is a walk that
crossed int3: it started in alignment padding and ran into the function
after it.

The engine's probes_as_returning_body walk is shared with a new
probe_tail_call, which reports where such a body tail-jumps.

Tests: test_tail_call_thunks.py (an EH thunk named by an
immediate is found; a tail jump into the middle of a function is refused;
an immediate naming the int3 padding before a thunk is refused).

19871ddc1324e0b448cb4e94ed89608b86a69078.message:
disasm: the gap sweep leaves alias bodies whole

The past-padding gap sweep (#239) counted only function bodies as covered,
so a method reached only through a vtable, still an alias entry when the
sweep runs, looked like a gap. In one title such a method opens with
`sub esp, 0x104` after a ret and padding, so the sweep made it a
gap_prologue start, and the build then cut it at a weak
immediate-reference start on one of its own switch arms. Three of the four
arms fell outside the body, and the dispatch lifted as an indirect tail
jump that missed at run time with the frame still on the stack. The same
blind spot split out-of-line loop tails, reached only by an alias's jcc,
into new functions, so each jcc became a call.

The sweep now counts each alias's measured body, clamped at the next
function start, as covered, and never makes an alias address a gap start.
A gap alias that tail jumps forward within its gap covers the target, so
the sweep leaves that target to be lifted inline through the alias, as
before the sweep; any call, table word or immediate naming it still makes
it a start.

1a8299f0174dbe8e5a0b2ef7786cd1824dcbde49.message:
feat(video): show the PVIDEO overlay in the framebuffer window

PVIDEO is the NV2A's video overlay: the GPU scales a YUY2 buffer from
guest memory over the framebuffer at scanout, behind an optional colour
key. Bink's Xbox player shows movies this way, so with nothing scanning it
out a movie left the screen on whatever the framebuffer last held.

- pvideo_scanout.h converts a pending bank to RGB and draws it at its
  output rectangle and scale, honouring the colour key. It refuses banks
  that are not pending, a stopped overlay, formats other than YUY2, and an
  image larger than the bytes it is given.
- The window thread takes a snapshot of PVIDEO's registers and, for each
  pending bank, copies the image, draws it, and clears the bank's bit in
  BUFFER, which is what the title waits on before reusing the memory. The
  copy is kept and drawn again until the next frame or STOP, since the
  title may overwrite the original once the bank is handed back.
- nv2a_hook_init makes the PVIDEO register page fault, so a title's
  writes reach the register model rather than the plain memory behind the
  aperture. It does so only there, because only a title that installs the
  hook routes those faults. The page's accesses and the scanout's snapshot
  share a lock.

Midtown Madness 3's startup movies were played and frame-captured through
this path before its fork moved to a D3D11 presenter.

tests/nv2a_pvideo adds the scanout (white, black and blue converted and
placed 1:1, rows doubled at half DT_DY, the colour key, each refusal) and
consume (bank 0 handed back leaves bank 1 pending).

1c9630f2bd890b693465f739cfb016e727798124.message:
posix: HANDLEs are table indices, not object pointers

A HANDLE was the w32_object pointer itself, so nothing could tell a real
object from any other pointer. The Ke* layer casts a dispatcher object
straight across -- `HANDLE hObject = (HANDLE)Object` in
KeWaitForSingleObject -- and under the pointer scheme that cast was
accidentally well-typed: wait_single() took the guest KEVENT's address for
a w32_object and locked its `lock` field. Burnout 3 dies there before the
title screen, faulting at 0x35F464 in pthread_mutex_lock, eight bytes into
the guest object at 0x35F45C. Win32 fails such a call and the kernel is
written against that; only POSIX dereferenced it.

A handle is now HTAB_TAG | (slot + 1) * 4 into a table of live objects. The
tag is not decoration: a bare (slot + 1) * 4 makes the first handles 4 and
8, and the bridge turns any guest word it does not recognise into a HANDLE
by cast, so a title passing a small bogus value would land on a live object
and signal someone else's event. With the handle checkable, three callers
that trusted the lookup are guarded -- CloseHandle, DuplicateHandle and
WaitForSingleObject faulted where they should return ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE.

Two bugs the checkable handle then exposed, both silent before:

  Ke*BasePriorityThread take a PKTHREAD, and the bridge passed
  XBOX_TO_NATIVE(object) -- a native pointer into guest memory that was
  never a thread handle. Every set did nothing and every query answered 0.
  The bridge now resolves the object to the handle that owns it, inverting
  the token -> object map the handle table already shares an index with.

  WaitForMultipleObjectsEx polls each handle with a zero timeout, so an
  invalid one read as "not signalled": the call sat out its timeout and
  answered STATUS_TIMEOUT where Win32 fails, and a title that reads a
  timeout as "not yet" retries forever. It now rejects the whole call up
  front, as Win32 does.

GetTempPathA, CreateDirectoryA, RemoveDirectoryA, GetFileAttributesA and
DeleteFileA come with it, each normalising se

pb_exec: rasterise a batch's triangles together on the worker pool

The pool took only triangles of 8,192 pixels or more, which fits a menu's
full-screen passes and misses a 3D level entirely: thousands of small
triangles per frame, each drawn on the executor thread while the workers
slept. Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel's first level ran at 5 fps with the

run. Worker k owns rows y % n == k for every triangle of the run, in
submission order, so each pixel still sees its triangles in the order the
title drew them. A run below the old pixel threshold stays on the executor
thread. GPU state cannot change inside a batch, so drawing at the end reads
the same state; vertices are copied because near-plane clipping passes

2649f5f76fd42d3180d29498731041b0bfa3ea63.message:
disasm: recover blocks that alias bodies branch to

_pass_cond_branch_orphans registers a conditional branch's target in a gap
for function bodies only. Alias bodies are known only after the passes that
register them, so their own branches were never examined: a jump from an
alias into unclaimed bytes was lowered to an unresolved-target stub that pops
just a return address. The block never ran, and esp came back short by the
block's own ret N.

Jet Set Radio Future's graphics device wrapper hit it on every Init: a
dispatcher reached only through a vtable (a tail-jump alias, 0x00154D70)
branches on its argument to two blocks after its own `ret 0xc`.
_pass_gap_prologues had already made the first (0x00154D82) a function,
cutting the alias short, and the second (0x00154DAA) fell in the gap. The
call came back 12 bytes low and the imbalance travelled up through every
lifted caller until a constructor stored its result in the wrong slot.

_pass_alias_branch_orphans runs once all aliases are known, applies the same
acceptance test (executable, unclaimed, returning body or tail-jump block)
and repeats until nothing new turns up.

inline packet.

2ef5e29a28f80ddbe9a8de7084683e64f2c6459b.message:
input: mouse + keyboard as an opt-in virtual pad (RECOMP_MKB)

A hidden window on its own thread registers for raw input with
RIDEV_INPUTSINK, so mouse deltas and keys arrive regardless of which
window presents. The poll side turns mouse movement since the last
poll into a proportional stick deflection -- the title integrates
deflection over its frame, so total rotation tracks total mouse travel
at any frame rate -- and lifts small corrections over the game's own
deadzone (radial, tunable) so they are not eaten.

Merged into xbox_InputGetState, which both read paths go through: the
emulated USB pad and the kernel's XInput ordinals. Buttons OR on top of
a real pad; the mouse owns the aim stick while it moves; WASD owns
movement while held. The pointer is hidden and confined while
captured; capture only applies while the process is foreground; F9
toggles.

Off by default (RECOMP_MKB=1), like RECOMP_KEYBOARD: a keyboard
silently acting as player 1 is surprising when a real pad is what you
meant to use. Knobs: RECOMP_MKB_SENS/_DZ/_ACC/_FULL/_INVERT_Y/
_SWAP_STICKS, or an mkb.ini beside the exe.

Brought up against Black: the title reads its pad through the XDK USB
stack, and the layer's state reaches usb_gamepad_report unchanged.

2fb0b4461d43bd48bd2f677537b93da46732e53b.message:
kernel: run held-off interrupts at the lower to DISPATCH, and test IRQ progress

With the gate on, a lower from a device IRQL to DISPATCH kept the gate and
ran no safe point: the thunk's safe point comes before the bridge, still
at the old level, so an interrupt posted while the thread was above
DISPATCH waited for its next kernel call, and a guest that went on at
DISPATCH with no kernel call left it posted. The console takes it at the
lower; KfLowerIrql now does too. Without the gate nothing is ever posted
and the added safe point returns on its first load.

tests/irq_progress measures interrupt service and DPC completion with the
gate and RECOMP_GUEST_LOCK on and one guest thread, so no hand-off can be
what makes progress, and checks the guest CPU counted no turn, switch or
preemption. Its kernel calls go through the thunk dispatch, and a timer
stand-in runs the timer thread's drain (xbox_DpcDrainTimer, a seam over
kernel_drain_dpcs). It covers a spin at PASSIVE with no kernel call (ISR
at once off the guest thread, DPC on the timer thread while the guest
spins), a spin at DISPATCH with kernel calls (ISR at the next call, DPC
held until the lower), a spin at DISPATCH on back edges only (posted,
logged past RECOMP_IRQ_SAFE_MS, run at the first kernel call;
RECOMP_IRQ_SAFE_FORCE delivers beside the holder), and IRQL 26 (refused
safe points, run at the lower to DISPATCH).

disasm: a measured jump table stops in front of its byte index table

MSVC's two-level switch packs the byte index table straight after the
dword table. Its first four bytes are small arm numbers, and read as a
dword they are an address low in the section: `00 02 02 00` is
0x20200, inside a .text that starts at 0x11000. resync_jump_tables
took it as one more arm. A dispatcher `mov eax, [ecx+N] ;
jmp [eax*4+table]` whose real arms are other functions then had a
fourth arm nobody could prove, and the closed-CFG proof refused the
method; Jet Set Radio Future has nine such vtable methods.

The forward walk now stops at an address a movzx names as a byte table.
A fourth word nothing names still counts, as before.

3d7c5f8eb024b4443b4359a9bfaa7be9af66ee01.message:
nv2a: opt-in flip hold to the guest's 60 Hz vblank (RECOMP_FLIP_PACING)

The executor acknowledged FLIP_STALL as soon as the walker reached it. On
the console the swap's software method queues the flip for a vblank and
the vblank DPC releases the stall. Without that hold a title presents at
whatever rate the executor can draw (front-end menus run at 85 flips/s
and more), while its vblank runs at 60. A title that registers a frame
counter also saw it count twice once vblanks reach it (D3D's vblank DPC,
plus the per-flip bump), so video and loads timed on it ran fast.

RECOMP_FLIP_PACING=1 (=edge for D3D's rule, a late frame waits for the
next vblank). Unset or 0, flips complete at once and frame counters are
bumped on every flip, as on v0.14.0. On, it also selects the 60 Hz vblank
schedule (RECOMP_VBLANK=paced), since the tick's ~50 Hz would pace to 50.

- FLIP_STALL arms a hold until the guest vblank count reaches the
  previous flip's vblank plus the swap's interval (the NO_OPERATION
  software method 1 D3D pushes before it). While held, the ack loop walks
  nothing, leaves DMA_GET behind PUT and does not acknowledge the PFB
  flush. The vblank is sampled when the walk starts, so a frame drawn in
  time is not held for one more vblank. No hold outlasts 100 ms, and none
  is taken while the vblank count is not moving.
- A registered frame counter stays with the toolkit's per-flip bump until
  the title moves it itself 3 times within 500 ms (its own vblank DPC at
  60 Hz). A foreign writer slower than that never takes it: a move more
  than 500 ms after the first one counted starts the count again from
  itself. A counter the title owned that stops moving for 250 ms goes
  back to the per-flip bump. Both changes log a line, and
  xbox_FrameCounterBump is the pure rule.
- The swap (frame counter, present) is counted when the hold is armed,
  not when it is released.
- The periodic [GPU] report gains a flip hold line.

46aee91e6df7006383a93453f3f43d207cd9be57.message:
recomp: lift in/out to runtime port I/O, and model the field pin at 0x80C0

`in` and `out` were lifted as no-ops, so `in al, dx` left AL holding
whatever it held before. D3D's vblank ISR reads the video encoder's field
pin from MCPX GPIO port 0x80C0, bit 5, and stores its inverse in the
device's field word. With the stale AL that word was "odd" on every
vblank, so D3DDevice_GetDisplayFieldStatus always reported D3DFIELD_ODD.
The XDK XMV player starts its clock only on a field that is not odd, so
with RECOMP_VBLANK=1 it never decoded a first frame and never un-paused
its stream voices: Burnout 3 stays on the loading screen before its EA
intro movie for good, with no APU interrupt ever raised. Without vblank
delivery the ISR never runs, the word stays 0 ("even"), and the movie
plays, which is why this only shows once vblanks are delivered.

The lifter now emits xbox_PortIn/xbox_PortOut. The runtime answers
0x80C0 with bit 5 = parity of the vblank count once vblanks are counted,
and a per-read toggle before the first one or with RECOMP_VBLANK off; it
reads every other port as 0 and logs the first access to each port.
xbox_VblankCount is the count of vblanks raised.

49534721f4b1046883953d94383fa193e338bd68.message:
disasm: a byte index table is never a table entry

MSVC's two-level switch maps a sparse case value to a dense arm number
through a byte table, `movzx eax, byte ptr [eax + table]`, parked right
after the dword table. Its bytes are small arm numbers and they decode:
`00 02 02 00` is a run of adds, which can wander into a proven exit now
that indirect tails close a body. The word that names such a table is
the movzx's own displacement, scanned as a table word while the
function holding it is still an unclaimed gap.

_is_byte_table refuses an address the sweep recorded as a byte table
(byte_tables) or whose first byte is below 0x0F: `add`, `or` and the
segment pushes, which no function starts with, the rule
_pass_jump_table_followers already uses. It applies to the whole gap
branch of _pass_data_ptr_targets and to every entry the escaping proof
follows.

Jet Set Radio Future: eleven byte tables had become entries with the
previous commit (0xEC090, 0xFFB60, 0x11A1DC among them), and plain
v0.15.0 accepts eight on its own (0x20F04, 0x37434, 0xD7EA0, 0xE0A08,
0xF0D9C, 0x10C254, 0x112441, 0x115F88: byte tables, zero fill and nop
runs). All are refused.

Tests: test_table_entry_byte_tables.py.

4f3307f3692065ecb6ffd7b0e62bf21d97da6dcf.message:
kernel: RECOMP_CONTIG_AVOID_IMAGE keeps contiguous blocks out of the image

The window and the RAM the image sits in are separate storage here, so
a contiguous block placed at an image page gives one physical number
two meanings, and a device model holding only the number has to guess.
Darkwatch's XPP lost that guess both ways: a 1200 KB block at
0x0045C000 covered its .data control-transfer buffer, and its OHCI
descriptors, allocated inside the block, resolved to the image and
read back zero. The pad never enumerated.

With the switch set, the allocator first searches outside the image's
pages, as the console's kernel does, and falls back to them only when
nothing else fits (an image whose BSS runs past 48 MB). It is opt-in
because it moves every block above the image, and game glue names some
blocks by address. memory_regressions gains a mode for it.

Reported, diagnosed and first patched by @ranzo312-cyber in #127.

54331d13ae89716027f569afadb11fe5888a286f.message:
rtl: run critical sections on the guest's own bytes (RECOMP_CS_MODE=guest)

The shadow mode maps every guest lock onto a host CRITICAL_SECTION --
correct, and it costs a host Enter and Leave per call, which a title
whose loader locks per block parsed pays a million times over: the
profile through Black's level load was three quarters ntdll, the host
lock calls themselves (the lookup memo of 3119f33 had already taken the
table walk out).

This mode runs the lock where the bytes are. The Xbox layout is NOT the
NT one -- measured, by dumping what titles hand over at first use
(RECOMP_CS_DUMP): a 28-byte structure with the type/size header and a
self-linked LIST_ENTRY first, LockCount at +0x10 (not +0x04), Recursion
at +0x14, OwningThread at +0x18. A first implementation against the NT
offsets never engaged -- one lock classified in a whole run -- which is
also why it could not be wrong in an interesting way. The uncontended
Enter is one interlocked compare on the guest word and no host call at
all; contended waits sleep on a host semaphore, one per lock, memoised;
the owner field holds the taking thread's TIB address.

Structures that do not read as critical sections -- the XDK hands some
over as plain tokens; one measured as an empty list entry -- fall back
to the shadow, classified once per address on the first call. The fast
path's own writes keep its classification true, and a shadow address is
never written by it, so the two never mix on one lock.

Black's level load, same machine, same script: the sub-5-fps window
went from two samples (CS memo) to zero, and the run's minimum from
1.26 to 6.81 fps. Off by default; the shadow remains the conservative
answer.

5bb9e04fda7062c62fff12636fbe8791a6881986.message:
kernel: opt-in one-CPU DISPATCH gate, IRQs at safe points, 60 Hz vblank

On the console one CPU runs everything, and titles build their locks on
it: a thread at DISPATCH_LEVEL keeps every DPC and every other thread out,
and an interrupt preempts whatever runs and returns to it. Here threads
run in parallel and IRQL is only a number, so a DPC walked a list a thread
was relinking at DISPATCH and looped there, and an ISR ran beside the code
it should have frozen.

Everything below is opt-in. With none of the keys set the kernel behaves
as v0.14.0 does, RECOMP_VBLANK=1 included.

- RECOMP_DISPATCH_GATE=1: the raise to DISPATCH_LEVEL takes one
  process-wide gate and the lower gives it back. Queued DPCs run on the
  guest thread at its raise and at its release point, under the gate
  (RECOMP_DPC_ON_RAISE=0 leaves them to the timer thread). Device
  interrupts (APU, OHCI, vblank) are posted while the gate is held and run
  by the holder at its next safe point: a kernel call or a gate release
  (RECOMP_IRQ_SAFE_POINTS=0 brings back the bounded hold-off, keyed on the
  gate; RECOMP_IRQ_SAFE_FORCE / _MS bound how long a post may wait). A
  timer's DPC runs on the timer thread only while the gate is free and is
  queued otherwise. The configuration is read once (INIT_ONCE), since
  device threads and the title ask at boot at the same time, and the
  release point reads the pending word with a full barrier after leaving
  the gate, so a post that saw the gate held is not missed on arm64.
- RECOMP_VBLANK=paced (or the gate on top of any RECOMP_VBLANK): vblank
  runs on an absolute nanosecond 60 Hz schedule on a waitable
  high-resolution timer, honours PCRTC_INTR_EN_0 and PMC_INTR_EN_0, and
  the acknowledgement of the DPC's PCRTC write moves to its own thread, so
  a late DPC no longer loses the vblank to the NV2A ack loop. Plain
  RECOMP_VBLANK=1 keeps v0.14.0's tick (16 ms on GetTickCount64 checked
  on the timer thread's 10 ms sleep), which now logs its rate every 600
  vblanks and is otherwise unchanged. xbox_VblankMode

kernel: opt-in deferral of file I/O APCs to the next alertable wait

xbox_SetDeferredIoApc(1) queues ReadFileEx/WriteFileEx completions per
thread and runs them at the thread's next alertable user-mode wait
(NtWaitForSingleObject[Ex], NtWaitForMultipleObjectsEx,
KeDelayExecutionThread), which then returns STATUS_USER_APC without
waiting. That is what the hardware does.

of Steel needs the deferral: its streamer (sub_00038EE0) marks a slot
busy after ReadFileEx and waits alertably on the slot's event for the
completion routine to clear the flag. Inline, the routine ran before
the flag was set, the slot stayed busy, and the next wait never ended.

up on, and the existing comment records that deferral made no
difference to Halo. It should become the default once other titles
have been run with it.

nv2a: RECOMP_STRIP_ALT_WINDING, triangle strips keep one winding

The executor expands a triangle strip as (i, i+1, i+2) for every i, so
every odd triangle winds the opposite way to its neighbour. A strip on
hardware keeps one winding by taking the first two vertices of each odd
triangle swapped. A back end that culls from the render state's cull
registers, or lights two-sided from the winding, therefore drops or
back-lights every second triangle of every strip.

Opt-in, off by default: with RECOMP_STRIP_ALT_WINDING unset the strip order
is unchanged and no title's output moves. Both strip expansions read it
(the transform path and the screen-space indexed path).

second triangle's vertex order, run once without the switch (1 2 3) and
once with it (2 1 3). With the switch forced off in the source the second
run fails; with it working both pass.

nv2a_vsh and nv2a_combiner pass on Windows (MSVC);

6abde563468619fae38690cb3ceede23a3632fba.message:
apu: a new instance starts with the DSP ack fresh; shutdown frees the GP/EP state

mcpx_apu_init_standalone after a mcpx_apu_shutdown in the same process kept
state from the instance before it:
- The doorbell ack's GPRST gate and its configuration are file statics. A GP
  held in reset when the last instance went away left the new instance's ack
  paused, and RECOMP_APU_DSP_ACK was read once per process. mcpx_apu_dsp_init
  now resets the gate (the GP counts as running, as in a fresh process) and
  the cached setting, which the first poll reads again.
- Shutdown never freed the GP/EP DSP state that mcpx_apu_dsp_init allocates,
  about 160 KB per cycle. mcpx_apu_dsp_finalize frees both and clears the
  pointers; shutdown calls it after the frame thread has been joined, clears
  g_state before the teardown, and destroys the lock and condition variables.
- The interrupt delivery kept a process-wide "TIB allocated" flag for a
  thread-local fs base, so a new instance's frame thread (a new OS thread)
  called the guest ISR on another thread's TIB. The flag is now per thread
  (g_fs_base itself starts at the main thread's TIB on every thread).
  The interrupt line is also lowered at init, so a line left up by the last
  instance does not call the ISR against the new one.

A DirectSound play already in flight when shutdown starts is still not
serialised against it; that predates this change and is left for its own fix.

tests/apu_lifecycle: a GP held in reset, then shutdown and init, acks again;
the ack setting is read again per instance (off, then auto); four
init/shutdown cycles open and close the device once each, and the heap does
not grow between cycles (macOS and glibc allocator counts; skipped under ASan
and where the host has none). Before this change: 3 of 6 checks fail (the
heap grew 492 KB over three cycles). The interrupt path needs a connected
guest ISR and is not covered here.

Kept apart from the queue-period and pacing commit so a change in output can
be traced to one or the other.

6b8a7b4127c9c49d5c70a4f066a15c55c827ba0b.message:
fix(apu): a named heap page is RAM only for the named block's bytes

The APU decides per 4 KB page whether a physical number is RAM or the
contiguous window: a page MmGetPhysicalAddress named from a heap address
is RAM. A page is shared, though. In Def Jam: Fight for NY the six-channel
mix buffer (voices 0xF8-0xFA, a window allocation) ends 344 bytes into a
page whose next 3.7 KB are a heap block the title named. The whole page
read RAM, so the buffer's last 28 frames played whatever RAM held there on
every lap: step clicks at 32-sample slice edges, about two a second in the
opening scene (386-422 in 330 s at the device; the v0.13-based build, whose
allocator never put the two side by side, had 2).

Heap blocks now remember being named (set by xbox_PhysNoteRamName on the
live block holding the address, cleared whenever the block is handed out
or freed), and xbox_PhysRamNamedAt(pa) answers per byte: a named page
counts only for bytes inside a live named block. The page map stays the
fast first test, so an unnamed page costs what it did; bytes the heap
table does not place keep the page's answer. The APU's classifier and its
diagnostic class use it.

With it the opening scene has 1 click at the device in 330 s, voices F8
and FA 3 and 1. apu_phys gains the shared-page case (fails without the
change); apu_phys, memory_regressions, windows_guest_layout,
kernel_regressions and kernel_physical_address pass with MSVC.

7a8e7be99adf10bf5da2d5e58ac2f425944fe88a.message:
runtime: MMX helpers through SSE2 intrinsics on x86-64

The MMX helpers were a function call with a lane-at-a-time loop for what
is one instruction. Every XDK codec leans on MMX -- the XMV video
decoder's IDCT and motion compensation are almost nothing else -- so a
title playing its attract loop paid ten to fifty times the instruction
for each, and Black played its menu videos at a quarter speed with the
rasteriser idle.

On x86-64 SSE2 is part of the ABI, so each helper is now one intrinsic
over the value's 64 bits, carried in and out through MOVQ. The 64-bit
semantics are exact: a variable shift's count is the whole register and
the hardware saturates it at the lane width, which is the same zero-
lanes/sign-fill the scalar loop clamped to. PSHUFW, PINSRW and PEXTRW
stay scalar -- MSVC demands compile-time immediates for their
intrinsics, and the lifter does not guarantee one.

The one place the two forms differ in shape is the pack group: the MMX
form's result interleaves at dword granularity (a's saturation low, b's
high), where the XMM form lays a across the low half and b across the
high half of 128 bits. Packing each operand against itself and taking
a's low dword beside b's restores the MMX layout. The first cut read
the XMM form's low half alone, which zeroed half of every IDCT output
and drew Black's videos in green stripes -- tests/mmx_helpers pins the
whole set against an independent scalar reference (2.4M comparisons),
which is how that was found.

Black's menu/attract videos, measured over a 60 s window: median 28.9
fps from 8.1; the worst sample 18.5 from 4.9.

83864be0af542fc745a320ad38854194cd30e0a7.message:
rtl: the guest-bytes classification is the header word, not a memo

Three notes from the #222 review, fixed by moving the classification
into the lock itself:

- The direct-mapped memo could be evicted while another thread held the
  lock through the guest bytes; the next Enter then took the shadow path
  and the two guarded the same lock independently. The classification is
  now the initialiser's own header word at +0x00 (Type 1, Size 4) -- it
  cannot disagree with itself between threads, and the statically-zeroed
  claim writes the same marker before first use.
- xbox_cs_sem is probed and insert-only under one host lock: a slot is
  never re-keyed and creation is single-threaded, so two racing first
  callers cannot each make a semaphore and leave a waiter asleep on one
  while the releaser signals the other. Lookup never inserts; a fast lock
  always has its entry because the first waiter created it.
- Mode 2 no longer falls back to the single shared lock: the fast path
  owns the guest bytes of what it classified, everything else needs the
  per-address shadow that mode 0 provides. The 'single' banner now
  prints only for mode 1.

Smoke-tested on Black (RECOMP_CS_MODE=guest, the level loader's 637k
lock pairs): boots to gameplay, no CS reports, no deadlocks.

8627159ec3e797f7105adda8c08fe21fb95d0589.message:
perf(apu): lock voices individually, as xemu does

A title's VOICE_LOCK arrives through fe_method on the title's own thread.
It took d->lock, which the frame thread holds across every voice of a
frame, so each lock the title wrote waited until mixing had finished. In
Midtown Madness 3 that was about 9% of the game thread in a race.

Each voice now has a spinlock, held by the voice processor while it mixes
that voice and by voice_lock while it flips the voice's lock flag. A title
waits only while its own voice is being mixed. The flags become one byte
per voice, so no 64-bit atomic read-modify-write is needed.

Measured on the Midtown Madness 3 fork, against a baseline that already
handed d->lock over between voices (uncapped race, two runs each): 146
to 155 fps, p99 frame time 9.0 to 8.3 ms. The game's output showed no new
clipping, jumps or dropouts.

tests/apu_vp: with d->lock held, as the frame holds it, a VOICE_LOCK from
another thread completes; while voice 3 is being mixed, a lock on voice 3
waits until it is done. On main the first check fails.

8f6c290cf0c7bb9703088ec5d8625fd32afdd726.message:
kernel_path: match file names ignoring case on POSIX hosts

The Xbox's file systems ignore case and titles rely on it: a title asks for
D:\Data\movies\INTRO.bik where the disc has Movies/intro.bik. A POSIX host's
file system does not, so the open failed with "not found" and the title
carried on without the file.

On POSIX, after the guest path is translated, each component that is not
there as spelled takes the spelling of the one directory entry that
matches it ignoring case. A path that exists as spelled costs one lstat. A
component nothing matches (a file about to be created) and everything after
it stays as the title asked. Windows and macOS file systems are already
case-insensitive and are untouched (the code is in the POSIX half only, and
on macOS the first lstat succeeds).

Test: tests/kernel_path gets a POSIX-only section. A tree Data/Movies/intro.bik
is translated from the spellings Data\Movies\intro.bik (unchanged),
Data\movies\INTRO.bik, DATA\MOVIES\Intro.BIK (folded), data\movies\New.bin
(directories fold, the new file keeps its name) and Nope\Sub\x.bin (nothing
matches, unchanged).

Verified: on Linux x86-64 (gcc) the section passes with this change and three
checks fail with kernel_path.c at v0.16.0. kernel_directory_posix,
kernel_file_relative, kernel_fatx_overwrite and kernel_file_status pass on
Linux; kernel_path passes on Windows (MSVC), where the section is skipped.

9c526201e2dea310f863766bdbd4682f2f85b3f4.message:
runtime: the SSE float helpers as intrinsics, to match the MMX ones

The XMM helpers were lane-wise C loops over a union -- the same shape the
MMX helpers had before e67818c, and the XMV decoder's colour blit runs
its chroma half through them, so the float side of every converted frame
paid four times the operations of the instructions. On x86-64 the SSE
register file is native: the arithmetic, compare, min/max, unpack and
conversion helpers are one intrinsic each now, carried by loadu/storeu
for the full-lane forms and MOVQ for the lane-preserving ones
(cvtpi2ps/cvtps2pi keep the destination's upper lanes, which the scalar
versions did by construction).

XMM_CMP_PRED switches over the eight named predicate intrinsics rather
than taking _mm_cmp_ps's immediate through a parameter -- MSVC rejects a
runtime immediate, the same reason PSHUFW stayed scalar in the MMX
conversion. XMM_SHUFFLE stays scalar for the same cause. The compares'
NaN semantics are the hardware's: EQ/LT/LE/ORD false and UNORD/NEQ/
NLT/NLE true on unordered, which the scalar switch matched, and MINPS/
MAXPS pass the second source through bit-exact on NaN. recomp_cmp_pred
is shared again rather than sitting in the #else: the lifter emits it
directly for scalar cmpss, and a first link failed on exactly that.

tests/xmm_helpers pins the set against an independent scalar reference:
3,385,850 comparisons over random registers and a pool of NaN payloads,
denormals, signed zeros and conversion edges -- zero divergences, with
the two NaN-payload cases arithmetic never pinned (both forms pick a
source operand; the intrinsics pick the one real addps did) counted
separately rather than failed.

Black's movies, which run the blit every frame: peak 35.1 fps from
29.9 on the same scenes.

a87818d11e735ef4aeffcd8ab9b79de7b89c7b07.message:
d3d8 combiners: compile once per HLSL text, no lookup while unchanged

The combiner shader cache is keyed by the whole NV2ACombinerState, and that
includes the constant colours (c0, c1, final_c0, final_c1), which the
generated HLSL never contains: it reads them from the constant buffer by
index. So every new constant colour was a new state and another D3DCompile
at O3 of a text already compiled. A title that fades or tints through a
combiner constant compiles during play, and past 128 such states the LRU
eviction compiles the same text again. In Def Jam: Fight for NY one scene
made 212 combiner states with 10 distinct texts, one text 201 times.

- compile_combiner_shader keeps one shader per distinct text (up to 256),
  with its own reference, so a state-cache eviction cannot release a shader
  another state shares. Each compile logs a line with the reuse count.
  RECOMP_PS_TEXT_CACHE=0 compiles every state as before.
- d3d8_combiners_prepare_draw reuses the entry the last lookup returned
  until the state is dirty again. The parsed state changes only when dirty
  and the cache only during a lookup, so that lookup would have returned
  the same entry; its LRU stamp is updated as a hit would.

WARP, MSVC 19.29 (tests/d3d8_smoke/test_combiner_reuse.c, new): 20
constant-only variants 85 ms of compiling -> 4.5 ms (one compile); the
lookup a draw with unchanged state no longer makes costs 1.1 us (hash and
compare of the 1,396-byte state). The test also checks that 200 such
variants share one shader through an eviction, that a different text gets
a different shader, and that prepare_draw binds what the lookup gives.
d3d8_a8, d3d8_states_smoke and d3d8_smoke pass.

disasm: table entries that close through proven exits outside their gap

Since the closed-CFG check (#179), a table word in a gap had to reach a
ret inside that gap, or be a bare vcall thunk. Jet Set Radio Future's
vtables name 103 methods that do neither, every one 16-byte aligned
behind padding, and three of them stopped its attract demo on an
unresolved indirect call:

  * 89 guarded virtual-call tails: `test eax, eax ; je done ; ... ;
    mov eax, [ecx] ; jmp [eax+N]`. An indirect jmp that is not a
    measured table refused the body, and the guard in front keeps
    probes_as_vcall_thunk from matching.
  * 9 dispatchers into other methods: `mov eax, [ecx+N] ;
    jmp [eax*4+table]`, whose arms are function starts outside the gap.
  * 8 error paths that leave by a direct jmp, after a jcc, to a helper
    nobody has found yet. _probes_as_tail_body follows only the first
    straight block, which ends at the ret in front of that jmp.

The proof is still a closed CFG. probes_as_callback_body gains two
things: a switch arm outside the gap is an exit when it is a proven
entry, and an `escapes` out-set collects the destinations of direct
branches that leave the gap for unproven code, counting the edge as an
exit so the caller can prove each destination on its own. The default
(escapes=None) refuses as before. allow_indirect_tails="mem" takes an
indirect tail only through a memory operand, a vtable slot or a
function-pointer field, never `jmp reg`.

_pass_data_ptr_targets tries _probes_as_escaping_body after the plain
probe and the vcall thunk: the body is proven with memory tails and
escapes, and every escape is proven the same way in its own gap, to a
depth of 8. A destination inside a known body refuses.

On JSRF this recovers 104 of the 113 (the rest wait on the byte index
tables of the next commits) and all three demo addresses. The
immediate pass and cc_boundary are untouched, and the engine's default
for an unresolved indirect jump (test_callback_cfg) still refuses.

b21a4deed906544d58162247a80c9f13e0a4ee36.message:
nv2a: RECOMP_TEX_BILINEAR and RECOMP_TEX_ANISO, opt-in CPU texture filtering

The CPU rasteriser takes the nearest texel whatever SET_TEXTURE_FILTER
asked for, so a floor or wall seen at a slant aliases and shimmers.

RECOMP_TEX_BILINEAR=1 blends the four nearest texels of every textured
pixel. RECOMP_TEX_ANISO=8 or 16 takes up to that many bilinear taps along
the longer of the pixel's two texel gradients and implies bilinear; any
other value leaves it off. Both are off by default and read once per
process, so with neither set every title draws exactly as before.

All three sampling paths take them:
- raster_triangle (pixel-position batches): the gradients are constant over
  a triangle, so the footprint is worked out once per triangle.
- the perspective path without combiners (xf_rows): the gradient is the
  coordinate one pixel right and one pixel down minus the coordinate here,
  so it stays perspective-correct. XfTri gains dl[3][2], the barycentric
  step per pixel, to evaluate them.
- the register-combiner stages (rc_texel, rc_stage_fetch): the same
  neighbour coordinates. rc_texel's existing tent blend moves into rc_tent
  so the title's own tent request and the aniso taps share it.

No mip levels: a minified texture is averaged along its stretched axis
only. GPU back ends have their own filtering and are not affected.

Test: tests/nv2a_tex_filter, one process per mode (nearest, bilinear,
aniso8, aniso16) on each of the three paths, 12 CTest cases. A two-texel
ramp checks the blend; a stripe texture of three texels to a pixel checks

b3c90cf55491ed11e8acd60f72093d3780ddad70.message:
lifter, runtime: x87 trig reduces with the 66-bit pi

fsin, fcos, fsincos and fptan lifted to libm inside
recomp_fp_trig_in_range. libm reduces with the exact pi; the x87 reduces
modulo pi/4 with a 66-bit pi, so above pi/4 it returns f(x * pi / pi66).
At 1e10 the two cosines differ in the 11th digit, and the x87's fsin(pi)
is 1.2246063538223773e-16, not libm's 1.2246467991473532e-16. A title
that runs sin() on an accumulated, never-wrapped angle drifts from libm
that way on a Pentium III, so the recompiled one has to drift too.

recomp_fp_trig_in_range stays the gate: it sets C2 and leaves st0 alone
for |x| >= 2^63, and the push in fsincos and fptan stays inside it. Inside
it the lifts now call recomp_x87_sin/cos/sincos/tan, which apply the
66-bit shift to libm's sin and cos by angle addition (versine form, one
rounding) and return libm's own value at |x| <= pi/4, where the hardware
does no reduction. Below |x| ~ 1.16e13 the shift costs no libm call beyond
the other one of the pair.

Tests: tests/x87_trig (ctest) runs each op as lifted, range check
included, against vectors from an mpmath model (model.py, not built;
worst error a third of the conformance tolerance) and two values measured
on hardware, checks C2 and the push out of range and the CRT's
`fsin; fnstsw ax; sahf; jp` / fprem1 loop through recomp_fprem; a second
build with plain libm must fail it. test_lifter_x87_trig.py checks the
emitted calls and compiles a lifted `fsin; fnstsw ax; sahf; jp` plus
fsincos/fptan, with plain libm as the negative control. tools/conformance
gains the trig operands (1e10 to 2^62, pi, 355, 2^63 and up, inf, NaN),
fsincos, and C2 read through fnstsw and through sahf.

apu: starvation reports add up small losses; switches parse =0; reset diagnostics

The RECOMP_AUDIO_HOST starvation check raised its reference
(deficit_max) on every small rise of the deficit, so a loss that arrived
in pieces below the jitter threshold was absorbed and never reported:
twenty 5 ms gaps reported nothing while one 100 ms gap reported 96 ms.
The reference now moves to the deficit only when a loss is reported, and
a loss counts only once the device has run dry (the backend's underrun
count rose): without a dry spell a rising deficit is the device's clock
(SDL's dummy driver runs about 3% slow) and the reference follows it as
before. After a dry spell it creeps at most 200 ppm, so real device
drift is not added to a pending loss; the 250 ms settle window after
each baseline covers backend staging at start. On a clock further off
than 200 ppm (the dummy driver) each dry spell can over-report by about
a buffer, and a single loss under one buffer is absorbed; real devices
sit well inside. The queue is read before the submit, as it was: both
backends count an underrun only when a poll sees the queue empty, and a
dry spell that starts mid-period gets no other poll. The frame-thread
idle rebase keeps drain and shutdown out of the count. A unit test
covers one large gap against many small ones of the same total, spaced
100 ms and 1 s apart, +-150 ppm drift over 600 s, a 3% fast or slow
clock that never runs dry, and a drain. apu_monitor runs with the three
switches =1, unset and =0, and each ctest says which to expect, so
reading =0 as on fails the off run.

The submission WAV records what the APU handed the backend, not what the
device played. The once-a-second line now reports wav/played sample
counts, starved_ms plus pending_ms (time the device inserted silence) and
refused submits; a refused buffer is in the WAV but never played, so
wav= counts every period handed over and refused= the ones dropped.

c18d741b67e27f168bfc0cb6ce68a14d29a8c404.message:
kernel files: Partition1\CACHE goes to <save>/TitleCache, not the game dir

The path table sent all of \Device\Harddisk0\Partition1 to the game dir
apart from UDATA and TDATA. E:\CACHE is the title's own scratch, and it
writes there: Burnout 3 opens CACHE\LocalCache00.bin and LocalCache08.bin
with FILE_OPEN_IF, so every run wrote into the extracted game files, and
all save dirs shared one cache.

CACHE now has its own rule beside UDATA and TDATA: it goes to
<save_dir>/TitleCache, or under RECOMP_SAVE_DIR when that is set. The
folder is not named CACHE because Z: and Partition3-5 (the cache
partitions behind X:, Y: and Z:) already map to <save_dir>/Cache, and on
a case-insensitive host (Windows, Proton, macOS) the two names are one
folder, where the title's files would mix with the utility-drive caches
and could collide by name.

The rest of Partition1 stays in the game dir, since a title may read its
assets through it (Wreckless links Z: to Partition1\). The rule stops at
a path boundary like the other two, so Partition1\cached.dat and CACHEX\
stay in the game dir. The fallback that keeps saves found only in the
game dir does not apply to CACHE: keeping a cache there would be the very
write this stops, and the title rebuilds it. That fallback now picks its
rule by the whole folder name, since TitleCache starts with the same
letter as TDATA.

The "Path init" log line now says "user data=" where it said
"udata/tdata=", since that root holds TitleCache as well; anything that
greps the log for the old text needs the new one.

tests/kernel_path (both backends): CACHE under the save dir and under
RECOMP_SAVE_DIR, Burnout 3's lower-case spelling, the bare directory, a
title link to Partition1\, xbox_path_tree, names that only start with
CACHE/UDATA/TDATA, E:\CACHE and Z:/Partition3/Partition5 in different
folders ignoring case, and the cache leaving the game dir next to legacy
UDATA and TDATA saves. With v0.14.0's kernel_path.c 10 checks fail.

lifter: model MXCSR; CVTSS2SI/CVTSD2SI round by its RC

STMXCSR and LDMXCSR fell to RECOMP_UNIMPL, so a store of MXCSR wrote
nothing. Jet Set Radio Future stores MXCSR every frame and refuses to run
a routine unless the rounding control says nearest; the check read
whatever that memory held. MXCSR is now TLS guest state (g_mxcsr, reset

the host's MXCSR is untouched.

range. recomp_cvt_si32 rounds by MXCSR.RC (the x87 encoding, so through
recomp_frndint), truncates for the CVTT forms, and returns the integer
indefinite for NaN, infinities and out-of-range values. CVTSD2SI from an
xmm register now reads the double lane.

c7a18177037d4fe74d1a581bd04087f390e72d14.message:
tools/recomp: opt-in preemption point at loop back edges (--back-edge-yield)

A guest loop that spins on another guest thread's flag and makes no
kernel call never gives the guest CPU back, so under RECOMP_GUEST_LOCK the
thread it waits for never runs. On the console the timer interrupt ends
its quantum. With --back-edge-yield the lifter emits RECOMP_BACK_EDGE(va)
before every goto that jumps backwards within a function: one relaxed
atomic load of g_xbox_guest_cpu_preempt (RECOMP_LOAD_RELAXED32:
__atomic_load_n, or __iso_volatile_load32 on MSVC), and a hand-off when a
waiter has waited its quantum. With the lock off the flag never sets.

The edges are off by default, so the generated code is the same as
before: they cost code size and a load in every loop, and only the guest
CPU lock needs them. The DISPATCH gate does not; its interrupts and DPCs
run at kernel calls and gate releases.

c9c9701f79642b8b865268f7565fd031caade28e.message:
recomp: an MSVC offset frame owns a frame

MSVC biases ebp into a large frame so more locals fit in an 8-bit
displacement: push ebp; lea ebp,[esp-0x70]; sub esp,0x274; ...;
add ebp,0x70; leave. _func_owns_a_frame only knew "push ebp; mov ebp,
esp" and the SEH prolog helpers, so such a function never published
ebp across its calls. A setjmp called from one saved the caller's frame
(the lifted setjmp reads g_seh_ebp), and after longjmp the
"add ebp,N; leave" epilogue returned with esp moved. It showed in
libjpeg's error recovery inside D3DX's JPEG loader: a non-JPEG texture
longjmps out, the loader returns 0x90 bytes high, and D3DX spins forever
on a corrupted ebx.

_func_has_offset_frame recognises push ebp; lea ebp,[esp +/- N], and
_func_owns_a_frame counts it. Only functions with that prologue change:
they publish g_ebp/g_seh_ebp before calls, as a classic frame does.

#197's general-ebp change (publish g_ebp in every function that uses
ebp) would cover this too; it is not in v0.14.0, so this keeps the
narrower rule. If #197 lands, this helper becomes redundant there and
can go.

Tests: test_seh_frame_owner.py (the offset frame owns a frame; lea ebp
from another register does not).

nv2a: SET_TRANSFORM_CONSTANT words skip the general dispatch

A title that skins or animates on the GPU uploads shader constants by the
hundred thousand a frame: in Def Jam: Fight for NY's fights about 200,000
SET_TRANSFORM_CONSTANT words, 70% of the stream. Each went through every
early check in nv2a_pb_exec_method and the range ladder of its default case
before reaching nv2a_vsh_constant_word. For such a word the dispatcher does
three things: its one-time setup, the register file, and the constant store.
nv2a_pb_exec_constant_word does the last two and declines the word until the
setup has run; the walk's two dispatch sites send 0x0B80..0x0BFC on the 3D
subchannel to it first. note() still counts every word.

Fixture loop, constant words in 32-word runs: MSVC 19.29 /O2 7.1 -> 2.3 ns a
word, GCC 13 -O2 7.1 -> 3.7 ns. At 200,000 words a frame that is about 1 ms
of the executor thread's frame back.

d8611d83d484d7f2401342f67224c882a2f4e866.message:
kernel: setting the end of file or allocation on a read-only handle is denied

NT's I/O manager refuses FileEndOfFileInformation and
FileAllocationInformation on a handle opened without FILE_WRITE_DATA, with
STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED, before the file system sees the call. A title that
opens a save with GENERIC_READ to load it and then calls XAPI SetEndOfFile
at the end of what it read reached the host SetEndOfFile, which failed with
err=5, logged "SetEndOfFile failed" once per file, and returned
STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL. Allocation on such a handle returned success on
Windows and STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL on POSIX.

All three paths (Win32 end-of-file, Win32 allocation, POSIX end-of-file and
allocation) now answer STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED for a read-only handle without
calling the host. When the granted access cannot be read, the host call
still decides. A genuine host failure now reports the granted access and
the file's path, and ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED maps to STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED.

Test: kernel_fatx_overwrite opens a 3588-byte file to read, reads it, and
sets its end of file and allocation: both STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED and the file

  same reason -- the helper moves esp, so there is no push/sub to find.

  (3033a5e). A thunk into a member subobject or a global object loads
  `this` first -- `mov ecx, [ecx+8]` (0x00452AC0) or `mov ecx, [0x0080C1F0]`

  form. It now allows one leading this-adjustment (mov ecx, [ecx+N] /

dc586ee39ebed55ebfddd1dabf213666655cfc5d.message:
disasm, recomp: decode a code section up to its virtual end, not only its file bytes

Spartan: Total Warrior's D3DX section has raw size 0x258 and virtual size
0x260; the `ret 0x10` ending D3DXMatrixLookAtLH crosses the raw end into
the zero fill the XBE loader maps. The disassembler read file bytes only,
so the ret never decoded, the translated function returned without
popping its arguments, the caller restored edi from the wrong slot, and
the front end quit into the game's fatal "Couldn't find section ''"
screen.

- BinaryImage.get_section_data gives an executable section
  min(virtual - raw, 14) bytes of the loader's zero fill. No instruction
  may start in it (linear_sweep and decode_at stop at the file end), so
  only an instruction crossing the raw end gains bytes. A gap alias that
  runs to the section bound ends where that instruction ends.
- The lifter reads up to a section's readable end (config.readable_end)
  and zero-fills past raw size, as the loader does; a body ending further
  is refused with a warning. The trailing-table scan stays in its own
  section, and the callback recovery from #176 bounds a candidate by the
  readable end too, so a callback cut the same way keeps its last
  instruction.
- A warning when a body ends on leave or pop ebp with nothing after it,
  once per cut end: those only ever precede a ret in compiler output.

Burnout 3 regenerates byte-identical with this change.

Tests: test_section_zero_fill.py (the cut ret decodes; nothing starts in
the fill; BSS-only sections get none), test_alias_bounds.py (a gap alias
keeps the ret cut by raw_size, and owns no more of the fill),
test_section_readable_end.py (readable_end, the zero-filled read, the
refusal), test_teardown_falloff.py (the leave / pop ebp warning, once).

e108d0e975e7830c35464f03fb6aa919fd790ead.message:
lifter: take the flags of xadd / lock xadd from the sum

"lock xadd" sat in _FLAGS_UNDEFINED, so a jcc right after it fell to the
`_flags` fallback that nothing assigns and the branch was never taken.
`lock xadd [refcount], -1 / jne` is InterlockedDecrement's shape -- every
COM Release compiles to it -- so Release destroyed the object whatever the
count was. Jet Set Radio Future freed the same object twice that way as soon
as its Direct3D device existed, corrupting the heap and spinning in
RtlAllocateHeap's free-list walk.

The atomic lowering now publishes the sum into _fa/_fas next to the
RECOMP_ATOMIC_ADD32 (the source is overwritten with the old value by the
same instruction, and another thread may move the destination before the
jcc), xadd joins _RESULT_SNAPSHOT_SETTERS so _make_condition reads that
snapshot, the zero-relative signed conditions are answered like add, and
the locked spellings are tracked as their bare instruction.

e1864d53195a5ae0f19b5d3da0f0ee60f1a05e45.message:
lifter, runtime: pushfd/popfd through g_eflags, and cpuid answers as the P3

pushfd, popfd and cpuid all lifted to RECOMP_UNIMPL no-ops. pushfd/popfd
is the "does this CPU have cpuid?" idiom, and as no-ops it left esp four
bytes off: an EFLAGS.ID + CPUID probe popped its caller's saved
registers.

The word is a thread-local g_eflags image. The arithmetic flags stay lazy
and are written into it only at a pushfd; nothing is published at calls,
rets or jumps. Outside pushfd, the only new code is where a jo/jp, seto/
setp, cmovo/cmovp, fcmovu/fcmovnu, lahf or sahf's preserved OF follows
cmp/sub/add or a logic op (4 functions on Burnout 3, which change from the
always-false fallback to the real flag):
- pushfd writes the tracked setter's CF/PF/ZF/SF/OF into g_eflags with
  publish_flags, then pushes recomp_pushfd(): g_eflags with DF from g_df
  and bit 1 set. publish_flags reads each flag through the condition a
  jcc on it uses (_make_condition), so the image and the branches agree.
  A flag the setter has no rule for keeps what g_eflags held, and the
  site carries a RECOMP_UNIMPL naming it (after adc, sbb, neg, the
  shifts, shld, imul, bt, bsf/bsr and the rotates). AF is not modelled.
  With no tracked setter at all (function entry, after a call, a join
  whose paths disagree, mul or rdtsc) the pushed word is g_eflags as last
  written, and the site says so in a comment. Not a RECOMP_UNIMPL: the
  EFLAGS.ID probe opens with exactly that pushfd and wants only bit 21.
- _make_condition gains the OF of cmp, sub and add, and the PF of sub,
  add and the logic ops, which had no rule: `cmp al, bl; pushfd` with
  al = -128, bl = 1 (wraps to 127, OF set) saved OF clear. OF is the top
  bit, at the operand's width and in its unsigned type, of the sign test
  (sub and add recover the original destination from the result and the
  source they snapshot); the logic ops clear it. A jo/jno/jp/jnp after
  these setters used the untracked `_flags` fallback, which is always
  false; it now takes the same rules. No existing conditio

POSIX file backend: opens relative to a RootDirectory handle

NT resolves an OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES name that is not a full path against its
RootDirectory handle, and XAPI's save-game code relies on it: it opens the
save directory, then each file in it by its bare name. The Win32 backend
joins such names to the handle's path (translate_obj_path); the POSIX
backend sent the bare name through the path table, which created it in the

rename path already did, for NtCreateFile (and so NtOpenFile/IoCreateFile),

eb7b1f5833205a24fcc0eda6eb4ed2df4f2bc2e3.message:
fix(apu): hold the frame while SSL's service routine restarts the sequencer

DirectSound's sample-limit service routine (XDK 5849; each SSL, 2048
samples, so every 43 ms) stops the sequencer and starts it again: SECTL
0x07, then 0x0F 150-400 us later. Hardware loses no slice to that. The
frame thread reads SECTL once per 32-sample frame, and a frame that read
it inside the gap took the lightweight branch, which plays the slice as
silence. In Def Jam: Fight for NY's opening scene that is about 1,300
holes of one slice of digital zero per 330 s at the device, each a
0.67 ms drop to zero, too small a step to count as a click.

mcpx_apu_frame_kind() now makes the frame thread's decision. A sequencer
that was rendering and reads off is held like a trapped front end: no
frame, and a wait that the title's next SECTL write ends, for up to 5 ms.
One that stays off longer (the title stopped it) gets lightweight frames
as before, so the software mixer and the test tone keep running, and is
not held again until the VP has rendered. Off before the VP ever rendered,
a trapped or halted front end and the test tone decide as before.

apu_monitor gains the frame decision (ten seconds of SSL stops: no frame
played silent; a long stop falls back; an APU that never ran is not
held). It fails with the hold taken out.

# xboxrecomp

```
 #   #  ####    ###   #   #         #####   ###    ###   #       ###
```
