1358825485.readme_excerpt:
# 🗡️🐎 shadowofthecolossus — Static Recompilation

A static recompilation of **Shadow of the Colossus (PS3, NPUA-80677)**, Bluepoint's
HD remaster, into a native Windows executable, built on
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). No emulator at runtime.

## Status

**Unreleased, pre-alpha. It boots, opens a window and flips. It draws nothing yet.**

The EBOOT lifts clean (16,114 functions, **0 unhandled instructions**), the eight
embedded SPU modules lift with it, and the first run reaches `cellGcmInit`,
registers both display buffers and runs the flip loop against an empty command
stream. It stalls before it opens `nico.psarc` because ps3recomp does not yet
implement **SPURS 2.0** — see [docs/spurs2-wall.md](docs/spurs2-wall.md).

Last built and run: 2026-09-05, against ps3recomp as of that date. Not yet
rebuilt against ps3recomp v0.16.0 (2026-10-19); the build layout and every
toolkit script `tools/relift.sh` calls are unchanged there.

| Phase | Status |
|---|---|
| Extract, decrypt, find functions, resolve NIDs | ✅ 180 imports, 173 named |
| Lift PPU | ✅ 16,114 functions, 0 unhandled |
| Lift SPU | ✅ 8 images |
| Build | ✅ 45 MB `shadow.exe` |
| First boot | ✅ reaches `cellGcmInit` + flip loop |
| PSARC (`nico.psarc` via HLE `cellFs`) | ⬜ |
| Graphics (live NV4097 → D3D12) | 🟡 engine up, 0 draw packets |
| SPURS (job queue into the lifted images) | ⬜ blocked on SPURS 2.0 upstream |
| Input / audio | ⬜ |

Per-session detail is in [PROGRESS.md](PROGRESS.md).

**Conformance:** this port is not yet registered in ps3recomp's regression gate
(`tools/regress_ports.toml`), so there is no milestone count to report.

## Screenshots

None yet: every frame so far is an empty clear. The first one that draws goes
here.

## Getting Started

You need your own copy of the PSN package. This repository contains no game
code, assets or keys, and never will.

### Quick start

Not available yet. A `Setup.cmd` is on the [roadmap](ROADMAP.md); until then use
the steps below.

### Step by step

Prerequisites: Windows 10/11, Python 3.9+ (`py` if `python` opens the Microsoft
Store), CMake 3.20+, Ninja, LLVM **clang-cl**, an [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net)
build (only for `--decrypt`), and a sibling
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) checkout with its runtime
built (`build/ps3recomp_runtime.lib`).

1. **Unpack the package** into the repo folder:
   ```sh
   python ../ps3recomp/tools/pkg_extract.py pkg/<name>.pkg extracted
   ```
2. **Decrypt the EBOOT.** Use the debug-signed EBOOT from the update package;
   it needs no key (the retail one needs a RAP, which this repo does not use):
   ```sh
   rpcs3 --decrypt game/EBOOT.BIN      # 5,297,872 B SELF -> 21,060,328 B ELF
   ```
3. **Lift** PPU + SPU and generate the HLE NID table (Git Bash):
   ```sh
   PS3RECOMP=../ps3recomp ./tools/relift.sh
   ```
4. **Build.** Release matters: an unoptimised build of 101 MB of generated C++
   measured 3x slower on the sister ports. `llvm-rc` is needed because clang-cl
   outside a VS dev prompt cannot find `rc.exe`.
   ```sh
   cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja \
       -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="C:/Program Files/LLVM/bin/clang-cl.exe" \
       -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="C:/Program Files/LLVM/bin/clang-cl.exe" \
       -DCMAKE_RC_COMPILER="C:/Program Files/LLVM/bin/llvm-rc.exe"
   cmake --build build
   ```
5. **Point `vfs/PS3_GAME` at the unpacked package** (a directory junction is
   enough; it is 6 GB) and run. Expected today: a window, a flip loop, and the
   FIOS workers parking on `wait for invalid cond 'fios worker cond'`.

The generated source (`src/recomp/`, `src/gen/`, `src/spu_gen/`) lands in
git-ignored directories and is never distributed.

## Usage

```sh
./tools/run.sh    # sets PS3_VFS_ROOT, PS3_HDD0_ROOT, RSX_LIVE_DRAW=1; extra args go to shadow.exe
```

There is no `--headless --record` mode yet; it belongs in ps3recomp's boot
harness and is on the [roadmap](ROADMAP.md).

## Building from source

Steps 3–4 above. `tools/relift.sh` explains its flags inline; the reasoning
behind `--code-end 0x4ECD54`, the decrypt route and the SPU images is in
[docs/lifting.md](docs/lifting.md).

```
  PSN PKG ─► USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN ─► .elf ─► ppu_lifter ─► C++ ─┐
              (NPDRM SELF)    (decrypt)  (16,114 fns)       ├─► link ps3recomp ─► shadow.exe
                              8 SPU ELFs ─► spu_lifter ─►───┘        (harness + HLE)
           USRDIR/SHADOW/nico.psarc (6.0 GiB) ────────────────────► game data (fed, not lifted)
```

## License

[MIT](LICENSE), covering this repository's own tooling, scripts and notes. It
does not cover, and this repository does not distribute, PS3 firmware, game
code, game assets or keys. `pkg/`, `extracted/`, `game/`, `vfs/`, `analysis/`
and the lifted output are git-ignored. There is no RAP, klicensee or key of any
kind in this repository or its history.

## Contributors

See [CONTRIBUTORS.md](CONTRIBUTORS.md). Contributions are welcome under
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md); please read "Where your code comes from"
first.

## Related projects

This port is one of the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) titles
and follows the shared recomp house style. Fixes the runtime needs go upstream there, not here.

- [flOw](https://github.com/sp00nznet/flow) · [simpsonsarcade-ps3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/simpsonsarcade-ps3) — sister ports of the same shape
- [tmpsn](https://github.com/sp00nznet/tmpsn) — Twisted Metal PSOne Classic, the firmware-emulator port this one was first expected to resemble
- [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) — used here as a black-box tool (`--decrypt`) and as a behavioural oracle; no RPCS3 code is in this repo

remaining interpreted SPU time comes from four of them (0xA68 in the
Wws_Job policy module, 0x5318 and 0x87E8 in the mixer job).

06aa9375568380b75c2a35b9bd91959aa321310b.message:
sceNp: tickets, account region and network time answer OFFLINE

sceNpManagerRequestTicket2, GetTicket, GetTicketParam,
GetAccountRegion and GetNetworkTime were not implemented, so their
imports answered CELL_OK with nothing written. A title that asked for a
ticket waited for a GOT_TICKET manager event that never came, and one
that read the region or the time used whatever was in its buffer.

Implement them with RPCS3's argument checks and offline answers: without
a psnr server the NP manager is OFFLINE and so are these
(SCE_NP_ERROR_OFFLINE), and there is never a ticket, so GetTicket
reports a size of 0 and GetTicketParam INVALID_STATE. Signed in to a
psnr server, which issues no tickets, a request is answered at once with
a GOT_TICKET event carrying an error instead of a ticket size; the
region is the fake account's (US, English) and the network time is the
host clock as a CellRtcTick.

06b2292def31186d507aa8cfd38ed487ec220a9c.message:
.github/workflows: pin the five third-party actions to commit SHAs

release.yml fires on `push: tags: ['v*']` with `permissions: contents:
write`, so every action it invokes runs holding a token that can write to
this repo and attach release assets. Referenced by floating major tag, any
of those five actions could be retargeted upstream -- a tag is mutable, and
whoever controls it controls what executes inside that job. Pinning to a
commit SHA makes the referenced code immutable.

Each SHA is the commit the action's current major tag points at, so this
changes no behaviour: the same code runs, it just can no longer be swapped
out from under us. The readable version stays in a trailing comment because
a bare SHA tells a later reader nothing about how stale the pin is.

Only `uses:` lines and their comments change -- 13 references across all
five workflows, no other workflow edits.

(cherry picked from commit 903d023f4a88ace083b0d9843fd3cf71a40f6572)

0e8b9ef2ca28fae79e8e24d2dede074581350fb7.message:
rsx engine: a depth snapshot is the region the texture names

The engine's host depth target is at least canvas-sized
(eng_zdepth_get), but a depth texture covers only the top-left
width x height of it. eng_zdepth_snapshot resolved the whole target and
the Metal resolve sampled it with normalized coordinates, so a 128x160
shadow map in the corner of a 1280x720 target was stretched over the
whole canvas and the lookups landed outside the map.

eng_zdepth_snapshot takes the texture's size and asks the backend for
that region (clamped to the target); a cached snapshot is reused only at
the same size. The Metal resolve reads the depth 1:1 (src.read at the
fragment's pixel) instead of sampling it, so a smaller snapshot is the
top-left region. The Vulkan backend's copy already works this way.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) samples small shadow maps from
canvas-sized zetas. In the port, this together with #424 and the port's
other depth-texture changes removes the dark rectangles on the ground
under shadows; the effect was not isolated per change.

Tests: test_color_feedback_engine (a 128x160 texture over a 256x256 zeta
asks for a 128x160 snapshot), test_metal_depth_readback (a 2x2 snapshot
holds the top-left texels 1:1).

11690a51b493e28537e6b0601ce9bf3cc5016233.message:
spu: fi on 32-bit lanes, frest/frsqest tables without a gather

fi's fixed-point magnitude is 2^32 + d with d = base * 2^19 - step * y,
so one unsigned compare gives the normalisation and 32-bit lanes hold
the rest: no widening to 64-bit lanes and back.

The fraction tables are read with one cross-lane permute per eight
entries and a select on the row, not a gather: on Zen 2 the gather made
frest slower than the scalar loop. Throughput of frest + fi (the
reciprocal pair): GCC 8.5 ns scalar, 9.5 before, 6.4 now; clang 12.1
scalar, 6.1 before, 5.4 now. test_spu_float_est still finds no
mismatch under either compiler.

118b6281a756697391f178e523a409e0b1f60ce1.message:
cellGcmSys: GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS sets how long a FIFO park may stand

When the drain stops on a self-jump park and `put` has moved, it waits
GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS (50 ms) for the title to patch the park and then follows
`put`. That suits a title that leaves a park standing when it switches
segments. It does not suit one that appends commands right after the
park, moves `put` there and patches the park last: if the patch comes
after the grace, the drain skips the commands in between.

God of War HD does the latter, and while it loads its menu the two stores
have been more than 50 ms apart: the drain jumped from 0x57C40 to put
0x5AA2C, dropped ~11 KB of commands with a fence among them, and the boot
stopped (once in about 45 runs). The RSX itself would wait.

GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS=<ms> now sets the grace; the default is unchanged.

13a7676ba2139314035649dd94cc7bc075de2868.message:
perf(spu): copy only the reserved lines of a PUT under the lock-line lock

A PUT whose span touches a reserved line held the global lock-line lock for
the whole copy, keeping every other SPU's GETLLAR/PUTLLC waiting behind a
multi-line memcpy. Only the reserved lines can be inside a peer's
compare-and-commit window. In a multi-line span the other lines are now
copied first, without the lock, as the unreserved path already copies a
whole span; the locked pass then copies the lines it skipped and notifies
every reserved line, including one reserved after its unlocked copy.

That late line is notified but not copied again: between the two passes a
peer can reserve it, read our bytes and commit, and a second copy would
write that commit back over. Single-line spans keep the single locked copy.

test_spu_lockline_peer: an unaligned PUT over a reserved middle line raises
once, lands exactly, and leaves the bytes either side alone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

147e59a79e63cefcf0c2f53fc7314d83f54167e2.message:
rsx_d3d12: pass the FP depth-export bits of SHADER_CONTROL

Draws recorded only the 32-bit-exports bit of SET_SHADER_CONTROL, so a
fragment program that replaces the fragment depth (bits 1-3) was
translated without SV_Depth. God of War HD's resolve pass writes the
scene depth it reads from the 2x-AA depth surface into the resolved
one this way; without it the pass wrote the quad's own depth (0), and
every depth-tested pass after it failed everywhere: the stencil
shadows, the fog, rain, the waterfall mist and the glows.

The draw now records the export bits (32-bit exports and depth export)
as fp_ctrl, part of the pipeline key, and hands them to the
decompiler, which already emits SV_Depth from r1.z.

15265cf84c72fa3def867b7732f498108cd8f863.message:
feat(tools): --handled and --image-ids for SPU program discovery

build_spu_workloads --input discovers every embedded SPU ELF in a carrier,
lifts it and registers it by fingerprint, and reports coverage as complete
only when every program is registered. A title that already registers some
programs another way (a hand-reviewed lift, an interpreter route) could not
use it without registering those twice, and its content-derived image ids
(0x10000000 | sha prefix) cannot be reviewed or kept stable against ids the
title already uses.

--handled JSON {sha256: reason}: such programs are not lifted, count as
covered and carry the reason in inventory.json. --image-ids JSON
{sha256: id}: every registered program takes its pinned id; a discovered
program missing from the map is reported unsupported, so coverage fails
instead of silently assigning one. Entries naming programs that were not
discovered are errors. With both, inventory.json's `complete` is a usable
build gate: a newly discovered SPU program cannot go unregistered silently.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

1530be7cfd1295f9db57e380a3dc2314770a82c1.message:
ppu_lifter: per-function copy of the memory model; PPU_FAST_FP

A guest store goes through vm_base + ea, a byte pointer the compiler
cannot tell apart from the memory-model globals, so the inline load and
store paths reloaded vm_base, ppu_vm_size, ppu_hle_inject_base and the
two enable flags after every store. Each lifted function now copies them
into a local at entry (PPU_MM_SNAP) and its accesses use the copy. They
are all set before guest code runs. The SPU reservation bitmap and the
store watches can change while a function runs, so those are still read
from the globals. Code outside lifted functions keeps vm_read*_inl and
vm_write*_inl, which now take a fresh copy per access.

PPU_FAST_FP, off unless the build defines it, drops the NaN checks in
ppu_fp_bin and ppu_fmadd_core. The host's NaN differs from the PPC one
only in its sign and in which of two NaN operands propagates.

God of War HD, func_001BEFA4, built with FMA3: 6,195 instructions before,
5,855 with the copy, 4,553 with PPU_FAST_FP as well (branches 1,342,
1,063, 583).

test_ppu_lift.py: the conformance driver defines PPU_NO_INLINE_LOADS. Its
vm_read*/vm_write* are its own functions, and its statements do not run
inside a lifted function.

170be32ac21c17795a97d244d8fa559ed47e21f0.message:
ftrace: a span for each HLE import call

PS3_FTRACE recorded syscalls and timer sleeps but not HLE imports, so a
guest thread blocked or busy inside an import (a file read, a SPURS
wait, a lock taken hundreds of thousands of times) showed up nowhere.
ps3_hle_call's exit guard now closes a PS3_FT_HLE span (who = thread,
a = NID, b = guest lr) for calls at least PS3_FTRACE_MIN_US long. With
the trace off it costs one load per call.

This is what found God of War HD's 360 ms frame: 320,355 lwmutex
lock/unlock pairs in it (PS3_FTRACE_MIN_US=0), against 71 in a normal
frame.

1891b8fe718534bef9d143c7b665beb762adbc07.message:
gcm: count the drain's own ring recycle as the JUMP to begin

Once a title has been seen to overrun its ring, the drain recycles the
ring itself when current nears end. A title whose callback also
recycles (cellGcm_fifo_recycle) can be in that callback at the same
moment: it writes its JUMP and put, and only then marks itself waiting,
so a pass that read the mark clear still teleports get to begin. The
callback then waits for a backward JUMP that never comes, because get
is already at begin == put, and gives up after 2 s of no progress.

God of War HD stopped for 2-4 s this way at random points in about
half of the gameplay runs. Counting the teleport as the backward JUMP
ends the callback's wait at once.

1be9e80d533ae0ff253fa169f5d2f5f783a1364d.message:
rsx_shader_msl: compile a vertex program's position invariant

Titles draw the same geometry twice with two different vertex programs,
the second pass testing EQUAL against the depth the first one wrote. The
RSX runs the position arithmetic instruction by instruction, so both
programs land on the same depth. The Metal compiler optimises each
program on its own (it may fuse a multiply and an add into one FMA in one
of them and not in the other), the two depths can then differ in the last
bit, and the EQUAL pass leaves holes.

Resistance: Fall of Man's foliage writes depth through an alpha-tested
program, then colour through one that also lights it, with
SET_DEPTH_FUNC EQUAL.

The translator now marks a vertex program's position [[position,
invariant]], and the Metal backend compiles guest programs with
MTLCompileOptions.preserveInvariance (macOS 11 and later), so programs
that compute the position the same way get the same bits.
PS3RECOMP_MSL_INVARIANT=0 leaves the position as it was.

test_shader_msl checks the vertex program's MSL for
"[[position, invariant]]" (and for "[[position" under
PS3RECOMP_MSL_INVARIANT=0).

1c7c1d914374d59451f5b73421119af501606cfb.message:
rsx engine: a scissored CLEAR_SURFACE clears only the scissor

RSX clears what the surface clip and the scissor let through. The engine
cleared every colour and depth target whole, whatever the scissor said.

Resistance: Fall of Man's co-op split screen renders both views into one
2x1 antialiased 1280x720 scene target: the scissor on the left half, a
colour and depth clear and player 1's view, then the scissor on the right
half, a clear and player 2's view. The second clear wiped player 1's view,
and the left half of the screen was black under the HUD.

sink_clear now asks eng_clear_rect what the clear may write: the clip
from the origin, then the scissor (eng_scissor_rect, the draw path's
scissor code moved into a function). Only a scissor narrower than the
clip makes a clear partial; a clip smaller than the target alone stays a
whole clear, as before. A partial clear goes to two new optional backend
hooks, clear_color_rect and clear_depth_stencil_rect. A backend without
them, or PS3RECOMP_ENG_RECT_CLEAR=0, clears whole as before. A depth clear
that covers everything the zeta was ever bound with (ext_w/ext_h) stays
whole, and a partial depth clear keeps had_write.

The Metal backend records a rectangle clear as a clear record with the
rectangle in its scissor and encodes it as a pass of its own: the
attachment is loaded and a full-target triangle under that scissor writes
the colour, or the depth and stencil with the test always passing. Such a
record is never folded into a pass's load action.

New test_clear_rect in test_rsx_draw_engine (the co-op frame, whole and
empty scissors, a zeta only bound at a small clip, a backend without the
hooks), and test_metal_rect_clears.m (tools/test_metal_rect_clears.py) on
the GPU: a rectangle clear of the right half keeps the left half, for
colour, depth and stencil, and a whole clear after one covers the target.

211cdd81b7f8b2b4e27f2a0fd998ed6351379558.message:
rsx: vertex array addresses wrap at 28 bits

VERTEX_DATA_BASE_OFFSET was added to an array's offset as a plain 32-bit
(or 64-bit) sum. A sum at or past 0x10000000 then pointed past the end
of the location's 256 MB address space, and the fetch read nothing.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) puts its per-frame world lighting
stream (attribute 4, UB256 x4) at base + offset = 0x1Fxxxxxx. Read
unwrapped it decodes as zeros, and buildings, snow and terrain render
saturated blue. Taken modulo 2^28 it is local 0x0Fxxxxxx, where the
stream is, and the world is lit.

rsx_dsp_resolve_vertex_offset (rsx_dispatch.h) masks base + array
offset to 28 bits before the location translation; the element offset
is added after. The fetch plan's stable span and per-element fetch
(rsx_vertex_compact.c) and the live-draw fetches (rsx_live_draw.c) use
it. Sums below 2^28 are unchanged.

test_vertex_fetch_plan: a stream at base + offset = 0x10000100 reads
local 0x100 through both the stable span and the per-element fetch, and
the random plans also draw bases with high bits set.

21c14a650a346b18a4f79c82689ad5c060c34693.message:
rsx_d3d12: guest depth/stencil state and samplers in the guest-FP pipelines

Every guest-FP pipeline had a fixed LESS_EQUAL depth test with writes,
no stencil, and four static samplers (s0 point/clamp for the dbgfont
atlas, s1-s3 linear/wrap), whatever the title set. In God of War HD:

- Its stencil shadow volumes marked nothing, and the shadow pass, a
  full-screen reverse-subtract quad meant only for the marked pixels,
  darkened the whole frame (0.16 -> 0.012 on a lit pixel).
- Depth state ignored: rain and blood particles were rejected.
- Unit 0 was point-sampled and clamped. The soldiers wrap their texture
  atlas (v up to ~2), sampled the transparent bottom row and drew
  nothing over an untextured base; Kratos' tattoo and skirt came out
  white; textures shimmered.

Depth test/write/func and front/back stencil (func, ops, masks) are
packed per draw into a PSO key (rsx_zs_key); the stencil reference is
set per draw. The cull key now always carries the front face, which
two-sided stencil needs with culling off. Samplers are four descriptor
tables built from each unit's TEXTURE_ADDRESS/FILTER/CONTROL0/BORDER
(one cached descriptor per distinct state); units without guest state
keep the old two defaults.

23540a1007e37f28c404c3adfa8ea2d22e188194.message:
rsx_d3d12: cache converted vertices within a draw

Indexed lists (shared vertices), strips and fans (each vertex in up to
three triangles) and indexed quads expand one guest vertex into several
output vertices, and each one was fetched again: 16 attributes, each with
its own address resolve and conversion, for every reference. God of War
HD's gameplay frames expand ~370k vertices through these paths and the
fetch was a third of the frame.

A direct-mapped cache on the low index bits (8192 entries, 2 MB) keeps
the converted 256-byte vertex; a hit is a memcpy. It is dropped at every
draw, since attribute state and the guest arrays may change between
draws. Measured in GoW HD gameplay: vertex time per 20 frames 0.80 s ->
0.29 s, ~9.0 -> ~12.1 fps. VTX_CACHE_CHECK=1 refetches on every lookup
and counts differences: 0 in 312M lookups. VTX_NOCACHE=1 disables it.

My own mistake resolving the #496 / #472 conflict, and the cause of wave 3

closing pad_status_take() at the end of #472's block, and
pad_host_release() ran on into the next 20 lines of file-scope code. Every
platform fails to compile libs/input/cellPad.c, which every target builds.

it is not, and #496 is the first merge in that span.

27745b54d1b60e5232e48a1234a182fc6f52e113.message:
ppu_lifter: inline guest stores, the store side of the inline loads

Every lifted store called vm_write8/16/32/64 out of line. In God of War
HD gameplay those calls were about a fifth of the main thread.

The generated header now has vm_write*_inl beside vm_read*_inl. A store
is done in place when vm_inl_ok accepts the address, no store diagnostic
is armed (vm_inline_st_ok: PPU_WVAL, PPU_WWATCH, PT), the barrier watch
and the null-page sweep are idle, and no SPU holds a reservation on the
line (g_spu_coh_bits). Anything else goes to the out-of-line store as
before. PPU_NO_INLINE_STORES keeps the calls, and the runtime's own files
keep them through PPU_NO_INLINE_LOADS.

Re-lift to pick it up. God of War HD: the main thread runs about 14.8 ms
a frame instead of 16.2 with the HLE lookup cache, vm_write32 is gone
from its profile and vm_write64 is 1.2%. The executable grows from 57 to
87 MB.

fetch read frequency 0 and 1 as an ordinary per-vertex array whatever the
bit. rsx_vertex_freq_plain() names the ordinary case (frequency 0, or 1 with
division); rsx_vertex_element_index, the compact fetch's shared span and the
legacy rsx_fetch_attrib use it.

ppu: test the SPU reserved-line bitmap inline on guest stores

Every guest store called spu_coh_is_reserved, and in God of War HD
gameplay that call was 9.5% of the main PPU thread's samples. Most of it
was not the call: spu_coh_reserve stored s_coh_armed = 1 and or-ed the
line's bit into the bitmap on every GETLLAR, the same values each time.
The SPURS kernel reserves the same few lines over and over, so those
cache lines kept moving to the SPU threads' cores, and each PPU store
missed on them.

  they change.
- spu_coh_bitmap.h publishes the bitmap as g_spu_coh_bits, NULL until
  the first reservation, and spu_coh_line_reserved tests it inline.
  VM_WRITE_COH in ppu_loader.cpp and ppu_memory.h, and
  vm_block_reserved, use it. s_coh_armed goes away.
- g_spu_coh_bits is one merged definition per program (selectany /
  weak), so the loader fixtures, which link ppu_loader.cpp without
  spu_coherency.c, still link and see no reserved lines.

3099075391d4105873242cd4c3f3555ed43fe397.message:
ppu_lifter: --insn-patches lifts patched instructions as run-time switches

A patch that changes an instruction word in .text does nothing to a
lifted title, which never executes the guest's code words. Making it a
second lift means a second build of the whole title for one changed
word, and a port that wants it optional ships two.

--insn-patches FILE takes {"patches": [{addr, orig, new, guard}, ...]}.
Each patched instruction is lifted in both forms and emitted as

    if (guard) { <new> } else { <orig> }  /* insn patch 0x...: orig -> new */

guard being an int the port defines and sets before the guest runs; each
function that uses a guard declares it extern "C". The original's branch
label and the code around it are unchanged. The lift stops when the
input does not hold orig at addr (a patch set for one build of a title
never lands on another), when a patch is at an address no lifted
function covers, or when new is a branch, sc or CR op (it would need
labels and call targets the function was not lifted with). The patches
reach the parallel workers too; a mismatch there raises instead of
exiting, so the pool does not hang on a dead worker.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) caps its campaign's frame rate in
code. The port lifts the cap's instructions this way and turns 60 fps on
or off from its settings, with one build.

New tools/test_ppu_lifter_insn_patches.py: a patched branch and a
patched li lift in both forms behind their guards, with the guard
declarations and the branch label in place; a wrong orig stops the lift
serially and with two workers; a patch at an address no function covers
stops it. docs/TOOLS.md describes the file with a generic example.

3bbd31bf98ab6e5f5ff8ef3a950891515376942d.message:
fix(ppu_lifter): resolve a jump-table base that was spilled to the stack

A switch dispatcher inside a loop, in a function with high register
pressure, TOC-loads its table base once, spills it, and reloads it at the
dispatch, then reuses the base register for the case address:

    lwz r10,d(r2) ; std r10,s(r1) ; ...
    ld r11,s(r1) ; lwzx r0,r9,r11 ; add r11,r0,r11 ; mtctr r11 ; bctr

discover_jump_tables took the `add` after the table load as r11's nearest
definition, and the stack reload before it was not a TOC load either, so the
dispatcher was dropped and its bctr lifted to an unresolved indirect call. A
retail title's 32-case dispatcher did exactly this; the main thread's case-1
call never ran and it went on with an uninitialised object, then stalled.

The base search now considers only definitions before the table load, and a
stack reload is followed to the nearest preceding store of that slot and the
stored register's TOC load. Over the whole retail executable (217
dispatchers) this adds exactly that dispatcher and changes no other table.
Two vectors in test_ppu_jumptables: the spilled, reused base; a reload of a
slot nothing stored stays unresolved. The first fails without the fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

3bf0233d06ff7d1d181a80754a0fbf7a16cfc253.message:
cellAudio: WASAPI keeps 60 ms queued, and the mixing thread runs ahead of the guest

On Windows the shared-mode stream asked for a 20 ms device buffer, and the
mixing thread ran at normal priority. A title that keeps every core busy
with PPU and SPU threads takes the CPU from the mixing thread often enough
for those 20 ms to run dry, and each time is an audible click or stutter.
Movie playback (Bink) was the worst case.

- The buffer is 60 ms by default; PS3_AUDIO_BUF_MS=<10..500> sets it.
- The mixing thread asks for THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL and joins the
  MMCSS "Pro Audio" task when the service is there. avrt.dll is loaded at
  run time, so nothing new is linked.
- AUDIO_RATE=1 also reports underruns: passes that found the device queue
  under half a block (it is about to play silence). The first 64 blocks are
  not counted, while the stream fills.

The guest still sees 256-sample blocks at 48 kHz paced by the device clock;
only how far ahead of the device the mixer may run changes (up to the buffer
size, so up to ~40 ms more output latency by default).

Seen with inFAMOUS 2 on a Ryzen 5 5600 (6 cores, all of them busy): with
the 20 ms buffer its Bink cutscenes stuttered audibly; with this change
they play cleanly. Only the Windows (WASAPI) path is touched.

3e9311c6287b1220d57e99b3a2a7d3e45a1cf7db.message:
cellGcmSys: forget a park once the walker has left it

The walker gives a self-JUMP park GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS with the same put to
be patched, then resyncs to put. Its record of the park (address, put,
start time) was only cleared by that resync. A park the walker left any
other way -- the title patched it into a JUMP elsewhere, or wrote
commands over it -- kept its start time, so when the walker next stopped
at the same address with the same put, the new park was taken for the
old one. Its grace had run out long before, the resync fired at once,
and the commands the title was about to link in were dropped with the
fences and labels in them. A title that reuses its command blocks
meets its parks again at the same address, frame after frame.

Clear the record as soon as the walker reads anything other than that
park's own self-JUMP: a new park always starts a fresh grace. The three
variables move from the JUMP branch to file scope for that, under the
same names.

41bae9560bd0def7d49aa3675e89fa388e27f74e.message:
rsx_d3d12: stage guest textures in a shared upload ring; LRU slots

Each texture slot had its own committed upload buffer, created with the
texture whenever the slot took a new size or format. In God of War HD's
texture bursts, when new effects first appear, creating resources was
most of the cost: one report interval had 50 new textures, 67 ms of
CreateCommittedResource (41 ms of it for the upload buffers) against
18 ms of decoding.

- Uploads are staged in one persistently mapped upload buffer, 32 MB per
  frame in flight, reset where that frame index's command allocator is
  reset (its copies have finished by then). A texture that does not fit

44ec7ee2574b1f94820756e1f08ab22e876e845e.message:
test(ppu_lifter): a spilled-base switch spans its cases past the first blr

A function inventory that ends functions at their first blr leaves a
switch's case blocks, which sit after an early-return blr and share a later
epilogue, outside the declared range. main() already extends the enclosing
function over the cases of every resolved dispatcher; it could not when the
dispatcher itself was dropped, which is what the spilled table base caused.

End-to-end guard: a tiny big-endian ELF64 with such a function (base
TOC-loaded, spilled, reloaded and the register reused for the target; three
offset-table cases past the first blr), lifted by the real main() from a
--functions list cut at the first blr. The bctr must become a computed goto
to internal case labels, the shared epilogue must be inside the function and
the following function must stay separate. Without the spilled-base fix the
dispatcher is not found and four of the six checks fail; no separate extent
change is needed.

45c634575e648b55b2da417f0a17fff1d65aaf92.message:
Merge PR #421: opt-in per-thread MFC engine lookup cache (@tekulvw)

Conflict with #243 (@Kurtisone, wave 2) at the top of mfc_for(). Both PRs
make the same function cheaper, from different ends, and both are kept.

#243's fix is the SPU_PCSAMPLE hoist: the old guard only latched `started`
when the variable was actually set, so with SPU_PCSAMPLE unset every MFC
channel access paid a getenv -- a tenth of the samples in a Twisted Metal
profile. It sets `checked` either way. #421 adds the generation-checked
per-thread cache in front, which returns before the claim lock on a hit.

#421 was written against master, so its hunk carries the pre-#243 `started`
form. Taking it as written would have reverted #243 while keeping its test
-- and #243 ships test_spu_mfc_env_once.c precisely to catch that, so this
one would have failed loudly rather than silently. Resolved anyway as
#421's cache check first, then #243's once-only latch, then the lock.

Composition is fine in that order: the first call misses the cache, falls
through and starts the sampler thread, and later calls that hit the cache
return before a getenv they no longer need to reach.

There is only one mfc_for() in the file -- the Win32 primitives it uses are
shimmed on POSIX by win32_compat.h -- so there is no second copy needing
the same resolution.

4609b3f0bf7db6fdf3a9c36a5037b0be230b8d7c.message:
spu: halt and iret longjmps without unwinding on 64-bit Windows

On 64-bit Windows longjmp unwinds every host frame between it and its
setjmp: RtlUnwindEx, with a function-table lookup and a virtual unwind per
frame. The SPU runtime longjmps on every halt back to spu_run_with_halt (a
SPURS policy module's run ends that way) and on every iret back to the
drain loop that took the interrupt.

spu_jmp_no_unwind() zeroes the jmp_buf's Frame right after setjmp returns
0, which makes longjmp restore the registers directly. These jumps only
cross C frames of the runtime and of lifted code, which have no destructors
or __finally blocks. SPU_LONGJMP_UNWIND=1 keeps the unwinding jump. No
change on other platforms.

48958fefdf401b95dc3c8ad1d1d15461db2eb89a.message:
ppu: a host thread gives its callback stack slot back when it exits

Slots were handed out by a counter and never returned, so once 64 host
threads had ever made a guest callback, every later thread shared the
last slot and the original bug came back. A movie player starts several
threads per movie, so a normal session gets there. Keep a 64-bit in-use
mask instead: a thread takes the lowest free slot on its first callback
and a thread_local owner releases it when the thread exits. Only more
than 64 live threads making callbacks at once share a slot now.

The test first runs 100 short-lived threads one after another, each
making a callback: they all get the first slot back, and the two
concurrent threads after them still get different stacks. Both checks
fail without the release.

4b8de9100d4cc959a5ccf37c51067d416691dc7a.message:
spu: lifted known-target branches tail-call their target (SPU_DIRECT)

A lifted cross-function branch with a known target (br, the conditional
branches, a fall-through into the next function) set the trampoline and
returned, and the drain loop then called the target: a host return, a
loop pass and an indirect call for every transfer. Most of those steps
have nothing for the drain to do. SPU_DIRECT tail-calls the target with
clang's musttail when that is so: the target is not LS 0, this is not
the run's first transfer, the target is not a registered stack-reset
entry (a 1024-byte hint table, set at registration), and no interrupt
is pending with interrupts enabled. Everything else takes the trampoline
as before, and so does every compiler without musttail.

The drain-step diagnostics (SPU_LOCKSTEP, SPU_TAILRET, SPU_PCHIST,
SPU_NO_LS0_END, SPU_EXITTRACE, SPU_STEPTRACE, SPU_JOBDRAIN,
SPURS_PM_FLOW) turn it off, and PS3_SPU_DIRECT=0 does too.

spu_drain_call now restores the enclosing drain's drain_ret_pc on the
way out instead of 0. The enclosing loop used to re-set it on its next
step; with direct tail calls the code after a nested call can run on for
a long time before it takes one.

In the inFAMOUS 2 port (about 18.8k such sites) the open-world walk went
from 34.5 to 36.3 fps (+5.4%), with SPU time per frame from 128 to 121 ms.

5461d040a9f1788492c9746b087ac5c6d0a79a25.message:
rsx_metal_backend: drain the staging arena's autoreleased reference on the walker

The arena is dropped on Metal's completion thread when the pool is full,
but it was autoreleased on the FIFO walker: the driver's -[MTLBuffer
contents] autoreleases the buffer, and the walker is a PPU host thread
with no autorelease pool, so that reference lived until the thread
exited and no dropped arena was ever freed. In a retail title the
device's allocated size grew from ~0.9 GB to 28.6 GB over a long session
while the engine's object table stayed flat (~1,080 live slots, ~286 MB
of textures), until allocations failed and the renderer's checked guard
tripped. With the fix a long hold that created ~145,000 engine objects
stayed at ~315 MB.

The growth block in eng_stage_reserve gets a pool of its own; the other
-contents queries in the file already sit inside one.

test_metal_stage_pool now records 64 arenas on a pool-less pthread with
the pool full of buffers too small for one, and requires every dropped
arena freed (weak references) while that thread is alive. Without the
fix all 64 stay live and the device grows 256 MB; with it, none and 0.

604bc92130d086c1c483ff97baf35614367ac26c.message:
rsx_shader_msl: cache HLSL -> MSL translations, in memory and optionally on disk

A guest pipeline's first use on Metal decompiles both programs,
translates each HLSL to MSL (glslang + spirv-cross), compiles the MSL
and builds the pipeline state, all on the RSX thread in the middle of a
frame. In inFAMOUS 2 the translation was 83% of that: 218 first uses
over two minutes of play cost 2.1 s, with single frames of up to
366 ms, against ~16% for newLibraryWithSource and under 1% for the
pipeline state, which Metal caches itself.

Keep the MSL the way rsx_shader_spirv.cpp keeps SPIR-V: in memory, and
with PS3RECOMP_MSL_CACHE=<dir> in one file per stage + HLSL text +
PS3RECOMP_MSL_FAST setting. The file header names the glslang and
spirv-cross versions and the translator's build, so a file any other
combination wrote is a miss, as is a damaged one; files are written
under a temporary name and renamed. Unset, nothing touches the disk.

byte-swapped copies, while every LS diagnostic is off (the gates read 0
once the first access has read their switches); otherwise the generic path

cellSysutilNpEula: answer the PSN terms check through its callback

sceNpEulaCheckEulaStatus asks whether the player has accepted the
title's PSN terms of service, and the answer comes later, through the
callback the title passed, on one of its cellSysutilCheckCallback polls.
None of the three real exports was implemented (the module had only a
made-up cellSysutilNpEulaCheck), so the imports answered CELL_OK and the
callback never came. A title that waits for the answer behind a "Please
wait..." box waits there for the rest of the run; inFAMOUS 2 does it the
first time it tries to go online.

Implement CheckEulaStatus, Abort and ShowCurrentEula as RPCS3 does: one
request at a time (ALREADY_INITIALIZED otherwise), the callback queued
from the next sysutil poll, Abort turning a pending answer into ABORTED.
The answer depends on the connection. Offline, the default, the terms
cannot be fetched and the callback gets SCE_NP_EULA_ERROR, which is what
a console without a connection gets and what makes a title leave its
online features alone; RPCS3's ALREADY_ACCEPTED would send it on to ask
an offline NP manager for a ticket. With PS3_NET_ONLINE=1 or a psnr
server the answer is RPCS3's, ALREADY_ACCEPTED, version 1.
ShowCurrentEula has nothing to show and closes on the next poll.

cellNetCtl exports its PS3_NET_ONLINE check as ps3_netctl_online for
this.

643bcf75c0882ab00f41816de0163214e917158c.message:
sys_mutex: MUTEX_WATCH=2 reports long waiters without changing the wait

MUTEX_WATCH=1 replaces the blocking lock with 5 s timed slices, and on
macOS pthread_mutex_timedlock is a 200 us trylock poll. That changes the
timing enough to hide some hangs. With MUTEX_WATCH=2 an infinite
sys_mutex_lock stays a plain blocking pthread_mutex_lock: the waiter
records itself in a slot (64 of them) before it blocks and clears the
slot once it has the lock, and a reporter thread, started on first use,
prints every waiter blocked for 5 s or more every 5 s, with the mutex id
and name, the caller's LR and the owner thread and lock count.

MUTEX_WATCH is now read as a number, so =1 and =2 pick the mode.

sync_stress runs under both modes (sync_stress_mutex_watch1/2).

64782329d5f9cb063530f82a0900bea17b4d25b2.message:
sys_mutex: destroy refuses a mutex that is held or has waiters (EBUSY)

lv2 returns EBUSY for sys_mutex_destroy on a mutex that is locked or
that a thread is blocked acquiring. Ours destroyed the host mutex under
the blocked thread, and the next sys_mutex_create in the same slot
initialised a new one over it: everyone else then used the new mutex
and the blocked thread waited on the dead one for good.

sys_mutex_info.waiters counts the threads blocked acquiring a mutex:
around the acquire in sys_mutex_lock (both timeout returns give it back)
and around the re-lock in sys_cond_wait. Destroy returns EBUSY while the
lock count or that is nonzero, and logs the first 16 refusals.

Found in the Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) port while chasing the
hang after its level-1 intro movie. It was not that hang's cause.

tests/sync_stress/test_mutex_destroy.c (ctest mutex_destroy): held;
held with a blocked locker; a timed lock that times out; a thread
blocked on the host lock with the guest count at 0; a cond_wait
re-lock; then free, destroyed, and ESRCH after.

6aaea446bc2f4e6d89378176b5155b10fb7474fd.message:
rsx engine: honour the polygon offset (SET_POLY_OFFSET_*)

The draw engine ignored SET_POLY_OFFSET_{POINT,LINE,FILL}_ENABLE,
SCALE_FACTOR and BIAS, so every draw was drawn without the offset a
title asked for. Shadow casters, decals and projected shadows are drawn
with an offset so they do not fight the depth they sit on.

Resistance: Fall of Man sets a polygon offset for its character shadow
maps, its terrain decals and its projected shadows; all of them were
drawn without it.

A new optional backend hook, set_depth_bias(slope, units, depth_bits),
is called before every draw like the stencil reference, with the enable
that matches what the primitive rasterises as (POINT, LINE or FILL) and
the zeta's depth bits (16 for Z16, 24 for Z24S8). Both terms are 0 while
the offset is off, and a NaN term reads 0. PS3RECOMP_ENG_POLY_OFFSET=0
draws without it, as before. The pass dump's draw log shows "po
factor/bias" for an offset draw.

The Metal backend keeps the offset in the draw record and sets
setDepthBias:slopeScale:clamp: per draw. Its depth targets are
Depth32Float, whose bias unit is 2^-24 over [0.5, 1), so Z24 units carry
over as they are and a Z16 unit is 256 of them.

New test_polygon_offset in test_rsx_draw_engine: 0/0 with the offset off
or only its values set, FILL's values against a Z24S8 and a Z16 zeta,
LINE applying to a line list and not to a triangle, a NaN factor, and
0/0 again once it is disabled.

New test_metal_poly_offset (a CMake target where the HLSL -> MSL
translation is built, run twice in macos.yml): a constant-depth triangle
at 0.75 drawn on the GPU through the engine and the Metal backend lands
at 0.75 + 2^-16 with BIAS 256 on Z24S8 and with BIAS 1 on Z16, a
SCALE_FACTOR alone does not move it, and with PS3RECOMP_ENG_POLY_OFFSET=0
nothing does.

7306cf7088e50276094c01afebbe40fb1a37d291.message:
gcm: pass over NOP runs, and decode 3D method runs a command at a time

The FIFO walker decoded every word through the full header path, and
every data word through a translation, a stack of per-word switches and
two calls. In God of War HD gameplay that was most of the drain thread:

- NOP words. The title builds command blocks on SPUs into fixed-size
  reservations and leaves the rest of each one zero: about 4.6 million
  NOPs a second against 1.2 million command headers. A run of zero
  words is now passed over at once, up to put or the end of the 1 MB
  IO page.
- 3D method runs. A run inside one IO page with no per-word diagnostic
  on translates its offset once and skips the per-word checks, none of
  which can match subchannel 0/1 methods.
- Vertex-program microcode and constants, about five million words a
  second (the title re-uploads each draw's program and constants).
  rsx_process_vp_run handles an incrementing run inside the microcode
  or constant window in one call.

GCM_WORD_STATS counts NOPs one by one, so it now counts as a per-word
diagnostic and keeps the old path.

Tests: test_rsx_vp_run checks that the run call leaves rsx_state exactly
as the words do one by one (200,000 random runs, including rewrites of
the same microcode and runs that must be refused); test_gcm_nop_runs
checks method order around NOP runs, a run stopping at put inside the
zeros, and a run at the end of an IO page. The walker tests that stub
rsx_process_method also stub the new call.

Walker time per drain went from about 610 to 440 us, and the drain
thread from 26% to 18% of a core.

78ecbff514ba47da165d1cb2b6942c04bbb3d6b6.message:
release.yml: scope the write token to the job that publishes

The workflow declared `permissions: contents: write` at workflow level, so
every job inherited a token that can push commits and move tags. Only
`publish` uses it, and only for `gh release create`/`gh release upload`.

`package` never writes to the repository -- it configures CMake, compiles
the tree and runs every tools/test_*.py under `python` -- yet it held the
write token while doing so, on a commit that a tag can point at without
ever having gone through the push workflows. That is 75 test scripts today
and 47 more arriving with this release, all executing next to a credential
they have no use for.

So: workflow default drops to `contents: read` (which is also what any job
added here later inherits), `package` says `contents: read` explicitly, and
`publish` declares `contents: write` for itself. Releases live in the
`contents` scope, so `contents: write` is the narrowest permission that
still publishes; there is no `releases` scope to ask for instead.

Nothing else in the file needs a scope from this token. The artifact upload
and download both talk to the artifact service with the runner's own token,
and `actions: read` is only required for pulling artifacts from a different
run or repository, which this does not do.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit bc48602e492d9d1389f039760f1063698c44ed4f)

7d8d507ff4caf110fec313957e72e28e66b9fac6.message:
lift_jobmods: lift each job module at the link base its header names

Every WWS job module was lifted at LS 0x4000, the job code buffer. The
module header carries the address it is linked for at +0x28, after the
0xC0DEC0DE magic at +0x20: 0x4000 for almost every module, but
Resistance: Fall of Man ships 2 of its 15 modules linked at 0x7000.
Lifted at 0x4000, every function and branch target of those was 0x3000
short of where the job manager runs them.

module_base() reads it, and falls back to 0x4000 when the header has no
magic or names 0, an unaligned base or one that would run past local
store. It replaces BASE everywhere in the per-module loop: the ELF
wrapper, --base, the extra-function range, the +0x30 seed, the manual
link and switch-table targets and the manifest's base.

tools/test_lift_jobmods_base.py: module_base on six synthetic headers,
then a 0x7000 and a 0x4000 module lifted end to end, with functions and
manifest at their own base.

7f226c4d76534ebbf2887e9763d9d70ce622c57e.message:
rsx_draw_engine: a compressed texture is never a render target's output

sink_bind_textures matched every texture against the colour targets and
zetas at its offset. No surface colour format is block-compressed, so a
DXT1/DXT23/DXT45 texture cannot be reading what a target rendered; its
data came from memory. Matched anyway, it found whatever target sat at
that offset, and the draw was dropped as an incompatible feedback read.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) samples a 16x16 DXT1 texture at the
offset of its 1280x720 colour target, and that draw was dropped.

A compressed texture now skips both surface lookups and is uploaded
from memory like any other texture.

test_color_feedback_engine: a DXT1 texture at the current target's
offset draws, with no feedback copy.

ppu_lifter: put the likely hint on the inline access branch

__builtin_expect sat on vm_mm_ok's return value, where there is no
branch to attach it to, so it was gone by the time the helper was
inlined. The compiler then laid the slow-path call out inside the hot
path: every inline access ended in a taken jmp over it. The hint is now
on the if in each vm_read*_mm / vm_write*_mm, and the slow-path blocks
move to the end of the function.

gameplay frame goes from 17.6/17.4 to 16.9/17.2 ms, alternating with the
previous build in one session.

Two conflicts with #472 (@erikomis), which landed earlier in this wave and
rewrote the same poll loop. The second one is the interesting kind: taking
#496's hunk verbatim compiles and silently breaks #472.

master's poll loop opened and closed controllers inline. #472 moved all of
that into pad_sdl_hotplug(), which closes a detached pad through
pad_sdl_close(p, 1) -- and that is the function that keeps s_sdl_last_guid[p]
so the pad is reopened into the SAME port when it comes back, which is the
whole point of #472. #496 (written against master) re-adds an inline
"!SDL_GameControllerGetAttached(gc) -> Close(); controllers[i] = NULL" in the
loop, with no GUID bookkeeping. Merged as written, that closes the pad behind
pad_sdl_hotplug()'s back and the port assignment is lost.

So the structure is #472's and the behaviour change is #496's: the branch
stays "if (!gc)" and the state reset becomes pad_host_release().

One integration fix beyond either PR. #472 introduced a THIRD place that
resets the host state -- pad_sdl_close() itself, which #496 never saw because
it did not exist on master. Left alone, #496's centred sticks would be
restored on every path except hot-unplug, which is precisely the case #496's
own comment calls out ("A pad unplugged mid-game kept its last report the
same way"). pad_sdl_close() now calls pad_host_release() too, so all four
reset paths agree: 0 is full deflection up and left, and 128 is centre.

81344af1d05eea6877c7fa4963141a49aa71ab27.message:
spu: update event_status atomically

event_status is written from more than one host thread: the SPU's own
(Sn from a list stall, the tag-group event, its own Lr poll, WrEventAck)
and others (a PPU store or a peer SPU's PUT/PUTLLC raising Lr through
spu_coherency.c). Each side did a plain read-modify-write, so a raise
that read the word before the other side wrote it put the stale value
back and the other side's bit was lost.

In Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107), after START the PPU rewrites the
SPURS line about 14k times (cellSpursReadyCountStore), each raising Lr
on the job-manager SPU. One of those raises overwrote the Sn the SPU had
just set for a stalled DMA list, and the WWS job manager waited for its
interrupt for ever with the list parked: the first gameplay frame never
finished. With this it reaches gameplay.

SPU_EVENT_SET / SPU_EVENT_CLEAR (spu_context.h) are atomic fetch-or /
fetch-and (_InterlockedOr/And under _MSC_VER), and all six write sites
go through them.

Also, WrEventAck keeps Sn pending while a list is still parked
(list_stall_stat non-zero): a resumed list runs inline inside the
MFC_WrListStallAck that resumes it, so its next stall can land before
the handler acknowledges the event it was taken for. That guard alone
did not fix the hang above.

Tests: test_spu_event_atomic (Sn raised and acked on one thread while
another raises and acks Lr, 5M rounds: never lost; with the plain
operators it is lost tens of thousands of times) and
test_spu_event_ack_sn (the WrEventAck guard through the real
spu_channels.c).

87defcf2f0f70ac2290b585ac469a5efb81d41ee.message:
spu_workload: images with a parameter area the loader fills in

A raw-SPU program the PPU streams into local store is found by the
fingerprint of the run it wrote. Some programs carry a parameter block
the PPU fills in before every load (heap pointers, per-level values, the
SPU's own MMIO window), so the loaded run never fingerprints the same
twice and no registration can match it.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) loads its second raw-SPU program with
0x50 such bytes at the end of the image. One run loaded it as
47C9CB480016D493, a Continue from a later checkpoint as 5771C48D28664765;
the second found no lifted entry ("no lifted image is registered") and
the game hung.

spu_workload_register_img_masked(fp, fn, image_id, name, size, var_off,
var_len) registers an image whose fingerprint is taken with
[var_off, var_off + var_len) as zero; for an image cut from an ELF whose
parameter block is zero there, that is simply the image's fingerprint.
spu_workload_find_img_masked(data, n, ...) matches a run of exactly that
size against it whatever the area holds. raw_spu_start falls back to it
when the plain lookup of a proxy-loaded run finds nothing, and says so in
its log line. Plain registrations and lookups are unchanged.

New test_spu_workload_masked (tools/test_spu_workload_masked.py): two
loads with different parameters resolve to the masked image, a change
outside the area or a different length does not, the plain lookup still
finds the image as it is in the ELF, and a registration whose area does
not fit is refused. test_spu_raw_start stubs the new lookup.

894d38ba7eb5d7c9803991ad92cfc2bd259631e0.message:
metal: host-surface mode renders into a launcher's IOSurfaces

A title that replaces its executable (sys_game_process_exitspawn, which
a port does as an exec) loses every AppKit object with the old process
image: its window closes and the new image opens another. Resistance:
Fall of Man (BCUS98107) does this going from the EBOOT's menus to
game.self, so starting the campaign closed the window and opened a new
one.

With PS3RECOMP_HOST_SURFACES=<bootstrap name> in the environment the
Metal backend opens no window and never touches NSApplication. It looks
the name up, sends ATTACH, maps the control page and wraps the IOSurfaces
it gets back as render targets. Engine and vtable presents end in one of
those surfaces instead of a drawable; the completion handler publishes it
and sends a FRAME wake. The protocol and the surface state machine
(FREE -> RENDERING -> READY -> READING) are in rsx_host_surface.h, shared
by both ends; when every surface is busy the game takes back the oldest
unread one, so it never waits on the window. The image an exec brings up
attaches again by the same name. If nothing answers, the backend opens a
window of its own as before. The pump reports -1 once the launcher closes
its window or dies.

Without a launcher, rsx_metal_backend_export_window_state() puts the
window's frame and fullscreen state in PS3RECOMP_WINDOW_STATE before an
exec, and the next image's window opens there.

The engine's present also counts a guest frame
(rsx_metal_backend_note_guest_frame), which feeds PS3RECOMP_METAL_FPS
and the launcher's title.

New test_metal_host_surface (macos.yml), against a launcher fixture in
the same process: the state machine; init attaches with no window;
engine and vtable presents land in the surfaces; 40 unread presents
reclaim instead of stalling; a resize asks for new surfaces; `closed`
reaches the pump; a second init attaches again.

8e34ab19bf2e13bfe9e8e99d866a851757e1c5b0.message:
rsx: WPOS in the RSX window convention (SET_SHADER_WINDOW origin and pixel centers)

The fragment translator read WPOS as the host position, whose origin is the
top left, and nothing looked at SET_SHADER_WINDOW (0x1D88). With the window
origin BOTTOM the RSX counts WPOS.y up from the bottom edge, so a pass that
builds its UV from WPOS, e.g. uv = wpos * (1/W, -1/H) + (0, 1), sampled its
source vertically mirrored. Rasterization is already right; only what WPOS
reports changes.

- rsx_fp_decompiler: WPOS reads go through _rsx_wpos(input.position). A
  buffered program defines it from fp_alpha: y = height - y when fp_alpha.y
  (the window height) is nonzero, and fp_alpha.z added to x and y as the
  pixel-center bias. An unbuffered program defines it as the identity. A
  program that does not read WPOS emits no helper and stays byte-identical.
- rsx_draw_engine: fills the two unused fp_alpha lanes per draw from
  SET_SHADER_WINDOW: the height (bits 0-11) when the origin (bits 12-15) is
  BOTTOM, else 0; -0.5 when the pixel centers (bits 16-19) are INTEGER, else 0.
  Backends that fill fp_alpha themselves and leave .y/.z at 0 keep the host
  position.
- test_fp_decompiler: the helper and the WPOS read in buffered and unbuffered
  programs, and no helper for a program that does not read WPOS.

9002559916323d0623083f8592622730f58c0b5a.message:
rsx_d3d12: present a small batch held back across two flips

The display-clear present holds back a batch smaller than a quarter of
the largest frame seen, as an intermediate of a title that clears the
display several times per flip. That maximum never comes down. God of
War HD plays a movie inside the game as one quad a frame, after
hundreds of draws a frame of game: every movie frame was held back,
the quads piled up until a quarter of the game's size, and the screen
showed one frame every few seconds while the movie's sound played on.

A batch still small when a second flip has landed is not an
intermediate. It is presented, and its size becomes the frame size.

Reproduced on the opening cinematic, which is presented the same way,
with the maximum set to 1000 once and presents at the display clear
already in use: 0 presents a second, the held draws growing by 30 every
second; with the change, one frame is held and then all 30 are
presented. The rendering check passes.

9088b37c42b16f23389f8d0129e446ce487d4bef.message:
vulkan/draw engine: reuse readback staging, refresh changed textures in place

Every readback and every texture upload allocated, mapped and freed its own
host buffer, and every changed texture was re-created (an allocation and a
synchronous layout submit) with the old one released. Those are driver
round trips, and on Windows/NVIDIA they took from tens of milliseconds up
to seconds each under load.

- vk_stage_get: one grow-only host buffer for readbacks (colour and depth)
  and one for uploads, reused after their submission completes and freed
  in vk_eng_shutdown.
- rsx_draw_backend.texture_upload_ordered: a backend whose texture_upload
  is ordered after every draw already handed to it gets a changed 2D
  texture rewritten in place when its mip count is unchanged. Vulkan sets
  it (every draw and upload submits and waits); Metal and the test stubs
  leave it 0 and keep create-and-swap. Volumes always create-and-swap.
- vk_eng_texture_upload rejects a mip past the levels the image was
  created with.

90f510fc3c5a99ed96bfb9598e47d8aa62a1099f.message:
vulkan engine: per-target colour mask and blend enable for MRT sets

Every attachment of an engine pipeline took target A's COLOR_MASK and
BLEND_ENABLE. The RSX gives targets B..D their own: a nibble each of
COLOR_MASK_MRT (0x0370) and a bit each of BLEND_ENABLE_MRT (0x036C). The
draw engine already decodes both into rsx_be_render_state and keys the
pipeline on them, and the Metal backend applies them; this does the same on
Vulkan.

Giving every target A's state is wrong both ways. inFAMOUS 2's light
volumes add into target A with B and C masked off, and on Vulkan every light
was added into the G-buffer as well (blown-out props, rectangles around
each light); its material passes write B and C's alpha while A's alpha is
masked, which left them stale.

- The device enables independentBlend when it has it (s_vk.indep_blend_ok);
  without it every target keeps A's state, as before.
- PS3RECOMP_VK_MRT_MASK takes the values PS3RECOMP_METAL_MRT_MASK does:
  1 (default) the hardware rule, 0 target A's state everywhere (the old
  behaviour, to bisect a title that depended on it), 2 only a target masked
  off entirely is off, with per-target blend.

Single-target pipelines are unchanged.

99ff41af923dea02fc61bfd3fa06537e9733778a.message:
spu_raw: SPU_RunCntl = 0 stops a running raw SPU

Writing 0 to SPU_RunCntl only set the context's status word. A raw SPU
parked in a channel wait kept its host thread, so the RunCntl = 1 that
followed was dropped as "already up": the program the PPU had just
streamed into local store never ran, and the old one could later resume
its old registers over the new image.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) does this to raw SPU 1 on every
checkpoint reload (stop it, stream its program in again, start it). The
restart was dropped, and after dying the checkpoint reload launched the
player into the sky.

RunCntl = 0 now sets stop_request on the context, wakes its channel
waits and returns once the host thread has left (up to ~4 s, logged if
it does not). The channel layer honours the request at every rdch and
rchcnt, inside its blocking channel wait and in the full out-mailbox
wait, and halts the SPU there through the spu_run_with_halt landing
pad. The run thread then publishes a plain stopped status (no stop
code, no stop-and-signal interrupt), releases the context's coherency
registration and MFC slot, and clears started. A start while the
thread is still up is now logged instead of being dropped silently.

New test_spu_raw_runcntl_stop (tools/test_spu_raw_runcntl_stop.py),
through the real spu_raw.c, spu_channels.c and registry: a program
parked in rdch SPU_RdInMbox stops on RunCntl = 0 before the store
returns, and the next program streamed into the same SPU runs.
test_spu_raw_start stubs the two release calls.

9a3fbffde2d1c89da8f4f74c4dd0f8088b62c2db.message:
ppu_hle: a fast path for leaf imports; lwmutex lock/unlock use it

Every HLE import goes through ps3_hle_call's guard and bookkeeping: the
TOC save and restore (with an out-of-line store to the guest stack),
the GCM pump, the profiler breadcrumb, the in-flight table. God of War
HD takes an lwmutex about 640,000 times in the frame where the first
fight's next wave spawns (its allocator), and that overhead was a large
part of each call.

ps3_hle_register_fast(nid, fn) registers a fast form beside the full
handler for an import that runs no guest code, leaves r2 alone and does
not block. ps3_hle_call tries it first; the fast form returns 0 to take
the full call. sys_lwmutex_lock's fast form takes a lock that is free or
already the caller's, and leaves a lock that has to wait (and every call
while PS3_LWMUTEX_TRACE is on) to the full handler, so a blocked thread
still shows in the in-flight table. sys_lwmutex_unlock's always
finishes. Fast calls do not appear in PS3_FTRACE.

God of War HD: that frame 235 -> 167 ms (two runs); 354 ms before the
atomic lwmutex. The rendering check passes.

9aad0f9bf10c0e85aa382c16e29a8aabb275ed70.message:
ppu_lifter: one compare per inline guest access

The inline load and store paths tested each access against the enable
flag, the null page, the raw SPU windows, the end of the mapping and the
gcm ref-poll word, and the compiler turned the chain into a run of setcc
and and instructions: about eleven per access. The per-function copy of
the memory model now holds the inline range as one span from 0x10000
(0 while a diagnostic is armed), and an access checks
(ea - 0x10000) <= span - n, with span - n computed once per function.

The range is the old checks' or narrower: an access that straddles
0xE0000000 now goes out of line. The ref-poll word is special only to
vm_read32, so only the 32-bit load still tests it. Checked over edge
addresses, sizes, mapping ends and flag settings against the old
predicate: no other difference.

God of War HD: func_001BEFA4 4,553 to 3,273 instructions, the executable
83 to 60 MB, and the median gameplay frame 20.0 to 17.4 ms, alternating
with the previous build in one session.

a20903d25bfa75c9cc99cc775621fd189132e2aa.message:
tools/host_window: reap the game with a blocking waitpid

DISPATCH_PROC_EXIT can fire a moment before the child is reapable, so
the WNOHANG reap in child_exited() saw nothing and returned; the source
does not fire again, and the host stayed up with its window open after
the game had gone. Seen when the whole process group got SIGTERM: the
host only went away at its own SIGKILL fallback, or not at all.

The child has exited when the notification arrives (an exec does not
raise EXIT), so a blocking reap in an EINTR loop returns at once. If the
pid was already reaped elsewhere the host exits anyway. begin_close()
also calls child_exited() itself 2 s after the SIGKILL fallback, in case
the notification never comes.

With the game: SIGTERM to the process group, the host exits rc 0 after
3.2 s (before: it stayed up until SIGKILL).

rsx_vp_decompiler: branch on the transform branch bits; leaders up to slot 544

has 544 slots (RSX_DSP_VP_INSTR). Past slot 511 no block was opened, so
every later branch closed a block that was never opened, main() ended
early and the program did not compile.

picks optional paths with them ran every path. They now test bit
D3[23:27] of SET_TRANSFORM_BRANCH_BITS against D3[28], as RPCS3's
GetOptionalBranchCond does; the CC condition does not apply. The outcome
is baked into the program, so the draw engine and live_draw read the
register and key the pipeline on it, only for programs that use BRB or

ab2783bda49461e10edfe5d8282f50b23eae9da1.message:
spu: interpreter rejoins lifted code inside resident code regions

spu_lifted_lookup, the interpreter's check for a lifted entry at its pc,
only searched ctx->image_id. For a job that a policy module streams into
local store, that is the policy module's image, so the interpreter never
found the job's own lifted functions. Once it was entered anywhere in a
job (a function the lifter didn't find, a resume point), it ran the rest
of the job interpreted, callees included.

Resolve addresses inside a resident code region against the region's
image first, as spu_indirect_branch already does.

God of War HD's SCREAM mixer reaches two of its job's DSP dispatchers
through a pointer table the function finder doesn't see. Each call ran
the dispatcher and every kernel it jumps to interpreted: 8-11M SPU
instructions a second in gameplay, and 20-53% of the audio blocks empty.
With this change it is ~13k a second and the kernels run lifted.

test_spu_lifted_start checks the lookup against the streamed-job setup
test_resident_code_regions already builds.

b19ac284e1f5cfa94c3d5a2326206a4eda0cda09.message:
rsx engine: honour user clip planes (SET_USER_CLIP_PLANE_CONTROL)

An RSX vertex program writes six clip distances into o5.yzw and o6.yzw,
but which planes count, and which side of each is kept, is register
state: NV4097_SET_USER_CLIP_PLANE_CONTROL (0x1478), one 4-bit op per
plane, 0 disabled, 1 ENABLE_LT, 2 ENABLE_GE. The engine ignored the
register, so nothing was ever clipped. A planar reflection clips its
mirrored scene at the mirror plane this way; without it everything
behind the plane (in inFAMOUS 2, the riverbed under the water) was drawn
into the reflection.

Do what RPCS3 does (fill_user_clip_data and the VP reg_table): for each
enabled plane the vertex shader gets an SV_ClipDistance output, the
distance as written for GE (keeps d >= 0) and negated for LT (keeps
d <= 0); a disabled plane in the same vector gets 0.5 and never clips.
rsx_vp_apply_user_clip adds the outputs to the decompiled HLSL after the
last declared varying, so the user varyings keep their locations, and
the per-plane ops join the pipeline key. A draw with no plane enabled
compiles the same program as before. The Vulkan device enables
shaderClipDistance when it has it.

PS3RECOMP_ENG_USER_CLIP=0 ignores the register, as before.

b3a75d9838299538e3379429bf2a36071c12bd58.message:
ppu: each host thread runs HLE -> guest callbacks on a stack of its own

ppu_guest_call and ppu_guest_call_ct started every callback at the
guest EA 0xCFFE0000. The variable holding it was thread-local, its value
was not, so callbacks running at the same time on two host threads built
their frames over each other, and a callback nested in another started
on top of the outer one's frame. 0xCFFE0000 is also inside RSX local
memory (0xC0000000 + 256 MB).

In Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) the movie player's cellAdec and
cellVdec callbacks run at once on its two MoviePlayerStream threads. The
adec callback's scoped mutex guard read back a NULL mutex, unlocked NULL
and left the player mutex locked for good, so the game hung after the
level-1 intro movie.

The top 16 MB of the stack region (VM_CB_STACK_REGION, 64 slots of
256 KB) now holds one callback stack per host thread, and
vm_stack_allocate stops below it. A callback nested in another starts
0x400 below the outer one's live stack pointer, past its protected zone.

runtime/ppu/tests/test_ppu_guest_call_stack.cpp
(tools/test_ppu_guest_call_stack.py): two host threads inside a
callback at once, each nesting a second one, every frame filled and
checked afterwards.

b6880e6aa86fc2d1acf4ce1edfa64d91f1c5f19e.message:
spu: SSE4.1/AVX2 forms of the per-lane integer and quadword helpers

The integer, compare, shift/rotate, multiply and quadword byte-shift helpers
have NEON forms on arm64 and fall back to their scalar per-byte/per-lane
reference loops everywhere else. On x86 those loops (rotqby and its family
are 16 single-byte moves each) were most of the lifted SPU code's time: a
Bink video decoder ran at 6-7 fps.

- SPU_X86 (x86 with SSE4.1, not NEON, not SPU_SCALAR_HELPERS/SPU_SCALAR_INT)
  gives each NEON-only helper an SSE4.1 twin: a/sf/ai/sfi, and/or/xor(i),
  the word, halfword and byte compares (and immediates), selb, ah/sfh(i),
  absdb, avgb, cg/bg, addx/sfx, the mpy family, cntb, xsbh/xshw and cwd.
- The quadword byte shifts and rotates (shlqby, rotqby, rotqmby and their
  bi/immediate forms) are one pshufb with a computed control.
- shl/rot/rotm/rotma need per-lane variable shifts and take the AVX2
  vpsllvd/vpsrlvd/vpsravd forms when __AVX2__ is set; without it they keep
  the scalar reference.
- cbd/chd/cwd/cdd generate their control word with word stores instead of a
  16-byte loop, on every host (the result is the same bytes).

Helpers without a cheap x86 form keep calling their reference.

tests/test_spu_int_x86.c checks every x86 form against spu_X_ref on 2M
random and edge-value cases, and the new generate-controls against the old
loops.

Measured on Windows (Ryzen 5 5600, clang-cl, /arch:AVX2), inFAMOUS 2: the
Bink movies go from 6-7 fps to 30 fps, and in-game frame rate is about 15%
higher.

vulkan: free the batching rings, their pool and the snapshot bounce buffer at shutdown

The engine shutdown left s_eb's four rings and descriptor pool (VK_DRAW_BATCH=1)
and the depth snapshot bounce buffer (batching on or off) alive, so
vkDestroyDevice reported leaked objects under the validation layer and the
lavapipe jobs failed. s_snap_st moves to file scope and goes with the snapshot
pool; vk_eb_release flushes, destroys the rings and the pool and lets the next
vk_eb_on decide again.

b730e080191640609cff3106eebb9c5a20a2e170.message:
vulkan: keep engine constants in ordinary memory, not read back from the UBO

The engine's vertex/pixel constants were written straight into the shared
uniform buffer, and every batched draw then memcpy'd them out of it into its
ring slice. That buffer is host-coherent, which is write-combined and uncached
on most drivers, so the copy was a read from uncached memory: ~40 us for the
~8 KB of constants a draw carries, 85% of vk_eng_draw's time in God of War:
Ascension's first level.

The constants now live in a host allocation laid out like the UBO. Batched
draws copy from it into their slice; unbatched draws copy it into the shared
UBO before writing their descriptors, as before.

threads spin in. cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo records the host thread that
walks the FIFO (g_gcm_drain_tid), and PS3_SAMPLE_DRAIN=1 skips every
other thread, so the histogram is the drain's own cost.

(ucrtbase at a quarter of the drain thread's samples).

c40829d770b7b30e48c33b4e82f6396d56b7838e.message:
runtime: buffer stdout and stderr and flush them on a timer, not an unbuffered stdout

ppu_run set stdout unbuffered so that a killed run keeps every line it
printed. With mingw-w64 that makes every character its own write():
__mingw_pformat hands an unbuffered FILE one fputc per character. Under
Wine into a pipe each write costs microseconds, and a title that logs
over a thousand lines a second spent most of its logging threads' time
there; lines from two threads also interleaved character by character.

ps3_stdio_init() (runtime/platform/ps3_stdio.c), called from ppu_run,
gives stdout and stderr a 64 KB buffer each and flushes them from a small
thread every PS3_STDIO_FLUSH_MS milliseconds (default 50), at exit, on
abort() and from the unhandled-exception filter (on POSIX through
win32_compat's signal dispatcher). A crash flush asks the flush thread
and waits at most a second, so a fault inside printf cannot hang it on
the stream lock. A killed run loses at most one interval.
PS3_STDIO_UNBUFFERED=1 restores the old unbuffered stdout.

runtime/platform/tests/test_stdio_flush.c checks, from a parent reading
the child's pipes: buffered by default, flushed within the interval
while the child is alive, flushed at exit, on abort() and on a SIGSEGV,
and unbuffered with PS3_STDIO_UNBUFFERED=1. Linux and macOS CI run it.

test_ppu_entry_arguments.cpp links ppu_loader.cpp on its own and gets a
no-op ps3_stdio_init.

c4a54cbdb95111bc01b66edf49774f3b626cae70.message:
spu_drain: run the per-hop hooks' common case inline

Every trampoline hop called yz_lockstep_tick and spu_task_launch_check,
and spu_task_launch_check called spu_check_stack_reset in another file.
Each spu_drain_call also called spu_depth_guard, which wrote a ring and
a counter shared by all SPU threads. With their switches off the hooks
return almost at once, but an SPU thread takes millions of hops a
second: in God of War HD gameplay they were about a fifth of each SPU
thread's samples.

- spu_drain_call and SPU_DRAIN (through spu_drain_hop) do what the hooks
  do by default inline: the recent-pc ring, the step count with the
  LS 0 job-complete check, and the PM flow record.
- spu_task_launch_check runs in full when SPU_NO_LS0_END, SPU_EXITTRACE,
  SPU_STEPTRACE or SPU_JOBDRAIN is set. Lockstep and the stack-reset
  check are called only when lockstep is not off and an entry is
  registered.
- spu_drain_call tests the depth limit inline. spu_depth_guard drops its
  shared ring and reports this thread's recent hops instead.

c74e3bf9530594767ade9df92ba9f55f0af8f089.message:
Run GCM handlers from blocked semaphore waits (Windows)

A flip, vblank or user-command handler is guest code, so it runs when a
guest thread reaches an HLE call or a timer sleep and pumps. A title that
waits for its flip handler in sys_semaphore_wait -- God of War HD's main
thread does, every frame -- sat there until some other thread happened to
pump: a median 0.76 ms between the RSX reaching the flip and the main
thread waking, 1.7 ms at p90.

The GCM layer now sets an auto-reset event whenever it marks something
pending, and sys_semaphore_wait waits on that event as well as the
semaphore. When the event fires, the waiting thread runs ppu_gcm_pump,
as a timer sleep does, and re-checks the semaphore. cellGcm_wait_pump is
linked weakly, so the runtime still links without the GCM library; the
POSIX path is unchanged.

God of War HD, frame limit off, alternated in one session: median frame
17.3/17.1 ms before, 15.8/16.6 ms after; flip reached to main thread
awake 0.76 ms to 0.02 ms. sync_stress passes.

c9fc36a15d379d157f5a6d43947cbd9da0a2ed46.message:
rsx_texture_decode: step the swizzled offset instead of re-interleaving

A swizzled texture was decoded texel by texel, and each texel's offset
came from rsx_swizzle_offset, which interleaves x's and y's bits one at
a time: about ten iterations a texel. In God of War HD that loop was
most of the CPU decode in the texture bursts that stall the drain when
new effects first appear.

x's and y's bits land on separate positions of the offset, so it is the
OR of a y part, computed once a row, and an x part stepped with the
dilated increment (d - mask) & mask. Checked against
rsx_swizzle_offset for every texel of every power-of-two size up to
4096x4096 (rows sampled past 256): no difference. test_texture_layout
now decodes a swizzled image of every size up to 128x128, square or
not, and checks where each texel lands.

God of War HD: texture time in the worst burst 0.27 -> 0.07-0.10 s;
the frames it stretched 112 -> 74 ms and 101 -> 73 ms; frames of 45 ms
or more over a run 13 -> 10.

cd4383ec19274822747b37d8a8dee17e5241579f.message:
lv2: register syscall 22 as _sys_process_exit

On real lv2 (and RPCS3's binding table) syscall 22 is _sys_process_exit,
the exit every game issues; the table only registered 3 (sys_process_exit3,
the number bare-metal/newlib images issue).

A guest issuing 22 fell into the catch-all stub, which reports success -- so
the guest kept executing after its exit. Observed with a minimal test ELF:
its tail loop (goto back to the exit call) ran forever because the process
never died, and the host had to kill it from outside.

Register 22 as an alias of the same handler. The constants are named after
the kernel symbols (RPCS3: 3 = sys_process_exit3, 22 = _sys_process_exit,
26 = _sys_process_exit2, so no 'EXIT2' spelling appears), with the leading
underscore of the kernel symbol noted in a comment rather than in the name.
Compiler-agnostic; two files.

Verified: the same ELF now exits cleanly (sys_process_exit(code=0), host
exit code 0) with a plain MSVC build, and its sys_fs output stays
byte-identical to a fresh RPCS3 run. The change is a plain table entry;
clang/GCC builds are unaffected by construction.
