# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   └── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse
│   ├── hardware/             # cellGem, cellCamera, cellUsbd
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
└── docs/                     # See the Documentation table below
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

HLE implementations of the PS3 system libraries, written for this project. RPCS3 is a behavioural reference, not a code source. Most modules are complete. The ones still marked Partial are the media decoders (cellVdec, cellAdec, cellDmux, cellAtrac, cellAdecAtrac3p) and cellSpurs. [docs/MODULE_STATUS.md](docs/MODULE_STATUS.md) has one row per module and is the source for the counts.

| **Kernel Memory** | sys_memory, sys_mmapper (containers, shared mem) | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Filesystem** | sys_fs (path mapping, real I/O) | ✅ Complete |
| **Filesystem** | cellFs (real file I/O, dir ops, stat, path translation) | ✅ Complete |
| **Save System** | cellSaveData (callback-driven, PARAM.SFO), cellGame | ✅ Complete |
| **Input** | cellPad (XInput/SDL2), cellKb, cellMouse | ✅ Complete |
| **Audio** | cellAudio (WASAPI/SDL2, mixing thread, multi-port) | ✅ Complete |
| **Video Output** | cellVideoOut (resolution config, 720p default) | ✅ Complete |
| **Codecs** | cellPngDec, cellJpgDec, cellGifDec (stb_image) | ✅ Complete |
| **Font** | cellFont (stb_truetype backend + fallback metrics) | ✅ Complete |
| **Network** | sys_net (BSD sockets, P2P), cellNet, cellNetCtl, cellHttpUtil, cellSsl, sceNp*, sceNpTrophy, sceNpMatching2 + Score over [psnr](docs/ONLINE.md) | ✅ Complete |

| **Fibers** | cellFiber (PPU fiber scheduler via Windows Fibers/ucontext) | ✅ Complete |

Every row is exercised by CI on every push, and **all three are green on
`master`** — the PPU boot scaffold ratchet that had been red since before v0.11.0
([#139](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/issues/139)) is at zero on all
four toolchains. The rows below describe what those jobs actually do, not what a
green tick would imply: building the runtime and passing the suites is not the
same as running a game, and only one row claims that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter + 8 test suites | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | null (headless software) |
| Runs a recompiled game | **yes** | **no** | no |

Linux builds and passes the same suites under both GCC and Clang, and runs

a runner with no display and no GPU. It is not a renderer — no depth, no
blending, no textures — so Linux is still one real backend, plus the same PPU
boot scaffold macOS needs, away from running a title.

Both non-Windows platforms are blocked on the *same* two things, in this order.

**1. The PPU boot scaffold, on POSIX.** This is the shared blocker and the only
one that gates "runs a recompiled game" on both. `ppu_loader.cpp`,
`boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled *per game* rather than into
the library, and were Win32-only — thread creation, `VirtualAlloc`, SEH, stack
walking. v0.10.0 took it to zero errors on POSIX and put it under CI so it
cannot rot again, and ported the guest-pointer trap, thread-locals and host
backtraces. What is left is running it: load a lifted image on POSIX and reach
the guest's first instruction, then `main`. Until that works, neither platform
can run a title no matter how good its renderer is.

**2. One real backend each.** The RSX abstraction landed in v0.10.0 (#101, #102,
#103) — texture conversion, the `TEXTURE_CONTROL1` crossbar, texture layout and
a neutral draw record all live outside the D3D12 file now, so a backend no
longer has to reimplement them to draw anything.

- **macOS** has the furthest to go that is *interesting* rather than
  mechanical: [@slushiimusic](https://github.com/slushiimusic)'s Metal backend

  title exists to run.
- **Linux** has no renderer at all — the headless backend is a CPU triangle
  filler for CI, deliberately. Vulkan is the obvious target, and it starts from
  the same neutral draw record Metal reads.

macOS and Linux, and it will keep saying "no" until a title actually boots to
gameplay on one of them. Building the runtime, passing the suites and rendering


## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

We're building HLE implementations based on RPCS3's module system. **97 modules complete, 1 partial (media decode)** — 219 files and ~76,000 lines under `libs/`.

| Category | Modules | Status |
|----------|---------|--------|
| **Kernel Threading** | sys_ppu_thread, sys_mutex, sys_cond, sys_semaphore, sys_rwlock | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Events** | sys_event (queues, ports, flags), sys_timer | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Memory** | sys_memory, sys_mmapper (containers, shared mem) | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Filesystem** | sys_fs (path mapping, real I/O) | ✅ Complete |
| **Filesystem** | cellFs (real file I/O, dir ops, stat, path translation) | ✅ Complete |
| **Save System** | cellSaveData (callback-driven, PARAM.SFO), cellGame | ✅ Complete |
| **Input** | cellPad (XInput/SDL2), cellKb, cellMouse | ✅ Complete |
| **Audio** | cellAudio (WASAPI/SDL2, mixing thread, multi-port) | ✅ Complete |
| **Video Output** | cellVideoOut (resolution config, 720p default) | ✅ Complete |
| **Codecs** | cellPngDec, cellJpgDec, cellGifDec (stb_image) | ✅ Complete |
| **Font** | cellFont (stb_truetype backend + fallback metrics) | ✅ Complete |
| **Network** | sys_net (BSD sockets), cellNet, cellNetCtl, cellHttpUtil, cellSsl, sceNp*, sceNpTrophy | ✅ Complete |
| **Hardware** | cellUsbd (USB), cellCamera (PS Eye), cellGem (PS Move) — stub, no devices | ✅ Complete |
| **Sync** | cellSync (atomic spinlocks, LF queue), cellSync2 (OS-backed) | ✅ Complete |
| **System** | cellRtc, cellMsgDialog, cellOskDialog, cellUserInfo, cellGameExec | ✅ Complete |
| **Localization** | cellL10n (UTF-8/16/32/UCS-2, ISO-8859-1, generic converter) | ✅ Complete |
| **Resolution** | cellResc (display modes, scaling, interlace, aspect ratio) | ✅ Complete |
| **Fibers** | cellFiber (PPU fibers via Windows Fibers/ucontext) | ✅ Complete |
| **AV Config** | cellAvconfExt (audio output info, gamma, sound availability) | ✅ Complete |
| **Input Util** | cellKey2char (HID scancode → Unicode, US-101 layout) | ✅ Complete |
| **Graphics** | cellGcmSys (cmd buffer, IO mapping, tile/zcull, flip handlers, timestamps, FIFO walker + ring recycle), RSX command processor (NV47xx parsing, state tracking, backend callbacks), **live D3D12 backend** (executes the title's real NV4097 vertex/fragment p

1390324399.description: Crazy Taxi (PS3/PSN, NPUB30242) statically recompiled to native Windows with ps3recomp. Boots to the title and attract demo.
1390324399.readme_excerpt:
# crazytaxi-ps3 — Crazy Taxi (PS3), static recompilation

`NPUB30242`, the 2010 PSN release (Sega), a port of the Dreamcast game.
Recompiled to native Windows with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp)
and built in its shared house style, like its sister ports
[gh3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/gh3) and
[simpsonsarcade-ps3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/simpsonsarcade-ps3).

Crazy Taxi has two other recompilations here: the Dreamcast SH-4 original
([crazytaxi](https://github.com/sp00nznet/crazytaxi)) and the Xbox 360 XBLA build
([ctxbla](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ctxbla)).

![Crazy Taxi attract demo running natively](docs/media/hero.gif)

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Logos](docs/media/logos.png) | ![Title screen](docs/media/title.png) |
| ![Attract demo](docs/media/attract_1.png) | ![Attract demo](docs/media/attract_2.png) |
| ![Attract demo](docs/media/attract_3.png) | ![Attract demo](docs/media/attract_4.png) |

## Status

**Alpha.** Boots through the loading screen, ESRB/Sega/CRI logos and the
"Press START" title into the in-engine attract demo, which renders the city
correctly and without flicker. Nothing past the title has been tried yet.

| Area | State |
|---|---|
| PKG extract, EBOOT decrypt | Works (free-license EBOOT; see [docs/extracting.md](docs/extracting.md)) |
| PPU lift | 8,655 functions, 197 imports across 16 libraries, builds first time |
| SPU | 2 embedded images lifted; the CRI task (image 1) dispatches through SPURS |
| Graphics | Logos, title, attract demo and high-score table render correctly, no black frames |
| Audio | CRI ADX sound bank loads; output not checked |
| Input | Not tried past the title screen |
| Menus, gameplay | Not reached |

What's next is in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md), and the per-session log is in
[docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md).

## Getting Started

You need your own copy of the game. No game code, data or keys come with this
repo, and the recompiled source isn't distributed. You generate it locally from
your own dump.

Prerequisites (Windows 11):

- Visual Studio 2022 with the C++ workload and **clang-cl** (LLVM component)
- CMake ≥ 3.20, Ninja, Python 3.11+ with `pycryptodome`
- Git Bash (for `tools/relift.sh`)
- A checkout of [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) with
  `build-gate/ps3recomp_runtime.lib` built (default path `G:/recomp/ps3`; set
  `PS3RECOMP_DIR` and `PS3RECOMP_RUNTIME_LIB` for CMake and `PS3RECOMP` for
  `relift.sh` if yours is elsewhere). Until they are merged, the checkout needs
  two branches on top of `master`: `fix/fp-flow-control`, [#187](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/187) (without it the city
  draws black) and `fix/jobchain-join-flip-marker-securefile`,
  [#185](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/185) (without it about one
  frame in six flashes black)
- A scetool-format key file holding the NPDRM `appldr` keys and `NP_klic_free` / `NP_klic_key`

Steps:

1. Put the game's PKG(s) in `pkg/` and build the disc tree in `vfs/PS3_GAME/`,
   then decrypt the EBOOT to `game/EBOOT.elf`. The exact commands, and why the
   retail EBOOT needs a RAP, are in [docs/extracting.md](docs/extracting.md).
2. Lift and generate: `./tools/relift.sh` (writes
   `imports.json`, `analysis/`, `src/recomp/`, `src/gen/`, `src/spu_gen/`).
3. Build: `python build.py` (configures CMake + Ninja under the MSVC
   environment and builds `build/crazytaxi.exe`, Release).
4. Run:

   ```bash
   PS3_VFS_ROOT=vfs RSX_LIVE_DRAW=1 PS3_MAIN_STACK_LV2=1 \
       ./build/crazytaxi vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf
   ```

   A 1280x720 window opens. It shows "NOW LOADING", the ESRB, Sega and CRIWARE
   logos, then the title screen. Leave it at the title and the
   attract demo starts. The window title shows FPS, draws per frame and size.

## Usage

Headless capture, pressing START at 30 s and dumping every 120th frame:

```bash
mkdir -p scratch/frames
PAD_SCRIPT="30:0x0008" LD_FRAME_DUMP=scratch/frames LD_FRAME_DUMP_EVERY=120 \
PS3_VFS_ROOT=vfs RSX_LIVE_DRAW=1 PS3_MAIN_STACK_LV2=1 \
    ./build/crazytaxi vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf
```

`LD_FRAME_DUMP`'s directory has to exist before the run, or nothing is written.
Pad masks: START `0x0008`, CROSS `0x4000`.

## Building from source

Steps 2 and 3 above. Run `tools/relift.sh` again whenever ps3recomp's lifter
changes. Run `python build.py` again when the runtime library or this repo
changes. `--code-end 0x2A2598` in `relift.sh` matters: it sits just past the
`.lib.stub` trampolines, and `.rodata` follows in the same executable segment.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE), covering this repo's own build scripts and docs. Crazy Taxi is
© Sega. The screenshots and GIF are from the running recompilation and are here
only to show progress.

1390522941.description: Tornado Outbreak (PS3, BLUS30371) - static recompilation with ps3recomp. In game.
1390522941.readme_excerpt:
# tornado — Tornado Outbreak (PS3), static recompilation

`BLUS30371`, disc release (Loose Cannon Studios / Konami, 2009). Recompiled with
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp).

![Tornado Outbreak running natively on Windows: the tornado tears through the farmers' market](docs/media/hero.gif)

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Title screen](docs/media/title.png) | ![Main menu](docs/media/menu.png) |
| ![Story intro](docs/media/intro.png) | ![Dialogue](docs/media/dialogue.png) |
| ![The market](docs/media/market.png) | ![Gameplay](docs/media/gameplay.png) |

The window title shows the presented FPS, the draws in the last frame and the
backbuffer size, e.g. `Tornado Outbreak | FPS: 30.57 | draws: 58 | 1280x720`.

## Status

**In game.** Logos and Bink intro, title, main menu, New Game (the save is
created), the story intro and dialogue, then the first level (`jb_intro`) with
the tornado under player control, pulling apart the farmers' market. Rendering
is correct without any debug overrides. Gameplay runs at about 10–16 fps.

Known: a few seconds into the level, a comic-style white transition fills the
screen and does not clear. See [docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md).

## Why this title

Picked from a sweep of all 1,019 decryptable disc EBOOTs for low SPU load
(`ps3games/_triage/disc_sweep/`):

| | code | functions | SPU images in EBOOT | imports |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guitar Hero III | 9.7 MB | 28,987 | 5 (615 KB) | 229 |
| **Tornado Outbreak** | 5.3 MB | **17,138** | **1 (5 KB)** | **103** |

The one SPU image is a raw-SPU memcpy engine the PPU drives by mailbox. Wwise
runs two small audio jobs on a SPURS job chain.

## Building

```bash
./tools/relift.sh          # imports.json, functions.json, lifted tree, NID table, SPU image
python build.py            # cmake + ninja under the MSVC environment clang-cl needs
PS3_VFS_ROOT=vfs RSX_LIVE_DRAW=1 PS3_MAIN_STACK_LV2=1 \
    ./build/tornado vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf
```

`vfs/` is the disc tree (`PS3_GAME/...`). `game/EBOOT.elf` and
`vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf` are the decrypted EBOOT:

```bash
python ../twistedmetal/tools/decrypt_self.py vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN \
    --keys ../GT5P/data/keys -o game/EBOOT.elf
```

`PS3_MAIN_STACK_LV2=1` is required: the game's SPU memcpy picks its path by
comparing the destination with the stack's top nibble (see progress.md).

Headless, into gameplay (START, CROSS through the menu, New Game and the intro,
then the left stick forward from 252 s to 300 s; frames with `LD_FRAME_DUMP=<dir>`,
`LD_FRAME_DUMP_FROM=<frame>` to start late):

```bash
S="18:0x0008,50:0x4000,70:0x4000"; for t in $(seq 95 8 240); do S="$S,$t:0x4000"; done
PAD_SCRIPT="$S" PAD_STICK="128,0,128,128,252,300" LD_FRAME_DUMP=frames \
PS3_VFS_ROOT=vfs RSX_LIVE_DRAW=1 PS3_MAIN_STACK_LV2=1 ./build/tornado vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf
```

`PAD_SCRIPT` presses are wall-clock timed, so a slow boot can shift which
screen a press lands on.

The Wwise SPURS jobs must be captured and lifted once (`spu_miss/`, see
`tools/relift.sh`) or the game wedges after the New Game save.

## Legal

No game code, assets or keys here, only analysis and build configuration.

`BLUS31083`, disc release (Backbone Entertainment / Warner Bros., 2012): 30-odd
Midway and Atari arcade games behind a 3D front end. Recompiled to native
Windows with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), in the same
house style as its sister ports
[gh3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/gh3), [tornado](https://github.com/sp00nznet/tornado),

## Status

**Alpha — in game.** Boots through the logo movies (skipped: nothing decodes
them), the title screen, the profile notice and the game carousel, then loads
an arcade ROM set and runs it: Vindicators Part II plays its attract loop inside
the bezel art at about 25 fps. Coin input registers.

| Area | State |
|---|---|
| EBOOT decrypt | Works (disc EBOOT, `decrypt_self.py`) |
| PPU lift | 10,060 functions, 191 imports across 18 libraries, builds first time |
| SPU | No embedded ELF images; two raw SPURS render jobs (41,856 B and 816 B) cut from `.data` and lifted, 0 MISSes |
| Graphics | Title, menus, carousel and the emulated game render correctly; 0 dropped draws |
| Movies (`cellSail`) | Not decoded; each AVI is reported as played-to-end |
| Audio | Not checked |
| Input | START, CROSS, SELECT (coin) register. Each game opens a menu (Free Play, Score Attack, Controls); pressing CROSS through it hasn't yet produced a played credit |

Next steps are in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md); what was fixed and how it was found
is in [docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md).

## Getting Started

You need your own copy of the game. No game code, data or keys come with this
repo, and the recompiled source isn't distributed: you generate it locally from
your own dump.

Prerequisites (Windows 11):

- Visual Studio 2022 with the C++ workload and **clang-cl** (LLVM component)
- CMake ≥ 3.20, Ninja, Python 3.11+ with `pycryptodome`
- Git Bash (for `tools/relift.sh`)
- A checkout of [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). The
  default path is `G:/recomp/ps3`; elsewhere, set `PS3RECOMP_DIR` (Windows
  path, for `build.py`) and `PS3RECOMP` (Git Bash path, for `relift.sh`).
  It needs `build-gate/ps3recomp_runtime.lib` built. The checkout's
  `libs/spurs/cellSpurs.c` needs the Join fix from
  [#185](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/185), and
  `libs/codec/cellSail.c` the `STATE_CHANGED` events from
  [#190](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/190); both
  files are compiled into this port from the checkout, see `CMakeLists.txt`.
- A SELF decrypter: [`tools/decrypt_self.py`](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal/blob/main/tools/decrypt_self.py)
  from twistedmetal plus a scetool-format key file with the `appldr` keys (not
  supplied), or RPCS3 (`rpcs3 --decrypt EBOOT.BIN`)

Steps:

1. Extract the disc so the tree is `vfs/PS3_GAME/...` (`PARAM.SFO`,
   `USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN`, `USRDIR/0B/*.SR`, the three AVIs).
2. Decrypt the EBOOT, and put a copy next to the original:

   ```bash
   python path/to/twistedmetal/tools/decrypt_self.py vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN \
       --keys path/to/keys -o game/EBOOT.elf
   cp game/EBOOT.elf vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf
   ```

3. Lift and generate: `./tools/relift.sh` (writes `imports.json`, `analysis/`,
   `src/recomp/`, `src/gen/`, `spu_miss/`, `src/spu_gen/`; about a minute).
4. Build: `python build.py` (configures CMake + Ninja under the MSVC
   environment and builds `build/midway.exe`, Release; a few minutes).
5. Run:

   ```bash
   PS3_VFS_ROOT=vfs RSX_LIVE_DRAW=1 PS3_MAIN_STACK_LV2=1 \
       ./build/midway vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf
   ```

   A 1280x720 window opens: black for a few seconds while the logo movies are
   skipped, then "PRESS START BUTTON". The window title shows FPS, draws per
   frame and size.

## Usage

Headless (no window; works over RDP), START at the title, CROSS through the
profile notice and the carousel into Vindicators Part II, a frame every 300
flips to `scratch/fr/` (the directory must exist):

```bash
mkdir -p scratch/fr
PAD_SCRIPT="15:0x0008,25:0x4000,32:0x4000,39:0x4000,46:0x4000,53:0x4000" \
LD_FRAME_DUMP=scratch/fr LD_FRAME_DUMP_EVERY=300 \
PS3_VFS_ROOT=vfs RSX_LIVE_DRAW=1 PS3_MAIN_STACK_LV2=1 \
    ./build/midway --headless vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf
```

`--record out.mp4` pipes frames to ffmpeg; let the program exit on its own or
the MP4 has no index. Pad masks: START `0x0008`, CROSS `0x4000`, SELECT
`0x0001`. `PAD_SCRIPT` times are wall-clock, so a slow boot can move a press
onto a different screen.

## Building from source

Steps 3 and 4 above. Run `tools/relift.sh` again whenever ps3recomp's lifter
changes, and `python build.py` when the runtime library or this repo changes.
`--code-end 0x2525AC` in `relift.sh` matters: it sits just past the
`.lib.stub` trampolines, and `.rodata` follows in the same executable segment.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE), covering this repo's own build scripts and docs. Midway Arcade
Origins is © Warner Bros. Interactive; the arcade games are © their owners. The
screenshots are from the running recompilation and are here only to show
progress.

1394816513.description: Stand-in PSN matchmaking rooms and leaderboards for statically recompiled PS3 titles (ps3recomp)
1394816513.readme_excerpt:
# psnr

A stand-in for PSN's matchmaking rooms and leaderboards, for PS3 titles
statically recompiled with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp).
It is the PS3 counterpart of [xlive](https://github.com/sp00nznet/xlive). The
server hands out rooms and each peer's address; the players' game traffic then
goes directly between them.

## Status

**v0.1.0, alpha.**
- **Server:** rooms (Matching2-style) and leaderboards (Score-style) work, and
  the C client works. Both are tested against each other on Windows and Linux.
- **Games:** Simpsons Arcade plays an online match as two instances on one
  machine: create match, Quick Match, lobby, characters, then Stage 1
  together, in sync. Game traffic goes peer to peer. The work is
  [ps3recomp#200](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/200) (draft)
  and the lifter fix
  [ps3recomp#202](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/202), on top
  of the merged
  [ps3recomp#196](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/196).
  [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) has the rest.

## Screenshots

The status page (`http://127.0.0.1:36101/`) with one room open and two
leaderboards:

![Status page](docs/status.png)

## Getting Started

### Quick start

1. Download this repository as a zip and unpack it.
2. Double-click **`Setup.cmd`** (Windows) or run **`./setup.sh`** (Linux/macOS).
   - The script checks for Go and asks before installing it (winget, about
     70 MB).
   - It then builds the server and leaves a **`Start psnr.cmd`** (or
     `start-psnr.sh`) launcher in the folder.
3. Run the launcher, then open http://127.0.0.1:36101/ in a browser.

If setup fails, it prints one line saying what to do and where the full log is.

### Step by step

Prerequisites: Go 1.22 or newer (`go version`). On Windows, a new terminal
window is needed after installing Go before `go` is on `PATH`.

1. Build:
   ```
   cd server
   go build -o psnr.exe .     # "psnr" on Linux/macOS
   ```
2. Run:
   ```
   psnr.exe
   ```
   Expected output:
   ```
   2026/09/29 02:17:35 psnr 0.1.0: clients on [::]:36100
   2026/09/29 02:17:35 status page on http://127.0.0.1:36101/
   ```
3. Open http://127.0.0.1:36101/. It shows no rooms and no leaderboards until a
   client connects.

Players connect to TCP 36100. Ports, flags and Docker are covered in
[docs/running.md](docs/running.md).

## Usage

```
psnr -addr :36100 -http 127.0.0.1:36101 -v    # log every room event
docker compose up -d                          # same thing, in a container
curl http://127.0.0.1:36101/api/stats         # rooms and boards as JSON
```

To talk to it from C, add `client/psnr.c` and `client/psnr.h` to the build:

```c
psnr_client* c = psnr_connect("server", 36100, "NPWR00860_00", "alice",
                              3658 /* P2P port */, &user_id, public_ip);
uint32_t req = psnr_send(c, PSNR_SEARCH_ROOMS, body, len);   /* async */
psnr_msg m;
while (psnr_poll(c, &m) == 1) {        /* replies and pushes, never blocks */
    /* m.req == req for its reply; m.req == 0 for MEMBER_JOINED etc. */
    psnr_msg_free(&m);
}
```

Every message is documented in [docs/api.md](docs/api.md).

### Playing online

A recompiled title goes online when these are set in its environment (this
needs a ps3recomp build with
[#200](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/200); its `docs/ONLINE.md`
has the full list):

```
PS3_NET_ONLINE=1           # real sockets instead of the offline stubs
PSNR_SERVER=host[:port]    # this server
PS3_NP_ONLINE_ID=homer     # the player's name; also gives the instance its own console identity
PS3_NET_P2P_PORT=3658      # the UDP/TCP port peers reach this player on
PS3_VERBOSE=0              # keep diagnostic logging from slowing the game down
```

Two instances on one machine need different `PS3_NP_ONLINE_ID`s and
`PS3_NET_P2P_PORT`s. Across machines, each player's P2P port must be reachable
by the others.

## Docs

- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md): the parts, why the client has
  no threads, and why game traffic doesn't go through the server
- [docs/api.md](docs/api.md): the protocol
- [docs/running.md](docs/running.md): flags, ports, Docker, state
- [lab/](lab/README.md): players behind NATing routers, in Docker (`lab/run.sh`)

## Building from source

```
go vet ./...
go test ./...      # also builds and runs client/test_psnr.c if a C compiler is on PATH
```

To test the C client on its own against a running server:

```
cc -std=gnu11 -o test_psnr client/psnr.c client/test_psnr.c    # add -lws2_32 on Windows
./test_psnr 127.0.0.1 36100
```

## Security

There are no accounts or passwords, and everyone in a room learns the other
players' IP addresses. Run it for people you'd let onto your network. Details
are in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

psnr is an independent project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony
Interactive Entertainment; PlayStation and PSN are its trademarks. It contains
no Sony code or game content, and implements its own protocol. You need your
own legally obtained copies of the games.

1398817675.readme_excerpt:
# Killzone for Windows (native PC port)

A native Windows port of Killzone (PlayStation 2, 2004) by [drakolordx7](https://github.com/drakolordx7). The game's code is recompiled to C++ with [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp), so it runs as a PC program with mouse and keyboard aim, high frame rates, higher resolutions and ultrawide support.

> **This project is abandoned.** It is no longer maintained and the repository is archived, so issues and pull requests are closed. The code is free to fork and continue under the license below.

[Download the last build (v0.1.7)](https://github.com/drakolordx7/KillzoneRecomp/releases/latest)

No game files are included; you need your own disc image of Killzone: the US version (SCUS-97402) or, from v0.1.6, the European version (SCES-52893, English/Russian/Greek). The game detects which one you have. Not affiliated with Sony or Guerrilla Games.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit
- CPU with SSE4.1: Intel Core 2 (45 nm, Penryn), AMD FX (Bulldozer) or newer. Newer CPUs get the faster AVX and AVX2 code automatically
- GPU with Direct3D 11, Direct3D 12 or Vulkan

## Usage

1. Unzip the build into a folder and run `killzone.exe`.
2. In the launcher, browse to your Killzone `.iso`.
3. Pick your settings and press Play.

Settings are in `killzone.ini` and saves in `disc\mc0` (US) or `disc_pal\mc0` (Europe), all next to `killzone.exe`. Unzipping a build over an older one keeps settings and saves.

Mouse and keyboard work out of the box, and so do controllers with the original PS2 layout. The launcher's Controls tab lists the keys; change them in `killzone.ini` under `[Bindings]`. Ultrawide, intro skip, toggle sprint and the graphics options are in the launcher too; `README.txt` in the zip lists the controls.

## Reporting problems

The project is archived, so new issues can't be opened. The [closed and open issues](https://github.com/drakolordx7/KillzoneRecomp/issues?q=is%3Aissue) list the known problems. `killzone.log` in the game folder (and `killzone.prev.log` for the run before) shows what happened in a run.

## Contributing

- The repository is archived and takes no pull requests. Fork it to continue the work; `master` is what the releases were built from.
- `ext/PS2Recomp` is the `killzone` branch of [drakolordx7/PS2Recomp](https://github.com/drakolordx7/PS2Recomp). General runtime fixes belong upstream in PS2Recomp.
- Building needs Windows x64, Visual Studio 2022 or later, CMake, Ninja and Python 3:
  1. `git clone --recursive https://github.com/drakolordx7/KillzoneRecomp`
  2. Put the PCSX2 source in `ext/pcsx2` (commit `646df006a4`), the [PCSX2 Windows dependencies](https://github.com/PCSX2/pcsx2-windows-dependencies/releases/tag/latest-windows-dependencies) in `ext/kzgs/deps` and the SDL3 VC development package in `ext/sdl3`.
  3. Copy `SCUS_974.02` from your disc into `game/`. For European disc support, also put `SCES_528.93` in `work/pal/elf/` (optional; without it the build is US only).
  4. `tools\scripts\build_ps2recomp.bat`, then `python tools\scripts\regen.py` (writes about 20,000 C++ files to `generated/`; `regen.py --pal` writes the European set to `generated_pal/`), then `tools\scripts\build.bat RelWithDebInfo`.
  5. `tools\scripts\make_release.ps1 -Version x.y.z -From build\RelWithDebInfo` makes the release zip.
- Reverse-engineering notes and measurements are in [`docs/findings.md`](docs/findings.md); runtime changes are described in [`patches/README.md`](patches/README.md).

## Credits

123bf526d26913cdae31ec5b6bc54dbac29646eb.message:
The launcher updates the port from its GitHub releases (Windows)

When the launcher opens it reads the repository's release list -- not
GitHub's "latest release", which leaves pre-releases out, and every
release so far is one -- on a thread nothing waits for, and offers the
newest release above its own version that has a Windows zip with a
SHA-256 digest: "Update to ..." in the footer opens an Update panel with
the release's notes, Install Update and Release Page.

Install Update (src/install/update.cpp): the zip is downloaded into
.update/ beside the program (WinHTTP), checked against the size and digest
GitHub lists, unpacked (install/zip.h, CRC-checked; the '\' names of
PowerShell's Compress-Archive taken), and each file swapped in: the old one
renamed to <name>.old, which Windows allows for the running program and its
DLLs, the new one moved into its place. A failed swap puts back every file
swapped so far; a failed try leaves nothing. game/, gamedata/ and an
existing dod3.ini are never written. The launcher then starts the new
dod3.exe and closes; the new one's first start removes the .old files and
says what it was updated from. The approach follows King Kong
Recompiled's updater (MIT).

Settings > System > Check for Updates (DOD3_UPDATE_CHECK = 0 turns it
off). The Mac's app is replaced another way: compiled out there for now.

Checked: a build acting as 0.4.0 (DOD3_UPDATE_AS) found 0.4.1 on GitHub,
downloaded it, matched its digest and installed it -- the folder then
equal to the 0.4.1 zip file for file but for dod3.ini, which kept the
player's line -- and started 0.4.1. From a local release
(DOD3_UPDATE_API, DOD3_UPDATE_ZIP): the new build cleaned up after itself
and said "Updated from"; a wrong digest installed nothing; a file held
open mid-swap put every file back (1,736 files unchanged).

done now: a thread nobody can join has its host thread released when it

the last.

2e87a0061f01bcc59898b233381bd923b15c3441.message:
Loads: the package loader's reads natively; DOD3_LOAD_LOG; DOD3_PROF on macOS

What a load waits on, measured on the Mac (start-up, New Game -> prologue):
the game thread, running Unreal's package loader. Reads take ~85 us and the
I/O and inflate threads are idle over 80% of a load; the loader is millions
of tiny reads, each a virtual call to FArchiveAsync::Serialize and the
guest's memcpy, both lifted with a page-table test on every load and store.

src/patches/archive_native.cpp, through the function registry (no re-lift):
- FArchiveAsync::Serialize (func_00141420): bytes already in the precache
  buffer, with the read done, are one memcpy; anything else (outside the
  buffer, a read in flight, pages a diagnostic watches, overlap) runs the
  lifted body. Over 99.9% of reads take the native path.
- FLinkerLoad::Serialize (func_0014A32C), which only forwards to the
  archive: straight to the native one.
- FLinkerLoad::operator<<(FName&) (thunk func_0014A62C): index and number
  in one step; an index outside the name map is the lifted one's to report.
DOD3_ARCHIVE_NATIVE=0 turns them off. 1.01 only (eboot.h).

Measured, interleaved runs, with ps3recomp 9b62c14 (one TLS lookup a
virtual call):
- start-up to the title's loading frame: 3.18 -> 2.95 s (fastest of 6
  each; medians 3.32 -> 3.00)
- New Game load span: 1.85-1.91 -> 1.56-1.60 s (3 runs each); its
  blocking frame 406-412 -> 311-312 ms; the 48-package load 27-29 -> 24
  frames
Chapter 0 plays as before (live run, frame grabs).

Tools for the next ones:
- DOD3_LOAD_LOG=1 (patches/load_idle.cpp): the start-up's steps timed from
  the process's launch, each load's span, frames and longest frame, the
  native/lifted read counts, and every frame over 100 ms (handed to the
  profiler's slow-frame report on both platforms).
- DOD3_PROF on macOS (src/os/macos/prof_mac.cpp): the Windows profiler's
  switches and report (DOD3_PROF_TREE, _CALLERS, _REPORT), from inside the
  process: thread_suspend and a frame-pointer walk, names fr

4656b695d8017022b37524e2d18ef1075af1f5ef.message:
Crash report for an end that raises no exception; the log flushed first

abort(), std::terminate, the C runtime's invalid-argument and pure-call
checks end the process in a fast fail the exception filter never sees: the
game closed with no [crash] line, and a log on disk lost its last 200 ms of
buffered lines with it -- the shape of issue 3's log, which stops mid-boot.
Each now writes "[crash] <what> on thread <name>" with the stack and flushes
both streams before the process goes; the exception filter flushes stdout
too now, not only stderr. One abort() the port has is the lifted libsre
LFQueue push path's assertion trap (src/kernel/spurs_lfqueue.cpp), which
the zlib tasks use while the boot loads its packages.

527495dd5dcdb40857935efe907df16842d910a9.message:
The lifted libsre built with PPU_INLINE_VM too

It includes the game's ppu_recomp.h. Since the ps3recomp v0.18 lifter,
code lifted without PPU_INLINE_VM opens each function with a copy of the
memory model (PPU_MM_SNAP) that only a header from a v0.18 lift defines;
libsre is lifted at build time, the game's header comes from an older
lift, and the build failed. With PPU_INLINE_VM, libsre takes the game's
inline fast path, which falls back to the full accessors wherever they
matter (an SPU's reserved line, the raw SPU window, the diagnostics).

checks against a cache and merges pipeline lists. The upstream merge changed
the shader text, so the 0.4.0 cache holds only 584 of the 1,494 programs a
sweep of every chapter met; the next release's cache is to be rebuilt this

c01e96c6a88df4941f1129ff6ca950777081be17.message:
Frame rate: a cap is shown at even intervals, and Adaptive

The camera juddered at any frame rate, with a controller as with the
mouse. The camera's own law holds frame by frame (the turn is what the
stick and the frame's time say it should be); what was uneven was the
time each frame stayed on screen.

Capped: the game's frames are exactly 16.67 ms of simulation at 60, but
they were presented 13 to 20 ms apart. The renderer's pacer (fork
8b9a035) is turned on whenever a cap is in force, and told the cap's
period: at 60, 1 to 7% of the presents are now more than 15% off the one
before, against 40 to 65%.

Uncapped: the frames take 5 to 20 ms each, half of them more than 15%
off the one before, and each is simulated for the time the last one
took, so a steady turn comes out at 60 to 210 degrees a second from
frame to frame. There is no slack to pace that in. DOD3_FPS=adaptive
(Frame Rate: Adaptive on the Graphics Settings page) is a cap that
follows the scene: the highest of 120, 110, 100, 90, 80, 72, 66, 60, 55,
50, 45, 40, 36, 33, 30 at which 95 in 100 of the last second and a
half's frames were made in time with 4% to spare. It steps down at once
and up after two seconds within reach, so it stays put for long
stretches and the pacer can do its work. In a played session it sat at
120 with 0 to 2% of the presents more than 15% off the one before (the
arrivals: 44 to 53%); on a loaded machine, about 3% at 60 to 70 where
uncapped averaged 115 to 120 on paper.

DOD3_FPS_ADAPT=<quantile>,<margin>,<seconds> and DOD3_FPS_ADAPT_LOG=1
are in the debugging guide with RSX_PRESENT_PACE_LOG.

Not measured: v-sync on with a cap that does not divide the display's
refresh rate.

d7812558337fdf7ce50429ba1ef31f253c0fc7be.message:
Draw Distance and Tree Detail

Two rows on the Advanced Graphics page, for the scenery that appears in
front of the player in the open areas.

Draw Distance (DOD3_DRAW_DISTANCE = 2, 3, 5, 10): the engine's
MaxDrawDistanceScale, which the scene renderer multiplies every
primitive's own cull distance by each frame. Live. It moves the props,
bushes and small trees that have such a distance.

Tree Detail (DOD3_TREE_LOD = 2, 3, 5, 10): the SpeedTrees have four
distances of their own (the model's detail from 500 to 6,000 units, the
flat billboard from 8,000, nothing past 12,000 to 16,000 for most trees
of the first chapter's coast), which the draw distance does not reach.
They are copied into the tree's scene proxy when it is made, and read
from there once, as the tree's meshes are put in the draw lists. So the
proxy's are multiplied as it is made: USpeedTreeComponent::
CreateSceneProxy (func_00817FD4, a virtual and the constructor's only
caller) is replaced in the function registry. Trees already in the
scene keep what they were added with -- writing a live proxy changes
nothing on screen, which is why earlier attempts at this from outside
showed nothing -- so the row says "from the next area".

Checked in three runs to the same spot on the coast's landing stage:
at 0.2 the woods on either side are gone, at 1 the pines on the cliff
are their soft billboards, at 3 they are their models and a tree past
the far bank is drawn that was not. And set from the page itself to 3
before the level was loaded: all 64 trees' proxies hold three times
their components' distances.

What still appears late is what the game has not loaded yet: the further
parts of a level are streamed in as the player nears them.

1.01 only (the addresses are not mapped for 1.00, where the tree row is
left out). No re-lift is needed.

da6a1a510cf4d30c0393f7f16a17add079c3a177.message:
Aspect Ratio: the HUD fitted into the view; 16:10; movies and the title as on that screen

In a view boxed to another shape the HUD's canvas is the view's: moved to
its corner and as big as it is. The HUD lays itself out on 1280x720 whatever
the canvas, so at 21:9 it ran off the bottom of the view. Now
Sqex03GameHUD.DrawHUD hands its canvas to the port (bridge 17) and
src/patches/hud_aspect.cpp makes the canvas's top transform a scale and a
move that put the 16:9 HUD in the middle of the view, as big as fits; the
canvas reports 1280x720 meanwhile, as the HUD's native code places some
things by its size. The markers placed on the view (enemy gauges, lock-on,
talk icons) are mapped back through it in hooks on UCanvas::execProject and
ASqex03GameHUD::CalcTransformPosition, so they stay on their targets. The
30 full-screen layers of the HUD's scripts -- fades, dimming, filters, the
dying overlay, the screen-split effect -- are marked by the script patch and
cover the whole view. A narrower view's room above and below the HUD is
clipped (through the depth, the 2D canvas having no depth test): the HUD
keeps a bar parked above itself there.

The HUD's begin also tells the present the view's shape each frame, and the
setting the screen's (ps3recomp: rsx_present_set_screen_aspect), so that
the title, menus and movies are 16:9 in the middle of that screen: a 16:9
window set to 21:9 shows what a 21:9 screen would.

16:10 is a choice of the setting (and auto takes a window narrower than
16:9): the view keeps its FOV and is taller. The fit only runs when the
setting has boxed the view, so 16:9 is as it was.

1.00 keeps the HUD as it was (the hooks' addresses are 1.01's) and gets the
present's half. Replay regression: 110 of 110 frames identical.

df1c0b49f15cc73df2c64de6f90f3c5a69969912.message:
The setup takes the US PSN release's game package in place of the disc

Drakengard 3 was also sold on PSN in the US (NPUB31251). Its game package,
UP0082-NPUB31251_00-DOD3MAINGAME0000 (1.00), holds the disc's files but for
four: an executable of its own build, COALESCED_INT.BIN as an .EDAT, both
under the buyer's licence, a PARAM.SFO of its own, and a PS3TOC.TXT whose
one line names that .EDAT. The port runs the disc release's 1.01 executable
and reads the config from its update, so neither locked file is wanted.

The setup now takes the package in the disc's slot, checked by the SHA-1 its
footer carries, and unpacks it as the disc is laid out (PS3_GAME/...),
leaving out its EBOOT.BIN and the .EDAT; the file list's line goes back to
the disc's, which makes the list the disc's own (checked by its hash). The
update is the disc release's for either: the PSN release's own 1.01 update
and the European release (NPEB01407, a build of its own) are refused with
what to add instead. An installed game is now told by its PARAM.SFO and
PS3TOC.TXT, not by EBOOT.BIN, which a 1.01 build never reads there.

pkg_extract takes an optional layout naming where each entry goes (or that
it is left out). The setup's pages, README.md, docs/PLAYING.md and
docs/BUILDING.md name the PSN package beside the disc.

Tested: an install from the package with the update and a DLC pack has
8,791 files identical to a disc install's, the others as above; a new game
from it reaches the chapter 1 battle at 60 fps, the settings pages in place
and the config read from the update. The disc installed over it, and the
package over that, each swap the game and keep the update and the DLC.

## Contents - [About](#about) - [Installing](#installing) - [Building](#building) - [Status](#status) - [How it fits together](#how-it-fits-together) - [Legal](#legal) - [Credits](#credits) ## About A native PC port of **Drakengard 3** (Drag-On Dragoon 3, PlayStation 3, BLUS31197) for Windows, macOS and Linux, made by static recompilation of the game's code on the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) toolkit. The game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C++ ahead of time and built into a normal executable, with the PS3's system libraries replaced by native implementations and the RSX graphics by Direct3D 12, Metal or Vulkan. There is no emulation at run time. ![The start of the game, running natively on Windows](docs/images/opening.jpg) **Nothing of the game is in this repository.** You need your own copy of Drakengard 3: the US disc and the game's 1.01 update, plus whatever DLC you own. The installer takes them from there. If this helped you, consider [buying me a coffee](https://ko-fi.com/soyjack) ## Installing What you need: - A PC with Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), a GPU with Direct3D 12 and a CPU with AVX2 (Intel Haswell / AMD Zen or newer), or a Mac with Apple silicon on macOS 13 or newer. About 16 GB of free disk space, 10 GB more for the Japanese voice pack and about 3 GB for the Spanish translation. - Your copy of the game, US release, as either: - the disc (BLUS31197), dumped to a folder or a **decrypted** `.iso` ([PS3 Disc Dumper](https://github.com/13xforever/ps3-disc-dumper) writes one; an image from an ordinary disc tool is still encrypted and is refused), or - the PSN release (NPUB31251): the game's package as a PlayStation 3 downloads it (`UP0082-NPUB31251_00-DOD3MAINGAME0000`, 15.6 GB). No licence files are needed. Other regions, the European PSN release among them, are refused. - The 1.01 update, as the package a PlayStation 3 downloads: `UP0082-BLUS31197_00-DOD3PATCH0000000-A0101-V0101-PE.pkg`. This is the disc release's update; the PSN release takes it too. - Optionally, the DLC packages you own (`UP0082-NPUB31251_00-...`). No licence files are needed. - Optionally, mods: the Spanish fan translation and the DLC Undub (Japanese voices for the DLC chapters), which the launcher installs on its Mods page; see [docs/PLAYING.md](docs/PLAYING.md#mods). Windows: 1. Download `dod3-recomp--win64.zip` from the [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) and unzip it anywhere (not inside Program Files). 2. Run `dod3.exe`. SmartScreen may warn the first time, as the program is not signed: "More info", then "Run anyway". 3. In the setup that opens, add your files (the disc image or folder, or the PSN game package; the update package; any DLC packages) with Add Files / Add Folder, in any order, then Install. The game's files are copied into the `game` folder next to `dod3.exe` (a few minutes). 4. Play. From then on `dod3.exe` opens the launcher: Play, and the game's mods, DLC and settings. macOS: 1. Download `dod3-recomp--macos-arm64.zip` from the [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases), unzip it and move "Drakengard 3 Recompiled.app" to Applications. 2. The app is not notarised, so macOS refuses it the first time. On macOS 15 and later: open it once, then allow it in System Settings > Privacy & Security ("Open Anyway"). On macOS 13 and 14: Control-click the app, choose Open, then Open again. 3. The setup opens as on Windows. The game's files go into `~/Library/Application Support/Drakengard 3 Recompiled`. Linux (x86-64; the Steam Deck included), experimental: 1. Download `dod3-recomp--linux-x86_64.tar.gz` from the [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) and unpack it anywhere you can write to. It needs a Vulkan 1.3 driver (Mesa's RADV, ANV, or NVIDIA's), SDL2 (`sdl2` or `sdl2-compat`; SteamOS has it) and glibc 2.38 or newer. 2. Run `dod3` in the folder. The setup opens as on Windows, and the game's files are copied into the `game` folder beside it. Add Files uses the desktop's picker (kdialog or zenity); without either, `./dod3 --install ` in a terminal does the same. 3. On a Steam Deck: install from Desktop Mode, then add `dod3` to Steam as a non-Steam game to play it in Game Mode. `dod3.log` beside it says what happened if it does not start. Settings (resolution, display mode, frame-rate cap, anti-aliasing, field of view, draw distance, skipping the intro, the keyboard's keys) are in the launcher's Settings, in the game's own Settings menu (Graphics Settings, System Settings, Advanced Graphics and Picture Settings), or in `dod3.ini`. [docs/PLAYING.md](docs/PLAYING.md) has the controls, the saves, the Japanese voices, and what to do if something goes wrong. ## Building The port is built in three steps: the game's PPU code is lifted to C++, its SPU programs are lifted, and the whole is compiled with CMake. Lifting needs the game's executable, so you need your own copy of the game first. 1. **Toolchain.** Windows: Visual Studio 2022 or newer (the Build Tools are enough, with "Desktop development with C++" and the Windows SDK), LLVM with clang-cl, CMake 3.20 or later, Ninja, Python 3.11 or later, Git for Windows, and vcpkg with `zlib:x64-windows` and `sdl2:x64-windows` (`VCPKG_ROOT`, or `C:\vcpkg`). macOS: Xcode's command-line tools and, from Homebrew, `cmake ninja python zlib sdl2 glslang spirv-cross`. Linux: Clang, CMake, Ninja, Python and the SDL2, zlib, Vulkan and glslang development files (Ubuntu 24.04 package names, and the Steam Deck's distrobox, in [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md#prerequisites)). All three also need a decrypted `libsre.prx` from the PS3 firmware ([docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md#the-games-files)). 2. **The sources.** ```sh git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp cd dod3-recomp python3 -m venv .venv # py -3 -m venv .venv on Windows .venv/bin/pip install -r ps3recomp/tools/requirements.txt -r tools/requirements.txt ``` 3. **The game's files.** Any built `dod3` (a release's, or one from another machine) installs the game into the repository root, which decrypts the update's executable to `elf/EBOOT_101.ELF` and lays out `game/disc`: ```sh DOD3_INSTALL_BASE=. path/to/dod3 --install [DLC .pkg ...] ``` 4. **Lift the PPU code** (a few minutes; about 550 MB of C++ in `recompiled_101/`): ```sh .venv/bin/python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_loader.py elf/EBOOT_101.ELF -o out/v101/ .venv/bin/python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_lifter.py elf/EBOOT_101.ELF \ --functions out/v101/EBOOT_101.functions.json \ --hle-stubs out/v101/EBOOT_101.imports.json \ --code-end 0x157fc00 \ --nonvolatile-locals \ --hook 0x000C1E50 --hook 0x00EE7728 --hook 0x00272E58 \ -o recompiled_101/ ``` 5. **Lift the SPU programs** into `spu/`, with the native fast paths hooked in: ```sh tools/lift_spu.sh ``` 6. **Compile.** Windows, from a plain command prompt (the script finds Visual Studio, LLVM, CMake and vcpkg): ```bat tools\build_win.bat ``` macOS: ```sh cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build ``` A clean build takes about 15 minutes, nearly all of it the lifted code. 7. **Run** the game installed in the repository root: ```sh DOD3_INSTALL_BASE=. build/dod3 ``` [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md) has the CMake options, the developer run form, packaging a release and regenerating the committed tables; [docs/TECHNICAL.md](docs/TECHNICAL.md) how the port works; [docs/DEBUGGING.md](docs/DEBUGGING.md) the switches, profiling and the regression tests; [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) the layout of the tree and the conventions. ## Status | | | |---|---| | Windows 10/11, Direct3D 12 | Playable. 60 fps at 4K on an RTX 4090 / i9-13900K (chapter 1 through the heavy destruction scene, open areas, the village); 120 fps holds at lower resolutions | | Windows, Vulkan | Experimental (`RSX_BACKEND = vulkan`) | | Linux, Vulkan | Experimental. Tested on a Steam Deck (SteamOS, Desktop Mode): the chapter 1 battle at 55-65 fps uncapped, the heaviest moments in the 40s; Gaming Mode not yet tried | | macOS 13+, Apple silicon, Metal | Playable. 60 fps at 1080p in battle on an M1 Pro | | Game version | The 1.01 update (required) | | DLC | All 20 packs, including the Japanese voice pack | What the port adds over the original: any internal resolution (supersampling included), windowed, borderless or full-screen display, wider screens (16:10, 21:9, 32:9), a frame-rate cap of your choice (60 and 120 tested) or one that follows the scene, with the frames shown at even intervals, FXAA or MSAA, anisotropic filtering, a wider field of view, sharper shadows, a longer draw distance for scenery and for trees, HDR (Windows and macOS: the light the game clips at white goes up to your display's peak), a depth of field and bloom drawn smoothly at high resolutions, depth of field and the blood on the screen each on or off, skipping the intro logos and movie, pausing or muting when the window is in the background, keyboard and mouse, trophies (a pop-up as you earn one, and their list in the launcher), cheats, and the button prompts of the pad you hold -- set in the launcher, or in a Graphics Settings, a System Settings, an Advanced Graphics and a Picture Settings page added to the game's own Settings menu. The launcher also installs your DLC and two fan-made mods (the Spanish translation, with the added pages in Spanish, and the DLC Undub), and on Windows updates the port from its releases. Known issues: the game has been tested on few machines, and at 16:10, 21:9 and 32:9 some of the HUD is still out of place. ## How it fits together ``` elf/EBOOT_101.ELF --ppu_loader/ppu_lifter--> recompiled_101/*.cpp (the game's PPU code as C++) SPU programs --tools/lift_spu.sh------> spu/ (SPURS tasks, jobs, the audio DSP) src/ ---------------------------> the port: the runner, native fast paths, the settings menu, the installer ps3recomp/ ---------------------------> runtime, HLE libraries, the RSX draw engine and its backends ``` The executable `dod3` installs the game from your files (a Dear ImGui setup, `src/install/` and `src/ui/`), then opens a launcher for its mods, DLC and settings, and runs it. ## Legal This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Square Enix, Access Games or Sony Interactive Entertainment. 04045ed1cb62931d4a89920985661d2b232b8d0e.message:
spu_interp: SPU_INTERP_STATS also lists where the interpreter is entered

Entries are credited to the image that owns the resident code region, so
the list names the lift that is missing them. Entries spread over a code
body mean its lift isn't dispatched at all; a few hot ones inside an
otherwise lifted body are resume points (return addresses after an SPU
interrupt) or function starts the lifter didn't find. In God of War HD the
remaining interpreted SPU time comes from four of them (0xA68 in the
Wws_Job policy module, 0x5318 and 0x87E8 in the mixer job).

06aa9375568380b75c2a35b9bd91959aa321310b.message:
sceNp: tickets, account region and network time answer OFFLINE

sceNpManagerRequestTicket2, GetTicket, GetTicketParam,
GetAccountRegion and GetNetworkTime were not implemented, so their
imports answered CELL_OK with nothing written. A title that asked for a
ticket waited for a GOT_TICKET manager event that never came, and one
that read the region or the time used whatever was in its buffer.

Implement them with RPCS3's argument checks and offline answers: without
a psnr server the NP manager is OFFLINE and so are these
(SCE_NP_ERROR_OFFLINE), and there is never a ticket, so GetTicket
reports a size of 0 and GetTicketParam INVALID_STATE. Signed in to a
psnr server, which issues no tickets, a request is answered at once with
a GOT_TICKET event carrying an error instead of a ticket size; the
region is the fake account's (US, English) and the network time is the
host clock as a CellRtcTick.

06b2292def31186d507aa8cfd38ed487ec220a9c.message:
.github/workflows: pin the five third-party actions to commit SHAs

release.yml fires on `push: tags: ['v*']` with `permissions: contents:
write`, so every action it invokes runs holding a token that can write to
this repo and attach release assets. Referenced by floating major tag, any
of those five actions could be retargeted upstream -- a tag is mutable, and
whoever controls it controls what executes inside that job. Pinning to a
commit SHA makes the referenced code immutable.

Each SHA is the commit the action's current major tag points at, so this
changes no behaviour: the same code runs, it just can no longer be swapped
out from under us. The readable version stays in a trailing comment because
a bare SHA tells a later reader nothing about how stale the pin is.

Only `uses:` lines and their comments change -- 13 references across all
five workflows, no other workflow edits.

(cherry picked from commit 903d023f4a88ace083b0d9843fd3cf71a40f6572)

0e0eebc657b9e5579faaec91f40acd9d846c39c8.message:
rsx_d3d12: drop the texture-slot SRVs that overwrote the SRV heap

vp_upload_tex_slot wrote an SRV for each uploaded texture at heap slot
1+slot. Nothing reads those: every draw writes its own SRVs into its
window at DRAW_SRV_BASE. Since VP_TEX_SLOTS went to 96 they cover heap
slots 1..96, over the offscreen-RT SRVs and the windows of the first
draws of the frame, so a texture uploaded late in the pre-pass (a new
or animated one) replaced a descriptor an earlier draw had already
written.

0e8b9ef2ca28fae79e8e24d2dede074581350fb7.message:
rsx engine: a depth snapshot is the region the texture names

The engine's host depth target is at least canvas-sized
(eng_zdepth_get), but a depth texture covers only the top-left
width x height of it. eng_zdepth_snapshot resolved the whole target and
the Metal resolve sampled it with normalized coordinates, so a 128x160
shadow map in the corner of a 1280x720 target was stretched over the
whole canvas and the lookups landed outside the map.

eng_zdepth_snapshot takes the texture's size and asks the backend for
that region (clamped to the target); a cached snapshot is reused only at
the same size. The Metal resolve reads the depth 1:1 (src.read at the
fragment's pixel) instead of sampling it, so a smaller snapshot is the
top-left region. The Vulkan backend's copy already works this way.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) samples small shadow maps from
canvas-sized zetas. In the port, this together with #424 and the port's
other depth-texture changes removes the dark rectangles on the ground
under shadows; the effect was not isolated per change.

Tests: test_color_feedback_engine (a 128x160 texture over a 256x256 zeta
asks for a 128x160 snapshot), test_metal_depth_readback (a 2x2 snapshot
holds the top-left texels 1:1).

118b6281a756697391f178e523a409e0b1f60ce1.message:
cellGcmSys: GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS sets how long a FIFO park may stand

When the drain stops on a self-jump park and `put` has moved, it waits
GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS (50 ms) for the title to patch the park and then follows
`put`. That suits a title that leaves a park standing when it switches
segments. It does not suit one that appends commands right after the
park, moves `put` there and patches the park last: if the patch comes
after the grace, the drain skips the commands in between.

God of War HD does the latter, and while it loads its menu the two stores
have been more than 50 ms apart: the drain jumped from 0x57C40 to put
0x5AA2C, dropped ~11 KB of commands with a fence among them, and the boot
stopped (once in about 45 runs). The RSX itself would wait.

GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS=<ms> now sets the grace; the default is unchanged.

147e59a79e63cefcf0c2f53fc7314d83f54167e2.message:
rsx_d3d12: pass the FP depth-export bits of SHADER_CONTROL

Draws recorded only the 32-bit-exports bit of SET_SHADER_CONTROL, so a
fragment program that replaces the fragment depth (bits 1-3) was
translated without SV_Depth. God of War HD's resolve pass writes the
scene depth it reads from the 2x-AA depth surface into the resolved
one this way; without it the pass wrote the quad's own depth (0), and
every depth-tested pass after it failed everywhere: the stencil
shadows, the fog, rain, the waterfall mist and the glows.

The draw now records the export bits (32-bit exports and depth export)
as fp_ctrl, part of the pipeline key, and hands them to the
decompiler, which already emits SV_Depth from r1.z.

1530be7cfd1295f9db57e380a3dc2314770a82c1.message:
ppu_lifter: per-function copy of the memory model; PPU_FAST_FP

A guest store goes through vm_base + ea, a byte pointer the compiler
cannot tell apart from the memory-model globals, so the inline load and
store paths reloaded vm_base, ppu_vm_size, ppu_hle_inject_base and the
two enable flags after every store. Each lifted function now copies them
into a local at entry (PPU_MM_SNAP) and its accesses use the copy. They
are all set before guest code runs. The SPU reservation bitmap and the
store watches can change while a function runs, so those are still read
from the globals. Code outside lifted functions keeps vm_read*_inl and
vm_write*_inl, which now take a fresh copy per access.

PPU_FAST_FP, off unless the build defines it, drops the NaN checks in
ppu_fp_bin and ppu_fmadd_core. The host's NaN differs from the PPC one
only in its sign and in which of two NaN operands propagates.

God of War HD, func_001BEFA4, built with FMA3: 6,195 instructions before,
5,855 with the copy, 4,553 with PPU_FAST_FP as well (branches 1,342,
1,063, 583).

test_ppu_lift.py: the conformance driver defines PPU_NO_INLINE_LOADS. Its
vm_read*/vm_write* are its own functions, and its statements do not run
inside a lifted function.

159a47de817b1ef3206f4df7ddab80ceb0312801.message:
ps3_indirect_call: one thread-local lookup a call, not two

On macOS every access to a __thread variable is a call to tlv_get_addr, and
the fast path made two a call: the recursion depth before it and the
trampoline after it. Unreal's package loader is virtual calls through and
through, and in a load tlv_get_addr was up to a fifth of the game thread's
samples (5-20%, in-process sampler). Both variables are this file's
thread-locals, so they are one per-thread block at a fixed distance; the
fast path looks up the trampoline's address once and reaches the depth by
that distance (worked out at the first call). Same behaviour; the depth
test (tools/test_ppu_dispatch_depth.py) passes.

Measured on the Mac, Drakengard 3 start-up to the title, interleaved runs:
3.23 -> 3.14 s median (5 runs each). Where a thread-local is a load off a
register (Windows, Linux) it saves an instruction or two.

ftrace: a span for each HLE import call

PS3_FTRACE recorded syscalls and timer sleeps but not HLE imports, so a
guest thread blocked or busy inside an import (a file read, a SPURS
wait, a lock taken hundreds of thousands of times) showed up nowhere.
ps3_hle_call's exit guard now closes a PS3_FT_HLE span (who = thread,
a = NID, b = guest lr) for calls at least PS3_FTRACE_MIN_US long. With
the trace off it costs one load per call.

This is what found God of War HD's 360 ms frame: 320,355 lwmutex
lock/unlock pairs in it (PS3_FTRACE_MIN_US=0), against 71 in a normal
frame.

180e324be8066b0566143dcfb403bdbbb1403a0b.message:
Draw engine: the guest pipeline list, and the caches rebuilt from it

A backend's caches hold what the decompilers made of a title's programs --
the D3D12 bytecode cache and its pipeline-state list -- so a change to a
decompiler leaves them stale, and only playing everything again refilled
them (the v0.17 merge left a release's cache matching 584 of 1,494
programs). The engine now also keeps what the title gave.

Every pipeline the engine translates is written once, by its key, as a line
of <dir>/guest_pipelines.txt: the two programs by hash (their bytes once each
in <dir>/guest_programs.bin), every input the decompilers take (shader
control, cube, volume, vertex-texture, shadow-compare, texel-addressed and
texel-op units), the vertex layout, the target format and count, the render
state field by field by name, and the hashes of the HLSL made of it then.
<dir> is PS3RECOMP_GUEST_DIR, else PS3RECOMP_DXBC_CACHE; PS3RECOMP_GUEST_LIST=0
records nothing.

RSX_GUEST_REBUILD=1 runs the list through the decompilers and the backend's
pipeline_create as they are now, on the build workers, when the engine
starts, and exits: the bytecode and the pipeline states are made again
without playing, and <dir>/guest_remap.txt lists each pipeline whose HLSL
changed (old and new hashes). RPCS3 keeps its shader cache the same way.

Drakengard 3, one level: 328 pipelines recorded (260 KB of lines, 575 KB of
programs); rebuilt into an empty cache in 11 s including the game's start,
328 built, the same 344 bytecode files byte for byte as play made, every
rebuilt pipeline state one that play had built.

1891b8fe718534bef9d143c7b665beb762adbc07.message:
gcm: count the drain's own ring recycle as the JUMP to begin

Once a title has been seen to overrun its ring, the drain recycles the
ring itself when current nears end. A title whose callback also
recycles (cellGcm_fifo_recycle) can be in that callback at the same
moment: it writes its JUMP and put, and only then marks itself waiting,
so a pass that read the mark clear still teleports get to begin. The
callback then waits for a backward JUMP that never comes, because get
is already at begin == put, and gives up after 2 s of no progress.

God of War HD stopped for 2-4 s this way at random points in about
half of the gameplay runs. Counting the teleport as the backward JUMP
ends the callback's wait at once.

1be9e80d533ae0ff253fa169f5d2f5f783a1364d.message:
rsx_shader_msl: compile a vertex program's position invariant

Titles draw the same geometry twice with two different vertex programs,
the second pass testing EQUAL against the depth the first one wrote. The
RSX runs the position arithmetic instruction by instruction, so both
programs land on the same depth. The Metal compiler optimises each
program on its own (it may fuse a multiply and an add into one FMA in one
of them and not in the other), the two depths can then differ in the last
bit, and the EQUAL pass leaves holes.

Resistance: Fall of Man's foliage writes depth through an alpha-tested
program, then colour through one that also lights it, with
SET_DEPTH_FUNC EQUAL.

The translator now marks a vertex program's position [[position,
invariant]], and the Metal backend compiles guest programs with
MTLCompileOptions.preserveInvariance (macOS 11 and later), so programs
that compute the position the same way get the same bits.
PS3RECOMP_MSL_INVARIANT=0 leaves the position as it was.

test_shader_msl checks the vertex program's MSL for
"[[position, invariant]]" (and for "[[position" under
PS3RECOMP_MSL_INVARIANT=0).

1c7c1d914374d59451f5b73421119af501606cfb.message:
rsx engine: a scissored CLEAR_SURFACE clears only the scissor

RSX clears what the surface clip and the scissor let through. The engine
cleared every colour and depth target whole, whatever the scissor said.

Resistance: Fall of Man's co-op split screen renders both views into one
2x1 antialiased 1280x720 scene target: the scissor on the left half, a
colour and depth clear and player 1's view, then the scissor on the right
half, a clear and player 2's view. The second clear wiped player 1's view,
and the left half of the screen was black under the HUD.

sink_clear now asks eng_clear_rect what the clear may write: the clip
from the origin, then the scissor (eng_scissor_rect, the draw path's
scissor code moved into a function). Only a scissor narrower than the
clip makes a clear partial; a clip smaller than the target alone stays a
whole clear, as before. A partial clear goes to two new optional backend
hooks, clear_color_rect and clear_depth_stencil_rect. A backend without
them, or PS3RECOMP_ENG_RECT_CLEAR=0, clears whole as before. A depth clear
that covers everything the zeta was ever bound with (ext_w/ext_h) stays
whole, and a partial depth clear keeps had_write.

The Metal backend records a rectangle clear as a clear record with the
rectangle in its scissor and encodes it as a pass of its own: the
attachment is loaded and a full-target triangle under that scissor writes
the colour, or the depth and stencil with the test always passing. Such a
record is never folded into a pass's load action.

New test_clear_rect in test_rsx_draw_engine (the co-op frame, whole and
empty scissors, a zeta only bound at a small clip, a backend without the
hooks), and test_metal_rect_clears.m (tools/test_metal_rect_clears.py) on
the GPU: a rectangle clear of the right half keeps the left half, for
colour, depth and stencil, and a whole clear after one covers the target.
