# Haze Recomp

Experimental Windows port of **Haze** for PS3, built with
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Targets the USA disc
**BLUS30094**, disc version **01.02**, application version **01.00**.

The Windows installer prepares your ISO, downloads verified firmware from Sony,
and installs a ready-to-play launcher. It uses a per-user MSI internally. See
[installation and upgrades](docs/installing.md) and the
[automated release process](docs/releasing.md).

Menus, opening-scene gameplay, audio output, and checkpoint saves have been
tested. Keyboard/mouse and SDL controller support are implemented. Performance,
rendering, and campaign compatibility are still in development. Full campaign
completion is not validated. Experimental invite-code campaign co-op has passed
two-instance local gameplay, departure and rejoin tests; separate-machine and
home-router validation is pending. Internet play requires a configured service;
see [co-op setup and limitations](docs/co-op.md). Native PAMF movies
play with synchronized video and audio; Escape or the current confirm binding skips them.

## Install

Run `HazeRecomp-<version>-Setup.exe` from [Releases](https://github.com/zdiemer/haze-recomp/releases),
choose your ISO, and click **Install**. The installer downloads the required
RPCS3 helper and Sony firmware, prepares the game, and installs the launcher.
When it finishes, click **Play Haze**. Subsequent launches use **Haze Recomp**
in the Start menu. No separate tools or development environment are needed.

![Haze installer: choose the ISO and installation folder](docs/images/installer.png)

After the installer prepares the game, the launcher is ready to use:

![Haze installer: installation complete with Play Haze](docs/images/installer-complete.png)

The tested disc-decrypted image is `Haze (USA) (En,Fr,Es).iso`
(8,498,184,192 bytes), BLUS30094, disc version 01.02 / application version 01.00.
Its **SHA-256** is:

```text
e778fff687b4a122146d23160fe1fefdff14dddb5d5709b257cff76832dc2520
```

Check your image with PowerShell:

```powershell
Get-FileHash -LiteralPath 'D:\PS3\Haze (USA) (En,Fr,Es).iso' -Algorithm SHA256
```

This identifies the tested ISO byte for byte. Setup also checks the disc metadata
and executable hashes; other regions, encrypted raw dumps and updated executables
are unsupported. Supply your own disc image; none is included in releases.

## Build from source

Requires Windows x64, Visual Studio C++ tools with the Windows SDK, Clang,
CMake and Ninja components, Python 3.11+, Git, and 7-Zip. Supply your own
readable (disc-decrypted) game image, RPCS3 executable for EBOOT decryption,
and installed PS3 firmware. Game files and firmware are not included.

Run from the repository root in PowerShell, replacing the example paths:

```powershell
git submodule update --init --recursive
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r external/ps3recomp/requirements.txt

# Extract the disc and decrypt its executable.
.\scripts\extract.ps1 -Iso 'C:\path\to\Haze.iso'
.\scripts\decrypt.ps1 -Rpcs3 'C:\path\to\rpcs3.exe'

# Generate native translations of the game and firmware code.
$env:PS3_DEV_FLASH = 'C:\path\to\dev_flash'
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/haze.py analyze
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/haze.py lift --jobs 4
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/haze.py lift-spu
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/lift_audio_plugins.py
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/lift_firmware.py

.\scripts\build.ps1
# Or double-click build/haze/HazeLauncher.exe after building.
.\scripts\play.ps1
```

**HazeLauncher.exe** starts the game without a scripting console, preserves
save/settings/cache paths and retains session logs. Native dialogs select
missing game or firmware paths. After a failed run, or from the **Haze Recomp
diagnostics** shortcut (`HazeLauncher.exe --diagnostics`), it exports a redacted
diagnostics ZIP to attach to an issue; see the [launcher guide](docs/executable-launcher.md#diagnostics-reports).

Already extracted files belong in `game/disc/PS3_GAME/`, including `PARAM.SFO`
and `USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN`. Decryption produces `USRDIR/EBOOT.ELF`. Set
`PS3_DEV_FLASH` again when launching from a new shell, unless firmware is in
`local/tools/rpcs3/dev_flash`.

The PPU lift is an initial translation; additional function recovery may be
needed before a fresh lift boots or runs correctly.

The executable is `build/haze/HazeRecomp.exe`. Saves live in
`local/state/savedata`, session logs in `local/sessions`, and reusable shaders
in `local/cache/rsx-shaders`. Game assets, generated translations, and build
outputs are ignored by Git. The first launch installs about 4 GB of game data.

## Controls and settings

| Action | Default input |
| --- | --- |
| Move / look | WASD / mouse |
| Fire / zoom | Left / right mouse |
| Reload / use | R / E |
| Jump / crouch | Space / Ctrl |
| Switch weapon | X or mouse wheel |
| Grenade / Nectar or play dead | G / Q |
| Melee | F |
| Menu confirm / back | Enter / Esc (Space / X also work) |
| Open / close pause menu | Esc (in nested menus, goes back one page) |
| Release or recapture mouse | F1 |

Menus also support the pointer: left click selects, right click goes back.
Enter and Esc keep their menu actions regardless of gameplay bindings. Holding
either key across a menu boundary cannot trigger another action. Space remains
jump during gameplay; Enter retains the Start binding outside menus by default.
Bindings accept function, numpad and punctuation keys and separate WheelUp /
WheelDown directions; see [docs/control-settings.md](docs/control-settings.md).
SDL gamepads connect automatically. Game vibration plays on the controller in
use, including PlayStation, Switch and Steam virtual pads, while the game window
has focus. Bindings, mouse sensitivity, controller
options, and startup skipping live in [config/input.ini](config/input.ini)
and reload while running. Action names above assume Haze's default controller
layout; zoom and crouch can be changed from toggle to hold in the game's settings.

**Settings > Control Setup** opens PC Controls for bindings, sensitivity,
deadzones, vibration and prompt style. Select a binding to capture an input, review any
conflicts, then **Apply**. **Back** discards edits; **Defaults** requires Apply.
**Game control options** opens the original controller layout and toggle/hold
settings.

**Player Profile** on the main menu shows your current name. Use **Edit profile
name** to type with the keyboard (Enter accepts, Escape cancels), or use **Add
character**, **Delete last character**, and **Clear name** with a controller.
**Apply** saves the name; **Back** discards pending edits. Names use 3–16 ASCII
letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens and must start with a letter. The name
is stored alongside your saves in `player-name.txt`; changing it preserves the
internal profile key, existing save directories, and campaign progression.

The main-menu footer opens **Desktop Options** through the current Select
binding (Tab by default) or a mouse click. **Add to Steam** lets you select a
local account and confirm registration with the executable launcher and artwork;
close Steam first. The pause-menu footer opens **Quit to Desktop** directly.
Quit confirmation defaults to Cancel and waits for active saves and settings
before shutting down.

Open **Video Setup** or **Sound Setup** from the main or pause menu for PC
Video and Audio settings. Changes are staged until **Apply**; **Back** discards
edits. Display changes offer a 15-second **Keep/Revert** confirmation. Render
resolution and shadow resolution require restarting.

Alternatively, edit [config/graphics.ini](config/graphics.ini), then press **F6** to apply
filtering, FXAA, sharpening, exposure, VSync, frame-limit, and performance-overlay changes live.
Editing alone does not apply changes; the window title reports the reload result.
Display mode, monitor, window size, render resolution, and shadow resolution
changes made in the file require restarting.

The Video page offers **Performance overlay** (Off / Compact / Expanded) and
**Overlay position** (four corners). **F7** cycles modes during gameplay or menus
and saves the preference. Compact is a tiny, single-line presentation FPS counter
with a text shadow. Expanded adds mean presentation interval, guest flips (not
simulation rate), draw packets per guest frame,
cached textures, and process working-set RAM. CPU/GPU timings are marked N/A
because the normal renderer does not expose reliable per-frame measurements.
Launch overrides remain in effect after reloading.
Defaults are borderless at the monitor's desktop resolution with a 30 FPS cap.
Override resolution for one run with
`.\scripts\play.ps1 -RenderResolution 1920x1080`.

## Development

Run regression checks with `.\scripts\build.ps1 -Test`, or use
`-RuntimeOnly -Test` for checks without building the game executable.
For a bounded diagnostic run, use `.\scripts\run.ps1 -Seconds 90`;
logs and captures go to `local/runs`.

See the [script guide](scripts/README.md) for diagnostics, microbenchmarks,
build internals and command migrations.

Worktrees can reuse a prepared checkout's SDK, Python environment, generated
translations, and game assets while keeping their own builds and logs:

```powershell
.\scripts\build.ps1 -SharedRoot 'C:\path\to\haze-recomp'
.\scripts\play.ps1 -SharedRoot 'C:\path\to\haze-recomp'
```

Use `-SdkRoot` on the build command to select a separate SDK checkout.
The native build downloads a pinned shared LGPL FFmpeg package for movie
decoding. `-FFmpegRoot` selects an unpacked development package for offline
builds. See [movie playback](docs/movie-playback.md) for formats and validation.

## Experimental browser build

The Wasm64/WebGL2 build supports menus and opening-scene gameplay, but remains
slow and experimental. After preparing the game and translations above, install
Emscripten and run:

```powershell
py -3 scripts/bootstrap-wasm.py
.\scripts\build-wasm.ps1 -Emsdk 'C:\path\to\emsdk'
py -3 scripts/serve-wasm.py --firmware-dir 'C:\path\to\dev_flash'
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8085/> in a 64-bit Chromium browser. The build requires
shared memory and about 8 GiB of addressable linear memory; the local server
provides the required isolation headers. Click to enable sound and fullscreen;
F1 releases the mouse. Add `?debug=1` for controls and logs. Browser saves use
IndexedDB, separately from native saves. Browser network play is not implemented.
Native FFmpeg movie playback is not part of the experimental browser build.

Use `scripts/playtest-wasm.py --profile-after 30` with your normal playtest
arguments to record worker CPU profiles. Summarize a run with
`py -3 scripts/diagnose.py browser-cpu local/wasm-tests/<run>`.
The report ranks self samples per worker and shows callers from leaf to root;
`--top`, `--stack-depth`, and `--json` control the output. It also accepts raw
Chromium `.cpuprofile` files. Counts are samples, not elapsed time; idle and wait
functions remain visible, and workers are reported separately.

## License

The port scaffold derives from ps3recomp's MIT-licensed template; see
[LICENSE](LICENSE). Input prompt artwork is by Kenney; its license is included
in [assets/input-prompts](assets/input-prompts).
Native movie decoding dynamically links FFmpeg under LGPLv3. Its license and
documentation are installed under `share/ffmpeg`; the matching shared libraries
remain replaceable beside the executable.

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

Every row is exercised by CI on every push, and **all three are green on
`master`** — the PPU boot scaffold ratchet that had been red since before v0.11.0
([#139](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/issues/139)) is at zero on all
four toolchains. The rows below describe what those jobs actually do, not what a
green tick would imply: building the runtime and passing the suites is not the
same as running a game, and only one row claims that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter + 8 test suites | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | null (headless software); Vulkan (opt-in) |
| Runs a recompiled game | **yes** | **no** | no |

The gap on macOS is the PPU boot scaffold — `ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp`
and the HLE dispatch are still Win32-only (thread creation, VirtualAlloc, SEH,
stack walking), and they are compiled per-game rather than into the library.
So macOS builds the runtime, renders through Metal and passes the full test
suite, but cannot yet load and run a title. `ps3recomp_host` drives
cellGcm → RSX → Metal end to end without a game, which is what makes further
graphics work possible there.

Linux builds and passes the same suites under both GCC and Clang, and runs
`ps3recomp_host` end to end, on every push. Its backend is the null backend's
headless software path: a host-memory framebuffer with a CPU triangle filler,
enough to prove the guest's command stream produced the pixels it asked for on
a runner with no display and no GPU. It is not a renderer — no depth, no
blending, no textures — so Linux is still one real backend, plus the same PPU
boot scaffold macOS needs, away from running a title.

### What each platform needs next

Both non-Windows platforms are blocked on the *same* two things, in this order.

**1. The PPU boot scaffold, on POSIX.** This is the shared blocker and the only
one that gates "runs a recompiled game" on both. `ppu_loader.cpp`,
`boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled *per game* rather than into
the library, and were Win32-only — thread creation, `VirtualAlloc`, SEH, stack
walking. v0.10.0 took it to zero errors on POSIX and put it under CI so it
cannot rot again, and ported the guest-pointer trap, thread-locals and host
backtraces. What is left is running it: load a lifted image on POSIX and reach
the guest's first instruction, then `main`. Until that works, neither platform
can run a title no matter how good its renderer is.

**2. One real backend each.** The RSX abstraction landed in v0.10.0 (#101, #102,
#103) — texture conversion, the `TEXTURE_CONTROL1` crossbar, texture layout and
a neutral draw record all live outside the D3D12 file now, so a backend no
longer has to reimplement them to draw anything.

- **macOS** has the furthest to go that is *interesting* rather than
  mechanical: [@slushiimusic](https://github.com/slushiimusic)'s Metal backend
  (#96) does clear, flip, guest vertex fetch, a pipeline-state cache and blend
  translation. Reaching D3D12 parity means the guest's own fragment programs
  through the decompiler, then textures. `ps3recomp_host` already drives
  cellGcm → RSX → Metal with no lifted game, so each step is testable before a
  title exists to run.
- **Linux** has an opt-in Vulkan backend (`-DPS3RECOMP_RSX_VULKAN=ON`). With
  guest programs on (glslang at build time, `PS3RECOMP_VK_GUEST_PROGRAMS=1`) it
  runs on the shared register-file draw engine, the path Metal takes, and every
  `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on it -- including render-to-texture, MRT and
  depth textures; without them it draws the null backend's fixed-function
  contract. It has not run a recompiled title yet. The default is still the
  headless backend, a CPU triangle filler for CI, deliberately.

**Deliberately not claimed:** the table above says "no" for running a game on
macOS and Linux, and it will keep saying "no" until a title actually boots to
gameplay on one of them. Building the runtime, passing the suites and rendering
through `ps3recomp_host` are all real, and none of them is that.

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

01fe84583e4ddb9fac5b7ceac3e188e159ec0ec0.message:
perf(spu): skip overlay signature scans and verified-code walks for data GETs

Every MFC GET calls spu_overlay_note_get, which keeps streamed-code
residency current. Two of its steps cost every GET, whatever was copied:

- A GET of 512 bytes or more, once any content-signature source was
  registered, was memcmp'd against every signature source in turn: up to
  SPU_OVL_SRC_MAX, and a title streaming WWS job modules registers dozens.
  Most such GETs are vertex, index or job data, not code.
- spu_dcache_note_get walked every verified image's bounds and segments
  to bump the epoch of any image whose code the GET overwrote.

A Linux profile of MAG Training puts spu_overlay_note_get at 0.70 ms of
SPU-thread CPU per frame.

Signature sources' first 8 bytes now go into an insert-only set, built
and published exactly like the existing source-EA set: inserted before the
source count's release store, probed after its acquire load. The scan runs
only when the GET's first 8 bytes are a registered prefix or its EA is a
registered source; otherwise no entry could match, so nothing changes.
Verified segments mark their 128-byte LS blocks in a bitmap before the
image is published, and spu_dcache_note_get returns at once for a GET that
touches no marked block. Matches, registration order and epochs are
unchanged whenever the scan or walk runs.

Synthetic job chain on macOS arm64, 16 verified images and 90 signature
sources registered, none matching the data: a small job (one 128 B and two
1 KiB GETs, one PUT) costs 473-480 ns on fork main, 376-378 ns with this
change, and 381-388 ns with no sources registered.
tools/test_spu_overlay_allsize.py now also checks that a 1 KiB data GET
with an unknown EA does no scan (it fails on fork main), and that a GET
sharing a signature's prefix still scans and matches nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

02ea4fc3ac1ee8b7ba4dba0af9e0422328035348.message:
feat(video): D3D12 engine colour snapshot

Implement color_snapshot for the D3D12 engine backend: an immutable copy of
a colour target, recorded after every draw already recorded and before the
next, for a draw that samples the target it renders to. Without it such
reads sampled guest memory, which does not hold what the GPU rendered.

The copy is a plain texture marked as a snapshot. surface_view accepts it
as a parent so the engine can apply the texture's crossbar, binding resolves
a view to either parent kind, and releasing the snapshot releases its views
and retires it on the fence.

The real-adapter fixture checks, under the debug layer: a pass-through view
samples the target, the snapshot keeps the contents at the time of the
copy while a live view sees a later clear, a draw into the target can
sample its own snapshot, and release frees the views (50/50 on an RTX
5090).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

07b5698a849f3f9ab7d43255b475073fcdc9ab05.message:
feat(memory): opt-in guest write watch for retained guest data

PS3RECOMP_VM_WRITE_WATCH=1 (default off) lets a consumer that keeps a
copy of guest memory, such as a renderer retaining unchanged assets
between frames, learn that a range is unchanged without reading it.

- vm_watch(ea, len) write-protects the host pages covering a guest range
  and returns an epoch. A later user-space write to such a page (PPU, SPU
  DMA, runtime/HLE copies) faults once. The handler records a new epoch
  for the page, makes it writable and lets the write proceed.
- vm_clean_since(range, epoch) is true while no page of the range has
  been written since that watch. vm_watch_stats counts watches, faults,
  notes and forgotten pages.
- The handler touches only atomics and the faulting page's protection,
  so it is safe on threads holding runtime locks. Faults it does not own
  chain to the previous SIGSEGV/SIGBUS handler, or go to the Windows
  vectored-handler search.
- Kernel writes into guest memory fail with EFAULT/ERROR_NOACCESS on a
  protected page instead of faulting. Every OS writer announces itself
  with vm_note_write or vm_note_host_write first:
  - sys_fs read;
  - cellFsRead and cellFsReadWithOffset;
  - the libs cellFs read;
  - sys_net recv and recvfrom;
  - the cellHttp body recv;
  - the sysPrxForUser and cellSsl random bytes;
  - the cellSaveData file read.
- With PS3RECOMP_VM_WRITE_WATCH_STRICT=1, vm_note_write_check makes an
  unannounced writer's access error fatal, naming the site.
- The runtime's own protection and commit changes release the pages they
  touch, through vm_watch_hooks.h. That covers vm_commit, vm_protect,
  vm_shutdown and the POSIX VirtualAlloc/VirtualFree/VirtualProtect. A
  read-only protection pins the pages so they are never watched. The
  watch therefore never restores or keeps a protection the runtime did
  not ask for.
- Host-page granularity: 16 KB on Apple Silicon, 4 KB elsewhere.

With the option unset nothing is installed or protected. The hooks stay
null, and the announcement calls

0acc9ef35efdbf20f92af9353234af5ae1614cc3.message:
perf(video): size the D3D12 engine's shader-visible heap for a whole frame

Per-draw descriptor tables (20 entries each) are carved from one
shader-visible CBV/SRV/UAV heap, and the ring restarts only after a full GPU
wait. At 65536 entries a Training frame of about 2,800 draws filled it
about every 3,300 draws, adding roughly 0.65 GPU waits per frame
(wait_srv_tables). Create the heap at 1,000,000 entries, the limit every
resource binding tier allows, and fall back to 65536 (with a log line) when
the device refuses; PS3RECOMP_D3D12_ENGINE_SMALL_HEAP=1 forces the fallback
for diagnosis.

The real-adapter fixture checks the large heap and that 4000 draws need no
descriptor-ring wait (66/66 under the debug layer); with the forced fallback
exactly those two checks fail, as expected.

0bc55efc082acedb76d86af3de14b119731da6d8.message:
perf(video): collapse repeated vertex references through a direct table (#52)

rsx_vertex_remap_build hashed every vertex reference of every draw into a
table sized for the largest draw seen so far. After one character-sized
draw, every small draw probed a table far larger than its cache. On Linux
that was about 3.1 ms of the FIFO thread per frame.

- When a draw's references share one base index and span a vertex-id range
  at most four times the reference count, they are collapsed through a
  direct table over that range. That is the common indexed mesh.
- Otherwise the hash uses only as many slots as the draw needs.

Both give the same first-use order, unique count and occurrence map as
before, so the engine and the live draw path upload identical vertices
and indices.

test_vertex_fetch_plan checks both paths against a straightforward
first-use collapse over random lists: dense, sparse, mixed base indices,

15f2a229f83f5d2f4b68fa1fd362aaacdeb9f82f.message:
perf(gcm): opt-in walker wake when an SPU transfer fills the hole it parked on (#56)

A title whose SPU jobs write reserved holes into the command stream
pre-fills each hole with a jump-to-self, and the walker parks there. The
fill is an SPU DMA, and nothing on that path kicks the walker. Only a PPU
store to put, a backend completion or the frame clock's idle timeout
(4 ms in MAG) starts the next pass. A walker that reaches a hole before
the job fills it can sit out most of that timeout, holding back the frame
and every job waiting on a label behind the hole.

With PS3RECOMP_GCM_PARK_KICK=1 (default off, read once):
- A pass that ends on a park records the parked word's guest address.
- The first SPU PUT that covers that address (through the existing
  g_spu_put_hook) takes it and kicks the consumer (cellGcm_fifo_kick_notify).
- The walker re-reads the word after recording it, so a fill that landed
  in between still kicks.
- The next pass starts unarmed.
- PS3RECOMP_RSX_INFLIGHT_LOG=1 prints parks and kicks every two seconds.

tools/test_gcm_park_kick.py covers:
- nothing armed with the switch off;
- transfers next to the park not taking it;
- the rest of the hole not taking it;
- the write onto the park taking it exactly once;
- the next pass running past the filled hole, unarmed.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(video): opt-in staging of only the vertex constant rows a program reads (#79)

* perf(video): stage only the vertex constant rows a program reads

A changed vertex-constant block went to the backend whole, 8 KB a draw,
however few of its 512 rows the program reads: much of the Metal backend's
staging memmove on the RSX thread.

rsx_vp_analyze_constants reports the rows a transform program reads: the
span of the constants its instructions name, or every row when one indexes
through an address register, the program has flow control, or it does not
terminate. The engine keeps that span in its vertex-layout memo and, when
the backend has the new optional bind_vs_constant_rows, hands over the block
with that span; the backend stages just those rows and the viewport
transform's two, leaving the others as whatever staging held. A copy is
reused for the next draw only when it holds every row that draw's program
reads. Backends without the hook, the built-in program and any program not
analysed still bind the whole block. Metal and batched Vulkan implement it.

Tests: the analysis (a span, none, indexed, flow control, unterminated); the
engine through a stub backend (the span and its values, rebinds, a program
reading rows the copy lacks, an indexed program, a full copy serving a
narrower program, a written constant, a backend without the hook); a
headless real-Metal pixel test drawing each of three constants as a colour
from staging prefilled with something else; and the batched Vulkan fixture
binding through the new path every fourth draw against per-operation
submission.

21124b5fb11dcca35821242b7343c86bbad481fa.message:
perf(video): opt-in Vulkan release of pinned images without waiting

PS3RECOMP_VK_PIN_RELEASE_NOWAIT=1 (default off). When the draw engine
releases a colour or depth image the native side still pins, the Vulkan
backend flushed the batch and waited for it, then waited for every
presentation, on the FIFO thread. A title that publishes a native-rendered
surface each frame swaps its engine surface for the staged image and
releases the old one, so that wait (about 7 ms each, two per frame on the
measured title) sat between the native Main commit and the rest of the
frame's command stream.

With the option and the batched engine:
- The release submits the open batch without waiting. An empty batch is
  submitted too: every batch ends in a full dependency on everything
  submitted before it, presents included, so the batch's ticket covers all
  earlier work that may use the image. The ticket is kept with the image.
- When the last native pin goes (after the native side's own fences), the
  image is destroyed at once if that ticket has completed, or parked on a
  bounded list (64) that the completion reap destroys once it has. Parked
  images are destroyed without the presentation wait, which the ticket
  already covers; shutdown idles the device and destroys any left.
- Room on the list is reserved at release time, so the last-pin callback
  never waits. With no room left, the release waits as before.
Off, or without the batched engine, nothing changes.

tools/check_native_owner_vulkan.py runs the real-GPU owner fixture (the
validation layer is required and any VUID fails it) a third time with the
option. The new check pins a colour target, records a clear behind a large
depth job, releases it (returning without waiting), drops the last pin, and
requires the image to be parked or destroyed, the reap to destroy it once
its ticket completes, and no validation error; then 72 pinned releases
against 64 slots must wait exactly for the 8 that did not fit and leave
nothing behind. On an RX 7900 XTX (RADV) the release took 0.03

227d4074ee3c35224a6e0b3d78af835f9e579037.message:
fix(video): accept a running direct present at the Vulkan native boundary

Since presents are direct (2babf82d), each submits with its own fence and
nothing waits for it; it runs in the owner scope, so it is often the latest
original submission. The native boundary accepted only a completed fence or
a pending E5 ticket, so a present still on the GPU refused the next native
Main with -4. On Linux with GPU group 0, which reaches the next Main
sooner, that ended the candidate after 17 clean frames.

- A fence of the direct-present ring counts as an ordered boundary while
  pending, as an E5 ticket does: it is on the queue (never held) and reads
  only the offscreen target, so native work queued after it runs after it.
- Original work held behind a reservation reaches the queue once the
  reserved native batch is submitted, which needs only queue_mu: the
  boundary now waits for that up to 50 ms instead of refusing at once,
  and logs a rate-limited line if it is still held afterwards.

requires the boundary to accept it while it is pending; it fails without
this change. Owner fixture (batched off and on), present-cost fixture and
the public native regression pass on RX 7900 XTX / RADV under validation.

perf(video): opt-in D3D12 engine present without a GPU wait

Every present submitted and then waited for the GPU to finish the frame.
With PS3RECOMP_D3D12_ENGINE_ASYNC_PRESENT=1 a present submits and presents

into it, and recording into a back buffer waits only if the GPU has not yet

advances. Default behaviour is unchanged.

chain on the test queue (and skips these checks where a session cannot
create one): default presents wait every frame; async presents submit once
per frame, do not wait every frame, tag the back buffers with fences, and
leave later frames intact. 76/76 under the debug layer in an interactive

2702224f5cc0b86cbd005d4fb8a43cde41e9dc81.message:
perf(video): opt-in merging of same-target Vulkan engine draws into one render pass (#50)

Each Vulkan engine draw recorded its own full ALL_COMMANDS dependency, an
image barrier per target and a render pass begin/end, even when batched: a
MAG frame records thousands of passes of one small draw each. The Metal
backend encodes each run of same-attachment draws in one pass.

With PS3RECOMP_VK_MERGE_PASSES=1 (batched recording only, default off), a
draw into the framebuffer of the pass the previous draw left open continues
it, and skips the pipeline bind and dynamic state the pass already holds.
Every other recorded operation, every submission and every target release
ends the pass first. A draw that samples one of the open pass's colour
targets, directly or through a crossbar view, starts a new pass, so its
reads stay ordered after the earlier writes as before.

test_vulkan_batched_engine gains a "merged" mode whose readback must equal
per-operation submission byte for byte under synchronization validation,
draws that sample the other target through a view, and checks of the
sampled-target rule. The inflight log counts passes, merged draws, feedback
breaks and skipped pipeline binds.

docs: design note for host-format vertex streams instead of float4

The register-file engine collapses every draw's references and decodes
every attribute to float4 before upload: about 7 ms per frame on the Linux
FIFO thread.

The note proposes, for draws that qualify (no topology rebuild, plain
array attributes in formats the host fetch converts):
- copy each attribute's referenced range byte-swapped into host order;
- copy indices as u16 relative to the range;
- describe the formats so the GPU's fixed-function vertex fetch converts
  them, with the shaders unchanged.

It also covers exactness (the one SNORM16 edge), pipeline identity, what
copy-at-record keeps, steps, a default-off switch and tests.

2857c41e0b2be97f6bd5ca3b3b933b41efe516fc.message:
fix(video): show a deferred present as soon as its capture is queued

The first Linux A/B of PS3RECOMP_VK_DEFER_HELD_PRESENT=1 cut the update
median from about 43.5 ms to 36 ms, but the window showed only about 18-23
frames a second against 30 guest flips (display p95 interval 92-155 ms):
the pump made a pending show only when no reservation was held at all, and
with Main reserving every frame one usually was, so about two thirds of the
deferred captures were superseded before they could be shown.

A show depends only on its own capture having reached the queue: it reads the
offscreen target and writes a swapchain image, which neither a native batch
nor held original work touches, and it orders after its capture by queue
order. So the pump now makes the show once the capture's submission has left
the hold (its fence is no longer held), whether or not a newer reservation
holds other work by then, submitting and presenting it directly rather than
through the hold. Such a submission does not become the native boundary while
a hold is active. The end of a hold also wakes the host thread
(cellGcm_fifo_kick_notify) when a show is pending, so it is shown without
waiting for the next timed pass.

The Vulkan owner fixture also checks the wake; the Vulkan fixtures that
build the backend stub cellGcm_fifo_kick_notify as they stub the flip count.

2917aa0d4855f0525e3362c7fd00b20f8b9d3f87.message:
perf(spu): x86 vector forms of the byte permute, insertion and logic helpers (#41)

93 integer/permute helpers in spu_helpers.h have NEON forms, but on x86
they fall back to their scalar references. For the byte-granular ones
that is a 16-iteration byte loop through the stack and 16 single-byte
stores into the result. The next instruction usually reads the whole
register or its preferred word back, so the store-to-load forward fails
on every use. The unaligned-load idiom (lqd/lqx, then rotqby by the
low address bits, then a scalar use) hits this on nearly every access.

Add x86 forms behind SSSE3, which every x86-64 runtime build already has
through -msse4.1. They mirror the NEON ones, and the scalar definitions
stay as the fallback and the test oracle:
- rotqby, rotqbyi, rotqbybi, shlqby, shlqbyi, shlqbybi, rotqmby,
  rotqmbyi and rotqmbybi: one pshufb, with out-of-range indices selecting
  zero as the NEON table lookup does
- cbd, chd, cwd and cdd: the insertion control built in a register
- and, or, xor, nand, nor, andc, orc, andi, ori, xori and selb: SSE2,
  instead of two 64-bit halves that a 16-byte read then fails to forward
  from. nand, nor, andc and orc gain _ref forms for the test.

AVX is never required. With -march=x86-64-v3 the same forms compile to
their VEX encodings.

tests/test_spu_int_x86.c compares all 24 helpers with their references
bit for bit: every count from -300 to 300 for the shifts and rotates,
including counts outside the architectural range, every base residue and
immediate for the insertion controls, and 200000 random operand sets for
the logic. CMake registers it on x86 hosts. The Linux and Windows
workflows run it at -mssse3, -msse4.1 and x86-64-v3.

2940d438d5541c7c8b3a7377bbd84ff9c4c5b560.message:
feat(rsx): Metal present thread halves

With PS3RECOMP_RSX_PRESENT_THREAD=1 on the draw-engine path, an engine
present no longer waits on the in-flight semaphore or nextDrawable on the
presenting thread. It encodes the recorded work and the ordinary present
pass (FXAA, CAS, gamma) into a staging texture of the drawable's size and
format, commits, and returns. The present thread then waits on the
in-flight semaphore, takes the drawable, copies the staging texture into
it 1:1 and presents.

The stage is the original owner's commit; the show is not, and it takes
neither the owner gate nor the consumer lease. Native frame records split
accordingly: the stage carries the final GPU event, the show the
presentation or skip, under their own mutex. Critical-trace CLOCK spans
move to the present thread; the stage emits FLUSH type 3. Off, nothing is
created and eng_present is unchanged. The vtable path says once that it
is unsupported.

Headless real-Metal fixture: off is inert, stage and show, GPU order
against a later write, drop-oldest without blocking, shutdown discard,
and the windowed show on a detached CAMetalLayer with a resize:
tools/test_metal_present_thread.py.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

2babf82d17f291b1411cefe6867149f5a76a3a1a.message:
perf(video): present Vulkan engine frames directly, read back on request

Every Vulkan present copied the whole frame into host memory, waited for
the copy (and so for all of the frame's GPU work), then blitted it into the
window and waited again. On the draw engine path a present is now direct,
as on Metal: one submission blits the flipped surface into the offscreen
target and the target into the swapchain image, waiting for the image on
the GPU and signalling its present, and the CPU waits for nothing. A ring
of three present command buffers and fences keeps frames in flight; a slot
is reused once its fence has signalled.

The read-back present stays for the fixed-function path, for the presents
PS3RECOMP_VK_DUMP writes (only every PS3RECOMP_VK_DUMP_EVERY'th now reads
back) and for every present under PS3RECOMP_VK_PRESENT_READBACK=1, which
the host's --split-present check sets. presented_center() reports only a
read-back present's pixel.

tools/test_vulkan_present_cost.py checks that both modes leave identical
frames under the validation layer (synchronization included, headless or
windowed) and times the present call. RX 7900 XTX, RADV, batched engine,
1280x720: windowed at a 50 ms frame pace with 400 blended full-screen
draws, 6.44 ms -> 0.20 ms median per present; headless 3.03 ms -> 1.11 ms
(the rest is the frame's batch flush and ring back-pressure).

2c354021cf78584f12ac9d56b6c99fc754880b42.message:
perf(video): opt-in on-disk Vulkan pipeline cache (#62)

Engine pipelines are compiled on the thread that walks the FIFO, on the
draw that first needs them, with no pipeline cache. Every run recompiles
every pipeline, and each first use is a hitch on the frame-rate-limiting
thread.

With PS3RECOMP_VK_PIPELINE_CACHE=<existing directory>:
- Every pipeline (engine, legacy and the depth-conversion compute) is
  created through one VkPipelineCache.
- The cache is loaded at device creation from
  vk-pipelines-<vendor>-<device>.bin in that directory.
- It is saved there through a temporary file renamed into place, at
  shutdown and after every 32 new pipelines, so a killed run keeps most of
  them.
- A file whose header names another device, driver build or cache version
  is not loaded: the cache starts empty and the file is replaced.
Unset, pipelines are created without a cache, as before.

tools/test_vulkan_batched_engine.py runs the batched stream twice through
a cache directory. The first run must start new and save one file, the
second must load it, and both must read back identically to per-operation
submission under validation.

feat(video): watch a ring header at FIFO arrival

Add cellGcm_native_handoff_ring_watch for a ring header written by a
writer the caller does not control, such as an SPU job writing its own
command segment. Nothing is read at arm time and there is no publish
step: when the FIFO consumer reaches the header, its two words (and up to
two masked tail words) are compared and the watch reports once through
its callback, before the header is decoded. The FIFO never waits for a
watch.

Every watch reports exactly one status and retires: arrived, mismatch,
skipped (a JUMP out of the ring span before the header, or a consumer
resync), expired (max_flips FIFO flips) or VM retired. Watches share the
existing 64-entry registry, duplicate-header rule and cancel semantics.
The ordinary path is unchanged while no handoff is armed.

376bb4d3b45e67d456296c189bd6d82628ad49a6.message:
feat(video): count depth-sourced texture reads that reach no depth store

A texture that reads an address last written as depth is served by a depth
snapshot (D24 formats), a GPU depth view, or a store of the depth into
guest memory. When the backend has none of these for the format (no
depth_readback, depth_store_z24 or depth_z24_view, or they fail), the
texture silently read guest memory as it was, which can be stale.

Count each such read, report the first one on stderr with the format,
address and which backend operations are missing, and expose the count
(rsx_draw_engine_depth_unstored_count). The D3D12 engine adds it to its
stats line. The draw-engine fixture covers a backend without any of the
three.

feat(pad): keyboard on pad port 0 from the Linux SDL game window

macOS maps the window keyboard to controller port 0 and Windows has an

controller could not drive the game. PS3RECOMP_PAD_SDL_KEYBOARD (CMake

4028d97f30235c5e9753b3ccb3cf03f643be46e1.message:
perf(video): opt-in larger deferred report queue bound

In early-release mode, records that are already applied stay queued until
their command buffer completes, so their completion is still verified. A title
releasing about a thousand labels per frame fills the 1024-record queue while
the GPU is still behind. Every frame, the consumer then waits on the full queue
until the previous frame's work completes: about 10 ms per frame in the
native-Main measurements.

PS3RECOMP_RSX_DEFERRED_REPORT_CAPACITY=<n> (1024..8192, default 1024) raises
that bound. Guest-visible order, early application and completion
verification are unchanged. The frames-ahead bound still limits how far the
consumer runs ahead.

Two exact queue speedups:
- issuing tickets only the unissued tail, which are the only records
  without a ticket;
- the VM-overlap scan returns at once when no unapplied record is queued.

The inflight log adds capacity= and capacity_waits=. The queue test covers a
raised bound, ticket assignment across issues and the storage wrap.

49865e7e1e3a68b004dac2bad841ffbb6290f364.message:
perf(spu): replay the micro-interpreter's decoded runs while their words are unchanged

The WWS job manager regenerates the same register save/restore stub at
the top of local store and calls it on every interrupt. No lift can exist
for it, so spu_smc_microstep interprets it, re-decoding the same words
every time. A Linux attribution run of MAG Training put 84% of all
interpreter time on that one entry: about 10.7k calls per frame at about
335 ns each.

spu_smc_microstep now keeps a small per-thread cache of decoded straight
runs: from the entry to the first unconditional branch (bi, bisl, iret,
br, bra, brsl, brasl), over the instructions it already handles. A run
replays only while its live words still equal the bytes it was decoded
from (memcmp), and it stops at the first store landing inside the run,
which the stubs use to rewrite themselves; the ordinary microstep then
continues from the next instruction. A run holding a conditional branch
or anything outside that set is remembered as uncacheable and always
takes the ordinary path. Each op does exactly what its case in the
microstep does. The instruction-level observers keep the ordinary path: a
PC observer, original-work stepping, or a critical arrival PC inside the
run. PS3RECOMP_SPU_SMC_TRACE=0 turns the cache off.

A 121-instruction save stub costs 226 -> 145 ns per call on macOS arm64.

New differential test (runtime/spu/tests/test_spu_smc_trace.c,
tools/test_spu_smc_trace.py). It generates random stubs from the
microstep's set: register stores and loads near the stub, stores into
the stub itself, arithmetic and immediates, every unconditional
terminator with and without the interrupt-enable bits, and some with a
conditional branch inside. Each stub runs three times from the same state
(build, replay, after its words change), and the test compares digests of
the registers, the whole local store, pc, interrupt enable and trampoline
with the cache off and on. Mutating the replay (an off-by-one ai, or
ignoring a store into the run) makes it fail. tools/tes

present that completes it first is not counted twice. This lets a per-present
dump run exercise the deferral instead of bypassing it.

with the option present_finish returns at once, the pump leaves the
completion pending while the hold lasts and then writes the dump, whose centre

before.

perf(video): opt-in plain-method path through the FIFO walker; lock-free picture readiness (#54)

4ec61a701ed7d422950932ff4cc828722c6726a5.message:
perf(spurs): wake only the worker a dispatch fills; opt-in self-dispatch (#80)

Each SPURS instance's coordinator and all its policy-module workers slept
on one condition variable, and every event woke all of them: a dispatch, a
PM returning, a committed write to the instance's request line. The idle
workers then queued for the instance lock in front of the one that had
been given work, only to find nothing and sleep again. With six lanes a
serial chain of policy-module runs, each requesting the next, paid that
herd on every hop.

Each worker now sleeps on its own condition variable, and a dispatch wakes
only the worker it filled. The instance's variable wakes only the
coordinator (request-line commits, a PM returning, API changes). Stop and a
failed start wake every worker. Admission is unchanged: the coordinator's
per-slot selection moves verbatim into spurs_dispatch_slot().

PS3RECOMP_SPURS_SELF_DISPATCH=1 (off by default) also lets a worker whose
PM returns call spurs_dispatch_slot() for its own slot under the same
locks, as each SPU's own kernel selects its next workload on hardware. A
PM that requests the next stage of a chain and returns then continues on
the same thread with no wake at all. The scheduler's switches are read
once before the instance's threads start.

A synthetic chain through the real scheduler (new: tests/bench_spurs_pm_hop.c,
tools/test_spurs_pm_hop.py) alternates two manufactured workloads, each PM
raising the other's ready count with GETLLAR/PUTLLC and exiting. Request to
next PM start, macOS arm64, us per hop (wall), 4000 hops, 3 runs:

  lanes   fork main   this change   + SELF_DISPATCH=1
    1        6.8          7.5            2.3
    4       23.9          7.6            5.4
    6       37.0          7.5            7.1

A request a PPU raises with a plain store while the workers sleep waits for
the coordinator's 1 ms timed pass (ppu-idle mode: about 1.05 ms from store
to PM start); this change does not address that.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

4f3de351f26708677faf367c8f44e052e8b0a8a2.message:
perf(timer): opt-in yield to the deadline for short usleeps on POSIX

sys_timer_usleep on POSIX was a bare nanosleep. The game polls its job waits
with usleep(1) and usleep(10); on Linux such a nanosleep returns only after
the kernel's timer slack (50 us by default) plus a wakeup, so each poll saw a
finished job tens of microseconds late. The Windows branch already busy-waits
with a yield for sub-millisecond sleeps.

PS3RECOMP_USLEEP_SPIN_US=<n> (default 0 = off): a usleep shorter than n
microseconds yields (sched_yield) until a CLOCK_MONOTONIC deadline instead of
sleeping; longer ones, and every one with the option unset, still nanosleep.
The guest result is CELL_OK either way.

5df945e2595abecdea90ae245909bf38cc160b6b.message:
perf(spu): return from spu_drain_call without its loop's frame when nothing is pending (#82)

Every lifted brsl/bisl ends in spu_drain_call, so it runs once per guest
call. Nearly always the callee has returned through SPU_RET while its host
frame was live: no transfer is pending and the pc is already the call's
return pc. The loop then only did its exit bookkeeping, but every call paid
for the loop's frame first: an interrupt frame holding a jmp_buf, the
thread-local addresses, the depth guard. A Linux profile of MAG Training put
spu_drain_call's own time at 7.3 ms of SPU-thread CPU per frame, the largest
runtime symbol.

spu_drain_call now checks that case first, as a leaf: no pending transfer,
pc equal to the return pc, and the depth guard initialised with the depth
below half its limit. It then clears region_dispatch_valid and
drain_ret_pc, which is exactly what the loop did on that path, and returns.
Everything else runs the unchanged loop, now spu_drain_call_loop
(noinline): a pending transfer, a different pc, the depth guard's first use
or upper half.

New: runtime/spu/tests/bench_spu_call_dispatch.c with
tools/test_spu_call_dispatch.py, which times the lifter's call brackets,
using hand-written stand-ins, through the real drain and dispatchers (an
empty registered leaf, SPU_RET). macOS arm64, MAG runtime defaults, ns per
call, 3 runs:

  brsl (direct call + drain)              3.4 -> 2.0
  bisl via spu_indirect_branch_mt + drain 6.9 -> 5.6
  bisl via spu_indirect_branch + drain   14.5 -> 13.6

In CI it checks that every call reached the leaf and returned (host depth
and drain return pc back to 0). All tools/test_spu_*.py,
test_original_work*.py and test_mfc*.py pass.

5e533c9ad8736a7062183f69e5b2800f55198d2c.message:
perf(video): opt-in Vulkan descriptor-set reuse with dynamic constant offsets (#57)

Every batched Vulkan engine draw allocated a descriptor set and wrote 34
descriptors: two constant blocks, 16 samplers and 16 images. That happened
even when the draw sampled exactly what the previous draw did. The constant
blocks are new arena allocations per draw, so the sets could never match.
vk_eng_write_descriptors was about 2 ms of the Linux FIFO thread per frame,
before the driver's share.

With PS3RECOMP_VK_DESCRIPTOR_REUSE=1 (default off; batched recording only;
read at init):
- Engine pipelines use layouts of their own that declare the two constant
  blocks UNIFORM_BUFFER_DYNAMIC. A set then holds only textures, samplers
  and which buffer and size the blocks have, and each draw binds its
  block offsets.
- A draw whose views, samplers and block buffers and sizes match the
  previous draw's in the same batch binds the same set. Images released
  while a batch is open are destroyed only after it completes, so a view
  handle seen again within the batch is the same view.
- PS3RECOMP_RSX_INFLIGHT_LOG=1 prints sets written and reused.

test_vulkan_batched_engine gains a "reuse" mode. Its readback must equal
per-operation submission byte for byte under synchronization validation,
and same-texture draws must share sets.

5f61d988f552a2aa88c21174f3d9f612025a881b.message:
perf(spu): skip the MFC engine lookup for parameter and status channels (#77)

A DMA from lifted code is six channel writes (LSA, EAH, EAL, Size, TagID,
Cmd) and a tag wait is three operations (WrTagMask, WrTagUpdate,
RdTagStat). Every one of them went through mfc_for(), the lookup of the
context's private MFC engine: a thread-local cache probe with MAG's
SPU_MFC_LOOKUP_CACHE=1, a shared reader lock and a list walk without it.
Only the command and the tag-update write use the engine. The parameter
channels and the tag mask just latch a value in the context, and every
MFC read channel (tag status, tag mask, list stall status, atomic status)
returns latched context state; mfc_channel_read never touches its engine
argument. Those channels now skip the lookup. The values stored and
returned are the same; the engine is still created by the first command
or tag update, as before when a context's first MFC operation was a
command.

A synthetic job chain through the real channel, MFC and lock-line paths
(new: runtime/spu/tests/bench_spu_job_chain.c, tools/test_spu_job_chain.py)
measures, on macOS arm64 with MAG's runtime defaults, ns per operation:

                         fork main   this change
  parameter wrch            4.6         2.0
  tag wait                 15.4         8.5
  128 B GET + tag wait     81.4        59.2
  GETLLAR + PUTLLC         86.8        58.0
  small job               430.9       352.3   (memcpy floor 107)
  job + completion        519.0       418.0

A job is a 128-byte descriptor GET, two 1 KiB input GETs, an output PUT,
three tag waits and a GETLLAR/PUTLLC completion increment. The test checks
every job's output and the completion counters; in CI it runs 2000 jobs,
and --jobs N prints the timings. It also times one hop of a two-thread

feat(video): async submission and completion status for the D3D12 engine

an async submission reads stays valid until its terminal status, and

6cbc4c3efe9f18deebd073c2f20fbd2d52750735.message:
perf(spu): x86 vector forms of the float conversion helpers (#48)

On x86 the SPU float/integer conversions and fi had no vector form:
spu_cflts and spu_fi had NEON forms only and fell back to the scalar
reference (not even inlined in lifted code), and spu_cfltu, spu_csflt and
spu_cuflt were scalar loops on every architecture. The fa/fm/fma family
sent every lane it could not prove exact to the noinline per-lane fix-up:
an exponent-0 operand with a nonzero fraction, an exponent gap of 30 or
more in fa, a result below 2^-126, or an fma sum rounded onto a 24-bit
boundary.

Conversions and fi (SSE4.1; AVX widens integers in one f64x4):
- cflts/cfltu: SPU zeros made +0, x * 2^scale (one multiply, two above
  2^127), CVTTPS2DQ; its 0x80000000 out-of-range value is the negative
  bound and is flipped for nonnegative words; cfltu converts [2^31, 2^32)
  less 2^31 and saturates at 2^32, Inf and NaN by an integer compare.
- csflt/cuflt: the word widened to a double exactly, its 29 low bits
  cleared (truncation to 24 bits), narrowed exactly, then the scale applied
  to the exponent field with saturation and flush as spu__sf_pack does.
- fi: the NEON arithmetic with PMULLD and an unsigned compare.
cfltu, csflt and cuflt gain _ref forms; NEON keeps its forms unchanged.

fa/fs/fm/fma/fms/fnms (AVX2 and SSE4.1), now handled in the vector:
- an SPU zero (biased exponent 0, any fraction) is made +0 before the op;
  a zero factor gives +0, and for fma the addend as it is;
- the sum (fa, and fma's add) is a TwoSum; where it was rounded away from
  zero it takes one step toward zero at bit 53 before the 29 low bits are
  cleared, so no exponent gap and no 24-bit boundary needs the slow path;
- a result below 2^-126 is +0, cleared before narrowing so no denormal is
  formed (operands are flushed first too: no denormal microcode assists).
What remains for the per-lane fix-up is an extended-range operand that a
zero factor does not absorb and a result at or above 2^128.

SPU_FLOATFIX_STATS=1 now also counts, per reason, the lanes tha

6d6f5a602661ef782d2b9d54e14958a70462e723.message:
feat(video): opt-in GPU-only depth reads through a backend view

A texture fetch that reads a depth target's bytes as linear A8R8G8B8 or
D8R8G8B8 stores the depth into guest memory first: commit, wait for the
GPU, convert, copy, then build the texture. On one queue that wait covers
every command buffer ahead of it, so sampling a depth another renderer
just wrote blocks the FIFO until that renderer's GPU work completes.

PS3RECOMP_RSX_GPU_DEPTH_VIEW=1 (read at engine init, default off) asks the
backend for a new optional depth_z24_view: the Z24S8 conversion and a copy
into a fresh texture are appended to the next submission after the draws
recorded so far, the engine submits asynchronously and binds the view. The
texels equal the stored alias's; the view is reused while the depth is
unchanged. Guest memory is not written and the target stays guest_dirty,
so later consumers that need the bytes still get the synchronous store.
Metal implements the view; backends without it keep the store and the
engine says so.

Also link the draw-engine fixture (render-ablation registry and shared
stubs) so tools/test_rsx_immediate_vertices.py and the CI step build
again, and add tools/test_metal_depth_z24.py for the real-device test.

6f330b5ab68341b86d5ab9f261244a05513608d7.message:
perf(video): copy only written vertex constants per draw, and reuse unchanged uploads (#51)

Every engine draw copied all 512 transform constants (8 KB) into vp_cb and
handed the block to the backend, which copied it again. The batched Vulkan
path then memset and refilled 8 KB of its arena per draw, and Metal staged
another 8 KB copy. On Linux the FIFO thread spent about 5 ms per frame in
memmove and memset.

- rsx_dispatch records the span of constant slots written since the last
  take (uploads, seeding, init). The engine copies only that span into
  vp_cb, and the viewport epilogue only when it moved; either bumps vp_cb's
  version.
- A new optional backend hook, rebind_vs_constants, is called instead of
  bind_vs_constants when vp_cb has not changed since the last bind. Return
  0 and the engine binds the bytes as before.
- Vulkan (batched) points the draw at the previous draw's arena copy while
  that batch is still open; per-operation mode keeps binding. A bound
  block no longer pays a memset before its copy.
- Metal reuses the previous draw's staged copy until the stage is handed
  to a command buffer.
- D3D12 has no hook and binds every draw, as before.

Tests: test_rsx_draw_engine covers the dispatcher's dirty span, slots
written between draws reaching the next bind, rewritten slots, viewport
changes, refused rebinds and backends without the hook.
test_vulkan_batched_engine repeats constants with rebinds in every mode,
so sync, batched and merged readbacks still have to match.

feat(ppu): inline guest stores for a generated header, and the header tool

Lifts made before 12158c45 call the out-of-line vm_read*/vm_write* for every
guest load and store, and even 12158c45's lifter inlines only the loads. On a
Mac profile of the game thread the guest accessors were about a fifth of it.

tools/ppu_header_inline.py adds the inline fast paths to an already generated
ppu_recomp.h without relifting -- the lifted bodies call vm_read32(...) /
vm_write32(...) either way, so function bodies, hooks and splices stay
byte-identical. For an old header it adds 12158c45's load preamble; with
--stores (the only thing it adds to a header that already has the loads) it
adds vm_write*_inl and macros that store directly only when the out-of-line
store would do nothing else:
- the runtime allows it: vm_inline_store_ok, newly exported, is cleared by the
  same store diagnostics in the environment that turn the out-of-line fast
  path off (PPU_WVAL, PPU_WWATCH, PPU_WWATCH_DYNAMIC, PT);
- no dynamic store watch is armed (barrier/sync watch, null-page sweep, the
  critical-write range, exported as g_vm_critical_range);
- the address is in [0x10000, 0xE0000000), inside the mapping, and not the
  GCM put wake word;
- neither the first nor the last byte is on a line the coherence bitmap marks.

lines -- takes the out-of-line store unchanged. The value and its byte order
are the out-of-line store's; aligned stores are single-copy atomic. A
provenance.json gains a transform record with the before/after digests.

with PPU_NO_INLINE_STORES, as they do for the loads.

79ca568af53b44282e472a39da34c2d2157beffc.message:
perf(spu): longjmp without SEH unwinding at every SPU landing site on Win64 (#59)

On 64-bit Windows longjmp unwinds every host frame between it and its setjmp
(RtlUnwindEx, with a function-table lookup and a virtual unwind per frame). The
SPU runtime longjmps on every halt back to spu_run_with_halt, on restarts and
service halts back to the two service landing pads, and on every iret back to the
drain loop that took the interrupt. In MAG's Training on a Ryzen 9 9950X3D that
was about 5 ms of CPU per frame in RtlUnwindEx/RtlVirtualUnwind2/
RtlLookupFunctionEntry.

spu_jmp_no_unwind() (new header spu_jmp.h) zeroes the jmp_buf's Frame right after
setjmp returned 0, so longjmp restores the registers directly. The jumps cross only
C frames of this runtime and of lifted code, which have no destructors or __finally
blocks. SPU_LONGJMP_UNWIND=1 keeps the unwinding jump. No change on other
platforms.

Adapted from upstream ps3recomp 4609b3f0 ("spu: halt and iret longjmps without
unwinding on 64-bit Windows"), which covers spu_run_with_halt and the iret frame;
this also covers the two service landing pads (restart and service halt).

MAG Training on Windows (3 alternating rounds, against the same build without it):
21.10 -> 22.17 flips/s (+5.1%), p95 55.2 -> 53.6 ms.

7e09ea45a337fe496f57779b8d242d029900d9df.message:
perf(video): grow the Vulkan batch arenas when a full arena ends a batch (#60)

Each batch slot's host arena starts at 4 MiB, and an engine draw reserves
roughly 11-12 KB of it: vertices, u32 indices and both constant blocks. A
batch therefore ended, and was submitted, after about 350 draws whenever
nothing else ended it first. Each early submission also ends a merged
render pass (PS3RECOMP_VK_MERGE_PASSES). Today deferred-report tickets
usually end batches sooner; with a larger report batch the arena becomes
the limit.

When a batch has to be submitted because its arena is full, the size every
slot grows to when it is next opened doubles, up to 32 MiB. Growth happens
only on a freshly opened, idle slot, through the same path as before.
PS3RECOMP_RSX_INFLIGHT_LOG=1 prints arena-forced flushes and the current
arena size.

test_vulkan_batched_engine draws 160 large draws (64 KB of vertices each)
with no ticket between them. Every mode must still read back identically,
and in batched mode a full arena must grow the slots.

899f06c96a7cc9086e182822b76847d3baeb0163.message:
perf(spu): opt-in PPU store fast path for lines with no live reservation

PS3RECOMP_PPU_STORE_FASTPATH=1 lets a plain PPU store to a PPU-only line
skip the reservation break (ppu_resv_break_line) and the epoch bump
(epoch_written) when no PPU load-reserve is live on the line. Off, which is
the default, nothing changes: the switch is read once, and every shard-path
store breaks and bumps as before.

A PPU-only line is one the PPU has load-reserved and no SPU or watch has an
interest in. Every store to such a line holds the line's shard and, on exit,
scanned all registered PPU contexts and walked the epoch bucket chain. A main
PPU thread profile spent about 13% of its CPU there (store_unlock, break_line,
store_lock and the bitmap check), on lines that are marked forever once any
thread load-reserves them, while almost none had a reservation in flight.

Lines with SPU interest or a watch are not affected: spu_coh_ppu_store_lock
still re-checks the interest under the shard and sends those stores through
the lock-line lock and spu_coh_notify_write, so an SPU taking GETLLAR, and a
PUTLLC compare-and-commit, see exactly the serialization they did before.

Memory-ordering argument. With tracking on, ppu_load_reserve32/64 run, while
holding the lock-line lock and the line's shard:
  1. spu_coh_ppu_live_add(line)   (counts the reservation),
  2. read the line epoch and the reserved value, set the token.
The count stays up until that thread's store-conditional has returned, or
until the same thread load-reserves again, when spu_coh_ppu_live_drop runs.
A shard-path store writes guest memory and then reads the count, inside one
shard critical section, and skips the break and bump only on zero. The two
critical sections exclude each other, so in any execution one of them came
first:
  - load-reserve first: its count is visible to the store (shard release ->
    acquire), so the store breaks and bumps; the store-conditional checks the
    epoch and compares-and-swaps under the same shard, sees the bump and fails;
  - store firs

9192f907d07cfab8d914abf863ba16f0ecd2b486.message:
perf(spu): opt-in shard path for plain PPU stores to idle SPU lines

Once any SPU had reserved a line, every later plain PPU store to it took the
process-wide lock-line lock. On a Mac profile of the game thread that was
about 0.9 ms per update blocked in spu_lockline_lock_hybrid from vm_write32,
plus the notify around it, from scene-update stores to lines an SPU had once
reserved but almost never held at the time.

PS3RECOMP_PPU_STORE_SHARD_IDLE=1 (default off; needs
PS3RECOMP_PPU_STORE_LIVE_SPU=1) lets such a store take the line's shard --
the path PPU-only lines already take -- while the line is idle: no SPU
context counts a reservation on it (rechecked under the shard) and it carries
no sticky mark.

The lock-line lock protected these stores from two kinds of writer:
- an SPU PUTLLC, which compares and then copies the whole line under the
  lock. It commits only while its context counts the line, and the count is
  raised under the line's shard, so a store holding the shard that finds the
  count at zero cannot overlap a commit;
- host code that read-modify-writes guest lines under the lock. Every such
  section now marks its lines first with spu_coh_host_rmw_mark (a sticky bit
  set under each line's shard, so no shard-path store is in flight once it is
  set): the SPURS HLE kernel's workload counters, signal bits and event flags,
  the workload-flag consume, the taskset task bits, signalled and enabled
  bits, and the cellSync queue words. Lines marked with spu_coh_reserve(NULL)
  and watched lines are sticky too.
Writers that only write (MFC puts, report publication, plain host stores) may
overlap a shard-path store on one line, as they already may on PPU-only
lines: both write bytes and bump the epoch atomically. Store-conditionals
keep the lock-line lock, since a shard-only one would not exclude an MFC put
to the other words of its line. Off, nothing changes: the marks return at
once and stores keep the lock.

a016ed9419539f7bda62fb717590443d814160d4.message:
fix(audio): pace cellAudio block reads on the clock, not on device pulls (#40)

* fix(audio): pace cellAudio block reads on the clock, not on device pulls

The POSIX mixing thread read a guest block whenever the SDL queue had room,
within a four-block cap. CoreAudio drains that queue 512 frames (two
blocks) at a time, so each pull produced two guest reads about 1 ms apart,
then none for about 10 ms. Against the real device, 50% of read intervals
were under 2 ms.

A guest mixer that writes one block per period notification, just in time,
has not written the second block of each pair yet. About half of what it
plays is silence: a title's movie mixer filled only 97-115 of 188 blocks
per second and sounded broken up.

audio_pace now schedules reads on the monotonic clock (block k at
epoch + k * 256/48000 s), whatever chunk size the device pulls. The
cushion for those pulls is silence queued once at the device:
- prime: 4 blocks of silence before the first read;
- low: 1 block of silence when the queue runs dry;
- high: at 12 blocks queued, move the schedule one period later.

Against CoreAudio the queue holds 21-27 ms at each read, about 5-10 ms more
than before, with no read interval under 2 ms. Behaviour with no device,
the dummy-driver clock, suspension recovery and stalled devices is kept.

PS3RECOMP_AUDIO_PACING=queue keeps the previous pacing for A/B runs.
test_posix_audio_pacing.py now runs every mode under both pacings and adds
two modes: two-block device pulls, and the shared pacer driven with a
WASAPI-shaped device.

two guest reads back to back per period. This is the same pairing that

a2f9c69a151960d5872e19086c7b13759671bbdc.message:
perf(spu): make the DMA observer hooks free when both are off (#71)

* perf(spu): make the DMA observer hooks free when both are off

Every SPU DMA called spu_dma_disposition_begin, which called
audio_chronology_dma_begin, and later the before/after/finish hooks, even
with SPU_DMA_DISPOSITION and AUDIO_CHRONOLOGY unset. On Windows each
begin also did three InterlockedCompareExchange "loads" of the observers'
ready words (two for the chronology, one for the receipts). A locked
compare-exchange takes the cache line exclusively even when it fails, so
every SPU thread bounced those two lines on every DMA: about 3.7 ms of CPU
per frame in MAG Training on Windows, with chronology off.

Both switches are read once and fixed for the run. The first DMA now reads
them as before and, when both observers are off, sets
g_spu_dma_hooks_off, a word alone on its cache line that nothing writes
again. The four hooks become static inline wrappers: begin tests that word
and fills an inert token; before, after and finish test the token and
return. The out-of-line bodies, renamed *_slow, are unchanged and still run
whenever either observer is on, so receipts, chronology records, errno and
last-error preservation are as before.

A synthetic micro-benchmark of 32-byte mfc_do_transfer GET/PUT pairs on
macOS (arm64), where the ready loads were already plain acquire loads,
goes from 25.3 to 20.4 ns per transfer on one thread and from 24.4 to
20.1 ns on four. The Windows saving is larger, since the contended locked
operations go away as well.

tools/test_spu_dma_disposition.py gains a hooks-off mode: with both
observers off the flag is set after the first DMA and the copies are
unchanged; with either on it stays clear.

a548774c92a4b3988a606b6170d39b0eff477414.message:
perf(ppu): opt-in fast path in the out-of-line guest accessors

PS3RECOMP_VM_FAST_ACCESSORS (CMake option, default OFF) starts each
out-of-line vm_read*/vm_write* in ppu_loader.cpp with a fast path: the plain
big-endian load or store and an immediate return, for an access that needs
none of the work after it. Off, nothing is compiled and the accessors are
unchanged. The definition is PUBLIC because ppu_loader.cpp is compiled by the
game target.

Why: lifts made before the lifter's inline loads (12158c45) call these for
every guest load and store. On a Linux profile of a title's main PPU thread
the accessors were about 22% of its CPU: vm_read32 alone 10.5% (range checks,
a dozen getenv-guarded probes, two TLS stores and a spin detector per call),
vm_write64/32 7%, and vm_hotmap 1.8% (a non-inlined call whose only work is
an environment gate). A host micro-benchmark against the real ppu_loader.cpp
measures 3.95 ns per access today, 1.83-1.96 ns with the fast path, and
1.45-1.64 ns fully inlined, so the fast path recovers most of the gap without
a re-lift.

The accessors are compiled under _slow names and the public vm_read*/
vm_write* become small wrappers that do the fast path and otherwise tail-call
the original body. A fast path inside the original bodies (the first version)
still paid their whole frame on every call: callee saves and, on a hardened
toolchain, the stack-protector canary for their diagnostic buffers. On the
game that version moved vm_read32 only from 9.95% to 7.3% of main-thread CPU,
with the canary load the hottest instruction.

Reads take the fast path when vm_inline_ok (no read diagnostic in the
environment: the gate ppu_recomp.h's inline loads already use) and the
address is in [0x10000, 0xE0000000) -- not the null page, not the raw SPU
problem-state window whose loads pop mailboxes -- is not the GCM ref-poll
word, and is inside ppu_vm_size.

Stores take it when no store diagnostic is in the environment (PPU_WVAL,
PPU_WWATCH, PPU_WWATCH_DYNAMIC, PT), no sync-line probe is armed, no null-page

fix(video): enable sampler anisotropy on the Vulkan owner device

The Vulkan device was created without samplerAnisotropy, and the native
owner reported anisotropy as known but never as enabled. A native
frontend on that owner therefore refused every anisotropic sampler
(MAG_NATIVE_UNSUPPORTED). On Linux this refused the first native Main
scene of a running title outright; the Metal path has no such gate.

Enable the feature whenever the device reports it, and report it in the
owner's enabled features, as the BC and depth-bounds features already
are. The engine's own samplers never request anisotropy, so the original
renderer's behaviour is unchanged. test_native_owner_vulkan already

b2c660c2d496c7cbf67dda7dbf6d20d0c395c2a6.message:
perf(spu): opt-in per-thread heap storage for the SPU decode cache

PS3RECOMP_SPU_DECODE_CACHE_HEAP (CMake option, default OFF) moves the SPU
interpreter's 2 MiB decode table out of static TLS. Off, the source compiles
exactly as before.

The table was 2 MiB of the process's 2.13 MiB static TLS block, and glibc
clears the whole block for every new host thread in the thread that creates
it. Every SPURS task runs on a new host thread, so on Linux the game's main
PPU thread spent about 8% of its CPU in cellSpursCreateTaskWithAttribute ->
pthread_create, mostly a 2 MiB memset in _dl_allocate_tls_init, before the
page faults behind it. Every other host thread (render workers, audio) paid
the same at startup.

With the option, a thread allocates its table with calloc on its first
interpreted instruction and frees it at thread exit through a pthread key
(an FLS slot on Windows). The storage is still owned by the thread and
nothing is retained after it exits, which is why the table was in TLS. A
thread that never interprets pays nothing. If the allocation fails the thread
decodes without the cache, the same path as SPU_INTERP_DECODE_CACHE=0. The
table is still revalidated on every instruction, so its contents and the
decoded results are unchanged.

A thread pool for SPURS task threads was considered first. It would remove
pthread_create entirely, but a reused thread carries the previous task's
thread-local state (about sixty TLS variables across the SPU runtime, the
lifted-job exit buffers, the original-work observer's per-thread worker
registration and the stack-range cleanup at thread exit), so changing thread
identity is the larger and riskier change.

tools/test_spu_interpreter_handoff.py now builds and runs every mode with
both storages, checks on ELF hosts that the heap variant leaves spu_interp.o
with under 1 MiB of static TLS, and links the job I/O recorder that the
fixture's sources started to need.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
