b75a60eb5a0d724e97eccb86f7ad159dbb547608.message:
perf(spurs): wake the coordinator when a write lands on the request line

A PPU raises a SPURS ready count, signal or flag with a plain store or a
store-conditional on the instance's first line, and neither woke the
coordinator. The request waited for the coordinator's next timed pass,
about 1 ms (1-2 ms on Windows), with every SPU idle. SPU atomics already
kicked it through the line-commit hook, and the HLE ready-count calls
through the API unlock; PPU stores did not.

The scheduler now keeps a coherence watch (spu_coh_watch_add) on the
request line while it runs. Every real write to the line then calls
spurs_request_line_written: PPU store or CAS, MFC put, SPU atomic, or a
host store through the coherent paths. That holds under the default
coherence scheme and under PS3RECOMP_COH_VERSIONS, which implements the
same watch API. The callback only sets the kick and wakes the coordinator,
which re-reads the guest bytes as on any pass. It is a wake hint with no
guest state, so it is on by default; PS3RECOMP_SPURS_STORE_WAKE=0 leaves
the line unwatched. The scheduler's own bookkeeping writes (the consumed
request, the current contention) are skipped by a thread-local flag, so a
dispatch does not schedule a second, empty pass. The watch is removed once
the scheduler's threads have joined. Like any watched line, PPU stores to
the request line take the coherent commit path.

tests/bench_spurs_pm_hop.c's PPU stand-in now stores through vm_write8,
the coherent path a PPU store takes. With the workers asleep (ppu-idle),
store to PM start on macOS arm64, us: 1054 -> 17 p50 on one lane, 1053 ->
16 on six. tools/test_spurs_pm_hop.py asserts the woken case starts well
inside the timed pass and the STORE_WAKE=0 case does not.
tests/test_spurs_workload_flag.c, which links the scheduler without the
coherence unit, stubs the watch API.

c125ff1e66247d604af5257be498e49c1a88a645.message:
feat(video): Vulkan completion tickets, checked flush and GPU depth views

The Vulkan engine backend had no submit_async, completion_status or
submit_and_wait_checked, so on Vulkan deferred reports never deferred, a
checked SET_REFERENCE could not certify, and PS3RECOMP_RSX_EARLY_LABEL_RELEASE,
PS3RECOMP_RSX_EARLY_FIFO_SYNC, the frames-ahead bound and
PS3RECOMP_RSX_GPU_DEPTH_VIEW had nothing to act on.

Stage E5 of rsx_vulkan_backend.c:

- A completion ticket is a fence submitted with no command buffer after
  everything so far; drawing is still one waited submission per operation,
  so nothing recorded is left unsubmitted, and the fence signals only after
  all earlier queue work (engine, native renderer, present). A ring of 64
  fences retires strictly in order; a full ring waits for its oldest.
- submit_and_wait_checked waits for a ticket. Any failed submission, fence
  wait or recording call latches; tickets then report -1.
- depth_z24_view: depth aspect to a buffer, a compute pass
  (vulkan/rsx_vk_depth_z24.comp, integer-exact rounding, the CPU path's
  clamp and NaN rule) to D24S8 words in place, a copy into a fresh RGBA8
  image whose view mapping composes the A8R8G8B8/D8R8G8B8 decode rotation
  with the crossbar, all in a command buffer of its own that starts and
  ends with full memory dependencies, submitted as a ticket without a wait.
  A released in-flight view, and the depth it reads, are destroyed when
  the ticket retires.
- depth_store_z24 and depth_z24_texture use the same conversion behind
  PS3RECOMP_VK_GPU_Z24=1 (default off: the engine keeps depth_readback plus
  its CPU conversion).
- The native boundary accepts a pending ticket as the ordered boundary, as
  Metal's asynchronous boundary does; native passes order imported images
  against all earlier queue work.
- PS3RECOMP_RSX_INFLIGHT_LOG=1 adds an [rsx inflight vulkan] line.

Depth formats other than D32_SFLOAT(_S8_UINT) are refused with one message.
docs/RSX_EARLY_LABEL_RELEASE.md records the Vulkan audit of both facts the
early switches

c1c07bfea7c540311332d6c546790c1c2762117f.message:
perf(spu): opt-in thread pool for async SPU tasks on POSIX

Every async SPU task dispatch created and detached a host thread with a
256 MB stack reservation; the game starts several per update (about 2,200
thread births in under six seconds on a Mac profile), each paying the
creation, a cold stack and fresh thread-local state, the SPU decode cache
among it.

PS3RECOMP_SPU_TASK_POOL=1 (default off) runs them on reused threads. A task
is handed to the pool only when a pool thread is idle and waiting for it
(more idle threads than queued tasks); otherwise a new pool thread is created
for it, as before. So every task still starts at once on a thread of its own
-- one that waits for another task can never be queued behind it -- and the
thread count never falls below the running tasks. An idle pool thread exits
after two seconds without work. "[spu_workload] task pool:" reports tasks,
reuses, creations and retirements. Off, a thread per task as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

c20e56ef4cf703587318808f98fb8c3dbec2b0b9.message:
perf(spu): x86 vector forms of the per-lane SPU helper families and a leaner shufb (#43)

Most per-lane SPU integer helpers had NEON forms only; on x86 they ran as
scalar loops over 4, 8 or 16 lanes. They now have SSSE3 forms, with each
scalar spu_X_ref kept as the fallback and the test oracle:

- byte, halfword and word compares and their immediate forms
  (ceqb/cgtb/clgtb, ceqh/cgth/clgth, ceq/cgt/clgt, *i);
- word and halfword add/subtract and immediates (a/ai/sf/sfi, ah/ahi/sfh/sfhi);
- the 16x16 multiplies (mpy, mpyu, mpyh, mpyhh, mpyhhu, mpys, mpya, mpyhha,
  mpyhhau, mpyi, mpyui);
- cntb, the sign extends (xsbh, xshw, xswd), absdb and avgb;
- the immediate rotates and shifts (rothi, roti, rotmahi, rotmai);
- gather bits and form select masks (gb, gbh, gbb, fsm, fsmh, fsmb).

The variable per-lane shifts, carry/borrow and clz/orx/sumb keep the scalar
form.

spu_shufb (SSE4.1) now selects in host byte order directly: result byte h
depends only on control byte h at the same host position, and SPU source
byte k sits at host byte k^3, so the four byte swaps into SPU order and back
are gone. spu__xperm marks out-of-range indices with one saturating add
instead of a min, compare and mask.

test_spu_int_x86 compares every new form with its reference: random
operands, shared lanes, the shufb special selectors and every shift count
(21.5M checks, 78 helpers, clang and gcc at -mssse3, -msse4.1 and
-march=x86-64-v3); test_spu_shufb passes.

busiest notified lines had a holder in 0-6% of their writes (two lines about a
third of the time), and the PPU side of it was store-conditionals with no
holder at all.

PS3RECOMP_PPU_STORE_LIVE_SPU=1 (default off) counts, per line (a hashed table),
the SPU contexts holding a reservation: a context counts itself at its GETLLAR
before it reads the line (spu_coh_reserve and the GETLLAR fast path) and stops
when its reservation ends on its own thread (PUTLLC either way, PUTLLUC, a
GETLLAR of another line, unregister). A reservation that another agent
invalidates stays counted until then, so the count is never below the holders.
A locked notify that finds the count at zero, and no watch or context-less
interest on the line, returns after the PPU-side bookkeeping instead of
walking. Lines marked without a context (watches, the SPURS HLE lines) are
never skipped.

The lock-line lock itself is still taken by every such write: host code, the
SPURS HLE kernel among it, relies on it to make its read-modify-writes of these
lines atomic against PPU stores, so only the walk goes. Why skipping is safe: a
GETLLAR raises the count (seq_cst) before reading the line, and the notify
reads it after the write and a full fence, so either the notify sees it or the
GETLLAR's read sees the write. A slot shared by several lines only keeps the
walk. SPU_COH_LINE_HIST now also reports how often the line was counted.

tools/test_ppu_store_live_spu.py builds the real coherence and PPU store code
with an emulated GETLLAR/PUTLLC (the spu_channels.c protocol, tracking calls
included) and runs it off and on: the walk is skipped exactly when no holder is
counted, a counted holder

c782315806c45627b7dd52fa36e874d977223b53.message:
feat(video): reserved queue order for Vulkan native submissions

The reserved-order Main commit fixes the native submission's queue place at
the native boundary and encodes it later on the worker; Metal does that by
enqueueing an empty command buffer. A Vulkan queue has no such slot, and a
timeline semaphore that later original submissions wait on deadlocks: the
native signal is submitted after those waits on the same queue, and
implementations (Mesa's queue thread) process a queue's submissions in order.

rsx_vulkan_backend_queue_order (rsx_native_owner.h, rsx_native_queue_order)
keeps the order on the CPU instead:

- reserve(), under the native lease, starts a hold: every original queue
  submission (engine batches and tickets, presents, depth views) is recorded
  in order with its fence instead of reaching the queue; the owner
  bookkeeping runs as if it had been submitted.
- submit(), once, from any thread without the lease, submits the native
  batch, then every held submission in order, and ends the hold; NULL
  abandons the reservation with the same release.
- While a hold is active, waiting on a held fence first waits for the
  release and a status read reports it pending (vkQueueSubmit needs the
  fence externally synchronised), swapchain presents and device-idle waits
  wait for it, and the native lease reports -4 so nothing native overtakes
  held work.

The owner fixture checks, per-operation and batched, that a clear recorded
after a reservation lands after a native clear submitted 150 ms later from
another thread (the readback waits for it), that abandoning releases held
work, and that the lease is refused during the hold. The Vulkan fixtures now
also reject validation THREADING ERROR reports.

perf(spu): exact x86 vector path for extended-range single-precision lanes

After #48, SPU_FLOATFIX_STATS in MAG Training on Windows still showed many
fa/fm/fma lanes reaching the per-lane scalar fix-up: ext 13.4M/24.6M/48.2M
and, for fma, zero-b 128.5M. The zero-a/zero-b lanes were extended-range
lanes too: the counter only counts lanes that took the fix-up, but its
classifier tested for a zero operand before an exponent-255 one, so fma(ext,

included, taken for the whole vector when the fast path leaves a lane out:

  fraction), exact for every biased exponent 1..255; exponent 0 gives +0;
- the op, TwoSum and the step toward zero are the fast path's;
- the result is packed by hand: biased exponent 1..255, sign | 0x7FFFFFFF
  at or above 2^129, +0 below 2^-126, as spu__sf_pack saturates and flushes.

are gone on x86 (NEON keeps its own). The classifier now reports ext before
zero, on NEON too.

exponent 255: 15.6/8.7/26.4 -> 6.2/4.4/7.4; one in four: 6.3/4.5/6.1 ->
4.9/3.3/5.6; none: 2.6/1.7/3.2, unchanged.

test_spu_float_exact runs its three passes a second time on x86 through the
wide path alone (spu__x8_*_w / spu__x4_*_w), so that path meets every class
pair, every fma exponent triple and the random generators (447M lanes):
clang and gcc at -msse4.1, x86-64-v3, x86-64-v4, clang-cl, and Rosetta.

c7e8a986429de6ce04b0c0177fa8e9c38620d5c9.message:
perf(gcm): opt-in lazy issue of applied report records under early release (#68)

Every FIFO pass ended by issuing its queued report records: one backend
completion ticket per pass. On the batched Vulkan engine each ticket
submits the open batch and ends a merged render pass. Under early label
release the records are already applied at their FIFO position, so the
ticket only lets their completion be verified. On Linux, raising
PS3RECOMP_RSX_DEFERRED_REPORT_BATCH from 32 to 256 (capacity 8192) took MAG
Training from +11.9% to +18.6% over main with pass merging on. The pass-end
issue keeps a floor of one ticket per pass whatever the batch.

With PS3RECOMP_RSX_EARLY_LAZY_ISSUE=1 (default off; needs early label
release), a pass ends by issuing only when a queued record is still
unapplied (gated), so that record's publication latency is unchanged.
Applied records are issued when the batch fills, at a dependency, or at
capacity, as before.

test_gcm_early_label_release covers:
- applied records left unissued at pass end until the batch fills;
- a gated record still issued at the end of its pass and published on
  completion;
- the switch off issuing every pass as before.

cef8b7a5f3dcadb3c419f2deb7bfed446ed82e00.message:
perf(ppu): opt-in skip of reservation-break scans with none open

Every write to an SPU-interested line (spu_coh_notify_write) and every
successful stwcx./stdcx. scanned the registry of every guest thread context
for a reservation to break (ppu_resv_break_line, ppu_resv_break); on a Mac
profile of the game thread the line scan alone was about 8%. Most of the time
no other thread is between a load-reserve and its store-conditional.

PS3RECOMP_PPU_RESV_OPEN_COUNT=1 (default off) counts the threads with a
reservation open: a thread counts itself once at its load-reserve and stops at
its store-conditional (or its next load-reserve). The breaks skip their scan
when no other thread has one open; the plain-store and range breaks, which
also take the caller's own reservation, skip only when none is open at all.

Safe because a load-reserve raises the count (seq_cst) before it reads the
reserved value and a break reads it (seq_cst) after the store it follows: a
reservation the break did not see counted reads its value after that store,
so it already includes it. A count left high (a thread that never issued its
store-conditional) only keeps the scan. Off, nothing changes.

tools/test_ppu_store_fastpath.py passes with the count on (no violations in
the reservation-checked modes; the unchecked control still shows them).

d1889f4eed0ea22781a35c7506315cdb6a879a2c.message:
feat(video): opt-in batched Vulkan engine recording

Every Vulkan engine operation was one submission the CPU waited for, so with
native work queued the FIFO consumer blocked at the next draw until all of it
completed, early label release or not.

PS3RECOMP_VK_BATCHED_ENGINE=1 (stage E6, default off, read at engine init)
records operations into one command buffer per batch and submits only at a
ticket, the checked flush, submit_and_wait, a CPU read (which also waits),
the native boundary and each present (which do not), or when the batch is
full (PS3RECOMP_VK_BATCH_MAX_OPS, default 2048).

- Each operation starts with a full dependency on everything before it, so
  GPU order is the per-operation order.
- Vertices, indices and constants go into the batch's own host-visible arena
  (4 MiB, grown on demand) and each draw gets a fresh descriptor set from the
  batch's pool; one operation's allocations never span two batches.
- Batches are E5 tickets. PS3RECOMP_VK_BATCH_SLOTS (default 16, at most 32)
  may be in flight; a slot is reused only after its ticket completed.
- Images, buffers, framebuffers and pipelines released while a batch may use
  them are destroyed when the last ticket that could reference them retires.
  Releasing a natively pinned image first finishes recorded work, since the
  native side's fences do not cover work recorded after its boundary.
- The engine flush submits an (empty, if need be) batch, so the owner gate
  still sees a real boundary. GPU depth views record into the batch.

Also fixes the per-operation draw binding the vertex buffer before it may
have been created (caught by the new test under validation).

tools/test_vulkan_batched_engine.py runs one synthetic stream (clears,
seeding, uploads and re-uploads, feedback snapshots, blended and depth-tested
draws with per-draw constants, texture and pipeline release mid-stream,
tickets, depth views, presents) per operation and batched, under validation
with synchronization validation, and requires identical readback; behind
~300 ms of forei

d1aefd9da5a084854d8356d2b46ffb519c09e61c.message:
feat(video): opt-in early label release at FIFO position

With deferred reports, label releases and reports reach guest memory only
after the backend command buffer that follows them completes, so a guest
polling a progress label waits for all GPU work queued ahead of that buffer.

PS3RECOMP_RSX_EARLY_LABEL_RELEASE=1 applies NV406E/NV4097 label releases
and the SDK's synthesized reports at their FIFO position. A record is
applied early only behind already-applied records, so guest-visible order
is unchanged; it stays queued until genuine completion to verify the
backend, is never applied twice, and a failure still latches. Waiting
progress then waits only for unapplied records; capacity pressure still
waits for everything. The diagnostic ring-progress word stays gated.

PS3RECOMP_RSX_EARLY_FIFO_SYNC=1 additionally lets a checked SET_REFERENCE
commit recorded work without waiting (a queued receipt still verifies it
and a failure freezes certification), and drops the GPU wait from the
NV406E acquire barrier and the NV0039 pre-copy flush.

Both rest on the draw engine copying every GPU input at record time and
writing GPU results to guest memory only through synchronous readbacks.
Default off; refused on the live report batch path.

feat(ftrace): record the trace's base clock reading in its header (#84)

PS3_FTRACE writes span times relative to the ps3_ft_now() reading taken
when the trace starts, and the header did not say what that reading was,
so a trace could not be lined up with samples taken on the same clock --
for example to restrict a perf profile to the windows the trace shows
only one SPU busy.

The header now ends with base_ns=<reading> clock=<CLOCK_MONOTONIC|QPC>.
base_ns plus a span's microsecond time is the absolute clock value: Linux
`perf record -k CLOCK_MONOTONIC` samples (perf script prints seconds) and
macOS CLOCK_MONOTONIC on POSIX, QueryPerformanceCounter scaled to
nanoseconds on Windows. The existing keys keep their order and meaning;
tools/ftrace_report.py only prints the header.

New synthetic test (tests/test_ftrace_header.c, tools/test_ftrace_header.py):
it records a span, dumps the trace, and checks that base_ns falls between
the readings around the first hook and that base_ns plus the span's t0
equals the absolute reading it was recorded with.

dcc460827cfd2a46351feb4e6951ec94b83de304.message:
fix(lv2): publish event queues only once initialised; push under the table lock (#67)

* fix(lv2): publish event queues only once initialised; push under the table lock

Host producers -- cellAudio's period thread, SPURS, SPU groups -- resolve an event
queue by key and push into it from their own threads, while the guest creates and
destroys queues. sys_event_queue_create set active=1 right after memset() and
initialised the queue's lock and condition variable only afterwards;
sys_event_find_queue_by_key and sys_event_queue_push_by_id read active without any
lock. A producer that saw the new queue entered a zeroed lock: on Windows,
EnterCriticalSection on a zeroed CRITICAL_SECTION faults writing near 0x24. MAG hit
it on about 1 in 6 engine starts (cellAudio's thread pushing the audio-period
notify while the game created its notify queue). On POSIX a zeroed pthread mutex
only works by accident on glibc. Destroy had the mirror race: it deleted the lock
before clearing active.

- Both create paths initialise the lock, condition variable and fields first and
  publish active last with a release store.
- Destroy clears active first (release), then destroys the primitives.
- sys_event_queue_push_by_id and sys_event_find_queue_by_key hold the table lock
  around the check (acquire load) and the push. event_queue_push does not block.
- The Windows table lock is initialised once (InitOnceExecuteOnce) instead of

de1e7ecc3d9a02fc1f78f53a9ff2192ab3542ba0.message:
perf(spu): opt-in register promotion in the SPU lifter (--promote-regs) (#46)

Lifted SPU code keeps every register in ctx->gpr[], a union array in an
escaped context: each result is stored and each operand reloaded, and
every local-store write (char-typed) forces the LS base and every
register to be re-read.

--promote-regs keeps the registers a lifted function names in C locals
and the LS base in a local. ctx->gpr is made coherent only where anything
else can look at it: before every host return and every out-of-line call
that takes ctx (calls and drains, channel ops, stop, halt), with locals
re-read after such a call returns. A forward may-dirty dataflow decides
which registers to store; a backward liveness (a store reads every
possibly dirty register) decides which to re-read. Lifted functions never
setjmp, so every longjmp (halt, restart, interrupt unwind) leaves through
one of those calls, after the store. The return straight after a stop or
halt call stores nothing, as that call may itself change registers.

The locals are a plain vector type converted at each use: as the u128
union, clang splits each into scalar halves and spills them. Promoted LS
accesses take the hoisted base, on x86 with SSSE3 as one load or store
and one byte shuffle; their per-access diagnostic gates are compiled only
with -DSPU_LS_DIAG=1, and registration reports once when an LS diagnostic
is requested without them. --promote-max-regs N leaves functions naming
more than N registers unpromoted. The default lift is byte-for-byte
unchanged.

tools/test_spu_promote_regs.py runs a neutral synthetic program through
the real drain, channels, halt, a depth-0 restart into the interpreter
and an interrupt taken and returned, against the plain lift and the
interpreter, with missing-store and missing-reload bug controls and a
register cap that mixes promoted and plain functions.

In MAG (Windows, x86-64-v3, three alternating Training rounds) promoting
the streamed job modules raised guest flips 6.8%, lifted SPU samples
-13%. Squashes perf/spu-l

deca261b7aaf46a74523473b4ce4a201d5e52058.message:
feat(spu): count the identical-transfer back-off in SPU_DMA_REPEAT_LOG (#76)

mfc_submit's watchdog treats a job that re-issues the same transfer 256
times as an episode: it yields for the first SPU_DMA_REPEAT_BACKOFF_MS
(default 2) and then sleeps 1 ms per repeat until the transfer changes or
30 s pass. A job polling an RSX label, a ring-space counter or a peer
job's flag lands in that sleep, and a Windows Sleep(1) lasts 1-2 ms, so
the back-off can sit on a frame's serial SPU path. Nothing reported how
often it slept.

With SPU_DMA_REPEAT_LOG set, each episode line now also reports its
yields, sleeps and the wall time the sleeps took. Every 256th sleep on a
thread prints that thread's totals since start, and the per-image totals
gain slept_us. The episode clock is QPC / CLOCK_MONOTONIC instead of
GetTickCount64, which moves in ~16 ms steps on Windows. With the log
unset, the back-off is unchanged and does no timing.

tools/test_spu_dma_poll.py checks the counters on its delayed-producer
fixture, which now has a real millisecond clock: with no yield window,
769 sleeps took 1036 ms and the episode 1155 ms on macOS; with an
unbounded window the same wait was 770 yields and 119 ms.

df6df96865a5d0c64949a180c3d8767c6f2bb5b3.message:
fix(video): count Vulkan pump and host-present time in PS3RECOMP_RSX_FIFO_BUSY (#66)

The FIFO-busy accounting charges consumer-thread time outside every span
to "other". On Metal, the window pump and host-driven presents have spans
(PUMP, PRESENT_HOST). On Vulkan they did not, so on Windows and Linux the
event pump (PeekMessage or SDL plus the native OSK and pad sampling) and
the host present outside the engine present and swapchain waits (the
present ring's fence waits and copies) all landed in "other". A Windows
run showed about 2.6 ms of "other" per 10.9 ms update against 0.4 ms of
draw, with nothing to say what it was.

Wrap rsx_vulkan_backend_pump_messages in PUMP and
rsx_vulkan_backend_present in PRESENT_HOST, as Metal does. Accounting
only: with PS3RECOMP_RSX_FIFO_BUSY unset each call is a load and a return.

e5f3e002e763220eac636bcbdb56f5b22424584a.message:
feat(video): D3D12 engine depth as D24S8 words on the GPU

Implement depth_store_z24 and depth_z24_view for the D3D12 engine backend
with one compute conversion. The stored value for a depth d is
round-half-up(clamp(d, 0, 1) * (2^24 - 1)), NaN as 0, which is what the
engine's CPU store computes in double precision; the shader reproduces it
exactly in 32-bit integers (d is m * 2^-s with a 24-bit m, so the product
is a 48-bit value kept in two words, rounded and shifted by s). The
integer method was checked against the double formula on 4.4 million
float inputs with no difference.

- depth_store_z24 writes the big-endian words into a buffer, copies it
  back and stores the rows into guest memory (one wait, 4 bytes a pixel,
  no CPU conversion).
- depth_z24_view builds a linear A8R8G8B8/D8R8G8B8 texture of the words
  with the given crossbar, encoded after the recorded draws, without
  waiting: with PS3RECOMP_RSX_GPU_DEPTH_VIEW the engine samples depth
  through it and guest memory is left alone.

The real-adapter fixture, under the debug layer, checks the store against
depth_readback plus the CPU conversion over a target holding two depths,
partial stores with a destination pitch, and that a view samples exactly
like a texture uploaded from the decoded words (58/58, RTX 5090).

e61e3af3d424d0c8c354f4d986f45c0e79775ab1.message:
perf(video): hash texture contents in eight independent lanes (#75)

The texture cache hashes a texture's bytes in full when its sparse check
changes, on its turn every eight frames, for small textures every frame, for
picture-backed contents and on every miss. That hash was a single
xor-multiply chain over 8-byte words, so each multiply waited on the one
before: about 8 GB/s on an M-series core, 1.1 ms of the Mac RSX thread a
frame in Training.

eng_hash_bytes runs eight chains over interleaved words, each step folding
its high bits down, then folds the lanes, tail and length together and
mixes them: 35 GB/s on the same core. The value is only ever compared with
values made by the same function in the same run (the cache and the
binding-capture check, which now share it), so nothing else changes.

test_texture_content_hash checks every single-byte and single-bit change
across lane and tail boundaries, words trading places, lengths, and that
the cache still re-uploads changed bytes; it prints the speed against the
old chain.

e7185547ac5141865bcbc7b02041f674f2820125.message:
fix(memory): pin pages under SDK-owned protection, and count refused watches

The Linux lane's diagnostic PS3RECOMP_SPURS_FLAG_GUARD write-protects a
guest page itself and single-steps writes through it. If the write watch
held the same page, the two would fight over its protection: the guard
making the page writable would silently end the watch's protection while
the watch still counted the page as clean.

- The rule is documented in vm_watch.h and vm_watch_hooks.h. SDK code
  that changes a guest page's protection itself calls
  vm_watch_forget_host(page, size, 0) (or vm_watch_forget) first. That
  pins the pages: the watch releases them if it held them and refuses to
  arm them until the runtime makes them writable again (vm_commit,
  vm_protect).
- Refused vm_watch calls on pinned pages are counted
  (vm_watch_stats.refused).
- Releasing a page on any protection change now always undoes the
  watch's own read-only protection before the caller applies its own.
  Previously only a writable change did, which left a pinned page
  read-only by the watch.

Test: a read-only vm_protect and an SDK component's pin both make
vm_watch refuse, counted; a page pinned while watched is writable
again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

e78084d7285c4e40bb0e7b8c66d7769ec6eee995.message:
feat(video): reserved queue order for native submissions on the D3D12 engine

The D3D12 counterpart of rsx_vulkan_backend_queue_order. reserve(), under
the native lease at the boundary, fixes the next native submission's place
on the engine's direct queue; submit(), once, from any thread, executes the
native lists and signal and then the engine work held behind them.

A queue wait on a fence the native batch signals later cannot hold that
place, because the queue runs in order and the wait would come first. The
order is kept on the CPU instead:

- While a reservation is active, each engine submission (its closed list
  and fence value) is kept in order instead of reaching the queue; the
  engine's bookkeeping runs as if it had been submitted.
- The engine records into one command list per allocator, so a held list
  is never reset before it reaches the queue.
- A wait on a held fence value blocks until submit() runs, a present waits
  for the hold to end, and the native lease reports busy meanwhile.
- submit() without a batch abandons the reservation the same way; an
  invalid batch is refused and releases it too.

submit_info is rsx_native_d3d12_submit (lists, signal fence and value).
Off unless PS3RECOMP_RSX_NATIVE_OWNER=1 with the engine on. Fixture under
the debug layer: 129/129 headless and 134/134 with a real swap chain,
including a native clear recorded before, and submitted after, a held
engine clear on another thread.

ed2c306d7f65ba76c1a91ba7c6156bb8c77a3dfa.message:
docs: design note for encoding backend commands on a second RSX thread

The FIFO thread both walks the command stream and encodes every draw into
the host API, and it limits MAG's frame rate on Linux (97% busy) and the
Mac (91%). This note proposes splitting at the backend vtable:
- The walker keeps everything guest-visible: FIFO order, labels, reports,
  early release, holes and parks, and the engine's copy-at-record.
- An encoder thread owns the backend, fed by an SPSC ring of operations.
- Created objects get proxy handles, and tickets get proxy tickets.
- Readbacks and checked flushes drain the ring.
- Order, labels, inputs and outputs follow explicit rules.
- It covers backpressure, the per-backend approach (Metal commit handover
  first), a default-off switch, tests and what it does not buy.

Proposal only; nothing is implemented.

ee27c337720575d09535908a5b796590ea326799.message:
fix(spu): order the PPU line epoch against the store it counts

The default coherence scheme's line epoch is a PPU store-conditional's ABA
check: a shard-path store writes its data and then advances the epoch, and a
load-reserve reads the epoch and then the data. Both were relaxed, so a
load-reserve could see the store's new epoch with its old data and commit
over that store. test_spu_coherency's shard race caught it on Apple arm64,
failing 15 of 30 runs at -O1 (the known 1-in-9 flake of
test_spu_context_registries). The epoch is now advanced with release and read
with acquire: 0 of 30. x86 code is unchanged (TSO). In the lifted runtime the
store-conditional's value compare hid it unless the store hit another word of
the line.

A plain cellFsOpen (and sys_fs_open) of an NPD container decrypted it into
<file>.dec beside the source and served that. That is right for an EDAT,
which hardware returns as plaintext once the title has primed its key, but
not for SDATA: only cellFsSdataOpen decrypts SDATA, and a plain open returns
the container's own bytes, the ones cellFsStat sizes. MAG's launcher copies
game.psarc.sdat into game data that way. It read stat-size bytes, got the
shorter plaintext, failed on the final short read, and left a truncated
4 MiB copy that the engine then preferred, with fios archive errors. Every
host is affected; it showed up on a fresh Windows game-data install.

  EDAT resolves as before. cellFsSdataOpen still decrypts through
  edat_resolve.

  the read-only disc tree. It goes to $PS3RECOMP_EDAT_CACHE, by default a
  ps3recomp-edat directory under the host temp directory, keyed by the
  source path.
- cellFsWrite (ppu_fs) now flushes after fwrite, as sys_fs_write and
  cellFs.c already do. Its bytes reached the OS only when stdio flushed, so
  a killed run left a system-cache index with a zero header, and fios then
  revalidated it one 512-byte open/read/close at a time (about 4,000
  reopens of cache.idx, minutes on Windows).

f199b04db9f2296db839db5c851fe875e0256cad.message:
feat(video): opt-in Vulkan present that does not wait for a reserved order

With a reserved queue order (a native batch reserved ahead of original work),
a direct present had to wait for the reservation to end: its swapchain
present waits on a semaphore that a held submission signals, so it cannot
reach the queue first. The present runs on the host frame clock, the thread
that also drains the FIFO, so every such wait also held back the RSX labels
the guest polls. Measured on Linux with PS3RECOMP_VK_PRESENT_TIMING=1, in game
almost all of a present's ~6 ms was this wait.

PS3RECOMP_VK_DEFER_HELD_PRESENT=1 (default off) splits a present made while a
reservation is held:
- the capture (the flipped surface blitted into the offscreen target) is
  recorded and submitted at once; it queues behind the held work, so it still
  captures exactly the flipped frame, after the native batch;
- the show (acquire, blit into the swapchain image, present) is left pending
  and made by rsx_vulkan_backend_pump_messages, on the same host thread, once
  no reservation is held. It has its own ring of command buffers, fences and
  acquire semaphores, and its fences count as present fences for the native
  boundary and for image destruction.
At most one show is pending: a later capture, or an ordinary present, takes
its place and the older frame is counted as superseded. "[RSX vulkan]
deferred held present" reports deferred, served, superseded and failed
shows. Off, the present path is unchanged and the pump returns at once.

The Vulkan owner fixture gains two runs with the option (per-operation and
batched engine) next to the three without it. A present during a 150 ms
reservation returns at once with its capture held behind the reservation;
with the option, the pump leaves the show pending while the hold lasts, a
second present supersedes the first, and the show is made after the native
submit; the offscreen target then holds the native batch's green, so the
capture ran after it. Without the option the deferred state is never touched.

f233db9ef366897298e9a69820e56d9ffdb48607.message:
perf(video): opt-in Metal encode thread for the recorded draws (#73)

* perf(video): opt-in Metal encode thread for the recorded draws

PS3RECOMP_RSX_ENCODE_THREAD=1 (default off, read at engine init) moves the
Metal backend's record replay -- encoding the recorded draws, clears, copies
and resolves into a command buffer, and committing it -- off the FIFO walker
onto a thread of its own.

At every point the walker would have encoded and committed, it makes the
command buffer, enqueues it (fixing its place on the queue, so every later
command buffer from any thread runs after it), tracks it, takes its
completion ticket and hands the staging arena over, then passes the buffer
and the record array to the encode thread and records on into another array.
A present, a wait or a readback then runs on the walker as before with
nothing left to encode. Labels, reports and tickets stay on the walker.

A released texture or pipeline keeps its slot until the encode thread has
finished the last batch that can name it; a walker wait on a handed-over
command buffer first waits for the encode thread to commit it. Waiting for
the encode thread is charged to an encode_wait PS3RECOMP_RSX_FIFO_BUSY
category; PS3RECOMP_RSX_INFLIGHT_LOG=1 prints its jobs, records and waits.
The encoder state filter is per thread. Draw and present diagnostics keep
the single-thread path.

tools/test_metal_encode_thread.py drives the real engine through the Metal
backend headless: 64 colour cells with a clear part-way, tickets every four
draws and after every draw, and vertex bytes rewritten after each draw, read
back byte-identical with and without the thread; plus the slot rules for
released targets and pipelines. It needs glslang and spirv-cross (skips
without them). test_metal_first_nonblack links the render-ablation hook the
encode path now keeps reachable.

f5ea3c631c4d60c0fbf65dac61cda41ec29dbfb6.message:
perf(spu): opt-in async SPU task thread pool on Windows, with per-task thread hygiene (#47)

PS3RECOMP_SPU_TASK_POOL=1 reused host threads for async SPU tasks only on
POSIX; Windows still created a thread per task (about 300 a second in MAG),
each with a 256 MB reservation, a stack guarantee, cold TLS and decode caches,
and an exit-time registration scrub.

The pool moves to runtime/spu/spu_task_pool.inc and serves both platforms
with the same rules: a task is handed to a pool thread only when one is idle
and waiting for it, otherwise a new thread is created, so every task still
starts at once on a thread of its own; idle threads exit after 2 s. Windows
pool threads keep the 256 MB reservation and the 256 KB stack guarantee.
spu_workload_async_pool_shutdown() stops reuse and waits for idle threads.

A reused thread must give the next task what a fresh thread gave it:
- Lock-line reservers and MFC engines are keyed by spu_context address, and
  job contexts are stack locals. One that leaks past its unregister was
  dropped only at thread exit (Windows) or never (POSIX). On a reused thread
  the next task's context lands at the same address and inherits the leaked
  MFC engine, and a PPU store writes into its frames through the stale
  reserver. The stack-range scrub now runs after every task, pooled or not,
  on both platforms; on POSIX the range comes from pthread_getattr_np or
  pthread_get_stackaddr_np.

ffa271dca6ab19c9afa86b341141675c048a88ec.message:
perf(spu): opt-in per-thread heap storage for the SPU decode cache

PS3RECOMP_SPU_DECODE_CACHE_HEAP (CMake option, default OFF) moves the SPU
interpreter's 2 MiB decode table out of static TLS. Off, the source compiles
exactly as before.

The table was 2 MiB of the process's 2.13 MiB static TLS block, and glibc
clears the whole block for every new host thread in the thread that creates
it. Every SPURS task runs on a new host thread, so on Linux the game's main
PPU thread spent about 8% of its CPU in cellSpursCreateTaskWithAttribute ->
pthread_create, mostly a 2 MiB memset in _dl_allocate_tls_init, before the
page faults behind it. Every other host thread (render workers, audio) paid
the same at startup.

With the option, a thread allocates its table with calloc on its first
interpreted instruction and frees it at thread exit through a pthread key
(an FLS slot on Windows). The storage is still owned by the thread and
nothing is retained after it exits, which is why the table was in TLS. A
thread that never interprets pays nothing. If the allocation fails the thread
decodes without the cache, the same path as SPU_INTERP_DECODE_CACHE=0. The
table is still revalidated on every instruction, so its contents and the
decoded results are unchanged.

A thread pool for SPURS task threads was considered first. It would remove
pthread_create entirely, but a reused thread carries the previous task's
thread-local state (about sixty TLS variables across the SPU runtime, the
lifted-job exit buffers, the original-work observer's per-thread worker
registration and the stack-range cleanup at thread exit), so changing thread
identity is the larger and riskier change.

tools/test_spu_interpreter_handoff.py now builds and runs every mode with
both storages, checks on ELF hosts that the heap variant leaves spu_interp.o
with under 1 MiB of static TLS, and links the job I/O recorder that the
fixture's sources started to need.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   └── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse
│   ├── hardware/             # cellGem, cellCamera, cellUsbd
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
└── docs/                     # See the Documentation table below
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

HLE implementations of the PS3 system libraries, written for this project. RPCS3 is a behavioural reference, not a code source. Most modules are complete. The ones still marked Partial are the media decoders (cellVdec, cellAdec, cellDmux, cellAtrac, cellAdecAtrac3p) and cellSpurs. [docs/MODULE_STATUS.md](docs/MODULE_STATUS.md) has one row per module and is the source for the counts.

| **Kernel Events** | sys_event (queues, ports, flags), sys_timer | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Memory** | sys_memory, sys_mmapper (containers, shared mem) | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Filesystem** | sys_fs (path mapping, real I/O) | ✅ Complete |
| **Filesystem** | cellFs (real file I/O, dir ops, stat, path translation) | ✅ Complete |
| **Save System** | cellSaveData (callback-driven, PARAM.SFO), cellGame | ✅ Complete |
| **Input** | cellPad (XInput/SDL2), cellKb, cellMouse | ✅ Complete |
| **Audio** | cellAudio (WASAPI/SDL2, mixing thread, multi-port) | ✅ Complete |
| **Video Output** | cellVideoOut (resolution config, 720p default) | ✅ Complete |
| **Codecs** | cellPngDec, cellJpgDec, cellGifDec (stb_image) | ✅ Complete |
| **Font** | cellFont (stb_truetype backend + fallback metrics) | ✅ Complete |
| **Network** | sys_net (BSD sockets, P2P), cellNet, cellNetCtl, cellHttpUtil, cellSsl, sceNp*, sceNpTrophy, sceNpMatching2 + Score over [psnr](docs/ONLINE.md) | ✅ Complete |
| **Hardware** | cellUsbd (USB), cellCamera (PS Eye), cellGem (PS Move) — stub, no devices | ✅ Complete |
| **Sync** | cellSync (atomic spinlocks, LF queue), cellSync2 (OS-backed) | ✅ Complete |

| **Fibers** | cellFiber (PPU fiber scheduler via Windows Fibers/ucontext) | ✅ Complete |

# Awesome REA

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Open-source reverse-engineering projects, reimplementations and compatible alternatives, plus [REA](https://github.com/morluto/rea) tools and resources. **REA usage is not required.**

[Website](https://awesomerea.com) · [Suggest a project](https://github.com/kaixinbaba/awesome-rea/issues/new?template=1-project.yml) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

An independent, unofficial directory. Sources reviewed, software not independently tested. See the [website](https://awesomerea.com/#directory) for evidence, licenses and limitations.

## Directory

<!-- catalog:start -->
<!-- Generated from src/projects.json and src/locales by npm run readme. -->

183 projects & resources · 6 categories

### Developer & security tools

- [OpenBSD netcat study](<https://github.com/NullLabTests/OpenBSD_netcat_REA>) — Static REA and Ghidra analysis of an OpenBSD netcat binary.
- [REA — Reverse Engineer Anything](<https://github.com/morluto/rea>) — Upstream CLI and MCP toolkit for agent-assisted software analysis.
- [AFL++](<https://github.com/AFLplusplus/AFLplusplus>) — State-of-the-art coverage-guided fuzzer grown from AFL, with custom mutators, power schedules and optional QEMU/Unicorn modes.
- [flashrom](<https://github.com/flashrom/flashrom>) — Utility to identify, read, write, verify and erase firmware flash chips, with many programmers and chipsets supported.
- [Impacket](<https://github.com/fortra/impacket>) — Python classes for working with network protocols (SMB, MSRPC, Kerberos and related stacks), plus example packet tools.
- [OpenOCD](<https://github.com/openocd-org/openocd>) — Open On-Chip Debugger: debug, in-system programming and boundary-scan for embedded targets via JTAG/SWD adapters.
- [pefile](<https://github.com/erocarrera/pefile>) — Pure-Python module to parse and work with PE files: headers, sections, imports/exports and related Windows binary structures.
- [REHex](<https://github.com/solemnwarning/rehex>) — Cross-platform hex editor for reverse engineers: inspect and annotate binary data, with comments, types and file comparison.
- [YARA-X](<https://github.com/VirusTotal/yara-x>) — VirusTotal’s Rust rewrite of YARA: compile and match YARA-style rules against files and memory, separate from the original C engine.
- [Volatility 3](<https://github.com/volatilityfoundation/volatility3>) — Framework for extracting digital artifacts from volatile memory (RAM) samples, independent of the system under investigation.
- [Keystone](<https://github.com/keystone-engine/keystone>) — Lightweight multi-architecture assembler framework: turn instruction text into machine code through a common API.
- [iaito](<https://github.com/radareorg/iaito>) — Official Qt GUI for the radare2 reverse-engineering framework, aiming for simplicity and command/feature/keybinding parity.
- [edb-debugger](<https://github.com/eteran/edb-debugger>) — Qt graphical debugger for AArch32, x86 and x86-64, inspired by OllyDbg; Linux is the only officially supported platform for now.
- [Project IceStorm](<https://github.com/YosysHQ/icestorm>) — Documents the Lattice iCE40 FPGA configuration bitstream format and supplies simple tools for analysing and creating bitstreams.
- [Remill](<https://github.com/lifting-bits/remill>) — Static binary-translation library that lifts AArch64, SPARC, x86 and amd64 machine code into LLVM bitcode.
- [Microsoft Detours](<https://github.com/microsoft/Detours>) — Library for monitoring and instrumenting Windows API calls by intercepting functions; distributed in source form; not for Store apps.

### Games & game engines

- [OpenBattlefield2](<https://github.com/Moxnatiy/OpenBattlefield2>) — Incomplete Refractor 2 reimplementation with REA investigation tooling; original game required.
- [GunZRs](<https://github.com/OpenRsG/GunZRs>) — Rust game port with a separate REA investigation framework; original assets required.
- [OpenRCT2](<https://github.com/OpenRCT2/OpenRCT2>) — RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 engine reimplementation; original game files required.
- [OpenMW](<https://github.com/OpenMW/openmw>) — Morrowind engine and editor reimplementation; original game data required, mod compatibility varies.
- [OpenTTD](<https://github.com/OpenTTD/OpenTTD>) — Transport Tycoon Deluxe-style simulation with optional free graphics, sound and music.
- [ScummVM](<https://github.com/scummvm/scummvm>) — Replacement engines for supported classic adventures and RPGs; original game data usually required.
- [free-heroes4 (openh4)](<https://github.com/tallowmere/free-heroes4>) — Unfinished Heroes of Might and Magic IV engine and inspection tools; original GOG game data required.
- [Rook](<https://github.com/AsyncFinn/rook>) — Early Rust Roblox-engine reimplementation for local places and Luau scripts; not a Roblox server client.

1415140214.readme_excerpt: # Disgaea D2 WINPORT — Windows / DirectX 12 ## Versão pública oficial do projeto — 0.2.4 Stable Baixe o **instalador** ou o **ZIP portátil** em [Releases](https://github.com/LUUKASR1/disgaea-d2-recomp-windows/releases/latest). **Comandos:** abra **Controles** ou **Guia de comandos** no início para consultar o teclado. O guia acompanha o idioma do launcher e usa títulos com contorno e cores inspiradas no jogo. Seleção direta pelo mouse dentro do jogo ainda não está disponível. **Atualizações:** o launcher verifica novas versões estáveis ao abrir. Em **Arquivos e suporte**, você pode verificar manualmente ou desligar a consulta automática. O botão de download abre a release no GitHub; feche o jogo e o launcher antes de instalar. **Saves:** use **Meus saves — abrir pasta** na tela inicial ou **Arquivos e suporte → Abrir pasta de saves**. **Como usar meu save** mostra o destino e as instruções; feche o jogo e faça backup antes de copiar. Idioma do launcher: **Português (Brasil) / English**, com seleção abaixo de WIN PORT. Selecione sua própria **ISO USA compatível** e o PKG da atualização **BLUS31313 US 1.40**; DLCs são opcionais. A primeira preparação baixa ferramentas portáteis e compila o jogo automaticamente no seu computador. Precisa de internet e pode demorar. Não requer instalar ferramentas manualmente nem importar firmware. **DirectX 12**, configurações de resolução interna/saída, janela/tela cheia sem bordas, VSync, Hz e FSR 1 espacial. Vulkan, DLSS, Frame Generation e Android ainda não estão disponíveis. HUD após upscaling permanece experimental e desligado por padrão. [Instalação, saves, requisitos e limitações / Installation, saves, requirements and limitations](docs/RELEASE-0.2.4.md) · [Reportar erro / Report a bug](https://github.com/LUUKASR1/disgaea-d2-recomp-windows/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml) A versão oficial reutiliza `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DisgaeaD2Recomp-Graphics-Preview` por compatibilidade com a linha testada. Não apague essa pasta. Outros perfis são preservados, sem migração universal automática. **Save do PS3:** [guia de importação experimental — PT-BR / English](docs/SAVES-PS3.md). A compatibilidade com saves reais do console ainda não foi validada. ## Official project release — 0.2.4 Stable **Controls:** open **Controls** or **Command guide** on Home to view the keyboard mapping. The guide follows the launcher language, with outlined headings and game-inspired colors. Direct pointer selection inside the game is not available yet. **Updates:** the launcher checks for newer stable releases at startup. Under **Files and support**, check manually or disable automatic checks. The download button opens the GitHub release; close the game and launcher before installing. **Saves:** use **My saves — open folder** on Home or **Files and support → Open save folder**. **How to use my save** shows the destination and instructions; close the game and back up before copying. Launcher languages: **Português (Brasil) / English**, selected below WIN PORT. 1415334132.description: Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
1415334132.readme_excerpt:
# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

Every row is exercised by CI on every push, and **all three are green on
`master`** — the PPU boot scaffold ratchet that had been red since before v0.11.0
([#139](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/issues/139)) is at zero on all
four toolchains. The rows below describe what those jobs actually do, not what a
green tick would imply: building the runtime and passing the suites is not the
same as running a game, and only one row claims that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter + 8 test suites | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | null (headless software); Vulkan (opt-in) |
| Runs a recompiled game | **yes** | **no** | no |

The gap on macOS is the PPU boot scaffold — `ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp`
and the HLE dispatch are still Win32-only (thread creation, VirtualAlloc, SEH,
stack walking), and they are compiled per-game rather than into the library.
So macOS builds the runtime, renders through Metal and passes the full test
suite, but cannot yet load and run a title. `ps3recomp_host` drives
cellGcm → RSX → Metal end to end without a game, which is what makes further
graphics work possible there.

Linux builds and passes the same suites under both GCC and Clang, and runs
`ps3recomp_host` end to end, on every push. Its backend is the null backend's
headless software path: a host-memory framebuffer with a CPU triangle filler,
enough to prove the guest's command stream produced the pixels it asked for on
a runner with no display and no GPU. It is not a renderer — no depth, no
blending, no textures — so Linux is still one real backend, plus the same PPU
boot scaffold macOS needs, away from running a title.

### What each platform needs next

Both non-Windows platforms are blocked on the *same* two things, in this order.

**1. The PPU boot scaffold, on POSIX.** This is the shared blocker and the only
one that gates "runs a recompiled game" on both. `ppu_loader.cpp`,
`boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled *per game* rather than into
the library, and were Win32-only — thread creation, `VirtualAlloc`, SEH, stack
walking. v0.10.0 took it to zero errors on POSIX and put it under CI so it
cannot rot again, and ported the guest-pointer trap, thread-locals and host
backtraces. What is left is running it: load a lifted image on POSIX and reach
the guest's first instruction, then `main`. Until that works, neither platform
can run a title no matter how good its renderer is.

**2. One real backend each.** The RSX abstraction landed in v0.10.0 (#101, #102,
#103) — texture conversion, the `TEXTURE_CONTROL1` crossbar, texture layout and
a neutral draw record all live outside the D3D12 file now, so a backend no
longer has to reimplement them to draw anything.

- **macOS** has the furthest to go that is *interesting* rather than
  mechanical: [@slushiimusic](https://github.com/slushiimusic)'s Metal backend
  (#96) does clear, flip, guest vertex fetch, a pipeline-state cache and blend
  translation. Reaching D3D12 parity means the guest's own fragment programs
  through the decompiler, then textures. `ps3recomp_host` already drives
  cellGcm → RSX → Metal with no lifted game, so each step is testable before a
  title exists to run.
- **Linux** has an opt-in Vulkan backend (`-DPS3RECOMP_RSX_VULKAN=ON`). With
  guest programs on (glslang at build time, `PS3RECOMP_VK_GUEST_PROGRAMS=1`) it
  runs on the shared register-file draw engine, the path Metal takes, and every
  `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on it -- including render-to-texture, MRT and
  depth textures; without them it draws the null backend's fixed-function
  contract. It has not run a recompiled title yet. The default is still the
  headless backend, a CPU triangle filler for CI, deliberately.

**Deliberately not claimed:** the table above says "no" for running a game on
macOS and Linux, and it will keep saying "no" until a title actually boots to
gameplay on one of them. Building the runtime, passing the suites and rendering
through `ps3recomp_host` are all real, and none of them is that.

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Auto-generate HLE stubs from RPCS3 modules
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   ├── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   │   └── atomic.h          # PS3 atomic operations (lwarx/stwcx)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       ├── sys_prx.h         # PRX module loading
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations (from RPCS3's module system)
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse, cellGem
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
├── patches/                  # Patches for upstream tools
│   └── xenonrecomp-ppu.patch # XenonRecomp adaptations for PPU (Cell != Xenon)
│
└── docs/                     # Documentation (incl. ARCHITECTURE, RUNTIME, SPU_LIFTER, RSX_GRAPHICS, ...)
    ├── ARCHITECTURE.md        # Cell processor and recomp pipeline deep-dive
    ├── GETTING_STARTED.md     # How to recompile your first PS3 game
    ├── MODULE_STATUS.md       # Implementation status of all HLE modules
    ├── MODULES_REFERENCE.md   # Detailed per-module documentation
    ├── RUNTIME.md             # Runtime reference: VM, PPU/SPU contexts, types
    ├── SYSCALLS.md            # All LV2 kernel syscall implementations
    ├── NID_SYSTEM.md          # PS3 NID linking system explained
    ├── TOOLS.md               # Recompiler pipeline tools reference
    ├── BUILDING.md            # Build system, compilers, platform notes
    ├── GAME_PORTING_GUIDE.md  # Step-by-step game porting walkthrough
    └── PLATFORM_ABSTRACTION.md # Win32/POSIX cross-platform details
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

We're building HLE implementations based on RPCS3's module system. **97 modules complete, 1 partial (media decode)** — 219 files and ~76,000 lines under `libs/`.

| Category | Modules | Status |
|----------|---------|--------|
| **Kernel Threading** | sys_ppu_thread, sys_mutex, sys_cond, sys_semaphore, sys_rwlock | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Events** | sys_event (queues, ports, flags), sys_timer | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Memory** | sys_memory, sys_mmapper (containers, shared mem) | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Filesystem** | sys_fs (path mapping, real I/O) | ✅ Complete |
| **Filesystem** | cellFs (real file I/O, dir ops, stat, path translation) | ✅ Complete |
| **Save System** | cellSaveData (callback-driven, PARAM.SFO), cellGame | ✅ Complete |
| **Input** | cellPad (XInput/SDL2), cellKb, cellMouse | ✅ Complete |
| **Audio** | cellAudio (WASAPI/SDL2, mixing thread, multi-port) | ✅ Complete |
| **Video Output** | cellVideoOut (resolution config, 720p default) | ✅ Complete |
| **Codecs** | cellPngDec, cellJpgDec, cellGifDec (stb_image) | ✅ Complete |
| **Font** | cellFont (stb_truetype backend + fallback metrics) | ✅ Complete |
| **Network** | sys_net (BSD sockets, P2P), cellNet, cellNetCtl, cellHttpUtil, cellSsl, sceNp*, sceNpTrophy, sceNpMatching2 + Score over [psnr](docs/ONLINE.md) | ✅ Complete |
| **Hardware** | cellUsbd (USB), cellCamera (PS Eye), cellGem (PS Move) — stub, no devices | ✅ Complete |
| **Sync** | cellSync (atomic spinlocks, LF queue), cellSync2 (OS-backed) | ✅ Complete |
| **System** | cellRtc, cellMsgDialog, cellOskDialog, cellUserInfo, cellGameExec | ✅ Complete |
| **Localization** | cellL10n (UTF-8/16/32/UCS-2, ISO-8859-1, generic converter) | ✅ Complete |
| **Resolution** | cellResc (display modes, scaling, interlace, aspect ratio) | ✅ Complete |
| **Fibers** | cellFiber (PPU fibers via Windows Fibers/ucontext
