# God of War II HD for Windows (PS3 static recompilation)

A native Windows x64 build of **God of War II HD** (PlayStation 3, **NPUA80491 v01.00**, the US PSN release),
made by *static recompilation*: the game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code is translated ahead of time into C/C++ and
compiled with clang for x86-64. It runs on a re-implementation of the PS3 system libraries with a Direct3D 12
renderer, WASAPI audio and XInput/keyboard input. It is not an emulator: there is no interpreter or JIT for the
game's main code.

**This repository contains no game code or data.** You bring your own legally obtained copy of the game and your
licence file; the build decrypts, translates and compiles everything **on your PC**, and nothing built from your copy
leaves it.

It is the Windows continuation of [gow2-recomp](https://github.com/andrebrumdev/gow2-recomp) (macOS / Apple
Silicon, by andrebrumdev) on the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) engine (by sp00nznet).

## Features

* High frame rates: an own frame limiter (30 to 1000 fps, default 300), with **162 fps** as the G-Sync / FreeSync
  cap for 165 Hz displays, and even frame pacing when the game runs below the cap.
* **Resolution scale** 1x to 4x (default 2x = 2560x1440), borderless or windowed (**F11** switches), 16:9.
* **Port Settings** (**F1**, or L3 outside gameplay): frame-rate cap, display mode, resolution scale, fps counter and
  checkpoints, drawn in the game's own menu style. Saved in `port_settings.ini` next to the game exe.
* **F10** fps counter.
* **Checkpoints**: **F6** saves the game's latest checkpoint with a picture; **F1 > Load Checkpoint** lists them and
  loads one in game.
* The game's **Full Frame** option (game Options) works, prerendered movies included.
* All 45 prerendered movies at full length with picture/sound sync; in a movie SELECT pauses picture and sound,
  holding START skips.
* XInput controllers and the keyboard; input only while the window has focus. Game saves work.

## Requirements

* **Windows 10 or 11, x64**, a CPU with **AVX2** (x86-64-v3: Intel Haswell / AMD Excavator or newer) and a
  **Direct3D 12** GPU.
* **Disk:** about **7.5 GB** when built from an installed game folder (install folder 5.8 GB: movie cache 4.7 GB,
  build intermediates 0.8 GB; 0.95 GB of tools; 0.27 GB of downloads while they are unpacked), about **14 GB** when
  built from the PSN package (its 6.5 GB of game files are extracted into the install folder and stay there, because
  the game reads them while it runs).
* **Your game**, God of War II HD **NPUA80491 v01.00**, either
  * the game folder (with `PARAM.SFO`, `USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` and `USRDIR/gow2.psarc`), e.g. RPCS3's
    `dev_hdd0/game/NPUA80491` or a dump from your PS3, **or**
  * the PSN package `UP9000-NPUA80491_00-GODOFWARIIHDUS00.pkg` (any file name; the full game, about 7 GB, not an
    update),
* and **your licence** `UP9000-NPUA80491_00-GODOFWARIIHDUS00.rap` (RPCS3: `dev_hdd0/home/<user>/exdata`), or an
  `EBOOT.ELF` you decrypted yourself.
* An internet connection for the first build (about 270 MB of tools). No Visual Studio, MSYS2, CMake or admin rights.

## Quick start: Gow2HD-Windows.exe

1. Download **Gow2HD-Windows.exe** from the [releases](https://github.com/sethlikepie/Gow2HD-Windows/releases) (or
   install it from [Quiver](https://quiverlauncher.com)) and run it. It is not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen
   asks once: **More info → Run anyway**.
2. **Game:** the launcher looks for your game folder or `.pkg` (RPCS3 folders, Downloads, Desktop, Documents, next
   to the exe). If it does not find it, press **FOLDER** (installed game folder) or **.PKG** (PSN package), or drop
   the folder or file on the window.
3. **Licence:** it looks for the `.rap` the same way; otherwise pick it or drop it on the window.
4. Press **BUILD**. The launcher downloads pinned, SHA-256-checked tools (an embeddable Python, llvm-mingw, FFmpeg),
   runs `build.py` from the sources bundled in the exe and then starts the game. The first build takes about
   **10 minutes** on a 16-thread desktop (about one more minute to unpack a `.pkg`). After that, **PLAY** starts the
   game.

Everything goes to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\GoW2-Windows` (changeable). **REMOVE BUILD** in the launcher deletes the build and
the tools again; your saves, checkpoints and settings stay. Command-line options (`--play`,
`--silent-build --game <dir>|--pkg <file> --rap <file> --out <dir>`, `--remove-build`, `--check-update`, ...):
[launcher/NOTES.md](launcher/NOTES.md).

## Play

The game starts borderless at 2x resolution with a 300 fps cap. No arguments or environment variables are needed;
`gow2hd.exe` in the install folder can also be started directly.

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| **F1** (L3 outside gameplay) | Port Settings: frame-rate cap (30 / 60 / 120 / 144 / **162** / 165 / 240 / 300 / 1000), display mode, resolution scale, fps counter, checkpoints |
| **F6** | Save Checkpoint |
| **F10** | fps counter on / off |
| **F11** | borderless / windowed |
| SELECT / hold START in a movie | pause / skip (prerendered movies) |

Keyboard as a pad: Enter = Start, Tab = Select, Space = X, E = Circle, J = Square, K = Triangle, WASD = left stick,
arrows = right stick, LShift = L1, Q = R1, LCtrl = L2, R = R2, F = L3, G = R3. Controllers: XInput (Xbox, or
PlayStation pads through Steam Input / DS4Windows).

**Checkpoints:** F6 (or F1 > *Save Checkpoint*) saves the game's latest checkpoint, with a picture of where it was
taken, to `checkpoints\` next to the game exe. F1 > *Load Checkpoint* lists them (newest first): X loads one in game
(during gameplay or the pause menu, any level), Square/Delete moves it to `checkpoints\deleted\`, O goes back. A
checkpoint is the game's own (the last one it passed), not the exact spot where you pressed F6. Checkpoints are
separate from the game's save slots, and REMOVE BUILD keeps them.

**Saves** live in `%APPDATA%\ps3recomp\dev_hdd0\home\00000001\savedata`. The log of the last run is `gow2.log` next
to the game exe (the previous one is `gow2.prev.log`).

## Known issues

* Only **NPUA80491 v01.00** (US PSN) is supported; other regions or versions fail the hash checks.
* An **AVX2** CPU is required (the game exe is built for x86-64-v3).
* `Gow2HD-Windows.exe` is **not code-signed**: SmartScreen warns on the first start, and some antivirus tools distrust a
  new unsigned exe that downloads and runs a compiler.
* The **indexed-draw optimisation** of the renderer is **off** by default: with it on, a QTE (button-prompt) sequence
  can go out of sync with its animation. Combat is somewhat slower without it.
* **Start-up hang recovery:** on some launches Windows stops handing back a swap-chain buffer during the boot logos;
  a watchdog hides and shows the window for a moment (~0.6 s, `[PWD82]` in the log) and the game continues.
* The **WARNING screen** lasts about 30 s (slow level loading through many small reads). **Real-time cutscenes**
  cannot be skipped (prerendered movies can).
* Music: one long session reported the music stopping in a later scene (Colossus) while other sounds kept playing.
  v0.1.0 fixes a runtime lock bug that silenced a music stream in exactly this way in the sister God of War port; if
  it still happens, please report it with the log.
* **Full Frame:** menus, gameplay and prerendered movies are tested with it on; real-time cutscenes in Full Frame
  are not yet.
* **Checkpoints:** tested in the Rhodes levels (other areas show raw level names in the list); loading during a death
  screen, a QTE or a boss fight is untested.
* The **display-mode** toggle in Port Settings has had less testing than the other options.
* The launcher's first-time setup needs mouse and keyboard (file pickers); no gamepad navigation there yet (Quiver
  kiosk users: finish the setup once on the desktop).
* Removing the app in Quiver does not delete the ~7 GB build in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\GoW2-Windows`: use **REMOVE BUILD**
  in the launcher first.
* Harmless upstream oddities: ~40 `[vm] OOB` lines in the log during save I/O; the Colossus bone corruption and some
  placeholder normals are repaired in the renderer.

## Reporting bugs

Open an [issue](https://github.com/sethlikepie/Gow2HD-Windows/issues) with:

* what you did and what happened (a screenshot helps for graphics bugs);
* **`gow2.log`** from the install folder (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\GoW2-Windows` unless you changed it; the run before is
  `gow2.prev.log`);
* for build or launcher problems, **`build.log`** from the same folder (**SHOW LOG** in the launcher opens it);
* your CPU, GPU, Windows version, and whether you built from the game folder or the `.pkg`.

The logs contain file paths of your PC (for example your Windows user name); edit them out if you prefer. Never
attach game files, your `.rap` or anything else from the install folder.

## Build from source (without the launcher)

```
python tools\fetch_tools.py C:\gow2\tools
python build.py --game "D:\RPCS3\dev_hdd0\game\NPUA80491" --rap "D:\UP9000-NPUA80491_00-GODOFWARIIHDUS00.rap" ^
                --tools C:\gow2\tools --out C:\gow2\game
rem or from the PSN package:
python build.py --pkg "D:\Downloads\UP9000-NPUA80491_00-GODOFWARIIHDUS00.pkg" --rap "D:\UP9000-NPUA80491_00-GODOFWARIIHDUS00.rap" ^
                --tools C:\gow2\tools --out C:\gow2\game
```

Python 3.11+ is enough (the Windows *embeddable* CPython zip works; no packages needed). `python build.py
--print-tools` lists the pinned tools (llvm-mingw 20260922 and an FFmpeg LGPL build).

With `--pkg`, `build.py` first checks the package (PS3 package, content id, complete download, the full game v01.00
rather than an update) and extracts `PARAM.SFO`, `ICON0.PNG` and `USRDIR\*` into `<out>\game\NPUA80491`, which is
then the game folder. The extractor (`winport/buildlib/pkg.py`, the package format as RPCS3 and pkg2zip read it) uses
Windows' own AES (CNG), streams, can resume, and checks `EBOOT.BIN` and `gow2.psarc` against the same SHA-256 pins.

`build.py` checks the game files (sizes and SHA-256 of `EBOOT.BIN` and `gow2.psarc`), decrypts `EBOOT.BIN` with your
licence (a Python port of the kit's `tools/unself`, with Windows' AES), runs the kit's pinned PPU lifter, patch
scripts and kit delta and the seven SPU lifts (each checked against the hashes in `gow2-recomp/kit/`), applies the
port's changes to the lifted code (`winport/lift_patches/`), lifts the SCREAM audio mixer jobs (`winport/scream/`),
extracts the movie cache from `gow2.psarc`, compiles the engine runtime and the game, and installs everything into
`--out`. Running it again skips the finished steps (about 2 s when nothing changed). It prints
`PROGRESS <0-100> <message>` lines and, on failure, one `ERROR <message>` line (details in `<out>\.build\build.log`).
Options: `--elf <EBOOT.ELF>` instead of `--rap`, `--jobs N`.

Every behaviour switch of the port is an environment variable with a built-in default (`winport/host/wp_release.c`
lists the defaults); setting one overrides it, which is how the diagnostic modes (frame capture, profiler, test
scripts) are turned on.

## Repository layout

* `ps3recomp/`: the engine (upstream snapshot + Windows changes: pad, audio, movies, saves, perf, GCM).
* `gow2-recomp/`: the upstream game kit: function bounds, lift patch scripts, SPU glue, kit hashes.
* `winport/`: the Windows port: `d3d12/` renderer, `host/` (start-up defaults, Windows helpers), `scream/` (native
  SCREAM mixer), `lift_patches/` (changes to the generated lift), `buildlib/` (build steps), `spu_simd/`.
* `build.py`: the one build entry point. `tools/`: `fetch_tools.py`, `check_no_game_data.py` (pre-commit guard).
* `launcher/`: `Gow2HD-Windows.exe` (C++ Win32, no dependencies): setup wizard, verified downloads, runs `build.py`,
  starts the game. `launcher\build.cmd` bundles the build sources into it; see `launcher/NOTES.md`.
* [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each release.

# MotorStorm Monument Valley native recompilation tooling

Work in progress: Windows runner, translation tools, a modified [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) runtime and growing handwritten native x86 game operations for MotorStorm 1. A playable native race has **not** been demonstrated. This repository distributes source glue and documentation; game binaries, assets, firmware, generated guest code, keys, saves and captures stay local.

**You must supply your own legally obtained game files.** The source license covers this tooling, not the game. Setup and generation run locally; this repository provides no game downloads.

Start with [setup and build](docs/BUILDING.md), then [running and capturing](docs/OPERATIONS.md). Track atomic work in [GitHub issues](https://github.com/robbe1912/motorstorm-mv-recomp/issues). [Documentation index](docs/README.md) groups the research by topic.

[Asset extraction and reconstruction](docs/assets/README.md) records reusable texture, mesh and material contracts, with a [MotorStorm worked example](docs/assets/MOTORSTORM.md) and notes for a future Rust implementation.

See [vendor provenance and licenses](docs/VENDOR.md) and [publication audit](docs/REPOSITORY.md). Source licensing does not grant rights to the game or guarantee immunity from legal claims. No affiliation with Sony or the original developers.

1416262654.readme_excerpt:
# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

Every row is exercised by CI on every push, and **all three are green on
`master`** — the PPU boot scaffold ratchet that had been red since before v0.11.0
([#139](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/issues/139)) is at zero on all
four toolchains. The rows below describe what those jobs actually do, not what a
green tick would imply: building the runtime and passing the suites is not the
same as running a game, and only one row claims that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter + 8 test suites | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | null (headless software); Vulkan (opt-in) |
| Runs a recompiled game | **yes** | **no** | no |

The gap on macOS is the PPU boot scaffold — `ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp`
and the HLE dispatch are still Win32-only (thread creation, VirtualAlloc, SEH,
stack walking), and they are compiled per-game rather than into the library.
So macOS builds the runtime, renders through Metal and passes the full test
suite, but cannot yet load and run a title. `ps3recomp_host` drives
cellGcm → RSX → Metal end to end without a game, which is what makes further
graphics work possible there.

Linux builds and passes the same suites under both GCC and Clang, and runs
`ps3recomp_host` end to end, on every push. Its backend is the null backend's
headless software path: a host-memory framebuffer with a CPU triangle filler,
enough to prove the guest's command stream produced the pixels it asked for on
a runner with no display and no GPU. It is not a renderer — no depth, no
blending, no textures — so Linux is still one real backend, plus the same PPU
boot scaffold macOS needs, away from running a title.

### What each platform needs next

Both non-Windows platforms are blocked on the *same* two things, in this order.

**1. The PPU boot scaffold, on POSIX.** This is the shared blocker and the only
one that gates "runs a recompiled game" on both. `ppu_loader.cpp`,
`boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled *per game* rather than into
the library, and were Win32-only — thread creation, `VirtualAlloc`, SEH, stack
walking. v0.10.0 took it to zero errors on POSIX and put it under CI so it
cannot rot again, and ported the guest-pointer trap, thread-locals and host
backtraces. What is left is running it: load a lifted image on POSIX and reach
the guest's first instruction, then `main`. Until that works, neither platform
can run a title no matter how good its renderer is.

**2. One real backend each.** The RSX abstraction landed in v0.10.0 (#101, #102,
#103) — texture conversion, the `TEXTURE_CONTROL1` crossbar, texture layout and
a neutral draw record all live outside the D3D12 file now, so a backend no
longer has to reimplement them to draw anything.

- **macOS** has the furthest to go that is *interesting* rather than
  mechanical: [@slushiimusic](https://github.com/slushiimusic)'s Metal backend
  (#96) does clear, flip, guest vertex fetch, a pipeline-state cache and blend
  translation. Reaching D3D12 parity means the guest's own fragment programs
  through the decompiler, then textures. `ps3recomp_host` already drives
  cellGcm → RSX → Metal with no lifted game, so each step is testable before a
  title exists to run.
- **Linux** has an opt-in Vulkan backend (`-DPS3RECOMP_RSX_VULKAN=ON`). With
  guest programs on (glslang at build time, `PS3RECOMP_VK_GUEST_PROGRAMS=1`) it
  runs on the shared register-file draw engine, the path Metal takes, and every
  `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on it -- including render-to-texture, MRT and
  depth textures; without them it draws the null backend's fixed-function
  contract. It has not run a recompiled title yet. The default is still the
  headless backend, a CPU triangle filler for CI, deliberately.

**Deliberately not claimed:** the table above says "no" for running a game on
macOS and Linux, and it will keep saying "no" until a title actually boots to
gameplay on one of them. Building the runtime, passing the suites and rendering
through `ps3recomp_host` are all real, and none of them is that.

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

071aa55d6559c7c1793c919188ea4261e1cda1a1.message:
Shaders: first-time compiles no longer hold the frame

New shaders compiled on the threads that run the game: vertex programs on
the command-recording thread (FXC 30-170 ms each, a dozen per room) and
"urgent" pipelines -- composites and full-screen passes -- inline on the
render thread, one after another. Entering a new room froze the game for
up to a second.

- Vertex programs compile on the thread pool. The slot is published with
  its blob pending; draws that need it are left out until it lands, and
  urgent ones wait for it.
- Urgent pipelines go to the shader workers at the head of the queue, built
  in parallel at normal priority; the frame waits for all of them.
- The wait for background builds is one 4 ms budget per frame, shared by
  the prepass and the draw loop (was up to 16 ms whenever a first-time
  compile was in flight -- a stutter on every new shader). A build from the
  disk caches takes about a millisecond, so those still land in time.
- HITCHDBG=1 logs frames over 45 ms with VS compile time, inline FP builds
  and waits.

SPU job contexts from a pool; audio pacing and diagnostics

  local store included) as a ~270 KB stack local, and every SPU task runs on

  in ~2 ms instead of ~4, and its audio mixer keeps ~85-93 of the ~94 rounds

  at highest priority (SPU_SERVICE_PRIO=0 reverts); SPU_TASK_PRIO_IMG and

  together (AUDIO_ROOM_GATE=1 reverts).

treated those current points as "no proposal", so an interpolated neighbour
pulled only the shared seam points and tore the triangles: dark spikes at
Steve's mouth and a cut through his hair (JP F9: 254 of 440 conflicted draws
partly moved). Conflicted draws now veto their vertices, and the weld spreads
the veto over the connected surface. CV_POSE_CONFLICT_VETO=0 restores the old
merge.

F9 copied the pose history on the render thread while the next batch's pose
was already running, so every captured draw had another batch's history.
While a capture records, the producer now lets the drawn batch finish before
starting the next pose.

1d286a0bc304a2ebfc3fdf7e8885d6d56525606a.message:
PPU: user-mode lwmutex lock word instead of a kernel semaphore

sys_lwmutex was backed by a Win32 semaphore, so every lock and unlock was a
system call even when uncontended. Guest code takes lwmutexes thousands of
times a frame (allocators, job queues); sampling Code Veronica's main thread
put ~28% of it inside those calls. The slot now holds the lock word itself:
an uncontended lock/unlock is one interlocked operation, a contended lock
spins briefly and then sleeps on WaitOnAddress, honouring the guest timeout.
Any thread may still release it, as with the semaphore.

249500dc8262dd08586b618ac7a1f6ed738b523e.message:
Processors without AVX2: *_SSE4.exe, started by the normal executable

The SPU code is built for Haswell (/arch:AVX2), and the instructions that
flag brings (MOVBE, BMI2, FMA...) also reach shared inline code: on an
i3-2120 (issue #12) the NID hash at boot hit MOVBE and the game died with
0xC000001D before drawing anything. Processors without AVX2 -- Sandy/Ivy
Bridge, older Xeons, AMD FX, Nehalem/Westmere -- could not run the port.

- cpu_tier.cpp (new): runs from .CRT$XCB, before every constructor. If
  the processor lacks a Haswell feature (AVX2, FMA, BMI1/2, MOVBE, LZCNT,
  F16C), it starts *_SSE4.exe beside it with the same arguments and
  returns its exit code; without one it shows a clear message instead of
  an illegal instruction. On AVX2 processors it returns at once.
  CV_CPU_FORCE_COMPAT=1 takes the compatibility path for tests.
- CV_CPU_COMPAT (CMake): builds everything for SSE4.1 (SSSE3 pshufb for
  shufb), the SPU code included, as *_SSE4.exe. build-release.cmd builds
  it with CV_BUILD_COMPAT=1 (EU, plus US/JP with CV_BUILD_US/JP).
- spu_helpers.h: without hardware FMA, spu_fma/fms/fnms use an exact
  float product in double plus one add instead of ucrt's software fmaf.
  With FMA (the AVX2 build) the exact fmaf is unchanged.
- distribution/build.py builds eu-sse4/us-sse4/jp-sse4 from the
  build-release*-sse4 objects (never the AVX2 ones) and keeps earlier
  digests; empacotar_release.py packages the three _SSE4 executables when
  all three exist.
- READMEs: CV_BUILD_COMPAT, and the Visual Studio/LLVM note now matches
  the vswhere lookup.

Tested in a clean copy: the AVX2 executable boots as before (title screen
at 30 FPS); CV_CPU_FORCE_COMPAT=1 hands over to the _SSE4 one, which
reaches the title screen. Under Intel SDE, -snb makes the normal
executable start the _SSE4 one, and the _SSE4 one ran 4 minutes under
-wsm (no AVX) with SPU jobs dispatching and no invalid instruction. Every
AVX instruction left in it is in the MSVC STL's runtime-dispatched
vector_algorithms. distribution/build.py was n

26301fcf3cd572caa7ad656c996002e51ffc5b07.message:
D3D12: show Code Veronica gameplay without freezing

- Raise MAX_OFF_RTS 16 -> 31. Gameplay uses 17 surfaces; the one left
  without a slot (0x00A9C000) is where the finished frame is blitted and
  then drawn to the display, so the screen stayed black.
- Feed inline fragment constants through b1 (fp_k[]) instead of baking

  program reused the first draw's constants (zero lights).

- Raise VP_VS_CACHE 16 -> 256 and VP_FP_CACHE 256 -> 4096. Evicting VS
  slot 0 shifted every vs_idx and re-keyed every cached FP pipeline;
  ~90% of a gameplay frame went to recompiling shaders.
- GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS: only treat a FIFO jump-park as abandoned after it
  has stood that long. Code Veronica parks at 0x198060 and patches it
  later; skipping to put dropped its draws and fences and froze the game.
- Blits into a display buffer copy into the backbuffer.
- Diagnostics: F12/CV_AUTOCAP rsxcap with zeta/ztest/zfunc in the

267510f98f479da09f77b18a91ac107e4d0957d6.message:
Cut CPU spin in Code Veronica's 3D cutscenes (~4.15 -> ~3.6 cores)

- sys_ppu_thread_yield: after 16 yields < 200 us apart, nap
  PPU_YIELD_NAP_US (default 100 us) on a high-resolution timer. The game's
  30 fps limiter spins on yield + timebase for the last ms of every frame;
  its main thread went from 0.88 to 0.45 cores.
- GETLLAR polling: a context re-reading an unchanged line it still holds a
  reservation on sleeps until the line is written (writers already notify;
  1 ms timeout as a net). Image-10 tasks did ~1M GETLLAR/s on one line that
  changes ~3700 times/s; now ~30k/s and the lock-line lock dropped from 18%
  to 2% of SPU thread time. SPU_POLL_WAIT=0 reverts. spu_ch_wake passes
  through the waiter's lock so a wake cannot fall between check and sleep.
- Drain loops: the per-step checks are inline (spu_step_check); the full
  spu_task_launch_check only runs for step diagnostics, registered
  stack-reset entries or policy modules. yz_lockstep_tick only when
  lockstep is on. spu_depth_guard writes its shared ring only near the
  limit (it bounced a cache line between every SPU thread).
- cellSpursCreateTask claims the task and opens its join record before
  setting the ready bits: a sibling's exit could start the task, and finish
  it, before the creator claimed it, which then ran it twice.
- Diagnostics: SPU_LL_HIST=1 (lock lines GETLLAR'd, PUTLLC ok/fail);
  REJECTED DMA transfers name the job and the thread's previous job.
- SPU_TASK_POOL stays off: it still freezes (malformed transfer at img=10
  pc=0x20D54) and used more CPU than thread-per-task.

D3D12: reuse vertex-constant banks and converted vertices

Profiling the FIFO drain in Code Veronica's lighter scene (~6600 draws
a frame) put ~80% of its work in two places:

  it back from the write-combined upload heap. rsx_state now counts

  points at the previous draw's bank (vcb_slot) instead of copying.
  99% of banks are reused in that scene.

  heap, each slot written twice, and strips and indexed meshes fetched
  every vertex 3-6 times. Vertices are now converted into a per-call
  memo keyed by index and copied out in one go; about half are reused.

4b81587013d3853a30161456068dfe29dcaf6a27.message:
D3D12: render on its own thread, overlapping the FIFO drain

The frame clock drained the FIFO and then built and submitted the D3D12
frame on the same thread, and the guest's main thread spent most of each
frame polling a label the drain could not write while a frame rendered.

render_frame() now freezes the recording batch into s_rb (draw list and
count, upload-stream parity, FP and vertex-texture snapshot arenas,
present flag), points recording at the other draw buffer and arenas, and
hands the batch to a rsx_render thread. At most one batch is in flight:
the next freeze waits for the render thread, which waits for the GPU
after submitting so both upload halves are free again. Render-side code
reads the batch only through s_rb.

While waiting, the drain thread services messages sent to its window,
and the FPS title is posted to it instead of SetWindowText from the
render thread, so neither side can block on the other. VS cache eviction
and shutdown wait for the render thread. RSX_RENDER_THREAD=0 restores the
inline render.

Cell and corridor: ~28 / ~19 -> 30 / 30 fps (the game's cap).

4cee10b976eaa6985fff238beedf551a293c5ff8.message:
PPU: fast path for guest memory accessors; per-frame timeline

Every lifted load and store calls vm_read*/vm_write*, and those had grown a
stack of watch/trace hooks that ran on every access even when unconfigured.
With the lighter on in Code Veronica the game's main thread is the critical
path, and sampling it put the accessors at roughly a third of its time. Each
accessor now takes a fast path (bounds, null-page, SPU raw registers and
reservation coherency, GCM ref polling) unless a diagnostic is configured;
PS3_VM_DIAG=1 forces the full path. The reserved-line test is inlined.
Lighter scene: ~17.7 -> ~21-23 fps.

PS3_TIMELINE=1 adds a [TL] report every ~5 s: ms per presented frame for the
FIFO drain, frame_clock sleeps (split by whether work was waiting), present,
render-thread record and GPU wait, and usleep time per guest thread. It is
what showed the drain and render threads idle and the main thread busy.

598d4f0a03b4a8e947ac963861ea596301367da0.message:
D3D12: validate vertex-texture snapshots once per FIFO drain pass

vtex_record asked GetWriteWatch whether the bound vertex texture had been
written on every draw that bound it. Code Veronica's bone-matrix texture is
1 MB (256 pages), and the lighter's cube shadow multiplies the character
draws, so that syscall was most of the FIFO drain. Every draw of one drain
pass was queued before the pass read `put`, and a title may not rewrite data
the RSX has yet to read, so a snapshot checked once holds for the rest of the
pass (g_gcm_drain_epoch). VTEX_EPOCH=0 restores the per-draw check.
Lighter scene drain: ~30 -> ~17 ms a frame; ~21 -> ~22-24 fps.

Also: frame_clock skips its 1 ms sleep when the drain stopped at a flip with
the next frame queued (GCM_FLIP_NOSLEEP=0 to disable); the sys_event_flag
wait no longer calls getenv per call; more [TL] events (vertex upload, draw
calls, pump, ticks, and the main thread's SPU-join / event-flag / lwmutex
waits).

D3D12: refresh the depth view after a live resolution change

Changing RES_SCALE while running recreates the shared depth buffer, but the

page fault and a lost device. The view is now rewritten whenever the depth
buffer is recreated. The draw texture-window cache, which matches windows by
resource pointer, is also dropped whenever resources are actually released,

8a39c4395f83bb9928b4ec7e4cf4e83126bcb572.message:
D3D12: vertex conversion on the GPU (RSX_GPU_VFETCH), FIFO thread cuts

RSX_GPU_VFETCH=1 makes the vertex shader read the guest's own vertex
bytes and convert them. The FIFO thread writes an 8-byte record per
output vertex (guest index, draw descriptor) and copies each draw's
vertex range once, raw, instead of converting every vertex into a
256-byte slot. Draws with too wide a range are converted on the CPU into
the same buffer. The draw's first record comes in a root constant (b2);
SV_VertexID did not include the start vertex. Shaders and pipelines of
this mode are cached apart (-vfetch). Code Veronica JP, flooded room:
about 36 -> 58 FPS with the 60 FPS limit. VF_CHECK=N compares N vertices
against the CPU conversion; VF_DUMP=1 writes the first wrapped programs.

Launcher: "Vertices na GPU (experimental)" on the Desempenho page, off by
default, in all 13 languages; fixed once the game runs. The page's cards
are shorter so the sixth ends above the Jogar button.

FIFO thread cuts, all modes:
- fp_guest_program_size remembers readable 4 KB guest pages instead of a
  VirtualQuery per draw (~10% of the thread in heavy rooms);
- draw_arrays liveness every 200000 draws, BindZcull logged 8 times.

9994311eca2bbbf4156bba66ca82ce2904b75887.message:
D3D12: sample cube textures as cubes (water reflection, lighter)

fp_build_pso handed the fragment decompiler a cube mask of 0, and the
text pass that was meant to turn Texture2D into TextureCube looked for
declarations the decompiler no longer emits. Every cube unit was read
as a 2D texture with a cube view bound: Code Veronica's flooded-room
water reflection returned one flat bluish colour instead of the room,
so the water lacked the greenish pattern the PS3 and RPCS3 show.

- The cube mask goes to the decompiler, which declares TextureCube and
  samples with the 3-component direction (through RSX_CUBEDIR;
  RSX_CUBE_FLIP=x|y|z mirrors it for orientation tests).
- Cubes of Y16_X16 lookups (the lighter's shadow face/texel tables) are
  read through the point sampler: filtered, they blended indices across
  face seams and drew black lines out from the flame
  (CUBE_LUT_LINEAR=1 restores linear).
- RSX_ADDR wrap mode passes the coordinate through; the static samplers
  already wrap, and frac() broke derivatives at seams.

Experiments kept behind switches: RSX_TEX_MIPS=1 (upload mip chains),
TEX_NOGAMMA_FP, RSX_DXC_DEBUG=1 (debuggable DXIL for RenderDoc), and

D3D12: stop render-frame stalls from texture churn and preemption

Lighter scene render frames over 50 ms went 34 -> 0 per run:
- Vertex textures: a changed matrix snapshot overwrote a fresh 1 MB texture
  and upload buffer every time (several ms each). It now reuses the oldest
  cached texture of the same shape not bound this frame and one upload
  buffer reused per frame; the cache ages by render frames, not the FPS
  counter that resets every second. VTEX_NOPOOL=1 restores the old path.
- Texture slots 96 -> 384, evicting an empty slot first and then the least
  recently used one (not the first slot unused this frame, which threw out
  textures about to be bound again), with a hint table so a lookup does not
  walk every slot. Slots past the fixed views (1+slot < RT_SRV_BASE) write no
  fixed view; draws bind through their own windows.
- The render and frame_clock threads run above normal priority
  (RSX_RENDER_PRIO=0 / FRAME_CLOCK_PRIO=0 to disable): busy guest pollers
  were preempting them for 20-50 ms at random draws.
Also [TEX-SLOW] and [PREPASS-SLOW] reports under PERF.

b3aaf23c72808cc39e8989e4e92ef5a16550575f.message:
Shaders: stop the flicker, the vanishing characters and the black screens

Code Veronica's lighting fragment programs carry 129 and 166 inline
constants, past the 128 the per-draw buffer held. Their constants became
literals and their pipelines were keyed on the values, which the game
rewrites every frame: they recompiled without end, and the draws using them
were skipped meanwhile -- the character flat or missing, the scene black for
seconds around the inventory. fp_k[] now holds 512.

- Vertex programs are keyed on their own code (through END) and start slot,
  not on whatever else sits in the store after them.
- The VS cache holds 4096 and replaces its least recently used program in
  place; FP pipelines are keyed on the VS content, so a replacement no
  longer re-keys every cached pipeline.
- The FP pipeline cache holds 16384.
- A pipeline first requested in the draw loop is waited for (out of the
  frame's 8 ms budget) instead of dropping the draw: a build from the disk
  caches takes about a millisecond.
- PERF reports build time and the draws really left out; the log notes
  programs past the constant limit and frames out of texture slots.

SPU: give MFC engine slots back when a run ends

  drops any slot whose context lived on its stack.

D3D12: RES_SCALE renders above the guest resolution

RES_SCALE=<f> (1 < f <= 4; 1.5 = 1080p) renders at f times the guest's
1280x720. The backend still records everything in guest pixels; the scale
is applied where they meet D3D12:

  at the scaled size (OffRT gains sc/pw/ph; lookups stay keyed on guest
  dims);

bedc24a654ab20890e454e730bb7ad2eecd4d3f8.message:
Fragment programs sized to their END: the dark outdoor scene renders

The backend read at most 4096 bytes of each RSX fragment program for its
snapshot, hash, constants, texture scan and compile. Programs past that
(up to 6592 bytes / 290 instructions / 122 constants in the dark outdoor
area) were cut, and the literal fallback accepted the prefix: the scene
came out near black, or neon with the lighter on.

- Programs are measured through END and copied at that exact length
  (fp_bytes per draw, FpJob buffers sized per job). Reads past the first
  page are checked with VirtualQuery; RSX_FP_PROGRAM_LIMIT (256 KiB) is a
  software safety ceiling, with a logged rejection past it.
- rsx_fp_decompiler: buffered and literal paths require END inside the
  given length; rsx_fp_decompile_alloc grows the HLSL buffer on
  RSX_FP_OUTPUT_TOO_SMALL up to RSX_FP_HLSL_LIMIT (8 MiB).
- Literal-constant programs (over 128 constants) key their cache on the
  values, so one draw's lighting is not reused for another.
- F12 capture: reads the bank the GPU used (s_rb.parity), names shaders by
  address + code hash, and lists step snapshots.
- Tests: CV_FP_TESTS=1 build-release.cmd builds and runs
  code_veronica_fp_tests (51 checks, including a 64 KiB program).

Made with GPT in the user's session; visual fix confirmed by the user.

stored in an ID3D12PipelineLibrary (shader_cache/pipelines.bin, saved

f7c0dea1acb40f26d74931a9bbb981adb52cf6c8.message:
Keep 60 FPS frame generation real: replay, no present wait, async compute

With FSR 3.1 frame generation on, the heavy JP room showed 23 real / 47 total
FPS (42.7 ms per real frame). Three changes bring it back:

- The FSR gate no longer turns the pose replay off, so the guest keeps its
  native 30 Hz loop (one draw per tick) and FSR gets both host presents.
  CV_FSR_GUEST=legacy selects the old twice-per-tick path, "30" one present
  per tick with FSR doubling it. Without FG nothing changes.
- rsx_fsr31_begin no longer waits for every SDK present before each real
  frame: the SDK paces the real frame about half a frame after the generated
  one, and that hold was added to every real frame. Captures, resize and
  context recreation still wait; CV_FSR_WAIT_PRESENTS=1 restores the wait.
- Generation runs on async compute (CV_FSR_ASYNC=0: game queue). FG cost
  ~3.5 ms of GPU per real frame; on the game queue the render thread waited
  4-7 ms for the GPU (56-59 real FPS, 28-29 logic ticks). Async kept 60 real
  FPS and 30 ticks with no GPU wait. User tested: good real FPS, no defects.

CV_FRAME_PROFILE also prints [FSR-GPU] per-stage GPU times. Test switches
CV_FSR_GUARD=0 and CV_FSR_VECTORS=0 remain, off by default.

Code Veronica's rm_1130 water draws two 138612-vertex meshes. With the
lighter lit, the frame reached the 393216-vertex limit and every draw
past it was dropped -- the post-processing chain and the copy to the
display -- so the screen flashed black near the water. 786432 vertices
holds the frame; the generic VP vertex buffer grows from 192 to 384 MB.

fd9a9dc94e0a98afbfecb846bb3f50ae8f83c433.message:
Code Veronica: native guest memset/memmove; D3D12: overlap recording with the GPU

Heavy rooms (JP, ~8800 draws a frame) went from ~44 to ~49 FPS with the
60 FPS limit; the prison cutscene from ~54 to ~59.

- The guest libc memset and memmove run natively (cv_native_libc.cpp, via
  the hook list; EU/US/JP addresses in cv_version.h). The lifted loops
  stored through vm_write64 per 8 bytes, ~14% of the main PPU thread.
  ppu_vm_fill/ppu_vm_move keep the stores' rules: SPU-reserved lines go
  under the lockline and are notified, the memory diagnostics keep the
  store-by-store path. CV_NATIVE_LIBC=0 runs the lifted bodies.
- RSX_SUBMIT_SPLIT=<N> (default 1024, 0 = off): the render thread prepares,
  records and submits the frame in parts of N draws, each with its own
  allocator. The per-draw prepass (texture uploads, SRV windows, pipeline
  lookups) used to run for the whole frame first, so the GPU sat idle for
  ~8 ms and then ran after recording ended; the wait after recording fell
  from ~10 to ~4 ms.
- PS3_TIMELINE also reports [GPUCMD]: draws, barriers, copies, target and
  pipeline changes per frame (counted through a copy of the command
  list's method table), and the GPU's own time per frame from timestamps
  placed on the CPU clock.

Code Veronica streams its voices and music (SetDataAndGetMemSize with

memory keep the old path.

intermittent slow intro leaves evidence in a normal log.

Extract everything and open **Code Veronica.exe**. | | [Veronica-PKG-Extractor-v1.0.1.zip](https://github.com/kastieloficial/RE-Code-Veronica-PS3-HD-Recomp-PC/releases/download/v1.5.0/Veronica-PKG-Extractor-v1.0.1.zip) | Separate, unchanged PKG preparation tool for your own game; RPCS3 extraction is also supported. | | [HD texture pack (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1t6yVG1yEC5dl3Td6jT4rhFj1EEwmbsAZ/view?usp=sharing) | Optional community HD textures for the US, EU and JP versions, adapted to this project. ## What is this? This is a native Windows x64 port of **Resident Evil Code: Veronica X** for PlayStation 3. It is not an emulator. The game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code is translated ahead of time into C/C++ with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), then compiled into a normal Windows executable. The PS3 system libraries are reimplemented, and the RSX graphics run on Direct3D 12. On top of that, the port adds its own launcher, modern graphics options, 60 FPS, frame generation, a speedrun-ready SRT overlay, practice tools and more. Everything is described below. ## Why the PS3 version I am a big fan of Resident Evil and of Capcom, and Code: Veronica is one of my favourite games in the series. I chose the PS3 version because it is the one many **speedrunners** use, and I wanted them to have a fast, stable PC version with tools made for practice: health, inventory, enemies and time on screen, plus the ability to jump to any room. The port is for **every player**: people who want to replay the game with higher resolution, 60 FPS and modern controllers, and also people who run it competitively. ## Built for speedrun practice Alongside a modern PC presentation, **Veronica Port is built for speedrun practice**. Repeat a difficult room, prepare a boss fight or work on an inventory route using tools available directly in the port. | Practice tool | What it helps you do | |---|---| | **Native SRT · F8** | Monitor player and enemy health, inventory, ammo and in-game time. | | **Room selection · F7** | Load a room and choose its entry point to repeat a section. | | **Save and load anywhere · F7** | Keep separate practice saves and return to a setup quickly. | | **Item menu · F6** | Prepare weapons and supplies for a specific test. | | **LiveSplit integration** | Use the included autosplitter that also attaches to the port. | Enable the optional practice tools in **Cheats**. They are tools for training; whether a run is eligible depends on its category and community rules. ## Supported versions Only the **PSN releases, version 01.00**, are supported. Each region has its own executable; they all share the same launcher, settings, saves and caches, and each launcher starts the right executable for the chosen game folder. | Region | Title ID | Executable | License file (.rap) | |---|---|---|---| | Europe | `NPEB00553` | `CodeVeronicaPort.exe` | Required | | United States | `NPUB30467` | `CodeVeronicaPort_US.exe` | Required | | Japan (*BIOHAZARD CODE: Veronica Kanzenban*) | `NPJB00135` | `CodeVeronicaPort_JP.exe` | Not needed | Game updates, disc releases and other versions are not supported. The launcher checks the version and tells you if a folder is not compatible. ## Requirements - Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. - A graphics card with **Direct3D 12** support. - The **Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable (x64)**. Without it, Windows reports a missing `MSVCP140.dll` or `VCRUNTIME140.dll`. - Your own copy of the game, as a folder (see below). **No PS3 firmware and no RPCS3 are needed to play.** ### Test PC The port was developed and tested on this PC, where the game was **completed from start to finish**: | Part | Model | |---|---| | CPU | AMD Ryzen 5 5600X | | GPU | AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT 12 GB | | RAM | 32 GB DDR4 | Other PCs should work, but this is the configuration that was actually tested. ## Preparing your game The port reads the game from a **folder**, not from a `.pkg` file. It works like the PS4 ports that use shadPS4-style game folders: the PKG must be **installed or extracted first**. A `.pkg` file cannot be opened directly. The folder you choose must contain `PARAM.SFO` and `USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN`: ``` NPEB00553\ (or NPUB30467 / NPJB00135) ├── PARAM.SFO ├── ICON0.PNG └── USRDIR\ ├── EBOOT.BIN └── BHCV\ ... ``` **Step by step** 1. **Get the game folder from your PKG. Choose either method:** - **Veronica PKG Extractor (optional, separate download):** when available, download `Veronica-PKG-Extractor-v1.0.zip` from the project's [Releases](https://github.com/kastiellcontato-design/re-cvx-ps3recomp/releases), alongside the latest port ZIP. Unzip the tool, open `VeronicaPKGExtractor.exe`, drop or select your PKG, choose a destination and click **Extract PKG**. It creates the `NPEB00553`, `NPUB30467` or `NPJB00135` folder with the original package files. Add that folder to the launcher. This tool is only for the three supported Code Veronica PSN base releases, version 01.00. - **RPCS3:** install your PKG using *File → Install Packages/Raps/Edats*. The game folder is at `RPCS3\dev_hdd0\game\NPEB00553` (or `NPUB30467` / `NPJB00135`). Add that folder to the launcher. RPCS3 is only needed for this preparation step. Both methods produce the game folder the port needs. **You only need one method.** If your game is already extracted, the extractor download is unnecessary. The launcher does not open PKGs directly, and the extractor does not create RAP licenses. 2. **Find your license (`.rap`)** for the European and American versions. It is the `.rap` file of the account that bought the game. In RPCS3 it is in `dev_hdd0\home\00000001\exdata`, with the title ID in its name (for example `EP0102-NPEB00553_00-…​.rap`). If the `.rap` file is inside the game folder, the launcher finds it on its own. **The Japanese version does not need a `.rap`.** 3. **Keep the original files as they are.** You do not need to decrypt anything: on the first start, the port decrypts `EBOOT.BIN` with your license into its own `eboot_cache` folder (it takes less than a second). Your game files are never modified. ## Installing and playing 1. Install the [Visual C++ Redistributable (x64)](https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe) if you do not have it yet. 2. Extract the whole ZIP to a folder where you can write, for example `C:\Games\CodeVeronica`. Do not run it from inside the ZIP or from `Program Files`, and keep all files together. 3. Open `CodeVeronicaPort.exe` (any of the three executables opens the same launcher). 4. On the **Games** page, add your game folder for each version you own, and the `.rap` for EU/US if it was not found automatically. 5. Select a version, adjust the graphics and controls, and press **PLAY**. The first sessions may stutter a little while shaders are compiled. They are saved in `shader_cache` and are not compiled again. **Where things are** (all inside the port folder): settings in `cv_launcher.ini`; saves in `gamedata\dev_hdd0\` (a different folder can be chosen in the launcher); caches in `shader_cache\` and `eboot_cache\` (safe to delete, they are rebuilt); screenshots in `screenshots\`; the last session's log in `run-log.txt`, useful when reporting a problem. The launcher can also check the GitHub releases and update itself (it can be turned off in the launcher). ## Features ### Launcher - Its own launcher, available in **13 languages**: Português (Brasil), English, Español, 日本語, Français, Deutsch, Italiano, Polski, Türkçe, العربية, 简体中文, 한국어 and Русский. - Game library with the three regions, version and license checks, and region flags. - Stays open during play as the **in-game options menu** (`Insert`/`F5`), so settings can be changed without leaving the game. - Pages: Games, Graphics, HUD, Saves & captures, Controls, Shortcuts, Patches, Mods, SRT, Cheats, Performance and Advanced (language, shader cache, live game log viewer). - Optional pause when the game window loses focus. ### Graphics and performance - **Render resolution**: 480p, native 720p, 1080p, 1440p and **4K** (3840×2160). Windowed, borderless window or fullscreen. - **Anti-aliasing**: FXAA (light) or SMAA (best). - **Anisotropic filtering**: 2x, 4x, 8x and 16x. - **Sharpening** with **AMD FSR 1 RCAS**, from 10% to 100%. - **Frame limit**: - **30 FPS (original)**: the same experience as the PS3, where the game runs at 30 FPS. - **60 FPS**: the game logic stays at its original 30 Hz and the extra frames come from **interpolating character and object poses**, so the timing of the game is kept. The integrated native smoothing path is selected automatically for EU/US/JP. - **AMD FSR 3.1 Frame Generation** (optional, 60 FPS mode only): up to 120 FPS when the PC holds 60 FPS. - **VSync** (60 FPS mode): no tearing. It cannot be used together with frame generation. - Performance overlay with FPS, frame time, CPU, GPU, RAM, VRAM and SPU/RSX load, in any corner. - Persistent shader and pipeline cache, loaded in the background, with optional progress note. - Movies (FMV) decoded with FFmpeg and ATRAC3plus audio decoded natively: no PS3 firmware needed. ### SRT for speedrunners


Native SRT and boss health bar during gameplay.

View the SRT panel in detail

A native **SRT** (speedrun tool) overlay drawn by the game itself, toggled with `F8`: - Character name and portrait, **health** (value, percentage and status: fine, caution, danger, poisoned, gas). - **In-game time**, saves, retries and first-aid sprays (F.A.S.). - **Enemies** with health bars and portraits, and **boss health bars** (in the panel, or centered at the top or bottom of the screen). - **Inventory** with the equipped weapon, ammo and the game's own item icons, read from your game files. - Any corner, row or column layout, inventory beside or below, size from 50% to 200%, background opacity, border, panel language, or a **separate window** you can place anywhere (for example on a second monitor or in OBS). - **LiveSplit official catalog:** in **Edit Splits → Game Name**, enter exactly **Resident Evil: Code: Veronica X (PS3 Recomp)**, then click **Activate → Settings**. Select **Compare Against → Game Time** for load removal. The optional ZIP includes ready-made Any%/S-Rank splits with icons and catalog setup instructions. [Setup guide](projects/code_veronica/livesplit/README.md). ### Practice tools, saves and items - **Archives** window (`F7`, enabled in Cheats): **load any room or map** (with the room's entry point) to practice a section, **save anywhere** into an independent save library with thumbnails, and **load** those saves at any time. - **Item menu** (`F6`, enabled in Cheats): put any item or weapon in the current character's inventory, or take one out, without leaving the game. - **Cheats**: infinite health and infinite ammo, switchable during play. - **Patches**: skip door animations, skip the opening logos and intro, plus your own patches in RPCS3's `patch.yml` format. - Choose where saves are stored. ### In-game RECOMP SETTINGS and character swap

In the game's own **OPTION** menu, the **RECOMP SETTINGS** page changes resolution, anti-aliasing, display mode, brightness, contrast, saturation, sharpening (FSR RCAS) and anisotropic filtering without opening the launcher, with **Reset colors** to go back to the defaults. At the top of the same page, **APPEARANCE** lets you **play as another character model**: press left/right to choose and see it in a rotating **360° preview**. There are 33 options: Claire (original and alternate outfit), Chris, Steve, Wesker, 26 zombie variants and two forms of Alexia (first form and human). The chosen look is also applied when you play as Chris, Steve or Wesker. It only changes how the character looks; the story, the controls and your save stay the same. ### Controls - **Xbox** (XInput), **PlayStation** (DualShock 4 and DualSense) and **Nintendo Switch** controllers, plus keyboard, all at the same time. - **Vibration** with an adjustable strength (0–200%). - Any key or button can be remapped, with several keys per action. - On-screen button icons for PlayStation, Xbox, Switch or keyboard, chosen automatically from the last device used, in HD. ##

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   └── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse
│   ├── hardware/             # cellGem, cellCamera, cellUsbd
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
└── docs/                     # See the Documentation table below
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

HLE implementations of the PS3 system libraries, written for this project. RPCS3 is a behavioural reference, not a code source. **About 93 modules complete and 5 partial** (media decode, SPURS), in roughly 260 files and 100,000 lines under `libs/`.

| Category | Modules | Status |
|----------|---------|--------|
| **Kernel Threading** | sys_ppu_thread, sys_mutex, sys_cond, sys_semaphore, sys_rwlock | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Events** | sys_event (queues, ports, flags), sys_timer | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Memory** | sys_memory, sys_mmapper (containers, shared mem) | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Filesystem** | sys_fs (path mapping, real I/O) | ✅ Complete |
| **Filesystem** | cellFs (real file I/O, dir ops, stat, path translation) | ✅ Complete |
| **Save System** | cellSaveData (callback-driven, PARAM.SFO), cellGame | ✅ Complete |
| **Input** | cellPad (XInput/SDL2), cellKb, cellMouse | ✅ Complete |
| **Audio** | cellAudio (WASAPI/SDL2, mixing thread, multi-port) | ✅ Complete |
| **Video Output** | cellVideoOut (resolution config, 720p default) | ✅ Complete |
| **Codecs** | cellPngDec, cellJpgDec, cellGifDec (stb_image) | ✅ Complete |
| **Font** | cellFont (stb_truetype backend + fallback metrics) | ✅ Complete |
| **Network** | sys_net (BSD sockets, P2P), cellNet, cellNetCtl, cellHttpUtil, cellSsl, sceNp*, sceNpTrophy, sceNpMatching2 + Score over [psnr](docs/ONLINE.md) | ✅ Complete |
| **Hardware** | cellUsbd (USB), cellCamera (PS Eye), cellGem (PS Move) — stub, no devices | ✅ Complete |
| **Sync** | cellSync (atomic spinlocks, LF queue), cellSync2 (OS-backed) | ✅ Complete |
| **System** | cellRtc, cellMsgDialog, cellOskDialog, cellUserInfo, cellGameExec | ✅ Complete |
| **Localization** | cellL10n (UTF-8/16/32/UCS-2, ISO-8859-1, generic converter) | ✅ Complete |
| **Resolution** | cellResc (display modes, scaling, interlace, aspect ratio) | ✅ Complete |
| **Fibers** | cellFiber (PPU fibers via Windows Fibers/ucontext) | ✅ Complete |
| **AV Config** | cellAvconfExt (audio output info, gamma, sound availability) | ✅ Complete |
| **Input Util** | cellKey2char (HID scancode → Unicode, US-101 layout) | ✅ Complete |
| **Graphics** | cellGcmSys (cmd buffer, IO mapping, tile/zcull, flip handlers, timestamps, FIFO walker + ring recycle), RSX command processor (NV47xx parsing, state tracking, backend callbacks), **live D3D12 backend** (executes the title's real NV4097 vertex/fragment programs — indexed draws, per-draw VP constants + textures, render-to-texture, MRT, FP predication), null backend (Win32 window) | ✅ Complete |
| **SPURS** | cellSpurs (management APIs, event flags, task/workload tracking), cellSpursJq (job queues with wait/signal), cellDaisy (real ring buffer FIFO) | ✅ Complete |
| **Core Runtime** | cellSysutil (BGM, cache, disc), cellSysmodule, sysPrxForUser (real lwmutex/lwcond/threads) | ✅ Complete |
| **Media Pipeline** | cellPamf (PAMF header + stream descriptors), cellDmux (callback sequencing), cellVdec (H.264/MPEG-2 through FFmpeg loaded at run time, opt-in), cellAtrac (ATRAC3plus, all-in-memory), cellAdec (callbacks, no decode yet), cellSail (state machine) | 🔨 Partial |

Full status tracking: [docs/MODULE_STATUS.md](docs/MODULE_STATUS.md)

## Documentation

We've written extensive docs covering every aspect of the project. Whether you're contributing, porting a game, or just trying to understand how PS3 static recompilation works, there's a doc for you.
