# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   └── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse
│   ├── hardware/             # cellGem, cellCamera, cellUsbd
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
└── docs/                     # See the Documentation table below
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

HLE implementations of the PS3 system libraries, written for this project. RPCS3 is a behavioural reference, not a code source. **About 93 modules complete and 5 partial** (media decode, SPURS), in roughly 260 files and 100,000 lines under `libs/`.

| Category | Modules | Status |
|----------|---------|--------|
| **Kernel Threading** | sys_ppu_thread, sys_mutex, sys_cond, sys_semaphore, sys_rwlock | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Events** | sys_event (queues, ports, flags), sys_timer | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Memory** | sys_memory, sys_mmapper (containers, shared mem) | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Filesystem** | sys_fs (path mapping, real I/O) | ✅ Complete |
| **Filesystem** | cellFs (real file I/O, dir ops, stat, path translation) | ✅ Complete |
| **Save System** | cellSaveData (callback-driven, PARAM.SFO), cellGame | ✅ Complete |
| **Input** | cellPad (XInput/SDL2), cellKb, cellMouse | ✅ Complete |
| **Audio** | cellAudio (WASAPI/SDL2, mixing thread, multi-port) | ✅ Complete |
| **Video Output** | cellVideoOut (resolution config, 720p default) | ✅ Complete |
| **Codecs** | cellPngDec, cellJpgDec, cellGifDec (stb_image) | ✅ Complete |
| **Font** | cellFont (stb_truetype backend + fallback metrics) | ✅ Complete |
| **Network** | sys_net (BSD sockets, P2P), cellNet, cellNetCtl, cellHttpUtil, cellSsl, sceNp*, sceNpTrophy, sceNpMatching2 + Score over [psnr](docs/ONLINE.md) | ✅ Complete |
| **Hardware** | cellUsbd (USB), cellCamera (PS Eye), cellGem (PS Move) — stub, no devices | ✅ Complete |
| **Sync** | cellSync (atomic spinlocks, LF queue), cellSync2 (OS-backed) | ✅ Complete |
| **System** | cellRtc, cellMsgDialog, cellOskDialog, cellUserInfo, cellGameExec | ✅ Complete |
| **Localization** | cellL10n (UTF-8/16/32/UCS-2, ISO-8859-1, generic converter) | ✅ Complete |
| **Resolution** | cellResc (display modes, scaling, interlace, aspect ratio) | ✅ Complete |
| **Fibers** | cellFiber (PPU fibers via Windows Fibers/ucontext) | ✅ Complete |
| **AV Config** | cellAvconfExt (audio output info, gamma, sound availability) | ✅ Complete |
| **Input Util** | cellKey2char (HID scancode → Unicode, US-101 layout) | ✅ Complete |
| **Graphics** | cellGcmSys (cmd buffer, IO mapping, tile/zcull, flip handlers, timestamps, FIFO walker + ring recycle), RSX command processor (NV47xx parsing, state tracking, backend callbacks), **live D3D12 backend** (executes the title's real NV4097 vertex/fragment programs — indexed draws, per-draw VP constants + textures, render-to-texture, MRT, FP predication), null backend (Win32 window) | ✅ Complete |
| **SPURS** | cellSpurs (management APIs, event flags, task/workload tracking), cellSpursJq (job queues with wait/signal), cellDaisy (real ring buffer FIFO) | ✅ Complete |
| **Core Runtime** | cellSysutil (BGM, cache, disc), cellSysmodule, sysPrxForUser (real lwmutex/lwcond/threads) | ✅ Complete |
| **Media Pipeline** | cellPamf (PAMF header + stream descriptors), cellDmux (callback sequencing), cellVdec (H.264/MPEG-2 through FFmpeg loaded at run time, opt-in), cellAtrac (ATRAC3plus, all-in-memory), cellAdec (callbacks, no decode yet), cellSail (state machine) | 🔨 Partial |
| **HTTP/HTTPS** | cellHttp (real HTTP/1.1 via native sockets), cellHttps (TLS stub with cert management) | ✅ Complete |
| **Misc/Export** | cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellPhotoExport/Import, cellGameRecording, cellPrint, cellRemotePlay | ✅ Complete |

Full status tracking: [docs/MODULE_STATUS.md](docs/MODULE_STATUS.md)

## Documentation

We've written extensive docs covering every aspect of the project. Whether you're contributing, porting a game, or just trying to understand how PS3 static recompilation works, there's a doc for you.

| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

48f8156846d64bde264dd4f6057757b373c4e4e9.message:
fix(toolkit): ps3_ms_now counts on macOS; MRT colour mask and blend per target, opt-in

ps3_ms_now() returned 0 on POSIX, so every timeout built on it
(GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS, GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS) never expired and the rate logs
read 0; it now uses CLOCK_MONOTONIC (upstream 91ee29f, found by the
profiling session).

The draw engine gave every target of an MRT set target A's colour mask
and blend. The RSX has COLOR_MASK_MRT (0x0370, an A,R,G,B nibble per
target) and BLEND_ENABLE_MRT (0x036C), and inFAMOUS 2 relies on them:
its cutscene G-buffer writes A=RGB, B=ARGB, C=AGB (the display buffer's
R keeps the shadow cascades p128/p135 accumulate) and its decals write
four targets. The hardware rule is decoded into the render state and the
pipeline key and applied per attachment in the Metal backend, as RPCS3
does -- but behind PS3RECOMP_METAL_MRT_MASK=1, default 0 (the old
behaviour), because in New Marais it tints the scene green: a channel
some other pass should write is not reaching that surface yet. Test in
test_rsx_draw_engine.

Diagnostics, all off by default: PS3RECOMP_ENG_MRTLOG=1|2 (each pass's
targets, masks and blend; colour clears), PS3RECOMP_METAL_TINT_PIPE
(paint what up to eight pipelines draw in solid colours),
PS3RECOMP_ENG_FPK_N (how many draws PS3RECOMP_ENG_FPK_PIPE logs).

fix(pad): controller hot-plug and live remapping in the in-game menu (pending toolkit patch)

A DualSense switched off and on again was never picked up until the game
restarted. cellPad opened controllers by SDL device index == PS3 port and
kept asking SDL_IsGameController(i); Homebrew's SDL2 is sdl2-compat on SDL3,
whose device-index list is refreshed only by SDL_NumJoysticks() or by the
SDL2 event filter (installed with an SDL window, which the Metal build never
creates), so index 0 kept the switched-off pad's old instance id forever.
Each poll now drains SDL's joystick/controller events, closes a removed
controller by its handle, and on a device event (or every second while a
port is free) rescans and opens what is new: the same pad gets its port
back by GUID, motors off, no stale rumble; ports 1-3 report
CELL_PAD_STATUS_ASSIGN_CHANGES. Polls are serialised (SetActDirect too).

The in-game menu's Controls tab gains a rebind table (keyboard, mouse,
controller per PS3 button; applies live, saved to the launcher's
input.toml), "Restore defaults", a live input mode (PS3_INPUT_MODE) and a
mouse camera on/off switch.

Toolkit side: infamous2-lle/patches/pending/pad-hotplug-live-remap.patch,
with tests test_pad_hotplug.c (faked SDL behaving like sdl2-compat) and
writer round-trips in test_pad_input_map.c. README/ROADMAP updated.

the fragment program reads the 24-bit depth copy on a free texture unit

live toggle). The mask program already fades itself to its cascade's
slice, so the reachable dusk scenes look the same; the doubled shadows of
Erik's daylight yard were not reproduced headless (ROADMAP, open).

hang with ref stuck at get == put. Flip requests and ticks carry a sequence
number now; the pump marks DONE only when no newer request is pending.

code; a numpy model reproduces 99.3% of a captured frame within ±1
(notes/spu_light/). With PS3RECOMP_ENG_GPU_LIGHT=07000B80:07384B80 the

readback), the draw engine runs the job's formula as a Metal pass when
the composite binds them, and gpu_light.c replaces the job's per-tile
routine (spu_replace_function) with one that only hands the frame's
matrix and light list to the engine. Walk 14.8 fps and dock 16 against

fix(toolkit): the stuck-get watchdog no longer overrides a self-JUMP park

The FIFO walker stops at a JUMP to its own address while inFAMOUS 2 links
its command blocks: it moves put to the ring start first and only then
rewrites the park as a JUMP to the new commands. The park has its own
time-based grace (GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS) for exactly that, but the generic
stuck-get watchdog counts drain passes: a park stops every pass at the same
get, so after 8 passes -- a few milliseconds -- it resynced to put before
the patch landed and dropped the frame's commands. The game then stopped
presenting for good: m2 on the daytime pier at ~40 s of gameplay
('stuck-get' at a 0x2055C940 self-jump, no 'jump-park' before it), and
about one New Marais run in five. Parks are now exempt from the pass
counter, as semaphore-acquire waits already were.

Not the cause of the cityfalls cutscene stall: most stalled runs there show
no stuck-get at all. Roadmap updated; validation runs queued.

8834f6f63080f04a680409d01917741a403d0158.message:
fix(toolkit): biased unsigned-remap textures expand on every fetch

SET_TEXTURE_ADDRESS bit 12 (CELL_GCM_TEXTURE_UNSIGNED_REMAP_BIASED) asks
the sampler to return every fetch of that unit re-centred to -1..1, not
only the TEX ops that carry EXP_TEX. The first version of the expansion
gated on EXP_TEX and never fired: inFAMOUS 2's deferred composite and its
sun pass read the normals G-buffer (0xE3C000, addr 0x00031303) with plain
TEX. Follow RPCS3's _process_texel: (round(x*255)-128)/127 on the biased
lanes (16-bit formats on 32767), after gamma and not on gamma lanes; an
EXP_TEX fetch takes x*2-1 and bypasses gamma. rsx_texture_expand_mask
marks 16-bit channels in bit 4; rsx_fp_texture_expand_units counts every
TEX/TXP/TXB/TXL on a biased unit.

Also: PS3RECOMP_ENG_MEMDUMP accepts "<n>s" (seconds after the first
frame) in place of a world frame, since frame counts drift with load
times; PS3RECOMP_ENG_SIGNLOG=1 lists units with signed or biased reads;
PS3RECOMP_ENG_TEXSTATE=1 prints the texture registers of full-screen
draws per fragment program; PS3RECOMP_METAL_PASS_LOG_FLUSH=1 logs the
slice a mid-frame submit_and_wait ends (the G-buffer pass lives there).

Tests: test_fp_decompiler 55/55, test_texture_layout, test_shader_msl

feat(port): decrypt the EBOOT and firmware without RPCS3 (tools/decrypt_self.py)

tools/decrypt_self.py turns a retail SELF into the ELF `rpcs3 --decrypt`
writes, byte for byte in layout (ELF header, program headers after it,
each segment at its p_offset, section headers at e_shoff, nothing else):
the NPDRM EBOOT.BIN with the player's .rap (rap_to_rif from rap2rifkey.py)
and the firmware .sprx (APP, key revision 0x1C). Based on
sp00nznet/twistedmetal's tools/decrypt_self.py (MIT). No key is in the
repository: they come from the player's key file (--keys / PS3_KEYS,
scetool format or name=hex lines), the RAP key also from PS3_RAP_KEY and
checked against its SHA-256. --selftest round-trips a synthetic SELF
(APP with a compressed segment, NPDRM local licence) with made-up keys.

rebuild.py: --decrypt-with auto|python|rpcs3 (auto: python when a key file
is given, RPCS3 stays the default and the fallback), --keys, --firmware DIR
(a dev_flash, its sys/external or any folder with the three .sprx). The
python path needs no RPCS3 and does not touch RPCS3's exdata; the checks
read the EBOOT's and the modules' key revision from their clear headers and
fail early on a key the file lacks. The decrypted modules are checked
against the hashes of the tested firmware 4.93 build, like the EBOOT.
install.json's dev_flash follows --firmware when it is a dev_flash tree.

rap2rifkey.py imports pycryptodome lazily so rebuild.py can parse a key
file before the venv exists.

fix(toolkit): _bx2 fetches always expand; stencil in the depth snapshot; on-demand frame dump

The fragment decompiler expanded a texture read to x*2-1 only when the
unit's SET_TEXTURE_ADDRESS asked for UNSIGNED_REMAP_BIASED. The _bx2
modifier (EXP_TEX, OPDEST bit 21) belongs to the instruction and expands
every lane whatever the texture's remap says. 213 of inFAMOUS 2's ~615
fragment programs read with TEX_bx2: every tangent-space normal map came
in unsigned (flat, wrong shading on all normal-mapped materials) and the
prop occlusion volumes' 8x8x8 cone LUT, whose values sit symmetrically
round 128, gave cone directions in one octant only, so the whole box
counted as occluded: solid black cubes round cafe tables and crates.
rsx_fp_texture_bx2_units names the units; the biased-remap rule stays
for plain fetches.

The depth-as-A8R8G8B8 snapshot now carries the stencil in its B lane
(a X32_Stencil8 view of the depth target): the deferred composite reads
its material flags there (bit 7 ambient scale, bit 5 no-SSAO) and the
occlusion volumes exclude characters through bit 6.

Tools: PS3RECOMP_METAL_DUMP_TRIGGER=<file> dumps every render target and
the next frame's pass log when the file appears (infamous2-lle
tools/play_dump.sh: play in a window, press Enter at the bad frame);

(0x100000 up, 0x200000 down, 0x400000 left, 0x800000 right); a log line

perf(rsx): build a frame's new shaders in parallel (PS3_SHADER_PARALLEL)

The toolkit half is patches/pending/shader-parallel.patch (Metal backend,
the PS3_SHADER_PARALLEL live toggle, an ftrace kind for the encode wait).
A pipeline miss now returns its handle at once and its HLSL -> MSL
translation, Metal library compile and pipeline state are built on a pool
of worker threads (PS3_SHADER_WORKERS, default performance cores minus
five, at least 2). Before any submission is encoded (flush, present, the
encoder thread) every pipeline its draws use is waited for, and the
waiting thread runs queued builds meanwhile, so no draw is skipped. Two
misses sharing a program translate it once; the function table, the
cache counters and the MSL buffers are per call or under a lock, and the
translator's once-only state is set up before the first worker starts.
Framebuffer-fetch pipelines stay serial (the copies fallback needs to
know at once). PS3_SHADER_PARALLEL=0 is the old path; PS3_SHADER_ASYNC=1
is unchanged.

9be4e99f1ef1bf49c214c0025967f4d391e716a6.message:
fix(port): block on RSX semaphore acquires so the composite sees the SPU light

Each frame inFAMOUS 2's FIFO copies the normals and depth targets into XDR
(0x07000B80 / 0x07384B80), writes label 134, and acquires label 137, which
the SPU light task writes once it has replaced those copies with the light
buffers (32x40 tiles around each light, zero elsewhere). With the toolkit
default the walker falls through the acquire, so the deferred composite's
textures were hashed and uploaded while XDR still held the normals and
depth: glossy props (Cole's Amp, the boat hull, bins, the winch) blew out
white because the depth copy's high byte drove the env-cube specular, the
lighting came out in normal colours with per-target MRT masks, and the
tiles the SPU had already written showed as screen-aligned rectangles.

run.sh now exports GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1 and GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS=200 (both
overridable), the bounded blocking acquire. The bound relies on
ps3_ms_now() counting on macOS (CLOCK_MONOTONIC, toolkit commit 48f8156);
no acquire timed out from boot to the pier and the frame count over 250 s
is within noise. ROADMAP: root cause, dump recipe, what is left to check.

9cf4a3ada29582d2497dfb02f8cf3331d40f2583.message:
fix(toolkit): fragment programs honour perspective_corr on texcoord reads SRC2 bit 31 (perspective_corr) multiplies a TC0..TC9 read by 1/w on the RSX, and the decompiler ignored it. New Marais's water writes uv*w into TC2 from the vertex program and samples its screen copy (VRAM 0x00E3C000) through TC2 with the bit set; read raw, uv*w lands far outside the copy and the river came out black. The read is now tcN * _rsx_inv_w(position) (RPCS3's * gl_FragCoord.w): glslang paths define RSX_FRAGCOORD_W_IS_RCP, since SPIR-V FragCoord.w and Metal's [[position]].w are already 1/w; under FXC the helper divides. 163 New Marais pixel shaders use the bit; others are byte-identical. Tests in test_fp_decompiler and test_shader_msl. Also two off-by-default diagnostics: RSX_FP_NAN_COLOR=1 (FP outputs that would be NaN magenta, Inf cyan) and PS3RECOMP_ENG_FPK_PIPE=

(the FP constants each draw through pipeline p receives).

a32c5f7982a670698054a8603a33739e8b688ff8.message:
fix(toolkit): PPU threads start with VSCR[NJ]=1; exact stfs/lfs, NJ-aware vcmp*fp, PPC NaN for fsqrt

The PS3 starts every PPU thread in VMX non-Java mode (RPCS3: nj = true),
but our zeroed context left VSCR at 0, so ~45k vmaddfp/vaddfp/... sites
kept denormals the PS3 flushes to zero (4.9M denormal operands/results in
a 7-minute New Marais walk). PS3_VSCR_NJ=0 restores the old value.

Also follow the PowerISA where RPCS3's interpreter uses host conversions:
- stfs/stfsx/stfsu/stfsux select the single word from the double's bits
  (truncation) instead of a rounding (float) cast; lfs keeps SNaNs;
- vcmpeqfp/vcmpgefp/vcmpgtfp/vcmpbfp flush denormal operands under NJ;
- fsqrt/frsqrte give the default +QNaN (x86 hosts gave a negative one).

Measured with a -DPPU_FP_AUDIT build over the same walk: 318M stfs, 655M
vcmp lanes, 0 sqrt/lfs NaNs, and none of these three changes altered a
single result in inFAMOUS 2; fps unchanged (A/B within noise). PPU
conformance: 0 failing ops; the three ISA-vs-RPCS3 deviations are accepted
only when ours equals an independent ISA reference (compare.py, README).

fix(toolkit): deliver GCM callbacks at sys_timer_usleep; light pass on the GPU by default (walk ~15 fps)

inFAMOUS 2 defers its FIFO put to its flip handler and then waits for the
ref register with usleep only. The runtime ran GCM callbacks only at HLE
imports, so the title depended on another thread's HLE calls; once the
light job finished at once (GPU light pass), ~1 run in 3 hung with get ==
put at a JUMP. ppu_gcm_pump now also runs at sys_timer_usleep/sleep: six
runs out of six clean.

Also: the light job's tile walk is skipped (light_skip_4578: iterator
atomics, label 135 and yield bookkeeping kept, no tile DMA); both copies
keep their write-back (the SSAO job reads the depth one); the SPU
runtime overhead cuts of ba8cd16 are back (+8%); a stuck-ref diagnostic
and per-job SPU DMA logs. run.sh enables the GPU light pass. New Marais
walk 14.3-15.0 fps, dock 16. SSAO job mapped (notes/ssao/).

b33bfc946e06eb3b3a9526f9a660526e3928aaaf.message:
fix(toolkit): SPU decrementer overflow; interrupt, atomic and label rate statistics

SPU_RdDec scaled elapsed nanoseconds by 79.8 MHz in 64 bits, which wraps
231 s after the context's base stamp; the SPURS kernel context never
rewrites its decrementer, so every timed loop on it saw the counter jump
forward by ~16 s of ticks at 231 s, 462 s, 693 s. Seconds and remainder are
scaled separately now.

Diagnostics for the cutscene stall, all off unless set: SPU_IRQSTAT (takes/s
per SPU with the last srr0 and events), SPU_ATOMICSTAT (GETLLARs per SPU
with the last line polled), RSX_LABELSTAT (back-end label writes per
window), and the SPU_STEPCAP dump now prints the loop's code words.

Roadmap: the stalled SPU runs the Edge geometry job (jobmod d0d15ec83992)
in lifted code, in a loop that leaves only on its time budget or when the
work drains, through the atomic output-ring allocation.

b3957499dbf4a2a915e919757c5b1cf4a93987dd.message:
fix(port): run the guest off the main thread when windowed on macOS

The Metal backend creates its window and pumps events with dispatch_sync onto
the main queue, and main() ran the guest on the main thread, which never
services that queue. The frame clock blocked in its first event pump, the FIFO
stopped draining, and the title spun on a fence: ./run.sh showed a grey
window that never drew (headless never pumps, so captures were unaffected).

Windowed, the guest now runs on its own thread with the 256 MB host stack
every guest thread gets, and the main thread turns the CFRunLoop. Headless
keeps the old layout. Verified: the window presents at ~29 fps through the
menu and the attract video.

check turned up along the way, all in the fork's patch:

ba8cd1605aacbb5d60c91aaed5e5c06986be9bb9.message:
perf(toolkit): cut SPU runtime overhead found by the first profile

A profile of the docks cutscene and pier put 23-31% of SPU time in runtime
helpers rather than the game's job code. The biggest pieces:

- spu_task_launch_check, run on every drain step, read five diagnostic
  flags atomically per call; with none set it now takes a short path that
  keeps only the end-of-job check.
- spu_check_stack_reset, also per step, read a thread-local (_tlv_get_addr
  on macOS) before comparing pc with its few entries; the compare is first.
- spu_overlay_note_get walked every registered overlay source on every DMA
  GET. A summary of the table (a bitset of the address sources' EAs, the
  union of the fixed-lift LS ranges, the 512-byte signature floor) skips GETs
  that cannot match anything; matches and their order are unchanged.
  Sources are only registered in constructors, before any SPU runs.
- cflts/cfltu: a NEON path (multiply by 2^scale, FCVTZS/FCVTZU) for lanes
  with an ordinary exponent; exponent-0 lanes forced to 0, any exponent-255
  lane takes the exact path. tests/test_spu_cflt_fast.c: 102.4 M conversions
  over all 256 scales and edge values, 0 mismatches.
- spu_ls_read128/spu_ls_write128 were left out of line in every lifted SPU
  file; they are always_inline now, with the watch hook kept out of line
  (both its call sites are behind the debug flag).

Before/after fps and SPU split pending the next profile run.

bb8235ef1a2ba90b7bdb84fa6fe87e6d40fd8295.message:
perf(toolkit): row copy for unscaled 2D blits; pacing, QoS, extra-SPU and usleep-spin knobs

New Marais profile (tools/profile_run.sh newmarais, samples at 250/400 s):
the 5 SPU threads are the title's own lifted SPURS kernel at ~96% busy
(~55% lifted job code, ~35% lifter runtime), the RSX thread spends
~50 ms of CPU per frame, a quarter of it in nv3089_blit copying the
1280x720 G-buffer surfaces to XDR pixel by pixel through vm_read32 /
vm_write32 for the SPU lighting. In the walking phase nobody is
saturated (SPUs 68%, RSX 55%, main thread 52% in the usleep(10)
light-task wait, the kicker thread 98% in usleep): the pipeline is
latency-bound there.

- cellGcmSys.c: unscaled NV3089 blits copy a row at a time with memmove
  and per-128-byte-line reservation bookkeeping (NV3089_ROWCOPY, default
  1; =0 restores the per-pixel copy the PPU_WWATCH/PPU_WVAL diagnostics
  see). The blit disappears from the RSX profile; fps unchanged at the
  dock, where the RSX is not the limit. cellGcm_drain_sema_blocked()
  reports a drain parked on a semaphore acquire.
- main.cpp: GCM_FLIP_IMMEDIATE=1 completes the flip at present time
  instead of on the 16 ms tick; GCM_SEMA_FASTPOLL=1 polls the parked
  drain every 1 ms instead of 4; PS3_HOT_QOS=1 raises the frame clock
  (and, in lv2_register.c, the SPU threads) to above-normal priority /
  QOS_CLASS_USER_INTERACTIVE. Interleaved A/B (base/exp/base/exp, 480 s):
  dock 12-13 fps and walk 7-8 fps on both sides, no proven gain; all off.
- lv2_register.c: SPURS_EXTRA_SPUS=<n> creates the CellSpursKernelGroup
  with n more threads cloned from the title's last one (r3 = spu num),
  keeps the workload max-contention bytes raised, and mirrors the
  signal-notification writes to the clones. Parked: libsre caps each
  workload's readyCount at its nSpus, so the clones never get work.
- sys_timer.c: PS3_USLEEP_SPIN_US=<n> makes POSIX guest sleeps of n us or
  less spin with sched_yield instead of nanosleep (macOS nanosleep(3 us)
  takes >= 50 us; the Windows branch always spun below 1 ms). 1

is set or clipping is off). PS3RECOMP_ENG_DEPTH_CLAMP=0 = old (live
toggle after PS3T_ENG_POLY_OFFSET). Headless next to the dock warehouse:

without; no fps cost.

persistent buffer dropped) twice in a dense street at ~20 fps, with

c8e3a00a2cd22f26905fc9a66e70e6cf6965d4a7.message:
fix(toolkit): Y16_X16 crossbar rule; FP debug output; gameplay-relative pad script

Y16_X16 (and HILO8) textures encode their crossbar in 16-bit blocks and
present the two channels interleaved R-G-R-G, or R-R-R-G when CONTROL1's
high word (the remap override) is set (RPCS3 decoded_remap). inFAMOUS 2's
water reads its 64x64 wave map through .yw with the override set; through
the plain ARGB table .w was the resource's empty alpha, 1.0, so every wave
normal was tilted by a whole unit. The engine now passes CONTROL1's bit 16
to the texture cache key and the backend.

Diagnostics: RSX_FP_DEBUG=<fp hash>:<n>:<reg[.swz]> returns the register
after the n-th emitted instruction as colour target 0 (an intermediate of a
long shader, on screen); PS3RECOMP_ENG_WORLD_MARK=<path> (+ _AFTER=<sec>)
marks the first gameplay frame and PAD_SCRIPT times written w<sec> count
from it, so a scripted walk lands on the same spot regardless of loading
time; the triggered pass log skips empty flush slices.

d72f62b64c2c0e1140b9f845919f6032a1dfc889.message:
feat: lift New Marais's relocatable SPU job code (spu_lifter --relocatable)

New Marais's SPU jobs are ~30 position-independent blobs the SPURS kernel
streams from the EBOOT (0x8E8C00-0x928150) to a different local-store
address on every run, so no fixed-address lift matched and they all ran
on the SPU interpreter.

Toolkit (patch):
- spu_lifter.py --relocatable: lift at LS 0; every LS address the code
  derives from its own position (link values, tail-branch pcs, drain
  return pcs, lqr/stqr, fallthrough and stub pcs) adds
  spu_context.code_base. Nested calls save and restore it; bra/brasl stay
  absolute and dispatch by address.
- runtime: spu_overlay_register_region_reloc(); a GET from the region's EA
  makes it resident at whatever LS address it targets. Dispatch (the lookup,
  the indirect branch, the fast path, the musttail path and the drain loop)
  resolves pc - lsa and sets code_base. Relocatable images answer only for
  their own id, never a wildcard. Resident code slots go from 4 to 16
  (SPU_RESIDENT_CODE_SLOTS), since a job batch stages eight or nine modules.

Port:
- tools/lift_relocmods.py finds the blobs by their shared header, lifts all
  30 and writes spu/relocmods_register.c. PS3_RELOCMODS=0 turns them off.

Measured in New Marais (same scripted route, a second game instance
running in both runs):

  interpreted SPU instructions over 8 min   14.8 G -> 2.4 G
  audio blocks with sound                   ~35%   -> 64-86%
  frame rate                                11-16  -> 10-16 (unchanged)

Rendering checked: Amp swing and running through the bayou draw correctly.
What stays interpreted: libsre's taskset-policy body at image 0x2A180
(LS 0xA00) and the register-save stub at LS 0x3FEC0.

fix(gfx): sun shadows inverted and 1.25x misplaced (pier at dusk)

Two toolkit bugs in every sun-shadow lookup, found at the start of the
dusk save (Cole on the pier) by recomputing the cascade mask on the CPU
from OCCDUMP data and reading the GPU's own values with FP_PATCH:

- The RSX depth compare is "stored texel OP reference" (RPCS3 flips the
  operator for its API samplers); the shadow helper compared the other
  way, so with the game's zfunc GREATER lit and shadowed were swapped:
  dark planks with bright streaks where shadows should be.
  PS3RECOMP_ENG_SHADOW_CMP=0 = old (live toggle).
- The 1024x1024 cascades live in a 1280-wide depth buffer at 0x0F2F0000
  and depth-format textures sampled the copy of the whole buffer, so
  every lookup landed 1.25x too far along x: no shadow under Cole,
  detached shadows of far casters, cascades 2/3 nearly shadowless. The
  copy is now the texture's top-left corner, as the colour-format copy
  was. PS3RECOMP_ENG_ZTEX_CROP=0 = old (live toggle).

After both, all three cascades match the game's math (mean |diff| 0.04 /
0.09 / 0.09) and the pier is sunlit with Cole's shadow at his feet.

dd686bb7a2a64c9385bdc695818f3129f208bdcf.message:
feat(toolkit): 3D textures; pad-script stick; draw-engine diagnostics

The dark translucent boxes round props were the occlusion-volume pass
(p113) looking up its per-prop cone LUT: an 8x8x8 volume texture
(SET_TEXTURE_FORMAT dimension 3, CONTROL3 depth 8) that the engine
uploaded as its first 8x8 slice and the decompiler sampled in 2D. 3D
textures now go end to end: rsx_swizzle_offset_3d (Morton x,y,z), a 3D
span and per-slice decode/upload in the draw engine, optional backend
entries texture_create_3d/texture_upload_3d (Metal MTLTextureType3D;
other backends keep the first slice as before), a volume mask the
fragment decompiler declares as Texture3D and samples with three
coordinates (TXP divides them by w), and the mask in the pipeline key.

Depth snapshots (the zeta read as a colour texture) are invalidated by
every depth-writing draw, so a reader later in the frame resolves again.

Diagnostics, all opt-in: PS3RECOMP_ENG_SKIP_FP (skip draws by fragment
program hash; PS3RECOMP_ENG_SHADER_DUMP writes manifest.txt with p= to
fp/vp hashes), PS3RECOMP_METAL_DBG_DUMPTEX (read back the texture a
pipeline samples), PS3RECOMP_ENG_TEXSTATE_PIPE (a pipeline's texture
registers with dimension, depth and border colour), PS3RECOMP_ENG_FPK_AFTER
and the [vpk] vertex-constant dump, PS3RECOMP_ENG_VPC_WATCH, TCONST_SLOT

the rest of the frame. The hung walks of that night sat exactly where such a
resync leaves the walker (get on the ring JUMP at put, park_off 0).

walker saw pass in steps of at most GCM_STALL_GAP_MS (live, default 100;

feat(diag): live A/B toggle file (PS3_TOGGLE_FILE) and tools/ab_live.sh

PS3_TOGGLE_FILE=<file> names a text file, one NAME=value per line, that the
frame clock re-reads every 250 ms when its mtime/size/inode changes. It
switches performance and debug knobs while the game runs, so an fps A/B
compares the same scene at the same moment inside one run. The idea comes from
gow3_pc's GOW3_TOGGLE_FILE; no code was taken from it.

Toolkit side (patches/pending/live-toggles.patch, fold into the toolkit
patch): include/ps3emu/ps3_toggles.h holds header-only state (weak, as in
ps3_ftrace.h, so the self-contained test compiles keep linking).
libs/misc/ps3_toggles.c holds the poll. Watchers rewrite the module-local ints
the hot paths always read, so without the variable behaviour and cost are as
before. Live: VCACHE (off drops the persistent buffers, on starts empty),
TEXHASH_FULL, SKIP_FP, SPU_FASTJOB, SPU_STUB_MICRO, SPU_STACK_HINT,
PS3_SPU_DRAIN_INLINE (new), PS3_DISPLAY_GAMMA, PS3_SHARPEN, PS3_AA, PS3_ANISO
(part of the sampler key) and PS3RECOMP_METAL_FPS. Each change logs
"[toggle] NAME old -> new" and leaves a PS3_FT_TOGGLE mark. PS3_FTRACE_KINDS
filters span kinds.

The same patch carries two texture re-hash fixes: textures under 64 bytes
are hashed bytewise, where they used to be never re-hashed, and the full hash
is due by age (last_full_frame, staggered per slot), where an alternate-frame
texture could miss its (frame + slot) & 7 turn forever.

every PERIOD s in a profile_run.sh run, and ftrace_report.py --phases splits

fix(gcm): decode the new-form FIFO JUMP; flip/catch-up stats

Measured whether the walker's fixed 64 KB catch-up draws frames it never
shows: it never fires in inFAMOUS 2, which flips through the import and
puts no flip word in its stream (0 catch-ups, every one of 8109 flip
requests presented in a 300 s walk), although its city frames are
1.5-2.3 MB of commands. The walk's hitches are first-use shader builds
(cold cache, drain on the CPU 85-97%) and, for the rest, the RSX thread
off the CPU (5-15% of the drain) on a host deep in swap.

- GCM_FLIP_STATS=1: flips, presents, never-shown flips, catch-ups,
  command bytes per frame, new-form JUMPs every 10 s; long drains with
  their CPU time.
- The walker decodes the RSX's second JUMP form (offset | 1) as well as
  0x20000000 | offset, in the main loop and the park check
  (libs/video/gcm_fifo_decode.h, tests/gcm_fifo_decode;
  GCM_FIFO_JUMP_NEW=0 = old). inFAMOUS 2 emits none.

The endless "Please wait..." box at dusk came back: after the PSN connect
dialog ends cancelled, inFAMOUS 2 still asks sceNpEulaCheckEulaStatus
(NID 0x59D1629A), which was unresolved, so its callback never came and the
game's online state machine waited in state 14 with its spinner up. The
toolkit now implements cellSysutilNpEula (CheckEulaStatus, Abort,
ShowCurrentEula, after RPCS3): the answer arrives through the callback on
the next sysutil poll, SCE_NP_EULA_ERROR offline (the game gives up
quietly: state 24, spinner closed), already-accepted with PS3_NET_ONLINE=1.

of a silent CELL_OK.

press (it did nothing before). Both send REQUEST_EXITGAME, then end the
process with status 0 after PS3_QUIT_GRACE_MS (3 s), never mid-save.
PS3_QUIT=1 is a new live toggle.

# inFAMOUS 2 — static recompilation for PC (macOS) 🌐 **English** · [Português (BR)](README.pt-BR.md) A native port of **inFAMOUS 2** (PS3, digital release `NPUA80638`) to **macOS/arm64**, built with static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C/C++ and compiled into a native executable, with graphics on Metal. a save being written finishes first | | Texture packs and more image effects (clarity, curves, colour presets) | 🧪 since v0.2.8, waiting for a windowed test | | Saves and trophies (in `~/Library/Application Support`), saves manager in the app | ✅ | | Brazilian Portuguese dub and subtitles (default), other languages your copy ships, DLC | ✅ | | The app: install, rebuild, play, settings, controls, saves, debug mode | ✅ [v0.2.16 alpha](https://github.com/erikomis/infamous2-recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.16) | | The app updates itself | ✅ since v0.2.7 (confirmed 2026-10-23: 0.2.7 updated itself to 0.2.9) | | Add to Steam (Big Picture with the controller) | 🧪 since v0.2.7, waiting for a test with Steam | | Whole game | ❓ nobody has gone past 1% yet | | Linux and Windows | ⏳ planned | Details and next steps in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). ## Download and play You need an Apple-silicon Mac and your own copy of inFAMOUS 2 (the PSN release `NPUA80638`, for example installed in [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net) with its `.rap` licence). > **Game version: 1.03 only.** The port is built for the game with its **1.03 > update** (`APP_VER 01.03`). Download `infamous2-recomp_0.2.22_aarch64.dmg` from the [v0.2.22 release](https://github.com/erikomis/infamous2-recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.22) (the [releases page](https://github.com/erikomis/infamous2-recomp/releases) lists any newer one) and drag the app to Applications. It is not notarized: the first time, right-click > Open (or System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway). 2. The app lists what your Mac still needs (Xcode Command Line Tools, a few Homebrew packages) and installs it with your OK. 3. Pick your game folder; the `.rap` is found on its own. Decryption uses RPCS3 if you have it, or your own key file and the PS3 firmware (a `dev_flash` folder or Sony's `PS3UPDAT.PUP`). No keys ship with the app. 4. **Install** (the first rebuild takes a few minutes), then **Play**. From v0.2.7 on, the app updates itself: the Updates card on Home offers **Download and install**, then **Restart to finish** (signed and checked; "Check for updates automatically" can be turned off). After an update it offers **Rebuild the game**. On v0.2.6 or older, install the new app by hand once. The release ships no game files: the app recompiles the game on your Mac. ## The app [`launcher/`](launcher/README.md) is a desktop app (Tauri) that does all of this without a terminal, in the game's own look: Home (your copy's art, PLAY, quick settings, last save, status), Graphics, Performance, Game, Controls and Advanced. - **Install / rebuild** with a progress bar: checks and installs the tools, finds your copy and its `.rap`, decrypts with RPCS3 or without it. - **Graphics:** window, fullscreen or borderless, screen, vsync, gamma, anisotropic filtering, FXAA or SMAA, sharpening (CAS), vibrance, contrast, MetalFX upscaling, fps counter, and ready-made profiles (Performance / Balanced / Quality). macOS Game Mode turns on in fullscreen. - **Controls:** remap keyboard, mouse and controller, mouse camera, vibration; **audio** volume and output; **game language** (the ones your copy ships), with the voice and the subtitles/menus each in its own language if you like (e.g. English voice, Portuguese subtitles). - **Saves:** list, back up, restore, import/export with RPCS3, `.zip`. - **Trophies:** the game's trophies with your unlocks (names and icons from your copy), and a "Trophy unlocked" notice in the game. - **Community patches** from your own RPCS3 patch file: skip the intro, a wider field of view. - **Debug mode** (Advanced > Debug mode): play normally while the game logs what goes wrong (missing functions, shader/texture failures, GPU stalls, SPU faults, audio falling behind, files it cannot open, frame-rate drops) and keeps a timed index of the session; press **F12** in the game (or **Capture this frame** in the app) when something looks wrong: it saves the frame's render targets and a screenshot of the next frame exactly as the window shows it (`surf/screen_-.png`, after supersampling, sharpening, colour effects and the F1 menu). Afterwards **Analyse** runs `infamous2-lle/tools/log_triage.py` on the session and lists the top issues (also in `triage.md` in the session folder, for a developer or an agent to go through), and **Create .zip** packs it all for an issue. Details in [launcher/README.md](launcher/README.md#debug-mode-report-a-problem). Plus a **game log viewer** that follows the log live. - **Updates card:** downloads and installs a newer app version (signed, verified, one click and a restart), and offers a rebuild when the installed game is older than the app's sources. - **Your copy's icon** in the Dock for the app and the game (read from your install, never shipped). - **Play shortcut** (Home > Status): a "Play inFAMOUS 2" icon on the Desktop that opens the app and starts the game at once with your settings. - **Add to Steam** (Home > Status, optional): inFAMOUS 2 as a non-Steam game with cover art made from your copy, to start from Big Picture with the controller; **Remove from Steam** takes it out again. **In the game,** F1 (fn+F1), Cmd+, or L3+R3 opens the **in-game menu**: image (gamma, sharpening, FXAA/SMAA, vibrance, contrast, clarity, curves, colour presets, MetalFX, vsync, display mode, internal resolution, aspect ratio), audio volume, controls (live remapping of keyboard, mouse and controller, "play with" controller / keyboard and mouse / both, vibration, mouse), the game's voice and text languages, a performance HUD (fps, frame time, CPU/GPU) and **Quit game**. A DualSense that switches off comes back by itself within about a second. | | | | --- | --- | | [](launcher/docs/screenshots/home.en.png) | [](launcher/docs/screenshots/graphics.png) | CI builds it for macOS, Windows and Linux on every change (the game itself builds only on macOS so far); the installers are not signed yet. ## Known problems - Fixed in v0.2.12: sun shadows were inverted and out of place (dark ground with bright hard-edged streaks, no shadow under Cole, shadows detached from what cast them). The shadow-map compare ran the wrong way round, and the maps were read through a copy 1.25x too wide. The doubled sun shadows on some ground in daylight most likely had the same cause; not confirmed in a window yet. - A rare hang during the city load: seen in 2 of 9 headless runs on a heavily loaded Mac, with and without the v0.2.12 shadow fix. Report it if it happens to you. - The first time the game shows a new effect, its shaders have to be built, which stalls the game. A frame's new shaders now build in parallel on a few worker threads and nothing is drawn without them (`PS3_SHADER_PARALLEL=0` restores the old one-at-a-time build): in New Marais the worst such frame went from ~340 ms to ~100 ms with a filled shader cache and from ~3 s to ~1 s with an empty one. Windowed play caches the translations, so each one is paid once; `PS3_SHADER_ASYNC=1` builds them in the background instead (some objects appear a moment late). - Fixed in v0.2.5: facades turned away from the sun (and Cole's back and sides) went black, and sun shadows were missing everywhere. The sun shadow maps were read from an empty colour buffer at the same address as their depth buffer, so every surface counted as sunlit and the unclamped sun term went negative on the far side. The occlusion-volume passes (soft contact shadows), skipped while they were the suspect, are drawn again since v0.2.8. - Windows and Linux are not supported yet. - With less than about 3 GB free on the disk the game shows a "not enough space" error at boot, which in the window is just a black screen. ## Work in progress What is being worked on now (details in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md)): - **Playing the whole story:** nobody has gone past 1% yet, so later missions may break; `tools/play_capture.sh` records what a graphics bug needs in a windowed session. - **Doubled sun shadows in daylight:** most likely gone with the v0.2.12 shadow fix; waiting for a look in a window, in daylight. - **The rare city-load hang** (see Known problems): so far seen only on a heavily loaded Mac. - **MetalFX temporal upscaling, HDR (EDR) and TAA:** not started; the temporal ones need motion vectors. - **Windows and Linux:** planned. - **Pull requests to [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp):** 68 of Erik's PRs have been merged; the latest batch, on 2026-10-26, took most of rounds 6 to 8 and the polygon-offset fix (#562). A few are still open (#470 and #545 among them), plus issue #546, a proposal for internal resolution, texture packs and more grading upstream. ## Building from source The app does all of this for you; by hand, from a terminal: ### What you need - An Apple Silicon Mac (tested on an M4 Pro, macOS 27). - A legitimate copy of inFAMOUS 2 installed in [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), **with the 1.03 update** (`APP_VER 01.03`; the base game 01.00 does not work), its license (`.rap`) and the PS3 firmware installed there. - Xcode Command Line Tools and Homebrew: ```sh brew install cmake ninja sdl2 glslang spirv-cross spirv-tools python@3.12 python3.12 -m venv .venv ``` ### Building ```sh git clone https://github.com/erikomis/infamous2-recomp.git cd infamous2-recomp tools/setup_toolkit.sh # toolkit in ./ps3recomp-fork .venv/bin/pip install -r ps3recomp-fork/requirements.txt ``` Then one command does the rest (decrypt, translate, compile), from your copy and its licence: ```sh python3 infamous2-lle/tools/rebuild.py --game "/dev_hdd0/game/NPUA80638" --rap ``` `--dry-run` lists the steps and checks every prerequisite first. By default the EBOOT and the firmware are decrypted with RPCS3; without RPCS3, pass your own key file (scetool format) with `--keys KEYFILE`, and the firmware as Sony's `PS3UPDAT.PUP` with `--firmware PS3UPDAT.PUP`. No keys ship with this repository. The manual recipe is in [`infamous2-lle/README.md`](infamous2-lle/README.md#rebuilding). Translation takes a few minutes and compiling ~80 s on an M4 Pro. ## Playing from the terminal ```sh cd infamous2-lle ./run.sh ``` A controller (DualSense tested) works out of the box. One that is switched off and on again mid-game (a DualSense on Bluetooth that went to sleep), or plugged in later, is picked up again by itself, on the PS3 port it had; no restart needed. Keyboard and mouse add on top of it: | Key | PS3 | | --- | --- | | W A S D | le

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   └── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management

│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations

│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
```
