# Imabikisō · PC Recompilation **Bringing 忌火起草 to PC, with an experimental machine-translated English edition.** An independent, community-led project built with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). **Windows prototype · Early scenes running · English preview · Work in progress** [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [Progress](#progress) · [What works](#what-works-today) · [Build & source](#code-and-building) · [English translation](#english-machine-translation) · [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)
--- Imabikisō is a Japanese horror visual novel from Chunsoft. This project explores running the PS3 release **BLJM60042 / 01.00** as a native PC program through static recompilation, alongside tools for extracting, understanding and patching its scripts. **The port uses the original game's code recompiled through ps3recomp.** The earlier custom C++ engine experiment was abandoned and is no longer part of the current source tree. The goal is to preserve the original engine and behavior; complete fidelity has not yet been achieved or verified. The remaining C++ archive/script tools support extraction and translation rather than replacing the game engine. The current prototype boots, renders the opening and reaches the first classroom narration. A separate English preview replaces some menus and opening text. **This is an experimental developer build, not a finished port or a verified full playthrough.** No game executable, generated game code, disc image, fonts, sound or video is included. You need your own game dump and locally generated files to build and run the native port. ## Screenshots Actual captures from the native PC prototype, showing the **English machine-translation draft**. The title logo remains Japanese. Captured on 14 October 2026; click an image for the full 1280 × 720 PNG. | English title menu | Opening prologue | |:---:|:---:| | [![Title screen with New Game and Continue in English](docs/screenshots/01-english-menu.png)](docs/screenshots/01-english-menu.png) | [![Opening scene displaying Why me in English](docs/screenshots/02-prologue-why-me.png)](docs/screenshots/02-prologue-why-me.png) | | **New Game / Continue** | **“Why me……?”** | | Prologue narration | First classroom text | |:---:|:---:| | [![Prologue displaying A hallucination. It has to be.](docs/screenshots/03-prologue-hallucination.png)](docs/screenshots/03-prologue-hallucination.png) | [![School scene with the first classroom narration in English](docs/screenshots/04-classroom-english.png)](docs/screenshots/04-classroom-english.png) | | **“A hallucination. It has to be.”** | **First classroom narration rendered in English** | [Full-resolution gallery and captions](docs/screenshots/README.md). These stills show rendering and text only; occasional audio gaps remain. ## Progress ![Development progress: estimated overall engineering readiness 51%; detailed breakdown below](docs/assets/progress.png) **Updated: 15 October 2026.** The chart is a planning estimate based on the milestones below. It is **not** an automated compatibility score, a percentage of the story that is playable, or a release-date prediction. Full-game compatibility remains largely untested. | Workstream | Estimate | Current evidence | Still to do | |---|---:|---|---| | Boot & runtime | 90% | Startup, system callbacks, fonts and initial loading run | Regression tests and less common system paths | | Graphics & pacing | 75% | Opening and classroom render at ~60 presentations/s; NV0039 buffer copies implemented (fixes the purple/green panorama scenes); glyphs no longer drawn into the game's text atlas (fixes striped/ghost letters) | Wider effects coverage, scene regressions | | Input & save/load | 65% | Keyboard/controller confirmation and early save/load exercised | Longer sessions, all menus and save-slot edge cases | | Audio | 55% | Mixer consumes guest blocks on a steady 5.33 ms clock (half-written blocks gone); SPU busy-waits removed | Occasional voice starvation, longer-session checks | | Movies | 70% | All movies (MPEG-1 1280x720) decoded natively on the PC and handed to Sofdec; logo jingle in sync, decode tasks ~0.3 ms instead of ~50 ms | Alpha/effect movies and seamless loops across many scenes still to be checked | | Full-game validation | 10% | Opening and first classroom tested | Branches, routes, endings, long-session stability | | English story coverage | 0.17% draft | 33 of 19,018 exported script entries; 27 UI labels separately | Machine translation, layout checks, context and terminology review | Overall **51%** is a weighted planning score, rounded to a whole number. It deliberately gives substantial weight to audio, movies and full-game testing. [Weights and definitions](docs/roadmap.md#how-the-percentages-work) · [Source data](docs/progress.json). ## What works today - PS3 startup proceeds through the early initialization barriers and system callbacks. - The live renderer displays the opening, backgrounds and first story text. - Font handling, text encoding and callback thread-local state have been corrected for the tested paths. - Input responds after a pad capability structure fix. Japanese confirmation uses **Circle**. - Early save data is written and loaded with the correct filename. - A separate English preview displays the title-menu labels, prologue and first classroom lines. - The script tools can read archives, export stable text IDs and rebuild a translated script archive with structural checks. ## Known problems **Occasional audio gaps remain.** Crackling is largely gone since the mixer was paced, but a voice stream can still briefly starve. Movies are decoded natively and played smoothly in the scenes tested; alpha/effect movies elsewhere are unchecked. One freeze was seen once when the opening movie started from the title screen (an SPU decode task was halted); it did not reproduce in later runs. The rest of the game has not been validated. Later effects, menus, choices, routes and long sessions may expose rendering errors, freezes or crashes. Some UI text is stored in images and remains Japanese. There is no release date yet. See the [roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) for the next milestones and what must pass before a playable release. ## English machine translation The planned English edition will use **machine translation assisted by AI**. It will be labeled as such; it is not an official localization or a professional human translation. The current preview contains **33 draft script entries and 27 menu/dialog labels**. That is a small technical and layout test, not a translated game. Story coverage is calculated from the 19,018 exported main-script entries; menu labels are counted separately because the full UI inventory is not complete. The intended workflow is to translate by stable script ID, preserve control instructions, use a consistent glossary, and check the result in-game for overflow, missing glyphs and broken choices. Human corrections are welcome. The English files load from a separate local preview directory with separate saves/settings. [English preview text](translations/en/preview.json) · [Translation workflow](translations/README.md) · [Patching documentation](docs/patching.md) ## Code and building | Directory | Contents | |---|---| | [`src/`](src/) | Supporting C++ archive, script and translation tools | | [`native/`](native/) | Native port runner, ABI bridges and CMake integration | | [`launcher/`](launcher/) | Windows launcher: setup from your own disc image, language choice, settings, Play | | [`patches/ps3recomp/`](patches/ps3recomp/) | Local runtime/lifter fixes against a pinned upstream commit | | [`translations/`](translations/) | English draft text and workflow | | [`docs/`](docs/) | Format research, progress data and technical notes | | [`tools/`](tools/) | Progress-chart generation and diagnostics | ### Build the asset and translation tools Requirements: CMake 3.20+, a C++20 compiler and Ninja (or another CMake generator). Non-Windows builds also need Iconv. ```sh cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure ``` ```sh imbk verify "Imabikisou (Japan).iso" imbk sns text "Imabikisou (Japan).iso" out/lines.tsv imbk unpack "Imabikisou (Japan).iso" out/disc imbk patch "Imabikisou (Japan).iso" out/translation.tsv out/disc ``` These commands build the supporting tools, **not the native game executable**. The native game uses the ps3recomp integration below; there is no custom replacement-engine target. ### Build the native port The tested configuration is **Windows x64, Direct3D 12, clang-cl and an AVX2-capable CPU**. Other configurations are not validated by this project. The public sources require your locally decrypted ELF and locally lifted PPU/SPU sources; those are intentionally excluded. The SDK changes are pinned to `a2c20108af45174dbb7d3e2f87f6acaaef09c6b4`. This is a developer workflow, not a one-click installer. Follow [native/README.md](native/README.md) for patch application, private inputs, configuration and controls. ## Next milestones - [ ] Eliminate the reproducible audio interruptions in the opening jingle. - [ ] Keep movie decoding and sound synchronized through demanding sections. - [ ] Validate longer play sessions, choices and save/load regressions. - [ ] Extend the English machine-translation pipeline with glossary and layout checks. - [ ] Record a representative progress video with the current limitations clearly identified. ## People, tools and acknowledgements This is a human-directed project developed with assistance from **ChatGPT / Codex (OpenAI)** and **Claude Opus (Anthropic)** for code, reverse-engineering analysis, debugging and translation experiments. AI assistance does not imply endorsement by either company, and generated suggestions still need testing and review. Special thanks to **sp00nznet and the ps3recomp contributors** for the recompilation framework, and to the original creators of Imabikisō. Additional testing, technical contributions and corrections are welcome. ## License and game files Project code is MIT-licensed; see [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). # ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).


## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

1420202924.readme_excerpt:
# Folklore Native Port

An experimental native port of Folklore for PlayStation 3, using game-specific static recompilation with [PS3Recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp).

**An experimental Windows Owner Build Kit is available.** It generates and compiles the native executable from your own supported copy, then creates a launcher and separate save profile. A fresh ZIP installation has completed on the development PC. Clean-machine installation and gameplay acceptance of this exact kit remain pending.

| I want to | Go here |
| --- | --- |
| Download the Owner Build Kit | [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/dawoodtogoo2020-code/folklore-native-port/releases) |
| Build and install from my own copy | [Installation instructions and limits](INSTALL.md) |
| Generate textures from my own copy | [Texture tool instructions](tools/textures/README.md) |
| Review changes and validation | [Owner build notes](docs/OWNER_BUILD.md), [earlier source preview](docs/SOURCE_PREVIEW.md) |
| Read about motion-control support | [Motion controls](docs/MOTION_CONTROLS.md) |
| See known engine problems | [Open issues and fix plans](docs/OPEN_ISSUES.md) |
| Report a reproducible problem | [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/dawoodtogoo2020-code/folklore-native-port/issues) |

## What is included

- `engine/`: the current PS3Recomp development fork, with Vulkan/hybrid rendering, DLSS diagnostics and projection fixes, texture replacement loading and motion-control backends.
- `client/`: authored native boot integration, launcher, platform and development build tools.
- `Install.py`: graphical owner-copy setup. The release kit also includes validated public CACAO shaders.
- `tools/textures/`: archive extraction, heuristic classification, 2x/4x pack generation, resumable verification and synthetic tests. No game artwork is bundled.
- `scripts/` and `tests/`: the earlier bounded PPU probe and frame-rate constant scanner, with independent synthetic tests.

[The original export manifest](docs/source-export.json) identifies the earlier source-preview revisions and file hashes; subsequent changes are tracked in Git. The Owner Build Kit contains a separate package manifest. Private histories, captured game payloads and generated game executables are excluded. See [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for component licensing.

## What works and what is pending

Private Windows development builds have reached menus and gameplay, loaded saves, exercised ultrawide presentation and used locally generated texture packs. These observations do not establish a clean public installation or full campaign correctness.

The owner-copy pipeline now derives bounded function/import metadata, reproduces 26 PPU and 27 SPU acceptance outputs, validates shader inputs and builds without Git or private development directories. Python and MSYS2 CLANG64 dependencies are installed separately. See [the build validation receipt](docs/owner-build-validation.json).

The source adds physical-sensor paths for SDL controllers, original DS3/SXS and GameSir, plus an optional stick-flick mapping and Nintendo face-button positioning. Mocked tests pass; physical soul-capture acceptance remains open.

The isolated renderer changes pass offline compilation, shader validation and synthetic motion tests. They have not been accepted through matched gameplay captures. DLSS jitter/performance, HDR/exposure, asynchronous frame alignment, AO/transparency, audio continuity and 60 FPS garment physics remain active work. Hybrid lighting retains rasterized primary shading and simplified secondary materials; it is not complete source-faithful path tracing. Frame generation is not accepted gameplay functionality.

Windows is the development target. Linux/Steam Deck, Android and macOS do not have validated public player packages. Do not infer gameplay or platform support from source presence or a passing CPU test.

## Validation tools

The small public probe tests require Python 3 and no game files:

```sh
python -B -m unittest discover -s tests
```

Texture tests require Pillow and use synthetic images/archives:

```sh
python -B -m unittest discover -s tools/textures
```

DLSS motion analyzer and projection tests:

```sh
python -B -m unittest discover -s engine/tests -p test_analyze_dlss_motion.py
python -B engine/tests/test_dlss_projection.py --cc clang++ --out build/projection-test
```

`scripts/frame_constants.py --elf path/to/EBOOT.elf` scans an owner's decrypted executable for timing-constant leads. It does not change the game or prove which subsystem controls physics. `scripts/leaf_probe.py --help` describes the bounded PPU probe. Neither command installs the port.

## License and collaboration

Original standalone material identified in [LICENSE](LICENSE) is source available under a custom personal-use license. The combined engine/native runtime includes GPL-2.0-only material and retains GPL rights, with MIT/LGPL/other notices for its components. Root personal-use restrictions do not override those rights. Read [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) before reuse or distribution.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for collaboration. Do not post game assets, firmware, keys, saves, generated game code or private diagnostics in issues. This is an unofficial project; no rights to Folklore content or trademarks are granted.

# God of War: Ascension for PC

A native Linux port of **God of War: Ascension** (PlayStation 3, BCUS98232), built by static
recompilation with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp).

The game's PPU and SPU machine code is translated ahead of time into C/C++ and compiled together with
a runtime that reimplements the PS3 hardware and firmware libraries: LV2 system calls, SPURS, GCM,
the RSX graphics chip (on Vulkan), audio, video decoding, input and file systems. There is no
emulator and no interpreter in the main path. This repository holds the game-specific part of the
port: the pipeline that turns your dump into a native executable, the PC entry point, input, settings,
the in-game menu and the launcher.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **You must own an original copy of the game.** This repository contains no part of God of War:
> Ascension: no executables, assets, translated code or game license keys, and it does not download
> them. The port only works with files you dump yourself from a copy you legally own: the BCUS98232
> Blu-ray disc and the 1.12 update obtained for it. Everything is generated locally from those files
> and must stay on your machine.
>
> - Do not share the game files, the generated executable, the translated code (`out/`,
>   `recompiled/`, `spu/`) or anything else produced from the game. They are derived from copyrighted
>   material.
> - Requests for game files, keys or ready-made builds are not answered and are removed from the issues
>   and the [Discord](https://discord.gg/HCHyR3GYWm).
> - This project does not help to run pirated copies and is not a way to play the game without buying
>   it.
>
> This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Santa Monica
> Studio. God of War is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment.

## Status

**Work in progress, not playable yet.** The port boots, runs the menus and starts a new game, but the
first level runs far too slowly to play.

- Opening video, title screen, 3D menus, profile selection and the Single Player menu.
- A new game loads the first level, plays the opening cinematic in the engine and reaches player
  control: the first tutorials ("Dodge", "Attacks") respond to input.
- Performance (measured under Xvfb): 3D menu ~10 FPS, opening video ~28 FPS, new-game cinematic
  ~30 FPS, first level ~3 FPS. The current bottlenecks are SPU jobs (EDGE geometry) and the RSX
  thread.

**Known issues**
- The first level is not playable at its current frame rate.
- Rare SPURS kernel hangs when the kernel runs workloads on parallel threads (about 1 in 7 runs).
- Physical controllers are untested; keyboard and mouse are.
- No upscaling or adjustable internal resolution.
- Saving on exit is not guaranteed.

## What works

- **Static recompilation pipeline:** reads the disc image and the 1.12 update dumped from your own
  copy, accepts a user-supplied ELF and translates its PPU and SPU code, including the WWS
  job modules and the SPU code the game generates at run time.
- **Graphics:** the ps3recomp RSX backend on Vulkan, with a persistent shader cache and optional
  background shader compilation.
- **Input:** keyboard, mouse and SDL2 gamepads at the same time on port 0, with two remappable keys per
  PS3 button.
- **Launcher** (Tk): game status and save backups, display mode and window size, VSync, FPS counter,
  MangoHud and GameMode, controls, diagnostics switches and a live log with per-run history.
- **In-game menu** (Dear ImGui) and an FPS counter overlay.

## Requirements

- Linux x86-64 and a GPU with a Vulkan driver.
- clang, CMake, Ninja, 7-Zip, Vulkan headers, SDL2, FFmpeg and Python 3 with Tk.
- A legally owned copy of the game: an ISO dumped from your own BCUS98232 disc (version 1.00) and
  the PKG of the 1.12 update, plus a legally prepared ELF of the actual 1.12 game executable.
  Nothing is downloaded and no game file is provided.

**Build notes**
- The translated SPU code is compiled with `-march=x86-64-v3` (AVX2/FMA) by default. On a CPU without
  AVX2, configure with `-DPORT_SPU_MARCH=x86-64-v2`.
- The translated PPU sources are very large, so compiling them takes a lot of memory per job. Pick the
  number of parallel jobs to fit your RAM (`BUILD_JOBS` for `scripts/build.sh`, 6 by default;
  `-j` for `cmake --build`); fewer jobs use less memory but take longer.

## Building

### 1. Get the sources

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This port does **not** build against upstream ps3recomp. It needs the **`gowa-fixes` branch** of
> the fork [RichardFontoura/ps3recomp](https://github.com/RichardFontoura/ps3recomp/tree/gowa-fixes),
> which carries the runtime, SPURS, GCM/RSX/Vulkan, SPU and lifter fixes this game depends on.
> The fork's default branch (`master`) and upstream `sp00nznet/ps3recomp` do not have these fixes:
> always pass `--branch gowa-fixes` when cloning.

Clone both repositories side by side, with the fork on `gowa-fixes`:

```bash
mkdir gowa-src && cd gowa-src
git clone https://github.com/RichardFontoura/gowa-pc.git
git clone --branch gowa-fixes https://github.com/RichardFontoura/ps3recomp.git
git -C ps3recomp branch --show-current   # must print: gowa-fixes
```

The result is:

```
gowa-src/
├── gowa-pc/     this repository
└── ps3recomp/   the fork, on the gowa-fixes branch
```

`../ps3recomp` is the default location for the CMake presets and the scripts. If you keep the fork
somewhere else, point to it with `PS3RECOMP=/path/to/ps3recomp` (scripts) and
`-DPS3RECOMP_DIR=/path/to/ps3recomp` (CMake). When you update this repository, update the fork too,
since both move together:

```bash
git -C gowa-pc pull
git -C ps3recomp pull   # still on gowa-fixes
```

Then create a Python environment with the ps3recomp tool requirements. It can live anywhere;
activate it before running the scripts, or set `GOWA_PYTHON` to its interpreter:

```bash
python3 -m venv ~/.venvs/gowa
~/.venvs/gowa/bin/pip install -r ps3recomp/requirements.txt ninja
source ~/.venvs/gowa/bin/activate        # or: export GOWA_PYTHON=~/.venvs/gowa/bin/python
cd gowa-pc
```

### 2. Prepare the game files

```bash
scripts/extract_update.sh /path/to/patch-1.12.pkg   # -> game/update
scripts/extract_disc.sh /path/to/disc.iso           # -> game/disc (refuses incomplete ISOs)
```

Instead of passing the paths, you can set `GOWA_DUMPS` to a folder that holds the ISO and the PKG.

Supply a legally prepared ELF of the actual 1.12 game executable as `game/GOWA.update.ELF`,
then create the input link used by the pipeline:

```bash
ln -s GOWA.update.ELF game/EBOOT.ELF
```

With the 1.12 update, `USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` is only a small loader that starts `GOWA.SELF`, the real
game executable. The supplied ELF must correspond to that game executable, not the loader.
The `GOWA.update.ELF` filename also lets the runner select the update's boot path automatically.
The current source tree does not include a decryption tool or decryption constants. Keep the ELF
and all generated files local. Existing installations with this ELF/link can continue to the next step.

### 3. Translate and build

```bash
scripts/analyze.sh       # imports, ELF header, SPU images and the WWS job policy module -> analysis/
scripts/lift.sh          # PPU -> out/, recompiled/
python3 scripts/extract_jobmods_elf.py game/EBOOT.ELF --out analysis/jobmods
scripts/lift_spu.sh      # SPU images and the WWS policy module -> spu/
python3 ../ps3recomp/tools/lift_jobmods.py --jobmods analysis/jobmods \
    --out spu --register spu/jobmods_register.c
scripts/build.sh         # linux-vulkan preset by default (also linux-vulkan-debug, linux-null)
```

Incremental builds afterwards: `cmake --build build/linux-vulkan -j<jobs>`, with a job count that
fits your RAM.

**Optional: position-independent SPU fragments.** Some jobs copy SPU code to local-store addresses
chosen at run time. Without translated fragments the SPU interpreter runs that code, much more slowly.
To translate them, run the game once with `SPU_PIC_CAPTURE=<file>`, then
`python3 scripts/lift_spu_fragments.py <file> --overlay 210` and build again.

All generated files stay out of git: `game/` (extracted dumps and decrypted ELFs), `out/` and
`recompiled/` (translated PPU), `spu/` (translated SPU), `analysis/`, `build/`, `gamedata/` (saves
and the virtual HDD) and `scratch/` (temporary files).

## Playing

```bash
scripts/launcher.sh          # settings and the Play button
scripts/launcher.sh --play   # start straight away with the saved settings
scripts/run.sh               # diagnostic entry point (ignores the launcher settings)
```

The launcher needs Tk in the Python it runs with (`GOWA_PYTHON`, or `python3` from `PATH`). If that
Python has no Tk, `GOWA_TK_DIR` can point to an unpacked Tk 8.6 library folder (with `libtk8.6.so`
and `tk8.6/`).

Settings live in `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/gowa-pc/` (`GOWA_CONFIG_DIR` changes the folder):

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `settings.json` | launcher settings (schema 2; schema 1 is migrated on load) |
| `game.ini` | options shared with the in-game menu (`key=value`); the game gets its path in `GOWA_GAME_INI` |
| `last_run.log` | timestamped log of the last run started with Play |
| `logs/<UTC>-<id>/` | per-run history: raw output, JSONL events, metadata and an exit summary |
| `savedata_backups/` | save copies made before every run (the 10 most recent) |
| `frames.csv` | frame times, when enabled under Diagnostics |

### Launcher

- **Game:** installation status, save backup and restore (`gamedata/dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata`).
  Saves are copied before every run; a failed backup is logged and does not block the game. Restoring
  requires the game to be closed, asks for confirmation and backs up the current saves first.
- **Graphics:** display mode (windowed, borderless, fullscreen), window size (1280×720, 1600×900,
  1920×1080 or the monitor), VSync and the FPS counter (corner, scale, opacity and items), all stored
  in `game.ini`. MangoHud and GameMode prefix the command and are disabled when not installed.
- **Controls:** two keys per button, capture on click (key or mouse button), duplicate-key warning
  and a reset button.
- **Diagnostics:** `RSX_FRAME_CSV`, `RSX_VK_TEXTURE_COMPUTE`, `RSX_VK_RAW_TEXTURES`,
  `RSX_TEX_HASH_FULL`, `VDEC_PERF`, `SPURS_KERN_THREADS`, `SPURS_KERN_PARALLEL` and `GCM_FLIP_MIN_MS`.
  Only values that differ from the `scripts/run.sh` defaults are exported; a variable already set in
  the terminal wins.
- **Log:** the last 6000 lines with errors and gaps highlighted, counters, copy, clear and open
  folder. Clearing the view never deletes the per-run history.

### In game

**Insert** (or **R3 + L2** on a controller) opens the PC menu and **F10** toggles the FPS counter.
Both keys are reserved and cannot be remapped.

| PS3 button | Key 1 | Key 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Cross | Space | K |
| Square | Left mouse | J |
| Triangle | Right mouse | I |
| Circle | F | L |
| L1 / R1 | Left Shift / E | — |
| L2 / R2 | Q / R | — |
| L3 / R3 | Left Ctrl / Middle mouse | — / C |
| Start / Select | Escape / Tab | Enter / — |
| D-pad ↑ → ↓ ← | 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 | — |
| Evade (while held, WASD becomes the right stick) | Left Alt | — |

WASD is the left stick and the arrow keys the right stick. Keyboard, mouse and the first SDL gamepad
share port 0, and losing window focus releases all input. Remapping takes effect on the next run.

## How it works

| Part | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Pipeline | `scripts/` | Extracts the dumps, decrypts the executables, analyses the ELF and drives the PPU/SPU lifters |
| Translated code | `recompiled/`, `spu/` (generated) | The game's PPU functions and SPU programs as C/C++ |
| Runtime | [ps3recomp](https://github.com/RichardFontoura/ps3recomp) (`gowa-fixes`) | LV2 syscalls, HLE firmware libraries (SPURS, GCM, audio, video, file systems), SPU runtime and the RSX Vulkan backend |
| Entry point | `main.cpp`, `stubs.cpp` | Reserves guest memory, sets up the virtual file system, starts the runtime and the frame clock, and boots the game |
| PC layer | `pc/` | SDL2 input mapping (`input.cpp`), `game.ini` settings (`game_ini.cpp`) and the ImGui menu and FPS overlay (`overlay.cpp`) |
| Launcher | `launcher/` | Tk launcher: settings, controls, save backups, diagnostics and run logs |
| Tests | `tests/`, `scripts/test_pc.sh` | Input, settings and launcher unit tests that need no game assets, plus window smoke tests and benchmarks |

## Contributing

Bug reports, investigations and pull requests are welcome. Contributions reach `main` only through pull
requests from forks; direct pushes are blocked.

1. Fork the repository and create a branch in your fork.
2. Commit your change there and open a pull request against `main`.
3. A maintainer reviews it; once approved and with every conversation resolved, it is squashed into
   `main`. Pushing new commits after a review asks for a new review.

- **Report issues** with the log of the failing run (`last_run.log` or the folder under `logs/`), the
  build preset, your GPU and driver, and what was on screen.
- **Put fixes where they belong.** Hardware, syscall and firmware library behavior goes into the
  ps3recomp runtime (`gowa-fixes` branch); permanent fixes to translated code go into the lifters, never
  into generated files. This repository is for what is specific to this game and to the PC.
- **Do not skip work or hide failures**: no skipped jobs or draws, forced success codes, or sleeps and
  retries that mask a synchronisation bug. Preserve the game's logic, jobs and effects.
- **Document every function you add** with a comment that explains what it does, its parameters and
  any side effects.
- **Run the tests** that need no game assets before opening a pull request:
  ```bash
  scripts/test_pc.sh
  python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_launcher*.py'
  ```
  With `GOWA_UI_TEST=1` and `xvfb-run` the launcher tests also exercise the Tk pages.
- **Measure performance changes** on the same scene and settings, separating warm-up from steady state,
  and report FPS, frame times and the sample length. Menus and videos are not a substitute for gameplay.
- **Never commit game files**: executables, assets, keys or anything generated from them.

## Credits

- **sp00nznet** and the ps3recomp contributors:
  [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), the static recompilation toolkit and runtime
  this port is built on.
- [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc): the default input layout this port follows.

Also used: [SDL2](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL), [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org),
[Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui), [Vulkan](https://www.vulkan.org),
[PyCryptodome](https://www.pycryptodome.org), [Capstone](https://www.capstone-engine.org) and
[Tk](https://www.tcl.tk). Third-party components keep their own licenses.

## License

Third-party code retains its original license and copyright notices; this grant does not relicense

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)


## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

1421240608.readme_excerpt:
# Haze Recomp

Experimental Windows port of **Haze** for PS3, built with
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Targets the USA disc
**BLUS30094**, disc version **01.02**, application version **01.00**.

The Windows installer prepares your ISO, downloads verified firmware from Sony,
and installs a ready-to-play launcher. It uses a per-user MSI internally. See
[installation and upgrades](docs/installing.md) and the
[automated release process](docs/releasing.md).

Menus, opening-scene gameplay, audio output, and checkpoint saves have been
tested. Keyboard/mouse and SDL controller support are implemented. Performance,
rendering, and campaign compatibility are still in development. Full campaign
completion is not validated; online co-op is not implemented. Native PAMF movies
play with synchronized video and audio; Escape or the current confirm binding skips them.

## Install

Run `HazeRecomp-<version>-Setup.exe` from [Releases](https://github.com/zdiemer/haze-recomp/releases),
choose your ISO, and click **Install**. The installer downloads the required
RPCS3 helper and Sony firmware, prepares the game, and installs the launcher.
When it finishes, click **Play Haze**. Subsequent launches use **Haze Recomp**
in the Start menu. No separate tools or development environment are needed.

![Haze installer: choose the ISO and installation folder](docs/images/installer.png)

After the installer prepares the game, the launcher is ready to use:

![Haze installer: installation complete with Play Haze](docs/images/installer-complete.png)

The tested disc-decrypted image is `Haze (USA) (En,Fr,Es).iso`
(8,498,184,192 bytes), BLUS30094, disc version 01.02 / application version 01.00.
Its **SHA-256** is:

```text
e778fff687b4a122146d23160fe1fefdff14dddb5d5709b257cff76832dc2520
```

Check your image with PowerShell:

```powershell
Get-FileHash -LiteralPath 'D:\PS3\Haze (USA) (En,Fr,Es).iso' -Algorithm SHA256
```

This identifies the tested ISO byte for byte. Setup also checks the disc metadata
and executable hashes; other regions, encrypted raw dumps and updated executables
are unsupported. Supply your own disc image; none is included in releases.

## Build from source

Requires Windows x64, Visual Studio C++ tools with the Windows SDK, Clang,
CMake and Ninja components, Python 3.11+, Git, and 7-Zip. Supply your own
readable (disc-decrypted) game image, RPCS3 executable for EBOOT decryption,
and installed PS3 firmware. Game files and firmware are not included.

Run from the repository root in PowerShell, replacing the example paths:

```powershell
git submodule update --init --recursive
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r external/ps3recomp/requirements.txt

# Extract the disc and decrypt its executable.
.\scripts\extract.ps1 -Iso 'C:\path\to\Haze.iso'
.\scripts\decrypt.ps1 -Rpcs3 'C:\path\to\rpcs3.exe'

# Generate native translations of the game and firmware code.
$env:PS3_DEV_FLASH = 'C:\path\to\dev_flash'
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/haze.py analyze
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/haze.py lift --jobs 4
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/haze.py lift-spu
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/lift_audio_plugins.py
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/lift_firmware.py

.\scripts\build.ps1
# Or double-click build/haze/HazeLauncher.exe after building.
.\scripts\play.ps1
```

**HazeLauncher.exe** starts the game without a scripting console, preserves
save/settings/cache paths and retains session logs. Native dialogs select
missing game or firmware paths; see the [launcher guide](docs/executable-launcher.md).

Already extracted files belong in `game/disc/PS3_GAME/`, including `PARAM.SFO`
and `USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN`. Decryption produces `USRDIR/EBOOT.ELF`. Set
`PS3_DEV_FLASH` again when launching from a new shell, unless firmware is in
`local/tools/rpcs3/dev_flash`.

The PPU lift is an initial translation; additional function recovery may be
needed before a fresh lift boots or runs correctly.

The executable is `build/haze/HazeRecomp.exe`. Saves live in
`local/state/savedata`, session logs in `local/sessions`, and reusable shaders
in `local/cache/rsx-shaders`. Game assets, generated translations, and build
outputs are ignored by Git. The first launch installs about 4 GB of game data.

## Controls and settings

| Action | Default input |
| --- | --- |
| Move / look | WASD / mouse |
| Fire / zoom | Left / right mouse |
| Reload / use | R / E |
| Jump / crouch | Space / Ctrl |
| Switch weapon | X or mouse wheel |
| Grenade / Nectar or play dead | G / Q |
| Melee | F |
| Menu confirm / back | Enter / Esc (Space / X also work) |
| Open / close pause menu | Esc (in nested menus, goes back one page) |
| Release or recapture mouse | F1 |

Menus also support the pointer: left click selects, right click goes back.
Enter and Esc keep their menu actions regardless of gameplay bindings. Holding
either key across a menu boundary cannot trigger another action. Space remains
jump during gameplay; Enter retains the Start binding outside menus by default.
SDL gamepads connect automatically. Bindings, mouse sensitivity, controller
options, and startup skipping live in [config/input.ini](config/input.ini)
and reload while running. Action names above assume Haze's default controller
layout; zoom and crouch can be changed from toggle to hold in the game's settings.

**Settings > Control Setup** opens PC Controls for bindings, sensitivity,
deadzones and prompt style. Select a binding to capture an input, review any
conflicts, then **Apply**. **Back** discards edits; **Defaults** requires Apply.
**Game control options** opens the original controller layout and toggle/hold
settings.

The main-menu footer opens **Desktop Options** through the current Select
binding (Tab by default) or a mouse click. **Add to Steam** lets you select a
local account and confirm registration with the executable launcher and artwork;
close Steam first. The pause-menu footer opens **Quit to Desktop** directly.
Quit confirmation defaults to Cancel and waits for active saves and settings
before shutting down.

Open **Video Setup** or **Sound Setup** from the main or pause menu for PC
Video and Audio settings. Changes are staged until **Apply**; **Back** discards
edits. Display changes offer a 15-second **Keep/Revert** confirmation. Render
resolution and shadow resolution require restarting.

Alternatively, edit [config/graphics.ini](config/graphics.ini), then press **F6** to apply
filtering, FXAA, sharpening, exposure, VSync, frame-limit, and performance-overlay changes live.
Editing alone does not apply changes; the window title reports the reload result.
Display mode, monitor, window size, render resolution, and shadow resolution
changes made in the file require restarting.

The Video page offers **Performance overlay** (Off / Compact / Expanded) and
**Overlay position** (four corners). **F7** cycles modes during gameplay or menus
and saves the preference. Compact is a tiny, single-line presentation FPS counter
with a text shadow. Expanded adds mean presentation interval, guest flips (not
simulation rate), draw packets per guest frame,
cached textures, and process working-set RAM. CPU/GPU timings are marked N/A
because the normal renderer does not expose reliable per-frame measurements.
Launch overrides remain in effect after reloading.
Defaults are borderless at the monitor's desktop resolution with a 30 FPS cap.
Override resolution for one run with
`.\scripts\play.ps1 -RenderResolution 1920x1080`.

## Development

Run regression checks with `.\scripts\build.ps1 -Test`, or use
`-RuntimeOnly -Test` for checks without building the game executable.
For a bounded diagnostic run, use `.\scripts\run.ps1 -Seconds 90`;
logs and captures go to `local/runs`.

See the [script guide](scripts/README.md) for diagnostics, microbenchmarks,
build internals and command migrations.

Worktrees can reuse a prepared checkout's SDK, Python environment, generated
translations, and game assets while keeping their own builds and logs:

```powershell
.\scripts\build.ps1 -SharedRoot 'C:\path\to\haze-recomp'
.\scripts\play.ps1 -SharedRoot 'C:\path\to\haze-recomp'
```

Use `-SdkRoot` on the build command to select a separate SDK checkout.
The native build downloads a pinned shared LGPL FFmpeg package for movie
decoding. `-FFmpegRoot` selects an unpacked development package for offline
builds. See [movie playback](docs/movie-playback.md) for formats and validation.

## Experimental browser build

The Wasm64/WebGL2 build supports menus and opening-scene gameplay, but remains
slow and experimental. After preparing the game and translations above, install
Emscripten and run:

```powershell
py -3 scripts/bootstrap-wasm.py
.\scripts\build-wasm.ps1 -Emsdk 'C:\path\to\emsdk'
py -3 scripts/serve-wasm.py --firmware-dir 'C:\path\to\dev_flash'
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8085/> in a 64-bit Chromium browser. The build requires
shared memory and about 8 GiB of addressable linear memory; the local server
provides the required isolation headers. Click to enable sound and fullscreen;
F1 releases the mouse. Add `?debug=1` for controls and logs. Browser saves use
IndexedDB, separately from native saves. Browser network play is not implemented.
Native FFmpeg movie playback is not part of the experimental browser build.

Use `scripts/playtest-wasm.py --profile-after 30` with your normal playtest
arguments to record worker CPU profiles. Summarize a run with
`py -3 scripts/diagnose.py browser-cpu local/wasm-tests/<run>`.
The report ranks self samples per worker and shows callers from leaf to root;
`--top`, `--stack-depth`, and `--json` control the output. It also accepts raw
Chromium `.cpuprofile` files. Counts are samples, not elapsed time; idle and wait
functions remain visible, and workers are reported separately.

## License

The port scaffold derives from ps3recomp's MIT-licensed template; see
[LICENSE](LICENSE). Input prompt artwork is by Kenney; its license is included
in [assets/input-prompts](assets/input-prompts).
Native movie decoding dynamically links FFmpeg under LGPLv3. Its license and
documentation are installed under `share/ffmpeg`; the matching shared libraries
remain replaceable beside the executable.

6dd28c2b4861965b6e423ffcac8207d09e07adac.message:
cellSpurs: cellSpursBarrierInitialize and cellSpursGetTasksetInfo

Twisted Metal's post-FX library creates a Taskset2, a barrier for its six
tasks, the tasks, and then reads the taskset's workload id back with
cellSpursGetTasksetInfo. Neither NID (0x7FDF4FEF, 0x9FCB567B) had an
implementation.

- cellSpursBarrierInitialize(taskset, barrier, total): checks the
  arguments (non-null, 128-aligned, one to 128 tasks), zeroes the 128
  bytes, stores total at +0x04 and the taskset at +0x34. The SDK keeps
  the barrier opaque; the tasks meet at it from the SPU through code
  linked into their own images, and that code (BCES01010 task image, LS
  0xB540 notify, 0xB838 wait) counts arrivals up from 0 in the word at
  +0x00, completes when it reaches the total at +0x04, and keeps the
  tasks waiting for completion in a mask at +0x10 -- so a barrier
  initialised this way is one those tasks complete.
- cellSpursGetTasksetInfo(taskset, info): the taskset-level fields of
  CellSpursTasksetInfo (argument +0x2400, workload id +0x2408, last task
  +0x240C, size +0x241C) from the taskset itself; the 128 per-task
  entries before them are left zeroed, "no task", since nothing here
  tracks task state the way the SPU kernel does.

Both join the cellSpurs list in nid_database.py, so a generated NID table
picks them up.

Checked in Twisted Metal (BCES01010) on Linux, with the title's harness
registering both: the post-FX init creates its six tasks, and with the
taskset-corruption fix (separate PR) they pass the barrier frame after
frame.

8c0ce02a54455a7c2781ac4a7290d25106eb8300.message:
cellSpurs: keep native fields out of the guest's taskset

cellSpursCreateTask, cellSpursShutdownTaskset and cellSpursDestroyTaskset
still wrote the native CellSpursTaskset's taskCount (+0x04),
shutdownRequested (+0x08) and initialized (+0x00) into the guest's
taskset, on top of the big-endian layout spurs_taskset_init builds there.
Those bytes are the "running" bitset, which the SPU side of a taskset
reads. Nothing reads the native fields back.

After six tasks, taskCount's little-endian 6 at +0x04 read as tasks 37
and 38 running without being enabled. A task signalling another from the
SPU checks that the taskset is consistent first, so every such signal
failed with CELL_SPURS_TASK_ERROR_SRCH (0x80410905). In Twisted Metal
the post-FX tasks meet at a barrier whose last arrival wakes the others
that way. They stayed asleep, and SpuPostFX waited on them for good.

With the writes gone, the post-FX loop runs: 72 signals from SpuPostFX
and 139 task waits in a 200 s run, against a single round before.

f2eeb320964e8bc5c3df5859fecb22180acccc8c.message:
spu: wake a parked task when an SPU commits its signal

A task signals another from the SPU the way libspurs does it: a
GETLLAR/PUTLLC loop that sets the target's bit in the taskset's signalled
bitset. The parked task checks that guest bit in spu_taskset_wait_signal,
but it sleeps on s_sig_cv, which only the PPU-side signal path
broadcast. So a task signalled by another SPU noticed only when its 1 s
timed wait ran out.

Twisted Metal (BCES01010) chains its six post-FX tasks that way, several
rounds a frame. A frame of post-FX took 4.1 s from the PPU's signals to
the completion label, with every task re-entering WAIT_SIGNAL about a
second after the last.

A successful PUTLLC or PUTLLUC now calls spu_taskset_line_committed(),
which broadcasts s_sig_cv when the committed line holds the signalled
bitset of a taskset that has a task parked. A commit to that line that
did not signal the waiter only costs a spurious wake; the wait loop
re-checks its bit. With it the same frame takes 145 ms, and the next one
117 ms.

test_spu_taskset_wake drives the real channel path: a task parked on a
taskset must return within 400 ms of an SPU setting its bit with PUTLLC,
and with PUTLLUC, and must stay parked when the commit sets another
task's bit or another taskset's. The two wake checks fail without this
change (the waiter is still parked 400 ms after the commit); it runs on
Linux and macOS next to the lock-line peer test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 41305528f9551c462903724f50e6bb4f1cf37f3d)

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   └── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse
│   ├── hardware/             # cellGem, cellCamera, cellUsbd
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
└── docs/                     # See the Documentation table below
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

HLE implementations of the PS3 system libraries, written for this project. RPCS3 is a behavioural reference, not a code source. **About 93 modules complete and 5 partial** (media decode, SPURS), in roughly 260 files and 100,000 lines under `libs/`.

40180c9b5f03d3e125d80ac146be60c6edd0bfbb.message:
Patches: a new thread of higher priority than its creator runs until it blocks

The opening movie sometimes played without sound. The game's SurMixer thread
(prio 400) is created by a prio 1000 thread and creates the event queue whose
key its creator then passes to cellAudioSetNotifyEventQueue, with no
synchronisation of its own: lv2's scheduler guarantees the order. Host threads
run side by side, so about every other start the creator read a zero key, the
mixer was never notified and cellSail's sound was never taken.

sys_ppu_thread_create now waits (at most 200 ms, PS3_NO_PRIO_START=1 turns it
off) until such a thread reaches a blocking call: event queue receive, event
flag, semaphore or condition wait, sleeps.

49c5fe581f6b6705e3325c5d1ee3a9509f33a838.message:
Patches: a depth-texture comparison is depth FUNC reference (inverted shadows)

The RSX compares the stored depth with the reference, the reverse of the order the toolkit's shadow helper used. Receivers
were tinted with the shadow colour where they were lit and not where they were shadowed; the floor showed no shadow at all.

variable with getenv on each call for as long as it was unset. getenv walks the whole environment, and the SPU

the inputs before it left undefined: the host's import library came before the objects, so every runtime symbol the
module uses was undefined. The objects now come first. A system clang also links with lld and -static, as zig does,
so game.dll needs no libstdc++/libgcc DLLs next to it.

88e6cc842a7853e093e8dbab8ac053ac1ad51cc7.message:
macOS: 60 frames a second on a 120 Hz display instead of double speed

The game advances its animation a step per presented frame. The one-flip-per-
vblank cap in main.cpp's frame clock was left off on macOS, where the frame
thread used to be slow enough to stay near 60 by itself; since the 1 ms frame
loop sleep and the draw engine speed-ups of the Windows work, a ProMotion Mac's
CAMetalLayer let menus and movies run at 120 frames a second (SC2HD_FPS=1).
The cap now applies on every platform: 60.0.

The vblank clock was a flat 16 ms, 62.5 Hz, so everything ran 4% fast; the
tick is now 1000/60 ms, carried in thirds of a millisecond.

The porting notes also no longer list the 1 ms frame-loop sleep as
Windows-only: it is shared.

stretched over the whole swapchain. The SDL window is now resizable and
maximizable, F11 or Alt+Enter toggles borderless fullscreen, and the frame
keeps its aspect ratio with black bars, as on macOS.
