1421261662.readme_excerpt:
# Soulcalibur II HD Online — native build by static recompilation

This project runs the PlayStation 3 game **Soulcalibur II HD Online** natively on a Mac/PC. It is not an emulator: the game's
PowerPC (PPU) and Cell SPU code is translated ahead of time into C/C++ and compiled for your machine, on top of the
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) runtime. Graphics go through Metal on macOS and Vulkan on Linux and Windows, sound through SDL (WASAPI on Windows).

**You bring the game.** Nothing from the game, from Sony's firmware or from anyone's PS3 is in this repository or in the
release zip. On first start the launcher installs *your* copy of the game, translates it and compiles the result on *your*
computer. The translated code never leaves it.

> Status: **works on Apple Silicon Macs (Metal)**, and on Windows (Vulkan; tested on an Intel Core Ultra 7 258V / Arc 140V
> laptop, see [Known issues](#known-issues)). The host and the game module also build and run on Linux (a Vulkan window, tried
> only on a software rasteriser, including under WSL2).

## What you need

| | |
|---|---|
| Computer | Apple Silicon Mac (tested on an M4 Max, macOS 26) |
| Python | 3.10 or newer (`brew install python`, or python.org). Only the standard library is used |
| Disk | about 1.5 GB for the installed game and the build, plus about 60 MB for the compiler if it has to be downloaded |
| Internet | only on the first run, to download the compiler (see below) |
| Game | the PSN release **NPUB31366** (USA): the game package and its license; the 01.01 update package is optional |

The files look like `…SC2HDONLINEGAME1.rap` (license), a long-named `….pkg` (the game, about 700 MB, often inside a `.zip`) and
`UP0700-NPUB31366_00-SC2HDONLINEGAME1-A0101-V0100-PE.pkg` (the update). Versions 01.00 (the game alone) and 01.01 (with the update) are supported; the update is optional.

The translated game is compiled with the Xcode command line tools' `clang` if you have them (on Windows and Linux: a clang on
`PATH`, such as a MinGW clang), otherwise the launcher downloads
[zig](https://ziglang.org) 0.17.0 (about 55 MB, MIT, checked against a pinned SHA-256) into the data directory and uses its `zig cc`.
It asks before downloading (`--yes` answers for you). Either way the game is compiled for your own processor (`-march=native`):
built for the generic x86-64 baseline it is too slow in a fight on Windows, and most of the sound drops out.

## Quick start

```sh
unzip sc2hd-0.1.0-macos-arm64.zip
cd sc2hd
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine .      # only if macOS refuses to open the downloaded program

# first run: give it the game (the zip is fine as it is) and, optionally, its update; the .rap is found inside the zip
./sc2hd.py --pkg "Soulcalibur II HD Online (USA).zip" --pkg UP0700-NPUB31366_00-SC2HDONLINEGAME1-A0101-V0100-PE.pkg

# every later run
./sc2hd.py
```

`./sc2hd.py` is a Python 3.10+ script: on Windows (or if the execute bit is lost) start it as `py sc2hd.py` or `python3 sc2hd.py`.

If the license is not in the zip, add `--rap <file>.rap`. Give the game first and its update (if you want it) second. To add the update later, run again with both packages: the game is reinstalled and translated again (your saves are kept).

The first run takes a few minutes (about two on a fast machine):

1. **install** (seconds): unpacks the packages and decrypts them with your license;
2. **lift** (about 10 s): translates the game's PPU code and its five SPU programs to C/C++;
3. **compile** (about 30 s on eight cores): builds that into one library, `game.dylib`;
4. **run**.

Later runs go straight to step 4. Nothing is redone unless the inputs change.

## Options

```
./sc2hd.py [--fxaa | --no-fxaa] [--af N] [--window WxH] [--fullscreen] [--unlock | --unlock-save]
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--fxaa`, `--no-fxaa` | FXAA anti-aliasing of the finished picture (default on). It also softens the HUD a little (macOS) |
| `--af N` | anisotropic texture filtering 1 (off) … 16 (default 16) (macOS) |
| `--window WxH` | initial window size in points, e.g. `1600x900` (default 1280x720). The window can be resized; the 16:9 picture keeps its shape and the rest is black (macOS) |
| `--fullscreen` | start in fullscreen. In the game F11 or Alt+Enter (macOS: Ctrl+Cmd+F or the green button) switches between fullscreen and a window; the window can be resized and maximized, the picture keeps its 16:9 shape |
| `--unlock` | unlock all playable characters for this run, without finishing the game. The host sets the flags in the game's memory as it reads the save data and puts the original ones back when the game saves, so the save file keeps your own progress |
| `--unlock-save` | unlock all playable characters for good, by writing the flags into the save data file (before the game starts). It needs a save: on the very first run start the game once, let it create the save, quit, and run with `--unlock-save` again |
| `--data DIR` | where everything derived from the game lives (default `./data` in the directory you start from, or `SC2HD_HOME`) |
| `--compiler auto\|system\|zig` | which compiler builds the game library (default: a suitable system clang, else zig) |
| `build` / `run` | only build / only run |

`./sc2hd.py --help` lists the rest.

## Controls

The keyboard is mapped like a pad: arrows = D-pad, `Z` = ✕, `X` = ○, `A` = □, `S` = △, `Q`/`W` = L1/R1, `1`/`2` = L2/R2,
`Return` or `Esc` = Start (pauses a fight), `Tab` = Select. Closing the window (`Alt+F4`, macOS: `Cmd+Q`) quits. Game controllers go through SDL; the keyboard and
controllers are not yet tested thoroughly.

## Where things are

Everything derived from the game is in the data directory (`./data` unless you moved it):

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `hdd0/game/NPUB31366/` | the installed game (decrypted) |
| `hdd0/home/…/savedata/` | **your save data** |
| `games/NPUB31366-<version>/` (01.00 or 01.01) | the translated code and `module/game.dylib` |
| `toolchain/` | the downloaded compiler, if any |

Delete the data directory to start over (keep `hdd0/home` if you want your saves). **Do not share the data directory or the files in it:** they are
derived from the game.

## Known issues

- A frame from the end of the previous fight can flash for a moment between the fighter intro and the arena. The game's own
  screen-copy command is sometimes missing from the stream the recompiled code produces; the cause is not found yet.
- The intro and ending movies are decoded by a built-in H.264/AAC decoder (only what those movies use). The pictures follow
  the sound as the game takes it, with a fixed 100 ms allowance for the game's own buffering (`SC2HD_AV_OFFSET_MS` changes it);
  the game's timing feedback is not used, so the sync can be a little off.
- Online Mode is not available: the game shows its own "sign in to PlayStation Network" message and the menu stays usable.
- FXAA softens the HUD slightly. The game renders at 1280x720; there is no internal resolution scaling.
- MP3 music is decoded on the host; about 9 % of the frames differ slightly from the console's decoder at loud transients.
- Rare dropped frames from display-list decoding failures, mostly while a battle loads.
- Linux: the picture is shown in an SDL2 window through the toolkit's Vulkan backend (X11 or Wayland, closing the window quits). It has
  only run on Mesa's software rasteriser (llvmpipe), under Xvfb and in WSL2's WSLg, never on a real GPU: the picture is right, but a
  fight runs at about 10 frames a second there (in WSL2, Ubuntu's Mesa has no Vulkan driver for the GPU, so llvmpipe is what runs). There
  is no FXAA, no anisotropic filtering and the window is a fixed 1280x720. With no `DISPLAY` or `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` (or with
  `SC2HD_HEADLESS=1`), and when there is no Vulkan device, the host runs on the toolkit's null backend instead, with no window.
- Windows: the game is drawn through the Vulkan backend in an SDL window (D3D12 is only the fallback for a machine with no
  Vulkan driver, `SC2HD_D3D12=1`; it draws nothing after the intro). Menus and movies run at 60 frames a second, and so does a
  fight on an integrated GPU (Intel Arc 140V) once its stage has loaded (the first seconds, while its shaders are built, are
  slower); `SC2HD_FPS=1` prints the rate. The intro movie now plays in full
  (about two and a half minutes); Start skips it.

## How it works, building from source

- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md): the pieces (host, game library, launcher), how the game is installed, lifted and
  built, the ABI check.
- [docs/porting-notes.md](docs/porting-notes.md): what had to be done to the toolkit and to the game's own quirks to make it run.
- [docs/licensing.md](docs/licensing.md): the licenses of everything involved.

To build the release yourself you need git, cmake, ninja, Python 3.10+ and a C/C++ compiler (on Linux also the Vulkan and X11
headers, and the PulseAudio or ALSA headers for sound: `apt install libvulkan-dev libx11-dev libxext-dev libpulse-dev libasound2-dev`, and at
run time a Vulkan driver such as `mesa-vulkan-drivers`):

```sh
scripts/build_host.sh     # clones the pinned toolkit, applies patches/, builds the static dependencies and the host
SC2HD_TARGET=windows scripts/build_host.sh   # cross-compile for Windows with MinGW-w64 (clang preferred) into dist/host-windows
                          # (in Git Bash on Windows, plain scripts/build_host.sh builds the same natively)
scripts/package.sh        # a dist/sc2hd-<version>-<os>-<arch>.zip for every host that is built (macOS/Linux, Windows)
./sc2hd.py --pkg …       # in a checkout the launcher builds and runs the host from dist/ itself
```

In a source checkout `./sc2hd.py` needs no `--host-dir`: it uses `dist/host` (`dist/host-windows` on Windows) and runs
`scripts/build_host.sh` first if the host is missing or older than `src/`, `patches/` or the build scripts (on Windows it needs Git
for Windows' bash). `--no-host-build` skips that and uses `dist/` as it is.

04af69922d26655c57c1b1492c1e3feaa31e233e.message:
lifter: lswi/stswi and four unsigned VMX ops -- the SVML front end loads

The SVO browser could never load file:///kin/index.jsp: its URL parser
(func_0039BDB0) copies the scheme with an inlined 15-byte
'lswi r5,r31,15; stswi r5,r11,15', which the lifter emitted as /* TODO */.
The scheme stayed empty, no protocol handler matched 'file', the loader
factory returned NULL and the page stack waited forever -- with no OS call
and no log line.

Found by decompiling the call chain with Ghidra (navigate -> engine Load ->
FUN_003AA120 -> loader factory -> handler registry) and watching the parsed
request in gdb.

patches/ps3recomp/0004 implements lswi/stswi (bytes fill registers four at a
time, MSB first in the low word, wrapping r31 -> r0; NB 0 = 32) and
vmsumuhm, vsubuws, vmuloub, vmuleub. No real-instruction TODOs remain in
the lift (the rest are data words in .text).

The title now loads index.jsp, languageselect.jsp and the
svolanguageselect lump: it has reached its language-select menu.

Also: KZ2_SELFTEST=1 compares lifted strchr/strstr with the host's.

hle: resolve campaign start sound hang via sys_timer_usleep watchdog hook

handle 0x84070002) spun indefinitely in func_009AD268 via func_009B6098
(sys_timer_usleep 100ms) because its teardown was incomplete.

func_009AD268 spins for 5 consecutive iterations (~500ms), clear the
stream record handle's MSB and its status fields, releasing the wait.
The main thread and SPURS workers advance cleanly into campaign level asset
loading (FIOS). Also move kz2_hle_register() after lv2_init_syscalls() in
src/boot_main.cpp so custom syscall handlers are not overwritten at boot.

  tables) from 0x20000000 to 0xE8000000, and the HLE scratch heap to
  0xE9000000. The title's sys_mmapper heap, which this runtime allocates
  upward from 0x11000000, grew across 0x20000000; its allocator wrote
  strings over the control register and put went odd (0x13009).

b1ca0d4e415b53a5e8c1d33e90d762227131a6c2.message:
spu: lift the WWS policy module's interrupt vector; SPU jobs now run

The WWS job manager loads job code with an MFC list in stall-and-notify
mode and finishes the load in its SPU interrupt handler at LS 0xA2C, which
builds a register save/restore stub at 0x3FEC0 and returns through
0xA84/0xA90/0xAD0. None of these is a static branch target, so the lift had
no function there: the handler ran in the fallback interpreter and the PM
ended at 0xA60 every time. With them as --extra-funcs the PM cycles through
its job lists and the audio jobs (modules at 0xDD4B80 and 0xDE3300) are
streamed into LS 0x4000 and dispatched to their lifted overlays.

07d5a904f5ae7b77880e3988bdd965af605d7a10.message:
Cut geometry chain overhead: polling workers, reused jobs and buffers

Idle prepare workers slept on a condition variable, so each queued image-19
job waited about 12 us for a wake-up before its 35 us prepare. Workers now
poll for up to 100 us (WKC_GEOM_SPIN_US) before sleeping, a submit signals
a sleeper only when no worker is polling, and the chain thread polls up to
2 ms for its front job.

Each chain thread reuses finished jobs: source copies, the source-range
list and the adapted input keep their capacity (make_input can build into a
spare input's buffers). Output buffers now travel with the job to the
worker that prepares it; before, workers allocated fresh ones every prepare
and the chain thread freed them.

WKC_GEOM_STATS=1 prints per-job chain copy/wait/commit time, worker queue
delay and prepare time. WKC_AB_GEOM_CHAIN is the private A/B switch.

Same-process street A/B, heavy crowd: 29.4 vs 25.8 FPS (+14%), median
frame 33.7 vs 38.2 ms. Verify mode found no differences; 121 checks pass
in Debug and Release. Docs: README, FINDINGS, SPU, NATIVE_CODE, PATCHES
(also adds the missing 0134-0136 index rows), REFERENCE.

1e3ded68a034fa8f21da7cea8ef34c459f24338c.message:
Speed up the renderer's per-draw work (SDK patch 0133)

The renderer thread now limits the crowded street: slowing it to
efficiency-core speed cost 32% of FPS, against about 9% for the geometry
chain or image 20. Patch 0133 trims three per-draw costs without changing
any decoded value or key:

- vertex decode columns specialised for component count, with SSE4.1 for
  unsigned bytes and packed 11-11-10 (bit-identical; the differential test
  now runs every half value in every lane and all byte values, 122,404
  cases);
- a fragment-program memo keyed by location and offset that reuses size,
  inline constants and structural hash only when the program bytes compare
  equal (RSX_ENGINE_FP_MEMO_VERIFY=1 recomputed 8.1 million in-game reuses
  with no difference), dropping two 32 KB clears per draw;
- a four-lane texture change hash.

Same-process A/Bs on the crowded street: 43.9 vs 41.1 FPS (+7.0%) and
52.9 vs 49.8 FPS (+6.3%). 121 checks pass in Debug and Release.

27ab7df043b98170d6eed9be7e92d6d501d8d3a6.message:
Run image 20's render-command interpreter loop in C++

native_render_loop.cpp runs the display-list interpreter's loop: the
output-space check after each command, recording the command id, the fetch
through the 2 KB ring (refilling it from the display list and starting each
command's payload reads) and the table dispatch. It works on local-store
bytes with plain integers, makes the same local-store writes and DMA
requests in the same order, and leaves every register the command handlers
can read with its compiled value; the rare output flush keeps the compiled
code. The installer now also wraps the loop head (0x1308) and return path
(0x1968) at pinned hashes, extending the existing region in place. The loop
declines to the compiled code when a runtime per-transfer hook or LS debug
watch is active. WKC_NATIVE_RENDER_STATS=1 counts native passes.

All 96 captured street jobs replay byte-exact, every pass native; replayed
jobs take about 252 us against about 290 us compiled, and image 20 drops from
17-18 ms to 14.3 ms per crowded-street frame, which renders normally. Both
suites pass 121 checks.

Build image-20 command 12's draws in C++

0x9D58 is the second half of command 12. It refreshes three dirty constant
blocks (three transform rows, the bone matrices and M3*M2 with its
128-byte block, each uploaded through the compiled 0x1000), records the
vertex-attribute mask and a shader option, then walks the command's draw

offset and attribute mask, and writes the record back by DMA.

order and keeps r80-r85 exact at the 0xE50 call, the only callee that
saves them. Verify mode now also puts back the main memory the compiled
run read before the rerun, since the routine changes records it reads and
writes back. All 23,303 verified calls on the 96 street captures match and
replay is byte-exact. Replay drops from about 220 to about 212 us per job.

lanes name joints whose palette rows live in the skinning call's stack
frame) can't be adapted, so the chain drained every queued job and ran
the compiled job at once. Those drains were about half of all pipeline
drains on the crowded street.

as a declined prepare already did. A fallback records the guest writes the
compiled job makes (MFC PUTs, plain and list, through the PUT hook; atomic
line stores through the atomic trace hook) and logs exactly those ranges,
so queued copies it didn't touch stay valid. With commit_unknown every
later queued job had to be copied and prepared again, serially.

private A/B switch.

6be6095d0eb879edc7ad81f1fe3aa657fc80e548.message:
perf: pipeline native geometry jobs across worker threads

The crowded town street was limited by one thread: every image-19 geometry
job ran serially on the SPURS chain thread (~1,650 per frame), where the PS3
used up to five SPUs. Slowing only that thread cut FPS ~40%; slowing the
renderer or PPU threads changed nothing.

- Port: the chain thread copies a job's sources and adapts its input; a
  worker pool runs the pure-compute prepare. Commits stay on the chain thread
  in job order (inside the next image-19 scope after an 8-job window, or at a
  drain point). A recorded write log (native_geometry_order.h) recopies any
  job whose sources a later commit wrote; jobs that cannot finish natively run
  the compiled job at their commit turn. Workers use the chain thread's MXCSR
  and are stopped and joined at exit. WKC_GEOM_PIPELINE=<n> (0 = serial),
  WKC_GEOM_PIPELINE_VERIFY=1 re-prepares every 64th job and aborts on any
  difference. Finished jobs and source copies reuse their buffers.
- SDK 0127: sub-millisecond sys_timer_usleep blocks on a high-resolution
  waitable timer instead of spinning a whole core.
- SDK 0128: job-chain walker drain callback before non-job commands and exit.

Same-process street A/B (Vulkan, 30 FPS cap): 15.5 -> 26.5 FPS with three
workers. Verify mode: about 145,000 jobs compared, no mismatch, across street,
walking, forced-fallback stress, the plains transition and the avatar creator.
Debug and Release: all 119 checks pass. DirectX, story cutscenes and combat are
not yet run with the pipeline.

c09d985e3872146691aebe50b6f313cf992fdd05.message:
Raise the street frame rate at the 30 FPS limit (SDK patch 0134)

At the player's 30 FPS limit the crowded town street ran at about 18-24 FPS.
The game waits for each flip before building the next frame, so the frame is
serial: the game thread's work after the present, then the FIFO drain up to
the next flip, then the present. Patch 0134 shortens each part:

- inline guest loads and stores in the lifted PPU code for ordinary memory
  (PPU_RECOMP_INLINE_MEMORY; every special range, hook, watch and SPU
  reservation still takes the runtime functions). The game thread's part of
  the frame fell from 13.9 to 1.9 ms;
- asynchronous present: the frame and the window blit are submitted without
  the CPU waiting for the GPU (+6%);
- raw vertex fetch: the vertex program decodes the guest's own vertex bytes,
  as RPCS3 does (drain -1.5 ms per frame; frame dumps match the CPU path);
- no redundant Vulkan pipeline, dynamic state or descriptor sets per draw
  (5.11 -> 4.80 us per draw), constant-file copies only after a constant
  write, and a texture write watch for spans of 64 KB and up.

The geometry pipeline now defaults to seven prepare workers on 16 or more
hardware threads (+4% in heavy crowds). Private WKC_AB_* switches tie each
change to main.cpp's WKC_AB_GATE file for same-process A/Bs; wkc_ab.h now has
C linkage, without which the gate never reached the C runtime.

All changes switched together in one process: 22.4 vs 19.9 FPS (+12.5%) in a
moderate crowd, 20.0 vs 19.7 in the heaviest, which still take three vblanks
a frame. 121 checks pass in Debug and Release.

Run image 20's dirty-state flush in C++

0xAD50 runs before every draw command (five call sites, command 12's
first call among them). It waits for DMA tag 7 and then refreshes each
dirty block of render state: transform constants (0xA8E0, already C++),
the constant table command 25 fills (0x53C8, now C++: runs of table rows
uploaded eight constants at a time), a single status word, and the shader
block. The shader block copies halfword-swapped rows into the shader
setup area, uploads the fragment program through the compiled 0x7B0 and
emits SET_SHADER_PROGRAM, the texture-coordinate controls and
SET_SHADER_CONTROL.

Both routines keep the compiled stack frames and register values at every
compiled call. Verify mode now nests (each level keeps its own
snapshots), and it hides the C++ rerun's transfers instead of the compiled
run's, because a tag wait can complete transfers the compiled run already
reported. All 20,280 verified calls on the 96 street captures match, and
replay is byte-exact. Replay drops from about 236 to about 220 us per job.

1421399192.readme_excerpt:
# White Knight Chronicles II Recomp A native C++ port of **White Knight Chronicles II** built by recompiling the PS3 game code. Development starts with **White Knight Chronicles I**, which is included on the disc. [![White Knight Chronicles I crowded town street with many townspeople in the native Vulkan build](verification/screenshots/2026-10-22-native-geometry-chain-street.png)](docs/GALLERY.md) Crowded town street, native Vulkan build at the 30 FPS limit, 22 October 2026. Select the image for capture settings and the progress gallery, newest first.

Newest first, back to the first native screen: the milestones are in the gallery timeline. ## Status Early development build. The native Windows build reaches the WKC1 starting town and can resume from a local save. The long-term SPU target is complete replacement with readable project-written C++; current coverage is partial. **Verified** - Startup screens, title menus, movie playback and avatar creation. - Town rendering, short character movement, camera control and pause/resume. - Logic Stone targeting, saving one starting-town slot and loading it through Continue after restarting. - A dedicated **Triangle → System → Graphics Settings** panel with persistent preferences, the game's menu frame and a scrollbar. - The town-to-Balastor Plain transition after Continue, with short movement and camera control. DirectX foreground clipping is fixed on that route, and leaf-shaped foliage shadow cutouts are restored on both renderers. - **121 Windows regression checks** pass in both normal Debug and optimized Release. **Graphics settings:** windowed, borderless and fullscreen modes; named output resolutions; VSync; anisotropic filtering from Off to 16×; Off/FXAA anti-aliasing; 30/40/60 frame limits; and an optional transparent FPS overlay. Vulkan is the primary renderer. DirectX 12 is an experimental, restart-selected renderer. Window mode, output size, VSync, filtering, FXAA and the FPS overlay are integrated. Full rendering and transition parity remain in development. **Frame rate:** use the 30 FPS baseline. Higher limits can exceed 30 presentations/s, but area transitions, cutscene skips and walking currently have reported faults above 30. Window titles show only the game name. The optional in-game FPS overlay measures presentations and can include repeated animation states. Desktop launches disable inherited profilers, traces, input injection and GPU captures before runtime initialization. Normal play writes no diagnostic logs; the optional in-game FPS overlay remains your choice. ## Known issues - **Performance and game timing:** the crowded town street is the slowest scene. With the frame limit unlocked it now runs at about 23–41 FPS on Vulkan, up from about 15 before pipelined geometry jobs; DirectX views of the crowd read 17–22. At the 30 FPS limit, lighter crowds hold 30 FPS. Patches 0134 and 0136 gained about 13% in a moderate crowd. On 22 October, cutting the geometry chain's overhead took a heavy crowd from 25.8 to 29.4 FPS in a same-process A/B ([details](docs/NATIVE_CODE.md#geometry-chain-overhead-2026-10-22)). Running geometry jobs the native path cannot take as compiled jobs at their turn, instead of draining the pipeline, added 6–8% in the densest crowds, which now run at about 24–25 FPS ([details](docs/NATIVE_CODE.md#fewer-pipeline-drains-2026-10-22)). There the renderer's draws and the SPU command output (image 20) are the remaining cost ([details](docs/SPU.md#what-limits-the-frame-rate)). Movement still stutters, and loading and cutscene timing need further comparison with RPCS3. - **Rendering:** black flicker at Leonard's feet and the rotating Logic Stone effect remain open. DirectX shadow fidelity and darker grass are under investigation, and moving cloud shade and apparent grass density need matched comparisons with RPCS3. Earlier stretched hair/clothing strips and inverted shadows are fixed in inspected Vulkan views. - **Controls:** the game reads the sticks once per frame, so they feel slow and uneven wherever the frame rate drops; the frame-rate work is the main fix. Patch 0132 removed up to 16 ms of extra stick delay. Physical-controller consistency, especially at angles, still needs comparison. - **Gameplay coverage:** sustained traversal, combat, a complete playthrough and broader save compatibility remain unverified. Evidence, measurements and investigation history are in the [findings log](docs/FINDINGS.md); remaining runtime implementation gaps are tracked in the [runtime audit](docs/KILLZONE_FIX_AUDIT.md). ## Roadmap - **Features:** draw distance and fog controls, removal of menu background blur, and an in-game keyboard navigable with a gamepad. - **USA update 1.01 and DLC:** integrate the updated executable and content, then validate loading, gameplay and save compatibility. - **European DLC:** investigate content differences and compatibility with the USA build. An EU-only file entry has been identified; its purpose and compatibility remain unverified. - **Japanese release:** the game, DLC and all ten update packages are available for research. The long-term goal is to add **all Japanese-exclusive content with English translations**, plus **optional Japanese voiceovers**. - **Platforms:** Linux and Apple Silicon support are longer-term goals. Development continues on the original USA disc baseline, with WKC1 tested first. These are planned additions; update, DLC and cross-region runtime support are not verified yet. GeoNet compatibility is separate later research. ## How it works The game code is translated to C/C++ ahead of time and compiled with a runtime that implements the PS3 services it uses. Tested town-to-plains routes run with the SPU interpreter fallback forbidden, after five missing SPU entries were added to the static build. The fallback remains available for untested paths. Readable, project-written C++ runs the supported image-19 geometry jobs, pipelined across worker threads, all four image-23 visibility modes and the normal path of image 21, the event-flag set job. Image 20, the render-command builder, runs its interpreter loop and commands 25 and 12 in C++. Other SPU jobs, commands and inputs still run as compiled code. Everything about the SPU work is on one page, [SPU jobs and their replacement](docs/SPU.md): what each job does, how the port runs it, the problems found and fixed, what limits the frame rate and how a job is replaced. ## Building and documentation This repository contains project source, build tools, SDK patches and verification records. Building requires privately prepared game files from the **USA BLUS30784 version 01.00 disc**. Game files and generated game sources are kept outside this repository. | Page | Contents | | --- | --- | | [SPU jobs and their replacement](docs/SPU.md) | Start here for SPU work: the 24 jobs, how they run, problems fixed, what limits FPS and the replacement workflow | | [Build guide](docs/BUILD.md) | Requirements, private workspace layout, building, regression checks, play and diagnostic options | | [Findings log](docs/FINDINGS.md) | Verified results, measurements, open issues and investigation history, grouped by topic | | [Runtime patch notes](docs/PATCHES.md) | What each numbered SDK patch changes and how it was checked, newest first | | [Runtime subsystem notes](docs/SUBSYSTEMS.md) | Renderer, movie decoding, guest hooks, early SPURS and RSX patch notes, frame presentation and native text entry | | [Lessons for recompilers](docs/LESSONS.md) | Symptom index and reusable lessons on timing, rendering, SPU jobs and runtime services | | [Reference](docs/REFERENCE.md) | Glossary, environment variables and known game addresses | | [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | Execution model, remaining SPU fallback and modding scope | | [Native C++ execution work](docs/NATIVE_CODE.md) | Replacing SPU code with readable C++ and speeding up SPU jobs: evidence, work order and acceptance rules | | [DirectX parity audit](docs/DIRECTX_PARITY.md) | Vulkan fixes still missing from live DirectX, with evidence and next checks | | [Progress gallery](docs/GALLERY.md) | Dated screenshots, newest first | | [Runtime audit](docs/KILLZONE_FIX_AUDIT.md) | Runtime-fix comparison and remaining implementation gaps | | [Code review history](docs/CODE_REVIEW.md) | Review findings, fixes and the checks that were run | | [Contributing](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) | Contribution workflow and where new notes belong | ## Credits and license Built on the [PS3Recomp SDK](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). The pinned SDK revision is recorded in [project.json](project.json), its license is retained in [LICENSE.ps3recomp](LICENSE.ps3recomp), and local runtime changes are maintained as numbered patches. ## Special thanks Thank you to these projects for the ideas, references and improvements this port has drawn on: - [PS3Recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet and contributors - [Drakengard 3 recomp](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp) and [PS3Recomp fork](https://github.com/soyjxck/ps3recomp) by soyjxck - [PS3Recomp fork](https://github.com/NoahBPeterson/ps3recomp) by NoahBPeterson - [PS3Recomp fork](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/ps3recomp) by JonathanDC64 - [inFAMOUS 2 recomp](https://github.com/erikomis/infamous2-recomp) by erikomis - [Killzone 3 fix catalogue](https://gist.github.com/undecuple/2845432bf13e485634de122084d3fd56) by undecuple - [Soulcalibur II HD recomp](https://github.com/n0madic/Soulcalibur2HD-recomp) by n0madic - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) - [envytools](https://github.com/envytools/envytools) and the [PS3 Developer Wiki](https://www.psdevwiki.com/ps3/) - [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/) and [SDL](https://www.libsdl.org/)

records how the guard caught it and what to look at next. Patch 0018 caps

what named the heap.

Past the loading screen to the save prompt: patches 0019-0020

The loading screen waited on a particle job whose last task creates the
next phase from the SPU. Three SPURS taskset gaps on the fork kept that
from happening (tasks started twice, Taskset2 made as a 0x1900-byte
taskset without event flags, SPU-created tasks never started); with them
fixed the game shows its first-use save prompt, writes BCES01741-SYSDATA
and goes on to a black screen, which is next. STATUS has the chain and the
diagnostics that found it; gamedata/ (the emulated HDD) and the old lift
are ignored.

# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.pt-BR.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. > [!WARNING] > **Ainda experimental, mas já dá para zerar.** O [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor) jogou do começo ao fim no PC dele (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT). Em processadores comuns o jogo ainda é lento (~20 fps na luta contra o chefe num Ryzen 7 5700G), e ainda pode travar. Feito para Windows; no macOS (Apple Silicon) ele voltou a rodar, por enquanto só para testes. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Novembro de 2026, no Windows (e no Mac, em testes): - **O jogo inteiro, do boot ao fim:** o iSamigor zerou o jogo. Nos nossos testes: telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente; o renderizador Vulkan próprio do projeto, onde está o trabalho de desempenho; e o *live draw* (D3D12). - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas, melhorias e o **online** com a sua conta do site; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado no [site](https://gow-ascension.com.br/pt-br) a partir dos seus discos. Atualizado em 10 de novembro. As mudanças de novembro estão no branch [`ascension-perf`](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/tree/ascension-perf) até serem medidas no Windows. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.pt-BR.md](docs/MILESTONES.pt-BR.md) (em inglês: [MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md)). ### Desempenho O objetivo é rodar bem em processadores comuns, não só nos fortes. Desde 6 de novembro o caminho é **sair do modelo do PS3**: em vez de emular cada vez melhor as SPUs e o RSX, o trabalho deles vira código nativo do PC e da placa de vídeo, com a meta de não sobrar nenhuma emulação de SPU. > [!NOTE] > **Um erro de medida corrigido (9 de novembro):** o contador de fps do nosso renderizador Vulkan contava cada quadro duas vezes (o mesmo quadro era apresentado de novo ~1 ms depois, sem nada desenhado). Os números desse renderizador publicados antes valem a metade. Os de baixo já são quadros reais. A luta contra o chefe logo depois da cinemática de abertura, a cena mais pesada que medimos, num Ryzen 7 5700G (Windows, renderizador Vulkan do projeto, mediana de várias janelas de 5 s): | Quando | fps na luta | Thread de vídeo, por draw | | --- | --- | --- | | 9 de novembro, à noite | ~15-17 | ~17,5 µs | | 10 de novembro, de manhã | ~18 | ~16,0 µs | | 10 de novembro, à tarde | **~20** | **~15,0 µs** | **O que entrou de 6 a 10 de novembro** (cada parte medida e com a imagem conferida antes de virar padrão): - **Renderizador Vulkan próprio** (no ps3kit), onde está o trabalho de desempenho: o anti-aliasing que o jogo fazia nas SPUs (o MLAA delas não roda mais) agora é feito na placa de vídeo (SMAA, FXAA ou MLAA), filtro anisotrópico, vértices convertidos em lotes e um contador de fps compacto nas cores do jogo. - **60 fps:** o limite de 30 do jogo destravado, com o jogo andando na velocidade certa, e um limite de 60. Os carregamentos, que tinham ficado lentos com o destrave, voltaram a ~4,5 s. - **SPUs em código nativo:** três módulos de geometria do EDGE (218, 202 e 210) rodam inteiros como código nativo, cada um conferido contra o original em centenas de jobs gravados do próprio jogo (resultado idêntico). - **Thread de vídeo mais leve:** cópias 2D divididas entre 3 threads (4 → 1,7 ms por quadro); constantes dos shaders copiadas só quando mudam; os comandos de vídeo comuns despachados em bloco (-1,5 µs por draw); e as texturas: o jogo move ~150 texturas por segundo dentro da memória de vídeo, e agora uma textura movida fica com a imagem que já estava na placa em vez de ser decodificada e enviada de novo (texturas de 1,56 para 1,00 µs por draw). - **macOS:** voltou a compilar e a abrir o jogo (Vulkan sobre MoltenVK), ~24 fps no primeiro nível num Mac com Apple Silicon; ainda trava em parte das aberturas. **Para onde vai o quadro agora:** na luta, quem segura o quadro é o thread que executa os comandos de vídeo, e o maior custo dele é copiar os vértices que os jobs do EDGE acabaram de escrever (~5 dos ~15 µs de cada draw, perto de 50 MB por quadro). **Próximos passos:** levar essa geometria para a placa de vídeo (as posições calculadas na GPU, sem a cópia no processador), que deve ser o primeiro salto grande (estimativa de ~28-32 fps, ainda a medir); depois o resto do EDGE na GPU e os outros módulos das SPUs em código nativo. ### Estabilidade - **Corrigido:** num PC lento, o thread de vídeo desistia de uma espera depois de 2 s e perdia os comandos do quadro; o jogo ficava parado no carregamento do nível. - **Corrigido:** o travamento no nível com as listas de geometria esperando para sempre (uma escrita do processador principal se perdia no meio de uma operação atômica de uma SPU: de 3 travamentos em 5 rodadas para nenhum em 4). - **Corrigido:** o travamento com `CopyLocalMemory offset error` (um contador do Edge Zlib e a troca da tabela de streaming de texturas sem proteção): nenhum em 40 rodadas no nível. - **Protegido:** comandos de vídeo corrompidos (`FIFO error: possible desync`) não derrubam mais o thread do RSX, e um draw pedindo uma quantidade absurda de vértices é descartado em vez de travar o jogo. A causa da corrupção ainda está aberta. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); o jogo às vezes trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`); e houve um crash silencioso ~70-105 s depois de entrar no nível em duas rodadas. ### Multijogador online (em desenvolvimento) Os servidores originais do jogo ainda funcionam para quem joga no PS3, mas o jogo recompilado não entra na PSN. Por isso o projeto tem o próprio servidor (em Rust, ainda privado), no ar em [gow-ascension.com.br](https://gow-ascension.com.br) com o cadastro fechado por enquanto; o runtime manda para ele os nomes que o jogo procura. O servidor nunca se passa pela Sony: ele responde só o que o jogo espera, lido no código traduzido ou nas capturas do próprio jogo falando com ele. A partida usa o netcode do próprio jogo (uma malha P2P por UDP); como dois jogadores em casa quase nunca se alcançam direto (cada um atrás do seu roteador), os pacotes passam por um relay do servidor, e o jogo nem percebe. | Passo | Estado | | --- | --- | | Entrar online, Online Pass | ok | | Configuração do online (o jogo lê a nossa) | ok | | Termos de uso, perfil do multijogador guardado na conta | ok | | Tutorial pulado, lobby do guerreiro | ok | | Partida rápida: localização do jogador | ok | | Partida rápida: escolha do servidor de matchmaking | ok | | Conexão com o matchmaking (sessão SSL 3.0) | ok | | Dois jogadores casados numa partida, um deles host | ok (dois jogos no mesmo PC) | | A rede da partida pelo relay do servidor | ok (dois jogos no mesmo PC) | | Launcher: entrar na conta e jogar online | ok | | Partida entre dois PCs pela internet | **em andamento** | | A partida inteira, do lobby ao fim | falta | ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph PC["PC do jogador"] L["Launcher
conta e online"] G["Jogo recompilado
(runtime ps3kit)"] L -- "endereço, configuração e perfil" --> G end subgraph SRV["Servidor do projeto (Rust)"] API["Contas e API"] CFG["Configuração do online"] TUS["Perfil do multijogador
por conta"] GEO["Localização"] SAM["Matchmaking
(SSL 3.0)"] REL["Signaling e relay
(UDP)"] DB[("PostgreSQL")] TUS --> DB API --> DB end WEB["Site do projeto
perfil, ranking, painel"] G2["Jogo de outro jogador"] L -- "login por código" --> API L -- "configuração, perfil" --> CFG L -- "perfil" --> TUS G -- "TCP" --> GEO G -- "TCP + SSL" --> SAM G <-- "partida (UDP)" --> REL REL <-- "partida (UDP)" --> G2 WEB -- "HTTP" --> API ``` No ar no servidor e no site: as contas, o perfil do multijogador guardado por conta, o perfil público com nível e conquistas, o ranking (vazio até haver partidas), um painel administrativo e o login do launcher por código. Planejado: os troféus do jogo assinados e conferidos pelo servidor. **"Jogar offline" vai continuar sempre funcionando**: a campanha nunca vai pedir conta. ## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), instale o launcher pelo `AscensionLauncher__x64-setup.exe` das [releases](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/releases) e, na primeira vez, aponte a pasta `ascension` em **Avançado › Pasta do jogo**. Ele se atualiza sozinho quando sai uma versão nova.

JOGAR abre o jogo; o launcher se esconde até ele fechar. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Melhorias:** liga e desliga. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Abrir a pasta de melhorias** é onde entram as outras, como o **português do Brasil**, que a [página do site](https://gow-ascension.com.br/pt-br) monta no seu navegador a partir das imagens dos seus discos (nada é enviado). As melhorias incluídas são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo. - **Online:** entra na sua conta do site por um código (como numa TV) e liga o online; os troféus do jogo ficam na mesma aba.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

1422301465.readme_excerpt:
# God of War: Ascension for PC

A native Linux port of **God of War: Ascension** (PlayStation 3, BCUS98232), built by static
recompilation with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp).

The game's PPU and SPU machine code is translated ahead of time into C/C++ and compiled together with
a runtime that reimplements the PS3 hardware and firmware libraries: LV2 system calls, SPURS, GCM,
the RSX graphics chip (on Vulkan), audio, video decoding, input and file systems. There is no
emulator and no interpreter in the main path. This repository holds the game-specific part of the
port: the pipeline that turns your dump into a native executable, the PC entry point, input, settings,
the in-game menu and the launcher.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **You must own an original copy of the game.** This repository contains no part of God of War:
> Ascension: no executables, assets, translated code or game license keys, and it does not download
> them. The port only works with files you dump yourself from a copy you legally own: the BCUS98232
> Blu-ray disc and the 1.12 update obtained for it. Everything is generated locally from those files
> and must stay on your machine.
>
> - Do not share the game files, the generated executable, the translated code (`out/`,
>   `recompiled/`, `spu/`) or anything else produced from the game. They are derived from copyrighted
>   material.
> - Requests for game files, keys or ready-made builds are not answered and are removed from the issues
>   and the [Discord](https://discord.gg/HCHyR3GYWm).
> - This project does not help to run pirated copies and is not a way to play the game without buying
>   it.
>
> This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Santa Monica
> Studio. God of War is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment.

## Status

**Work in progress, not playable yet.** The port boots, runs the menus and starts a new game, but the
first level runs far too slowly to play.

- Opening video, title screen, 3D menus, profile selection and the Single Player menu.
- A new game loads the first level, plays the opening cinematic in the engine and reaches player
  control: the first tutorials ("Dodge", "Attacks") respond to input.
- Performance (measured under Xvfb): 3D menu ~10 FPS, opening video ~28 FPS, new-game cinematic
  ~30 FPS, first level ~3 FPS. The current bottlenecks are SPU jobs (EDGE geometry) and the RSX
  thread.

**Known issues**
- The first level is not playable at its current frame rate.
- Rare SPURS kernel hangs when the kernel runs workloads on parallel threads (about 1 in 7 runs).
- Physical controllers are untested; keyboard and mouse are.
- No upscaling or adjustable internal resolution.
- Saving on exit is not guaranteed.

## What works

- **Static recompilation pipeline:** reads the disc image and the 1.12 update dumped from your own
  copy, prepares the game executable from them and translates its PPU and SPU code, including the WWS
  job modules and the SPU code the game generates at run time.
- **Graphics:** the ps3recomp RSX backend on Vulkan, with a persistent shader cache and optional
  background shader compilation.
- **Input:** keyboard, mouse and SDL2 gamepads at the same time on port 0, with two remappable keys per
  PS3 button.
- **Launcher** (Tk): game status and save backups, display mode and window size, VSync, FPS counter,
  MangoHud and GameMode, controls, diagnostics switches and a live log with per-run history.
- **In-game menu** (Dear ImGui) and an FPS counter overlay.

## Requirements

- Linux x86-64 and a GPU with a Vulkan driver.
- clang, CMake, Ninja, 7-Zip, Vulkan headers, SDL2, FFmpeg and Python 3 with Tk.
- A legally owned copy of the game: an ISO dumped from your own BCUS98232 disc (version 1.00) and
  the PKG of the 1.12 update. Nothing is downloaded and no game file is provided.

**Build notes**
- The translated SPU code is compiled with `-march=x86-64-v3` (AVX2/FMA) by default. On a CPU without
  AVX2, configure with `-DPORT_SPU_MARCH=x86-64-v2`.
- The translated PPU sources are very large, so compiling them takes a lot of memory per job. Pick the
  number of parallel jobs to fit your RAM (`BUILD_JOBS` for `scripts/build.sh`, 6 by default;
  `-j` for `cmake --build`); fewer jobs use less memory but take longer.

## Building

### 1. Get the sources

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This port does **not** build against upstream ps3recomp. It needs the **`gowa-fixes` branch** of
> the fork [RichardFontoura/ps3recomp](https://github.com/RichardFontoura/ps3recomp/tree/gowa-fixes),
> which carries the runtime, SPURS, GCM/RSX/Vulkan, SPU and lifter fixes this game depends on.
> The fork's default branch (`master`) and upstream `sp00nznet/ps3recomp` do not have these fixes:
> always pass `--branch gowa-fixes` when cloning.

Clone both repositories side by side, with the fork on `gowa-fixes`:

```bash
mkdir gowa-src && cd gowa-src
git clone https://github.com/RichardFontoura/gowa-pc.git
git clone --branch gowa-fixes https://github.com/RichardFontoura/ps3recomp.git
git -C ps3recomp branch --show-current   # must print: gowa-fixes
```

The result is:

```
gowa-src/
├── gowa-pc/     this repository
└── ps3recomp/   the fork, on the gowa-fixes branch
```

`../ps3recomp` is the default location for the CMake presets and the scripts. If you keep the fork
somewhere else, point to it with `PS3RECOMP=/path/to/ps3recomp` (scripts) and
`-DPS3RECOMP_DIR=/path/to/ps3recomp` (CMake). When you update this repository, update the fork too,
since both move together:

```bash
git -C gowa-pc pull
git -C ps3recomp pull   # still on gowa-fixes
```

Then create a Python environment with the ps3recomp tool requirements. It can live anywhere;
activate it before running the scripts, or set `GOWA_PYTHON` to its interpreter:

```bash
python3 -m venv ~/.venvs/gowa
~/.venvs/gowa/bin/pip install -r ps3recomp/requirements.txt ninja
source ~/.venvs/gowa/bin/activate        # or: export GOWA_PYTHON=~/.venvs/gowa/bin/python
cd gowa-pc
```

### 2. Prepare the game files

```bash
scripts/extract_update.sh /path/to/patch-1.12.pkg   # -> game/update
scripts/extract_disc.sh /path/to/disc.iso           # -> game/disc (refuses incomplete ISOs)
scripts/decrypt_eboot.sh                            # update (default) or disc -> game/EBOOT.ELF
```

Instead of passing the paths, you can set `GOWA_DUMPS` to a folder that holds the ISO and the PKG.

With the 1.12 update, `USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` is only a small loader that starts `GOWA.SELF`, the real
executable. `decrypt_eboot.sh` turns both into plain ELF files that the lifter can read, using only the
files of your copy (no emulator involved). The game-specific data it needs is read from your own update
files on every run and is never stored or shipped in this repository, so the step fails without them.

### 3. Translate and build

```bash
scripts/analyze.sh       # imports, ELF header, SPU images and the WWS job policy module -> analysis/
scripts/lift.sh          # PPU -> out/, recompiled/
python3 scripts/extract_jobmods_elf.py game/EBOOT.ELF --out analysis/jobmods
scripts/lift_spu.sh      # SPU images and the WWS policy module -> spu/
python3 ../ps3recomp/tools/lift_jobmods.py --jobmods analysis/jobmods \
    --out spu --register spu/jobmods_register.c
scripts/build.sh         # linux-vulkan preset by default (also linux-vulkan-debug, linux-null)
```

Incremental builds afterwards: `cmake --build build/linux-vulkan -j<jobs>`, with a job count that
fits your RAM.

**Optional: position-independent SPU fragments.** Some jobs copy SPU code to local-store addresses
chosen at run time. Without translated fragments the SPU interpreter runs that code, much more slowly.
To translate them, run the game once with `SPU_PIC_CAPTURE=<file>`, then
`python3 scripts/lift_spu_fragments.py <file> --overlay 210` and build again.

All generated files stay out of git: `game/` (extracted dumps and decrypted ELFs), `out/` and
`recompiled/` (translated PPU), `spu/` (translated SPU), `analysis/`, `build/`, `gamedata/` (saves
and the virtual HDD) and `scratch/` (temporary files).

## Playing

```bash
scripts/launcher.sh          # settings and the Play button
scripts/launcher.sh --play   # start straight away with the saved settings
scripts/run.sh               # diagnostic entry point (ignores the launcher settings)
```

The launcher needs Tk in the Python it runs with (`GOWA_PYTHON`, or `python3` from `PATH`). If that
Python has no Tk, `GOWA_TK_DIR` can point to an unpacked Tk 8.6 library folder (with `libtk8.6.so`
and `tk8.6/`).

Settings live in `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/gowa-pc/` (`GOWA_CONFIG_DIR` changes the folder):

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `settings.json` | launcher settings (schema 2; schema 1 is migrated on load) |
| `game.ini` | options shared with the in-game menu (`key=value`); the game gets its path in `GOWA_GAME_INI` |
| `last_run.log` | timestamped log of the last run started with Play |
| `logs/<UTC>-<id>/` | per-run history: raw output, JSONL events, metadata and an exit summary |
| `savedata_backups/` | save copies made before every run (the 10 most recent) |
| `frames.csv` | frame times, when enabled under Diagnostics |

### Launcher

- **Game:** installation status, save backup and restore (`gamedata/dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata`).
  Saves are copied before every run; a failed backup is logged and does not block the game. Restoring
  requires the game to be closed, asks for confirmation and backs up the current saves first.
- **Graphics:** display mode (windowed, borderless, fullscreen), window size (1280×720, 1600×900,
  1920×1080 or the monitor), VSync and the FPS counter (corner, scale, opacity and items), all stored
  in `game.ini`. MangoHud and GameMode prefix the command and are disabled when not installed.
- **Controls:** two keys per button, capture on click (key or mouse button), duplicate-key warning
  and a reset button.
- **Diagnostics:** `RSX_FRAME_CSV`, `RSX_VK_TEXTURE_COMPUTE`, `RSX_VK_RAW_TEXTURES`,
  `RSX_TEX_HASH_FULL`, `VDEC_PERF`, `SPURS_KERN_THREADS`, `SPURS_KERN_PARALLEL` and `GCM_FLIP_MIN_MS`.
  Only values that differ from the `scripts/run.sh` defaults are exported; a variable already set in
  the terminal wins.
- **Log:** the last 6000 lines with errors and gaps highlighted, counters, copy, clear and open
  folder. Clearing the view never deletes the per-run history.

### In game

**Insert** (or **R3 + L2** on a controller) opens the PC menu and **F10** toggles the FPS counter.
Both keys are reserved and cannot be remapped.

| PS3 button | Key 1 | Key 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Cross | Space | K |
| Square | Left mouse | J |
| Triangle | Right mouse | I |
| Circle | F | L |
| L1 / R1 | Left Shift / E | — |
| L2 / R2 | Q / R | — |
| L3 / R3 | Left Ctrl / Middle mouse | — / C |
| Start / Select | Escape / Tab | Enter / — |
| D-pad ↑ → ↓ ← | 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 | — |
| Evade (while held, WASD becomes the right stick) | Left Alt | — |

WASD is the left stick and the arrow keys the right stick. Keyboard, mouse and the first SDL gamepad
share port 0, and losing window focus releases all input. Remapping takes effect on the next run.

## How it works

| Part | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Pipeline | `scripts/` | Extracts the dumps, decrypts the executables, analyses the ELF and drives the PPU/SPU lifters |
| Translated code | `recompiled/`, `spu/` (generated) | The game's PPU functions and SPU programs as C/C++ |
| Runtime | [ps3recomp](https://github.com/RichardFontoura/ps3recomp) (`gowa-fixes`) | LV2 syscalls, HLE firmware libraries (SPURS, GCM, audio, video, file systems), SPU runtime and the RSX Vulkan backend |
| Entry point | `main.cpp`, `stubs.cpp` | Reserves guest memory, sets up the virtual file system, starts the runtime and the frame clock, and boots the game |
| PC layer | `pc/` | SDL2 input mapping (`input.cpp`), `game.ini` settings (`game_ini.cpp`) and the ImGui menu and FPS overlay (`overlay.cpp`) |
| Launcher | `launcher/` | Tk launcher: settings, controls, save backups, diagnostics and run logs |
| Tests | `tests/`, `scripts/test_pc.sh` | Input, settings and launcher unit tests that need no game assets, plus window smoke tests and benchmarks |

## Contributing

Bug reports, investigations and pull requests are welcome. Contributions reach `main` only through pull
requests from forks; direct pushes are blocked.

1. Fork the repository and create a branch in your fork.
2. Commit your change there and open a pull request against `main`.
3. A maintainer reviews it; once approved and with every conversation resolved, it is squashed into
   `main`. Pushing new commits after a review asks for a new review.

- **Report issues** with the log of the failing run (`last_run.log` or the folder under `logs/`), the
  build preset, your GPU and driver, and what was on screen.
- **Put fixes where they belong.** Hardware, syscall and firmware library behavior goes into the
  ps3recomp runtime (`gowa-fixes` branch); permanent fixes to translated code go into the lifters, never
  into generated files. This repository is for what is specific to this game and to the PC.
- **Do not skip work or hide failures**: no skipped jobs or draws, forced success codes, or sleeps and
  retries that mask a synchronisation bug. Preserve the game's logic, jobs and effects.
- **Document every function you add** with a comment that explains what it does, its parameters and
  any side effects.
- **Run the tests** that need no game assets before opening a pull request:
  ```bash
  scripts/test_pc.sh
  python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_launcher*.py'
  ```
  With `GOWA_UI_TEST=1` and `xvfb-run` the launcher tests also exercise the Tk pages.
- **Measure performance changes** on the same scene and settings, separating warm-up from steady state,
  and report FPS, frame times and the sample length. Menus and videos are not a substitute for gameplay.
- **Never commit game files**: executables, assets, keys or anything generated from them.

## Credits

- **sp00nznet** and the ps3recomp contributors:
  [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), the static recompilation toolkit and runtime
  this port is built on.

1422375026.readme_excerpt:
# Drakengard 3 ### Native Windows port through static recompilation A source-only project building toward a complete, playable PC version of **Drakengard 3**. ![Source: PlayStation 3](https://img.shields.io/badge/source-PlayStation_3-003791) ![Target: Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/target-Windows_x64-0078D4) ![Game: NPUB31251 v1.01](https://img.shields.io/badge/game-NPUB31251_v1.01-6750A4) ![Stage: Active development](https://img.shields.io/badge/stage-active_development-D97706) [Progress](#progress) · [Screenshots](#rendering-progress) · [Getting started](#getting-started) · [Controls](#test-controls) · [Contributing](#contributing)
> **Native port in development. Gameplay with working controls is not yet confirmed.** > The Windows executable renders the intro, plays audio and reaches the main menu. > New game loading now passes the previous SPURS initialization failure and reaches > a story scene with advancing subtitles. Rendering stability and performance beyond > menus remain active work. ## The project The goal is a complete, playable native Windows recompilation of **Drakengard 3**. The project translates the PS3 executable into native code and replaces platform services where needed, with as much native execution and as little PS3 compatibility machinery as possible. **Windows x64 is the target platform.** Development currently targets **NPUB31251, version 1.01**. You supply the original game files; this repository contains the port's source, preparation tools and checks. Generated game code and local research notes stay outside version control. ## Progress | Area | Verified milestone | Remaining work | | --- | --- | --- | | Recompilation & runtime | PPU code and embedded SPU modules execute natively on Windows | Broader runtime and game compatibility | | Intro & audio | Rendering and playback confirmed; tested movie sections reach about 30 FPS | Validate later playback and transitions | | Title & menus | Title screen and main menu reached through normal keyboard input | Rendering stability and extended interaction | | New game loading | Corrected taskset initialization; reached a story scene with advancing subtitles | Validate subsequent transitions and loading times | | Input | Keyboard test controls and an XInput backend | Physical controller validation and Switch-mode 8BitDo support | | Gameplay & performance | A later scene continues rendering after a Start request | Confirm gameplay with control and improve performance beyond menus | The latest loading fix preserves the shared taskset argument during SPURS initialization. Previously it was discarded, leaving a task's memory allocator with a zero base. A bounded, hidden five-minute test continued past that failure after the correction. The latest verified checkpoint passed **26 native checks and 25 portable tests**. These validate specific runtime contracts and tooling; they do not establish complete game compatibility. A later scene measured roughly **5-6 FPS with diagnostic tracing enabled**, which is not a normal-build gameplay benchmark. The optional native audio decoder remains disabled by default. ## Rendering progress Captures from the native Windows build. These show rendering milestones; they do not establish gameplay readiness. **Title screen** ![Drakengard 3 title screen](assets/screenshots/native-title-screen.png) *The title screen, captured at approximately 29 FPS during an earlier test.* **Movie playback** ![Native movie rendering](assets/screenshots/native-movie-frame.png) *Video rendered from its YUV textures. Correcting framebuffer feedback removed persistent silhouettes and overlapping subtitles from this path.* ## Getting started **A fresh clone alone cannot build or run the game.** Building also requires your own game files and locally generated PPU/SPU sources, which are excluded from Git. Run the environment check from PowerShell in the project root: ```powershell .\scripts\doctor.ps1 ``` Once the local tools, game tree, and generated sources are prepared: ```powershell .\scripts\build-game.cmd .\scripts\check-native.ps1 .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests -v ```
Tool preparation and executable intake ```powershell .\scripts\bootstrap.ps1 python -m venv .venv .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r third_party\ps3recomp\tools\requirements.txt .\scripts\build-spu-extension.ps1 .\scripts\build-runtime.cmd .\scripts\check-toolchain.cmd .\scripts\check-ghidra.ps1 .\scripts\start-ghidra.ps1 ``` Bootstrap downloads official archives, records revisions and SHA-256 hashes locally, and checks published binary digests. Portable tools do not change global PATH or Java settings. For a completed, verified game image or directory, create a fresh intake report: ```powershell .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\inspect_input.py "PATH_TO_COMPLETED_IMAGE_OR_DIRECTORY" --download-complete --hash-all --out reports\intake-001.json ``` Intake reads metadata and hashes files. It does not extract ISO images or prove image authenticity. Recompilation needs a valid plain main ELF and the game's file tree. For your own SELF files, use RPCS3's documented extraction/decryption workflow before analyzing and lifting the executable. RPCS3 is used locally for reference runs. Firmware, accounts, licenses, and game files are not included.
## Test controls Tests run **hidden by default** and close automatically at the requested time limit. Use a fresh Run ID for each test: ```powershell .\scripts\run-game.ps1 -Run keyboard-test-001 -Seconds 300 -SkipIntro -CaptureFrames -KeyboardOnly ``` Add `-Interactive` to open a visible window. Focus it before using the keyboard; **F12** closes an interactive test. Rendering stability is still being investigated, so hidden captures remain the default. | Keyboard | Game action | | --- | --- | | Enter / Esc | Start; request a cutscene skip | | Space / Z | Cross / confirm | | Backspace / X | Circle / back | | Arrow keys | D-pad and left stick | | A / S | Square / Triangle | | Q / W | L1 / R1 | | 1 / 2 | L2 / R2 | | Tab | Select | `-KeyboardOnly` selects keyboard input even when an XInput controller is connected. An 8BitDo in Switch mode is not supported by the current backend. `-SkipIntro` (alias `-SkipMovies`) requests skips through ordinary Start presses while full-screen YUV movies are detected. It releases Start between presses and stops when movie frames stop arriving. The game decides whether a scene is skippable; menus receive no automatic confirmation presses. Engine-rendered scenes require manual input. ## Project layout | Directory | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `port/` | Windows runtime, platform compatibility, rendering integration, and native checks | | `scripts/` | Preparation, build, analysis, and bounded test runners | | `tests/` | Portable tooling tests | | `assets/` | Public screenshots | | `third_party/` | External source snapshots and their licenses | Local `input/`, `work/`, `tools/`, `build/`, `reports/`, and research notes stay outside version control. Game images, DLC, licenses, keys, memory dumps, and generated game code must remain local. ## Contributing Focused work on native execution, rendering, platform services, input and regression checks is welcome. For runtime reports, include the commit, game revision, reproduction steps, first failure and relevant performance measurements. Distinguish intro, menu, loading and gameplay results. Changes should implement the real operation and demonstrate its failure cases. Unsupported behavior must remain visible rather than being reported as successful completion. Keep game files, generated game code, saves, memory dumps and raw captures out of issues and patches. ## Source-only distribution This repository distributes project source, tooling, tests and selected screenshots. It includes **no game files, original executables, game licenses, keys or generated game code**. Supply your own local inputs and keep them in ignored directories. External source components retain their respective licenses. See the notices alongside them, including [the ps3recomp runtime notice](port/LICENSE.ps3recomp.txt). [GitHub repository](https://github.com/k1gs/Drakengard3Recompile) · [Original GitLab repository](https://gitlab.thebakerc.at/k1gs/drakengard-recompile) *Independent, unofficial project. Not affiliated with the game's rights holders.*

088befac6de09dad63a3fec66e8014d59b1f1e97.message:
ppu_loader: size per-thread TLS blocks by the TLS image, not image + 0x7000

Symptom: a title that creates more than 31 PPU threads (with a small TLS
image) gives the 32nd and every later thread the main thread's TLS, with no
message. Thread-locals that matter then collide: in Killzone 3 two threads
ended up reading one per-thread wait object, one waited forever on the other's
event queue and the level never started.

Cause: ppu_tls_new_block sized each block as memsz + 0x7000, rounded to a
page (0x8000 for a small image). The 0x7000 is the ABI's r13 bias: the guest
addresses TLS as r13 - 0x7000 + off with off < memsz, so nothing lives in it.
The 1 MB window at PPU_TLS_IMG then holds 31 blocks, and the fallback (return
0, the caller uses the main block) is silent.

Change: blocks are memsz rounded up to 4 KB (about 250 fit for a small
image); the first block still starts after the main block's image. When the
window is full, one line is logged before falling back to the shared block.

Verification: tools/test_ppu_tls_blocks.py builds the real
ppu_tls_new_block into a host program and requests 100 blocks with a
0x240-byte image. On v0.14.0 (a2c2010): granted 31/100, FAIL. With this
change: granted 100/100, no overlap with each other or the main image, image
copied into each, PASS. Also run in the Killzone 3 port (v0.13.0 base) since
2026-10-11: the thread that hung now waits on its own event queue.

0aead166fd65ab34bee01df19a341665800a727f.message:
cellGcm: a FIFO user command reaches the handler set with cellGcmSetUserHandler

Symptom: a title's cellGcmSetUserHandler callback never runs for the user
commands it puts in its command buffer. In Killzone 3 that callback submits
the per-frame job that lets the frame continue, so the level stalled.

Cause: the walker decodes GCM_SET_USER_COMMAND (method 0xEB00) as
subchannel 7 / method 0x0B00 and hands it to rsx_raise_user_cmd, the lv2
route: it posts an event to the RSX interrupt queue for a guest interrupt
thread. A title that registered its handler through the HLE
cellGcmSetUserHandler has no such thread; its handler runs from
ppu_gcm_pump. The branch then `continue`s, so the walker's later 0xEB00 case,
which calls cellGcmQueueUserCommand for the pump, is never reached.

Change: when an HLE user handler is registered, the 0x0B00 branch also
queues the command for the pump (cellGcmQueueUserCommand). The lv2 event is
still raised as before.

Verification: libs/video/tests/test_gcm_fifo_user_command.c (standalone,
includes cellGcmSys.c like test_gcm_user_command.c; graphics backends
stubbed) registers an HLE user handler, then five times puts one user
command in the ring, drains it with cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo and calls
ppu_gcm_pump. With this change the handler runs five times, each with its
command's argument, and the lv2 route is still taken five times (gcc and
clang). Against v0.14.0's cellGcmSys.c (a2c2010) the handler never runs
(5/5 fail). test_gcm_user_command.c still passes.

0fb35648aed8ca984638357c2e82c0e892c12c8b.message:
ppu_sysprx: sys_lwcond_t is +0x00 lwmutex EA, +0x04 queue id

Symptom: a title that reads lwcond+0x00 itself sees 0 there and treats the
lwcond as invalid (Killzone 3's file system layer checks it before every
wait and loops). The queue id is also written past the 8-byte structure,
over whatever the title keeps next to it.

Cause: the context-style sys_lwcond_create in ppu_sysprx.cpp writes the
lwmutex EA as a 64-bit value at +0x00 (so the EA lands at +0x04 and +0x00
reads 0) and the id at +0x08. sys_lwcond_t is 8 bytes: +0x00 u32 lwmutex
EA, +0x04 u32 queue id, which is also what libs/system/sysPrxForUser.h
declares as sys_lwcond_t_hle.

Change: 32-bit stores at +0x00 and +0x04 in sys_lwcond_create, and a 32-bit
read of +0x00 in sys_lwcond_wait. Wait/signal behaviour is unchanged.

Verification: tools/test_lwcond_layout.py builds the real
sys_lwcond_create and sys_lwcond_wait into a host program over stubbed
guest memory. With this change +0x00 holds the lwmutex EA, +0x04 a nonzero
id, nothing past +0x08 is written, and the wait finds the lwmutex. On
v0.14.0 (a2c2010) +0x00 reads 0, the EA is at +0x04 and the id is written
at +0x08 (2 of 3 checks fail; the wait found the lwmutex there only because
create and wait agreed on the wrong layout).

12158c45650cc5d00d228a62f98c3a204aacc300.message:
ppu_lifter: exact VMX, branch decode, integer, FP and decoding fixes

VMX
- runtime/ppu/ppu_vmx.h implements every VMX op exactly, and the lifter
  routes ops by raw XO: some had no disassembler name and lifted as no-ops.
  About 45 did nothing: the saturating adds/subs, vavg*, vmul[eo]*, vmsum*,
  vmhadd*/vmhradd*, vmladduhm, vrlh, the element and whole-vector shifts,
  vpk*, vsum*, vaddcuw/vsubcuw, vpkpx/vupk*px, vexptefp/vlogefp.
- Saturation sets VSCR[SAT], VSCR[NJ] is honoured, vcmp*. writes CR6;
  mtvscr/mfvscr are decoded, and VRSAVE reads back (ppu_context.vrsave).

Branches
- BO/BI come from the instruction word, so bdnzt/bdzf decrement CTR and
  test the condition (they were always taken); CTR is 64-bit.
- Every LK=1 form sets LR unconditionally.
- b<cond>lrl dispatches through ps3_indirect_call_to and leaves CTR alone.
- bl 0 / bcl 20,31,0 (get-PC) lift as get-PC, not as a call.

Integer
- XER[OV]/[SO] set by every OE form; compares and stwcx./stdcx. copy SO.
- rlwinm/rlwnm/rlwimi handle wrapping masks (MB > ME).
- mulld/mulli wrap, and lifted code builds with -fwrapv.
- mtxer keeps only the defined bits; mfocrf isolates its field.

Decoding: lswi/lswx/stswi/stswx, lwaux, stdbrx, stvlx/stvrx(l), lvrxl, td,
dst/dss.

FP: single-precision results (NaNs included) are single-format; fctiw/fctiwz
write the whole FPR; the FPSCR moves (mffs, mtfsf, mtfsfi, mtfsb0/1, mcrfs)
are implemented; FP record forms set CR1.

CR fusion checks the fused field's liveness past the branch target; it used
to fuse a compare that was re-tested after the label.

Guest loads in lifted code are inline (vm_read*_inl in the header preamble);
ppu_loader.cpp keeps the out-of-line accessors, and the inline path stands
down while a read diagnostic (PPU_RWATCH and friends) is armed.

conformance checks), the boot smoke and template pass, and the PPU

one case left (LWBRX#32) differs only because

for every report. Killzone 3 selects the main-memory report context and
issues about 160 reports per frame in a level (timestamps and occlusion
queries); none of them ever reached the memory it reads.

Cause: the FIFO walker ignored NV4097_SET_CONTEXT_DMA_REPORT (0x1A8) and
wrote every NV4097_GET_REPORT (0x1800) into the host s_report_data slots,
indexed by offset / 16, whatever context the title had selected.

Change: the walker records the context set by 0x1A8 (reset to local by
cellGcmInit and cellGcmTerminate). With the local context (0xFEED0000, the
default) a report goes to s_report_data as before. With the main-memory
context (0xFEED0001, or CELL_GCM_CONTEXT_DMA_REPORT_LOCATION_MAIN 0xBAD68000)
the report's offset is an IO offset and the 16-byte report is written
big-endian to gcm_io2ea(offset): u64 timestamp, u32 value, u32 0. An offset
with no IO mapping is skipped with a rate-limited log line. Report
timestamps now rise strictly, so two reports in one walker pass never share
or reverse a time stamp.

Verification: tests/gcm_reports (CTest, built with PS3RECOMP_BUILD_TESTS on
POSIX hosts like the host harness) builds a ring with local reports, a
switch to 0xFEED0001, main-memory reports of type 1 and 2, one unmapped
offset and a switch back, drains it once with cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo and
reads every slot back. Run as a MinGW-w64 build under Proton (this machine
has no Linux SDL2 for the POSIX runtime build): with this change 9/9 checks
pass; the same test linked against v0.14.0's cellGcmSys.c (a2c2010) fails
6/9 (main-memory slots keep their sentinel, the reports land in the host
area instead, timestamps not written). Carried as a local patch in the
Killzone 3 port (v0.13.0 base).

24286f4b3871aff53cf988448e1fc756956372dc.message:
cellGcm: in-FIFO flip wraps only the runtime's own command ring

Symptom: intermittently a title waits forever on a fence. Killzone 3
stopped about 16 s in, depending on where the walker's get offset was.

Cause: _cellGcmSetFlipCommand's HLE (gcm_flip_into_fifo) writes the flip
marker at ctx->current and then, when less than GCM_FLIP_WRAP_BYTES are
left before ctx->end and the walker is well past begin, wraps the context
it was given: a JUMP to begin after the marker and ctx->current = begin.
That is what the SDK's buffer-full callback does for the runtime's ring.
A title with its own buffer-full callback manages its own buffers, and its
context need not be a ring: Killzone 3 flips on a 0x30000-byte draw
context whose end moves down as it allocates from the top, so it always
looks nearly full. Rewinding it mid-frame cut the frame short, the fence
release in its tail never ran, and the title waited for it.

Change: wrap only when the context's buffer-full callback descriptor
(ctx + 0xC) still points at the runtime's callback
(GCM_FIFO_CALLBACK_SENTINEL_EA, installed by cellGcmSetupContext). Other
contexts get the marker and current advances past it, as when there is
room.

Verification: libs/video/tests/test_gcm_flip_wrap.c (standalone, includes
cellGcmSys.c like test_gcm_user_command.c) flips on two nearly full
contexts with the walker 0x28000 bytes past their begin: the ring made by
cellGcmSetupContext, and a title context with its own callback. With this
change the runtime ring wraps (marker, JUMP to begin, current = begin) and
the title context does not (marker, current past it), with gcc and clang.
Against v0.14.0's cellGcmSys.c (a2c2010) the title context is wrapped too
(1 of 2 fails). test_gcm_user_command.c still passes.

286d3ed9e33988664a79553b347bcf5af96d2673.message:
cellGcm: IO mapping table 16 -> 512 slots, no IO leak on refusal, iomap fills a free slot

Symptom: a title that maps many separate main-memory chunks loses the later
ones. Killzone 3 maps up to 38 one-megabyte chunks at level load and keeps
vertex buffers in them; after the 16th, cellGcmMapMainMemory failed, those
buffers had no IO offset and every geometry draw in a level was degenerate
(only effects over black).

Cause:
- CELL_GCM_MAX_IO_MAPPINGS is 16. libgcm has no such small fixed count; a
  mapping fails when the IO address space runs out.
- cellGcmMapMainMemory allocates the IO region before it looks for a free
  slot, so each refused call still consumes IO address space.
- cellGcm_syscall_iomap writes s_io_mappings[s_io_mapping_count]. After an
  unmap the count no longer points past the last used slot, so a new mapping
  overwrites a live one.

Change:
- 512 slots (16 bytes each; an assumed bound well above what titles use),
  overridable with -DCELL_GCM_MAX_IO_MAPPINGS=N.
- cellGcmMapMainMemory looks for a free slot before allocating the region.
- cellGcm_syscall_iomap takes a slot from find_free_mapping like the other
  mapping paths.
The return codes and every other mapping function are unchanged.

Verification: tools/test_gcm_io_mappings.py builds the real
find_free_mapping, gcm_io_alloc, cellGcmMapMainMemory and
cellGcm_syscall_iomap against stubs. On v0.14.0 (a2c2010): FAIL (15 chunks
before the first refusal, the refusal leaks IO space, iomap after an unmap
overwrites a live mapping). With this change: PASS (510 chunks with distinct
offsets, no leak, live mapping kept). Negative controls on a copy of this
branch: 16 slots fails the chunk check (14), a count-indexed iomap fails the
live-slot check. cellGcmSys.c passes cc -fsyntax-only. Used in the Killzone 3
port (v0.13.0 base): its level geometry draws with this change.
