40789072e4e6c70539b3e18cddb51a99d25c417e.message:
live-draw: depth buffers read as textures return the real depth

Symptom: a DEPTH24_D8 texture that reads a zeta comes back 0 or partly 0
in three common shapes: a full-screen read of a depth buffer whose first
pass used a smaller clip, a read of an address that is both a colour target
and a zeta, and a draw that reads the zeta it is depth-testing against
(deferred lighting, soft particles). Effects that depend on scene depth
(depth of field, fog, soft particles, deferred lighting) then see a flat 0.

Causes and changes (rsx_live_draw.c):
1. The R32F snapshot of a zeta keeps the clip size of the first pass that
   bound it (512x512 of a 1280x720 depth buffer, say), so later reads get 0
   outside that corner. zdepth_get now grows the snapshot to the largest
   clip bound since, within the depth resource (zdepth_grow_snapshot: a new
   resource, descriptors rewritten, the old one retired, re-resolved at the
   next read).
2. A depth-format read of an address that is also a colour target matched
   the colour surface first. When a written host zeta exists at that
   address the read now takes the zeta.
3. A draw that samples its own bound zeta with depth writes off read guest
   memory, which the host depth never reaches. It now reads the zeta's
   snapshot; the zeta cannot change during such a draw. A draw that writes
   the zeta it reads keeps the old fallback.

fp decompiler: the NV40 pack and unpack opcodes

PK4UB, UP4UB, PKG, UPG, PK4B, UP4B, PK2US, UP2US, PK2H and UP2H had no case:

ppu_lifter: big-endian lane order for ten VMX integer ops

Symptom: lifted code computes wrong results for vmulouh, vmsumshm, vadduws,
vadduhs and vpkuwum, and does nothing at all for vmsumuhm, vsubuws,
vpkswss, vsrb and vsrab, which were emitted as "/* TODO */" no-ops.

Cause: ctx->vr holds raw big-endian guest bytes. The first five handlers
read halfword and word lanes through int16_t*/uint32_t* casts, which gives
byte-reversed lanes (and the wrong lane pairing) on a little-endian host.
The other five had no lowering.

Change: one handler for the ten ops that assembles each halfword or word
lane from its bytes in big-endian order, computes the result as the AltiVec
PEM defines it (modulo, saturating or shift) and stores it back in the same
order. The five old handlers are removed.

Verification: tools/test_ppu_vmx_lanes.py lifts each op, compiles the
emitted C with the lifter's own preamble and compares vD with an independent
Python model of the instruction on 300 inputs per op (216 edge combinations
plus random vectors). With this change 10/10 ops agree on every input. On
v0.14.0 (a2c2010) all ten fail: five emit TODO, the other five differ on
244 to 292 of 300 inputs. tools/test_ppu_vcmp_record_cr6.py and
tools/test_ppu_lift.py pass before and after.

662270bdf366da3e360385f421ce5192f82b3443.message:
ppu_loader: indirect-call depth guard can be kept per coroutine

Symptom: a title whose guest jobs run on host coroutines (host fibers that
stand in for a guest fiber scheduler) works for a while, then every
indirect call on that thread is skipped by the recursion guard, even calls
to leaf functions ("[ppu] recursion cap ... skipping"); null calls and an
exit follow. Killzone 3 quit a few minutes into a level.

Cause: the guard in ps3_indirect_call_impl keeps one depth count per host
thread in a function-local thread_local. A coroutine that ends by switching
away from inside an indirect call never unwinds its frames, so each one
leaks its depth into the thread's count until the count passes the 4000
cap. The vcall stack pointer (g_vcall_sp) leaks the same way. Neither can be
reached from outside the function, so a coroutine layer has no way to keep
them per coroutine.

Change: the depth count moves to a file-scope thread-local, and two
accessors, ps3_ppu_dispatch_depth_slot() and ps3_ppu_vcall_sp_slot(), return
the current thread's counters. A coroutine layer saves *slot when it
switches away and restores it when it switches back. Threads that never
switch behave exactly as before.

Verification: tools/test_ppu_dispatch_depth.py builds the real
ppu_loader.cpp with runtime/ppu/tests/test_ppu_dispatch_depth.cpp. 5000
ucontext coroutines each go five ps3_indirect_call levels deep and switch
back to the home context without returning; the home side saves and
restores both counters around each switch. With this change all 5000
chains run to the bottom, the home thread's depth and vcall sp are 0
before and after, and a later indirect call runs. Against v0.14.0's
ppu_loader.cpp (a2c2010; the accessors do not exist, the test declares
them weak) only 800 of 5000 chains run: the guard trips at depth 4001 and
skips every call after that.

spu: SPU_RdDec wrapped 231 s after the base stamp

The decrementer scaled elapsed nanoseconds by 79.8 MHz before dividing, and
ns * 79800000 passes 2^64 at 231 s. A context that writes its decrementer
restamps the base and never gets there; the SPURS kernel context never writes
it, keeps the stamp from boot, and every timed loop on that SPU saw the
counter jump forward by ~16 s of ticks at 231 s, 462 s, 693 s... Scale the
whole seconds and the remainder separately.

83937a9bec73f4d16ed725122cfa65e955629946.message:
runtime: thread-locals stay thread-local under MinGW (__declspec(thread) only for MSVC)

Symptom (MinGW-w64 builds only): two PPU threads that exit close together
crash; one thread's sys_ppu_thread_exit longjmps toward a frame on the other
thread's stack. In Killzone 3 this is the two Bink threads exiting at the
end of the intro movie. The SPURS job mailboxes and the sysutil completion
drain guard are shared between threads the same way.

Cause: sys_ppu_thread.c, spurs_job.c, cellSpurs.c and cellSysutil.c pick
__declspec(thread) when _WIN32 is defined. MinGW GCC defines _WIN32 and
ignores that attribute ("'thread' attribute directive ignored"), so the
exit jmp_buf and its armed flag, g_spurs_job_mbox* and the completion
`draining` flag are plain process-wide globals there. The runtime's other
thread-local macros (PPU_THREAD_LOCAL, SPU_THREAD_LOCAL, SPU_TLS) already
test _MSC_VER.

Change: those four macros use __declspec(thread) only under _MSC_VER and
__thread / _Thread_local otherwise, like the others. MSVC and POSIX builds
are unchanged.

Verification: tools/test_mingw_tls.py finds every macro in runtime/ and
libs/ defined to __declspec(thread), keeps its surrounding preprocessor
conditionals and compiles a static variable with it as MinGW sees it
(x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc when present, else the host compiler with _WIN32
defined and __declspec(x) as __attribute__((x))), then checks the variable
is thread-local in the assembly. Without MinGW gcc the emulation runs only on
ELF hosts and only after two controls (__thread reads as thread-local, a
plain static does not) pass; otherwise, as on macOS, the test prints SKIP. With this change 9/9 qualifiers are
thread-local under both compilers; on v0.14.0 (a2c2010) 4 of 9 are
process-wide globals (spurs_job.c, sys_ppu_thread.c, cellSpurs.c,
cellSysutil.c). The four changed files pass -fsyntax-only with MinGW GCC and
host GCC.

8eb45f8647cde8750f675f5725ea0bd325ec9618.message:
cellFs: 64-bit sizes and offsets in ppu_fs on Windows

Symptom: on Windows a file larger than 2 GiB is mis-sized and mis-seeked.
With a MinGW-w64 (msvcrt) build cellFsStat fails with CELL_ENOENT (the CRT's
stat wrapper reports EOVERFLOW); with UCRT (llvm-mingw) it succeeds with a
truncated size. cellFsLseek and cellFsFstat truncate to 32 bits, so a read
after a seek past 4 GiB lands at the wrong offset.

Cause: ppu_fs.cpp uses stat() with a 32-bit st_size and fseek()/ftell()
with `long`, which is 32 bits on LLP64 Windows. LP64 hosts are unaffected.

Change: _stat64, _fseeki64 and _ftelli64 on Windows; stat, fseeko and ftello
elsewhere, for cellFsStat, cellFsLseek and cellFsFstat. A trailing slash is
stripped before _stat64, which rejects it (MinGW's stat wrapper used to
strip it). The FS_FSTAT_CAP diagnostic now parses and prints 64-bit values.

Verification: tools/test_ppu_fs_large_file.py builds a fixture that
includes ppu_fs.cpp, creates a sparse 5 GiB file with a marker near its end
and checks cellFsStat, cellFsLseek (SET and END), cellFsRead after the seek
and cellFsFstat. Built with x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++ (--build-only) and run
under Wine: master fails 6 of 7 checks (Stat 0x80010006, Lseek 0x40000008,
Fstat 0x40000010); with this change all 7 pass. On Linux it passes on both.

b3082644982c43d81c8bf47959317dc4cb3cfbf1.message:
cellGcm: give a parked FIFO time to be patched before following put

A self-JUMP at the write head parks the RSX, and when `put` had meanwhile
moved elsewhere the walker took that as the title having abandoned the park
and resynced to `put` at once. inFAMOUS 2 links its main-memory command
blocks the other way round: it ends a block in a park, writes the next
commands at the ring start, moves `put`, and only then rewrites the park as a
JUMP to them. A drain that landed between the two stores went straight to
`put` and dropped everything from the ring start up to it, the frame's fence
included, so the title waited on that label for the rest of the run and the
main menu froze.

Resync only once the same park has stood with the same `put` for longer than
a title takes between the two stores (50 ms). A park patched in time is
followed as before; the pass reports itself as "parked" in the meantime.

b6dc1e428b4b89c8385595551904bfb21c33d71a.message:
ppu_lifter: jump tables behind a tail-call epilogue

discover_jump_tables drops the blocks that end in `blr` from the backward
scan for the table base register: they return, so they cannot flow into the
dispatcher. An epilogue that leaves by a tail call ends the same way and
restores the same registers, and was not dropped. inFAMOUS 2's func_000B9BD0
loads the base's base into r30 in its prologue, has an early exit
`ld r30,0xE0(r1); ...; b 0xB8570`, and dispatches nineteen instructions later
through `lwz r11,-0x7F80(r30)`: the restore read as r30's nearest definition,
no base resolved, and the switch lifted to an unresolved indirect call.

A `b` leaves the function when it goes back past the function's entry or
forward to another function's entry. Both need func_starts; without them the
scan is bounded by the nearest `blr`, which an early return puts in the
middle of a function, so only `blr` is trusted there.

tools/test_ppu_jumptables.py: the backward shape (the inFAMOUS 2 one), the
forward one, and the no-func_starts control.

b883922940d53efafac47dcc0b63dac7535294c5.message:
rsx_draw_engine, vulkan: honour the depth bounds test

NV4097 SET_DEPTH_BOUNDS_TEST_ENABLE (0x0380) with SET_DEPTH_BOUNDS_MIN and
_MAX (0x0384, 0x0388, floats) rejects a fragment whose stored depth lies
outside the bounds, whatever the depth test says. The draw engine never
read those registers, so a bounded draw covered the whole target.

Twisted Metal's deferred renderer relies on it: its sun pass is bounded to
[0, 0.999984] (the geometry) and the sky drawn right after it to
[0.999984, 1] (the far plane), both with the depth test off. Unbounded, the
sky overwrote the sun light everywhere and the HDR buffer came out almost
black.

The enable is pipeline state (rsx_be_render_state.depth_bounds_test, part
of the pipeline key); the bounds reach the backend before every draw through
a new optional hook, set_depth_bounds, like the stencil reference, so moving
them does not build pipelines. Vulkan enables the depthBounds feature when
the device has it and sets the bounds dynamically, clamped to [0, 1];
without the feature the test stays off, as before, with one log line.
Metal and the fixed-function path leave the hook unset and draw as before.

Tests: test_rsx_draw_engine checks the key, the bounds and that moving them
builds no pipeline (4 new checks, failing without the engine change).
ps3recomp_host --depthbounds draws red at z = 0.25, then blue bounded to
[0, 0.5] and green bounded to [0.5, 1] with the depth test off, and expects
blue; it runs in the Vulkan workflow's engine pass under the validation
layer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

b8cb0c8ceafc1238f3fb38c6286db64794d9c885.message:
spu: hardware-exact float semantics, NEON paths, interpreter op fixes

Float (spu_helpers.h), rewritten from the SPU ISA, single and double
precision: truncation (round toward zero), denormal flush, the extended
range, saturation, frest's hardware table, fi, the compares (fceq/fcgt/
fcmeq/fcmgt) and the conversions (cflts/cfltu/csflt/cuflt). The previous
helpers were a GPL-derived port; these are written from the ISA alone and
checked against an exact-arithmetic referee.

Speed, bit-identical output: NEON forms of fa/fs/fm/fma/fms/fnms (1.6-4x
faster), of 60 per-lane integer ops, and of shufb (tbl); test_spu_float_neon
and test_spu_int_neon compare them against the scalar forms.

Interpreter (spu_interp.c):

live-draw: decode ZSTENCIL_CLEAR_VALUE by the zeta format (Z16)

Symptom: in the D3D12 live-draw backend a Z16 zeta cleared with 0xFFFF

edat: take the klicensee the title passes to sceNpDrmIsAvailable[2]

Symptom: a free (license type 3) or disc-bound EDAT under a title-specific
klicensee fails to open with -6 ("needs a RIF key"), even though the title
supplies its key the way it does on hardware.

Cause: on hardware a title passes its own klicensee to sceNpDrmIsAvailable
or sceNpDrmIsAvailable2 before it opens such a file, and the kernel keeps it
for later opens. The runtime has neither call, so the key is lost, and the
EDAT reader only tries the built-in platform klicensees.

Change: sceNp.c implements sceNpDrmIsAvailable and sceNpDrmIsAvailable2;
both hand a non-NULL klicensee to edat_add_klicensee() (new, edat.h) and
return CELL_OK. edat.c keeps up to 16 such keys, ignores duplicates, and
tries them before the built-in ones. Each key is still checked against the
file's dev_hash (AES-CMAC under klic ^ NP_OMAC_KEY_2 over header bytes
0x00-0x5F, the same check for NPD versions 2-4) before it is used, and each
block hash is checked as before. A license type 3 file that no key verifies
now fails with a message that names sceNpDrmIsAvailable. Projects that read
the key some other way can call edat_add_klicensee() themselves.

libs/filesystem/tests/test_edat_guest_klicensee.c with sceNp.c. The test

every block hash verified and the plaintext matching after

d0d67442f549faf07f8547adcb4fdc6e6dc74c08.message:
spu_channels: MFC engine table 8 -> 64 slots, and a full table is reported as an error

Symptom: intermittent stops where an SPU context waits forever on a DMA
tag that already completed. Killzone 3 holds eleven SPU contexts with an
MFC engine at once (policy-module contexts that keep their engine for as
long as their workload exists, plus SPU thread groups); the runtime prints
"more than 8 contexts hold an MFC engine at once; the rest share one".

Cause: the per-context engine table has SPU_MAX_CONTEXTS = 8 slots. Every
context past the eighth gets one shared fallback engine, where one
context's completion clears the tag bits another context is waiting on.
Eight is a thread group's worth, but a title can hold more contexts at
once than the machine has SPUs. The overflow was reported once, as a note.

Change: 64 slots (overridable with -DSPU_MAX_CONTEXTS). When the table is
still full, the shared engine stays as the last resort, but the runtime now
reports it as an error naming the table size, the context and the
consequence, at the first overflow lookup and again at 1000 and 1000000 so
it stays visible in a long log; s_mfc_overflow_lookups counts them. A
growable table can replace this later.

Verification: runtime/spu/tests/test_spu_mfc_slots.c (built as in the CI
workflows) keeps its 8-thread claim race over 32 rounds and adds: eleven
contexts held at once get eleven distinct engines and keep the state each
wrote; the table holds SPU_MAX_CONTEXTS contexts with no overflow; the next
context gets the overflow engine and the overflow is counted. With this
change 889 checks pass with gcc and clang, and the error line is printed
once. Against v0.14.0's spu_channels.c (a2c2010; the counter compiled as a
constant 0) 3 checks fail: the eleven contexts share engines, their state
is overwritten, and the overflow is not counted.

df3a7cbae234fb6701b6e1d1df2d3417b9e03a2a.message:
ppu_lifter: --chunks N cuts the source by guest address and rewrites only changed files

Symptom: any change to the lifter's input or to the lifter (a fix for one
opcode, one function's bounds) makes the build recompile nearly all of the
lifted source. For Killzone 3 (eight 600k-line chunks, 6.5-8 minutes and
2.5-4.4 GB of compiler memory each) that is 15-25 minutes per rebuild.

Cause: (1) chunks are cut every --chunk-lines emitted lines, so a change in
one function's line count moves every later cut point and changes the text of
every later chunk; (2) main() deletes the previous chunk set before writing,
so every file gets a new mtime even when its content is the same, and make or
ninja rebuild it.

Change:
- --chunks N (default 0 = off) cuts the source into N files by guest code
  bytes: chunk k holds the functions, in address order, of the range that
  carries the k-th N-th of the lifted bytes. That is a function of the
  function list alone, so the same functions always land in the same file. The
  function table goes to its own <source>_table.cpp, so a new function does
  not change the last chunk. A chunk over --chunk-lines lines prints a warning
  (MSVC's 16M-line limit).
- Every output file (header, chunks, table, the --single-file source) is
  written through write_if_changed: a temporary file and a rename, and only
  when the content differs, so unchanged files keep their mtime.
- Stale files of an earlier run (other cut points, the single-file source)
  are removed after writing instead of all files before.

How this relates to --chunk-lines (#216): --chunk-lines sets how large a
line-cut chunk may be (fewer lines per translation unit for hosts short on
memory) and stays the default mode; it now also profits from
write_if_changed. --chunks makes the cut points stable across relifts; with
it, --chunk-lines is only the warning threshold. Both can be used.

e99cbbf0a9c93d99b9ba43fbd142365f4403ba13.message:
fp decompiler: predicated writes are a select, not a lerp

Symptom: a fragment-program instruction executed under a condition code
(exec_if lt/eq/gt) changes components of its destination that the condition
leaves alone when either operand holds Inf, NaN or raw bits. Programs that
keep packed words in a register (the PK*/UP* pack/unpack pattern) read 0 or
NaN after a predicated MOV.

Cause: the predicated destination write was emitted as
lerp(dst, v, mask). lerp is arithmetic (dst + mask * (v - dst)): an Inf or NaN
in the unselected operand gives NaN (0 * Inf), and denormal and NaN bit
patterns are not preserved through the ALU.

Change: emit a per-component select, (mask != 0.0) ? v : dst, which FXC
compiles to movc. The unconditional path is unchanged.

Verification: libs/video/tests/test_fp_decompiler.c gains a case with a MOV
predicated on CC0 > 0 that checks the select form and that no lerp is
emitted. It fails on master (39 passed, 2 failed) and passes with this change
(41 passed, 0 failed). The same select has been in use in a D3D12 title port
under Proton; there a test with predicated writes over raw-bit and Inf/NaN
operands read 8 of 8 values back correctly, 4 of 8 with lerp.

cellHttp: response getters under their SDK names; RecvResponse into guest memory

Symptom: a title that reads an HTTP answer through
cellHttpResponseGetStatusCode, cellHttpResponseGetContentLength and
cellHttpResponseGetAllHeaders gets CELL_OK with the status unset and a NULL
header array, and drops every response. A body that outgrows the header read
is recv()'d into the host address equal to the guest buffer's EA (recv fails
with EFAULT, or writes into host memory).

Cause: the runtime has cellHttpGetStatusCode and
cellHttpGetResponseContentLength, whose computed NIDs match no firmware
import, and no cellHttpResponseGetAllHeaders, so the three imports take the
unresolved-NID path. In cellHttpRecvResponse the overflow copy translates
the guest buffer but the socket read does not.

Change: add cellHttpResponseGetStatusCode, cellHttpResponseGetContentLength
(0x80710017 when the response has no Content-Length) and
cellHttpResponseGetAllHeaders ({name, value} guest pointers followed by the
strings in the caller's pool; a size query with no pool writes only
*required; a pool too small returns NO_BUFFER). Titles call them before the
first cellHttpRecvResponse, so they read the headers first. The older
functions keep their names. cellHttpRecvResponse recv()s into the
translated guest buffer.

Verification: tools/test_http_response_getters.py builds
libs/network/tests/test_http_response_getters.c against a loopback
listener: a 200 answer with three headers and a 3000-byte body of which
only 100 bytes arrive with the headers, then a response without
Content-Length. On master: 4 failed (the three getters missing; the body

f110c349c230521f60cb5f27f7449fd90144e779.message:
cellSaveData: UserAutoSave keeps its ninth argument; handlers registered at init

Symptom: a title that saves with cellSaveDataUserAutoSave gets
cbResult->userdata == 0 in its stat and file callbacks. A title that keeps
its save state behind userdata writes through a null pointer and saves an
empty profile.

Cause: cellSaveDataUserAutoSave takes nine arguments; the ninth (userdata)
is in the caller's parameter save area at SP+112. UserAutoLoad already has
a context handler that reads it, UserAutoSave has none, and nothing in the
runtime calls cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers(), so both calls go through
the generic eight-argument binding unless a project registers the handlers
itself.

Change: a context handler for cellSaveDataUserAutoSave (NID 0x52AAC4FA),
the same as UserAutoLoad's, registered in
cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers(). It calls cellSaveDataAutoSave rather
than AutoSave2: AutoSave2 maps dirName to a host pointer and hands it to
AutoSave, which maps it again, so a host address below 4 GiB (seen on
Windows) would be read as a guest address. ppu_sysprx_register() now calls
cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers() next to np_score_register_ctx(), so
every project gets both handlers. A project that already calls it keeps
working: the first registration of a NID wins and both point at the same
handler.

Verification: tools/test_savedata_user_autosave.py checks that
ppu_sysprx_register() calls cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers(), then
builds libs/system/tests/test_savedata_user_autosave.c, which registers the
handlers into a local table and calls UserAutoLoad and UserAutoSave with a
userdata value at SP+112; the runner passes a scratch save root as argv[1].

rsx: antialiased surfaces at sample resolution

Symptom: a texture that reads an antialiased render target's memory sees
the wrong size. A 320x180 surface drawn with SQUARE_ROTATED_4 is a 640x360
image in memory (2x2 samples per pixel), but the host surface was created at
320x180, so a 640x360 texture read of it (its colour or its zeta) found
nothing to alias or a quarter of the data.

Cause: rsx_dsp_get_surface ignored SURFACE_FORMAT's antialias field (bits
12-15) and reported the clip rectangle in pixels.

Change:
- rsx_dispatch: rsx_dsp_surface gains antialias, aa_sx and aa_sy, and the
  clip rectangle is reported in samples: DIAGONAL_CENTERED_2 (3) is 2x1,
  SQUARE_CENTERED_4 (4) and SQUARE_ROTATED_4 (5) are 2x2; other modes stay
  1x1.
- rsx_live_draw and rsx_draw_engine: the viewport and scissor registers are
  in guest pixels, so the viewport epilogue maps NDC over clip / aa and the
  scissor is multiplied by aa_sx/aa_sy. Both backends read
  rsx_dsp_get_surface, so both need this to keep drawing over the whole
  target.

Verification:
- libs/video/tests/test_rsx_draw_engine.c, new test_antialiased_surface:
  a 128x64 target with scissor 8,4 32x16 and a full-pixel viewport in modes
  0, 3, 4 and 5 checks the created surface size, the scissor in samples and
  the viewport epilogue. master: 6 checks failed (surface 128x64 and
  scissor 8,4 32x16 in modes 3-5); with this change: all checks passed;
  with only the rsx_dispatch half: 6 failed (scissor unscaled, viewport
  scale 0.5).
- libs/video/tests/test_live_draw_aa_surface.c (new, D3D12, with the
  shared harness live_draw_test_harness.h): an 8x8-pixel target per mode is
  cleared to black, a white quad is drawn over the whole viewport with the
  scissor on the left 4 pixels, and the surface is read back. Built with
  MinGW-w64 and run under Proton (vkd3d) with one test-only local change
  that is not part of this commit (the depth-snapshot compute shader's
  RWTexture2D::GetDimensions removed, which vkd3d-shader does not compile).

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   └── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse
│   ├── hardware/             # cellGem, cellCamera, cellUsbd
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
└── docs/                     # See the Documentation table below
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

HLE implementations of the PS3 system libraries, written for this project. RPCS3 is a behavioural reference, not a code source. **About 93 modules complete and 5 partial** (media decode, SPURS), in roughly 260 files and 100,000 lines under `libs/`.

| Category | Modules | Status |
|----------|---------|--------|
| **Kernel Threading** | sys_ppu_thread, sys_mutex, sys_cond, sys_semaphore, sys_rwlock | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Events** | sys_event (queues, ports, flags), sys_timer | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Memory** | sys_memory, sys_mmapper (containers, shared mem) | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Filesystem** | sys_fs (path mapping, real I/O) | ✅ Complete |
| **Filesystem** | cellFs (real file I/O, dir ops, stat, path translation) | ✅ Complete |
| **Save System** | cellSaveData (callback-driven, PARAM.SFO), cellGame | ✅ Complete |
| **Input** | cellPad (XInput/SDL2), cellKb, cellMouse | ✅ Complete |
| **Audio** | cellAudio (WASAPI/SDL2, mixing thread, multi-port) | ✅ Complete |
| **Video Output** | cellVideoOut (resolution config, 720p default) | ✅ Complete |
| **Codecs** | cellPngDec, cellJpgDec, cellGifDec (stb_image) | ✅ Complete |
| **Font** | cellFont (stb_truetype backend + fallback metrics) | ✅ Complete |
| **Network** | sys_net (BSD sockets, P2P), cellNet, cellNetCtl, cellHttpUtil, cellSsl, sceNp*, sceNpTrophy, sceNpMatching2 + Score over [psnr](docs/ONLINE.md) | ✅ Complete |
| **Hardware** | cellUsbd (USB), cellCamera (PS Eye), cellGem (PS Move) — stub, no devices | ✅ Complete |
| **Sync** | cellSync (atomic spinlocks, LF queue), cellSync2 (OS-backed) | ✅ Complete |
| **System** | cellRtc, cellMsgDialog, cellOskDialog, cellUserInfo, cellGameExec | ✅ Complete |
| **Localization** | cellL10n (UTF-8/16/32/UCS-2, ISO-8859-1, generic converter) | ✅ Complete |
| **Resolution** | cellResc (display modes, scaling, interlace, aspect ratio) | ✅ Complete |
| **Fibers** | cellFiber (PPU fibers via Windows Fibers/ucontext) | ✅ Complete |
| **AV Config** | cellAvconfExt (audio output info, gamma, sound availability) | ✅ Complete |
| **Input Util** | cellKey2char (HID scancode → Unicode, US-101 layout) | ✅ Complete |
| **Graphics** | cellGcmSys (cmd buffer, IO mapping, tile/zcull, flip handlers, timestamps, FIFO walker + ring recycle), RSX command processor (NV47xx parsing, state tracking, backend callbacks), **live D3D12 backend** (executes the title's real NV4097 vertex/fragment programs — indexed draws, per-draw VP constants + textures, render-to-texture, MRT, FP predication), null backend (Win32 window) | ✅ Complete |

Full status tracking: [docs/MODULE_STATUS.md](docs/MODULE_STATUS.md)

# 🎮 Featured Native Port — Uncharted 3: Drake's Deception (BCES01175)

> **Project Status:** 🚧 Active Development

## About the Project

**Uncharted 3: Drake's Deception** is the flagship project built using the **ps3recomp** framework.

The goal is to transform the original PlayStation 3 executable into a fully native desktop application without relying on runtime emulation. Instead of interpreting the Cell processor instructions at runtime, the game's PPU and SPU code is statically recompiled into native C/C++ and linked against the ps3recomp runtime.

This project demonstrates the capabilities of static recompilation on one of the most technically demanding PlayStation 3 games ever released.

## Current Progress

The project has already reached several important milestones:

- ✅ Native PPU recompilation
- ✅ SPU recompilation and runtime integration
- ✅ Runtime, threading and virtual memory operational
- ✅ File system, archives and asset loading
- ✅ Audio subsystem initialization
- ✅ SPURS initialization
- ✅ RSX command processing
- ✅ Native Direct3D 12 rendering backend
- 🔄 Graphics pipeline completion
- 🔄 SPU task scheduling and rendering synchronization

### Status Summary (current focus)

Boot, runtime, filesystem/asset loading, SPURS initialization and the native
Direct3D 12 render pipeline are operational (the loading screen renders
correctly). The active frontier is **Phase 11 — SPU Handling** of the porting
guide: the SPU/SPURS asset-decode **completion** path.

Concretely, the front-end **main menu is not yet reached**. It is gated on the
render state-machine marking each resource *decode-ready* once its SPU-decoded
geometry lands, and on the menu-scene transition trigger. The deterministic SPU
executor and the lifted geometry decode are validated live end-to-end; the
remaining work is wiring the decode/residence **completion** back into the
render-readiness chain and the menu-scene construction. This is the documented
"hard part" for a complex AAA title.

**Next milestone:** a functional, rendered main menu (Phase 12).

## Future Goals

After the game reaches a fully playable state, future work will include:

- Native keyboard and mouse support
- Controller improvements
- High and unlocked frame rate support
- Performance optimization
- Modern multiplayer support using contemporary networking technologies
- Modding tools and debugging utilities

## Vision

The long-term objective is to preserve **Uncharted 3** as a native PC application while showcasing the capabilities of the **ps3recomp** framework.

The knowledge and improvements gained during this project will benefit future PlayStation 3 recompilation efforts.

## Legal Notice

This repository does **not** include any copyrighted Sony Interactive Entertainment or Naughty Dog assets.

Users must provide their own legally obtained PlayStation 3 game files.
Only clean-room tooling, runtime libraries and original source code are distributed.

# CellX2

### From Cell to Cross-Platform

CellX2 is an independent research project investigating PlayStation 3 software recompilation, Cell architecture translation, and the conditions required for correct execution.

The current phase focuses on understanding the PlayStation 3 PPU and SPU architectures, auditing existing open-source references, and establishing reproducible methods for validating instruction semantics.

## Project Goals

- Study the Cell Broadband Engine architecture.
- Investigate PowerPC PPU and SPU instruction semantics and translation.
- Research operating-system services and runtime requirements.
- Examine graphics, audio, input, synchronization, and lifecycle dependencies.
- Define small, reproducible tests for instruction correctness.
- Establish a minimal, verifiable execution path before making broader feasibility claims.

## Research Principles

- Correctness must be demonstrated through reproducible tests, not assumptions.
- Existing implementations are references, not unquestionable truth.
- Reference-project results must never be presented as CellX2 results.
- Source revisions, test inputs, expected outputs, and actual results must be recorded.
- Unsupported or unresolved behavior must remain explicit.
- Third-party code and documentation must be used in accordance with their licenses and applicable law.

## Current Status

**Phase:** Initial research and project organization.

The project has research notes and test specifications, but no independently executed CellX2 instruction test or end-to-end execution result is recorded yet. No successful execution of a complete commercial PlayStation 3 game has been established by CellX2.

## Reference Projects

- [PS3Recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp)
- [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3)

These are independent reference projects. CellX2 does not claim affiliation with or endorsement by their maintainers.

## Legal and Licensing Notes

CellX2 aims to develop original research, tools, and tests. Third-party software and documentation remain subject to their respective licenses and applicable law. This repository does not intend to distribute commercial game files or proprietary game assets without authorization.

## Roadmap

- [x] Establish an initial research baseline.
- [x] Record pinned reference project versions and commits.
- [x] Document the initial PPU and SPU research status.
- [x] Draft initial instruction-level test specifications.
- [ ] Complete ISA-backed expected vectors for the first SPU tests.
- [ ] Execute and record the first reproducible instruction-level test.
- [ ] Map runtime and system-service dependencies from a minimal test.
- [ ] Build and verify a small synthetic program before considering larger execution goals.

## Project Identity

**Project:** CellX2  
**Studio identity:** ZoutGameStudio

088befac6de09dad63a3fec66e8014d59b1f1e97.message:
ppu_loader: size per-thread TLS blocks by the TLS image, not image + 0x7000

Symptom: a title that creates more than 31 PPU threads (with a small TLS
image) gives the 32nd and every later thread the main thread's TLS, with no
message. Thread-locals that matter then collide: in Killzone 3 two threads
ended up reading one per-thread wait object, one waited forever on the other's
event queue and the level never started.

Cause: ppu_tls_new_block sized each block as memsz + 0x7000, rounded to a
page (0x8000 for a small image). The 0x7000 is the ABI's r13 bias: the guest
addresses TLS as r13 - 0x7000 + off with off < memsz, so nothing lives in it.
The 1 MB window at PPU_TLS_IMG then holds 31 blocks, and the fallback (return
0, the caller uses the main block) is silent.

Change: blocks are memsz rounded up to 4 KB (about 250 fit for a small
image); the first block still starts after the main block's image. When the
window is full, one line is logged before falling back to the shared block.

Verification: tools/test_ppu_tls_blocks.py builds the real
ppu_tls_new_block into a host program and requests 100 blocks with a
0x240-byte image. On v0.14.0 (a2c2010): granted 31/100, FAIL. With this
change: granted 100/100, no overlap with each other or the main image, image
copied into each, PASS. Also run in the Killzone 3 port (v0.13.0 base) since
2026-10-11: the thread that hung now waits on its own event queue.

0aead166fd65ab34bee01df19a341665800a727f.message:
cellGcm: a FIFO user command reaches the handler set with cellGcmSetUserHandler

Symptom: a title's cellGcmSetUserHandler callback never runs for the user
commands it puts in its command buffer. In Killzone 3 that callback submits
the per-frame job that lets the frame continue, so the level stalled.

Cause: the walker decodes GCM_SET_USER_COMMAND (method 0xEB00) as
subchannel 7 / method 0x0B00 and hands it to rsx_raise_user_cmd, the lv2
route: it posts an event to the RSX interrupt queue for a guest interrupt
thread. A title that registered its handler through the HLE
cellGcmSetUserHandler has no such thread; its handler runs from
ppu_gcm_pump. The branch then `continue`s, so the walker's later 0xEB00 case,
which calls cellGcmQueueUserCommand for the pump, is never reached.

Change: when an HLE user handler is registered, the 0x0B00 branch also
queues the command for the pump (cellGcmQueueUserCommand). The lv2 event is
still raised as before.

Verification: libs/video/tests/test_gcm_fifo_user_command.c (standalone,
includes cellGcmSys.c like test_gcm_user_command.c; graphics backends
stubbed) registers an HLE user handler, then five times puts one user
command in the ring, drains it with cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo and calls
ppu_gcm_pump. With this change the handler runs five times, each with its
command's argument, and the lv2 route is still taken five times (gcc and
clang). Against v0.14.0's cellGcmSys.c (a2c2010) the handler never runs
(5/5 fail). test_gcm_user_command.c still passes.

0fb35648aed8ca984638357c2e82c0e892c12c8b.message:
ppu_sysprx: sys_lwcond_t is +0x00 lwmutex EA, +0x04 queue id

Symptom: a title that reads lwcond+0x00 itself sees 0 there and treats the
lwcond as invalid (Killzone 3's file system layer checks it before every
wait and loops). The queue id is also written past the 8-byte structure,
over whatever the title keeps next to it.

Cause: the context-style sys_lwcond_create in ppu_sysprx.cpp writes the
lwmutex EA as a 64-bit value at +0x00 (so the EA lands at +0x04 and +0x00
reads 0) and the id at +0x08. sys_lwcond_t is 8 bytes: +0x00 u32 lwmutex
EA, +0x04 u32 queue id, which is also what libs/system/sysPrxForUser.h
declares as sys_lwcond_t_hle.

Change: 32-bit stores at +0x00 and +0x04 in sys_lwcond_create, and a 32-bit
read of +0x00 in sys_lwcond_wait. Wait/signal behaviour is unchanged.

Verification: tools/test_lwcond_layout.py builds the real
sys_lwcond_create and sys_lwcond_wait into a host program over stubbed
guest memory. With this change +0x00 holds the lwmutex EA, +0x04 a nonzero
id, nothing past +0x08 is written, and the wait finds the lwmutex. On
v0.14.0 (a2c2010) +0x00 reads 0, the EA is at +0x04 and the id is written
at +0x08 (2 of 3 checks fail; the wait found the lwmutex there only because
create and wait agreed on the wrong layout).

12158c45650cc5d00d228a62f98c3a204aacc300.message:
ppu_lifter: exact VMX, branch decode, integer, FP and decoding fixes

VMX
- runtime/ppu/ppu_vmx.h implements every VMX op exactly, and the lifter
  routes ops by raw XO: some had no disassembler name and lifted as no-ops.
  About 45 did nothing: the saturating adds/subs, vavg*, vmul[eo]*, vmsum*,
  vmhadd*/vmhradd*, vmladduhm, vrlh, the element and whole-vector shifts,
  vpk*, vsum*, vaddcuw/vsubcuw, vpkpx/vupk*px, vexptefp/vlogefp.
- Saturation sets VSCR[SAT], VSCR[NJ] is honoured, vcmp*. writes CR6;
  mtvscr/mfvscr are decoded, and VRSAVE reads back (ppu_context.vrsave).

Branches
- BO/BI come from the instruction word, so bdnzt/bdzf decrement CTR and
  test the condition (they were always taken); CTR is 64-bit.
- Every LK=1 form sets LR unconditionally.
- b<cond>lrl dispatches through ps3_indirect_call_to and leaves CTR alone.
- bl 0 / bcl 20,31,0 (get-PC) lift as get-PC, not as a call.

Integer
- XER[OV]/[SO] set by every OE form; compares and stwcx./stdcx. copy SO.
- rlwinm/rlwnm/rlwimi handle wrapping masks (MB > ME).
- mulld/mulli wrap, and lifted code builds with -fwrapv.
- mtxer keeps only the defined bits; mfocrf isolates its field.

Decoding: lswi/lswx/stswi/stswx, lwaux, stdbrx, stvlx/stvrx(l), lvrxl, td,
dst/dss.

FP: single-precision results (NaNs included) are single-format; fctiw/fctiwz
write the whole FPR; the FPSCR moves (mffs, mtfsf, mtfsfi, mtfsb0/1, mcrfs)
are implemented; FP record forms set CR1.

CR fusion checks the fused field's liveness past the branch target; it used
to fuse a compare that was re-tested after the label.

Guest loads in lifted code are inline (vm_read*_inl in the header preamble);
ppu_loader.cpp keeps the out-of-line accessors, and the inline path stands
down while a read diagnostic (PPU_RWATCH and friends) is armed.

16db6bca787b02f598a18b5b5efbbd7b2f882002.message:
cellGcm: GET_REPORT honours the report DMA context and writes main-memory reports to guest memory

Symptom: titles that keep their GPU reports in main memory read stale memory
for every report. Killzone 3 selects the main-memory report context and
issues about 160 reports per frame in a level (timestamps and occlusion
queries); none of them ever reached the memory it reads.

Cause: the FIFO walker ignored NV4097_SET_CONTEXT_DMA_REPORT (0x1A8) and
wrote every NV4097_GET_REPORT (0x1800) into the host s_report_data slots,
indexed by offset / 16, whatever context the title had selected.

Change: the walker records the context set by 0x1A8 (reset to local by
cellGcmInit and cellGcmTerminate). With the local context (0xFEED0000, the
default) a report goes to s_report_data as before. With the main-memory
context (0xFEED0001, or CELL_GCM_CONTEXT_DMA_REPORT_LOCATION_MAIN 0xBAD68000)
the report's offset is an IO offset and the 16-byte report is written
big-endian to gcm_io2ea(offset): u64 timestamp, u32 value, u32 0. An offset
with no IO mapping is skipped with a rate-limited log line. Report
timestamps now rise strictly, so two reports in one walker pass never share
or reverse a time stamp.

Verification: tests/gcm_reports (CTest, built with PS3RECOMP_BUILD_TESTS on
POSIX hosts like the host harness) builds a ring with local reports, a
switch to 0xFEED0001, main-memory reports of type 1 and 2, one unmapped
offset and a switch back, drains it once with cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo and
reads every slot back. Run as a MinGW-w64 build under Proton (this machine
has no Linux SDL2 for the POSIX runtime build): with this change 9/9 checks
pass; the same test linked against v0.14.0's cellGcmSys.c (a2c2010) fails
6/9 (main-memory slots keep their sentinel, the reports land in the host
area instead, timestamps not written). Carried as a local patch in the
Killzone 3 port (v0.13.0 base).

24286f4b3871aff53cf988448e1fc756956372dc.message:
cellGcm: in-FIFO flip wraps only the runtime's own command ring

Symptom: intermittently a title waits forever on a fence. Killzone 3
stopped about 16 s in, depending on where the walker's get offset was.

Cause: _cellGcmSetFlipCommand's HLE (gcm_flip_into_fifo) writes the flip
marker at ctx->current and then, when less than GCM_FLIP_WRAP_BYTES are
left before ctx->end and the walker is well past begin, wraps the context
it was given: a JUMP to begin after the marker and ctx->current = begin.
That is what the SDK's buffer-full callback does for the runtime's ring.
A title with its own buffer-full callback manages its own buffers, and its
context need not be a ring: Killzone 3 flips on a 0x30000-byte draw
context whose end moves down as it allocates from the top, so it always
looks nearly full. Rewinding it mid-frame cut the frame short, the fence
release in its tail never ran, and the title waited for it.

Change: wrap only when the context's buffer-full callback descriptor
(ctx + 0xC) still points at the runtime's callback
(GCM_FIFO_CALLBACK_SENTINEL_EA, installed by cellGcmSetupContext). Other
contexts get the marker and current advances past it, as when there is
room.

Verification: libs/video/tests/test_gcm_flip_wrap.c (standalone, includes
cellGcmSys.c like test_gcm_user_command.c) flips on two nearly full
contexts with the walker 0x28000 bytes past their begin: the ring made by
cellGcmSetupContext, and a title context with its own callback. With this
change the runtime ring wraps (marker, JUMP to begin, current = begin) and
the title context does not (marker, current past it), with gcc and clang.
Against v0.14.0's cellGcmSys.c (a2c2010) the title context is wrapped too
(1 of 2 fails). test_gcm_user_command.c still passes.

286d3ed9e33988664a79553b347bcf5af96d2673.message:
cellGcm: IO mapping table 16 -> 512 slots, no IO leak on refusal, iomap fills a free slot

Symptom: a title that maps many separate main-memory chunks loses the later
ones. Killzone 3 maps up to 38 one-megabyte chunks at level load and keeps
vertex buffers in them; after the 16th, cellGcmMapMainMemory failed, those
buffers had no IO offset and every geometry draw in a level was degenerate
(only effects over black).

Cause:
- CELL_GCM_MAX_IO_MAPPINGS is 16. libgcm has no such small fixed count; a
  mapping fails when the IO address space runs out.
- cellGcmMapMainMemory allocates the IO region before it looks for a free
  slot, so each refused call still consumes IO address space.
- cellGcm_syscall_iomap writes s_io_mappings[s_io_mapping_count]. After an
  unmap the count no longer points past the last used slot, so a new mapping
  overwrites a live one.

Change:
- 512 slots (16 bytes each; an assumed bound well above what titles use),
  overridable with -DCELL_GCM_MAX_IO_MAPPINGS=N.
- cellGcmMapMainMemory looks for a free slot before allocating the region.
- cellGcm_syscall_iomap takes a slot from find_free_mapping like the other
  mapping paths.
The return codes and every other mapping function are unchanged.

Verification: tools/test_gcm_io_mappings.py builds the real
find_free_mapping, gcm_io_alloc, cellGcmMapMainMemory and
cellGcm_syscall_iomap against stubs. On v0.14.0 (a2c2010): FAIL (15 chunks
before the first refusal, the refusal leaks IO space, iomap after an unmap
overwrites a live mapping). With this change: PASS (510 chunks with distinct
offsets, no leak, live mapping kept). Negative controls on a copy of this
branch: 16 slots fails the chunk check (14), a count-indexed iomap fails the
live-slot check. cellGcmSys.c passes cc -fsyntax-only. Used in the Killzone 3
port (v0.13.0 base): its level geometry draws with this change.

40789072e4e6c70539b3e18cddb51a99d25c417e.message:
live-draw: depth buffers read as textures return the real depth

Symptom: a DEPTH24_D8 texture that reads a zeta comes back 0 or partly 0
in three common shapes: a full-screen read of a depth buffer whose first
pass used a smaller clip, a read of an address that is both a colour target
and a zeta, and a draw that reads the zeta it is depth-testing against
(deferred lighting, soft particles). Effects that depend on scene depth
(depth of field, fog, soft particles, deferred lighting) then see a flat 0.

Causes and changes (rsx_live_draw.c):
1. The R32F snapshot of a zeta keeps the clip size of the first pass that
   bound it (512x512 of a 1280x720 depth buffer, say), so later reads get 0
   outside that corner. zdepth_get now grows the snapshot to the largest
   clip bound since, within the depth resource (zdepth_grow_snapshot: a new
   resource, descriptors rewritten, the old one retired, re-resolved at the
   next read).
2. A depth-format read of an address that is also a colour target matched
   the colour surface first. When a written host zeta exists at that
   address the read now takes the zeta.
3. A draw that samples its own bound zeta with depth writes off read guest
   memory, which the host depth never reaches. It now reads the zeta's
   snapshot; the zeta cannot change during such a draw. A draw that writes
   the zeta it reads keeps the old fallback.

fp decompiler: the NV40 pack and unpack opcodes

PK4UB, UP4UB, PKG, UPG, PK4B, UP4B, PK2US, UP2US, PK2H and UP2H had no case:
each was skipped with a TODO comment and its destination kept whatever it

host: --depthbounds skips where there is no depth bounds test

Vulkan workflow runs on (Mesa 25, LLVM 20.1.2) does not report depthBounds.

65806f3f3614fca3f40061a3ba0ff2cadfaa36b0.message:
ppu_lifter: big-endian lane order for ten VMX integer ops

Symptom: lifted code computes wrong results for vmulouh, vmsumshm, vadduws,
vadduhs and vpkuwum, and does nothing at all for vmsumuhm, vsubuws,
vpkswss, vsrb and vsrab, which were emitted as "/* TODO */" no-ops.

Cause: ctx->vr holds raw big-endian guest bytes. The first five handlers
read halfword and word lanes through int16_t*/uint32_t* casts, which gives
byte-reversed lanes (and the wrong lane pairing) on a little-endian host.
The other five had no lowering.

Change: one handler for the ten ops that assembles each halfword or word
lane from its bytes in big-endian order, computes the result as the AltiVec
PEM defines it (modulo, saturating or shift) and stores it back in the same
order. The five old handlers are removed.

Verification: tools/test_ppu_vmx_lanes.py lifts each op, compiles the
emitted C with the lifter's own preamble and compares vD with an independent
Python model of the instruction on 300 inputs per op (216 edge combinations
plus random vectors). With this change 10/10 ops agree on every input. On
v0.14.0 (a2c2010) all ten fail: five emit TODO, the other five differ on
244 to 292 of 300 inputs. tools/test_ppu_vcmp_record_cr6.py and
tools/test_ppu_lift.py pass before and after.

662270bdf366da3e360385f421ce5192f82b3443.message:
ppu_loader: indirect-call depth guard can be kept per coroutine

Symptom: a title whose guest jobs run on host coroutines (host fibers that
stand in for a guest fiber scheduler) works for a while, then every
indirect call on that thread is skipped by the recursion guard, even calls
to leaf functions ("[ppu] recursion cap ... skipping"); null calls and an
exit follow. Killzone 3 quit a few minutes into a level.

Cause: the guard in ps3_indirect_call_impl keeps one depth count per host
thread in a function-local thread_local. A coroutine that ends by switching
away from inside an indirect call never unwinds its frames, so each one
leaks its depth into the thread's count until the count passes the 4000
cap. The vcall stack pointer (g_vcall_sp) leaks the same way. Neither can be
reached from outside the function, so a coroutine layer has no way to keep
them per coroutine.

Change: the depth count moves to a file-scope thread-local, and two
accessors, ps3_ppu_dispatch_depth_slot() and ps3_ppu_vcall_sp_slot(), return
the current thread's counters. A coroutine layer saves *slot when it
switches away and restores it when it switches back. Threads that never
switch behave exactly as before.

Verification: tools/test_ppu_dispatch_depth.py builds the real
ppu_loader.cpp with runtime/ppu/tests/test_ppu_dispatch_depth.cpp. 5000
ucontext coroutines each go five ps3_indirect_call levels deep and switch
back to the home context without returning; the home side saves and
restores both counters around each switch. With this change all 5000
chains run to the bottom, the home thread's depth and vcall sp are 0
before and after, and a later indirect call runs. Against v0.14.0's
ppu_loader.cpp (a2c2010; the accessors do not exist, the test declares
them weak) only 800 of 5000 chains run: the guard trips at depth 4001 and
skips every call after that.

Symptom (MinGW-w64 builds only): two PPU threads that exit close together
crash; one thread's sys_ppu_thread_exit longjmps toward a frame on the other
thread's stack. In Killzone 3 this is the two Bink threads exiting at the

Cause: sys_ppu_thread.c, spurs_job.c, cellSpurs.c and cellSysutil.c pick

ignores that attribute ("'thread' attribute directive ignored"), so the
exit jmp_buf and its armed flag, g_spurs_job_mbox* and the completion

thread-local macros (PPU_THREAD_LOCAL, SPU_THREAD_LOCAL, SPU_TLS) already
test _MSC_VER.

__thread / _Thread_local otherwise, like the others. MSVC and POSIX builds
are unchanged.

conditionals and compiles a static variable with it as MinGW sees it
(x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc when present, else the host compiler with _WIN32
defined and __declspec(x) as __attribute__((x))), then checks the variable

plain static does not) pass; otherwise, as on macOS, the test prints SKIP. With this change 9/9 qualifiers are

8eb45f8647cde8750f675f5725ea0bd325ec9618.message:
cellFs: 64-bit sizes and offsets in ppu_fs on Windows

Symptom: on Windows a file larger than 2 GiB is mis-sized and mis-seeked.
With a MinGW-w64 (msvcrt) build cellFsStat fails with CELL_ENOENT (the CRT's
stat wrapper reports EOVERFLOW); with UCRT (llvm-mingw) it succeeds with a
truncated size. cellFsLseek and cellFsFstat truncate to 32 bits, so a read
after a seek past 4 GiB lands at the wrong offset.

Cause: ppu_fs.cpp uses stat() with a 32-bit st_size and fseek()/ftell()
with `long`, which is 32 bits on LLP64 Windows. LP64 hosts are unaffected.

Change: _stat64, _fseeki64 and _ftelli64 on Windows; stat, fseeko and ftello

b3082644982c43d81c8bf47959317dc4cb3cfbf1.message:
cellGcm: give a parked FIFO time to be patched before following put

A self-JUMP at the write head parks the RSX, and when `put` had meanwhile
moved elsewhere the walker took that as the title having abandoned the park
and resynced to `put` at once. inFAMOUS 2 links its main-memory command
blocks the other way round: it ends a block in a park, writes the next
commands at the ring start, moves `put`, and only then rewrites the park as a
JUMP to them. A drain that landed between the two stores went straight to
`put` and dropped everything from the ring start up to it, the frame's fence
included, so the title waited on that label for the rest of the run and the
main menu froze.

Resync only once the same park has stood with the same `put` for longer than
a title takes between the two stores (50 ms). A park patched in time is
followed as before; the pass reports itself as "parked" in the meantime.

b6dc1e428b4b89c8385595551904bfb21c33d71a.message:
ppu_lifter: jump tables behind a tail-call epilogue

discover_jump_tables drops the blocks that end in `blr` from the backward
scan for the table base register: they return, so they cannot flow into the
dispatcher. An epilogue that leaves by a tail call ends the same way and
restores the same registers, and was not dropped. inFAMOUS 2's func_000B9BD0
loads the base's base into r30 in its prologue, has an early exit
`ld r30,0xE0(r1); ...; b 0xB8570`, and dispatches nineteen instructions later
through `lwz r11,-0x7F80(r30)`: the restore read as r30's nearest definition,
no base resolved, and the switch lifted to an unresolved indirect call.

A `b` leaves the function when it goes back past the function's entry or
forward to another function's entry. Both need func_starts; without them the
scan is bounded by the nearest `blr`, which an early return puts in the
middle of a function, so only `blr` is trusted there.

tools/test_ppu_jumptables.py: the backward shape (the inFAMOUS 2 one), the
forward one, and the no-func_starts control.

b883922940d53efafac47dcc0b63dac7535294c5.message:
rsx_draw_engine, vulkan: honour the depth bounds test

NV4097 SET_DEPTH_BOUNDS_TEST_ENABLE (0x0380) with SET_DEPTH_BOUNDS_MIN and
_MAX (0x0384, 0x0388, floats) rejects a fragment whose stored depth lies
outside the bounds, whatever the depth test says. The draw engine never
read those registers, so a bounded draw covered the whole target.

Twisted Metal's deferred renderer relies on it: its sun pass is bounded to
[0, 0.999984] (the geometry) and the sky drawn right after it to
[0.999984, 1] (the far plane), both with the depth test off. Unbounded, the
sky overwrote the sun light everywhere and the HDR buffer came out almost
black.

The enable is pipeline state (rsx_be_render_state.depth_bounds_test, part
of the pipeline key); the bounds reach the backend before every draw through
a new optional hook, set_depth_bounds, like the stencil reference, so moving
them does not build pipelines. Vulkan enables the depthBounds feature when
the device has it and sets the bounds dynamically, clamped to [0, 1];
without the feature the test stays off, as before, with one log line.
Metal and the fixed-function path leave the hook unset and draw as before.

Tests: test_rsx_draw_engine checks the key, the bounds and that moving them
builds no pipeline (4 new checks, failing without the engine change).
ps3recomp_host --depthbounds draws red at z = 0.25, then blue bounded to
[0, 0.5] and green bounded to [0.5, 1] with the depth test off, and expects
blue; it runs in the Vulkan workflow's engine pass under the validation
layer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

b8cb0c8ceafc1238f3fb38c6286db64794d9c885.message:
spu: hardware-exact float semantics, NEON paths, interpreter op fixes

Float (spu_helpers.h), rewritten from the SPU ISA, single and double
precision: truncation (round toward zero), denormal flush, the extended
range, saturation, frest's hardware table, fi, the compares (fceq/fcgt/
fcmeq/fcmgt) and the conversions (cflts/cfltu/csflt/cuflt). The previous
helpers were a GPL-derived port; these are written from the ISA alone and
checked against an exact-arithmetic referee.

Speed, bit-identical output: NEON forms of fa/fs/fm/fma/fms/fnms (1.6-4x
faster), of 60 per-lane integer ops, and of shufb (tbl); test_spu_float_neon
and test_spu_int_neon compare them against the scalar forms.

Interpreter (spu_interp.c):
- fixes: mpyhha is RR (rt accumulates), rchcnt puts the count in the
  preferred word, mfspr and fscrrd read zero, bisl reads ra before writing
  the link (rt may alias ra), links and the next pc wrap at the end of local
  store, stopd reports code 0x3FFF;
- additions: bgx, mpyui, mpyhhau, rothmi, rotmah(i), bisled, dftsv and the
  double-precision ops (dfa/dfs/dfm/dfma/dfms/dfnms/dfnma, dfceq/dfcgt/
  dfcmeq/dfcmgt);
- bi/iret carry the interrupt enable/disable bits as the lifter decodes them,
  and an iret back to the interrupted pc restores the saved register file.

Lifter (spu_lifter.py):
- bisl/bisled read the target before writing the link, and bisled uses the
  right register; links wrap at the end of local store; stopd reports 0x3FFF.
- The lv2 stop-and-signal services that resume at the next instruction
  (0x100/0x110/0x111) no longer end a function: the lift resumes there when
  spu_stop reports the stop serviced, and returns as before otherwise.
- --merge-chunks groups contiguous chunks into one C function
  (--max-group-insns), and --return-entries splits a bound at each call's
  return address.

live-draw: decode ZSTENCIL_CLEAR_VALUE by the zeta format (Z16)

Symptom: in the D3D12 live-draw backend a Z16 zeta cleared with 0xFFFF
(its far plane) ends up at depth 0.0000152, so every LESS or LEQUAL draw
into it fails.

Cause: the live-draw clear decoded every ZSTENCIL_CLEAR_VALUE as Z24S8
(depth24 << 8 | stencil8). For a Z16 zeta (SURFACE_FORMAT depth field 1)
the value is a bare depth16 in bits 0-15 with no stencil.

Change: decode by sf.depth_format, as the draw engine's clear does since
#235: Z16 = (value & 0xFFFF) / 65535 with stencil 0, Z24S8 unchanged. The
existing "value 0 clears to 1.0" behaviour is kept for both formats.

the shared harness live_draw_test_harness.h) clears colour and depth, then

it. Built with MinGW-w64 and run under Proton (vkd3d) with one test-only

live-draw: fragment depth export, and texel size of depth-snapshot reads

Symptom: a fragment program that writes depth (SHADER_CONTROL depth-export
bits) leaves the primitive's interpolated depth in the zeta, so a
full-screen pass that rebuilds a depth buffer writes the quad's constant
depth. Separately, a DEPTH24_D8 texture with texel (unnormalised)
coordinates that is smaller than the zeta it reads samples a stretched copy
of the whole zeta instead of its top-left corner.

Cause: the fragment-program decompiler ignored SHADER_CONTROL bits 1-3
(0xE, depth export) and never declared SV_Depth; the live-draw PSO keys
masked the control word with 0x40 only, so they could not tell the two
programs apart. A depth texture bound to a zeta snapshot reads that host
resource, which is as large as the largest pass that used the zeta, but the
unnormalised-coordinate divisor was the texture's own size.

- rsx_fp_decompiler.c: with depth export set, the output is a struct with
  `float depth : SV_Depth`, written from r1.z (always the fp32 register,
  whatever the colour export width), clamped to [0,1], NaN to 0.
- rsx_live_draw.c: both PSO keys include the depth-export bits (0x4E); a
  texel-addressed DEPTH24_D8 unit whose bind takes a zeta snapshot divides

c55ddaa4379c2897d55f337096cb23e0dd2a6c3d.message:
edat: take the klicensee the title passes to sceNpDrmIsAvailable[2]

Symptom: a free (license type 3) or disc-bound EDAT under a title-specific
klicensee fails to open with -6 ("needs a RIF key"), even though the title
supplies its key the way it does on hardware.

Cause: on hardware a title passes its own klicensee to sceNpDrmIsAvailable
or sceNpDrmIsAvailable2 before it opens such a file, and the kernel keeps it
for later opens. The runtime has neither call, so the key is lost, and the
EDAT reader only tries the built-in platform klicensees.

Change: sceNp.c implements sceNpDrmIsAvailable and sceNpDrmIsAvailable2;
both hand a non-NULL klicensee to edat_add_klicensee() (new, edat.h) and
return CELL_OK. edat.c keeps up to 16 such keys, ignores duplicates, and
tries them before the built-in ones. Each key is still checked against the
file's dev_hash (AES-CMAC under klic ^ NP_OMAC_KEY_2 over header bytes
0x00-0x5F, the same check for NPD versions 2-4) before it is used, and each
block hash is checked as before. A license type 3 file that no key verifies
now fails with a message that names sceNpDrmIsAvailable. Projects that read
the key some other way can call edat_add_klicensee() themselves.

Verification: tools/test_edat_guest_klicensee.py builds
libs/filesystem/tests/test_edat_guest_klicensee.c with sceNp.c. The test

three blocks, the last partial) and checks: -6 before any key, -6 after
sceNpDrmIsAvailable2 with a key that does not verify dev_hash, then 0 with
every block hash verified and the plaintext matching after

d0d67442f549faf07f8547adcb4fdc6e6dc74c08.message:
spu_channels: MFC engine table 8 -> 64 slots, and a full table is reported as an error

Symptom: intermittent stops where an SPU context waits forever on a DMA
tag that already completed. Killzone 3 holds eleven SPU contexts with an
MFC engine at once (policy-module contexts that keep their engine for as
long as their workload exists, plus SPU thread groups); the runtime prints
"more than 8 contexts hold an MFC engine at once; the rest share one".

Cause: the per-context engine table has SPU_MAX_CONTEXTS = 8 slots. Every
context past the eighth gets one shared fallback engine, where one
context's completion clears the tag bits another context is waiting on.
Eight is a thread group's worth, but a title can hold more contexts at
once than the machine has SPUs. The overflow was reported once, as a note.

Change: 64 slots (overridable with -DSPU_MAX_CONTEXTS). When the table is
still full, the shared engine stays as the last resort, but the runtime now
reports it as an error naming the table size, the context and the
consequence, at the first overflow lookup and again at 1000 and 1000000 so
it stays visible in a long log; s_mfc_overflow_lookups counts them. A
growable table can replace this later.

Verification: runtime/spu/tests/test_spu_mfc_slots.c (built as in the CI
workflows) keeps its 8-thread claim race over 32 rounds and adds: eleven
contexts held at once get eleven distinct engines and keep the state each
wrote; the table holds SPU_MAX_CONTEXTS contexts with no overflow; the next
context gets the overflow engine and the overflow is counted. With this
change 889 checks pass with gcc and clang, and the error line is printed
once. Against v0.14.0's spu_channels.c (a2c2010; the counter compiled as a
constant 0) 3 checks fail: the eleven contexts share engines, their state
is overwritten, and the overflow is not counted.

d9870123ea646d8a9a4ad4cd56342d5bd7c57546.message:
spu_channels: SMC micro-interpreter addresses lqa/stqa at I16 << 2

Symptom: a self-modifying SPU stub that saves and restores registers with
stqa/lqa (a job manager's interrupt save/restore stub, written into the
local store at runtime) stores every register at the wrong address and
overwrites unrelated local-store bytes, including the job's stack.

Cause: spu_smc_microstep computed the absolute local-store address of
lqa/stqa as I16 << 4. For the RI16 form the address is I16 << 2 (SPU ISA),
which is what spu_interp.c and the lifter already use, so every access went
4x too high and wrapped around the local store.

Change: use I16 << 2 in the micro-interpreter, masked to a quadword as
before.

Verification: tools/test_spu_smc_lqa_stqa.py builds the real
spu_smc_microstep with the SPU headers into a host program, writes a stub of
76 stqa (r0..r75 to 0x3F9C0..), a bi, 76 lqa back and a second bi into the
local store, and runs both halves through the micro-interpreter. With this
change all 76 registers land in their own slot, all 76 are restored, and no
local-store byte outside the save area changes. On v0.14.0 (a2c2010) no
register lands in its slot and 1198 bytes outside the save area change.

df3a7cbae234fb6701b6e1d1df2d3417b9e03a2a.message:
ppu_lifter: --chunks N cuts the source by guest address and rewrites only changed files

Symptom: any change to the lifter's input or to the lifter (a fix for one
opcode, one function's bounds) makes the build recompile nearly all of the
lifted source. For Killzone 3 (eight 600k-line chunks, 6.5-8 minutes and
2.5-4.4 GB of compiler memory each) that is 15-25 minutes per rebuild.

Cause: (1) chunks are cut every --chunk-lines emitted lines, so a change in
one function's line count moves every later cut point and changes the text of
every later chunk; (2) main() deletes the previous chunk set before writing,
so every file gets a new mtime even when its content is the same, and make or
ninja rebuild it.

Change:
- --chunks N (default 0 = off) cuts the source into N files by guest code
  bytes: chunk k holds the functions, in address order, of the range that
  carries the k-th N-th of the lifted bytes. That is a function of the
  function list alone, so the same functions always land in the same file. The
  function table goes to its own <source>_table.cpp, so a new function does
  not change the last chunk. A chunk over --chunk-lines lines prints a warning
  (MSVC's 16M-line limit).
- Every output file (header, chunks, table, the --single-file source) is
  written through write_if_changed: a temporary file and a rename, and only
  when the content differs, so unchanged files keep their mtime.
- Stale files of an earlier run (other cut points, the single-file source)
  are removed after writing instead of all files before.

How this relates to --chunk-lines (#216): --chunk-lines sets how large a
line-cut chunk may be (fewer lines per translation unit for hosts short on
memory) and stays the default mode; it now also profits from
write_if_changed. --chunks makes the cut points stable across relifts; with
it, --chunk-lines is only the warning threshold. Both can be used.

200 synthetic functions of uneven guest size. On v0.14.0 (a2c2010): FAIL (

e99cbbf0a9c93d99b9ba43fbd142365f4403ba13.message:
fp decompiler: predicated writes are a select, not a lerp

Symptom: a fragment-program instruction executed under a condition code
(exec_if lt/eq/gt) changes components of its destination that the condition
leaves alone when either operand holds Inf, NaN or raw bits. Programs that
keep packed words in a register (the PK*/UP* pack/unpack pattern) read 0 or
NaN after a predicated MOV.

Cause: the predicated destination write was emitted as
lerp(dst, v, mask). lerp is arithmetic (dst + mask * (v - dst)): an Inf or NaN
in the unselected operand gives NaN (0 * Inf), and denormal and NaN bit
patterns are not preserved through the ALU.

Change: emit a per-component select, (mask != 0.0) ? v : dst, which FXC
compiles to movc. The unconditional path is unchanged.

Verification: libs/video/tests/test_fp_decompiler.c gains a case with a MOV
predicated on CC0 > 0 that checks the select form and that no lerp is
emitted. It fails on master (39 passed, 2 failed) and passes with this change
(41 passed, 0 failed). The same select has been in use in a D3D12 title port
under Proton; there a test with predicated writes over raw-bit and Inf/NaN
operands read 8 of 8 values back correctly, 4 of 8 with lerp.
