d7812558337fdf7ce50429ba1ef31f253c0fc7be.message:
Draw Distance and Tree Detail

Two rows on the Advanced Graphics page, for the scenery that appears in
front of the player in the open areas.

Draw Distance (DOD3_DRAW_DISTANCE = 2, 3, 5, 10): the engine's
MaxDrawDistanceScale, which the scene renderer multiplies every
primitive's own cull distance by each frame. Live. It moves the props,
bushes and small trees that have such a distance.

Tree Detail (DOD3_TREE_LOD = 2, 3, 5, 10): the SpeedTrees have four
distances of their own (the model's detail from 500 to 6,000 units, the
flat billboard from 8,000, nothing past 12,000 to 16,000 for most trees
of the first chapter's coast), which the draw distance does not reach.
They are copied into the tree's scene proxy when it is made, and read
from there once, as the tree's meshes are put in the draw lists. So the
proxy's are multiplied as it is made: USpeedTreeComponent::
CreateSceneProxy (func_00817FD4, a virtual and the constructor's only
caller) is replaced in the function registry. Trees already in the
scene keep what they were added with -- writing a live proxy changes
nothing on screen, which is why earlier attempts at this from outside
showed nothing -- so the row says "from the next area".

Checked in three runs to the same spot on the coast's landing stage:
at 0.2 the woods on either side are gone, at 1 the pines on the cliff
are their soft billboards, at 3 they are their models and a tree past
the far bank is drawn that was not. And set from the page itself to 3
before the level was loaded: all 64 trees' proxies hold three times
their components' distances.

What still appears late is what the game has not loaded yet: the further
parts of a level are streamed in as the player nears them.

1.01 only (the addresses are not mapped for 1.00, where the tree row is
left out). No re-lift is needed.

1423091603.readme_excerpt:
# Drakengard 3 Recompiled

A native PC port of **Drakengard 3** (Drag-On Dragoon 3, PlayStation 3,
BLUS31197) for Windows and macOS, made by static recompilation of the game's
code on the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) toolkit.

The game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C++ ahead of time and built
into a normal executable, with the PS3's system libraries replaced by native
implementations and the RSX graphics by Direct3D 12, Metal or Vulkan. There
is no emulation at run time.

![The start of the game, running natively on Windows](docs/images/opening.jpg)

**Nothing of the game is in this repository.** You need your own copy of
Drakengard 3: the US disc and the game's 1.01 update, plus whatever DLC you
own. The installer takes them from there.

If this helped you, consider [buying me a coffee](https://ko-fi.com/soyjack)

## Installing

What you need:

- A PC with Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), a GPU with Direct3D 12 and a CPU with
  AVX2 (Intel Haswell / AMD Zen or newer), or a Mac with Apple silicon on
  macOS 13 or newer. About 16 GB of free disk space, 10 GB more for the
  Japanese voice pack.
- Your disc, US release (BLUS31197), dumped to a folder or a **decrypted**
  `.iso` ([PS3 Disc Dumper](https://github.com/13xforever/ps3-disc-dumper)
  writes one; an image from an ordinary disc tool is still encrypted and is
  refused, as are other regions).
- The 1.01 update, as the package a PlayStation 3 downloads:
  `UP0082-BLUS31197_00-DOD3PATCH0000000-A0101-V0101-PE.pkg`.
- Optionally, the DLC packages you own (`UP0082-NPUB31251_00-...`). No
  licence files are needed.

Windows:

1. Download `dod3-recomp-<version>-win64.zip` from the
   [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) and unzip it
   anywhere (not inside Program Files).
2. Run `dod3.exe`. SmartScreen may warn the first time, as the program is not
   signed: "More info", then "Run anyway".
3. In the setup that opens, add your files (the disc image or folder, the
   update package, any DLC packages) with Add Files / Add Folder, in any
   order, then Install. The game's files are copied into the `game` folder
   next to `dod3.exe` (a few minutes).
4. Start Game.

macOS:

1. Download `dod3-recomp-<version>-macos-arm64.zip` from the
   [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases), unzip it and
   move "Drakengard 3 Recompiled.app" to Applications.
2. The app is not notarised, so macOS refuses it the first time. On macOS 15
   and later: open it once, then allow it in System Settings > Privacy &
   Security ("Open Anyway"). On macOS 13 and 14: Control-click the app,
   choose Open, then Open again.
3. The setup opens as on Windows. The game's files go into
   `~/Library/Application Support/Drakengard 3 Recompiled`.

Settings (resolution, display mode, frame-rate cap, anti-aliasing, field of
view, draw distance, skipping the intro) are in the game's own Settings
menu, under Graphics Settings, System Settings and Advanced Graphics, or in
`dod3.ini`.
[docs/PLAYING.md](docs/PLAYING.md) has the controls, the saves, the Japanese
voices, and what to do if something goes wrong.

## Building

The port is built in three steps: the game's PPU code is lifted to C++, its
SPU programs are lifted, and the whole is compiled with CMake. Lifting needs
the game's executable, so you need your own copy of the game first.

1. **Toolchain.** Windows: Visual Studio 2022 or newer (the Build Tools are
   enough, with "Desktop development with C++" and the Windows SDK), LLVM
   with clang-cl, CMake 3.20 or later, Ninja, Python 3.11 or later, Git for
   Windows, and vcpkg with `zlib:x64-windows` and `sdl2:x64-windows`
   (`VCPKG_ROOT`, or `C:\vcpkg`). macOS: Xcode's command-line tools and,
   from Homebrew, `cmake ninja python zlib sdl2 glslang spirv-cross`.

2. **The sources.**

   ```sh
   git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp
   cd dod3-recomp
   python3 -m venv .venv                    # py -3 -m venv .venv on Windows
   .venv/bin/pip install -r ps3recomp/tools/requirements.txt -r tools/requirements.txt
   ```

3. **The game's files.** Any built `dod3` (a release's, or one from another
   machine) installs the game into the repository root, which decrypts the
   update's executable to `elf/EBOOT_101.ELF` and lays out `game/disc`:

   ```sh
   DOD3_INSTALL_BASE=. path/to/dod3 --install <disc .iso or folder> <update .pkg> [DLC .pkg ...]
   ```

4. **Lift the PPU code** (a few minutes; about 550 MB of C++ in
   `recompiled_101/`):

   ```sh
   .venv/bin/python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_loader.py elf/EBOOT_101.ELF -o out/v101/
   .venv/bin/python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_lifter.py elf/EBOOT_101.ELF \
       --functions out/v101/EBOOT_101.functions.json \
       --hle-stubs out/v101/EBOOT_101.imports.json \
       --code-end 0x157fc00 \
       --nonvolatile-locals \
       --hook 0x000C1E50 --hook 0x00EE7728 --hook 0x00272E58 \
       -o recompiled_101/
   ```

5. **Lift the SPU programs** into `spu/`, with the native fast paths hooked
   in:

   ```sh
   tools/lift_spu.sh
   ```

6. **Compile.** Windows, from a plain command prompt (the script finds
   Visual Studio, LLVM, CMake and vcpkg):

   ```bat
   tools\build_win.bat
   ```

   macOS:

   ```sh
   cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
   cmake --build build
   ```

   A clean build takes about 15 minutes, nearly all of it the lifted code.

7. **Run** the game installed in the repository root:

   ```sh
   DOD3_INSTALL_BASE=. build/dod3
   ```

[docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md) has the CMake options, the developer
run form, packaging a release and regenerating the committed tables;
[docs/TECHNICAL.md](docs/TECHNICAL.md) how the port works;
[docs/DEBUGGING.md](docs/DEBUGGING.md) the switches, profiling and the
regression tests; [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) the layout of the tree
and the conventions.

## Status

| | |
|---|---|
| Windows 10/11, Direct3D 12 | Playable. 60 fps at 4K on an RTX 4090 / i9-13900K (chapter 1 through the heavy destruction scene, open areas, the village); 120 fps holds at lower resolutions |
| Windows, Vulkan | Experimental (`RSX_BACKEND = vulkan`) |
| macOS 13+, Apple silicon, Metal | Playable. 60 fps at 1080p in battle on an M1 Pro |
| Game version | The 1.01 update (required) |
| DLC | All 20 packs, including the Japanese voice pack |

What the port adds over the original: any internal resolution (supersampling
included), windowed, borderless or full-screen display, a frame-rate cap of
your choice (60 and 120 tested) or one that follows the scene, with the
frames shown at even intervals, FXAA or MSAA, anisotropic filtering, a wider
field of view, sharper shadows, a longer draw distance for scenery and for
trees, skipping the intro logos and movie, and pausing or muting when the
window is in the background -- all from a Graphics Settings, a System
Settings and an Advanced Graphics page added to the game's own Settings menu.

Known issues: the game has been tested on few machines.

## How it fits together

```
elf/EBOOT_101.ELF  --ppu_loader/ppu_lifter-->  recompiled_101/*.cpp  (the game's PPU code as C++)
SPU programs       --tools/lift_spu.sh------>  spu/                  (SPURS tasks, jobs, the audio DSP)
src/               --------------------------->  the port: the runner, native fast paths, the settings menu, the installer
ps3recomp/         --------------------------->  runtime, HLE libraries, the RSX draw engine and its backends
```

The executable `dod3` installs the game from your files (a Dear ImGui
installer, `src/install/` and `src/ui/`) and runs it.

## Legal

This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Square Enix, Access Games
or Sony Interactive Entertainment. Drakengard 3 and all of its assets belong
to their owners; none are included, and the port only runs from a copy of the
game you own.

The code in this repository is under the [MIT License](LICENSE). It builds on
ps3recomp (MIT) and includes Dear ImGui (MIT); see
[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

## Credits

- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet: the
  recompiler, the runtime and the PS3 library implementations. This port's
  changes to it are in the [soyjxck/ps3recomp](https://github.com/soyjxck/ps3recomp)
  fork, the `ps3recomp/` submodule.
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net): the reference for much of the PS3's behaviour,
  and the source of two techniques used here (write-watched texture memory,
  a guest clock that stops while the game is paused).
- [XenonRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/XenonRecomp) and
  [Unleashed Recompiled](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp): the
  model for a recompiled port, and for its installer.
- [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui) by Omar Cornut: the
  installer's user interface.

# 🍩 simpsonsarcade-ps3

> *"Mmm... native code."* — Homer J. Simpson, probably

A static recompilation of **The Simpsons Arcade Game** (PlayStation 3 / PSN) into a native
PC executable, built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). No emulator.

It is playable: intro, menus, saves, and the arcade game itself, with keyboard or pad. It also
plays **online** through [psnr](https://github.com/sp00nznet/psnr), a stand-in for PSN's
matchmaking.

![The Simpsons Arcade Game running natively](docs/media/hero.gif)

*Main menu → profile dialog → character select → Stage 1, captured from the native build.*

|---|---|
| ![Main menu](docs/media/04-main-menu.png) | ![Profile dialog](docs/media/05-profile-dialog.png) |
| ![Stage 1](docs/media/06-stage1.png) | ![Intro](docs/media/01-intro.png) |

## Status

| | |
|---|---|
| Boot, intro, menus, attract mode | ✅ |
| Gameplay (arcade core) | ✅ Stage 1 onward |
| Input | ✅ Keyboard; XInput pad when one is attached |
| Save / load | ✅ Settings and progress persist across boots |
| Graphics | ✅ RSX → D3D12 (`RSX_LIVE_DRAW=1`); no flash frames or garbled glyphs |
| Audio | ✅ Music (ATRAC3plus) and effects |
| Frame rate | ⚠️ 60 in menus, 35–57 in gameplay |
| **Online multiplayer (psnr)** | ✅ Create Match / Quick Match, lobby, co-op in sync |
| Online leaderboards | ❓ Not yet tried against psnr |

### Known issues

- **In-stage sound thins out when the frame rate drops.** The arcade core makes its sound per
  emulated frame, so below 60 fps its own sample stream has gaps.
- **Offline, the title shows its "sign in to post scores" notice.** That's expected without psnr.
  It doesn't block saving.

The full history, with measurements, is in [`PROGRESS.md`](PROGRESS.md).

## Online play (psnr)

The title's online mode works over [psnr](https://github.com/sp00nznet/psnr). psnr runs the
rooms; once players are matched, game traffic goes directly between them.

Tested: two players, both instances on one machine. Create Match, Quick Match, the online
lobby, character select, and the host's game setup transfer all work. Stage 1 then plays in sync
on both, with each player's input showing on both screens. The game allows up to four players;
three and four haven't been tried, and neither has play across two machines.

**Requirements.** Online needs ps3recomp changes that are still in review:
[#200](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/200) (NP matchmaking over psnr, and P2P
sockets) and [#202](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/202) (a lifter fix: without it,
the title's zlib corrupts the game setup it sends). Until they merge, build against a ps3recomp
checkout with both applied, and re-lift (`tools/relift.sh`).

**Two players on one machine:**

```bash
psnr                      # from the psnr repo; listens on :36100

# player 1 (hosts: Online Game → Create Match)
PS3_NET_ONLINE=1 PSNR_SERVER=127.0.0.1 PS3_NP_ONLINE_ID=homer PS3_NET_P2P_PORT=3658 \
PS3_VERBOSE=0 RSX_LIVE_DRAW=1 ./build/simpsons vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf

# player 2 (joins: Online Game → Quick Match)
PS3_NET_ONLINE=1 PSNR_SERVER=127.0.0.1 PS3_NP_ONLINE_ID=bart  PS3_NET_P2P_PORT=3659 \
PS3_VERBOSE=0 RSX_LIVE_DRAW=1 ./build/simpsons vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf
```

| Variable | Why |
|---|---|
| `PS3_NET_ONLINE=1`, `PSNR_SERVER` | Turn on real sockets and point at the psnr server. |
| `PS3_NP_ONLINE_ID` | The player's name. It also gives the instance its own console identity, which the game uses to tell players apart. |
| `PS3_NET_P2P_PORT` | The port other players reach this one on. Each instance on a machine needs its own. Across machines, open it to the other players. |
| `PS3_VERBOSE=0` | Required. With stderr redirected, the runtime otherwise logs every wait, which drops gameplay to about 1 fps, and the game then drops the other player as "not responding". |

Without these variables the game is offline, exactly as before.

## Building

Prereqs: Python 3.9+, CMake 3.20+, **clang-cl** + Ninja, and a sibling
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) checkout.

```bash
# 1. Decrypt your own legally obtained EBOOT.BIN to an ELF and lay out the game data:
#       vfs/PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO
#       vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf
#       vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/0B/SIMPSONS.SR, SIMPSONS_FW.SR

# 2. Lift the PPU image and generate the HLE NID table:
PS3RECOMP=../ps3recomp ./tools/relift.sh

# 3. Capture the SPU job binaries (the game builds them in memory, so they only exist
#    when cellSpurs dispatches them), then lift again to include them:
SPU_DUMP_MISS=spu_dump ./build/simpsons vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf
PS3RECOMP=../ps3recomp ./tools/relift.sh

# 4. Build (Release is the default; a debug build runs at a third of the speed):
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl
cmake --build build

# 5. Run:
RSX_LIVE_DRAW=1 ./build/simpsons vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf
```

**Controls (keyboard).** Arrows move · `Z` attack · `X` jump · `A`/`S` square/triangle ·
`Q`/`W` L1/R1 · `Enter` START · `Tab` SELECT. An XInput pad takes over when one is plugged in.

**Scripted runs.** `PAD_SCRIPT="15:0x0008,30:0x4000,..."` presses buttons at set frames, and
`LD_FRAME_DUMP=shots LD_FRAME_DUMP_EVERY=60` saves frames. Coin in with START (`0x0008`) once,
then use only CROSS (`0x4000`); START again opens the pause menu.

## The game

| | |
|---|---|
| **Title** | The Simpsons Arcade Game (PSN) |
| **Title ID** | `NPUB30563` |
| **Developer / Publisher** | Backbone Entertainment / Konami |
| **Original** | Konami's 1991 four-player arcade beat-'em-up |

The PSN release is an arcade emulator wrapped around the original 1991 ROM (inside
`SIMPSONS.SR`): the EBOOT emulates the Konami 052001, Z80, YM2151 and K053260. So this project
recompiles the emulator, and the game's own 6809 code is interpreted from the ROM. See
[`docs/emulator-architecture.md`](docs/emulator-architecture.md).

It is the same game as the Xbox 360 release, with a byte-identical `SIMPSONS.SR`, and a sibling
of the playable 360 port [`simpsonsarcade`](https://github.com/sp00nznet/simpsonsarcade). Both
CPUs are 64-bit big-endian PowerPC with VMX, so the 360 port served as a reference throughout.
See [`docs/360-crossref.md`](docs/360-crossref.md) and
[`docs/binary-analysis.md`](docs/binary-analysis.md).

## Legal

This repository contains **no copyrighted game code, assets, binaries, or encryption keys**, only
analysis notes, configuration and build tooling. You need your own legally obtained copy of the
game. This project is not affiliated with Konami, Backbone, Sony or Fox.

## Related projects

- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp): the PS3 runtime this links against
- [psnr](https://github.com/sp00nznet/psnr): the online server
- [simpsonsarcade](https://github.com/sp00nznet/simpsonsarcade): the Xbox 360 port of the same game
- [flOw](https://github.com/sp00nznet/flow) · [tokyojungle](https://github.com/sp00nznet/tokyojungle): sister PS3 ports
- [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): the emulator whose HLE research makes this possible

1423117739.description: Tekken 5 Dark Resurrection Online Native Port
1423117739.readme_excerpt:
# Tekken 5: Dark Resurrection Online — native Windows port

Tekken 5: Dark Resurrection (PS3, PlayStation Network release) running natively
on Windows. It is recompiled, not emulated. Online play runs through the
launcher's own lobby, like Tekken 6 Native Online.

<!-- RELEASE LINE: the version and date in the next two lines change with every release, when it is tagged
(docs/RELEASING.md "Cutting a release", step 2); the same lines are in docs/README.de.md. -->
**Release 1.2.3 (2026-11-10).** Download
`T5DR-Online-1.2.3.zip` from https://github.com/TheWishin/T5DROnline/releases

**Community Discord:** https://discord.gg/4DwDHAkk2x -- questions, matches, feedback.

**Offline play is ready:** all modes, 60 fps, Xbox pad and arcade stick tested.
**Online works:** tested between two players' PCs over the internet (direct
connection, 26 ms ping, 60 fps). Please end matches normally, not with Alt+F4.

Found a bug? Please report it (see "Bug reports" below).

Deutsch: `docs\README.de.md` in this folder.

**Languages:** the launcher speaks English, Deutsch, Español, 한국어, 日本語, Português (Brasil)
and Français (**Settings** -> **Language**).

## What is this?

- The PS3 game's program is translated to C++ ahead of time (static
  recompilation) and compiled into a normal Windows program. No emulator runs.
- The model is the same as
  [Tekken 6 Native Online](https://github.com/Ekspym/Tekken6-native-online).
  This repository and its releases contain **no part of the game**.
- You build the game on your own PC from **your own copy**: the PSN package
  (`.pkg`) and the license (`.rap`) from your own account. The launcher does
  this for you.
- Online play between friends works like Tekken 6 Native Online: log in (or
  play as a guest) in the launcher's Online tab, find an opponent, and the game
  starts directly in the fight. See "Online".

## Optional: the OpenRecomp-FGC launcher

Besides the T5DR launcher in the release zip there is a second, optional
launcher: [OpenRecomp-FGC](https://github.com/TheWishin/OpenRecomp-FGC/releases).
It runs Tekken 5 DR and Tekken 4 in one window, with a new Online page (player
table, chat on every page, ranked card), grouped settings and a simpler Build
page. The T5DR launcher keeps working, and both can use the same T5DR install.
Be online in one launcher at a time. Community for both:
the OpenRecomp-FGC Discord.

## Status (2026-10-21)

Tested on one development PC (Windows 11, 16-core Ryzen 9, RTX 3090). Online play was
tested between two real PCs over the internet (AMD/60 Hz vs Intel/240 Hz).

| Area | State |
|---|---|
| Start-up | Works. Boots, opens the window, reaches the title, menus, character select and fights. |
| Menus, fights | 60 fps, also with other programs busy on the PC. The game no longer busy-waits around its frames: about 30 % less CPU on 8 cores / 16 threads. Since 1.1.3 the game's own work and the translation of its drawing take about a quarter less processor time per fight frame, and a PC a little too slow for 60 fps runs fights at 45-55 fps instead of 30-45 (measured with slowed test games; real weak PCs are not measured yet). Since 1.1.4 two changes in the game's code save more processor time per frame on 4 cores under load (registers kept between calls: ~7 % on the main thread, ~18 % on the drawing thread; cheaper memory writes: 5-7 % and 15-25 %), and a frame goes to the graphics card beside the game's next one, so on a slowed 4-core test PC a late frame comes about 1 ms sooner. Since 1.1.5 a dedicated graphics card draws one frame while the game prepares the next, PCs with 2 cores get a 2-core mode, and BUILD GAME ends with a shader warm-up so the first fights on each stage no longer stutter. |
| Laptops, handhelds | **Power saving** (launcher Settings; Auto turns it on with a battery, a power-saving plan, a mobile processor or integrated graphics): fewer helper threads, no busy waiting, the same game online. Not tried on a real laptop or handheld yet. Since 1.1.4 integrated graphics also start with Internal resolution Auto, and the Play offline tab says when the processor ran well under its normal clock (it suggests Windows' power mode Best performance). |
| Game modes | Arcade, Ghost, Versus (two players on one PC), Survival and Practice work. Gallery and the game's own Online menu need Namco's and Sony's servers (gone) and say so. |
| Fighters, stages | All fighters and stages render correctly, including faces, floor shadows and background figures. Stage blur and the sun's glow look as on the PS3 at every internal resolution when Settings -> Stage blur / glow is On (Off, sharp and without the glow, is the default since 1.1.4). |
| Unlocks, costumes | Offline, in launcher Settings -> Unlocks (all off by default): all stages without the fights they normally take, Jinpachi and the random cell on the character select without clearing Arcade, and every customization item for 0 Fight Money (your save is backed up first). Online games use a fresh save of their own, the same on both PCs; only your custom costume comes from your own save, and both players see both costumes (1.1.3). Both PCs check the costume against the game's own item shop tables and fall back to the default one (1.1.4). |
| Display | Resizable window, borderless fullscreen (Alt+Enter or F11). **Internal resolution** from Lowest (0.5x) over Native (720p) to 1080p, 1440p and 4K, or Auto (the screen's step, at most 1080p on integrated graphics) (launcher Settings, `PS3_INTERNAL_RES`); every step checked in fights, menus, movies and character select. Less GPU work at 1080p and above (1.1.3). On integrated graphics Auto is the default (1.1.4). For weak or old graphics cards: Settings -> Graphics (Shadows, Effects, **Lowest (old graphics cards)**) (1.1.5). |
| Music, sound effects, movies | Work. |
| Controls | Keyboard, Xbox pads (XInput), DualShock 4 and DualSense over USB and Bluetooth (read directly, no Steam needed), arcade sticks and hitboxes (DirectInput), two local players, buttons set in the launcher (Settings -> Set up controllers) or in `controls.ini`. Short taps are never lost. Tried by a person: an Xbox pad and an arcade stick, every input came through, smooth. **Set up controllers** found no controller at all from 1.1.0 to 1.1.3; it works again (1.1.4). |
| Training tools | In Practice: an input display (each player's last inputs with how many frames each was held) and frame data after each exchange (startup, and who can act first: `+3`, `-12`), drawn sharp over the picture at any resolution. Launcher Settings -> Training overlay (Off / Inputs / Inputs + frame data, also in the other offline modes, online only your own inputs), F2 switches it in the game. Practice tools (offline): SELECT+3 puts both fighters back to the start or against a wall, the dummy blocks after the first hit / crouches / walks / sidesteps, 5 recording slots for the dummy (Settings -> Practice tools). Online: **training rooms** with a friend, endless health, nothing counted (1.1.5). See `docs\TRAINING.md` (in the release zip). |
| Input lag | A jab shows on screen about 35-40 ms after the press in fullscreen (the PS3 on a TV: ~42 ms plus the TV), a frame less than before. In a window add one frame (Windows draws the window). |
| Saving | Works. The in-game clock shows the real date. |
| Long sessions | The old memory bug (white screen after a few trips through the title) is fixed. |
| Online play | Works on one PC and through the public lobby server. Rollback netcode: 1 frame of input delay up to ~60 ms ping, 2 above, at least 3 above 150 ms and 4 above 250 ms (1.1.5) (Settings -> Online input delay; ranked: always 2, more above 150 ms), about 60 fps at 150 ms ping on an 8-thread PC (now and then a picture is shown twice), tested at 0/50/150 ms ping with packet loss. Played between two real PCs over the internet (2026-10-18). Quick and ranked search prefer opponents with a low ping (estimated through the nearest relay server, or the ping two players measured in the last 7 days) and widen the search while you wait. The Ping column, a found match, a challenge and an invite show the ping through the nearest relay server and whether the match will most likely be direct or relayed (1.1.5). Many cancelled matches in a row no longer break the open game. Nobody can pause an online fight. Matches connect even when a firewall blocks the game: through the relay when nothing else gets through (1.1.3), and there the game plays like a direct match at the same ping: the launcher forwards the game's packets the moment they arrive (1.1.4). |
| Online character select | Quick matches, rooms and friend invites also offer Jinpachi (top row, right end) and the game's random cell (top row, left end), for both players; ranked matches and tournament sets do not. Mokujin and the random cell draw anew in every match (1.1.4). |
| Casual choices | Challenges, invites and rooms: ask for P1, P2 or any side and for a stage (the stages have their real names), and **Rematch: swap sides** afterwards. **My health (casual)**: a health handicap from 150 % (since 1.1.7) down to 30 %, shown to both players. Ranked and tournaments stay as they are (1.1.5). |
| Intros, replays | Online, the fighters' intros (about 7 s) and the replay after a round (about 9 s) are skipped as soon as both players have pressed Start; one player alone skips nothing, and Start still never pauses an online fight (1.1.4). |
| Friends, invites | Accounts add friends by name on the Online tab's **Friends** page and see who is online, searching or in a match. **Invite** a friend to a casual match or your room: one click on Accept starts it. |
| Rooms | Lobby rooms for 2, or community rooms for up to 8 who take turns (winner stays, or everyone in turn); open, with a password or an invite code, or hidden (1.1.3). Friends who know a room's password always get in, even while strangers guess at it; the host sees how many wrong passwords came and can turn those networks away (1.1.4). **Training rooms** (1.1.5): practice with a friend, damage never KOs, hold SELECT to give up. |
| Tournaments | Accounts join tournaments on the Online tab (tournament hosts create them; for one of the 20 host slots, DM wishin): single or double elimination, sets of best of 3 or 5, up to 64 players; the server calls each set and the game starts by itself (1.1.3). |
| Alerts | In another window while you wait? When a match is found, someone joins your room, it is your turn in a room, a friend invites you, a tournament set is ready or your opponent asks for a rematch, the launcher plays a short chime and its taskbar button flashes until you are back (Settings -> Sound and taskbar flash; on by default; 1.1.4). |
| Replays | Every online match is saved (a few KB). The **Replays** tab plays it again in the game and checks that it is identical to the live match. |
| Spectating | **Watch** a friend's match, a room's match or a tournament set live in your own game, a few seconds behind and checked frame by frame; only when both players allow it (Settings -> Spectators) (1.1.3). A room's Watch also works between a match and its rematch, and friends and room members come first at a full match (1.1.4). |
| Launcher | English plus six translations: Deutsch, Español, 한국어, 日本語, Português (Brasil), Français, with nothing cut off at 100 % and 150 % display scaling. The Settings tab scrolls. Next to every name on the Online tab stands the game's own rank plate, read from your own game after BUILD GAME, and the window redraws more than twice as fast (1.1.4). **Check my problem** finds the known problems in this PC's logs, a **Stats** page shows every fighter's matches and win rate, your profile shows your record and your match history with **Watch replay** (1.1.5). Updates itself; from 1.1.5 only with updates signed by the project. |
| Build from your copy | Works on the development PC. A stopped helper process no longer hangs the build at "Translate code"; a file that fails to compile gets a second try (1.1.3). Unpacking needs far less memory, a package of another version (01.01) is named as such, and a step that prints nothing for long says so (1.1.5). |

## Requirements

**Minimum requirements:** Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), any 64-bit Intel or AMD
processor (one without SSE4.1 gets a slower build, see below; for 60 fps you
need the 4-core processor named below anyway),
a DirectX 12 graphics card (feature level 11_0: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 400 / GT 600
and newer, AMD Radeon HD 7000 and newer, Intel HD 4400 and newer) and 4 GB RAM.
For 60 fps in fights: a 4-core processor from about 2011 on (an Intel Core
i5-2500 with a GeForce GT 730 plays at 55-60). A 2-core processor (Core
i3-2100 / i3-3240) plays with the **Old PC** settings, which the launcher picks
by itself there (see `docs\WEAK_PC.md` (in the release zip)). The CPU matters
most: the game's main work runs on one core, so one fast core helps more than
many cores or a strong graphics card.

In detail:

- Windows 10 (version 1909 or newer) or Windows 11, 64-bit. Nothing else to
  install: no Visual C++ redistributable, no Visual Studio, no DirectX
  download. Windows "N" editions: the movies stay black without the Media
  Feature Pack; the rest works.
- A graphics card with Direct3D 12 (feature level 11_0 or higher) and a
  current driver. That is about: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 400 / GT 600 or newer
  (Fermi cards such as the old GT 730 run, slowly: about 20-35 fps), AMD
  Radeon HD 7000 or newer, Intel HD 4400 (2013) or newer -- Intel HD 4000 and
  older have no DirectX 12 driver, and Intel's drivers from 15.40.44.5107 (2021)
  on switch DirectX 12 off on HD 4200-5000 / Iris 5100-5200 (a security fix;
  15.40.42.5063 and older still have it, untested here). Tested on an NVIDIA RTX 3090, the Radeon
  graphics of a Ryzen 7950X and Windows' software renderer (WARP); players
  play on GT 730s. Laptops with two graphics chips use the fast one by default.
- A 64-bit Intel or AMD processor. AVX2 is not needed. The build selects
  faster code automatically: AVX1 for Sandy/Ivy Bridge when Windows supports
  it, x86-64-v3 for newer CPUs with its full feature set, and the baseline
  otherwise.
- Processors without SSE4.1 (Intel Core 2 before 2008 such as the E6000 and
  Q6600, AMD Phenom II, Athlon II, Athlon 64 X2): BUILD GAME picks a second
  build of the game for them by itself (`runtime\sse2`). It plays the same
  game (online too, with anyone) but needs about 1.3 times the processor time
  (measured on our PC: sound 1.4x, character animation 1.8x). These
  processors are slow for the game. Our estimates (no such PC has run it
  yet): Phenom II X4/X6 about 35-45 fps in fights, Core 2 Quad about 20-25,
  Core 2 Duo 10-15 with broken sound. **Check my problem** tells you before
  a build. Windows 11 24H2 and newer do not start on these processors
  at all; Windows 10 does.
- 4 GB RAM: the game uses about 0.8 GB (1.1 GB committed) in a fight; BUILD
  GAME runs as many compile jobs as the free memory allows.
- Speed: fights held 60 fps with 4 CPU threads in our tests (fast desktop
  cores); online against a far-away player (rollback, 150 ms) about 50 fps.
  A PC a little too slow for 60 fps runs fights at about 45-55 fps since 1.1.3.
  See [Low frame rate](TROUBLESHOOTING.md). Weak graphics:
  **Internal resolution** under [Playing](#playing).
- Any monitor: 60, 120, 144 Hz and more, also slower TVs (50 Hz). The game
  always runs at the PS3's 59.94 frames per second. Any Windows display
  scaling (100-200 %), several monitors.
- Any folder you can write to, on any drive, also with spaces or letters like
  ü or Ł in the name, or in your user name. Not in Program Files, not in a
  OneDrive folder, and keep the path short (under about 150 characters).
- About 1.5 GB of free disk space. After the build it uses about 1.1 GB, plus
  the 90 MB zip.
- An internet connection during the first build. About 50 KB of public key data
  (two text files) is fetched from github.com. Nothing about you or your game is
  sent.
- **Your own copy** of the game, exactly this one:
  **TEKKEN 5 DARK RESURRECTION ONLINE, US PSN, `NPUB30009`, version 01.00**.
  - the package: `.pkg`, 619,430,240 bytes
  - the license: `.rap` (16 bytes), named
    `UP0700-NPUB30009_00-UPDATE0000010000.rap`
  - since 1.1.9 also the European PSN release, **TEKKEN 5 DARK RESURRECTION, `NPEA00019`,

1423143266.readme_excerpt:
# Killzone Recomp Extended: Native Killzone PS2 Port for Windows PC

**Killzone Recomp Extended** is an unofficial native Windows PC port of **Killzone** (2004) for PlayStation 2 (PS2),
built through static recompilation. It combines the
[PS2Recomp static recompiler](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) with PCSX2-based GS, microVU, IPU, and SPU2
components.

The port supports Direct3D 11, Direct3D 12, and Vulkan rendering, high-refresh gameplay, ultrawide displays,
mouse-and-keyboard controls, gamepads, internal resolution scaling, and optional AMD FidelityFX FSR 1.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **NEW FEATURE: AMD FidelityFX FSR 3.1.6 Super Resolution**
>
> Vulkan now includes source-built FSR 3 Super Resolution through the explicit experimental-input mode. This is
> Super Resolution only, not frame generation, and its approximate temporal inputs can produce HUD or disocclusion
> ghosting. See the [experimental upscaler configuration](docs/configuration.md#experimental-presentation-upscaler).

> **Bring your own disc.** This repository contains no game code or data. You need a supported Killzone disc image:
> NTSC-U `SCUS-97402`, PAL `SCES-52893` (English/Russian/Greek), or PAL `SCES-52004`
> (English/French/German/Spanish/Italian/Dutch).

> [!NOTE]
> **Companion Blender add-on:** [Killzone Blender Importer](https://github.com/Tzeentchnet/Killzone-Blender-Importer)
> provides Blender 5.2 tools for inspecting and importing Killzone assets.

This community project continues [drakolordx7/KillzoneRecomp](https://github.com/drakolordx7/KillzoneRecomp) with
additional graphics, display, input, configuration, testing, and runtime work. The active development target is
Windows x64.

## Killzone PC port features

- D3D11, D3D12, and Vulkan renderers with internal resolution scaling up to 8x.
- Native 4:3 and 16:9 plus automatic, 21:9, and 32:9 ultrawide modes with centered HUD and menu presentation.
- Independent world and weapon field-of-view controls with zoom-preserving tangent-space scaling.
- High-refresh gameplay with real-time game-speed correction.
- Raw mouse aim, rebindable keyboard controls, SDL3 controllers, adjustable dead zone/range, and dynamic button
  prompts.
- Anisotropic filtering, FXAA, D3D11 SMAA, sharp scaling, CAS sharpening, and bounded 2x view distance.
- Default-off Vulkan FSR 1 spatial presentation, available through
  [experimental configuration](docs/configuration.md#experimental-presentation-upscaler).
- Default-off Vulkan FSR 3.1.6 Super Resolution in explicit experimental-input mode. This is SR only, not frame
  generation, and its synthetic depth/Optical Flow inputs can produce HUD or disocclusion ghosting.
- Launcher-managed display, graphics, controls, audio, disc, and isolated testing settings.
- US and two PAL executable versions supported from separately generated code sets in one executable.

## Build and play on Windows

### System and build requirements

- Windows 10/11 x64
- Visual Studio Build Tools 2022 or newer with **Desktop development with C++**
- CMake 3.24+, Python 3.11+, and an x64 CPU with SSE4.1
- A supported retail disc image

Clone with submodules:

```powershell
git clone --recursive https://github.com/Tzeentchnet/KillzoneRecomp-Extended
Set-Location .\KillzoneRecomp-Extended
```

The build can contain these separately generated executable versions:

| Disc | Boot executable | Languages | `regen.py` mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| NTSC-U `SCUS-97402` | `SCUS_974.02` | English | default |
| PAL `SCES-52893` | `SCES_528.93` | English, Russian, Greek | `--pal` |
| PAL `SCES-52004` | `SCES_520.04` | English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Dutch | `--eu` |

The US generated tree is required. When `generated_pal\` or `generated_eu\` is present during configuration, CMake
adds that prefixed code set to the same `killzone.exe`; omitting either directory disables only that matching disc.

Follow the [Killzone Recomp Extended building guide](docs/building.md) to provision locked dependencies, generate
private game-derived C++, and build `killzone.exe`. Start `launch_launcher.bat`, select your disc image, and configure
the port.

Player settings and bindings are documented in the
[configuration and controls guide](docs/configuration.md).

## Killzone PC port compatibility and status

This is a test build, not an official release.

- Boot, movies, menus, profile creation, campaign gameplay, save/load, mouse/keyboard, controllers, high-refresh
  timing, and clean shutdown have been validated on the current Windows build.
- D3D11, D3D12, and Vulkan are covered by ISO-free renderer tests. D3D12 is the reference backend.
- Intermittent effects or dialogue truncation can still occur during action-heavy combat. The current buffering
  mitigation reduces the problem but does not eliminate it.
- VSync is recommended; disabling it can produce substantial tearing.
- macOS/Apple Silicon work is experimental and deferred from the active release path.

Not implemented:

- Killzone Online, DNAS, network login, lobby, or multiplayer gameplay.
- DLSS, XeSS, FSR 2, or production-qualified temporal reconstruction. FSR 3 SR is available only as an explicit
  experiment using marked approximations; strict mode still fails closed because reliable gameplay depth, motion,
  and separate HUD/composition inputs are unavailable.
- HDR output; the current renderer presents composed SDR color.
- Distribution of retail assets, generated game code, saves, or memory-card images.

Technical status and evidence live in [Findings](docs/findings.md). Archived online research is preserved under
[Multiplayer](docs/multiplayer/README.md).

## Build, test, and contribute

The checked Windows workflow is:

```powershell
.\tools\scripts\cmake_preset.ps1 -Preset win-msvc-rel
.\tools\scripts\cmake_preset.ps1 -Preset win-msvc-tests -Action build
.\tools\scripts\cmake_preset.ps1 -Preset win-msvc-rel -Action test -Label iso-free
```

Equivalent clang-cl presets are available. See:

- [Building](docs/building.md)
- [Testing and diagnostics](docs/testing.md)
- [Documentation index](docs/README.md)
- [Runtime patch rationale](patches/README.md)
- [Release and distribution rules](docs/release.md)

Generated sources and retail inputs remain private. The committed dependency lock and generated manifest retain only
reproducible, protected-content-safe provenance.

## Repository layout

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/` | Port integration, launcher, input, timing, patches, and runtime hooks |
| `ext/kzgs`, `ext/kzvu`, `ext/kzipu`, `ext/kzspu2` | PCSX2-derived components |
| `ext/PS2Recomp` | Locked PS2Recomp runtime fork |
| `host/` | Renderer-independent host platform boundary |
| `config/` | Recompiler configurations and dependency/generated provenance |
| `patches/` | Reconstructible PS2Recomp changes and rationale |
| `tools/` | Build, regeneration, testing, profiling, and analysis scripts |
| `docs/` | User guides, technical evidence, and archived research |
| [`docs/xbrz_texture_upscaling.md`](docs/xbrz_texture_upscaling.md) | Feature contract, architecture, safety boundaries and acceptance gates for the xBRZ prototype |

## Credits

- [drakolordx7](https://github.com/drakolordx7) and contributors created the original Killzone recompilation and PC
  port foundation.
- [Ash01Live](https://github.com/Ash01Live) contributed the original field-of-view settings through
  [drakolordx7/KillzoneRecomp#21](https://github.com/drakolordx7/KillzoneRecomp/pull/21).
- [ran-j/PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) and its contributors provide the static recompiler and runtime
  foundation.
- [PCSX2](https://github.com/PCSX2/pcsx2) contributors provide the renderer, microVU, IPU, and SPU2 foundations.
- [AMD FidelityFX FSR 1](ext/kzgs/third_party/fsr1/README.md) provides the MIT-licensed spatial upscaling source.
- [AMD FidelityFX SDK](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK) provides the source-built FSR 3
  Super Resolution and Optical Flow implementation under its included notices.

Developed with AI assistance.

## License

Repository-owned code and documentation are MIT under [LICENSE](LICENSE), except for the components identified there
as GPL-3.0. PCSX2-derived libraries, PS2Recomp, the field-of-view contribution, and every compiled build remain
GPL-3.0; see [LICENSE-GPL-3.0](LICENSE-GPL-3.0).
The vendored [xBRZ sources](ext/kzgs/third_party/xbrz/README.md) retain their GPL notice and MAME linking exception.

Killzone is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This project is not affiliated with Sony or Guerrilla
Games.

007eca292e40aec1f9354f202e9443afa7a3248b.message:
vulkan: depth readback accepts D32_SFLOAT_S8_UINT and barriers both aspects

#231 made D32_SFLOAT_S8_UINT the first-choice depth format, which lavapipe,
RADV and the Switch all pick. #236's vk_eng_depth_readback still accepted
only D32_SFLOAT, so depth reinterpretation and the pass-dump zeta images did
nothing on those devices, and its DEPTH-only barrier on a depth+stencil image
is a validation error. The copy region stays DEPTH: its aspect still copies out
as 32-bit floats.

088befac6de09dad63a3fec66e8014d59b1f1e97.message:
ppu_loader: size per-thread TLS blocks by the TLS image, not image + 0x7000

Symptom: a title that creates more than 31 PPU threads (with a small TLS
image) gives the 32nd and every later thread the main thread's TLS, with no
message. Thread-locals that matter then collide: in Killzone 3 two threads
ended up reading one per-thread wait object, one waited forever on the other's
event queue and the level never started.

Cause: ppu_tls_new_block sized each block as memsz + 0x7000, rounded to a
page (0x8000 for a small image). The 0x7000 is the ABI's r13 bias: the guest
addresses TLS as r13 - 0x7000 + off with off < memsz, so nothing lives in it.
The 1 MB window at PPU_TLS_IMG then holds 31 blocks, and the fallback (return
0, the caller uses the main block) is silent.

Change: blocks are memsz rounded up to 4 KB (about 250 fit for a small
image); the first block still starts after the main block's image. When the
window is full, one line is logged before falling back to the shared block.

Verification: tools/test_ppu_tls_blocks.py builds the real
ppu_tls_new_block into a host program and requests 100 blocks with a
0x240-byte image. On v0.14.0 (a2c2010): granted 31/100, FAIL. With this
change: granted 100/100, no overlap with each other or the main image, image
copied into each, PASS. Also run in the Killzone 3 port (v0.13.0 base) since
2026-10-11: the thread that hung now waits on its own event queue.

0aead166fd65ab34bee01df19a341665800a727f.message:
cellGcm: a FIFO user command reaches the handler set with cellGcmSetUserHandler

Symptom: a title's cellGcmSetUserHandler callback never runs for the user
commands it puts in its command buffer. In Killzone 3 that callback submits
the per-frame job that lets the frame continue, so the level stalled.

Cause: the walker decodes GCM_SET_USER_COMMAND (method 0xEB00) as
subchannel 7 / method 0x0B00 and hands it to rsx_raise_user_cmd, the lv2
route: it posts an event to the RSX interrupt queue for a guest interrupt
thread. A title that registered its handler through the HLE
cellGcmSetUserHandler has no such thread; its handler runs from
ppu_gcm_pump. The branch then `continue`s, so the walker's later 0xEB00 case,
which calls cellGcmQueueUserCommand for the pump, is never reached.

Change: when an HLE user handler is registered, the 0x0B00 branch also
queues the command for the pump (cellGcmQueueUserCommand). The lv2 event is
still raised as before.

Verification: libs/video/tests/test_gcm_fifo_user_command.c (standalone,
includes cellGcmSys.c like test_gcm_user_command.c; graphics backends
stubbed) registers an HLE user handler, then five times puts one user
command in the ring, drains it with cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo and calls
ppu_gcm_pump. With this change the handler runs five times, each with its
command's argument, and the lv2 route is still taken five times (gcc and
clang). Against v0.14.0's cellGcmSys.c (a2c2010) the handler never runs
(5/5 fail). test_gcm_user_command.c still passes.

0fb35648aed8ca984638357c2e82c0e892c12c8b.message:
ppu_sysprx: sys_lwcond_t is +0x00 lwmutex EA, +0x04 queue id

Symptom: a title that reads lwcond+0x00 itself sees 0 there and treats the
lwcond as invalid (Killzone 3's file system layer checks it before every
wait and loops). The queue id is also written past the 8-byte structure,
over whatever the title keeps next to it.

Cause: the context-style sys_lwcond_create in ppu_sysprx.cpp writes the
lwmutex EA as a 64-bit value at +0x00 (so the EA lands at +0x04 and +0x00
reads 0) and the id at +0x08. sys_lwcond_t is 8 bytes: +0x00 u32 lwmutex
EA, +0x04 u32 queue id, which is also what libs/system/sysPrxForUser.h
declares as sys_lwcond_t_hle.

Change: 32-bit stores at +0x00 and +0x04 in sys_lwcond_create, and a 32-bit
read of +0x00 in sys_lwcond_wait. Wait/signal behaviour is unchanged.

Verification: tools/test_lwcond_layout.py builds the real
sys_lwcond_create and sys_lwcond_wait into a host program over stubbed
guest memory. With this change +0x00 holds the lwmutex EA, +0x04 a nonzero
id, nothing past +0x08 is written, and the wait finds the lwmutex. On
v0.14.0 (a2c2010) +0x00 reads 0, the EA is at +0x04 and the id is written
at +0x08 (2 of 3 checks fail; the wait found the lwmutex there only because
create and wait agreed on the wrong layout).

ppu_lifter: exact VMX, branch decode, integer, FP and decoding fixes

VMX
- runtime/ppu/ppu_vmx.h implements every VMX op exactly, and the lifter
  routes ops by raw XO: some had no disassembler name and lifted as no-ops.
  About 45 did nothing: the saturating adds/subs, vavg*, vmul[eo]*, vmsum*,
  vmhadd*/vmhradd*, vmladduhm, vrlh, the element and whole-vector shifts,
  vpk*, vsum*, vaddcuw/vsubcuw, vpkpx/vupk*px, vexptefp/vlogefp.
- Saturation sets VSCR[SAT], VSCR[NJ] is honoured, vcmp*. writes CR6;
  mtvscr/mfvscr are decoded, and VRSAVE reads back (ppu_context.vrsave).

Branches
- BO/BI come from the instruction word, so bdnzt/bdzf decrement CTR and
  test the condition (they were always taken); CTR is 64-bit.
- Every LK=1 form sets LR unconditionally.
- b<cond>lrl dispatches through ps3_indirect_call_to and leaves CTR alone.
- bl 0 / bcl 20,31,0 (get-PC) lift as get-PC, not as a call.

Integer
- XER[OV]/[SO] set by every OE form; compares and stwcx./stdcx. copy SO.
- rlwinm/rlwnm/rlwimi handle wrapping masks (MB > ME).
- mulld/mulli wrap, and lifted code builds with -fwrapv.
- mtxer keeps only the defined bits; mfocrf isolates its field.

Decoding: lswi/lswx/stswi/stswx, lwaux, stdbrx, stvlx/stvrx(l), lvrxl, td,
dst/dss.

FP: single-precision results (NaNs included) are single-format; fctiw/fctiwz
write the whole FPR; the FPSCR moves (mffs, mtfsf, mtfsfi, mtfsb0/1, mcrfs)
are implemented; FP record forms set CR1.

CR fusion checks the fused field's liveness past the branch target; it used
to fuse a compare that was re-tested after the label.

Guest loads in lifted code are inline (vm_read*_inl in the header preamble);

16db6bca787b02f598a18b5b5efbbd7b2f882002.message:
cellGcm: GET_REPORT honours the report DMA context and writes main-memory reports to guest memory

Symptom: titles that keep their GPU reports in main memory read stale memory
for every report. Killzone 3 selects the main-memory report context and
issues about 160 reports per frame in a level (timestamps and occlusion
queries); none of them ever reached the memory it reads.

Cause: the FIFO walker ignored NV4097_SET_CONTEXT_DMA_REPORT (0x1A8) and
wrote every NV4097_GET_REPORT (0x1800) into the host s_report_data slots,
indexed by offset / 16, whatever context the title had selected.

Change: the walker records the context set by 0x1A8 (reset to local by
cellGcmInit and cellGcmTerminate). With the local context (0xFEED0000, the
default) a report goes to s_report_data as before. With the main-memory
context (0xFEED0001, or CELL_GCM_CONTEXT_DMA_REPORT_LOCATION_MAIN 0xBAD68000)
the report's offset is an IO offset and the 16-byte report is written
big-endian to gcm_io2ea(offset): u64 timestamp, u32 value, u32 0. An offset
with no IO mapping is skipped with a rate-limited log line. Report
timestamps now rise strictly, so two reports in one walker pass never share
or reverse a time stamp.

Verification: tests/gcm_reports (CTest, built with PS3RECOMP_BUILD_TESTS on
POSIX hosts like the host harness) builds a ring with local reports, a
switch to 0xFEED0001, main-memory reports of type 1 and 2, one unmapped
offset and a switch back, drains it once with cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo and
reads every slot back. Run as a MinGW-w64 build under Proton (this machine
has no Linux SDL2 for the POSIX runtime build): with this change 9/9 checks
pass; the same test linked against v0.14.0's cellGcmSys.c (a2c2010) fails
6/9 (main-memory slots keep their sentinel, the reports land in the host
area instead, timestamps not written). Carried as a local patch in the
Killzone 3 port (v0.13.0 base).

24286f4b3871aff53cf988448e1fc756956372dc.message:
cellGcm: in-FIFO flip wraps only the runtime's own command ring

Symptom: intermittently a title waits forever on a fence. Killzone 3
stopped about 16 s in, depending on where the walker's get offset was.

Cause: _cellGcmSetFlipCommand's HLE (gcm_flip_into_fifo) writes the flip
marker at ctx->current and then, when less than GCM_FLIP_WRAP_BYTES are
left before ctx->end and the walker is well past begin, wraps the context
it was given: a JUMP to begin after the marker and ctx->current = begin.
That is what the SDK's buffer-full callback does for the runtime's ring.
A title with its own buffer-full callback manages its own buffers, and its
context need not be a ring: Killzone 3 flips on a 0x30000-byte draw
context whose end moves down as it allocates from the top, so it always
looks nearly full. Rewinding it mid-frame cut the frame short, the fence
release in its tail never ran, and the title waited for it.

Change: wrap only when the context's buffer-full callback descriptor
(ctx + 0xC) still points at the runtime's callback
(GCM_FIFO_CALLBACK_SENTINEL_EA, installed by cellGcmSetupContext). Other
contexts get the marker and current advances past it, as when there is
room.

Verification: libs/video/tests/test_gcm_flip_wrap.c (standalone, includes
cellGcmSys.c like test_gcm_user_command.c) flips on two nearly full
contexts with the walker 0x28000 bytes past their begin: the ring made by
cellGcmSetupContext, and a title context with its own callback. With this
change the runtime ring wraps (marker, JUMP to begin, current = begin) and
the title context does not (marker, current past it), with gcc and clang.
Against v0.14.0's cellGcmSys.c (a2c2010) the title context is wrapped too
(1 of 2 fails). test_gcm_user_command.c still passes.

286d3ed9e33988664a79553b347bcf5af96d2673.message:
cellGcm: IO mapping table 16 -> 512 slots, no IO leak on refusal, iomap fills a free slot

Symptom: a title that maps many separate main-memory chunks loses the later
ones. Killzone 3 maps up to 38 one-megabyte chunks at level load and keeps
vertex buffers in them; after the 16th, cellGcmMapMainMemory failed, those
buffers had no IO offset and every geometry draw in a level was degenerate
(only effects over black).

Cause:
- CELL_GCM_MAX_IO_MAPPINGS is 16. libgcm has no such small fixed count; a
  mapping fails when the IO address space runs out.
- cellGcmMapMainMemory allocates the IO region before it looks for a free
  slot, so each refused call still consumes IO address space.
- cellGcm_syscall_iomap writes s_io_mappings[s_io_mapping_count]. After an
  unmap the count no longer points past the last used slot, so a new mapping
  overwrites a live one.

Change:
- 512 slots (16 bytes each; an assumed bound well above what titles use),
  overridable with -DCELL_GCM_MAX_IO_MAPPINGS=N.
- cellGcmMapMainMemory looks for a free slot before allocating the region.
- cellGcm_syscall_iomap takes a slot from find_free_mapping like the other
  mapping paths.
The return codes and every other mapping function are unchanged.

Verification: tools/test_gcm_io_mappings.py builds the real
find_free_mapping, gcm_io_alloc, cellGcmMapMainMemory and
cellGcm_syscall_iomap against stubs. On v0.14.0 (a2c2010): FAIL (15 chunks
before the first refusal, the refusal leaks IO space, iomap after an unmap
overwrites a live mapping). With this change: PASS (510 chunks with distinct
offsets, no leak, live mapping kept). Negative controls on a copy of this
branch: 16 slots fails the chunk check (14), a count-indexed iomap fails the
live-slot check. cellGcmSys.c passes cc -fsyntax-only. Used in the Killzone 3
port (v0.13.0 base): its level geometry draws with this change.

40789072e4e6c70539b3e18cddb51a99d25c417e.message:
live-draw: depth buffers read as textures return the real depth

Symptom: a DEPTH24_D8 texture that reads a zeta comes back 0 or partly 0
in three common shapes: a full-screen read of a depth buffer whose first
pass used a smaller clip, a read of an address that is both a colour target
and a zeta, and a draw that reads the zeta it is depth-testing against
(deferred lighting, soft particles). Effects that depend on scene depth
(depth of field, fog, soft particles, deferred lighting) then see a flat 0.

Causes and changes (rsx_live_draw.c):
1. The R32F snapshot of a zeta keeps the clip size of the first pass that
   bound it (512x512 of a 1280x720 depth buffer, say), so later reads get 0
   outside that corner. zdepth_get now grows the snapshot to the largest
   clip bound since, within the depth resource (zdepth_grow_snapshot: a new
   resource, descriptors rewritten, the old one retired, re-resolved at the
   next read).
2. A depth-format read of an address that is also a colour target matched
   the colour surface first. When a written host zeta exists at that
   address the read now takes the zeta.
3. A draw that samples its own bound zeta with depth writes off read guest
   memory, which the host depth never reaches. It now reads the zeta's
   snapshot; the zeta cannot change during such a draw. A draw that writes
   the zeta it reads keeps the old fallback.

fp decompiler: the NV40 pack and unpack opcodes

PK4UB, UP4UB, PKG, UPG, PK4B, UP4B, PK2US, UP2US, PK2H and UP2H had no case:
each was skipped with a TODO comment and its destination kept whatever it
held. inFAMOUS 2's character materials convert sRGB<->linear with PK4UB->UPG
and PKG->UP4UB right before their outputs, so Cole's scalp rendered saturated

into the preamble only for a program that uses one of the opcodes, so every
other program's text is unchanged; the preamble buffer grows to hold them.

host: --depthbounds skips where there is no depth bounds test

The depth bounds test is an optional Vulkan feature, and the lavapipe the
Vulkan workflow runs on (Mesa 25, LLVM 20.1.2) does not report depthBounds.

65806f3f3614fca3f40061a3ba0ff2cadfaa36b0.message:
ppu_lifter: big-endian lane order for ten VMX integer ops

Symptom: lifted code computes wrong results for vmulouh, vmsumshm, vadduws,
vadduhs and vpkuwum, and does nothing at all for vmsumuhm, vsubuws,
vpkswss, vsrb and vsrab, which were emitted as "/* TODO */" no-ops.

Cause: ctx->vr holds raw big-endian guest bytes. The first five handlers
read halfword and word lanes through int16_t*/uint32_t* casts, which gives
byte-reversed lanes (and the wrong lane pairing) on a little-endian host.
The other five had no lowering.

Change: one handler for the ten ops that assembles each halfword or word
lane from its bytes in big-endian order, computes the result as the AltiVec
PEM defines it (modulo, saturating or shift) and stores it back in the same
order. The five old handlers are removed.

Verification: tools/test_ppu_vmx_lanes.py lifts each op, compiles the
emitted C with the lifter's own preamble and compares vD with an independent
Python model of the instruction on 300 inputs per op (216 edge combinations
plus random vectors). With this change 10/10 ops agree on every input. On
v0.14.0 (a2c2010) all ten fail: five emit TODO, the other five differ on
244 to 292 of 300 inputs. tools/test_ppu_vcmp_record_cr6.py and
tools/test_ppu_lift.py pass before and after.

662270bdf366da3e360385f421ce5192f82b3443.message:
ppu_loader: indirect-call depth guard can be kept per coroutine

Symptom: a title whose guest jobs run on host coroutines (host fibers that
stand in for a guest fiber scheduler) works for a while, then every
indirect call on that thread is skipped by the recursion guard, even calls
to leaf functions ("[ppu] recursion cap ... skipping"); null calls and an
exit follow. Killzone 3 quit a few minutes into a level.

Cause: the guard in ps3_indirect_call_impl keeps one depth count per host
thread in a function-local thread_local. A coroutine that ends by switching
away from inside an indirect call never unwinds its frames, so each one
leaks its depth into the thread's count until the count passes the 4000
cap. The vcall stack pointer (g_vcall_sp) leaks the same way. Neither can be
reached from outside the function, so a coroutine layer has no way to keep
them per coroutine.

Change: the depth count moves to a file-scope thread-local, and two
accessors, ps3_ppu_dispatch_depth_slot() and ps3_ppu_vcall_sp_slot(), return
the current thread's counters. A coroutine layer saves *slot when it
switches away and restores it when it switches back. Threads that never
switch behave exactly as before.

Verification: tools/test_ppu_dispatch_depth.py builds the real
ppu_loader.cpp with runtime/ppu/tests/test_ppu_dispatch_depth.cpp. 5000
ucontext coroutines each go five ps3_indirect_call levels deep and switch
back to the home context without returning; the home side saves and
restores both counters around each switch. With this change all 5000
chains run to the bottom, the home thread's depth and vcall sp are 0
before and after, and a later indirect call runs. Against v0.14.0's
ppu_loader.cpp (a2c2010; the accessors do not exist, the test declares
them weak) only 800 of 5000 chains run: the guard trips at depth 4001 and
skips every call after that.

runtime: thread-locals stay thread-local under MinGW (__declspec(thread) only for MSVC)

Symptom (MinGW-w64 builds only): two PPU threads that exit close together
crash; one thread's sys_ppu_thread_exit longjmps toward a frame on the other
thread's stack. In Killzone 3 this is the two Bink threads exiting at the
end of the intro movie. The SPURS job mailboxes and the sysutil completion
drain guard are shared between threads the same way.

Cause: sys_ppu_thread.c, spurs_job.c, cellSpurs.c and cellSysutil.c pick
__declspec(thread) when _WIN32 is defined. MinGW GCC defines _WIN32 and
ignores that attribute ("'thread' attribute directive ignored"), so the
exit jmp_buf and its armed flag, g_spurs_job_mbox* and the completion
`draining` flag are plain process-wide globals there. The runtime's other
thread-local macros (PPU_THREAD_LOCAL, SPU_THREAD_LOCAL, SPU_TLS) already
test _MSC_VER.

Change: those four macros use __declspec(thread) only under _MSC_VER and
__thread / _Thread_local otherwise, like the others. MSVC and POSIX builds
are unchanged.

Verification: tools/test_mingw_tls.py finds every macro in runtime/ and
libs/ defined to __declspec(thread), keeps its surrounding preprocessor
conditionals and compiles a static variable with it as MinGW sees it
(x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc when present, else the host compiler with _WIN32
defined and __declspec(x) as __attribute__((x))), then checks the variable
is thread-local in the assembly. Without MinGW gcc the emulation runs only on
ELF hosts and only after two controls (__thread reads as thread-local, a
plain static does not) pass; otherwise, as on macOS, the test prints SKIP. With this change 9/9 qualifiers are
thread-local under both compilers; on v0.14.0 (a2c2010) 4 of 9 are
process-wide globals (spurs_job.c, sys_ppu_thread.c, cellSpurs.c,
cellSysutil.c). The four changed files pass -fsyntax-only with MinGW GCC and

8eb45f8647cde8750f675f5725ea0bd325ec9618.message:
cellFs: 64-bit sizes and offsets in ppu_fs on Windows

Symptom: on Windows a file larger than 2 GiB is mis-sized and mis-seeked.
With a MinGW-w64 (msvcrt) build cellFsStat fails with CELL_ENOENT (the CRT's
stat wrapper reports EOVERFLOW); with UCRT (llvm-mingw) it succeeds with a
truncated size. cellFsLseek and cellFsFstat truncate to 32 bits, so a read
after a seek past 4 GiB lands at the wrong offset.

Cause: ppu_fs.cpp uses stat() with a 32-bit st_size and fseek()/ftell()
with `long`, which is 32 bits on LLP64 Windows. LP64 hosts are unaffected.

Change: _stat64, _fseeki64 and _ftelli64 on Windows; stat, fseeko and ftello
elsewhere, for cellFsStat, cellFsLseek and cellFsFstat. A trailing slash is
stripped before _stat64, which rejects it (MinGW's stat wrapper used to
strip it). The FS_FSTAT_CAP diagnostic now parses and prints 64-bit values.

Verification: tools/test_ppu_fs_large_file.py builds a fixture that
includes ppu_fs.cpp, creates a sparse 5 GiB file with a marker near its end
and checks cellFsStat, cellFsLseek (SET and END), cellFsRead after the seek
and cellFsFstat. Built with x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++ (--build-only) and run
under Wine: master fails 6 of 7 checks (Stat 0x80010006, Lseek 0x40000008,
Fstat 0x40000010); with this change all 7 pass. On Linux it passes on both.

b3082644982c43d81c8bf47959317dc4cb3cfbf1.message:
cellGcm: give a parked FIFO time to be patched before following put

A self-JUMP at the write head parks the RSX, and when `put` had meanwhile
moved elsewhere the walker took that as the title having abandoned the park
and resynced to `put` at once. inFAMOUS 2 links its main-memory command
blocks the other way round: it ends a block in a park, writes the next
commands at the ring start, moves `put`, and only then rewrites the park as a
JUMP to them. A drain that landed between the two stores went straight to
`put` and dropped everything from the ring start up to it, the frame's fence
included, so the title waited on that label for the rest of the run and the
main menu froze.

Resync only once the same park has stood with the same `put` for longer than
a title takes between the two stores (50 ms). A park patched in time is
followed as before; the pass reports itself as "parked" in the meantime.

b6dc1e428b4b89c8385595551904bfb21c33d71a.message:
ppu_lifter: jump tables behind a tail-call epilogue

discover_jump_tables drops the blocks that end in `blr` from the backward
scan for the table base register: they return, so they cannot flow into the
dispatcher. An epilogue that leaves by a tail call ends the same way and
restores the same registers, and was not dropped. inFAMOUS 2's func_000B9BD0
loads the base's base into r30 in its prologue, has an early exit
`ld r30,0xE0(r1); ...; b 0xB8570`, and dispatches nineteen instructions later
through `lwz r11,-0x7F80(r30)`: the restore read as r30's nearest definition,
no base resolved, and the switch lifted to an unresolved indirect call.

A `b` leaves the function when it goes back past the function's entry or
forward to another function's entry. Both need func_starts; without them the
scan is bounded by the nearest `blr`, which an early return puts in the
middle of a function, so only `blr` is trusted there.

tools/test_ppu_jumptables.py: the backward shape (the inFAMOUS 2 one), the
forward one, and the no-func_starts control.

b883922940d53efafac47dcc0b63dac7535294c5.message:
rsx_draw_engine, vulkan: honour the depth bounds test

NV4097 SET_DEPTH_BOUNDS_TEST_ENABLE (0x0380) with SET_DEPTH_BOUNDS_MIN and
_MAX (0x0384, 0x0388, floats) rejects a fragment whose stored depth lies
outside the bounds, whatever the depth test says. The draw engine never
read those registers, so a bounded draw covered the whole target.

Twisted Metal's deferred renderer relies on it: its sun pass is bounded to
[0, 0.999984] (the geometry) and the sky drawn right after it to
[0.999984, 1] (the far plane), both with the depth test off. Unbounded, the
sky overwrote the sun light everywhere and the HDR buffer came out almost
black.

The enable is pipeline state (rsx_be_render_state.depth_bounds_test, part
of the pipeline key); the bounds reach the backend before every draw through
a new optional hook, set_depth_bounds, like the stencil reference, so moving
them does not build pipelines. Vulkan enables the depthBounds feature when
the device has it and sets the bounds dynamically, clamped to [0, 1];
without the feature the test stays off, as before, with one log line.
Metal and the fixed-function path leave the hook unset and draw as before.

Tests: test_rsx_draw_engine checks the key, the bounds and that moving them
builds no pipeline (4 new checks, failing without the engine change).
ps3recomp_host --depthbounds draws red at z = 0.25, then blue bounded to
[0, 0.5] and green bounded to [0.5, 1] with the depth test off, and expects
blue; it runs in the Vulkan workflow's engine pass under the validation
layer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

b8cb0c8ceafc1238f3fb38c6286db64794d9c885.message:
spu: hardware-exact float semantics, NEON paths, interpreter op fixes

Float (spu_helpers.h), rewritten from the SPU ISA, single and double
precision: truncation (round toward zero), denormal flush, the extended
range, saturation, frest's hardware table, fi, the compares (fceq/fcgt/
fcmeq/fcmgt) and the conversions (cflts/cfltu/csflt/cuflt). The previous
helpers were a GPL-derived port; these are written from the ISA alone and
checked against an exact-arithmetic referee.

Speed, bit-identical output: NEON forms of fa/fs/fm/fma/fms/fnms (1.6-4x
faster), of 60 per-lane integer ops, and of shufb (tbl); test_spu_float_neon
and test_spu_int_neon compare them against the scalar forms.

Interpreter (spu_interp.c):
- fixes: mpyhha is RR (rt accumulates), rchcnt puts the count in the
  preferred word, mfspr and fscrrd read zero, bisl reads ra before writing
  the link (rt may alias ra), links and the next pc wrap at the end of local
  store, stopd reports code 0x3FFF;
- additions: bgx, mpyui, mpyhhau, rothmi, rotmah(i), bisled, dftsv and the
  double-precision ops (dfa/dfs/dfm/dfma/dfms/dfnms/dfnma, dfceq/dfcgt/
  dfcmeq/dfcmgt);
- bi/iret carry the interrupt enable/disable bits as the lifter decodes them,
  and an iret back to the interrupted pc restores the saved register file.

Lifter (spu_lifter.py):
- bisl/bisled read the target before writing the link, and bisled uses the
  right register; links wrap at the end of local store; stopd reports 0x3FFF.
- The lv2 stop-and-signal services that resume at the next instruction
  (0x100/0x110/0x111) no longer end a function: the lift resumes there when
  spu_stop reports the stop serviced, and returns as before otherwise.
- --merge-chunks groups contiguous chunks into one C function
  (--max-group-insns), and --return-entries splits a bound at each call's
  return address.

live-draw: decode ZSTENCIL_CLEAR_VALUE by the zeta format (Z16)

Symptom: in the D3D12 live-draw backend a Z16 zeta cleared with 0xFFFF
(its far plane) ends up at depth 0.0000152, so every LESS or LEQUAL draw
into it fails.

Cause: the live-draw clear decoded every ZSTENCIL_CLEAR_VALUE as Z24S8
(depth24 << 8 | stencil8). For a Z16 zeta (SURFACE_FORMAT depth field 1)
the value is a bare depth16 in bits 0-15 with no stencil.

Change: decode by sf.depth_format, as the draw engine's clear does since
#235: Z16 = (value & 0xFFFF) / 65535 with stencil 0, Z24S8 unchanged. The
existing "value 0 clears to 1.0" behaviour is kept for both formats.

the shared harness live_draw_test_harness.h) clears colour and depth, then
draws a white quad at depth 0.5 with depth test LESS: Z16 0xFFFF and
0xA000 must show it, Z16 0x4000 must hide it, Z24S8 0xFFFFFF00 must show
it. Built with MinGW-w64 and run under Proton (vkd3d) with one test-only
local change that is not part of this commit (the depth-snapshot compute
shader's RWTexture2D::GetDimensions removed, which vkd3d-shader does not

live-draw: fragment depth export, and texel size of depth-snapshot reads

Symptom: a fragment program that writes depth (SHADER_CONTROL depth-export
bits) leaves the primitive's interpolated depth in the zeta, so a
full-screen pass that rebuilds a depth buffer writes the quad's constant
depth. Separately, a DEPTH24_D8 texture with texel (unnormalised)
coordinates that is smaller than the zeta it reads samples a stretched copy
of the whole zeta instead of its top-left corner.

Cause: the fragment-program decompiler ignored SHADER_CONTROL bits 1-3
(0xE, depth export) and never declared SV_Depth; the live-draw PSO keys
masked the control word with 0x40 only, so they could not tell the two
programs apart. A depth texture bound to a zeta snapshot reads that host
resource, which is as large as the largest pass that used the zeta, but the
unnormalised-coordinate divisor was the texture's own size.

Change:
- rsx_fp_decompiler.c: with depth export set, the output is a struct with
  `float depth : SV_Depth`, written from r1.z (always the fp32 register,
  whatever the colour export width), clamped to [0,1], NaN to 0.
- rsx_live_draw.c: both PSO keys include the depth-export bits (0x4E); a
  texel-addressed DEPTH24_D8 unit whose bind takes a zeta snapshot divides

c55ddaa4379c2897d55f337096cb23e0dd2a6c3d.message:
edat: take the klicensee the title passes to sceNpDrmIsAvailable[2]

Symptom: a free (license type 3) or disc-bound EDAT under a title-specific
klicensee fails to open with -6 ("needs a RIF key"), even though the title
supplies its key the way it does on hardware.

Cause: on hardware a title passes its own klicensee to sceNpDrmIsAvailable
or sceNpDrmIsAvailable2 before it opens such a file, and the kernel keeps it
for later opens. The runtime has neither call, so the key is lost, and the
EDAT reader only tries the built-in platform klicensees.

Change: sceNp.c implements sceNpDrmIsAvailable and sceNpDrmIsAvailable2;
both hand a non-NULL klicensee to edat_add_klicensee() (new, edat.h) and
return CELL_OK. edat.c keeps up to 16 such keys, ignores duplicates, and
tries them before the built-in ones. Each key is still checked against the
file's dev_hash (AES-CMAC under klic ^ NP_OMAC_KEY_2 over header bytes
0x00-0x5F, the same check for NPD versions 2-4) before it is used, and each
block hash is checked as before. A license type 3 file that no key verifies
now fails with a message that names sceNpDrmIsAvailable. Projects that read
the key some other way can call edat_add_klicensee() themselves.

Verification: tools/test_edat_guest_klicensee.py builds
libs/filesystem/tests/test_edat_guest_klicensee.c with sceNp.c. The test
writes a synthetic NPD v3 license-3 EDAT (made-up key, content id and data;
three blocks, the last partial) and checks: -6 before any key, -6 after
sceNpDrmIsAvailable2 with a key that does not verify dev_hash, then 0 with
every block hash verified and the plaintext matching after
sceNpDrmIsAvailable with the right key. The runner passes a scratch
directory as argv[1]. On master the fixture does not link (neither call
exists; without them the file stays at -6). With this change all checks

d0d67442f549faf07f8547adcb4fdc6e6dc74c08.message:
spu_channels: MFC engine table 8 -> 64 slots, and a full table is reported as an error

Symptom: intermittent stops where an SPU context waits forever on a DMA
tag that already completed. Killzone 3 holds eleven SPU contexts with an
MFC engine at once (policy-module contexts that keep their engine for as
long as their workload exists, plus SPU thread groups); the runtime prints
"more than 8 contexts hold an MFC engine at once; the rest share one".

Cause: the per-context engine table has SPU_MAX_CONTEXTS = 8 slots. Every
context past the eighth gets one shared fallback engine, where one
context's completion clears the tag bits another context is waiting on.
Eight is a thread group's worth, but a title can hold more contexts at
once than the machine has SPUs. The overflow was reported once, as a note.

Change: 64 slots (overridable with -DSPU_MAX_CONTEXTS). When the table is
still full, the shared engine stays as the last resort, but the runtime now
reports it as an error naming the table size, the context and the
consequence, at the first overflow lookup and again at 1000 and 1000000 so
it stays visible in a long log; s_mfc_overflow_lookups counts them. A
growable table can replace this later.

Verification: runtime/spu/tests/test_spu_mfc_slots.c (built as in the CI
workflows) keeps its 8-thread claim race over 32 rounds and adds: eleven
contexts held at once get eleven distinct engines and keep the state each
wrote; the table holds SPU_MAX_CONTEXTS contexts with no overflow; the next
context gets the overflow engine and the overflow is counted. With this
change 889 checks pass with gcc and clang, and the error line is printed
once. Against v0.14.0's spu_channels.c (a2c2010; the counter compiled as a
constant 0) 3 checks fail: the eleven contexts share engines, their state
is overwritten, and the overflow is not counted.

d9870123ea646d8a9a4ad4cd56342d5bd7c57546.message:
spu_channels: SMC micro-interpreter addresses lqa/stqa at I16 << 2

Symptom: a self-modifying SPU stub that saves and restores registers with
stqa/lqa (a job manager's interrupt save/restore stub, written into the
local store at runtime) stores every register at the wrong address and
overwrites unrelated local-store bytes, including the job's stack.

Cause: spu_smc_microstep computed the absolute local-store address of
lqa/stqa as I16 << 4. For the RI16 form the address is I16 << 2 (SPU ISA),
which is what spu_interp.c and the lifter already use, so every access went
4x too high and wrapped around the local store.

Change: use I16 << 2 in the micro-interpreter, masked to a quadword as
before.

Verification: tools/test_spu_smc_lqa_stqa.py builds the real
spu_smc_microstep with the SPU headers into a host program, writes a stub of
76 stqa (r0..r75 to 0x3F9C0..), a bi, 76 lqa back and a second bi into the
local store, and runs both halves through the micro-interpreter. With this
change all 76 registers land in their own slot, all 76 are restored, and no
local-store byte outside the save area changes. On v0.14.0 (a2c2010) no
register lands in its slot and 1198 bytes outside the save area change.

df3a7cbae234fb6701b6e1d1df2d3417b9e03a2a.message:
ppu_lifter: --chunks N cuts the source by guest address and rewrites only changed files

Symptom: any change to the lifter's input or to the lifter (a fix for one
opcode, one function's bounds) makes the build recompile nearly all of the
lifted source. For Killzone 3 (eight 600k-line chunks, 6.5-8 minutes and
2.5-4.4 GB of compiler memory each) that is 15-25 minutes per rebuild.

Cause: (1) chunks are cut every --chunk-lines emitted lines, so a change in
one function's line count moves every later cut point and changes the text of
every later chunk; (2) main() deletes the previous chunk set before writing,
so every file gets a new mtime even when its content is the same, and make or
ninja rebuild it.

Change:
- --chunks N (default 0 = off) cuts the source into N files by guest code
  bytes: chunk k holds the functions, in address order, of the range that
  carries the k-th N-th of the lifted bytes. That is a function of the
  function list alone, so the same functions always land in the same file. The
  function table goes to its own <source>_table.cpp, so a new function does
  not change the last chunk. A chunk over --chunk-lines lines prints a warning
  (MSVC's 16M-line limit).
- Every output file (header, chunks, table, the --single-file source) is
  written through write_if_changed: a temporary file and a rename, and only
  when the content differs, so unchanged files keep their mtime.
- Stale files of an earlier run (other cut points, the single-file source)
  are removed after writing instead of all files before.

How this relates to --chunk-lines (#216): --chunk-lines sets how large a
line-cut chunk may be (fewer lines per translation unit for hosts short on
memory) and stays the default mode; it now also profits from
write_if_changed. --chunks makes the cut points stable across relifts; with
it, --chunk-lines is only the warning threshold. Both can be used.

Verification: tools/test_ppu_lifter_chunks.py drives write_source_files on
200 synthetic functions of uneven guest size. On v0.14.0 (a2c2010): FAIL (
