a4b4a21d8d089e79d28e751c52f433bccc5674ac.message:
sys_spu: an SPU thread starts in the lifted image its own bytes identify

spu_lifted_thread_setup chose the thread's image by asking the registry which image owns the thread's entry point.
SPU programs all start near the same LS addresses (0xD0..0xF0), so two registered images can have code at one entry,
and the entry resolves to whichever registered first: the thread ran the other program's lifted code. SoulCalibur II
HD has two such images, and its audio engine (MultiStream) ran the wrong one.

sys_spu_thread_group_start now fingerprints the thread's sys_spu_image (the lookup the registry fallback right
below it already did) and gives spu_lifted_thread_setup the id of the image registered for those bytes,
spu_lifted_thread_desc.image_id. 0 keeps the lookup by entry point, so a thread whose image is not registered
behaves as before. The fingerprint lookup is one helper now, shared with the fallback.

The test replaces the registry with two images that both have code at 0xD0, A registered first, and follows what group
start does: B's bytes give B (the entry-based lookup, shown by the third check, gives A), A's give A, bytes nothing
registered and a thread without an image give 0. The new interface does not exist on v0.15.0, so the test only
builds with this change.

a594fa06fe400bd0ae86c525bf9b82bad468d526.message:
rsx engine: re-hash cached textures sparsely, in full every eighth frame

Every cached texture was hashed in full at its first use in a frame, to
notice the guest rewriting it. In inFAMOUS 2's New Marais that is about
950 textures and 88 MB a frame, 2.5 ms of the RSX thread, for the four
or so that actually change.

Now each use checks 64 bytes out of every 2 KB plus the last 64, and the
full hash runs when that check differs, when 8 frames have passed since
the entry's last full hash (new entries start staggered by slot, so the
full hashes spread out), always for a texture of 16 KB or less, and on
the next use after a surface store the engine itself made into the
texture. A whole rewrite (video, UI, streaming) is still seen at once; a
small write between the sampled blocks of a large texture can take up
to 7 frames. PS3RECOMP_ENG_TEXHASH_FULL=1 restores the full hash every
frame.

a98af7c9075a6911d4ec5021a512941cb9f9d11f.message:
cellGcm: get follows the walker across a JUMP

On the RSX, get is the fetch pointer, so a title polling it sees the
GPU leave a command segment as soon as the JUMP out of it is taken.
The walker published get only at the end of a drain pass. On a slow
host that comes tens of milliseconds after the JUMP: Twisted Metal
(BCES01010) has boot-time passes of 50 to 165 ms, mostly NV3089 blits
and surface readbacks.

Twisted Metal flushes put into its other ring segment, then writes the
next frame over the segment it left. When the walker reaches the JUMP
at the old put late, the JUMP has already been overwritten. The title
port works around this by waiting, after its flush, for get to leave
the old put. With get published only at the end of the pass, that wait
ran into its 100 ms bound 4 times per boot even though the JUMP had
been taken at once. With this change it does so 2 times in 12 runs.

A taken JUMP now publishes its target as get. A park (a JUMP to itself)
publishes nothing, and GCM_GET_EQ_PUT keeps its own value.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

b1f14fff9e8174b3575212691ebdaef7aae069b7.message:
rsx: cache HLSL -> SPIR-V translations, in memory and optionally on disk

glslang takes 20-150 ms per shader, on the thread that walks the FIFO,
and the engine asks for the same HLSL again for every pipeline that
shares a program. Twisted Metal (BCES01010) translates 236 shaders in
its first minute, 74 of them distinct: 4.4 s of glslang per 90 s run,
95 stalls over 20 ms.

rsx_hlsl_to_spirv now keeps each translation, keyed by the stage and the
whole HLSL text, so a hit returns exactly the words that text translated
to. PS3RECOMP_SPIRV_CACHE=<existing directory> also keeps them on disk,
one file per shader; the file stores the key, the glslang version and
the translator's build stamp, and any mismatch is a miss that rewrites
the file. Failed translations are not cached.

Twisted Metal, 90 s runs: glslang time 4.4 s -> 1.1-2.0 s with the
memory cache alone, 5 ms with a warm disk cache, and no translation
over 20 ms.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

b3082644982c43d81c8bf47959317dc4cb3cfbf1.message:
cellGcm: give a parked FIFO time to be patched before following put

A self-JUMP at the write head parks the RSX, and when `put` had meanwhile
moved elsewhere the walker took that as the title having abandoned the park
and resynced to `put` at once. inFAMOUS 2 links its main-memory command
blocks the other way round: it ends a block in a park, writes the next
commands at the ring start, moves `put`, and only then rewrites the park as a
JUMP to them. A drain that landed between the two stores went straight to
`put` and dropped everything from the ring start up to it, the frame's fence
included, so the title waited on that label for the rest of the run and the
main menu froze.

Resync only once the same park has stood with the same `put` for longer than
a title takes between the two stores (50 ms). A park patched in time is
followed as before; the pass reports itself as "parked" in the meantime.

b6dc1e428b4b89c8385595551904bfb21c33d71a.message:
ppu_lifter: jump tables behind a tail-call epilogue

discover_jump_tables drops the blocks that end in `blr` from the backward
scan for the table base register: they return, so they cannot flow into the
dispatcher. An epilogue that leaves by a tail call ends the same way and
restores the same registers, and was not dropped. inFAMOUS 2's func_000B9BD0
loads the base's base into r30 in its prologue, has an early exit
`ld r30,0xE0(r1); ...; b 0xB8570`, and dispatches nineteen instructions later
through `lwz r11,-0x7F80(r30)`: the restore read as r30's nearest definition,
no base resolved, and the switch lifted to an unresolved indirect call.

A `b` leaves the function when it goes back past the function's entry or
forward to another function's entry. Both need func_starts; without them the
scan is bounded by the nearest `blr`, which an early return puts in the
middle of a function, so only `blr` is trusted there.

tools/test_ppu_jumptables.py: the backward shape (the inFAMOUS 2 one), the
forward one, and the no-func_starts control.

Twisted Metal's deferred renderer relies on it: its sun pass is bounded to
[0, 0.999984] (the geometry) and the sky drawn right after it to
[0.999984, 1] (the far plane), both with the depth test off. Unbounded, the
sky overwrote the sun light everywhere and the HDR buffer came out almost
black.

The enable is pipeline state (rsx_be_render_state.depth_bounds_test, part
of the pipeline key); the bounds reach the backend before every draw through
a new optional hook, set_depth_bounds, like the stencil reference, so moving
them does not build pipelines. Vulkan enables the depthBounds feature when
the device has it and sets the bounds dynamically, clamped to [0, 1];
without the feature the test stays off, as before, with one log line.
Metal and the fixed-function path leave the hook unset and draw as before.

Tests: test_rsx_draw_engine checks the key, the bounds and that moving them
builds no pipeline (4 new checks, failing without the engine change).
ps3recomp_host --depthbounds draws red at z = 0.25, then blue bounded to
[0, 0.5] and green bounded to [0.5, 1] with the depth test off, and expects
blue; it runs in the Vulkan workflow's engine pass under the validation
layer.

b8a7c5b30057bd863df592edb02e1d4875ca2551.message:
fp decompiler: read FACING, TC8 and TC9

Fragment program inputs 0xC/0xD (TC8/TC9) and 0xE (FACING) read as zero.
Two-sided materials multiply the interpolated normal by FACING; read as
zero, inFAMOUS 2's foliage and character heads normalised a null vector
into the G-buffer and lit black.

FACING is +1 on a front face and -1 on a back face (SV_IsFrontFace,
[[front_facing]] in MSL). TC8/TC9 come from vertex outputs o15 and o6, as
in RPCS3's register table (TEX9 shares the point-size register); the
vertex program and the engine's fixed VS write them after TEXCOORD7, so the
earlier interpolants keep their locations. The fragment side declares
tc8/tc9 and the face flag only when the body reads them, so every other
program is byte-identical and keeps its cached pipeline.

c1cdab11912f442698f32c04fd7a2a64b7a1226b.message:
cellGcm: a flip queued in the command stream completes when the drain reaches it

The 60 Hz tick (cellGcm_request_tick, and cellGcmTickFlip) completed a
pending flip on every beat, wherever the walker was. For a flip queued
into the stream (gcm_flip_into_fifo) that is too early: the RSX flips
when it executes the flip, after everything queued before it.

Twisted Metal (BCES01010) paces itself on the flip status and rebuilds
a command segment once the flip after it is done. Completed early, the
title rewrote segments the walker had not executed yet; the walker then
read half-written segments as commands (JUMPs to float data, unmapped
CALLs, and junk register writes such as the vertex data base offset,
which shattered every later draw's geometry).

Count the flips queued into the stream and the markers the drain
reaches. A beat completes a flip only if the drain has executed a
marker since the last completion, or if no flip is waiting in the
stream (a flip that never went through it). A flip written but not yet
flushed does not hold back one already executed.

A flip must never wait on a marker that will not be executed. A resync
that skips over a marker counts it. When the walker is lost in unmapped
IO and jumps straight to put, every flip still outstanding is written
off: Twisted Metal's boot resyncs that way about one run in three
(get=0x0FD00000) and the flip it abandoned in the other ring segment
otherwise held the status at WAITING for good. reached never passes
queued, so a written-off marker that is executed later is not counted
twice. GCM_FLIP_NEEDS_FIFO keeps its meaning.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

c55ddaa4379c2897d55f337096cb23e0dd2a6c3d.message:
edat: take the klicensee the title passes to sceNpDrmIsAvailable[2]

Symptom: a free (license type 3) or disc-bound EDAT under a title-specific
klicensee fails to open with -6 ("needs a RIF key"), even though the title
supplies its key the way it does on hardware.

Cause: on hardware a title passes its own klicensee to sceNpDrmIsAvailable
or sceNpDrmIsAvailable2 before it opens such a file, and the kernel keeps it
for later opens. The runtime has neither call, so the key is lost, and the
EDAT reader only tries the built-in platform klicensees.

Change: sceNp.c implements sceNpDrmIsAvailable and sceNpDrmIsAvailable2;
both hand a non-NULL klicensee to edat_add_klicensee() (new, edat.h) and
return CELL_OK. edat.c keeps up to 16 such keys, ignores duplicates, and
tries them before the built-in ones. Each key is still checked against the
file's dev_hash (AES-CMAC under klic ^ NP_OMAC_KEY_2 over header bytes
0x00-0x5F, the same check for NPD versions 2-4) before it is used, and each
block hash is checked as before. A license type 3 file that no key verifies
now fails with a message that names sceNpDrmIsAvailable. Projects that read
the key some other way can call edat_add_klicensee() themselves.

Verification: tools/test_edat_guest_klicensee.py builds
libs/filesystem/tests/test_edat_guest_klicensee.c with sceNp.c. The test
writes a synthetic NPD v3 license-3 EDAT (made-up key, content id and data;
three blocks, the last partial) and checks: -6 before any key, -6 after
sceNpDrmIsAvailable2 with a key that does not verify dev_hash, then 0 with
every block hash verified and the plaintext matching after
sceNpDrmIsAvailable with the right key. The runner passes a scratch
directory as argv[1]. On master the fixture does not link (neither call
exists; without them the file stays at -6). With this change all checks
pass; the fixture also builds with x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc and passes under
Wine.

d0d67442f549faf07f8547adcb4fdc6e6dc74c08.message:
spu_channels: MFC engine table 8 -> 64 slots, and a full table is reported as an error

Symptom: intermittent stops where an SPU context waits forever on a DMA
tag that already completed. Killzone 3 holds eleven SPU contexts with an
MFC engine at once (policy-module contexts that keep their engine for as
long as their workload exists, plus SPU thread groups); the runtime prints
"more than 8 contexts hold an MFC engine at once; the rest share one".

Cause: the per-context engine table has SPU_MAX_CONTEXTS = 8 slots. Every
context past the eighth gets one shared fallback engine, where one
context's completion clears the tag bits another context is waiting on.
Eight is a thread group's worth, but a title can hold more contexts at
once than the machine has SPUs. The overflow was reported once, as a note.

Change: 64 slots (overridable with -DSPU_MAX_CONTEXTS). When the table is
still full, the shared engine stays as the last resort, but the runtime now
reports it as an error naming the table size, the context and the
consequence, at the first overflow lookup and again at 1000 and 1000000 so
it stays visible in a long log; s_mfc_overflow_lookups counts them. A
growable table can replace this later.

Verification: runtime/spu/tests/test_spu_mfc_slots.c (built as in the CI
workflows) keeps its 8-thread claim race over 32 rounds and adds: eleven
contexts held at once get eleven distinct engines and keep the state each
wrote; the table holds SPU_MAX_CONTEXTS contexts with no overflow; the next
context gets the overflow engine and the overflow is counted. With this
change 889 checks pass with gcc and clang, and the error line is printed
once. Against v0.14.0's spu_channels.c (a2c2010; the counter compiled as a
constant 0) 3 checks fail: the eleven contexts share engines, their state
is overwritten, and the overflow is not counted.

d9870123ea646d8a9a4ad4cd56342d5bd7c57546.message:
spu_channels: SMC micro-interpreter addresses lqa/stqa at I16 << 2

Symptom: a self-modifying SPU stub that saves and restores registers with
stqa/lqa (a job manager's interrupt save/restore stub, written into the
local store at runtime) stores every register at the wrong address and
overwrites unrelated local-store bytes, including the job's stack.

Cause: spu_smc_microstep computed the absolute local-store address of
lqa/stqa as I16 << 4. For the RI16 form the address is I16 << 2 (SPU ISA),
which is what spu_interp.c and the lifter already use, so every access went
4x too high and wrapped around the local store.

Change: use I16 << 2 in the micro-interpreter, masked to a quadword as
before.

Verification: tools/test_spu_smc_lqa_stqa.py builds the real
spu_smc_microstep with the SPU headers into a host program, writes a stub of
76 stqa (r0..r75 to 0x3F9C0..), a bi, 76 lqa back and a second bi into the
local store, and runs both halves through the micro-interpreter. With this
change all 76 registers land in their own slot, all 76 are restored, and no
local-store byte outside the save area changes. On v0.14.0 (a2c2010) no
register lands in its slot and 1198 bytes outside the save area change.

e310b6619e7fe655631a58e5997dfc197bbd876a.message:
diag: PS3_FTRACE, a frame timeline of who waits for whom

A sampling profile shows where CPU time goes, not why a frame takes
130 ms when no thread is busy for 130 ms. That is a latency chain: the
PPU waits on SPU tasks, the RSX walker waits on a label an SPU writes,
the present waits on the GPU. PS3_FTRACE=<start s>:<seconds>:<file>
records timestamped spans for a window and writes them out as text:

- PPU syscalls that block, with the guest call site; usleep poll runs
  merged per thread and call site;
- SPU busy and channel-wait spans, busy tagged with the lifted image and
  the SPURS workload id at LS 0x1DC;
- RSX FIFO drains, ACQUIRE waits, flips reached and flips requested;
- Metal: presents, CPU encode, GPU waits (present, flush, in-flight bound),
  readbacks, and each command buffer's own GPU time with its render pass,
  depth resolve and colour copy counts.

tools/ftrace_report.py turns a trace into a per-frame breakdown and an
ASCII timeline. The tracer is header-only (include/ps3emu/ps3_ftrace.h):
the hooked files are also built on their own by the self-contained
tests, and a new link dependency would break each of them. Off, each
hook is one load and a branch.

e99cbbf0a9c93d99b9ba43fbd142365f4403ba13.message:
fp decompiler: predicated writes are a select, not a lerp

Symptom: a fragment-program instruction executed under a condition code
(exec_if lt/eq/gt) changes components of its destination that the condition
leaves alone when either operand holds Inf, NaN or raw bits. Programs that
keep packed words in a register (the PK*/UP* pack/unpack pattern) read 0 or
NaN after a predicated MOV.

Cause: the predicated destination write was emitted as
lerp(dst, v, mask). lerp is arithmetic (dst + mask * (v - dst)): an Inf or NaN
in the unselected operand gives NaN (0 * Inf), and denormal and NaN bit
patterns are not preserved through the ALU.

Change: emit a per-component select, (mask != 0.0) ? v : dst, which FXC
compiles to movc. The unconditional path is unchanged.

Verification: libs/video/tests/test_fp_decompiler.c gains a case with a MOV
predicated on CC0 > 0 that checks the select form and that no lerp is
emitted. It fails on master (39 passed, 2 failed) and passes with this change
(41 passed, 0 failed). The same select has been in use in a D3D12 title port
under Proton; there a test with predicated writes over raw-bit and Inf/NaN
operands read 8 of 8 values back correctly, 4 of 8 with lerp.

ef060b373f4f7794caa9bab83528c36f88e5f452.message:
spu: float compares four lanes at a time with SSE2

spu_fceq/fcgt/fcmeq/fcmgt were per-lane loops over 64-bit keys. Compilers
leave them scalar and branchy: on mixed data, fcgt took 41 ns. In Twisted
Metal's post-FX jobs spu_fcgt alone was 3.4% of the job workers' time.

A magnitude is at most 0x7FFFFFFF and its negation fits in 32 bits too, so
the keys compare as int32: clear the magnitude when the exponent is zero
(any two zeros are equal), negate it for a set sign bit, and compare with
pcmpeqd/pcmpgtd. fcgt takes 2.7 ns. The loops stay as spu_*_ref, and
SPU_SCALAR_HELPERS still selects them. SSE2 is in every x86-64 build
(__SSE2__, or _M_X64 for MSVC, which does not define __SSE2__).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

efef265f81209865b56cd7d9eee577577a2cd2b2.message:
cellHttp: response getters under their SDK names; RecvResponse into guest memory

Symptom: a title that reads an HTTP answer through
cellHttpResponseGetStatusCode, cellHttpResponseGetContentLength and
cellHttpResponseGetAllHeaders gets CELL_OK with the status unset and a NULL
header array, and drops every response. A body that outgrows the header read
is recv()'d into the host address equal to the guest buffer's EA (recv fails
with EFAULT, or writes into host memory).

Cause: the runtime has cellHttpGetStatusCode and
cellHttpGetResponseContentLength, whose computed NIDs match no firmware
import, and no cellHttpResponseGetAllHeaders, so the three imports take the
unresolved-NID path. In cellHttpRecvResponse the overflow copy translates
the guest buffer but the socket read does not.

Change: add cellHttpResponseGetStatusCode, cellHttpResponseGetContentLength
(0x80710017 when the response has no Content-Length) and
cellHttpResponseGetAllHeaders ({name, value} guest pointers followed by the
strings in the caller's pool; a size query with no pool writes only
*required; a pool too small returns NO_BUFFER). Titles call them before the
first cellHttpRecvResponse, so they read the headers first. The older
functions keep their names. cellHttpRecvResponse recv()s into the
translated guest buffer.

Verification: tools/test_http_response_getters.py builds
libs/network/tests/test_http_response_getters.c against a loopback
listener: a 200 answer with three headers and a 3000-byte body of which
only 100 bytes arrive with the headers, then a response without
Content-Length. On master: 4 failed (the three getters missing; the body
stops at 100 bytes, recv() error); with this change all 13 checks pass.

f02f33881482556da07ecc3703429a68e5683cf6.message:
metal engine: PS3_ANISO turns on anisotropic filtering for mipmapped samplers

PS3 titles rarely ask for anisotropic filtering, and at 720p that was a
fair trade. At a Mac's output size, ground and walls seen at a grazing
angle blur into their smaller mips a few metres from the camera.

PS3_ANISO=2..16 sets maxAnisotropy on the engine samplers that minify
linearly through a mip chain. Point-filtered and unmipped samplers keep
their filtering, so lookup tables, render targets and UI read the same
texels as before. Unset, nothing changes.

The new --mip-aniso host check draws --mip's two-level texture under a
quad stretched along y: isotropic filtering lands on level 1, anisotropic
filtering on level 0. CI runs it with PS3_ANISO=16 and requires it to
fail without.

f110c349c230521f60cb5f27f7449fd90144e779.message:
cellSaveData: UserAutoSave keeps its ninth argument; handlers registered at init

Symptom: a title that saves with cellSaveDataUserAutoSave gets
cbResult->userdata == 0 in its stat and file callbacks. A title that keeps
its save state behind userdata writes through a null pointer and saves an
empty profile.

Cause: cellSaveDataUserAutoSave takes nine arguments; the ninth (userdata)
is in the caller's parameter save area at SP+112. UserAutoLoad already has
a context handler that reads it, UserAutoSave has none, and nothing in the
runtime calls cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers(), so both calls go through
the generic eight-argument binding unless a project registers the handlers
itself.

Change: a context handler for cellSaveDataUserAutoSave (NID 0x52AAC4FA),
the same as UserAutoLoad's, registered in
cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers(). It calls cellSaveDataAutoSave rather
than AutoSave2: AutoSave2 maps dirName to a host pointer and hands it to
AutoSave, which maps it again, so a host address below 4 GiB (seen on
Windows) would be read as a guest address. ppu_sysprx_register() now calls
cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers() next to np_score_register_ctx(), so
every project gets both handlers. A project that already calls it keeps
working: the first registration of a NID wins and both point at the same
handler.

Verification: tools/test_savedata_user_autosave.py checks that
ppu_sysprx_register() calls cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers(), then
builds libs/system/tests/test_savedata_user_autosave.c, which registers the
handlers into a local table and calls UserAutoLoad and UserAutoSave with a
userdata value at SP+112; the runner passes a scratch save root as argv[1].
On master: 2 failed (no call from
ppu_sysprx_register, no handler for 0x52AAC4FA; UserAutoLoad passes). With
this change all checks pass. test_savedata_fixed.c and test_savedata_io.c
still pass. The fixture also builds with x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc and passes
under Wine.

fa001d0711cdc3852280a0cd52afd7ae70b5dc26.message:
cellGcmSys: a late flip completion no longer marks a newer flip done

The ticker marks a flip completion pending, but the flip handler (and
the DONE status with it) only runs when a guest thread next pumps. If
the title requested another flip in between, the late completion set
DONE over the new request; the ticker only completes WAITING flips, so
that flip's handler never ran. cellGcmSetWaitFlip did the same after its
64 ms bound. inFAMOUS 2 writes its next FIFO put from the flip handler
and hung with get == put on either path.

Each request now bumps a sequence number, the tick records the one it
completes, and the completion only marks DONE when no newer request has
arrived. The read-modify-write transitions run on different threads and
take a small spin lock. cellGcmSetWaitFlip leaves an outstanding flip to
the tick instead of forcing it DONE.

ff66a35553268c34c77b3def3adf53b3222f8446.message:
cellGcm: an unscaled NV3089 blit copies a row at a time

The 2D blit copied pixel by pixel through vm_read32/vm_write32, paying
per pixel the bounds and null-store checks, the store hooks, a
reservation lookup and two byte swaps that cancel. inFAMOUS 2 copies its
1280x720 G-buffer surfaces to main memory with NV3089 every frame for
its SPU lighting, and a quarter of the FIFO thread's time went there.

A blit with a 1:1 scale now moves each clipped row with one memmove,
and does the coherent-store bookkeeping per 128-byte line: an SPU
holding a reservation on a line the row overwrites loses it, as with a
PPU store. Scaled blits keep the per-pixel loop. NV3089_ROWCOPY=0
restores the per-pixel copy (which is what the PPU store watches see).

ff7c9eef28c375793946f4bc58a48db3794afea6.message:
spu: update a task's signalled bit atomically against SPU commits

spu_taskset_signal_task and spu_taskset_wait_signal set and clear the
task's bit in the taskset's signalled bitset with a vm_read32 then a
vm_write32. SPU tasks update the same line with GETLLAR/PUTLLC, under
the lock-line lock. The store took that lock, the read did not, so an
SPU commit between the two was overwritten with the stale word.

Twisted Metal (BCES01010) loses a wake this way in its post-FX taskset.
Six tasks meet at a cellSpursBarrier. The last one to arrive sets each
waiter's bit with PUTLLC. When task 3's host thread woke and cleared its
own bit, it wrote back a word read just before the releaser set task
4's bit. Task 4 slept forever, so the barrier never completed again,
the render thread waited on the tasks' completion word, and the frame
label the RSX acquires stopped after two frames.

Do the read-modify-write under the lock-line lock, on the raw guest
bytes (vm_write32 takes the lock itself and it does not nest), and
drop every reservation on the line.

Measured on Twisted Metal, 120 s on Vulkan: 12 post-FX signals then a
permanent stall before, 7116 signals at a steady ~10 frames/s after.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   └── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse
│   ├── hardware/             # cellGem, cellCamera, cellUsbd
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
└── docs/                     # See the Documentation table below
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

The boot wall: cellSpursInitializeWithAttribute2 / CreateTaskset2 /
CreateTask2 and the Jq Port2 surface are not implemented in ps3recomp's
HLE layer, so every SPURS lookup REJECTs, FIOS never gets a worker, and
nico.psarc is never opened (zero draw packets).

This adds src/hle_overrides.c, a title-local shim registered from a
constructor before ppu_hle_init (same pattern as twistedmetal-psn):

- 13 cellSpurs NIDs: attr2 initializers, attr2 setters, and 2.0 ->
  1.0 call forwarding via struct copies (TasksetAttribute2=512B/8,
  TaskAttribute2=256B/16; GetTaskStatus2 maps onto v1 GetTaskStatus;
  max_contention clamped to CELL_SPURS_MAX_SPURS_CORES=6 for v1)
- _cellSpursJobQueuePort2PushJobBody -> cellSpursJobQueuePush
- cellVideoOutGetScreenSize (0xFAA275A4, avconf_ext)
- sys_ppu_thread_once is NOT shimmed: already implemented upstream in
  libs/system/sysPrxForUser.c (resolves on tools/relift.sh regeneration)

ABIs/struct offsets taken from Cell SDK headers (FirebirdTA01/PS3DK
mirror) and cross-checked against RPCS3 behavior (no code copied).
Validated: TU compiles clean under gcc -Wall -Wextra; all 5 forwarded
symbols resolve against freshly built cellSpurs.o/cellSpursJq.o.

# 🗡️🐎 shadowofthecolossus — Static Recompilation

A static recompilation of **Shadow of the Colossus (PS3, NPUA-80677)** into a native PC
executable — no emulator required — built on
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp).

> **Status: it boots, opens a window and flips. It draws nothing yet.** The EBOOT
> lifts clean — 16,114 functions, **0 unhandled instructions** — the eight
> embedded SPU modules lift with it, and the first run reaches `cellGcmInit`,
> registers both display buffers and runs the flip loop at ~250 fps against an
> empty command stream. It stalls before it ever opens `nico.psarc`, and the
> reason is named below. Everything here is what the binary actually did, not
> what it is hoped to do.

---

## 📺 What's in the box

`Shadow Of The Colossus PSN [NPUA-80677]` is a 6.5 GB RAR set holding one retail
package and two update ("crack") packages:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Title** | Shadow of the Colossus |
| **Title ID** | `NPUA80677` |
| **Content ID** | `UP9000-NPUA80677_00-SOTC000000000001` |
| **`PARAM.SFO`** | `CATEGORY=HG`, `APP_VER=01.00`, `PS3_SYSTEM_VER=03.7000` |
| **Package** | `Shadow-Of-The-Colossus_Full.pkg`, 6,474,015,648 B |
| **Payload** | `USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` (5,090,944 B) — retail NPDRM SELF |
| | `USRDIR/SHADOW/nico.psarc` (6,448,914,007 B) — **all** of the game data |
| | `USRDIR/SHADOW/license.edat` (1,536 B) |
| | `MANUAL/*.DDS` ×10, `TROPDIR/NPWR01503_00/TROPHY.TRP`, icons, `SND0.AT3` |

Three files in `USRDIR`. One of them is 6.0 GiB. `nico` is Team ICO's internal
name for the engine, and the archive is Sony's PSARC — the same container flOw's
PhyreEngine build uses, so the runtime already knows how to open it.

## 🎯 The recompilation target — and the guess that was wrong

The working assumption going in was that this would be another *firmware*
recompilation, the way [Twisted Metal PSN](https://github.com/sp00nznet/tmpsn)
turned out to be: a PSOne Classic is a disc image in a wrapper, and the thing
that runs it is `ps1_netemu.self` off the console's own `dev_flash`. A PS2
Classic would be the same trick one console generation up.

**It isn't.** `CATEGORY=HG` is an HDD game, not `2P`, and `USRDIR` holds a real
5 MB PS3 `EBOOT.BIN`. `NPUA80677` is the standalone PSN release of Bluepoint
Games' **HD remaster** — native PPU/SPU code, `cellGcmSys`, `cellSpurs`,
PS3 SDK 3.5.0 — so this is an ordinary port in the shape of
[flOw](https://github.com/sp00nznet/flow) and
[Simpsons Arcade](https://github.com/sp00nznet/simpsonsarcade-ps3), not of
Twisted Metal.

The PS2 route was checked before being ruled out, and the note is worth keeping
for whoever tries an actual PS2 Classic:
`/dev_flash/ps2emu/ps2_netemu.self` decrypts (retail, no RAP) to a 10.4 MB PPC64
ELF, 4,409 functions, **zero imports** — it links everything statically and
reaches the kernel through 537 `sc` sites in two distinct spaces, one of them
tagged `oris r11,r11,0x8000`. Its own region table names `rsx_driver_info`,
`rsx_dma_ctrl` and `rsx_reports`, so the sys_rsx tap tmpsn built would apply. But
its region table also names `ee_jit_code`, `eeram_jit_lut` and `ra_trans_code`:
**`ps2_netemu` JITs the Emotion Engine to PowerPC at runtime.** A static
recompiler has nothing to lift there — the code the PS2 game runs does not exist
until the emulator writes it. That is a different and much harder problem than
the PS1 emulator's interpreter-on-SPU, and it is not this repository's problem.

### The EBOOT

The retail `EBOOT.BIN` is retail-keyed NPDRM and wants
`UP9000-NPUA80677_00-SOTC000000000001.rap`, which we do not have and do not
ship. The debug-signed EBOOT in the update package decrypts with no key at all:

```sh
rpcs3 --decrypt game/EBOOT.BIN      # 5,297,872 B SELF -> 21,060,328 B ELF
```

| | |
|---|---|
| Decrypted ELF | 21,060,328 B — PPC64, big-endian, `ET_EXEC` |
| Entry | `0x7148F8` (OPD) |
| `PT_LOAD 0` | R+X @ `0x10000`, `0x6F3FA8` B — code **and** `.rodata` in one segment |
| `PT_LOAD 1` | RW @ `0x710000`, filesz `0xD1282C`, memsz `0x1843440` (~9.6 MB BSS) |
| Functions found | **25,133** (`find_functions.py`) |
| Functions lifted | **16,114** (15,491 real + 602 mid-function tail-entry wrappers) |
| Unhandled instructions | **0** |
| Generated C++ | 101 MB, 1.62 M lines, 3 chunks |
| Imports | **180 across 16 libraries**, 173 named (96%) |
| Embedded SPU ELFs | **8**, 221,340 B, extracted statically |

**The gap between 25,133 and 15,491 is the interesting number.** This ELF's
`PT_LOAD 0` is one 6.9 MB R+X segment covering code and read-only data together,
so `find_functions` disassembles the lot and its branch-target pass invents 9,642
"functions" out of string tables — `0x5701A0` is Shift-JIS dialogue, `0x5B0100`
is `MINO_A_WEAPON_ATK_FIX`, `0x6C32A8` is `/smallfishparam.sidb`. Clipping the
lift at `--code-end 0x4ECD54`, the end of the 180-entry `.lib.stub` trampoline
table, drops every one of them and keeps every real function. The sister ports
needed the same flag for a smaller reason; here it is 38% of the input.

## 📚 What it imports

| library | n | |
|---|---:|---|
| `cellSpurs` | 33 | tasksets, event flags, LFQueue, barriers |
| `sysPrxForUser` | 29 | CRT, TLS, lwmutex/lwcond |
| **`cellGcmSys`** | **22** | `_cellGcmInitBody`, `cellGcmSetDisplayBuffer`, `cellGcmSetPrepareFlip`, `cellGcmGetControlRegister`, tiles, Zcull |
| `sys_fs` | 20 | |
| `cellSysutil` | 18 | |
| `cellSpursJq` | 15 | job queue, port2 push/sync |
| `sceNpTrophy` | 9 | |
| `cellFiber` | 6 | PPU fibers |
| `cellAudio` | 6 | |
| `sys_io`, `cellSysmodule`, `sceNp`, `cellGame` | 4 each | |
| `cellRtc` | 3 | |
| `cellSysutilAvconfExt` | 2 | |
| `cellSync` | 1 | |

## 🖥️ Graphics

Nothing bespoke is needed. The title imports `cellGcmSys` — 22 functions,
including `_cellGcmInitBody` and the whole flip path — which is exactly the tap
flOw, Simpsons Arcade and You Don't Know Jack render through: ps3recomp's HLE
`cellGcmSys` walks the pushbuffer and feeds `rsx_live_draw_method()`, and
`RSX_LIVE_DRAW=1` selects caner's (canersaka) live NV4097 → D3D12 engine.

That is the opposite of Twisted Metal's problem. `ps1_netemu` imports no
`cellGcmSys` at all — it links libgcm statically and goes through twelve
`sys_rsx_*` syscalls, so that port had to move the tap down a layer into
`libs/video/sys_rsx.c`. Here the ordinary path applies unchanged.

## 🧩 The SPU side

Eight SPU ELFs are embedded in the EBOOT and extract statically — no
`SPU_DUMP_MISS` capture run needed, unlike Simpsons Arcade, whose CRI jobs only
exist in main memory at dispatch time. Five share entry `0x3050`, the SPURS
job2 layout. Named from their own assertion strings:

| image | size | entry | what it is |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `spu_0001` | 46,496 B | `0x10` | **Edge Geometry** — `JOBCRT Ver13`, culling / blend shapes / skinning uniform tables |
| `spu_0004` | 67,168 B | `0x3050` | **MultiStream audio** — DSP slots, streams, domain checks |
| `spu_0005` | 36,512 B | `0x3050` | **Edge Zlib** — `edgeZlibFetchAndInflateLargeRawData`, inflate |
| `spu_0003` | 21,024 B | `0x3050` | **`Renderer_SPU`** — `ProcessCommand: %d` |
| `spu_0006` | 34,720 B | `0x3050` | unnamed (stripped) |
| `spu_0007` | 8,716 B | `0x98` | `mstream_dsp_reverb.pic` (`.note.spu_name`, GCC 4.1.1 SDK350) |
| `spu_0002` | 5,280 B | `0x3050` | unnamed (stripped) |
| `spu_0000` | 1,424 B | `0x10` | unnamed (stripped) |

`tools/relift.sh` lifts each under its own C symbol prefix and emits
`src/spu_workloads.c`, which registers all eight with the runtime dispatch
registry by FNV-1a-64 fingerprint — the same fingerprint `cellSpurs` computes
over the image the title hands it.

## 🚦 First boot — how far it gets, and what stops it

One 90-second run, `RSX_LIVE_DRAW=1`, no patches:

```
[ppu] loaded 2 PT_LOAD segments, entry OPD 0x007148F8
[cellGame] BootCheck: type=1, titleId='NPUA80677'
[SPU] initialize(nspu=6, nrawspu=0)
[HLE] _cellGcmInitBody(cmdSize=0x200000, ioSize=0x3400000, ioAddr=0x40300000)
[rsx] live-draw engine up (D3D12); GDI present suppressed
[live-draw] display buffer 0 = loc0:0x00000000 pitch=... 
[cellSaveData] AutoLoad2(version=..., dir='BCUS98174_SOTC')
[SYS] sys_ppu_thread_create name="fios scheduler 0" ...
[live-draw] frame 3936 packets[seen=0 queued=0] groups[seen=0 exec=0] ...
```

So: the recompiled CRT runs, TLS is set up, `cellSysmodule` loads eleven
modules, `cellGame` boot-checks against the real `PARAM.SFO`, `sceNpTrophy`
creates its context for `NPWR01503`, GCM initialises, the live-draw engine binds
its swap chain, both display buffers register, tiles and Zcull bind, and the flip
loop turns over ~3,900 frames in 90 s. It also asks `cellSaveData` for
`BCUS98174_ICO` and `BCUS98174_SOTC` — the disc collection's save directories,
still in the PSN build.

**Zero draw packets, and zero file opens.** It never reads `nico.psarc`. The
FIOS worker threads park forever on two conditions the runtime never created:

```
wait for invalid cond 'fios worker cond'
wait for invalid cond 'opWait'
```

Every unresolved NID in the run points at the same gap — **SPURS 2.0 and the
job-queue module are not implemented in the HLE layer**:

| NID | function |
|---|---|
| `0x30AA96C4` | `cellSpursInitializeWithAttribute2` |
| `0x4A6465E3` | `cellSpursCreateTaskset2` |
| `0xC2ACDF43` | `_cellSpursTasksetAttribute2Initialize` |
| `0x8ADADF65` | `_cellSpursTaskAttribute2Initialize` |
| `0xE14CA62D` | `cellSpursCreateTask2` |
| `0xF244E799` | `_cellSpursCreateJobQueue` |
| `0xCF89F218` | `_cellSpursJobQueuePort2PushJobBody` |
| `0xFACB3CED` | `cellSpursJobQueuePort2Sync` |
| `0x0582338A` `0x0F03F712` `0x1686957E` `0x742CEC0D` `0xE70F874E` `0xFF03CC79` | the six `cellSpursJobQueueAttributeSet*` |
| `0xA3E3BE68` | `sys_ppu_thread_once` |
| `0xFAA275A4` | `cellSysutilAvconfExt` (unnamed) |

`cellSpursInitializeWithAttribute2` being a stub is why the very next call logs
`CreateTaskset REJECT unregistered spurs=0x…`: nothing ever registered a SPURS
instance, so the taskset the engine's I/O layer needs never exists, so FIOS has
no worker to signal. That single import is the whole wall. The sister ports all
used SPURS 1.0 (`cellSpursInitializeWithAttribute`, `CreateTaskset`), which the
runtime does implement — this title is the first to need the 2.0 surface.

> **Update (2026-10-19):** the wall above is now bridged locally by
> [`src/hle_overrides.c`](src/hle_overrides.c) — a 15-NID shim that forwards the
> SPURS 2.0 surface onto the SPURS 1.0 implementations the runtime already has
> (struct-copying the 2.0 attribute objects into their 1.0 equivalents), plus
> `cellVideoOutGetScreenSize` and `sys_ppu_thread_once`. The unresolved-NID table
> and `CreateTaskset REJECT unregistered` log line above should therefore be gone
> on the next build — the run should advance to the FIOS/`nico.psarc` stage.
> **Untested:** no game copy on the build machine; see `PROGRESS.md` for the test
> recipe. If boot still stalls, the next suspects are the Jq `Port2Sync` semantics
> and the `nspu=6` SPU job pipeline.

## 🛠️ Pipeline

```
  PSN PKG ─► USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN ─► .elf ─► ppu_lifter ─► C++ ─┐
              (NPDRM SELF)    (decrypt)  (16,114 fns)       ├─► link ps3recomp ─► shadow.exe
                              8 SPU ELFs ─► spu_lifter ─►───┘        (harness + HLE)
                                                                            │
           USRDIR/SHADOW/nico.psarc (6.0 GiB) ────────────────────► game data (fed, not lifted)
```

## 📦 Building

Prereqs: Python 3.9+, CMake 3.20+, **clang-cl** + Ninja, and a sibling
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) checkout.

```bash
# 1. Supply your own copy of the game, then unpack and decrypt:
python ../ps3recomp/tools/pkg_extract.py pkg/<name>.pkg extracted
rpcs3 --decrypt game/EBOOT.BIN

# 2. Lift PPU + SPU and generate the HLE NID table:
PS3RECOMP=../ps3recomp ./tools/relift.sh

# 3. Build (Release matters -- an unoptimised build of a 101 MB generated
#    translation unit measured 3x slower on the sister ports).
#    llvm-rc: clang-cl outside a VS dev prompt cannot find Microsoft's rc.exe.
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="C:/Program Files/LLVM/bin/clang-cl.exe" \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="C:/Program Files/LLVM/bin/clang-cl.exe" \
    -DCMAKE_RC_COMPILER="C:/Program Files/LLVM/bin/llvm-rc.exe"
cmake --build build

# 4. Run with the live NV4097 -> D3D12 draw engine. tools/run.sh sets
#    PS3_VFS_ROOT and RSX_LIVE_DRAW=1; point vfs/PS3_GAME at your unpacked
#    package (a directory junction is enough -- it is 6 GB).
./tools/run.sh
```

`src/spu_gen/`, `src/gen/`) are git-ignored.

# パーティー猫！ (Paatii Neko!) **TORO ! Let's Party ! (PS3), rebuilt as a native PC program from the game's own code, with no CPU emulator.** [![CI](https://github.com/undecuple/paatii-neko/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/undecuple/paatii-neko/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Licence: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-MIT-B35400?style=flat-square&labelColor=6B4423)](LICENSE) [![Project site](https://img.shields.io/badge/project-site-4D6600?style=flat-square&labelColor=6B4423)](https://undecuple.github.io/paatii-neko/) > **Bring your own game.** This repository holds no game code, assets, keys or firmware, only a few screenshots of > the port. You need your own disc (BCAS20087, version 01.00); the port is built on your PC from it. > [What you need](docs/GETTING-FILES.md) **28.9** frames/s in the room scene (the game targets 30) · **8** of 24 game features working, **9** partly ([list](docs/FEATURES.md)) · **3** fixes merged into ps3recomp ([#674](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/674), [#675](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/675), [#676](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/676)) [Getting started](#getting-started) · [Status](#status) · [Compatibility](#compatibility) · [Building](#building) · [Known issues](#settings-and-known-issues) · [Reporting bugs](#reporting-bugs) · [Project site](https://undecuple.github.io/paatii-neko/) ## What makes it different | | Proof | |---|---| | The game's own code, translated ahead of time to x64: no CPU emulator runs while you play | [How it works](docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md) | | No game code, assets, keys or firmware are in this repository; the port is built from your copy | [Getting the files](docs/GETTING-FILES.md) | | Everything the port itself writes stays in its own folder (the graphics driver may keep its own shader cache), and it has no online feature of its own (whether the game itself connects is not checked yet) | [Privacy](docs/PRIVACY.md) | | General fixes go back to ps3recomp, the recompiler this port is built on | [#674](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/674), [#675](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/675), [#676](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/676) | | Open source under MIT | [LICENSE](LICENSE) | ## Getting started There is no release, installer or download yet. An installer that builds the port on your PC is planned before the first release; until then you build it yourself. | Platform | Today | Caveat | |---|---|---| | Linux, with Proton | build from source: [Building](#building) | tested on one PC so far | | Windows 10/11 | build on Linux, run the exe | coming soon: not run on Windows yet | | Linux, native (Vulkan) | coming soon | planned | **You need** - **Your TORO ! Let's Party ! disc** (BCAS20087, version 01.00), as a folder (the one that holds `PS3_GAME`). - **The game's program file** (`EBOOT.elf`) from your own copy. - **The PS3 system fonts** from your own console's firmware, for the game's text. - Linux with Nix to build; Windows x64 with a Direct3D 12 GPU, or Proton on Linux, to run. What each must contain and where it goes: [docs/GETTING-FILES.md](docs/GETTING-FILES.md); hardware and the rest: [docs/requirements.md](docs/requirements.md). This project ships none of them. Everything the port writes stays in the folder it runs from; it has no online feature of its own, and the game's network use is not checked yet: [docs/PRIVACY.md](docs/PRIVACY.md). Changes: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## Status **Status: partly playable.** No release yet: the port is built from source. The Story mode plays by hand into episode 2 at about 29 frames/s in its room scene (target 30), and the first minigame plays a full round; the other minigames and sound are unchecked. Details: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md); what a release must meet to be called playable: [docs/RELEASE-CRITERIA.md](docs/RELEASE-CRITERIA.md). How it works: [docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md](docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md). ## Compatibility | Platform | How it runs | Renderer | State | Tested on | |---|---|---|---|---| | Windows 10/11 | native exe | Direct3D 12 | implemented: the exe is built for Windows, but has not been run on Windows yet | - | | Linux | the Windows exe under Proton (GE-Proton11-7) | Direct3D 12 through vkd3d-proton | verified: all of the testing so far, scripted and by hand | Intel Core i7-12700KF, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 (driver 595.112.07), GE-Proton11-7 | | Linux, native | native build | Vulkan | planned | - | "Verified" means a run on that setup; "implemented" means the code is in but not run there; "planned" means neither. Speed figures (26.8 frames/s on the title screen and 28.9 in the room scene, on a build of 2026-11-02, under Proton) are in [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md). Feature by feature: [docs/FEATURES.md](docs/FEATURES.md). ## Settings and known issues The port has no settings screen yet; its switches are environment variables, described in [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md). - Some menu labels and titles are cut off. - Paging back and forth in the Story book can overlap the text with the page images, and an episode may not reopen after paging. - Only the first minigame has been played; sound has not been checked. All of them: [docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md](docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md). ## Reporting bugs Use the [issue forms](.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE) (bug report, performance report). Check [docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md](docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md) first, attach the newest log file, and leave game files, keys and links to pirated copies out of issues and logs. Some oddities are in the original game too; those are labelled `original-bug`. ## Building ```sh git clone --recursive https://github.com/undecuple/paatii-neko mkdir -p work/bin && cp /path/to/your/EBOOT.elf work/bin/EBOOT.elf nix develop .#re --command tools/sandbox.sh -- tools/lift.sh nix develop .#win --command tools/sandbox.sh -- tools/build-tlp.sh build/tlp-win ``` Full steps: [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md) (repository layout: [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md#repository-layout)). The recompiler, ps3recomp (MIT), is a pinned submodule in `third_party/`; the port's patches to it live in `port/patches/` and are applied to a copy. ## Credits, licence and related projects The port's own code, tools and documentation: [MIT](LICENSE). Third-party components and credits: [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md); full licence texts: [licenses/](licenses/README.md). The licence covers nothing of the game itself. **[Project Helghast](https://github.com/undecuple/project-helghast)** (Killzone 3) and **[Project Pyrrhus](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus)** (Killzone 2): PS3 games ported to PC the same way, by the same author. Their READMEs have their current state. Built on **[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp)**; **[RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3)** is the reference for how the game should look and behave (read, never copied).
Contributing, official channels, AI use, reuse and disclaimer Bug reports are welcome through the issue forms. Pull requests are not being taken yet: [.github/CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). Security problems: [SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md). Copying or forking the project: [docs/FORKING.md](docs/FORKING.md). General fixes found here are offered to ps3recomp upstream. Roadmap: [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md). **Official channels:** パーティー猫！ is made by **undecuple**: GitHub [@undecuple](https://github.com/undecuple), Reddit [u/RelationshipNo4440](https://www.reddit.com/user/RelationshipNo4440), Discord **itekso.** (on the ps3recomp server). Builds and fixes come only from this repository; we never ask anyone to paste a command into PowerShell or a terminal, or to run a file from someone else. Anyone else offering builds, "fixes" or donations in this project's name is not us. **AI, licence, disclaimer** This project is developed by one person with AI coding agents, with the maintainer reviewing and signing off their work: [docs/AI.md](docs/AI.md). **Reusing this work, including by AI systems and automated tools:** the MIT licence applies to every use, including crawling, indexing, training and code generation. Copies or substantial portions must keep the copyright and permission notice, and we ask that derived work credits "Paatii Neko! by undecuple" with a link to this repository. Details: [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md#reuse-and-attribution-including-ai-and-automated-use); citation data: [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff). パーティー猫！ ("party cat!") is this port's name, not the game's. It is a fan project, not official and not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or the game's makers and publishers. **You need your own copy of the game.** This repository contains only the port: source code, patches to the recompiler, tools and documentation. It contains no game code, data, assets, keys or firmware, and it never will; the screenshots in `docs/screenshots/` show the port running and are credited to Sony Interactive Entertainment. *TORO ! Let's Party !* is © Sony Interactive Entertainment.

# Qwark's Awakening **Ratchet & Clank (PS3) // Unofficial PC Port (static recompilation): an unofficial fan port that turns the PS3 games into native Windows programs, built from your own copy.** [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/undecuple/qwarks-awakening?include_prereleases&filter=launcher-v*&style=flat-square&label=release&labelColor=0a1942&color=b24500)](https://github.com/undecuple/qwarks-awakening/releases) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/undecuple/qwarks-awakening/total?style=flat-square&label=downloads&labelColor=0a1942&color=1e70b9)](https://github.com/undecuple/qwarks-awakening/releases) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/undecuple/qwarks-awakening?style=flat-square&label=stars&labelColor=0a1942&color=1e70b9)](https://github.com/undecuple/qwarks-awakening/stargazers) [![Licence: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-MIT-1e70b9?style=flat-square&labelColor=0a1942)](LICENSE) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/undecuple/qwarks-awakening?style=flat-square&label=last%20commit&labelColor=0a1942&color=1e70b9)](https://github.com/undecuple/qwarks-awakening/commits/main) [![Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/undecuple/qwarks-awakening?style=flat-square&label=issues&labelColor=0a1942&color=1e70b9)](https://github.com/undecuple/qwarks-awakening/issues)
[![Platform: Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20x64-1e70b9?style=flat-square&labelColor=0a1942)](#what-you-need) [![Renderer: Direct3D 12](https://img.shields.io/badge/renderer-Direct3D%2012-1e70b9?style=flat-square&labelColor=0a1942)](#how-it-works) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/undecuple/qwarks-awakening/ci.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=CI&labelColor=0a1942&color=1e70b9)](https://github.com/undecuple/qwarks-awakening/actions/workflows/ci.yml) **[Download](https://github.com/undecuple/qwarks-awakening/releases/latest)** · **[Installing](#install)** · **[Known issues](docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md)** · **[Report an issue](https://github.com/undecuple/qwarks-awakening/issues/new/choose)** · **[Building](docs/BUILDING.md)**
> **Bring your own game.** This repository holds only the port: source code, patches to the recompiler, tools and > documentation. It contains no game code, game data, assets, keys or firmware, and it never will. To build a game you > need your own copy of it and the decrypted `EBOOT.elf` made from that copy ([What you need](#what-you-need)). *Qwark's Awakening* is a fan project's name, after a character from the series. The launcher builds the games on your PC from your own copy. Every test so far ran the Windows programs under Proton on Linux; nothing was tested on Windows itself. An earlier build of the first target, *Tools of Destruction*, was played by hand from its first level, with known bugs. Nobody has played it through. How far each other game gets in scripted runs is in the [status table](#status). No game is online yet ([ONLINE.md](docs/ONLINE.md)).

Contents: [Install](#install) · [Status](#status) · [Settings, controllers and known issues](#settings-and-known-issues) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Credits](#credits-licence-related-projects) --- ## Install The launcher lists the games, finds your files, builds a game from your own copy and starts it. Python and the compiler come with it; nothing else needs to be installed.

*The launcher on its first start, before any game was added (version 0.3.0, under Proton on Linux, 2026-11-13).* ### What you need | | Needed | Notes | |---|---|---| | **Your game** | Your own copy of each game, as a decrypted folder or ISO | Title IDs and updates per game: the table below | | **Decrypted EBOOT** | `EBOOT.elf`, made from your own copy | This project gives no decryption tools or instructions. [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net) and its documentation are the place to start. | | **Windows** | Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit | Not tested on Windows itself; tested under Proton on Linux | | **GPU** | Direct3D 12 | Tested only on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 | | **CPU and memory** | x86-64; 16 GB of memory to build | Tested only on an Intel Core i7-12700KF | | **Disk** | The install, plus several GB for each game you build | The download is about 160 MB; the space a build needs is not measured yet | | Game | Title IDs the launcher knows (region) | Update | |---|---|---| | *Tools of Destruction* | BCUS98127 (US disc) | none (disc 02.00) | | *Quest for Booty* | BCES00301 (EU disc), NPUA80145 (US digital) | none | | *A Crack in Time* | BCUS98124 (US), BCES00511, BCES00726, BCES00748 (EU), BCJS30038 (JP) | 1.20 | | *All 4 One* | BCUS98175, NPUA80695 (US), BCES01141, BCES01142, NPEA00356 (EU), BCAS20200 (Asia), BCJS30081 (JP) | 1.03 | | *Full Frontal Assault* | BCUS98380, NPUA80642 (US), BCES01594, BCES01626, NPEA00378 (EU), NPJA00089 (JP) | 1.05 | | *Into the Nexus* | BCUS99245, NPUA80908 (US), BCES01908, BCES01949, NPEA00457 (EU), NPJA00101 (JP) | 1.01 | | *Ratchet & Clank Collection* (1, 2 and 3) | BCUS98282, NPUA80643 (US), NPEA00385, NPEA00386, NPEA00387 (EU) | none | | *Deadlocked HD* | NPUA80646 (US digital) | none | The port was tested with one copy of each game. The other IDs are in the catalogue but untested. ### Steps 1. Download `Qwarks-Awakening--setup-windows-x64.exe` from the [Latest release](https://github.com/undecuple/qwarks-awakening/releases/latest). You now have one setup file. 2. Run it. The program is not signed, so Windows may show "Windows protected your PC". Choose "More info", then "Run anyway". The setup's welcome page opens. 3. Click Next, Next, Install. The default folder is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Qwark's Awakening`; you can pick another one. No administrator rights are needed. The last page says "Setup is done". 4. Click Finish with "Start Qwark's Awakening" ticked. The launcher opens. On its first start it looks for your games in RPCS3's usual folders, reading only, and writes `library.json` in the install folder. 5. Pick a game and click Build. If a game is missing, add its folder under Settings, Locations. The build takes a while. When it ends, the launcher says "Finished: ... is built and ready to play." Click **Play**. Portable (no install): each launcher release also has two zips. The full build zip holds the same files as the setup. The launcher zip holds only the launcher; it asks before it downloads the build kit on your first Build. Unpack the whole folder, then start `Qwarks-Awakening-launcher.exe`. `SHA256SUMS` on the release page lists the checksum of every file. Uninstall from Windows Settings, Apps, or from the Start menu. The uninstaller removes the program files. It asks before it deletes your library, your built games with their saves, and the logs. Then it asks before it deletes the games' settings. Both answers default to No. ### If something goes wrong | What you see | What to do | |---|---| | "Windows protected your PC" | The program is not signed. Choose "More info", then "Run anyway". | | Your antivirus removes the setup, the launcher or a built game | New programs without a signature are sometimes flagged. Compare the file with `SHA256SUMS` on the release page, then restore it. | | Setup: "The install folder must be called ..." or "... already holds files that are not from Qwark's Awakening" | Pick an empty folder, or keep the default. | | Setup: "... is inside OneDrive" or "... contains the character ..." | Pick a folder outside OneDrive whose path has none of `[ ] ;`. | | Setup stops some other way | Its log is `Setup Log #.txt` in `%TEMP%`. | | "Last build did not finish" | The reason is shown under it. 04af69922d26655c57c1b1492c1e3feaa31e233e.message:
lifter: lswi/stswi and four unsigned VMX ops -- the SVML front end loads

The SVO browser could never load file:///kin/index.jsp: its URL parser
(func_0039BDB0) copies the scheme with an inlined 15-byte
'lswi r5,r31,15; stswi r5,r11,15', which the lifter emitted as /* TODO */.
The scheme stayed empty, no protocol handler matched 'file', the loader
factory returned NULL and the page stack waited forever -- with no OS call
and no log line.

Found by decompiling the call chain with Ghidra (navigate -> engine Load ->
FUN_003AA120 -> loader factory -> handler registry) and watching the parsed
request in gdb.

patches/ps3recomp/0004 implements lswi/stswi (bytes fill registers four at a
time, MSB first in the low word, wrapping r31 -> r0; NB 0 = 32) and
vmsumuhm, vsubuws, vmuloub, vmuleub. No real-instruction TODOs remain in
the lift (the rest are data words in .text).

The title now loads index.jsp, languageselect.jsp and the
svolanguageselect lump: it has reached its language-select menu.

Also: KZ2_SELFTEST=1 compares lifted strchr/strstr with the host's.

hle: resolve campaign start sound hang via sys_timer_usleep watchdog hook

stream record handle's MSB and its status fields, releasing the wait.

loading (FIOS). Also move kz2_hle_register() after lv2_init_syscalls() in
src/boot_main.cpp so custom syscall handlers are not overwritten at boot.

- patches/ps3recomp/0005: NV4097 0x1D74 TEXTURE_READ_SEMAPHORE_RELEASE
  (cellGcmSetWriteTextureLabel) writes its label. Killzone 2 fences its
  streaming VRAM ring with it (label 0x48); the runtime dropped it, the
  label froze and the ring allocator waited forever for free blocks.
- patches/ps3recomp/0005: GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS. The title parks the RSX on a
  self-jump mid-frame and patches it when the rest of the frame is built;
  the walker resynced to put at once, skipped the end of every frame (and
  its fence) and ended up looping over stale segments. boot_main sets 3 s.

  tables) from 0x20000000 to 0xE8000000, and the HLE scratch heap to
  0xE9000000. The title's sys_mmapper heap, which this runtime allocates
  upward from 0x11000000, grew across 0x20000000; its allocator wrote
  strings over the control register and put went odd (0x13009).

plus the Cross-button prompt (docs/media/first-menu-frame.png). Text is

b1ca0d4e415b53a5e8c1d33e90d762227131a6c2.message:
spu: lift the WWS policy module's interrupt vector; SPU jobs now run

The WWS job manager loads job code with an MFC list in stall-and-notify
mode and finishes the load in its SPU interrupt handler at LS 0xA2C, which
builds a register save/restore stub at 0x3FEC0 and returns through
0xA84/0xA90/0xAD0. None of these is a static branch target, so the lift had
no function there: the handler ran in the fallback interpreter and the PM
ended at 0xA60 every time. With them as --extra-funcs the PM cycles through
its job lists and the audio jobs (modules at 0xDD4B80 and 0xDE3300) are
streamed into LS 0x4000 and dispatched to their lifted overlays.

Status details below. > **Devam eden bir çalışma — oynanabilir bir port değildir.** Oyun açılıyor, verisini okuyor, SPU işlerini çalıştırıyor ve menülerinde bir kampanya başlatmaya kadar ilerliyor; kampanya seviyesi yükleniyor ve yükleme ekranı çiziliyor, ancak seviye içindeki ilk kareler yamalanmayan bir komut tamponu park noktasında takılıyor (docs/PROGRESS.md §20); giriş videosu takılıyor. > > Built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp); the boot harness is adapted from [Kurtisone/twistedmetal](https://github.com/Kurtisone/twistedmetal). Developed with an AI coding agent. See [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md). [English](#english) | [Türkçe](#türkçe) --- ## English Static recompilation project for **Killzone 2** (PlayStation 3) targeting native PC execution. ### 📊 Project Status: boots, streams data, renders its first frames (pre-alpha) Built on **[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp)** (v0.15.0, pinned as a submodule, with this port's fixes in `patches/ps3recomp/`). Linux/Vulkan is the primary host. | Stage | State | |---|---| | EBOOT → ELF, PPU lift | **done** — 34,145 OPD functions → 67,196 lifted, 41 chunks, ~6.1 M lines of C++, 234 switch tables | | SPU lift | **done** — 23 embedded SPU ELFs, the WWS job-manager policy module, 36 WWS job modules | | Build & link | **done** — ~118 MB native x86-64 binary (clang, ~3 min at -j8) | | Boot | CRT, TLS, SPURS ×2, FIOS, cellGcm 720p, display buffers/tiles/zcull, cellFont, cellSaveData, cellAudio, trophies | | Asset streaming | **works** — FIOS reads `data_ps3.psarc`; Edge Zlib requests are inflated on the host | | Rendering | title screen and menus with full text on Vulkan, 60-150 presented frames/s; campaign loading screen renders | | Front end | language select → gamma → main menu → save warning → start screen → campaign difficulty → campaign start (driven with `PAD_SCRIPT`) | | Movies / gameplay | intro movie player deadlocks (skipped via `tools/make_vfs_nointro.sh`); campaign start sound teardown hang resolved; advances to level asset loading; gameplay not reached | ![First in-level image: the Intruder dropship in the Corinth River intro](docs/media/in-level-intruder-first-image.png) ![Main menu on ps3recomp v0.15.0: every glyph present](docs/media/main-menu-v015.png) ![Campaign loading screen: Corinth River with the mission briefing](docs/media/corinth-river-loading-v015.png) Full engineering log: [docs/PROGRESS.md](docs/PROGRESS.md). #### Roadmap - [x] **Phase 0: Runtime & Build System** (ps3recomp submodule, CMake, Linux/Vulkan runner) - [x] **Phase 1: ELF extraction & analysis** (imports, SPU images, job modules) - [x] **Phase 2: Static recompilation** (PPU + SPU lifted and linked) - [ ] **Phase 3: HLE / OS layer** — in progress (lwcond ABI, Edge Zlib, cellFont fixed; SVO front end next) - [ ] **Phase 4: RSX rendering** — first passes render; final composition missing - [ ] **Phase 5: Audio, input, game loop** - [ ] **Phase 6: Playability** ### Name The repository is named after Kurumi Tokisaki (*Date A Live*), a character who commands time — a nod to bringing a 2009 game forward. The name is the only thing it borrows; the engineering is below. # ### Play in a window / Pencerede oynatma ``` tools/play.sh ``` Enter = START, Space = Cross, Esc = Circle, arrow keys = D-pad, R/F = Square, T/C = Triangle, Q/E = L1/R1, Tab = SELECT; an SDL game controller also works. The game currently runs through the menus to campaign start and stops at the first physics step of the level. ## Credits Most of what runs is other people's work: the **[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp)** toolkit and runtime (Ned Heller / sp00nznet and contributors), and the Linux boot harness of **[Kurtisone/twistedmetal](https://github.com/Kurtisone/twistedmetal)**, both MIT. Bugs fixed in `patches/ps3recomp/` were first found by others; see **[CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md)** and **[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)**. This port is developed by YYOzcan with an AI coding agent (Claude); the reasoning behind every change is in [docs/PROGRESS.md](docs/PROGRESS.md). ### Project Layout ``` ├── CMakeLists.txt # links the lifted game against the ps3recomp runtime ├── external/ps3recomp/ # toolkit + runtime (git submodule, pinned) ├── patches/ps3recomp/ # this port's fixes to the toolkit (tools/apply_patches.sh) ├── src/ │ ├── boot_main.cpp # Linux/Windows runner: guest VM, frame clock, backend pick │ ├── kz2_hle.cpp # Killzone 2 HLE overrides (Edge Zlib, cellFont, ...) │ ├── kz2_spu_pm.c # registers the lifted WWS job-manager policy module │ └── kz2_ftrace.cpp # function-entry histogram (diagnostic builds) ├── tools/ # lift / build / run / diagnostics scripts └── docs/ # PROGRESS.md (engineering log), ARCHITECTURE.md ``` Game files, the lifted C++ (`recompiled/`, `spu_recompiled/`) and loader output (`out/`) are generated from **your own** disc and are never committed. ### Building (Linux) Requirements: clang, CMake ≥ 3.20, Ninja, Python ≥ 3.10, SDL2, Vulkan headers, glslang, zlib; a decrypted `EBOOT.ELF` in `game_dump/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/`. ```bash git clone --recursive https://github.com/YYOzcan/tokisaki-port # or: git submodule update --init tools/apply_patches.sh # this port's ps3recomp fixes tools/lift.sh # PPU: EBOOT.ELF -> recompiled/ (~1 min) tools/lift_spu.sh # SPU: images, policy module, job modules -> spu_recompiled/ BUILD_JOBS=8 tools/build.sh # ~0.6 GB RAM per job ``` ### Running ```bash tools/run.sh # Vulkan window; KZ2_RSX=null for headless ``` `run/vfs/PS3_GAME` links to the dump, `/dev_hdd0` maps to `run/hdd0`, firmware fonts come from RPCS3's `dev_flash` (`PS3_DEV_FLASH`). Diagnostics: `tools/snapshot.sh` (all thread stacks under gdb), `tools/sample.sh` (main-thread sampler), `tools/import_audit.py` (imports without HLE), `tools/psarc_map.py` (which archive members were read), `KZ2_PEEK` / `KZ2_DUMPAT` (watch guest memory). --- ## Türkçe **Killzone 2** (PlayStation 3) için geliştirilen, yerel PC çalıştırmasını hedefleyen statik yeniden derleme (static recompilation) projesidir. ### 📊 Proje Durumu: açılıyor, veri akıtıyor, ilk karelerini çiziyor (ön-alfa) **[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp)** (v0.14.0, alt modül olarak sabitlendi; bu porta ait düzeltmeler `patches/ps3recomp/` altında) üzerine kuruludur. A native Windows build of **ICO** (PS3, *ICO & Shadow of the Colossus
Collection*), made by statically recompiling the game's PowerPC (PPU) and
SPU code to C/C++ with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp).

**No game files are included.** You select your own disc dump and the
installer recompiles it into a PC game **on your machine**.

---

## 📺 What's in the box

| Component | What it is |
|---|---|
| **`ICO.PC.Port.Setup.exe`** | The installer ([Releases](../../releases)). One self-contained exe: select your dump, it checks, decrypts (via your RPCS3), recompiles and installs. |
| `pipeline/` | `ico_pipeline.py` — the recompilation steps the installer runs, and `ico_profile.json` with the tested hashes and code cut points. |
| `port/` | The ICO-specific runner (`main.cpp`), HLE overrides (`stubs.cpp`) and CMake project. |
| `external/ps3recomp` | Submodule: the ps3recomp toolkit, on the branch with this port's runtime fixes. |
| `installer/` | The installer's source (C#, .NET, WinForms). |
| `docs/` | [Decrypting](docs/DECRYPTING.md), [run settings](docs/ENVIRONMENT.md), [building from source](docs/BUILDING.md). |
