## ⬇️ Installing

### Requirements

| You need | Why | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Windows 10/11 x64** | | |
| **A GPU with Direct3D 12** | Rendering | |
| **CPU with SSE4.1** | | AVX2 + FMA (Intel Haswell / AMD Zen or newer) gets the faster build. |
| **Your ICO disc dump** | Game data | *ICO & Shadow of the Colossus Collection*, **USA (BCUS98259)**, the `PS3_GAME` folder. |
| **[RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net) with the PS3 firmware installed** | Decrypts `ICO.self`; its `dev_flash` provides the ATRAC audio codec | **File → Install Firmware** in RPCS3. Tested with firmware 4.91. |
| Visual Studio Build Tools (C++, Clang, CMake) | Compiles the game | The installer offers to install it (≈6 GB, through winget). |
| Python 3.10+ | Runs the recompiler | The installer offers to install it. |
| ~5 GB free disk | Build + copied data | ~3 GB if you link to the dump instead of copying. |
| Internet during install | Downloads [SDL2](https://www.libsdl.org) 2.32.10 (7 MB, SHA-256 checked) | The controller backend for DualSense / DualShock 4. Without it the game builds with XInput controllers only. |

### Steps

1. **Dump your disc** with your own PS3 (e.g. with multiMAN or a Blu-ray
   drive that reads PS3 discs). You need the `PS3_GAME` folder.
2. **Install RPCS3** and its **PS3 firmware** (File → Install Firmware).
3. **Download `ICO.PC.Port.Setup.exe`** from [Releases](../../releases) and run it.
4. In the installer:
   1. **Your game** — select the `PS3_GAME` folder (or the dump folder that contains it).
   2. **Decrypt ICO.self** — keep *"Decrypt automatically with my RPCS3"* and point it
      at `rpcs3.exe`, **or** choose *"I already decrypted it"* and select your `ICO.elf`
      ([how to decrypt by hand](docs/DECRYPTING.md)).
   3. **PS3 firmware** — the `dev_flash` folder of RPCS3 (filled in automatically
      when it sits next to `rpcs3.exe`).
   4. **Installation folder** — a short path, e.g. `C:\Games`. Setup creates `ICO` inside it.
   5. **Build tools** — if anything shows ✖, click **Install...** and confirm.
5. Click **Install**. The first install takes **6–30 minutes** depending on the PC; most of
   it is compiling. *Show details* shows the full log, also saved to
   `<install>\logs\install.log`.
6. Click **Play**, or use the **ICO** shortcut on the desktop / Start menu. The installed game is `ico.exe`.

To **update**, run the new installer and select the same installation
folder. Your `ico.ini` edits and saves are kept.
To **uninstall**, delete the installation folder and the shortcuts.

## 🎮 Controls

**Controllers:** DualSense (PS5) and DualShock 4 (PS4) work natively, over
USB or Bluetooth, through SDL2 — with the PlayStation button layout the game
was made for. XInput (Xbox-compatible) controllers work too. A DualShock 3
needs a Windows driver that exposes it as a standard controller. Stick
diagonals keep their full speed (`PAD_SQUIRCLE=1`, default).

**Keyboard:** always active, alongside any controller:

| PS3 | Keyboard | | PS3 | Keyboard |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D-pad / left stick | Arrow keys | | L1 / R1 | Q / W |
| ✕ Cross | Z | | L2 / R2 | 1 / 2 |
| ◯ Circle | X | | Start | Enter |
| ▢ Square | A | | Select | Tab |
| △ Triangle | S | | | |

**Exit Game** is at the bottom of the title menu and of the pause menu.

Run settings live in `ico.ini` next to `ico.exe`; see
[docs/ENVIRONMENT.md](docs/ENVIRONMENT.md). The game's log is
`<install>\logs\ico.log` — attach it to bug reports.

## 🐞 Known issues

- **Long black screen before the first cinematic** (~25 s after the logos):
  the game is loading on the SPU; it is not frozen.
- **Some sound effects are missing**; the music plays.
- **A black screen after skipping a cinematic** can last a few seconds.
- **Moving or resizing the window can break the picture.** Keep the window
  in place for now.
- **Rare crash at start-up** (Windows reports `CoreMessaging.dll`, exception
  `0xe0464645`) was seen in early tests. Start the game again.
- **Only the US release** (BCUS98259) is supported. Other regions fail the
  hash check: the code cut points are specific to this executable.
- **No anti-aliasing**: the game's SPU Edge MLAA is skipped for speed
  (`ICO_SKIP_MLAA=1`); a PC AA/upscaler is planned.
- **Fixed 1280×720** window, no graphics menu yet.
- **One CPU core stays busy** while the game runs (the SPU renderer polls for work).
- **The first install is long** (6–30 min) and needs ~6 GB of Visual Studio
  Build Tools. A future release may ship more of the runtime prebuilt.
- **Only Windows** (Direct3D 12).

Found something else? [Open an issue](../../issues) with your
`logs\ico.log` and `logs\install.log`.

## 🛠️ How it works

```
 your PS3_GAME ──► ICO.self ──(your RPCS3 --decrypt)──► ICO.elf
                                                         │
             ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┤
             ▼                                           ▼
   ppu_loader + ppu_lifter                       extract_spu_images
   (--code-end 0x3BC7B4)                         spu_lifter × 6 (per-image --code-end)
   gen_hle_nids --all                            + MultiStream DSP overlay (+0x30000)
             │                                   + flashATRAC.pic from YOUR dev_flash (+0x33100)
             │                                   build_spu_workloads
             └──────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            ▼
         CMake + Ninja + clang-cl  ◄── port/ (main.cpp, stubs.cpp) + ps3recomp runtime
                            ▼
                <install>\ico.exe  +  ico.ini  +  vfs\PS3_GAME (your data)
```

| Stage | Tool (ps3recomp `tools/`) | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Load | `ppu_loader.py` | function table, imports, segments |
| PPU lift | `ppu_lifter.py --code-end 0x3BC7B4` | ~64 MB of C++ (2 chunks) |
| HLE table | `gen_hle_nids.py --all` | firmware NID → handler map |
| SPU | `extract_spu_images.py`, `spu_lifter.py`, `rebase_spu_elf.py`, `build_spu_workloads.py` | 6 images + 2 overlays, registry |
| Build | CMake / Ninja / clang-cl | `ico.exe` |

Everything the pipeline needs to know about the supported release — file
hashes, the PPU/SPU code ends, SPU overlay bases and extra entry points, the
run settings — is in [`pipeline/ico_profile.json`](pipeline/ico_profile.json).

## 📦 Building from source

For developers. See [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md) for the details.

```bash
git clone --recursive https://github.com/feanor-noldorin/ico-recomp.git
cd ico-recomp
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\pip install -r external\ps3recomp\requirements.txt -c pipeline\constraints.txt
.venv\Scripts\python pipeline\ico_pipeline.py --game-dir "D:\dumps\ICO\PS3_GAME" --rpcs3 C:\RPCS3\rpcs3.exe --dev-flash C:\RPCS3\dev_flash --install C:\Games\ICO --python .venv\Scripts\python.exe
```

Building the installer exe: `powershell -File tools\make_release.ps1`.

0650a59088532c1a0a3469cdd8812fa457a80bf0.message:
cellGcm: _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel queues the label wait and the flip

libgcm appends NV406E SEMAPHORE_OFFSET and SEMAPHORE_ACQUIRE for the
label, then the flip, so the RSX flips only once the label holds the
value. RPCS3's _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel writes the same two
methods into the context before its flip command. The import here
ignored its context, wrote the label itself from the PPU, and flipped
at call time: whoever owns the label was overruled, and the flip
waited for nothing.

Write the two semaphore methods into the context and queue the flip
behind them with gcm_flip_into_fifo, as _cellGcmSetFlipCommand already
does. A context that is not a mapped command buffer, or has no room,
falls back to the immediate form as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

0aead166fd65ab34bee01df19a341665800a727f.message:
cellGcm: a FIFO user command reaches the handler set with cellGcmSetUserHandler

Symptom: a title's cellGcmSetUserHandler callback never runs for the user
commands it puts in its command buffer. In Killzone 3 that callback submits
the per-frame job that lets the frame continue, so the level stalled.

Cause: the walker decodes GCM_SET_USER_COMMAND (method 0xEB00) as
subchannel 7 / method 0x0B00 and hands it to rsx_raise_user_cmd, the lv2
route: it posts an event to the RSX interrupt queue for a guest interrupt
thread. A title that registered its handler through the HLE
cellGcmSetUserHandler has no such thread; its handler runs from
ppu_gcm_pump. The branch then `continue`s, so the walker's later 0xEB00 case,
which calls cellGcmQueueUserCommand for the pump, is never reached.

Change: when an HLE user handler is registered, the 0x0B00 branch also
queues the command for the pump (cellGcmQueueUserCommand). The lv2 event is
still raised as before.

Verification: libs/video/tests/test_gcm_fifo_user_command.c (standalone,
includes cellGcmSys.c like test_gcm_user_command.c; graphics backends
stubbed) registers an HLE user handler, then five times puts one user
command in the ring, drains it with cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo and calls
ppu_gcm_pump. With this change the handler runs five times, each with its
command's argument, and the lv2 route is still taken five times (gcc and
clang). Against v0.14.0's cellGcmSys.c (a2c2010) the handler never runs
(5/5 fail). test_gcm_user_command.c still passes.

0e26194770079d251b113cbc28bb41e27199ac76.message:
sys_spu: an SPU's user event finds the port the PPU binds, and waits for it

An SPU's send_event (interrupt mailbox, code 0..63) was routed only through the ports the group binds with
sys_spu_thread_group_connect_event_all_threads, and answered ENOTCONN at once when there was none. Two things go
wrong with that:

- A port bound for one SPU thread with sys_spu_thread_connect_event was never found by the delivery, only by the
  plain out-mailbox path.
- The SPU thread starts running at sys_spu_thread_group_start while the PPU is still on its way to the connect
  calls that follow it (a real SPU needs far longer to boot than a lifted one). The first request of the program
  was answered ENOTCONN and the SPU program gave up. SoulCalibur II HD's audio engine (MultiStream) binds its ports
  with sys_spu_thread_connect_event, after group_start, and failed this way.

The delivery now looks at the thread's own bindings before the group's (spu_port_queue_locked) and, when the port
is not bound yet, waits for a binding for up to 200 ms on a condition variable that both connect calls signal
before it answers ENOTCONN. An SPU whose thread does not exist is answered at once, since nothing will bind its
port. The out-mailbox path reads the bindings through the same helper under the lock.

The test calls the real handlers and spu_deliver_user_event: bound for the thread, bound for the group, bound 40 ms
late either way, never bound (answers after about 200 ms) and an SPU with no thread (answers at once). On v0.15.0
it fails six checks; with the change it passes (five runs in a row).

0fb35648aed8ca984638357c2e82c0e892c12c8b.message:
ppu_sysprx: sys_lwcond_t is +0x00 lwmutex EA, +0x04 queue id

Symptom: a title that reads lwcond+0x00 itself sees 0 there and treats the
lwcond as invalid (Killzone 3's file system layer checks it before every
wait and loops). The queue id is also written past the 8-byte structure,
over whatever the title keeps next to it.

Cause: the context-style sys_lwcond_create in ppu_sysprx.cpp writes the
lwmutex EA as a 64-bit value at +0x00 (so the EA lands at +0x04 and +0x00
reads 0) and the id at +0x08. sys_lwcond_t is 8 bytes: +0x00 u32 lwmutex
EA, +0x04 u32 queue id, which is also what libs/system/sysPrxForUser.h
declares as sys_lwcond_t_hle.

Change: 32-bit stores at +0x00 and +0x04 in sys_lwcond_create, and a 32-bit
read of +0x00 in sys_lwcond_wait. Wait/signal behaviour is unchanged.

Verification: tools/test_lwcond_layout.py builds the real
sys_lwcond_create and sys_lwcond_wait into a host program over stubbed
guest memory. With this change +0x00 holds the lwmutex EA, +0x04 a nonzero
id, nothing past +0x08 is written, and the wait finds the lwmutex. On
v0.14.0 (a2c2010) +0x00 reads 0, the EA is at +0x04 and the id is written
at +0x08 (2 of 3 checks fail; the wait found the lwmutex there only because
create and wait agreed on the wrong layout).

1148eaca60f111203aa7ff38e58a927acdcbd353.message:
video/tests: a flip queued in the command stream

libs/video/tests/test_gcm_flip_stream.c compiles cellGcmSys.c in, like
test_gcm_flip_wrap.c, and checks on a title context:

1. _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel puts SEMAPHORE_OFFSET and
   SEMAPHORE_ACQUIRE for the label, then the flip marker, into the
   context, moves current past them, and leaves the label alone.
2. A tick before the drain is a vblank, not a flip.
3. Once the drain has executed up to the marker, the next tick
   completes the flip.
4. A flip written but not flushed does not complete; an executed one
   does, even with a newer flip written behind it and not flushed.
5. A flip the walker abandons when it resyncs out of unmapped IO does
   not hold back the flip status.

On master 8 of the 14 checks fail. tools/test_gcm_flip_stream.py builds
and runs it, so the existing tools/test_*.py sweep in CI covers it.

12158c45650cc5d00d228a62f98c3a204aacc300.message:
ppu_lifter: exact VMX, branch decode, integer, FP and decoding fixes

VMX
- runtime/ppu/ppu_vmx.h implements every VMX op exactly, and the lifter
  routes ops by raw XO: some had no disassembler name and lifted as no-ops.
  About 45 did nothing: the saturating adds/subs, vavg*, vmul[eo]*, vmsum*,
  vmhadd*/vmhradd*, vmladduhm, vrlh, the element and whole-vector shifts,
  vpk*, vsum*, vaddcuw/vsubcuw, vpkpx/vupk*px, vexptefp/vlogefp.
- Saturation sets VSCR[SAT], VSCR[NJ] is honoured, vcmp*. writes CR6;
  mtvscr/mfvscr are decoded, and VRSAVE reads back (ppu_context.vrsave).

Branches
- BO/BI come from the instruction word, so bdnzt/bdzf decrement CTR and
  test the condition (they were always taken); CTR is 64-bit.
- Every LK=1 form sets LR unconditionally.
- b<cond>lrl dispatches through ps3_indirect_call_to and leaves CTR alone.
- bl 0 / bcl 20,31,0 (get-PC) lift as get-PC, not as a call.

Integer
- XER[OV]/[SO] set by every OE form; compares and stwcx./stdcx. copy SO.
- rlwinm/rlwnm/rlwimi handle wrapping masks (MB > ME).
- mulld/mulli wrap, and lifted code builds with -fwrapv.
- mtxer keeps only the defined bits; mfocrf isolates its field.

Decoding: lswi/lswx/stswi/stswx, lwaux, stdbrx, stvlx/stvrx(l), lvrxl, td,
dst/dss.

FP: single-precision results (NaNs included) are single-format; fctiw/fctiwz
write the whole FPR; the FPSCR moves (mffs, mtfsf, mtfsfi, mtfsb0/1, mcrfs)
are implemented; FP record forms set CR1.

CR fusion checks the fused field's liveness past the branch target; it used
to fuse a compare that was re-tested after the label.

Guest loads in lifted code are inline (vm_read*_inl in the header preamble);
ppu_loader.cpp keeps the out-of-line accessors, and the inline path stands
down while a read diagnostic (PPU_RWATCH and friends) is armed.

fp decompiler: biased unsigned remap and _bx2 fetches return signed values

Two ways a fetch comes back re-centred to -1..1 were ignored, so the
shader saw 0..1 encodings:

- SET_TEXTURE_ADDRESS bit 12, UNSIGNED_REMAP_BIASED, applies to every
  fetch from the unit: (round(x*255)-128)/127 on the lanes the crossbar
  fills from a source channel (16-bit X16/Y16_X16 channels: /32767),
  after gamma and not on gamma lanes, and not on lanes the filter flags
  signed. rsx_texture_expand_mask computes the lanes, for the formats
  RPCS3 gives RSX_FORMAT_FEATURE_BIASED_NORMALIZATION.
- EXP_TEX (OPDEST bit 21, the _bx2 modifier) belongs to the instruction,
  not the texture: x*2-1 on every lane of any unit, bypassing gamma
  (RPCS3 _process_texel). It applies from every entry point.

inFAMOUS 2 reads its normals G-buffer through a biased unit and its
tangent-space normal maps and occlusion-cone lookup tables with TEX_bx2
(about a quarter of its fragment programs). Read unexpanded, every
normal leaned towards (1,1,1), normal maps had no effect, and the
occlusion volumes round props drew as dark boxes.

The engine passes the expand masks of the units a program samples
through a new entry point, rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_expand_ex,

16db6bca787b02f598a18b5b5efbbd7b2f882002.message:
cellGcm: GET_REPORT honours the report DMA context and writes main-memory reports to guest memory

Symptom: titles that keep their GPU reports in main memory read stale memory
for every report. Killzone 3 selects the main-memory report context and
issues about 160 reports per frame in a level (timestamps and occlusion
queries); none of them ever reached the memory it reads.

Cause: the FIFO walker ignored NV4097_SET_CONTEXT_DMA_REPORT (0x1A8) and
wrote every NV4097_GET_REPORT (0x1800) into the host s_report_data slots,
indexed by offset / 16, whatever context the title had selected.

Change: the walker records the context set by 0x1A8 (reset to local by
cellGcmInit and cellGcmTerminate). With the local context (0xFEED0000, the
default) a report goes to s_report_data as before. With the main-memory
context (0xFEED0001, or CELL_GCM_CONTEXT_DMA_REPORT_LOCATION_MAIN 0xBAD68000)
the report's offset is an IO offset and the 16-byte report is written
big-endian to gcm_io2ea(offset): u64 timestamp, u32 value, u32 0. An offset
with no IO mapping is skipped with a rate-limited log line. Report
timestamps now rise strictly, so two reports in one walker pass never share
or reverse a time stamp.

Verification: tests/gcm_reports (CTest, built with PS3RECOMP_BUILD_TESTS on
POSIX hosts like the host harness) builds a ring with local reports, a
switch to 0xFEED0001, main-memory reports of type 1 and 2, one unmapped
offset and a switch back, drains it once with cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo and
reads every slot back. Run as a MinGW-w64 build under Proton (this machine
has no Linux SDL2 for the POSIX runtime build): with this change 9/9 checks
pass; the same test linked against v0.14.0's cellGcmSys.c (a2c2010) fails
6/9 (main-memory slots keep their sentinel, the reports land in the host
area instead, timestamps not written). Carried as a local patch in the
Killzone 3 port (v0.13.0 base).

17bf55aa590b12b5e2c37c6885718526f8b59804.message:
cellGcm: NV3089 source origin is 12.4, the copy counted it 256 times too small

IMAGE_IN_POINT is 12.4 fixed point per axis, and DS_DX / DT_DY step the source with 20 fractional bits (1.0 =
0x100000). nv3089_blit's copy loops added the origin to that position as origin << 8, so a source offset counted
1/256 of what it is: for any origin under 256 texels the loops started at column 0 and row 0. The GPU paths in the
same function (rsx_live_draw_blit, rsx_live_draw_resolve_blit) already took origin >> 4, so the two disagreed, and
nv3089_engine_read, which writes the source rectangle back from the draw engine before the copy, took it as origin >> 4
for its start and << 8 for its end.

A title that resolves a supersampled scene in 512x512 tiles with a one texel origin (in_uv 0x00100010, SoulCalibur II HD,
six 2:1 blits) got the first row and column of every tile black: the loops read column 0 and row 0, which the engine
write-back (starting at 1) had not covered.

The origin now enters every computation as origin << 16 (nv3089_origin), in the engine write-back and in both copy
loops (linear and the NV309E swizzled one), so the loops read from the texel the origin names and the write-back covers
exactly what they read. Also reported by undecuple on the first version of this change, which made the write-back follow
the wrong loop.

The test plays the engine (guest_read stores, into the rectangle it is given, a pixel that names its own source position)
and checks that destination pixel (x, y) is the source pixel at (origin + x * scale, origin + y * scale), for origins of
0, 1, 3 and 20 texels at 1:1, 2:1 and 4:1; five of the six cases fail on v0.15.0.

1e6f4c8e744a66f6f5163f6f8def38470742e50b.message:
vulkan: colour feedback snapshots for draws that sample their own target

A draw that samples the colour target it is writing gets, on Metal, a
copy of that target taken just before it (rsx_draw_backend.color_snapshot).
In-place deferred lighting works this way: read the albedo, write the lit
colour over it. The Vulkan backend had no such hook, so the engine fell
back to the guest-memory bytes at the target's address, which hold
whatever was last stored there.

On Twisted Metal (BCES01010) the G-buffer's first target (0x00AB0000) is
also the UI target. Its lighting passes therefore read the previous
frame's menu instead of the albedo just drawn, lit it, and composited it
into the next frame. That is the red frame, the red and green splatter
and the white logo on its main menu.

vk_eng_color_snapshot copies the target into a new image of the same
format and size, and ends with a barrier so the copy is visible to the
next draw. Every operation here is already one synchronous submission,
so the copy is in command order. The copy is a COLOR object marked
`snapshot`, so the engine can take a crossbar view of it; it is never an
attachment, so releasing it drops no framebuffer. A lit frame asks for
one copy per light, so released copies return their images to a pool of
eight, drained at engine shutdown.

24286f4b3871aff53cf988448e1fc756956372dc.message:
cellGcm: in-FIFO flip wraps only the runtime's own command ring

Symptom: intermittently a title waits forever on a fence. Killzone 3
stopped about 16 s in, depending on where the walker's get offset was.

Cause: _cellGcmSetFlipCommand's HLE (gcm_flip_into_fifo) writes the flip
marker at ctx->current and then, when less than GCM_FLIP_WRAP_BYTES are
left before ctx->end and the walker is well past begin, wraps the context
it was given: a JUMP to begin after the marker and ctx->current = begin.
That is what the SDK's buffer-full callback does for the runtime's ring.
A title with its own buffer-full callback manages its own buffers, and its
context need not be a ring: Killzone 3 flips on a 0x30000-byte draw
context whose end moves down as it allocates from the top, so it always
looks nearly full. Rewinding it mid-frame cut the frame short, the fence
release in its tail never ran, and the title waited for it.

Change: wrap only when the context's buffer-full callback descriptor
(ctx + 0xC) still points at the runtime's callback
(GCM_FIFO_CALLBACK_SENTINEL_EA, installed by cellGcmSetupContext). Other
contexts get the marker and current advances past it, as when there is
room.

Verification: libs/video/tests/test_gcm_flip_wrap.c (standalone, includes
cellGcmSys.c like test_gcm_user_command.c) flips on two nearly full
contexts with the walker 0x28000 bytes past their begin: the ring made by
cellGcmSetupContext, and a title context with its own callback. With this
change the runtime ring wraps (marker, JUMP to begin, current = begin) and
the title context does not (marker, current past it), with gcc and clang.
Against v0.14.0's cellGcmSys.c (a2c2010) the title context is wrapped too

32a85600293ba2cf2a21bcb1150bcc0dbd6fb63a.message:
vulkan: present on its own command buffer, in two halves a host can split

The FIFO walker and the present shared one command buffer and one
fence, and a present waited for two GPU round trips: the engine's blit
of the flipped surface into the offscreen target, then the copy of that
target into the readback buffer. A host that presents on the walker's
thread holds the walker for all of that, about 1.3 ms per frame headless.
One that moves the present to a thread of its own still had to hold its
walker lock for the whole present, since both recorded into s_vk.cmd.

On Twisted Metal (BCES01010) that is the window in which the title
moves put to its other ring segment and starts writing its next frame
over the one it left, JUMP out of it included. The walker resumes 2.4 ms
later and executes the new frame's data as commands.

The present now has its own command pool, command buffer and fences,
and comes in two halves:

- rsx_vulkan_backend_present_begin() records the blit and the copy out
  and submits them without waiting. It reads the flipped surface, so it
  runs under the host's walker lock, but only for the recording.
- rsx_vulkan_backend_present_finish() waits for that copy, reads the
  centre pixel and the dump back, and blits into the window. It may run
  while the walker drains the next frame.

rsx_vulkan_backend_present() is both, so existing hosts see no
difference. The fixed-function path, which draws into the offscreen
target itself, still finishes inside present_begin.

What keeps the two halves apart:
- vkQueueSubmit, vkQueuePresentKHR and vkDeviceWaitIdle go through
  queue_mu, since the queue is now used from two threads.
- The walker's next command buffer starts with a full barrier after a
  present's copy. Its per-image barriers already order most work after
  earlier submissions; this one covers the rest.
- No image is destroyed while a present's copy may still read it.
- present_mu keeps a flip in the command stream (presented on the
  walker's thread) from overlapping a host thread's finish.

rsx: Y16_X16 and HILO8 crossbars present R-G-R-G, or R-R-R-G with the override

The two-channel 16-bit formats encode their crossbar in 16-bit blocks,
0xE4 or 0x4E only, and present the pair interleaved: RGBA = X,Y,X,Y, or
X,X,X,Y when CONTROL1's high word (the remap override, bit 16) is set
(RPCS3 fragment_texture::decoded_remap, which notes it was verified on
hardware). Through the plain ARGB table a .w read got the resource's

3d5d03bdc7f627a424fb53ce42175984d596a377.message:
runtime: classify syscall 14 by guest address segment

sys_process_is_spu_lock_line_reservation_address answered EINVAL for
every address above the 256 MB VM_MAIN window (0x00010000..0x1000FFFF),
including the rest of segment 0x1 that the same guest allocator hands
out. SPURS validates its management areas through this syscall during
cellSpursInitialize and aborts init on failure, so a legitimate
management area produced a spurious CELL_SPURS_CORE_ERROR_PERM and every
SPU job the instance would have run stayed unstarted.

The contract is RPCS3's process_is_spu_lock_line_reservation_address
(Emu/Cell/lv2/sys_process.cpp): classify by the address segment
(0x0/0x1/0x2/0xC/0xE reservation-capable; 0xF refuses RawSPU; 0xD
refuses; sys_vm mappings refuse, holes in the mapped region EINVAL; rest
EINVAL) with the flags masked to the two SPU bits. The old sys_vm EPERM
check is kept, now through the tracked mappings (g_sys_vm_maps): a
covered address answers EPERM, a hole in the mapped region EINVAL,
matching RPCS3's default branch.

The classification moves to runtime/syscalls/lv2_lock_line.c so
tests/syscalls can unit-test it without linking the syscall layer.

Test: tests/syscalls/test_lock_line (27 checks: segments 0x0/0x1/0x2/
0xC/0xE OK, 0xF EPERM with RawSPU, 0xD EPERM, sys_vm covered/hole/empty,
flag validation).

live-draw: depth buffers read as textures return the real depth

Symptom: a DEPTH24_D8 texture that reads a zeta comes back 0 or partly 0
in three common shapes: a full-screen read of a depth buffer whose first
pass used a smaller clip, a read of an address that is both a colour target
and a zeta, and a draw that reads the zeta it is depth-testing against
(deferred lighting, soft particles). Effects that depend on scene depth
(depth of field, fog, soft particles, deferred lighting) then see a flat 0.

Causes and changes (rsx_live_draw.c):
1. The R32F snapshot of a zeta keeps the clip size of the first pass that
   bound it (512x512 of a 1280x720 depth buffer, say), so later reads get 0
   outside that corner. zdepth_get now grows the snapshot to the largest
   clip bound since, within the depth resource (zdepth_grow_snapshot: a new
   resource, descriptors rewritten, the old one retired, re-resolved at the
   next read).
2. A depth-format read of an address that is also a colour target matched
   the colour surface first. When a written host zeta exists at that
   address the read now takes the zeta.
3. A draw that samples its own bound zeta with depth writes off read guest
   memory, which the host depth never reaches. It now reads the zeta's
   snapshot; the zeta cannot change during such a draw. A draw that writes
   the zeta it reads keeps the old fallback.

45baa4791a794597cfaa0d0d4879347cb637b581.message:
rsx engine: 2D transfers read FP16 colour targets

A transfer out of a render target first writes the GPU's pixels back to
guest memory (rsx_draw_engine_guest_read), but only A8R8G8B8 surfaces were
looked up. Twisted Metal renders its bloom and Sweet Tooth's flaming hair
into an FP16 RGBA target and copies that out with NV3089 for its SPU
post-FX; the copy found no surface, the SPUs got stale memory, and neither
the bloom nor the flames reached the image.

The lookup now takes FP16 RGBA targets too. A transfer counts 32-bit
pixels, so the readback covers every surface pixel the transfer's bytes
touch and stores exactly those bytes, as big-endian R,G,B,A halves: the
layout rsx_texture_decode reads W16_Z16_Y16_X16_FLOAT from. A transfer
INTO an FP16 target is still not pushed: color_target_write takes
A8R8G8B8 rows.

517fc717f73030d62dbaa9a991c118c6bd3cd6a2.message:
spu: the single-precision fast path four lanes at a time with AVX2

On x86, spu_fa/fs/fm/fma/fms/fnms took the per-lane path: each lane
widened to double on its own, and a call per instruction. arm64 has had
a NEON path doing the four lanes at once. This is the same path for
x86 with AVX2: the lanes widened to one f64x4 (exact), the operation,
the 29 low significand bits cleared, narrowed (exact). The lane rules are
the NEON ones: an ordinary single or a true +-0 keeps the vector result,
a zero result loses its sign, fa/fs also needs the exponents within 29,
and fma keeps a lane only when TwoSum says the add did not round onto a
24-bit boundary. Other lanes are redone one by one by the exact path.

test_spu_float_neon compares the vector path with the exact references
bit for bit; it now runs on x86 with AVX2 too, and in the Linux CI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

host: --depthbounds skips where there is no depth bounds test

The depth bounds test is an optional Vulkan feature, and the lavapipe the
Vulkan workflow runs on (Mesa 25, LLVM 20.1.2) does not report depthBounds.
There the backend falls back as designed, the green triangle wins and the
scene failed with exit 3, which proved nothing about the change.

rsx_vulkan_backend_depth_bounds() says whether draws honour the test (the
draw engine drives the backend and the device enabled depthBounds). Where
they do not -- that device, the fixed-function path, Metal, the null
backend -- the scene prints "skipped, no depth bounds test" and exits 0.
The Vulkan workflow turns that line into a notice for this scene only; its
other checks (exit code, validation messages, engine path) still apply, and
"nothing to check" still fails. On a device with the feature (lavapipe in
Mesa 26.2, RADV) the scene still runs and expects blue.

584181aba7a5fe736123213cefc269ea9a630e5c.message:
metal engine: each MRT target takes its own colour mask and blend enable

Every attachment of an MRT set took target A's COLOR_MASK and
BLEND_ENABLE. On the RSX, targets B..D have their own: a nibble each of
COLOR_MASK_MRT (0x0370, A,R,G,B at bits 0..3 of the nibble) and a bit
each of BLEND_ENABLE_MRT (0x036C), as RPCS3 reads them
(color_mask_*(index), blend_enabled_surface_*).

Giving every target A's state was wrong both ways. inFAMOUS 2's light
volumes add into target A with B and C masked off, and the shared state
added every light into the G-buffer: lit props blew out to white, with a
bright rectangle round each light. Its material passes write B and C's
alpha with A's alpha masked, which left them stale.

The engine decodes both registers into the render state (and the
pipeline key), and the Metal backend applies them per attachment.
PS3RECOMP_METAL_MRT_MASK=0 restores the old behaviour for bisecting.

backend presented before it had color_snapshot. The mode also requires
both textured draws to have run, so a rejected feedback draw cannot pass
by leaving the red in place. linux-vulkan.yml runs it in the
guest-program pass, under the validation layer.

627bba25c912461ed2afed98e6abaf60df5f2d02.message:
spurs_job: keep the job's first frame below its cache buffers

spu_run_spurs_job lays a job out as binary, I/O, output, scratch + stack,
then the cache-hinted inputs, so cacheBuffer[0] starts at the stack top.
$sp was set to stack_top - 16. A SPU function saves its link register in
its caller's frame at 16($sp), so the entry's first store wrote 16 bytes
over the start of cacheBuffer[0].

Twisted Metal's Edge geometry jobs keep their viewport there. They read
x = 0x3FF00 (the return address in $lr) and width = height = 0, so the
screen-space scale was zero, every triangle of a skinned mesh had zero
area, and the main view culled them all: Sweet Tooth was missing from the
main menu, while the shadow passes (which skip that culling) drew him.

Start $sp at stack_top - 32 so the caller's 32-byte frame is part of the
stack.

654483d8a3701fe3f6b139761773356836d4e9d9.message:
cellPad: the small motor rumbles at full strength, and a rumble lasts until it changes

A DualShock 3's small motor is on/off: motor[0] is 0 or 1. Forwarded as
motor * 257 it reached the host at 257/65535, 1/255 of full, which a pad
does not feel. And each SDL request ran for 100 ms, while a PS3 title
sets the motors once and they stay on until it sets them again, so a long
rumble stopped almost at once (inFAMOUS 2 only calls when the value
changes).

The small motor is now on at full, the large one keeps 0-255. The last
request per port is kept, sent with a 1 s duration and renewed from the
pad poll every 400 ms while it is non-zero, so it lasts as long as the
title wants and still stops within a second if the title stops polling.

gets the level fix.

65806f3f3614fca3f40061a3ba0ff2cadfaa36b0.message:
ppu_lifter: big-endian lane order for ten VMX integer ops

Symptom: lifted code computes wrong results for vmulouh, vmsumshm, vadduws,
vadduhs and vpkuwum, and does nothing at all for vmsumuhm, vsubuws,
vpkswss, vsrb and vsrab, which were emitted as "/* TODO */" no-ops.

Cause: ctx->vr holds raw big-endian guest bytes. The first five handlers
read halfword and word lanes through int16_t*/uint32_t* casts, which gives
byte-reversed lanes (and the wrong lane pairing) on a little-endian host.
The other five had no lowering.

Change: one handler for the ten ops that assembles each halfword or word
lane from its bytes in big-endian order, computes the result as the AltiVec
PEM defines it (modulo, saturating or shift) and stores it back in the same
order. The five old handlers are removed.

Verification: tools/test_ppu_vmx_lanes.py lifts each op, compiles the
emitted C with the lifter's own preamble and compares vD with an independent
Python model of the instruction on 300 inputs per op (216 edge combinations
plus random vectors). With this change 10/10 ops agree on every input. On
v0.14.0 (a2c2010) all ten fail: five emit TODO, the other five differ on
244 to 292 of 300 inputs. tools/test_ppu_vcmp_record_cr6.py and
tools/test_ppu_lift.py pass before and after.

662270bdf366da3e360385f421ce5192f82b3443.message:
ppu_loader: indirect-call depth guard can be kept per coroutine

Symptom: a title whose guest jobs run on host coroutines (host fibers that
stand in for a guest fiber scheduler) works for a while, then every
indirect call on that thread is skipped by the recursion guard, even calls
to leaf functions ("[ppu] recursion cap ... skipping"); null calls and an
exit follow. Killzone 3 quit a few minutes into a level.

Cause: the guard in ps3_indirect_call_impl keeps one depth count per host
thread in a function-local thread_local. A coroutine that ends by switching
away from inside an indirect call never unwinds its frames, so each one
leaks its depth into the thread's count until the count passes the 4000
cap. The vcall stack pointer (g_vcall_sp) leaks the same way. Neither can be
reached from outside the function, so a coroutine layer has no way to keep
them per coroutine.

Change: the depth count moves to a file-scope thread-local, and two
accessors, ps3_ppu_dispatch_depth_slot() and ps3_ppu_vcall_sp_slot(), return
the current thread's counters. A coroutine layer saves *slot when it
switches away and restores it when it switches back. Threads that never
switch behave exactly as before.

Verification: tools/test_ppu_dispatch_depth.py builds the real
ppu_loader.cpp with runtime/ppu/tests/test_ppu_dispatch_depth.cpp. 5000
ucontext coroutines each go five ps3_indirect_call levels deep and switch
back to the home context without returning; the home side saves and
restores both counters around each switch. With this change all 5000
chains run to the bottom, the home thread's depth and vcall sp are 0
before and after, and a later indirect call runs. Against v0.14.0's
ppu_loader.cpp (a2c2010; the accessors do not exist, the test declares
them weak) only 800 of 5000 chains run: the guard trips at depth 4001 and
skips every call after that.

6752b12939e5c6a34be15c85b9d1e813e19360ab.message:
cellGcm: bounded semaphore acquire; the stuck-get watchdog leaves waits alone

GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1 makes NV406E ACQUIRE block the drain, as the hardware
does, but the stuck-get watchdog counts drain passes, not time: a drain
that stops on an acquire, or on a self-JUMP park, stops every pass at the
same get, so after eight passes (a few milliseconds) it resynced to put
and dropped everything in between. For a park that happens before the
title has patched it into a JUMP to the commands it just wrote at the
ring start, i.e. before GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS has had a chance to run out.
inFAMOUS 2 stopped presenting for good that way in about one run in five
("stuck-get" at a self-jump with no "jump-park" before it).

A pass that stops on an acquire or a park now resets the watchdog; each
of those waits has its own bound. The acquire gets one:
GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS=<ms> consumes an acquire that has waited that long on
the same label and value, and says so, so a label nobody ever writes
cannot wedge the drain. inFAMOUS 2 acquires a label its SPU lighting job
writes every frame; with GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1 GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS=200 its
lit props stop flashing white and its characters stop rendering black.

cellFs: an AIO read keeps the fd's position and cannot interleave

comment says AIO reads are absolute and leave the fd's position alone; they
moved it, so the next cellFsRead continued from wherever the AIO stopped.

spirv-cross writes GLSL.std.450 FMax, FMin, FClamp and Normalize as
fast::max/min/clamp/normalize. Their result for a NaN operand is
undefined, and MTLMathModeSafe on the library does not change that. D3D's

and the guest programs were written for hardware that behaves that way.
inFAMOUS 2 has a sky/bloom pass that produced NaN on Metal only.

fmax/fmin; PS3RECOMP_MSL_FAST=1 keeps the fast:: spelling.

ns * 79800000 passes 2^64 at 231 s. A context that writes its decrementer
restamps the base and never gets there; the SPURS kernel context never writes
it, keeps the stamp from boot, and every timed loop on that SPU saw the
counter jump forward by ~16 s of ticks at 231 s, 462 s, 693 s... Scale the
whole seconds and the remainder separately.

runtime: thread-locals stay thread-local under MinGW (__declspec(thread) only for MSVC)

Symptom (MinGW-w64 builds only): two PPU threads that exit close together
crash; one thread's sys_ppu_thread_exit longjmps toward a frame on the other
thread's stack. In Killzone 3 this is the two Bink threads exiting at the
end of the intro movie. The SPURS job mailboxes and the sysutil completion
drain guard are shared between threads the same way.

Cause: sys_ppu_thread.c, spurs_job.c, cellSpurs.c and cellSysutil.c pick
__declspec(thread) when _WIN32 is defined. MinGW GCC defines _WIN32 and
ignores that attribute ("'thread' attribute directive ignored"), so the
exit jmp_buf and its armed flag, g_spurs_job_mbox* and the completion
`draining` flag are plain process-wide globals there. The runtime's other
thread-local macros (PPU_THREAD_LOCAL, SPU_THREAD_LOCAL, SPU_TLS) already
test _MSC_VER.

Change: those four macros use __declspec(thread) only under _MSC_VER and
__thread / _Thread_local otherwise, like the others. MSVC and POSIX builds
are unchanged.

Verification: tools/test_mingw_tls.py finds every macro in runtime/ and
libs/ defined to __declspec(thread), keeps its surrounding preprocessor
conditionals and compiles a static variable with it as MinGW sees it
(x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc when present, else the host compiler with _WIN32
defined and __declspec(x) as __attribute__((x))), then checks the variable
is thread-local in the assembly. Without MinGW gcc the emulation runs only on
ELF hosts and only after two controls (__thread reads as thread-local, a
plain static does not) pass; otherwise, as on macOS, the test prints SKIP. With this change 9/9 qualifiers are
thread-local under both compilers; on v0.14.0 (a2c2010) 4 of 9 are
process-wide globals (spurs_job.c, sys_ppu_thread.c, cellSpurs.c,
cellSysutil.c). The four changed files pass -fsyntax-only with MinGW GCC and
host GCC.

93cccd1d3c5332fff9bd13de773666c816b76198.message:
fp decompiler: honour perspective_corr on texcoord reads

SRC2 bit 31 (perspective_corr) on an instruction's texcoord read
multiplies the input by 1/w, as RPCS3's decompiler does ("Perspective
correct flag multiplies the result by 1/w"). The bit was ignored. A
vertex program that writes uv*w relies on it: inFAMOUS 2's water does,
for the screen copy it samples, and read raw the coordinates land far
outside the copy and the river renders black.

1/w comes from the fragment position. FXC (D3D12) gives SV_POSITION.w as
clip w, but glslang lowers it to SPIR-V FragCoord, whose w is already 1/w
(and Metal's [[position]] is (x, y, z, 1/w)), so the glslang paths define
RSX_FRAGCOORD_W_IS_RCP and the helper picks the right form. The helper is
emitted only when a program uses it, so every other program is
byte-identical.

a4b4a21d8d089e79d28e751c52f433bccc5674ac.message:
sys_spu: an SPU thread starts in the lifted image its own bytes identify

spu_lifted_thread_setup chose the thread's image by asking the registry which image owns the thread's entry point.
SPU programs all start near the same LS addresses (0xD0..0xF0), so two registered images can have code at one entry,
and the entry resolves to whichever registered first: the thread ran the other program's lifted code. SoulCalibur II
HD has two such images, and its audio engine (MultiStream) ran the wrong one.

sys_spu_thread_group_start now fingerprints the thread's sys_spu_image (the lookup the registry fallback right
below it already did) and gives spu_lifted_thread_setup the id of the image registered for those bytes,
spu_lifted_thread_desc.image_id. 0 keeps the lookup by entry point, so a thread whose image is not registered
behaves as before. The fingerprint lookup is one helper now, shared with the fallback.

The test replaces the registry with two images that both have code at 0xD0, A registered first, and follows what group
start does: B's bytes give B (the entry-based lookup, shown by the third check, gives A), A's give A, bytes nothing
registered and a thread without an image give 0. The new interface does not exist on v0.15.0, so the test only
builds with this change.

a594fa06fe400bd0ae86c525bf9b82bad468d526.message:
rsx engine: re-hash cached textures sparsely, in full every eighth frame

Every cached texture was hashed in full at its first use in a frame, to
notice the guest rewriting it. In inFAMOUS 2's New Marais that is about
950 textures and 88 MB a frame, 2.5 ms of the RSX thread, for the four
or so that actually change.

Now each use checks 64 bytes out of every 2 KB plus the last 64, and the
full hash runs when that check differs, when 8 frames have passed since
the entry's last full hash (new entries start staggered by slot, so the
full hashes spread out), always for a texture of 16 KB or less, and on
the next use after a surface store the engine itself made into the
texture. A whole rewrite (video, UI, streaming) is still seen at once; a
small write between the sampled blocks of a large texture can take up
to 7 frames. PS3RECOMP_ENG_TEXHASH_FULL=1 restores the full hash every
frame.

a6cfb0f07fd4226fe6daac59f931e31f3d47e538.message:
cellGcm: the NV3089 row copy takes its source origin as 12.4

IMAGE_IN_POINT is 12.4 fixed point and DS_DX / DT_DY step the source in
20 fractional bits, so the origin enters the copy as origin << 16. The
row copy used << 8, the same mistake as the per-pixel loop it was
written to match, and started at column 0 and row 0 for any origin
under 256 texels. It now uses nv3089_origin(), the helper #358
introduces for the per-pixel loops, defined the same way so the two
changes merge without a conflict.

a98af7c9075a6911d4ec5021a512941cb9f9d11f.message:
cellGcm: get follows the walker across a JUMP

On the RSX, get is the fetch pointer, so a title polling it sees the
GPU leave a command segment as soon as the JUMP out of it is taken.
The walker published get only at the end of a drain pass. On a slow
host that comes tens of milliseconds after the JUMP: Twisted Metal
(BCES01010) has boot-time passes of 50 to 165 ms, mostly NV3089 blits
and surface readbacks.

Twisted Metal flushes put into its other ring segment, then writes the
next frame over the segment it left. When the walker reaches the JUMP
at the old put late, the JUMP has already been overwritten. The title
port works around this by waiting, after its flush, for get to leave
the old put. With get published only at the end of the pass, that wait
ran into its 100 ms bound 4 times per boot even though the JUMP had
been taken at once. With this change it does so 2 times in 12 runs.

A taken JUMP now publishes its target as get. A park (a JUMP to itself)
publishes nothing, and GCM_GET_EQ_PUT keeps its own value.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

did not happen. Twisted Metal resets the flip status, takes about a
second to build its next frame here, and only then queues the flip: a
beat in between set DONE, the title took its new flip for done, and it
rebuilt the command segment the walker was still waiting in.

A flip requested outside the stream (cellGcmSetFlipCommand, or a 0xFEAD
word the drain meets) is now recorded, and the fallback completes that
one, once.

b1f14fff9e8174b3575212691ebdaef7aae069b7.message:
rsx: cache HLSL -> SPIR-V translations, in memory and optionally on disk

glslang takes 20-150 ms per shader, on the thread that walks the FIFO,
and the engine asks for the same HLSL again for every pipeline that
shares a program. Twisted Metal (BCES01010) translates 236 shaders in
its first minute, 74 of them distinct: 4.4 s of glslang per 90 s run,
95 stalls over 20 ms.

rsx_hlsl_to_spirv now keeps each translation, keyed by the stage and the
whole HLSL text, so a hit returns exactly the words that text translated
to. PS3RECOMP_SPIRV_CACHE=<existing directory> also keeps them on disk,
one file per shader; the file stores the key, the glslang version and
the translator's build stamp, and any mismatch is a miss that rewrites
the file. Failed translations are not cached.

Twisted Metal, 90 s runs: glslang time 4.4 s -> 1.1-2.0 s with the
memory cache alone, 5 ms with a warm disk cache, and no translation
over 20 ms.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

b3082644982c43d81c8bf47959317dc4cb3cfbf1.message:
cellGcm: give a parked FIFO time to be patched before following put

A self-JUMP at the write head parks the RSX, and when `put` had meanwhile
moved elsewhere the walker took that as the title having abandoned the park
and resynced to `put` at once. inFAMOUS 2 links its main-memory command
blocks the other way round: it ends a block in a park, writes the next
commands at the ring start, moves `put`, and only then rewrites the park as a
JUMP to them. A drain that landed between the two stores went straight to
`put` and dropped everything from the ring start up to it, the frame's fence
included, so the title waited on that label for the rest of the run and the
main menu froze.

Resync only once the same park has stood with the same `put` for longer than
a title takes between the two stores (50 ms). A park patched in time is
followed as before; the pass reports itself as "parked" in the meantime.

b6dc1e428b4b89c8385595551904bfb21c33d71a.message:
ppu_lifter: jump tables behind a tail-call epilogue

discover_jump_tables drops the blocks that end in `blr` from the backward
scan for the table base register: they return, so they cannot flow into the
dispatcher. An epilogue that leaves by a tail call ends the same way and
restores the same registers, and was not dropped. inFAMOUS 2's func_000B9BD0
loads the base's base into r30 in its prologue, has an early exit
`ld r30,0xE0(r1); ...; b 0xB8570`, and dispatches nineteen instructions later
through `lwz r11,-0x7F80(r30)`: the restore read as r30's nearest definition,
no base resolved, and the switch lifted to an unresolved indirect call.

A `b` leaves the function when it goes back past the function's entry or
forward to another function's entry. Both need func_starts; without them the
scan is bounded by the nearest `blr`, which an early return puts in the
middle of a function, so only `blr` is trusted there.

tools/test_ppu_jumptables.py: the backward shape (the inFAMOUS 2 one), the
forward one, and the no-func_starts control.

b883922940d53efafac47dcc0b63dac7535294c5.message:
rsx_draw_engine, vulkan: honour the depth bounds test

NV4097 SET_DEPTH_BOUNDS_TEST_ENABLE (0x0380) with SET_DEPTH_BOUNDS_MIN and
_MAX (0x0384, 0x0388, floats) rejects a fragment whose stored depth lies
outside the bounds, whatever the depth test says. The draw engine never
read those registers, so a bounded draw covered the whole target.

Twisted Metal's deferred renderer relies on it: its sun pass is bounded to
[0, 0.999984] (the geometry) and the sky drawn right after it to
[0.999984, 1] (the far plane), both with the depth test off. Unbounded, the
sky overwrote the sun light everywhere and the HDR buffer came out almost
black.

The enable is pipeline state (rsx_be_render_state.depth_bounds_test, part
of the pipeline key); the bounds reach the backend before every draw through
a new optional hook, set_depth_bounds, like the stencil reference, so moving
them does not build pipelines. Vulkan enables the depthBounds feature when
the device has it and sets the bounds dynamically, clamped to [0, 1];
without the feature the test stays off, as before, with one log line.
Metal and the fixed-function path leave the hook unset and draw as before.

Tests: test_rsx_draw_engine checks the key, the bounds and that moving them
builds no pipeline (4 new checks, failing without the engine change).
ps3recomp_host --depthbounds draws red at z = 0.25, then blue bounded to
[0, 0.5] and green bounded to [0.5, 1] with the depth test off, and expects
blue; it runs in the Vulkan workflow's engine pass under the validation
layer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

b8a7c5b30057bd863df592edb02e1d4875ca2551.message:
fp decompiler: read FACING, TC8 and TC9

Fragment program inputs 0xC/0xD (TC8/TC9) and 0xE (FACING) read as zero.
Two-sided materials multiply the interpolated normal by FACING; read as
zero, inFAMOUS 2's foliage and character heads normalised a null vector
into the G-buffer and lit black.

FACING is +1 on a front face and -1 on a back face (SV_IsFrontFace,
[[front_facing]] in MSL). TC8/TC9 come from vertex outputs o15 and o6, as
in RPCS3's register table (TEX9 shares the point-size register); the
vertex program and the engine's fixed VS write them after TEXCOORD7, so the
earlier interpolants keep their locations. The fragment side declares
tc8/tc9 and the face flag only when the body reads them, so every other
program is byte-identical and keeps its cached pipeline.

precision: truncation (round toward zero), denormal flush, the extended
range, saturation, frest's hardware table, fi, the compares (fceq/fcgt/
fcmeq/fcmgt) and the conversions (cflts/cfltu/csflt/cuflt). The previous
helpers were a GPL-derived port; these are written from the ISA alone and

  preferred word, mfspr and fscrrd read zero, bisl reads ra before writing

c1cdab11912f442698f32c04fd7a2a64b7a1226b.message:
cellGcm: a flip queued in the command stream completes when the drain reaches it

The 60 Hz tick (cellGcm_request_tick, and cellGcmTickFlip) completed a
pending flip on every beat, wherever the walker was. For a flip queued
into the stream (gcm_flip_into_fifo) that is too early: the RSX flips
when it executes the flip, after everything queued before it.

Twisted Metal (BCES01010) paces itself on the flip status and rebuilds
a command segment once the flip after it is done. Completed early, the
title rewrote segments the walker had not executed yet; the walker then
read half-written segments as commands (JUMPs to float data, unmapped
CALLs, and junk register writes such as the vertex data base offset,
which shattered every later draw's geometry).

Count the flips queued into the stream and the markers the drain
reaches. A beat completes a flip only if the drain has executed a
marker since the last completion, or if no flip is waiting in the
stream (a flip that never went through it). A flip written but not yet
flushed does not hold back one already executed.

A flip must never wait on a marker that will not be executed. A resync
that skips over a marker counts it. When the walker is lost in unmapped
IO and jumps straight to put, every flip still outstanding is written
off: Twisted Metal's boot resyncs that way about one run in three
(get=0x0FD00000) and the flip it abandoned in the other ring segment
otherwise held the status at WAITING for good. reached never passes
queued, so a written-off marker that is executed later is not counted
twice. GCM_FLIP_NEEDS_FIFO keeps its meaning.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

c55ddaa4379c2897d55f337096cb23e0dd2a6c3d.message:
edat: take the klicensee the title passes to sceNpDrmIsAvailable[2]

Symptom: a free (license type 3) or disc-bound EDAT under a title-specific
klicensee fails to open with -6 ("needs a RIF key"), even though the title
supplies its key the way it does on hardware.

Cause: on hardware a title passes its own klicensee to sceNpDrmIsAvailable
or sceNpDrmIsAvailable2 before it opens such a file, and the kernel keeps it
for later opens. The runtime has neither call, so the key is lost, and the
EDAT reader only tries the built-in platform klicensees.

Change: sceNp.c implements sceNpDrmIsAvailable and sceNpDrmIsAvailable2;
both hand a non-NULL klicensee to edat_add_klicensee() (new, edat.h) and
return CELL_OK. edat.c keeps up to 16 such keys, ignores duplicates, and
tries them before the built-in ones. Each key is still checked against the
file's dev_hash (AES-CMAC under klic ^ NP_OMAC_KEY_2 over header bytes
0x00-0x5F, the same check for NPD versions 2-4) before it is used, and each
block hash is checked as before. A license type 3 file that no key verifies
now fails with a message that names sceNpDrmIsAvailable. Projects that read
the key some other way can call edat_add_klicensee() themselves.

Verification: tools/test_edat_guest_klicensee.py builds
libs/filesystem/tests/test_edat_guest_klicensee.c with sceNp.c. The test
writes a synthetic NPD v3 license-3 EDAT (made-up key, content id and data;
three blocks, the last partial) and checks: -6 before any key, -6 after
sceNpDrmIsAvailable2 with a key that does not verify dev_hash, then 0 with
every block hash verified and the plaintext matching after
sceNpDrmIsAvailable with the right key. The runner passes a scratch
directory as argv[1]. On master the fixture does not link (neither call
exists; without them the file stays at -6). With this change all checks
pass; the fixture also builds with x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc and passes under
Wine.

d0d67442f549faf07f8547adcb4fdc6e6dc74c08.message:
spu_channels: MFC engine table 8 -> 64 slots, and a full table is reported as an error

Symptom: intermittent stops where an SPU context waits forever on a DMA
tag that already completed. Killzone 3 holds eleven SPU contexts with an
MFC engine at once (policy-module contexts that keep their engine for as
long as their workload exists, plus SPU thread groups); the runtime prints
"more than 8 contexts hold an MFC engine at once; the rest share one".

Cause: the per-context engine table has SPU_MAX_CONTEXTS = 8 slots. Every
context past the eighth gets one shared fallback engine, where one
context's completion clears the tag bits another context is waiting on.
Eight is a thread group's worth, but a title can hold more contexts at
once than the machine has SPUs. The overflow was reported once, as a note.

Change: 64 slots (overridable with -DSPU_MAX_CONTEXTS). When the table is

growable table can replace this later.

workflows) keeps its 8-thread claim race over 32 rounds and adds: eleven

d9870123ea646d8a9a4ad4cd56342d5bd7c57546.message:
spu_channels: SMC micro-interpreter addresses lqa/stqa at I16 << 2

Symptom: a self-modifying SPU stub that saves and restores registers with
stqa/lqa (a job manager's interrupt save/restore stub, written into the
local store at runtime) stores every register at the wrong address and
overwrites unrelated local-store bytes, including the job's stack.

Cause: spu_smc_microstep computed the absolute local-store address of
lqa/stqa as I16 << 4. For the RI16 form the address is I16 << 2 (SPU ISA),
which is what spu_interp.c and the lifter already use, so every access went
4x too high and wrapped around the local store.

Change: use I16 << 2 in the micro-interpreter, masked to a quadword as
before.

Verification: tools/test_spu_smc_lqa_stqa.py builds the real
spu_smc_microstep with the SPU headers into a host program, writes a stub of
76 stqa (r0..r75 to 0x3F9C0..), a bi, 76 lqa back and a second bi into the
local store, and runs both halves through the micro-interpreter. With this
change all 76 registers land in their own slot, all 76 are restored, and no
local-store byte outside the save area changes. On v0.14.0 (a2c2010) no
register lands in its slot and 1198 bytes outside the save area change.

e310b6619e7fe655631a58e5997dfc197bbd876a.message:
diag: PS3_FTRACE, a frame timeline of who waits for whom

A sampling profile shows where CPU time goes, not why a frame takes
130 ms when no thread is busy for 130 ms. That is a latency chain: the
PPU waits on SPU tasks, the RSX walker waits on a label an SPU writes,
the present waits on the GPU. PS3_FTRACE=<start s>:<seconds>:<file>
records timestamped spans for a window and writes them out as text:

- PPU syscalls that block, with the guest call site; usleep poll runs
  merged per thread and call site;
- SPU busy and channel-wait spans, busy tagged with the lifted image and
  the SPURS workload id at LS 0x1DC;
- RSX FIFO drains, ACQUIRE waits, flips reached and flips requested;
- Metal: presents, CPU encode, GPU waits (present, flush, in-flight bound),
  readbacks, and each command buffer's own GPU time with its render pass,
  depth resolve and colour copy counts.

tools/ftrace_report.py turns a trace into a per-frame breakdown and an
ASCII timeline. The tracer is header-only (include/ps3emu/ps3_ftrace.h):
the hooked files are also built on their own by the self-contained
tests, and a new link dependency would break each of them. Off, each
hook is one load and a branch.

e99cbbf0a9c93d99b9ba43fbd142365f4403ba13.message:
fp decompiler: predicated writes are a select, not a lerp

Symptom: a fragment-program instruction executed under a condition code
(exec_if lt/eq/gt) changes components of its destination that the condition
leaves alone when either operand holds Inf, NaN or raw bits. Programs that
keep packed words in a register (the PK*/UP* pack/unpack pattern) read 0 or
NaN after a predicated MOV.

Cause: the predicated destination write was emitted as
lerp(dst, v, mask). lerp is arithmetic (dst + mask * (v - dst)): an Inf or NaN
in the unselected operand gives NaN (0 * Inf), and denormal and NaN bit
patterns are not preserved through the ALU.

Change: emit a per-component select, (mask != 0.0) ? v : dst, which FXC
compiles to movc. The unconditional path is unchanged.

Verification: libs/video/tests/test_fp_decompiler.c gains a case with a MOV
predicated on CC0 > 0 that checks the select form and that no lerp is
emitted. It fails on master (39 passed, 2 failed) and passes with this change
(41 passed, 0 failed). The same select has been in use in a D3D12 title port
under Proton; there a test with predicated writes over raw-bit and Inf/NaN
operands read 8 of 8 values back correctly, 4 of 8 with lerp.

ef060b373f4f7794caa9bab83528c36f88e5f452.message:
spu: float compares four lanes at a time with SSE2

spu_fceq/fcgt/fcmeq/fcmgt were per-lane loops over 64-bit keys. Compilers
leave them scalar and branchy: on mixed data, fcgt took 41 ns. In Twisted
Metal's post-FX jobs spu_fcgt alone was 3.4% of the job workers' time.

A magnitude is at most 0x7FFFFFFF and its negation fits in 32 bits too, so
the keys compare as int32: clear the magnitude when the exponent is zero
(any two zeros are equal), negate it for a set sign bit, and compare with
pcmpeqd/pcmpgtd. fcgt takes 2.7 ns. The loops stay as spu_*_ref, and
SPU_SCALAR_HELPERS still selects them. SSE2 is in every x86-64 build
(__SSE2__, or _M_X64 for MSVC, which does not define __SSE2__).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

efef265f81209865b56cd7d9eee577577a2cd2b2.message:
cellHttp: response getters under their SDK names; RecvResponse into guest memory

Symptom: a title that reads an HTTP answer through
cellHttpResponseGetStatusCode, cellHttpResponseGetContentLength and
cellHttpResponseGetAllHeaders gets CELL_OK with the status unset and a NULL
header array, and drops every response. A body that outgrows the header read
is recv()'d into the host address equal to the guest buffer's EA (recv fails
with EFAULT, or writes into host memory).

Cause: the runtime has cellHttpGetStatusCode and
cellHttpGetResponseContentLength, whose computed NIDs match no firmware
import, and no cellHttpResponseGetAllHeaders, so the three imports take the
unresolved-NID path. In cellHttpRecvResponse the overflow copy translates
the guest buffer but the socket read does not.

Change: add cellHttpResponseGetStatusCode, cellHttpResponseGetContentLength
(0x80710017 when the response has no Content-Length) and
cellHttpResponseGetAllHeaders ({name, value} guest pointers followed by the
strings in the caller's pool; a size query with no pool writes only
*required; a pool too small returns NO_BUFFER). Titles call them before the
first cellHttpRecvResponse, so they read the headers first. The older
functions keep their names. cellHttpRecvResponse recv()s into the
translated guest buffer.

Verification: tools/test_http_response_getters.py builds
libs/network/tests/test_http_response_getters.c against a loopback
listener: a 200 answer with three headers and a 3000-byte body of which
only 100 bytes arrive with the headers, then a response without
Content-Length. On master: 4 failed (the three getters missing; the body
stops at 100 bytes, recv() error); with this change all 13 checks pass.

f02f33881482556da07ecc3703429a68e5683cf6.message:
metal engine: PS3_ANISO turns on anisotropic filtering for mipmapped samplers

PS3 titles rarely ask for anisotropic filtering, and at 720p that was a
fair trade. At a Mac's output size, ground and walls seen at a grazing
angle blur into their smaller mips a few metres from the camera.

PS3_ANISO=2..16 sets maxAnisotropy on the engine samplers that minify
linearly through a mip chain. Point-filtered and unmipped samplers keep
their filtering, so lookup tables, render targets and UI read the same
texels as before. Unset, nothing changes.

The new --mip-aniso host check draws --mip's two-level texture under a
quad stretched along y: isotropic filtering lands on level 1, anisotropic
filtering on level 0. CI runs it with PS3_ANISO=16 and requires it to
fail without.

f110c349c230521f60cb5f27f7449fd90144e779.message:
cellSaveData: UserAutoSave keeps its ninth argument; handlers registered at init

Symptom: a title that saves with cellSaveDataUserAutoSave gets
cbResult->userdata == 0 in its stat and file callbacks. A title that keeps
its save state behind userdata writes through a null pointer and saves an
empty profile.

Cause: cellSaveDataUserAutoSave takes nine arguments; the ninth (userdata)
is in the caller's parameter save area at SP+112. UserAutoLoad already has
a context handler that reads it, UserAutoSave has none, and nothing in the
runtime calls cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers(), so both calls go through
the generic eight-argument binding unless a project registers the handlers
itself.

Change: a context handler for cellSaveDataUserAutoSave (NID 0x52AAC4FA),
the same as UserAutoLoad's, registered in
cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers(). It calls cellSaveDataAutoSave rather
than AutoSave2: AutoSave2 maps dirName to a host pointer and hands it to
AutoSave, which maps it again, so a host address below 4 GiB (seen on
Windows) would be read as a guest address. ppu_sysprx_register() now calls
cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers() next to np_score_register_ctx(), so
every project gets both handlers. A project that already calls it keeps
working: the first registration of a NID wins and both point at the same
handler.

Verification: tools/test_savedata_user_autosave.py checks that
ppu_sysprx_register() calls cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers(), then
builds libs/system/tests/test_savedata_user_autosave.c, which registers the
handlers into a local table and calls UserAutoLoad and UserAutoSave with a
userdata value at SP+112; the runner passes a scratch save root as argv[1].
On master: 2 failed (no call from
ppu_sysprx_register, no handler for 0x52AAC4FA; UserAutoLoad passes). With
this change all checks pass. test_savedata_fixed.c and test_savedata_io.c
still pass. The fixture also builds with x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc and passes
under Wine.

fa001d0711cdc3852280a0cd52afd7ae70b5dc26.message:
cellGcmSys: a late flip completion no longer marks a newer flip done

The ticker marks a flip completion pending, but the flip handler (and
the DONE status with it) only runs when a guest thread next pumps. If
the title requested another flip in between, the late completion set
DONE over the new request; the ticker only completes WAITING flips, so
that flip's handler never ran. cellGcmSetWaitFlip did the same after its
64 ms bound. inFAMOUS 2 writes its next FIFO put from the flip handler
and hung with get == put on either path.

Each request now bumps a sequence number, the tick records the one it
completes, and the completion only marks DONE when no newer request has
arrived. The read-modify-write transitions run on different threads and
take a small spin lock. cellGcmSetWaitFlip leaves an outstanding flip to
the tick instead of forcing it DONE.

fcea4f992c195a643ebcb6b26ee16f13b9d1d91c.message:

as the hardware does. Simpsons Arcade (NPUB30563) then reads its data from
/dev_hdd0/game/NPUB30563/USRDIR, which mapped to an empty <root>/game/<id>,
and lost every asset read and its save load (gate: 16 regressions, bisected
to #359). On a miss there, the VFS fallback now tries <root>/PS3_GAME/.
Only for an HDD title: for a disc title that directory is the update dir.

ff66a35553268c34c77b3def3adf53b3222f8446.message:
cellGcm: an unscaled NV3089 blit copies a row at a time

The 2D blit copied pixel by pixel through vm_read32/vm_write32, paying
per pixel the bounds and null-store checks, the store hooks, a
reservation lookup and two byte swaps that cancel. inFAMOUS 2 copies its
1280x720 G-buffer surfaces to main memory with NV3089 every frame for
its SPU lighting, and a quarter of the FIFO thread's time went there.

A blit with a 1:1 scale now moves each clipped row with one memmove,
and does the coherent-store bookkeeping per 128-byte line: an SPU
holding a reservation on a line the row overwrites loses it, as with a
PPU store. Scaled blits keep the per-pixel loop. NV3089_ROWCOPY=0
restores the per-pixel copy (which is what the PPU store watches see).

ff7c9eef28c375793946f4bc58a48db3794afea6.message:
spu: update a task's signalled bit atomically against SPU commits

spu_taskset_signal_task and spu_taskset_wait_signal set and clear the
task's bit in the taskset's signalled bitset with a vm_read32 then a
vm_write32. SPU tasks update the same line with GETLLAR/PUTLLC, under
the lock-line lock. The store took that lock, the read did not, so an
SPU commit between the two was overwritten with the stale word.

Twisted Metal (BCES01010) loses a wake this way in its post-FX taskset.
Six tasks meet at a cellSpursBarrier. The last one to arrive sets each
waiter's bit with PUTLLC. When task 3's host thread woke and cleared its
own bit, it wrote back a word read just before the releaser set task
4's bit. Task 4 slept forever, so the barrier never completed again,
the render thread waited on the tasks' completion word, and the frame
label the RSX acquires stopped after two frames.

Do the read-modify-write under the lock-line lock, on the raw guest
bytes (vm_write32 takes the lock itself and it does not nest), and
drop every reservation on the line.

Measured on Twisted Metal, 120 s on Vulkan: 12 post-FX signals then a
permanent stall before, 7116 signals at a steady ~10 frames/s after.

community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development

on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

ps3recomp: even presents, the system clock

Fork 8b9a035 and 480da8d.

The clock: the slot list showed a save of October 2026 as made in
December 1933. On Windows the game was told the time since the PC was
started in place of the time since 1970, and on every platform the call
for the time zone did not exist, so the game's C library shifted that by
whatever its variables held. Both are the host's now. The date is kept
inside the save (a 64-bit count of seconds at +0x48 of PAYLOAD; the save
at hand holds 348,789, four days), so a save made before this shows the
5th of January 1970 until the game writes it again. PS3_TIME_LOG=1, in
the debugging guide, prints what the game was told.

The pacer (rsx_present_pace) does nothing until a host turns it on; the
next commit does. It is a new source file in the fork, so CMake has to
run again on an existing build folder. No re-lift is needed.
