ff66a35553268c34c77b3def3adf53b3222f8446.message:
cellGcm: an unscaled NV3089 blit copies a row at a time

The 2D blit copied pixel by pixel through vm_read32/vm_write32, paying
per pixel the bounds and null-store checks, the store hooks, a
reservation lookup and two byte swaps that cancel. inFAMOUS 2 copies its
1280x720 G-buffer surfaces to main memory with NV3089 every frame for
its SPU lighting, and a quarter of the FIFO thread's time went there.

A blit with a 1:1 scale now moves each clipped row with one memmove,
and does the coherent-store bookkeeping per 128-byte line: an SPU
holding a reservation on a line the row overwrites loses it, as with a
PPU store. Scaled blits keep the per-pixel loop. NV3089_ROWCOPY=0
restores the per-pixel copy (which is what the PPU store watches see).

ff7c9eef28c375793946f4bc58a48db3794afea6.message:
spu: update a task's signalled bit atomically against SPU commits

spu_taskset_signal_task and spu_taskset_wait_signal set and clear the
task's bit in the taskset's signalled bitset with a vm_read32 then a
vm_write32. SPU tasks update the same line with GETLLAR/PUTLLC, under
the lock-line lock. The store took that lock, the read did not, so an
SPU commit between the two was overwritten with the stale word.

Twisted Metal (BCES01010) loses a wake this way in its post-FX taskset.
Six tasks meet at a cellSpursBarrier. The last one to arrive sets each
waiter's bit with PUTLLC. When task 3's host thread woke and cleared its
own bit, it wrote back a word read just before the releaser set task
4's bit. Task 4 slept forever, so the barrier never completed again,
the render thread waited on the tasks' completion word, and the frame
label the RSX acquires stopped after two frames.

Do the read-modify-write under the lock-line lock, on the raw guest
bytes (vm_write32 takes the lock itself and it does not nest), and
drop every reservation on the line.

Measured on Twisted Metal, 120 s on Vulkan: 12 post-FX signals then a
permanent stall before, 7116 signals at a steady ~10 frames/s after.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   └── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse
│   ├── hardware/             # cellGem, cellCamera, cellUsbd
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
└── docs/                     # See the Documentation table below
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

HLE implementations of the PS3 system libraries, written for this project. RPCS3 is a behavioural reference, not a code source. **About 93 modules complete and 5 partial** (media decode, SPURS), in roughly 260 files and 100,000 lines under `libs/`.

a0622e0112512f8b8292a091d0790c86d3ab77b9.message:
M0.38: BATCHJOB 22/21 stall fixed - PM workload argument passed big-endian

The policy-module emulation copied the low half of the 64-bit workload
argument into both word 0 and word 1 of r4. GoW:A's wwsjob PM takes the job
list header from word 1 and an optional per-SPU status area from word 0; with
the header in word 0 it wrote status rows at header+0x130, inside
BatchJobList's list 1, so a 7-job list read a garbage 8th entry and the batch
wait counted 22 of 21 forever. SPURS_PM_ARG_BE=1 (port default) passes the
argument as the hardware does. No stall in a 1600 s run (4 of 4 before).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

d97d966584f428a991017857706472fe8d93eb55.message:
M0.26: give each SPU context its own MFC engine (fixes the varying stops)

mfc_for() kept 8 MFC engine slots keyed by context pointer, and job, task
and policy-module contexts never released theirs, so right after boot every
later context shared one fallback engine. One context's parked
stall-and-notify list then held another context's tag incomplete; a WWS
policy module spun on that tag wait and, because the port runs a SPURS
instance's modules on one host thread, every workload stopped (EDGE holes,
shapes B and D). spu_coh_unregister now releases the engine, a fresh PM
context releases it too, and the table has 64 slots with a per-thread cache.
A 560 s run reached 3020 flips with no stall.

Also: SPU_ATOM_EA takes up to 4 lines plus SPU_ATOM_PUTONLY; the [pm-hang]
report shows tag mask/status and parked lists; CreateTask logs a claim
failure.

d99c2c7b2534ec178994c1e0a26add77a49e1e51.message:
Graphics: blend constants and sub-rectangle textures (bloom, decals, shadow rectangles)

Two causes behind graphics bugs of the 2026-11-10 played session, both
fixed in the toolkit patch:

* The Vulkan backend mapped the constant blend factors (0x8001-0x8004) to
  ONE and never read SET_BLEND_COLOR. The game weights its bloom passes
  and fades floor decals with them. VK_BLEND_CONST=0 = old mapping.
* A texture declaring less than the target at its address got the whole
  target. The four shadow cascades share one depth target, so two of them
  added nothing to the shadow mask and left stepped rectangles on floors;
  a half-size colour pass read both halves of its source. RSX_SUBRECT_TEX=0
  = old behaviour.

STATUS.md has what was measured and what was not verified; DEBUGGING.md
has how a pass dump was read to find them.

f3f31f525182d926a86d6654b55c573f163e06e9.message:
M0.36: colour pass restored - SPU float helpers follow SPU rules (no NaN/Inf)

EDGE's triangle culler (geometry module 0xD618, used by colour/static jobs)
folds masks in with `fnms rt, mask, 0xFFFFFFFF, rc`. On the SPU 0xFFFFFFFF is
an extended-range number and 0 times it is 0; with host IEEE floats it was
NaN, `gb` saw bit 1 and every triangle was culled, so the colour pass was
never emitted. Single-precision helpers now treat exponent 255 as ordinary,
flush denormals, saturate and truncate (fast path kept for ordinary normals).
The menu cinematic and title screen now render.

Also: diagnostics SPU_DMA_EA_T0/_PC/_GETDUMP, SPU_LIST_EA (GETL elements),
SPU_BRTRACE, SPU_ITRACE, SPU_FORCE_BR; docs corrected (M0.35c "reads only

1427034372.readme_excerpt:
# God of War: Ascension — static recompilation (PS3)

> **Status: research / early bring-up. Not playable.** The game boots, plays its intro movies, shows the main menu
> with text and music, and runs the first level with the Vulkan backend at about 16-18 game frames per second in the
> corridor on a quiet host (about 14-15 with other programs busy; the game is very sensitive to CPU load) on a
> 6-core CPU with an RTX 3080, with no hangs in 25-minute runs. Nothing past the first corridor fight has been run yet. Where the time
> goes and what is being worked on is in [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md). Generic fixes go upstream to ps3recomp
> as small PRs. Contributions are welcome: see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

![Kratos chained in the first level, rendered by the recompiled game on Vulkan](docs/screenshots/level.jpg)

An attempt to statically recompile *God of War: Ascension* (PS3, `BCUS98232`) into a native Windows executable,
built on top of the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) toolkit (PPU lifter, SPU lifter,
HLE runtime, Vulkan/D3D12 RSX backends).

**This repository contains no game data, no firmware and no code derived from them.** You need your own legally
acquired copy of the game and (optionally) your own PS3 firmware dump. See [docs/LEGAL.md](docs/LEGAL.md).

| Main menu (text, music) | Intro movie (MPEG-2 through cellVdec) |
|---|---|
| ![Main menu](docs/screenshots/main-menu.jpg) | ![Intro movie](docs/screenshots/intro.jpg) |

Captured from the port's own Vulkan output (`PS3RECOMP_VK_DUMP`) on 2026-10-20, at 1280x720.

## What lives here

| Path | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `port/` | The game-specific port: `CMakeLists.txt`, `main.cpp` (runner), `stubs.cpp` (hooks), `lle_libsre.cpp` (optional firmware-SPURS LLE glue), `config.toml` |
| `patches/` | Patch against upstream ps3recomp (fixes and diagnostics found while bringing the game up) — meant to be upstreamed |
| `spu/images.json` | Description of the SPU images lifted for this title (policy module, SPURS kernel, ...) |
| `analysis/` | Python tools used to measure the binary (carving SPU blobs, PSARC TOC, xrefs, `findstore.py`, `make_spu_port.py`) |
| `scripts/` | Windows build helpers (`GOW_ROOT`-relative) |
| `launcher/` | Player launcher (Python/Tk): paths, setup check, play/stop with logs, save backups |
| `docs/` | Feasibility study (pt-BR), architecture notes, debugging playbook, related work, legal |
| `local/` | **Git-ignored.** Your game dump, decrypted ELF, firmware, lifted C++, toolchains, logs |

## Quick start

See [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md). In short: dump your disc, decrypt `EBOOT.BIN` to an ELF, run the
ps3recomp loader/lifter on it, apply `patches/`, configure with `scripts/cfg.bat`, build with `scripts/build.bat`,
run `MyGameRecomp.exe <path>/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf`.

## Playing

Once you have a build, `scripts\launch.bat` (or `python launcher\gow_launcher.py`) opens the launcher. Point it at
your `MyGameRecomp.exe` and your `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf`, press **Check setup**, then **Play**. It keeps a log
per run in `launcher/logs/`, can skip the intro movie, and backs up / restores your saves to `launcher/backups/`.
Every option maps to a runtime environment variable shown in its tooltip; see [launcher/README.md](launcher/README.md).

## Related projects

See [docs/RELATED_PROJECTS.md](docs/RELATED_PROJECTS.md): ps3recomp and its game ports, RPCS3 (used as an oracle),
XenonRecomp / UnleashedRecomp, N64: Recompiled, and others.

## License

The original work here (`port/`, `analysis/`, `scripts/`, `spu/`, `docs/` and the changes in `patches/`) is
[MIT](LICENSE): keep the copyright notice and please link back here. It builds on
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) (MIT) by its authors. Game assets, firmware and anything lifted
from them are **not** covered and must never be committed.

God of War is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment LLC. This is a fan research project, not affiliated with
or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Santa Monica Studio.

# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível, mas ainda lento (~9 fps). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot ao primeiro nível:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal e o primeiro nível, com o Kratos acorrentado. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~28 fps; o primeiro nível ainda roda a ~9 fps. O limite é o código das SPUs recompilado, não a placa de vídeo. - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo, controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md). ## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), abra o launcher: ```powershell .\scripts\windows\launcher.ps1 ```

JOGAR abre o jogo dentro da própria janela do launcher. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

Crash report for an end that raises no exception; the log flushed first

abort(), std::terminate, the C runtime's invalid-argument and pure-call
checks end the process in a fast fail the exception filter never sees: the
game closed with no [crash] line, and a log on disk lost its last 200 ms of
buffered lines with it -- the shape of issue 3's log, which stops mid-boot.

too now, not only stderr. One abort() the port has is the lifted libsre

the zlib tasks use while the boot loads its packages.

ps3recomp: even presents, the system clock

Fork 8b9a035 and 480da8d.

The clock: the slot list showed a save of October 2026 as made in
December 1933. On Windows the game was told the time since the PC was
started in place of the time since 1970, and on every platform the call
for the time zone did not exist, so the game's C library shifted that by
whatever its variables held. Both are the host's now. The date is kept
inside the save (a 64-bit count of seconds at +0x48 of PAYLOAD; the save
at hand holds 348,789, four days), so a save made before this shows the
5th of January 1970 until the game writes it again. PS3_TIME_LOG=1, in
the debugging guide, prints what the game was told.

The pacer (rsx_present_pace) does nothing until a host turns it on; the
next commit does. It is a new source file in the fork, so CMake has to
run again on an existing build folder. No re-lift is needed.

Frame rate: a cap is shown at even intervals, and Adaptive

The camera juddered at any frame rate, with a controller as with the
mouse. The camera's own law holds frame by frame (the turn is what the
stick and the frame's time say it should be); what was uneven was the
time each frame stayed on screen.

Capped: the game's frames are exactly 16.67 ms of simulation at 60, but
they were presented 13 to 20 ms apart. The renderer's pacer (fork
8b9a035) is turned on whenever a cap is in force, and told the cap's
period: at 60, 1 to 7% of the presents are now more than 15% off the one
before, against 40 to 65%.

Uncapped: the frames take 5 to 20 ms each, half of them more than 15%
off the one before, and each is simulated for the time the last one
took, so a steady turn comes out at 60 to 210 degrees a second from
frame to frame. There is no slack to pace that in. DOD3_FPS=adaptive
(Frame Rate: Adaptive on the Graphics Settings page) is a cap that
follows the scene: the highest of 120, 110, 100, 90, 80, 72, 66, 60, 55,
50, 45, 40, 36, 33, 30 at which 95 in 100 of the last second and a
half's frames were made in time with 4% to spare. It steps down at once
and up after two seconds within reach, so it stays put for long
stretches and the pacer can do its work. In a played session it sat at
120 with 0 to 2% of the presents more than 15% off the one before (the
arrivals: 44 to 53%); on a loaded machine, about 3% at 60 to 70 where
uncapped averaged 115 to 120 on paper.

DOD3_FPS_ADAPT=<quantile>,<margin>,<seconds> and DOD3_FPS_ADAPT_LOG=1
are in the debugging guide with RSX_PRESENT_PACE_LOG.

Not measured: v-sync on with a cap that does not divide the display's
refresh rate.

d7812558337fdf7ce50429ba1ef31f253c0fc7be.message:
Draw Distance and Tree Detail

Two rows on the Advanced Graphics page, for the scenery that appears in
front of the player in the open areas.

Draw Distance (DOD3_DRAW_DISTANCE = 2, 3, 5, 10): the engine's
MaxDrawDistanceScale, which the scene renderer multiplies every
primitive's own cull distance by each frame. Live. It moves the props,
bushes and small trees that have such a distance.

Tree Detail (DOD3_TREE_LOD = 2, 3, 5, 10): the SpeedTrees have four
distances of their own (the model's detail from 500 to 6,000 units, the
flat billboard from 8,000, nothing past 12,000 to 16,000 for most trees
of the first chapter's coast), which the draw distance does not reach.
They are copied into the tree's scene proxy when it is made, and read
from there once, as the tree's meshes are put in the draw lists. So the
proxy's are multiplied as it is made: USpeedTreeComponent::
CreateSceneProxy (func_00817FD4, a virtual and the constructor's only
caller) is replaced in the function registry. Trees already in the
scene keep what they were added with -- writing a live proxy changes
nothing on screen, which is why earlier attempts at this from outside
showed nothing -- so the row says "from the next area".

Checked in three runs to the same spot on the coast's landing stage:
at 0.2 the woods on either side are gone, at 1 the pines on the cliff
are their soft billboards, at 3 they are their models and a tree past
the far bank is drawn that was not. And set from the page itself to 3
before the level was loaded: all 64 trees' proxies hold three times
their components' distances.

What still appears late is what the game has not loaded yet: the further
parts of a level are streamed in as the player nears them.

1.01 only (the addresses are not mapped for 1.00, where the tree row is
left out). No re-lift is needed.

da6a1a510cf4d30c0393f7f16a17add079c3a177.message:
Aspect Ratio: the HUD fitted into the view; 16:10; movies and the title as on that screen

In a view boxed to another shape the HUD's canvas is the view's: moved to
its corner and as big as it is. The HUD lays itself out on 1280x720 whatever
the canvas, so at 21:9 it ran off the bottom of the view. Now
Sqex03GameHUD.DrawHUD hands its canvas to the port (bridge 17) and
src/patches/hud_aspect.cpp makes the canvas's top transform a scale and a
move that put the 16:9 HUD in the middle of the view, as big as fits; the
canvas reports 1280x720 meanwhile, as the HUD's native code places some
things by its size. The markers placed on the view (enemy gauges, lock-on,
talk icons) are mapped back through it in hooks on UCanvas::execProject and
ASqex03GameHUD::CalcTransformPosition, so they stay on their targets. The
30 full-screen layers of the HUD's scripts -- fades, dimming, filters, the
dying overlay, the screen-split effect -- are marked by the script patch and
cover the whole view. A narrower view's room above and below the HUD is
clipped (through the depth, the 2D canvas having no depth test): the HUD
keeps a bar parked above itself there.

The HUD's begin also tells the present the view's shape each frame, and the
setting the screen's (ps3recomp: rsx_present_set_screen_aspect), so that
the title, menus and movies are 16:9 in the middle of that screen: a 16:9
window set to 21:9 shows what a 21:9 screen would.

16:10 is a choice of the setting (and auto takes a window narrower than
16:9): the view keeps its FOV and is taller. The fit only runs when the
setting has boxed the view, so 16:9 is as it was.

1.00 keeps the HUD as it was (the hooks' addresses are 1.01's) and gets the
present's half. Replay regression: 110 of 110 frames identical.

1427200103.readme_excerpt:
# Drakengard 3 Recompiled

A native PC port of **Drakengard 3** (Drag-On Dragoon 3, PlayStation 3,
BLUS31197) for Windows and macOS, made by static recompilation of the game's
code on the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) toolkit.

The game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C++ ahead of time and built
into a normal executable, with the PS3's system libraries replaced by native
implementations and the RSX graphics by Direct3D 12, Metal or Vulkan. There
is no emulation at run time.

![The start of the game, running natively on Windows](docs/images/opening.jpg)

**Nothing of the game is in this repository.** You need your own copy of
Drakengard 3: the US disc and the game's 1.01 update, plus whatever DLC you
own. The installer takes them from there.

If this helped you, consider [buying me a coffee](https://ko-fi.com/soyjack)

## Installing

What you need:

- A PC with Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), a GPU with Direct3D 12 and a CPU with
  AVX2 (Intel Haswell / AMD Zen or newer), or a Mac with Apple silicon on
  macOS 13 or newer. About 16 GB of free disk space, 10 GB more for the
  Japanese voice pack.
- Your disc, US release (BLUS31197), dumped to a folder or a **decrypted**
  `.iso` ([PS3 Disc Dumper](https://github.com/13xforever/ps3-disc-dumper)
  writes one; an image from an ordinary disc tool is still encrypted and is
  refused, as are other regions).
- The 1.01 update, as the package a PlayStation 3 downloads:
  `UP0082-BLUS31197_00-DOD3PATCH0000000-A0101-V0101-PE.pkg`.
- Optionally, the DLC packages you own (`UP0082-NPUB31251_00-...`). No
  licence files are needed.

Windows:

1. Download `dod3-recomp-<version>-win64.zip` from the
   [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) and unzip it
   anywhere (not inside Program Files).
2. Run `dod3.exe`. SmartScreen may warn the first time, as the program is not
   signed: "More info", then "Run anyway".
3. In the setup that opens, add your files (the disc image or folder, the
   update package, any DLC packages) with Add Files / Add Folder, in any
   order, then Install. The game's files are copied into the `game` folder
   next to `dod3.exe` (a few minutes).
4. Start Game.

macOS:

1. Download `dod3-recomp-<version>-macos-arm64.zip` from the
   [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases), unzip it and
   move "Drakengard 3 Recompiled.app" to Applications.
2. The app is not notarised, so macOS refuses it the first time. On macOS 15
   and later: open it once, then allow it in System Settings > Privacy &
   Security ("Open Anyway"). On macOS 13 and 14: Control-click the app,
   choose Open, then Open again.
3. The setup opens as on Windows. The game's files go into
   `~/Library/Application Support/Drakengard 3 Recompiled`.

Settings (resolution, display mode, frame-rate cap, anti-aliasing, field of
view, draw distance, skipping the intro) are in the game's own Settings
menu, under Graphics Settings, System Settings and Advanced Graphics, or in
`dod3.ini`.
[docs/PLAYING.md](docs/PLAYING.md) has the controls, the saves, the Japanese
voices, and what to do if something goes wrong.

## Building

The port is built in three steps: the game's PPU code is lifted to C++, its
SPU programs are lifted, and the whole is compiled with CMake. Lifting needs
the game's executable, so you need your own copy of the game first.

1. **Toolchain.** Windows: Visual Studio 2022 or newer (the Build Tools are
   enough, with "Desktop development with C++" and the Windows SDK), LLVM
   with clang-cl, CMake 3.20 or later, Ninja, Python 3.11 or later, Git for
   Windows, and vcpkg with `zlib:x64-windows` and `sdl2:x64-windows`
   (`VCPKG_ROOT`, or `C:\vcpkg`). macOS: Xcode's command-line tools and,
   from Homebrew, `cmake ninja python zlib sdl2 glslang spirv-cross`.

2. **The sources.**

   ```sh
   git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp
   cd dod3-recomp
   python3 -m venv .venv                    # py -3 -m venv .venv on Windows
   .venv/bin/pip install -r ps3recomp/tools/requirements.txt -r tools/requirements.txt
   ```

3. **The game's files.** Any built `dod3` (a release's, or one from another
   machine) installs the game into the repository root, which decrypts the
   update's executable to `elf/EBOOT_101.ELF` and lays out `game/disc`:

   ```sh
   DOD3_INSTALL_BASE=. path/to/dod3 --install <disc .iso or folder> <update .pkg> [DLC .pkg ...]
   ```

4. **Lift the PPU code** (a few minutes; about 550 MB of C++ in
   `recompiled_101/`):

   ```sh
   .venv/bin/python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_loader.py elf/EBOOT_101.ELF -o out/v101/
   .venv/bin/python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_lifter.py elf/EBOOT_101.ELF \
       --functions out/v101/EBOOT_101.functions.json \
       --hle-stubs out/v101/EBOOT_101.imports.json \
       --code-end 0x157fc00 \
       --nonvolatile-locals \
       --hook 0x000C1E50 --hook 0x00EE7728 --hook 0x00272E58 \
       -o recompiled_101/
   ```

5. **Lift the SPU programs** into `spu/`, with the native fast paths hooked
   in:

   ```sh
   tools/lift_spu.sh
   ```

6. **Compile.** Windows, from a plain command prompt (the script finds
   Visual Studio, LLVM, CMake and vcpkg):

   ```bat
   tools\build_win.bat
   ```

   macOS:

   ```sh
   cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
   cmake --build build
   ```

   A clean build takes about 15 minutes, nearly all of it the lifted code.

7. **Run** the game installed in the repository root:

   ```sh
   DOD3_INSTALL_BASE=. build/dod3
   ```

[docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md) has the CMake options, the developer
run form, packaging a release and regenerating the committed tables;
[docs/TECHNICAL.md](docs/TECHNICAL.md) how the port works;
[docs/DEBUGGING.md](docs/DEBUGGING.md) the switches, profiling and the
regression tests; [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) the layout of the tree
and the conventions.

## Status

| | |
|---|---|
| Windows 10/11, Direct3D 12 | Playable. 60 fps at 4K on an RTX 4090 / i9-13900K (chapter 1 through the heavy destruction scene, open areas, the village); 120 fps holds at lower resolutions |
| Windows, Vulkan | Experimental (`RSX_BACKEND = vulkan`) |
| macOS 13+, Apple silicon, Metal | Playable. 60 fps at 1080p in battle on an M1 Pro |
| Game version | The 1.01 update (required) |
| DLC | All 20 packs, including the Japanese voice pack |

What the port adds over the original: any internal resolution (supersampling
included), windowed, borderless or full-screen display, a frame-rate cap of
your choice (60 and 120 tested) or one that follows the scene, with the
frames shown at even intervals, FXAA or MSAA, anisotropic filtering, a wider
field of view, sharper shadows, a longer draw distance for scenery and for
trees, skipping the intro logos and movie, and pausing or muting when the
window is in the background -- all from a Graphics Settings, a System
Settings and an Advanced Graphics page added to the game's own Settings menu.

Known issues: the game has been tested on few machines.

## How it fits together

```
elf/EBOOT_101.ELF  --ppu_loader/ppu_lifter-->  recompiled_101/*.cpp  (the game's PPU code as C++)
SPU programs       --tools/lift_spu.sh------>  spu/                  (SPURS tasks, jobs, the audio DSP)
src/               --------------------------->  the port: the runner, native fast paths, the settings menu, the installer
ps3recomp/         --------------------------->  runtime, HLE libraries, the RSX draw engine and its backends
```

The executable `dod3` installs the game from your files (a Dear ImGui
installer, `src/install/` and `src/ui/`) and runs it.

## Legal

This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Square Enix, Access Games
or Sony Interactive Entertainment. Drakengard 3 and all of its assets belong
to their owners; none are included, and the port only runs from a copy of the
game you own.

The code in this repository is under the [MIT License](LICENSE). It builds on
ps3recomp (MIT) and includes Dear ImGui (MIT); see
[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

## Credits

- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet: the
  recompiler, the runtime and the PS3 library implementations. This port's
  changes to it are in the [soyjxck/ps3recomp](https://github.com/soyjxck/ps3recomp)
  fork, the `ps3recomp/` submodule.
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net): the reference for much of the PS3's behaviour,
  and the source of two techniques used here (write-watched texture memory,
  a guest clock that stops while the game is paused).
- [XenonRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/XenonRecomp) and
  [Unleashed Recompiled](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp): the
  model for a recompiled port, and for its installer.
- [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui) by Omar Cornut: the
  installer's user interface.

1427566696.readme_excerpt:
# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível, mas ainda lento (~9 fps). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot ao primeiro nível:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal e o primeiro nível, com o Kratos acorrentado. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~28 fps; o primeiro nível ainda roda a ~9 fps. O limite é o código das SPUs recompilado, não a placa de vídeo. - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo, controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md). ## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), abra o launcher: ```powershell .\scripts\windows\launcher.ps1 ```

JOGAR abre o jogo dentro da própria janela do launcher. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível, mas ainda lento (~16-17 fps). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot ao primeiro nível:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal e o primeiro nível, com o Kratos acorrentado. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~30 fps; o primeiro nível a ~16-17 fps (era ~9). O limite é o código das SPUs recompilado, não a placa de vídeo: o job de geometria por draw (módulo 218) é o maior custo, e está sendo reescrito como código nativo, validado contra jobs gravados do jogo, sem precisar rodá-lo. - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo, controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md). ## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), abra o launcher: ```powershell .\scripts\windows\launcher.ps1 ```

JOGAR abre o jogo dentro da própria janela do launcher. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

cdb581579fd7ba76d429fab741828ce9e04161d6.message:
Low-CPU update: fewer threads on weaker PCs, support for CPUs without AVX2

- SPURS: on PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the lanes/kernels spin less, wake the
  main thread sooner and run on fewer threads (4-thread PCs: ~10 fps -> ~29 fps,
  8 threads: ~38 -> ~50 fps). Big PCs keep the old behaviour.
- Vertex workers spin far less after each job, fewer workers on small CPUs.
- The once-per-second thread scan only walks the game's own threads.
- No exclusive core reservations on PCs with fewer than 20 CPU threads;
  P-core pinning only on hybrid CPUs with at least 8 P-core threads.
- CPUs without AVX2/FMA/BMI2 (pre-2013 Intel, AVX-less Pentium/Celeron, AMD before
  2015): Setup/the updater detect this and build an SSE4.1 compatibility version
  automatically (same results, slower). The game also checks the CPU at startup and
  shows a clear message instead of crashing.

1427668959.readme_excerpt:
# inFamous PC

> **Official repo: [github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn).**
> Only download the Setup from the [Releases page](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn/releases) here.
> Forks are not supported, and bugs from forks won't be fixed.

An unofficial native Windows port of **inFamous** (PlayStation 3, 2009, European
release `BCES00220`). The game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code is statically
recompiled to x86-64 C/C++ with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp),
so it runs as a normal Windows program rather than under an emulator.

**This repository contains no game code or data.** You build the game yourself,
on your own PC, from your own copy of the game.

## Easy install

Download **inFamous Setup.exe** from the latest release, run it, choose your
`.iso` (an encrypted image works with its `.dkey` next to it) or your game
folder (the one with `PS3_GAME` in it), pick an install location and press
**Install**.

Setup checks for Python and the C++ build tools and offers to install them,
copies the game out of the disc image, regenerates the recompiled code from your
copy, builds it and adds an inFamous shortcut. Running Setup again on the same
folder updates or repairs the install and only redoes what changed.

## Updating

When a new version is published here, players update in place instead of reinstalling:
**Update now** in Setup (it finds the existing install), the **Update inFamous** shortcut in
the Start menu, or `Update inFamous.cmd` in the install folder. The updater compares every file
with this repository, downloads only what changed, regenerates the game code only if the
port's patches changed, and recompiles only the affected parts. Installs made with an older
Setup need one run of the new Setup on the same folder first.

## Requirements

- Your own inFamous disc dump, European release (`BCES00220`).
- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with Direct3D 12 support.
- A CPU with SSE4.1 (2008 or newer). On CPUs without AVX2 (Intel before 2013, Pentium/Celeron
  without AVX, AMD before 2015) Setup builds a slower compatibility version automatically.
  On PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the game uses fewer threads and less CPU (tested down to 4 threads).
- [Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) with "Add python.exe to
  PATH" ticked.
- [Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/)
  with the **Desktop development with C++** workload and the **C++ Clang
  Compiler for Windows** component.
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), only if your `PS3_GAME\USRDIR` has `EBOOT.BIN`
  but no decrypted `EBOOT.elf`. Setup uses it to decrypt the executable.
- About 10 GB of free disk space and 16 GB of RAM.

## Building manually

```bat
cd installer
cargo build --release
target\release\infamous-installer --game "D:\Dumps\inFamous"
```

`infamous-installer doctor` checks the requirements only. Finished steps are
skipped when you run it again, so an interrupted install continues where it
stopped. See [installer/README.md](installer/README.md) for every step and the
maintainer commands.

## Playing

Run **inFamous** (the shortcut Setup made). It opens a small options window first
(vsync, frame cap, resolution, language and more, saved to `settings.ini`);
**Play** starts the game. The same settings are in the game's pause menu under
**Settings**. Controllers work as on the console, and keyboard and mouse are supported.

**F10** opens the in-game trainer: God Mode, Infinite Energy, Refill Health,
Max Health x2/x5/x10, Add XP, Karma +/-, Kill Enemies / Civilians, Super Speed
and Player Model (play as Zeke, Trish, Kessler, Alden or John). Set `TRAINER=0`
to turn it off.

## DLSS and FSR (optional)

The game can use NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA or AMD FSR for upscaling, and AMD FSR frame generation.
They are not included in the download because NVIDIA and AMD distribute their SDKs themselves,
but both are free and take a few minutes to add.

- **DLSS** needs an NVIDIA RTX graphics card.
- **FSR** works on any modern GPU (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel). FSR 4 needs a Radeon RX 9000 card;
  other cards get FSR 3.1 automatically.

**1. Download the SDK(s) you want.** You need the **source code**, not a Windows or Linux demo.
On the page, click the green **Code** button, then **Download ZIP**. If you go through the
Releases page instead, pick **Source code (zip)**, not the files with "demo" or "samples" in the name.

| For | Download | Rename the extracted folder to |
|---|---|---|
| DLSS / DLAA | [github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS) | `dlss-sdk` |
| FSR and frame generation | [github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK) | `fsr-sdk` |

**2. Put the folder(s) in your inFamous install folder**, next to `infamous-recomp` and
`ps3recomp`:

```
inFamous\
  dlss-sdk\        <- contains include\ and lib\
  fsr-sdk\         <- contains Kits\
  infamous-recomp\
  ps3recomp\
  ...
```

Make sure you don't end up with a folder inside a folder (`dlss-sdk\DLSS-main\include`).
`include` (DLSS) or `Kits` (FSR) must be directly inside.

**3. Rebuild the game once.** Open a Command Prompt in the install folder and run:

```bat
type nul > .installer\update.pending
"Update inFamous.cmd"
```

This rebuilds the game with the SDK(s), which takes a while. Any later update also picks them up
automatically, so you only do this once.

**4. Turn it on in game:** pause, then **Settings**, then **Upscaling** (DLAA, DLSS Quality /
Balanced / Performance, FSR Native AA / Quality / Balanced / Performance) and **Frame
Generation**. The same options are in the launcher's options window. Upscaling and frame
generation apply after a restart.

If the **Upscaling** row is missing, the build didn't find the SDK: check the folder names and
layout from step 2, then repeat step 3.

## How it works

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `ps3recomp` | The recompiler toolkit and runtime: PPU and SPU lifters, HLE system libraries, RSX on Direct3D 12, audio and input |
| `infamous-recomp` | The inFamous-specific parts: program entry, game stubs and fixes, asset tools |
| `installer` | Setup and the command-line installer: reads the disc, regenerates the code from your game, applies `installer/patches`, builds |
| `installer/infamous.toml` | Everything about the game and the port: pipeline steps, generated files, build and launch settings |
| `installer/generated.lock` | Hashes of each generated file before and after the port's patches |

## Credits

- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet and
  contributors (see [ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md](ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md)).
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), used to decrypt the game executable.
- Sucker Punch Productions, for the game.
- [Lorenzo Aiello](https://github.com/aiellolorenzo23) and [ibrahimpuri](https://github.com/ibrahimpuri), for their support.

04487251f923b1531ca69dffe4f779b630caa6c2.message:
des_options: run speed no longer halves above 30 fps

After physics the game checks whether a character that wants to move
faster than 5 m/s covered less than 1/30 m this step, i.e. under 1 m/s
at 30 fps. If it did, the root-motion speed factor drops by 0.8x a step
to 0.5. At 120 fps a step is a quarter as long, so a dash that starts
from a slow run (stamina still recovering) trips the test, falls to
3.2 m/s, and stays there because 3.2 m/s is still under the 4 m/s the
test now means.

The lift now replaces 0x00273D38, a two-line wrapper around that test,
with des_move_post. It runs the game's test and then, under DES_FPS,
redoes it with the step's real length and per-30 Hz rates. The lift
recipe gains 0x273D38=des_move_post.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

05172651f6a8b50162faf10135eb0675c42e6c7d.message:

Closing the keyboard (Circle, Start, Enter or Esc) used pop(), which

opened the keyboard, not the menu, so the keyboard now only hides itself
and gives the focus back to the document below if that is showing.

used to leave the menu bar up; now it doesn't. A keyboard opened over the
open menu still leaves the menu open.

with their output under DES_SCRATCH:

  regression save; the player's save goes back on exit) and run a file
  of console commands ("sleep N", "stick <lx> <ly> <secs>").

  uncapped; RSX_PRESENT from the lock state once per batch.

- abboot.sh (shared boot for knobab/kprof), kabsum.sh (A/B means),
  profsym.py (prof dump by function, from the linker map).

des_console takes an optional wait cap, for `prof <tid> <secs>`.

port: wrapper UI: live frame rate, startup shader pass, resizable window, crash and issue reports

- DES_FPS is read at every flip request, so the Settings row (and the
  console's setenv) changes the frame rate during play; 0 or empty puts
  back the game's own mode.
- The shader cache is filled at startup through boot_main's
  ps3_title_prework hook (des_prework.cpp, ps3recomp's
  rsx_shader_precompile), after the window opens, behind a "Preparing the
  shaders" window with a bar and Skip. precompile.stamp skips it when the
  archives, the exe and fp_variants.txt are unchanged. DES_PRECOMPILE=0 /
  force.
- The UI draws on the window-sized back buffer and drops its wrapped
  buffers before a resize (the overlay's release hook), so it stays sharp
  at any window size.
- The F1 bar flickered: no more backdrop-filter in the styles.

port: mouse look turns the follow camera

Mouse look (#55) added the mouse's turn to the follow camera's yaw and
pitch at the entry of its update (0x00119670), and the camera never
turned: the update keeps no angles from one frame to the next. Each
frame it works yaw (+0x134) and pitch (+0x130) out again from the eye
and the target, adds the right stick's turn, and places the eye from
the result, so the angles written at the entry were thrown away.

The turn now goes in where the stick's does. The entry still takes the
counts once a game frame (and drops them for a set-angle request, a
look-at target, the R3 auto-turn and after a gap). A hook at the
update's stick test (0x0011C910) makes a frame with a turn count as one
where the stick moved, so the camera holds the new pitch and draws the
eye at the placed one at once, as with the stick. A hook after the
angles are rebuilt (0x0011C758) adds the turn, with pitch kept inside
the camera's limits; the update then adds the stick's turn and places
the camera from the new angles in the same frame.

41607bb59b02ec1108ca6393b06982aaf06e9bdf.message:
tools/des: profsym.py counts each profile sample once

A `profrip` dump has a fourth table, "--- exclusive by address ---", and
profsym.py summed every table whose header contains "--- exclusive", so
each sample in an exe function was counted twice: once in the
per-function table and once at its address. With the default 40 address
rows that inflated the top functions (image 2's region 0x4498 at 12.9%
instead of 8.8% in a Tutorial profile); with PROF_RIP_ROWS=4096 it
doubled nearly every exe function (render_frame at 19.3% instead of
10.4% in a Palace profile). DLL rows were not doubled, since the two
tables name them differently.

It now reads the per-function table only, or with a third argument
"addr" the by-address table only, summed by function. A `prof` dump
(no address table) gives the same output as before.

467157a6e20aca15bcd7b4e0a052efdc2655506f.message:
port: particle effects repeat 30 times a second at any frame rate

An effect emitter repeats by re-entering its own state, in the FFX
scene update 0x013B74B8. The test runs once an update, before the
state's time steps by dt, and the time restarts at 0, so an emitter
whose interval is a frame or less emits on every update: 60 times a
second at 60 fps, 240 at 240. The boss fog walls churned two to eight
times as fast as at 30 fps, and looked darker, their particles being
recycled younger.

des_fx_state holds such a re-entry until the state has lasted 1/30 s
and starts the new state's time with the part of a frame past it, so
the loop runs 30 times a second at any frame rate. Other transitions
and slower loops are left alone. Nothing changes at 30 fps or without
DES_FPS; DES_FXFIX=0 turns it off live.

At the 1-1 boss fog, the fog's change over 1/30 s (divided by its
brightness): 0.039-0.047 at 30 fps; 0.089-0.090 at 60 and 0.150 at 120
without the fix, 0.030-0.043 and 0.053 with it.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

The game jumps on L3 while dashing (C in the layout). In the Souls games

scripts: apply_boot_patches.py waits for a chunk another program holds

VS Code's C/C++ extension opens a chunk about 3 s after the lifter writes
it and keeps it open for about 10 s without write sharing. When the boot
patch ran in that window, the write failed with PermissionError and the
chunk stayed unpatched. That happened in 3 of 3 test re-lifts in which the
lifter rewrote only the chunk with func_00AC8078. Today's lifter rewrites
every chunk on every lift, which makes the race rarer but not impossible.

The write is now retried every half second for up to 30 s. If the chunk
is still locked after that, the script names the file, says the patch is
not applied and exits with 1. Nothing else changes: without a lock, the
output and the patched chunk are byte for byte the same as before.

54606b8ba8d724a65099800b8c7f0fd8dd529ac3.message:
build: pin the ps3recomp commit the port needs (ps3recomp.pin)

The port finds ps3recomp through PS3RECOMP_DIR (by default the nested
ps3recomp/ clone) and nothing says which ps3recomp a revision of the port
needs. ps3recomp.pin names one exact commit of the fork, and for a release
the fork's tag on it (des-<upstream version>-<n>, docs/54); never a branch.
It starts at the fork's current master, which the merged render resolution
change needs.

- Configure (port/cmake/Ps3recompPin.cmake) warns when the checkout does
  not contain the pinned commit. A newer checkout, or one with local
  changes, is fine. -DDES_REQUIRE_PIN=ON, for release and player builds,
  stops unless the checkout is exactly that commit with no changes to
  tracked files; a ps3recomp folder without git must carry a copy of the
  pin whose commit matches.
- tools/release/pin_ps3recomp.py shows, checks and changes the pin: check
  --remote asks the fork that the commit is on its master and that the tag
  points to it, check --release requires a tag, set rewrites the pin from a
  checkout, local compares a checkout like configure does.
- .github/workflows/pin.yml runs the self-test and check --remote.

741d3a58ed766797ddaeb6e32558f90ff3c888ad.message:
port: the ChrIns worker stores its done flag before its done event

At high frame rates the game could freeze for good: frames kept coming at
about 10 fps, but the player, the camera and the pad stopped. The main
thread was parked in the character step's handshake (0x002A6660), waiting
on the worker's done event, and the worker was idle on its queue.

Each frame the main thread kicks the step (0x002A6E28: done flag = 0,
done event cleared, a message posted) and waits for the event. The worker
(ChrInsManThread::Thread, 0x002A6AA8) runs a message only while the flag
is 0; it runs the step, sets the event, and only then stores 1 to the
flag. Between those two stores the main thread can wake, finish its frame
and kick again, so its "flag = 0" lands before the worker's "flag = 1".
The worker then skips the new message and the main thread waits forever.
The order is the game's own (bl 0x009E0148, then li r0,1 / stb r0,0x1C(r25)
at 0x002A6BCC..0x002A6BD8); the lift and lv2 sync semantics keep it. On a
PS3 the window is a few instructions on a thread that keeps running. Here
the woken main thread can take the worker's core right after the event's
mutex is released, and at 240 fps the next kick comes a few milliseconds
later, sooner still under CPU load.

des_chrins.cpp registers the game's loop with the flag stored before the
event is set, so a kick can only come after it. Every call, return address
and stack slot is the game's. The thread is entered only through a
function pointer (0x00C3A878 -> ps3_indirect_call), so the registration
replaces it without a re-lift. DES_CHRINSFIX=0 keeps the game's lifted
loop; DES_CHRINSFIX=2 runs this loop in the game's order, for A/B runs. A
step request that finds the flag already 1 is logged (at most 4 lines).

port: the cutscene camera blends through an Euler flip instead of holding a key

With DES_CUTFPS=1, des_cut_cam blends the cutscene camera's 30 Hz keys.
A step whose rotation angles turn more than 0.5 rad keeps the nearest
key, so that real shot changes stay cuts. The arrival cutscene has one
such step at t = 13.3 s: a 0.01 m move with a 3.14 rad turn (docs/40).
It is the same rotation written as the other set of Euler angles: the
later key's other angles are within 0.01 rad of the earlier key. Above
30 fps the hold shows as a hitch.

0x00054D48 builds the camera's rotation from (x, y, z) as Rx(x) Rz(z)
Ry(y), with row vectors, so Z is the middle turn and
Rx(x + pi) Rz(pi - z) Ry(y + pi) is the same matrix. When the two keys'
angles are more than 0.5 rad apart but the later key's other angles are
within 0.5 rad of the earlier key, the rotation now blends to those other
angles. Otherwise the guard keeps the nearest key, as before. Plain
2 pi wraps per axis were already handled by angle_delta.

DES_CUTEULER=0 (live) keeps the nearest key at a flip, as before.
DES_CUTLOG=1 now prints both rotation keys and the later key's other
angles for each jump or flip, and counts the flips. Without DES_CUTFPS
nothing changes. No hook sites change, so no re-lift is needed. docs/62
has the derivation.

cutscene at 120 fps with DES_CUTLOG=1: the step at 13.3 s blends (calls
between keys 3000, all blended, Euler flips 4, jumps 0). The same run

94974b4ca9760965307421cf9d67b76292283eaf.message:
port: build without debug information by default (DES_DEBUG_INFO)

The link has no /DEBUG, so it writes no PDB and drops the /Zi debug
information the compiles put in the objects. Making it still costs CPU
time and a lot of memory: lifted chunk 004 took 185 s of CPU with /Zi
and 143 s without (+29%), chunk 009 228 s and 161 s (+42%), and a chunk
job's peak memory goes from about 2.4 GB to 5.8 to 6.9 GB with /Zi. Four
chunk jobs at once (the README's --parallel 4) can need over 20 GB.

The code is nearly the same without /Zi. In a full build, 13 of the 14
lifted chunks, the lifted libsre and the SPU images came out
byte-identical in code and data. /Zi nudges clang's code generation in
3 of chunk 004's 8,162 functions, each one byte longer with it, the same
on every rebuild. In the UI it changes two functions in modal.cpp (same
size, other instruction bytes) and a few exception tables.

DES_DEBUG_INFO=ON brings /Zi back for des_boot, the SPU images and the
UI, and links des_boot.pdb. It keeps /OPT:REF,ICF on, which /DEBUG
would otherwise turn off, so it links like the default build.

a8effc854bea0f8dcb4806bb265965f3c1ebd35a.message:
tools/des: a takeover puts the save back only over what the gone run left

A takeover put the gone run's backup back without looking. If the run
had been killed between its own copy back and letting the lock go, and
the player had played since, that play was overwritten. If only the
script had been killed, its game could still be running and write the
save while the backup went back.

The takeover now first stops that run's game: only the des_boot pids in
the run's pid file, and only from a staged test copy that started
before the file was written, so a pid reused since is left alone. Then
it puts the backup back only if the folder is empty, or holds only files
of the backup or of the save the run swapped in. The lock now keeps a
list of those files with their md5s (des_save_note, and des_save_swap,
which levelcap.sh and regress.sh now use for the swap). Any other file
may be newer play. In that case the folder, the lock and the backup are
left alone. The run exits, and the message lists those files and says
how to go on: DES_SAVE_TAKEOVER=restore:<id> or keep:<id>. The id is
that lock's, so a leftover setting does not apply to a later lock.

If the backup is missing or has changed, the message now says so,
instead of saying "the backup is still there". Signals that come while
the backup goes back take effect once the copy is done.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

  this copy sends n position packets a second, at most every second

UI: trophy pop-ups reach the screen (the overlay keeps the UI awake)

frame() keeps the UI awake while the overlay is busy, but it looked the
overlay up with find_document, which searched only the focus stack. The
overlay is a passive document, so the lookup returned null and busy was
false. The UI went to sleep on the frame that created a toast: the toast
never got "open" (it stays at opacity 0), and nothing drew it after that.
The same cut the menu hint after the start screen ("Press F1 ...", 2.5 s)
to the 600 ms grace period. find_document now searches the passive
documents after the stack. Only the overlay is passive; the other callers
look up the menu bar, which is on the stack.

Awake for a pop-up with no document up, the pads are no longer fed to
RmlUi. Start reached the hidden menu bar as the Menu command and opened
it. The pads now stay the game's, as when the UI sleeps, and the chord
opens the menu. The game's input is not held: no document is visible.

A closing toast or menu hint is removed at most 1 s after its time, even
if its transition never reports its end, so a pop-up cannot keep the UI
awake.

tools: regress_route.py ends each stick hold half a frame early

A hold's PAD_STICK window was the hold's game time over the game/real
rate. At 30 fps that is a whole number of real frames, so the window
ended right on the frame after the last one wanted, and the runtime's
GetTickCount64 (steps of about 16 ms) decided whether that frame got the
stick too: the 8 s walk came out 240 or 241 frames, the 5 s walk on 150
or 151, and the 1.5 s camera turn, by the same arithmetic, 45 or 46.

The turn is the one that shows. In the six 30 fps runs of the game-clock
route the walk on set off in one of two directions 8 degrees apart,
three runs each, with the player's positions the same to the centimetre
within each group: on to the wall, as in the accepted set, or past it to
a message about 5 m further, and s3_turn/s4_on 15-19% apart. The left
stick holds did not line up with the two groups.

Less half a frame step, the window ends between two frames, so at 30 fps
the holds are 240, 45 and 150 frames every time. Under DES_FPS a frame
step is a few milliseconds and this changes nothing that matters. The
hold report adds the half frame back, so "by the clock map" still reads
the game time the frames held.

c7b28f253cd215ee7b57168174404e24ab0a217d.message:
port: loading screen souls turn at the 30 fps rate at any frame rate

Above 30 fps the two soul icons by the small logo on the loading
screens turned too fast: eight times as fast at 240 fps. Each soul is a
100-cell flipbook, and the game moves it one cell an update, once a
frame, without looking at the frame's step.

Two screens draw them. At boot, 0x0015AE10 steps the screen's fade and
calls 0x0015AA00, which steps the cells (+0x20, +0x24). On level loads
the NowLoading dialog's update, 0x008CD078, steps its cells (+0xF8,
+0xFC); its fade already goes by dt. Loads that start a cutscene were
fine, since cutscenes hold the game at 30 fps.

load_souls_rate and nowloading_souls_rate hook the two updates. With
DES_FPS set they count the frame in 30 Hz steps (kFrameDt at boot, the
dialog's own dt in f1), take whole steps with the rest carried over, and
set the cells one short so the game's own +1 lands there. The boot hook
scales the fade's step the same way. At 30 fps this is one step a frame,
as on the PS3. DES_UIFIX=0 turns both off live.

Cells per second, 240 fps: boot 226 before, 29.6 after; level load
(cutscene lock off) 208 before, 29.8 after. At 60 fps 29.6 and 30.3;
at 30 fps one a frame, as before.

da3238cc87609220de60043bda68b1b050a8a571.message:
ci: draft a GitHub release from a version tag

Nothing makes releases today. This adds the workflow and the two scripts it
runs (docs/54). Only a pushed tag v<x.y.z> or v<x.y.z>-<pre> starts it; no
manual run, no branch push. The release it creates stays a draft until the
maintainer publishes it by hand.

- tools/release/package.py check-tag: the tag is v<VERSION> (VERSION as
  committed at the tag), on origin/master, and the ps3recomp.pin committed
  with it names a fork release tag. Then the workflow checks the pin
  against the fork.
- tools/release/changelog.py: the notes, from the merge commits since the
  previous release (pull request titles, grouped by branch prefix), then
  the pinned ps3recomp and the fork's pull requests since the last pin.
- tools/release/package.py build: one zip of redistributable files, the
  port's tracked files and ps3recomp's at the pinned commit with a copy of
  the pin and release-info.txt, plus SHA256SUMS. Entries are sorted, dated
  with the commit time and given fixed permissions, so the same tag gives
  the same zip. The game-file check runs on everything in it.
- release-check.yml runs the same steps on pull requests that change them,
  packages twice and requires the same zip both times.

The release needs VERSION, ps3recomp.pin and the game-file check, which
come in their own pull requests; until they are in, the tag checks stop it.
/dist/ (the scripts' output) is ignored.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

e108a7883c1ddad7ba7ec9c33863f227ea4bf20d.message:
port: character fades at the 30 fps rate

A character's effect list multiplies the model's alpha by each node's fade
every frame. Two node types step their fade by a fixed amount a call,
without dt: type 16 (a fade-in, or a fade by distance from the player) by
0.05 and type 14 (a model fade with sounds) by 1/30 (docs/42, 2.4). Above
30 fps they finish early: at 240 fps a 0.67 s fade takes 83 ms and a 1 s
fade 125 ms.

des_fade_rate runs after the four loads of those steps (--insn-hooks) and
scales the step by the frame's 30 Hz steps, as des_viewer_rate does for the
character creation previews. The clamps to 0 and 1 come after the step, so
nothing overshoots. Nothing changes at 30 fps or without DES_FPS.
DES_FADEFIX=0 turns it off live; DES_FADELOG=1 prints every step.
