# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   └── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse
│   ├── hardware/             # cellGem, cellCamera, cellUsbd
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
└── docs/                     # See the Documentation table below
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível, mas ainda lento (~16-17 fps). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot ao primeiro nível:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal e o primeiro nível, com o Kratos acorrentado. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~30 fps; o primeiro nível a ~16-17 fps (era ~9). O limite é o código das SPUs recompilado, não a placa de vídeo: o job de geometria por draw (módulo 218) é o maior custo, e está sendo reescrito como código nativo, validado contra jobs gravados do jogo, sem precisar rodá-lo. - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo, controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md). ## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), abra o launcher: ```powershell .\scripts\windows\launcher.ps1 ```

JOGAR abre o jogo dentro da própria janela do launcher. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). 33ff21bf4165485a6f1f9854a97c065e2d9f39ce.message:
Downloadable content: "Add DLC from RPCS3..." in the engine menu

The engine menu's new Downloadable content section lists the installed
packs and imports the user's own from RPCS3's folder (or a PS3 copy of the
game's HDD folder), on a thread with a progress bar. engine_dlc.cpp:

- finds the game folder and licence folders from whatever level the user
  picks (RPCS3's folder, dev_hdd0, dev_hdd0\game, the game's folder);
- lists the packs there, installed (install.dat_) or still waiting in
  bin\NN (download.dat_, or an encrypted download.edat);
- per pack, all files or none: copies plain files and decrypts the paid
  packs' licence-type-2 EDATs with the RIF key from the matching .rap (the
  published RAP-to-RIF conversion, AES via BCrypt), through ps3recomp's own
  edat_decrypt_file, which checks every block's hash;
- keeps the decrypted files under their .edat names (the runtime opens a file
  without the NPD header as it is) and records the packs in install.dat_ as
  the game's installer would.

Tested off Windows (tools/test_dlc_import.cpp) on a sample of real packs and
licences: all six paid packs and the free ones install, sizes match, a
missing or wrong licence leaves its pack out with nothing written, and a
second import is a no-op. folklore/docs/DLC.md has the format and the steps.

The bloom reduces the scene to 640x480 with one sample per pixel, so it

640x480 pixel and composites with a cubic B-spline. patches/0059 now
hashes shaders from the constants block on with rsx_tex[N] read as
rsx_texN: the depth of field pass was missed when a cube map was bound.

Fix 1.10 capturing every Folk at once: cellPadGetCapabilityInfo overran

The 1.10 executable calls cellPadGetCapabilityInfo (new in 1.10) on every
pad update, with its CellPadCapabilityInfo on the stack just below the
CellPadData it has just read. ps3recomp sized that struct by

CELL_PAD_MAX_CAPABILITY_INFO (32) and zeroed all of it, so 128 bytes of the
game's pad data were wiped. The motion sensor words then read 0 -- full
scale on the PS3, an instant pull -- and every Folk was captured at once,
with motion controls on and a DualShock 3's sensors live. patches/0055.

shader taking cos() of its own texture times a large constant -- smooth

restores the old sampling for comparison (patches/0054).

1428300417.readme_excerpt:
# Folklore (PS3) — native PC recompilation

If you like this feel free to buy me a coffee :) https://ko-fi.com/mavab

Folklore (Game Republic / SCE, 2007) statically recompiled from its PS3
executable to native x86-64 Windows code with
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). There is no emulator: the
game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C++ and runs on a runtime that
stands in for the PS3's OS, with Direct3D 12 for graphics.

**This repository contains no game code and no Sony code.** You build the game
yourself from **your own disc**; setup does the translation on your PC. No PS3
firmware is needed: the SPU job system the game runs on (SPURS) is
reimplemented here ([`folklore/docs/SPURS.md`](folklore/docs/SPURS.md)).

**Status:** playable on the author's PC (Windows 11, Ryzen 7 7800X3D): it boots,
does the first-boot install, and plays, including capturing Folks with
the original motion controls. Expect rough edges.
[`folklore/docs/STATUS.md`](folklore/docs/STATUS.md) is the full engineering
log.

### New in v0.64: HDR, keyboard and mouse

- **HDR output**: on a display with Windows' HDR on, the sun, skies, glowing
  Ids and magic go brighter than white towards your display's peak, while
  the HUD, text and menus stay at paper white. Brightness follows Windows'
  own HDR settings by default, so the picture matches HDR off; both levels
  can be set by hand. On the launcher's Graphics page and in the engine menu.
- **Keyboard and mouse**: play with them, a controller, or both at once.
  The mouse turns the camera (sensitivity, invert, and a lift past the
  game's dead zone); two movement keys together run, as a stick does. Every
  button, both sticks' directions, *Walk* and *Capture motion* can be
  rebound on the launcher's new **Controls** page or in the engine menu.
- **Ultrawide comic-book scenes**: the story pages' panels are full width
  again (they were drawn at three quarters of their width at 21:9).

### v0.62: smoother play and a tidier ultrawide HUD

- **No more quarter-second freezes in fights**: a hold-up between the game
  and the renderer, every few seconds in heavy combat, is gone.
- **Clean fade-in after Load Game**: no more half-drawn frames (a black
  screen with only the HUD, flickering pieces) while the new area's shaders
  are built; the loading screen stays up until the area is ready.
- **Ultrawide HUD**: speech bubbles keep the game's proportions beside the
  character speaking; place names, the item pick-up box and the boss capture
  bar stay in one piece; the Search prompt, the player-select arrows and the
  capture bonus sparkles stay where they belong.
- **Auto-capture** now finishes the boss captures where you swing the
  controller left and right.

### v0.6: save slots

The launcher's new **Saves** page lets you keep as many saves as you like and
choose which one the game plays before you press Play. Each slot shows the
picture of the area it was saved in, the character and place, both
characters' chapters, the play time and when it was saved. Start a **New
slot**, **Import** saves (RPCS3's too), **Duplicate**, **Export** (ready for
RPCS3) or **Delete** one. See [*Save slots*](#save-slots).

### v0.5: the launcher

![Folklore launcher, Game page](docs/images/launcher_game.png)

**FolkloreLauncher.exe** (double-click **run_launcher.bat**) sets the game
up in one window: your disc dump, the 1.10 update and your DLC, each checked
as you choose it, and every graphics, display and gameplay setting. Then
press **Play**. No scripts or settings files to edit; the in-game engine
menu is still there too. See [*The launcher*](#the-launcher).

Also in v0.5: licences (.rap) added from a button, the title bar showing the
real render size, and a fix for the logo movie looping over a blue screen
when the game was started outside run.ps1 in a project folder.

### What's better than on the PS3

All of these are in the in-game engine menu (**L3 + R3** or **F1**); each can
be turned back to the original.

- **Frame rate**: 60 fps or unlimited (up to your display's refresh rate),
  with physics stepped to match so cloth and hair stay stable.
- **Resolution**: up to 3x the PS3's 1280×720, borderless fullscreen.
- **Ultrawide**: 21:9, 32:9 or your display's shape, with a wider field of
  view rather than a stretched picture; the map and gauges move out to the
  screen's edges (with a *How far out* slider), and menus, speech bubbles
  and fades stay where they belong.
- **Anti-aliasing**: SMAA (sharp, clean edges) or FXAA.
- **HDR**: on an HDR display, the sun, skies, glowing Ids and magic go
  brighter than white towards your display's peak, while the HUD and menus
  stay at a comfortable paper white.
- **Sharper textures**: finer texture levels in the distance, plus up to 16x
  anisotropic filtering and optional sharpening.
- **Ambient occlusion**: soft shading where surfaces meet — corners, under
  ledges, around characters' feet.
- **Soft shadows**: the characters' shadows with soft edges instead of hard,
  stair-stepped ones.
- **Soft-edged foliage**: grass, leaves and fences with smooth edges instead
  of ones cut pixel by pixel, which crawl and shimmer as the camera moves.
- **Full-resolution reflections**: the water reflections, which the game
  draws at a quarter of the screen's size, drawn at the render resolution.
- **Smooth depth of field**: a soft, round blur using the game's own focus,
  without the original's doubled image.
- **Smooth bloom**: a steady glow, without the original's flicker.
- **Cleaner Id souls**: the enemies' souls as a soft shimmer (or a clear
  translucent shape) instead of pixel static.
- **Faster busy scenes**: objects drawn again and again (Doolin's streets)
  reuse work instead of being redrawn from scratch, unchanged models stay on
  the graphics card instead of being copied every frame, and large textures
  are no longer re-read every frame — boss fights hold 60 fps.
- **A launcher**: set the game's folders, DLC and every setting in one
  window, then Play.
- **Quality of life**: skip the opening logos with Start, save backups and
  restores, no RPCS3 needed to decrypt the game, downloadable content added
  from the menu, motion controls on any controller with motion sensors.
- **Keyboard and mouse**: play with them, a controller, or both at once;
  the mouse turns the camera, and every button can be rebound in the
  launcher or the engine menu.

Builds can be made from the v1.00 disc or from the game's **1.10 update**
(rumble, and the newer Folk data), and the **downloadable content** you bought
can be added from the in-game menu — see
[*1.10 with the DLC, step by step*](#110-with-the-dlc-step-by-step).

---

## Requirements — read this first

You need **both** of these. Neither is in this repository and neither can be
downloaded from it.

### 1. Your own Folklore disc: North American or European release

- **Title ID BCUS98147 (North America) or BCES00050 (Europe), disc version
  1.00.** The code is translated from those exact executables; the Japanese
  release will not work. A build is made from one of them and runs that one
  ([`folklore/docs/REGIONS.md`](folklore/docs/REGIONS.md)).
- **Optionally, the 1.10 update** for your release. A build can be made from
  the update's executable instead (it adds rumble, the game's own Vibration
  option, and the newer table of Folks that later downloadable content uses);
  it still reads everything else from your disc dump. See *The 1.10 update*
  below.
- Dumped from your disc to a **folder** (the "JB folder" format RPCS3 uses): a
  folder that contains `PS3_GAME\`, with `PS3_GAME\PARAM.SFO` and
  `PS3_GAME\USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN` in it. Your dump is only ever read, never
  written to.

### 2. The game's EBOOT: nothing to do

The dumped `PS3_GAME\USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN` is encrypted; setup and the game
decrypt it themselves (no RPCS3 needed) into a `decrypted\` folder here —
nothing is written to your dump. An `EBOOT.elf` RPCS3 already wrote beside it
(*Utilities → Decrypt PS3 Binaries*) is used as it is. The decrypted file is
**6,518,936 bytes** (BCUS98147) or **6,518,912 bytes** (BCES00050); setup
checks this. ([`folklore/docs/SELF.md`](folklore/docs/SELF.md) has how.)

`decrypted\` holds the game's own code: like `folklore.exe`, don't share it.

### The 1.10 update (optional)

Install the update in RPCS3 (**File → Install Packages/Raps/Edats**, choose
the update's `.pkg`). RPCS3 puts it in `dev_hdd0\game\BCUS98147` (or
`BCES00050`) inside its own folder — not in your disc dump, even though
RPCS3's game list shows the game as 1.10 and *Open game folder* opens the
dump. Its `USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN` is decrypted here too: the European one needs
nothing, the North American one its licence (`UP9000-BCUS98147_00-FOLKLORE20000003.rap`),
which RPCS3 installs with the update into `dev_hdd0\home\<user>\exdata` —
setup finds it there. Give setup both folders:

```powershell
.\setup.ps1 -GameDir D:\Games\BCUS98147 -UpdateDir D:\RPCS3\dev_hdd0\game\BCUS98147
```

setup lifts the update's executable instead of the disc's and saves both
folders; `build.ps1` and `run.ps1` work as before. On each start the game
copies the update's three data files (`LMonS2.bi5_`, a corrected Spanish
text file, and their list) from the update folder into `hdd0\` here and
records them as installed, as the game itself would; neither folder is
written to. `.\setup.ps1 -GameDir <dump>` without `-UpdateDir` goes back to
the disc version. Saves are the same files in both versions.

### Also needed

- **Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit**, a Direct3D 12 graphics card, and a CPU with
  AVX2 (x86-64-v3: Intel Haswell / AMD Zen or newer).
- About **30 GB** free on the drive you clone to (tools, build files, and the
  game's own first-boot install of several GB).
- An internet connection for setup (it downloads its tools).
- A controller: any XInput pad, or for motion controls a **DualShock 4**,
  **DualSense** (or Edge), **Switch Pro Controller** (USB or Bluetooth, no
  extra software), or a **DualShock 3** with
  [DsHidMini](https://github.com/nefarius/DsHidMini) in **SXS** mode.

---

## Building

Clone this repository (or download it as a ZIP and unzip it) somewhere with
the space free — a short path such as `D:\Folklore` is best. Open
**PowerShell** in that folder and run these one at a time:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\setup.ps1
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\build.ps1
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\run.ps1
```

1. **setup.ps1** (15–30 minutes, once)
   - **First it asks for your dump**: a folder picker (choose the folder that
     contains `PS3_GAME`). It is checked; if something is wrong (still
     encrypted, wrong version) it says what and asks again. You can also pass
     it: `.\setup.ps1 -GameDir D:\Games\BCUS98147`
   - Then it runs on its own: downloads Git, CMake, Ninja, Python and FFmpeg
     into `tools\`, and — only if you have no Visual Studio with clang-cl —
     Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools (about 6 GB, one UAC prompt; the Visual
     Studio Installer always goes on C:).
   - Translates the game's code from your `EBOOT.elf` into
     `folklore\src\recomp\` (about a minute). It stays on your PC.
   - Builds the ps3recomp runtime library.
2. **build.ps1** compiles about 1.5 million lines of translated C++: roughly
   10–30 minutes the first time on a modern 8-core CPU, incremental after
   that. Result: `folklore\build\folklore.exe`.
3. **run.ps1** starts the game and writes `logs\run-<date-time>.log`. It
   uses the game folder you gave setup (saved in `folklore_settings.ini`), and
   the game's first boot copies several GB of data into `hdd1\`.
   **run.bat** does the same with a double-click (any run.ps1 options can
   follow it, e.g. `run.bat -ResetInstall`).

Or, after build.ps1, double-click **run_launcher.bat** instead of run.ps1:
[the launcher](#the-launcher) asks for the same folders in its own window and
starts the game with Play.

With both releases (an EU copy of this folder beside it, see *Sharing what
you built*), `.\build_all.ps1` builds this folder, brings the EU copy up to
date and builds that too; then `run.bat` in either folder runs its build.
Once the 1.10 copies exist (`package_all.ps1 -UsUpdateDir/-EuUpdateDir`, see
*Sharing what you built*) it builds those as well.

### If something fails

- Every step writes a log in `logs\` (`setup-*.log`, `build.log`,
  `run-*.log`); the error message names the one to look at.
- **setup can't find clang-cl after installing Build Tools**: open *Visual
  Studio Installer* → Modify → Individual components → tick *C++ Clang Compiler
  for Windows* and *MSBuild support for LLVM (clang-cl)*, then run setup.ps1
  again.
- **"Could not decrypt ... needs its licence"** (North American 1.10 update):
  install the update's `.rap` in RPCS3 (*File → Install Packages/Raps/Edats*),
  or put it in a `licences` folder here.
- **"not a v1.00 EBOOT of a supported release"**: your disc is the Japanese
  release, or you gave `-GameDir` the 1.10 update's EBOOT (give the update
  folder as `-UpdateDir`, with `-GameDir` your disc dump). Only BCUS98147 and
  BCES00050 work.
- **"not the 1.10 update of a supported release"**: the `-UpdateDir` folder
  is not the 1.10 update — most often the disc dump was given instead of
  RPCS3's `dev_hdd0\game\<title id>` (see *The 1.10 update*). An old
  `USRDIR\EBOOT.elf` there made from the wrong EBOOT also causes it: delete it.
- **Both releases:** a build follows the dump setup lifted. `.\setup.ps1
  -GameDir <dump of the other release>` switches it (setup lifts the game code
  again, then `build.ps1` rebuilds everything). To keep one of each, use two
  copies of this folder.
- setup and build are safe to re-run; each step skips what is already done.

---

## Playing

### The launcher

![Folklore launcher, Graphics page](docs/images/launcher_graphics.png)

**FolkloreLauncher.exe** (built beside folklore.exe, and in every package)
sets everything up in one window before the game starts. Double-click
**run_launcher.bat** to open it: in the project folder it opens the one in
`folklore\build` with this folder's settings, `hdd0`, saves and logs (the
ones `run.ps1` uses).


- **Game**: your disc dump and, for a 1.10 build, the installed 1.10 update,
  each checked the way the game checks them; where saves and installed data
  go; optional firmware fonts.
- **Saves**: your save slots, each with the picture of the area it was saved
  in, the character and place, both characters' chapters, the play time and
  when it was saved. Choose the slot the game plays, start a **New slot**,
  **Import...** saves (from RPCS3 too), **Duplicate**, **Export...** or
  **Delete...** one;
  see [*Save slots*](#save-slots).
- **DLC**: the packs installed, **Add DLC from RPCS3...** and **Add licences
  (.rap)...**, and any pack still missing its licence.
- **Graphics**, **Display**, **Gameplay**: every setting of the in-game
  engine menu, including the ones that only apply when the game starts.
- **Controls**: motion controls, keyboard and mouse, and the key bindings
  (click one, then press the key, mouse button or wheel direction for it).
- **Dump textures this run** (Graphics page): the next Play starts the game
  with the texture dump on, into `textures\dump` (as `run.ps1
  -DumpTextures`); not kept between runs.
- **Play** saves `folklore_settings.ini` and starts folklore.exe;
  **Support on Ko-fi** beside it opens the project's
  [Ko-fi page](https://ko-fi.com/mavab).

Its picture is `launcher_art.jpg` (or `.png`) in the project folder (or
beside the launcher): put your own copy of the cover art there and it fills
the left-hand panel. It is not in the repository; without it the launcher
shows the plain panel in the screenshots above.

**Icon**: `folklore_icon.ico` in the project folder becomes the icon of both

time build.ps1 runs. Like the art it comes from the game, so it is not in the
repository; without it both get Windows' default icon.

**From a package**: unzip, double-click `run_launcher.bat`, choose your disc
dump (and the 1.10 update for a 1.10 build) on the Game page, press Play.

### Save slots

Folklore keeps each save in its own folder (`BCUS98147-SAVEDATA-0000`,
`-0001`, ...; `BCES00050-...` for the European relea

cdb581579fd7ba76d429fab741828ce9e04161d6.message:
Low-CPU update: fewer threads on weaker PCs, support for CPUs without AVX2

- SPURS: on PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the lanes/kernels spin less, wake the
  main thread sooner and run on fewer threads (4-thread PCs: ~10 fps -> ~29 fps,
  8 threads: ~38 -> ~50 fps). Big PCs keep the old behaviour.
- Vertex workers spin far less after each job, fewer workers on small CPUs.
- The once-per-second thread scan only walks the game's own threads.
- No exclusive core reservations on PCs with fewer than 20 CPU threads;
  P-core pinning only on hybrid CPUs with at least 8 P-core threads.
- CPUs without AVX2/FMA/BMI2 (pre-2013 Intel, AVX-less Pentium/Celeron, AMD before
  2015): Setup/the updater detect this and build an SSE4.1 compatibility version

1428463673.readme_excerpt:
# inFamous PC

An unofficial native Windows port of **inFamous** (PlayStation 3, 2009, European
release `BCES00220`). The game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code is statically
recompiled to x86-64 C/C++ with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp),
so it runs as a normal Windows program rather than under an emulator.

**This repository contains no game code or data.** You build the game yourself,
on your own PC, from your own copy of the game.

## Easy install

Download **inFamous Setup.exe** from the latest release, run it, choose your
`.iso` (an encrypted image works with its `.dkey` next to it) or your game
folder (the one with `PS3_GAME` in it), pick an install location and press
**Install**.

Setup checks for Python and the C++ build tools and offers to install them,
copies the game out of the disc image, regenerates the recompiled code from your
copy, builds it and adds an inFamous shortcut. Running Setup again on the same
folder updates or repairs the install and only redoes what changed.

## Updating

When a new version is published here, players update in place instead of reinstalling:
**Update now** in Setup (it finds the existing install), the **Update inFamous** shortcut in
the Start menu, or `Update inFamous.cmd` in the install folder. The updater compares every file
with this repository, downloads only what changed, regenerates the game code only if the
port's patches changed, and recompiles only the affected parts. Installs made with an older
Setup need one run of the new Setup on the same folder first.

## Requirements

- Your own inFamous disc dump, European release (`BCES00220`).
- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with Direct3D 12 support.
- A CPU with SSE4.1 (2008 or newer). On CPUs without AVX2 (Intel before 2013, Pentium/Celeron
  without AVX, AMD before 2015) Setup builds a slower compatibility version automatically.
  On PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the game uses fewer threads and less CPU (tested down to 4 threads).
- [Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) with "Add python.exe to
  PATH" ticked.
- [Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/)
  with the **Desktop development with C++** workload and the **C++ Clang
  Compiler for Windows** component.
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), only if your `PS3_GAME\USRDIR` has `EBOOT.BIN`
  but no decrypted `EBOOT.elf`. Setup uses it to decrypt the executable.
- About 10 GB of free disk space and 16 GB of RAM.

## Building manually

```bat
cd installer
cargo build --release
target\release\infamous-installer --game "D:\Dumps\inFamous"
```

`infamous-installer doctor` checks the requirements only. Finished steps are
skipped when you run it again, so an interrupted install continues where it
stopped. See [installer/README.md](installer/README.md) for every step and the
maintainer commands.

## Playing

Run **Play inFamous** (or the inFamous shortcut Setup made). Controllers work as
on the console, and keyboard and mouse are supported. F10 opens the settings
menu for vsync, frame cap, resolution and more (saved to `settings.ini`).

## How it works

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `ps3recomp` | The recompiler toolkit and runtime: PPU and SPU lifters, HLE system libraries, RSX on Direct3D 12, audio and input |
| `infamous-recomp` | The inFamous-specific parts: program entry, game stubs and fixes, asset tools |
| `installer` | Setup and the command-line installer: reads the disc, regenerates the code from your game, applies `installer/patches`, builds |
| `installer/infamous.toml` | Everything about the game and the port: pipeline steps, generated files, build and launch settings |
| `installer/generated.lock` | Hashes of each generated file before and after the port's patches |

## Credits

- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet and
  contributors (see [ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md](ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md)).
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), used to decrypt the game executable.
- Sucker Punch Productions, for the game.

2600b5bbeb184054c2bf44a318a71fb7eeb742c3.message:
Sample RSX 3D volume textures as Texture3D (fixes #272) (#307)

* rsx(d3d12): honour guest sampler addressing and filtering

The VP path bound 16 static samplers: s0 point+clamp (for the backend's
own glyph atlas) and s1-s15 trilinear+wrap, whatever the guest asked for.
Any guest texture on unit 0 was therefore point-sampled and clamped. In
MotorStorm the race cloud layer samples unit 0 with wrapping UVs, so it
collapsed to its edge colour and the clouds disappeared.

Record NV4097 TEXTURE_ADDRESS/FILTER/CONTROL0/BORDER_COLOR per draw and
bind an immutable 16-sampler table (root parameter 3) per draw, following
ps3recomp 9c08b94's addressing tables, plus decoding of min/mag/mip
filter, LOD bias, min/max LOD and anisotropy. States with no exact D3D12
equivalent (legacy clamp, mirror-once-border, convolution, disabled units)
and the fallback atlas/colour pipelines keep the previous fixed policy.
Draws are no longer concatenated across a sampler change. Tables are
released at the next frame after render_frame's full GPU drain.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JtDhrQ2oyyK7eHHHxyKU9v

* rsx(d3d12): keep guest sampler tables in a persistent heap

The first version created a fresh shader-visible sampler heap every
frame (plus one per 128 distinct tables) and released it at the next
frame. In a MotorStorm race that churn ended in a failed
CreateDescriptorHeap after about 100 s, and the linear memcmp lookup
grew with every table recorded in the frame.

Keep one base heap across frames so repeated sampler states reuse their
table and the bound heap rarely changes. Look tables up by hash. Add
overflow heaps only for a frame that needs more than 128 distinct
tables; they are released, and the base heap is recycled from slot 0,
at the next render_frame after its full GPU drain. Log the first
overflows and the HRESULT/device-removed reason if a heap cannot be
created.

* ppu_lifter: resolve jump-table bases spilled to the stack

A switch whose table base is loaded from the TOC (one or two levels),
stored to a stack slot, reloaded at the dispatch and then reused for the
case address was dropped:

    lwz r30,d1(r2) ; lwz r5,d2(r30) ; std r5,s(r1) ...
    ld r6,s(r1) ; lwzx r0,r9,r6 ; add r6,r0,r6 ; mtctr r6 ; bctr

discover_jump_tables took the `add` after the table load as the base's
nearest definition, and before it the stack reload was not a TOC load
either. The bctr lifted to ps3_indirect_call(ctx); return; an indirect
tail call that skips the epilogue, and none of the case targets was
registered. MotorStorm's Havok solver switch in hkExportImpulsesAndRhs
(called from hkMultiThreadedSimulation::processNextJob) has this shape;
a hard collision takes it, the worker returns with clobbered
callee-saved registers, reads through NULL and the main thread waits
forever in waitForStepWorldFinished (#155).

The base search now considers only definitions before the table load.
A stack reload is followed to the nearest preceding store of that slot,
stopping at any frame change, and the stored register is resolved as a
one- or two-level TOC load. Based on upstream sp00nznet/ps3recomp
3bbd31b (one-level spilled bases); the two-level case is added here
because the MotorStorm dispatcher loads its base through a TOC-addressed
global.

1428828361.readme_excerpt:
# MotorStorm Monument Valley native recompilation tooling

Work in progress: Windows runner, translation tools, a modified [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) runtime and growing handwritten native x86 game operations for MotorStorm 1. A playable native race has **not** been demonstrated. This repository distributes source glue and documentation; game binaries, assets, firmware, generated guest code, keys, saves and captures stay local.

**You must supply your own legally obtained game files.** The source license covers this tooling, not the game. Setup and generation run locally; this repository provides no game downloads.

Start with [setup and build](docs/BUILDING.md), then [running and capturing](docs/OPERATIONS.md). Track atomic work in [GitHub issues](https://github.com/robbe1912/motorstorm-mv-recomp/issues). [Documentation index](docs/README.md) groups the research by topic.

[Asset extraction and reconstruction](docs/assets/README.md) records reusable texture, mesh and material contracts, with a [MotorStorm worked example](docs/assets/MOTORSTORM.md) and notes for a future Rust implementation.

See [vendor provenance and licenses](docs/VENDOR.md) and [publication audit](docs/REPOSITORY.md). Source licensing does not grant rights to the game or guarantee immunity from legal claims. No affiliation with Sony or the original developers.

# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível, mas ainda lento (~16-17 fps). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot ao primeiro nível:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal e o primeiro nível, com o Kratos acorrentado. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~30 fps; o primeiro nível a ~16-17 fps (era ~9). O limite é o código das SPUs recompilado, não a placa de vídeo: o job de geometria por draw (módulo 218) é o maior custo, e está sendo reescrito como código nativo, validado contra jobs gravados do jogo, sem precisar rodá-lo. - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo, controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md). ## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), abra o launcher: ```powershell .\scripts\windows\launcher.ps1 ```

JOGAR abre o jogo dentro da própria janela do launcher. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

1428966995.readme_excerpt:
# PORTal: ports nativos de consolas a PC

Directorio de los ports **nativos y no oficiales** a PC que están apareciendo en GitHub, en tres categorías:

- **PS4**: Bloodborne, God of War III, Uncharted, Shadow of the Colossus, inFAMOUS, Driveclub, P.T., CTR… (el código x86-64 corre directo + runtime propio).
- **PS2**: Jak and Daxter (OpenGOAL), Ratchet & Clank, Sly Cooper, God of War, Ace Combat 5, ICO… (recompilación estática con PS2Recomp, decompilaciones, motores reescritos).
- **PS3 / Xbox 360**: Sonic Unleashed, Skate 3, Fable II, Dead Rising 2, Saints Row, Demon's Souls, Drakengard 3, Tekken… (XenonRecomp, ReXGlue SDK, ps3recomp).
Muestra para cada juego **todos los ports que existen** y para cada port:

- **Estado**: completo / jugable / parcial / temprano / no jugable
- **Rendimiento** reportado (FPS, resolución y hardware)
- **Fallos conocidos**
- Plataformas, versión del juego requerida (CUSA), en qué proyecto se basa
- Métricas en vivo: estrellas, commits de la semana, última release y si el repo fue **eliminado** (DMCA)
- **Reportes de la comunidad** enviados desde un formulario

Además tiene un **Radar** que encuentra solo los ports nuevos.

## Cómo funciona

```
data/catalog.json      ← curado a mano: juegos, ports, estado, rendimiento, fallos
data/github.json       ← automático: métricas de cada repo del catálogo
data/candidates.json   ← automático: radar de repos nuevos detectados
data/reports.json      ← automático: reportes de rendimiento (issues con label "reporte")
data/ignore.json       ← repos que el radar no debe volver a proponer
```

`scripts/update.mjs` corre en GitHub Actions **cada 6 horas** (`.github/workflows/site.yml`):

1. **Refresca** cada repo del catálogo con la API de GitHub. Si un repo desaparece, lo marca como eliminado y conserva los últimos datos.
2. **Radar**: hace ~30 búsquedas en GitHub (`"pc port" ps4`, `CUSA vulkan port`, `bbport`, `ps2recomp`, `ps3recomp`, `rexglue`, `xenonrecomp`, `"xbox 360" recomp`…)
   y revisa los forks nuevos de los proyectos base (bbport, SpartanPort…). A cada repo le lee el README y lo clasifica (`scripts/lib.mjs`):
   - suma puntos por: PS4/CUSA, "native", "PC port", "bring your own dump", runtimes conocidos, Vulkan…
   - descarta: **spam/piratería** (torrent, t.me, repack…), **homebrew hacia PS4** (GoldHEN, OpenOrbis), **herramientas** (launchers, wikis, traducciones) y otras consolas.
   - detecta la **consola de origen** (PS4, PS2, PS3 o Xbox 360) por nombre, descripción, códigos de producto (CUSA, SLUS/SCES, BLUS/NPUB, xex) y herramientas base.
   - descarta también ports a celulares u otras consolas (Switch, PS5, Vita) y forks de emuladores (PCSX2, RPCS3, Xenia).
   - extrae CUSA, plataformas, cifras de FPS y una pista de estado ("playable", "start to finish"…), y adivina el juego.
3. Cuando aparecen candidatos nuevos **abre un issue** "Radar: N ports nuevos" para revisarlos. Confirmar uno = moverlo a `catalog.json`.
4. Lee los issues con label `reporte` (formulario `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/reporte.yml`) y los muestra en la ficha del port.
5. **Detecta actualizaciones importantes** (`analyzeRelease` en `scripts/lib.mjs`): lee las notas de cada release nueva
   (en inglés, español o portugués) y la marca como **grande** si trae mejoras de FPS ("+25% FPS", "30 → 60 fps", "+FPS"),
   3 o más funciones nuevas (FSR 4, DLSS, frame generation, online, ultrawide…; solo cuentan las que no estaban en la release anterior),
   un hito ("start to finish", "de principio a fin") o un salto de versión con novedades. También avisa si un repo desaparece.
   Todo queda en `data/updates.json` y en el feed `data/feed.xml`.
6. **Avisos**: comenta en el issue "seguir" de cada port (formulario `seguir.yml`, botón 🔔 Avisarme en la ficha) y en el issue
   global con label `avisos`. Quien esté suscripto recibe mail y notificación en la app de GitHub.
7. Hace commit de `data/` y publica el sitio en la rama `gh-pages` (GitHub Pages).

### Favoritos y notificaciones

- **★ Favorito** en la ficha de cada port: se guarda en tu navegador. Hay un filtro "Mis favoritos" y la campana 🔔
  del encabezado cuenta las novedades grandes de tus favoritos desde tu última visita.
- **🔔 Avisarme**: abre (o crea) el issue de seguimiento de ese port en GitHub → mail + push en la app de GitHub.
- **Todas las novedades**: suscribirse al issue `avisos`.
- **Notificación del navegador**: se activa en la pestaña Novedades; avisa al abrir el sitio.
- **RSS/Atom**: `https://isidropenh.github.io/PORTal/data/feed.xml`.

El sitio es HTML/CSS/JS estático, sin dependencias ni build (`index.html`, `assets/`).

## Publicación

Ya está andando: el sitio se publica en **https://isidropenh.github.io/PORTal/** desde la rama `gh-pages`,
que el workflow regenera en cada actualización. No hace falta tocar Settings.
Para forzar una actualización: **Actions → "Actualizar y publicar" → Run workflow**.

## Desarrollo local

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000          # abrir http://localhost:8000
node scripts/test.mjs                # tests del clasificador y del catálogo
GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) node scripts/update.mjs   # refrescar datos a mano
```

## Agregar o corregir un port

Editar `data/catalog.json`. Campos de cada port:

| campo | valores |
|---|---|
| `platform` (del juego) | `ps4`, `ps2`, `ps3`, `x360` |
| `type` | `native` (x86-64 original + runtime), `recomp` (recompilación estática), `decomp`, `reimpl` (motor reescrito), `wrapper` (fork de emulador) |
| `status` | `complete`, `playable`, `partial`, `early`, `research` |
| `platforms` | `windows`, `linux`, `macos` |
| `performance`, `issues`, `features` | listas de texto |

`node scripts/test.mjs` valida el catálogo.

## Aviso

Solo se enlaza a código fuente. Ningún proyecto listado incluye archivos de juego ni firmware; todos requieren un dump de tu propia copia.
No se aceptan enlaces a descargas de juegos.

0650a59088532c1a0a3469cdd8812fa457a80bf0.message:
cellGcm: _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel queues the label wait and the flip

libgcm appends NV406E SEMAPHORE_OFFSET and SEMAPHORE_ACQUIRE for the
label, then the flip, so the RSX flips only once the label holds the
value. RPCS3's _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel writes the same two
methods into the context before its flip command. The import here
ignored its context, wrote the label itself from the PPU, and flipped
at call time: whoever owns the label was overruled, and the flip
waited for nothing.

Write the two semaphore methods into the context and queue the flip
behind them with gcm_flip_into_fifo, as _cellGcmSetFlipCommand already
does. A context that is not a mapped command buffer, or has no room,
falls back to the immediate form as before.

0ba1229e2c0b4b6003604a06e80fb330dccc1083.message:
sys_ppu_thread: non-joinable threads free their slot when they end

sys_ppu_thread_create ignored its flags and made every thread joinable, so a
thread created without SYS_PPU_THREAD_CREATE_JOINABLE stayed FINISHED after
its exit and held its slot for good. Once 63 such threads had run, every
later create returned CELL_EAGAIN.

joinable is now flags & 1. A non-joinable (or detached) thread frees its
slot at the end of ppu_host_thread_proc, after closing its event and handle
(Windows) or destroying its mutex/cond (POSIX, where the host thread is
detached at creation), under the table lock. sys_ppu_thread_exit leaves the
freeing to that epilogue; the main thread is still marked FINISHED there.
The create log line shows the flags.

tests/test_ppu_thread_slots.c (tools/test_ppu_thread_slots.py): 192
non-joinable threads created and finished in turn all succeed and leave no
slot in use; 63 unjoined joinable threads still fill the table, and a join
frees a slot. Fails on master at the 64th create (0x80010001).

0bd8f34314bc6c29741548bfdd8d690ce351bc5a.message:
cellGcmSys: main-memory maps take the first free IO pages; none before Init

gcm_io_alloc was a bump pointer that survived cellGcmInit, so a title that
maps main memory before Init got its next map placed on top of Init's
command-buffer window, and the FIFO walker then read the wrong memory.

gcm_io_alloc now picks the lowest run of free 1MB pages from the IO -> EA
table (never io page 0) and returns 0xFFFFFFFF when none is free.
cellGcmMapMainMemory refuses with CELL_GCM_ERROR_NO_IO_PAGE_TABLE before
cellGcmInit and when IO space is full, and logs the io it returns. The
cellGcmAddressToOffset auto-map runs only after Init.

tests/test_gcm_io_alloc.c (tools/test_gcm_io_alloc.py): a map before Init
is refused; after Init maps land at 0x800000, 0xE00000 and 0x1000000 and the
Init window is kept; freed holes are reused; IO-full refusal.

tools/test_gcm_io_mappings.py follows the change: its harness now has the
IO page table, GCM_IO_PAGES and an initialised GCM, measures the leak on
the page table, and checks that a map before Init is refused.

0e26194770079d251b113cbc28bb41e27199ac76.message:
sys_spu: an SPU's user event finds the port the PPU binds, and waits for it

An SPU's send_event (interrupt mailbox, code 0..63) was routed only through the ports the group binds with
sys_spu_thread_group_connect_event_all_threads, and answered ENOTCONN at once when there was none. Two things go
wrong with that:

- A port bound for one SPU thread with sys_spu_thread_connect_event was never found by the delivery, only by the
  plain out-mailbox path.
- The SPU thread starts running at sys_spu_thread_group_start while the PPU is still on its way to the connect
  calls that follow it (a real SPU needs far longer to boot than a lifted one). The first request of the program
  was answered ENOTCONN and the SPU program gave up. SoulCalibur II HD's audio engine (MultiStream) binds its ports
  with sys_spu_thread_connect_event, after group_start, and failed this way.

The delivery now looks at the thread's own bindings before the group's (spu_port_queue_locked) and, when the port
is not bound yet, waits for a binding for up to 200 ms on a condition variable that both connect calls signal
before it answers ENOTCONN. An SPU whose thread does not exist is answered at once, since nothing will bind its
port. The out-mailbox path reads the bindings through the same helper under the lock.

The test calls the real handlers and spu_deliver_user_event: bound for the thread, bound for the group, bound 40 ms
late either way, never bound (answers after about 200 ms) and an SPU with no thread (answers at once). On v0.15.0
it fails six checks; with the change it passes (five runs in a row).

test_gcm_flip_wrap.c, and checks on a title context:

1. _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel puts SEMAPHORE_OFFSET and
   SEMAPHORE_ACQUIRE for the label, then the flip marker, into the
   context, moves current past them, and leaves the label alone.
2. A tick before the drain is a vblank, not a flip.
3. Once the drain has executed up to the marker, the next tick
   completes the flip.
4. A flip written but not flushed does not complete; an executed one
   does, even with a newer flip written behind it and not flushed.

122690f29d9d566a679fce9944c4718a674ed79b.message:
fp decompiler: biased unsigned remap and _bx2 fetches return signed values

Two ways a fetch comes back re-centred to -1..1 were ignored, so the
shader saw 0..1 encodings:

- SET_TEXTURE_ADDRESS bit 12, UNSIGNED_REMAP_BIASED, applies to every
  fetch from the unit: (round(x*255)-128)/127 on the lanes the crossbar
  fills from a source channel (16-bit X16/Y16_X16 channels: /32767),
  after gamma and not on gamma lanes, and not on lanes the filter flags
  signed. rsx_texture_expand_mask computes the lanes, for the formats
  RPCS3 gives RSX_FORMAT_FEATURE_BIASED_NORMALIZATION.
- EXP_TEX (OPDEST bit 21, the _bx2 modifier) belongs to the instruction,
  not the texture: x*2-1 on every lane of any unit, bypassing gamma
  (RPCS3 _process_texel). It applies from every entry point.

inFAMOUS 2 reads its normals G-buffer through a biased unit and its
tangent-space normal maps and occlusion-cone lookup tables with TEX_bx2
(about a quarter of its fragment programs). Read unexpanded, every
normal leaned towards (1,1,1), normal maps had no effect, and the
occlusion volumes round props drew as dark boxes.

The engine passes the expand masks of the units a program samples
through a new entry point, rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_expand_ex,
and hashes them into the pipeline key. A program with neither feature
is byte-identical.

d3d12: key the per-draw vertex program cache on the program, not on the store behind it

vp_get_vs hashed the microcode from SET_TRANSFORM_PROGRAM_START to the end of everything uploaded. A title that
keeps several programs resident and uploads another one behind the program it draws with changes that hash on
every upload, so nearly every draw missed the cache and ran D3DCompile on the FIFO thread. SoulCalibur II HD on
Windows stalled after its opening movie that way, and its audio, fed from the same frame loop, starved.

The hash now ends at the program's end bit (rsx_vp_program_size_instrs, which the Metal backend and the draw engine
already use), and the decompiler is given that length. The cache holds 128 programs instead of 16: a fight in that
title draws with more than 16, and an eviction shifts the slots the recorded draws point at.

Not built with MSVC and not run on a D3D12 device from this branch: checked with a mingw -fsyntax-only (no new
diagnostics). The stall went away on Windows with this change carried as a patch on v0.14.0 (the toolkit this port was
started on); there is no benchmark of this change alone.

17bf55aa590b12b5e2c37c6885718526f8b59804.message:
cellGcm: NV3089 source origin is 12.4, the copy counted it 256 times too small

IMAGE_IN_POINT is 12.4 fixed point per axis, and DS_DX / DT_DY step the source with 20 fractional bits (1.0 =
0x100000). nv3089_blit's copy loops added the origin to that position as origin << 8, so a source offset counted
1/256 of what it is: for any origin under 256 texels the loops started at column 0 and row 0. The GPU paths in the
same function (rsx_live_draw_blit, rsx_live_draw_resolve_blit) already took origin >> 4, so the two disagreed, and
nv3089_engine_read, which writes the source rectangle back from the draw engine before the copy, took it as origin >> 4
for its start and << 8 for its end.

1e6f4c8e744a66f6f5163f6f8def38470742e50b.message:
vulkan: colour feedback snapshots for draws that sample their own target

A draw that samples the colour target it is writing gets, on Metal, a
copy of that target taken just before it (rsx_draw_backend.color_snapshot).
In-place deferred lighting works this way: read the albedo, write the lit
colour over it. The Vulkan backend had no such hook, so the engine fell
back to the guest-memory bytes at the target's address, which hold
whatever was last stored there.

On Twisted Metal (BCES01010) the G-buffer's first target (0x00AB0000) is
also the UI target. Its lighting passes therefore read the previous
frame's menu instead of the albedo just drawn, lit it, and composited it
into the next frame. That is the red frame, the red and green splatter
and the white logo on its main menu.

vk_eng_color_snapshot copies the target into a new image of the same
format and size, and ends with a barrier so the copy is visible to the
next draw. Every operation here is already one synchronous submission,
so the copy is in command order. The copy is a COLOR object marked
`snapshot`, so the engine can take a crossbar view of it; it is never an
attachment, so releasing it drops no framebuffer. A lit frame asks for
one copy per light, so released copies return their images to a pool of
eight, drained at engine shutdown.

32a85600293ba2cf2a21bcb1150bcc0dbd6fb63a.message:
vulkan: present on its own command buffer, in two halves a host can split

The FIFO walker and the present shared one command buffer and one
fence, and a present waited for two GPU round trips: the engine's blit
of the flipped surface into the offscreen target, then the copy of that
target into the readback buffer. A host that presents on the walker's
thread holds the walker for all of that, about 1.3 ms per frame headless.
One that moves the present to a thread of its own still had to hold its
walker lock for the whole present, since both recorded into s_vk.cmd.

On Twisted Metal (BCES01010) that is the window in which the title
moves put to its other ring segment and starts writing its next frame
over the one it left, JUMP out of it included. The walker resumes 2.4 ms
later and executes the new frame's data as commands.

The present now has its own command pool, command buffer and fences,
and comes in two halves:

- rsx_vulkan_backend_present_begin() records the blit and the copy out
  and submits them without waiting. It reads the flipped surface, so it
  runs under the host's walker lock, but only for the recording.
- rsx_vulkan_backend_present_finish() waits for that copy, reads the
  centre pixel and the dump back, and blits into the window. It may run
  while the walker drains the next frame.

rsx_vulkan_backend_present() is both, so existing hosts see no
difference. The fixed-function path, which draws into the offscreen
target itself, still finishes inside present_begin.

What keeps the two halves apart:
- vkQueueSubmit, vkQueuePresentKHR and vkDeviceWaitIdle go through
  queue_mu, since the queue is now used from two threads.
- The walker's next command buffer starts with a full barrier after a
  present's copy. Its per-image barriers already order most work after
  earlier submissions; this one covers the rest.
- No image is destroyed while a present's copy may still read it.
- present_mu keeps a flip in the command stream (presented on the
  walker's thread) from overlapping a host thread's finish.

spu_dma: the identical-transfer halt also needs wall time

mfc_submit halts an SPU after SPU_DMA_REPEAT_LIMIT (256) identical
transfers in a row, on the reasoning that a job doing nothing but the same
DMA is wedged. A job that polls a value another agent writes does the same:
God of War: Ascension's EDGE geometry jobs wait for ring space by re-reading
an RSX label until the GPU catches up. 256 reads take well under a
millisecond, so the guard halted healthy jobs and the frame never completed.

Halt only when the repeats have also lasted SPU_DMA_REPEAT_SECS (default
30 s) of wall time. A truly wedged job is still caught, 30 s later.

3ca13f66211402f8d9b2e62a1ad9d6a92334f04e.message:
fix(template): mmap the guest arena on POSIX so vm_commit can mprotect it

The POSIX branch of alloc_guest_vm() allocated the 0xE0000000-byte flat
arena with calloc. glibc serves an allocation that size from its own mmap
chunk and returns a pointer 16 bytes past the page start, so vm_base was
never page-aligned. vm_commit() hands vm_base + addr to mprotect, which
rejects unaligned addresses with EINVAL; every commit failed, and
sys_memory_allocate answered CELL_ENOMEM to every call. A title that
retries the allocation spins forever (Warhawk: 19.7 M calls in 60 s).

Map the arena with mmap(MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS|MAP_NORESERVE) instead,
as runtime/memory/vm.h already does: page-aligned, zero-filled, lazily
backed. ppu_vm_size and the Windows VirtualAlloc path are unchanged.
macOS was unaffected only because libmalloc page-aligns large blocks.

Verified: Warhawk NPEA00017 boots headless on Linux to its intro movie;
check_ppu_scaffold.py reports no regression.

3d5d03bdc7f627a424fb53ce42175984d596a377.message:
runtime: classify syscall 14 by guest address segment

sys_process_is_spu_lock_line_reservation_address answered EINVAL for
every address above the 256 MB VM_MAIN window (0x00010000..0x1000FFFF),
including the rest of segment 0x1 that the same guest allocator hands
out. SPURS validates its management areas through this syscall during
cellSpursInitialize and aborts init on failure, so a legitimate
management area produced a spurious CELL_SPURS_CORE_ERROR_PERM and every
SPU job the instance would have run stayed unstarted.

The contract is RPCS3's process_is_spu_lock_line_reservation_address
(Emu/Cell/lv2/sys_process.cpp): classify by the address segment
(0x0/0x1/0x2/0xC/0xE reservation-capable; 0xF refuses RawSPU; 0xD
refuses; sys_vm mappings refuse, holes in the mapped region EINVAL; rest
EINVAL) with the flags masked to the two SPU bits. The old sys_vm EPERM
check is kept, now through the tracked mappings (g_sys_vm_maps): a
covered address answers EPERM, a hole in the mapped region EINVAL,
matching RPCS3's default branch.

The classification moves to runtime/syscalls/lv2_lock_line.c so
tests/syscalls can unit-test it without linking the syscall layer.

Test: tests/syscalls/test_lock_line (27 checks: segments 0x0/0x1/0x2/
0xC/0xE OK, 0xF EPERM with RawSPU, 0xD EPERM, sys_vm covered/hole/empty,
flag validation).

45baa4791a794597cfaa0d0d4879347cb637b581.message:
rsx engine: 2D transfers read FP16 colour targets

A transfer out of a render target first writes the GPU's pixels back to
guest memory (rsx_draw_engine_guest_read), but only A8R8G8B8 surfaces were
looked up. Twisted Metal renders its bloom and Sweet Tooth's flaming hair
into an FP16 RGBA target and copies that out with NV3089 for its SPU
post-FX; the copy found no surface, the SPUs got stale memory, and neither
the bloom nor the flames reached the image.

The lookup now takes FP16 RGBA targets too. A transfer counts 32-bit
pixels, so the readback covers every surface pixel the transfer's bytes
touch and stores exactly those bytes, as big-endian R,G,B,A halves: the
layout rsx_texture_decode reads W16_Z16_Y16_X16_FLOAT from. A transfer
INTO an FP16 target is still not pushed: color_target_write takes
A8R8G8B8 rows.

English. PS3_LANG takes a CELL_SYSUTIL_LANG_* number (0..19) or a code

4f223b376f890582608dcd00a3ae2b3ab9e7b483.message:
cellAudio: let WASAPI shared mode convert the 48 kHz stereo float stream

The Windows backend opens the default render endpoint in shared mode with

device's own mix format unless the stream asks the audio engine to
convert, so on any output not running exactly that format (44.1 kHz, 5.1,
24-bit PCM mix) IAudioClient::Initialize fails with
AUDCLNT_E_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT (0x88890008), the backend gives up and every
title runs silent.

on both Initialize attempts (event-driven and polled). The flags are
defined locally when the SDK headers predate them.

517fc717f73030d62dbaa9a991c118c6bd3cd6a2.message:
spu: the single-precision fast path four lanes at a time with AVX2

On x86, spu_fa/fs/fm/fma/fms/fnms took the per-lane path: each lane
widened to double on its own, and a call per instruction. arm64 has had
a NEON path doing the four lanes at once. This is the same path for
x86 with AVX2: the lanes widened to one f64x4 (exact), the operation,
the 29 low significand bits cleared, narrowed (exact). The lane rules are
the NEON ones: an ordinary single or a true +-0 keeps the vector result,
a zero result loses its sign, fa/fs also needs the exponents within 29,
and fma keeps a lane only when TwoSum says the add did not round onto a
24-bit boundary. Other lanes are redone one by one by the exact path.

test_spu_float_neon compares the vector path with the exact references
bit for bit; it now runs on x86 with AVX2 too, and in the Linux CI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

57570462551fcc9c6f2391276953b1a5c91c48f1.message:
cellFiber: the SDK's scheduler API in place of the made-up one

libs/spurs/cellFiber.{c,h} exposed cellFiberPpuInitialize/Finalize, a CellFiber handle, a
four-argument cellFiberPpuCreateFiber(fiber, entry, arg, attr), SwitchFiber, Sleep/Wakeup and
error codes from 0x80410801. None of that is the SDK's. The HLE binds by name, so a title
importing the real cellFiberPpuCreateFiber landed in the four-argument function and read its
eight arguments from the wrong registers.

The SDK's PPU fibers are scheduler based, and this implements them:

- _cellFiberPpuInitialize, _cellFiberPpuSchedulerAttributeInitialize and
  _cellFiberPpuAttributeInitialize (attributes are zeroed, 256 bytes each);
- cellFiberPpuInitializeScheduler / FinalizeScheduler, and
  cellFiberPpuCreateFiber(scheduler, fiber, entry, arg, priority, eaStack, sizeStack, attr);
- cellFiberPpuRunFibers: runs the fibers on the calling thread until every one has ended, lowest
  priority number first, creation order among equals. A scheduler whose fibers wait for a signal
  from another thread waits for it instead of returning;
- WaitSignal / SendSignal (a signal sent early is kept), JoinFiber (from a fiber, which hands
  control back to the scheduler meanwhile, or from any thread, with the exit status), Yield,
  Exit and Self.

Each fiber runs the guest entry through the PPU thread trampoline on its own host stack (ucontext,
Windows fibers on Windows) with its own ppu_context; r1 is inside the guest stack the caller
passed, r3 the argument, and the entry's return value the exit status. The error codes are the
SDK's 0x8076xxxx, and the structures have the SDK's sizes and 128-byte alignment (scheduler 512,
fiber 896, both attributes 256).

Not implemented: the contents of the attributes, and the cellFiberPpuUtil* worker control. Yield,
Exit and Self follow the documented behaviour and are covered by the unit test only; the port that
this was written for does not call them.

tests/fiber_switch is rewritten for the new API: run order and arguments, guest stack point

584181aba7a5fe736123213cefc269ea9a630e5c.message:
metal engine: each MRT target takes its own colour mask and blend enable

Every attachment of an MRT set took target A's COLOR_MASK and
BLEND_ENABLE. On the RSX, targets B..D have their own: a nibble each of
COLOR_MASK_MRT (0x0370, A,R,G,B at bits 0..3 of the nibble) and a bit
each of BLEND_ENABLE_MRT (0x036C), as RPCS3 reads them
(color_mask_*(index), blend_enabled_surface_*).

Giving every target A's state was wrong both ways. inFAMOUS 2's light
volumes add into target A with B and C masked off, and the shared state
added every light into the G-buffer: lit props blew out to white, with a
bright rectangle round each light. Its material passes write B and C's
alpha with A's alpha masked, which left them stale.

The engine decodes both registers into the render state (and the
pipeline key), and the Metal backend applies them per attachment.
PS3RECOMP_METAL_MRT_MASK=0 restores the old behaviour for bisecting.

6752b12939e5c6a34be15c85b9d1e813e19360ab.message:
cellGcm: bounded semaphore acquire; the stuck-get watchdog leaves waits alone

GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1 makes NV406E ACQUIRE block the drain, as the hardware
does, but the stuck-get watchdog counts drain passes, not time: a drain
that stops on an acquire, or on a self-JUMP park, stops every pass at the
same get, so after eight passes (a few milliseconds) it resynced to put
and dropped everything in between. For a park that happens before the
title has patched it into a JUMP to the commands it just wrote at the
ring start, i.e. before GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS has had a chance to run out.
inFAMOUS 2 stopped presenting for good that way in about one run in five
("stuck-get" at a self-jump with no "jump-park" before it).

A pass that stops on an acquire or a park now resets the watchdog; each
of those waits has its own bound. The acquire gets one:
GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS=<ms> consumes an acquire that has waited that long on
the same label and value, and says so, so a label nobody ever writes
cannot wedge the drain. inFAMOUS 2 acquires a label its SPU lighting job
writes every frame; with GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1 GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS=200 its
lit props stop flashing white and its characters stop rendering black.

between the backend's R,G,B,A and the guest's A8R8G8B8. Both copied a
byte at a time, testing TEX_RGBA for every pixel, and at the -O2 the
runtime builds with GCC vectorises neither.

copy, the two loops were about a quarter of the FIFO thread's CPU time
during boot (in-process sampling of that thread: 19.5% guest_read,
9.0% guest_wrote).

(eng_row_convert), and the TEX_RGBA case is a memcpy per row. A
1280x720 frame converts in 0.55 ms instead of 0.98 ms with the
runtime's flags (GCC 16, -O2 -msse4.1), with identical output. In the
same Twisted Metal window the two functions drop to 14.2% and 6.9%.

moved it, so the next cellFsRead continued from wherever the AIO stopped.
And titles issue AIO reads from several threads at once (FIOS media threads,
audio streamers) on the same fd, so another thread's seek could land between
the seek and the read.

Hold the stream lock (flockfile / _lock_file, the lock stdio's own calls
take) across the seek, the read and the seek back to the saved position.
The request id counter is atomic for the same reason.

tools/test_ppu_fs_aio.py builds runtime/ppu/tests/test_fs_aio.cpp: on
master the cellFsRead after an AIO read gets the wrong bytes, and 3373 of
8000 AIO reads racing from four threads return someone else's data; with
this change both pass.
