57570462551fcc9c6f2391276953b1a5c91c48f1.message:
cellFiber: the SDK's scheduler API in place of the made-up one

libs/spurs/cellFiber.{c,h} exposed cellFiberPpuInitialize/Finalize, a CellFiber handle, a
four-argument cellFiberPpuCreateFiber(fiber, entry, arg, attr), SwitchFiber, Sleep/Wakeup and
error codes from 0x80410801. None of that is the SDK's. The HLE binds by name, so a title
importing the real cellFiberPpuCreateFiber landed in the four-argument function and read its
eight arguments from the wrong registers.

The SDK's PPU fibers are scheduler based, and this implements them:

- _cellFiberPpuInitialize, _cellFiberPpuSchedulerAttributeInitialize and
  _cellFiberPpuAttributeInitialize (attributes are zeroed, 256 bytes each);
- cellFiberPpuInitializeScheduler / FinalizeScheduler, and
  cellFiberPpuCreateFiber(scheduler, fiber, entry, arg, priority, eaStack, sizeStack, attr);
- cellFiberPpuRunFibers: runs the fibers on the calling thread until every one has ended, lowest
  priority number first, creation order among equals. A scheduler whose fibers wait for a signal
  from another thread waits for it instead of returning;
- WaitSignal / SendSignal (a signal sent early is kept), JoinFiber (from a fiber, which hands
  control back to the scheduler meanwhile, or from any thread, with the exit status), Yield,
  Exit and Self.

Each fiber runs the guest entry through the PPU thread trampoline on its own host stack (ucontext,
Windows fibers on Windows) with its own ppu_context; r1 is inside the guest stack the caller
passed, r3 the argument, and the entry's return value the exit status. The error codes are the
SDK's 0x8076xxxx, and the structures have the SDK's sizes and 128-byte alignment (scheduler 512,
fiber 896, both attributes 256).

Not implemented: the contents of the attributes, and the cellFiberPpuUtil* worker control. Yield,
Exit and Self follow the documented behaviour and are covered by the unit test only; the port that
this was written for does not call them.

tests/fiber_switch is rewritten for the new API: run order and arguments, guest stack point

584181aba7a5fe736123213cefc269ea9a630e5c.message:
metal engine: each MRT target takes its own colour mask and blend enable

Every attachment of an MRT set took target A's COLOR_MASK and
BLEND_ENABLE. On the RSX, targets B..D have their own: a nibble each of
COLOR_MASK_MRT (0x0370, A,R,G,B at bits 0..3 of the nibble) and a bit
each of BLEND_ENABLE_MRT (0x036C), as RPCS3 reads them
(color_mask_*(index), blend_enabled_surface_*).

Giving every target A's state was wrong both ways. inFAMOUS 2's light
volumes add into target A with B and C masked off, and the shared state
added every light into the G-buffer: lit props blew out to white, with a
bright rectangle round each light. Its material passes write B and C's
alpha with A's alpha masked, which left them stale.

The engine decodes both registers into the render state (and the
pipeline key), and the Metal backend applies them per attachment.
PS3RECOMP_METAL_MRT_MASK=0 restores the old behaviour for bisecting.

both textured draws to have run, so a rejected feedback draw cannot pass
by leaving the red in place. linux-vulkan.yml runs it in the
guest-program pass, under the validation layer.

627bba25c912461ed2afed98e6abaf60df5f2d02.message:
spurs_job: keep the job's first frame below its cache buffers

spu_run_spurs_job lays a job out as binary, I/O, output, scratch + stack,
then the cache-hinted inputs, so cacheBuffer[0] starts at the stack top.
$sp was set to stack_top - 16. A SPU function saves its link register in
its caller's frame at 16($sp), so the entry's first store wrote 16 bytes
over the start of cacheBuffer[0].

Twisted Metal's Edge geometry jobs keep their viewport there. They read
x = 0x3FF00 (the return address in $lr) and width = height = 0, so the
screen-space scale was zero, every triangle of a skinned mesh had zero
area, and the main view culled them all: Sweet Tooth was missing from the
main menu, while the shadow passes (which skip that culling) drew him.

Start $sp at stack_top - 32 so the caller's 32-byte frame is part of the
stack.

63415273254ff8e9025630fe619a66c746d21b26.message:
rsx engine: fragment-program debug knobs keyed by structural hash

Finding which pass paints a wrong smear, halo or black band, and why,
took either a guess from a shader listing or a pipeline handle that
changes from run to run with the order programs are first drawn in. A
fragment program's structural hash does not change, so the knobs below
name programs by it.

- The pipeline log and RSX_ENGINE_SHADER_DUMP's .fp.txt print each guest
  fragment program's hash (rsx_fp_structural_hash seeded with the FNV
  offset basis). The pipeline cache keeps it, so a draw has it for free.
- RSX_ENGINE_SKIP_FP=<hex>[,<hex>...] drops every draw through those
  programs.
- RSX_ENGINE_REGDUMP_FP=<hex>[,<hex>...] prints the non-zero RSX
  registers at the first draw through each, to diff a broken pass's state
  against a working one.
- RSX_FP_DEBUG=<hex>:<n>:<reg[.swz]> makes that program export register
  <reg> as it stood after its <n>-th instruction as colour target 0 with
  alpha 1: an intermediate of a long shader seen on screen.

All are read once and cost a compare per draw when unset.

6356a9ef96bce4b7be311cff20c2d9533bada9d5.message:
spu/tests: the signalled bit against an SPU commit to the same word

Two cases, built with the lock-line lock as in test_spu_lockline_peer.c
rather than raced for. A peer SPU has the bitset line reserved, the main
thread holds the lock, a second thread starts the host operation and is
held at the lock, an SPU commit sets another task's bit under the lock,
and only then is the host operation let through.

- spu_taskset_signal_task(task 4) against a commit of task 3's bit:
  both bits must be set.
- spu_taskset_wait_signal(task 3) consuming its signal against a commit
  of task 4's bit: task 4's bit must survive.

On master both fail (0x08000000 for 0x18000000, 0 for 0x08000000),
the same lost bits as Twisted Metal's post-FX barrier. Run in the Linux
and macOS workflows next to the SPURS task wake test.

cellPad: the small motor rumbles at full strength, and a rumble lasts until it changes

A DualShock 3's small motor is on/off: motor[0] is 0 or 1. Forwarded as
motor * 257 it reached the host at 257/65535, 1/255 of full, which a pad
does not feel. And each SDL request ran for 100 ms, while a PS3 title
sets the motors once and they stay on until it sets them again, so a long
rumble stopped almost at once (inFAMOUS 2 only calls when the value
changes).

The small motor is now on at full, the large one keeps 0-255. The last
request per port is kept, sent with a 1 s duration and renewed from the
pad poll every 400 ms while it is non-zero, so it lasts as long as the
title wants and still stops within a second if the title stops polling.
Zero stops the motors at once. XInput holds its motors itself and only
gets the level fix.

6752b12939e5c6a34be15c85b9d1e813e19360ab.message:
cellGcm: bounded semaphore acquire; the stuck-get watchdog leaves waits alone

GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1 makes NV406E ACQUIRE block the drain, as the hardware
does, but the stuck-get watchdog counts drain passes, not time: a drain
that stops on an acquire, or on a self-JUMP park, stops every pass at the
same get, so after eight passes (a few milliseconds) it resynced to put
and dropped everything in between. For a park that happens before the
title has patched it into a JUMP to the commands it just wrote at the
ring start, i.e. before GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS has had a chance to run out.
inFAMOUS 2 stopped presenting for good that way in about one run in five
("stuck-get" at a self-jump with no "jump-park" before it).

A pass that stops on an acquire or a park now resets the watchdog; each
of those waits has its own bound. The acquire gets one:
GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS=<ms> consumes an acquire that has waited that long on
the same label and value, and says so, so a label nobody ever writes
cannot wedge the drain. inFAMOUS 2 acquires a label its SPU lighting job
writes every frame; with GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1 GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS=200 its
lit props stop flashing white and its characters stop rendering black.

rsx engine: convert a transfer's rows a pixel at a time, not a byte at a time

rsx_draw_engine_guest_read and _guest_wrote move a 2D transfer's pixels
between the backend's R,G,B,A and the guest's A8R8G8B8. Both copied a
byte at a time, testing TEX_RGBA for every pixel, and at the -O2 the
runtime builds with GCC vectorises neither.

On Twisted Metal (BCES01010), once #334 removed the NV3089 per-pixel
copy, the two loops were about a quarter of the FIFO thread's CPU time
during boot (in-process sampling of that thread: 19.5% guest_read,
9.0% guest_wrote).

Each pixel is now one 32-bit load, one rotate and one store
(eng_row_convert), and the TEX_RGBA case is a memcpy per row. A
1280x720 frame converts in 0.55 ms instead of 0.98 ms with the
runtime's flags (GCC 16, -O2 -msse4.1), with identical output. In the
same Twisted Metal window the two functions drop to 14.2% and 6.9%.

7208d22b25b342696685640d1a715278e17e74f9.message:
cellFs: an AIO read keeps the fd's position and cannot interleave

cellFsAioRead did a bare seek + fread on the fd's shared FILE*. Its own
comment says AIO reads are absolute and leave the fd's position alone; they
moved it, so the next cellFsRead continued from wherever the AIO stopped.
And titles issue AIO reads from several threads at once (FIOS media threads,
audio streamers) on the same fd, so another thread's seek could land between
the seek and the read.

Hold the stream lock (flockfile / _lock_file, the lock stdio's own calls
take) across the seek, the read and the seek back to the saved position.
The request id counter is atomic for the same reason.

tools/test_ppu_fs_aio.py builds runtime/ppu/tests/test_fs_aio.cpp: on
master the cellFsRead after an AIO read gets the wrong bytes, and 3373 of
8000 AIO reads racing from four threads return someone else's data; with
this change both pass.

7c1d6f128d3d5af2b0e992cb4e2fa88271931fa4.message:
cellGcmSys: don't let a wrapped ring overwrite commands the RSX hasn't read

God of War HD fills its 3 MB command ring at boot and wraps it through the
runtime's buffer-full callback. Three things then let it write over
commands the walker had not reached, after which the walker decoded vertex
floats as JUMPs (0x3F800000 -> JUMP 0x1F800000) and resynced away frames:

- The recycle waited for g_gcm_fifo_drained_ea == begin, which is also true
  before the walker has moved at all, so it often didn't wait. It now waits
  for the walker to take a backward JUMP, i.e. the JUMP-to-begin it wrote.
- The wait gave up after 2 s in total. A ring of hundreds of tiny frames
  takes the draw engine far longer than that, and it was making progress.
  The bound is now 2 s without progress (60 s overall).
- While that callback waits, the title's context still reads
  current == end, which the drain's own overrun recycle took as an overrun
  and teleported get to begin, dropping the tail. It stands down while the
  callback is waiting.

The drain also stops at every flip unless backlogged, and measured the
backlog as put - get, so a wrapped ring (put behind get, the most backlogged
case) looked like no backlog at all. It is now measured around the ring when
both pointers are inside the title's context; other layouts are unchanged.

GCM_RECDBG reports the walker during the recycle wait, and
GCM_DRAINDBG_EVERY=<n> sets how often GCM_DRAINDBG logs a pass. Not run
against the other ports' regression gate (their games aren't here).

88187d115b6f3904501b1ef8e1b2707b7aed56c6.message:
Log caps: stop the counter at its limit (PS3_LOG_FIRST)

About 300 diagnostics were capped with `static int _n; if (_n++ < N)`. On a hot path
(MFC channel accesses, DMA, the SPU drain and workload loops) the signed counter passes
2^31, wraps negative, `_n < N` is true again and the line prints on every call: millions
of "[spu] drain-resume" lines in a long fight.

include/ps3emu/log_first.h has PS3_LOG_FIRST(ctr, limit), `((ctr) < (limit) && ++(ctr))`:
true for the first `limit` evaluations, then false, and the counter stops at the limit.
Every `x++ < N` cap in libs/ and runtime/ now uses it, and so do the `if (x++ >= N)
return;` forms (as `if (!PS3_LOG_FIRST(x, N)) return;`).

Left alone on purpose:
- the four periodic lines (`n < N || n % P == 0`: cellGcmGetReport, EventFlagSet, the
  WAIT_SIGNAL line, the usercmd line) need a counter that keeps going; three are now
  unsigned (wrapping is defined) and the fourth was already unsigned long;
- unit tests under runtime/*/tests, where the counter is a mismatch count;
- `s_exit_seen++ == 0`, a one-shot flag.

tests/test_log_first.c (registered as the ctest `log_first`) covers the stop at the limit,
INT_MAX, array-element counters, a variable limit and an OR-ed condition.

93cccd1d3c5332fff9bd13de773666c816b76198.message:
fp decompiler: honour perspective_corr on texcoord reads

SRC2 bit 31 (perspective_corr) on an instruction's texcoord read
multiplies the input by 1/w, as RPCS3's decompiler does ("Perspective
correct flag multiplies the result by 1/w"). The bit was ignored. A
vertex program that writes uv*w relies on it: inFAMOUS 2's water does,
for the screen copy it samples, and read raw the coordinates land far
outside the copy and the river renders black.

1/w comes from the fragment position. FXC (D3D12) gives SV_POSITION.w as
clip w, but glslang lowers it to SPIR-V FragCoord, whose w is already 1/w
(and Metal's [[position]] is (x, y, z, 1/w)), so the glslang paths define
RSX_FRAGCOORD_W_IS_RCP and the helper picks the right form. The helper is
emitted only when a program uses it, so every other program is
byte-identical.

a4b4a21d8d089e79d28e751c52f433bccc5674ac.message:
sys_spu: an SPU thread starts in the lifted image its own bytes identify

spu_lifted_thread_setup chose the thread's image by asking the registry which image owns the thread's entry point.
SPU programs all start near the same LS addresses (0xD0..0xF0), so two registered images can have code at one entry,
and the entry resolves to whichever registered first: the thread ran the other program's lifted code. SoulCalibur II
HD has two such images, and its audio engine (MultiStream) ran the wrong one.

sys_spu_thread_group_start now fingerprints the thread's sys_spu_image (the lookup the registry fallback right
below it already did) and gives spu_lifted_thread_setup the id of the image registered for those bytes,
spu_lifted_thread_desc.image_id. 0 keeps the lookup by entry point, so a thread whose image is not registered
behaves as before. The fingerprint lookup is one helper now, shared with the fallback.

The test replaces the registry with two images that both have code at 0xD0, A registered first, and follows what group
start does: B's bytes give B (the entry-based lookup, shown by the third check, gives A), A's give A, bytes nothing
registered and a thread without an image give 0. The new interface does not exist on v0.15.0, so the test only
builds with this change.

a594fa06fe400bd0ae86c525bf9b82bad468d526.message:
rsx engine: re-hash cached textures sparsely, in full every eighth frame

Every cached texture was hashed in full at its first use in a frame, to
notice the guest rewriting it. In inFAMOUS 2's New Marais that is about
950 textures and 88 MB a frame, 2.5 ms of the RSX thread, for the four
or so that actually change.

Now each use checks 64 bytes out of every 2 KB plus the last 64, and the
full hash runs when that check differs, when 8 frames have passed since
the entry's last full hash (new entries start staggered by slot, so the
full hashes spread out), always for a texture of 16 KB or less, and on
the next use after a surface store the engine itself made into the
texture. A whole rewrite (video, UI, streaming) is still seen at once; a
small write between the sampled blocks of a large texture can take up
to 7 frames. PS3RECOMP_ENG_TEXHASH_FULL=1 restores the full hash every
frame.

a6cfb0f07fd4226fe6daac59f931e31f3d47e538.message:
cellGcm: the NV3089 row copy takes its source origin as 12.4

IMAGE_IN_POINT is 12.4 fixed point and DS_DX / DT_DY step the source in
20 fractional bits, so the origin enters the copy as origin << 16. The
row copy used << 8, the same mistake as the per-pixel loop it was
written to match, and started at column 0 and row 0 for any origin
under 256 texels. It now uses nv3089_origin(), the helper #358
introduces for the per-pixel loops, defined the same way so the two
changes merge without a conflict.

a8572e9962344fe5cb49b78f7b647888fcce15c1.message:
cellGcmSys: publish get past a semaphore RELEASE before its label

The FIFO walker wrote a RELEASE's label at once but published the control
register's get only at a JUMP and at the end of the pass. On the RSX the
semaphore write lands after the command has been fetched, so a title that
sees the label may read get once and take it as the RSX's position.
Ratchet & Clank: Tools of Destruction waits for a label, reads get, then
spins until its own put equals it; the snapshot from before the RELEASE
never did, and boot stalled there.

The RELEASE now publishes get past the whole command (unless
GCM_GET_EQ_PUT is set), then a release fence, then the label.
test_gcm_get_on_release drives OFFSET/RELEASE and a two-method
ACQUIRE+RELEASE through the walker and reads both from a user-command
probe mid-pass, with and without GCM_GET_EQ_PUT.

a98af7c9075a6911d4ec5021a512941cb9f9d11f.message:
cellGcm: get follows the walker across a JUMP

On the RSX, get is the fetch pointer, so a title polling it sees the
GPU leave a command segment as soon as the JUMP out of it is taken.
The walker published get only at the end of a drain pass. On a slow
host that comes tens of milliseconds after the JUMP: Twisted Metal
(BCES01010) has boot-time passes of 50 to 165 ms, mostly NV3089 blits
and surface readbacks.

Twisted Metal flushes put into its other ring segment, then writes the
next frame over the segment it left. When the walker reaches the JUMP
at the old put late, the JUMP has already been overwritten. The title
port works around this by waiting, after its flush, for get to leave
the old put. With get published only at the end of the pass, that wait
ran into its 100 ms bound 4 times per boot even though the JUMP had
been taken at once. With this change it does so 2 times in 12 runs.

A taken JUMP now publishes its target as get. A park (a JUMP to itself)
publishes nothing, and GCM_GET_EQ_PUT keeps its own value.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

b1f14fff9e8174b3575212691ebdaef7aae069b7.message:
rsx: cache HLSL -> SPIR-V translations, in memory and optionally on disk

glslang takes 20-150 ms per shader, on the thread that walks the FIFO,
and the engine asks for the same HLSL again for every pipeline that
shares a program. Twisted Metal (BCES01010) translates 236 shaders in
its first minute, 74 of them distinct: 4.4 s of glslang per 90 s run,
95 stalls over 20 ms.

rsx_hlsl_to_spirv now keeps each translation, keyed by the stage and the
whole HLSL text, so a hit returns exactly the words that text translated
to. PS3RECOMP_SPIRV_CACHE=<existing directory> also keeps them on disk,
one file per shader; the file stores the key, the glslang version and
the translator's build stamp, and any mismatch is a miss that rewrites
the file. Failed translations are not cached.

Twisted Metal, 90 s runs: glslang time 4.4 s -> 1.1-2.0 s with the
memory cache alone, 5 ms with a warm disk cache, and no translation
over 20 ms.

b883922940d53efafac47dcc0b63dac7535294c5.message:
rsx_draw_engine, vulkan: honour the depth bounds test

NV4097 SET_DEPTH_BOUNDS_TEST_ENABLE (0x0380) with SET_DEPTH_BOUNDS_MIN and
_MAX (0x0384, 0x0388, floats) rejects a fragment whose stored depth lies
outside the bounds, whatever the depth test says. The draw engine never
read those registers, so a bounded draw covered the whole target.

Twisted Metal's deferred renderer relies on it: its sun pass is bounded to
[0, 0.999984] (the geometry) and the sky drawn right after it to
[0.999984, 1] (the far plane), both with the depth test off. Unbounded, the
sky overwrote the sun light everywhere and the HDR buffer came out almost
black.

The enable is pipeline state (rsx_be_render_state.depth_bounds_test, part
of the pipeline key); the bounds reach the backend before every draw through
a new optional hook, set_depth_bounds, like the stencil reference, so moving
them does not build pipelines. Vulkan enables the depthBounds feature when
the device has it and sets the bounds dynamically, clamped to [0, 1];
without the feature the test stays off, as before, with one log line.
Metal and the fixed-function path leave the hook unset and draw as before.

Tests: test_rsx_draw_engine checks the key, the bounds and that moving them
builds no pipeline (4 new checks, failing without the engine change).
ps3recomp_host --depthbounds draws red at z = 0.25, then blue bounded to
[0, 0.5] and green bounded to [0.5, 1] with the depth test off, and expects
blue; it runs in the Vulkan workflow's engine pass under the validation
layer.

b8a7c5b30057bd863df592edb02e1d4875ca2551.message:
fp decompiler: read FACING, TC8 and TC9

Fragment program inputs 0xC/0xD (TC8/TC9) and 0xE (FACING) read as zero.
Two-sided materials multiply the interpolated normal by FACING; read as
zero, inFAMOUS 2's foliage and character heads normalised a null vector
into the G-buffer and lit black.

FACING is +1 on a front face and -1 on a back face (SV_IsFrontFace,
[[front_facing]] in MSL). TC8/TC9 come from vertex outputs o15 and o6, as
in RPCS3's register table (TEX9 shares the point-size register); the
vertex program and the engine's fixed VS write them after TEXCOORD7, so the
earlier interpolants keep their locations. The fragment side declares
tc8/tc9 and the face flag only when the body reads them, so every other
program is byte-identical and keeps its cached pipeline.

c1cdab11912f442698f32c04fd7a2a64b7a1226b.message:
cellGcm: a flip queued in the command stream completes when the drain reaches it

The 60 Hz tick (cellGcm_request_tick, and cellGcmTickFlip) completed a
pending flip on every beat, wherever the walker was. For a flip queued
into the stream (gcm_flip_into_fifo) that is too early: the RSX flips
when it executes the flip, after everything queued before it.

Twisted Metal (BCES01010) paces itself on the flip status and rebuilds
a command segment once the flip after it is done. Completed early, the
title rewrote segments the walker had not executed yet; the walker then
read half-written segments as commands (JUMPs to float data, unmapped
CALLs, and junk register writes such as the vertex data base offset,
which shattered every later draw's geometry).

Count the flips queued into the stream and the markers the drain
reaches. A beat completes a flip only if the drain has executed a
marker since the last completion, or if no flip is waiting in the
stream (a flip that never went through it). A flip written but not yet
flushed does not hold back one already executed.

A flip must never wait on a marker that will not be executed. A resync
that skips over a marker counts it. When the walker is lost in unmapped
IO and jumps straight to put, every flip still outstanding is written
off: Twisted Metal's boot resyncs that way about one run in three
(get=0x0FD00000) and the flip it abandoned in the other ring segment
otherwise held the status at WAITING for good. reached never passes
queued, so a written-off marker that is executed later is not counted
twice. GCM_FLIP_NEEDS_FIFO keeps its meaning.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

e25898001640a13ef2863ec42b22c278740e9b3b.message:
spurs: update taskset bitsets atomically on task create and exit (#340 follow-up)

The ready/pending/enabled bitsets (+0x10/+0x20/+0x30) share the taskset's
first 128-byte line with the SPU task library (GETLLAR/PUTLLC). Three host
writers updated them without the lock-line lock around the whole change:

- cellSpursCreateTask searched the enabled bitset for a free id with
  vm_read8 and set the bit later in spurs_taskset_add_task;
- spurs_taskset_add_task set enabled and ready with spurs_bitset_set (a
  vm_read32 outside the lock, a vm_write32 inside it);
- spu_taskset_task_exited cleared the exiting task's bits under ts_lock,
  which no other writer of the line takes.

A task exit landing between CreateTask's read and its write was undone: the
exited task's enabled bit came back with no task behind it, and
cellSpursJoinTask2 on that id never returned. Killzone 3 hit it at quit to
menu: Havok's thread-pool destructor joined task 0 forever.

- spurs_taskset_take_slot(): the free-id search and the enabled bit as one
  step under the lock-line lock, so two callers never get the same id either.
- spurs_taskset_bitset_update(): a single bit set or clear on the raw guest
  bytes under the lock-line lock, then spu_coh_notify_write; add_task uses it.
- spu_taskset_task_exited: the bitset updates and the start scan under the
  lock-line lock, the dispatches after it is released.

Follows the signalled-bit fix (#340), which named these writers as left out.
New test runtime/spu/tests/test_spurs_taskset_bits_atomic.c, built like that
PR's: on the old code the exited task's bit comes back (0xE0000000 for
0x60000000); with the fix 6/6 pass.

e2ff37f3b699c5514c51f510d52ec1134c08b3e2.message:
rsx textures: present X16 like B8 (value in R, G and B)

X16 decodes to a one-channel R16 resource, but rsx_texture_component_remap
read it through the ARGB lanes, where G and B are the resource's empty
components. A crossbar that sources G or B therefore sampled zero.

God of War: Ascension's menu and HUD font atlas is X16 sampled through
crossbar 0xAAEE (every output from G or B): every glyph came out with zero
colour and zero alpha, so all text was invisible while the button icons
(DXT) drew fine. Present X16 the way B8 already is: the value in R, G and B,
A opaque.

e310b6619e7fe655631a58e5997dfc197bbd876a.message:
diag: PS3_FTRACE, a frame timeline of who waits for whom

A sampling profile shows where CPU time goes, not why a frame takes
130 ms when no thread is busy for 130 ms. That is a latency chain: the
PPU waits on SPU tasks, the RSX walker waits on a label an SPU writes,
the present waits on the GPU. PS3_FTRACE=<start s>:<seconds>:<file>
records timestamped spans for a window and writes them out as text:

- PPU syscalls that block, with the guest call site; usleep poll runs
  merged per thread and call site;
- SPU busy and channel-wait spans, busy tagged with the lifted image and
  the SPURS workload id at LS 0x1DC;
- RSX FIFO drains, ACQUIRE waits, flips reached and flips requested;
- Metal: presents, CPU encode, GPU waits (present, flush, in-flight bound),
  readbacks, and each command buffer's own GPU time with its render pass,
  depth resolve and colour copy counts.

tools/ftrace_report.py turns a trace into a per-frame breakdown and an
ASCII timeline. The tracer is header-only (include/ps3emu/ps3_ftrace.h):
the hooked files are also built on their own by the self-contained
tests, and a new link dependency would break each of them. Off, each
hook is one load and a branch.

eb2cd1b02c739e5f293b8e39de8cf8bf64a168d4.message:
cellVdec: time stamps and frame rate for MPEG-2 pictures

Two things kept God of War: Ascension's menu video (MPEG-2, played through
its own player that paces display by time) on its first picture:

- Its demuxer sends every access unit without a time stamp (pts/dts both
  0xFFFFFFFF_FFFFFFFF). The picture item carried that through, so the player
  never saw time advance. An AU without a PTS now gets the next one on the
  stream's clock (one frame at the decoded frame rate, 90 kHz; 3003 when the
  rate is unknown), and a missing DTS takes the PTS.
- CellVdecMpeg2Info's frame_rate_code (+5) was left 0, which MPEG-2 calls
  forbidden; the player looks up the picture duration from it and got 0.
  Fill frame_rate_code from the decoded rate (nearest of the eight MPEG-2
  codes, 29.97 when unknown), plus aspect_ratio_information (+4) and
  progressive_sequence (+6).

vdec_ffmpeg reports the stream's frame duration (AVCodecContext.framerate) in
the new VdecFfPicture.frame_ticks.

ef060b373f4f7794caa9bab83528c36f88e5f452.message:
spu: float compares four lanes at a time with SSE2

spu_fceq/fcgt/fcmeq/fcmgt were per-lane loops over 64-bit keys. Compilers
leave them scalar and branchy: on mixed data, fcgt took 41 ns. In Twisted
Metal's post-FX jobs spu_fcgt alone was 3.4% of the job workers' time.

A magnitude is at most 0x7FFFFFFF and its negation fits in 32 bits too, so
the keys compare as int32: clear the magnitude when the exponent is zero
(any two zeros are equal), negate it for a set sign bit, and compare with
pcmpeqd/pcmpgtd. fcgt takes 2.7 ns. The loops stay as spu_*_ref, and
SPU_SCALAR_HELPERS still selects them. SSE2 is in every x86-64 build
(__SSE2__, or _M_X64 for MSVC, which does not define __SSE2__).

f02f33881482556da07ecc3703429a68e5683cf6.message:
metal engine: PS3_ANISO turns on anisotropic filtering for mipmapped samplers

PS3 titles rarely ask for anisotropic filtering, and at 720p that was a
fair trade. At a Mac's output size, ground and walls seen at a grazing
angle blur into their smaller mips a few metres from the camera.

PS3_ANISO=2..16 sets maxAnisotropy on the engine samplers that minify
linearly through a mip chain. Point-filtered and unmipped samplers keep
their filtering, so lookup tables, render targets and UI read the same
texels as before. Unset, nothing changes.

The new --mip-aniso host check draws --mip's two-level texture under a
quad stretched along y: isotropic filtering lands on level 1, anisotropic
filtering on level 0. CI runs it with PS3_ANISO=16 and requires it to
fail without.

f616c301bde5a46ffd7f529caa9a43a383e1cd17.message:
rsx_d3d12: tell the FP decompiler the export width the draw used

vp_get_fp_pso decompiled every fragment program with RSX_FP_CTRL_AUTO,
which picks r0 as the colour export if the program wrote r0 at all. Each
draw already records SET_SHADER_CONTROL's 32-bit-exports bit (fp_exp32,
part of the pipeline key); the Metal, Vulkan and live-draw paths pass the
control word, this one threw it away.

The guess fails on programs that use r0 as a temp and export through h0.
God of War HD's 2x-AA resolve samples two adjacent subsamples A and B,
computes (B - A) / 2 in r0 and A + that in h0, and with r0 exported the
resolved scene was nearly black: the menu showed its HUD over black and
gameplay only the HUD. Passing the bit, both render their 3D scene.

The depth-export bits aren't recorded per draw, so they stay off, as they
were under AUTO. RSX_FP_CTRL_AUTO=1 restores the guess, as in live-draw.

d3d12_clear ignored the CLEAR_SURFACE mask and cleared colour for every
clear. God of War HD clears depth (mask 0x1, or 0x3 with stencil) on its
final surface between compositing the scene into it and drawing the HUD,
so the scene was wiped and only the HUD survived: the main menu showed

after the existing first-12 trace.

fa001d0711cdc3852280a0cd52afd7ae70b5dc26.message:
cellGcmSys: a late flip completion no longer marks a newer flip done

The ticker marks a flip completion pending, but the flip handler (and
the DONE status with it) only runs when a guest thread next pumps. If
the title requested another flip in between, the late completion set
DONE over the new request; the ticker only completes WAITING flips, so
that flip's handler never ran. cellGcmSetWaitFlip did the same after its
64 ms bound. inFAMOUS 2 writes its next FIFO put from the flip handler
and hung with get == put on either path.

Each request now bumps a sequence number, the tick records the one it
completes, and the completion only marks DONE when no newer request has
arrived. The read-modify-write transitions run on different threads and
take a small spin lock. cellGcmSetWaitFlip leaves an outstanding flip to
the tick instead of forcing it DONE.

guest face culling is honoured now, so every odd triangle came out

ff66a35553268c34c77b3def3adf53b3222f8446.message:
cellGcm: an unscaled NV3089 blit copies a row at a time

The 2D blit copied pixel by pixel through vm_read32/vm_write32, paying
per pixel the bounds and null-store checks, the store hooks, a
reservation lookup and two byte swaps that cancel. inFAMOUS 2 copies its
1280x720 G-buffer surfaces to main memory with NV3089 every frame for
its SPU lighting, and a quarter of the FIFO thread's time went there.

A blit with a 1:1 scale now moves each clipped row with one memmove,
and does the coherent-store bookkeeping per 128-byte line: an SPU
holding a reservation on a line the row overwrites loses it, as with a
PPU store. Scaled blits keep the per-pixel loop. NV3089_ROWCOPY=0
restores the per-pixel copy (which is what the PPU store watches see).

ff7c9eef28c375793946f4bc58a48db3794afea6.message:
spu: update a task's signalled bit atomically against SPU commits

spu_taskset_signal_task and spu_taskset_wait_signal set and clear the
task's bit in the taskset's signalled bitset with a vm_read32 then a
vm_write32. SPU tasks update the same line with GETLLAR/PUTLLC, under
the lock-line lock. The store took that lock, the read did not, so an
SPU commit between the two was overwritten with the stale word.

Twisted Metal (BCES01010) loses a wake this way in its post-FX taskset.
Six tasks meet at a cellSpursBarrier. The last one to arrive sets each
waiter's bit with PUTLLC. When task 3's host thread woke and cleared its
own bit, it wrote back a word read just before the releaser set task
4's bit. Task 4 slept forever, so the barrier never completed again,
the render thread waited on the tasks' completion word, and the frame
label the RSX acquires stopped after two frames.

Do the read-modify-write under the lock-line lock, on the raw guest
bytes (vm_write32 takes the lock itself and it does not nest), and
drop every reservation on the line.

Measured on Twisted Metal, 120 s on Vulkan: 12 post-FX signals then a
permanent stall before, 7116 signals at a steady ~10 frames/s after.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)

│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

tools: hwprobe ring110 Layer 2 analysis, c1 control fixed

Layer 2 measures when a ring block is latched for output: the probe
writes PN-coded markers at a swept offset after the read index
changes, and an audio capture shows whether each marker played in
the same lap (hit) or one lap later (miss). The analysis was not
written yet.

analyze_layer2.py joins the run's CSV and a WAV capture: noise floor
from the leading silence, matched-filter detection of every code,
Delta = a(test) - a(ref) per trial, hit/miss/no-clear classes, a
logistic fit per j with the 50 % point and its interval, the
per-j estimates of x_latch and their agreement, recorder drift
against the console timebase, and the false-alarm rate on
reference-only trials. A cut-off capture or truncated CSV is
reported, not fitted. synth_layer2.py builds CSV and WAV pairs from
a model with drift, smear, noise and faults; 36 tests cover both.

Reviewing main.c against the spec found one defect: control c1
wrote block r at o = 3P, which is late under every hypothesis, so it
could never be the always-hit control. It now writes block r+3 at
o = 2P, which latches at x + 3P >= 16 ms.

defect it catches); ruff is clean; the Layer 2 SELF builds. A
synthetic end-to-end run with x = 2.6 ms and +85 ppm drift recovers

jq2: trace why a worker parks and what held each job

The #106 trace showed q0 jobs waiting 4.1-4.4 ms in the queue while its
workers were 65 % idle, but not whether the guest ordered that wait,
the host was slow to take a job, or every worker was busy.

- IDLE (26) carries the park reason in the top byte of a: empty,
  unwritten, held, no free slot, paused, unclassified; depth is
  saturated to 24 bits. Old traces read reason 0.
- HELD (27), one per admitted job: visible in the ring (timestamped
  under the queue lock at the push) to admissible (the release of the
  barrier on its tag, if later), with the tag and that SYNC's mask.
- BARRIER (28), one per barrier: the pass that consumed the SYNC to the
  release in complete(), with tags, mask and the jobs it waited for.

scheduling, intake order and locking are unchanged.

0596add39e1d7d24c6db7ad32721f9105b5f1622.message:
win32_compat: give SetThreadPriority levels their QoS class on macOS

apply_priority called pthread_setschedparam and then
pthread_set_qos_class_self_np. On Darwin any setschedparam call, in
either order and even with the current value, resets the thread to QoS
0x00, and every later QoS call fails with EPERM (ignored), so every
level ended at 0x00 (#123).

macOS now sets only the QoS class, with the relative priority (-15..0)
ordering levels that share a class. A running thread other than the
caller cannot be given a class from outside: SetThreadPriority fails
with ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED and one stderr line instead of silently
dropping it. A refused QoS call is reported once with its errno. A
suspended thread's level, NORMAL included, is applied by the
trampoline under s_lock before `started` is published.

No macOS caller reaches this today: the PPU and audio SetThreadPriority
calls sit in _WIN32 branches, so title threads keep their creator's
class. Linux and Windows are unchanged.

Verified: new t0 test thread_qos (self and suspended threads per level,
both refusals) fails 24 times on the old shim and on each of 7
mutants; usleep_precise now checks the class differs between levels;
t0 293/293, tools tests, gcc in ubuntu:24.04, TSan 10 repeats.

07f1aed3f94ade1499033b533d50c43ae102bc58.message:
cellGame: report 40 GiB - 256 KiB free above 4 GiB, so hddFreeSizeKB * 1024 cannot wrap

Games turn hddFreeSizeKB into bytes as hddFreeSizeKB * 1024 in 32 bits.
With 4 GiB or more free that wraps, and what is left is whatever the host
disk's free space happens to be modulo 4 GiB: a few MB on some disks, so the
install check fails with "not enough space" at random. inFAMOUS 2 refused
to boot that way with 41.7 GB free. RPCS3 reports 40 GiB - 256 KiB in every
one of these calls for the same reason (its x1024 is 0xFFFC0000, nearly
4 GiB after the wrap).

cellGameBootCheck, cellGameDataCheck and the cellGameDataCheckCreate(2)
status callback's get block now report the measured value below 4 GiB,
where it cannot wrap and a nearly full disk still reads as one, and
RPCS3's figure above.
PS3_GAME_FREE_SPACE_RAW=1 reports the measured value always, as before.

test_game_space: the 12 GiB case now expects 40 GiB - 256 KiB (and checks
the wrapped byte count), plus 4 GiB - 4 KiB reported as is, exactly 4 GiB
replaced, and the raw switch. It needed a ppu_vfs_root stub to link again,
and macos.yml now runs it with the other self-contained sysutil tests.

092caa941112f958ed93896b70f4a10453ed9281.message:
cellAudio: pace the POSIX mixer on the clock, guard on the queue

Pacing on the device queue alone (00c82f56) fixed the rate but took
the device's pull pattern as the guest's: SDL on macOS pulls two blocks
at a time, so mixes and guest audio events came in pairs (mix interval
p50 0-1 ms, p90 11 ms on a title replay) where the PS3 fires every
5.333 ms.

The mixer now keeps one block per period on the monotonic clock,
deadline n = anchor + n * 16e6/3 ns from the integer n, slept to with
clock_nanosleep(TIMER_ABSTIME) on Linux and the critical timer on
macOS. The queue only guards the drift between the device's clock and
the host's: at a deadline with 6 blocks queued the period is skipped,
before a deadline with fewer than 2 the mixer catches up and restarts
the cadence, and a wake more than 4 periods late restarts it instead of
mixing a burst. The decision is a pure function (audio_pace.h).

Ftrace pace reason 4 marks a restart; reason 3 (the SDL_Delay wait) is
retired and stays reserved.

Verified: test_audio_pace (t0) simulates the device: a two-block puller
gives every mix exactly one period apart over 1e6 periods (187.5/s, no
drift) and settles from an empty queue; 0.1 % slower and faster devices
never overrun 6 blocks or run dry; a 50 ms stall restarts once without
a burst. Seven header mutants (fixed 5333333 ns step, both guard
comparisons, each guard off, no stall restart, catch-up without a
restart) each fail it. Host smoke on macOS: 2000 periods at 187.499/s,
wake late p50 27 us, p90 51 us. t0 321/321; gcc-16 builds and passes
the test.

0b874166c7bb5caa389d351863a417367ffb4362.message:
perf(spu): NEON fi and cflts on ARM64

On ARM64 spu_fi (the frest/frsqest interpolation step) and spu_cflts fell
through to the per-lane scalar references. Those loops are too large to
inline, so every use in lifted float code became an out-of-line call with the
vector registers spilled around it. This adds NEON forms beside the AVX2 ones
from #500; the other estimate and conversion helpers keep their references.

- fi: the reference's fixed-point arithmetic in 32-bit lanes; the 33-bit
  magnitude 2^32 + (base << 19) - step * y is split on the borrow of the low
  word.
- cflts, scales 0..127: multiply by 2^scale (exact, or an overflow that
  FCVTZS saturates like the SPU), FCVTZS, and exponent-0 / exponent-255 lanes
  patched to 0 / the saturated bound. Other scales use the reference.

test_spu_fi_cflts_neon compares both with the references over 5.6M vectors
(every exponent, fi's borrow edge, all cflts scales) in the default FPCR and
under round-toward-zero plus flush-to-zero, the mode SPU_FLOAT_RZ runs lifted
code in. On non-ARM64 hosts, or with SPU_SCALAR_HELPERS, it compares the
references with themselves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

0b9f5e4e589dde4f80241e45a81c6002d2e20f62.message:
sys_timer: sleep usleep on a critical kevent timer on macOS

nanosleep on macOS is coalesced: a 10 ms sleep wakes 2.5-5 ms late,
about a quarter to a half of the request. The console's usleep is
accurate, and a guest that paces itself with usleep(period - elapsed)
then misses its deadline; in one title the audio producer's
once-per-frame sleep overslept by 21.7 % and the reader caught it.

Sleeps of 20 us or more now wait on a kevent EVFILT_TIMER with
NOTE_CRITICAL, which is exempt from coalescing, in a kqueue opened and
closed per call. A time-constraint thread policy was tried first and
rejected: it drops the thread's QoS class irreversibly. A failing
kqueue/kevent logs once and the call finishes with nanosleep. The
typed option ppu.precise_usleep (default on) selects the old path.
Windows and Linux are unchanged.

Verified: test usleep_precise (t0 state modes, stress timing):
QoS class and sched priority unchanged across a sleep at four
priority levels, option off never takes the timer, no fd growth over
64 threads, a refused kqueue still sleeps the full time; 10 ms x 200
overshoot p90 0.051 ms on vs 2.51 ms off. t0 291/291, config gate,
TSan 16 threads x 10 s, gcc-16 and Ubuntu gcc 13 syntax.

0daa76131d0da7bb0d2f219a3941a1838f9c674c.message:
rsx_draw_engine: INVALIDATE_L2 drops the texture cache (#64)

The engine rechecked a cached texture against guest memory at most once
per presented frame, so a guest rewrite in place (same offset, format,
size) after the first sample of a frame was sampled stale until the next
flip, whether or not the guest sent NV4097_INVALIDATE_L2. The #64 Metal
fixture showed it: FF204060 where FFA0B0C0 was written.

The recheck gate is now a texture epoch that advances at every presented
frame and at every INVALIDATE_L2 (any argument; over-invalidating only
costs a hash). Without the method nothing changes: one recheck per
frame. The D3D12 live-draw path takes the same epoch.

Evidence: PSL1GHT cellGcmSetInvalidateTextureCache emits 0x1FD8 with
type 1 (texture) or 2 (vertex texture); the RESC stream sends it every
flip. RPCS3 6e4b784d1 ignores the method because it learns of guest
writes through page protection, which this runtime does not have. No
firmware RE of the method.

0x1FD8 is HANDLED with the draw engine as consumer.

Verified: test_metal_invalidate_l2 (now active, t0) passes, and fails
with FF204060 when the route is disabled; test_rsx_texture_epoch drives
eng_texture_slot with no GPU and fails 4 checks on the same mutant.
ctest -R 'gcm|rsx' 28/28; gcc-16 builds of the engine tests. The D3D12
change is not built here (Windows only).

14cdf890470aedeb6588fa6a0d254401ff573a01.message:
vm: keep guard pages on an arena that commits on first touch

The template reserves the 4 GB guest space and commits a 64 KB block
when a guest access faults on it. Recommitting the whole block also
reset the protection of a guest stack's guard page inside it to
read-write, and vm_protect could not make the guard in the first
place: VirtualProtect refuses pages that are only reserved, so every
guest thread's stack guard failed on such an arena.

The handler now commits only the block's reserved pages, and
vm_protect commits a reserved span with the protection asked for.
A read or write fault on a page another thread committed between the
fault and the handler's query is retried instead of passed on, as the
old blanket recommit did by accident; a fault on a committed page
that does not allow the access still goes to the next handler.

Verified: one title on Windows starts its guest threads with their
guard pages and runs. The race is from review, not observed.

299533fcc74eb33a35869a8a8b4dca839f5fa9ea.message:
ppu_lifter: recover module TOC from OPD majority when .got section name is absent

Stripped homebrew ELFs (e.g. PSL1GHT EBOOT.BIN with an emptied shstrtab)
carry no usable section names. When the entry descriptor is detected as
bogus (toc word repeats the code word) the existing fallback only tries
.got+0x8000; with no .got name in shstrtab that lookup finds nothing and
the bogus toc word is kept as THE module TOC. Every 'ld r2, N(r1)' TOC
restore is then lowered with that garbage constant and the guest spins
forever in the first OPD-hook poll (TanakaDOOM-cGcm: 0x103F8 vs true
0xA3328).

Fallback when .got is absent: scan data segments for OPD descriptor
pairs {known-function-start, toc} and take the most frequent toc
(>= 8 votes). OPD descriptors are 16 bytes in ELF64 {code64, toc64};
reading consecutive DWORD pairs would let code_hi == 0 elect 0x0 as
the majority TOC (TanakaDOOM: 1832 bogus votes vs 1817 real ones).

Re-lifting TanakaDOOM-cGcm v0.3 prints
  OPD-majority toc = 0xA3328 (1817 descriptors)
and the rebuilt native executable's full init TTY matches the RPCS3
reference line for line (previously: silent 'b .' infinite loop).

Only the bogus-entry + no-.got path is new; ELFs with section names
take the unchanged .got+0x8000 route.

2e0280848c24d52e70ff9afbf32204e2e207f1e3.message:
D3D12: pick the high-performance adapter in both renderers, with a WARP fallback

The live renderer created its device with D3D12CreateDevice(NULL), the default adapter, which on a dual-GPU laptop is the integrated GPU. Neither renderer had a device on a machine without a D3D12 driver (a VM), and the backend's adapter loop recognised software adapters by DXGI_ADAPTER_FLAG_SOFTWARE only, although the Basic Render Driver (WARP, vendor 0x1414 device 0x008C) has been seen enumerated without that flag in a Windows VM.

rsx_d3d12_device.h creates the device for both: the hardware adapters in EnumAdapterByGpuPreference order (EnumAdapters1 order without IDXGIFactory6), software adapters skipped by the flag or by the Basic Render Driver's ids, then the default adapter, then WARP through IDXGIFactory4::EnumWarpAdapter. RSX_D3D12_WARP=1 uses WARP only, RSX_D3D12_WARP=0 never uses it. A failed attempt is logged with its HRESULT, and the device that was created gets one "[D3D12] device" line (adapter name, vendor and device ids, software or not, VRAM). The backend keeps CELLMARK_IGPU, which now orders the low-power adapter first.

The order is a pure function, rsx_pick_device; libs/video/tests/test_d3d12_device_pick.c checks it against fake adapter lists (attempt sequence and result for each case) and runs in the Linux and macOS self-contained RSX test steps.

2e561567de9591b632fd96a041977a727a6fda3a.message:
hwprobe: spuexh, the SPU instruction sweep on a console's SPUs

The exhaustive SPU harness compares the toolkit's helpers with a scalar
reference, but nothing checked either against a real SPU. spuexh runs
the same generator (runtime/spu/tests/spu_exh_gen.h, included
unchanged) and the same block hashes on the console: each op is the
real instruction word, built from the decode table, stored in a stub in
local store, synced and called, so no compiler stands between the
measurement and the silicon. Special probe A asks whether the SPU
executes the DP compares and dftsv at all; special probe B runs the
prefixes the toolkit leaves undecoded, one word per thread group, behind
staged configs. A host dry run executes the same SPU ELF in the
toolkit's interpreter.

Safety, from two reviews before first contact: writes only under
/dev_hdd0/tmp/hwprobe/ (outdir validated); a launch without its
exception queue starts nothing; no join without a bound: exit status is
polled against a deadline, then terminate, and a failed terminate stops
the probe without joining; collateral workers of a faulted group are
re-run alone before a FAULT is attributed; each special-B word is
logged before it runs; FPSCR is set to a defined state and recorded per
launch; the LS arenas are checked against the image and the stack at
build time; all configs run with screen=0 (the RSX label wait is not
bounded).

Verified on a CECHC04 (4.81 REBUG): stage0 193/193 hashes equal to the
scalar reference and the interpreter, generator digests 37/37 equal;
probe A: the SPU rejects dfceq, dfcmeq, dfcgt, dfcmgt and dftsv as
invalid instructions (join cause 4; GetExitStatus 0x8001000f on the
stopped thread; terminate 0); smoke 186 ops equal, 7 differ from both
references (cflts/cfltu at scales 0-2 on raw words, fesd on raw
words). Host: 41 tests pass, dry runs equal to the cloud runs, ruff
clean; ring110 and lv2conf still build.

MinGW: header-defined shared data with selectany, and timespec_get on msvcrt

37b09103f8065cdaf8fc6d500e6e1d3ef62b378c.message:
ps3_env_once: a named helper keyed by name instead of a getenv macro

Review on #515: the macro only existed under GNU C, so MSVC built the same
files with plain getenv and still went green; it would collide with a test
that defines getenv itself (#243's counting fixture); and its cache was per
call site, a rule for the whole file that nothing enforced while other PRs
edit those files.

ps3_env_once("NAME") is an ordinary static inline function. It keeps a
small table per translation unit keyed by the name's text (FNV hash, then
an exact compare), filled once per name under an atomic claim, so any
argument works and two call sites reading the same name share one lookup.
MSVC, clang-cl, gcc and clang compile the same code; getenv is left alone,
and only the call sites that ask for caching get it. A name of 48
characters or more, or one arriving after the 64 slots are taken, goes to
getenv every time.

spurs_job.c, spu_workload.c and ppu_fs.cpp call it at the sites the macro
covered. gen_diagnostics_index.py also recognises ps3_env_once("..."), so
the generated index lists the same 709 knobs as before.

tests/test_env_once.c counts getenv calls by name: one lookup across two
call sites and a name built at run time, NULL cached for an unset
variable, a long name and a full table still read correctly. CI runs it as
C and C++ on macOS and Linux, and with cl (C and /TP) and clang-cl on
Windows.

39743c7b6170fd444aa4e5037e521c49ac08f514.message:
sceNpSignaling: connections for Matching2 room members, context ids from 1, ActivateConnection

On the console Matching2 connects room members through sceNpSignaling, so a
title that activates a connection to a member and waits for its handler
events sees the member come up. Here the Matching2 room code had no link to
sceNpSignaling, context ids started at 0 (which titles read as "no context"),
ActivateConnection was an offline stub and the event values were not the
SDK's, so such a title never saw its peers connect.

- Context ids start at 1.
- AddExtendedHandler stores a second handler per context.
- ActivateConnection makes a PENDING connection to the peer NP ID; it turns
  ACTIVE when Matching2 reports the member up (np_signaling_room_peer, called
  from signal_member in sceNpMatching2.c).
- Events use the SDK values (DEAD 0, ESTABLISHED 1, EXT_PEER_ACTIVATED 10,
  EXT_MUTUAL_ACTIVATED 12) and go to the handler and the extended handler;
  the EXT events go to the extended handler only.
- GetConnectionInfo takes the SDK's code argument and writes that member of
  the info union. GetConnectionStatus, GetPeerNetInfo and the new
  GetConnectionFromNpId answer from the member record.
- CreateCtx and ActivateConnection work once sceNpInit has run, as
  sceNpBasic does (sceNpSignalingInit has no NID).

spu: cflts/cfltu model exponent-0 saturation and stop at I8 <= 14

The console sweep and lanes dumps (hwprobe spuexh r007/r008, CECHC04
4.81) showed cflts/cfltu differing from the model only at small I8
fields. With sh = be + 23 - I8, an exponent-0 input (zero or denormal)
has a zero significand but still saturates on sh, as the hardware does:
cflts at sh >= 8 by sign, cfltu at sh >= 9 (sign 1 gives 0), sh == 8
does not saturate. The scalar and AVX2 helpers and the Python oracle
follow. For I8 <= 14, sh >= 264 is reachable, where the hardware gives
values no fitted rule reproduces; the interpreter and the lifter stop
there with a named "unmodelled cflts/cfltu scale (I8=N, #126)" rather
than run on a result the console would not produce. The helpers keep a
documented saturation for direct callers. Compiler intrinsics emit
I8 >= 46, so compiled code is not affected.

Verified: 22551 of 22551 hardware lanes in the modelled region match
(scalar, gcc-16, and AVX2 under Rosetta); the old exponent-0 rule fails
spu_numeric_semantics and 19 lanes, a stop threshold of 13 fails
spu_interp_loop and the lifter test; t0 303/303, long spu_exhaustive
passes.

42684058fadb75953ebd5ef4f213cef08b027fbf.message:
spu_coherency: holder list as a contiguous array, prefetched

Every notifier walks the whole reservation-holder list with the lock line
held: PUTLLC, PUTLLUC, plain PUTs to marked lines and every PPU store to
one. A title can keep dozens of holders registered and walk the list
~100k times a second. The linked list's malloc'd nodes were a cache miss
per holder on top of the miss on each holder's resv_valid; an array
removes the first, and prefetching resv_valid a few entries ahead
overlaps the second.

Same lock, same membership rules: append on first reservation,
swap-remove on unregister and on forget_range.

53650c7dc3adab81f331e1c7b09d1e84632e5ab3.message:
rsx engine: honour SET_ZMIN_MAX_CONTROL's depth clamp

NV4097_SET_ZMIN_MAX_CONTROL (0x1D78, cellGcmSetZMinMaxControl) turns
clipping at the near and far planes off and depth clamping on. The engine
ignored it and always clipped. Shadow-map passes draw their casters with
clipping off and the clamp on ("pancaking"): a caster between the light and
the cascade's near plane lands on depth 0 instead of being cut away.
Clipped, tall casters fell in front of the near cascade's tight depth range
and were cut, so in inFAMOUS 2 a building's shadow on the street showed from
afar and vanished up close.

The render state gets depth_clamp, set as RPCS3's Vulkan renderer does:
clamp when the clamp nibble is set or near/far clipping is off. It is part
of the pipeline key. rsx_dispatch_init seeds the NV40 reset value 1 (clip,
no clamp), so a never-written register still clips. Metal applies it with
setDepthClipMode per draw; Vulkan sets depthClampEnable when the device has
depthClamp, which init now enables. A backend without it clips, as before.
PS3RECOMP_ENG_DEPTH_CLAMP=0 always clips.

test_metal_depth_clamp draws a triangle in front of the near plane through
the engine and the Metal backend: clipped for the reset value and 0x1,
clamped to depth 0 for 0x10, 0x11 and 0x0, and clipped in every case with
PS3RECOMP_ENG_DEPTH_CLAMP=0 (macos.yml runs both).

5537980d864859bb977fe9eca399be1f52a2729b.message:
jq2: trace the image each job ran (ftrace kind 29)

Kinds 22-28 split a jq2 job's wait into queue, held, ready and
execution time but did not say which job program ran (#93), so a slow
chain could not be traced to a binary a port could lift (#87).

PS3_FT_JQ2_IMAGE (29) spans the identification inside each traced
job's JOB span; b indexes an image table the dump writes as J lines.
The identity is the registry's FNV-1a-64 fingerprint of the binary as
staged in local store, with its EA and size. A per-worker cache keyed
by EA and size is reused only while the word-wise content hash still
matches, so a changed or restaged binary at one address gets a new
entry. One mutex assigns dense indexes; each table slot has one
writer and is published with a release store. With tracing off no
start hook is installed and nothing new runs.

Verified: 8 new test_jq2_executor modes; 6 fail without the executor
change (overflow and off test the recorder alone), all 79 jq2 tests
pass with it, t0 278/278, TSan x10 on trace-image-concurrent and
trace-concurrent, gcc-16 -fsyntax-only clean. Title replays: 5 table
entries per 75 s window, identification 0.2 % of job time, 0 drops.

59d1533befa247abdf69cf3be2acb794eaa1891a.message:
rsx engine: emulate the depth-bounds test where the backend has none (Metal)

SET_DEPTH_BOUNDS_TEST_ENABLE (0x0380) passes a fragment only where the
depth already stored at its pixel lies in [MIN, MAX] (0x0384, 0x0388); the
fragment's own depth plays no part. Vulkan has the test and the engine
already hands it the bounds (set_depth_bounds). Metal has no usable
equivalent, so there the test was ignored, and deferred renderers that bound
their light volumes and per-cascade shadow passes with it drew those passes
over every pixel their geometry covered. In inFAMOUS 2 that put sun-shadow
and light shapes far from where they belong.

When the backend has no set_depth_bounds, the fragment program does the
test:
- eng_depth_bounds_prepare takes a float copy of the current zeta
  (depth_snapshot, reused until the zeta's depth_serial moves) before the
  draw, so a bounded draw that also writes depth is tested against the
  depth before it, as one draw is on the hardware;
- the copy goes on a texture unit the program does not sample and has not
  declared as a cube or volume;
- rsx_fp_apply_depth_bounds reads it there with Load at the fragment's pixel
  and discards outside fp_dbounds, a float4 added after fp_alpha;
- the unit is part of the pipeline key and the bounds are constants, so
  moving the bounds does not build a pipeline;
- bounds are saturated into [0, 1] (NaN as 0) and [0, 1] is no bound.
PS3RECOMP_ENG_DEPTH_BOUNDS=0 ignores the test there, as before.

test_shader_msl checks the HLSL patch (behind the alpha-test wrapper, the
MRT form, a cube unit refused, a unit beside a cube) and its MSL.
test_metal_depth_bounds draws through the engine and the Metal backend: a
zeta at 0.25 on the left and 0.75 on the right, then a full-screen draw
bounded to [0.5, 1] lands on the right only, [0, 0.5] on the left only, and
[0, 1], the test off or PS3RECOMP_ENG_DEPTH_BOUNDS=0 everywhere (macos.yml
runs it both ways).

hits, shared and exclusive registry locks. The counters are
thread-local and folded into shared totals every 4096 events, so

5fbbf5ec4a46b1556ea7e05bf18762383f4a87ae.message:
spu: turn the MFC lookup cache on by default

mfc_for takes the process-wide registry read lock on every MFC
channel access. In one title's replay (3+3 interleaved runs, mains
power, Automatic) the lock was over half of the frame-queue workers'
CPU: about 167 M shared acquisitions in a 60 s profile window at
about 0.40 us each, against 5.5 ns for an uncontended pair on the
same Mac, so the cost is contention on the lock word, not the number
of lookups (counted with SPU_MFC_STATS). With the cache 99.7 % of
lookups hit; the frame queue's main job fell from 1.29 to 0.42 ms,
worker CPU from 113 s to 44 s per 60 s, with fps and stale audio
blocks unchanged or better. Low Power runs were disturbed by host
load but moved the same way beyond their spread (main job CPU per job
1.63 -> 0.68 ms).

Off stays the locked reference path (=0 or false). The fixtures now
take the expected mode as an argument, and the drivers run them with
the option unset, off and on, so a changed default fails the unset
run.

Verified: t0 282/282, tools tests, config gate, tsan spu_mfc tests;
the unset run fails with the default put back to 0.

61186beffdbdeb636d2c487d507a1e247294ebc3.message:
spu_coherency: the lock-line spin sleeps after ~1 ms

SwitchToThread only hands the core to a thread queued on the same processor,
and Sleep(0) only to one of equal or higher priority, so neither reaches a
lower-priority holder waiting for a core. When every core is busy, waiters
above the holder's priority can keep it off the CPU for tens of
milliseconds. After six rounds of 4096 pauses (~1 ms) the waiter now
Sleep(1)s. SPU_LOCKLINE_SLEEP=0 keeps the plain spin.

6c7650db06e162f8f0e91e895de5721e4d037af8.message:
ios_run: stop the device app when the host ends a run

A device run ended by a timeout, Ctrl-C or a killed devicectl stopped
the child's process group, which is devicectl and not the app, so the
app could keep running on the device (#108). In the 2026-11-01 canary
devicectl's terminate (SIGTERM) did not end it either, only SIGKILL
did: the title blocked SIGTERM in every thread, fixed in the title.
The tool must not depend on an app that honours SIGTERM.

Device mode now resolves the installed bundle directory before the
launch (no bundle, no launch), records the pid whose executable sits
directly in that bundle once devicectl reports the launch, and when
the run ends without the app's own status sends terminate, waits a
bounded grace on the process list, escalates to SIGKILL and verifies
the pid is gone. The report's app_cleanup says which step ended it;
a failed or unverified cleanup fails the run and a timeout never reads
as a clean one. Each devicectl call is bounded; the cleanup runs under
the tool's signal deferral so a second Ctrl-C cannot skip it.

Verified: test_ios_run (61 tests, 1 Linux-only skip) with a stateful
fake xcrun: self-exit, SIGTERM, ignored SIGTERM then SIGKILL, failed
SIGKILL, foreign or reused pid, hung calls, unreadable listing. On an
iPhone 16 Pro Max with --timeout 25: an app that ignores SIGTERM ends
as app_cleanup sigkill; the fixed app ends with devicectl (exited).
Both runs fail as timed out.

The immediate domains pass -1024..1023 and wide values straight to
the helpers, but an instruction carries only its own field: ai holds a
10-bit signed I10, il an I16. 19 hashes (immh 10, immw 9) therefore
checked inputs no guest can produce, and a hardware sweep of the real
instructions could not be compared against them.

zero-extended as the decoder forms in spu_interp_tables.inc. The
generator stream in spu_exh_gen.h and the op table format are unchanged
(a hardware probe includes the generator verbatim and parses the table).

encodable reference over 290 blocks at stride 1; an 11-bit I10 and an
untruncated il each show as differences; native vs scalar 0 differ;

7e975c9e5a83b43e34f302dbe84815d0a1fda864.message:
Fragment programs: honour the per-source input precision modifiers

DWORD2 bits 19-21, 22-24 and 25-27 hold a 3-bit input precision modifier for SRC0, SRC1 and SRC2. The hardware clamps the operand to that precision's range after abs and before negate: 1 half, 2 fixed12, 3 fixed9, 4 saturate. The decompiler ignored the field, so a program that relies on the clamp (a soft-particle fade multiplied by |depth difference| with the source marked fixed9) saw the raw value.

The decompiler now emits clamp() around the source after abs and before negate. Branch instructions are left alone. test_fp_decompiler checks every modifier value on every source slot, the abs/clamp/negate order, and a synthetic hand-encoded soft-particle program (TEX, TEX, ADD with an inline constant, MUL r0, tex, |r5| with SRC1 fixed9) through the whole decompile.

8051655e8ee5a4ade15f4c819de86e56d03c997d.message:
feat(video): R32F and RGBA32F colour targets in the Vulkan engine

The register-file engine on Vulkan rendered only into RGBA8 and RGBA16F, so
a surface declared with SET_SURFACE_FORMAT colour 0xC (A32B32G32R32F) or 0xD
(B32F) got no colour target and its draws were lost. Titles render small
reductions, such as a scene's average luminance, into 1x1 targets like these.
Both 32-bit float formats are required colour attachments in Vulkan 1.0;
blending into them is optional, so a device without it draws those targets
unblended and says so once.

New host scenes --float-rt and --float-rt-r draw a blended triangle into an
RGBA32F or R32F surface and sample it back through W32_Z32_Y32_X32_FLOAT or
X32_FLOAT. The Vulkan workflow runs both under the validation layer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

is in the decrypted firmware set): NOT_INITIALIZED before init, CELL_OK
for an unknown id, a known connection goes INACTIVE without activated
or mutual and queues no callback. A later activate on a member still in
the room returns to ACTIVE (peer_up; inference, RPCS3 restarts a

guest spans are checked before the lock is taken, so a range stop never
leaves it held.

855840c6b38e272494bc5b1cbb492ffa798b3058.message:
platform: measure timed waits on the monotonic clock (#128)

The POSIX paths of timed waits turned a relative timeout into an
absolute CLOCK_REALTIME deadline: lv2 event queue, event flag,
semaphore, cond and mutex, the Win32 shim, cellSync2, the SPURS poll,
the SPU WAIT_SIGNAL slice, the trophy lifecycle wait and the sys_timer
worker. A wall-clock step shortened or stretched a guest timeout.

- runtime/platform/host_clock.{h,c}: host_monotonic_ns moves out of
  sys_timer.c; a failing clock read aborts instead of returning junk.
- runtime/platform/host_wait.{h,c}: a monotonic budget built once per
  wait and recomputed after every wake; ps3_cond_init_monotonic (Linux
  condattr CLOCK_MONOTONIC), ps3_cond_wait_monotonic (macOS
  pthread_cond_timedwait_relative_np), ps3_mutex_lock_monotonic (try,
  then bounded backoff), and a pthread_once-gated static CV whose signal
  side passes the same gate. Win32 native paths are unchanged.
- lv2 waits take one budget outside the predicate loop; timeout 0 is
  infinite, expiry is CELL_ETIMEDOUT, and each object keeps its
  arbitration at expiry. A host wait error is CELL_EFAULT with waiter
  counts unwound (it used to loop or count as success); pollers that
  cannot return an error stop with the new kind host-wait-error.
- ps3__deadline_ms, the timed posix_sem entry point and darwin_compat.h
  are gone; every consumer links host_clock.c and host_wait.c.

Evidence: RPCS3 lv2_obj::wait_timeout (6e4b784d1) measures elapsed
time on a monotonic source; no firmware evidence. Design: #128 comment.

Verified: test-only clock and native-wait seams compiled into the real
loop (test_host_wait_monotonic, abs and rel backends), real lv2
consumers through an expiry (test_timeout_monotonic), the timer worker
across a false wake (test_timer_monotonic), the shim
(test_win32_compat_wait), a native lower-bound probe;
host_wait_mutants seeds 11 bugs (REALTIME deadline, budget reset,
timeout 0 immediate, ns carry, us overflow, cond mutex not retaken,
host error as timeout or wake, semaphore loopi

sceNpTrophy: pace RegisterContext statuses by rate over 120 vblanks

RegisterContext held its caller for 256 vblanks (4.27 s) for a
128-trophy context: statuses were posted every ceil(120 / events)
vblanks, which clamps to 1 above 120 events. A title's boot stalls
for the difference (measured: COMPLETE 255 vblanks after the first
status in 33 boot logs).

Evidence: RPCS3 at d00d8023 (sceNpTrophy.cpp:766-832) paces by
wall clock, 2 s over all events. In 4.81 firmware the client PRX
holds no timing: RegisterContext blocks on an IPC to VSH, which
posts the statuses over sysutil slot 299, so RPCS3 is the timing
oracle. Event k is now due once elapsed * events >= (k - 1) * 120,
so any count completes by v0 + 120.

trophy_poll also wakes waiters on a poll that delivers nothing: the
COMPLETE, and that empty poll left the registration thread asleep
until its 4 ms wait slice ran out.

92cc39a60e3ba45a8758f70154ce60a69b7d242e.message:
fix(video): keep stale engine releases off live Vulkan objects

Vulkan engine handles were reused lowest-slot-first, so a late or
duplicated release of an old handle freed whatever object owned that slot
by then. In one title a colour target's slot ended up holding a texture, so
the next colour feedback draw could not snapshot its target and the frame
stalled.

This is a defensive change. It does not find where the stale handle comes
from. Slots are now handed out round-robin, so a released handle is not
reused at once. A release through the wrong kind's call (texture, colour
target, depth target) is refused and logged, and the live object is kept.

978b3125c218bb635f7cde53332135b53b81efbd.message:
sys_event: quiesce a destroyed queue, also for timer sends

v0.19.0's destroy modes (#622) let FORCE destroy retire a queue while a
receiver or a timer send was between its unlocked active check and the
queue lock; a create could then reuse the slot, reinitialise the
pthread objects the old operation was about to lock, and the old
operation could consume or deliver into the new queue. Every queue
operation now pins its slot through completion, FORCE destroy waits
for the pins before it destroys the native primitives or frees the
slot, and the table never re-initialises a live primitive.
timer_send_event takes the same admission; its sleep path is
unchanged. event_queue_destroy joins t0 and tsan.

Verified on macOS arm64: the test fails on the old code (hook-ordered
interleaving, or a TSan report for the plain read), passes with the fix;

A WASAPI stream stays on the device it was opened on. When Windows
changed the default (a DualSense or a headset plugged in, a choice in

a359f3da4075b6770fdf744a17e37f0fcebc4561.message:
spu_interp: fast loop for pure interpretation, one-load fetch

A Time Profiler of interpreted SPU jobs put 29-31 % of worker CPU in
spu_interp_run_inner's per-step checks. For an image with image_id < 0
and nothing observing, every step still loaded the observer, tested
three diagnostic gates, stored g_spu_interp_last_pc to a process-wide
word and fetched the instruction as four byte loads.

A `general` flag now says whether any of that can fire. While it is
clear a step only compares pc with 0xA70 and re-reads image_id (a DMA
command inside a step can change it), then runs the one inlined
spu_step. last_pc is written at the returns; its only readers run
after a run returns. The fetch is one aligned load and a byte swap.

Verified: new t0 test spu_interp_loop runs six programs (0xA70 HLE,
0x110 event stop, image change mid-run) in fast, observer, diag and
image modes against hand-derived results; it also passes on the old
loop and fails with the 0xA70 check, the image_id re-read or the
last_pc store removed. t0 286/286, tools tests, gcc-16 syntax. -O3
hot path 52 -> 33 instructions; interpreted microbench median 0.805x.
