a4ab49f752c8e9c5c269d31c72457d41f016a58a.message:
cellPamf: reader calls on an uninitialised reader return INVALID_ARG

pamf_host() hands out a fresh, zeroed slot for any reader EA it has not
seen. That is right for cellPamfReaderInitialize and wrong for every
other call: a getter on a reader the title never initialised got a slot
with pamfAddr NULL and read the PAMF header through it.
PlayStation All-Stars Battle Royale (BCUS98472) does exactly that when
its attract movie never opens: cellPamfReaderGetPresentationStartTime
faulted reading NULL+0x18, right after cellSailPlayer's CreateDescriptor
for movies/attract.pam.

Every call except Initialize now goes through pamf_get(), which returns
the reader a successful Initialize set up at that EA and NULL otherwise,
including after a failed Initialize. The existing !reader checks then
return CELL_PAMF_ERROR_INVALID_ARG (GetMuxRateBound returns 0).

tools/test_pamf_uninit_reader.py builds the real cellPamf.c into
libs/codec/tests/test_pamf_uninit_reader.c: every reader call on a
never-initialised and a failed reader, then a well-formed header that
must still parse. It crashes (SIGSEGV) on the old code and passes now.

a5146cde297922d95cca629bada50c6edb91ad68.message:
spu_interp: one dispatch per instruction, pc and steps in locals

After the decode table and the fast loop, an interpreted step still
took two indirect branches (a switch on the form computing every
field, then a switch on the op) and went through memory for ctx->pc
and for steps, which the compiler spilled around the jump table:
49-51 instructions from the loop head to the op's br at -O2.

The generator now emits an op-only table plus per-op form macros; each
handler binds only its own form's operand, so naming another form's
field does not compile. spu_exec is one inlined switch shared by the
fast and general paths. pc and steps are locals: ctx->pc is stored
before channel ops, local-store accesses and stop/halt/trap, on taken
branches (cross-thread pc samplers), and at the top of every general
iteration. image_id is no longer reloaded per step; a channel op that
leaves an image raises `general`, since only an MFC command can switch
it. spu_decode1 and spu_step stay as reference entry points.

-O2 arm64: 21 instructions to the op's br, one indirect branch, no
memory access for pc or steps. Interpreted microbench median 0.49x of
the previous loop.

Verified: decode parity over all 2^32 words at 4 pcs, 0 mismatches;
2M-trial execution differential against the old interpreter (full
context, LS, steps, last_pc, out-of-line calls), 0 differences;
spu_decode and spu_interp_loop extended, each failing on 15 mutants;

a64b92a1b59ed662b757358c3e7d116c5e56d703.message:
vmx: compute vmaddfp/vnmsubfp without a libm call per lane

Without -mfma, MinGW implements fmaf as a slow software routine, and
vmx_vmaddfp and vmx_vnmsubfp called it once per lane. Add vmx_fmaf: the
hardware instruction with __FMA__, otherwise one exact double sum rounded to
float, falling back to fmaf only on a rounding midpoint or outside the normal
float range, so every lane is bit-identical to fmaf. Adds tests/test_vmx_fmaf.c.

a6f26600d902b702053400003d3a5db33334bd15.message:
syscalls: pin semaphore and rwlock calls across destroy

v0.19.0's sync primitives (#621) decided "nobody blocked" from counts:
a semaphore destroy after a post but before the woken waiter returned
destroyed the mutex and condition the waiter still held, and an rwlock
destroy in a timed reader's polling gap retired the lock under it.
Calls now pin their slot through return and destroy answers EBUSY
while one is in flight. A timed rwlock acquire also checked the lock
before the clock after a sleep and could succeed past its deadline; it
now times out once the deadline has passed (a try that succeeds at the
deadline wins: inference, no firmware evidence). sync_semantics joins
t0 and tsan.

Verified on macOS arm64: the test fails on the old code (hook-ordered
interleaving, or a TSan report for the plain read), passes with the fix;
ctest --preset tsan --repeat until-fail:10 green; t0 320/320; lv2conf
green.

a7d948181cf611c9f94d41fadc2f9e3eaf052178.message:
tools: spu_scalar_no_simd reads real assembly under clang-cl, vectorizers off

Under clang-cl the check was blind: `-S` and `-std=gnu17` are GNU
spellings clang-cl ignores with a warning, so it built an executable and
read that as assembly. It now compiles through tools/host_cc.py, which
asks clang-cl for /FA.

Reading real assembly showed pshufb in the scalar builds on Win64: the
compiler's SLP vectorizer turns the byte loop's fixed SPU_W reorder into
a pshufb of its own once a u128 argument arrives in memory. That is the
scalar algorithm compiled, not the SIMD helper the switches remove, so
every build is made with -fno-tree-vectorize -fno-tree-slp-vectorize
(both gcc and clang spell them so). The vector build keeps its explicit
pshufb, so the blindness check still holds.

pshufb, SPU_SCALAR_HELPERS and SPU_SCALAR_INT none; ctest
spu_scalar_no_simd passes; WSL Arch gcc passes.

aa796862dac84f953d42bf267f99d22e8a596577.message:
tests: run the lv2conf cases against the HLE syscall table

The hwprobe lv2conf cases record what the console's lv2 returns. The
same cases need a host backend so the toolkit's answers can be put
next to the console's.

lv2conf_host.c implements conf.h over the runtime's guest memory and
enters the registered table by slot number through lv2_try_syscall,
so a slot bound to the wrong handler shows as a wrong answer and an
empty slot as the loader's own outcome (ENOSYS slot or the
unimplemented-syscall stop). test_lv2conf runs every case in a forked
child with an alarm, so a stop, hang or crash becomes a result row
(stop, hang, crash, exit) instead of ending the run; two-thread and
hardware-only cases are written as SKIP. POSIX only (fork, alarm),
so the target is not built on Windows.

compare_lv2conf.py is the only comparator: per group match, differs,
only-in-A/B and skipped; TIME rows are summarised and never compared;
a divergence file (case, key or *, issue, reason) lists accepted
differences, and an unlisted difference or a stale entry fails. The
ctest lv2conf_conformance drives the runner and the comparator; it
compares against tests/syscalls/lv2conf/golden.csv when present.

Verified: 48 synthetic tests in tools/test_hwprobe_lv2conf.py, each
check shown to fail with its rule removed; the ctest passes on the
host run.

aca2b25c22a013adc0a5f30b1b85f703de6dd27b.message:
ppu_sysprx: contended sys_lwmutex_trylock returns CELL_EBUSY

A trylock on an lwmutex another thread holds returned 0x8001000B
(CELL_ETIMEDOUT), despite the "// EBUSY" comment beside it. lv2 answers
a contended trylock with CELL_EBUSY (0x8001000A); ETIMEDOUT belongs to a
lock whose timeout expired. Titles that poll with trylock and test for
EBUSY take the busy case as a failure: FIOS in PlayStation All-Stars
Battle Royale (BCUS98472) logs "sys_lwmutex_trylock failed on mutex
'dearchiver_opticalFunnel': -2147418101" on every contended poll, and
stops logging it once trylock returns EBUSY.

tools/test_lwmutex_trylock_busy.py builds the real handler over stub
guest memory: it fails on the old return code and passes with this one.

b2f64c9048e308929020ade7eea76df898b34ca1.message:
cellSpurs: take the firmware's checks for seven SPURS calls

Seven SPURS answers came from upstream without firmware provenance
(#127), and two reported success for work not done (#130). Each now
follows libsre 4.81's check order (firmware RE; module offsets in the
comments, notes in the research repo):

- cellSpursRequestIdleSpu: ALIGN on an unaligned instance, INVAL above
  8 SPUs, STAT on a CellSpurs2 (flag 0x40) and on an instance in
  exception, in the policy-module error family.
- cellSpursSetMaxContention: ALIGN, STAT in exception, INVAL for a wid
  at or above 16 (32 on CellSpurs2). The clamp to 8 is the firmware's
  own (li r5,8), so the #130 premise was wrong; it stays, now cited.
- cellSpursAttributeEnableSystemWorkload: NULL, ALIGN, INVAL, PERM and
  BUSY as the firmware checks them, and it stores the flag, priorities,
  max SPU and preemption mask instead of writing nothing.
- _cellSpursWorkloadFlagReceiver: the policy-module family, not core.
- cellSpursInitializeWithAttribute2, cellSpursCreateTaskset2,
  cellSpursCreateTask2: the attribute, alignment, revision and taskset
  checks of their creators.

CellSpursAttribute takes the firmware layout (revision, sdkVersion,
nSpus, priorities, exitIfNoWork, prefix, flags, container, two unread
words, swlPriority +0x38, swlMaxSpu +0x40, swlIsPreem +0x44) with an
offsetof assert per field and a size bound of 0x200.

Verified: spurs_error_codes and the newly registered spurs_api_limits

bf111c8e500337c724e999852f9fae2b19eaec62.message:
spu_interp: decode by one 2048-entry table indexed by insn >> 21

A Time Profiler of interpreted SPU jobs puts 37-38 % of the audio
queue's worker CPU and 28-31 % of the frame queue's in spu_decode1.
It walked a fixed cascade of eight generated switch functions and
three channel compares per executed instruction, and computed every
immediate field up front.

Every SPU opcode field (4 to 11 bits) is a prefix of bits 31..21, so
the cascade's result, precedence included, is a pure function of
insn >> 21. gen_spu_interp.py now applies the cascade order to all
2048 prefixes and emits one table of (op, immediate form);
spu_decode1 loads one entry and computes only the field that form
needs. spu_ins and the execute switch are unchanged.

Verified: an off-tree harness compared every spu_ins field of the
old and new decoder over all 2^32 words at pc 0 and 0x3FFFC, plus
2048 prefixes x 64 random low patterns at random pcs: 0 mismatches.
New t0 test spu_decode pins precedence and field boundaries; it fails
under an injected RI10/RI16 collision decoded in the wrong order and
under a wrong lqd/stqd scale. t0 and all tools tests pass; gcc-16
builds the test.

c0b6f3457218543882ad9f9ba04ecf8f19c2840e.message:
tools: hwprobe lv2conf, syscall conformance cases run on a PS3

The lv2 HLE is checked against RPCS3 and firmware reading, never
against the console itself. lv2conf is one set of case sources, in
portable C behind a small API (conf.h: raw syscall by number, guest
scratch, big-endian accessors, observation rows), that runs on the
console as a hwprobe SELF and, through a second backend, on the host
against the toolkit's registered syscall table.

189 cases in 14 groups: time, mutex, cond, semaphore, rwlock, event
queue and port, event flag, memory, memory containers, process,
ppu_thread, timer, the #96 slots, and two-thread cases. Each case
cites RPCS3 at the pin for its expected result, records relations
instead of raw ids, and destroys what it creates. The probe writes
the versioned hwprobe header, one row per observation, a per-case
watchdog and a progress file.

Cases that call slots the stock firmware leaves unassigned, or
numbers past the table, are not included: on CFW several of those
slots are hooked (peek/poke, syscall8), and one such run froze the
console.

Verified on a CECHC04 (4.81 CEX, Cobra 7.5): three unattended full
runs, 189/189 cases each, identical CASE rows, no UI overlaps. The
SELF builds without warnings; the case sources pass a host
-Wall -Wextra syntax check.

c21c90009655f5340ea0090cbd6fc9b47573d6ca.message:
spu: dfceq, dfcmeq, dfcgt, dfcmgt and dftsv stop as invalid

A CBE SPU raises an SPU error for each of the five words: the hwprobe
spuexh special probe A ran each alone in its own thread group on a
CECHC04 (4.81 REBUG); none executed, the group ended with join cause 4
and the stopped thread's exit status read 0x8001000F (CELL_ESTAT). The
interpreter and the lifter computed a result and ran on.

gen_spu_interp.py maps their prefixes to .word, so the interpreter
takes its unimplemented-op stop at the word's pc. The lifter emits the
same named stop (word, pc, image) rather than the .word fallthrough,
which tolerates data in .text: these are opcodes the console rejects.
Their helpers, the sweep rows and the dtsv generator domain go (dtsv
was the last domain, so no other domain's stream or hash changes).

Verified: spu_decode, spu_interp_loop (all four run modes) and
test_spu_lifter_invalid_dp.py fail with the five decoded again and
pass now; t0 303/303, long spu_exhaustive passes; the decode table
regenerates identically; gcc-16 builds the touched targets.

Fixes #124.

cd7b79fe4d1e0450cb28f7f558cf4e199781d4ae.message:
tools: hwprobe ps3console, run a probe on the console end to end

Running a probe by hand meant an FTP upload, two webMAN requests, a
second play after the 8001003A error that usually follows a finished
run, polling for the result and fetching it; each step was easy to
get wrong, and an early unmount ends the probe.

ps3console.py run uploads the SELF and an optional config, mounts it,
plays, and waits for the probe: activity in its _runid.txt,
_last.txt or result files means it started, and play is never pressed
again in that launch; with no activity for a whole --run-window it
plays again, up to three times. A result counts as complete only
when _last.txt, which hwp_result_note_last writes after fclose, names
it. The FTP control connection drops a few seconds after a SELF
starts, so every poll reconnects on failure. The image is unmounted
only after the results are fetched, and left mounted, with a named
error, when the probe may still be running. Only the mount, unmount
and play paths can be requested.

Verified: 11 tests with a fake FTP and HTTP server (drop and
reconnect, no unmount before fetch or after activity, one retry for a
silent play, none while running, allow-list refusals), each shown to
fail with its guard removed; one full lv2conf run on a CECHC04 through
the tool (probe started, 189 cases, fetched, unmounted).

d2406f1c1efe03097b09b3b52b81cb38b4dddb75.message:
rsx_capture: write ps3diff.rsx/2 with a backend-neutral machine record

The capture's machine record had fixed `macos` and `metal` fields, so
a Vulkan capture (Linux, Windows) would have to write host values into
fields that name another system. /2 records os, os_version, backend
(metal or vulkan), device and driver; the writer emits only /2 and
refuses an environment without a known backend.

Python (ps3diff) and C++ (rsx_replay) each read through one registry
of schema readers that normalize into a single model; /1 maps to
os=macOS, backend=metal, device=gpu, driver=metal. Comparison and
replay consume only the normalized model, so a /1 capture compares
with the /2 manifest its replay writes. The input hash and the draw
and frame state tags keep their /1 domain: the envelope version is
not input semantics, and equal state must hash equal across versions.
Mixed schemas in one file and an unknown schema fail by name. /1 is
deprecated only after /2 has carried a full title A/B (#129).

Verified: ctest t0 345/345; rsx_capture and rsx_replay ctests; new
synthetic /1 and /2 cases (cross-version equality, machine mismatch
is not-comparable, mixed and unknown schemas); dropping the /1
normalizer's backend mapping fails test_rsx_capture.py. g++-16
syntax-checks rsx_capture.cpp.

e56af258bee1b8941c5aac14d0c420b9a6dfc4ab.message:
perf(spu): four-lane SSE4.1 form of the single-precision helpers

x86 builds without AVX2 (the default -msse4.1 runtime and lifted code) ran
fa/fs/fm/fma/fms/fnms one lane at a time through the scalar fast path, and
those helpers topped a Linux profile of a title's SPU work. The AVX2 form's
lane rules now also run as two f64x2 halves on SSE4.1. Each half widens
exactly, operates, clears the 29 low significand bits and narrows exactly. A
lane keeps that result only where it is provably the truncated SPU result:
ordinary single or true zero operands, an exponent gap for adds, a
normal-range result, and the TwoSum boundary check for fma. Every other lane
takes the existing per-lane path. SSE4.1 has no FMA instruction, so nothing
can be contracted.

The tests are synthetic. test_spu_float_vector_scalar compares the selected
vector form with the scalar per-lane forms bit for bit. It covers every
edge-word triple (+-0, biased exponent 0 with fractions, smallest normal,
largest finite, biased exponent 255, Smax) and random lanes aimed at
2^-126/2^128, cancellation and wide gaps. On x86 both float tests build with

e659e386d673d2a8f3b0dfa652a9339c4a3fcbf8.message:
ps3_ftrace: write and read zstd-compressed traces

A PS3_FTRACE trace is 100-400 MB of text, and the runs we keep were
compressed by hand afterwards, which ftrace_report.py could not read.

The recorder writes a zstd stream when the path ends in .zst. The
header stays free of a libzstd link (self-contained tests compile the
hooked files alone), so the text is piped into a zstd child started by
posix_spawn with an argv and no shell. zstd missing from PATH is a
named [ftrace] error when recording starts, not at exit. The dump
builds <path>.partial and renames it only when zstd exits 0; SIGPIPE
is ignored only while writing, and the child gets fds 0-2 only on
macOS and glibc 2.34+. Windows refuses a .zst path at start.

ftrace_report.py tells zstd from text by the frame magic and decodes
line by line through compression.zstd (3.14+) or a `zstd -dc` child,
whose exit status is checked at EOF. A truncated or corrupt stream is
exit 2 from either decoder; no report from a partial trace.

Verified: ctest t0 346/346; ftrace_zst covers atexit and quick_exit
recordings, zstd missing, children that fail, die or close stdin
early, and an fd-leak probe (removing the SIGPIPE ignore or the
CLOEXEC default fails it). test_ftrace_report.py gives identical
--json for text, stdlib and subprocess decoding. g++ 13 (podman) and
gcc-16 compile C and C++ includers.

f5f7842ffa4d067d92202060f97bd586516b034d.message:
spu_interp: decode by one 2048-entry table indexed by insn >> 21

A Time Profiler of interpreted SPU jobs in one title put 37 % of the
audio queue's worker CPU and 29 % of the frame queue's in
spu_decode1. It walked a fixed cascade of eight generated switch
functions and three channel compares per executed instruction, and
computed every immediate field up front.

Every SPU opcode field (4 to 11 bits) is a prefix of bits 31..21, so
the cascade's result, precedence included, is a pure function of
insn >> 21. gen_spu_interp.py now applies the cascade order to all
2048 prefixes and emits one table of (op, immediate form);
spu_decode1 loads one entry and computes only the field that form
needs. spu_ins and the execute switch are unchanged.

Verified: an off-tree harness compared every spu_ins field of the
old and new decoder over all 2^32 words at pc 0 and 0x3FFFC (0
mismatches). A synthetic decode microbenchmark ran 1.90x faster
(10M decodes, 0.118 s -> 0.062 s mean of 5). The new test spu_decode
pins the field boundaries of all 15 immediate forms; precedence
between colliding prefixes was checked off-tree with an injected
collision. The full test suite passes
(23/23, 22/22 before); gcc-16 builds and passes spu_decode. The
generator reproduces spu_interp_tables.inc byte for byte.

  the descriptor pool are not rewound, later submissions refuse, and

  VirtualAlloc and a temp manifest path.

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**The POSIX boot path runs in CI, but not yet with a retail title in this
tree.** `ps3recomp_boot_smoke` loads a synthetic PPU ELF through
`ppu_loader.cpp`, the HLE dispatch, guest threads, the frame clock and the
renderer. CI also builds and boots that ELF through `templates/project` on
macOS and Linux. That proves the per-game scaffold runs on both hosts; it is
not a compatibility claim for a retail game.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível e à primeira luta contra um chefe, mas ainda lento (~18-23 fps no nível, 13-21 na luta). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot à primeira luta contra um chefe:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~50-55 fps; o primeiro nível a ~22-27 fps, conforme a cena (era ~9); a luta contra o chefe a 13-21. Atrasando um thread de cada vez e medindo quanto o quadro atrasa junto, o limite hoje é o thread que executa os comandos de vídeo (o RSX do RPCS3) e o thread principal do jogo, não as SPUs nem a placa de vídeo. Partes pesadas das SPUs já rodam como código nativo, cada uma conferida contra o original: a geometria por draw (índices, skinning, normais e tangentes) e o pós-processamento que suaviza as bordas da imagem. O foco agora é deixar o jogo mais leve para processadores comuns: o uso total de CPU já caiu ~10% (de 7,2 para 6,4 núcleos no menu) sem perder fps, e o próximo passo é a espera pelas consultas de oclusão (ZCULL) no thread do RSX. Esses números são de um Ryzen 5 5600G com uma RX 7600; num Ryzen 7 9800X3D com uma RX 9070 XT (RSX do RPCS3, Vulkan), o jogo chega a 60 fps fora das lutas e cai para cerca da metade nelas. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); e o jogo às vezes trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`). - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md).

## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), instale o launcher pelo `AscensionLauncher__x64-setup.exe` das [releases](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/releases) e, na primeira vez, aponte a pasta `ascension` em **Avançado › Pasta do jogo**. Ele se atualiza sozinho quando sai uma versão nova.

JOGAR abre o jogo; o launcher se esconde até ele fechar. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

cdb581579fd7ba76d429fab741828ce9e04161d6.message:
Low-CPU update: fewer threads on weaker PCs, support for CPUs without AVX2

- SPURS: on PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the lanes/kernels spin less, wake the
  main thread sooner and run on fewer threads (4-thread PCs: ~10 fps -> ~29 fps,
  8 threads: ~38 -> ~50 fps). Big PCs keep the old behaviour.
- Vertex workers spin far less after each job, fewer workers on small CPUs.
- The once-per-second thread scan only walks the game's own threads.
- No exclusive core reservations on PCs with fewer than 20 CPU threads;
  P-core pinning only on hybrid CPUs with at least 8 P-core threads.
- CPUs without AVX2/FMA/BMI2 (pre-2013 Intel, AVX-less Pentium/Celeron, AMD before
  2015): Setup/the updater detect this and build an SSE4.1 compatibility version
  automatically (same results, slower). The game also checks the CPU at startup and
  shows a clear message instead of crashing.

# inFamous PC

An unofficial native Windows port of **inFamous** (PlayStation 3, 2009, European
release `BCES00220`). The game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code is statically
recompiled to x86-64 C/C++ with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp),
so it runs as a normal Windows program rather than under an emulator.

**This repository contains no game code or data.** You build the game yourself,
on your own PC, from your own copy of the game.

## Easy install

Download **inFamous Setup.exe** from the latest release, run it, choose your
`.iso` (an encrypted image works with its `.dkey` next to it) or your game
folder (the one with `PS3_GAME` in it), pick an install location and press
**Install**.

Setup checks for Python and the C++ build tools and offers to install them,
copies the game out of the disc image, regenerates the recompiled code from your
copy, builds it and adds an inFamous shortcut. Running Setup again on the same
folder updates or repairs the install and only redoes what changed.

## Updating

When a new version is published here, players update in place instead of reinstalling:
**Update now** in Setup (it finds the existing install), the **Update inFamous** shortcut in
the Start menu, or `Update inFamous.cmd` in the install folder. The updater compares every file
with this repository, downloads only what changed, regenerates the game code only if the
port's patches changed, and recompiles only the affected parts. Installs made with an older
Setup need one run of the new Setup on the same folder first.

## Requirements

- Your own inFamous disc dump, European release (`BCES00220`).
- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with Direct3D 12 support.
- A CPU with SSE4.1 (2008 or newer). On CPUs without AVX2 (Intel before 2013, Pentium/Celeron
  without AVX, AMD before 2015) Setup builds a slower compatibility version automatically.
  On PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the game uses fewer threads and less CPU (tested down to 4 threads).
- [Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) with "Add python.exe to
  PATH" ticked.
- [Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/)
  with the **Desktop development with C++** workload and the **C++ Clang
  Compiler for Windows** component.
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), only if your `PS3_GAME\USRDIR` has `EBOOT.BIN`
  but no decrypted `EBOOT.elf`. Setup uses it to decrypt the executable.
- About 10 GB of free disk space and 16 GB of RAM.

## Building manually

```bat
cd installer
cargo build --release
target\release\infamous-installer --game "D:\Dumps\inFamous"
```

`infamous-installer doctor` checks the requirements only. Finished steps are
skipped when you run it again, so an interrupted install continues where it
stopped. See [installer/README.md](installer/README.md) for every step and the
maintainer commands.

## Playing

Run **Play inFamous** (or the inFamous shortcut Setup made). Controllers work as
on the console, and keyboard and mouse are supported. F10 opens the settings
menu for vsync, frame cap, resolution and more (saved to `settings.ini`).

## How it works

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `ps3recomp` | The recompiler toolkit and runtime: PPU and SPU lifters, HLE system libraries, RSX on Direct3D 12, audio and input |
| `infamous-recomp` | The inFamous-specific parts: program entry, game stubs and fixes, asset tools |
| `installer` | Setup and the command-line installer: reads the disc, regenerates the code from your game, applies `installer/patches`, builds |
| `installer/infamous.toml` | Everything about the game and the port: pipeline steps, generated files, build and launch settings |
| `installer/generated.lock` | Hashes of each generated file before and after the port's patches |

## Credits

- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet and
  contributors (see [ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md](ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md)).
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), used to decrypt the game executable.
- Sucker Punch Productions, for the game.

English | [Português (BR)](README.pt-BR.md) # Demon's Souls PC — native static recompilation for Windows x64 [![Listed on PlayPorted](https://playported.com/badge.svg)](https://playported.com/ports/1006-demons-souls/) **An unofficial, experimental native Windows port of *Demon's Souls* (PS3 North America, BLUS30443), built with static recompilation.** The game's PowerPC/SPU machine code is translated ahead-of-time to C, compiled to a native x64 executable, and linked against hand-written clean-room reimplementations of the PS3 system libraries — no general-purpose emulation at runtime. Rendering uses Direct3D 12, audio uses WASAPI, and a WPF/.NET 8 launcher handles managed installation, SHA-256 integrity verification, and startup. This project is for people who own a legal copy of the game and want to play it natively on a modern Windows PC. It is **not** an emulator and ships **no game content**: you supply the game files yourself, from your own copy. [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Leonardorobertomotalvao/demons-souls-pc)](https://github.com/Leonardorobertomotalvao/demons-souls-pc/releases/latest) [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-alpha--experimental-orange)](#status--roadmap) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Leonardorobertomotalvao/demons-souls-pc)](https://github.com/Leonardorobertomotalvao/demons-souls-pc/stargazers) [![Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/Leonardorobertomotalvao/demons-souls-pc)](https://github.com/Leonardorobertomotalvao/demons-souls-pc/issues) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%2010%2F11%20x64-blue)](#requirements) > **This repository contains no game code, game data, saves, firmware, BIOS, keys, or game executables.** You must supply your own legally-obtained copy. See [Legal disclaimer](#legal-disclaimer). > > **Launcher version history:** [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## Features All items below were **verified on one single reference machine** (the author's Windows 10 box — Ryzen 5 5500, 16 GB RAM, HDD). Nothing transfers automatically to other machines; see [Status / Roadmap](#status--roadmap). - **Full boot up to Boletaria**: logos, auto-save notice, intro with sound and subtitles, title screen, character creation, tutorial, the Nexus, and Boletarian Palace 1-1. - **D3D12 rendering**: lit/textured scenes, shadows, HUD, particles, light shafts and haze; shaders are precompiled (the game does not pause to compile shaders). - **Save/load works**, including menu sounds. - **60 FPS runtime profile**, approved via runtime identity verification. On the reference machine, 1-1 with `DES_FPS=60` and `VBLANK_MHZ=240000` measured ~120 FPS — not a general claim. - **Startup audio-silence bug fixed at the root**: a libmixer notify-queue race, documented in `docs/34-audio-notify-startup-race.md`, fixed by `patches/des-audio-notify-fix.patch`, validated by A/B runs (PCM reaches WASAPI with the fix ON and does not with it OFF; 3752/3752 and 8442/8442 notifications across two test sets) and audibly validated by the author on an isolated installation. - **Launcher (Alpha 0.2)**: imports/prepares/repairs a managed installation from your local ISO or `PS3_GAME` copy, enforces identity gates (unapproved runtimes are blocked), records every operation as JSONL traces. On an intact installation, full verify takes ~4 s reading **0 bytes** (NTFS/USN identity confirmation); re-preparing from the same ISO takes ~9 s. - **Architecture**: complete PPU boot, recompiled SPU code images, SPURS HLE with task coordination, cellAudio/cellAtrac/cellFs/camera/input reimplementations, in-game UI via RmlUi. ## Status / Roadmap **Current state: Alpha 0.2 — experimental prototype.** Validated on one reference machine only. There are no guarantees about stability, performance, or compatibility on any other machine. **In development** (open items): - Transparency effects that vanish for single frames (fog wall, soul aura, snow). - Cutscene handling above 30 Hz. - Physics validation above 60 FPS. - More controllers (keyboard+mouse and DualSense USB/BT-HID are what have been touched; other pads untested). - Persistent user configuration. **Not implemented / known limits:** - Online/network: nothing implemented. - Only the first area is verified — the rest of the game is untested. - Full SPURS/SPU LLE: an earlier experiment was abandoned (`docs/22-libsre-lle-attempt.md`); the runtime uses HLE plus recompiled SPU images. - Cutscenes revert to 30 Hz above 30; physics > 60 FPS untested (the original game runs at 30). Project history and technical chronicle: `docs/00-feasibility.md` through `docs/35-launcher-prepare-optimization.md`. ## Requirements ### To play (prebuilt launcher package) - Windows 10/11 x64; a GPU with D3D12 feature level 12.0+. - The self-contained launcher package from [Releases](https://github.com/Leonardorobertomotalvao/demons-souls-pc/releases/latest) — no .NET install needed. - **Your own legal copy of the game** (PS3 USA, BLUS30443), and a decrypted `EBOOT.ELF` produced **from your own copy** — e.g. the executable dump feature of RPCS3, or `scetool` with public keys. The project never decrypts anything for you and never ships decryption. - Disk space for the managed installation (a copy of the game data plus vfs and profile). ### To build from source - Windows 10/11 x64; VS 2022 Build Tools (C++ + Windows SDK with `d3d12.h`), CMake ≥ 3.20, Ninja, and the clang used by the fork. - Python 3.11+ with `ps3recomp/requirements.txt` (pycryptodome, capstone, construct, tabulate, tqdm) for the analysis tooling. - .NET SDK 8 (launcher). - RPCS3 (or scetool with public lv0/metldr keys) to decrypt **your own copy** — the project distributes no decryption and no keys. - Ghidra optional (analysis). ## Installation ### End users (prebuilt launcher) 1. Download `DemonSoulsPC-Launcher-Windows-x64-.zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/Leonardorobertomotalvao/demons-souls-pc/releases/latest) and extract the **whole** zip into a writable folder, keeping the `Launcher\` folder together. 2. Run `Launcher\DemonsSouls.Launcher.exe`. 3. **SELECT LOCAL ISO** — the launcher mounts your game image read-only, identifies the edition by `PARAM.SFO` (BLUS30443 · 01.00), and fills the source path. If Windows refuses the mount, double-click the ISO in Explorer and try again. 4. You must also supply: an **approved** `des_boot.exe` runtime and the `EBOOT.ELF` from your own decrypted copy (recommended route: RPCS3's executable dump). The launcher does **not** decrypt protected `EBOOT.BIN` files; without an approved ELF identity, PLAY stays locked. 5. Click **PREPARE** (or **REPAIR**) — it copies and verifies everything into a managed installation (resumable by SHA-256; your original `PS3_GAME` folder is never modified). 6. Under **Advanced**, confirm the paths, pick 60 FPS, and click **PLAY** — every start verifies the runtime and EBOOT SHA-256 before releasing the button. 7. For isolated testing, set `DEMONS_SOULS_LAUNCHER_HOME` to a scratch folder. The launcher never touches its own preferences. ### From source The launcher has a single reproducible build: ```powershell git clone https://github.com/Leonardorobertomotalvao/demons-souls-pc demons-souls-pc cd demons-souls-pc dotnet publish launcher-alpha02-hotfix\DemonsSouls.Launcher.csproj -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true -o ..\launcher-build # → ..\launcher-build\DemonsSouls.Launcher.exe ``` The runtime is **not** a one-button build: clone the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/ps3recomp) fork at commit `add3cac07e29b4457ab24303804bfcc96056ba5a`, apply `patches/des-audio-notify-fix.patch`, set up MSVC (`scripts/vsenv.bat`), place your own decrypted game files in `work\game\` (per `docs/03-setup.md`), and build the CMake targets (port + runtime) for x64 → `port\build\des_boot.exe`. **Honesty about reproducibility:** on the author's toolchain the audio-fix build reproduces `83B23813254C542575244F394ED31A3BE2BBD276E6A1D70372D2C6C12A77AE7E` byte-exactly; other toolchains may differ in bytes. The launcher approves runtimes by identity (SHA-256) — to run your own build, reproduce your installation's own gates. ## Usage ### Launcher Open `DemonsSouls.Launcher.exe` → the **Installation** tab wizard shows every requirement in real time (image/source, prepared `EBOOT.ELF`, approved native executable, destination, disk space) → **PREPARE / REPAIR** → **Advanced** paths → 60 FPS → **PLAY**. ### Command line (reproducible, no GUI) ```text --fps-compatibility --installation --profile

--runtime --elf → JSON verdict (approved / blocker) --prepare-iso --iso --destination

[--elf ] [--runtime ] → exit codes 2/3/4 name the exact missing requirement --verify --installation → full integrity check --import, --repair, --detect-tools, --self-test, --window-test ``` `--prepare-iso` also accepts `--source-image` to reuse the previously registered ISO identity (seconds instead of minutes on repeat runs). ### Approved runtime identities The launcher refuses unapproved runtimes ("60 FPS blocked — check the paths under Advanced and try again"): | Build | SHA-256 | Status | |---|---|---| | Alpha 0.2 stable | `88087725D7CB858B644D8D183329EB72E1C820B365ED2B34EBD6E2AC281F0933` | Approved | | Alpha 0.2 audio fix | `83B23813254C542575244F394ED31A3BE2BBD276E6A1D70372D2C6C12A77AE7E` | Approved (audibly validated by the author) | | Any other `des_boot.exe` | — | **Blocked by design** | ### Diagnostics (common symptoms) | Symptom | Likely cause | Where to look | |---|---|---| | "60 FPS blocked" | runtime under Advanced is not an approved build | identity table above; `docs/34` | | "The selected folder must contain installation.json" | pointed at the parent folder | point at the manifest subfolder, or run PREPARE | | Total silence at boot (`[audio-peak] peak=0.0000`) | libmixer race (fixed since Alpha 0.2-audiofix) | `docs/34`; A/B via `scripts/audio-ab-diagnostic.ps1` | | Native executable SHA mismatch | installation manifest points at an old runtime | REPAIR with an approved runtime | | Where are the logs | — | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DemonsSoulsPCLauncher\logs\` | ## FAQ **Is this an emulator?** No. Static recompilation translates the game's machine code ahead-of-time, once, into native x64 code. There is no general-purpose CPU emulation at runtime — PS3 system libraries are reimplemented natively, and rendering/audio go through Direct3D 12/WASAPI. **Does the download include the game?** No. The Releases page contains only the launcher and tooling — no game code, no game data, no firmware, no keys. You must supply your own legally-obtained copy, and the launcher verifies identities before letting you play. **Where do I get the game?** You don't get it from here. This project requires a copy of the PS3 game that you legally own; you decrypt its own EBOOT locally on your machine (RPCS3 executable dump or scetool with public keys). Fix the Nexus freeze: PPU reservations at the 128-byte line granule

cellSpursQueuePopBody could mark itself waiting on a non-empty queue: it
read the push index mid-push, an SPU then finished the push seeing no
waiter, and the PPU's stwcx. of the waiting mark still succeeded because
reservations were checked per word and the CAS compares only that word.
HighGraphics then slept forever in sys_event_queue_receive. On the Cell the
reservation granule is the line, so the SPU's PUTLLC would have failed it.

- ppu_resv_break_line: a committed write to a line an SPU has reserved
  (PUTLLC, PUTLLUC, DMA put, coherent PPU store) breaks every PPU
  reservation in that line; called from spu_coh_notify_write*.
- ppu_stwcx32/stdcx64 take the line lock before re-checking their own
  reservation, closing the window between re-check and CAS.

Nexus route: 4/4 runs froze before, 0/6 with the fix (~60 fps to the end).

Also: PS3_HANG_DUMP (named native stacks of every thread and each event
queue waiter with its registers/memory when no frame is presented for N s)
and HANG_WATCH_LINE/HANG_WATCH_Q (in-memory protocol ring, printed by the
dump) -- the tools that caught it. See docs/NEXUS_FREEZE_FIX.md.

1429996058.readme_excerpt:
# Demon's Souls Port PC

**Demon's Souls (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.**

![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimental-orange) ![Plataforma](https://img.shields.io/badge/plataforma-Windows-blue) ![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)

Português (Brasil) · [English](README.en.md)

Este projeto traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado.

> [!WARNING]
> É um experimento. O jogo inicia e o tutorial é jogável, mas ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim, e as áreas além do tutorial foram testadas só por pouco tempo (com saves de outras pessoas). Só funciona no Windows.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído**: nem o código, nem os arquivos do disco, nem o firmware do PS3. Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a versão americana **BLUS30443 (1.00)**, tirada do seu disco, e do firmware oficial do PS3 instalado no RPCS3. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo, o firmware ou chaves. É um projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment, a FromSoftware ou a Bluepoint.

## Onde estamos

Outubro de 2026, no Windows:

- **Do boot ao tutorial**: avisos, menu principal, criação de personagem, cinemática de abertura e o tutorial (corredor, pátio, combate com os hollows, a torre). Os saves funcionam.
- **Nome do personagem**: selecione o campo na criação e digite pelo teclado do PC. Enter confirma e Esc cancela; o limite de tamanho é o do jogo.
- **Renderizador próprio em Direct3D 12** (o "live draw" do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto): sombras, névoa, partículas suaves, adaptação de exposição, profundidade de campo e oclusão do sol e dos lens flares.
- **60 fps**: o patch "Unlock FPS" do RPCS3 (Gibbed e Whatcookie), aplicado como código. O corredor do tutorial fica em ~59 fps e o pátio com combate entre 46 e 59 fps. O modo original de 30 fps (`-Fps30`) fica cravado em 30.
- **Resolução**: janela de 720p a 4K, e a cena renderizada internamente em até 4× (2560×1440, 3840×2160...) pela GPU, com a CPU praticamente igual (`-Resolution`, `-Scale`). **AMD FSR 1** (EASU + RCAS) para renderizar menor e ampliar, e **FXAA** (`-Fsr`, `-Fxaa`, `-Sharpen`).
- **Outras áreas**: com um save de outra pessoa (decriptado e levado a qualquer mundo por `scripts/save_decrypt.py` e `scripts/save_warp.py`), Nexus, Boletaria, Latria, Tempestades e o Vale carregam e jogam.
- **Cinemáticas em vídeo** (`.pam`), tocadas pelo [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org) com som: a abertura, a tela-título e a introdução da história.
- **Áudio** completo, sem cortes: músicas, vozes e efeitos (MultiStream + ATRAC, com o codec do seu firmware).
- **O kernel real do SPURS** (`libsre`, do seu firmware) roda recompilado, não emulado por aproximação.
- **Problemas conhecidos**: cenas pesadas ainda esbarram na CPU e na apresentação dos quadros. As medições dependem da cena; veja [PERFORMANCE.md](docs/PERFORMANCE.md). Frame generation pode reduzir o FPS base e continua experimental. Algumas partículas podem faltar, e o céu às vezes estoura em áreas externas.

O diário técnico completo, com cada problema encontrado e como foi resolvido, está em [docs/REPORT.md](docs/REPORT.md).

## Do que você precisa

- **Windows 10 ou 11** e uma placa de vídeo com Direct3D 12. Foi testado numa Radeon RX 7600.
- **O jogo**: o seu disco **Demon's Souls (USA), BLUS30443**, extraído e decriptado. Uma pasta `PS3_GAME` tirada com o [ps3-disc-dumper](https://github.com/13xforever/ps3-disc-dumper) já serve. Se você tem uma ISO encriptada do Redump, decripte-a antes com o PS3Dec e a chave (`.dkey`) do seu disco, e extraia.
- **O [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net) com o firmware oficial do PS3 instalado** (`PS3UPDAT.PUP` do site da Sony). Ele decripta o `EBOOT.BIN` e o `libsre.sprx`, e a pasta `dev_flash` dele serve o codec de áudio.
- **Para compilar**:
  - Visual Studio 2022 ou mais novo, com "Desenvolvimento para desktop com C++" e o componente **"C++ Clang tools for Windows"** (clang-cl);
  - Python 3.10+ e Git no PATH;
- **[ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org)** no PATH (`winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`) ou em `third_party\ffmpeg\bin`, para os vídeos. Sem ele o jogo pula as cinemáticas.
  - ~20 GB livres e **16 GB de RAM** ou mais. O código gerado tem ~2,4 GB e um build do zero leva de 30 a 60 minutos.

## Compilando

```
demons-souls-port-pc/
  port/          o programa (main, ponte com o jogo, CMake)
  lle/           a ponte para o kernel SPURS do firmware
  patches/       as mudanças deste projeto no ps3recomp
  scripts/       preparação, build, jogo e testes
  docs/          diário técnico, variáveis de ambiente, testes automáticos
  third_party/   o ps3recomp com o patch (criado pelo setup; fora do git)
  work/          o seu disco e tudo o que sai dele (fora do git, nunca suba isso)
```

No PowerShell, na pasta do repositório:

1. **Preparar o ambiente** (uma vez). Clona o ps3recomp no commit usado, aplica `patches/ps3recomp.patch` e cria o ambiente Python:

   ```powershell
   .\scripts\windows\setup.ps1
   ```

2. **Colocar o disco** em `work\disc`, de modo que exista `work\disc\PS3_GAME\USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN`.

3. **Gerar o código**. Decripta o `EBOOT.BIN` e o `libsre.sprx` com o seu RPCS3, traduz o código do jogo e do kernel SPURS e extrai os programas SPU (alguns minutos):

   ```powershell
   .\scripts\windows\prepare.ps1 -Rpcs3 "C:\caminho\do\rpcs3"
   ```

4. **Compilar**:

   ```powershell
   .\scripts\windows\build.ps1          # -Jobs 6 se faltar memória
   ```

## Jogando

**`Jogar.bat`** inicia o jogo diretamente. A tela inicial e o menu de configurações durante a gameplay do port foram removidos; F1, Esc e L3+R3 não abrem mais essa interface. O menu original do jogo continua funcionando. A nova tela de menu pode chamar `scripts/windows/play.ps1` com os parâmetros abaixo e variáveis de [ENVIRONMENT.md](docs/ENVIRONMENT.md). O antigo `settings.ini` da interface não é carregado. Na primeira execução, informe o RPCS3 pela linha de comando.

Pela linha de comando:

```powershell
.\scripts\windows\play.ps1 -Rpcs3 "C:\caminho\do\rpcs3"   # da primeira vez (fica lembrado)
.\scripts\windows\play.ps1                                 # depois
.\scripts\windows\play.ps1 -Fps30                          # o jogo original, a 30 fps
.\scripts\windows\play.ps1 -Uncapped                       # sem limite de 60 fps (experimental)
.\scripts\windows\play.ps1 -Resolution 1080p               # 1080p, 1440p, 4k ou LxA (a cena renderiza em 2x/3x)
.\scripts\windows\play.ps1 -Resolution 4k -Scale 2         # escolhe a resolução interna (1 a 4x 1280x720)
.\scripts\windows\play.ps1 -Resolution 1080p -Fullscreen   # tela cheia sem bordas
.\scripts\windows\play.ps1 -Resolution 4k -Fsr             # AMD FSR 1: renderiza menor e amplia (GPU mais fraca)
.\scripts\windows\play.ps1 -Fxaa                           # anti-aliasing FXAA
.\scripts\windows\play.ps1 -FrameGen                       # interpolação experimental; pode reduzir o FPS base
```

**Frame generation** (`-FrameGen`): interpolação experimental por comparação de imagens, sem profundidade ou vetores do jogo. A apresentação agora usa uma thread própria: na cena pesada testada em 1080p, passou de 26,85 FPS base no caminho serial para 34,37, contra 36,13 sem geração. Ainda acrescenta atraso, pode produzir rastros e não garante o dobro de quadros visíveis. Mantenha desligado para priorizar resposta do controle; medições e limites em [PERFORMANCE.md](docs/PERFORMANCE.md).

**F11** ou **Alt+Enter** alternam entre janela e tela cheia durante o jogo.

**Controle**: funcionam direto, com os botões na posição do controle do PS3:
- controles XInput (Xbox ou compatíveis);
- **DualShock 4** (PS4) e **DualSense** (PS5), por USB ou Bluetooth, lidos direto, sem DS4Windows nem Steam. Share/Create é Select, Options é Start, e o clique do touchpad também é Select.

**Teclado** (usado quando não há controle):

| Tecla | Botão | Tecla | Botão |
|---|---|---|---|
| Setas | andar / direcional | Enter | Start |
| Z | ✕ | Tab | Select |
| X | ◯ | Q / W | L1 / R1 |
| A | □ | 1 / 2 | L2 / R2 |
| S | △ | | |

A câmera só gira pelo controle por enquanto.

Os saves ficam em `work\gamedata\dev_hdd0` e o log em `work\logs`.

## Testes automáticos

`scripts\windows\autotest.ps1` roda o jogo por um tempo fixo com entrada programada (botões e analógicos, sem ninguém jogando), mede o fps e guarda o log. Serve para testar uma mudança sempre no mesmo trajeto. Veja [docs/AUTOTEST.md](docs/AUTOTEST.md). Todas as variáveis de ambiente (diagnóstico, renderizador, áudio) estão em [docs/ENVIRONMENT.md](docs/ENVIRONMENT.md).

## Créditos

- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. Este projeto é um conjunto de mudanças em cima dele (`patches/`).
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net): referência de comportamento do PS3, a decriptação e o firmware que você instala nele. O patch "Unlock FPS" de BLUS30443 é de Gibbed e Whatcookie.
- [Ascension](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc) (God of War: Ascension no PC, mesmo runtime): várias correções de SPU vieram de lá.
- Demon's Souls é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. Desenvolvido pela FromSoftware.

## Licença

MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo. O ps3recomp tem a sua própria licença (MIT).

# Killzone HD — Native Linux Port

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Linux%20x86--64-blue.svg)](https://github.com/maiconjsv/killzone_pc)
[![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-WIP%20%E2%80%94%20boots%20to%20Vulkan%20window-orange.svg)](https://github.com/maiconjsv/killzone_pc)

> **Native Linux port of Killzone HD (PS3 · BCES01743 / BCES01744) via PPU→C++ static recompilation.**
>
> Keywords: ps3recomp · static recompilation · PowerPC → x86 · PS3 emulation · Guerrilla Engine · Killzone PC port · Vulkan · SPURS · wws_job

A work-in-progress port of **Killzone HD** (Guerrilla Games / Sony, 2012) to native Linux,
built with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) — a toolkit that statically
lifts PS3 PPU (PowerPC 64-bit big-endian) machine code to equivalent C++ that runs natively
on x86-64, without an emulator.

---

## What works today

| Feature | Status |
|---|---|
| EBOOT decryption & lift (PPU→C++) | ✅ |
| Vulkan window opens | ✅ |
| FIOS streaming cache | ✅ |
| SPURS / wws_job workload init | ✅ |
| RSX / GCM command stream | ✅ boots, clears surfaces |
| SPU staged-job dispatch | 🔧 in progress |
| First rendered frame | 🔧 in progress |
| Gameplay | ⏳ |

---

## How it works

```
EBOOT.BIN (PS3 encrypted)
  └─ RPCS3 decrypt → EBOOT.ELF (raw PPC64 BE ELF)
       └─ ppu_loader.py  → EBOOT.functions.json (function/import map)
       └─ ppu_lifter.py  → src/recomp/ppu_recomp_*.cpp (C++ per basic block)
       └─ gen_hle_nids.py → src/gen/ppu_hle_nids.cpp (HLE syscall table)

CMake (clang-18, Vulkan) links recomp + ps3recomp runtime → KillzoneHD binary
```

The ps3recomp runtime handles:
- **PS3 VM** — 256 MB guest address space mapped into host memory
- **HLE** — PS3 system calls (cellFs, cellSpurs, cellGcm, cellAudio, …) re-implemented in C
- **SPU emulation** — SPURS policy modules run via lifted SPU C or an interpreter
- **RSX/GCM** — translated to Vulkan via a thin command-stream translator

---

## Prerequisites

- **Linux x86-64** — Ubuntu 22.04+ or equivalent
- **clang-18**: `sudo apt install clang-18`
- **Vulkan**: `sudo apt install libvulkan-dev vulkan-tools`
- **CMake 3.20+**, **Ninja**: `sudo apt install cmake ninja-build`
- **Python 3.10+**: `sudo apt install python3 python3-venv`
- A **legal copy** of Killzone HD (BCES01743 / BCES01744)

---

## Quick start

### 1 — Clone

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/maiconjsv/killzone_pc.git
cd killzone_pc
```

### 2 — Get the decrypted ELF

The PS3 `EBOOT.BIN` is encrypted. Use [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net) to decrypt it:

1. `flatpak install flathub net.rpcs3.RPCS3`
2. Open RPCS3 → **Configuration → Install Firmware** → select `PS3UPDAT.PUP`
3. **Utilities → Decrypt PS3 Binaries** → select your `EBOOT.BIN`
4. Copy the resulting ELF to `killzone-hd/game/EBOOT.ELF`

### 3 — Build and run

```bash
./build.sh --run
```

The script runs `ppu_lifter.py`, configures CMake with clang-18 + Vulkan, compiles, and
launches the game. To build only (no run):

```bash
./build.sh
```

### Manual run

```bash
cd killzone-hd
PS3RECOMP_VK_WINDOW=1 \
PS3_VFS_ROOT=./assets/extracted \
PS3_TITLE="Killzone HD" \
PS3_EVF_OK_IF_MISSING=1 \
./build/KillzoneHD game/EBOOT.ELF
```

---

## Asset extraction (optional)

The game ships ~3.4 GB of assets in `DATA_PS3.PSARC` inside the ISO:

```bash
python3 scripts/extract_psarc.py \
    "Killzone (Europe) (EnFrDeEsItNl)/Killzone (Europe).iso" \
    killzone-hd/assets/extracted/
```

---

## Repository layout

```
killzone_pc/
├── build.sh                     # One-shot build + run script
├── killzone-hd/
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt           # Build with Vulkan + ps3recomp
│   ├── main.cpp                 # Host entry, Vulkan window, PPU dispatch
│   ├── stubs.cpp                # Game-specific HLE patches
│   ├── game/                    # Put EBOOT.ELF here (not committed)
│   ├── src/recomp/              # Generated PPU→C++ (do not edit)
│   ├── src/gen/                 # Generated HLE NID table (do not edit)
│   └── out/                     # Loader analysis JSON
├── tools/ps3recomp/             # Recompilation toolkit (submodule)
├── scripts/                     # Helper scripts (PSARC extract, …)
└── docs/                        # Technical notes
```

---

## Environment variables

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `PS3RECOMP_VK_WINDOW=1` | Open a Vulkan render window |
| `PS3_VFS_ROOT=<path>` | Root of extracted PS3 filesystem |
| `PS3_TITLE=<name>` | Window title |
| `PS3_EVF_OK_IF_MISSING=1` | Don't crash on missing event flags |
| `SPURS_PM_CLAIMLOG=1` | Log wws_job PM claim/stage counts |
| `SPURS_PM_PIPE=1` | Detailed SPURS pipeline trace |
| `SPURS_PM_FRESH=1` | Fresh SPU context per PM dispatch |

---

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Good first areas:

- **HLE stubs** — unimplemented PS3 syscalls (grep for `[hle] unresolved NID`)
- **SPU workloads** — wws_job staged-job interpreter coverage
- **Audio** — `cellAudio` backend is minimal
- **RSX** — improve GCM→Vulkan translation fidelity

Please open an issue before starting large work.

---

## Related projects

| Project | Description |
|---|---|
| [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) | The PPU→C++ lift toolkit this port is built on |
| [KillzoneRecomp](https://github.com/drakolordx7/KillzoneRecomp) | Killzone PS2 original PC port |
| [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net) | PS3 emulator — reference for HLE |
| [Zelda64Recomp](https://github.com/zeldaret/Zelda64Recomp) | Inspiration: N64 static recomp |

---

## Legal

This project contains **no proprietary game assets or code**.
You must supply your own legal copy of Killzone HD.
The lifted C++ output is transformative interoperability work; all original copyrights
remain with Guerrilla Games / Sony Interactive Entertainment.

10036dbff1459d1a3d5c4913a3047eff28f3aef7.message:
Setup: the first Python without curl or tar (Wine, CrossOver)

Setup's first step downloads Python with Windows' own curl.exe and unpacks it with its tar.exe, from System32. Wine
and CrossOver ship neither, so a Mac player on CrossOver stopped at "Setup could not start its first download", and the
log did not say why.

When curl or tar does not start, the host now does it itself. Machines that have curl and tar work as before.
- setup_http.cpp downloads with WinHTTP, which Windows and Wine both have. It does what the curl line does:
  - https only, TLS 1.2 or later;
  - redirects followed, but never from https to http;
  - a minute's timeouts;
  - a Range request carrying on from the .part file. A 200 answer starts the file over; a 206 for another range
    deletes it.
  Cancel closes its handles, which ends the call it is in.
- setup_unzip.cpp unpacks the zip:
  - stored and deflated entries, inflated by stb_image's zlib, which the UI already builds;
  - each file's CRC-32 checked;
  - zip64, encryption and several disks refused.
  The names go through the same check as tar's, and the archive's size and SHA-256 are checked first, as before.
- FIX lines (the reason under Details) now also go to the log, so a report has them.
- DES_SETUP_NO_SYSTEM_TOOLS=1 hides curl and tar, for tests.
- crc32.hpp is report.cpp's CRC-32, now shared with the zip reader, and its table is built once in a thread-safe way.
- docs/88 section 5 describes the fallback.

Off Windows nothing changes: setup_http.cpp has no download there, so a missing curl fails as before.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

1375e434db45d5dde7c3a8d6b701386aada64b86.message:
ui: the menus' renderer on the GPU layer (step V4)

render_gpu.cpp is render_d3d12.cpp with each D3D12 call made through
ps3recomp's GPU layer (gpu.h) instead, so the menus can later draw on any
of its backends. It is a copy, not a rewrite: the same shaders, layers,
2x MSAA targets and resolves, filters (blur, drop shadow, colour
matrices, masks), clip mask on the shared stencil buffer, gradients,
blend factor, HDR pass, read_back and the two game models with depth,
and on D3D12 the same command for each call today's renderer makes.

- Shaders: the same HLSL, compiled once at start by the layer's compile
  service (gpu_sc_compile_layout, DXBC target) with today's FXC call, so
  the bytecode is the same.
- Pipelines, the binding layout, the texture table pool, samplers and the
  null table are made once at start (pipelines once per state, as
  today's PSO map); a draw takes no allocation, map lookup or getenv
  that today's does not.
- Textures sit in one 4096-entry table pool, one entry each, as today's
  descriptor heap; frames in flight have their own rings and recorder
  slots, and what RmlUi lets go of is freed when the GPU is past it.

Two ways in (renderer.hpp, under PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL only):
- ui::gpu::create(device, first_slot, back_buffers, images): on a
  gpu_device of the caller's, the back buffers given as its textures.
- ui::gpu::create_d3d12(device, queue, images): on the D3D12 device and
  queue d3d12::create takes, through gpu_d3d12_create_on and
  gpu_d3d12_texture_on (ps3recomp's step V4).

host.cpp's make_renderer takes DES_UI_RENDER=gpu for it in builds with
the route switch, and falls back to D3D12 if it cannot start; without
the variable nothing changes. host.hpp gets an init overload that takes
the renderer from the caller (for a test, and later for the core's own
device). CMake gives host.cpp and render_gpu.cpp the switch's define, and
render_gpu.cpp gpu.h's folder, inside the route switch's block.

With the switch off nothing changes: des_ui's objects built from this
commit match the start

1de3a23e3fb3df7c2ac173f6b7d8f0ab5bbe7a11.message:
Freestanding game module: no C++ exceptions (setup's link, #304)

Setup's link of des_game.dll stops with "undefined symbol:
__CxxFrameHandler3", referenced from the .xdata of ppu_recomp_005, _010
and more (issue #304).

The freestanding module is C++ compiled with /EHsc and linked with
/NODEFAULTLIB: no C runtime, so no C++ unwind handler. That held while no
module function had a local with a destructor. ps3recomp #212 (pinned by
#297) gave every lifted function that calls the guest setjmp a scope
object, ps3_sjlj_scope, whose destructor drops its slots. Under /EHsc
clang has to run that destructor when a call throws, so the 7 chunks with
a setjmp call get __CxxFrameHandler3 as an unwind handler. Every setup
since #297 lifts again and then fails at the link. The single-exe build
links the C runtime and was not affected.

The module never throws or catches, so it is now compiled with C++
exceptions off: /EHs-c- on Windows and -fno-exceptions on Linux, beside
/GR- and -fno-rtti and for the same reason. On Linux the missing names
are __gxx_personality_v0 and _Unwind_Resume, and -z defs fails that link
too. A host longjmp still unwinds through the module's frames by their
unwind tables. The guest-setjmp code does not need the destructor on that
path: the guest longjmp sets the slot list itself, and the thread proc
empties it after a thread exit.

Both game build descriptions gain the flag for the four C++ objects
(ppu, libsre, spu_workloads, des_game_module). The Windows one matches
CMake's commands again (game_build_desc.py --check --commands-only, as
CI's job does). With setup's commands and the pinned clang, the 8 chunks
with the guest setjmp or longjmp no longer need __CxxFrameHandler3
(llvm-nm), and a link of them with game_module and game_libc leaves only
the other chunks' functions and the port's own names undefined. With
master's flags the same link lacks __CxxFrameHandler3, as in the issue.
The Linux objects no longer need __gxx_personality_v0 or _Unwind_Resume.

Problem reports: put the player's save in the zip

So that a reported problem can be loaded where it happened, instead of
played up to again, both kinds of report now hold the save: Report an
issue (the menu) and the crash, hang and lost-graphics dialog's Report on
GitHub.

report::save_files takes each save folder in the game's save root, found
as cellSaveData.c finds it (PS3_SAVEDATA_ROOT, else
gamedata/dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata in the working folder; the
crash dialog's process has the game's environment and working folder).
Each goes in as save/<folder>/<file>. Two kinds of file stay out:

- the folder's two pictures (ICON0.PNG, PIC1.PNG), which are the game's
  art;
- a file the runtime is still writing (.<name>.tmp).

If a file changed or was being written while the folder was read, the
folder is read again, at most twice and half a second apart. The limits
are 8 MB a file and 32 MB in all; a Demon's Souls save is ten 256 KB
files. game.txt (and the crash issue's System block) gets one line: the
folder, how many files and KB, how many minutes before the report it was
saved, and whether the game was saving meanwhile.

The save holds the characters and their names, and the issue is public.
So the texts that said a report has no save data now say it holds the
save, with the characters' names: the menu's box, the crash dialog's
three, the README and docs/74. The port writes its own PARAM.SFO, so no

28976ab4226b504ec3fd411369e1299fc5cbd7f7.message:
tests: ui_render_compare, the menus drawn by both renderers and compared

render_gpu.cpp's proof. On one D3D12 device (the PC's GPU, or WARP with
--warp) one stream of RmlUi calls feeds four renderers through a tee:
today's (d3d12::create), render_gpu.cpp over the same D3D12 objects
(gpu::create_d3d12, what DES_UI_RENDER=gpu runs), render_gpu.cpp on a
gpu_d3d12_create_on device with the back buffers named as its textures
(gpu::create), and today's once more as a control. After every frame
their pictures are read back and compared byte for byte, and at each
page's end their own read_backs too. Each renderer's command list calls
are counted per page (ui_render_compare_hooks.c patches the list's
vtable), and the counts must be the same.

Pages, 24 frames each by default: the six Settings tabs and the
pre-launch Settings, the five setup screens, a page of rounded clips and
overflow, a filters page (every filter, masks, gradients, so MSAA layers
and resolves) at 1280x720 and at an odd size, and on FP16 scRGB back
buffers the Interface tab, the filters and the clips. With PS3_VFS_ROOT
naming the game's folder, as for a run, also the sword cursor and the
lizard (the game's own textures, read where they are, nothing copied),
in SDR and HDR. The UI's settings and data go to a scratch folder
(--scratch), never the player's.

Some GPUs do not draw the same frame alike every time: on this PC's
NVIDIA GPU today's renderer's two models change by one step at a few
pixels between identical frames, and the control (today's renderer
twice) differs from itself there as much as render_gpu.cpp does. On the
test's still pages a difference only at such pixels is reported as the
GPU's; anywhere else, or on WARP, any byte fails.

Results: on WARP every page 0 differing bytes in every frame, SDR and
HDR, models too. On the GPU every page but the two model pages 0 bytes,
and the model pages differ only where every renderer's own picture,
the control's too, changed between frames. On every page each
renderer's call counts are the same. Exit

321100db17aabfc68fa5c19d8a59a06581ce73c5.message:
Build: DES_SPLIT stops at configure when an SPU native hook is not a host function

The SPU native hooks and blocks in scripts/build_spu.py are runtime
functions the lifted SPU code calls by name. In a split build each one
reaches the game module through PS3_GAME_HOST_FUNCS (ps3recomp's
ps3emu/game_module.h). A name missing there fails only the module's link,
and only a build with the lift links the module (setup's compile on the
player's PC), so #249's spu_hook_entry_scan got through CI.

Configure now reads every "ADDR=SYMBOL" and "ADDR-END=SYMBOL" in
build_spu.py and stops, naming them, when one is not an X(SYMBOL) in the
pinned game_module.h. CI's two build-description jobs configure the split
build, so the next hook that misses the list fails the port's pull request.

Checked with CI's configure (placeholder lift, DES_SPLIT=ON
DES_SPLIT_FREESTANDING=ON): it passes with ps3recomp 92bf11ea, and with the
header before it, it stops on spu_hook_entry_scan.

323bcf2464625a91ecbfab977bbc787395dc779b.message:
UI: the game gets its controls back a second after a menu closes

While a document is up, the game sees neutral pads (cellPad_set_host_hold),
and it got them back only once every key (virtual keys 1-0xFE, mouse
buttons too) and every pad button and stick was at rest. So the press that
closed the menu doesn't reach the game. But a key or pad that reads as
held for good, as a driver can leave one until a restart, kept the
controls from the game for the whole run.

Issue #298: a DualShock 3 on the BthPS3 drivers worked in the start
screen but not in the game. Some starts only; a restart of the PC
fixed it, and so did turning the start screen off. The game's own pad
read saw the pad connected ("keyboard input on port 0 (merged with the
pad)").

- The hold lets go once nothing is held, as before, or a second after
  the last document closed. Then the log names every key held and each
  pad's state ("[ui] the game gets its controls back a second after the
  menu closed, with this still held: ...").
- The menu's copy of pad_hid_sony.h's PadHidSonyState lacked the slot
  byte the runtime added for vibration (10 bytes, not 8). With two or
  more PlayStation pads, the poll wrote past the menu's array and the
  menu read the second pad from the wrong offsets, which could also
  keep the pads from reading as at rest. The copy has the field now, and
  a static_assert checks the size.
- docs/32 says so.

5e4ba3601888487575b8ee33150828f0ba0eae68.message:
Depth of field and bloom at render scales above 100%

Above 100% (RSX_SCALE), blurred areas showed offset copies and stripes
instead of a smooth blur. The depth of field's 640x360 buffers were scaled
with the scene, but its blur (16 taps, programs B41881 and B41C81) reads at
texture-space offsets one texel apart at the game's size. At 200% the taps
skipped every other texel, and the downsample into the buffer read a quarter
of what it read at 100%.

The game's start now sets RSX_SCALE_MIN=640 (run_defaults), unless the
environment has it. Targets of 640 px or less keep the game's size: in every
capture checked that is only the post chain (depth of field 640x360, bloom
320x180 and 160x90, exposure 64x64 and 16x16). The scene and the shadow
atlas still scale. RPCS3's "Minimum Scalable Dimension" is the same setting.

Checked on a Palace capture, with the composite showing only the blurred
buffer: smooth at 100%, copies and stripes at 200%, smooth again at 200%
with the threshold. The whole frame at 200% stays within 1/255 of 100% on
average. docs/37 has the write-up.

tools/release: retry the source downloads, and take FFmpeg's from the fork when ffmpeg.org is down

release.yml's "Third-party sources" step downloads vkd3d's and FFmpeg's
source archives fresh every time, one try each. On 2026-11-04 ffmpeg.org
stopped answering, and the release dry run failed on it ("urlopen error
timed out"), so no release could be made until it came back.

Now each address gets three tries (10 s and 30 s apart), then the next
one. FFmpeg's second address is the fork's FFmpeg release
(ffmpeg-8.1.3-2), which attaches the source archive it was built from:
the same bytes (SHA-256 7138d28c..., checked against host.yml's pin).
The SHA-256 still decides, so a copy can't change what ships; the wrong
bytes from one address skip its other tries.

Checked with ffmpeg.org down: three timeouts there, then the fork's
copy, both archives in place, exit 0.
