6ac632e26e9b7b9d66066821b0ceda41d6c2e814.message:
Port: menu mouse, place each dialog by the game's own draw matrix

A dialog's spots were placed by composing the layout maps up its host
chain, and the hosts are guessed from the pieces' words and rects. A
wrong host moved a whole menu. In play the pause menu was made anew,
and rule 4 (a loose pointer) gave the new bar to one of its small
arrow guides: the tabs were squeezed into slivers 12 px wide under the
arrows, and clicks on the tabs missed.

The game itself knows the place. The renderer each dialog is drawn
with (0x00F60BD0's r4) holds the current matrix at +0x30, and as a
dialog's draw begins it maps the dialog's host layout to the canvas,
slides included. A dialog's canvas map is now that matrix and then its
own layout-to-rect map. Composing up the chain is kept only for a draw
without a renderer.

The matrix also checks the hosts. The five rules now run twice: first
each takes only a piece at the dialog's place in the canvas, then, for
the dialogs still without a host, any piece (a host piece's rect stays
put while it slides). That fixes hosts the rules got wrong: the
inventory's arrows given to the pause menu's arrow guides, a list's
second row given to its first, and the new pause bar given to an
arrow guide.

The census (DES_MENU_MOUSE_LOG=3) prints each dialog's matrix and
whether its host is at its place. Since the spots now slide with their
menu, the menus' log (DES_MENU_MOUSE_LOG=1) also prints the menus once
their spots come to rest in new places, not only when the set changes.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

7c25d9ad1f4097a98ff36ee5ff460b605d0a8300.message:
Pin: ps3recomp c8dda63e (a guest longjmp lands in its setjmp's frame)

ps3recomp #212 is merged. The lifter now handles the SDK's setjmp and
longjmp. Before, the lifted longjmp restored the guest registers and then
returned to its own C caller, so execution went on in the wrong function.

In Demon's Souls that is Lua's error throw. A tester's game closed with
no crash report in the Penetrator fight (1-3). The boss script errors at
line 86 ("attempt to compare nil with number"), the game's own bug, which
a PS3 catches. Here the throw came back into the interpreter, which read
a NULL pointer, and the game ended itself.

The game module ABI goes from 3 to 4: the host hands the module the C
library's _setjmp and longjmp, and the module hands the host its setjmp
list. Both game build descriptions say 4, and the Linux one lists
game_libc/setjmp.h, which the lifted chunks now include (the Windows one
had it already, through clang's intrin.h). The lifter changed, so setup
lifts the game again on the first start after the update.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

7c90c40e243e4a553e959d2a3774906f2ca0afaf.message:
port: the sun flare takes the probe's latest count above 30 fps (#290)

The flare's three readers (0x003E2D38, and in 0x003E5750 and 0x003E6368)
read report 1024 only once label 0x52 has reached the probe query's
counter, and otherwise keep the count they have. At 30 fps the RSX has
walked the last probe by the next frame's first check. Above 30 fps the
main thread runs 2-3 probes ahead of it, so the check fails every frame
and the count stays at whatever a rare pass took: the sun through walls,
or gone in the open. A trace at the reported Stonefang spot, uncapped
(about 315 fps), passed the check about once per camera sweep in 130 s.

des_sun_gate runs after each reader's load of the label (insn hooks at
0x003E2DF0, 0x003E6330, 0x003E6518) and raises it to at least the
counter, so the reader takes the latest stored count. With the fix the
held count followed the stored one within one check, at the same frame
rate. Only with DES_FPS; DES_SUNFIX=0 turns it off live. docs/28, "Sun
flare stuck above 30 fps".

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

7ef59983f9e18a6a30a170f4fbbf50dfb90ce379.message:
CI: cache the wrapper UI's FreeType, RmlUi and stb sources

port/ui/CMakeLists.txt clones FreeType, RmlUi and stb by commit, so not
shallow, in every configure of the port or the UI. On #320's run these
configures took 67-102 s each, most of it those clones:

- ci.yml, Linux: Wrapper UI, configure 91 s; Game build description,
  configure 95 s.
- ci.yml, Windows: Configure 67 s.
- host.yml, Windows: Configure des_host 71 s.
- host.yml, Linux: Configure des_host 102 s; the both-routes configure
  clones them again.

Each job now caches a copy of the three without .git, keyed on
port/ui/CMakeLists.txt (one per system), and hands it to the configure
through FetchContent's FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_<NAME>. On a miss, the
configure clones as before and the step after it keeps the copy, which
also serves a second configure in the same job.

tools/ci/fetch_src.py does both halves for every shell:
- "args" prints the -D lines when the copy is complete (its .complete
  file, written last), else nothing, so the configure clones.
- "keep" copies <build>/_deps/<name>-src. It never fails the job: a failed
  copy is removed, so no half copy is saved.

The game build descriptions name none of these sources, so their check
is unaffected.

9c41cbadc4c000e6e1132849d5d2767928232295.message:
tools/des: halimg compares an HDR snapshot in 8-bit codes when its paper white is known

Under the vk rule an HDRP pair was held to 1e-3, with at most 0.01% of
the pixels allowed up to 8/255 (relative to the larger of 1 and the
value). That bound is in the snapshot's linear units, while the pixels
it is for, ones that sampled the next texel of an 8-bit texture, differ
by a step that grows with the paper white. At the settings a player
uses (RSX_HDR_WHITE=400, scale 300, AA 2, aniso 16) Vulkan's snapshots
of capsetu's courtyard and fog wall failed it with 19 and 119 pixels,
where the frames' own 8-bit shots pass: in codes those pixels are 1 to
5 apart, scattered one by one, nothing above 8.

- halimg.py --hdr-white <paper white, nits / 80> [--hdr-curve
  gamma|srgb]: under vk an HDRP pair is turned back into the codes the
  blit decoded (gamma 2.2, or the sRGB curve for RSX_HDR_GAMMA=1) and
  held to the 8-bit rule, heat map included. A NaN fails. Without it,
  and in the hdr mode, the rule is as it was.
- halgate.sh reads the paper white from A's "HDR snap" line and the
  curve from its "HDR: on" line.
- docs/120's G3 line says so.

The self-test gains the round trips (both curves), 120 pixels 4 codes
off (fails without the white, passes with it), 0.06% of pixels 2 codes
off and 0.02% 12 codes off (fail), the hdr mode and a NaN (fail).

c7c5d0550e3fe146e3738350829e53e4b941c0be.message:
tools: hal_symbols.sh allows glslang's classes in the spv objects

On a runtime built with the GPU layer's spv target (PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL_SPV)
the check failed on 25 symbols, none of them the new path's own names:

- _Avx2WmemEnabledWeakValue (3): wchar.h defines it selectany, as the
  fallback of _Avx2WmemEnabled, in every object that includes it.
- ?_OptionsStorage@?1??__local_stdio_printf_options@@... (2): in C++, the
  UCRT's inline stdio options keep their storage in an external
  function-local static.
- glslang's classes (20), all in gpu_shader_spv.cpp: TShader::parse's
  short form makes a TShader::ForbidIncluder there, and GlslangToSpv
  takes an spv::SpvBuildLogger, so their inline virtual functions,
  vtables and RTTI are emitted beside glslang's own, with its linkage.

The first two go with the other header symbols. glslang:: and spv::
symbols (MSVC and Itanium spellings) pass only in gpu_shader_spv*.cpp
objects, the same rule as ps3recomp's CI check. On that build it now
reads 0 outside; a planted glslang class in another object still fails.

Physics cap: go by the last 8 frames, so 30 fps steps every frame

At 30 fps (Frame rate 30, DES_FPS=30) the game's step is the real frame
time, and frames come a little under and over 1/30 s by turns (44% under,
by at most 0.35 ms, in one run). des_phys_rate tested each frame on its
own: a frame under 1/30 skipped its step (the time it held was still short
of a step), and the next long frame stepped its own dt and dropped that
time. Replaying that run's 2,775 frames through the rule: 33% of the
steps skipped, the world 32% behind game time, and the cap on and off
1,802 times, which turned the in-between poses (DES_RAGINTERP,
DES_PARTINTERP) on and off from frame to frame. Ragdolls, debris and stuck
arrows jittered.

- The cap now goes on when the mean of the last 8 frames is under 0.85/n,
  and off when it is over 0.95/n. At 30 fps it stays off and every frame
  steps its own dt, as the game did. The same frames give 1 skipped step.
- Under the cap, a frame of 1/n or longer still steps its own dt, but it
  keeps the time the short frames before it held.
- des_phys_kf acts only under the cap. The ride test runs under the cap.
- Above about 35 fps nothing changes: replayed fast stretches skip the
  same steps as before.

e4cc08a9a6ac2614ac9c0dd2e46d0ac466ee474c.message:
A processor without SSE4.1 gets a clear message, not a crash

Issues #349 and #350: a player's Pentium E5400 crashed with c000001d as the window opened. The runtime and the game module
are built with SSE4.1, and that CPU doesn't have it, so the first such instruction ended the program (pmovsxdq in
create_window, rsxc_d3d12.c). The crash dialog then asked them to report it, with nothing saying what was wrong.

des_cpu_check.cpp now asks the processor first, and says so if SSE4.1 is missing. It runs ahead of the C++ static
initializers, and is the one source here built without SSE4.1, so it can run on such a processor. The check comes
before setup too, so nobody spends time on a build that can't run.

AVX, LZCNT, AES and the like in the exe are in Microsoft's runtime and mbedTLS, which ask the CPU before using them. SSE4.1
is the only one the program assumes, so it is the only one checked.

The README now names the requirement. CI runs the check both ways (DES_TEST_OLD_CPU=1, and plainly) on both systems.

There is no processor without SSE4.1 here: the message was checked with DES_TEST_OLD_CPU=1, on the path it takes.

ebd14fd32eec85949fc5ead1ae6460611f8b026f.message:
Port: the viewport command waits for room in the render ring (des_viewport_room)

HighGraphics writes its commands to a 1 MB ring that SPU image 2 reads.
Every writer waits in usleep(30) until its command fits, except the
viewport command's (0x00D22670): with the ring full, or 16 bytes free, it
sleeps once and writes its 32 bytes anyway. On a PS3 image 2 frees the
room in time; here a busy PC can hold image 2's thread for milliseconds,
and the write took put onto get or 16 bytes past it. Every writer's check
then passed, HighGraphics wrote a lap over commands image 2 had not read,
and image 2 halted: the world stopped drawing (soaks at 120 fps on a busy
PC, 2 of 23; with image 2 held up on purpose, an overrun in 5 of 15).

An instruction hook after the sleep (0x00D229A4) sleeps on in the same
usleep(30) while the command does not fit, as the other writers do, and
logs each wait. DES_RINGFIX=0 turns it off. Needs a re-lift (only
ppu_recomp_029.cpp changes). docs/117.

ec1b9e91020e42ece19b1ee2f4fc576991c6c9c1.message:
des_prework: free the last shader pass's texts once it is done

run_passes resets the precompile module before each target's pass, but
not after the last one. So whenever the start's shader pass runs (after a
session that drew new fragment-program variants, or after an update), the
last target's work stays allocated for the rest of the session: every
decompiled HLSL text (3,654 on the US disc, 44 MB), the programs and the
pipeline index's rows.

It now resets after the last pass too. Nothing reads that state after it:
the rows were handed to the renderer during the pass
(rsx_out_pso_index_add, _ready), and run_pass leaves s_state at 3, so
des_prework_status no longer asks for the counts. reset() waits for the
compile threads first.

Found with a scratch walk of the process heap 30 s into the Tutorial
(d3d12, the regression save, DES_PRECOMPILE=force): busy blocks 113.5 MB ->
69.1 MB; text blocks 10,711 (44.0 MB) -> 2,481 (0.3 MB); the heap's
committed regions 81.9 -> 53.8 MB. A start whose passes are all up to date
queued nothing, so it changes nothing there.

# Soulbrandt **Demon's Souls, running natively on PC.** [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt?filter=v%2A&sort=semver&display_name=tag&label=release&color=orange)](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases/latest) [![downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/latest/total?label=downloads&color=brightgreen)](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases/latest) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1565536292324769832?label=Discord&logo=discord&logoColor=white&color=5865F2)](https://discord.gg/BzmwDeca8s)
Soulbrandt is a PC port of *Demon's Souls* (PS3, 2009). The game's original code has been converted to run directly on Windows and Linux, with no emulator. You need your own copy of the game: the US version, **BLUS30443** (version 1.00). This project includes no game files. ## Status **0.1.0, the first release, is an alpha.** Download it from the [Releases](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases) page. The game plays from start to finish (a tester has beaten it), but not every part has been tried on every setting, so expect bugs. What [isn't supported yet](#not-supported-yet) is below; please [report](#problems) anything you find. Questions and help: [Discord](https://discord.gg/BzmwDeca8s). ## Highlights - Up to 240 fps or unlocked, with the game's timing fixed. Up to 4K, ultrawide, 16:10 and HDR. - Online play on this project's own server: messages, bloodstains, ghosts, co-op and invasions. - Roll in any direction while locked on, not only forward, back, left or right. - A stat respec in the Nexus (optional): get back the souls your levels cost and spend them again. - Keyboard and mouse, Xbox controllers, DualSense and DualShock 4. ## Features Press **F1** (or **L3 + R3** on a controller) at any time to open the menu. Most settings apply right away. Each setting has a short help text in the menu. **Picture** - Frame rates of 30 (the original), 60, 120, 144, 165 or 240 fps, a number of your own, or unlocked. The game's timing is fixed so it still plays the way it should. Above 60 fps is less tested. - Cutscenes play at 30 fps by default, as they judder above it. You can play them at your frame rate instead. - V-sync on or off, "Even frames" for smooth motion, and G-Sync / FreeSync. - Render resolution up to 300% (4K), ultrawide aspect ratios (21:9 and 32:9), and 16:10 for the Steam Deck's screen. - Anti-aliasing (FXAA or SMAA), anisotropic filtering up to 16x, texture filtering and a sharp scaling filter. - HDR on HDR displays (Windows), with settings for brightness, peak and shadows. - Turn off the game's depth of field and motion blur. - Window or fullscreen (Alt+Enter switches). - Two renderers (Settings > Display > Renderer): DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Windows starts on DirectX 12, Linux on Vulkan. **Controls** - Xbox controllers, DualSense and DualShock 4, over USB or Bluetooth, with vibration. Pick which controller the game uses when several are connected. - Keyboard and mouse, laid out like the Souls games on PC. To turn the camera with the mouse, turn on **Mouse look** in Settings > Controls. - Change which buttons and keys do what. - Mouse sensitivity, inverted axes, and switching lock-on targets with a flick of the mouse. - **Roll in any direction while locked on**: the roll goes where the stick points. It's on by default; turn off **Roll toward the stick** in Settings > Controls for the original's four directions. - The mouse in the game's own menus: point and click. Experimental, and off by default. **HUD** - Move, resize, hide or show each part of the HUD. - Change its size, and choose where it goes on wide screens. **Game** - Skip the logos and the opening movie, and go straight into your last save. - **Stat respec**: the Maiden in Black, or the statue in front of where you wake in the Nexus, puts your stats back to your class's and gives back the souls your levels cost, to spend again. Off by default: turn on **Stat respec in the Nexus** in Settings > Game. - Use several soul items at once, as Drop does. On by default: turn off **Use several souls at once** in Settings > Game for the original's one at a time. **Online** - On by default, on this project's own server: messages, bloodstains, ghosts, co-op and invasions. - Setup asks for your online name. You can change it, or turn online play off, in Settings > Network. - A matchmaking password, so you meet only your friends. - Show or hide other players' messages, bloodstains and ghosts. **The program** - A setup that builds the game from your copy, with an Original and an Enhanced preset (see [How to play](#how-to-play)). - Updates: the game checks for a new version at start and asks before changing anything. Your saves and settings are kept, and you can go back one version. - In the menu, the Large Sword of Moonlight is the cursor and a crystal lizard dances in the corner. Both can be turned off. - Trophies, with pop-ups. Setup can bring your trophies and save across from RPCS3. - **Report an issue** in the menu opens a GitHub issue with your PC's details filled in, and a zip to attach that includes your save, so the problem can be seen where it happened. It has no game files. If the game crashes or stops responding, a window offers to do the same. ## What you need - Your own copy of Demon's Souls for the PS3, US version (BLUS30443, version 1.00), as a folder with `PS3_GAME` in it. Setup cannot use ISO files yet. - RPCS3, the free PS3 emulator, with the PS3 system software installed (4.93, the version Sony offers now). Setup has it unlock the game's encrypted files. (Or decrypt the files yourself: see below.) - Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) with a graphics card that supports DirectX 12, or Linux (see [Linux](#linux)). - A processor with SSE4.1, which most have since about 2011. - An internet connection during setup. Setup downloads a compiler and Python (about 60 MB on Windows, about 130 MB on Linux). ## How to play These steps are for the release download. 1. Download the zip for Windows (`DemonsSoulsRecomp-X.Y.Z-windows.zip`) or the tarball for Linux (`DemonsSoulsRecomp-X.Y.Z-linux.tar.xz`), and unpack it into a folder of its own. 2. Start `Soulbrandt.exe` (on Linux, `Soulbrandt`). Setup opens. 3. Pick how setup gets your game's files: - **Import from RPCS3**: setup finds the game in RPCS3's list and has your RPCS3 unlock its files. It can bring your save, trophies and some settings across too. - **I have decrypted files**: your disc copy, plus the 28 files you decrypted yourself (`EBOOT.elf`, the `.sdat` files and `libsre.prx`). - **Show me how**: step by step, with free tools only. 4. Start the build. It runs on your PC and can take a while; setup shows an estimate first. You can stop it and carry on later. 5. Pick a preset: **Original** plays as on the PS3; **Enhanced** sets 60 fps, a resolution that fits your display, SMAA, 16x anisotropic filtering, fullscreen, and HDR when Windows has HDR on for your display. Then a few choices (HDR among them, on Windows) and your online name. You can change anything later in Settings. Then press **Play**. Windows may warn you the first time you start `Soulbrandt.exe` ("Windows protected your PC"), because the program isn't signed yet. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If setup says your `libsre.prx` came out different, your RPCS3 probably has PS3 system software 4.90. Install 4.93 in RPCS3 (*File > Install Firmware*) and try again. If RPCS3 is set to run as administrator, setup cannot start it: untick that in `rpcs3.exe`'s Properties. ### Linux CI builds the Linux program on every change, and each release includes a Linux download. It needs x86-64 Linux with glibc 2.35 or newer, a Vulkan driver, and `curl` and `tar`. Nothing else needs installing. The game renders on Vulkan, and setup prepares its shaders. If Vulkan can't start, the game falls back to its older renderer on vkd3d (DirectX 12 on Vulkan), which compiles shaders as it goes, with long pauses when a new area loads. Linux is newer and less tested than Windows. So far it has run in WSL (Ubuntu 24.04) and, on the older renderer, on one Steam Deck. The Vulkan renderer hasn't run on a real Linux graphics driver yet ([docs/106](docs/106-setup-on-linux.md)). macOS is not supported. On a Steam Deck, keys and the mouse stay out of the game while its controls are on, because Steam's desktop layout presses them too. To use a keyboard on a docked Deck, set `PAD_KEYBOARD_WITH_PAD=1`. ### Online play Online play is on by default and uses this project's own server. Setup asks for your online name; you can change it, or turn online play off, in Settings > Network. RPCS3 players use other servers, so you won't meet them. What the server keeps about you is in the [privacy note](PRIVACY.md). ### Not supported yet - Only the US version (BLUS30443) works. The European version is being looked at; other versions are not supported. - Setup can't read ISO files, and it needs RPCS3 to unlock the game's files (or files you decrypted yourself). - macOS isn't supported, and running the Windows download through CrossOver hasn't been tested all the way through. Linux is less tested than Windows, and the Steam Deck has had one test so far. - On-screen button prompts always show PlayStation buttons, even with a keyboard or an Xbox controller. ### Problems Use **Report an issue** in the menu (F1), or open an [issue](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/issues). For questions and help, join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/BzmwDeca8s). Report security problems privately, as [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) says. ## Building from source This is the technical part. The full notes are in [`docs/`](docs/). **Tools** | Windows | Linux | |---|---| | Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, LLVM (clang), CMake, Ninja, Python 3, Git Bash | clang or GCC, CMake, Ninja, Python 3, SDL2, Vulkan and FFmpeg development files, vkd3d ([details](docs/76-native-linux.md#building)) | On Windows, step 4 downloads FFmpeg's MPEG-2 video decoder for the game's movies (about 1 MB) and puts it beside `des_boot.exe`. If that download fails, the build says so and goes on, and the movies then need Microsoft's free [MPEG-2 Video Extension](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9n95q1zzpmh4) from the Microsoft Store; without either, they play their sound with no picture. (A paid app called "MPEG-2 Video Extensions", from another publisher, is a different thing; you don't need it.) **From your copy of the game** - The game disc's files (`PS3_GAME`) - [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), to decrypt the game's `EBOOT.BIN` - `libsre.prx` from your PS3 firmware, decrypted **Steps** 1. Get this repository, and its runtime inside it: ```sh git clone https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt.git cd Soulbrandt git clone https://github.com/JonathanDC64/ps3recomp.git ``` `ps3recomp.pin` names the ps3recomp commit this version of the port needs. `python tools/release/pin_ps3recomp.py local` checks your checkout against it. 2. In RPCS3, decrypt `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` (*Utilities > Decrypt PS3 Binaries*) to `work/game/EBOOT.ELF`. Copy `PS3_GAME/ICON0.PNG` next to it, for the program's icon. 3. Convert the game's main code: ```sh python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_loader.py work/game/EBOOT.ELF -o work/loader python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_lifter.py work/game/EBOOT.ELF \ --functions work/loader/EBOOT.functions.json --hle-stubs work/loader/EBOOT.imports.json \ --override-funcs "0x167AC88=ds_malloc,0x167AC58=ds_free,0x273D38=des_move_post,0x724E40=des_menu_tick" \ --insn-hooks @port/insn_hooks.txt --shadow-stack --chunk-lines 150000 --output work/recomp -j 16 python ps3recomp/tools/gen_hle_nids.py --all --out work/recomp/hle_nid_table.cpp python scripts/apply_boot_patches.py work/recomp ``` Then the SPU code with `python scripts/build_spu.py --eboot work/game/EBOOT.ELF` ([docs/09](docs/09-spu-spurs.md)), which first cuts the SPU programs out of the EBOOT, and libsre with `python scripts/build_libsre.py `. The lifter's flags above are also in `scripts/lift_ppu.json`, which setup reads; change both together. 4. Compile the runtime, then the game. On Windows: ```sh cmake -S ps3recomp -B ps3recomp/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \ -DPS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL=ON cmake -S port -B port/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl \ -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE= -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG= -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS_DEBUG= cmake --build ps3recomp/build --target ps3recomp_runtime rsx_shader_precompile cmake --build port/build --target des_boot --parallel 4 ``` `PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL=ON` builds the portable renderer: DirectX 12 through it, the default, and Vulkan beside it (Settings > Display > Renderer). Without it the game runs on the legacy renderer only. Its first configure downloads glslang and SPIRV-Tools at their pinned commits. On Linux, see [docs/76](docs/76-native-linux.md#building). 5. Copy `tools/des/local.env.example` to `tools/des/local.env`, set `PS3_VFS_ROOT` in it to the folder that holds `PS3_GAME`, and start the game with `tools/des/play.sh`. A direct start of `des_boot.exe` goes through setup instead, and keeps its saves in `port/build/gamedata`. Everything made from your copy of the game stays in `work/` and `gamedata/`, which git ignores. **Never share your build:** it contains code converted from your game. **For developers** - Each setting's help text ends with its name in brackets, such as `(DES_FPS)`. The same name works as an environment variable, which wins over the menu. - `-DDES_SPLIT=ON` also builds the game the way setup does: `des_host` plus the game as a separate library ([docs/57](docs/57-dll-split.md)). - `-DDES_DEV=ON` makes a developer build, with cheats and a Developer tab in Settings ([docs/55](docs/55-dev-cheats.md)). Never share one as a release. - The renderer is the portable one ([docs/120](docs/120-portable-renderer.md)): DirectX 12 by default, or Vulkan in Settings > Display > Renderer, then restart. If Vulkan fails to start, the game runs on DirectX 12 and says why. `RSX_BACKEND=legacy` runs the renderer from before it: retired, kept unchanged as a fallback, with no more fixes. A build has it when its ps3recomp is configured with `PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL=ON`, as in the steps above and in the released Windows build. ## Legal This project contains only its own code, scripts and documentation. It has no game code, no game files, no Sony firmware and no keys; you make those from your own copy ([docs/05](docs/05-legal.md)). *Demon's Souls* is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment, FromSoftware or Atlus. ## Credits - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet and its contributors: the recompiler and runtime this port is built on - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): a reference for how the PS3 behaves (no RPCS3 code is copied) - [RmlUi](https://github.com/mikke89/RmlUi) and [FreeType](https://freetype.org) for the menus, adapted from [Dusklight](https://github.com/TwilitRealm/dusklight)'s interface code - [SMAA](https://www.iryoku.com/smaa/) for the SMAA setting, [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org) for the movies, and [vkd3d](https://gitlab.winehq.org/wine/vkd3d) and [SDL](https://www.libsdl.org) for Linux Settings > About and [`port/ui/NOTICE.md`](port/ui/NOTICE.md) list the menus' parts with their licences. M0.27: lift EDGE code fragments per placement; interpreter rejoins overlays (~8.6 frames/s)

The EDGE jobs stage 19 small EBOOT code fragments from LS 0x11090, each at a
few addresses. analysis/lift_edge_frags.py lifts one image per (source EA,
LSA) placement (45, images 300+) from SPU_LSA_GETLOG runs; the runtime
registers them with spu_overlay_register_region_at() and marks the span
resident on that exact GET (resident_code grows from 4 to 16 slots). EDGE is
now 0% interpreted (~8.3 frames/s).

The interpreter's rejoin check (spu_lifted_lookup) only knew the context's
own image, so after one unlifted branch target inside a streamed job module
it interpreted the rest of the job. It now resolves like the dispatcher
(resident spans, task, overlay, image): interpreted time fell from ~1.5 s to
~0.1 s per 20 s and MeshProcJobs from 8% to 1% of the kernel thread.

M0.38: BATCHJOB 22/21 stall fixed - PM workload argument passed big-endian

The policy-module emulation copied the low half of the 64-bit workload
argument into both word 0 and word 1 of r4. GoW:A's wwsjob PM takes the job
list header from word 1 and an optional per-SPU status area from word 0; with
the header in word 0 it wrote status rows at header+0x130, inside

wait counted 22 of 21 forever. SPURS_PM_ARG_BE=1 (port default) passes the
argument as the hardware does. No stall in a 1600 s run (4 of 4 before).

context releases it too, and the table has 64 slots with a per-thread cache.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

f3f31f525182d926a86d6654b55c573f163e06e9.message:
M0.36: colour pass restored - SPU float helpers follow SPU rules (no NaN/Inf)

EDGE's triangle culler (geometry module 0xD618, used by colour/static jobs)
folds masks in with `fnms rt, mask, 0xFFFFFFFF, rc`. On the SPU 0xFFFFFFFF is
an extended-range number and 0 times it is 0; with host IEEE floats it was
NaN, `gb` saw bit 1 and every triangle was culled, so the colour pass was
never emitted. Single-precision helpers now treat exponent 255 as ordinary,
flush denormals, saturate and truncate (fast path kept for ordinary normals).
The menu cinematic and title screen now render.

Also: diagnostics SPU_DMA_EA_T0/_PC/_GETDUMP, SPU_LIST_EA (GETL elements),
SPU_BRTRACE, SPU_ITRACE, SPU_FORCE_BR; docs corrected (M0.35c "reads only
the descriptor" was a logging gap).

1430305904.readme_excerpt:
# God of War: Ascension — static recompilation (PS3)

> **Status: research / early bring-up. Not playable.** The game boots, plays its intro movies, shows the main menu
> with text and music, and reaches the first level with the Vulkan backend, at about 1.5 game frames per second.
> Some long runs still corrupt guest memory around the same point of the level; the current hunt is in
> [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md). Generic fixes go upstream to ps3recomp as small PRs.

![Kratos chained in the first level, rendered by the recompiled game on Vulkan](docs/screenshots/level.jpg)

An attempt to statically recompile *God of War: Ascension* (PS3, `BCUS98232`) into a native Windows executable,
built on top of the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) toolkit (PPU lifter, SPU lifter,
HLE runtime, Vulkan/D3D12 RSX backends).

**This repository contains no game data, no firmware and no code derived from them.** You need your own legally
acquired copy of the game and (optionally) your own PS3 firmware dump. See [docs/LEGAL.md](docs/LEGAL.md).

| Main menu (text, music) | Intro movie (MPEG-2 through cellVdec) |
|---|---|
| ![Main menu](docs/screenshots/main-menu.jpg) | ![Intro movie](docs/screenshots/intro.jpg) |

Captured from the port's own Vulkan output (`PS3RECOMP_VK_DUMP`) on 2026-10-20, at 1280x720.

## What lives here

| Path | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `port/` | The game-specific port: `CMakeLists.txt`, `main.cpp` (runner), `stubs.cpp` (hooks), `lle_libsre.cpp` (optional firmware-SPURS LLE glue), `config.toml` |
| `patches/` | Patch against upstream ps3recomp (fixes and diagnostics found while bringing the game up) — meant to be upstreamed |
| `spu/images.json` | Description of the SPU images lifted for this title (policy module, SPURS kernel, ...) |
| `analysis/` | Python tools used to measure the binary (carving SPU blobs, PSARC TOC, xrefs, `findstore.py`, `make_spu_port.py`) |
| `scripts/` | Windows build helpers (`GOW_ROOT`-relative) |
| `launcher/` | Player launcher (Python/Tk): paths, setup check, play/stop with logs, save backups |
| `docs/` | Feasibility study (pt-BR), architecture notes, debugging playbook, related work, legal |
| `local/` | **Git-ignored.** Your game dump, decrypted ELF, firmware, lifted C++, toolchains, logs |

## Quick start

See [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md). In short: dump your disc, decrypt `EBOOT.BIN` to an ELF, run the
ps3recomp loader/lifter on it, apply `patches/`, configure with `scripts/cfg.bat`, build with `scripts/build.bat`,
run `MyGameRecomp.exe <path>/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf`.

## Playing

Once you have a build, `scripts\launch.bat` (or `python launcher\gow_launcher.py`) opens the launcher. Point it at
your `MyGameRecomp.exe` and your `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf`, press **Check setup**, then **Play**. It keeps a log
per run in `launcher/logs/`, can skip the intro movie, and backs up / restores your saves to `launcher/backups/`.
Every option maps to a runtime environment variable shown in its tooltip; see [launcher/README.md](launcher/README.md).

## Related projects

See [docs/RELATED_PROJECTS.md](docs/RELATED_PROJECTS.md): ps3recomp and its game ports, RPCS3 (used as an oracle),
XenonRecomp / UnleashedRecomp, N64: Recompiled, and others.

## License

The original work here (`port/`, `analysis/`, `scripts/`, `spu/`, `docs/` and the changes in `patches/`) is
[MIT](LICENSE): keep the copyright notice and please link back here. It builds on
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) (MIT) by its authors. Game assets, firmware and anything lifted
from them are **not** covered and must never be committed.

God of War is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment LLC. This is a fan research project, not affiliated with
or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Santa Monica Studio.

1430307002.readme_excerpt:
# God of War: Ascension for PC

A native Linux port of **God of War: Ascension** (PlayStation 3, BCUS98232), built by static
recompilation with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp).

The game's PPU and SPU machine code is translated ahead of time into C/C++ and compiled together with
a runtime that reimplements the PS3 hardware and firmware libraries: LV2 system calls, SPURS, GCM,
the RSX graphics chip (on Vulkan), audio, video decoding, input and file systems. There is no
emulator and no interpreter in the main path. This repository holds the game-specific part of the
port: the pipeline that turns your dump into a native executable, the PC entry point, input, settings,
the in-game menu and the launcher.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **You must own an original copy of the game.** This repository contains no part of God of War:
> Ascension: no executables, assets, translated code or game license keys, and it does not download
> them. The port only works with files you dump yourself from a copy you legally own: the BCUS98232
> Blu-ray disc and the 1.12 update obtained for it. Everything is generated locally from those files
> and must stay on your machine.
>
> - Do not share the game files, the generated executable, the translated code (`out/`,
>   `recompiled/`, `spu/`) or anything else produced from the game. They are derived from copyrighted
>   material.
> - Requests for game files, keys or ready-made builds are not answered and are removed from the issues
>   and the [Discord](https://discord.gg/HCHyR3GYWm).
> - This project does not help to run pirated copies and is not a way to play the game without buying
>   it.
>
> This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Santa Monica
> Studio. God of War is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment.

## Status

**Work in progress, not playable yet.** The port boots, runs the menus and starts a new game, but the
first level runs far too slowly to play.

- Opening video, title screen, 3D menus, profile selection and the Single Player menu.
- A new game loads the first level, plays the opening cinematic in the engine and reaches player
  control: the first tutorials ("Dodge", "Attacks") respond to input.
- Performance (measured under Xvfb): 3D menu ~10 FPS, opening video ~28 FPS, new-game cinematic
  ~30 FPS, first level ~3 FPS. The current bottlenecks are SPU jobs (EDGE geometry) and the RSX
  thread.

**Known issues**
- The first level is not playable at its current frame rate.
- Rare SPURS kernel hangs when the kernel runs workloads on parallel threads (about 1 in 7 runs).
- Physical controllers are untested; keyboard and mouse are.
- No upscaling or adjustable internal resolution.
- Saving on exit is not guaranteed.

## What works

- **Static recompilation pipeline:** reads the disc image and the 1.12 update dumped from your own
  copy, accepts a user-supplied ELF and translates its PPU and SPU code, including the WWS
  job modules and the SPU code the game generates at run time.
- **Graphics:** the ps3recomp RSX backend on Vulkan, with a persistent shader cache and optional
  background shader compilation.
- **Input:** keyboard, mouse and SDL2 gamepads at the same time on port 0, with two remappable keys per
  PS3 button.
- **Launcher** (Tk): game status and save backups, display mode and window size, VSync, FPS counter,
  MangoHud and GameMode, controls, diagnostics switches and a live log with per-run history.
- **In-game menu** (Dear ImGui) and an FPS counter overlay.

## Requirements

- Linux x86-64 and a GPU with a Vulkan driver.
- clang, CMake, Ninja, 7-Zip, Vulkan headers, SDL2, FFmpeg and Python 3 with Tk.
- A legally owned copy of the game: an ISO dumped from your own BCUS98232 disc (version 1.00) and
  the PKG of the 1.12 update, plus a legally prepared ELF of the actual 1.12 game executable.
  Nothing is downloaded and no game file is provided.

**Build notes**
- The translated SPU code is compiled with `-march=x86-64-v3` (AVX2/FMA) by default. On a CPU without
  AVX2, configure with `-DPORT_SPU_MARCH=x86-64-v2`.
- The translated PPU sources are very large, so compiling them takes a lot of memory per job. Pick the
  number of parallel jobs to fit your RAM (`BUILD_JOBS` for `scripts/build.sh`, 6 by default;
  `-j` for `cmake --build`); fewer jobs use less memory but take longer.

## Building

### 1. Get the sources

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This port does **not** build against upstream ps3recomp. It needs the **`gowa-fixes` branch** of
> the fork [RichardFontoura/ps3recomp](https://github.com/RichardFontoura/ps3recomp/tree/gowa-fixes),
> which carries the runtime, SPURS, GCM/RSX/Vulkan, SPU and lifter fixes this game depends on.
> The fork's default branch (`master`) and upstream `sp00nznet/ps3recomp` do not have these fixes:
> always pass `--branch gowa-fixes` when cloning.

Clone both repositories side by side, with the fork on `gowa-fixes`:

```bash
mkdir gowa-src && cd gowa-src
git clone https://github.com/RichardFontoura/gowa-pc.git
git clone --branch gowa-fixes https://github.com/RichardFontoura/ps3recomp.git
git -C ps3recomp branch --show-current   # must print: gowa-fixes
```

The result is:

```
gowa-src/
├── gowa-pc/     this repository
└── ps3recomp/   the fork, on the gowa-fixes branch
```

`../ps3recomp` is the default location for the CMake presets and the scripts. If you keep the fork
somewhere else, point to it with `PS3RECOMP=/path/to/ps3recomp` (scripts) and
`-DPS3RECOMP_DIR=/path/to/ps3recomp` (CMake). When you update this repository, update the fork too,
since both move together:

```bash
git -C gowa-pc pull
git -C ps3recomp pull   # still on gowa-fixes
```

Then create a Python environment with the ps3recomp tool requirements. It can live anywhere;
activate it before running the scripts, or set `GOWA_PYTHON` to its interpreter:

```bash
python3 -m venv ~/.venvs/gowa
~/.venvs/gowa/bin/pip install -r ps3recomp/requirements.txt ninja
source ~/.venvs/gowa/bin/activate        # or: export GOWA_PYTHON=~/.venvs/gowa/bin/python
cd gowa-pc
```

### 2. Prepare the game files

```bash
scripts/extract_update.sh /path/to/patch-1.12.pkg   # -> game/update
scripts/extract_disc.sh /path/to/disc.iso           # -> game/disc (refuses incomplete ISOs)
```

Instead of passing the paths, you can set `GOWA_DUMPS` to a folder that holds the ISO and the PKG.

Supply a legally prepared ELF of the actual 1.12 game executable as `game/GOWA.update.ELF`,
then create the input link used by the pipeline:

```bash
ln -s GOWA.update.ELF game/EBOOT.ELF
```

With the 1.12 update, `USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` is only a small loader that starts `GOWA.SELF`, the real
game executable. The supplied ELF must correspond to that game executable, not the loader.
The `GOWA.update.ELF` filename also lets the runner select the update's boot path automatically.
The current source tree does not include a decryption tool or decryption constants. Keep the ELF
and all generated files local. Existing installations with this ELF/link can continue to the next step.

### 3. Translate and build

```bash
scripts/analyze.sh       # imports, ELF header, SPU images and the WWS job policy module -> analysis/
scripts/lift.sh          # PPU -> out/, recompiled/
python3 scripts/extract_jobmods_elf.py game/EBOOT.ELF --out analysis/jobmods
scripts/lift_spu.sh      # SPU images and the WWS policy module -> spu/
python3 ../ps3recomp/tools/lift_jobmods.py --jobmods analysis/jobmods \
    --out spu --register spu/jobmods_register.c
scripts/build.sh         # linux-vulkan preset by default (also linux-vulkan-debug, linux-null)
```

Incremental builds afterwards: `cmake --build build/linux-vulkan -j<jobs>`, with a job count that
fits your RAM.

**Optional: position-independent SPU fragments.** Some jobs copy SPU code to local-store addresses
chosen at run time. Without translated fragments the SPU interpreter runs that code, much more slowly.
To translate them, run the game once with `SPU_PIC_CAPTURE=<file>`, then
`python3 scripts/lift_spu_fragments.py <file> --overlay 210` and build again.

All generated files stay out of git: `game/` (extracted dumps and decrypted ELFs), `out/` and
`recompiled/` (translated PPU), `spu/` (translated SPU), `analysis/`, `build/`, `gamedata/` (saves
and the virtual HDD) and `scratch/` (temporary files).

## Playing

```bash
scripts/launcher.sh          # settings and the Play button
scripts/launcher.sh --play   # start straight away with the saved settings
scripts/run.sh               # diagnostic entry point (ignores the launcher settings)
```

The launcher needs Tk in the Python it runs with (`GOWA_PYTHON`, or `python3` from `PATH`). If that
Python has no Tk, `GOWA_TK_DIR` can point to an unpacked Tk 8.6 library folder (with `libtk8.6.so`
and `tk8.6/`).

Settings live in `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/gowa-pc/` (`GOWA_CONFIG_DIR` changes the folder):

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `settings.json` | launcher settings (schema 2; schema 1 is migrated on load) |
| `game.ini` | options shared with the in-game menu (`key=value`); the game gets its path in `GOWA_GAME_INI` |
| `last_run.log` | timestamped log of the last run started with Play |
| `logs/<UTC>-<id>/` | per-run history: raw output, JSONL events, metadata and an exit summary |
| `savedata_backups/` | save copies made before every run (the 10 most recent) |
| `frames.csv` | frame times, when enabled under Diagnostics |

### Launcher

- **Game:** installation status, save backup and restore (`gamedata/dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata`).
  Saves are copied before every run; a failed backup is logged and does not block the game. Restoring
  requires the game to be closed, asks for confirmation and backs up the current saves first.
- **Graphics:** display mode (windowed, borderless, fullscreen), window size (1280×720, 1600×900,
  1920×1080 or the monitor), VSync and the FPS counter (corner, scale, opacity and items), all stored
  in `game.ini`. MangoHud and GameMode prefix the command and are disabled when not installed.
- **Controls:** two keys per button, capture on click (key or mouse button), duplicate-key warning
  and a reset button.
- **Diagnostics:** `RSX_FRAME_CSV`, `RSX_VK_TEXTURE_COMPUTE`, `RSX_VK_RAW_TEXTURES`,
  `RSX_TEX_HASH_FULL`, `VDEC_PERF`, `SPURS_KERN_THREADS`, `SPURS_KERN_PARALLEL` and `GCM_FLIP_MIN_MS`.
  Only values that differ from the `scripts/run.sh` defaults are exported; a variable already set in
  the terminal wins.
- **Log:** the last 6000 lines with errors and gaps highlighted, counters, copy, clear and open
  folder. Clearing the view never deletes the per-run history.

### In game

**Insert** (or **R3 + L2** on a controller) opens the PC menu and **F10** toggles the FPS counter.
Both keys are reserved and cannot be remapped.

| PS3 button | Key 1 | Key 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Cross | Space | K |
| Square | Left mouse | J |
| Triangle | Right mouse | I |
| Circle | F | L |
| L1 / R1 | Left Shift / E | — |
| L2 / R2 | Q / R | — |
| L3 / R3 | Left Ctrl / Middle mouse | — / C |
| Start / Select | Escape / Tab | Enter / — |
| D-pad ↑ → ↓ ← | 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 | — |
| Evade (while held, WASD becomes the right stick) | Left Alt | — |

WASD is the left stick and the arrow keys the right stick. Keyboard, mouse and the first SDL gamepad
share port 0, and losing window focus releases all input. Remapping takes effect on the next run.

## How it works

| Part | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Pipeline | `scripts/` | Extracts the dumps, decrypts the executables, analyses the ELF and drives the PPU/SPU lifters |
| Translated code | `recompiled/`, `spu/` (generated) | The game's PPU functions and SPU programs as C/C++ |
| Runtime | [ps3recomp](https://github.com/RichardFontoura/ps3recomp) (`gowa-fixes`) | LV2 syscalls, HLE firmware libraries (SPURS, GCM, audio, video, file systems), SPU runtime and the RSX Vulkan backend |
| Entry point | `main.cpp`, `stubs.cpp` | Reserves guest memory, sets up the virtual file system, starts the runtime and the frame clock, and boots the game |
| PC layer | `pc/` | SDL2 input mapping (`input.cpp`), `game.ini` settings (`game_ini.cpp`) and the ImGui menu and FPS overlay (`overlay.cpp`) |
| Launcher | `launcher/` | Tk launcher: settings, controls, save backups, diagnostics and run logs |
| Tests | `tests/`, `scripts/test_pc.sh` | Input, settings and launcher unit tests that need no game assets, plus window smoke tests and benchmarks |

## Contributing

Bug reports, investigations and pull requests are welcome. Contributions reach `main` only through pull
requests from forks; direct pushes are blocked.

1. Fork the repository and create a branch in your fork.
2. Commit your change there and open a pull request against `main`.
3. A maintainer reviews it; once approved and with every conversation resolved, it is squashed into
   `main`. Pushing new commits after a review asks for a new review.

- **Report issues** with the log of the failing run (`last_run.log` or the folder under `logs/`), the
  build preset, your GPU and driver, and what was on screen.
- **Put fixes where they belong.** Hardware, syscall and firmware library behavior goes into the
  ps3recomp runtime (`gowa-fixes` branch); permanent fixes to translated code go into the lifters, never
  into generated files. This repository is for what is specific to this game and to the PC.
- **Do not skip work or hide failures**: no skipped jobs or draws, forced success codes, or sleeps and
  retries that mask a synchronisation bug. Preserve the game's logic, jobs and effects.
- **Document every function you add** with a comment that explains what it does, its parameters and
  any side effects.
- **Run the tests** that need no game assets before opening a pull request:
  ```bash
  scripts/test_pc.sh
  python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_launcher*.py'
  ```
  With `GOWA_UI_TEST=1` and `xvfb-run` the launcher tests also exercise the Tk pages.
- **Measure performance changes** on the same scene and settings, separating warm-up from steady state,
  and report FPS, frame times and the sample length. Menus and videos are not a substitute for gameplay.
- **Never commit game files**: executables, assets, keys or anything generated from them.

## Credits

- **sp00nznet** and the ps3recomp contributors:
  [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), the static recompilation toolkit and runtime
  this port is built on.
- [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc): the default input layout this port follows.

Also used: [SDL2](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL), [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org),
[Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui), [Vulkan](https://www.vulkan.org),
[PyCryptodome](https://www.pycryptodome.org), [Capstone](https://www.capstone-engine.org) and
[Tk](https://www.tcl.tk). Third-party components keep their own licenses.

## License

third-party portions. See [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for the ps3recomp templates,
Dear ImGui, bundled fonts/stb components, and the provenance of the historical decryption tools.

1430364870.readme_excerpt:
# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível, mas ainda lento (~16-17 fps). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot ao primeiro nível:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal e o primeiro nível, com o Kratos acorrentado. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~30 fps; o primeiro nível a ~16-17 fps (era ~9). O limite é o código das SPUs recompilado, não a placa de vídeo: o job de geometria por draw (módulo 218) é o maior custo, e está sendo reescrito como código nativo, validado contra jobs gravados do jogo, sem precisar rodá-lo. - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo, controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md).

## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), abra o launcher: ```powershell .\scripts\windows\launcher.ps1 ```

JOGAR abre o jogo dentro da própria janela do launcher. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

SPURS_READY_LEVEL=1 is now on by default: without it RsxSync's round-2 job
waited for a kick that never came and the render thread spun on frame slot

All runs now stop at frame ~12 in the same place: func_0037D548 copies
past the end of a block in the heap at 0x14FB8F68 and zeroes the next free
node's header, and the first-fit walk func_00397318 loops on it. STATUS
records how the guard caught it and what to look at next. Patch 0018 caps

what named the heap.

fixed the game shows its first-use save prompt, writes BCES01741-SYSDATA
and goes on to a black screen, which is next. STATUS has the chain and the
diagnostics that found it; gamedata/ (the emulated HDD) and the old lift

# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.pt-BR.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. > [!WARNING] > **Ainda experimental, mas já dá para zerar.** O [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor) jogou do começo ao fim no PC dele (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT). Em processadores comuns o jogo ainda é lento (~24 fps no primeiro nível num Ryzen 7 5700G, 13-21 na luta contra o chefe), e ainda pode travar. Feito para Windows; no macOS (Apple Silicon) ele voltou a rodar, por enquanto só para testes. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Novembro de 2026, no Windows (e no Mac, em testes): - **O jogo inteiro, do boot ao fim:** o iSamigor zerou o jogo. Nos nossos testes: telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas, melhorias e o **online** com a sua conta do site; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado no [site](https://gow-ascension.com.br/pt-br) a partir dos seus discos. As mudanças de novembro estão no branch [`ascension-perf`](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/tree/ascension-perf) até serem medidas no Windows. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.pt-BR.md](docs/MILESTONES.pt-BR.md) (em inglês: [MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md)). ### Desempenho O objetivo é rodar bem em processadores comuns, não só nos fortes. Primeiro nível, num Ryzen 7 5700G (cada número medido no Windows, na mesma cena): | Onde | Começo de novembro | Hoje (5 de novembro) | RPCS3 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Primeiro nível, PC inteiro (8 núcleos, 16 threads) | ~21-23 fps | **~24 fps** | 35-40 fps | | Primeiro nível, só 4 núcleos (8 threads) | ~14-15 fps | **~17-18 fps** | | | Menu principal | ~50-55 fps | ~50-55 fps | | | Luta contra o chefe | 13-21 fps | ainda não medida de novo | | Num Ryzen 7 9800X3D com uma RX 9070 XT (RSX do RPCS3, Vulkan), o jogo chega a 60 fps fora das lutas e cai para cerca da metade nelas. **O que rendeu em novembro** (cada mudança medida sozinha, com o jogo alternando entre ligado e desligado na mesma rodada, num PC de 4 núcleos): - O código do processador principal compilado com perfil de uso real do jogo (PGO): ~6 ms a menos por quadro (~10%). Estendido ao código das SPUs e ao runtime: ~1 ms a mais. - O thread principal do jogo com prioridade acima do normal: -2,7 ms por quadro. - Os jobs do fim do quadro espalhados por até 4-5 SPUs: -2,1 ms por quadro. - O thread do RSX dormindo quando a fila de comandos está vazia, em vez de girar: ~8% a menos; as SPUs escolhendo sozinhas o próximo trabalho: ~1,6% a menos. - Mais partes do módulo de geometria das SPUs (o EDGE) em código nativo, conferidas contra o original: o job mais pesado dele ficou 28% mais rápido. **Para onde vai o quadro agora:** o RSX saiu do caminho crítico nos dois PCs de teste (a espera dele entre as duas passadas da geometria caiu de 9-12 ms para ~0,1 ms). Hoje o quadro é ~55% o EDGE (o módulo 218 das SPUs), mais os jobs de renderização no começo e no fim. Dentro do EDGE, o maior desperdício achado são as interrupções do gerenciador de jobs no meio de cada job: custam tanto quanto o código do próprio job. **Próximos passos:** diminuir essas interrupções, deixar mais leve a cópia de dados das SPUs (DMA em lista), refazer o PGO com o código novo e, depois, o culling do EDGE em código nativo (o banco de teste dele já reproduz as 412 chamadas gravadas do nível). ### Estabilidade - **Corrigido:** o travamento no nível com as listas de geometria esperando para sempre (uma escrita do processador principal se perdia no meio de uma operação atômica de uma SPU: de 3 travamentos em 5 rodadas para nenhum em 4). - **Corrigido:** o travamento com `CopyLocalMemory offset error` (um contador do Edge Zlib e a troca da tabela de streaming de texturas sem proteção): nenhum em 40 rodadas no nível. - **Protegido:** comandos de vídeo corrompidos (`FIFO error: possible desync`) não derrubam mais o thread do RSX, e um draw pedindo uma quantidade absurda de vértices é descartado em vez de travar o jogo. A causa da corrupção ainda está aberta. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); o jogo às vezes trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`); e houve um crash silencioso ~70-105 s depois de entrar no nível em duas rodadas. ### Multijogador online (em desenvolvimento) Os servidores originais do jogo ainda funcionam para quem joga no PS3, mas o jogo recompilado não entra na PSN. Por isso o projeto tem o próprio servidor (em Rust, ainda privado), no ar em [gow-ascension.com.br](https://gow-ascension.com.br) com o cadastro fechado por enquanto; o runtime manda para ele os nomes que o jogo procura. O servidor nunca se passa pela Sony: ele responde só o que o jogo espera, lido no código traduzido ou nas capturas do próprio jogo falando com ele. A partida usa o netcode do próprio jogo (uma malha P2P por UDP); como dois jogadores em casa quase nunca se alcançam direto (cada um atrás do seu roteador), os pacotes passam por um relay do servidor, e o jogo nem percebe. | Passo | Estado | | --- | --- | | Entrar online, Online Pass | ok | | Configuração do online (o jogo lê a nossa) | ok | | Termos de uso, perfil do multijogador guardado na conta | ok | | Tutorial pulado, lobby do guerreiro | ok | | Partida rápida: localização do jogador | ok | | Partida rápida: escolha do servidor de matchmaking | ok | | Conexão com o matchmaking (sessão SSL 3.0) | ok | | Dois jogadores casados numa partida, um deles host | ok (dois jogos no mesmo PC) | | A rede da partida pelo relay do servidor | ok (dois jogos no mesmo PC) | | Launcher: entrar na conta e jogar online | ok | | Partida entre dois PCs pela internet | **em andamento** | | A partida inteira, do lobby ao fim | falta | ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph PC["PC do jogador"] L["Launcher
conta e online"] G["Jogo recompilado
(runtime ps3kit)"] L -- "endereço, configuração e perfil" --> G end subgraph SRV["Servidor do projeto (Rust)"] API["Contas e API"] CFG["Configuração do online"] TUS["Perfil do multijogador
por conta"] GEO["Localização"] SAM["Matchmaking
(SSL 3.0)"] REL["Signaling e relay
(UDP)"] DB[("PostgreSQL")] TUS --> DB API --> DB end WEB["Site do projeto
perfil, ranking, painel"] G2["Jogo de outro jogador"] L -- "login por código" --> API L -- "configuração, perfil" --> CFG L -- "perfil" --> TUS G -- "TCP" --> GEO G -- "TCP + SSL" --> SAM G <-- "partida (UDP)" --> REL REL <-- "partida (UDP)" --> G2 WEB -- "HTTP" --> API ``` No ar no servidor e no site: as contas, o perfil do multijogador guardado por conta, o perfil público com nível e conquistas, o ranking (vazio até haver partidas), um painel administrativo e o login do launcher por código. Planejado: os troféus do jogo assinados e conferidos pelo servidor. **"Jogar offline" vai continuar sempre funcionando**: a campanha nunca vai pedir conta. ## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), instale o launcher pelo `AscensionLauncher__x64-setup.exe` das [releases](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/releases) e, na primeira vez, aponte a pasta `ascension` em **Avançado › Pasta do jogo**. Ele se atualiza sozinho quando sai uma versão nova.

JOGAR abre o jogo; o launcher se esconde até ele fechar. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Melhorias:** liga e desliga. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Abrir a pasta de melhorias** é onde entram as outras, como o **português do Brasil**, que a [página do site](https://gow-ascension.com.br/pt-br) monta no seu navegador a partir das imagens dos seus discos (nada é enviado). As melhorias incluídas são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo. - **Online:** entra na sua conta do site por um código (como numa TV) e liga o online; os troféus do jogo ficam na mesma aba.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

1430390521.readme_excerpt:
# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível, mas ainda lento (~16-17 fps). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot ao primeiro nível:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal e o primeiro nível, com o Kratos acorrentado. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~30 fps; o primeiro nível a ~16-17 fps (era ~9). O limite é o código das SPUs recompilado, não a placa de vídeo: o job de geometria por draw (módulo 218) é o maior custo, e está sendo reescrito como código nativo, validado contra jobs gravados do jogo, sem precisar rodá-lo. - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo, controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md).

## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), abra o launcher: ```powershell .\scripts\windows\launcher.ps1 ```

JOGAR abre o jogo dentro da própria janela do launcher. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

0650a59088532c1a0a3469cdd8812fa457a80bf0.message:
cellGcm: _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel queues the label wait and the flip

libgcm appends NV406E SEMAPHORE_OFFSET and SEMAPHORE_ACQUIRE for the
label, then the flip, so the RSX flips only once the label holds the
value. RPCS3's _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel writes the same two
methods into the context before its flip command. The import here
ignored its context, wrote the label itself from the PPU, and flipped
at call time: whoever owns the label was overruled, and the flip
waited for nothing.

Write the two semaphore methods into the context and queue the flip
behind them with gcm_flip_into_fifo, as _cellGcmSetFlipCommand already
does. A context that is not a mapped command buffer, or has no room,
falls back to the immediate form as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

0ba1229e2c0b4b6003604a06e80fb330dccc1083.message:
sys_ppu_thread: non-joinable threads free their slot when they end

sys_ppu_thread_create ignored its flags and made every thread joinable, so a
thread created without SYS_PPU_THREAD_CREATE_JOINABLE stayed FINISHED after
its exit and held its slot for good. Once 63 such threads had run, every
later create returned CELL_EAGAIN.

joinable is now flags & 1. A non-joinable (or detached) thread frees its
slot at the end of ppu_host_thread_proc, after closing its event and handle
(Windows) or destroying its mutex/cond (POSIX, where the host thread is
detached at creation), under the table lock. sys_ppu_thread_exit leaves the
freeing to that epilogue; the main thread is still marked FINISHED there.
The create log line shows the flags.

tests/test_ppu_thread_slots.c (tools/test_ppu_thread_slots.py): 192
non-joinable threads created and finished in turn all succeed and leave no
slot in use; 63 unjoined joinable threads still fill the table, and a join
frees a slot. Fails on master at the 64th create (0x80010001).

0bd8f34314bc6c29741548bfdd8d690ce351bc5a.message:
cellGcmSys: main-memory maps take the first free IO pages; none before Init

gcm_io_alloc was a bump pointer that survived cellGcmInit, so a title that
maps main memory before Init got its next map placed on top of Init's
command-buffer window, and the FIFO walker then read the wrong memory.

gcm_io_alloc now picks the lowest run of free 1MB pages from the IO -> EA
table (never io page 0) and returns 0xFFFFFFFF when none is free.
cellGcmMapMainMemory refuses with CELL_GCM_ERROR_NO_IO_PAGE_TABLE before
cellGcmInit and when IO space is full, and logs the io it returns. The
cellGcmAddressToOffset auto-map runs only after Init.

tests/test_gcm_io_alloc.c (tools/test_gcm_io_alloc.py): a map before Init
is refused; after Init maps land at 0x800000, 0xE00000 and 0x1000000 and the
Init window is kept; freed holes are reused; IO-full refusal.

tools/test_gcm_io_mappings.py follows the change: its harness now has the
IO page table, GCM_IO_PAGES and an initialised GCM, measures the leak on
the page table, and checks that a map before Init is refused.

0e26194770079d251b113cbc28bb41e27199ac76.message:
sys_spu: an SPU's user event finds the port the PPU binds, and waits for it

An SPU's send_event (interrupt mailbox, code 0..63) was routed only through the ports the group binds with
sys_spu_thread_group_connect_event_all_threads, and answered ENOTCONN at once when there was none. Two things go
wrong with that:

- A port bound for one SPU thread with sys_spu_thread_connect_event was never found by the delivery, only by the
  plain out-mailbox path.
- The SPU thread starts running at sys_spu_thread_group_start while the PPU is still on its way to the connect
  calls that follow it (a real SPU needs far longer to boot than a lifted one). The first request of the program
  was answered ENOTCONN and the SPU program gave up. SoulCalibur II HD's audio engine (MultiStream) binds its ports
  with sys_spu_thread_connect_event, after group_start, and failed this way.

The delivery now looks at the thread's own bindings before the group's (spu_port_queue_locked) and, when the port
is not bound yet, waits for a binding for up to 200 ms on a condition variable that both connect calls signal
before it answers ENOTCONN. An SPU whose thread does not exist is answered at once, since nothing will bind its
port. The out-mailbox path reads the bindings through the same helper under the lock.

The test calls the real handlers and spu_deliver_user_event: bound for the thread, bound for the group, bound 40 ms
late either way, never bound (answers after about 200 ms) and an SPU with no thread (answers at once). On v0.15.0
it fails six checks; with the change it passes (five runs in a row).

1148eaca60f111203aa7ff38e58a927acdcbd353.message:
video/tests: a flip queued in the command stream

libs/video/tests/test_gcm_flip_stream.c compiles cellGcmSys.c in, like
test_gcm_flip_wrap.c, and checks on a title context:

1. _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel puts SEMAPHORE_OFFSET and
   SEMAPHORE_ACQUIRE for the label, then the flip marker, into the
   context, moves current past them, and leaves the label alone.
2. A tick before the drain is a vblank, not a flip.
3. Once the drain has executed up to the marker, the next tick
   completes the flip.
4. A flip written but not flushed does not complete; an executed one
   does, even with a newer flip written behind it and not flushed.
5. A flip the walker abandons when it resyncs out of unmapped IO does
   not hold back the flip status.

On master 8 of the 14 checks fail. tools/test_gcm_flip_stream.py builds
and runs it, so the existing tools/test_*.py sweep in CI covers it.

122690f29d9d566a679fce9944c4718a674ed79b.message:
fp decompiler: biased unsigned remap and _bx2 fetches return signed values

Two ways a fetch comes back re-centred to -1..1 were ignored, so the
shader saw 0..1 encodings:

- SET_TEXTURE_ADDRESS bit 12, UNSIGNED_REMAP_BIASED, applies to every
  fetch from the unit: (round(x*255)-128)/127 on the lanes the crossbar
  fills from a source channel (16-bit X16/Y16_X16 channels: /32767),
  after gamma and not on gamma lanes, and not on lanes the filter flags
  signed. rsx_texture_expand_mask computes the lanes, for the formats
  RPCS3 gives RSX_FORMAT_FEATURE_BIASED_NORMALIZATION.
- EXP_TEX (OPDEST bit 21, the _bx2 modifier) belongs to the instruction,
  not the texture: x*2-1 on every lane of any unit, bypassing gamma
  (RPCS3 _process_texel). It applies from every entry point.

inFAMOUS 2 reads its normals G-buffer through a biased unit and its
