| **Audio** | cellAudio (WASAPI/SDL2, mixing thread, multi-port) | ✅ Complete |
| **Video Output** | cellVideoOut (resolution config, 720p default) | ✅ Complete |
| **Codecs** | cellPngDec, cellJpgDec, cellGifDec (stb_image) | ✅ Complete |
| **Font** | cellFont (stb_truetype backend + fallback metrics) | ✅ Complete |
| **Network** | sys_net (BSD sockets, P2P), cellNet, cellNetCtl, cellHttpUtil, cellSsl, sceNp*, sceNpTrophy, sceNpMatching2 + Score over [psnr](docs/ONLINE.md) | ✅ Complete |
| **Hardware** | cellUsbd (USB), cellCamera (PS Eye), cellGem (PS Move) — stub, no devices | ✅ Complete |

cdb581579fd7ba76d429fab741828ce9e04161d6.message:
Low-CPU update: fewer threads on weaker PCs, support for CPUs without AVX2

- SPURS: on PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the lanes/kernels spin less, wake the
  main thread sooner and run on fewer threads (4-thread PCs: ~10 fps -> ~29 fps,
  8 threads: ~38 -> ~50 fps). Big PCs keep the old behaviour.
- Vertex workers spin far less after each job, fewer workers on small CPUs.
- The once-per-second thread scan only walks the game's own threads.
- No exclusive core reservations on PCs with fewer than 20 CPU threads;
  P-core pinning only on hybrid CPUs with at least 8 P-core threads.
- CPUs without AVX2/FMA/BMI2 (pre-2013 Intel, AVX-less Pentium/Celeron, AMD before
  2015): Setup/the updater detect this and build an SSE4.1 compatibility version
  automatically (same results, slower). The game also checks the CPU at startup and
  shows a clear message instead of crashing.

# inFamous PC

> **Official repo: [github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn).**
> Only download the Setup from the [Releases page](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn/releases) here.
> Forks are not supported, and bugs from forks won't be fixed.

An unofficial native Windows port of **inFamous** (PlayStation 3, 2009, European
release `BCES00220`). The game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code is statically
recompiled to x86-64 C/C++ with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp),
so it runs as a normal Windows program rather than under an emulator.

**This repository contains no game code or data.** You build the game yourself,
on your own PC, from your own copy of the game.

## Easy install

Download **inFamous Setup.exe** from the latest release, run it, choose your
`.iso` (an encrypted image works with its `.dkey` next to it) or your game
folder (the one with `PS3_GAME` in it), pick an install location and press
**Install**.

Setup checks for Python and the C++ build tools and offers to install them,
copies the game out of the disc image, regenerates the recompiled code from your
copy, builds it and adds an inFamous shortcut. Running Setup again on the same
folder updates or repairs the install and only redoes what changed.

## Updating

When a new version is published here, players update in place instead of reinstalling:
**Update now** in Setup (it finds the existing install), the **Update inFamous** shortcut in
the Start menu, or `Update inFamous.cmd` in the install folder. The updater compares every file
with this repository, downloads only what changed, regenerates the game code only if the
port's patches changed, and recompiles only the affected parts. Installs made with an older
Setup need one run of the new Setup on the same folder first.

## Requirements

- Your own inFamous disc dump, European release (`BCES00220`).
- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with Direct3D 12 support.
- A CPU with SSE4.1 (2008 or newer). On CPUs without AVX2 (Intel before 2013, Pentium/Celeron
  without AVX, AMD before 2015) Setup builds a slower compatibility version automatically.
  On PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the game uses fewer threads and less CPU (tested down to 4 threads).
- [Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) with "Add python.exe to
  PATH" ticked.
- [Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/)
  with the **Desktop development with C++** workload and the **C++ Clang
  Compiler for Windows** component.
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), only if your `PS3_GAME\USRDIR` has `EBOOT.BIN`
  but no decrypted `EBOOT.elf`. Setup uses it to decrypt the executable.
- About 10 GB of free disk space and 16 GB of RAM.

## Building manually

```bat
cd installer
cargo build --release
target\release\infamous-installer --game "D:\Dumps\inFamous"
```

`infamous-installer doctor` checks the requirements only. Finished steps are
skipped when you run it again, so an interrupted install continues where it
stopped. See [installer/README.md](installer/README.md) for every step and the
maintainer commands.

## Playing

Run **inFamous** (the shortcut Setup made). It opens a small options window first
(vsync, frame cap, resolution, language and more, saved to `settings.ini`);
**Play** starts the game. The same settings are in the game's pause menu under
**Settings**. Controllers work as on the console, and keyboard and mouse are supported.

**F10** opens the in-game trainer: God Mode, Infinite Energy, Refill Health,
Max Health x2/x5/x10, Add XP, Karma +/-, Kill Enemies / Civilians, Super Speed
and Player Model (play as Zeke, Trish, Kessler, Alden or John). Set `TRAINER=0`
to turn it off.

## DLSS and FSR (optional)

The game can use NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA or AMD FSR for upscaling, and AMD FSR frame generation.
They are not included in the download because NVIDIA and AMD distribute their SDKs themselves,
but both are free and take a few minutes to add.

- **DLSS** needs an NVIDIA RTX graphics card.
- **FSR** works on any modern GPU (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel). FSR 4 needs a Radeon RX 9000 card;
  other cards get FSR 3.1 automatically.

**1. Download the SDK(s) you want.** You need the **source code**, not a Windows or Linux demo.
On the page, click the green **Code** button, then **Download ZIP**. If you go through the
Releases page instead, pick **Source code (zip)**, not the files with "demo" or "samples" in the name.

| For | Download | Rename the extracted folder to |
|---|---|---|
| DLSS / DLAA | [github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS) | `dlss-sdk` |
| FSR and frame generation | [github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK) | `fsr-sdk` |

**2. Put the folder(s) in your inFamous install folder**, next to `infamous-recomp` and
`ps3recomp`:

```
inFamous\
  dlss-sdk\        <- contains include\ and lib\
  fsr-sdk\         <- contains Kits\
  infamous-recomp\
  ps3recomp\
  ...
```

Make sure you don't end up with a folder inside a folder (`dlss-sdk\DLSS-main\include`).
`include` (DLSS) or `Kits` (FSR) must be directly inside.

**3. Rebuild the game once.** Open a Command Prompt in the install folder and run:

```bat
type nul > .installer\update.pending
"Update inFamous.cmd"
```

This rebuilds the game with the SDK(s), which takes a while. Any later update also picks them up
automatically, so you only do this once.

**4. Turn it on in game:** pause, then **Settings**, then **Upscaling** (DLAA, DLSS Quality /
Balanced / Performance, FSR Native AA / Quality / Balanced / Performance) and **Frame
Generation**. The same options are in the launcher's options window. Upscaling and frame
generation apply after a restart.

If the **Upscaling** row is missing, the build didn't find the SDK: check the folder names and
layout from step 2, then repeat step 3.

## How it works

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `ps3recomp` | The recompiler toolkit and runtime: PPU and SPU lifters, HLE system libraries, RSX on Direct3D 12, audio and input |
| `infamous-recomp` | The inFamous-specific parts: program entry, game stubs and fixes, asset tools |
| `installer` | Setup and the command-line installer: reads the disc, regenerates the code from your game, applies `installer/patches`, builds |
| `installer/infamous.toml` | Everything about the game and the port: pipeline steps, generated files, build and launch settings |
| `installer/generated.lock` | Hashes of each generated file before and after the port's patches |

cellAdec: decode AC3 through the run-time FFmpeg loader

cellAdec only produced silence, 1024 stereo samples an access unit, whatever the codec. A title that sizes its PCM ring from bsiInfo+0x14 (channels x 4 bytes a sample) then took the wrong number of samples for an AC3 5.1 movie track: 341 sample frames per 1536-sample AC3 frame.

StartSeq flushes the decoder and Close frees it. The AU bytes and info are copied before AUDONE, which hands the AU buffer back to the title. Without a decoder (no FFmpeg build, PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG=0, a damaged AU) AC3 gives silence of the real frame size, 1536 samples in the channels the frame header names; other codecs keep the old 1024-sample stereo silence. The PCM block moves from the 16 KB per-handle scratch to its own 64 KB per handle in the HLE inject window.

test_adec_ac3 (libs/codec/tests, streams made by the ffmpeg program at test time) checks the silence sizes with and without the library, and that every access unit of a 5.1 stream equals FFmpeg's own decode sample for sample; two swapped channels and one dropped AU must be caught.

0b874166c7bb5caa389d351863a417367ffb4362.message:
perf(spu): NEON fi and cflts on ARM64

On ARM64 spu_fi (the frest/frsqest interpolation step) and spu_cflts fell
through to the per-lane scalar references. Those loops are too large to
inline, so every use in lifted float code became an out-of-line call with the
vector registers spilled around it. This adds NEON forms beside the AVX2 ones
from #500; the other estimate and conversion helpers keep their references.

- fi: the reference's fixed-point arithmetic in 32-bit lanes; the 33-bit
  magnitude 2^32 + (base << 19) - step * y is split on the borrow of the low
  word.
- cflts, scales 0..127: multiply by 2^scale (exact, or an overflow that
  FCVTZS saturates like the SPU), FCVTZS, and exponent-0 / exponent-255 lanes
  patched to 0 / the saturated bound. Other scales use the reference.

test_spu_fi_cflts_neon compares both with the references over 5.6M vectors
(every exponent, fi's borrow edge, all cflts scales) in the default FPCR and
under round-toward-zero plus flush-to-zero, the mode SPU_FLOAT_RZ runs lifted
code in. On non-ARM64 hosts, or with SPU_SCALAR_HELPERS, it compares the
references with themselves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

118fe4bcd1648c98c8ceb32981548c94bf1fa14d.message:
spurs: d11 cut PUTLLC storm overhead (TLS-batched count + memcmp screen)

Direction 11 (MFC 64 Bits War). Probe data (SPU_MFCWAR_PROF, d11prof):
War1/War2 = 73M+84M atomic rounds, PUTLLC ~550-970ns/op vs GETLLAR ~75ns;
notify/commit ~1us on the global table lock; llc entry overhead ~170ns/op.

Two fixes, both in spu_mfc_atomic's PUTLLC case:
- F1: g_spu_putllc_count was a single volatile incremented by every PUTLLC
  on every SPU thread: in a 6-thread line storm each increment is an RFO
  round trip on one shared cache line. Only consumer is the PM flow trace's
  fuzzy run-scoped delta, so count in TLS and fold every 1024 ops
  (max skew 1023*threads).
- F2 (memcmp screen): a PUTLLC that fails because the LINE CHANGED no
  longer takes the line lock (hardware fails those without locking).
  Unlocked memcmp screens the verdict; screen-equal still re-verifies
  under the lock exactly as before, so no false success is possible;
  a torn screen read can only produce a benign false fail (retry).

A/B 3 rounds median (base d10 vs cand): SPU MFC 64 Bits War -5.8% (3/3),
PPU/SPU MFC 64 Bits War -5.1% (3/3), PUTLLC -1.9% (3/3), PUT -1.6% (3/3),
Large PUT -7.5% (3/3); 12/12 PASS x6 runs. Formal: 12/12 PASS,
152,927 -> 147,121 ms total (-3.8%); War 9,592->8,778 / 12,457->11,635.
PUTLLUC +8% formal (+5.4% A/B median) has no mechanism on the untouched
PUTLLUC path; read as layout/noise, flagged in HANDOFF.

168c94fb0a21d199a73af6e5a809f59c408ab715.message:
fs: SDK open flags and error codes in the raw syscalls, EBADF/EMFILE/EINVAL in cellFs, file times, dot entries

sys_fs.h spelt the open flags as hex guesses (O_CREAT 0x100, O_EXCL 0x400,
O_APPEND 0x2000); the SDK values are octal (0100, 0200, 02000), as
libs/filesystem/cellFs.h already has them. A guest libc's
open(O_WRONLY|O_CREAT) of a new file (0x41) never saw O_CREAT and failed
ENOENT, fopen("a") (0x441) was read as O_EXCL and overwrote from offset 0, and
O_EXCL itself was never honoured.

sys_fs (the raw lv2 syscalls):
- O_CREAT|O_EXCL on an existing file is CELL_EEXIST. The "w+b" create
  fallback runs only when the open failed because the file does not exist, so
  a file that merely failed "r+b" (share lock, permissions) is not truncated.
- fd and dir slots are claimed and released under a lock, after the host
  handle is open. The unlocked find-free-then-mark-active let two concurrent
  opens take the same slot and share one FILE*. A full table is CELL_EMFILE
  (was ENOMEM).
- lseek that fails (negative target) is CELL_EINVAL with the offset unchanged.
  The MSVC CRT drops its buffer on a failed seek, so the old position is
  restored explicitly.
- readdir reports sizeof(CellFsDirent) = 0x102 per entry, 0 at the end, not
  name length + 2.
- mkdir on any existing path is EEXIST (a file of that name was ENOENT);
  unlink of a directory is EISDIR; rmdir answers ENOTDIR / ENOTEMPTY / ENOENT /
  EIO instead of ENOENT for everything.

ppu_fs (cellFs imports):
- CELL_FS_EIO was 0x80010001, which is CELL_EAGAIN; it is 0x8001002B. Added
  CELL_FS_EBADF (0x8001002A) for reads, writes, seeks, fstat, readdir and
  fgetblocksize on an fd that is not open, and CELL_FS_EMFILE (0x8001002C)
  when the fd table is full.
- cellFsLseek: an unknown whence and a seek before the start of the file are
  CELL_EINVAL with the offset left where it was.
- cellFsStat / cellFsFstat write the host file's atime, mtime and ctime
  (they were written as 0, i.e. 1970). Fstat uses the 64-bit stat so a file
  past 2 GiB still reports them.

1cf9de49b734e9f2cf36c729e07b838e8416f768.message:
sys_ppu_thread: Windows join no longer frees the slot under the exiting thread

sys_ppu_thread_exit signals finish_event from inside the thread body, which
then still unwinds through the host thread's epilogue. On Windows the joiner
woke at the signal, freed the slot and closed the handles; the epilogue then
wrote to the closed handle and put the slot it had just freed back to
FINISHED, where it stayed. The table lost a slot per join. Join, and detach
of a finished thread, now wait for the host thread to end first (bounded at
5 s so a thread kept running past its exit cannot hang the joiner), as
pthread_join already does on POSIX.

Joining yourself is EDEADLK (it waited on its own finish event forever); a
second joiner of the same thread is EINVAL instead of both waiting and both
freeing the slot.

Test: tests/syscalls/test_ppu_thread_join.c, registered with ctest. It
includes sys_ppu_thread.c and runs real host threads.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

1d66b8e65d74b2f9803fc100e88d36c425ba697c.message:
SPURS: start tasks an SPU creates in another taskset

An SPU task creates a task by setting its enabled and pending bits with
a PUTLLC on the taskset's first line. The runtime started enabled tasks
only when a task of the same taskset exited, and
spu_taskset_start_pending had no caller, so a task created from another
taskset never ran.

God of War: Ascension's particle work runs in two phases: five tasks in
one taskset each add to a shared count, and the one that completes it
creates five tasks in a sibling taskset from the SPU; the main thread
waits for those (0x9C7668 == 0x9C767C). The second phase never started
and the game stopped on its first frames.

Every taskset made through cellSpursCreateTaskset/Taskset2 is now
registered, and a committed line that is a registered taskset's first
line starts its enabled, ready or pending tasks that are not running.

Ref: arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc (ps3kit 0019) and
MaChInEgUn3/God-of-War-Ascension-Recompiled (M0.23) found the same
two-phase pattern.

spurs: split spu_coh_notify_write_locked for ef_line_end's held-lock contract

cellSpurs.c's ef_line_end runs the reservation kill while the caller
holds the table lock (the whole point of the event-flag RMW span).
d4 made spu_coh_notify_write self-contained -- it takes the table lock
itself -- so ef_line_end re-acquired a non-recursive lock on the same
thread and deadlocked: test_spurs_scheduler hung past the 15s firmware
timeout on every Linux/macOS CI lane, and the Windows lane only escaped
by never scheduling the contending interleaving.

Add spu_coh_notify_write_locked (walk only, caller holds the lock),
route spu_coh_notify_write through it, and switch ef_line_end over.
All other callers take only the per-line lock, so the self-contained
variant stays correct for them.

d3 pass all 8 scenarios; d4..pre-fix hang in cellSpursAddWorkload ->
spu_coh_notify_write -> spu_lockline_lock; with this fix all 8 PASS.

299533fcc74eb33a35869a8a8b4dca839f5fa9ea.message:
ppu_lifter: recover module TOC from OPD majority when .got section name is absent

Stripped homebrew ELFs (e.g. PSL1GHT EBOOT.BIN with an emptied shstrtab)
carry no usable section names. When the entry descriptor is detected as
bogus (toc word repeats the code word) the existing fallback only tries
.got+0x8000; with no .got name in shstrtab that lookup finds nothing and
the bogus toc word is kept as THE module TOC. Every 'ld r2, N(r1)' TOC
restore is then lowered with that garbage constant and the guest spins
forever in the first OPD-hook poll (TanakaDOOM-cGcm: 0x103F8 vs true
0xA3328).

Fallback when .got is absent: scan data segments for OPD descriptor
pairs {known-function-start, toc} and take the most frequent toc
(>= 8 votes). OPD descriptors are 16 bytes in ELF64 {code64, toc64};
reading consecutive DWORD pairs would let code_hi == 0 elect 0x0 as
the majority TOC (TanakaDOOM: 1832 bogus votes vs 1817 real ones).

Re-lifting TanakaDOOM-cGcm v0.3 prints
  OPD-majority toc = 0xA3328 (1817 descriptors)
and the rebuilt native executable's full init TTY matches the RPCS3
reference line for line (previously: silent 'b .' infinite loop).

Only the bogus-entry + no-.got path is new; ELFs with section names
take the unchanged .got+0x8000 route.

Merge PR #572: halt and iret longjmp without unwinding on 64-bit Windows (@MaChInEgUn3)

Two conflicts, and the second one is the interesting one: #434 (earlier in
this wave) reached for a different tool for the same problem.

cleanly, so keeping this one means the two jump sites behave the same way,

2e0280848c24d52e70ff9afbf32204e2e207f1e3.message:
D3D12: pick the high-performance adapter in both renderers, with a WARP fallback

The live renderer created its device with D3D12CreateDevice(NULL), the default adapter, which on a dual-GPU laptop is the integrated GPU. Neither renderer had a device on a machine without a D3D12 driver (a VM), and the backend's adapter loop recognised software adapters by DXGI_ADAPTER_FLAG_SOFTWARE only, although the Basic Render Driver (WARP, vendor 0x1414 device 0x008C) has been seen enumerated without that flag in a Windows VM.

rsx_d3d12_device.h creates the device for both: the hardware adapters in EnumAdapterByGpuPreference order (EnumAdapters1 order without IDXGIFactory6), software adapters skipped by the flag or by the Basic Render Driver's ids, then the default adapter, then WARP through IDXGIFactory4::EnumWarpAdapter. RSX_D3D12_WARP=1 uses WARP only, RSX_D3D12_WARP=0 never uses it. A failed attempt is logged with its HRESULT, and the device that was created gets one "[D3D12] device" line (adapter name, vendor and device ids, software or not, VRAM). The backend keeps CELLMARK_IGPU, which now orders the low-power adapter first.

The order is a pure function, rsx_pick_device; libs/video/tests/test_d3d12_device_pick.c checks it against fake adapter lists (attempt sequence and result for each case) and runs in the Linux and macOS self-contained RSX test steps.

cellGcmSys: the guest's offset tables follow every map and unmap

cellGcmGetOffsetTable copied the host tables into the guest window and
handed out pointers to that copy, but nothing updated the copy after
that. Titles keep the pointers and convert addresses inline,
ioAddress[ea >> 20] with 0xFFFF and up meaning unmapped, so every
mapping made after the hand-out was invisible to them.

God of War: Ascension maps more main memory after taking the table,
keeps an intro-loader command buffer in it and converts that buffer's
current pointer to `put` itself. The lookup gave -1, the FIFO walker
ran past the end of the commands into shader microcode, and the loader
waited forever for `get` to reach its buffer.

From the first hand-out on, populate_offset_table and
clear_offset_table write each entry they change through to the guest
copy. test_gcm_io_mappings checks that a map and an unmap after the
hand-out reach it.

31626e690cad490a2c4836c35f5d081b3cb600dc.message:
MinGW: header-defined shared data with selectany, and timespec_get on msvcrt

g_spu_coh_bits (spu_coh_bitmap.h) and g_ps3_ft (ps3_ftrace.h) are defined in their headers and were weak on every toolchain except MSVC. Under MinGW-w64 a weak definition is a PE weak external with a per-object default: every object that includes the header gets its own .weak.<name>.<object> copy, and C++ objects reach the symbol through a .refptr indirection. Use selectany (a COMDAT 'any', as the MSVC branch does) on MinGW as well, so one definition is kept and every object sees the same variable. Other toolchains are unchanged.

test_shared_header_data stores through a C object, reads through a C++ object and compares the addresses of both variables.

spu_interp.c and spu_workload.c call the C11 timespec_get, which the UCRT has and msvcrt.dll does not; a MinGW-w64 targeting msvcrt fails with an implicit declaration and an undeclared TIME_UTC. runtime/platform/mingw_timespec_get.h supplies both from QueryPerformanceCounter on that target only (both callers subtract two readings, so monotonic time is enough).

37b09103f8065cdaf8fc6d500e6e1d3ef62b378c.message:
ps3_env_once: a named helper keyed by name instead of a getenv macro

Review on #515: the macro only existed under GNU C, so MSVC built the same
files with plain getenv and still went green; it would collide with a test
that defines getenv itself (#243's counting fixture); and its cache was per
call site, a rule for the whole file that nothing enforced while other PRs
edit those files.

ps3_env_once("NAME") is an ordinary static inline function. It keeps a
small table per translation unit keyed by the name's text (FNV hash, then
an exact compare), filled once per name under an atomic claim, so any
argument works and two call sites reading the same name share one lookup.
MSVC, clang-cl, gcc and clang compile the same code; getenv is left alone,
and only the call sites that ask for caching get it. A name of 48
characters or more, or one arriving after the 64 slots are taken, goes to
getenv every time.

spurs_job.c, spu_workload.c and ppu_fs.cpp call it at the sites the macro
covered. gen_diagnostics_index.py also recognises ps3_env_once("..."), so
the generated index lists the same 709 knobs as before.

tests/test_env_once.c counts getenv calls by name: one lookup across two
call sites and a name built at run time, NULL cached for an unset
variable, a long name and a full table still read correctly. CI runs it as
C and C++ on macOS and Linux, and with cl (C and /TP) and clang-cl on
Windows.

39743c7b6170fd444aa4e5037e521c49ac08f514.message:
sceNpSignaling: connections for Matching2 room members, context ids from 1, ActivateConnection

On the console Matching2 connects room members through sceNpSignaling, so a
title that activates a connection to a member and waits for its handler
events sees the member come up. Here the Matching2 room code had no link to
sceNpSignaling, context ids started at 0 (which titles read as "no context"),
ActivateConnection was an offline stub and the event values were not the
SDK's, so such a title never saw its peers connect.

- Context ids start at 1.
- AddExtendedHandler stores a second handler per context.
- ActivateConnection makes a PENDING connection to the peer NP ID; it turns
  ACTIVE when Matching2 reports the member up (np_signaling_room_peer, called
  from signal_member in sceNpMatching2.c).
- Events use the SDK values (DEAD 0, ESTABLISHED 1, EXT_PEER_ACTIVATED 10,
  EXT_MUTUAL_ACTIVATED 12) and go to the handler and the extended handler;
  the EXT events go to the extended handler only.
- GetConnectionInfo takes the SDK's code argument and writes that member of
  the info union. GetConnectionStatus, GetPeerNetInfo and the new
  GetConnectionFromNpId answer from the member record.
- CreateCtx and ActivateConnection work once sceNpInit has run, as
  sceNpBasic does (sceNpSignalingInit has no NID).
- New test libs/network/tests/test_np_signaling_rooms.c, run in all three
  workflows; test_np_matching2.c checks the member reaches sceNpSignaling.

42684058fadb75953ebd5ef4f213cef08b027fbf.message:
spu_coherency: holder list as a contiguous array, prefetched

Every notifier walks the whole reservation-holder list with the lock line
held: PUTLLC, PUTLLUC, plain PUTs to marked lines and every PPU store to
one. A title can keep dozens of holders registered and walk the list
~100k times a second. The linked list's malloc'd nodes were a cache miss
per holder on top of the miss on each holder's resv_valid; an array
removes the first, and prefetching resv_valid a few entries ahead
overlaps the second.

Same lock, same membership rules: append on first reservation,
swap-remove on unregister and on forget_range.

42c0471d6ebda1fec9e571ecb466ef43ac83bf7e.message:
cellSpurs: the SPURS2 entry points God of War: Ascension boots through

The title sets SPURS up with cellSpursInitializeWithAttribute2, creates
three Taskset2s and its worker tasks with cellSpursCreateTask2, and
drives one workload through the workload flag. None of these were
registered, so each call was faked as CELL_OK: the instance was never
created, every workload and taskset added to it was refused, and the
tasks never existed.

- cellSpursInitializeWithAttribute2: a CellSpurs2 (8 KB), cleared whole.
  The runtime still schedules 16 workloads, which covers this title.
- cellSpursAttributeEnableSystemWorkload: accepted; the runtime has no
  system service work to run.
- _cellSpursTasksetAttribute2Initialize / cellSpursCreateTaskset2: a
  0x2900-byte taskset, registered as a Taskset2 so the exit-code array
  the SPU side of JoinTask2 reads is kept up to date.
- _cellSpursTaskAttribute2Initialize / cellSpursCreateTask2: creates the
  task with the context and LS pattern from the attribute, then signals
  it, as the firmware does.
- cellSpursGetWorkloadFlag / _cellSpursWorkloadFlagReceiver: the flag
  word at +0x6C and the receiver at +0x77, set up at initialize. The
  scheduler treats a lowered flag as work for the receiver and raises it
  again when it takes the receiver.

4481340eb28869cd316895fcea275ca1edc99f06.message:
tests: serialize the bits_atomic harness on the per-line lock (d4)

The take_slot-vs-exit scenario models the task exit as a raw byte write
under the global table lock. That was the serialization point on master,
where take_slot itself blocked on that lock. d4 moved take_slot (and the
real exit path) onto the bitset line's own lock, so the harness write
raced a take_slot that never blocked: it read the enabled bitset before
the exit's clear landed, handed out id 2, and the freed id 0 stayed
enabled-bit-clear -- 4 passed, 2 failed on every Linux/macOS lane.

Hold the line lock around the harness clear (the order the real
spu_taskset_task_exited uses) and take it before spawning the host op so
the op parks on it as before. Bisect: master and d3 6/6, d4 fails;
with this, 5/5 runs of 6/6 in WSL (gcc 13.3).

53650c7dc3adab81f331e1c7b09d1e84632e5ab3.message:
rsx engine: honour SET_ZMIN_MAX_CONTROL's depth clamp

NV4097_SET_ZMIN_MAX_CONTROL (0x1D78, cellGcmSetZMinMaxControl) turns
clipping at the near and far planes off and depth clamping on. The engine
ignored it and always clipped. Shadow-map passes draw their casters with
clipping off and the clamp on ("pancaking"): a caster between the light and
the cascade's near plane lands on depth 0 instead of being cut away.
Clipped, tall casters fell in front of the near cascade's tight depth range
and were cut, so in inFAMOUS 2 a building's shadow on the street showed from
afar and vanished up close.

The render state gets depth_clamp, set as RPCS3's Vulkan renderer does:
clamp when the clamp nibble is set or near/far clipping is off. It is part
of the pipeline key. rsx_dispatch_init seeds the NV40 reset value 1 (clip,
no clamp), so a never-written register still clips. Metal applies it with
setDepthClipMode per draw; Vulkan sets depthClampEnable when the device has
depthClamp, which init now enables. A backend without it clips, as before.
PS3RECOMP_ENG_DEPTH_CLAMP=0 always clips.

test_metal_depth_clamp draws a triangle in front of the near plane through
the engine and the Metal backend: clipped for the reset value and 0x1,
clamped to depth 0 for 0x10, 0x11 and 0x0, and clipped in every case with
PS3RECOMP_ENG_DEPTH_CLAMP=0 (macos.yml runs both).

53d9ecdb55af7426b36a93346100c94e90f6adf2.message:
rsx engine: VTC slice gather written from the NV_texture_compression_vtc spec

eng_unvtc_3d_slice() is rewritten from the Khronos NV_texture_compression_vtc
specification alone, which the comment now cites as the only source (the
RPCS3 link is gone). Block i of slice z is at
(4 * floor(z / 4) * blocks + i * n + z % 4) * block_bytes, n the layer count
of z's group: 4, or d % 4 for the last group. For full groups that is the
spec's blockIndex formula; for the last group the formula stores the slices
one after another, which contradicts the spec's prose (4x4x2 and 4x4x3
blocks) for d % 4 >= 2, and the prose is followed, as before.

The rewrite was made without the earlier code in view. A standalone check
compares it with a direct implementation of the spec's blockIndex for every
block of eleven volumes (d % 4 == 0 or 1) and with the prose layout for
d = 1..7, 10 and 11, at 8 and 16 bytes per block, under ASan and UBSan.
The three volume tests in test_rsx_draw_engine pass unchanged.

59d1533befa247abdf69cf3be2acb794eaa1891a.message:
rsx engine: emulate the depth-bounds test where the backend has none (Metal)

SET_DEPTH_BOUNDS_TEST_ENABLE (0x0380) passes a fragment only where the
depth already stored at its pixel lies in [MIN, MAX] (0x0384, 0x0388); the
fragment's own depth plays no part. Vulkan has the test and the engine
already hands it the bounds (set_depth_bounds). Metal has no usable
equivalent, so there the test was ignored, and deferred renderers that bound
their light volumes and per-cascade shadow passes with it drew those passes
over every pixel their geometry covered. In inFAMOUS 2 that put sun-shadow
and light shapes far from where they belong.

When the backend has no set_depth_bounds, the fragment program does the
test:
- eng_depth_bounds_prepare takes a float copy of the current zeta
  (depth_snapshot, reused until the zeta's depth_serial moves) before the
  draw, so a bounded draw that also writes depth is tested against the
  depth before it, as one draw is on the hardware;
- the copy goes on a texture unit the program does not sample and has not
  declared as a cube or volume;
- rsx_fp_apply_depth_bounds reads it there with Load at the fragment's pixel
  and discards outside fp_dbounds, a float4 added after fp_alpha;
- the unit is part of the pipeline key and the bounds are constants, so
  moving the bounds does not build a pipeline;
- bounds are saturated into [0, 1] (NaN as 0) and [0, 1] is no bound.
PS3RECOMP_ENG_DEPTH_BOUNDS=0 ignores the test there, as before.

test_shader_msl checks the HLSL patch (behind the alpha-test wrapper, the
MRT form, a cube unit refused, a unit beside a cube) and its MSL.
test_metal_depth_bounds draws through the engine and the Metal backend: a
zeta at 0.25 on the left and 0.75 on the right, then a full-screen draw
bounded to [0.5, 1] lands on the right only, [0, 0.5] on the left only, and
[0, 1], the test off or PS3RECOMP_ENG_DEPTH_BOUNDS=0 everywhere (macos.yml
runs it both ways).

5d3494a95a038e295cfa2aaf245d3f55cb2549bc.message:
lv2 sync primitives: error returns, timeouts and destroy rules

Mutex:
- sys_mutex_trylock of a non-recursive mutex the caller already holds is
  EDEADLK, as sys_mutex_lock already answers. The host try-acquire succeeds
  for the owner (a CRITICAL_SECTION re-enters), so the guest was told it had
  taken a second level of a mutex that has none.
- A timeout past 2^40 us is treated as forever (mutex, semaphore, cond,
  rwlock). lv2_usec_deadline multiplies by the QPC frequency in 64 bits, so
  2^63 or ~0 wrapped to a deadline in the past and timed out at once.

Condition variables:
- The Windows timed wait runs on a QPC deadline. GetTickCount64 advances in
  system-timer ticks, so a 2 ms wait took ~15.7 ms even with the timer raised
  to 1 ms; it now takes ~2.2 ms.

Semaphores: destroy with a thread blocked on it is EBUSY (as lv2) instead of
closing the handle under the waiter, which then spun on a deleted lock.

Reader-writer locks: create/destroy take a table lock (two creates could pick
the same slot); destroy while held is EBUSY; rlock/wlock honour their timeout
and return ETIMEDOUT (it was ignored and the call blocked for good); unlocking
a read lock nobody holds is EPERM instead of releasing an unheld SRWLOCK /
pthread rwlock. POSIX gets the same reader count the Windows branch had.

Attribute names for the diagnostics were read from the wrong offsets; they are
now mutex 0x20, cond 0x10, semaphore and rwlock 0x18.

lwmutex (ppu_sysprx.cpp): trylock of a held lwmutex returns CELL_EBUSY
(0x8001000A), not 0x8001000B, which is CELL_ETIMEDOUT; sys_lwmutex_t.attribute
is protocol | recursive instead of the protocol alone.

cellSyncMutex*: CELL_SYNC_ERROR_ALIGN for a mutex that is not 4-byte aligned.

Tests: tests/sync_stress/test_sync_semantics.c (mutex, semaphore, rwlock, cond),
tests/sync_stress/test_cellsync_mutex.c, both under ctest, and
tools/test_lwmutex_semantics.py.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

61186beffdbdeb636d2c487d507a1e247294ebc3.message:
spu_coherency: the lock-line spin sleeps after ~1 ms

SwitchToThread only hands the core to a thread queued on the same processor,
and Sleep(0) only to one of equal or higher priority, so neither reaches a
lower-priority holder waiting for a core. When every core is busy, waiters
above the holder's priority can keep it off the CPU for tens of
milliseconds. After six rounds of 4096 pauses (~1 ms) the waiter now
Sleep(1)s. SPU_LOCKLINE_SLEEP=0 keeps the plain spin.

693100152dbad2948168e4da0396aeb714bc4161.message:
spu_context: quadword LS access as one load/store and a word-swap pshufb on SSSE3 x86 (SPU_LS_VEC)

spu_ls_read128/write128 on x86 swapped each word with a bswap through four
32-bit memory accesses. In lifted code the register the four stores write is
read back by the next 16-byte load, which cannot be store-forwarded from
four narrower stores: a stall on every lqd/lqx/stqd. On an SSSE3 x86 host the
quadword is now one 16-byte access plus one pshufb that byte-swaps each word,
the x86 counterpart of the NEON rev32 path. The block comment above already
described this form. SPU_LS_VEC=0 keeps the scalar form; MSVC without
__SSSE3__ keeps it too.

6bea2d5992bb418ae4402a7a947947eba71c2ec5.message:
spu channels: ordered wakeups, masked RdEventStat, word SRR0, aligned atomic LSA

Four channel and atomic-command behaviours that guest code can observe:

- A blocking channel read tests its predicate and goes to sleep under
  ch_wait_lock, but producers (mailbox and signal writes, Lr raises, tag
  and stall events) made the predicate true and called spu_ch_wake without
  it. A wake that landed between the reader's test and its sleep found
  nobody waiting and was lost, so the read completed only at the 10 ms
  re-poll. spu_ch_wake now passes through ch_wait_lock before waking, which
  orders it after the reader is either asleep or has not yet tested.

- SPU_RdEventStat returned every pending event. It returns the events that
  are pending and enabled, the condition rchcnt and the blocking wait
  already used, so a pending but masked event (an Lr left by a lost
  reservation, an Sn) no longer shows up in a read waiting on a different
  set.

- SPU_WrSRR0 kept all 32 bits. SRR0 holds a word-aligned local-store
  address, so it keeps value & 0x3FFFC, which is what SPU_RdSRR0 and iret
  see.

- GETLLAR, PUTLLC and PUTLLUC used MFC_LSA unmasked. The MFC moves the
  reservation line to and from a 128-byte aligned local-store address and
  ignores the low seven bits of the LSA. An unaligned LSA put the line at
  the wrong place, and one in the last 128 bytes of local store copied the
  line past the end of the store and over the context behind it.

runtime/spu/tests/test_spu_channel_semantics.c covers all four (run by
tools/test_spu_channel_semantics.py). Its wake test holds ch_wait_lock to
stand in for a reader between its test and its sleep and checks that the
producer's wake does not complete until the reader is asleep.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

6bf420ad1a520bb6b5bc187db4b14e3325eeb607.message:
GCM: GCM_REPORT_SPU_HOLD_MS, a report waits while SPU tasks run a round

The walker takes no time between two GET_REPORTs; a real RSX spends the
frame drawing. A title that turns reports into task signals can then
signal round N+1 while the tasks are still in round N, and a signal sent
to a busy task is taken by whatever wait it reaches next.

God of War: Ascension's RsxSync posts a post-process batch on a report
and signals five tasks. With SPU_SIG_TRACE: batch 2 was posted while two
of them were still on batch 1, its signal ended the other three's
barrier waits, all five then waited for batch 2's signal, which had
been spent, and the RSX waited for their label for good.

GCM_REPORT_SPU_HOLD_MS=<ms> (off by default): while any task that waits
for signals in rounds is out of WAIT_SIGNAL, or parked with its signal
bit set, a GET_REPORT stops the drain pass unconsumed, like an ACQUIRE,
for up to <ms>; a held pass is not "stuck-get". spu_taskset_round_busy()
reports such tasks: a task joins the set on its first WAIT_SIGNAL and
leaves it when it exits, so a task that never waits holds nothing up.

The idea is arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc's (ps3kit patch 0029).

A window can be resized (the Metal window always could; the Vulkan one was created fixed), but the picture did not

  layer), and the display pass fits the picture into it, centred, black around it, filtered when it is scaled. The
  headless and host-surface targets are the size the title asked for and are filled as before.

- the window is a fullscreen-primary one, so the green button works, and PS3RECOMP_FULLSCREEN=1 starts in fullscreen

Vulkan
- the SDL window is created resizable (minimum 320x180); F11 or Alt+Enter switches it to borderless fullscreen on its
  display and back, with the cursor hidden meanwhile. PS3RECOMP_FULLSCREEN=1 starts in fullscreen, as does the older
  PS3RECOMP_VK_FULLSCREEN.
- the frame is blitted into the largest centred rectangle of its aspect ratio and the rest of the swapchain image is
  cleared to black.
- the swapchain is recreated on the next present after a size, maximize, restore or fullscreen change, and presents are
  skipped while the window is minimized: with no drawable area the out-of-date swapchain could not be recreated at
  0x0 and the window was dropped.

7e975c9e5a83b43e34f302dbe84815d0a1fda864.message:
Fragment programs: honour the per-source input precision modifiers

DWORD2 bits 19-21, 22-24 and 25-27 hold a 3-bit input precision modifier for SRC0, SRC1 and SRC2. The hardware clamps the operand to that precision's range after abs and before negate: 1 half, 2 fixed12, 3 fixed9, 4 saturate. The decompiler ignored the field, so a program that relies on the clamp (a soft-particle fade multiplied by |depth difference| with the source marked fixed9) saw the raw value.

The decompiler now emits clamp() around the source after abs and before negate. Branch instructions are left alone. test_fp_decompiler checks every modifier value on every source slot, the abs/clamp/negate order, and a synthetic hand-encoded soft-particle program (TEX, TEX, ADD with an inline constant, MUL r0, tex, |r5| with SRC1 fixed9) through the whole decompile.

8051655e8ee5a4ade15f4c819de86e56d03c997d.message:
feat(video): R32F and RGBA32F colour targets in the Vulkan engine

The register-file engine on Vulkan rendered only into RGBA8 and RGBA16F, so
a surface declared with SET_SURFACE_FORMAT colour 0xC (A32B32G32R32F) or 0xD
(B32F) got no colour target and its draws were lost. Titles render small
reductions, such as a scene's average luminance, into 1x1 targets like these.
Both 32-bit float formats are required colour attachments in Vulkan 1.0;
blending into them is optional, so a device without it draws those targets
unblended and says so once.

New host scenes --float-rt and --float-rt-r draw a blended triangle into an
RGBA32F or R32F surface and sample it back through W32_Z32_Y32_X32_FLOAT or
X32_FLOAT. The Vulkan workflow runs both under the validation layer.

previous owner's object (0 reads as "unknown", which never filters).

the command itself) resolves its private engine through mfc_for(), which
took the SRW claim lock + slot walk on every call because the one-entry
TLS cache was opt-in (SPU_MFC_LOOKUP_CACHE=1). SPU_MFC_PROF showed ~32

already makes a stale cache hit impossible; this flips the default
(=0 still restores the always-locked path).

92cc39a60e3ba45a8758f70154ce60a69b7d242e.message:
fix(video): keep stale engine releases off live Vulkan objects

Vulkan engine handles were reused lowest-slot-first, so a late or
duplicated release of an old handle freed whatever object owned that slot
by then. In one title a colour target's slot ended up holding a texture, so
the next colour feedback draw could not snapshot its target and the frame
stalled.

This is a defensive change. It does not find where the stale handle comes
from. Slots are now handed out round-robin, so a released handle is not
reused at once. A release through the wrong kind's call (texture, colour
target, depth target) is refused and logged, and the live object is kept.

96257d3764889f056165937757ddf4d5f6d051ac.message:
spurs: give every 128-byte line its own lock + version word (direction 4)

The global lock-line lock serialized writers of DIFFERENT lines against
each other: every PPU coherent store, lwarx/stwcx, DMA PUT into a
marked line, and SPU PUTLLC/PUTLLUC queued on one lock even when no
two of them touched the same 128 bytes. RPCS3 solves this with per-line
reservation words (g_reservations: 512 u64 words aliasing every 64 KiB,
128-byte data compare still the authority); do the same here.

- spu_coherency: 512 u64 words at 64-byte stride (one word per cache
  line), bit6 = per-line exclusive lock, bits 7+ = advisory version
  (+0x80 per committed write). spu_linelock_lock/unlock/bump/release
  (+range variants, ascending order for deadlock freedom). The 128-byte
  data compare stays the commit authority; the version is an advisory
  A-B-A token, exactly like RPCS3's counter.
- spu_linelock_release folds bump+unlock into ONE atomic add: 0x40
  carries out of the lock bit into the version field (+0x80, lock
  cleared). Hot paths pay 2 atomics per op, not 3.
- spu_lockline_lock demoted to a pure TABLE lock: it now guards only
  the holder/watch lists and the bitmap's first mark.
  spu_coh_notify_write/_except take it internally, so every writer
  runs: line-lock -> write -> release -> notify-after-release.
- All writers converted: PPU coherent stores (VM_WRITE_COH,
  vm_memcpy_to/vm_memset, ppu_stwcx32/ppu_stdcx64), SPU PUTLLC
  (direction-3 pre-check survives) and PUTLLUC, DMA SDCRZ + PUT into
  marked lines, cellSync (mutex CAS/init, queue apply/and), cellSpurs
  (EventFlag RMW, workload flag/ready/signal/CURCONT words, JoinTask2
  state record), spurs_taskset bitsets, spu_workload (exit record,
  task_exited range, signalled), gcm row copy. Census-named unhooked
  writers (cellFsRead, tty receipts, spu_raw proxy, spurs queue memcpy)
  stay safe: the data compare is still the authority. The libs
  (cellSpurs/cellSync/spurs_taskset) turned out to be writers too --
  via helper wrappers the census attributed elsewhere.

cellPamf: reader calls on an uninitialised reader return INVALID_ARG

pamf_host() hands out a fresh, zeroed slot for any reader EA it has not
seen. That is right for cellPamfReaderInitialize and wrong for every
other call: a getter on a reader the title never initialised got a slot
with pamfAddr NULL and read the PAMF header through it.
PlayStation All-Stars Battle Royale (BCUS98472) does exactly that when
its attract movie never opens: cellPamfReaderGetPresentationStartTime
faulted reading NULL+0x18, right after cellSailPlayer's CreateDescriptor
for movies/attract.pam.

Every call except Initialize now goes through pamf_get(), which returns
the reader a successful Initialize set up at that EA and NULL otherwise,
including after a failed Initialize. The existing !reader checks then
return CELL_PAMF_ERROR_INVALID_ARG (GetMuxRateBound returns 0).

tools/test_pamf_uninit_reader.py builds the real cellPamf.c into
libs/codec/tests/test_pamf_uninit_reader.c: every reader call on a
never-initialised and a failed reader, then a well-formed header that
must still parse. It crashes (SIGSEGV) on the old code and passes now.

aca2b25c22a013adc0a5f30b1b85f703de6dd27b.message:
ppu_sysprx: contended sys_lwmutex_trylock returns CELL_EBUSY

A trylock on an lwmutex another thread holds returned 0x8001000B
(CELL_ETIMEDOUT), despite the "// EBUSY" comment beside it. lv2 answers
a contended trylock with CELL_EBUSY (0x8001000A); ETIMEDOUT belongs to a
lock whose timeout expired. Titles that poll with trylock and test for
EBUSY take the busy case as a failure: FIOS in PlayStation All-Stars
Battle Royale (BCUS98472) logs "sys_lwmutex_trylock failed on mutex
'dearchiver_opticalFunnel': -2147418101" on every contended poll, and
stops logging it once trylock returns EBUSY.

tools/test_lwmutex_trylock_busy.py builds the real handler over stub
guest memory: it fails on the old return code and passes with this one.

b3150f3c37d3297b4e05740f6f2e1a5ebed55fb6.message:
rsx_vertex_fetch: expand missing attribute components (w = 1.0f)

When an attribute array is bound with fewer than 4 components (such as a 3-component position stream (x, y, z)), hardware graphics standards expand missing components to (y=0.0f, z=0.0f, w=1.0f).

If guest code leaves constant register vertex_data4f zeroed, leaving w=0.0f on a 3-component position array causes clip-space w to evaluate to 0.0f after vertex shader projection, prompting the hardware clipper to discard every vertex (100% geometry culling).

Fills missing w=1.0f and y,z=0.0f to ensure standard hardware compliance.

registers such code by source EA: a GET of it at any LS address makes that

(nvhw/tile.c, tile_translate_addr, PFB_NV41 path; MIT, its notice is kept

mcbits 3, partbits 1, colbits_lo 10, partshift 7, the tile's bank as
bankoff. The pitches are envytools' tile_pitch_valid set, which is the
list cellGcmSetTile takes. Four in-block bits (4, 7, 9, 10) and the block
grid anchored at the tile's first 16 KB block differ from the model and
keep the RSX's layout as the title's depth-of-field job reads and writes it.

compared against it only as a black box: same address for every 32-byte
block of the title's tile 4 and for 1.3M sampled addresses over every
valid pitch, banks 0-3 and five tile offsets. A pitch outside the
SetTile list now has no tiled address.

c88becc1a7197b296936cc8b01d6ab893c76ad77.message:
SPURS: 32 workloads on a CellSpurs2; the kernel context's tempArea

God of War: Ascension adds 18 workloads to its CellSpurs2. The workload
table, AddWorkload and the coordinator stopped at 16, so the last two,
EDGE2 and RsxSync, were refused, and the frame pipeline that runs
through RsxSync never started.

- A CellSpurs2 instance (cellSpursInitializeWithAttribute2) takes wids
  16-31 in their own instance fields, libspurs' layout: readyCount in
  the idle-SPU bytes at 0x10, state at 0xC0, signal bits in the be u16
  at 0x78, info at 0x1000. Its current and maximum contention bytes
  hold two 4-bit counts, the low nibble for wid & 15 and the high one
  for wid | 16. flags1 (0x74) gets SF1_32_WORKLOADS (0x40). Both other
  ports of this title arrived at the same layout.
- AddWorkload, the coordinator, the policy workers, ReadyCount*,
  SetMaxContention/SetPriorities, RemoveWorkload, GetWorkloadInfo and
  the flag receiver go through wkl_*_off and wkl_count_*; spurs_policy.c
  keeps 32 workloads per instance.
- The policy module's kernel context gets the instance's first line in
  tempArea (LS 0x100..0x17F) at entry and at every cellSpursModulePoll,
  as the kernel copies it when it selects a workload. The title's job
  code reads flags1 there before it looks a wid >= 16 up.
- _cellSpursWorkloadFlagReceiver and the coordinator lowered the
  workload flag with vm_write32 under spu_lockline_lock. vm_write32 takes
  that lock itself when an SPU holds a reservation on the line, and it is
  not recursive: the main thread hung inside the receiver call as soon
  as RsxSync (wid 17) could be named. ef_w32 stores the word plainly, as
  ef_w16 does.

ccd4155977a7d437670718640d4a87a9ef57cfe1.message:
cellGcm: set context end to wrap JUMP slot (begin + size - 4)

In cellGcmSetupContext, cdata + 0x4 (end) was set to cmdbuf + cmdSize
instead of cmdbuf + cmdSize - 4. Per the Cell GCM specification and the
SDK, the last 4 bytes of the command buffer are reserved for the wrap JUMP
instruction back to begin.

When a title writes its own JUMP-to-begin at context end (such as MLB The
Show 16), an end value at cmdbuf + cmdSize places the JUMP 4 bytes past the
allocated buffer into adjacent memory. Once that memory is overwritten by
subsequent allocations, the RSX walker fails to wrap, walks into data, and
hangs until timeout.

Additionally:
- In the RSX walker drain overrun check, a ring filled exactly to end is
  legal and full rather than an overrun, so check cur > end.
- When placing a wrap JUMP, end is itself the last 32-bit slot, so use
  (cur <= end) ? cur : end.
- Added verification of end calculation to test_gcm_flip_wrap.

cd926aa1e20de9db3b2cf4c99ba3bc9bdfcf5068.message:
ppu_hle: cache each thread's NID lookups; ppu_gcm_pump looks before it locks

ps3_hle_call found a handler by scanning g_ctx (about a hundred entries)
and then g_hle_nids (over a thousand), both linearly, on every call. God
of War HD makes about 95k HLE calls a second in gameplay, most of them
cellGcmAddressToOffset and _sys_memcpy, and ps3_hle_call was 6.5% of its
main thread.

- A per-thread slot per NID keeps the g_ctx index or the table index,
  with the table sizes it was filled against: a registration made after
  the first call is still found, and no slot is ever read half-written.
- ppu_gcm_pump, called on every HLE call and timer sleep, returns at once
  when nothing is pending instead of taking the pump and swapping both
  pending words, three atomic operations on lines the ticker thread
  writes. A notification posted just after the check is delivered by the
  next pump, as one posted while another thread holds the pump is.

ps3_hle_call fell to 1.5% of the main thread.

d2fd066a48eb8441464382bce20b5607b4e9bbab.message:
spurs: skip the lock-line lock for PUTLLCs that cannot succeed (direction 3)

In a lock-line contention storm (spurs_test SpinLock: 8 SPUs
spin-GETLLAR/PUTLLC on one line), ~7 of every 8 PUTLLCs are losers whose
reservation a peer's commit already killed. Hardware fails those without
any lock; we used to take the one global lock-line lock anyway. A
SPU_POLLTRACE run measured the storm ceiling at ~90k locked ops/s.

Pre-check the reservation atomically (resv_valid + resv_ea); when it is
dead the branch selection is identical to always-locking, so the lock is
skipped only where the outcome was already certain.

Also tried gating spu_coh_notify_write's per-peer spu_ch_wake on
parked-only waiters: REVERTED after bisect showed it was not the cost
(and it widens the lost-wakeup race against the 10 ms sleep timeout).

Measured (SPURS_PROF+SPU_POLLTRACE runs, same session): atomic op rate
~200k/s -> ~800k/s in the storm; SpinLock 383,091 -> 333,770ms (-13%);

condition (Ping-Pong 15s -> 8+min livelock); the committed form keeps

d3d5917b1cec072ce90a6b10c2f5e1f5e88c4605.message:
D3D12: bind X16 and the other decoded 16/32-bit formats; FP DDX/DDY

God of War: Ascension's first-use screens drew their text as solid
blocks. Its font atlas is X16 (0x94, linear 256x256, pitch 512), a
distance field, and three things stood between it and a glyph:

- d3d12_bind_texture recorded only B8, A8R8G8B8, G8B8, DXT and the
  half-float format, so the atlas was never bound. It now also takes
  X16, Y16_X16, X32_FLOAT and Y16_X16_FLOAT, which rsx_texture_layout
  already decodes (the title's post-process passes bind the last two).
- The draw-time SRV picked its DXGI format from a second list of its
  own and fell back to R8 for anything else: an R16 upload behind an R8
  view, which sampled nothing. vp_tex_dxgi() now gives the upload and
  the view the same format, from rsx_texture_layout's class.
- The fragment decompiler left DDX/DDY as unhandled ops. The glyph edge
  width is max(|ddx|, |ddy|) of the texture coordinate; now ddx()/ddy().

TEXFMT_ALL=1 logs every distinct texture a draw binds, whatever its
format; TEXFMTDBG only shows the formats this backend already binds.

The same three gaps are described in arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc's
ps3kit patch 0021, for the live draw engine.

d813e14cd2325dbe0af650f350242dc1e5594a00.message:
sys_event: queue destroy honours its mode, timed receive runs to an absolute deadline

sys_event_queue_destroy:
- An unknown mode is EINVAL. A plain destroy while receivers are blocked is
  EBUSY and leaves them blocked. SYS_EVENT_QUEUE_DESTROY_FORCE wakes every
  receiver with CELL_ECANCELED. The mode argument was ignored and the lock
  was deleted under a receiver parked with no timeout, which then never
  woke. Receivers are counted (sys_event_queue_info.waiters) so destroy
  knows when the last one has left.
- Ports connected to a destroyed queue are disconnected: a send answers
  ENOTCONN instead of landing in whatever queue next reuses the slot.

sys_event_queue_receive (Windows): a timeout of a millisecond or more waits
to an absolute QPC deadline, rounded up. The wait used a truncated per-wake
timeout (1500 us became 1 ms) that restarted in full after every wake that
found the queue empty, so a contended timed receive could overrun without
bound. The POSIX branch no longer reports a timeout when an event arrived
with it.

Test: tests/sync_stress/test_event_queue_destroy.c, registered with ctest.

Merge PR #466: hand rsx_state only the methods with outside effects (@tekulvw)

This is the second pair the plan singled out -- #466 against the #548 -> #554
chain on cellGcmSys.c and the five GCM tests -- and unlike the first one it
did conflict. The five test files merged clean; cellGcmSys.c had two.

The top of the drain pass is a both-added local: #554's wdiag from
gcm_word_diag() and #466's legacy_state_live. Both kept.

The second is the substance. #466 gates rsx_process_method() so that with the
draw engine up and no vtable backend registered, only methods with effects
outside rsx_state are handed over -- the state it builds is never read
otherwise. But #554 had already funnelled every 3D method through a new
gcm_3d_method(), from two call sites: the method-run loop and the single-method
path. #466's hunk patches the single-method site, which is the one it could see
on master.

Applying it there verbatim leaves the method-run loop ungated -- the common
path for a real title, since that is the one that decodes runs -- so the
optimisation would have looked present and done close to nothing, with nothing
failing. So the gate goes inside gcm_3d_method() instead, with
legacy_state_live passed in (it is computed once per drain pass and both
callers are in that function), and both call sites updated.

rsx_get_backend() and rsx_draw_engine_enabled(), and a backend can be
registered while the walker is running. #466 computes it per pass; that stands.

Merge PR #525: the interpreter rejoins inside resident regions (@rigaz29)

#525's rule -- inside a resident code region, the region's image owns the
address, so an interpreter entered mid-job finds the job's lifted functions
instead of running the rest interpreted -- is already in the tree. #419 and
#420 (wave 4) moved that same ownership order into spu_lifted_lookup_full(),
where it also handles a pending verified region (NULL rather than a stale
image) and falls back through the resident task and overlay; #436 put its
registry memo under it and #481 put a dispatch cache in front.

So #525's hunk rewrites spu_lifted_lookup() back to a two-case function and
takes #419/#420/#436/#481 out with it. The resolution keeps the wave-4
version, which implements #525's rule as a strict superset.

This is a no-op merge for the function, which is worth saying plainly rather
than leaving implied: #525 is in the release because the behaviour it asks
for is in the release, not because its diff survived.

Its tests do survive and are the reason this is verifiable rather than
asserted. The three assertions #525 adds to test_resident_code_regions
merged cleanly and now run against wave 4's resolver: the rejoin probe
resolves each streamed job's own code at its LSA, and an overwritten buffer
falls back to the base image. All three agree with the wave-4 behaviour --
checked, because an assertion written against a two-case lookup could easily
have contradicted the pending-region case that #419/#420 added.

e56af258bee1b8941c5aac14d0c420b9a6dfc4ab.message:
perf(spu): four-lane SSE4.1 form of the single-precision helpers

x86 builds without AVX2 (the default -msse4.1 runtime and lifted code) ran
fa/fs/fm/fma/fms/fnms one lane at a time through the scalar fast path, and
those helpers topped a Linux profile of a title's SPU work. The AVX2 form's
lane rules now also run as two f64x2 halves on SSE4.1. Each half widens
exactly, operates, clears the 29 low significand bits and narrows exactly. A
lane keeps that result only where it is provably the truncated SPU result:
ordinary single or true zero operands, an exponent gap for adds, a
normal-range result, and the TwoSum boundary check for fma. Every other lane
takes the existing per-lane path. SSE4.1 has no FMA instruction, so nothing
can be contracted.

The tests are synthetic. test_spu_float_vector_scalar compares the selected
vector form with the scalar per-lane forms bit for bit. It covers every
edge-word triple (+-0, biased exponent 0 with fractions, smallest normal,
largest finite, biased exponent 255, Smax) and random lanes aimed at
2^-126/2^128, cancellation and wide gaps. On x86 both float tests build with
-msse4.1 -ffp-contract=off. On a Ryzen 7800X3D, the SSE4.1 and AVX2 forms
both had 0 mismatches over 96.7M lanes against scalar and 446.8M lanes
against the exact references. Time per vector: fa 10.9 -> 5.7 ns, fm 9.3 ->
2.8 ns, fma 11.2 -> 5.3 ns.

e95b5827f53ee41da3ead590ebe44c1565f946a3.message:
lv2 SPU group syscalls: destroy of a running group, group_start state, error returns

- sys_spu_thread_group_destroy freed the context and local store of a thread
  that was still running, a use-after-free inside that thread (a middleware
  shutdown writes its quit word and destroys without a join). It now waits up
  to 250 ms for running threads to stop and otherwise answers CELL_EBUSY with
  nothing freed.
- group_start on a group with a running lifted thread is CELL_ESTAT instead of
  running the setup over the live context; an unknown group is ESRCH.
- A new group's unused thread slots are invalid (MAX_SPU_THREADS) rather than
  index 0, which is another group's thread.
- About 20 error paths set r3 to a CELL_E* code and then returned -1;
  lv2_try_syscall stores the return value in r3, so the guest saw
  0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF. They return the code.
- get_exit_status of a running thread is CELL_ESTAT (it was ENOSYS's value),
  get_spu_cfg stores the value through its pointer argument, connect_event on
  an unknown thread is ESRCH, and image_import answers CELL_EFAULT /
  CELL_ENOEXEC instead of -14 / -8.

Games that render on CPU and only memcpy frames into the GCM VRAM mapping (e.g. TanakaDOOM-cGcm, a Chocolate Doom port) emit zero RSX commands, so the D3D12 backend never presents and the window stays black while game logic, audio and flip tracking all run fine.

cellGcmSys: add cellGcm_current_scanout() reading the module's own s_display_buffers (in this mode the draw engine table may not exist at all, so cellGcmSys is the authoritative source).

rsx_d3d12_backend: add scanout_auto_present(), called from render_frame after guest_fb_present. It only fires when the frame had zero draw records; it copies the current scanout buffer up with A,R,G,B -> R,G,B,A byte order (big-endian guest pixels) and alpha forced to 0xFF into an R8G8B8A8 placed footprint.

Env: SCANOUT_FB=0 disables, GCM_GUEST_FB takes precedence, SCANOUT_FB_DBG=1 logs offset/pitch.

Scope: verified on TanakaDOOM-cGcm v0.3 (title screen, menu, E1M1 gameplay render correctly). Covers CPU-blit frames only; games mixing CPU blits with RSX overlays are untested.

fix(build): export the runtime's probed SSE4.1 requirement to consumers

The runtime probes -msse4.1 and, when the compiler accepts it, builds itself
with it so spu_shufb and the other static-inline SPU helpers take their
pshufb/blendv paths. The flag was PRIVATE, so a game target linking
ps3recomp_runtime compiled the same helpers in its lifted SPU code without
it and fell back to the scalar forms on x86-64 compilers whose baseline lacks
SSE4.1 (gcc and clang for generic x86-64). It is now PUBLIC; hosts where the
probe fails (Apple clang on arm64) are unchanged.

tools/test_spu_isa_consumer.py configures a real CMake consumer (a C
executable and a C++ object library) against the SDK, requires the consumers'
compile commands to carry -msse4.1 exactly when the probe passed, checks SPU
shuffle/selector semantics in both, and repeats with the probe forced off. It
skips when CMake, Ninja or a compiler is missing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

f5f7842ffa4d067d92202060f97bd586516b034d.message:
spu_interp: decode by one 2048-entry table indexed by insn >> 21

A Time Profiler of interpreted SPU jobs in one title put 37 % of the
audio queue's worker CPU and 29 % of the frame queue's in
spu_decode1. It walked a fixed cascade of eight generated switch
functions and three channel compares per executed instruction, and
computed every immediate field up front.

Every SPU opcode field (4 to 11 bits) is a prefix of bits 31..21, so
the cascade's result, precedence included, is a pure function of
insn >> 21. gen_spu_interp.py now applies the cascade order to all
2048 prefixes and emits one table of (op, immediate form);
spu_decode1 loads one entry and computes only the field that form
needs. spu_ins and the execute switch are unchanged.

Verified: an off-tree harness compared every spu_ins field of the
old and new decoder over all 2^32 words at pc 0 and 0x3FFFC (0
mismatches). A synthetic decode microbenchmark ran 1.90x faster
(10M decodes, 0.118 s -> 0.062 s mean of 5). The new test spu_decode
pins the field boundaries of all 15 immediate forms; precedence
between colliding prefixes was checked off-tree with an injected
collision. The full test suite passes
(23/23, 22/22 before); gcc-16 builds and passes spu_decode. The
generator reproduces spu_interp_tables.inc byte for byte.

f6c37edcbc790b95e91813e432348bdb68350951.message:
Merge PR #499: depth read as a texture converts on the GPU, with LRU eviction (@n0madic)

Merged after the #502 -> #507 chain as the plan requires. Six conflicts, and
one of them was a correctness regression waiting to happen.

Routine unions:
- rsx_draw_engine.h: #439's texture_upload_ordered flag and #499's
  depth_as_color backend hook, both appended to rsx_draw_backend.
- surface reuse: #422's "same sample grid" condition with #499's last_use
  touch (and #499's braces, which the shared `return i;` needs).
- the zdepth snapshot: #507's eng_zdepth_snapshot(i, w, h) signature with
  #499's last_use touch -- #499 was written against the one-argument form.
- the test file: #502/#507's depth_pass/sample_depth helpers and #499's
  stub_depth_as_color/depth_pass_then_read_as, which git offered as one
  conflict because they share four middle lines and a trailer. Both chains
  reconstructed with their own copy of the shared lines; all four helpers
  present, every test in the file called, brace-checked.

The one that mattered: eng_zdepth_to_guest's per-row conversion. #460
factored it into the vectorizable eng_depth_row_to_guest(), and #499 carries
the inline loop it was written against. The two agree exactly on Z24 --
#460 even kept #499's comment about quantizing in double -- but on **Z16**
#460's helper computes (u32)(d * 65535.0f + 0.5f) in float, where #499's
version is explicit: (u32)((double)d * 65535.0 + 0.5), because "in float the
product rounds first and a value within 0.002 of a half could go the other
way", and it has to match bit for bit what #499's new GPU depth_as_color path
produces.

Taking #460's call site alone would have left #499's Z16 readback off by one
LSB against its own GPU path, on a subset of depth values, with both PRs
green on their own. The call site stays #460's one-liner and the helper's Z16
path is quantized in double, with #499's comment moved to where the code now
lives.

f8b674e9260191a098d6285ffaf89c22026b31ec.message:
Merge PR #504: vertex array addresses wrap at 28 bits (@erikomis)

#504 replaces two plain `plan->base_offset + fetch->desc.offset` additions
with rsx_dsp_resolve_vertex_offset(), which wraps at 28 bits as the hardware
does. One of its two hunks merged clean -- the prefix used to compute
stable_base. The other conflicted, because #458 (earlier in this wave)
restructured the fetch loop from per-vertex to attribute-major and #504's
hunk patches the per-vertex form it was written against.

Kept #458's attribute-major switch, and applied #504's wrap at the
per-vertex site #458 retains as its fallback -- which its hunk could no
longer reach. Verified afterwards that both base_offset uses in the file go
through rsx_dsp_resolve_vertex_offset(): a wrap applied on one of two paths
is worse than none, because the two would disagree about where a vertex is.

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**The POSIX boot path runs in CI, but not yet with a retail title in this
tree.** `ps3recomp_boot_smoke` loads a synthetic PPU ELF through
`ppu_loader.cpp`, the HLE dispatch, guest threads, the frame clock and the
renderer. CI also builds and boots that ELF through `templates/project` on
macOS and Linux. That proves the per-game scaffold runs on both hosts; it is
not a compatibility claim for a retail game.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```

├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

449836c8b89b5003f56e011e5d7bcf17a8b6af0b.message:
Static recompilation of Bakugan: Battle Brawlers (PS3) for Windows x64

The PlayStation 3 release (BLES00758) is lifted ahead of time to C++ with
ps3recomp and linked against a small HLE runtime, so the result is an ordinary
Windows executable rendering through Direct3D 12 -- no emulator and no
interpretation at run time.

Boots, plays every publisher FMV, the opening and the narrative intro (H.264/AAC
through Media Foundation), and reaches the title screen, all menus, the mode
selector and the in-game keyboard at 30 FPS. 3D models, gameplay and sound
effects are still missing; the RSX render target never receives geometry.

The port's own work -- D3D12 backend and depth handling, Media Foundation video
path, SPURS LF queue, taskset shutdown, keyboard input -- is captured in
patches/ and applied by the pipeline, so the toolkit checkout stays disposable.

No game code, assets, keys or lifted sources are included: everything is
regenerated from the user's own disc dump.

6d71be564f1a7c2e9e3354e30664e86139f5d1e9.message:
video: alias the guest's render-target resolve to the live target

Battle Arena draws into the 1120x584 offscreen target 0xEAB0000 and then
resolves it with NV3089 into 0xDF60000, which the final composite samples as a
texture. Nothing in the D3D12 backend writes rendered colour back to guest
memory - rsx_live_draw.c and rsx_draw_engine.c do, but only the Vulkan path
initialises them - so that resolve copied zeros and the whole 3D layer came out
black.

When a 4-byte blit's source is a live target, record its 64K page as an alias of
that target and consult the alias where a texture is bound to an offset. The
backend keeps the target at 1120x584 (the guest's 2x storage is not simulated),
so the alias is 1:1: no readback and no GPU stall. The attract screen's
full-screen quad samples the same destination and now shows the scene.

With the composite fixed, what is left of the 3D layer is the deformation inside
the target: giant triangles and stretched textures, still to be traced through
viewport/clip, depth and vertex-program translation.

Patch 0007.

d3d427eff908b36d475863c470487ac68351c5ad.message:
audio: lift the SPU mixer path and make the menu scores play

The menus open SNDP scores carrying 16-bit little-endian PCM at 44.1 kHz, so
the earlier note blaming every silence on ATRAC3 was wrong for these tracks.
Implement the inbound SPU queues and the `stop 0x110` service (bind, receive,
resume; keys are 32-bit values, not output ports, and handlers also publish
the result in PPU r3). Multistream copies two kernels to LS `0x32D80` with
entry `0x32D98` and no static image to lift, so tools/build_audio_overlays.py
generates them relocated and registers them as overlay images 6/7, recognised
by signature because the game stages their bytes on the heap first.

Fix the returns between interpreter and compiled code, drop a getenv per MFC
access, and enable the toolkit's existing SIMD helpers through source-scoped
-msse4.1/-mavx2 flags plus a startup CPU check, so the large PPU lift does not
rebuild. The mixer keeps a 256/48000 s pulse and PPU sleeps ask for
high-resolution timers. Delivery intervals went from ~47 ms for 10.7 ms of
audio to 16-30 ms, and the audible cut went away with SSE4.1 enabled.

Renderer: raise per-draw signature, samplers and textures from 4 to 16 units,
and cache failed PSOs instead of recompiling the same shader on every draw -
the repeated 0x80070057 attempts had dropped the frame rate to a fraction of
the target.

Battle Arena does emit geometry: captures show 438-600 draws and content in
`0x0EAB0000`, so the old "zero geometry" reading described the menu, not the
fight. Characters and stage still do not appear correctly.

Patch series: 0005 (SPU events and timing), 0006 (D3D12 texture units and PSO
cache).
