God of War: Ascension — port nativo para PC

Recompilação estática do PS3 · Windows e Linux (SteamOS) · Direct3D 12 · sem emulador · traga o seu disco

Windows e Linux · Como jogar · Estado atual · Requisitos · Perguntas frequentes · Novidades · English

> **Projeto de fãs, sem fins lucrativos, sem relação com a Sony.** *God of War* é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. Este repositório **não contém o jogo** nem o firmware: você precisa da **sua própria cópia** do jogo (BCUS98232). O **update 1.04** e o **firmware oficial do PS3** são **gratuitos**, baixados direto da Sony (links em [Como jogar](#como-jogar)). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Para jogar, baixe o [Otavix Launcher](https://github.com/otavix010/otavix-launcher/releases/latest).** Ele baixa este port, gera o jogo no seu PC e o mantém atualizado sozinho. O port recebe **cerca de 6 atualizações por dia**, feitas a partir dos reports e pedidos dos jogadores: para relatar um problema ou pedir algo, use **"Reportar problema"** na página do jogo no launcher. O relatório já vai com o log, as configurações e as fotos, e é por ele que as correções saem mais rápido. > > **To play, download the [Otavix Launcher](https://github.com/otavix010/otavix-launcher/releases/latest).** It downloads this port, makes the game on your PC and keeps it updated by itself. The port gets **about 6 updates a day**, driven by players' reports and requests: to report a problem or ask for something, use **"Report a problem"** on the game's page in the launcher. The report carries the log, the settings and the screenshots, and that is how fixes come out fastest. ![Capítulo 16 a 66 FPS num Ryzen 7 9800X3D](docs/imagens/cap16_9800x3d.png) [English summary below](#english-summary) ## Versões: Windows e Linux O port tem **duas versões**, geradas a partir do mesmo código e do mesmo disco: | | **Windows** | **Linux / SteamOS** | |---|---|---| | Situação | **estável**, campanha completa jogada | **beta** (desde o Otavix Launcher 1.0.92) | | Sistema | Windows 10/11 64 bits, GPU com Direct3D 12 | SteamOS (Steam Deck, Legion Go S) e Linux 64 bits, pelo Proton | | Como jogar | pelo launcher, ou `gerar.cmd` e `jogar.cmd` | pelo launcher, ou `scripts/linux/gerar.sh` e `jogar.sh` | | Vídeo | Direct3D 12 | Direct3D 12 pelo Proton (vkd3d, sobre Vulkan) | | Build | AVX-512 se a CPU tiver, senão AVX2, senão a **compatível** (sem AVX2, mais lenta) | portátil (AVX2) | | Desempenho medido | [tabela abaixo](#desempenho-medido) | [tabela abaixo](#desempenho-medido) e [docs/desempenho_portatil.md](docs/desempenho_portatil.md) | Nas duas, **você traz o seu disco**: o launcher gera o jogo no seu aparelho a partir da sua cópia. Detalhes do Linux: [Linux / SteamOS (beta)](#linux--steamos-beta). ## O que é Um port **nativo** do *God of War: Ascension* (PS3, 2013) para Windows e Linux. Não é um emulador: o código do jogo é **traduzido para C/C++ e compilado** para x86-64 (recompilação estática), em cima do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) do sp00nznet. Como o código do jogo não pode ser distribuído, **o seu PC gera e compila a parte do jogo a partir da sua cópia**. Um comando só faz tudo. | | | |---|---| | ![Fase 1, luta com a Fúria](docs/imagens/fase1_dodge.png) | ![Fase 1, close da Fúria](docs/imagens/fase1_furia.png) | ## Como jogar ### Recomendado: pelo Otavix Launcher O [Otavix Launcher](https://github.com/otavix010/otavix-launcher/releases/latest) junta tudo num lugar só: baixa este port, confere se o Python e as ferramentas do Visual Studio estão instalados, pede só a pasta do disco (o update 1.04 e o firmware o gerador baixa da Sony; quem já tiver os arquivos, inclusive o PS3UPDAT.PUP, pode escolhê-los), gera o jogo para a sua CPU e abre com as opções de vídeo e os saves. Quando sai uma versão nova, ele avisa e atualiza. É o jeito mais simples; o caminho à mão vem a seguir. ### À mão **1. O que você precisa ter:** só a sua cópia do jogo. O update 1.04 e o firmware do PS3 são gratuitos, e o gerador baixa os dois sozinho dos servidores oficiais da Sony (o RPCS3 não é mais necessário). | O quê | Onde conseguir | |---|---| | **O jogo**: a cópia do disco do *God of War: Ascension* **BCUS98232** (EUA) | A sua cópia, numa pasta que contenha `PS3_GAME`, ou ainda compactada (`.7z`, `.zip`, `.rar` ou `.iso` decriptada): o gerador extrai uma vez (uns 35 GB livres). | | **O update 1.04** (grátis, ~235 MB) | **Baixado sozinho pelo gerador.** Se preferir baixar você mesmo: **[o update 1.04 no servidor da Sony](http://b0.ww.np.dl.playstation.net/tppkg/np/BCUS98232/BCUS98232_T76/5525fbb7b6b5456d/UP9000-BCUS98232_00-GOWABDPATCH00001-A0104-V0100-PE.pkg)** (o arquivo `.pkg`; SHA-1 do arquivo `5a94c17aa07cb5181a505d3429c88ea3d9f4e4d0`). Tem que ser a **1.04**: as versões 1.05 em diante não servem. Se você já instalou a 1.04 no RPCS3, serve também a pasta `RPCS3\dev_hdd0\game\BCUS98232`. | | **O firmware oficial do PS3** (grátis, ~200 MB) | **Baixado sozinho pelo gerador**, do servidor de atualização do PS3. Se preferir baixar você mesmo: na [página oficial da PlayStation](https://www.playstation.com/pt-br/support/hardware/ps3/system-software/), botão **"Baixar atualização do PS3"** (o arquivo `PS3UPDAT.PUP`, que o gerador aceita direto). Também serve a pasta do RPCS3 com o firmware instalado. | **2. Instale as ferramentas (uma vez só)**, num terminal: ``` winget install Python.Python.3.12 winget install Microsoft.VisualStudio.2022.BuildTools --override "--quiet --wait --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Workload.VCTools --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Llvm.Clang --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.CMake.Project --includeRecommended" ``` **3. Baixe este repositório** (botão *Code > Download ZIP*, ou `git clone`) e extraia numa pasta **sem espaços no caminho**, por exemplo `C:\gow-ascension-pc`. **4. Clique duas vezes em `gerar.cmd`** e escolha a pasta do disco. Ele faz o resto sozinho: - confere as ferramentas e baixa o FFmpeg; - baixa o update 1.04 e o firmware oficiais (ou usa os seus: `-Update` e `-Firmware`); - prepara os arquivos do jogo, sem copiar os 34 GB do disco; - decripta o executável; - traduz e compila, escolhendo a build certa para a sua CPU. Num Ryzen 7 9800X3D (8 núcleos) leva ~5 minutos; num PC de 4 núcleos, bem mais. Se parar no meio, rode de novo: ele continua de onde parou. Versão nova do port: baixe por cima e rode `gerar.cmd -RefazerDe 4` num terminal. Ele refaz só a tradução e a compilação, sem repetir o disco, o update e o firmware. **5. Jogue com `jogar.cmd`.** O log fica em `out\jogo.log` e os saves em `saves\`. Opções (defina antes de abrir o `jogar.cmd`; pelo launcher, elas ficam nas configurações do jogo): - `GOWA_FLIP_HZ`: limitador, padrão 60. Acima de 60 o jogo **acelera** (parte da lógica avança por quadro); `0` = sem limite, com teto de 240. - `GOWA_RES_SCALE`: resolução interna, 1 = 720p, 2 = 1440p, 3 = 4K. - `GOWA_VRR`: VRR (G-SYNC / FreeSync), padrão 1: cada quadro vai para a tela assim que fica pronto, sem esperar a atualização dela. Num monitor sem VRR a imagem pode rasgar em movimento; `0` volta ao vsync (cada quadro espera a tela). - `GOWA_OSD=1`: medidor de desempenho na tela (FPS, ms por quadro, uso e temperatura da CPU e da GPU, VRAM e RAM; a temperatura da CPU some quando o Windows só tem a zona térmica da ACPI, que em muitos desktops fica parada). Vem desligado; **F10** liga e desliga durante o jogo (`GOWA_OSD_TECLA=0` desativa a tecla). - **Tela cheia sem bordas:** **F11** ou **Alt+Enter** (também o botão maximizar, ou Win+Cima) cobrem o monitor mantendo 16:9, com faixas pretas em telas de outro formato; F11, Alt+Enter ou **Esc** voltam para a janela. `GOWA_TELA_CHEIA=1` já abre assim. - `GOWA_AUDIO_MUTE=1`: sem som. O jogo grava um resumo de desempenho em `desempenho.json`, ao lado do exe (ou em `GOWA_PERF_JSON`): CPU, GPU e FPS médio, p1 e mínimo do tempo jogando. Não é enviado a lugar nenhum; o launcher só manda, e só com a sua autorização. Detalhes de cada etapa, e como fazer à mão: [docs/COMO_GERAR.md](docs/COMO_GERAR.md). ### Linux / SteamOS (beta) A versão Linux roda no SteamOS (Steam Deck, Legion Go S) e em outros Linux, pelo Proton. Já foi testada de ponta a ponta num **Legion Go S** (veja o desempenho): o launcher gera e abre o jogo (versão 1.0.92 ou mais nova do Otavix Launcher). Precisa de um Proton instalado na Steam, de `curl`, `python3`, `tar` e `xz`, de um processador com AVX2 e de uns 15 GB livres. À mão: `bash scripts/linux/gerar.sh --disco ` (o update e o firmware são opcionais: `--update`, `--firmware`) e depois `bash jogar.sh`. O log fica em `out/jogo.log`. Sempre chame os dois scripts pelo `bash`. No SteamOS o launcher também cria o atalho do jogo na Steam. A geração é feita no próprio aparelho (traduz e compila o jogo uma vez, leva um bom tempo num portátil). ## Como funciona O PS3 tem um processador central (PPU, PowerPC), seis co-processadores vetoriais (SPUs) e uma GPU (RSX): - **PPU**: o executável do jogo é traduzido para C++ função por função pelo tradutor do ps3recomp, com os remendos do port aplicados por scripts. - **SPU**: os programas das SPUs (jobs do SPURS, o EDGE de geometria, as tarefas de malha, o gerenciador de políticas) também viram C. Os laços mais pesados podem virar **núcleos vetoriais** gerados por scripts (AVX-512 ou AVX2), conferidos bit a bit. O código que o jogo carrega nas SPUs em tempo de execução e que não foi traduzido roda num interpretador. - **SPURS**: a biblioteca de agendamento das SPUs (libsre) roda o código do firmware oficial (LLE). - **RSX**: os comandos da GPU são desenhados em **Direct3D 12**, com os shaders do RSX convertidos para HLSL. - **Áudio**: WASAPI, até 8 canais. Vídeos (MPEG-2) com FFmpeg. ## Estado atual - **A campanha foi jogada inteira**, do primeiro ao último capítulo, no port (08/11/2026, engine 0.11.2). Vídeos, menus e saves funcionam. - **60 FPS travados** em um Ryzen 7 9800X3D, com o limitador ligado (padrão). O desempenho depende muito da CPU (veja abaixo). - **Atualizações todos os dias**, a partir dos relatos dos jogadores. Combate pesado = checkpoint Cyn300; começo do jogo = checkpoint Stint500. Num processador antigo de verdade, com núcleos mais lentos, a queda é maior. | Máquina | Cena | Versão normal (AVX2) | Versão compatível (sem AVX2) | |---|---|---|---| | **PC 1** (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, Windows) | combate pesado | 67,7–69,3 FPS | 24,0–24,3 FPS | | **Portátil** (Legion Go S, SteamOS, 15 W) | combate pesado | ~25 FPS | 9,7 FPS | | **Portátil** (15 W) | começo do jogo | ~48 FPS | 24,6 FPS | ### Portátil (Linux): Lenovo Legion Go S Hardware: Lenovo Legion Go S (83N6), **AMD Ryzen Z1 Extreme** (8 núcleos, 16 threads), GPU integrada **Radeon 780M** (RDNA3), 32 GB de RAM de fábrica, com 8 GB reservados para a GPU (VRAM) e ~23 GB para o sistema (a VRAM reservada é configurável; ainda vamos testar com mais), SteamOS 3.10, Proton GE-Proton11-7. Port: build portátil (AVX2), 6 SPUs (padrão em aparelho com bateria), resolução interna 1280x720. Medido **sem o limitador de 60**, em 15 amostras de 5 s depois de carregar o checkpoint, com o Kratos parado na cena (não é o Cap. 16 nem a fase 1 do PC): | Cena | 15 W | 30 W | |---|---|---| | Começo do jogo | **46–49 FPS** (25 min seguidos: média 48, mínimo 42,7, sem queda) | — | | Cenas médias (Lan260, Fury300) | **~44 FPS** (mín. ~39–41) | **65–68 FPS** (mín. ~59–67; com o limitador de 60 fica travado em 60) | | Combate pesado, muitos inimigos (Cyn300) | **~24 FPS** (mín. ~23), áudio pode cortar | em medição | Nenhum travamento nem queda do jogo em cerca de 140 rodadas de teste. O combate pesado é o que estamos otimizando agora (no PC 1, essa mesma cena roda a ~48 FPS sem limitador). Os números por rodada estão em [docs/desempenho_portatil.md](docs/desempenho_portatil.md); o arquivo bruto fica no próprio aparelho de teste (`~/gowa-linux-teste/banc/resultados.txt`). > **A build que o `gerar.cmd` produz agora tem o mesmo desempenho da nossa.** Os passes de desempenho que aplicamos ao longo do desenvolvimento entram na geração (`scripts/otimizar.py`). No notebook, no cap. 16, a build gerada empatou com a nossa (antes da automação, ela dava 3,9 FPS). Depois disso, com a fixação de threads desligada em CPUs com menos de 12 processadores lógicos, ela chegou a **~8 FPS** (média de 200 s de fase, rodadas intercaladas). O PGO fica de fora; o que ainda difere está no fim de [docs/COMO_GERAR.md](docs/COMO_GERAR.md). ![Capítulo 16 no notebook com a build sem AVX-512](docs/imagens/cap16_notebook_portatil.png) O que medimos num PC fraco (4 núcleos, sem AVX-512), o que ajudou, o que não ajudou e como medir: [docs/DESEMPENHO_PC_FRACO.md](docs/DESEMPENHO_PC_FRACO.md). ## Requisitos - **Windows 10/11 64 bits** e GPU com **Direct3D 12**, ou **Linux/SteamOS** com Proton (beta, veja [acima](#linux--steamos-beta); precisa de CPU com AVX2 e uns 15 GB livres). - **CPU com AVX2** (Intel Haswell em diante, AMD Zen em diante). **Com AVX-512** (Ryzen 7000/9000, Intel 11ª geração desktop) é muito mais rápido; o `gerar.ps1` escolhe sozinho. - **Sem AVX2** (Core i de 1ª, 2ª e 3ª geração, Xeon E3/E5 v1 e v2, AMD FX, APUs A8): existe a versão **Compatível**, que o gerador escolhe sozinho. 1432723098.readme_excerpt:
# Ben 10 Omniverse PC — Linux

Recompilação nativa em desenvolvimento da versão PS3 **BLUS31017 01.00** de
Ben 10 Omniverse. O arquivo fornecido foi identificado como PS3: o runtime PS2
do God of War II não é compatível com ele. Reaproveitamos o leitor de disco e a
organização da experiência de importação desse projeto; PPU/SPU usam ps3recomp.

**Prévia nativa experimental, sem release pronto para uso.** O início da primeira
fase funciona, mas desempenho e compatibilidade da campanha ainda estão em
validação. Abrir o jogo e testar algumas ações não certifica o jogo inteiro.

Os últimos ensaios de combate ficaram aproximadamente entre 10 e 18 quadros
novos por segundo. A meta de 30 FPS não foi atingida. As experiências de
paralelismo e envio Vulkan em lotes estão preservadas, desligadas por padrão;
veja [docs/PERFORMANCE.md](docs/PERFORMANCE.md).

A execução nativa já chegou ao menu 3D, à criação/reabertura de save e à
primeira fase **Training Time**, incluindo a cena 3D e os diálogos. Uma correção
no registro RSX `WINDOW_OFFSET` recuperou a imagem que o pós-processamento
estava apagando. Os seis logos de abertura em PAM continuam omitidos;
já foram observados movimento, transformação em Four Arms, ataques e saída
de áudio pelo PulseAudio. A navegação por teclado foi exercitada pelo caminho
de eventos SDL. O launcher local já inicia o executável preparado, mas ainda
não substitui a preparação e tradução inicial do disco.
Também foram traduzidos onze módulos PPU, 24 programas SPU de mídia e oito
variantes OVIS do firmware do próprio disco. Veja
[docs/VALIDATION.md](docs/VALIDATION.md).

## Abrir no computador já preparado

```bash
scripts/install-launcher.sh
```

Abra **Ben 10 Omniverse PC (Experimental)** no menu de aplicativos. O launcher
oferece tela cheia, dois perfis, recompilação dos arquivos já traduzidos e
diagnóstico. Requer Python 3 com Tk, Docker para recompilar, sessão systemd,
X11/Xwayland, PulseAudio/PipeWire e driver Vulkan. No Fedora, o módulo Tk faz
parte de `python3-tkinter`.

O perfil equilibrado usa dois workers SPU; o de compatibilidade usa um.
Os saves desse launcher ficam em `~/.local/share/Ben10OmniversePC/user`,
separados dos testes. Fechar a janela encerra o processo do jogo. Espere a
gravação do save terminar antes de fechá-lo.

Controles: WASD move, Z/Espaço pula e confirma, C/V atacam, setas selecionam
alienígenas, Q retorna à forma humana, F combina com ataques especiais e
Enter inicia/pausa; Esc também pausa. IJKL controla o analógico direito. O backend também oferece
controles via SDL; não foi testado um controle físico nesta validação.

Após o build, as bibliotecas ausentes e o SDL2 usado na compilação são copiados
da própria imagem de ferramentas para `artifacts/native-libs`. Nenhuma biblioteca
do sistema é substituída. `artifacts/host-libraries.json` registra origem e hashes.
Para repetir somente essa etapa: `python3 tools/prepare_host_libraries.py`.

## Preparação local

O importador valida metadados, versão, limites de arquivos e o SHA-256 do
executável antes de extrair. O ZIP/ISO original permanece inalterado.

```bash
git submodule update --init --recursive
python3 tools/apply_runtime_patches.py
docker build -t ben10-omniverse-tools:local -f docker/Dockerfile .
python3 tools/import_game.py '/caminho/jogo.iso'
```

Os arquivos importados ficam em `~/.local/share/Ben10OmniversePC/game`.
O executável SELF do disco precisa ser convertido para ELF com uma ferramenta
compatível. Na validação local, RPCS3 foi usado com `--decrypt` e `--installfw`;
não usamos emulação como substituto da recompilação escolhida para este projeto.

`tools/analyze_elf.py` valida o ELF, identifica funções/imports e extrai imagens
SPU. Os resultados são separados por SHA-256. As ferramentas de ps3recomp
traduzem esses arquivos localmente; `scripts/build-native.sh` compila as fontes
geradas com Clang 18 e o backend Vulkan de Linux. O build usa duas tarefas e um
limite de 4 GiB de RAM em um contêiner sem rede.

Uma tradução local das partes identificadas pode ser reproduzida depois de
importar e descriptografar o EBOOT:

```bash
data="$HOME/.local/share/Ben10OmniversePC"
elf="$data/game/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf"
hash=3ed23bca61cc9e392582e0c2cf0f114f24ce746f5724a2ab194e5aba944f1bea
python3 tools/analyze_elf.py "$elf" --output "$data/native/analysis"
python3 third_party/ps3recomp/tools/ppu_lifter.py "$elf" \
  --functions "$data/native/analysis/$hash/functions.json" \
  --hle-stubs "$data/native/analysis/$hash/imports.json" \
  --chunk-lines 150000 --jobs 2 --output "$data/native/ppu"
python3 third_party/ps3recomp/tools/build_spu_workloads.py \
  --images "$data/native/analysis/$hash/spu" --lifted "$data/native/spu" \
  --out "$data/native/spu/spu_workloads.c" \
  --register-fn ben10_register_embedded_spu --constructor --title ben10
python3 tools/lift_jobs.py "$elf" --output "$data/native/jobs"
python3 tools/lift_overlays.py "$elf" --images "$data/native/analysis/$hash/spu" \
  --output "$data/native/overlays"
# Opcional: tradução experimental da mídia, usando o firmware 4.25 do disco.
# "decrypted" deve conter os onze .prx descriptografados listados em
# tools/lift_firmware_ppu.py; dev_flash é a árvore extraída desse firmware.
python3 tools/lift_firmware_spu.py /caminho/dev_flash/sys/external/flashATRAC.pic \
  --output "$data/native/firmware-spu"
python3 tools/lift_firmware_ppu.py /caminho/decrypted \
  --output "$data/native/firmware-ppu"
python3 tools/lift_codec_spu.py "$data/native/firmware-ppu" \
  --output "$data/native/firmware-codecs"
scripts/build-native.sh
```

`analyze_elf.py` preserva análises anteriores: se a pasta do hash já existir,
use os resultados existentes ou escolha outro destino. As fontes traduzidas,
o ELF e o executável gerado são dados locais do usuário.

`scripts/test-linux.sh` executa os testes sintéticos; o GitHub Actions faz o
mesmo sem ROM ou firmware. Isso não certifica gameplay.
`scripts/probe-native.sh 30` faz um teste nativo limitado, com saves de
diagnóstico separados. Um timeout desse teste não significa sucesso.
A mídia recompilada continua opcional e pode ser diagnosticada com:

```bash
BEN10_LLE_MEDIA=1 \
BEN10_FIRMWARE_PPU_DIR="$data/native/firmware-ppu" \
PS3_DEV_FLASH=/caminho/dev_flash \
scripts/probe-native.sh 60
```

`libsre` fornece somente os quatro exports `cellOvis`; o scheduler continua
na implementação pública corrigida. O tradutor de codecs também separa os
segmentos OVIS sobrepostos, preservando o ELF original para fingerprints e DMA.
Para regenerar apenas essas variantes a partir de um inventário já traduzido:

```bash
python3 tools/lift_spu_variants.py "$data/native/firmware-codecs"
```

O diagnóstico `BEN10_HOST_VIDEO=1`, usado junto de `BEN10_LLE_MEDIA=1`, mantém
o player SAIL recompilado e usa o `cellVdec` com FFmpeg do runtime. Requer as
bibliotecas FFmpeg com a mesma versão principal dos headers usados no build.
Nesse teste foram observados decodificação de AUs e callbacks de vídeo; a
imagem ainda não foi apresentada corretamente. Não é uma opção pronta para uso.

O build local ativa AVX2 apenas quando o processador oferece esse recurso.
As regressões verificam a aritmética vetorial contra a referência escalar;
essa verificação não é uma medição de FPS do jogo.

Em CPUs locais com AVX2 e FMA3, o script também ativa o caminho exato de
geometria delimitado à thread do job. Um replay do mesmo trabalho consumiu cerca
de 39% menos tempo, com saída idêntica; isso não equivale
a 39% mais FPS. A investigação e os limites estão em
[docs/PERFORMANCE.md](docs/PERFORMANCE.md). Para recompilar pelo caminho anterior:

```bash
BEN10_VERTEX_FMA=OFF scripts/build-native.sh
```

Nada derivado do jogo deve ser adicionado ao Git. Dados, código traduzido,
firmware, saves, logs, binários e chaves são ignorados. Consulte
[THIRD_PARTY.md](THIRD_PARTY.md) para a procedência do código aberto.

## Referência e limitações

O [port macOS do mesmo título](https://github.com/andrebrumdev/ben10-omniverse-recomp)
documenta o início do jogo e depende de um fork privado de runtime. Esta
adaptação Linux usa a base pública: é necessário implementar e testar o que
estiver faltando, incluindo integração de jobs SPU, mídia e callbacks.

O projeto GodOfWar2PC de origem permanece intacto. Nenhum arquivo do jogo ou
arte original do Ben 10 é distribuído aqui. O código novo do projeto usa
GPL-3.0, com componentes MIT identificados separadamente.

O executor Linux aceita `PS3_JOB_WORKERS=2` para executar jobs independentes
em paralelo. A fila tem limite, IDs SPU distintos e espera pelas conclusões reais
antes de comandos de controle e barreiras. O padrão continua serial enquanto
ampliamos a validação. No teste da introdução de Training Time, dois workers
atingiram aproximadamente 12 flips/s, contra 6–7 no caminho serial; essa amostra
não é uma certificação de desempenho do jogo inteiro. `PS3_JOB_WORKERS=1`
seleciona explicitamente o comportamento serial.

# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível e à primeira luta contra um chefe, mas ainda lento (~18-23 fps no nível, 13-21 na luta). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot à primeira luta contra um chefe:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~30-40 fps; o primeiro nível a ~18-23 fps, conforme a cena (era ~9); a luta contra o chefe a 13-21. O limite é o trabalho das SPUs recompilado, não a placa de vídeo. Partes pesadas já rodam como código nativo, cada uma conferida contra o original: a geometria por draw (índices, skinning, normais e tangentes) e o pós-processamento que suaviza as bordas da imagem. O próximo passo é reduzir os custos que todo trabalho das SPUs paga, para o ganho valer no jogo inteiro e o fps ficar estável. Esses números são de um Ryzen 5 5600G com uma RX 7600; num Ryzen 7 9800X3D com uma RX 9070 XT (RSX do RPCS3, Vulkan), a luta das criaturas do primeiro nível fica em ~45-57 fps. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); e o jogo às vezes trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`). - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md).

## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), abra o launcher, `launcher\AscensionLauncher.exe`:

JOGAR abre o jogo dentro da própria janela do launcher. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

1432805531.readme_excerpt: # Project 8 Plus [website](https://project8.maxleiter.com/) | [docs](https://project8.maxleiter.com/docs) Project 8 Plus is a PC port of [Tony Hawk's Project 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Hawk%27s_Project_8) (the PS3 version). This is not emulation; the P8 Plus launcher builds a PC [recomp](https://recompedia.com/) as a native Windows (or, experimentally, Linux) program. P8 Plus provides: - Support for custom soundtracks, HD textures, and updated smoothed models - A full Lua modding API and level/script editor - Uncapped FPS and ultrawide support - Keyboard and Xbox controller support (with updated in-game button/key prompts) - Bugfixes for issues encountered in the original game You provide your own copy of Project 8 and [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net/) (which is used to decrypt the ROM at setup). No original Tony Hawk's Project 8 assets or code are provided here. Project 8 Plus was made by running Opus 5.5 in a loop for a few weeks. ## Download **[Download the latest release](https://github.com/MaxLeiter/project-8-plus/releases/latest)** (`Project8Plus-0.9.0-windows-x64.zip`) You need: - Your own copy of Tony Hawk's Project 8 for PS3: the US disc (BLUS30011, version 01.02), dumped to a folder - [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net/) during setup - Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a DirectX 12 graphics card - About 4 GB of free space, and an internet connection during setup To install: 1. Unzip the download anywhere and run `THP8 Launcher.cmd`. 2. Pick your game folder and RPCS3, keep the recommended options, and press **Start building**. The build takes about 20–25 minutes and only happens once. 3. Press **Play**. **Play original** starts the unmodified game without P8 Plus additions. ## HD Textures The majority (~5000) of the game's textures and models are upscaled by an AI model on your own graphics card after install. It takes about an hour on a modern card and you can play while it runs in the background. The launcher downloads the upscaler by itself (44 MB). You can turn HD textures off in the launcher. ## Modding The launcher's **Mods** page lets you manage your mods. Mods can be written with the Lua scripting API ([docs](https://project8.maxleiter.com/docs)). Working examples are in [`mod/examples`](mod/examples). ### Level Creator https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4702b8d0-d43c-4b5c-880a-c62b6b0625f3 The desktop level editor lets you create and script levels with a visual editor. Hotloading is supported when the game is running: the game updates with each edit in real-time. ## Credits - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet, the static recompiler this project builds on - [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net/), used to decrypt your copy during setup - HD textures use the 4xTextureDAT2 model by Phhofm ([CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)) License: MIT (LICENSE). Third-party notices: NOTICE (Windows download), NOTICE_linux (Linux download), NOTICE_HD (the HD pack).

1432824064.readme_excerpt:
# Killzone 2 Blender importer

Blender 5.2 extension for independently decoded assets from the US retail
release of Killzone 2 (`BCUS98116`, app/disc version `01.01`,
`RTTIBin<1.58>`).

No game data is included. Use this extension only with data you are legally
entitled to inspect.

## Technical format documentation

Reverse-engineered notes for analysts and technical artists are available in
the [file-format documentation](docs/README.md). The notes cover PSARC, CORE,
geometry, textures, materials, levels, entities, skeletons, and animation, and
explicitly distinguish validated behavior from guesses and unknown fields.

## Current support

| Capability | Status |
|---|---|
| Extracted `.core` files | Supported |
| Static triangle meshes and normalized-position reconstruction | Supported |
| Packed vertex streams, normals, tangents, and UVs | Supported |
| Expanded rest skeletons | Supported |
| ES00 animation fallback poses and parent hierarchy | Supported |
| Compact skinned vertices and three-weight skinning | Supported |
| Packed KZ2 `EA02` rotation, translation, and scale tracks | Supported |
| Blender Actions with native clip timing | Supported for CORE and compatible cached entities |
| Retail 2D texture formats (`RGBA8`, DXT1/3/5, RGBA16F) | Supported |
| Local render-effect graphs and profile-driven preview materials | Supported |
| Named sampler nodes, source color spaces, and 64x1 ramps | Supported |
| Packed YUV lightmap reconstruction with separate sun occlusion | Supported |
| Local object references | Supported |
| PSARC catalog/extraction library | Supported in the pure-Python API |
| All 44 retail level direct serializers | Supported with exact framing |
| Recursive big-endian Lua 5.1 `GameScript` structure | Supported, never executed |
| Static map placements and parent transforms | Supported |
| Entity placeholder props and destructible model parts | Supported |
| Persistent PSARC entity catalog and sidebar import | Supported |
| Campaign/MP map hierarchy and direct PSARC level import | Supported |
| Complete-map and individual-section collections | Supported |
| Dedicated skybox geometry in level manifests | Supported |
| Cached skinned entities with armatures and weights | Supported |
| Blender-correct Z-up map orientation | Supported |
| LOD, multi-mesh, and switch wrappers | Supported |
| Per-instance lightmap textures and `LMUVShift` | Supported |
| Exact-ID external textures, buffers, effects, and shaders | Supported with a source PSARC |
| Cubemap parsing and face/mip preservation | Supported in the pure-Python API |
| Cubemap conversion to Blender environments | Not yet mapped |
| Gameplay entities, collision, particles, lights, zones, and AI records | Parsed as typed metadata; not all have Blender adapters |
| Scalar/user animation channels | Parsed and reported, not mapped |

## Install

1. Build or download `io_scene_killzone2-<version>.zip`.
2. In Blender 5.2, open **Edit > Preferences > Get Extensions**.
3. Use **Install from Disk** and select the ZIP.
4. Enable **Killzone 2 Asset Importer** if Blender does not enable it
   automatically.

To build the ZIP from this repository:

```powershell
python .\tools\build_extension.py
```

The build is written to `.\dist\io_scene_killzone2-<version>.zip`, using the
version declared in `blender_manifest.toml`.

## Import

Open **3D View > Sidebar > KZ2 Tools** for the extension's dedicated menu.
The sidebar can still launch the extracted CORE file picker. It also provides
complete level, individual section, and cached entity import directly from
`data_ps3.psarc`. Each sidebar section is collapsible.

Extracted `.core` files can also be imported by dragging them from a file
manager into the 3D Viewport or Outliner, which opens the import options as a
dialog. **File > Import > Killzone 2 CORE** accepts several files at once;
each file is imported into its own collection.

![KZ2 Tools sidebar with extracted CORE, level, and cached entity import controls](docs/images/Blender_KZ2_Menu.png)

To cache importable assets and maps:

1. Open the KZ2 Tools sidebar and choose **Settings**.
2. Select the matching authorized retail `data_ps3.psarc`.
3. Run **Scan / Rescan Assets and Maps** once.
4. Use **Import Complete Level** to choose Campaign or Multiplayer, select a
   map and section, then choose **Import Entire Map** or **Import Section**.
5. To import one entity instead, choose a category, optionally search by asset
   name or source map, select a result, and choose **Import Entity**.

The level browser contains all 10 campaign levels and all 8 retail multiplayer
maps. Campaign entries expose the exact `LevelSection` hierarchy and enabled
lumps from the optimized root manifest rather than grouping files only by path
name. Whole-map imports deduplicate COREs shared by multiple sections and put
them in a **Shared** child collection. Section-specific geometry is placed in
named child collections. The **Skybox Geometry** option is enabled by default
and includes dedicated skybox COREs such as the Corinth River/The New Sun and
The Cruiser skies.

Level imports include supported direct `StaticMeshInstance` environment
placements and mesh-backed `EntityPlaceHolder` props. Materials and textures,
entity props, skybox geometry, UV flipping, and scale can be controlled in the
sidebar. Gameplay scripts are never executed, and parsed collision, lights,
particles, zones, audio, and AI metadata do not yet all have Blender object
adapters.

![Imported Killzone 2 level geometry and props with decoded materials and textures](docs/images/Blender_KZ2_MapImport.png)

*Imported level geometry with placed props and preview materials.*

The cached-entity browser groups results into maps/environment, characters,
vehicles, weapons, props, and other assets. It displays 12 results per page
with first, previous, next, and last-page controls. Duplicate names include a
compact source map/section label so map-local variants remain distinguishable.

![Rigged Killzone 2 vehicle imported as a cached entity](docs/images/Blender_KZ2_RiggedModels.png)

*A cached rigged entity imported with its material preview.*

> [!WARNING]
> The first scan may take several minutes because the archive contains thousands
> of CORE entries. Expect it to take longer when `data_ps3.psarc` is on an
> external USB drive. Later entity selection uses the persisted cache and does
> not repeat the scan unless you explicitly rescan or the archive changes.


Complete levels can contain hundreds of megabytes of optimized CORE data and
thousands of placements, so an entire-map import can take several minutes.
Import one section first when validating settings. The importer opens the
PSARC once, reuses the persistent SQLite dependency resolver and mesh-template
caches, and imports each physical CORE only once even when multiple sections
reference it.


### Cached entity animations

When **Animations** is enabled, a cached entity import creates Actions for
EA02 clips whose `SkeletonAnimationBoneMap` exactly matches one imported
armature. Actions use the game animation-state name when available and have a
fake user so inactive clips remain in the `.blend` file.

![Playback of an imported full-body EA02 animation in Blender](docs/images/Blender_KZ2_full_body_animation.gif)

*Full-body EA02 animation played from an imported Blender Action.*

For `HGH_Dropship [45]`, the body rig imports these Actions:

- `HGH_Dropship - Hover`
- `HGH_Dropship - Neutral`
- `HGH_Dropship - Approach`
- `HGH_Dropship - Fly Away`

To view one, select the dropship armature (`Skeleton_342`), change a Dope
Sheet editor to **Action Editor**, and select the Action from its dropdown.
The importer now leaves this armature selected at frame 1. The last compatible
imported clip is active immediately after import.


## Pure-Python API

The binary readers do not import `bpy`:

```python
from io_scene_killzone2.kz2_assets import CoreDecoder, CoreFile, Psarc

archive = Psarc.open(r"E:\path\to\data_ps3.psarc")
entry = archive.get("LocalCachePS3/lumps/example.core")
core = CoreFile.from_bytes(archive.read_entry(entry), source=entry.path)
decoder = CoreDecoder(core)
```

Decoded texture payloads can also be accessed without Blender:

```python
from io_scene_killzone2.kz2_assets.model import Texture
from io_scene_killzone2.kz2_assets.textures import decode_texture_surface

for record, texture in decoder.iter_type("Texture"):
    if isinstance(texture, Texture) and texture.texture_type == 0:
        surface = decode_texture_surface(texture)
        print(record.display_id, surface.width, surface.height)
```

## Tests

Synthetic tests contain no copyrighted game payload:

```powershell
python -m unittest discover -s .\tests -v
```

Blender-side builder tests also use synthetic data. They run under Blender's
Python or the `bpy` wheel from PyPI (`pip install bpy==5.2.*`, Python 3.13)
and are skipped otherwise.

Optional private integration tests use the local archive without copying any
asset into this repository:

```powershell
$env:KZ2_PSARC = "E:\path\to\data_ps3.psarc"
python -m unittest .\tests\test_local_archive.py -v
```

### Full retail archive audit

Developers can audit every physical `.core` entry without extracting or
writing game assets:

```powershell
python .\tools\audit_retail_archive.py `
  "E:\path\to\data_ps3.psarc" `
  --output .\kz2-audit.json
```

The deterministic JSON report contains aggregate type, reference, animation,
skinning, framing, and decoder diagnostics. It includes logical asset paths
and object metadata for failures, but no serialized payloads or decoded game
assets. The command exits nonzero if a CORE cannot be framed or a registered
decoder rejects an object. Use `--structure-only` for a faster framing pass,
or omit the positional path after setting `KZ2_PSARC`.

## Known limitations

- Only the `BCUS98116 01.01` / `RTTIBin<1.58>` profile is accepted.
- All 44 confirmed retail level direct classes are framed and retained.
  Static render placements and mesh-backed entity props create visual
  Blender objects. Collision, particles, lights, portals, zones, cameras,
  scripts, and AI/navigation records remain typed metadata for later
  adapters.
- Entity/model render links and state-based destructibility model parts are
  decoded. The full selected-section dependency graph and gameplay behavior
  are not; ambiguous exact class/name resources therefore remain visible
  diagnostic empties instead of selecting an arbitrary definition.
- LOD and switch source order, keys, and distances are preserved. Blender
  initially hides non-primary variants because the exact runtime LOD
  comparison, equality behavior, distance origin, and distance unit remain
  unproven.
- Render-effect graphs are preserved, but compiled PS3 shaders are not
  generally translated into equivalent Blender shaders. Proven profiles
  select representative base color and opacity inputs, and static packed
  lightmaps are reconstructed. Profile-specific normal signs, packed
  specular channels, response-ramp coordinates, emissive effects, and IBL
  paths remain unconnected until their shader arithmetic is validated.
- Cubemap faces and mips are parsed but are not yet converted from the
  game's Y-up face basis to Blender environment images.
- Blend targets, collision shapes, render probes, and gameplay-specific
  direct records are not yet instantiated as specialized Blender data.
- Scalar/user animation channels are not yet mapped to custom properties,
  materials, or shape keys. Clips containing only those channels are skipped.
- `SkeletonAnimationBoneMap` semantics are only partially understood. The
  current importer uses the validated direct Edge joint-index order and
  requires matching metadata when reusing an existing armature.
- Additive and composite animation semantics have not been proven. Decoded
  transform clips are currently applied as absolute local transforms.
- Unknown `EA02` flags,
  [retail interstitial header variants](docs/animation.md#retail-interstitial-header-variants),
  and unsupported format revisions fail closed rather than creating
  incomplete or fabricated Actions.

1432901344.readme_excerpt:
# Killzone Mercenary Recomp

[![Windows quality gates](https://github.com/Tzeentchnet/KillzoneMercenary-Recomp/actions/workflows/windows-quality.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Tzeentchnet/KillzoneMercenary-Recomp/actions/workflows/windows-quality.yml)

An unofficial project to statically recompile the PlayStation Vita release of
*Killzone Mercenary* (PCSA00107) into a native Windows x64 executable. The
executable renders through Direct3D 12 or Vulkan and targets 30 fps or
higher.

**Goal and scope:** [docs/GOAL.md](docs/GOAL.md) ·
**Milestones:** [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md) ·
**Where we are:** [docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md](docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md) ·
**Contributor/agent rules:** [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md)

## How it works

```text
your lawful dump
  -> external Vita3K (install/decrypt, post-link ELF dump only)
  -> validated runtime-image manifest
  -> armrecomp: ARM/Thumb -> C for every game module   ("decompile")
  -> MSVC + vitarecomp runtime/HLE + this Windows host  ("recompile")
  -> native kzmrecomp_host.exe --renderer=dx12|vulkan
```

The framework is [`Tzeentchnet/vitarecomp`](https://github.com/Tzeentchnet/vitarecomp),
a fork of [`sp00nznet/vitarecomp`](https://github.com/sp00nznet/vitarecomp).
It provides the recompiler, the runtime/HLE, and the DX12/Vulkan backends.
Vita3K is used only as an external content-preparation tool and source-code
reference. Its runtime output is not a review gate, and it is not forked,
extended, linked, or shipped.

## Current status

**M0 foundation done. M1 (lift and link) and M2 (into title code) are in
progress.** The game does not boot yet.

- All three runtime images lift to C that compiles cleanly: 96.37% of
  executable bytes covered, 99.897% of emitted instructions translated,
  3,770 explicit traps left.
- The host, the content validation, and both renderer backends work, using a
  self-test scene.
- An opt-in local generated bundle (`KZMRECOMP_GENERATED_SOURCE_DIR`) builds
  into the host, which can load, bind, and enter it through one strict
  `vita_guest_call`. Public builds have no bundle and exit 9
  (`title_not_implemented`) in title mode.
- Next: the first run on a real local bundle, then fix the first strict
  failure it reports (M2).

This repository contains no game data, generated title code, firmware, keys,
or playable build.

## Getting the source

The reusable recompilation framework is pinned as the
`third_party/vitarecomp` Git submodule. Clone recursively, or initialize it
after cloning:

```powershell
git clone --recurse-submodules `
  https://github.com/Tzeentchnet/KillzoneMercenary-Recomp.git `
  KillzoneMercenary-Recomp
Set-Location KillzoneMercenary-Recomp
git submodule update --init --recursive
git submodule status
```

## Content boundary

This project does not distribute Sony Interactive Entertainment or Guerrilla
Cambridge content. Users must provide their own lawfully obtained copy of the
game and use authorized external tooling to prepare any required local data.
Retail archives, installed Vita data, decrypted modules, generated title code,
keys, licenses, saves, traces, captures, and shader caches must remain outside
Git. See [docs/CONTENT_POLICY.md](docs/CONTENT_POLICY.md).

## Configure, build, and test

Prerequisites:

- Windows x64
- CMake 3.25 or newer
- Visual Studio 2022
- PowerShell 7 or Windows PowerShell 5.1
- official Microsoft DXC `1.8.2505.32`
- Vulkan SDK headers when building the Vulkan backend

Point `VITARECOMP_DXC_ROOT` at the extracted official compiler package. Set
`VULKAN_SDK` when the Vulkan SDK is not already discoverable:

```powershell
$env:VITARECOMP_DXC_ROOT = '<dxc-package-root>'
$env:VULKAN_SDK = '<vulkan-sdk-root>'
cmake --preset windows-x64-debug
cmake --build --preset windows-x64-debug
ctest --preset windows-x64-debug
```

Equivalent `windows-x64-relwithdebinfo` and `windows-x64-release` presets are
provided. More details are in [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md), including
the exact clean-clone verification commands and public-only
[quality gates](docs/QUALITY_GATES.md).

The generated-bundle opt-in is intentionally absent from every preset. Local
users must provide both an explicit validated staging directory and its bound
raw runtime manifest; hosted CI never supplies, uploads, caches, or builds a
private bundle.

## Native host

The bounded renderer smoke path needs no private content:

```powershell
out\build\windows-x64-debug\Debug\kzmrecomp_host.exe `
  --self-test --renderer=dx12 --adapter=warp --frames=4
```

Supported options are `--content-root`, `--manifest`,
`--renderer=dx12|vulkan`, `--adapter`, `--validation`, `--log-level`,
`--self-test`, `--frames`, and `--help`. Renderer selection never falls back.
Paths and content hashes are redacted from structured logs. See
[docs/NATIVE_HOST.md](docs/NATIVE_HOST.md) for manifest rules, exit codes, and
the strict conditional title-execution boundary.

Vulkan can be selected just as explicitly:

```powershell
out\build\windows-x64-debug\Debug\kzmrecomp_host.exe `
  --self-test --renderer=vulkan --adapter=hardware `
  --validation --frames=4
```

An unavailable backend, adapter, or requested validation layer is an error.
The host never falls back from Vulkan to DX12, from hardware to WARP, or to an
emulator/JIT.

## Reference material

- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): process boundaries, pipeline, and
  the target runtime design
- [Native host](docs/NATIVE_HOST.md): options, exit codes, and the strict
  title-entry path
- [Generated-source provenance](docs/generated-source-provenance.md): how a
  local generated bundle is validated and staged
- [Research record](docs/research/README.md): curated CPU/loader findings
  and asset-format facts from earlier work
- [Generated-source staging](tools/generated/Stage-GeneratedSources.ps1)
  and its [synthetic regression](tests/Test-StageGeneratedSources.ps1)
- [Vita3K patch series](patches/vita3k/README.md): the frozen two-patch
  post-link ELF dump for an external checkout
- [Pending framework patches](patches/vitarecomp/README.md): fixes waiting
  to land in the framework fork
- Historical records: [migration manifest](MIGRATION.md) and
  [M0 verification](docs/FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION.md)

## Repository layout

- `cmake/` — project CMake modules
- `config/` — tracked configuration templates
- `docs/` — public architecture, build, and content-boundary documentation
- `patches/vita3k/` — minimal source patches for an external Vita3K workflow
- `src/game/` — title-specific bindings and compatibility code
- `src/host/` — native Windows host code
- `tests/` — public and synthetic tests only
- `tools/content/` — local content inspection and safety tools
- `tools/generated/` — generic generated-source staging tools
- `third_party/vitarecomp/` — pinned framework submodule

## Private-content guard

Before committing, stage the intended files and run:

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File tools/content/Guard-PrivateContent.ps1
```

The guard rejects known private/generated path classes. Optional private roots
can be listed in ignored `config/private-roots.txt` or in the
`KZM_RECOMP_PRIVATE_ROOTS` environment variable (semicolon-separated on
Windows). The guard complements review; it is not a legal-content detector.

## M0 evidence

Title-entry test commands and results are in
[docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md](docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md#title-entry-validation).

The accepted M0 checkpoint used framework
`f3408e1ea73b724c7ba3a644633938c220f2cc2a` and game report revision
`36fef0e94ab99d1fc6e1903f02a388013eb3585d`. The complete matrix and redacted
private acceptance are recorded in
[docs/FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION.md](docs/FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION.md).

Public hosted runs:

- framework [Windows quality gates
  40185631954](https://github.com/Tzeentchnet/vitarecomp/actions/runs/40185631954);
- game foundation [Windows quality gates
  40186098886](https://github.com/Tzeentchnet/KillzoneMercenary-Recomp/actions/runs/40186098886);
- game verification report [Windows quality gates
  40189417323](https://github.com/Tzeentchnet/KillzoneMercenary-Recomp/actions/runs/40189417323).

## License and trademarks

Project-authored files are licensed under
[GPL-2.0-or-later](LICENSE). The `third_party/vitarecomp` submodule is a
separate work and retains its own license files and notices; those notices are
not replaced by this repository's license.

*Killzone*, *Killzone Mercenary*, PlayStation, and PlayStation Vita are
trademarks of their respective owners. This project is not affiliated with or
endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Guerrilla.

0650a59088532c1a0a3469cdd8812fa457a80bf0.message:
cellGcm: _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel queues the label wait and the flip

libgcm appends NV406E SEMAPHORE_OFFSET and SEMAPHORE_ACQUIRE for the
label, then the flip, so the RSX flips only once the label holds the
value. RPCS3's _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel writes the same two
methods into the context before its flip command. The import here
ignored its context, wrote the label itself from the PPU, and flipped
at call time: whoever owns the label was overruled, and the flip
waited for nothing.

Write the two semaphore methods into the context and queue the flip
behind them with gcm_flip_into_fifo, as _cellGcmSetFlipCommand already
does. A context that is not a mapped command buffer, or has no room,
falls back to the immediate form as before.

0ba1229e2c0b4b6003604a06e80fb330dccc1083.message:
sys_ppu_thread: non-joinable threads free their slot when they end

sys_ppu_thread_create ignored its flags and made every thread joinable, so a
thread created without SYS_PPU_THREAD_CREATE_JOINABLE stayed FINISHED after
its exit and held its slot for good. Once 63 such threads had run, every
later create returned CELL_EAGAIN.

joinable is now flags & 1. A non-joinable (or detached) thread frees its
slot at the end of ppu_host_thread_proc, after closing its event and handle
(Windows) or destroying its mutex/cond (POSIX, where the host thread is
detached at creation), under the table lock. sys_ppu_thread_exit leaves the
freeing to that epilogue; the main thread is still marked FINISHED there.
The create log line shows the flags.

tests/test_ppu_thread_slots.c (tools/test_ppu_thread_slots.py): 192
non-joinable threads created and finished in turn all succeed and leave no
slot in use; 63 unjoined joinable threads still fill the table, and a join
frees a slot. Fails on master at the 64th create (0x80010001).

0bd8f34314bc6c29741548bfdd8d690ce351bc5a.message:
cellGcmSys: main-memory maps take the first free IO pages; none before Init

gcm_io_alloc was a bump pointer that survived cellGcmInit, so a title that
maps main memory before Init got its next map placed on top of Init's
command-buffer window, and the FIFO walker then read the wrong memory.

gcm_io_alloc now picks the lowest run of free 1MB pages from the IO -> EA
table (never io page 0) and returns 0xFFFFFFFF when none is free.
cellGcmMapMainMemory refuses with CELL_GCM_ERROR_NO_IO_PAGE_TABLE before
cellGcmInit and when IO space is full, and logs the io it returns. The
cellGcmAddressToOffset auto-map runs only after Init.

tests/test_gcm_io_alloc.c (tools/test_gcm_io_alloc.py): a map before Init
is refused; after Init maps land at 0x800000, 0xE00000 and 0x1000000 and the
Init window is kept; freed holes are reused; IO-full refusal.

tools/test_gcm_io_mappings.py follows the change: its harness now has the
IO page table, GCM_IO_PAGES and an initialised GCM, measures the leak on
the page table, and checks that a map before Init is refused.

0e26194770079d251b113cbc28bb41e27199ac76.message:
sys_spu: an SPU's user event finds the port the PPU binds, and waits for it

An SPU's send_event (interrupt mailbox, code 0..63) was routed only through the ports the group binds with
sys_spu_thread_group_connect_event_all_threads, and answered ENOTCONN at once when there was none. Two things go
wrong with that:

- A port bound for one SPU thread with sys_spu_thread_connect_event was never found by the delivery, only by the
  plain out-mailbox path.
- The SPU thread starts running at sys_spu_thread_group_start while the PPU is still on its way to the connect
  calls that follow it (a real SPU needs far longer to boot than a lifted one). The first request of the program
  was answered ENOTCONN and the SPU program gave up. SoulCalibur II HD's audio engine (MultiStream) binds its ports
  with sys_spu_thread_connect_event, after group_start, and failed this way.

The delivery now looks at the thread's own bindings before the group's (spu_port_queue_locked) and, when the port
is not bound yet, waits for a binding for up to 200 ms on a condition variable that both connect calls signal
before it answers ENOTCONN. An SPU whose thread does not exist is answered at once, since nothing will bind its
port. The out-mailbox path reads the bindings through the same helper under the lock.

The test calls the real handlers and spu_deliver_user_event: bound for the thread, bound for the group, bound 40 ms
late either way, never bound (answers after about 200 ms) and an SPU with no thread (answers at once). On v0.15.0
it fails six checks; with the change it passes (five runs in a row).

1148eaca60f111203aa7ff38e58a927acdcbd353.message:
video/tests: a flip queued in the command stream

libs/video/tests/test_gcm_flip_stream.c compiles cellGcmSys.c in, like
test_gcm_flip_wrap.c, and checks on a title context:

1. _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel puts SEMAPHORE_OFFSET and
   SEMAPHORE_ACQUIRE for the label, then the flip marker, into the
   context, moves current past them, and leaves the label alone.
2. A tick before the drain is a vblank, not a flip.
3. Once the drain has executed up to the marker, the next tick
   completes the flip.
4. A flip written but not flushed does not complete; an executed one
   does, even with a newer flip written behind it and not flushed.
5. A flip the walker abandons when it resyncs out of unmapped IO does
   not hold back the flip status.

On master 8 of the 14 checks fail. tools/test_gcm_flip_stream.py builds
and runs it, so the existing tools/test_*.py sweep in CI covers it.

122690f29d9d566a679fce9944c4718a674ed79b.message:
fp decompiler: biased unsigned remap and _bx2 fetches return signed values

Two ways a fetch comes back re-centred to -1..1 were ignored, so the
shader saw 0..1 encodings:

- SET_TEXTURE_ADDRESS bit 12, UNSIGNED_REMAP_BIASED, applies to every
  fetch from the unit: (round(x*255)-128)/127 on the lanes the crossbar
  fills from a source channel (16-bit X16/Y16_X16 channels: /32767),
  after gamma and not on gamma lanes, and not on lanes the filter flags
  signed. rsx_texture_expand_mask computes the lanes, for the formats
  RPCS3 gives RSX_FORMAT_FEATURE_BIASED_NORMALIZATION.
- EXP_TEX (OPDEST bit 21, the _bx2 modifier) belongs to the instruction,
  not the texture: x*2-1 on every lane of any unit, bypassing gamma
  (RPCS3 _process_texel). It applies from every entry point.

inFAMOUS 2 reads its normals G-buffer through a biased unit and its
tangent-space normal maps and occlusion-cone lookup tables with TEX_bx2
(about a quarter of its fragment programs). Read unexpanded, every
normal leaned towards (1,1,1), normal maps had no effect, and the
occlusion volumes round props drew as dark boxes.

The engine passes the expand masks of the units a program samples
through a new entry point, rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_expand_ex,
and hashes them into the pipeline key. A program with neither feature
is byte-identical.

156c591084b9e2a75c1074273cf8d0b03ce98ac7.message:
d3d12: key the per-draw vertex program cache on the program, not on the store behind it

vp_get_vs hashed the microcode from SET_TRANSFORM_PROGRAM_START to the end of everything uploaded. A title that
keeps several programs resident and uploads another one behind the program it draws with changes that hash on
every upload, so nearly every draw missed the cache and ran D3DCompile on the FIFO thread. SoulCalibur II HD on
Windows stalled after its opening movie that way, and its audio, fed from the same frame loop, starved.

The hash now ends at the program's end bit (rsx_vp_program_size_instrs, which the Metal backend and the draw engine
already use), and the decompiler is given that length. The cache holds 128 programs instead of 16: a fight in that
title draws with more than 16, and an eviction shifts the slots the recorded draws point at.

Not built with MSVC and not run on a D3D12 device from this branch: checked with a mingw -fsyntax-only (no new
diagnostics). The stall went away on Windows with this change carried as a patch on v0.14.0 (the toolkit this port was
started on); there is no benchmark of this change alone.

17bf55aa590b12b5e2c37c6885718526f8b59804.message:
cellGcm: NV3089 source origin is 12.4, the copy counted it 256 times too small

IMAGE_IN_POINT is 12.4 fixed point per axis, and DS_DX / DT_DY step the source with 20 fractional bits (1.0 =
0x100000). nv3089_blit's copy loops added the origin to that position as origin << 8, so a source offset counted
1/256 of what it is: for any origin under 256 texels the loops started at column 0 and row 0. The GPU paths in the
same function (rsx_live_draw_blit, rsx_live_draw_resolve_blit) already took origin >> 4, so the two disagreed, and
nv3089_engine_read, which writes the source rectangle back from the draw engine before the copy, took it as origin >> 4
for its start and << 8 for its end.

A title that resolves a supersampled scene in 512x512 tiles with a one texel origin (in_uv 0x00100010, SoulCalibur II HD,
six 2:1 blits) got the first row and column of every tile black: the loops read column 0 and row 0, which the engine
write-back (starting at 1) had not covered.

The origin now enters every computation as origin << 16 (nv3089_origin), in the engine write-back and in both copy
loops (linear and the NV309E swizzled one), so the loops read from the texel the origin names and the write-back covers
exactly what they read. Also reported by undecuple on the first version of this change, which made the write-back follow
the wrong loop.

The test plays the engine (guest_read stores, into the rectangle it is given, a pixel that names its own source position)
and checks that destination pixel (x, y) is the source pixel at (origin + x * scale, origin + y * scale), for origins of
0, 1, 3 and 20 texels at 1:1, 2:1 and 4:1; five of the six cases fail on v0.15.0.

1e6f4c8e744a66f6f5163f6f8def38470742e50b.message:
vulkan: colour feedback snapshots for draws that sample their own target

A draw that samples the colour target it is writing gets, on Metal, a
copy of that target taken just before it (rsx_draw_backend.color_snapshot).
In-place deferred lighting works this way: read the albedo, write the lit
colour over it. The Vulkan backend had no such hook, so the engine fell
back to the guest-memory bytes at the target's address, which hold
whatever was last stored there.

On Twisted Metal (BCES01010) the G-buffer's first target (0x00AB0000) is
also the UI target. Its lighting passes therefore read the previous
frame's menu instead of the albedo just drawn, lit it, and composited it
into the next frame. That is the red frame, the red and green splatter
and the white logo on its main menu.

vk_eng_color_snapshot copies the target into a new image of the same
format and size, and ends with a barrier so the copy is visible to the
next draw. Every operation here is already one synchronous submission,
so the copy is in command order. The copy is a COLOR object marked
`snapshot`, so the engine can take a crossbar view of it; it is never an
attachment, so releasing it drops no framebuffer. A lit frame asks for
one copy per light, so released copies return their images to a pool of
eight, drained at engine shutdown.

32a85600293ba2cf2a21bcb1150bcc0dbd6fb63a.message:
vulkan: present on its own command buffer, in two halves a host can split

The FIFO walker and the present shared one command buffer and one
fence, and a present waited for two GPU round trips: the engine's blit
of the flipped surface into the offscreen target, then the copy of that
target into the readback buffer. A host that presents on the walker's
thread holds the walker for all of that, about 1.3 ms per frame headless.
One that moves the present to a thread of its own still had to hold its
walker lock for the whole present, since both recorded into s_vk.cmd.

On Twisted Metal (BCES01010) that is the window in which the title
moves put to its other ring segment and starts writing its next frame
over the one it left, JUMP out of it included. The walker resumes 2.4 ms
later and executes the new frame's data as commands.

The present now has its own command pool, command buffer and fences,
and comes in two halves:

- rsx_vulkan_backend_present_begin() records the blit and the copy out
  and submits them without waiting. It reads the flipped surface, so it
  runs under the host's walker lock, but only for the recording.
- rsx_vulkan_backend_present_finish() waits for that copy, reads the
  centre pixel and the dump back, and blits into the window. It may run
  while the walker drains the next frame.

rsx_vulkan_backend_present() is both, so existing hosts see no
difference. The fixed-function path, which draws into the offscreen
target itself, still finishes inside present_begin.

What keeps the two halves apart:
- vkQueueSubmit, vkQueuePresentKHR and vkDeviceWaitIdle go through
  queue_mu, since the queue is now used from two threads.
- The walker's next command buffer starts with a full barrier after a
  present's copy. Its per-image barriers already order most work after
  earlier submissions; this one covers the rest.
- No image is destroyed while a present's copy may still read it.
- present_mu keeps a flip in the command stream (presented on the
  walker's thread) from overlapping a host thread's finish.

spu_dma: the identical-transfer halt also needs wall time

mfc_submit halts an SPU after SPU_DMA_REPEAT_LIMIT (256) identical
transfers in a row, on the reasoning that a job doing nothing but the same
DMA is wedged. A job that polls a value another agent writes does the same:
God of War: Ascension's EDGE geometry jobs wait for ring space by re-reading
an RSX label until the GPU catches up. 256 reads take well under a
millisecond, so the guard halted healthy jobs and the frame never completed.

Halt only when the repeats have also lasted SPU_DMA_REPEAT_SECS (default
30 s) of wall time. A truly wedged job is still caught, 30 s later.

3ca13f66211402f8d9b2e62a1ad9d6a92334f04e.message:
fix(template): mmap the guest arena on POSIX so vm_commit can mprotect it

The POSIX branch of alloc_guest_vm() allocated the 0xE0000000-byte flat
arena with calloc. glibc serves an allocation that size from its own mmap
chunk and returns a pointer 16 bytes past the page start, so vm_base was
never page-aligned. vm_commit() hands vm_base + addr to mprotect, which
rejects unaligned addresses with EINVAL; every commit failed, and
sys_memory_allocate answered CELL_ENOMEM to every call. A title that
retries the allocation spins forever (Warhawk: 19.7 M calls in 60 s).

Map the arena with mmap(MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS|MAP_NORESERVE) instead,
as runtime/memory/vm.h already does: page-aligned, zero-filled, lazily
backed. ppu_vm_size and the Windows VirtualAlloc path are unchanged.
macOS was unaffected only because libmalloc page-aligns large blocks.

Verified: Warhawk NPEA00017 boots headless on Linux to its intro movie;
check_ppu_scaffold.py reports no regression.

3d5d03bdc7f627a424fb53ce42175984d596a377.message:
runtime: classify syscall 14 by guest address segment

sys_process_is_spu_lock_line_reservation_address answered EINVAL for
every address above the 256 MB VM_MAIN window (0x00010000..0x1000FFFF),
including the rest of segment 0x1 that the same guest allocator hands
out. SPURS validates its management areas through this syscall during
cellSpursInitialize and aborts init on failure, so a legitimate
management area produced a spurious CELL_SPURS_CORE_ERROR_PERM and every
SPU job the instance would have run stayed unstarted.

The contract is RPCS3's process_is_spu_lock_line_reservation_address
(Emu/Cell/lv2/sys_process.cpp): classify by the address segment
(0x0/0x1/0x2/0xC/0xE reservation-capable; 0xF refuses RawSPU; 0xD
refuses; sys_vm mappings refuse, holes in the mapped region EINVAL; rest
EINVAL) with the flags masked to the two SPU bits. The old sys_vm EPERM
check is kept, now through the tracked mappings (g_sys_vm_maps): a
covered address answers EPERM, a hole in the mapped region EINVAL,
matching RPCS3's default branch.

The classification moves to runtime/syscalls/lv2_lock_line.c so
tests/syscalls can unit-test it without linking the syscall layer.

Test: tests/syscalls/test_lock_line (27 checks: segments 0x0/0x1/0x2/
0xC/0xE OK, 0xF EPERM with RawSPU, 0xD EPERM, sys_vm covered/hole/empty,
flag validation).

45baa4791a794597cfaa0d0d4879347cb637b581.message:
rsx engine: 2D transfers read FP16 colour targets

A transfer out of a render target first writes the GPU's pixels back to
guest memory (rsx_draw_engine_guest_read), but only A8R8G8B8 surfaces were
looked up. Twisted Metal renders its bloom and Sweet Tooth's flaming hair
into an FP16 RGBA target and copies that out with NV3089 for its SPU
post-FX; the copy found no surface, the SPUs got stale memory, and neither
the bloom nor the flames reached the image.

The lookup now takes FP16 RGBA targets too. A transfer counts 32-bit
pixels, so the readback covers every surface pixel the transfer's bytes
touch and stores exactly those bytes, as big-endian R,G,B,A halves: the
layout rsx_texture_decode reads W16_Z16_Y16_X16_FLOAT from. A transfer
INTO an FP16 target is still not pushed: color_target_write takes

4f223b376f890582608dcd00a3ae2b3ab9e7b483.message:
cellAudio: let WASAPI shared mode convert the 48 kHz stereo float stream

The Windows backend opens the default render endpoint in shared mode with
a fixed 48 kHz, 2-channel IEEE-float format. Shared mode only accepts the
device's own mix format unless the stream asks the audio engine to
convert, so on any output not running exactly that format (44.1 kHz, 5.1,
24-bit PCM mix) IAudioClient::Initialize fails with
AUDCLNT_E_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT (0x88890008), the backend gives up and every
title runs silent.

Pass AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_AUTOCONVERTPCM | AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_SRC_DEFAULT_QUALITY
on both Initialize attempts (event-driven and polled). The flags are
defined locally when the SDK headers predate them.

517fc717f73030d62dbaa9a991c118c6bd3cd6a2.message:
spu: the single-precision fast path four lanes at a time with AVX2

On x86, spu_fa/fs/fm/fma/fms/fnms took the per-lane path: each lane
widened to double on its own, and a call per instruction. arm64 has had
a NEON path doing the four lanes at once. This is the same path for
x86 with AVX2: the lanes widened to one f64x4 (exact), the operation,
the 29 low significand bits cleared, narrowed (exact). The lane rules are
the NEON ones: an ordinary single or a true +-0 keeps the vector result,
a zero result loses its sign, fa/fs also needs the exponents within 29,
and fma keeps a lane only when TwoSum says the add did not round onto a
24-bit boundary. Other lanes are redone one by one by the exact path.

test_spu_float_neon compares the vector path with the exact references
bit for bit; it now runs on x86 with AVX2 too, and in the Linux CI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

57570462551fcc9c6f2391276953b1a5c91c48f1.message:
cellFiber: the SDK's scheduler API in place of the made-up one

libs/spurs/cellFiber.{c,h} exposed cellFiberPpuInitialize/Finalize, a CellFiber handle, a
four-argument cellFiberPpuCreateFiber(fiber, entry, arg, attr), SwitchFiber, Sleep/Wakeup and
error codes from 0x80410801. None of that is the SDK's. The HLE binds by name, so a title
importing the real cellFiberPpuCreateFiber landed in the four-argument function and read its
eight arguments from the wrong registers.

The SDK's PPU fibers are scheduler based, and this implements them:

- _cellFiberPpuInitialize, _cellFiberPpuSchedulerAttributeInitialize and
  _cellFiberPpuAttributeInitialize (attributes are zeroed, 256 bytes each);
- cellFiberPpuInitializeScheduler / FinalizeScheduler, and
  cellFiberPpuCreateFiber(scheduler, fiber, entry, arg, priority, eaStack, sizeStack, attr);
- cellFiberPpuRunFibers: runs the fibers on the calling thread until every one has ended, lowest
  priority number first, creation order among equals. A scheduler whose fibers wait for a signal
  from another thread waits for it instead of returning;
- WaitSignal / SendSignal (a signal sent early is kept), JoinFiber (from a fiber, which hands
  control back to the scheduler meanwhile, or from any thread, with the exit status), Yield,
  Exit and Self.

Each fiber runs the guest entry through the PPU thread trampoline on its own host stack (ucontext,
Windows fibers on Windows) with its own ppu_context; r1 is inside the guest stack the caller
passed, r3 the argument, and the entry's return value the exit status. The error codes are the
SDK's 0x8076xxxx, and the structures have the SDK's sizes and 128-byte alignment (scheduler 512,
fiber 896, both attributes 256).

Not implemented: the contents of the attributes, and the cellFiberPpuUtil* worker control. Yield,
Exit and Self follow the documented behaviour and are covered by the unit test only; the port that
this was written for does not call them.

tests/fiber_switch is rewritten for the new API: run order and arguments, guest stack point

584181aba7a5fe736123213cefc269ea9a630e5c.message:
metal engine: each MRT target takes its own colour mask and blend enable

Every attachment of an MRT set took target A's COLOR_MASK and
BLEND_ENABLE. On the RSX, targets B..D have their own: a nibble each of
COLOR_MASK_MRT (0x0370, A,R,G,B at bits 0..3 of the nibble) and a bit
each of BLEND_ENABLE_MRT (0x036C), as RPCS3 reads them
(color_mask_*(index), blend_enabled_surface_*).

Giving every target A's state was wrong both ways. inFAMOUS 2's light
volumes add into target A with B and C masked off, and the shared state
added every light into the G-buffer: lit props blew out to white, with a
bright rectangle round each light. Its material passes write B and C's
alpha with A's alpha masked, which left them stale.

The engine decodes both registers into the render state (and the
pipeline key), and the Metal backend applies them per attachment.
PS3RECOMP_METAL_MRT_MASK=0 restores the old behaviour for bisecting.

rsx engine: fragment-program debug knobs keyed by structural hash

changes from run to run with the order programs are first drawn in. A

- RSX_FP_DEBUG=<hex>:<n>:<reg[.swz]> makes that program export register

rather than raced for. A peer SPU has the bitset line reserved, the main
thread holds the lock, a second thread starts the host operation and is
held at the lock, an SPU commit sets another task's bit under the lock,
and only then is the host operation let through.

- spu_taskset_signal_task(task 4) against a commit of task 3's bit:
  both bits must be set.
- spu_taskset_wait_signal(task 3) consuming its signal against a commit
  of task 4's bit: task 4's bit must survive.

On master both fail (0x08000000 for 0x18000000, 0 for 0x08000000),
the same lost bits as Twisted Metal's post-FX barrier. Run in the Linux
and macOS workflows next to the SPURS task wake test.

cellPad: the small motor rumbles at full strength, and a rumble lasts until it changes

rumble stopped almost at once (inFAMOUS 2 only calls when the value
changes).

request per port is kept, sent with a 1 s duration and renewed from the

title wants and still stops within a second if the title stops polling.

6752b12939e5c6a34be15c85b9d1e813e19360ab.message:
cellGcm: bounded semaphore acquire; the stuck-get watchdog leaves waits alone

GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1 makes NV406E ACQUIRE block the drain, as the hardware
does, but the stuck-get watchdog counts drain passes, not time: a drain
that stops on an acquire, or on a self-JUMP park, stops every pass at the
same get, so after eight passes (a few milliseconds) it resynced to put
and dropped everything in between. For a park that happens before the
title has patched it into a JUMP to the commands it just wrote at the
ring start, i.e. before GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS has had a chance to run out.
inFAMOUS 2 stopped presenting for good that way in about one run in five
("stuck-get" at a self-jump with no "jump-park" before it).

A pass that stops on an acquire or a park now resets the watchdog; each
of those waits has its own bound. The acquire gets one:
GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS=<ms> consumes an acquire that has waited that long on
the same label and value, and says so, so a label nobody ever writes
cannot wedge the drain. inFAMOUS 2 acquires a label its SPU lighting job
writes every frame; with GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1 GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS=200 its
lit props stop flashing white and its characters stop rendering black.

rsx engine: convert a transfer's rows a pixel at a time, not a byte at a time

rsx_draw_engine_guest_read and _guest_wrote move a 2D transfer's pixels
between the backend's R,G,B,A and the guest's A8R8G8B8. Both copied a
byte at a time, testing TEX_RGBA for every pixel, and at the -O2 the
runtime builds with GCC vectorises neither.

On Twisted Metal (BCES01010), once #334 removed the NV3089 per-pixel
copy, the two loops were about a quarter of the FIFO thread's CPU time
during boot (in-process sampling of that thread: 19.5% guest_read,
9.0% guest_wrote).

Each pixel is now one 32-bit load, one rotate and one store
(eng_row_convert), and the TEX_RGBA case is a memcpy per row. A
1280x720 frame converts in 0.55 ms instead of 0.98 ms with the
runtime's flags (GCC 16, -O2 -msse4.1), with identical output. In the
same Twisted Metal window the two functions drop to 14.2% and 6.9%.

7208d22b25b342696685640d1a715278e17e74f9.message:
cellFs: an AIO read keeps the fd's position and cannot interleave

cellFsAioRead did a bare seek + fread on the fd's shared FILE*. Its own
comment says AIO reads are absolute and leave the fd's position alone; they
moved it, so the next cellFsRead continued from wherever the AIO stopped.
And titles issue AIO reads from several threads at once (FIOS media threads,
audio streamers) on the same fd, so another thread's seek could land between
the seek and the read.

Hold the stream lock (flockfile / _lock_file, the lock stdio's own calls
take) across the seek, the read and the seek back to the saved position.
The request id counter is atomic for the same reason.

tools/test_ppu_fs_aio.py builds runtime/ppu/tests/test_fs_aio.cpp: on
master the cellFsRead after an AIO read gets the wrong bytes, and 3373 of
8000 AIO reads racing from four threads return someone else's data; with
this change both pass.
