d0d67442f549faf07f8547adcb4fdc6e6dc74c08.message:
spu_channels: MFC engine table 8 -> 64 slots, and a full table is reported as an error

Symptom: intermittent stops where an SPU context waits forever on a DMA
tag that already completed. Killzone 3 holds eleven SPU contexts with an
MFC engine at once (policy-module contexts that keep their engine for as
long as their workload exists, plus SPU thread groups); the runtime prints
"more than 8 contexts hold an MFC engine at once; the rest share one".

Cause: the per-context engine table has SPU_MAX_CONTEXTS = 8 slots. Every
context past the eighth gets one shared fallback engine, where one
context's completion clears the tag bits another context is waiting on.
Eight is a thread group's worth, but a title can hold more contexts at
once than the machine has SPUs. The overflow was reported once, as a note.

Change: 64 slots (overridable with -DSPU_MAX_CONTEXTS). When the table is
still full, the shared engine stays as the last resort, but the runtime now
reports it as an error naming the table size, the context and the
consequence, at the first overflow lookup and again at 1000 and 1000000 so
it stays visible in a long log; s_mfc_overflow_lookups counts them. A
growable table can replace this later.

Verification: runtime/spu/tests/test_spu_mfc_slots.c (built as in the CI
workflows) keeps its 8-thread claim race over 32 rounds and adds: eleven
contexts held at once get eleven distinct engines and keep the state each
wrote; the table holds SPU_MAX_CONTEXTS contexts with no overflow; the next
context gets the overflow engine and the overflow is counted. With this
change 889 checks pass with gcc and clang, and the error line is printed
once. Against v0.14.0's spu_channels.c (a2c2010; the counter compiled as a
constant 0) 3 checks fail: the eleven contexts share engines, their state
is overwritten, and the overflow is not counted.

d161acb8d5c9911c40d2453c006b56e0909094e0.message:
sys_fs: a title's own path hook, ps3_vfs_title_hook

A port that serves some of the title's files from elsewhere -- a mod's
files beside the player's own, files chosen by what the title is doing --
sets ps3_vfs_title_hook, and every host path the three translators settle
on passes through it. It is asked before the PS3_GAME fallback, which would
reshape the path of a file only the hook has, and again after it, for the
shape the fallback settled on; a path it rewrote is one it leaves alone.

sys_fs's /dev_hdd0 branch resolves a path in place only when the file is
there, else it falls to the USRDIR flattening; it now asks the hook before
it looks, so a file the hook serves under /dev_hdd0 is found where the
title asked for it. (Drakengard 3 serves the DLC chapters' Japanese movies
this way, which its Bink player opens through raw sys_fs.)

d168a5412110cf959786a00f50c91f133683ae30.message:
rsx engine: decode an index run per width, reuse a repeated pipeline key

After NoahBPeterson's fork of ps3recomp (2b0def4dba), adapted:
- A draw's index run is decoded by a loop of its own per index width and
  restart mode into room reserved once, where each index was assembled a
  byte at a time with the width tested per index, and pushed one by one.
  Restart indices still become cuts at the reference position they fall
  on. (On a vertex cache miss; RSX_ENGINE_SLOW=1 decodes as before.)
- The pipeline key is reused while every input of it repeats the last
  draw's -- the programs' keys, the masks and their per-unit arrays, the
  layout, the target format and count, and the render state byte for byte
  (it is zeroed before it is decoded) -- instead of hashed again a byte at
  a time.
The replay regression is byte-identical; rsx_replay --bench -0.4 to -1.8%
of the engine's CPU per present on the captures.

d2c054aa7d5b8eaf0b56eb8c90d1cb911b3d733b.message:
ppu_lifter: registers written back where they changed and are read, runs under one page test, SSE AltiVec

--nonvolatile-locals kept a function's registers in C locals and wrote
all of them back to the context before every call and return: 10.1
million stores at the 450,000 transfers of Drakengard 3's executable,
most of them of a value the context already held or nobody would read.
tools/ppu_nv_dirty.py (new; its module comment has the reasoning)
rewrites each lifted body instead:

- a forward dataflow knows which locals have been assigned since the
  context last agreed with them, and only those are stored;
- of the scratch registers (r0, r3-r12, f0-f13, v0-v19, CTR, the
  volatile CR fields, the carry) only those something reads before
  writing: each function is summarised, the summaries are solved over
  the call graph, and code outside the lift is held to the ABI. 3.7
  million stores are left;
- every CR field a function uses, and XER's carry, is a local of its
  own, with mfcr/mtcrf and the CR save slot followed;
- the saves of a prologue share one page test (30,161 functions), and
  so does any run of four or more loads and stores at constant offsets
  from one unchanged register with no label or call between them
  (686,658 accesses in 87,593 runs);
- the base of guest memory is a local, and the trampoline drain after a
  call is left out where the callee cannot have set the trampoline.

The AltiVec operations a compiler made scalar loops of are one helper
each in the source preamble, SSE on x86-64 and a portable form
elsewhere: lvlx/lvrx (a loop over sixteen bytes with a test in it came
to 190 instructions and a dozen branches a site, and the title has
11,800), lvsl/lvsr, vmaxfp/vminfp (four signbit calls a site with
MSVC's library), vctsxs/vctuxs, and the bitwise ones, whose destination
no longer reads as an operand. The dot compares take CR6 from the mask.
The float helpers' NaN rules stay a function instead of being inlined
at every operation (a float-heavy function's object: 318 KB -> 244 KB).
lmw/

ppu_lifter: VSCR[NJ] a constant in a binary with no mtvscr

The VMX float helpers read VSCR for its NJ bit (flush denormals) on

d9870123ea646d8a9a4ad4cd56342d5bd7c57546.message:
spu_channels: SMC micro-interpreter addresses lqa/stqa at I16 << 2

Symptom: a self-modifying SPU stub that saves and restores registers with
stqa/lqa (a job manager's interrupt save/restore stub, written into the
local store at runtime) stores every register at the wrong address and
overwrites unrelated local-store bytes, including the job's stack.

Cause: spu_smc_microstep computed the absolute local-store address of
lqa/stqa as I16 << 4. For the RI16 form the address is I16 << 2 (SPU ISA),
which is what spu_interp.c and the lifter already use, so every access went
4x too high and wrapped around the local store.

Change: use I16 << 2 in the micro-interpreter, masked to a quadword as
before.

Verification: tools/test_spu_smc_lqa_stqa.py builds the real
spu_smc_microstep with the SPU headers into a host program, writes a stub of
76 stqa (r0..r75 to 0x3F9C0..), a bi, 76 lqa back and a second bi into the
local store, and runs both halves through the micro-interpreter. With this
change all 76 registers land in their own slot, all 76 are restored, and no
local-store byte outside the save area changes. On v0.14.0 (a2c2010) no
register lands in its slot and 1198 bytes outside the save area change.

bump moves a menu cursor a step, and the run that was to load a save

df3a7cbae234fb6701b6e1d1df2d3417b9e03a2a.message:
ppu_lifter: --chunks N cuts the source by guest address and rewrites only changed files

Symptom: any change to the lifter's input or to the lifter (a fix for one
opcode, one function's bounds) makes the build recompile nearly all of the
lifted source. For Killzone 3 (eight 600k-line chunks, 6.5-8 minutes and
2.5-4.4 GB of compiler memory each) that is 15-25 minutes per rebuild.

Cause: (1) chunks are cut every --chunk-lines emitted lines, so a change in
one function's line count moves every later cut point and changes the text of
every later chunk; (2) main() deletes the previous chunk set before writing,
so every file gets a new mtime even when its content is the same, and make or
ninja rebuild it.

Change:
- --chunks N (default 0 = off) cuts the source into N files by guest code
  bytes: chunk k holds the functions, in address order, of the range that
  carries the k-th N-th of the lifted bytes. That is a function of the
  function list alone, so the same functions always land in the same file. The
  function table goes to its own <source>_table.cpp, so a new function does
  not change the last chunk. A chunk over --chunk-lines lines prints a warning
  (MSVC's 16M-line limit).
- Every output file (header, chunks, table, the --single-file source) is
  written through write_if_changed: a temporary file and a rename, and only
  when the content differs, so unchanged files keep their mtime.
- Stale files of an earlier run (other cut points, the single-file source)

e99cbbf0a9c93d99b9ba43fbd142365f4403ba13.message:
fp decompiler: predicated writes are a select, not a lerp

Symptom: a fragment-program instruction executed under a condition code
(exec_if lt/eq/gt) changes components of its destination that the condition
leaves alone when either operand holds Inf, NaN or raw bits. Programs that
keep packed words in a register (the PK*/UP* pack/unpack pattern) read 0 or
NaN after a predicated MOV.

Cause: the predicated destination write was emitted as
lerp(dst, v, mask). lerp is arithmetic (dst + mask * (v - dst)): an Inf or NaN
in the unselected operand gives NaN (0 * Inf), and denormal and NaN bit
patterns are not preserved through the ALU.

Change: emit a per-component select, (mask != 0.0) ? v : dst, which FXC
compiles to movc. The unconditional path is unchanged.

Verification: libs/video/tests/test_fp_decompiler.c gains a case with a MOV
predicated on CC0 > 0 that checks the select form and that no lerp is
emitted. It fails on master (39 passed, 2 failed) and passes with this change
(41 passed, 0 failed). The same select has been in use in a D3D12 title port
under Proton; there a test with predicated writes over raw-bit and Inf/NaN
operands read 8 of 8 values back correctly, 4 of 8 with lerp.

sys_time: the wall clock on Windows is the wall clock; sys_time_get_timezone

A title's C library makes the date it shows, and stamps its saves with,
from two system calls. Both were wrong:

sys_time_get_current_time (145), Windows: answered the performance
counter divided into seconds, which is the time since the PC was
started, as the time since 1970. A machine up for four days told the
title it was the 5th of January 1970. It is now the host's wall clock,
read once and carried on by the guest's ticks, so it stands still while
the title is paused like the guest's other clocks. POSIX already used
the host's.

sys_time_get_timezone (144), every platform: was not there. The
dispatcher answered CELL_OK and wrote nothing, and the library went on
with whatever its two variables held. It now gives the host's zone:
minutes east of UTC without summer time, and the summer time in force
(0 or 60).

Drakengard 3 stamped a save of October 2026 as December 1933 with both
wrong, and as the 5th of January 1970 once the zone was right and the
clock still was not. With both, PS3_TIME_LOG=1 (new: the first answer of
each call) shows the title told 2026-10-11 23:34:52 UTC, zone 0, summer
time 60, on a machine set to British time.

The comments about these numbers colliding with the event flag calls
are gone: they do not (event flags are 82 to 87 and 118, 132, 139).

efef265f81209865b56cd7d9eee577577a2cd2b2.message:
cellHttp: response getters under their SDK names; RecvResponse into guest memory

Symptom: a title that reads an HTTP answer through
cellHttpResponseGetStatusCode, cellHttpResponseGetContentLength and
cellHttpResponseGetAllHeaders gets CELL_OK with the status unset and a NULL
header array, and drops every response. A body that outgrows the header read
is recv()'d into the host address equal to the guest buffer's EA (recv fails
with EFAULT, or writes into host memory).

Cause: the runtime has cellHttpGetStatusCode and
cellHttpGetResponseContentLength, whose computed NIDs match no firmware
import, and no cellHttpResponseGetAllHeaders, so the three imports take the
unresolved-NID path. In cellHttpRecvResponse the overflow copy translates
the guest buffer but the socket read does not.

Change: add cellHttpResponseGetStatusCode, cellHttpResponseGetContentLength
(0x80710017 when the response has no Content-Length) and
cellHttpResponseGetAllHeaders ({name, value} guest pointers followed by the
strings in the caller's pool; a size query with no pool writes only
*required; a pool too small returns NO_BUFFER). Titles call them before the
first cellHttpRecvResponse, so they read the headers first. The older
functions keep their names. cellHttpRecvResponse recv()s into the
translated guest buffer.

Verification: tools/test_http_response_getters.py builds
libs/network/tests/test_http_response_getters.c against a loopback
listener: a 200 answer with three headers and a 3000-byte body of which
only 100 bytes arrive with the headers, then a response without
Content-Length. On master: 4 failed (the three getters missing; the body
stops at 100 bytes, recv() error); with this change all 13 checks pass.

f110c349c230521f60cb5f27f7449fd90144e779.message:
cellSaveData: UserAutoSave keeps its ninth argument; handlers registered at init

Symptom: a title that saves with cellSaveDataUserAutoSave gets
cbResult->userdata == 0 in its stat and file callbacks. A title that keeps
its save state behind userdata writes through a null pointer and saves an
empty profile.

Cause: cellSaveDataUserAutoSave takes nine arguments; the ninth (userdata)
is in the caller's parameter save area at SP+112. UserAutoLoad already has
a context handler that reads it, UserAutoSave has none, and nothing in the
runtime calls cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers(), so both calls go through
the generic eight-argument binding unless a project registers the handlers
itself.

Change: a context handler for cellSaveDataUserAutoSave (NID 0x52AAC4FA),
the same as UserAutoLoad's, registered in
cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers(). It calls cellSaveDataAutoSave rather
than AutoSave2: AutoSave2 maps dirName to a host pointer and hands it to
AutoSave, which maps it again, so a host address below 4 GiB (seen on
Windows) would be read as a guest address. ppu_sysprx_register() now calls
cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers() next to np_score_register_ctx(), so
every project gets both handlers. A project that already calls it keeps
working: the first registration of a NID wins and both point at the same
handler.

Verification: tools/test_savedata_user_autosave.py checks that
ppu_sysprx_register() calls cellSaveData_register_ctx_handlers(), then
builds libs/system/tests/test_savedata_user_autosave.c, which registers the
handlers into a local table and calls UserAutoLoad and UserAutoSave with a
userdata value at SP+112; the runner passes a scratch save root as argv[1].
On master: 2 failed (no call from
ppu_sysprx_register, no handler for 0x52AAC4FA; UserAutoLoad passes). With
this change all checks pass. test_savedata_fixed.c and test_savedata_io.c
still pass. The fixture also builds with x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc and passes

ppu_nv_dirty: the merged lifter's CR forms keep their fields apart

split_flags matches the lifter's CR and XER statements as text, and a
function with one it does not know keeps CR and XER whole -- and its
callers then take it to read every flag. The merged lifter writes five
new ones, and Drakengard 3's lift went from no whole-flag functions to
40,593:

- a conditional branch decodes BO/BI from the word and tests one CR bit
  at any shift, `(ctx->cr >> 29) & 1`: bit sh % 4 of field 7 - sh / 4;
- stwcx./stdcx. copy XER[SO] into CR0;
- a vcmp record form sets CR6 as `(ctx->cr & ~0xF0u) | (_c6 << 4)`;
- an FP record form sets CR1 from the FPSCR;
- mfocrf reads only the fields FXM names, `ctx->cr & 0xF0000000u`.

Each is now its field (or fields) in split form. ppu_vmx.h's helpers
(vmx_vaddfp, ...) count as vector helpers -- the result first and written
whole, the operands after it -- so the pass loads no destination before
one.

f788adc836653bf2717af4eef5566eeaf12f20a4.message:
spu_channels: the engine lookup answers from a per-thread copy

The merge brought upstream's registry of private MFC engines, which takes
its read lock on every lookup -- and every DMA looks its engine up. Two
interlocked operations on one cache line that every SPU thread shares,
per transfer; the fork's 64-slot table had answered from a per-thread
copy of the last answer.

mfc_for now keeps that copy again (context, engine, and a generation),
good while no node has been freed since it was taken: s_mfc_gen counts
frees, bumped under the writer lock before the node goes. A node lives
until its owner releases it, which only happens once the owner has
stopped using the context, so a thread holding a copy for a live context
always holds a live node; a new context at a freed one's address -- the
next job's stack context -- finds the count moved and asks the registry.
SPU_MFC_TLS=0 asks the registry every time.

Drakengard 3, hub, uncapped 720p, the build without and with it run back
to back with 0.2.5 in between: SPU image 1 0.84 -> 0.72 ms of CPU a
frame (0.2.5: 0.74), the frame rate 168.5 -> 181.5 (0.2.5: 176.6 and
177.9). The registry tests (test_spu_context_registries, both the
concurrent-lookup and the slot cases) pass.

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests the runtime on Linux (GCC and Clang), and builds the
Vulkan backend on lavapipe under the validation layer. A green check means the
runtime built and the tests passed. It does not mean a game ran.

| | Linux |
|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes |
| Render backend | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes**, with the Vulkan backend |

**The PPU boot scaffold is compiled per game**, not into the library:
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch. `ps3recomp_host`
drives cellGcm → RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on,
Vulkan runs the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw engine;
without them, the null backend's fixed-function path. Every `ps3recomp_host`
scene passes with the Vulkan backend, including render-to-texture, MRT, depth
textures, cube maps and stencil. The null backend stays the headless fallback,
a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   └── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse
│   ├── hardware/             # cellGem, cellCamera, cellUsbd
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
└── docs/                     # See the Documentation table below
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

HLE implementations of the PS3 system libraries, written for this project. RPCS3 is a behavioural reference, not a code source. **About 93 modules complete and 5 partial** (media decode, SPURS), in roughly 260 files and 100,000 lines under `libs/`.

1433466655.readme_excerpt: # God of War: Ascension (PS3) Native PC Port An x86-64 static recompilation port of God of War: Ascension for Windows. The project translates the original PlayStation 3 binary and embedded SPU workloads into native C and C++ using the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) toolchain. ## How it works Traditional emulators interpret or JIT-compile machine code at runtime. This port uses static recompilation, converting the game ahead of time so it compiles into a normal 64-bit Windows executable: The game binary (`EBOOT.ELF`) is split and translated into eight C++ translation units (`src/gen/ppu_recomp_*.cpp`). Syscalls and OS library calls resolve through high-level emulation (HLE) shims in `src/compat/`. Embedded SPU binaries, including Sony's WWS Job System Policy Module and Edge Geometry code, are lifted into C and execute across host worker threads. The RSX (NV4097) graphics pipeline renders through a Direct3D 12 backend. It reads command packets directly from the GCM ring buffer, handles descriptor binding and pipeline states, and presents through a standard DXGI swapchain. Game data streams through an asynchronous Virtual File System (VFS) mapped to local disk instead of the PS3 Blu-ray drive. The Win32 window message loop runs on its own thread, isolated from the 60 Hz RSX presentation ticker so the window stays responsive even during long file loads. Controller input maps through XInput with keyboard fallbacks. ## Status [View detailed tables and classification methodology](docs/status.md) Firmware coverage measures imported PS3 OS functions against working high-level emulation handlers and offline-safe stubs. Hardware metrics are parsed directly from live runtime execution logs. Speed remains at 0% (not reached) until in-game level gameplay begins. Regenerate the dashboard and status documents with: ```bash python tools/gen_status.py ``` ## Current status | Component | Status | Details | |---|---|---| | PPU code lifting | Working | 19,570 functions across 8 translation units; 17 concurrent guest threads | | SPU / SPURS workloads | Working | 5 lifted SPU images; WWS job policy module running with zero interpreter fallbacks | | VFS streaming | Working | Asynchronous disk streaming reaches ~23 MB/s across 22 archive descriptors | | RSX presentation | Working | Direct3D 12 swapchain presents live-draw frames with active FIFO command processing | | RSX FIFO processing | Working | GCM offset tables mapped, JUMP/CALL validation in place | | FIOS synchronization | Working | Real Win32 event wait queues with FIFO condition variable ordering | | Audio engine | Partial | CellAudio initialized with WASAPI output backend and stubs | | In-game gameplay | Not reached | Boot progression advances through intro loops and title presentation | Technical notes and bring-up logs live in [docs/](file:///C:/IfItWorksItWorks/Project/gowassension/docs/) and [.planning/](file:///C:/IfItWorksItWorks/Project/gowassension/.planning/). ## Requirements - Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) - Visual Studio 2022 (MSVC v143 or `clang-cl`) with C++20 support - CMake 3.24 or newer - Ninja - Python 3.10 or newer - A legally dumped copy of God of War: Ascension (PS3) ## Building from source ### 1. Clone with submodules ```bash git clone --recursive https://github.com/YJuDeAd/gow-ascension-pc-port cd gowassension ``` If you cloned without `--recursive`, initialize them now: ```bash git submodule update --init --recursive ``` ### 2. Add your game files Copy your decrypted game files into the `vfs` folder: ```text vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.ELF vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN vfs/PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO ``` Game assets and executables are not included in this repository. ### 3. Apply upstream runtime patches Apply the required compatibility fixes to the local `ps3recomp` tree: ```powershell git -C ps3recomp apply ../patches/ps3recomp_current.patch ``` ### 4. Compile Build the `ps3recomp` runtime library first, then build the main executable: ```powershell # Build ps3recomp runtime cmake -S ps3recomp -B ps3recomp/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build ps3recomp/build # Build the game executable cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build ``` The output binary is written to `build/gow_ascension.exe`. ## Running Launch the port with the PowerShell runner: ```powershell # Run with Direct3D 12 graphics enabled .\tools\run_port.ps1 -LiveDraw # Interactive mode (no automatic timeout) .\tools\run_port.ps1 -Interactive # Custom resolution .\tools\run_port.ps1 -LiveDraw -Width 1920 -Height 1080 -TimeoutSeconds 30 ``` Default settings can also be edited in `config.toml`: ```toml [video] width = 1280 height = 720 vsync = "on" live_draw = true [input] auto_pad_start = false deadzone = 7849 ``` ## Repository layout ```text gowassension/ ├── .planning/ Roadmaps, phase specs, and verification records ├── analysis/ Function maps, symbol tables, and SPU/PPU triage data ├── docs/ Architecture notes and bring-up progress logs ├── patches/ Patches for the upstream ps3recomp runtime ├── ps3recomp/ Upstream runtime and lifter tools (submodule) ├── src/ │ ├── main.cpp Window setup, thread orchestration, main loop │ ├── boot_main.cpp Alternative boot harness │ ├── hle_extra.cpp Additional HLE handlers │ ├── compat/ Game-specific HLE overrides (GCM, FIOS, SPURS, sync) │ └── gen/ Machine-generated PPU and SPU code ├── tools/ Automation scripts for lifting, testing, and triage ├── twistedmetal/ Reference PS3 port implementation (submodule) ├── vfs/ Virtual file system root for game data └── CMakeLists.txt Root build configuration ``` ## Contributing Pull requests and issues are welcome. A few rules keep the codebase maintainable: - Keep `ps3recomp/` and `twistedmetal/` as read-only upstream references. All game-specific overrides, patches, and shims belong in `src/compat/` or `patches/`. - Never hand-edit files in `src/gen/`. Those are generated by the lifters. If a lifted function needs different behavior, change the lifter script or override the symbol in `src/compat/`. - Automation scripts in `tools/` should be cross-platform Python (`.py`) or PowerShell (`.ps1`). - Compile generated code in Release mode (`-O2` / `/O2`) without full debug PDBs to avoid consuming tens of gigabytes of disk space. ### Where to help right now - Implementing real Win32 condition variables in `src/compat/ascension_hle.cpp` for `sys_lwcond`. The existing stub drops signals, leaving media worker threads stuck. - Translating NV4097 microcode into HLSL to draw the first 3D passes once scenes finish loading. - Optimizing SPU-assisted skinning and vertex buffer decompression in Edge Geometry. - Building a real audio output backend for CellAudio callbacks. ## Legal This is an independent preservation and research project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Santa Monica Studio. This repository does not contain any copyrighted game assets, proprietary Sony code, encryption keys, or disc images. You must provide your own legally obtained copy of the game.

cdb581579fd7ba76d429fab741828ce9e04161d6.message:
Low-CPU update: fewer threads on weaker PCs, support for CPUs without AVX2

- SPURS: on PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the lanes/kernels spin less, wake the
  main thread sooner and run on fewer threads (4-thread PCs: ~10 fps -> ~29 fps,
  8 threads: ~38 -> ~50 fps). Big PCs keep the old behaviour.
- Vertex workers spin far less after each job, fewer workers on small CPUs.
- The once-per-second thread scan only walks the game's own threads.
- No exclusive core reservations on PCs with fewer than 20 CPU threads;
  P-core pinning only on hybrid CPUs with at least 8 P-core threads.
- CPUs without AVX2/FMA/BMI2 (pre-2013 Intel, AVX-less Pentium/Celeron, AMD before
  2015): Setup/the updater detect this and build an SSE4.1 compatibility version
  automatically (same results, slower). The game also checks the CPU at startup and
  shows a clear message instead of crashing.

1433467979.readme_excerpt:
# inFamous PC — русская версия (BCES00609)

> **Это неофициальный форк.** Автор порта — **[whompay](https://github.com/whompay)**, оригинальный
> репозиторий: [github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn).
> Форк поддерживает европейское издание **BCES00609** (Великобритания, Россия, Австралия, Португалия)
> и добавляет русский язык интерфейса порта и ряд доработок (список ниже).
> Об ошибках этой версии пишите в [Issues форка](https://github.com/Just-Adikus/inFAMOUSreborn/issues),
> а не автору оригинала: оригинальный проект форки не поддерживает.

Неофициальный нативный порт **inFamous** (PlayStation 3, 2009) для Windows. Код игры для процессора
PowerPC (PPU) и сопроцессоров SPU статически рекомпилирован в x86-64 C/C++ с помощью
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), поэтому игра работает как обычная программа
Windows, а не в эмуляторе.

**В репозитории нет ни кода, ни данных игры.** Игра собирается на вашем ПК из вашей собственной копии.

## Поддерживаемые версии игры

| Издание | Код | Статус |
|---|---|---|
| Европа: Великобритания, Россия, Австралия, Португалия (в т. ч. Platinum, Essentials) | **BCES00609** | основная версия этого форка |
| Европа: Франция, Германия, Испания, Италия, Нидерланды | BCES00220 | тоже работает |

У обоих изданий **один и тот же исполняемый файл** (SHA-256 расшифрованного `EBOOT.elf`:
`095d851432f3b55179cd725b46838ffedb3e5eb9f73889e52b6f11f3d3f494fd`), поэтому порт подходит к обоим.
Проверить свой диск можно так (после расшифровки EBOOT в RPCS3):

```bat
certutil -hashfile "...\PS3_GAME\USRDIR\EBOOT.elf" SHA256
```

## Что добавлено в этом форке

- **Поддержка BCES00609** в установщике (оригинал принимает только BCES00220).
- **Русский язык по умолчанию.** Игра запускается на русском (меню, субтитры, озвучка из
  `russian.psarc`); язык меняется в настройках (**Language / Язык**).
- **Русский интерфейс порта:** меню настроек, пункты «Настройки» и «Выйти из игры» в паузе,
  окна сохранения и загрузки. Шрифт порта собирается из русского шрифта игры (с кириллицей),
  латиница добирается из английского.
- **Кириллица в системных окнах** сохранения и сообщений (в оригинале там «кракозябры»).
- **Слоты сохранений прямо в игре.** При сохранении можно выбрать «Новый слот» вместо перезаписи
  единственного сохранения, при загрузке — любой слот. Перед загрузкой слота текущее сохранение
  автоматически копируется в слот «Резерв» (хранятся 5 последних). Отключить: `SAVEDATA_SLOTS=0`.
- **Менеджер сохранений** `Сохранения inFamous.cmd`: те же слоты вне игры — переименование,
  удаление, резервные копии.
- **Подсказки для клавиатуры и мыши:** «ЛКМ» / «ПКМ» вместо «LMB» / «RMB»; экран «Управление»
  показывает клавиатуру и мышь вместо геймпада.
- **QTE с прицеливанием** (например, миссия «Обед с Сашей»): мышь двигает виртуальный левый стик
  и держит прицел на месте, **ЛКМ** работает как «крестик», подсказки на экране меняются на мышь.
  Настройки: `PAD_MOUSE_LSTICK_RANGE` (чувствительность, 300), `PAD_MOUSE_LSTICK_LMB=0`,
  `PAD_MOUSE_LSTICK_ABS=0` (вернуть поведение оригинала).
- **Для слабых ПК:** адаптивная дальность прорисовки настроена на 30 FPS (снижается до 0,8 от PS3
  при FPS ниже 28 и возвращается выше 34). Перекрытие кадров рендера (`RF_TRIPLE`/`RF_EARLY`)
  выключено — на части систем оно вешало вывод изображения (чёрный экран со звуком).

## Простая установка

Скачайте **inFamous Setup.exe** из последнего [релиза этого форка](https://github.com/Just-Adikus/inFAMOUSreborn/releases),
запустите, выберите образ `.iso` (зашифрованный образ работает вместе с `.dkey` рядом) или папку
игры (ту, где лежит `PS3_GAME`), укажите папку установки и нажмите **Install**.

Setup проверит Python и инструменты сборки C++ и предложит их установить, скопирует игру из образа,
заново сгенерирует рекомпилированный код из вашей копии, соберёт его и создаст ярлык inFamous.
Повторный запуск Setup на той же папке обновляет или чинит установку и переделывает только то,
что изменилось.

## Обновление

Когда в форке выходит новая версия, установку можно обновить на месте: **Update now** в Setup
(он найдёт существующую установку), ярлык **Update inFamous** в меню «Пуск» или
`Update inFamous.cmd` в папке установки. Обновлятор сравнивает файлы с **этим форком**, скачивает
только изменившиеся, перегенерирует код игры, только если изменились патчи порта, и
перекомпилирует только затронутое. Установки, сделанные старым Setup, сначала нужно один раз
обработать новым Setup на той же папке.

> Установка из этого форка обновляется из форка, установка из оригинала — из оригинала.
> Если запустить Setup оригинала на папке этого форка, он вернёт её к оригиналу (без русских правок).

## Требования

- Собственный дамп диска inFamous: **BCES00609** (или BCES00220).
- Windows 10 или 11 (64-бит), видеокарта с поддержкой Direct3D 12.
- Процессор с SSE4.1 (2008 г. и новее). На процессорах без AVX2 (Intel до 2013 г., Pentium/Celeron
  без AVX, AMD до 2015 г.) Setup сам соберёт более медленную совместимую версию. На ПК с 16 и
  меньше потоками игра использует меньше потоков и меньше нагружает процессор.
- [Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) с отмеченным пунктом «Add python.exe to PATH».
- [Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/) с нагрузкой
  **Desktop development with C++** и компонентом **C++ Clang Compiler for Windows**.
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net) — только если в `PS3_GAME\USRDIR` есть `EBOOT.BIN`, но нет
  расшифрованного `EBOOT.elf`. Setup использует его для расшифровки.
- Около 10 ГБ свободного места и 16 ГБ оперативной памяти.

## Сборка вручную

```bat
cd installer
cargo build --release
target\release\infamous-installer --game "D:\Dumps\inFamous"
```

Нужен [Rust](https://rustup.rs). `infamous-installer doctor` только проверяет требования. Готовые
шаги при повторном запуске пропускаются, так что прерванная установка продолжается с того же места;
`--regen` начинает генерацию кода заново (нужно после обновления версии порта). Все шаги и команды
сопровождающего описаны в [installer/README.md](installer/README.md) (на английском).

## Игра

Запускайте **inFamous** (ярлык, который создал Setup). Сначала откроется небольшое окно настроек
(вертикальная синхронизация, ограничение кадров, разрешение, язык и т. д., сохраняются в
`settings.ini`), кнопка **Play** запускает игру. Те же настройки есть в меню паузы игры, пункт
**Настройки**. Геймпад работает как на консоли, поддерживаются клавиатура и мышь.

**Управление с клавиатуры:** WASD — движение, Shift — бег, мышь — камера, ЛКМ — выстрел (R1),
ПКМ — прицеливание (L1), Q — поглощение электричества (L2), R — барьер (R2), V — импульсный радар (L3),
Пробел / C / F / E — прыжок / уклонение / ближний бой / взаимодействие, Ctrl и стрелки — крестовина,
Esc — пауза, Tab — карта.

**F10** открывает встроенный трейнер: бессмертие, бесконечная энергия, восстановление здоровья,
здоровье x2/x5/x10, опыт, карма +/-, убрать врагов / мирных, суперскорость и модель игрока
(Зик, Триш, Кесслер, Олден, Джон). Отключить: `TRAINER=0`.

## DLSS и FSR (по желанию)

Игра умеет NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA или AMD FSR для масштабирования и генерацию кадров AMD FSR. Их нет в
сборке, потому что NVIDIA и AMD распространяют свои SDK сами, но оба бесплатны и подключаются за
несколько минут.

- **DLSS** нужна видеокарта NVIDIA RTX.
- **FSR** работает на любой современной видеокарте (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel). FSR 4 требует Radeon RX 9000,
  остальные карты автоматически получают FSR 3.1.

> Если игра упирается в процессор (низкий FPS при слабой загрузке видеокарты), DLSS почти не поможет,
> а **генерация кадров FSR** заметно добавит плавности ценой небольшой задержки управления.

**1. Скачайте нужные SDK.** Нужен **исходный код**, а не демо: на странице нажмите зелёную кнопку
**Code**, затем **Download ZIP** (или на странице Releases — **Source code (zip)**).

| Для | Скачать | Переименуйте распакованную папку в |
|---|---|---|
| DLSS / DLAA | [github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS) | `dlss-sdk` |
| FSR и генерация кадров | [github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK) | `fsr-sdk` |

**2. Положите папки в папку установки inFamous**, рядом с `infamous-recomp` и `ps3recomp`:

```
inFamous\
  dlss-sdk\        <- внутри include\ и lib\
  fsr-sdk\         <- внутри Kits\
  infamous-recomp\
  ps3recomp\
  ...
```

Проследите, чтобы не получилась папка в папке (`dlss-sdk\DLSS-main\include`): `include` (DLSS) или
`Kits` (FSR) должны лежать сразу внутри.

**3. Один раз пересоберите игру.** Откройте командную строку в папке установки и выполните:

```bat
type nul > .installer\update.pending
"Update inFamous.cmd"
```

Пересборка займёт время. Последующие обновления подхватят SDK сами.

**4. Включите в игре:** пауза → **Настройки** → **Масштабирование** (DLAA, DLSS Quality / Balanced /
Performance, FSR Native AA / Quality / Balanced / Performance) и **Генерация кадров**. Те же
параметры есть в окне настроек лаунчера. Применяются после перезапуска.

Если строки **Масштабирование** нет, сборка не нашла SDK: проверьте имена и расположение папок из
шага 2 и повторите шаг 3.

## Как это устроено

| Путь | Что внутри |
|---|---|
| `ps3recomp` | Набор инструментов рекомпиляции и рантайм: лифтеры PPU и SPU, HLE системных библиотек, RSX на Direct3D 12, звук и ввод |
| `infamous-recomp` | Части, специфичные для inFamous: точка входа, заглушки и исправления игры, инструменты для ресурсов |
| `installer` | Setup и консольный установщик: читает диск, генерирует код из вашей игры, применяет `installer/patches`, собирает |
| `installer/infamous.toml` | Всё об игре и порте: шаги генерации, генерируемые файлы, настройки сборки и запуска |
| `installer/generated.lock` | Хэши каждого генерируемого файла до и после патчей порта |

## Авторы

- **[whompay](https://github.com/whompay)** — автор порта inFamous PC
  ([оригинальный репозиторий](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn)).
- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) — sp00nznet и участники
  (см. [ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md](ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md)).
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net) — используется для расшифровки исполняемого файла игры.
- Sucker Punch Productions — за игру.
- [Lorenzo Aiello](https://github.com/aiellolorenzo23) и [ibrahimpuri](https://github.com/ibrahimpuri) — за поддержку
  оригинального проекта.
- [Just-Adikus](https://github.com/Just-Adikus) — русская версия и поддержка BCES00609 (этот форк).

# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível e à primeira luta contra um chefe, mas ainda lento (~18-23 fps no nível, 13-21 na luta). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot à primeira luta contra um chefe:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~30-40 fps; o primeiro nível a ~18-23 fps, conforme a cena (era ~9); a luta contra o chefe a 13-21. O limite é o trabalho das SPUs recompilado, não a placa de vídeo. Partes pesadas já rodam como código nativo, cada uma conferida contra o original: a geometria por draw (índices, skinning, normais e tangentes) e o pós-processamento que suaviza as bordas da imagem. O próximo passo é reduzir os custos que todo trabalho das SPUs paga, para o ganho valer no jogo inteiro e o fps ficar estável. Esses números são de um Ryzen 5 5600G com uma RX 7600; num Ryzen 7 9800X3D com uma RX 9070 XT (RSX do RPCS3, Vulkan), a luta das criaturas do primeiro nível fica em ~45-57 fps. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); e o jogo às vezes trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`). - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md).

## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), abra o launcher, `launcher\AscensionLauncher.exe`:

JOGAR abre o jogo dentro da própria janela do launcher. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

  baja) en vez de en el hilo RSX; mientras tanto se saltan los dibujos que lo necesitan (el

  HLSL se repetia en cada dibujo: ~1.000 por cuadro).
- Primera visita a la fase 1 con la cache fria, 2K->4K FSR: el peor cuadro jugando pasa de
  264 ms a 80 ms. GOWA_ASYNC_SHADERS=0 vuelve a compilar en el hilo RSX.

326b57da6a5dbf5dddc03bd142a9b566417e49ce.message:
live draw: raw vertex slot views cover whole strides (AMD reads the last vertex as zero otherwise)

A slot view of (n-1)*stride+esz bytes (a 12-byte position in a 16-byte stride) has SizeInBytes/stride = n-1 vertices for AMD's input assembler: the last vertex of every slot draw read as zero. In the opening movie the second triangle of the quad collapsed and the culling removed it, leaving a black triangle over half the picture. The view now covers n strides; only the guest's bytes are copied, the tail is zero. Also LD_NO_CULL=1 and GOWA_VSLOT_DBG=<frame> as probes.

902890d4e48c552b61cbfeefddb97ba4b0957d2f.message:
framegen: middle and real frames presented by a thread of their own (GOWA_FG_ASYNC)

The RSX thread did both presents and, waiting half an interval for the real frame, woke every 200 us while also walking the FIFO: RSX-present went from 50% to 87% of a core and the game from 58 to 33-45 FPS. Now it draws the middle frame into one of two textures of its own, submits, and hands (k, due) over; the FG-present thread shows the middle frame, sleeps until due on a high resolution timer (a new job wakes it) and shows the real one. Jobs whose buffers the RSX thread is rewriting are dropped; the check and the submission are under a lock the RSX thread holds while submitting a frame. Present is serialized by a lock (RSX, movie and FG threads). Phase 1, 1440p -> 4K FSR: the game at 59.8 FPS and 120 frames/s on screen (before: 33-45 and 63-104). GOWA_FG_ASYNC=0 is the old way.

aeab225bdf7440f4cb0a59316ebb6ac01c77aeec.message:
libs/video: FIFO walker rewinds to the run's start when out of step

The rare freeze on slow PCs: the PPU was still writing a draw block and the
words past the new ones were the previous lap's, which also decode as a
block. The walker ran through them, stopped after THEIR flip word, and when
the title finished writing, its position was inside a command of the new
block (the data of a NOP). Holding there never ends; going on walks garbage.

Now every settle point (pass start, park opening, after a branch, a hold)
first re-decodes the current straight run from where it began (the last
JUMP/CALL/RET or park opening that passed the check), with the words as
they are now. If that does not land exactly on the walker, it rewinds to
the run's start and runs the block again, now complete (a few commands
repeat: draws and label writes of the same value). At most once per start
every 200 ms, only for a start less than 64 KB behind; GOWA_PARK_REWIND=0
turns it off. Holds with the bad word at the walker also print the jump
history (and the SPU PUT ring with GOWA_PUTRING).

On a 4-core laptop: 4 hangs in 9 runs before, 0 in 17 after.

launcher: first run without the game prepared; FG on by default on 100 Hz+ monitors

When there is no game yet (no disc link, no compiled executable or no firmware) JUGAR reads PREPARAR JUEGO: it asks for the player's disc folder (PS3_GAME checked; European or US), the 1.04 update .pkg or offers to download it from Sony's server, and the RPCS3 folder with the firmware (looked for in the usual places first), then runs gerar.ps1 in a console window and refreshes when it ends. e9d6fbb055368c2a2404a4a403c3b2b602e5a194.message:
live draw: raw vertex slots with a misaligned stride go up packed

D3D12 wants each vertex element aligned to min(4, its size). The game's snorm16x4 normals and many unorm8x4 attributes are interleaved in strides that are not a multiple of 4, so every other vertex started at a 2-byte boundary and AMD's fetch read shifted bytes: blotches on Kratos' skin, the Fury grey and black. Those slots are now copied element by element at a tight stride (still raw, no float conversion). GOWA_VSLOT_CHECK=1 decodes the raw slots on the CPU and compares them with the compact path's conversion.

f29bab954bc51c886c6d0ec598384c5d53e8dad9.message:
live draw: meter and frame generation on their own fences; meter shows resolution and FG; FG through FSR

The on-screen meter and the frame generation's delayed frame used the frame's fence, ++g.fence_value and its auto-reset event from the movie / present threads, racing the RSX thread: the game hung (a wait missed its signal) or crashed in ntdll (a list reset while in flight), and ld_flush's 'the next signal is fence_value + 1' broke. Each has its own fence, value and event now, the meter a lock. The meter has a second line, RES <internal> -> <output> FSR and FG SI/NO with the presented fps; the window title shows the same resolution text. With GOWA_FSR the frame generation scales the frame through EASU + RCAS too. GOWA_OSD_SAMPLER=0/2 turns the meter's sampler off / without the GPU temperature.

f2e68c92ee1ef313d8fe99c962bf44b779385aec.message:
live draw: GOWA_FSR=1, FSR 1 style upscaling (EASU + RCAS) to the display size

The swap chain is made at the display's size (GOWA_OUT_W/H, else the primary monitor's mode) and the presented surface, game or movie, goes up in two passes: EASU, edge adaptive spatial upsampling, then RCAS sharpening (GOWA_FSR_SHARP stops, default 0.2). Our own HLSL of AMD's published FSR 1.0 algorithms. With GOWA_RES_SCALE=2 (2560x1440) to 3840x2160 phase 1 ran at 57.9 fps on an RX 6800 XT. Also: the MakeWindowAssociation for Alt+Enter, and LD_FRAME_DUMP writes frame_N_out.ppm, the backbuffer as presented.

1433590133.readme_excerpt:
# God of War: Ascension — port nativo para PC (brunoGowAscension)

> **Proyecto de fans, sin ánimo de lucro y sin relación con Sony.** *God of War* es marca registrada de Sony Interactive Entertainment. Este repositorio **no contiene el juego** ni el firmware: necesitas **tu propia copia** del juego. La actualización 1.04 y el firmware oficial del PS3 son **gratuitos** y se descargan de Sony.

![La Furia a 4K con FSR 1](docs/imagenes/furia_4k_fsr.jpg)

[English summary below](#english-summary)

## Qué es

Un port **nativo** de *God of War: Ascension* (PS3, 2013) para Windows. No es un emulador: el código del juego se **traduce a C/C++ y se compila** para tu PC (recompilación estática), sobre el [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) de sp00nznet. Como el código del juego no se puede repartir, **tu PC genera y compila la parte del juego a partir de tu copia**; el lanzador lo hace por ti.

Esta versión parte del port de [otavix010](https://github.com/otavix010/gow-ascension-pc) (todo su historial está aquí) y añade:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Disco europeo** | Funciona con la copia europea **BCES01741** además de la americana BCUS98232 (el ejecutable es siempre el de la actualización 1.04 americana; los datos, los de tu disco). |
| **Español completo** | Textos, voces y cinemáticas en español (y en inglés, francés y portugués). Antes las cinemáticas salían mudas y en el juego solo se oían efectos con un disco europeo. |
| **Tarjetas AMD** | Arreglados dos fallos de dibujo que solo pasaban en AMD: un triángulo negro tapando la mitad de la cinemática de apertura y manchas en la piel de Kratos (la Furia salía gris). |
| **FSR 1** | Renderizado a 1440p (o la resolución que elijas) escalado a la de tu monitor con FSR 1 (EASU + RCAS). |
| **Generación de cuadros (experimental)** | El juego sigue a sus 60 fps y en pantalla salen **120 cuadros por segundo** (va en un hilo propio). |
| **Texturas compartidas** | Las texturas que el juego copia a otra parte de la memoria se reutilizan en vez de subirse otra vez a la GPU: menos tirones en las peleas grandes y la VRAM deja de crecer (de 6,8 GB a 1,5 GB en la fase 1). |
| **Lanzador `GowAscension.exe`** | Con el estilo de los menús del juego. La primera vez pide la carpeta de tu copia y lo prepara todo solo (descarga la actualización y el firmware de Sony e instala lo que falte); después, ajustes y **JUGAR**. |
| **Pantalla completa** | Alt+Intro o F11 pasan de ventana a pantalla completa sin bordes (antes la imagen se congelaba). |
| **Medidor en pantalla** | FPS, resolución, generación de cuadros, modelo de tarjeta gráfica, CPU, GPU y memoria (F10). |

![Fase 1 a 4K con FSR 1](docs/imagenes/fase1_4k_fsr.jpg)

## Cómo jugar

### 1. Lo que necesitas

| Qué | Dónde |
|---|---|
| **El juego**: tu copia del disco de *God of War: Ascension*, europea (BCES01741) o americana (BCUS98232) | Una carpeta que contenga `PS3_GAME`. |
| **La actualización 1.04** (gratuita, ~235 MB) | El lanzador la descarga del servidor oficial de Sony. |
| **El firmware oficial del PS3** (gratuito, ~200 MB) | El lanzador descarga `PS3UPDAT.PUP` del servidor oficial de Sony (o usa el que tengas en RPCS3). No hace falta RPCS3. |
| **Python 3.10+** y **Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools** con C++ y Clang | Si faltan, el lanzador los instala con `winget` (te lo pregunta antes). También vale un LLVM aparte en `C:\Program Files\LLVM`. |

### 2. Descarga la última versión

Baja el `.zip` de la [última versión](https://github.com/serbru20066666/brunoGowAscension/releases/latest) y descomprímelo entero en una carpeta **sin espacios en la ruta** (por ejemplo `C:\Juegos\brunoGowAscension`).

### 3. Abre `GowAscension.exe`

![El lanzador](docs/imagenes/lanzador.jpg)

1. **Elige la carpeta de tu copia del juego** (la que contiene `PS3_GAME`).
2. **EMPEZAR**: el lanzador descarga la actualización 1.04 y el firmware de Sony, instala lo que falte y traduce y compila el juego para tu CPU, con el progreso en la ventana. Unos 8 minutos en un PC de 8 núcleos, más en uno de 4. Solo se hace una vez.
3. Ya preparado, muestra los **ajustes** y **JUGAR**. Mientras juegas, el lanzador se oculta y vuelve al cerrar el juego.

Ajustes del lanzador (se guardan en `%APPDATA%\GowAscensionLanzador\ajustes.json`):

- **Resolución de renderizado**: 720p, 1440p, 4K o 2880p.
- **Escalado FSR 1** y su **nitidez**: escala la imagen a la resolución de tu monitor, que se detecta sola.
- **Modo de pantalla**: pantalla completa sin bordes o ventana de cualquier tamaño. Durante el juego, Alt+Intro o F11 alternan.
- **Idioma**: español, inglés, francés o portugués.
- **Límite de fps**: 60 (como en el PS3) o 30. Las animaciones avanzan por cuadro: por encima de 60 los golpes y los labios se adelantan al sonido.
- **Generación de cuadros (experimental)**: 120 cuadros por segundo en pantalla con el juego a 60, en monitores de 100 Hz o más. Apagada por defecto.
- **Sincronía vertical**, **medidor en pantalla** (F10) y **sonido**.

**CARPETA DEL JUEGO** cambia a otra copia del disco sin volver a compilar. Las partidas guardadas van a `saves\`; el registro de la última partida, a `out\jogo.log`.

`Lanzador.cmd` abre el mismo lanzador como script de PowerShell. Sin lanzador: `gerar.cmd` (o `gerar.ps1 -Disco ... -Update ... -Firmware ...`) prepara el juego y `jogar.cmd` lo abre; las opciones son variables de entorno (`GOWA_RES_SCALE`, `GOWA_FSR`, `GOWA_FULLSCREEN`, `GOWA_LANG`, `GOWA_FRAMEGEN`, `GOWA_OSD`...). Detalles de la generación: [docs/COMO_GERAR.md](docs/COMO_GERAR.md) (en portugués).

## Rendimiento medido

Fase 1 (la pelea con la Furia), Core i7-14700KF + Radeon RX 6800 XT, monitor 4K a 144 Hz, build sin AVX-512:

| Configuración | El juego | En pantalla |
|---|---|---|
| 720p | ~50 fps | ~50 |
| 1440p + FSR 1 a 4K | ~58 fps | ~58 |
| 1440p + FSR 1 a 4K + generación de cuadros | **59,8 fps** | **120 cuadros/s** |

El límite está en la CPU (el hilo principal del juego). Las CPUs con AVX-512 van bastante más rápido (ver [el README de otavix](docs/README.otavix.pt.md)). En CPUs con núcleos de rendimiento y de eficiencia (Intel 12.ª generación en adelante) la fijación de hilos se desactiva sola: medido, rendía menos.

## Problemas conocidos

- **Tirón la primera vez que entras en cada zona**: los shaders se compilan al vuelo y quedan en caché; la segunda vez desaparece.
- **FSR 4 no**: es el escalado por IA de AMD y solo funciona en las Radeon RX 9000. FSR 2 y 3 necesitan vectores de movimiento que este juego no da; por eso FSR 1.
- El juego completo, de principio a fin, **todavía no está verificado**.

## English summary

A **native PC port** of *God of War: Ascension* (PS3) by **static recompilation**, on top of [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), based on [otavix010's port](https://github.com/otavix010/gow-ascension-pc) (its whole history is kept). **Bring your own copy**: no game code, data or firmware here. This fork adds European disc (BCES01741) support, full Spanish (voices and cinematics), fixes for two AMD-only rendering bugs, FSR 1 upscaling to the monitor's resolution, frame generation on its own thread (the game at 60 FPS and 120 frames/s on screen), Alt+Enter / F11 borderless full screen, an on-screen meter, and a launcher in the game's menu style (**`GowAscension.exe`** in the release zip) that prepares everything on first run: it asks for your disc folder, downloads the free 1.04 update and the official PS3 firmware from Sony, installs missing tools and compiles the game; then it shows the settings and PLAY. RPCS3 is not needed. License: MIT for the code (otavix010 and contributors; this fork's changes by Bruno Cardenas Torres); `scripts/gpl/unself.py` and `scripts/gpl/pup_libsre.py` are GPL-2.0. *God of War* is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment; this is a non-commercial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony.

cellAdec: decode AC3 through the run-time FFmpeg loader

cellAdec only produced silence, 1024 stereo samples an access unit, whatever the codec. A title that sizes its PCM ring from bsiInfo+0x14 (channels x 4 bytes a sample) then took the wrong number of samples for an AC3 5.1 movie track: 341 sample frames per 1536-sample AC3 frame.

AC3 (codecType 2) now decodes through the loader cellVdec already uses (ps3_ffmpeg_get, no new FFmpeg symbols) into interleaved big-endian float in the decoder's channel order, one 1536-sample frame per access unit, its size in the PcmItem and in bsiInfo+0x14. StartSeq flushes the decoder and Close frees it. The AU bytes and info are copied before AUDONE, which hands the AU buffer back to the title. Without a decoder (no FFmpeg build, PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG=0, a damaged AU) AC3 gives silence of the real frame size, 1536 samples in the channels the frame header names; other codecs keep the old 1024-sample stereo silence. The PCM block moves from the 16 KB per-handle scratch to its own 64 KB per handle in the HLE inject window.

test_adec_ac3 (libs/codec/tests, streams made by the ffmpeg program at test time) checks the silence sizes with and without the library, and that every access unit of a 5.1 stream equals FFmpeg's own decode sample for sample; two swapped channels and one dropped AU must be caught.

06b2292def31186d507aa8cfd38ed487ec220a9c.message:
.github/workflows: pin the five third-party actions to commit SHAs

release.yml fires on `push: tags: ['v*']` with `permissions: contents:
write`, so every action it invokes runs holding a token that can write to
this repo and attach release assets. Referenced by floating major tag, any
of those five actions could be retargeted upstream -- a tag is mutable, and
whoever controls it controls what executes inside that job. Pinning to a
commit SHA makes the referenced code immutable.

Each SHA is the commit the action's current major tag points at, so this
changes no behaviour: the same code runs, it just can no longer be swapped
out from under us. The readable version stays in a trailing comment because
a bare SHA tells a later reader nothing about how stale the pin is.

Only `uses:` lines and their comments change -- 13 references across all
five workflows, no other workflow edits.

(cherry picked from commit 903d023f4a88ace083b0d9843fd3cf71a40f6572)

0b874166c7bb5caa389d351863a417367ffb4362.message:
perf(spu): NEON fi and cflts on ARM64

On ARM64 spu_fi (the frest/frsqest interpolation step) and spu_cflts fell
through to the per-lane scalar references. Those loops are too large to
inline, so every use in lifted float code became an out-of-line call with the
vector registers spilled around it. This adds NEON forms beside the AVX2 ones
from #500; the other estimate and conversion helpers keep their references.

- fi: the reference's fixed-point arithmetic in 32-bit lanes; the 33-bit
  magnitude 2^32 + (base << 19) - step * y is split on the borrow of the low
  word.
- cflts, scales 0..127: multiply by 2^scale (exact, or an overflow that
  FCVTZS saturates like the SPU), FCVTZS, and exponent-0 / exponent-255 lanes
  patched to 0 / the saturated bound. Other scales use the reference.

test_spu_fi_cflts_neon compares both with the references over 5.6M vectors
(every exponent, fi's borrow edge, all cflts scales) in the default FPCR and
under round-toward-zero plus flush-to-zero, the mode SPU_FLOAT_RZ runs lifted
code in. On non-ARM64 hosts, or with SPU_SCALAR_HELPERS, it compares the
references with themselves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

0e8b9ef2ca28fae79e8e24d2dede074581350fb7.message:
rsx engine: a depth snapshot is the region the texture names

The engine's host depth target is at least canvas-sized
(eng_zdepth_get), but a depth texture covers only the top-left
width x height of it. eng_zdepth_snapshot resolved the whole target and
the Metal resolve sampled it with normalized coordinates, so a 128x160
shadow map in the corner of a 1280x720 target was stretched over the
whole canvas and the lookups landed outside the map.

eng_zdepth_snapshot takes the texture's size and asks the backend for
that region (clamped to the target); a cached snapshot is reused only at
the same size. The Metal resolve reads the depth 1:1 (src.read at the
fragment's pixel) instead of sampling it, so a smaller snapshot is the
top-left region. The Vulkan backend's copy already works this way.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) samples small shadow maps from
canvas-sized zetas. In the port, this together with #424 and the port's
other depth-texture changes removes the dark rectangles on the ground
under shadows; the effect was not isolated per change.

Tests: test_color_feedback_engine (a 128x160 texture over a 256x256 zeta
asks for a 128x160 snapshot), test_metal_depth_readback (a 2x2 snapshot
holds the top-left texels 1:1).

11690a51b493e28537e6b0601ce9bf3cc5016233.message:
spu: fi on 32-bit lanes, frest/frsqest tables without a gather

fi's fixed-point magnitude is 2^32 + d with d = base * 2^19 - step * y,
so one unsigned compare gives the normalisation and 32-bit lanes hold
the rest: no widening to 64-bit lanes and back.

The fraction tables are read with one cross-lane permute per eight
entries and a select on the row, not a gather: on Zen 2 the gather made
frest slower than the scalar loop. Throughput of frest + fi (the
reciprocal pair): GCC 8.5 ns scalar, 9.5 before, 6.4 now; clang 12.1
scalar, 6.1 before, 5.4 now. test_spu_float_est still finds no
mismatch under either compiler.

118b6281a756697391f178e523a409e0b1f60ce1.message:
cellGcmSys: GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS sets how long a FIFO park may stand

When the drain stops on a self-jump park and `put` has moved, it waits
GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS (50 ms) for the title to patch the park and then follows
`put`. That suits a title that leaves a park standing when it switches
segments. It does not suit one that appends commands right after the
park, moves `put` there and patches the park last: if the patch comes
after the grace, the drain skips the commands in between.

God of War HD does the latter, and while it loads its menu the two stores
have been more than 50 ms apart: the drain jumped from 0x57C40 to put
0x5AA2C, dropped ~11 KB of commands with a fence among them, and the boot
stopped (once in about 45 runs). The RSX itself would wait.

GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS=<ms> now sets the grace; the default is unchanged.

13a7676ba2139314035649dd94cc7bc075de2868.message:
perf(spu): copy only the reserved lines of a PUT under the lock-line lock

A PUT whose span touches a reserved line held the global lock-line lock for
the whole copy, keeping every other SPU's GETLLAR/PUTLLC waiting behind a
multi-line memcpy. Only the reserved lines can be inside a peer's
compare-and-commit window. In a multi-line span the other lines are now
copied first, without the lock, as the unreserved path already copies a
whole span; the locked pass then copies the lines it skipped and notifies
every reserved line, including one reserved after its unlocked copy.

That late line is notified but not copied again: between the two passes a
peer can reserve it, read our bytes and commit, and a second copy would
write that commit back over. Single-line spans keep the single locked copy.

test_spu_lockline_peer: an unaligned PUT over a reserved middle line raises
once, lands exactly, and leaves the bytes either side alone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

147e59a79e63cefcf0c2f53fc7314d83f54167e2.message:
rsx_d3d12: pass the FP depth-export bits of SHADER_CONTROL

Draws recorded only the 32-bit-exports bit of SET_SHADER_CONTROL, so a
fragment program that replaces the fragment depth (bits 1-3) was
translated without SV_Depth. God of War HD's resolve pass writes the
scene depth it reads from the 2x-AA depth surface into the resolved
one this way; without it the pass wrote the quad's own depth (0), and
every depth-tested pass after it failed everywhere: the stencil
shadows, the fog, rain, the waterfall mist and the glows.

The draw now records the export bits (32-bit exports and depth export)
as fp_ctrl, part of the pipeline key, and hands them to the
decompiler, which already emits SV_Depth from r1.z.

15265cf84c72fa3def867b7732f498108cd8f863.message:
feat(tools): --handled and --image-ids for SPU program discovery

build_spu_workloads --input discovers every embedded SPU ELF in a carrier,
lifts it and registers it by fingerprint, and reports coverage as complete
only when every program is registered. A title that already registers some
programs another way (a hand-reviewed lift, an interpreter route) could not
use it without registering those twice, and its content-derived image ids
(0x10000000 | sha prefix) cannot be reviewed or kept stable against ids the
title already uses.

--handled JSON {sha256: reason}: such programs are not lifted, count as
covered and carry the reason in inventory.json. --image-ids JSON
{sha256: id}: every registered program takes its pinned id; a discovered
program missing from the map is reported unsupported, so coverage fails
instead of silently assigning one. Entries naming programs that were not
discovered are errors. With both, inventory.json's `complete` is a usable
build gate: a newly discovered SPU program cannot go unregistered silently.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

1530be7cfd1295f9db57e380a3dc2314770a82c1.message:
ppu_lifter: per-function copy of the memory model; PPU_FAST_FP

A guest store goes through vm_base + ea, a byte pointer the compiler
cannot tell apart from the memory-model globals, so the inline load and
store paths reloaded vm_base, ppu_vm_size, ppu_hle_inject_base and the
two enable flags after every store. Each lifted function now copies them
into a local at entry (PPU_MM_SNAP) and its accesses use the copy. They
are all set before guest code runs. The SPU reservation bitmap and the
store watches can change while a function runs, so those are still read
from the globals. Code outside lifted functions keeps vm_read*_inl and
vm_write*_inl, which now take a fresh copy per access.

PPU_FAST_FP, off unless the build defines it, drops the NaN checks in
ppu_fp_bin and ppu_fmadd_core. The host's NaN differs from the PPC one
only in its sign and in which of two NaN operands propagates.

God of War HD, func_001BEFA4, built with FMA3: 6,195 instructions before,
5,855 with the copy, 4,553 with PPU_FAST_FP as well (branches 1,342,
1,063, 583).

test_ppu_lift.py: the conformance driver defines PPU_NO_INLINE_LOADS. Its
vm_read*/vm_write* are its own functions, and its statements do not run
inside a lifted function.
