643bcf75c0882ab00f41816de0163214e917158c.message:
sys_mutex: MUTEX_WATCH=2 reports long waiters without changing the wait

MUTEX_WATCH=1 replaces the blocking lock with 5 s timed slices, and on
macOS pthread_mutex_timedlock is a 200 us trylock poll. That changes the
timing enough to hide some hangs. With MUTEX_WATCH=2 an infinite
sys_mutex_lock stays a plain blocking pthread_mutex_lock: the waiter
records itself in a slot (64 of them) before it blocks and clears the
slot once it has the lock, and a reporter thread, started on first use,
prints every waiter blocked for 5 s or more every 5 s, with the mutex id
and name, the caller's LR and the owner thread and lock count.

MUTEX_WATCH is now read as a number, so =1 and =2 pick the mode.

sync_stress runs under both modes (sync_stress_mutex_watch1/2).

64782329d5f9cb063530f82a0900bea17b4d25b2.message:
sys_mutex: destroy refuses a mutex that is held or has waiters (EBUSY)

lv2 returns EBUSY for sys_mutex_destroy on a mutex that is locked or
that a thread is blocked acquiring. Ours destroyed the host mutex under
the blocked thread, and the next sys_mutex_create in the same slot
initialised a new one over it: everyone else then used the new mutex
and the blocked thread waited on the dead one for good.

sys_mutex_info.waiters counts the threads blocked acquiring a mutex:
around the acquire in sys_mutex_lock (both timeout returns give it back)
and around the re-lock in sys_cond_wait. Destroy returns EBUSY while the
lock count or that is nonzero, and logs the first 16 refusals.

Found in the Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) port while chasing the
hang after its level-1 intro movie. It was not that hang's cause.

tests/sync_stress/test_mutex_destroy.c (ctest mutex_destroy): held;
held with a blocked locker; a timed lock that times out; a thread
blocked on the host lock with the guest count at 0; a cond_wait
re-lock; then free, destroyed, and ESRCH after.

6aaea446bc2f4e6d89378176b5155b10fb7474fd.message:
rsx engine: honour the polygon offset (SET_POLY_OFFSET_*)

The draw engine ignored SET_POLY_OFFSET_{POINT,LINE,FILL}_ENABLE,
SCALE_FACTOR and BIAS, so every draw was drawn without the offset a
title asked for. Shadow casters, decals and projected shadows are drawn
with an offset so they do not fight the depth they sit on.

Resistance: Fall of Man sets a polygon offset for its character shadow
maps, its terrain decals and its projected shadows; all of them were
drawn without it.

A new optional backend hook, set_depth_bias(slope, units, depth_bits),
is called before every draw like the stencil reference, with the enable
that matches what the primitive rasterises as (POINT, LINE or FILL) and
the zeta's depth bits (16 for Z16, 24 for Z24S8). Both terms are 0 while
the offset is off, and a NaN term reads 0. PS3RECOMP_ENG_POLY_OFFSET=0
draws without it, as before. The pass dump's draw log shows "po
factor/bias" for an offset draw.

The Metal backend keeps the offset in the draw record and sets
setDepthBias:slopeScale:clamp: per draw. Its depth targets are
Depth32Float, whose bias unit is 2^-24 over [0.5, 1), so Z24 units carry
over as they are and a Z16 unit is 256 of them.

New test_polygon_offset in test_rsx_draw_engine: 0/0 with the offset off
or only its values set, FILL's values against a Z24S8 and a Z16 zeta,
LINE applying to a line list and not to a triangle, a NaN factor, and
0/0 again once it is disabled.

New test_metal_poly_offset (a CMake target where the HLSL -> MSL
translation is built, run twice in macos.yml): a constant-depth triangle
at 0.75 drawn on the GPU through the engine and the Metal backend lands
at 0.75 + 2^-16 with BIAS 256 on Z24S8 and with BIAS 1 on Z16, a
SCALE_FACTOR alone does not move it, and with PS3RECOMP_ENG_POLY_OFFSET=0
nothing does.

7306cf7088e50276094c01afebbe40fb1a37d291.message:
gcm: pass over NOP runs, and decode 3D method runs a command at a time

The FIFO walker decoded every word through the full header path, and
every data word through a translation, a stack of per-word switches and
two calls. In God of War HD gameplay that was most of the drain thread:

- NOP words. The title builds command blocks on SPUs into fixed-size
  reservations and leaves the rest of each one zero: about 4.6 million
  NOPs a second against 1.2 million command headers. A run of zero
  words is now passed over at once, up to put or the end of the 1 MB
  IO page.
- 3D method runs. A run inside one IO page with no per-word diagnostic
  on translates its offset once and skips the per-word checks, none of
  which can match subchannel 0/1 methods.
- Vertex-program microcode and constants, about five million words a
  second (the title re-uploads each draw's program and constants).
  rsx_process_vp_run handles an incrementing run inside the microcode
  or constant window in one call.

GCM_WORD_STATS counts NOPs one by one, so it now counts as a per-word
diagnostic and keeps the old path.

Tests: test_rsx_vp_run checks that the run call leaves rsx_state exactly
as the words do one by one (200,000 random runs, including rewrites of
the same microcode and runs that must be refused); test_gcm_nop_runs
checks method order around NOP runs, a run stopping at put inside the
zeros, and a run at the end of an IO page. The walker tests that stub
rsx_process_method also stub the new call.

Walker time per drain went from about 610 to 440 us, and the drain
thread from 26% to 18% of a core.

78ecbff514ba47da165d1cb2b6942c04bbb3d6b6.message:
release.yml: scope the write token to the job that publishes

The workflow declared `permissions: contents: write` at workflow level, so
every job inherited a token that can push commits and move tags. Only
`publish` uses it, and only for `gh release create`/`gh release upload`.

`package` never writes to the repository -- it configures CMake, compiles
the tree and runs every tools/test_*.py under `python` -- yet it held the
write token while doing so, on a commit that a tag can point at without
ever having gone through the push workflows. That is 75 test scripts today
and 47 more arriving with this release, all executing next to a credential
they have no use for.

So: workflow default drops to `contents: read` (which is also what any job
added here later inherits), `package` says `contents: read` explicitly, and
`publish` declares `contents: write` for itself. Releases live in the
`contents` scope, so `contents: write` is the narrowest permission that
still publishes; there is no `releases` scope to ask for instead.

Nothing else in the file needs a scope from this token. The artifact upload
and download both talk to the artifact service with the runner's own token,
and `actions: read` is only required for pulling artifacts from a different
run or repository, which this does not do.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit bc48602e492d9d1389f039760f1063698c44ed4f)

7d8d507ff4caf110fec313957e72e28e66b9fac6.message:
lift_jobmods: lift each job module at the link base its header names

Every WWS job module was lifted at LS 0x4000, the job code buffer. The
module header carries the address it is linked for at +0x28, after the
0xC0DEC0DE magic at +0x20: 0x4000 for almost every module, but
Resistance: Fall of Man ships 2 of its 15 modules linked at 0x7000.
Lifted at 0x4000, every function and branch target of those was 0x3000
short of where the job manager runs them.

module_base() reads it, and falls back to 0x4000 when the header has no
magic or names 0, an unaligned base or one that would run past local
store. It replaces BASE everywhere in the per-module loop: the ELF
wrapper, --base, the extra-function range, the +0x30 seed, the manual
link and switch-table targets and the manifest's base.

tools/test_lift_jobmods_base.py: module_base on six synthetic headers,
then a 0x7000 and a 0x4000 module lifted end to end, with functions and
manifest at their own base.

7f226c4d76534ebbf2887e9763d9d70ce622c57e.message:
rsx_draw_engine: a compressed texture is never a render target's output

sink_bind_textures matched every texture against the colour targets and
zetas at its offset. No surface colour format is block-compressed, so a
DXT1/DXT23/DXT45 texture cannot be reading what a target rendered; its
data came from memory. Matched anyway, it found whatever target sat at
that offset, and the draw was dropped as an incompatible feedback read.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) samples a 16x16 DXT1 texture at the
offset of its 1280x720 colour target, and that draw was dropped.

A compressed texture now skips both surface lookups and is uploaded
from memory like any other texture.

test_color_feedback_engine: a DXT1 texture at the current target's
offset draws, with no feedback copy.

ppu_lifter: put the likely hint on the inline access branch

__builtin_expect sat on vm_mm_ok's return value, where there is no
branch to attach it to, so it was gone by the time the helper was
inlined. The compiler then laid the slow-path call out inside the hot
path: every inline access ended in a taken jmp over it. The hint is now
on the if in each vm_read*_mm / vm_write*_mm, and the slow-path blocks
move to the end of the function.

gameplay frame goes from 17.6/17.4 to 16.9/17.2 ms, alternating with the
previous build in one session.

Two conflicts with #472 (@erikomis), which landed earlier in this wave and
rewrote the same poll loop. The second one is the interesting kind: taking
#496's hunk verbatim compiles and silently breaks #472.

master's poll loop opened and closed controllers inline. #472 moved all of
that into pad_sdl_hotplug(), which closes a detached pad through
pad_sdl_close(p, 1) -- and that is the function that keeps s_sdl_last_guid[p]
so the pad is reopened into the SAME port when it comes back, which is the
whole point of #472. #496 (written against master) re-adds an inline
"!SDL_GameControllerGetAttached(gc) -> Close(); controllers[i] = NULL" in the
loop, with no GUID bookkeeping. Merged as written, that closes the pad behind
pad_sdl_hotplug()'s back and the port assignment is lost.

So the structure is #472's and the behaviour change is #496's: the branch
stays "if (!gc)" and the state reset becomes pad_host_release().

One integration fix beyond either PR. #472 introduced a THIRD place that
resets the host state -- pad_sdl_close() itself, which #496 never saw because
it did not exist on master. Left alone, #496's centred sticks would be
restored on every path except hot-unplug, which is precisely the case #496's
own comment calls out ("A pad unplugged mid-game kept its last report the
same way"). pad_sdl_close() now calls pad_host_release() too, so all four
reset paths agree: 0 is full deflection up and left, and 128 is centre.

81344af1d05eea6877c7fa4963141a49aa71ab27.message:
spu: update event_status atomically

event_status is written from more than one host thread: the SPU's own
(Sn from a list stall, the tag-group event, its own Lr poll, WrEventAck)
and others (a PPU store or a peer SPU's PUT/PUTLLC raising Lr through
spu_coherency.c). Each side did a plain read-modify-write, so a raise
that read the word before the other side wrote it put the stale value
back and the other side's bit was lost.

In Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107), after START the PPU rewrites the
SPURS line about 14k times (cellSpursReadyCountStore), each raising Lr
on the job-manager SPU. One of those raises overwrote the Sn the SPU had
just set for a stalled DMA list, and the WWS job manager waited for its
interrupt for ever with the list parked: the first gameplay frame never
finished. With this it reaches gameplay.

SPU_EVENT_SET / SPU_EVENT_CLEAR (spu_context.h) are atomic fetch-or /
fetch-and (_InterlockedOr/And under _MSC_VER), and all six write sites
go through them.

Also, WrEventAck keeps Sn pending while a list is still parked
(list_stall_stat non-zero): a resumed list runs inline inside the
MFC_WrListStallAck that resumes it, so its next stall can land before
the handler acknowledges the event it was taken for. That guard alone
did not fix the hang above.

Tests: test_spu_event_atomic (Sn raised and acked on one thread while
another raises and acks Lr, 5M rounds: never lost; with the plain
operators it is lost tens of thousands of times) and
test_spu_event_ack_sn (the WrEventAck guard through the real
spu_channels.c).

87defcf2f0f70ac2290b585ac469a5efb81d41ee.message:
spu_workload: images with a parameter area the loader fills in

A raw-SPU program the PPU streams into local store is found by the
fingerprint of the run it wrote. Some programs carry a parameter block
the PPU fills in before every load (heap pointers, per-level values, the
SPU's own MMIO window), so the loaded run never fingerprints the same
twice and no registration can match it.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) loads its second raw-SPU program with
0x50 such bytes at the end of the image. One run loaded it as
47C9CB480016D493, a Continue from a later checkpoint as 5771C48D28664765;
the second found no lifted entry ("no lifted image is registered") and
the game hung.

spu_workload_register_img_masked(fp, fn, image_id, name, size, var_off,
var_len) registers an image whose fingerprint is taken with
[var_off, var_off + var_len) as zero; for an image cut from an ELF whose
parameter block is zero there, that is simply the image's fingerprint.
spu_workload_find_img_masked(data, n, ...) matches a run of exactly that
size against it whatever the area holds. raw_spu_start falls back to it
when the plain lookup of a proxy-loaded run finds nothing, and says so in
its log line. Plain registrations and lookups are unchanged.

New test_spu_workload_masked (tools/test_spu_workload_masked.py): two
loads with different parameters resolve to the masked image, a change
outside the area or a different length does not, the plain lookup still
finds the image as it is in the ELF, and a registration whose area does
not fit is refused. test_spu_raw_start stubs the new lookup.

894d38ba7eb5d7c9803991ad92cfc2bd259631e0.message:
metal: host-surface mode renders into a launcher's IOSurfaces

A title that replaces its executable (sys_game_process_exitspawn, which
a port does as an exec) loses every AppKit object with the old process
image: its window closes and the new image opens another. Resistance:
Fall of Man (BCUS98107) does this going from the EBOOT's menus to
game.self, so starting the campaign closed the window and opened a new
one.

With PS3RECOMP_HOST_SURFACES=<bootstrap name> in the environment the
Metal backend opens no window and never touches NSApplication. It looks
the name up, sends ATTACH, maps the control page and wraps the IOSurfaces
it gets back as render targets. Engine and vtable presents end in one of
those surfaces instead of a drawable; the completion handler publishes it
and sends a FRAME wake. The protocol and the surface state machine
(FREE -> RENDERING -> READY -> READING) are in rsx_host_surface.h, shared
by both ends; when every surface is busy the game takes back the oldest
unread one, so it never waits on the window. The image an exec brings up
attaches again by the same name. If nothing answers, the backend opens a
window of its own as before. The pump reports -1 once the launcher closes
its window or dies.

Without a launcher, rsx_metal_backend_export_window_state() puts the
window's frame and fullscreen state in PS3RECOMP_WINDOW_STATE before an
exec, and the next image's window opens there.

The engine's present also counts a guest frame
(rsx_metal_backend_note_guest_frame), which feeds PS3RECOMP_METAL_FPS
and the launcher's title.

New test_metal_host_surface (macos.yml), against a launcher fixture in
the same process: the state machine; init attaches with no window;
engine and vtable presents land in the surfaces; 40 unread presents
reclaim instead of stalling; a resize asks for new surfaces; `closed`
reaches the pump; a second init attaches again.

8e34ab19bf2e13bfe9e8e99d866a851757e1c5b0.message:
rsx: WPOS in the RSX window convention (SET_SHADER_WINDOW origin and pixel centers)

The fragment translator read WPOS as the host position, whose origin is the
top left, and nothing looked at SET_SHADER_WINDOW (0x1D88). With the window
origin BOTTOM the RSX counts WPOS.y up from the bottom edge, so a pass that
builds its UV from WPOS, e.g. uv = wpos * (1/W, -1/H) + (0, 1), sampled its
source vertically mirrored. Rasterization is already right; only what WPOS
reports changes.

- rsx_fp_decompiler: WPOS reads go through _rsx_wpos(input.position). A
  buffered program defines it from fp_alpha: y = height - y when fp_alpha.y
  (the window height) is nonzero, and fp_alpha.z added to x and y as the
  pixel-center bias. An unbuffered program defines it as the identity. A
  program that does not read WPOS emits no helper and stays byte-identical.
- rsx_draw_engine: fills the two unused fp_alpha lanes per draw from
  SET_SHADER_WINDOW: the height (bits 0-11) when the origin (bits 12-15) is
  BOTTOM, else 0; -0.5 when the pixel centers (bits 16-19) are INTEGER, else 0.
  Backends that fill fp_alpha themselves and leave .y/.z at 0 keep the host
  position.
- test_fp_decompiler: the helper and the WPOS read in buffered and unbuffered
  programs, and no helper for a program that does not read WPOS.

9002559916323d0623083f8592622730f58c0b5a.message:
rsx_d3d12: present a small batch held back across two flips

The display-clear present holds back a batch smaller than a quarter of
the largest frame seen, as an intermediate of a title that clears the
display several times per flip. That maximum never comes down. God of
War HD plays a movie inside the game as one quad a frame, after
hundreds of draws a frame of game: every movie frame was held back,
the quads piled up until a quarter of the game's size, and the screen
showed one frame every few seconds while the movie's sound played on.

A batch still small when a second flip has landed is not an
intermediate. It is presented, and its size becomes the frame size.

Reproduced on the opening cinematic, which is presented the same way,
with the maximum set to 1000 once and presents at the display clear
already in use: 0 presents a second, the held draws growing by 30 every
second; with the change, one frame is held and then all 30 are
presented. The rendering check passes.

9088b37c42b16f23389f8d0129e446ce487d4bef.message:
vulkan/draw engine: reuse readback staging, refresh changed textures in place

Every readback and every texture upload allocated, mapped and freed its own
host buffer, and every changed texture was re-created (an allocation and a
synchronous layout submit) with the old one released. Those are driver
round trips, and on Windows/NVIDIA they took from tens of milliseconds up
to seconds each under load.

- vk_stage_get: one grow-only host buffer for readbacks (colour and depth)
  and one for uploads, reused after their submission completes and freed
  in vk_eng_shutdown.
- rsx_draw_backend.texture_upload_ordered: a backend whose texture_upload
  is ordered after every draw already handed to it gets a changed 2D
  texture rewritten in place when its mip count is unchanged. Vulkan sets
  it (every draw and upload submits and waits); Metal and the test stubs
  leave it 0 and keep create-and-swap. Volumes always create-and-swap.
- vk_eng_texture_upload rejects a mip past the levels the image was
  created with.

90f510fc3c5a99ed96bfb9598e47d8aa62a1099f.message:
vulkan engine: per-target colour mask and blend enable for MRT sets

Every attachment of an engine pipeline took target A's COLOR_MASK and
BLEND_ENABLE. The RSX gives targets B..D their own: a nibble each of
COLOR_MASK_MRT (0x0370) and a bit each of BLEND_ENABLE_MRT (0x036C). The
draw engine already decodes both into rsx_be_render_state and keys the
pipeline on them, and the Metal backend applies them; this does the same on
Vulkan.

Giving every target A's state is wrong both ways. inFAMOUS 2's light
volumes add into target A with B and C masked off, and on Vulkan every light
was added into the G-buffer as well (blown-out props, rectangles around
each light); its material passes write B and C's alpha while A's alpha is
masked, which left them stale.

- The device enables independentBlend when it has it (s_vk.indep_blend_ok);
  without it every target keeps A's state, as before.
- PS3RECOMP_VK_MRT_MASK takes the values PS3RECOMP_METAL_MRT_MASK does:
  1 (default) the hardware rule, 0 target A's state everywhere (the old
  behaviour, to bisect a title that depended on it), 2 only a target masked
  off entirely is off, with per-target blend.

Single-target pipelines are unchanged.

99ff41af923dea02fc61bfd3fa06537e9733778a.message:
spu_raw: SPU_RunCntl = 0 stops a running raw SPU

Writing 0 to SPU_RunCntl only set the context's status word. A raw SPU
parked in a channel wait kept its host thread, so the RunCntl = 1 that
followed was dropped as "already up": the program the PPU had just
streamed into local store never ran, and the old one could later resume
its old registers over the new image.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) does this to raw SPU 1 on every
checkpoint reload (stop it, stream its program in again, start it). The
restart was dropped, and after dying the checkpoint reload launched the
player into the sky.

RunCntl = 0 now sets stop_request on the context, wakes its channel
waits and returns once the host thread has left (up to ~4 s, logged if
it does not). The channel layer honours the request at every rdch and
rchcnt, inside its blocking channel wait and in the full out-mailbox
wait, and halts the SPU there through the spu_run_with_halt landing
pad. The run thread then publishes a plain stopped status (no stop
code, no stop-and-signal interrupt), releases the context's coherency
registration and MFC slot, and clears started. A start while the
thread is still up is now logged instead of being dropped silently.

New test_spu_raw_runcntl_stop (tools/test_spu_raw_runcntl_stop.py),
through the real spu_raw.c, spu_channels.c and registry: a program
parked in rdch SPU_RdInMbox stops on RunCntl = 0 before the store
returns, and the next program streamed into the same SPU runs.
test_spu_raw_start stubs the two release calls.

9a3fbffde2d1c89da8f4f74c4dd0f8088b62c2db.message:
ppu_hle: a fast path for leaf imports; lwmutex lock/unlock use it

Every HLE import goes through ps3_hle_call's guard and bookkeeping: the
TOC save and restore (with an out-of-line store to the guest stack),
the GCM pump, the profiler breadcrumb, the in-flight table. God of War
HD takes an lwmutex about 640,000 times in the frame where the first
fight's next wave spawns (its allocator), and that overhead was a large
part of each call.

ps3_hle_register_fast(nid, fn) registers a fast form beside the full
handler for an import that runs no guest code, leaves r2 alone and does
not block. ps3_hle_call tries it first; the fast form returns 0 to take
the full call. sys_lwmutex_lock's fast form takes a lock that is free or
already the caller's, and leaves a lock that has to wait (and every call
while PS3_LWMUTEX_TRACE is on) to the full handler, so a blocked thread
still shows in the in-flight table. sys_lwmutex_unlock's always
finishes. Fast calls do not appear in PS3_FTRACE.

God of War HD: that frame 235 -> 167 ms (two runs); 354 ms before the
atomic lwmutex. The rendering check passes.

9aad0f9bf10c0e85aa382c16e29a8aabb275ed70.message:
ppu_lifter: one compare per inline guest access

The inline load and store paths tested each access against the enable
flag, the null page, the raw SPU windows, the end of the mapping and the
gcm ref-poll word, and the compiler turned the chain into a run of setcc
and and instructions: about eleven per access. The per-function copy of
the memory model now holds the inline range as one span from 0x10000
(0 while a diagnostic is armed), and an access checks
(ea - 0x10000) <= span - n, with span - n computed once per function.

The range is the old checks' or narrower: an access that straddles
0xE0000000 now goes out of line. The ref-poll word is special only to
vm_read32, so only the 32-bit load still tests it. Checked over edge
addresses, sizes, mapping ends and flag settings against the old
predicate: no other difference.

God of War HD: func_001BEFA4 4,553 to 3,273 instructions, the executable
83 to 60 MB, and the median gameplay frame 20.0 to 17.4 ms, alternating
with the previous build in one session.

a20903d25bfa75c9cc99cc775621fd189132e2aa.message:
tools/host_window: reap the game with a blocking waitpid

DISPATCH_PROC_EXIT can fire a moment before the child is reapable, so
the WNOHANG reap in child_exited() saw nothing and returned; the source
does not fire again, and the host stayed up with its window open after
the game had gone. Seen when the whole process group got SIGTERM: the
host only went away at its own SIGKILL fallback, or not at all.

The child has exited when the notification arrives (an exec does not
raise EXIT), so a blocking reap in an EINTR loop returns at once. If the
pid was already reaped elsewhere the host exits anyway. begin_close()
also calls child_exited() itself 2 s after the SIGKILL fallback, in case
the notification never comes.

With the game: SIGTERM to the process group, the host exits rc 0 after
3.2 s (before: it stayed up until SIGKILL).

rsx_vp_decompiler: branch on the transform branch bits; leaders up to slot 544

every later branch closed a block that was never opened, main() ended

picks optional paths with them ran every path. They now test bit
D3[23:27] of SET_TRANSFORM_BRANCH_BITS against D3[28], as RPCS3's
GetOptionalBranchCond does; the CC condition does not apply. The outcome
is baked into the program, so the draw engine and live_draw read the

ab2783bda49461e10edfe5d8282f50b23eae9da1.message:
spu: interpreter rejoins lifted code inside resident code regions

spu_lifted_lookup, the interpreter's check for a lifted entry at its pc,
only searched ctx->image_id. For a job that a policy module streams into
local store, that is the policy module's image, so the interpreter never
found the job's own lifted functions. Once it was entered anywhere in a
job (a function the lifter didn't find, a resume point), it ran the rest
of the job interpreted, callees included.

Resolve addresses inside a resident code region against the region's
image first, as spu_indirect_branch already does.

God of War HD's SCREAM mixer reaches two of its job's DSP dispatchers
through a pointer table the function finder doesn't see. Each call ran
the dispatcher and every kernel it jumps to interpreted: 8-11M SPU
instructions a second in gameplay, and 20-53% of the audio blocks empty.
With this change it is ~13k a second and the kernels run lifted.

test_spu_lifted_start checks the lookup against the streamed-job setup
test_resident_code_regions already builds.

b19ac284e1f5cfa94c3d5a2326206a4eda0cda09.message:
rsx engine: honour user clip planes (SET_USER_CLIP_PLANE_CONTROL)

An RSX vertex program writes six clip distances into o5.yzw and o6.yzw,
but which planes count, and which side of each is kept, is register
state: NV4097_SET_USER_CLIP_PLANE_CONTROL (0x1478), one 4-bit op per
plane, 0 disabled, 1 ENABLE_LT, 2 ENABLE_GE. The engine ignored the
register, so nothing was ever clipped. A planar reflection clips its
mirrored scene at the mirror plane this way; without it everything
behind the plane (in inFAMOUS 2, the riverbed under the water) was drawn
into the reflection.

Do what RPCS3 does (fill_user_clip_data and the VP reg_table): for each
enabled plane the vertex shader gets an SV_ClipDistance output, the
distance as written for GE (keeps d >= 0) and negated for LT (keeps
d <= 0); a disabled plane in the same vector gets 0.5 and never clips.
rsx_vp_apply_user_clip adds the outputs to the decompiled HLSL after the
last declared varying, so the user varyings keep their locations, and
the per-plane ops join the pipeline key. A draw with no plane enabled
compiles the same program as before. The Vulkan device enables
shaderClipDistance when it has it.

PS3RECOMP_ENG_USER_CLIP=0 ignores the register, as before.

b3a75d9838299538e3379429bf2a36071c12bd58.message:
ppu: each host thread runs HLE -> guest callbacks on a stack of its own

ppu_guest_call and ppu_guest_call_ct started every callback at the
guest EA 0xCFFE0000. The variable holding it was thread-local, its value
was not, so callbacks running at the same time on two host threads built
their frames over each other, and a callback nested in another started
on top of the outer one's frame. 0xCFFE0000 is also inside RSX local
memory (0xC0000000 + 256 MB).

In Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) the movie player's cellAdec and
cellVdec callbacks run at once on its two MoviePlayerStream threads. The
adec callback's scoped mutex guard read back a NULL mutex, unlocked NULL
and left the player mutex locked for good, so the game hung after the
level-1 intro movie.

The top 16 MB of the stack region (VM_CB_STACK_REGION, 64 slots of
256 KB) now holds one callback stack per host thread, and
vm_stack_allocate stops below it. A callback nested in another starts
0x400 below the outer one's live stack pointer, past its protected zone.

runtime/ppu/tests/test_ppu_guest_call_stack.cpp
(tools/test_ppu_guest_call_stack.py): two host threads inside a
callback at once, each nesting a second one, every frame filled and
checked afterwards.

b6880e6aa86fc2d1acf4ce1edfa64d91f1c5f19e.message:
spu: SSE4.1/AVX2 forms of the per-lane integer and quadword helpers

The integer, compare, shift/rotate, multiply and quadword byte-shift helpers
have NEON forms on arm64 and fall back to their scalar per-byte/per-lane
reference loops everywhere else. On x86 those loops (rotqby and its family
are 16 single-byte moves each) were most of the lifted SPU code's time: a
Bink video decoder ran at 6-7 fps.

- SPU_X86 (x86 with SSE4.1, not NEON, not SPU_SCALAR_HELPERS/SPU_SCALAR_INT)
  gives each NEON-only helper an SSE4.1 twin: a/sf/ai/sfi, and/or/xor(i),
  the word, halfword and byte compares (and immediates), selb, ah/sfh(i),
  absdb, avgb, cg/bg, addx/sfx, the mpy family, cntb, xsbh/xshw and cwd.
- The quadword byte shifts and rotates (shlqby, rotqby, rotqmby and their
  bi/immediate forms) are one pshufb with a computed control.
- shl/rot/rotm/rotma need per-lane variable shifts and take the AVX2
  vpsllvd/vpsrlvd/vpsravd forms when __AVX2__ is set; without it they keep
  the scalar reference.
- cbd/chd/cwd/cdd generate their control word with word stores instead of a
  16-byte loop, on every host (the result is the same bytes).

Helpers without a cheap x86 form keep calling their reference.

tests/test_spu_int_x86.c checks every x86 form against spu_X_ref on 2M
random and edge-value cases, and the new generate-controls against the old
loops.

Measured on Windows (Ryzen 5 5600, clang-cl, /arch:AVX2), inFAMOUS 2: the
Bink movies go from 6-7 fps to 30 fps, and in-game frame rate is about 15%
higher.

vulkan: free the batching rings, their pool and the snapshot bounce buffer at shutdown

The engine shutdown left s_eb's four rings and descriptor pool (VK_DRAW_BATCH=1)
and the depth snapshot bounce buffer (batching on or off) alive, so
vkDestroyDevice reported leaked objects under the validation layer and the
lavapipe jobs failed. s_snap_st moves to file scope and goes with the snapshot
pool; vk_eb_release flushes, destroys the rings and the pool and lets the next
vk_eb_on decide again.

b730e080191640609cff3106eebb9c5a20a2e170.message:
vulkan: keep engine constants in ordinary memory, not read back from the UBO

The engine's vertex/pixel constants were written straight into the shared
uniform buffer, and every batched draw then memcpy'd them out of it into its
ring slice. That buffer is host-coherent, which is write-combined and uncached
on most drivers, so the copy was a read from uncached memory: ~40 us for the
~8 KB of constants a draw carries, 85% of vk_eng_draw's time in God of War:
Ascension's first level.

The constants now live in a host allocation laid out like the UBO. Batched
draws copy from it into their slice; unbatched draws copy it into the shared
UBO before writing their descriptors, as before.

threads spin in. cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo records the host thread that
walks the FIFO (g_gcm_drain_tid), and PS3_SAMPLE_DRAIN=1 skips every
other thread, so the histogram is the drain's own cost.

(ucrtbase at a quarter of the drain thread's samples).

c40829d770b7b30e48c33b4e82f6396d56b7838e.message:
runtime: buffer stdout and stderr and flush them on a timer, not an unbuffered stdout

ppu_run set stdout unbuffered so that a killed run keeps every line it
printed. With mingw-w64 that makes every character its own write():
__mingw_pformat hands an unbuffered FILE one fputc per character. Under
Wine into a pipe each write costs microseconds, and a title that logs
over a thousand lines a second spent most of its logging threads' time
there; lines from two threads also interleaved character by character.

ps3_stdio_init() (runtime/platform/ps3_stdio.c), called from ppu_run,
gives stdout and stderr a 64 KB buffer each and flushes them from a small
thread every PS3_STDIO_FLUSH_MS milliseconds (default 50), at exit, on
abort() and from the unhandled-exception filter (on POSIX through
win32_compat's signal dispatcher). A crash flush asks the flush thread
and waits at most a second, so a fault inside printf cannot hang it on
the stream lock. A killed run loses at most one interval.
PS3_STDIO_UNBUFFERED=1 restores the old unbuffered stdout.

runtime/platform/tests/test_stdio_flush.c checks, from a parent reading
the child's pipes: buffered by default, flushed within the interval
while the child is alive, flushed at exit, on abort() and on a SIGSEGV,
and unbuffered with PS3_STDIO_UNBUFFERED=1. Linux and macOS CI run it.

test_ppu_entry_arguments.cpp links ppu_loader.cpp on its own and gets a
no-op ps3_stdio_init.

c4a54cbdb95111bc01b66edf49774f3b626cae70.message:
spu_drain: run the per-hop hooks' common case inline

Every trampoline hop called yz_lockstep_tick and spu_task_launch_check,
and spu_task_launch_check called spu_check_stack_reset in another file.
Each spu_drain_call also called spu_depth_guard, which wrote a ring and
a counter shared by all SPU threads. With their switches off the hooks
return almost at once, but an SPU thread takes millions of hops a
second: in God of War HD gameplay they were about a fifth of each SPU
thread's samples.

- spu_drain_call and SPU_DRAIN (through spu_drain_hop) do what the hooks
  do by default inline: the recent-pc ring, the step count with the
  LS 0 job-complete check, and the PM flow record.
- spu_task_launch_check runs in full when SPU_NO_LS0_END, SPU_EXITTRACE,
  SPU_STEPTRACE or SPU_JOBDRAIN is set. Lockstep and the stack-reset
  check are called only when lockstep is not off and an entry is
  registered.
- spu_drain_call tests the depth limit inline. spu_depth_guard drops its
  shared ring and reports this thread's recent hops instead.

c74e3bf9530594767ade9df92ba9f55f0af8f089.message:
Run GCM handlers from blocked semaphore waits (Windows)

A flip, vblank or user-command handler is guest code, so it runs when a
guest thread reaches an HLE call or a timer sleep and pumps. A title that
waits for its flip handler in sys_semaphore_wait -- God of War HD's main
thread does, every frame -- sat there until some other thread happened to
pump: a median 0.76 ms between the RSX reaching the flip and the main
thread waking, 1.7 ms at p90.

The GCM layer now sets an auto-reset event whenever it marks something
pending, and sys_semaphore_wait waits on that event as well as the
semaphore. When the event fires, the waiting thread runs ppu_gcm_pump,
as a timer sleep does, and re-checks the semaphore. cellGcm_wait_pump is
linked weakly, so the runtime still links without the GCM library; the
POSIX path is unchanged.

God of War HD, frame limit off, alternated in one session: median frame
17.3/17.1 ms before, 15.8/16.6 ms after; flip reached to main thread
awake 0.76 ms to 0.02 ms. sync_stress passes.

c9fc36a15d379d157f5a6d43947cbd9da0a2ed46.message:
rsx_texture_decode: step the swizzled offset instead of re-interleaving

A swizzled texture was decoded texel by texel, and each texel's offset
came from rsx_swizzle_offset, which interleaves x's and y's bits one at
a time: about ten iterations a texel. In God of War HD that loop was
most of the CPU decode in the texture bursts that stall the drain when
new effects first appear.

x's and y's bits land on separate positions of the offset, so it is the
OR of a y part, computed once a row, and an x part stepped with the
dilated increment (d - mask) & mask. Checked against
rsx_swizzle_offset for every texel of every power-of-two size up to
4096x4096 (rows sampled past 256): no difference. test_texture_layout
now decodes a swizzled image of every size up to 128x128, square or
not, and checks where each texel lands.

God of War HD: texture time in the worst burst 0.27 -> 0.07-0.10 s;
the frames it stretched 112 -> 74 ms and 101 -> 73 ms; frames of 45 ms
or more over a run 13 -> 10.

cd4383ec19274822747b37d8a8dee17e5241579f.message:
lv2: register syscall 22 as _sys_process_exit

On real lv2 (and RPCS3's binding table) syscall 22 is _sys_process_exit,
the exit every game issues; the table only registered 3 (sys_process_exit3,
the number bare-metal/newlib images issue).

A guest issuing 22 fell into the catch-all stub, which reports success -- so
the guest kept executing after its exit. Observed with a minimal test ELF:
its tail loop (goto back to the exit call) ran forever because the process
never died, and the host had to kill it from outside.

Register 22 as an alias of the same handler. The constants are named after
the kernel symbols (RPCS3: 3 = sys_process_exit3, 22 = _sys_process_exit,
26 = _sys_process_exit2, so no 'EXIT2' spelling appears), with the leading
underscore of the kernel symbol noted in a comment rather than in the name.
Compiler-agnostic; two files.

Verified: the same ELF now exits cleanly (sys_process_exit(code=0), host
exit code 0) with a plain MSVC build, and its sys_fs output stays
byte-identical to a fresh RPCS3 run. The change is a plain table entry;
clang/GCC builds are unaffected by construction.

ce9ea45331fc6c88b8b77ff3d20fd837a02bea66.message:
cellPad: a port with no controller reports centred sticks, not zero

cellPadInit zeroed the host state, and with the SDL2 backend (every
non-Windows build) and no controller plugged in nothing ever set the
sticks again. Port 0 is served with no device behind it, so titles read
all four axes as 0: both sticks pushed to the top-left corner. Windows
was spared only because its keyboard fallback writes 128 on every poll.

In Twisted Metal the car drove itself in circles and the chase camera
pitched up at the sky, so the player's own vehicle left the screen within
seconds of a match starting. With the sticks held at 128 (PAD_STICK) the
car stays in front of the camera for the whole match.

pad_host_release() puts a port at rest (no buttons, sticks at 128) at
init and whenever a backend finds no device on it, which also stops an
unplugged pad from keeping its last report.

ps3recomp_host --audio-pad, which CI runs on Linux and macOS with no
controller, now reads port 0 and requires all four sticks at 128. With
master's cellPad.c it reads 0 on each and fails.

d5759c227b426baeb97eb3e4078f091db5500a11.message:
cellSysutil: ps3_host_quit, for the window's close button and Cmd+Q

Closing the game's window stopped the presents and left the game
running with no window until it was killed, and Cmd+Q did nothing: the
host turns a plain run loop with no app menu, so AppKit had no Quit to
send it to.

ps3_host_quit does what the console's Quit Game does. Every registered
sysutil callback gets CELL_SYSUTIL_REQUEST_EXITGAME on the title's next
poll, and a title that tidies up and calls sys_process_exit ends there.

ended for it with exit(0), so stdio is flushed and the atexit handlers
run, but never while a save is being written: cellSaveData counts the
saves in flight (ps3_savedata_busy), and the quit waits up to 10 s for
that to reach 0. It runs on its own thread, so the caller returns at
once, and a second request is ignored.

template on a closed window.

d682e9c49e2bfbbb7fb30f003acaa3a9e46d4f15.message:
rsx_d3d12: draw indexed triangle lists with their indices

The VP path expanded every indexed draw into a triangle list, copying the
256-byte converted vertex once per index reference. God of War HD gameplay
makes 6.4M references a second to 2.0M distinct vertices, about 2,300
indexed draws a frame, so the drain wrote ~1.6 GB/s into the upload heap
and the indexed uploads took ~20 ms of a 55 ms frame.

Indexed TRIANGLES now convert each distinct vertex once, straight into the
vertex buffer, and keep their indices in a new per-frame u32 index buffer
(vp_ib, double-buffered by frame parity like vp_vb). The record carries
the index range and is drawn with DrawIndexedInstanced, base vertex at
the run's first vertex. Batches that the list path merged (a BEGIN/END
stream cut into counts that are not multiples of 3) continue the same
run: they share its vertices and append indices. A run that would leave
the tables (index >= 2^20) or overflow the buffers falls back to the list
path, as do the other primitives. VTX_LIST=1 restores the expansion.

VTX_STATS=1 reports, every 5 s, draws by primitive, index references
against distinct vertices, conversions, attribute formats and the time
the indexed uploads take.

Gameplay: indexed uploads ~20 ms -> ~12 ms a frame, 18.2 -> 20.6 fps
(VTX_LIST=1 against the default, same build).

d7054ab6a820c28ec38c00393e9073d8f7402119.message:
spu: estimates, interpolate and float/int conversions four lanes at a time with AVX2

spu_fi, spu_frest, spu_frsqest, spu_cflts, spu_cfltu, spu_csflt and
spu_cuflt computed one lane at a time, while fa/fm/fma already have an
AVX2 path. frest followed by fi is how SPU code divides, so the scalar
loops sit in the middle of the hot loops of lifted jobs.

Each instruction's lane rule is integer work on the bit fields, so the
vector forms are exact by construction and no lane falls back:
- fi: the 33-bit fixed-point magnitude on 64-bit lanes, then one
  normalising shift picked per lane;
- frest/frsqest: the fraction tables read with a gather;
- cflts/cfltu: the significand shifted with per-lane variable shifts,
  saturated with compares;
- csflt/cuflt: the integer's exact double gives its top bit and the next
  23 bits, truncated.

The scalar versions stay as spu_*_ref and are still used without AVX2.
test_spu_float_est.c checks every one bit for bit against them (random
words, normal/extended-range boundaries, zeros, denormals, integers of
every magnitude, every scale immediate); linux.yml runs it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

daa17fbccb66d40e67197bdbf1e16f3bb9a9cc39.message:
ppu_loader: re-check the reservation once the lock-line lock is held

stwcx./stdcx. check the caller's reservation, then take the lock-line lock
for a line an SPU has reserved, then CAS. An SPU commit that lands
between the check and the lock breaks the reservation (via
ppu_resv_break_line, under that lock) too late to be seen, and the CAS
goes ahead on a line whose other words just changed. Re-check under the
lock.

dc37f00b2d8c883b3b1f3eb45445d40adfc779f4.message:
sysPrxForUser lwmutex: an atomic lock word; the semaphore only wakes

Every sys_lwmutex_lock and _unlock went through a Win32 semaphore, two
kernel calls a pair even when nobody else wanted the lock. On the PS3
an uncontended lwmutex is a few atomic operations in user space. God of
War HD makes about 320,000 pairs in one frame when the first fight's
next wave spawns, and that frame took 360 ms.

Each slot now has a state word: 0 free, 1 held, 2 held with a waiter.
Lock is a compare-and-swap 0 -> 1, unlock an exchange to 0; only a
contended lock sleeps on the semaphore (now a wake channel that starts
empty), and only an unlock that finds 2 posts it. A waiter that times
out leaves the word at 2, so a later unlock may post a wake nobody
takes; the next waiter consumes it and waits again. Recursion, timeouts
(ETIMEDOUT), trylock (EBUSY), unlock from another thread and unlock of
a free lock behave as before. sys_lwcond_wait releases and re-takes the
lock through the same two helpers; tools/test_lwcond_layout.py stubs
them.

God of War HD: HLE time in that frame 200 -> 66 ms (traced), the frame
354 -> 234 ms, and the boot-time stalls at 21.8 s and 27.5 s about a
fifth shorter. The rendering check passes.

ddf65a66d17efe396ec7594c9555e99b098eb895.message:
vulkan: VK_DRAW_BATCH=1 records engine draws, depth snapshots, texture uploads and clears into one submission

Every engine draw used to submit its own command buffer and wait on a fence,
because the vertex, index and uniform buffers and the descriptor set are
single objects rewritten per draw. With VK_DRAW_BATCH=1 a draw takes slices
of three host-visible ring buffers and a descriptor set from a pool, records
into the open command buffer behind a full memory barrier (render-to-texture
ordering without hazard tracking), and only a pending counter grows. Depth
snapshots copy through a persistent device-local buffer, texture uploads
stage through a ring and record a buffer-to-image copy, and colour and
depth/stencil clears record too. vk_begin, every object destroy, the present
and the engine's submit point flush first, so all other backend work still
sees everything before it complete. VK_DRAW_BATCH_MAX (default 512, max 1024)
caps the draws per submission. Off by default.

eb5c6832611192c72eb52130957e24d743bcbb2f.message:
spu: SPU_IRQWAIT_DIAG reports an SPU waiting for an interrupt that never comes

An SPU that enables interrupts and spins until its handler runs looks,
from outside, like any busy SPU. SPU_IRQWAIT_DIAG=1 reports it: every
2^22 dispatches with interrupts enabled and nothing pending to take (24
lines at most), the pc, the event status and mask and the MFC list-stall
mask and status. SPU_IRQWAIT_LS=<hex> adds 16 bytes of local store, for
the waiter's own state once its layout is known.

In Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) this showed the WWS job manager
waiting for an Sn interrupt whose event bit was already gone.

The dispatch loop calls it only when interrupts are enabled with nothing
pending, behind g_spu_irqwait_diag (an SPU_GATE like g_spu_smc_watch):
-1 until the first call reads the variable, then 0 or 1, so with it off
the loop pays one predictable load.

runtime/spu/tests/test_spu_irqwait_diag.c
(tools/test_spu_irqwait_diag.py): off by default, the gate settles at 0;
on, exactly one report per 2^22 waits, with the expected state.

ec5a7a6f257eb849585140ebd38c73a44b7a4a57.message:
rsx engine: release a depth target's stale snapshot

A depth clear invalidates the sampleable snapshot of a depth target and
the next DEPTH24_D8 read takes a new one, but the old one was never
released. A shadow map cleared and read every frame leaked one backend
texture per frame per depth target. On Metal the object table filled
during play, and every texture created after that came back as 0 and
sampled black. Release the old snapshot when a new one replaces it, and
when the depth target is recreated at a larger size. Metal keeps a
released object until no recorded draw can still name it, and Vulkan
hands back the same handle refilled, which is left alone.

cellVdecOpen wrote the slot index as the handle, so the first decoder a
title opened got handle 0. Some titles treat a 0 handle as "no decoder
open": Killzone 2's movie player
keeps the handle as its "decoder open" flag, its AU submit returns
without calling cellVdecDecodeAu while the handle is 0, and the intro
movie stalls with no AU ever decoded.

The handle is now the slot index plus one. Every entry point maps it
back, 0 and out-of-range handles are rejected with CELL_VDEC_ERROR_ARG,
and the callback receives the handle the title was given.

test_vdec_decode checks that Open never returns 0, that StartSeq(0) and
StartSeq(0xFFFFFFFF) are rejected, and that the callback's first
argument is the handle Open returned.

The runtime's explicit -O2 was tied to Release and RelWithDebInfo, and

with no CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE matched neither, so the whole runtime (FIFO
walker, draw engine, MFC) and every lifted PPU TU compiled at -O0. The

f825519199b20712213504374feedd4586008d9d.message:
cellGcmSys: a resync replays the label releases it skips; re-read a park before leaving it

A FIFO resync moves get straight to put. The fences in the skipped range were
already swept up, but a label release in it was simply lost, and a title
that waits on that label waits for the rest of the run. inFAMOUS 2's light
task kicker waits on a texture-read release (0x1D74) that sits in a
command block an SPU job writes; a jump-park resync that stepped over it
froze the title in its first open-world area.

- After the fence sweep, the skipped range is walked as a command stream:
  each header and its data, NOPs, flip markers and self-JUMP parks stepped
  over, forward JUMPs inside the range followed, stopping at a CALL, a
  RETURN or a word that is not a method header. NV406E SEMAPHORE_OFFSET /
  RELEASE (0x64/0x6C) are replayed into the label window as the walker
  does, and the NV4097 semaphore context, offset and back-end /
  texture-read releases (0x01A4, 0x1D6C, 0x1D70, 0x1D74) go through
  rsx_process_method, so they land where the walker would have written
  them (label window or main memory, byte swap included). Draws in the
  range are still dropped.
- The jump-park resync reads the park word again first. An SPU job that
  fills an Edge-style command-buffer hole (a self-JUMP until it is
  written) can land between the pass's read and the resync, which would
  then jump over the commands just written.

libs/video/tests/test_gcm_resync_labels.c (run by
tools/test_gcm_resync_labels.py) parks the walker in front of a NOP, an
NV406E release, a forward JUMP over non-command words and an NV4097
release, waits out GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS and checks that the resync wrote the
first label and handed the second to rsx_process_method.

#504 replaces two plain `plan->base_offset + fetch->desc.offset` additions
with rsx_dsp_resolve_vertex_offset(), which wraps at 28 bits as the hardware
does. One of its two hunks merged clean -- the prefix used to compute
stable_base. The other conflicted, because #458 (earlier in this wave)
restructured the fetch loop from per-vertex to attribute-major and #504's
hunk patches the per-vertex form it was written against.

longer reach. Verified afterwards that both base_offset uses in the file go
through rsx_dsp_resolve_vertex_offset(): a wrap applied on one of two paths
is worse than none, because the two would disagree about where a vertex is.

Merge PR #444: verified job-module regions and embedded SPU program coverage (@tekulvw)

The interesting conflict of the wave so far. #444 refactors the --jobmods
loop in tools/lift_jobmods.py into a lift_module() helper (so --engine-elf
can share it) and adds reachable()/module_code_end()/module_seeds(). #488
(@erikomis, wave 3) rewrote that same loop for a different reason: the LS
address a module is linked for comes out of its header at +0x28, and is
0x7000 rather than 0x4000 for some of Resistance: Fall of Man's modules.
Lifting those at 0x4000 puts every lifted address 0x3000 short of where
the job manager runs them.

#444 was written against master, so lift_module() and module_seeds()
hardcode BASE throughout -- the ELF wrap base, --base, the seed window,
base + 0x30, the manual-link and switch-table scans, and the manifest's
"base" field. Taking #444's side as written compiles, runs, and silently
reverts #488 on exactly the modules #488 exists for. Nothing in CI would
have caught it: no test ships a 0x7000 module.

Resolved by keeping #444's refactor and threading #488's base through it.
module_seeds(raw, base=BASE) and lift_module(..., base=BASE), and the
--jobmods loop passes base=module_base(raw). module_base() itself is #488's,
unchanged.

The --engine-elf path keeps BASE, and that is correct rather than an
oversight: find_engine_modules() only accepts an image whose header says
+0x28 == BASE, so every module it yields is linked at 0x4000 by
construction. The same goes for the code-slice and region-registration
arithmetic in lift_engine_elf()/emit_register_verified().

Dropped on the way through: #488's "sha = name.split('_')[1]", assigned and
never read.

tools/build_spu_workloads.py is a plain both-added conflict in the argparse
block -- #549's --merge-chunks and #444's --handled/--image-ids. All three
kept.

fb89154950c6ffb10e3d92e06da99258af5d363a.message:
rsx_d3d12: depth surfaces per zeta offset, readable as textures

The guest path had one depth buffer, cleared whenever a pass changed
targets. God of War HD keeps two depth surfaces: the scene's 2x-AA one
at 0x17F0000 and a resolved one at 0x2240000. Its resolve pass samples
the AA depth as an A8R8G8B8 texture to compute fog and the alpha the
shadow pass blends with. That surface never existed in guest memory,
so the read returned nothing: distant cliffs came out black and the
whole scene too dark.

- Each zeta offset gets its own D24S8 surface (R24G8_TYPELESS, so it
  can also be read). It keeps its contents across passes and is
  cleared only by the guest's own clears. Passes without a depth
  surface keep the shared buffer as before.
- A colour target of NONE with a depth surface binds no RTV (a
  depth-only pass). The register now defaults to target A, as libgcm
  sets it, so a title that never writes it still draws.
- A draw sampling a depth surface reads a colour copy refreshed just
  before it when the depth has changed since the last copy: the bytes
  a guest sees in memory for D24S8 read as A8R8G8B8 (A = depth[23:16],
  R = depth[15:8], G = depth[7:0], B = stencil).
- The pool grows a surface for a larger pass, never shrinks it, and
  evicts an entry no pass used this frame.

fe84fa460d078b41fdad94f702554ea41a01ebe8.message:
Merge PR #436: memoize indirect-dispatch registry lookups per thread (@tekulvw)

The largest semantic conflict in the release so far. #436 was written
against master, where spu_lifted_lookup() was a single spu_lookup() and
spu_indirect_branch() carried the identity-ownership order inline. Wave 4
changed both: #419/#420 moved the ownership order into
spu_lifted_lookup_full(), and #481 put a per-thread dispatch cache in
front of it in spu_lifted_lookup().

Taken as written, #436 replaces spu_lifted_lookup()'s whole body with
"return spu_lookup_memoized(lsa, ctx ? ctx->image_id : 0)" and replaces
spu_indirect_branch()'s call with its own inline identity walk. That
compiles, and it deletes #481's dispatch cache outright while forking the
ownership order into a second copy that would then drift from the
resolver's. Three PRs' worth of wave-4 work, silently undone.

So the structure stays wave 4's and #436 goes in underneath it, which is
where it belongs and what it was for: spu_lifted_lookup_full() now makes
every one of its registry probes through spu_lookup_memoized() instead of
spu_lookup(). The resolver issues up to three probes per resolution
(resident_task, then resident_ovl, then image_id) and the first two
usually miss, and a generation-keyed memo that caches misses is exactly
the thing that stops each of those walking the address's hash chain again
-- which is the cost #436's own commentary describes.

The two layers compose rather than overlap: #481's cache is keyed on the
resolved answer for a (context, residency) pair and only stores hits;
#436's is keyed on (address, image) at the registry and stores misses too.
Definition order checked -- memo at 1633, resolver at 1673, cache at 1747.

Tests: #436 adds test_registry_lookup_memo and wave 4 added
test_verified_resident_code_regions, test_resident_interpreter_rejoin and
test_dispatch_cache. git offered them as one conflict because they share a
trailer; all four are kept and all four now run from main(). Verified that
every test defined in the file is called

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

HLE implementations of the PS3 system libraries, written for this project. RPCS3 is a behavioural reference, not a code source. Most modules are complete. The ones still marked Partial are the media decoders (cellVdec, cellAdec, cellDmux, cellAtrac, cellAdecAtrac3p) and cellSpurs. [docs/MODULE_STATUS.md](docs/MODULE_STATUS.md) has one row per module and is the source for the counts.

words past the new ones were the previous lap's, which also decode as a

every 200 ms, only for a start less than 64 KB behind; GOWA_PARK_REWIND=0
turns it off. Holds with the bad word at the walker also print the jump
history (and the SPU PUT ring with GOWA_PUTRING).

Controller: diagonals reach the dodge, and taps and flicks shorter than a frame are not lost

  diagonal read 61% per axis. Now a radial deadzone rescaled to the full range, and RPCS3's squircle

  centre before the next read, never reached the game. Reads are stamped with the game's frame count

  250 ms) is still reported, so the logic sees it once; a long hold is released at once. A sampler thread reads
