# God of War: Ascension — port nativo para PC

> **Projeto de fãs, sem fins lucrativos, sem relação com a Sony.** *God of War* é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. Este repositório **não contém o jogo** nem o firmware: você precisa da **sua própria cópia** do jogo (BCUS98232). O **update 1.04** e o **firmware oficial do PS3** são **gratuitos**, baixados direto da Sony (links em [Como jogar](#como-jogar)).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Para jogar, baixe o [Otavix Launcher](https://github.com/otavix010/otavix-launcher/releases/latest).** Ele baixa este port, gera o jogo no seu PC e o mantém atualizado sozinho. O port recebe **cerca de 6 atualizações por dia**, feitas a partir dos reports e pedidos dos jogadores: para relatar um problema ou pedir algo, use **"Reportar problema"** na página do jogo no launcher. O relatório já vai com o log, as configurações e as fotos, e é por ele que as correções saem mais rápido.
>
> **To play, download the [Otavix Launcher](https://github.com/otavix010/otavix-launcher/releases/latest).** It downloads this port, makes the game on your PC and keeps it updated by itself. The port gets **about 6 updates a day**, driven by players' reports and requests: to report a problem or ask for something, use **"Report a problem"** on the game's page in the launcher. The report carries the log, the settings and the screenshots, and that is how fixes come out fastest.

![Capítulo 16 a 66 FPS num Ryzen 7 9800X3D](docs/imagens/cap16_9800x3d.png)

[English summary below](#english-summary)

## O que é

Um port **nativo** do *God of War: Ascension* (PS3, 2013) para Windows. Não é um emulador: o código do jogo é **traduzido para C/C++ e compilado** para x86-64 (recompilação estática), em cima do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) do sp00nznet.

Como o código do jogo não pode ser distribuído, **o seu PC gera e compila a parte do jogo a partir da sua cópia**. Um comando só faz tudo.

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Fase 1, luta com a Fúria](docs/imagens/fase1_dodge.png) | ![Fase 1, close da Fúria](docs/imagens/fase1_furia.png) |

## Como jogar

### Recomendado: pelo Otavix Launcher

O [Otavix Launcher](https://github.com/otavix010/otavix-launcher/releases/latest) junta tudo num lugar só: baixa este port, confere se o Python e as ferramentas do Visual Studio estão instalados, pede só a pasta do disco (o update 1.04 e o firmware o gerador baixa da Sony; quem já tiver os arquivos, inclusive o PS3UPDAT.PUP, pode escolhê-los), gera o jogo para a sua CPU e abre com as opções de vídeo e os saves. Quando sai uma versão nova, ele avisa e atualiza. É o jeito mais simples; o caminho à mão vem a seguir.

### À mão

**1. O que você precisa ter:** só a sua cópia do jogo. O update 1.04 e o firmware do PS3 são gratuitos, e o gerador baixa os dois sozinho dos servidores oficiais da Sony (o RPCS3 não é mais necessário).

| O quê | Onde conseguir |
|---|---|
| **O jogo**: a cópia do disco do *God of War: Ascension* **BCUS98232** (EUA) | A sua cópia, numa pasta que contenha `PS3_GAME`, ou ainda compactada (`.7z`, `.zip`, `.rar` ou `.iso` decriptada): o gerador extrai uma vez (uns 35 GB livres). |
| **O update 1.04** (grátis, ~235 MB) | **Baixado sozinho pelo gerador.** Se preferir baixar você mesmo: **[o update 1.04 no servidor da Sony](http://b0.ww.np.dl.playstation.net/tppkg/np/BCUS98232/BCUS98232_T76/5525fbb7b6b5456d/UP9000-BCUS98232_00-GOWABDPATCH00001-A0104-V0100-PE.pkg)** (o arquivo `.pkg`; SHA-1 do arquivo `5a94c17aa07cb5181a505d3429c88ea3d9f4e4d0`). Tem que ser a **1.04**: as versões 1.05 em diante não servem. Se você já instalou a 1.04 no RPCS3, serve também a pasta `RPCS3\dev_hdd0\game\BCUS98232`. |
| **O firmware oficial do PS3** (grátis, ~200 MB) | **Baixado sozinho pelo gerador**, do servidor de atualização do PS3. Se preferir baixar você mesmo: na [página oficial da PlayStation](https://www.playstation.com/pt-br/support/hardware/ps3/system-software/), botão **"Baixar atualização do PS3"** (o arquivo `PS3UPDAT.PUP`, que o gerador aceita direto). Também serve a pasta do RPCS3 com o firmware instalado. |

**2. Instale as ferramentas (uma vez só)**, num terminal:
```
winget install Python.Python.3.12
winget install Microsoft.VisualStudio.2022.BuildTools --override "--quiet --wait --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Workload.VCTools --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Llvm.Clang --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.CMake.Project --includeRecommended"
```

**3. Baixe este repositório** (botão *Code > Download ZIP*, ou `git clone`) e extraia numa pasta **sem espaços no caminho**, por exemplo `C:\gow-ascension-pc`.

**4. Clique duas vezes em `gerar.cmd`** e escolha a pasta do disco. Ele faz o resto sozinho:
- confere as ferramentas e baixa o FFmpeg;
- baixa o update 1.04 e o firmware oficiais (ou usa os seus: `-Update` e `-Firmware`);
- prepara os arquivos do jogo, sem copiar os 34 GB do disco;
- decripta o executável;
- traduz e compila, escolhendo a build certa para a sua CPU.

Num Ryzen 7 9800X3D (8 núcleos) leva ~5 minutos; num PC de 4 núcleos, bem mais. Se parar no meio, rode de novo: ele continua de onde parou.

Versão nova do port: baixe por cima e rode `gerar.cmd -RefazerDe 4` num terminal. Ele refaz só a tradução e a compilação, sem repetir o disco, o update e o firmware.

**5. Jogue com `jogar.cmd`.** O log fica em `out\jogo.log` e os saves em `saves\`.

Opções (defina antes de abrir o `jogar.cmd`; pelo launcher, elas ficam nas configurações do jogo):
- `GOWA_FLIP_HZ`: limitador, padrão 60. Acima de 60 o jogo **acelera** (parte da lógica avança por quadro); `0` = sem limite, com teto de 240.
- `GOWA_RES_SCALE`: resolução interna, 1 = 720p, 2 = 1440p, 3 = 4K.
- `GOWA_OSD=1`: medidor de desempenho na tela (FPS, ms por quadro, uso e temperatura da CPU e da GPU, VRAM e RAM; a temperatura da CPU some quando o Windows só tem a zona térmica da ACPI, que em muitos desktops fica parada). Vem desligado; **F10** liga e desliga durante o jogo (`GOWA_OSD_TECLA=0` desativa a tecla).
- **Tela cheia sem bordas:** **F11** ou **Alt+Enter** (também o botão maximizar, ou Win+Cima) cobrem o monitor mantendo 16:9, com faixas pretas em telas de outro formato; F11, Alt+Enter ou **Esc** voltam para a janela. `GOWA_TELA_CHEIA=1` já abre assim.
- `GOWA_AUDIO_MUTE=1`: sem som.

O jogo grava um resumo de desempenho em `desempenho.json`, ao lado do exe (ou em `GOWA_PERF_JSON`): CPU, GPU e FPS médio, p1 e mínimo do tempo jogando. Não é enviado a lugar nenhum; o launcher só manda, e só com a sua autorização.

Detalhes de cada etapa, e como fazer à mão: [docs/COMO_GERAR.md](docs/COMO_GERAR.md).

## Como funciona

O PS3 tem um processador central (PPU, PowerPC), seis co-processadores vetoriais (SPUs) e uma GPU (RSX):

- **PPU**: o executável do jogo é traduzido para C++ função por função pelo tradutor do ps3recomp, com os remendos do port aplicados por scripts.
- **SPU**: os programas das SPUs (jobs do SPURS, o EDGE de geometria, as tarefas de malha, o gerenciador de políticas) também viram C. Os laços mais pesados podem virar **núcleos vetoriais** gerados por scripts (AVX-512 ou AVX2), conferidos bit a bit. O código que o jogo carrega nas SPUs em tempo de execução e que não foi traduzido roda num interpretador.
- **SPURS**: a biblioteca de agendamento das SPUs (libsre) roda o código do firmware oficial (LLE).
- **RSX**: os comandos da GPU são desenhados em **Direct3D 12**, com os shaders do RSX convertidos para HLSL.
- **Áudio**: WASAPI, até 8 canais. Vídeos (MPEG-2) com FFmpeg.

## Estado atual

- Abre, passa pelos vídeos e menus, carrega saves e roda a **fase 1** e o **Capítulo 16** (a parte mais pesada que testamos) com imagem correta.
- **60 FPS travados** nas duas cenas num Ryzen 7 9800X3D, com o limitador ligado (padrão).
- O jogo inteiro, do começo ao fim, **ainda não foi verificado**.
- Só a versão **BCUS98232 (EUA) 1.04**: o `gerar.ps1` confere o executável e recusa outras.

## Desempenho medido

**Capítulo 16** (a cena mais pesada) e **fase 1**, em FPS de jogo, **sem o limitador de 60** (é como dá para comparar máquinas). **O hardware muda tudo**: o gargalo é a CPU, e CPUs com AVX-512 rodam bem mais rápido.

| PC | CPU | GPU | Build | Cap. 16 | Fase 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Principal | Ryzen 7 9800X3D (8/16, AVX-512) | RTX 5080 | AVX-512 | **~68** | **~84** |
| PC teste 2 | Core i5-11400F (6/12, AVX-512) | RX 9060 XT | AVX-512 (Rocket Lake) | **~32** (1ª execução) | — |
| Notebook | Core i5-10300H (4/8, sem AVX-512, ~2,8 GHz sustentado) | GTX 1650 | sem AVX-512 | **~8** | — |

> **A build que o `gerar.cmd` produz agora tem o mesmo desempenho da nossa.** Os passes de desempenho que aplicamos ao longo do desenvolvimento entram na geração (`scripts/otimizar.py`). No notebook, no cap. 16, a build gerada empatou com a nossa (antes da automação, ela dava 3,9 FPS). Depois disso, com a fixação de threads desligada em CPUs com menos de 12 processadores lógicos, ela chegou a **~8 FPS** (média de 200 s de fase, rodadas intercaladas). O PGO fica de fora; o que ainda difere está no fim de [docs/COMO_GERAR.md](docs/COMO_GERAR.md).

![Capítulo 16 no notebook com a build sem AVX-512](docs/imagens/cap16_notebook_portatil.png)

O que medimos num PC fraco (4 núcleos, sem AVX-512), o que ajudou, o que não ajudou e como medir: [docs/DESEMPENHO_PC_FRACO.md](docs/DESEMPENHO_PC_FRACO.md).

## Requisitos

- **Windows 10/11 64 bits** e GPU com **Direct3D 12**.
- **CPU com AVX2** (Intel Haswell em diante, AMD Zen em diante). **Com AVX-512** (Ryzen 7000/9000, Intel 11ª geração desktop) é muito mais rápido; o `gerar.ps1` escolhe sozinho.
- 16 GB de RAM. Espaço: ~3 GB para a geração e a build (o disco do jogo não é copiado).

## Problemas conhecidos

- **Engasgo na primeira entrada de cada área**: os pipelines de shader são compilados na hora e ficam em cache; da segunda vez some.
- **Sem o limitador de 60** o jogo **acelera**, porque parte da lógica avança por quadro.
- **Trava do leitor da GPU em PC lento**: corrigida. O leitor executava blocos de comandos que a PPU ainda escrevia; na variante rara, ele saía de passo com o bloco (ficava no meio dos dados de um comando) e agora volta ao início do trecho. No notebook: antes, 4 travas em 9 rodadas; depois, 17 rodadas sem nenhuma. Se a imagem congelar, relate com o `out\jogo.log` (procure `[park-settle]`).
- Travas raras de carregamento ainda em investigação.
- PC fraco (4 núcleos, sem AVX-512) roda, mas abaixo de 10 FPS nas partes pesadas.

## Licença e créditos

- **Nosso código e ferramentas: [MIT](LICENSE).** O RPCS3 (GPL-2.0) foi usado como referência de comportamento; o código foi revisado linha a linha contra o do RPCS3 e nenhum trecho foi copiado. A única coincidência literal são duas tabelas de valores medidos do hardware, herdadas do ps3recomp.
- **[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp)**, de Ned Heller (sp00nznet), MIT: o tradutor, o runtime e o motor de desenho em que o port se apoia. Ele vem dentro deste repositório, em `ps3recomp/`: o primeiro commit importa a v0.15.0 sem mudanças, e as nossas alterações vêm em commits separados logo depois.
- **`scripts/gpl/unself.py` e `scripts/gpl/pup_libsre.py` são GPL-2.0** (`scripts/gpl/COPYING`): o decriptador de SELF, que segue o `unself.cpp` do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3), e o que tira o `libsre.sprx` do `PS3UPDAT.PUP`, que segue o instalador de firmware do RPCS3. Os dois rodam como programas separados.
- **Chaves**: nenhuma chave foi criada por nós. As de decriptação de executáveis são lidas do código-fonte do RPCS3: o `gerar.ps1` baixa dois arquivos dele (`key_vault.cpp/.h`, numa versão fixa) para `dl\rpcs3_chaves`, ou usa os que você indicar com `-ChavesRpcs3`. A KLIC do jogo sai da sua própria cópia. O `ps3recomp` embutido traz, como o original, chaves públicas de formatos do PS3.
- **[FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org)** (LGPL), baixado pelo `gerar.ps1` dos builds do BtbN, para os vídeos.
- God of War e God of War: Ascension são marcas da Sony Interactive Entertainment. Este projeto não é afiliado nem endossado pela Sony.

---

## English summary

A **native PC port** of *God of War: Ascension* (PS3), made by **static recompilation**: the game's PPU and SPU code is translated to C/C++ and compiled for x86-64 on top of [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). The GPU command stream is rendered with Direct3D 12, and SPURS runs the official libsre module (LLE).

**Easiest: the [Otavix Launcher](https://github.com/otavix010/otavix-launcher/releases/latest)**, which downloads this port, asks for your folders, generates the game for your CPU and starts it. **Bring your own disc**: no game code or data and no firmware here. You need your own copy of the game (BCUS98232). Update 1.04 and the official PS3 firmware are free from Sony, and `gerar.cmd` downloads both from Sony's servers by itself (or use your own: [update 1.04 .pkg](http://b0.ww.np.dl.playstation.net/tppkg/np/BCUS98232/BCUS98232_T76/5525fbb7b6b5456d/UP9000-BCUS98232_00-GOWABDPATCH00001-A0104-V0100-PE.pkg) (must be exactly 1.04), and `PS3UPDAT.PUP` from [PlayStation's PS3 system software page](https://www.playstation.com/en-us/support/hardware/ps3/system-software/); RPCS3 is no longer needed). Install Python and the Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools with Clang (commands above), download this repository to a path without spaces, double-click **`gerar.cmd`** (it asks for the disc folder, then downloads the update and firmware, decrypts your copy, translates and builds; ~4 minutes on an 8-core Ryzen 7 9800X3D), then play with **`jogar.cmd`**.

Status: boots, menus, chapter 1 and chapter 16 play with correct image, 60 FPS locked on a Ryzen 7 9800X3D; the full game is not verified yet. Performance is CPU-bound and much better with AVX-512: ~68 FPS uncapped in chapter 16 on a 9800X3D, ~32 on an i5-11400F, ~8 on a 4-core laptop without AVX-512. The build `gerar.cmd` produces includes the same performance passes as ours (`scripts/otimizar.py`); only PGO is left out. Thread pinning is now off on CPUs with fewer than 12 logical processors (+4% on the laptop), and the GPU command reader no longer hangs on slow PCs.

License: our code is MIT; ps3recomp is MIT (Ned Heller); `scripts/gpl/unself.py` and `scripts/gpl/pup_libsre.py` are GPL-2.0 (they follow RPCS3's unself.cpp and firmware installer). Decryption keys are read from RPCS3's source (downloaded at a pinned commit). *God of War* is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment; this is a non-commercial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony.

06856e78122b2c0bfff43dc46674bff6aebff8dc.message:
EDGE nativo: laço EC08 do E550 (skinning de 4 ossos) em AVX-512, menos a última volta

O laço em software pipelining mistura 4 ossos por vértice (pesos u8 * 1/255, 3 linhas da paleta),
grava as linhas com a coluna w trocada (selb r97/r84) e transforma a posição no lugar. O nativo faz os
pares 0..n-2 (dois por vez em 16 faixas, com as contas exatas do runtime: entrada de expoente 0 como
zero, RZ embutido, formas cruas sem achatar, |r| >= 0x7F7FFFFF pelo caminho exato) e deixa nos 43
registradores vivos da entrada do laço (scripts_edge/vivos_laco.py) os valores do último par, com as
mesmas operações do fim da volta; o laço traduzido roda a última volta. Gancho novo 'antes_vk' no
edge_nativo.py (entra antes do núcleo vk do laço). Sem AVX-512, só o caminho exato por u128.
Conferência: 300/300 nas gravações da fase 1 e do capítulo 16. Jobs do EDGE na reprodução da fase 1:
2,9 -> 2,4/2,5 ms com as 4 partes (eram 2,7 com as 3 de antes). GOWA_EC08_VETOR=0 desliga o caminho
vetorial; GOWA_EC08_STATS=1 conta as chamadas.

áudio: prioridade alta para a SPU que mixa o som; marca só para medir (sem espera)

A espera pelo jogo (98835b5) piorou muito com o processador apertado (691 buracos contra 38 em 80 s):
o escritor do GoW anda com o índice de leitura e nunca escreve o bloco que está sendo lido. Medido
com a marca: o jogo escreve 6 a 7 blocos adiantado, por PUT de DMA de uma SPU (o workload de áudio
da SPURS), então o silêncio vem dessa SPU sem CPU por mais de ~37 ms. Agora a SPU que roda o
workload que escreve nos anéis do cellAudio fica em THREAD_PRIORITY_HIGHEST enquanto ele roda
(GOWA_AUDIO_SPU_PRIO=0 desliga). A marca continua, só para o log: blocos atrasados e o
adiantamento do jogo (média, mínimo e histograma) na linha [audio].

Biblioteca de PSOs gravada fora da thread de desenho (report 858; provável 875/672)

A biblioteca de pipelines do D3D12 (até 65 MB) era serializada e gravada em
disco na thread do RSX, toda vez que uma área nova trazia PSOs novos. O desenho
parava até o disco terminar: congelamentos de vários segundos com o SSD em uso
alto (858) e, quando passava de ~5 s, o Windows marcava a janela como "não
respondendo"; fechada assim, ela sai com 0xCFFFFFFF (875, 672; nos dois o log
para logo depois de uma gravação). Agora uma thread de trabalho serializa e
grava (o ID3D12PipelineLibrary se sincroniza sozinho), uma gravação por vez, e
o log mostra quanto cada parte levou.

Validação: cap16 200 s a 1x e a 3x; série de boot 11/11 sem trava (antigo e
novo iguais); luta do chefe (heca975) 230 s sem trava, fps igual.

98835b5cddcbed057bfb9029b9df4b6014b76bb6.message:
áudio: espera pelo jogo, thread com MMCSS e log de saúde do som (reports 285, 286, 259, 299, 346)

O relógio do dispositivo guiava a leitura do anel do jogo sem saber se o jogo já tinha escrito o
próximo bloco: num PC em que a tarefa de áudio do jogo (um job de SPU) atrasa, o bloco era lido
antes e tocava como silêncio, um engasgo em qualquer tamanho de buffer. Agora cada bloco consumido
guarda uma marca (um NaN) na última amostra; com o próximo bloco ainda marcado e mais de dois
blocos na fila do dispositivo, a leitura espera o jogo (é aí que o buffer de 100 ms passa a dar
tempo a ele), e um bloco lido ainda marcado conta como atrasado e toca silêncio sem a marca chegar
à mistura. GOWA_AUDIO_ESPERA=0 volta ao comportamento antigo.
A thread de mixagem entra no MMCSS "Pro Audio" com prioridade time-critical (o Xeon do 285 tem
todos os núcleos ocupados pelas SPUs). No log do jogo: [audio] a cada 10 s quando houve atraso ou
dispositivo vazio (senão a cada 60 s), e uma linha quando o jogo para de escrever o som por 3 s.

# God of War: Ascension — port nativo para PC

> **Projeto de fãs, sem fins lucrativos, sem relação com a Sony.** *God of War* é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. Este repositório **não contém o jogo** nem o firmware: você precisa da **sua própria cópia** do jogo (BCUS98232). O **update 1.04** e o **firmware oficial do PS3** são **gratuitos**, baixados direto da Sony (links em [Como jogar](#como-jogar)).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Para jogar, baixe o [Otavix Launcher](https://github.com/otavix010/otavix-launcher/releases/latest).** Ele baixa este port, gera o jogo no seu PC e o mantém atualizado sozinho. O port recebe **cerca de 6 atualizações por dia**, feitas a partir dos reports e pedidos dos jogadores: para relatar um problema ou pedir algo, use **"Reportar problema"** na página do jogo no launcher. O relatório já vai com o log, as configurações e as fotos, e é por ele que as correções saem mais rápido.
>
> **To play, download the [Otavix Launcher](https://github.com/otavix010/otavix-launcher/releases/latest).** It downloads this port, makes the game on your PC and keeps it updated by itself. The port gets **about 6 updates a day**, driven by players' reports and requests: to report a problem or ask for something, use **"Report a problem"** on the game's page in the launcher. The report carries the log, the settings and the screenshots, and that is how fixes come out fastest.

![Capítulo 16 a 66 FPS num Ryzen 7 9800X3D](docs/imagens/cap16_9800x3d.png)

[English summary below](#english-summary)

## O que é

Um port **nativo** do *God of War: Ascension* (PS3, 2013) para Windows. Não é um emulador: o código do jogo é **traduzido para C/C++ e compilado** para x86-64 (recompilação estática), em cima do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) do sp00nznet.

Como o código do jogo não pode ser distribuído, **o seu PC gera e compila a parte do jogo a partir da sua cópia**. Um comando só faz tudo.

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Fase 1, luta com a Fúria](docs/imagens/fase1_dodge.png) | ![Fase 1, close da Fúria](docs/imagens/fase1_furia.png) |

## Como jogar

### Recomendado: pelo Otavix Launcher

O [Otavix Launcher](https://github.com/otavix010/otavix-launcher/releases/latest) junta tudo num lugar só: baixa este port, confere se o Python e as ferramentas do Visual Studio estão instalados, pede só a pasta do disco (o update 1.04 e o firmware o gerador baixa da Sony; quem já tiver os arquivos, inclusive o PS3UPDAT.PUP, pode escolhê-los), gera o jogo para a sua CPU e abre com as opções de vídeo e os saves. Quando sai uma versão nova, ele avisa e atualiza. É o jeito mais simples; o caminho à mão vem a seguir.

### À mão

**1. O que você precisa ter:** só a sua cópia do jogo. O update 1.04 e o firmware do PS3 são gratuitos, e o gerador baixa os dois sozinho dos servidores oficiais da Sony (o RPCS3 não é mais necessário).

| O quê | Onde conseguir |
|---|---|
| **O jogo**: a cópia do disco do *God of War: Ascension* **BCUS98232** (EUA) | A sua cópia, numa pasta que contenha `PS3_GAME`, ou ainda compactada (`.7z`, `.zip`, `.rar` ou `.iso` decriptada): o gerador extrai uma vez (uns 35 GB livres). |
| **O update 1.04** (grátis, ~235 MB) | **Baixado sozinho pelo gerador.** Se preferir baixar você mesmo: **[o update 1.04 no servidor da Sony](http://b0.ww.np.dl.playstation.net/tppkg/np/BCUS98232/BCUS98232_T76/5525fbb7b6b5456d/UP9000-BCUS98232_00-GOWABDPATCH00001-A0104-V0100-PE.pkg)** (o arquivo `.pkg`; SHA-1 do arquivo `5a94c17aa07cb5181a505d3429c88ea3d9f4e4d0`). Tem que ser a **1.04**: as versões 1.05 em diante não servem. Se você já instalou a 1.04 no RPCS3, serve também a pasta `RPCS3\dev_hdd0\game\BCUS98232`. |
| **O firmware oficial do PS3** (grátis, ~200 MB) | **Baixado sozinho pelo gerador**, do servidor de atualização do PS3. Se preferir baixar você mesmo: na [página oficial da PlayStation](https://www.playstation.com/pt-br/support/hardware/ps3/system-software/), botão **"Baixar atualização do PS3"** (o arquivo `PS3UPDAT.PUP`, que o gerador aceita direto). Também serve a pasta do RPCS3 com o firmware instalado. |

**2. Instale as ferramentas (uma vez só)**, num terminal:
```
winget install Python.Python.3.12
winget install Microsoft.VisualStudio.2022.BuildTools --override "--quiet --wait --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Workload.VCTools --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Llvm.Clang --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.CMake.Project --includeRecommended"
```

**3. Baixe este repositório** (botão *Code > Download ZIP*, ou `git clone`) e extraia numa pasta **sem espaços no caminho**, por exemplo `C:\gow-ascension-pc`.

**4. Clique duas vezes em `gerar.cmd`** e escolha a pasta do disco. Ele faz o resto sozinho:
- confere as ferramentas e baixa o FFmpeg;
- baixa o update 1.04 e o firmware oficiais (ou usa os seus: `-Update` e `-Firmware`);
- prepara os arquivos do jogo, sem copiar os 34 GB do disco;
- decripta o executável;
- traduz e compila, escolhendo a build certa para a sua CPU.

Num Ryzen 7 9800X3D (8 núcleos) leva ~5 minutos; num PC de 4 núcleos, bem mais. Se parar no meio, rode de novo: ele continua de onde parou.

Versão nova do port: baixe por cima e rode `gerar.cmd -RefazerDe 4` num terminal. Ele refaz só a tradução e a compilação, sem repetir o disco, o update e o firmware.

**5. Jogue com `jogar.cmd`.** O log fica em `out\jogo.log` e os saves em `saves\`.

Opções (defina antes de abrir o `jogar.cmd`; pelo launcher, elas ficam nas configurações do jogo):
- `GOWA_FLIP_HZ`: limitador, padrão 60. Acima de 60 o jogo **acelera** (parte da lógica avança por quadro); `0` = sem limite, com teto de 240.
- `GOWA_RES_SCALE`: resolução interna, 1 = 720p, 2 = 1440p, 3 = 4K.
- `GOWA_VRR`: VRR (G-SYNC / FreeSync), padrão 1: cada quadro vai para a tela assim que fica pronto, sem esperar a atualização dela. Num monitor sem VRR a imagem pode rasgar em movimento; `0` volta ao vsync (cada quadro espera a tela).
- `GOWA_OSD=1`: medidor de desempenho na tela (FPS, ms por quadro, uso e temperatura da CPU e da GPU, VRAM e RAM; a temperatura da CPU some quando o Windows só tem a zona térmica da ACPI, que em muitos desktops fica parada). Vem desligado; **F10** liga e desliga durante o jogo (`GOWA_OSD_TECLA=0` desativa a tecla).
- **Tela cheia sem bordas:** **F11** ou **Alt+Enter** (também o botão maximizar, ou Win+Cima) cobrem o monitor mantendo 16:9, com faixas pretas em telas de outro formato; F11, Alt+Enter ou **Esc** voltam para a janela. `GOWA_TELA_CHEIA=1` já abre assim.
- `GOWA_AUDIO_MUTE=1`: sem som.

O jogo grava um resumo de desempenho em `desempenho.json`, ao lado do exe (ou em `GOWA_PERF_JSON`): CPU, GPU e FPS médio, p1 e mínimo do tempo jogando. Não é enviado a lugar nenhum; o launcher só manda, e só com a sua autorização.

Detalhes de cada etapa, e como fazer à mão: [docs/COMO_GERAR.md](docs/COMO_GERAR.md).

## Como funciona

O PS3 tem um processador central (PPU, PowerPC), seis co-processadores vetoriais (SPUs) e uma GPU (RSX):

- **PPU**: o executável do jogo é traduzido para C++ função por função pelo tradutor do ps3recomp, com os remendos do port aplicados por scripts.
- **SPU**: os programas das SPUs (jobs do SPURS, o EDGE de geometria, as tarefas de malha, o gerenciador de políticas) também viram C. Os laços mais pesados podem virar **núcleos vetoriais** gerados por scripts (AVX-512 ou AVX2), conferidos bit a bit. O código que o jogo carrega nas SPUs em tempo de execução e que não foi traduzido roda num interpretador.
- **SPURS**: a biblioteca de agendamento das SPUs (libsre) roda o código do firmware oficial (LLE).
- **RSX**: os comandos da GPU são desenhados em **Direct3D 12**, com os shaders do RSX convertidos para HLSL.
- **Áudio**: WASAPI, até 8 canais. Vídeos (MPEG-2) com FFmpeg.

## Estado atual

- Abre, passa pelos vídeos e menus, carrega saves e roda a **fase 1** e o **Capítulo 16** (a parte mais pesada que testamos) com imagem correta.
- **60 FPS travados** nas duas cenas num Ryzen 7 9800X3D, com o limitador ligado (padrão).
- O jogo inteiro, do começo ao fim, **ainda não foi verificado**.
- Só a versão **BCUS98232 (EUA) 1.04**: o `gerar.ps1` confere o executável e recusa outras.

## Desempenho medido

**Capítulo 16** (a cena mais pesada) e **fase 1**, em FPS de jogo, **sem o limitador de 60** (é como dá para comparar máquinas). **O hardware muda tudo**: o gargalo é a CPU, e CPUs com AVX-512 rodam bem mais rápido.

| PC | CPU | GPU | Build | Cap. 16 | Fase 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Principal | Ryzen 7 9800X3D (8/16, AVX-512) | RTX 5080 | AVX-512 | **~68** | **~84** |
| PC teste 2 | Core i5-11400F (6/12, AVX-512) | RX 9060 XT | AVX-512 (Rocket Lake) | **~32** (1ª execução) | — |
| Notebook | Core i5-10300H (4/8, sem AVX-512, ~2,8 GHz sustentado) | GTX 1650 | sem AVX-512 | **~8** | — |

> **A build que o `gerar.cmd` produz agora tem o mesmo desempenho da nossa.** Os passes de desempenho que aplicamos ao longo do desenvolvimento entram na geração (`scripts/otimizar.py`). No notebook, no cap. 16, a build gerada empatou com a nossa (antes da automação, ela dava 3,9 FPS). Depois disso, com a fixação de threads desligada em CPUs com menos de 12 processadores lógicos, ela chegou a **~8 FPS** (média de 200 s de fase, rodadas intercaladas). O PGO fica de fora; o que ainda difere está no fim de [docs/COMO_GERAR.md](docs/COMO_GERAR.md).

![Capítulo 16 no notebook com a build sem AVX-512](docs/imagens/cap16_notebook_portatil.png)

O que medimos num PC fraco (4 núcleos, sem AVX-512), o que ajudou, o que não ajudou e como medir: [docs/DESEMPENHO_PC_FRACO.md](docs/DESEMPENHO_PC_FRACO.md).

## Requisitos

- **Windows 10/11 64 bits** e GPU com **Direct3D 12**.
- **CPU com AVX2** (Intel Haswell em diante, AMD Zen em diante). **Com AVX-512** (Ryzen 7000/9000, Intel 11ª geração desktop) é muito mais rápido; o `gerar.ps1` escolhe sozinho.
- 16 GB de RAM. Espaço: ~3 GB para a geração e a build (o disco do jogo não é copiado).

## Problemas conhecidos

- **Engasgo na primeira entrada de cada área**: os pipelines de shader são compilados na hora e ficam em cache; da segunda vez some.
- **Sem o limitador de 60** o jogo **acelera**, porque parte da lógica avança por quadro.
- **Trava do leitor da GPU em PC lento**: corrigida. O leitor executava blocos de comandos que a PPU ainda escrevia; na variante rara, ele saía de passo com o bloco (ficava no meio dos dados de um comando) e agora volta ao início do trecho. No notebook: antes, 4 travas em 9 rodadas; depois, 17 rodadas sem nenhuma. Se a imagem congelar, relate com o `out\jogo.log` (procure `[park-settle]`).
- Travas raras de carregamento ainda em investigação.
- PC fraco (4 núcleos, sem AVX-512) roda, mas abaixo de 10 FPS nas partes pesadas.

## English summary

A **native PC port** of *God of War: Ascension* (PS3), made by **static recompilation**: the game's PPU and SPU code is translated to C/C++ and compiled for x86-64 on top of [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). The GPU command stream is rendered with Direct3D 12, and SPURS runs the official libsre module (LLE).

**Easiest: the [Otavix Launcher](https://github.com/otavix010/otavix-launcher/releases/latest)**, which downloads this port, asks for your folders, generates the game for your CPU and starts it. **Bring your own disc**: no game code or data and no firmware here. You need your own copy of the game (BCUS98232). Update 1.04 and the official PS3 firmware are free from Sony, and `gerar.cmd` downloads both from Sony's servers by itself (or use your own: [update 1.04 .pkg](http://b0.ww.np.dl.playstation.net/tppkg/np/BCUS98232/BCUS98232_T76/5525fbb7b6b5456d/UP9000-BCUS98232_00-GOWABDPATCH00001-A0104-V0100-PE.pkg) (must be exactly 1.04), and `PS3UPDAT.PUP` from [PlayStation's PS3 system software page](https://www.playstation.com/en-us/support/hardware/ps3/system-software/); RPCS3 is no longer needed). Install Python and the Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools with Clang (commands above), download this repository to a path without spaces, double-click **`gerar.cmd`** (it asks for the disc folder, then downloads the update and firmware, decrypts your copy, translates and builds; ~4 minutes on an 8-core Ryzen 7 9800X3D), then play with **`jogar.cmd`**.

Status: boots, menus, chapter 1 and chapter 16 play with correct image, 60 FPS locked on a Ryzen 7 9800X3D; the full game is not verified yet. Performance is CPU-bound and much better with AVX-512: ~68 FPS uncapped in chapter 16 on a 9800X3D, ~32 on an i5-11400F, ~8 on a 4-core laptop without AVX-512. The build `gerar.cmd` produces includes the same performance passes as ours (`scripts/otimizar.py`); only PGO is left out. Thread pinning is now off on CPUs with fewer than 12 logical processors (+4% on the laptop), and the GPU command reader no longer hangs on slow PCs.

License: our code is MIT; ps3recomp is MIT (Ned Heller); `scripts/gpl/unself.py` and `scripts/gpl/pup_libsre.py` are GPL-2.0 (they follow RPCS3's unself.cpp and firmware installer). Decryption keys are read from RPCS3's source (downloaded at a pinned commit). *God of War* is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment; this is a non-commercial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony.

04d68ed26d3a93f0d3b190ffd6d177388026372b.message:
feat(render): state-only replay of recorded RSX method writes

Add mag-render-adapter-core::rsx_state_preamble. When native work has
replaced part of a recorded command list, the RSX commands after it may
still depend on the render state that list would have left. The encoder
takes recorded method writes in source order and keeps only the
requested state classes as a callable command block:

- NV4097 methods are classified as program, vertex constants, vertex
  input, texture binding, raster or attachment state, or as work (clear,
  primitive, draw, synchronisation, no-operation);
- work and no-operations are always dropped, and a keep set that names a
  work class is refused;
- kept writes stay in source order (a program upload keeps its slot,
  data and start order); consecutive increasing methods share one
  incrementing packet, which executes as the same single writes;
- the block ends in a return;
- unclassified methods, other subchannels and overflow are refused before
  any output.

Synthetic tests cover each rule. Nothing runs unless a host calls it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(render): opt-in GPU group-zero deformation through the packet compute prefix

Add a public GPU path for group 0 (instanced wind), off by default
behind MAG_RENDER_GPU_GROUP_ZERO=1, so the per-vertex deformation can
leave the CPU:

- shaders/render_frontend/group_zero.wgsl evaluates the group-zero
  deformation of group-zero-deformation.md per expanded vertex in
  binary32 and writes the position and the slot-12 colour row;
- behaviour::group_zero splits deform_group_zero into
  validate_group_zero (every refusal and the per-instance placements)
  and deform_vertex, with the CPU arithmetic unchanged, and adds the
  specification's position_tolerance;
- glue::gpu_group_zero embeds the kernel's MSL, HLSL and SPIR-V
  (translated at build time with the pinned Naga), encodes the inputs,
  appends the dispatch and its produced vertex buffer to a packet, plans
  the vertex-input layout, and refuses visibly whenever it cannot
  promise the CPU result within tolerance;
- the shared deformation store makes the CPU-or-GPU choice once per
  item, so the passes of one item never mix the two;
- SceneBuilder gains compute dispatches; the vertex-input GPU plan
  carries its vertex count;
- the scene adapter exposes the same inputs as GPU work.

Tests compare a binary32 reference of the kernel with the CPU
deformation within tolerance, round-trip the dispatch through the
native packet validator, and cover every refusal.
tools/check_group_zero_gpu.py runs the kernel on Metal against the CPU.

register. The prepare, start, frame_poll and stop slots now accept up to
eight registrants, called in registration order (stop in reverse). The
trace and payload slots keep a single owner, because they share per-call
scratch or return a decision.

With nothing registered every slot stays null. With one registrant the
slot holds its function directly, so existing single-extension builds
call exactly what they called before.

perf: ship the accepted runtime defaults on every host (#136)

* perf: ship the accepted runtime defaults on every host

Installer builds ran only the four compiled SPU defaults, plus two more
that main.cpp turned on for macOS alone. Every accepted hosted run also
used a set of RSX, PPU and SPU switches, and an installer-built Linux
client with them went from 4.6 to 21.5 guest fps (flips 3.7 -> 13.1/s).

mag_apply_runtime_defaults() now sets, on every host:
- PS3RECOMP_GCM_INLINE_NO_GPU_WAIT and MAG_NATIVE_CONSUMER, moved out of
  the __APPLE__ block (their reasons are not Metal-specific);
- deferred RSX reports (capacity 4096), early label release with early
  FIFO sync, and the GPU depth view;
- the PPU store fast path, framed SPU regions, the interpreter's rejoin
  prefilter and the SPURS workload stack argument;
- on Linux, the Vulkan backend's batched engine.

Each is set only when the variable is absent, so an explicit value (0
included) still turns it off for comparison. Diagnostics stay off.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: apply the runtime defaults before the SDK's constructors read them

The SDK reads its deferred-report and early-release switches in
cellGcmSys.c's gcm_deferred_initialize(), an __attribute__((constructor))
that runs before main(). The defaults applied in main() were too late for
them: a Linux build reached 11.5 fps instead of 21.0, and never logged
"[deferred reports] enabled" or "[early release]".

A new constructor in the executable (src/mag_runtime_defaults_early.cpp)
applies the same defaults first. On ELF it runs at priority 101, ahead of
default-priority constructors. Mach-O ignores priorities, but this object
is linked before the SDK's static library, so it still runs first. MSVC
has no such constructors (the SDK initializes these switches lazily), and
main()'s call still covers it. Explicit values still win, and applying the
defaults twice changes nothing.

A test builds an SDK-style constructor into a static library and checks it
sees every defa

2e6cdf841c34b4cd0d9b5eef2d10894a843f4e2a.message:
perf(build): lift indirectly reached WWS job code (--static-indirect) (#155)

The streamed-jobs stage bounded each WWS job module's lifted code by direct
branches from its header entry. Code a job reaches only through indirect
branches (jump tables, computed calls, explicit return addresses) lay past
that bound, was never lifted or registered, and ran in the SPU interpreter:
most of the workers' interpreted time in Training.

The installer recipe now passes the lifter's existing --static-indirect, which
follows the indirect-branch targets a static pass proves. A job whose
extended lift fails is retried with the direct bound, and lifted job code is
entered only when the verified region's expected bytes match local store.
This changes generated SPU coverage on every platform.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

2f44452ff06d5afa1a3b0df024c023b26843a4cd.message:
feat(diagnostics): opt-in watchdog for stalled job-completion waits (#113)

MAG_JOB_WAIT_WATCHDOG=<ms> reports, once per wait, a job whose
completion wait at 0x0023D7D0 has run past the threshold while one of
the seven progress slots is still behind the job's marker. The line is
"[mag job-wait watchdog] {json}" with the job, pool index, module (and
name where the existing table has one), marker, container, base, all
seven slots, the lagging slots, elapsed time, predicate passes and the
last predicate arguments and result.

It hooks the existing MagGraphicsTraceScope seam that the retail lift
already places on the wait and its predicate (0x00A047D8), so no new
function hook is added. It only reads guest memory and never changes a
return value or releases a wait. Unset or invalid, the cached threshold
is zero and each scope pays one branch.

feat(render): native GPU timing on Vulkan (#55)

* feat(render): opt-in GPU timing of Vulkan native scene submissions

MAG_RENDER_NATIVE_GPU_TIMING=1 printed nothing on Vulkan. Each native scene
submission now writes a GPU timestamp at its start and its end on its own
two-query pool per slot. Once its fence signals it prints one line in the
Metal backend's format (first 256 submissions; seconds on the device clock):

  [mag native gpu timing] generation=.. ticket=.. status=.. available=..
    gpu_start_seconds=.. gpu_end_seconds=.. gpu_ms=.. backend=vulkan

A submission counts as timed only after the queue accepted it. A device

3c40d338838d826abd3063763d5475596e11b17c.message:
perf(build): use x86-64-v3 code generation when the build CPU supports it (#144)

* perf(build): use x86-64-v3 code generation when the build CPU supports it

The installer compiles MAG on the player's own machine, so the build CPU is
the play CPU. A new MAG_X86_LEVEL option (cmake/MagX86Level.cmake) chooses
the x86-64 code generation level for Linux and Windows builds:

- auto (default): a configure-time cpuid/xgetbv probe checks the build CPU
  and OS for the whole x86-64-v3 set (AVX2, FMA, BMI1/2, F16C, LZCNT,
  MOVBE, the v2 set and the YMM state) and selects v3, else baseline.
  Cross builds, cl.exe and compilers without the switch stay at baseline.
- v3: -march=x86-64-v3 (clang-cl: /clang:-march=x86-64-v3) unconditionally.
- baseline: exactly the previous flags.

v3 always adds -ffp-contract=off (clang-cl: /clang:-ffp-contract=off, since
clang-cl ignores the plain switch and /fp:precise still contracts). Both go
to every C and C++ unit through directory compile options set before the
runtime subdirectory and the executable: MAG's sources, the lifted PPU units,
the lifted SPU units (which had no contraction switch) and the runtime.
macOS and arm64 are unchanged.

The configure output prints the chosen level and each x86 binary's receipt
records it as x86_level. The installer passes nothing; MAG_X86_LEVEL in the
installer's environment is a troubleshooting override (Windows and Linux),
and the recipe's cmake_args accepts -DMAG_X86_LEVEL=auto|v3|baseline. The
CI runtime compile checks apply the level as the real build does.

Measured on Linux (Ryzen 7800X3D): +6.1% title frame rate in Training
(12.93 vs 12.19 guest flips/s, best in all 3 alternating rounds, 0 SPU
assertions) with -march=x86-64-v3 -ffp-contract=off.

fix(player): present each executed guest flip once (#90)

* fix(player): present each executed guest flip once

After presenting a taken flip receipt, the frame clock recorded the guest's
flip request count, then presented the latest receipt again whenever its
executed flip count differed from that. Whenever the guest had requested a
flip the FIFO had not executed yet, the same image was presented a second
time; with a blocking present, the thread that also drains the FIFO waited
an extra display refresh for it. On Linux/Vulkan this showed as about 1.25
host presents per guest flip.

Both checks now use the presented receipt's own executed flip count, kept in
a small MagFramePresentState, so the outer pass presents only a receipt it
has not shown, which still catches flips executed between the passes. A
synthetic test covers taken receipts with requests running ahead and a newer
receipt the passes did not take.

659189096335745bdeae759d53af801a5d7cdca7.message:
feat(render): position-only reservations through the native worker

A caller can now fix Main's native queue position at the boundary,
before its packet is planned, and commit the packet into that position
later. Nothing changes unless these entry points are used.

- mag_render_client_worker_reserve_position reserves the next imported
  subgraph commit's position and ticket and returns the receipt that
  commit will carry. One may be outstanding at a time (BUSY); backends
  without support return UNSUPPORTED.
- mag_render_client_worker_submit_scene_subgraph_imported_v3_at admits
  a packet and commits it into that position. Its imports are bound
  then and validated by the backend when it encodes.
  - Negative is definitely uncommitted and releases the position.
  - Zero is accepted, with the reservation's receipt.
  - A failure where nothing reached the GPU (for example a stale import
    at encoding) is a declined commit: a FAILED terminal receipt that
    doesn't fail the session closed. Uncertain failures keep the
    existing fail-closed path.
- mag_render_client_worker_abandon_position releases it unused, and
  close releases an unconsumed position first.
- While a position is outstanding, every other commit is refused with
  BUSY, because the backend would otherwise encode it into that
  position.
- The reserved commit's encode and commit is shared by both paths
  (encode_reserved). The existing reserved path behaves as before.

Test: on the actor,
- a second reservation is BUSY;
- a commit into the wrong position is refused and its preparation
  cancelled, while the position stays;
- the right one commits with the reserved ticket;
- close releases an unconsumed position.
The Metal compat fixture covers the native late import check.

72432938bdc75bf5dec1eb1f9a5169583417ab85.message:
feat(render): stored-depth bounds on D3D12 through the depth bounds test (#111)

Native Main uses stored-depth bounds for its gated lighting and fog draws.
Vulkan evaluates them with the device's depth bounds test (#24); D3D12
refused every pipeline and scene with bounds, so such a Main was refused
outright on Windows.

D3D12's depth bounds test is the same predicate: it passes exactly when
min <= the depth already in the attachment <= max, both ends inclusive,
before any colour or stencil effect. So on D3D12:

- mag_native_create_v2 now reaches the D3D12 backend, which keeps an owner
  feature only when it is both known and enabled and the device confirms
  it (OPTIONS2.DepthBoundsTestSupported, ID3D12Device2, and
  ID3D12GraphicsCommandList1 on each slot list);
- a v3 pipeline with raster.depth_bounds_enabled is the ordinary state
  built as a pipeline state stream with DEPTH_STENCIL1's
  DepthBoundsTestEnable, only with that feature and a depth format;
  otherwise it stays UNSUPPORTED;
- each bounds draw of a v5 scene sets its range with OMSetDepthBounds
  (other draws of a bounds pipeline admit [0, 1]). As on Vulkan and Metal,
  a bounds draw needs a bounds pipeline (INVALID otherwise) that does not
  write depth (UNSUPPORTED otherwise).

The D3D12 compat fixture runs the Vulkan fixture's cases: depth 0.25 and
0.75 in the two halves, a full quad at 0.5 with depth test and writes off,
and bounds [0.2,0.3], [0.7,0.8], [0.25,0.25], [0.75,0.75], [0.5,0.5] and
[0,1] light exactly the halves the inclusive predicate selects; a
depth-writing bounds draw and a bounds pipeline without the owner feature
are refused. RTX 5090 (driver 32.0.16.1088) under the debug layer: passed,
no errors.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

OpenSSL looks for certificate authorities where it was built, finds none on
a player's Mac, and every HTTPS request failed verification. It was reported

hostname checks are unchanged. The Windows bootstrapper download uses the

perf(windows): time the frame clock with the performance counter (#141)

The host frame clock releases the 60 Hz vblank and flip ticks from
elapsed milliseconds. On Windows GetTickCount64 advances only on the
system tick, in 15-16 ms steps even under timeBeginPeriod(1), so ticks
were released in bursts on that grid and some vblanks came 30 ms after

already CLOCK_MONOTONIC in milliseconds.

CLOCK_MONOTONIC elsewhere, so other hosts see the same values as
before. The synthetic test checks granularity and monotonicity and
models the frame clock loop. On the Windows desktop the model gives
16.5 ms median and 31.6 ms worst spacing with GetTickCount64 (two gaps
over 24 ms in 120 ticks), and 17.0 ms median and 19.0 ms worst with the
new clock.

fix(installer): keep a failed attempt's output and retry past bytecode caches (#121)

* fix(installer): keep a failed attempt's output and retry past bytecode caches

Retry build could never get past a real failure. The build runs the managed
Python, which writes bytecode caches into the verified tool trees, so the
retry's inventory check refused every managed Python and wheel ("Managed
tool inventory changed; choose fresh storage"). By then the retry had
already deleted the failed attempt's lift and build output.

  scratch home, so bytecode is no longer written into managed tools.

  rebuilds them from the verified sources. Any other change is still refused.

  MAG, managed tools when incomplete) beside that attempt's journal under
  logs/attempts/<n>/ instead of deleting them. Only the most recent failed
  attempt keeps its output; older attempts keep their logs and journal.

feat(tools): discover indirect-branch targets in WWS job modules (#57)

* feat(tools): discover indirect-branch targets in WWS job modules

The job lifter bounded each module by direct branches from its header entry,
so code reached only through indirect branches stayed interpreted unless a
runtime interpreter-attribution report named it. Add a static pass that
proves indirect targets and follows them to a fixed point:

- forward constant propagation over reachable code (il/ila/ilhu/ilh/iohl,
  ai/a/sf/ori, the position-independent brsl-to-next idiom, and quadword
  loads from known addresses rotated by a known byte count), with the SPU
  ABI at calls (r80-r127 survive, callees start unknown);
- targets of bi/bisl/bisled/biz/binz/bihz/bihnz whose register is known;
- an explicit return address built in $r0 when control leaves through a
  branch that does not set the link;
- bounded jump tables (shli/clgti/a/lqx/rotqby[/a]/brnz/bi in one
  straight-line run with no other entry), taking exactly N+1 entries or none.

Every candidate's direct-flow closure must be defined, non-zero SPU code
inside the module that no known-address access or jump table touches;
candidates that later overlap data are banned and the pass repeats. A module
whose statically extended lift fails falls back to the direct bound, and the
rejection is recorded. --attribution entries combine with the static ones,
--direct-only restores the old bound, and --data-code-pointers opts in to a
validated heuristic for function pointers held only in module data.

9252afc95dafda82c751f23258fe42fca6b472d8.message:
fix(render): keep Rust thread stacks usable beside the runtime's static TLS (#46)

glibc takes each thread's static TLS and guard out of the stack size the
thread is created with. The engine carries over 2 MiB of static TLS, so a
Rust thread's default 2 MiB stack kept only about 20 KiB usable on Linux:
the render client thread overflowed as soon as the Vulkan validation layer
or the driver compiled the first native Main pipeline.

- On glibc, the engine sets RUST_MIN_STACK (unless the caller did) to 8 MiB
  plus the overhead glibc reports, before any Rust thread starts. Every
  Rust thread then keeps 8 MiB usable.
- The render client thread, where platform pipelines compile, asks for
  16 MiB usable through mag_render_native::thread_stack::with_overhead,
  which adds the same overhead to an explicit size.

macOS and Windows allocate TLS apart from the stack and keep their sizes,
plus the larger explicit client stack.

Tests: tests/thread_stack_tls.rs runs a thread with a deep stack probe in a
binary that has 3 MiB of static TLS (no libtest harness, whose threads
would carry it too). tests/test_runtime_defaults.py does the same for the
RUST_MIN_STACK default. Both overflow on Linux without the overhead.

feat(render): native depth bias (constant plus slope, no clamp) (#54)

Raster validation refused every pipeline with depth bias. Source polygon
offset (for example decals drawn with factor -1 and units -100) is a
constant in units of the minimum resolvable depth difference plus a slope
factor, with no clamp, which Metal, Vulkan and D3D12 all apply the same
way. Validation now admits bias with a zero clamp; a nonzero clamp stays
unsupported (it needs an optional Vulkan feature). Metal sets the bias on
every draw (encoder state persists), Vulkan sets it in the pipeline's
rasterization state, and D3D12 sets it in the rasterizer state, refusing a
fractional or out-of-range constant, which has no exact integer form. The
pipeline identity now includes the bias fields.

aa03c7531e0c79494bbd84b90f71440d2b784a9f.message:
fix(render): positioned commits work across threads: no re-pin, release order, capacity backpressure, refusal logging and a cross-thread harness (#110)

* fix(render): a positioned commit's admission ignores submitted work, with refusal logging and a cross-thread harness

In a host's state-first Main path (R83), the late positioned commit was
refused with BUSY (-4) every time, and the game wedged. The likely
cause is the admission table's limit of two: prepared admissions plus
submitted work whose terminals are unread. A host waiting on GPU work
queued behind the held position leaves those terminals unread.

- A positioned commit's admission no longer counts submitted work. The
  position already holds its in-flight slot, which was checked when it
  was reserved (pending + ready < 2).
- Every worker check that refuses logs which one it was:
  [mag native worker refusal] check=admission-bound |
  reserve-position-busy | reserve-position-device |
  commit-while-position | positioned-commit-no-position, with the
  outstanding position against the requested one, and the prepared,
  pending and ready counts.

Cross-thread harness (Metal compat fixture, real owner, real registered
worker through its C entry points, one real draw with the fixture's
scene programs):
- the boundary thread makes an ordinary commit whose terminal stays
  unread, reserves a position with its imports, and queues later
  original work;
- it then tries the next ordinary commit, which is refused while the
  position is held and its preparation cancelled;
- a late thread commits into the position (first variant) or declines
  it (second variant).

Both variants pass: the later work completes, and the position's ticket
reaches a terminal on the worker's receipt poll.

abc16b24375365d1049e65496640266aa251b2ed.message:
perf(render): reuse the native scene submission arrays

SceneDevice::submit built every description array of a submission afresh:
a Vec<Vec<..>> of texture bindings per draw, a Vec<Vec<..>> of buffer
bindings per draw, the per-dispatch binding sets, frames, images, draws and
passes (thousands of draws per frame on the measured title). On a Linux
profile of the native render worker the allocator traffic around them was a
large share of the thread's time.

The device now keeps these arrays (SubmitScratch) and clears them each
submission instead of reallocating. Nested per-draw vectors become one flat
array plus a (start, count) range per draw. The flat arrays are filled
completely before the pointer-carrying entries (frames, draws, passes) are
built, so no pointer handed to the native encoder can move; those entries
are only read by the synchronous native submit call, as before, and the next
submission rebuilds them. The sampler cache writes its bindings and table
into the device's scratch through the new resolve signature.

A new test records every field the native encoder reads, following each
pointer (resources, images, dispatch bindings, pass attachments, every draw
with its buffer and texture bindings), and requires three successive
submissions through one device, the later two reusing warm scratch, to
describe the same scene. Recorded on the previous code, the same fixture
gives the identical snapshot.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(build): keep the SPU decode cache off the thread stack on Linux

glibc carves a thread's static TLS out of its stack. The runtime's SPU
interpreter decode cache is a 2 MiB thread_local by default, so the
installer-built Linux binaries carry 2.1 MiB of static TLS and every
thread created with a 1 MiB stack fails (pthread_create: EINVAL). The SPURS
workers are such threads: on Ubuntu 24.04 the launcher's
cellSpursInitializeWithAttribute returned CELL_SPURS_CORE_ERROR_NOMEM, the
taskset was rejected, the decompression job for game.psarc.sdat could not
start and the launcher crashed. macOS and Windows keep TLS apart from the
stack and are unaffected.

Linux now configures the runtime with PS3RECOMP_SPU_DECODE_CACHE_HEAP=ON
(runtime-2026.11.08 and later), which allocates the cache per thread on
first use; an explicit -D...=OFF still wins. Synthetic check: a fixture
project configures ON for Linux, OFF for Darwin and Windows, and honours an
explicit choice.

b161974783079384ea6f109f3b3d791643f34ccf.message:
fix(controls): do not re-acquire a held mouse lock on every click (#164)

Click-to-recapture re-acquired the mouse lock on every button press in the
game window, even while the lock held. Re-acquiring moves the pointer to
the centre and discards motion observed around it, so look motion around
each shot or aim press could be lost, on Linux and on Windows. The Linux
motion trace showed the extra acquisitions after clicks.

A click now takes the cursor back only when the lock is not held: relative
mode is off, or the backend found the lock gone (SDL: relative mode or the
grab lost, or the pointer outside the window; Windows: the confinement no
longer matches). Focus returning still re-applies it.

The core test checks that clicks with the lock held never re-acquire it
and keep the motion around them, and that a click after the lock was lost
takes it back; it fails with the old behaviour.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

b3e22c2792bd1ed4141b17ff8a7f3506d36b81c8.message:
feat(render): adapt a captured Shadow run to the native cascade pass

Add mag-render-adapter-scene::shadow_run. A Shadow run has the Depth
input format, so its sources are the Depth source capture of its cohort
camera slot. plan_shadow_run (and plan_shadow_casters, which takes a light
per-item view) turns that capture into native depth-only draws:

- mag_render_behavior::shadow::describe_cascade_pass gives the pass:
  region, viewport, clear, state and the enabled-group casters in cohort
  order. Terminating items are not cohort members, and repeated items
  draw nothing;
- each caster is routed with shadow::caster_preparation from its mesh
  group and its captured geometry source;
- the geometry is the run's retained immutable partitions;
- the transform follows Main's rule: the four column vectors at bytes
  32-95 of the item's transform record.

Questions the behaviour crate leaves open are decided here, as the Depth
capture does, and stated in the module:

- the transform rows (question 2) come from Main's rule, not light-view
  maths;
- row 42 (question 5) is unused by a depth-only draw;
- culling (question 7) is a caller policy, back faces by default;
- groups 3 and 4 refuse unless the caller allows undeformed drawing.

An unprepared caster refuses the run unless the caller chooses to omit and
list it. There are 8 synthetic tests, including one end to end through
copy_depth_sources. Nothing runs unless a host calls it.

ba0531c0f619f7707799024381b7b27d320023b4.message:
feat(render): opt-in reserved-order Main commit on Vulkan (#23)

The worker's reserved-order commit (MAG_RENDER_MAIN_ASYNC_COMMIT) needs the
backend to fix a submission's queue place at the native boundary and encode
it later without the owner lease. Vulkan reported UNSUPPORTED and committed
synchronously.

With MAG_RENDER_VULKAN_RESERVED_COMMIT=1 and a host that provides the new
MagRenderVulkanQueueOrder (looked up through the weak
mag_render_host_vulkan_queue_order when a device is created; the client
bridge forwards the SDK's rsx_vulkan_backend_queue_order):

- reserve_scene validates the imports under the lease, takes the host's
  reservation (original queue work is held from then on) and allocates the
  ticket; a second reservation, other submissions and close are BUSY;
- submit_scene_v5 encodes the reservation without the lease, admitting only
  the imports validated at reservation, and hands its batch to the host's
  submit, which queues it ahead of the held original work;
- abandon_scene_reservation, and any encoding failure before submission,
  release the reservation so held work proceeds.

Without the switch or the host hook, reservations stay UNSUPPORTED and the
worker keeps its counted synchronous fallback.

The Vulkan compat fixture (before its deliberate queue gate) checks the
reservation contract as the Metal one does -- busy, close refused, abandon,
encode with the reserved ticket from another thread, completion -- and that
an original clear recorded after the reservation lands after the native
clear submitted ~100 ms later. The native checker also rejects validation
THREADING ERROR reports.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ca2d015fc0f3a378cda68acfa0572fef31d2dd42.message:
feat(render): stored-depth bounds on Vulkan through the depth bounds test (#24)

Native Main uses stored-depth bounds for its gated lighting and fog draws.
Metal evaluates them in a compiler-injected fragment prologue on a snapshot
of the stored depth: the fragment is killed unless min <= stored <= max, and
the pass writes no depth. Vulkan refused every pipeline and scene with bounds,
so such a Main was refused outright.

The device's depth bounds test is that predicate: it passes exactly when
minDepthBounds <= the depth already in the attachment <= maxDepthBounds, both
ends inclusive, before any colour or stencil effect. So on Vulkan:

- a v3 pipeline with raster.depth_bounds_enabled is created with
  depthBoundsTestEnable and dynamic depth bounds, from the ordinary fragment
  program (no Metal aux), only when the owner device has the depthBounds
  feature enabled (MagRenderHostOwnerV2); otherwise it stays UNSUPPORTED;
- each bounds draw of a v5 scene sets its range with vkCmdSetDepthBounds; the
  shared validator already requires a loaded depth attachment, no stencil
  writes and ranges inside [0, 1], and as on Metal the draw's pipeline must not
  write depth (UNSUPPORTED otherwise).

The packet validator now refuses only a stored-depth (aux) program without
bounds; bounds with an ordinary program are left to the backend, where Metal
and D3D12 pipeline creation still refuse them.

The Vulkan compat fixture writes depth 0.25 and 0.75 into the two halves of a
target, then draws a full quad with bounds at 0.5 with depth test and writes
off: [0.2,0.3], [0.7,0.8], [0.25,0.25], [0.75,0.75], [0.5,0.5] and [0,1] light
exactly the halves the inclusive predicate selects, and a depth-writing bounds
draw is refused (RX 7900 XTX, validation and synchronization validation).

de496cf453d9ff7124bb54dc55ffd9fa1d7a9575.message:
feat(render): opt-in resident uploaded images on Vulkan (#26)

Every Vulkan scene image with an upload was a new VkImage, a new allocation
and a buffer-to-image copy on every submission, destroyed at retirement;
Metal keeps such images resident.

With MAG_RENDER_VULKAN_RESIDENT_IMAGES=1 (default off), an uploaded image
that no pass attaches and that is not the diagnostic output -- its contents
are exactly its upload bytes -- is kept after its submission and reused, with
no allocation and no copy, by a later scene whose image has the same shape
and byte-identical upload:

- identity: the same never-GPU-written upload buffer version, no comparison;
- content: a hash picks candidates, the bytes are compared in full, and the
  buffer then takes the identity path.

An image is inserted only after the queue accepted the submission that
uploaded it; every submission sampling it holds a reference until it
retires, and an image evicted while referenced is destroyed at its last
release (4096 entries, 256 MiB of upload bytes, oldest use first). The layout
the last encoding left is the next one's starting layout. The memory census
reports resident entries (out[4]) and bytes; MAG_RENDER_FIFO_TIMING=1 prints
[mag native resident images] counters, as on Metal.

The Vulkan compat fixture samples an 8x8 texture (new authored
scene_textured_fragment.wgsl with scene_lit_vertex) from buffer A, from a
different buffer with the same bytes, from one with other bytes, and from A
again: each readback is that submission's texture, the cache holds two
images, and hits allocate nothing (RX 7900 XTX, validation and
synchronization validation).

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

f2a81cbbb84059dbc565a0a1a8c229680e46d506.message:
fix(render): a positioned commit never waits on work behind its position, and a declined one completes its ticket (#108)

In a host's state-first Main path (R82), the first positioned commit was
refused with BUSY 50 times and the game then hung with no GPU
completions.

- The positioned commit's admission waited for in-flight capacity, that
  is, for earlier submissions to complete, while the position was held.
  A positioned admission now skips that wait: the position already holds
  its in-flight slot, which was checked when it was reserved.
- A declined position completed nothing. Its command buffer was
  committed empty, but no receipt was ever published for its ticket.
  The host had already published Main's state with that ticket and
  waited on its terminal forever.
  - mag_render_client_worker_decline_position releases the position
    empty and publishes a completed terminal receipt (nothing drawn).
  - A positioned admission that is refused now declines its position
    this way.
  - A definite failure of a positioned commit (nothing reached the GPU)
    also completes its ticket empty instead of reporting FAILED.

Compat (Metal, real queue): original work committed after a held
reservation stays queued behind it, and is released both by abandoning
the reservation (committed empty) and by encoding into it.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

f461269fda5f34d40e13f18fc4309149ce31ca31.message:
perf(render): fixed-size keys for the native sampler cache

Every scene submission resolved its explicit samplers by building a heap
Vec<u8> key per texture binding, collecting the distinct states into a
BTreeMap keyed by those vectors, building a second BTreeMap from key to table
index, and building the key again for every binding to look it up. On a Linux
profile of the native render worker this resolution was about a fifth of the
worker thread's time.

The key is now a fixed [u8; 72] array with the same bytes in the same order
(known_fields, the eight u32 fields, then the four scalars and the border by
bit pattern, all little-endian), so building, comparing and storing one
allocates nothing. The distinct states of a submission go into a sorted
scratch vector the cache keeps and clears between submissions (a stable sort
keeping the last occurrence of each key, as the ordered map did), and a
binding's table index is a binary search in it. The persistent entries map
keeps the same key order, so table order, indices, eviction choice and the
1024-entry limits are unchanged.

Tests keep the previous resolution as a reference and require identical
results: the key bytes for 2000 generated states; the distinct states, their
order and every binding's index over 400 generated submissions with repeated
and near-identical states; and the edge states that must stay distinct by bit
pattern (0.0 and -0.0, two NaN payloads), plus scratch reuse across a smaller
and an empty submission.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

group-enable word whose low 16 bits, the u16 at +0x4a, are the
enabled-group mask. MainSetupRecord::decode read the high half at
+0x48. Read +0x4a and add vector 10 (bytes 00 07 00 FE give 0x00FE).

The Shadow caster selection now takes the mask as 16 bits, the mask's
own width, so the whole 32-bit word cannot be passed in by mistake.

f529e062f968022ab9e91c1c2e06bc94ec421e2e.message:
perf(windows): cache getenv for the runtime and MAG sources (#140)

The static UCRT getenv takes the environment lock and compares every
variable on each call: about 1.9 us per call with ~110 variables on the
Windows desktop, and about 18 us per call when eight threads poll at
once, because the lock serialises them. The runtime polls its switches
with getenv on hot paths, and macOS already caches them
(src/mag_env_cache.cpp); Windows had no equivalent.

A force-included header renames getenv and the CRT environment writes
(_putenv, _putenv_s, _wputenv, _wputenv_s, putenv) in the runtime and in
MAG's own sources. The cache publishes an immutable record per name;
every write forwards to the CRT and then invalidates all records, so
runtime defaults, player settings and explicit overrides are seen as
before. Lifted PPU and firmware units call neither and keep their
compile commands. MAG_GETENV_CACHE=0 forwards every lookup to the CRT.

The synthetic test covers inherited values, overrides, removal,
assignments, wide writes, case-insensitive names, readers racing a
writer and the cache-off path, and prints timings: 30 ns cached against
1.9 us from the CRT on one thread, and 40 ns against 17.9 us on eight.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

f8419df497026ebf5604a94a749cc074c788fc09.message:
perf(render): opt-in packet handover and worker-only validation for Main (#84)

Two default-off ways to take scene-packet work off the FIFO thread. Off,
everything is byte-identical.

MAG_RENDER_PACKET_HANDOFF=1, through the new
mag_render_client_worker_prepare_scene_imported_v3_owned and
..._submit_scene_subgraph_imported_v3_owned entries:
- The worker borrows the packet's large byte ranges instead of copying
  them on the calling thread: role-0 buffer bytes, and the texels of
  unkeyed images whose subresources already lie at their packed 16-aligned
  offsets in one range. Everything else is copied as before.
- The upload snapshots reference those same bytes:
  ResourceDelta::CreateShared adopts shared immutable bytes, and an update
  copies them on write. So neither the caller's thread nor the actor copies
  them.
- The caller keeps the ranges unchanged until MagRenderPacketOwner.release,
  which is called exactly once, from any thread, in every outcome. That
  includes refusal, a disabled handover (then after an ordinary copy) and a
  mismatched record.

MAG_RENDER_VALIDATE_ON_WORKER=1:
- The calling thread copies an imported packet without validating it.
  Today it validates twice: the import-free packet, then with its imports.
- The actor validates it once, at admission. The caller still waits for
  admission, so a refused packet is refused before any effect.

Tests:
- A handed-over packet is borrowed, not copied, and prepares the same
  uploads as the copy.
- It is released exactly once, after the last upload snapshot drops.
- A packet copied without validation is still refused by the full
  validation.
- The owner entries release in every outcome; owner record layout matches
  the C header.
- Shared snapshots are adopted without a copy and copied on write.

Measurement (ignored test handover_cost, M-series, release build): for a
32 MiB buffer, copy plus double validation plus snapshot copy went from
1.38 ms to under 0.01 ms.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fe57d65f713fa8ea64486947fb5bc7203f07d6a1.message:
fix(render): refuse D3D12 batch commands that name buffers outside the batch

A batch command must only use buffers the batch declares as resources. The
Metal and Vulkan backends refuse any other buffer as INVALID. D3D12 looked the
handle up on the device first and returned STALE for a handle that is not
live there (for example one from another device generation), so the same
malformed batch got a different refusal on D3D12.

Check membership in the batch before the device lookup for dispatch
bindings and for draw vertices, indices and colour readback. Single-frame
submission is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

# mag-recomp

A native static recompilation of *MAG* (BCUS98110, retail v1.0) for the PlayStation 3, built on the
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) SDK. macOS on Apple Silicon (Metal) is the primary
target; Windows x86_64 and Linux x86_64 builds use Vulkan.

> **Unofficial fan project — bring your own copy.** Not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive
> Entertainment or Zipper Interactive. This repository contains **no game code, assets, keys or
> firmware**, and no code generated from them. You must supply files from your own legitimately owned
> copy, and everything generated from them stays on your machine. Read the full [legal notice](NOTICE.md)
> before using this project.

## What is here

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/` | Input validation, PPU/SPU/firmware lifting drivers, launcher/engine handoff, opt-in trace hooks |
| `src/` | Runtime glue for the recompiled launcher and engine, and default-off trace diagnostics |
| `profiles/` | Pinned identities of the expected inputs, lifter configurations and allowed SDK revisions |
| `tests/` | Synthetic tests and fixtures; none contain game data |
| `docs/` | SPU batch preparation, the clean-room reimplementation method, and [development notes](docs/development/README.md) on workflow, the SDK fork, run verification and performance |
| `installer/` | One-button installer that runs the whole build on your machine from your own copy |

Only the v1.0 retail release is supported; any other release or modified file is refused.

## Status

Installer-built MAG has been tested on three systems:

- **macOS** (Apple Silicon, Metal): signs in and has joined online matches on a community server.
- **Windows** (x86_64, Vulkan): signs in, plays the Training mission and has joined online matches
  on a community server. Movies play through an FFmpeg the installer downloads.
- **Linux** (x86_64, Vulkan; tested on Ubuntu 24.04): signs in, plays the Training mission and has
  joined online matches on a community server.

Online play needs a compatible community server, which is not part of this repository. MAG connects
to `play.magtest.online` by default. The game is not complete: rendering has known gaps, audio
stutters, performance work is ongoing, and frame rates vary by system.

## Building

See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md). In outline: install the host dependencies, check out the pinned
ps3recomp revisions, supply and validate your own inputs, generate the recompiled sources locally,
then build the launcher and engine with CMake.

The [installer](installer/README.md) does all of that for you: choose your game folder and an
installation folder, click **Build MAG**, and it downloads pinned build tools, runs every step on
your computer and packages the result. Download it from a release.

New macOS builds also include a [native settings panel](docs/player-settings.md) for the game server,
display mode, output resolution and FXAA. Open **MAG → Settings…** while playing, or hold **Option**
when launching to open setup first. Settings survive updates and rebuilds.

## For players

You build MAG on your own computer from your own copy; nothing game-derived is ever downloaded.

1. **Get the installer** for your system (macOS on Apple Silicon, Windows 10/11 x86_64, or Ubuntu
   24.04+ x86_64) from a release, or from the build you were given.
2. **Prepare your game folder** as described in the [installer guide](installer/README.md#using-it).
   Use the files from your disc dump exactly as they are. In particular,
   `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/run/mag/ps3/game.psarc.sdat` must be the unmodified disc file: copies that were
   modded, patched for a server, or taken from an emulator's installed game are refused, because
   MAG itself applies your server choice to it.
3. **Click Build MAG.** It takes a while (most of an hour or more) and needs about 20 GB of free space. If it stops, **Retry build**
   continues where it left off.
4. **First launch.** The installer's output is not signed, so the system asks once:
   - **macOS:** if MAG "cannot be opened", Control-click (or right-click) `MAG.app`, choose
     **Open**, then **Open** again. Do the same for the installer itself.
   - **Windows:** if SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", click **More info**, then
     **Run anyway**.
   - **Linux:** if the installer has no PolicyKit dialog (for example over SSH), install the
     build packages first:

     ```sh
     sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends clang lld build-essential git pkg-config ca-certificates libssl-dev zlib1g-dev libx11-dev libxext-dev libxrandr-dev libxcursor-dev libxi-dev libxfixes-dev libxss-dev libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libgl1-mesa-dev libasound2-dev libpulse-dev libudev-dev libvulkan-dev libvulkan1 mesa-vulkan-drivers
     ```
   - **Windows, once the game starts:** Windows Security asks whether to allow public and private
     networks to access the app. Choose **Allow** for both (this may need an administrator) so you
     can play online.
   - **macOS, once MAG starts:** if macOS asks for a permission for MAG, choose **Allow**.
5. **Choose your player name.** You need one to play online. The server is already set
   (`play.magtest.online`); change it only if you were given another.
   - **macOS:** the setup window opens on first launch. Fill in **Player name** (and **Game server**
     if needed), then click **Play MAG**.
   - **Windows:** double-click `MAG.exe`. The first time, a small window asks for your name.
   - **Linux:** run it once from the MAG folder with your name: `./MAG --name YourName`
     (add `--server <address>` for another server).

   A name has 3 to 15 letters, digits, `-` or `_`, and starts with a letter. MAG remembers it, and
   types it in for you when the game asks you to sign in: just confirm it. On Linux that sign-in box
   is a small text window. [Player settings](docs/player-settings.md) has the details.
6. **Use a controller.** A standard USB or Bluetooth gamepad works on every system and is the
   recommended way to play. On Linux the keyboard also works as a controller while the game window
   has focus, until a controller is connected (set `PAD_NO_KEYBOARD=1` to turn it off):

   | Keys | Controller |
   | --- | --- |
   | X / Z / C / V | Cross / Square / Circle / Triangle |
   | Return / Space | Start / Select |
   | Q / E, R / T, F / G | L1 / R1, L2 / R2, L3 / R3 |
   | Arrow keys | D-pad |
   | WASD / IJKL | Left / right stick |

   On Windows, a controller is needed to play matches. The keyboard only covers menus (arrow keys,
   Z / X / A / S for the face buttons, Return for Start), has no camera or aim, and is ignored
   whenever any controller is present, including virtual gamepads created by Steam Input or
   remote-desktop and streaming software. Mouse aim is not available on any system yet.

**If a download fails** (for example during a GitHub outage), retry later. Or point the installer
at a folder of previously downloaded tools with `build --cache <folder>`, or at a mirror with
`MAG_INSTALLER_MIRRORS`; see [Downloads](installer/README.md#downloads). Every tool is checked
against its pinned hash, so a mirror cannot change what you install.

**Your saves** are in the installation folder's `home/gamedata`. Keep that folder (and back it up)
when you move or rebuild MAG.

**If something goes wrong,** each launch writes its logs in the installation folder, under
`logs/launch-*/` (`launcher.log`, then `engine.log`). On Windows and Linux, a launch that needs
something from you, such as a player name, also leaves its message in `home/player/launch-message.txt`.

**If MAG crashes at start on an older CPU** (Windows or Linux), rebuild with `MAG_X86_LEVEL=baseline`
set in the installer's environment, into a new installation folder; see
[BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md#x86-64-code-generation-windows-and-linux).

## Releases

Versions follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) and are managed by
[release-please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please) from Conventional Commit messages; see
[CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) once the first release is cut. There are no prebuilt game binaries,
because any build of the game contains code generated from it. Each release carries only the source
and the installers for macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows (x86_64), which CI builds from that release's
source. An installer contains tooling and source only (this repository's and the pinned ps3recomp
SDK's); it builds the game on your machine from your own copy.

## Contributing

Contributions must never include game files, anything derived from them, or output of tools run on
them. CI runs `tools/check_public_tree.py`, which rejects binaries, original game file types,
generated-code signatures, embedded byte images and machine-specific paths. See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)
for the rules that apply to people and coding agents alike.

## Licence

This project's code is released under the [MIT License](LICENSE). The ps3recomp SDK it builds on is
separately MIT-licensed ([LICENSE.ps3recomp](LICENSE.ps3recomp)). The licence covers only this
repository's code and grants nothing in the game, its files or anything generated from them; see the
[legal notice](NOTICE.md).
