c74e3bf9530594767ade9df92ba9f55f0af8f089.message:
Run GCM handlers from blocked semaphore waits (Windows)

A flip, vblank or user-command handler is guest code, so it runs when a
guest thread reaches an HLE call or a timer sleep and pumps. A title that
waits for its flip handler in sys_semaphore_wait -- God of War HD's main
thread does, every frame -- sat there until some other thread happened to
pump: a median 0.76 ms between the RSX reaching the flip and the main
thread waking, 1.7 ms at p90.

The GCM layer now sets an auto-reset event whenever it marks something
pending, and sys_semaphore_wait waits on that event as well as the
semaphore. When the event fires, the waiting thread runs ppu_gcm_pump,
as a timer sleep does, and re-checks the semaphore. cellGcm_wait_pump is
linked weakly, so the runtime still links without the GCM library; the
POSIX path is unchanged.

God of War HD, frame limit off, alternated in one session: median frame
17.3/17.1 ms before, 15.8/16.6 ms after; flip reached to main thread
awake 0.76 ms to 0.02 ms. sync_stress passes.

c9fc36a15d379d157f5a6d43947cbd9da0a2ed46.message:
rsx_texture_decode: step the swizzled offset instead of re-interleaving

A swizzled texture was decoded texel by texel, and each texel's offset
came from rsx_swizzle_offset, which interleaves x's and y's bits one at
a time: about ten iterations a texel. In God of War HD that loop was
most of the CPU decode in the texture bursts that stall the drain when
new effects first appear.

x's and y's bits land on separate positions of the offset, so it is the
OR of a y part, computed once a row, and an x part stepped with the
dilated increment (d - mask) & mask. Checked against
rsx_swizzle_offset for every texel of every power-of-two size up to
4096x4096 (rows sampled past 256): no difference. test_texture_layout
now decodes a swizzled image of every size up to 128x128, square or
not, and checks where each texel lands.

God of War HD: texture time in the worst burst 0.27 -> 0.07-0.10 s;
the frames it stretched 112 -> 74 ms and 101 -> 73 ms; frames of 45 ms
or more over a run 13 -> 10.

cd4383ec19274822747b37d8a8dee17e5241579f.message:
lv2: register syscall 22 as _sys_process_exit

On real lv2 (and RPCS3's binding table) syscall 22 is _sys_process_exit,
the exit every game issues; the table only registered 3 (sys_process_exit3,
the number bare-metal/newlib images issue).

A guest issuing 22 fell into the catch-all stub, which reports success -- so
the guest kept executing after its exit. Observed with a minimal test ELF:
its tail loop (goto back to the exit call) ran forever because the process
never died, and the host had to kill it from outside.

Register 22 as an alias of the same handler. The constants are named after
the kernel symbols (RPCS3: 3 = sys_process_exit3, 22 = _sys_process_exit,
26 = _sys_process_exit2, so no 'EXIT2' spelling appears), with the leading
underscore of the kernel symbol noted in a comment rather than in the name.
Compiler-agnostic; two files.

Verified: the same ELF now exits cleanly (sys_process_exit(code=0), host
exit code 0) with a plain MSVC build, and its sys_fs output stays
byte-identical to a fresh RPCS3 run. The change is a plain table entry;
clang/GCC builds are unaffected by construction.

ce9ea45331fc6c88b8b77ff3d20fd837a02bea66.message:
cellPad: a port with no controller reports centred sticks, not zero

cellPadInit zeroed the host state, and with the SDL2 backend (every
non-Windows build) and no controller plugged in nothing ever set the
sticks again. Port 0 is served with no device behind it, so titles read
all four axes as 0: both sticks pushed to the top-left corner. Windows
was spared only because its keyboard fallback writes 128 on every poll.

In Twisted Metal the car drove itself in circles and the chase camera
pitched up at the sky, so the player's own vehicle left the screen within
seconds of a match starting. With the sticks held at 128 (PAD_STICK) the
car stays in front of the camera for the whole match.

pad_host_release() puts a port at rest (no buttons, sticks at 128) at
init and whenever a backend finds no device on it, which also stops an
unplugged pad from keeping its last report.

ps3recomp_host --audio-pad, which CI runs on Linux and macOS with no
controller, now reads port 0 and requires all four sticks at 128. With
master's cellPad.c it reads 0 on each and fails.

d5759c227b426baeb97eb3e4078f091db5500a11.message:
cellSysutil: ps3_host_quit, for the window's close button and Cmd+Q

Closing the game's window stopped the presents and left the game
running with no window until it was killed, and Cmd+Q did nothing: the
host turns a plain run loop with no app menu, so AppKit had no Quit to
send it to.

ps3_host_quit does what the console's Quit Game does. Every registered
sysutil callback gets CELL_SYSUTIL_REQUEST_EXITGAME on the title's next
poll, and a title that tidies up and calls sys_process_exit ends there.
One that has not done so within PS3_QUIT_GRACE_MS (default 3000) is
ended for it with exit(0), so stdio is flushed and the atexit handlers
run, but never while a save is being written: cellSaveData counts the
saves in flight (ps3_savedata_busy), and the quit waits up to 10 s for
that to reach 0. It runs on its own thread, so the caller returns at
once, and a second request is ignored.

template on a closed window.

d682e9c49e2bfbbb7fb30f003acaa3a9e46d4f15.message:
rsx_d3d12: draw indexed triangle lists with their indices

The VP path expanded every indexed draw into a triangle list, copying the
256-byte converted vertex once per index reference. God of War HD gameplay
makes 6.4M references a second to 2.0M distinct vertices, about 2,300
indexed draws a frame, so the drain wrote ~1.6 GB/s into the upload heap
and the indexed uploads took ~20 ms of a 55 ms frame.

Indexed TRIANGLES now convert each distinct vertex once, straight into the
vertex buffer, and keep their indices in a new per-frame u32 index buffer
(vp_ib, double-buffered by frame parity like vp_vb). The record carries
the index range and is drawn with DrawIndexedInstanced, base vertex at
the run's first vertex. Batches that the list path merged (a BEGIN/END
stream cut into counts that are not multiples of 3) continue the same
run: they share its vertices and append indices. A run that would leave
the tables (index >= 2^20) or overflow the buffers falls back to the list
path, as do the other primitives. VTX_LIST=1 restores the expansion.

VTX_STATS=1 reports, every 5 s, draws by primitive, index references
against distinct vertices, conversions, attribute formats and the time
the indexed uploads take.

Gameplay: indexed uploads ~20 ms -> ~12 ms a frame, 18.2 -> 20.6 fps
(VTX_LIST=1 against the default, same build).

d7054ab6a820c28ec38c00393e9073d8f7402119.message:
spu: estimates, interpolate and float/int conversions four lanes at a time with AVX2

spu_fi, spu_frest, spu_frsqest, spu_cflts, spu_cfltu, spu_csflt and
spu_cuflt computed one lane at a time, while fa/fm/fma already have an
AVX2 path. frest followed by fi is how SPU code divides, so the scalar
loops sit in the middle of the hot loops of lifted jobs.

Each instruction's lane rule is integer work on the bit fields, so the
vector forms are exact by construction and no lane falls back:
- fi: the 33-bit fixed-point magnitude on 64-bit lanes, then one
  normalising shift picked per lane;
- frest/frsqest: the fraction tables read with a gather;
- cflts/cfltu: the significand shifted with per-lane variable shifts,
  saturated with compares;
- csflt/cuflt: the integer's exact double gives its top bit and the next
  23 bits, truncated.

The scalar versions stay as spu_*_ref and are still used without AVX2.
test_spu_float_est.c checks every one bit for bit against them (random
words, normal/extended-range boundaries, zeros, denormals, integers of
every magnitude, every scale immediate); linux.yml runs it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

daa17fbccb66d40e67197bdbf1e16f3bb9a9cc39.message:
ppu_loader: re-check the reservation once the lock-line lock is held

stwcx./stdcx. check the caller's reservation, then take the lock-line lock
for a line an SPU has reserved, then CAS. An SPU commit that lands
between the check and the lock breaks the reservation (via
ppu_resv_break_line, under that lock) too late to be seen, and the CAS
goes ahead on a line whose other words just changed. Re-check under the
lock.

God of War HD hung before the menu about one boot in eight on this class
of race: a SPURS LFQueue push read "no waiter" while the consumer
registered as one in another word of the line, so no signal was sent.

dc37f00b2d8c883b3b1f3eb45445d40adfc779f4.message:
sysPrxForUser lwmutex: an atomic lock word; the semaphore only wakes

Every sys_lwmutex_lock and _unlock went through a Win32 semaphore, two
kernel calls a pair even when nobody else wanted the lock. On the PS3
an uncontended lwmutex is a few atomic operations in user space. God of
War HD makes about 320,000 pairs in one frame when the first fight's
next wave spawns, and that frame took 360 ms.

Each slot now has a state word: 0 free, 1 held, 2 held with a waiter.
Lock is a compare-and-swap 0 -> 1, unlock an exchange to 0; only a
contended lock sleeps on the semaphore (now a wake channel that starts
empty), and only an unlock that finds 2 posts it. A waiter that times
out leaves the word at 2, so a later unlock may post a wake nobody
takes; the next waiter consumes it and waits again. Recursion, timeouts
(ETIMEDOUT), trylock (EBUSY), unlock from another thread and unlock of
a free lock behave as before. sys_lwcond_wait releases and re-takes the
lock through the same two helpers; tools/test_lwcond_layout.py stubs
them.

God of War HD: HLE time in that frame 200 -> 66 ms (traced), the frame
354 -> 234 ms, and the boot-time stalls at 21.8 s and 27.5 s about a
fifth shorter. The rendering check passes.

ddf65a66d17efe396ec7594c9555e99b098eb895.message:
vulkan: VK_DRAW_BATCH=1 records engine draws, depth snapshots, texture uploads and clears into one submission

Every engine draw used to submit its own command buffer and wait on a fence,
because the vertex, index and uniform buffers and the descriptor set are
single objects rewritten per draw. With VK_DRAW_BATCH=1 a draw takes slices
of three host-visible ring buffers and a descriptor set from a pool, records
into the open command buffer behind a full memory barrier (render-to-texture
ordering without hazard tracking), and only a pending counter grows. Depth
snapshots copy through a persistent device-local buffer, texture uploads
stage through a ring and record a buffer-to-image copy, and colour and
depth/stencil clears record too. vk_begin, every object destroy, the present
and the engine's submit point flush first, so all other backend work still
sees everything before it complete. VK_DRAW_BATCH_MAX (default 512, max 1024)
caps the draws per submission. Off by default.

eb5c6832611192c72eb52130957e24d743bcbb2f.message:
spu: SPU_IRQWAIT_DIAG reports an SPU waiting for an interrupt that never comes

An SPU that enables interrupts and spins until its handler runs looks,
from outside, like any busy SPU. SPU_IRQWAIT_DIAG=1 reports it: every
2^22 dispatches with interrupts enabled and nothing pending to take (24
lines at most), the pc, the event status and mask and the MFC list-stall
mask and status. SPU_IRQWAIT_LS=<hex> adds 16 bytes of local store, for
the waiter's own state once its layout is known.

In Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) this showed the WWS job manager
waiting for an Sn interrupt whose event bit was already gone.

The dispatch loop calls it only when interrupts are enabled with nothing
pending, behind g_spu_irqwait_diag (an SPU_GATE like g_spu_smc_watch):
-1 until the first call reads the variable, then 0 or 1, so with it off
the loop pays one predictable load.

runtime/spu/tests/test_spu_irqwait_diag.c
(tools/test_spu_irqwait_diag.py): off by default, the gate settles at 0;
on, exactly one report per 2^22 waits, with the expected state.

ec5a7a6f257eb849585140ebd38c73a44b7a4a57.message:
rsx engine: release a depth target's stale snapshot

A depth clear invalidates the sampleable snapshot of a depth target and
the next DEPTH24_D8 read takes a new one, but the old one was never
released. A shadow map cleared and read every frame leaked one backend
texture per frame per depth target. On Metal the object table filled
during play, and every texture created after that came back as 0 and
sampled black. Release the old snapshot when a new one replaces it, and
when the depth target is recreated at a larger size. Metal keeps a
released object until no recorded draw can still name it, and Vulkan
hands back the same handle refilled, which is left alone.

f0b28621560813837b79d5a8469b382195b4773a.message:
cellPad: look at an empty XInput slot once a second

XInputGetState on a slot with nothing plugged in costs about 140 us
here, against 2 us on a connected one, and the backend is polled at
least once a frame. With one controller in slot 0, the three empty
slots were 0.6 ms of every frame of God of War HD's main thread (inside
cellPadGetInfo2), about 0.45 ms of it in the driver.

An empty slot is now polled again only after a second, staggered by
slot so one poll never pays for all of them. A pad plugged in is seen
within a second; a connected one is read on every poll as before.

over 15 s (what is left is the GCM pump inside the call).

f0e061a514eb7c66ce0dc104f7621a87cd50f433.message:
rsx: take the vertex-program methods first, one diagnostic gate per FIFO word

Most of a frame's method stream is vertex-program constants and
microcode. In God of War HD gameplay that is about 140k constant vec4
uploads and 70k microcode headers a second, and each of those words went
through the FIFO walker's per-word checks and then about fifty
comparisons in rsx_process_method before reaching its handler.

- rsx_process_method handles SET_TRANSFORM_PROGRAM_LOAD,
  SET_TRANSFORM_PROGRAM[], SET_TRANSFORM_CONSTANT_LOAD and
  SET_TRANSFORM_CONSTANT[] before its other checks. None of the checks
  they skip matches these methods.
- A microcode word that rewrites the bytes already there no longer sets
  vp_dirty, so the flag means what its comment says: the program
  changed. Titles upload a draw's program before every draw. Nothing in
  this tree reads the flag yet.
- The walker reads its per-word diagnostic switches (GCM_SUBCH7,
  GCM_OBJDBG, GCM_SUBCH_GATE, GCM_VAL_WATCH, GCM_METHOD_HIST,
  RSX_LIVE_FEED_DBG, the live and dispatch draw engines) once per drain,
  instead of testing each of them for every data word.

f366a95b94023316413e0358bb4d1b487fb6ad4e.message:
cellVdec: never hand the guest handle 0

cellVdecOpen wrote the slot index as the handle, so the first decoder a
title opened got handle 0. Some titles treat a 0 handle as "no decoder
open": Killzone 2's movie player
keeps the handle as its "decoder open" flag, its AU submit returns
without calling cellVdecDecodeAu while the handle is 0, and the intro
movie stalls with no AU ever decoded.

The handle is now the slot index plus one. Every entry point maps it
back, 0 and out-of-range handles are rejected with CELL_VDEC_ERROR_ARG,
and the callback receives the handle the title was given.

test_vdec_decode checks that Open never returns 0, that StartSeq(0) and

f825519199b20712213504374feedd4586008d9d.message:
cellGcmSys: a resync replays the label releases it skips; re-read a park before leaving it

A FIFO resync moves get straight to put. The fences in the skipped range were
already swept up, but a label release in it was simply lost, and a title
that waits on that label waits for the rest of the run. inFAMOUS 2's light
task kicker waits on a texture-read release (0x1D74) that sits in a
command block an SPU job writes; a jump-park resync that stepped over it
froze the title in its first open-world area.

- After the fence sweep, the skipped range is walked as a command stream:
  each header and its data, NOPs, flip markers and self-JUMP parks stepped
  over, forward JUMPs inside the range followed, stopping at a CALL, a
  RETURN or a word that is not a method header. NV406E SEMAPHORE_OFFSET /
  RELEASE (0x64/0x6C) are replayed into the label window as the walker
  does, and the NV4097 semaphore context, offset and back-end /
  texture-read releases (0x01A4, 0x1D6C, 0x1D70, 0x1D74) go through
  rsx_process_method, so they land where the walker would have written
  them (label window or main memory, byte swap included). Draws in the
  range are still dropped.
- The jump-park resync reads the park word again first. An SPU job that
  fills an Edge-style command-buffer hole (a self-JUMP until it is
  written) can land between the pass's read and the resync, which would
  then jump over the commands just written.

libs/video/tests/test_gcm_resync_labels.c (run by
tools/test_gcm_resync_labels.py) parks the walker in front of a NOP, an
NV406E release, a forward JUMP over non-command words and an NV4097
release, waits out GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS and checks that the resync wrote the
first label and handed the second to rsx_process_method.

does. One of its two hunks merged clean -- the prefix used to compute

Merge PR #444: verified job-module regions and embedded SPU program coverage (@tekulvw)

The interesting conflict of the wave so far. #444 refactors the --jobmods
loop in tools/lift_jobmods.py into a lift_module() helper (so --engine-elf
can share it) and adds reachable()/module_code_end()/module_seeds(). #488
(@erikomis, wave 3) rewrote that same loop for a different reason: the LS
address a module is linked for comes out of its header at +0x28, and is
0x7000 rather than 0x4000 for some of Resistance: Fall of Man's modules.
Lifting those at 0x4000 puts every lifted address 0x3000 short of where
the job manager runs them.

#444 was written against master, so lift_module() and module_seeds()
hardcode BASE throughout -- the ELF wrap base, --base, the seed window,
base + 0x30, the manual-link and switch-table scans, and the manifest's
"base" field. Taking #444's side as written compiles, runs, and silently
reverts #488 on exactly the modules #488 exists for. Nothing in CI would
have caught it: no test ships a 0x7000 module.

Resolved by keeping #444's refactor and threading #488's base through it.
module_seeds(raw, base=BASE) and lift_module(..., base=BASE), and the
--jobmods loop passes base=module_base(raw). module_base() itself is #488's,
unchanged.

The --engine-elf path keeps BASE, and that is correct rather than an
oversight: find_engine_modules() only accepts an image whose header says
+0x28 == BASE, so every module it yields is linked at 0x4000 by
construction. The same goes for the code-slice and region-registration
arithmetic in lift_engine_elf()/emit_register_verified().

Dropped on the way through: #488's "sha = name.split('_')[1]", assigned and
never read.

tools/build_spu_workloads.py is a plain both-added conflict in the argparse
block -- #549's --merge-chunks and #444's --handled/--image-ids. All three

fb89154950c6ffb10e3d92e06da99258af5d363a.message:
rsx_d3d12: depth surfaces per zeta offset, readable as textures

The guest path had one depth buffer, cleared whenever a pass changed
targets. God of War HD keeps two depth surfaces: the scene's 2x-AA one
at 0x17F0000 and a resolved one at 0x2240000. Its resolve pass samples
the AA depth as an A8R8G8B8 texture to compute fog and the alpha the
shadow pass blends with. That surface never existed in guest memory,
so the read returned nothing: distant cliffs came out black and the
whole scene too dark.

- Each zeta offset gets its own D24S8 surface (R24G8_TYPELESS, so it
  can also be read). It keeps its contents across passes and is
  cleared only by the guest's own clears. Passes without a depth
  surface keep the shared buffer as before.
- A colour target of NONE with a depth surface binds no RTV (a
  depth-only pass). The register now defaults to target A, as libgcm
  sets it, so a title that never writes it still draws.
- A draw sampling a depth surface reads a colour copy refreshed just
  before it when the depth has changed since the last copy: the bytes
  a guest sees in memory for D24S8 read as A8R8G8B8 (A = depth[23:16],
  R = depth[15:8], G = depth[7:0], B = stencil).
- The pool grows a surface for a larger pass, never shrinks it, and
  evicts an entry no pass used this frame.

fe84fa460d078b41fdad94f702554ea41a01ebe8.message:
Merge PR #436: memoize indirect-dispatch registry lookups per thread (@tekulvw)

The largest semantic conflict in the release so far. #436 was written
against master, where spu_lifted_lookup() was a single spu_lookup() and
spu_indirect_branch() carried the identity-ownership order inline. Wave 4
changed both: #419/#420 moved the ownership order into
spu_lifted_lookup_full(), and #481 put a per-thread dispatch cache in
front of it in spu_lifted_lookup().

Taken as written, #436 replaces spu_lifted_lookup()'s whole body with
"return spu_lookup_memoized(lsa, ctx ? ctx->image_id : 0)" and replaces
spu_indirect_branch()'s call with its own inline identity walk. That
compiles, and it deletes #481's dispatch cache outright while forking the
ownership order into a second copy that would then drift from the
resolver's. Three PRs' worth of wave-4 work, silently undone.

So the structure stays wave 4's and #436 goes in underneath it, which is
where it belongs and what it was for: spu_lifted_lookup_full() now makes
every one of its registry probes through spu_lookup_memoized() instead of
spu_lookup(). The resolver issues up to three probes per resolution
(resident_task, then resident_ovl, then image_id) and the first two
usually miss, and a generation-keyed memo that caches misses is exactly
the thing that stops each of those walking the address's hash chain again
-- which is the cost #436's own commentary describes.

The two layers compose rather than overlap: #481's cache is keyed on the
resolved answer for a (context, residency) pair and only stores hits;
#436's is keyed on (address, image) at the registry and stores misses too.
Definition order checked -- memo at 1633, resolver at 1673, cache at 1747.

Tests: #436 adds test_registry_lookup_memo and wave 4 added
test_verified_resident_code_regions, test_resident_interpreter_rejoin and
test_dispatch_cache. git offered them as one conflict because they share a
trailer; all four are kept and all four now run from main(). Verified that
every test defined in the file is called

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│

│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

HLE implementations of the PS3 system libraries, written for this project. RPCS3 is a behavioural reference, not a code source. Most modules are complete. The ones still marked Partial are the media decoders (cellVdec, cellAdec, cellDmux, cellAtrac, cellAdecAtrac3p) and cellSpurs. [docs/MODULE_STATUS.md](docs/MODULE_STATUS.md) has one row per module and is the source for the counts.

| Category | Modules | Status |
|----------|---------|--------|
| **Kernel Threading** | sys_ppu_thread, sys_mutex, sys_cond, sys_semaphore, sys_rwlock | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Events** | sys_event (queues, ports, flags), sys_timer | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Memory** | sys_memory, sys_mmapper (containers, shared mem) | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Filesystem** | sys_fs (path mapping, real I/O) | ✅ Complete |
| **Filesystem** | cellFs (real file I/O, dir ops, stat, path translation) | ✅ Complete |
| **Save System** | cellSaveData (callback-driven, PARAM.SFO), cellGame | ✅ Complete |
| **Input** | cellPad (XInput/SDL2), cellKb, cellMouse | ✅ Complete |
| **Audio** | cellAudio (WASAPI/SDL2, mixing thread, multi-port) | ✅ Complete |
| **Video Output** | cellVideoOut (resolution config, 720p default) | ✅ Complete |
| **Codecs** | cellPngDec, cellJpgDec, cellGifDec (stb_image) | ✅ Complete |
| **Font** | cellFont (stb_truetype backend + fallback metrics) | ✅ Complete |
| **Network** | sys_net (BSD sockets, P2P), cellNet, cellNetCtl, cellHttpUtil, cellSsl, sceNp*, sceNpTrophy, sceNpMatching2 + Score over [psnr](docs/ONLINE.md) | ✅ Complete |

1437112336.readme_excerpt: # Project Pyrrhus **Killzone 2 (PS3) as a native Windows program, built on your PC from your own copy: an unofficial port by static recompilation.** [![CI](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![pre-release 0.1.13](https://img.shields.io/badge/pre--release-0.1.13-b4500f?style=flat-square&labelColor=17130f)](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/releases/tag/v0.1.13) [![Licence: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-MIT-b4500f?style=flat-square&labelColor=17130f)](LICENSE) [![Ask DeepWiki](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepWiki-Ask-b4500f?style=flat-square&labelColor=17130f)](https://deepwiki.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus) > **Bring your own game.** This repository holds no game code, assets, keys or firmware, and downloads none. You > need your own Killzone 2 disc dump, its 1.29 update and the decrypted EBOOT made from your copy > ([what each must contain](docs/GETTING-FILES.md)). | | | | | |---|---|---|---| | **23-33 fps** in the first level, scripted runs under Proton (PS3: 30) · [proof](docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md#frame-rate) | **4 disc regions** accepted, US tested · [proof](docs/GETTING-FILES.md#regions) | **0 game files** in the repo or the downloads · [proof](docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md#in-short) | **About 18 minutes** to build with four jobs · [proof](docs/BUILDING.md#steps) | **[Download](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/releases)** · **[Install walkthrough and FAQ](docs/FAQ.md)** · **[Known issues](docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md)** · **[Reporting bugs](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/issues/new/choose)** · **[More](#more)** ## Play it **Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit):** 1. Download `Project-Pyrrhus-setup.exe` (or the portable zip) from the [releases page](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/releases). 2. Point it at your disc dump, the 1.29 update and the decrypted EBOOT; if you play the game in RPCS3, "Use my RPCS3 install" finds them. 3. Start the game from the launcher. *Caveat:* native Windows is not yet confirmed by us (players report playing there). The first start translates and builds the game on your PC, which takes a while. It needs a CPU with AVX and FMA3 and a Direct3D 12 graphics card ([requirements](docs/requirements.md)). **Linux:** 1. Run the same Windows download under Proton, for example as a non-Steam game in Steam. *Caveat:* the installer and the zip are made for Windows and not checked under Proton; we test the built game under GE-Proton ([known issues](docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md)). ## What makes it different | Claim | Proof | |---|---| | A native Windows x64 program: the game's own code, recompiled ahead of time; no CPU emulator runs while you play (the graphics commands are translated at run time) | [How it works](docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md#in-short) | | Most of the game's SPU post-processing runs as native C by default (each job has a switch back), giving the same output bits as the recompiled jobs on the tested inputs | [How it works](docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md#what-kind-of-port-is-this) | | Field of view (45-75) and FSR 1 upscaling as rows on the game's own Display page (FSR 1 checked in the menu only, not yet in play) | [Features](docs/FEATURES.md), [roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md) | | Shaders built during the load from a shipped list: pauses over 0.1 s in the first minute fell from 18-20 to 2 in paired scripted runs (not yet measured in an installed copy) | [Known issues](docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md#frame-rate) | | The setup checks your files before building and names what is wrong | [Getting your files](docs/GETTING-FILES.md#what-the-first-run-check-can-print) | ## Coming soon Not done yet, and said openly: a steady 30 frames per second, the campaign past the first level, loading checkpoint saves back, 5.1 surround sound, and multiplayer (offline bots and self-hosted online). Where each stands: [roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md) and [feature table](docs/FEATURES.md). ## Status **Status:** [v0.1.13](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/releases/tag/v0.1.13) is a pre-release, partly playable: the intro movie plays, the menus run with sound, and the first level loads and can be played. Speed is below the PS3's 30 frames per second in our scripted runs. MIT licence. Direct3D 12 only. ### Compatibility One row per setup. *Verified* means we ran it on that setup; *implemented* means the code is in but we have not run it there; *planned* means neither. Full dated table: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md). | Platform | How it runs | Renderer | State | Tested on | |---|---|---|---|---| | Windows 11 | native exe | Direct3D 12 | players report playing (issue #13); not run by us | a player's laptop: RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (21-28 fps in the first part of the first level, their report) | | Windows 10 | native exe, in a virtual machine | Direct3D 12 | installer, first-run build and uninstall verified; the game starts and stops at its graphics device (no GPU there) | 6 cores, 8 GB, no GPU, 2026-10-27 and 2026-10-28 | | Linux | the Windows exe under Proton | Direct3D 12 | verified: the first level loads and plays in our scripted runs, about 23 fps over one 330 s run (2026-10-22) and a median of 32.6 fps in short turn-and-walk windows (2026-10-29), against the PS3's 30; hand play is not measured | GE-Proton11-7, i7-12700KF, RTX 4060 | Optional features, same three states (both new in 0.1.7): | Feature | State | Tested on | |---|---|---| | Options > Display: field of view (45-75, 45 is the original), first-person only | verified in play under Proton (45, 60, 75) | GE-Proton11-7, RTX 4060 | | Options > Display: upscaling (Off / FSR 1) and sharpness | implemented; drawn in the menu under Proton, not yet checked in play; adds about 0.4-1.3 ms of graphics time per frame at 2560x1440 in our tests | GE-Proton11-7, RTX 4060 | ## Install in detail **You need:** - **Your Killzone 2 disc**, dumped as a folder or as a decrypted `.iso`: US (BCUS98116, tested), or Europe (BCES00081), Asia (BCAS20066) or Japan (BCJS30032), which are accepted but untested: the code is the same, the data differs, and no one has played them through yet ([docs/GETTING-FILES.md](docs/GETTING-FILES.md#regions)). - **The 1.29 update of the same region** from your copy (on a PS3 or in RPCS3: the `dev_hdd0/game/` folder, such as `dev_hdd0/game/BCUS98116`). - **The decrypted 1.29 EBOOT** (`EBOOT.elf`), made from that update's `EBOOT.BIN`. - Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) with a CPU that has AVX and FMA3 (about 2013 or later), 16 GB of RAM advised for the build, and a Direct3D 12 graphics card: [docs/requirements.md](docs/requirements.md). No CPU emulator runs while you play. If you play the game in the PS3 emulator RPCS3, the setup can find all three in your RPCS3 install ("Use my RPCS3 install"). What each must contain: [docs/GETTING-FILES.md](docs/GETTING-FILES.md). This project ships none of them and gives no decryption steps. 1. Download the Windows installer (recommended) or the portable zip from <!-- version -->[v0.1.13](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/releases/tag/v0.1.13)<!-- /version --> on the [releases page](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/releases) (every release is a pre-release for now). 2. Run it and point it at your disc dump, the 1.29 update and the decrypted EBOOT. 3. It translates and builds the game's code on your machine; no game code, assets or keys are shipped or downloaded. 4. Start the game from the launcher. Do not install into a OneDrive folder. The settings files (`keybinds.ini`, `gameplay.ini`; the latter is created with its defaults on the first start, and an existing one is never changed) are in `%APPDATA%\Project Pyrrhus`, or next to `kz2.exe` in the portable zip. More: [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md), [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## How it works The game's PPU and SPU code is recompiled ahead of time to native x64; the graphics commands are translated to Direct3D 12 at run time; the system libraries are reimplemented on PC APIs. Details: [docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md](docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md). Settings and controls: [docs/FEATURES.md](docs/FEATURES.md), [docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md](docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md). Building it yourself: [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md). ## More [Features](docs/FEATURES.md) · [Screenshots](docs/SCREENSHOTS.md) · [Requirements](docs/requirements.md) · [How it works](docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md) · [Accessibility](docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md) · [Roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md) · [Release criteria](docs/RELEASE-CRITERIA.md) · [What goes online](docs/PRIVACY.md) · [How AI was used](docs/AI.md) · [Contributing](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Related projects **[Project Helghast](https://github.com/undecuple/project-helghast)**: Killzone 3 (PS3) ported to PC the same way. Project Pyrrhus uses its method and reuses its general runtime work (ps3recomp fixes, renderer, SPU job system), adapted to Killzone 2. Most patches in `port/patches/` come from there; the rest are Killzone 2's own. Its builds are pre-releases on its [releases page](https://github.com/undecuple/project-helghast/releases), as this project's are. This port currently supports Direct3D 12 only. For a Vulkan version of a Killzone 2 port, please use [Tokisaki Port](https://github.com/YYOzcan/tokisaki-port), which is developed separately by its own author. ## Official channels Project Pyrrhus is made by **undecuple**: GitHub [@undecuple](https://github.com/undecuple), Reddit [u/RelationshipNo4440](https://www.reddit.com/user/RelationshipNo4440), Discord **itekso.** (on the ps3recomp server). Builds and fixes come only from this repository's [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/releases); we never ask anyone to paste a command into PowerShell or a terminal. Anyone else offering builds, "fixes" or donations in this project's name is not us. ## Contributing Pull requests are welcome: [.github/CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). ## How AI was used This project is developed by one person with AI coding agents, with the maintainer reviewing and merging their work: [docs/AI.md](docs/AI.md). ## Licence and disclaimer The port's own code, tools and documentation: [MIT](LICENSE). Third-party components and credits: [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md). The licence covers nothing of the game itself. Security problems: [SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md). Reuse, including by AI systems and automated tools: [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md#reuse-and-attribution-including-ai-and-automated-use). *Pyrrhus* is the Helghast capital where most of Killzone 2 is fought; Project Pyrrhus is a fan project, not official and not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Guerrilla Games. **You need your own copy of the game.** This repository contains only the port: source code, patches to the recompiler, tools and documentation. cellSaveData, sceNpTrophy: PS3_GAMEDATA_ROOT moves saves and trophies out of the working directory

Saves and trophies live under ./gamedata, relative to wherever the game
was launched from, so opening a port from another directory (a
launcher, a shortcut, the Finder) starts it without its saves. With
PS3_GAMEDATA_ROOT=<dir> the save root becomes
<dir>/dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata and the trophy store
<dir>/trophies, so a port can point both at a fixed per-user place. An
explicit sceNpTrophySetStoragePath still wins; unset, nothing changes.

0650a59088532c1a0a3469cdd8812fa457a80bf0.message:
cellGcm: _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel queues the label wait and the flip

libgcm appends NV406E SEMAPHORE_OFFSET and SEMAPHORE_ACQUIRE for the
label, then the flip, so the RSX flips only once the label holds the
value. RPCS3's _cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel writes the same two
methods into the context before its flip command. The import here
ignored its context, wrote the label itself from the PPU, and flipped
at call time: whoever owns the label was overruled, and the flip
waited for nothing.

Write the two semaphore methods into the context and queue the flip
behind them with gcm_flip_into_fifo, as _cellGcmSetFlipCommand already
does. A context that is not a mapped command buffer, or has no room,
falls back to the immediate form as before.

0ba1229e2c0b4b6003604a06e80fb330dccc1083.message:
sys_ppu_thread: non-joinable threads free their slot when they end

sys_ppu_thread_create ignored its flags and made every thread joinable, so a
thread created without SYS_PPU_THREAD_CREATE_JOINABLE stayed FINISHED after
its exit and held its slot for good. Once 63 such threads had run, every
later create returned CELL_EAGAIN.

joinable is now flags & 1. A non-joinable (or detached) thread frees its
slot at the end of ppu_host_thread_proc, after closing its event and handle
(Windows) or destroying its mutex/cond (POSIX, where the host thread is
detached at creation), under the table lock. sys_ppu_thread_exit leaves the
freeing to that epilogue; the main thread is still marked FINISHED there.
The create log line shows the flags.

tests/test_ppu_thread_slots.c (tools/test_ppu_thread_slots.py): 192
non-joinable threads created and finished in turn all succeed and leave no
slot in use; 63 unjoined joinable threads still fill the table, and a join
frees a slot. Fails on master at the 64th create (0x80010001).

0e26194770079d251b113cbc28bb41e27199ac76.message:
sys_spu: an SPU's user event finds the port the PPU binds, and waits for it

An SPU's send_event (interrupt mailbox, code 0..63) was routed only through the ports the group binds with
sys_spu_thread_group_connect_event_all_threads, and answered ENOTCONN at once when there was none. Two things go
wrong with that:

- A port bound for one SPU thread with sys_spu_thread_connect_event was never found by the delivery, only by the
  plain out-mailbox path.
- The SPU thread starts running at sys_spu_thread_group_start while the PPU is still on its way to the connect
  calls that follow it (a real SPU needs far longer to boot than a lifted one). The first request of the program
  was answered ENOTCONN and the SPU program gave up. SoulCalibur II HD's audio engine (MultiStream) binds its ports
  with sys_spu_thread_connect_event, after group_start, and failed this way.

The delivery now looks at the thread's own bindings before the group's (spu_port_queue_locked) and, when the port
is not bound yet, waits for a binding for up to 200 ms on a condition variable that both connect calls signal
before it answers ENOTCONN. An SPU whose thread does not exist is answered at once, since nothing will bind its
port. The out-mailbox path reads the bindings through the same helper under the lock.

The test calls the real handlers and spu_deliver_user_event: bound for the thread, bound for the group, bound 40 ms
late either way, never bound (answers after about 200 ms) and an SPU with no thread (answers at once). On v0.15.0
it fails six checks; with the change it passes (five runs in a row).

122690f29d9d566a679fce9944c4718a674ed79b.message:
fp decompiler: biased unsigned remap and _bx2 fetches return signed values

Two ways a fetch comes back re-centred to -1..1 were ignored, so the
shader saw 0..1 encodings:

- SET_TEXTURE_ADDRESS bit 12, UNSIGNED_REMAP_BIASED, applies to every
  fetch from the unit: (round(x*255)-128)/127 on the lanes the crossbar
  fills from a source channel (16-bit X16/Y16_X16 channels: /32767),
  after gamma and not on gamma lanes, and not on lanes the filter flags
  signed. rsx_texture_expand_mask computes the lanes, for the formats
  RPCS3 gives RSX_FORMAT_FEATURE_BIASED_NORMALIZATION.
- EXP_TEX (OPDEST bit 21, the _bx2 modifier) belongs to the instruction,
  not the texture: x*2-1 on every lane of any unit, bypassing gamma
  (RPCS3 _process_texel). It applies from every entry point.

inFAMOUS 2 reads its normals G-buffer through a biased unit and its
tangent-space normal maps and occlusion-cone lookup tables with TEX_bx2
(about a quarter of its fragment programs). Read unexpanded, every
normal leaned towards (1,1,1), normal maps had no effect, and the
occlusion volumes round props drew as dark boxes.

The engine passes the expand masks of the units a program samples
through a new entry point, rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_expand_ex,
and hashes them into the pipeline key. A program with neither feature
is byte-identical.

d3d12: key the per-draw vertex program cache on the program, not on the store behind it

vp_get_vs hashed the microcode from SET_TRANSFORM_PROGRAM_START to the end of everything uploaded. A title that
keeps several programs resident and uploads another one behind the program it draws with changes that hash on

already use), and the decompiler is given that length. The cache holds 128 programs instead of 16: a fight in that
title draws with more than 16, and an eviction shifts the slots the recorded draws point at.

diagnostics). The stall went away on Windows with this change carried as a patch on v0.14.0 (the toolkit this port was

17bf55aa590b12b5e2c37c6885718526f8b59804.message:
cellGcm: NV3089 source origin is 12.4, the copy counted it 256 times too small

IMAGE_IN_POINT is 12.4 fixed point per axis, and DS_DX / DT_DY step the source with 20 fractional bits (1.0 =
0x100000). nv3089_blit's copy loops added the origin to that position as origin << 8, so a source offset counted
1/256 of what it is: for any origin under 256 texels the loops started at column 0 and row 0. The GPU paths in the
same function (rsx_live_draw_blit, rsx_live_draw_resolve_blit) already took origin >> 4, so the two disagreed, and
nv3089_engine_read, which writes the source rectangle back from the draw engine before the copy, took it as origin >> 4
for its start and << 8 for its end.

A title that resolves a supersampled scene in 512x512 tiles with a one texel origin (in_uv 0x00100010, SoulCalibur II HD,
six 2:1 blits) got the first row and column of every tile black: the loops read column 0 and row 0, which the engine
write-back (starting at 1) had not covered.

The origin now enters every computation as origin << 16 (nv3089_origin), in the engine write-back and in both copy
loops (linear and the NV309E swizzled one), so the loops read from the texel the origin names and the write-back covers
exactly what they read. Also reported by undecuple on the first version of this change, which made the write-back follow
the wrong loop.

The test plays the engine (guest_read stores, into the rectangle it is given, a pixel that names its own source position)
and checks that destination pixel (x, y) is the source pixel at (origin + x * scale, origin + y * scale), for origins of
0, 1, 3 and 20 texels at 1:1, 2:1 and 4:1; five of the six cases fail on v0.15.0.

18993f185aa89d35a2b7c7cb2d25483e00508434.message:
metal engine: PS3_AA=fxaa and PS3_SHARPEN in the present pass

Both off by default; off, the present is the same copy (and gamma) it
was.

PS3_AA=fxaa runs FXAA 3.11 (quality preset 29, luma from RGB, alpha
kept) over the display buffer at the guest's resolution, into a texture
of its own, before the present samples it. PS3_SHARPEN=0..1 adds AMD
FidelityFX CAS (the non-scaling form) to the present pass itself, with
its taps one source texel apart, ahead of the video out gamma. CAS
weighs its sharpening by the headroom in each 3x3 neighbourhood, so it
does not ring or clip where an edge is already at black or white.

test_metal_present_post.m drives eng_blit_to_display on synthetic
images: off is an exact copy, FXAA blends a staircase and leaves flat
areas and alpha alone, CAS steepens a soft edge, less at 0.2 than at 1.

1ba3657c934543fc430162ece2638d552502ff08.message:
rsx engine: 3D textures

A unit whose SET_TEXTURE_FORMAT dimension is 3 with a depth in CONTROL3
was uploaded as its first slice and sampled as a 2D texture. inFAMOUS 2's
occlusion volumes look up an 8x8x8 cone table that way, and every prop
and character got a dark box round it.

- rsx_swizzle_offset_3d: the Morton order of a swizzled volume (x, y and
  z bits interleaved while each axis has bits left).
- The engine sizes a volume by its slices (halving with each level),
  de-swizzles a slice into rows and decodes it with the 2D path, and
  uploads each slice through two optional backend calls,
  texture_create_3d / texture_upload_3d. The cache keys an entry by its
  depth as well. A backend without them keeps the old first-slice
  behaviour.
- The fragment decompiler takes a volume mask: such a unit is declared
  Texture3D and sampled with three coordinates (TXP divides them by w).
  The new rsx_fp_decompile_buffered_shadow_color_expand_vol_ex carries the
  mask; the other entry points pass none, so 2D-only programs are
  byte-identical.
- Metal implements the two calls with MTLTextureType3D.

1e6f4c8e744a66f6f5163f6f8def38470742e50b.message:
vulkan: colour feedback snapshots for draws that sample their own target

A draw that samples the colour target it is writing gets, on Metal, a
copy of that target taken just before it (rsx_draw_backend.color_snapshot).
In-place deferred lighting works this way: read the albedo, write the lit
colour over it. The Vulkan backend had no such hook, so the engine fell
back to the guest-memory bytes at the target's address, which hold
whatever was last stored there.

On Twisted Metal (BCES01010) the G-buffer's first target (0x00AB0000) is
also the UI target. Its lighting passes therefore read the previous
frame's menu instead of the albedo just drawn, lit it, and composited it
into the next frame. That is the red frame, the red and green splatter
and the white logo on its main menu.

vk_eng_color_snapshot copies the target into a new image of the same
format and size, and ends with a barrier so the copy is visible to the
next draw. Every operation here is already one synchronous submission,
so the copy is in command order. The copy is a COLOR object marked
`snapshot`, so the engine can take a crossbar view of it; it is never an
attachment, so releasing it drops no framebuffer. A lit frame asks for
one copy per light, so released copies return their images to a pool of
eight, drained at engine shutdown.

32a85600293ba2cf2a21bcb1150bcc0dbd6fb63a.message:
vulkan: present on its own command buffer, in two halves a host can split

The FIFO walker and the present shared one command buffer and one
fence, and a present waited for two GPU round trips: the engine's blit
of the flipped surface into the offscreen target, then the copy of that
target into the readback buffer. A host that presents on the walker's
thread holds the walker for all of that, about 1.3 ms per frame headless.
One that moves the present to a thread of its own still had to hold its
walker lock for the whole present, since both recorded into s_vk.cmd.

On Twisted Metal (BCES01010) that is the window in which the title
moves put to its other ring segment and starts writing its next frame
over the one it left, JUMP out of it included. The walker resumes 2.4 ms
later and executes the new frame's data as commands.

The present now has its own command pool, command buffer and fences,
and comes in two halves:

- rsx_vulkan_backend_present_begin() records the blit and the copy out
  and submits them without waiting. It reads the flipped surface, so it
  runs under the host's walker lock, but only for the recording.
- rsx_vulkan_backend_present_finish() waits for that copy, reads the
  centre pixel and the dump back, and blits into the window. It may run
  while the walker drains the next frame.

rsx_vulkan_backend_present() is both, so existing hosts see no
difference. The fixed-function path, which draws into the offscreen
target itself, still finishes inside present_begin.

What keeps the two halves apart:
- vkQueueSubmit, vkQueuePresentKHR and vkDeviceWaitIdle go through
  queue_mu, since the queue is now used from two threads.
- The walker's next command buffer starts with a full barrier after a
  present's copy. Its per-image barriers already order most work after
  earlier submissions; this one covers the rest.
- No image is destroyed while a present's copy may still read it.
- present_mu keeps a flip in the command stream (presented on the

spu_dma: the identical-transfer halt also needs wall time

mfc_submit halts an SPU after SPU_DMA_REPEAT_LIMIT (256) identical
transfers in a row, on the reasoning that a job doing nothing but the same
DMA is wedged. A job that polls a value another agent writes does the same:
God of War: Ascension's EDGE geometry jobs wait for ring space by re-reading
an RSX label until the GPU catches up. 256 reads take well under a
millisecond, so the guard halted healthy jobs and the frame never completed.

Halt only when the repeats have also lasted SPU_DMA_REPEAT_SECS (default
30 s) of wall time. A truly wedged job is still caught, 30 s later.

3ca13f66211402f8d9b2e62a1ad9d6a92334f04e.message:
fix(template): mmap the guest arena on POSIX so vm_commit can mprotect it

The POSIX branch of alloc_guest_vm() allocated the 0xE0000000-byte flat
arena with calloc. glibc serves an allocation that size from its own mmap
chunk and returns a pointer 16 bytes past the page start, so vm_base was
never page-aligned. vm_commit() hands vm_base + addr to mprotect, which
rejects unaligned addresses with EINVAL; every commit failed, and
sys_memory_allocate answered CELL_ENOMEM to every call. A title that
retries the allocation spins forever (Warhawk: 19.7 M calls in 60 s).

Map the arena with mmap(MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS|MAP_NORESERVE) instead,
as runtime/memory/vm.h already does: page-aligned, zero-filled, lazily
backed. ppu_vm_size and the Windows VirtualAlloc path are unchanged.
macOS was unaffected only because libmalloc page-aligns large blocks.

Verified: Warhawk NPEA00017 boots headless on Linux to its intro movie;
check_ppu_scaffold.py reports no regression.

3d5d03bdc7f627a424fb53ce42175984d596a377.message:
runtime: classify syscall 14 by guest address segment

sys_process_is_spu_lock_line_reservation_address answered EINVAL for
every address above the 256 MB VM_MAIN window (0x00010000..0x1000FFFF),
including the rest of segment 0x1 that the same guest allocator hands
out. SPURS validates its management areas through this syscall during
cellSpursInitialize and aborts init on failure, so a legitimate
management area produced a spurious CELL_SPURS_CORE_ERROR_PERM and every
SPU job the instance would have run stayed unstarted.

The contract is RPCS3's process_is_spu_lock_line_reservation_address
(Emu/Cell/lv2/sys_process.cpp): classify by the address segment
(0x0/0x1/0x2/0xC/0xE reservation-capable; 0xF refuses RawSPU; 0xD
refuses; sys_vm mappings refuse, holes in the mapped region EINVAL; rest
EINVAL) with the flags masked to the two SPU bits. The old sys_vm EPERM
check is kept, now through the tracked mappings (g_sys_vm_maps): a
covered address answers EPERM, a hole in the mapped region EINVAL,
matching RPCS3's default branch.

The classification moves to runtime/syscalls/lv2_lock_line.c so
tests/syscalls can unit-test it without linking the syscall layer.

Test: tests/syscalls/test_lock_line (27 checks: segments 0x0/0x1/0x2/
0xC/0xE OK, 0xF EPERM with RawSPU, 0xD EPERM, sys_vm covered/hole/empty,
flag validation).

45baa4791a794597cfaa0d0d4879347cb637b581.message:
rsx engine: 2D transfers read FP16 colour targets

A transfer out of a render target first writes the GPU's pixels back to
guest memory (rsx_draw_engine_guest_read), but only A8R8G8B8 surfaces were
looked up. Twisted Metal renders its bloom and Sweet Tooth's flaming hair
into an FP16 RGBA target and copies that out with NV3089 for its SPU
post-FX; the copy found no surface, the SPUs got stale memory, and neither
the bloom nor the flames reached the image.

The lookup now takes FP16 RGBA targets too. A transfer counts 32-bit
pixels, so the readback covers every surface pixel the transfer's bytes
touch and stores exactly those bytes, as big-endian R,G,B,A halves: the
layout rsx_texture_decode reads W16_Z16_Y16_X16_FLOAT from. A transfer
INTO an FP16 target is still not pushed: color_target_write takes
A8R8G8B8 rows.

4f223b376f890582608dcd00a3ae2b3ab9e7b483.message:
cellAudio: let WASAPI shared mode convert the 48 kHz stereo float stream

The Windows backend opens the default render endpoint in shared mode with
a fixed 48 kHz, 2-channel IEEE-float format. Shared mode only accepts the
device's own mix format unless the stream asks the audio engine to
convert, so on any output not running exactly that format (44.1 kHz, 5.1,
24-bit PCM mix) IAudioClient::Initialize fails with
AUDCLNT_E_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT (0x88890008), the backend gives up and every
title runs silent.

Pass AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_AUTOCONVERTPCM | AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_SRC_DEFAULT_QUALITY
on both Initialize attempts (event-driven and polled). The flags are
defined locally when the SDK headers predate them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

517fc717f73030d62dbaa9a991c118c6bd3cd6a2.message:
spu: the single-precision fast path four lanes at a time with AVX2

On x86, spu_fa/fs/fm/fma/fms/fnms took the per-lane path: each lane
widened to double on its own, and a call per instruction. arm64 has had
a NEON path doing the four lanes at once. This is the same path for
x86 with AVX2: the lanes widened to one f64x4 (exact), the operation,
the 29 low significand bits cleared, narrowed (exact). The lane rules are
the NEON ones: an ordinary single or a true +-0 keeps the vector result,
a zero result loses its sign, fa/fs also needs the exponents within 29,
and fma keeps a lane only when TwoSum says the add did not round onto a
24-bit boundary. Other lanes are redone one by one by the exact path.

test_spu_float_neon compares the vector path with the exact references
bit for bit; it now runs on x86 with AVX2 too, and in the Linux CI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

57570462551fcc9c6f2391276953b1a5c91c48f1.message:
cellFiber: the SDK's scheduler API in place of the made-up one

libs/spurs/cellFiber.{c,h} exposed cellFiberPpuInitialize/Finalize, a CellFiber handle, a
four-argument cellFiberPpuCreateFiber(fiber, entry, arg, attr), SwitchFiber, Sleep/Wakeup and
error codes from 0x80410801. None of that is the SDK's. The HLE binds by name, so a title
importing the real cellFiberPpuCreateFiber landed in the four-argument function and read its
eight arguments from the wrong registers.

The SDK's PPU fibers are scheduler based, and this implements them:

- _cellFiberPpuInitialize, _cellFiberPpuSchedulerAttributeInitialize and
  _cellFiberPpuAttributeInitialize (attributes are zeroed, 256 bytes each);
- cellFiberPpuInitializeScheduler / FinalizeScheduler, and
  cellFiberPpuCreateFiber(scheduler, fiber, entry, arg, priority, eaStack, sizeStack, attr);
- cellFiberPpuRunFibers: runs the fibers on the calling thread until every one has ended, lowest
  priority number first, creation order among equals. A scheduler whose fibers wait for a signal
  from another thread waits for it instead of returning;
- WaitSignal / SendSignal (a signal sent early is kept), JoinFiber (from a fiber, which hands
  control back to the scheduler meanwhile, or from any thread, with the exit status), Yield,
  Exit and Self.

Each fiber runs the guest entry through the PPU thread trampoline on its own host stack (ucontext,
Windows fibers on Windows) with its own ppu_context; r1 is inside the guest stack the caller
passed, r3 the argument, and the entry's return value the exit status. The error codes are the
SDK's 0x8076xxxx, and the structures have the SDK's sizes and 128-byte alignment (scheduler 512,
fiber 896, both attributes 256).

Not implemented: the contents of the attributes, and the cellFiberPpuUtil* worker control. Yield,
Exit and Self follow the documented behaviour and are covered by the unit test only; the port that
this was written for does not call them.

tests/fiber_switch is rewritten for the new API: run order and arguments, guest stack point

COLOR_MASK_MRT (0x0370, A,R,G,B at bits 0..3 of the nibble) and a bit
each of BLEND_ENABLE_MRT (0x036C), as RPCS3 reads them
(color_mask_*(index), blend_enabled_surface_*).

Giving every target A's state was wrong both ways. inFAMOUS 2's light
volumes add into target A with B and C masked off, and the shared state
added every light into the G-buffer: lit props blew out to white, with a
bright rectangle round each light. Its material passes write B and C's
alpha with A's alpha masked, which left them stale.

The engine decodes both registers into the render state (and the
pipeline key), and the Metal backend applies them per attachment.
PS3RECOMP_METAL_MRT_MASK=0 restores the old behaviour for bisecting.

spurs_job: keep the job's first frame below its cache buffers

spu_run_spurs_job lays a job out as binary, I/O, output, scratch + stack,
then the cache-hinted inputs, so cacheBuffer[0] starts at the stack top.
$sp was set to stack_top - 16. A SPU function saves its link register in
its caller's frame at 16($sp), so the entry's first store wrote 16 bytes
over the start of cacheBuffer[0].

Twisted Metal's Edge geometry jobs keep their viewport there. They read
x = 0x3FF00 (the return address in $lr) and width = height = 0, so the
screen-space scale was zero, every triangle of a skinned mesh had zero
area, and the main view culled them all: Sweet Tooth was missing from the
main menu, while the shadow passes (which skip that culling) drew him.

Start $sp at stack_top - 32 so the caller's 32-byte frame is part of the
stack.

  against a working one.
- RSX_FP_DEBUG=<hex>:<n>:<reg[.swz]> makes that program export register

rather than raced for. A peer SPU has the bitset line reserved, the main
thread holds the lock, a second thread starts the host operation and is
held at the lock, an SPU commit sets another task's bit under the lock,
and only then is the host operation let through.

- spu_taskset_signal_task(task 4) against a commit of task 3's bit:
  both bits must be set.
- spu_taskset_wait_signal(task 3) consuming its signal against a commit
  of task 4's bit: task 4's bit must survive.

On master both fail (0x08000000 for 0x18000000, 0 for 0x08000000),
the same lost bits as Twisted Metal's post-FX barrier. Run in the Linux
and macOS workflows next to the SPURS task wake test.

cellPad: the small motor rumbles at full strength, and a rumble lasts until it changes

motor * 257 it reached the host at 257/65535, 1/255 of full, which a pad
does not feel. And each SDL request ran for 100 ms, while a PS3 title
sets the motors once and they stay on until it sets them again, so a long
rumble stopped almost at once (inFAMOUS 2 only calls when the value
changes).

The small motor is now on at full, the large one keeps 0-255. The last
request per port is kept, sent with a 1 s duration and renewed from the
pad poll every 400 ms while it is non-zero, so it lasts as long as the
title wants and still stops within a second if the title stops polling.

gets the level fix.

6752b12939e5c6a34be15c85b9d1e813e19360ab.message:
cellGcm: bounded semaphore acquire; the stuck-get watchdog leaves waits alone

GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1 makes NV406E ACQUIRE block the drain, as the hardware
does, but the stuck-get watchdog counts drain passes, not time: a drain
that stops on an acquire, or on a self-JUMP park, stops every pass at the
same get, so after eight passes (a few milliseconds) it resynced to put
and dropped everything in between. For a park that happens before the
title has patched it into a JUMP to the commands it just wrote at the
ring start, i.e. before GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS has had a chance to run out.
inFAMOUS 2 stopped presenting for good that way in about one run in five
("stuck-get" at a self-jump with no "jump-park" before it).

A pass that stops on an acquire or a park now resets the watchdog; each
of those waits has its own bound. The acquire gets one:
GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS=<ms> consumes an acquire that has waited that long on
the same label and value, and says so, so a label nobody ever writes
cannot wedge the drain. inFAMOUS 2 acquires a label its SPU lighting job
writes every frame; with GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1 GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS=200 its
lit props stop flashing white and its characters stop rendering black.

byte at a time, testing TEX_RGBA for every pixel, and at the -O2 the
runtime builds with GCC vectorises neither.

copy, the two loops were about a quarter of the FIFO thread's CPU time
during boot (in-process sampling of that thread: 19.5% guest_read,

1280x720 frame converts in 0.55 ms instead of 0.98 ms with the
runtime's flags (GCC 16, -O2 -msse4.1), with identical output. In the
same Twisted Metal window the two functions drop to 14.2% and 6.9%.

7208d22b25b342696685640d1a715278e17e74f9.message:
cellFs: an AIO read keeps the fd's position and cannot interleave

cellFsAioRead did a bare seek + fread on the fd's shared FILE*. Its own
comment says AIO reads are absolute and leave the fd's position alone; they
moved it, so the next cellFsRead continued from wherever the AIO stopped.

audio streamers) on the same fd, so another thread's seek could land between
the seek and the read.

take) across the seek, the read and the seek back to the saved position.
The request id counter is atomic for the same reason.

master the cellFsRead after an AIO read gets the wrong bytes, and 3373 of
8000 AIO reads racing from four threads return someone else's data; with
this change both pass.

7c1d6f128d3d5af2b0e992cb4e2fa88271931fa4.message:
cellGcmSys: don't let a wrapped ring overwrite commands the RSX hasn't read

God of War HD fills its 3 MB command ring at boot and wraps it through the
runtime's buffer-full callback. Three things then let it write over
commands the walker had not reached, after which the walker decoded vertex
floats as JUMPs (0x3F800000 -> JUMP 0x1F800000) and resynced away frames:

- The recycle waited for g_gcm_fifo_drained_ea == begin, which is also true
  before the walker has moved at all, so it often didn't wait. It now waits
  for the walker to take a backward JUMP, i.e. the JUMP-to-begin it wrote.
- The wait gave up after 2 s in total. A ring of hundreds of tiny frames
  takes the draw engine far longer than that, and it was making progress.
  The bound is now 2 s without progress (60 s overall).
- While that callback waits, the title's context still reads
  current == end, which the drain's own overrun recycle took as an overrun
  and teleported get to begin, dropping the tail. It stands down while the
  callback is waiting.

The drain also stops at every flip unless backlogged, and measured the
backlog as put - get, so a wrapped ring (put behind get, the most backlogged
case) looked like no backlog at all. It is now measured around the ring when
both pointers are inside the title's context; other layouts are unchanged.

GCM_RECDBG reports the walker during the recycle wait, and
GCM_DRAINDBG_EVERY=<n> sets how often GCM_DRAINDBG logs a pass. Not run
against the other ports' regression gate (their games aren't here).

undefined, and MTLMathModeSafe on the library does not change that. D3D's

and the guest programs were written for hardware that behaves that way.
inFAMOUS 2 has a sky/bloom pass that produced NaN on Metal only.
The generated MSL now uses the precise:: overloads, which follow IEEE
fmax/fmin; PS3RECOMP_MSL_FAST=1 keeps the fast:: spelling.

93cccd1d3c5332fff9bd13de773666c816b76198.message:
fp decompiler: honour perspective_corr on texcoord reads

SRC2 bit 31 (perspective_corr) on an instruction's texcoord read
multiplies the input by 1/w, as RPCS3's decompiler does ("Perspective
correct flag multiplies the result by 1/w"). The bit was ignored. A
vertex program that writes uv*w relies on it: inFAMOUS 2's water does,
for the screen copy it samples, and read raw the coordinates land far
outside the copy and the river renders black.

1/w comes from the fragment position. FXC (D3D12) gives SV_POSITION.w as
clip w, but glslang lowers it to SPIR-V FragCoord, whose w is already 1/w
(and Metal's [[position]] is (x, y, z, 1/w)), so the glslang paths define
RSX_FRAGCOORD_W_IS_RCP and the helper picks the right form. The helper is
emitted only when a program uses it, so every other program is
byte-identical.

a4b4a21d8d089e79d28e751c52f433bccc5674ac.message:
sys_spu: an SPU thread starts in the lifted image its own bytes identify

spu_lifted_thread_setup chose the thread's image by asking the registry which image owns the thread's entry point.
SPU programs all start near the same LS addresses (0xD0..0xF0), so two registered images can have code at one entry,
and the entry resolves to whichever registered first: the thread ran the other program's lifted code. SoulCalibur II
HD has two such images, and its audio engine (MultiStream) ran the wrong one.

sys_spu_thread_group_start now fingerprints the thread's sys_spu_image (the lookup the registry fallback right
below it already did) and gives spu_lifted_thread_setup the id of the image registered for those bytes,
spu_lifted_thread_desc.image_id. 0 keeps the lookup by entry point, so a thread whose image is not registered
behaves as before. The fingerprint lookup is one helper now, shared with the fallback.

The test replaces the registry with two images that both have code at 0xD0, A registered first, and follows what group
start does: B's bytes give B (the entry-based lookup, shown by the third check, gives A), A's give A, bytes nothing
registered and a thread without an image give 0. The new interface does not exist on v0.15.0, so the test only
builds with this change.

a594fa06fe400bd0ae86c525bf9b82bad468d526.message:
rsx engine: re-hash cached textures sparsely, in full every eighth frame

Every cached texture was hashed in full at its first use in a frame, to
notice the guest rewriting it. In inFAMOUS 2's New Marais that is about
950 textures and 88 MB a frame, 2.5 ms of the RSX thread, for the four
or so that actually change.

Now each use checks 64 bytes out of every 2 KB plus the last 64, and the
full hash runs when that check differs, when 8 frames have passed since
the entry's last full hash (new entries start staggered by slot, so the
full hashes spread out), always for a texture of 16 KB or less, and on
the next use after a surface store the engine itself made into the
texture. A whole rewrite (video, UI, streaming) is still seen at once; a
small write between the sampled blocks of a large texture can take up
to 7 frames. PS3RECOMP_ENG_TEXHASH_FULL=1 restores the full hash every
frame.

under 256 texels. It now uses nv3089_origin(), the helper #358
introduces for the per-pixel loops, defined the same way so the two

a8572e9962344fe5cb49b78f7b647888fcce15c1.message:
cellGcmSys: publish get past a semaphore RELEASE before its label

The FIFO walker wrote a RELEASE's label at once but published the control
register's get only at a JUMP and at the end of the pass. On the RSX the
semaphore write lands after the command has been fetched, so a title that
sees the label may read get once and take it as the RSX's position.
Ratchet & Clank: Tools of Destruction waits for a label, reads get, then
spins until its own put equals it; the snapshot from before the RELEASE
never did, and boot stalled there.

The RELEASE now publishes get past the whole command (unless
GCM_GET_EQ_PUT is set), then a release fence, then the label.
test_gcm_get_on_release drives OFFSET/RELEASE and a two-method
ACQUIRE+RELEASE through the walker and reads both from a user-command
probe mid-pass, with and without GCM_GET_EQ_PUT.

a98af7c9075a6911d4ec5021a512941cb9f9d11f.message:
cellGcm: get follows the walker across a JUMP

On the RSX, get is the fetch pointer, so a title polling it sees the
GPU leave a command segment as soon as the JUMP out of it is taken.
The walker published get only at the end of a drain pass. On a slow
host that comes tens of milliseconds after the JUMP: Twisted Metal
(BCES01010) has boot-time passes of 50 to 165 ms, mostly NV3089 blits
and surface readbacks.

Twisted Metal flushes put into its other ring segment, then writes the
next frame over the segment it left. When the walker reaches the JUMP
at the old put late, the JUMP has already been overwritten. The title
port works around this by waiting, after its flush, for get to leave
the old put. With get published only at the end of the pass, that wait
ran into its 100 ms bound 4 times per boot even though the JUMP had
been taken at once. With this change it does so 2 times in 12 runs.

A taken JUMP now publishes its target as get. A park (a JUMP to itself)
publishes nothing, and GCM_GET_EQ_PUT keeps its own value.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

b1f14fff9e8174b3575212691ebdaef7aae069b7.message:
rsx: cache HLSL -> SPIR-V translations, in memory and optionally on disk

glslang takes 20-150 ms per shader, on the thread that walks the FIFO,
and the engine asks for the same HLSL again for every pipeline that
shares a program. Twisted Metal (BCES01010) translates 236 shaders in
its first minute, 74 of them distinct: 4.4 s of glslang per 90 s run,
95 stalls over 20 ms.

rsx_hlsl_to_spirv now keeps each translation, keyed by the stage and the
whole HLSL text, so a hit returns exactly the words that text translated
to. PS3RECOMP_SPIRV_CACHE=<existing directory> also keeps them on disk,
one file per shader; the file stores the key, the glslang version and
the translator's build stamp, and any mismatch is a miss that rewrites
the file. Failed translations are not cached.

Twisted Metal, 90 s runs: glslang time 4.4 s -> 1.1-2.0 s with the
memory cache alone, 5 ms with a warm disk cache, and no translation
over 20 ms.

b883922940d53efafac47dcc0b63dac7535294c5.message:
rsx_draw_engine, vulkan: honour the depth bounds test

NV4097 SET_DEPTH_BOUNDS_TEST_ENABLE (0x0380) with SET_DEPTH_BOUNDS_MIN and
_MAX (0x0384, 0x0388, floats) rejects a fragment whose stored depth lies
outside the bounds, whatever the depth test says. The draw engine never
read those registers, so a bounded draw covered the whole target.

Twisted Metal's deferred renderer relies on it: its sun pass is bounded to
[0, 0.999984] (the geometry) and the sky drawn right after it to
[0.999984, 1] (the far plane), both with the depth test off. Unbounded, the
sky overwrote the sun light everywhere and the HDR buffer came out almost
black.

The enable is pipeline state (rsx_be_render_state.depth_bounds_test, part
of the pipeline key); the bounds reach the backend before every draw through
a new optional hook, set_depth_bounds, like the stencil reference, so moving
them does not build pipelines. Vulkan enables the depthBounds feature when
the device has it and sets the bounds dynamically, clamped to [0, 1];
without the feature the test stays off, as before, with one log line.
Metal and the fixed-function path leave the hook unset and draw as before.

Tests: test_rsx_draw_engine checks the key, the bounds and that moving them
builds no pipeline (4 new checks, failing without the engine change).
ps3recomp_host --depthbounds draws red at z = 0.25, then blue bounded to
[0, 0.5] and green bounded to [0.5, 1] with the depth test off, and expects
blue; it runs in the Vulkan workflow's engine pass under the validation
layer.

b8a7c5b30057bd863df592edb02e1d4875ca2551.message:
fp decompiler: read FACING, TC8 and TC9

Fragment program inputs 0xC/0xD (TC8/TC9) and 0xE (FACING) read as zero.
Two-sided materials multiply the interpolated normal by FACING; read as
zero, inFAMOUS 2's foliage and character heads normalised a null vector
into the G-buffer and lit black.

FACING is +1 on a front face and -1 on a back face (SV_IsFrontFace,
[[front_facing]] in MSL). TC8/TC9 come from vertex outputs o15 and o6, as
in RPCS3's register table (TEX9 shares the point-size register); the
vertex program and the engine's fixed VS write them after TEXCOORD7, so the
earlier interpolants keep their locations. The fragment side declares
tc8/tc9 and the face flag only when the body reads them, so every other
program is byte-identical and keeps its cached pipeline.
