c1cdab11912f442698f32c04fd7a2a64b7a1226b.message:
cellGcm: a flip queued in the command stream completes when the drain reaches it

The 60 Hz tick (cellGcm_request_tick, and cellGcmTickFlip) completed a
pending flip on every beat, wherever the walker was. For a flip queued
into the stream (gcm_flip_into_fifo) that is too early: the RSX flips
when it executes the flip, after everything queued before it.

Twisted Metal (BCES01010) paces itself on the flip status and rebuilds
a command segment once the flip after it is done. Completed early, the
title rewrote segments the walker had not executed yet; the walker then
read half-written segments as commands (JUMPs to float data, unmapped
CALLs, and junk register writes such as the vertex data base offset,
which shattered every later draw's geometry).

Count the flips queued into the stream and the markers the drain
reaches. A beat completes a flip only if the drain has executed a
marker since the last completion, or if no flip is waiting in the
stream (a flip that never went through it). A flip written but not yet
flushed does not hold back one already executed.

A flip must never wait on a marker that will not be executed. A resync
that skips over a marker counts it. When the walker is lost in unmapped
IO and jumps straight to put, every flip still outstanding is written
off: Twisted Metal's boot resyncs that way about one run in three
(get=0x0FD00000) and the flip it abandoned in the other ring segment
otherwise held the status at WAITING for good. reached never passes
queued, so a written-off marker that is executed later is not counted
twice. GCM_FLIP_NEEDS_FIFO keeps its meaning.

e25898001640a13ef2863ec42b22c278740e9b3b.message:
spurs: update taskset bitsets atomically on task create and exit (#340 follow-up)

The ready/pending/enabled bitsets (+0x10/+0x20/+0x30) share the taskset's
first 128-byte line with the SPU task library (GETLLAR/PUTLLC). Three host
writers updated them without the lock-line lock around the whole change:

- cellSpursCreateTask searched the enabled bitset for a free id with
  vm_read8 and set the bit later in spurs_taskset_add_task;
- spurs_taskset_add_task set enabled and ready with spurs_bitset_set (a
  vm_read32 outside the lock, a vm_write32 inside it);
- spu_taskset_task_exited cleared the exiting task's bits under ts_lock,
  which no other writer of the line takes.

A task exit landing between CreateTask's read and its write was undone: the
exited task's enabled bit came back with no task behind it, and
cellSpursJoinTask2 on that id never returned. Killzone 3 hit it at quit to
menu: Havok's thread-pool destructor joined task 0 forever.

- spurs_taskset_take_slot(): the free-id search and the enabled bit as one
  step under the lock-line lock, so two callers never get the same id either.
- spurs_taskset_bitset_update(): a single bit set or clear on the raw guest
  bytes under the lock-line lock, then spu_coh_notify_write; add_task uses it.
- spu_taskset_task_exited: the bitset updates and the start scan under the
  lock-line lock, the dispatches after it is released.

Follows the signalled-bit fix (#340), which named these writers as left out.
New test runtime/spu/tests/test_spurs_taskset_bits_atomic.c, built like that
PR's: on the old code the exited task's bit comes back (0xE0000000 for
0x60000000); with the fix 6/6 pass.

e2ff37f3b699c5514c51f510d52ec1134c08b3e2.message:

read it through the ARGB lanes, where G and B are the resource's empty
components. A crossbar that sources G or B therefore sampled zero.

crossbar 0xAAEE (every output from G or B): every glyph came out with zero
colour and zero alpha, so all text was invisible while the button icons
(DXT) drew fine. Present X16 the way B8 already is: the value in R, G and B,
A opaque.

e310b6619e7fe655631a58e5997dfc197bbd876a.message:
diag: PS3_FTRACE, a frame timeline of who waits for whom

A sampling profile shows where CPU time goes, not why a frame takes
130 ms when no thread is busy for 130 ms. That is a latency chain: the
PPU waits on SPU tasks, the RSX walker waits on a label an SPU writes,
the present waits on the GPU. PS3_FTRACE=<start s>:<seconds>:<file>
records timestamped spans for a window and writes them out as text:

- PPU syscalls that block, with the guest call site; usleep poll runs
  merged per thread and call site;
- SPU busy and channel-wait spans, busy tagged with the lifted image and
  the SPURS workload id at LS 0x1DC;
- RSX FIFO drains, ACQUIRE waits, flips reached and flips requested;
- Metal: presents, CPU encode, GPU waits (present, flush, in-flight bound),
  readbacks, and each command buffer's own GPU time with its render pass,
  depth resolve and colour copy counts.

tools/ftrace_report.py turns a trace into a per-frame breakdown and an
ASCII timeline. The tracer is header-only (include/ps3emu/ps3_ftrace.h):
the hooked files are also built on their own by the self-contained
tests, and a new link dependency would break each of them. Off, each
hook is one load and a branch.

cellVdec: time stamps and frame rate for MPEG-2 pictures

Two things kept God of War: Ascension's menu video (MPEG-2, played through
its own player that paces display by time) on its first picture:

- Its demuxer sends every access unit without a time stamp (pts/dts both
  0xFFFFFFFF_FFFFFFFF). The picture item carried that through, so the player
  never saw time advance. An AU without a PTS now gets the next one on the
  stream's clock (one frame at the decoded frame rate, 90 kHz; 3003 when the
  rate is unknown), and a missing DTS takes the PTS.
- CellVdecMpeg2Info's frame_rate_code (+5) was left 0, which MPEG-2 calls
  forbidden; the player looks up the picture duration from it and got 0.
  Fill frame_rate_code from the decoded rate (nearest of the eight MPEG-2
  codes, 29.97 when unknown), plus aspect_ratio_information (+4) and
  progressive_sequence (+6).

the new VdecFfPicture.frame_ticks.

ef060b373f4f7794caa9bab83528c36f88e5f452.message:
spu: float compares four lanes at a time with SSE2

spu_fceq/fcgt/fcmeq/fcmgt were per-lane loops over 64-bit keys. Compilers
leave them scalar and branchy: on mixed data, fcgt took 41 ns. In Twisted
Metal's post-FX jobs spu_fcgt alone was 3.4% of the job workers' time.

A magnitude is at most 0x7FFFFFFF and its negation fits in 32 bits too, so
the keys compare as int32: clear the magnitude when the exponent is zero
(any two zeros are equal), negate it for a set sign bit, and compare with
pcmpeqd/pcmpgtd. fcgt takes 2.7 ns. The loops stay as spu_*_ref, and
SPU_SCALAR_HELPERS still selects them. SSE2 is in every x86-64 build
(__SSE2__, or _M_X64 for MSVC, which does not define __SSE2__).

metal engine: PS3_ANISO turns on anisotropic filtering for mipmapped samplers

PS3 titles rarely ask for anisotropic filtering, and at 720p that was a
fair trade. At a Mac's output size, ground and walls seen at a grazing
angle blur into their smaller mips a few metres from the camera.

PS3_ANISO=2..16 sets maxAnisotropy on the engine samplers that minify
linearly through a mip chain. Point-filtered and unmipped samplers keep
their filtering, so lookup tables, render targets and UI read the same
texels as before. Unset, nothing changes.

The new --mip-aniso host check draws --mip's two-level texture under a
quad stretched along y: isotropic filtering lands on level 1, anisotropic
filtering on level 0. CI runs it with PS3_ANISO=16 and requires it to
fail without.

rsx_d3d12: tell the FP decompiler the export width the draw used

which picks r0 as the colour export if the program wrote r0 at all. Each
draw already records SET_SHADER_CONTROL's 32-bit-exports bit (fp_exp32,
part of the pipeline key); the Metal, Vulkan and live-draw paths pass the
control word, this one threw it away.

The guess fails on programs that use r0 as a temp and export through h0.
God of War HD's 2x-AA resolve samples two adjacent subsamples A and B,
computes (B - A) / 2 in r0 and A + that in h0, and with r0 exported the
resolved scene was nearly black: the menu showed its HUD over black and
gameplay only the HUD. Passing the bit, both render their 3D scene.

The depth-export bits aren't recorded per draw, so they stay off, as they
were under AUTO. RSX_FP_CTRL_AUTO=1 restores the guess, as in live-draw.

fa001d0711cdc3852280a0cd52afd7ae70b5dc26.message:
cellGcmSys: a late flip completion no longer marks a newer flip done

The ticker marks a flip completion pending, but the flip handler (and
the DONE status with it) only runs when a guest thread next pumps. If
the title requested another flip in between, the late completion set
DONE over the new request; the ticker only completes WAITING flips, so
that flip's handler never ran. cellGcmSetWaitFlip did the same after its
64 ms bound. inFAMOUS 2 writes its next FIFO put from the flip handler
and hung with get == put on either path.

Each request now bumps a sequence number, the tick records the one it
completes, and the completion only marks DONE when no newer request has
arrived. The read-modify-write transitions run on different threads and
take a small spin lock. cellGcmSetWaitFlip leaves an outstanding flip to
the tick instead of forcing it DONE.

guest face culling is honoured now, so every odd triangle came out
back-facing and was culled. God of War HD draws its splash and loading
screens as 4-index strip quads; the lower-right half of each was missing.
Swap two vertices on odd triangles, as upload_strip_vp already does.

cellGcm: an unscaled NV3089 blit copies a row at a time

The 2D blit copied pixel by pixel through vm_read32/vm_write32, paying
per pixel the bounds and null-store checks, the store hooks, a
reservation lookup and two byte swaps that cancel. inFAMOUS 2 copies its
1280x720 G-buffer surfaces to main memory with NV3089 every frame for
its SPU lighting, and a quarter of the FIFO thread's time went there.

A blit with a 1:1 scale now moves each clipped row with one memmove,
and does the coherent-store bookkeeping per 128-byte line: an SPU
holding a reservation on a line the row overwrites loses it, as with a
PPU store. Scaled blits keep the per-pixel loop. NV3089_ROWCOPY=0
restores the per-pixel copy (which is what the PPU store watches see).

ff7c9eef28c375793946f4bc58a48db3794afea6.message:
spu: update a task's signalled bit atomically against SPU commits

spu_taskset_signal_task and spu_taskset_wait_signal set and clear the
task's bit in the taskset's signalled bitset with a vm_read32 then a
vm_write32. SPU tasks update the same line with GETLLAR/PUTLLC, under
the lock-line lock. The store took that lock, the read did not, so an
SPU commit between the two was overwritten with the stale word.

Twisted Metal (BCES01010) loses a wake this way in its post-FX taskset.
Six tasks meet at a cellSpursBarrier. The last one to arrive sets each
waiter's bit with PUTLLC. When task 3's host thread woke and cleared its
own bit, it wrote back a word read just before the releaser set task
4's bit. Task 4 slept forever, so the barrier never completed again,
the render thread waited on the tasks' completion word, and the frame
label the RSX acquires stopped after two frames.

Do the read-modify-write under the lock-line lock, on the raw guest
bytes (vm_write32 takes the lock itself and it does not nest), and
drop every reservation on the line.

Measured on Twisted Metal, 120 s on Vulkan: 12 post-FX signals then a
permanent stall before, 7116 signals at a steady ~10 frames/s after.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   └── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse
│   ├── hardware/             # cellGem, cellCamera, cellUsbd
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
└── docs/                     # See the Documentation table below
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

HLE implementations of the PS3 system libraries, written for this project. RPCS3 is a behavioural reference, not a code source. Most modules are complete. The ones still marked Partial are the media decoders (cellVdec, cellAdec, cellDmux, cellAtrac, cellAdecAtrac3p) and cellSpurs. [docs/MODULE_STATUS.md](docs/MODULE_STATUS.md) has one row per module and is the source for the counts.

| **Kernel Filesystem** | sys_fs (path mapping, real I/O) | ✅ Complete |
| **Filesystem** | cellFs (real file I/O, dir ops, stat, path translation) | ✅ Complete |
| **Save System** | cellSaveData (callback-driven, PARAM.SFO), cellGame | ✅ Complete |
| **Input** | cellPad (XInput/SDL2), cellKb, cellMouse | ✅ Complete |
| **Audio** | cellAudio (WASAPI/SDL2, mixing thread, multi-port) | ✅ Complete |
| **Video Output** | cellVideoOut (resolution config, 720p default) | ✅ Complete |
| **Codecs** | cellPngDec, cellJpgDec, cellGifDec (stb_image) | ✅ Complete |
| **Font** | cellFont (stb_truetype backend + fallback metrics) | ✅ Complete |
| **Network** | sys_net (BSD sockets, P2P), cellNet, cellNetCtl, cellHttpUtil, cellSsl, sceNp*, sceNpTrophy, sceNpMatching2 + Score over [psnr](docs/ONLINE.md) | ✅ Complete |
| **Hardware** | cellUsbd (USB), cellCamera (PS Eye), cellGem (PS Move) — stub, no devices | ✅ Complete |
| **Sync** | cellSync (atomic spinlocks, LF queue), cellSync2 (OS-backed) | ✅ Complete |
| **System** | cellRtc, cellMsgDialog, cellOskDialog, cellUserInfo, cellGameExec | ✅ Complete |
| **Localization** | cellL10n (UTF-8/16/32/UCS-2, ISO-8859-1, generic converter) | ✅ Complete |
| **Resolution** | cellResc (display modes, scaling, interlace, aspect ratio) | ✅ Complete |
| **Fibers** | cellFiber (PPU fiber scheduler via Windows Fibers/ucontext) | ✅ Complete |
| **AV Config** | cellAvconfExt (audio output info, gamma, sound availability) | ✅ Complete |

Full status tracking: [docs/MODULE_STATUS.md](docs/MODULE_STATUS.md)

perf(toolkit): the WWS interrupt stub runs on the microstepper; iret restore and ori there

(never lifted: it only exists at run time) runs on every interrupt and was

machine is not shared with a busy Steam.

33a46f59cb3be13934b42e92a32dd779075de37e.message:
fix(toolkit): translate the NV40 pack/unpack fragment opcodes

The fork's fragment decompiler had no case for PK4UB, UP4UB, PKG, UPG (nor PK4B/UP4B, PK2H/UP2H, PK2US/UP2US): each was skipped with a TODO comment and the destination kept its previous value. inFAMOUS 2's character materials use PK4UB->UPG and PKG->UP4UB as their sRGB<->linear conversion right before the outputs, so Cole's scalp rendered saturated green and skin tones were off. Implemented after RPCS3's FragmentProgramDecompiler (packUnorm4x8 bitcast into a float, _builtin_pkg/_builtin_upg with linear_to_srgb/srgb_to_linear). An unhandled opcode now prints its number and raw words in the dumped shader.

Metal diagnostics: PS3RECOMP_METAL_PASS_LOG=2 splits a pass per pipeline/texture set; _MIN/_EVERY and PS3RECOMP_METAL_SURF_DUMP_MIN make the frame thresholds configurable (the cutscene never reached the 1000-record default). Analysis helpers: passlog.py, psfeatures.py, surfstats.py, greenshare.py.

37c946b286f8187075f5e78d574ea1cb871bd0d1.message:
perf(toolkit): no depth resolve for texture units the FP never reads; PS3_FTRACE frame timeline

PS3_FTRACE=<start>:<seconds>:<file> records who waits for whom (PPU
blocking syscalls and usleep runs with their guest call site, SPU
busy/wait, RSX ACQUIRE waits, drains, flips, presents, Metal encode,
GPU waits, readbacks and each command buffer's GPU time and pass
count); tools/ftrace_report.py turns it into a per-frame breakdown and
an ASCII timeline.

It showed the New Marais walk present spending 46 ms of GPU in 1120
render passes, 1075 broken by depth resolves: forward materials (FP
3e92fd7ffdfc0f5f, tex0 x constant) leave a unit enabled on the depth
buffer, and each of their depth writes invalidated the copy. The engine
now resolves depth only for units rsx_fp_texture_mask says the program
samples (PS3RECOMP_ENG_ZRESOLVE_UNREAD=1 restores the old behaviour).
Interleaved A/B, same binary: walk 11.9/11.3 fps vs 7.5/7.5, dock 14
vs 12, present GPU 4.7 ms vs 44 ms, frames identical.
PS3RECOMP_ENG_RESOLVE_LOG=1 names the FPs behind the resolves.

48f8156846d64bde264dd4f6057757b373c4e4e9.message:
fix(toolkit): ps3_ms_now counts on macOS; MRT colour mask and blend per target, opt-in

ps3_ms_now() returned 0 on POSIX, so every timeout built on it
(GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS, GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS) never expired and the rate logs
read 0; it now uses CLOCK_MONOTONIC (upstream 91ee29f, found by the
profiling session).

The draw engine gave every target of an MRT set target A's colour mask
and blend. The RSX has COLOR_MASK_MRT (0x0370, an A,R,G,B nibble per
target) and BLEND_ENABLE_MRT (0x036C), and inFAMOUS 2 relies on them:
its cutscene G-buffer writes A=RGB, B=ARGB, C=AGB (the display buffer's
R keeps the shadow cascades p128/p135 accumulate) and its decals write
four targets. The hardware rule is decoded into the render state and the
pipeline key and applied per attachment in the Metal backend, as RPCS3
does -- but behind PS3RECOMP_METAL_MRT_MASK=1, default 0 (the old
behaviour), because in New Marais it tints the scene green: a channel
some other pass should write is not reaching that surface yet. Test in
test_rsx_draw_engine.

Diagnostics, all off by default: PS3RECOMP_ENG_MRTLOG=1|2 (each pass's
targets, masks and blend; colour clears), PS3RECOMP_METAL_TINT_PIPE
(paint what up to eight pipelines draw in solid colours),
PS3RECOMP_ENG_FPK_N (how many draws PS3RECOMP_ENG_FPK_PIPE logs).

49cd56e0033809bfd17267c09a83f9765947cec5.message:
fix(pad): controller hot-plug and live remapping in the in-game menu (pending toolkit patch)

A DualSense switched off and on again was never picked up until the game
restarted. cellPad opened controllers by SDL device index == PS3 port and
kept asking SDL_IsGameController(i); Homebrew's SDL2 is sdl2-compat on SDL3,
whose device-index list is refreshed only by SDL_NumJoysticks() or by the
SDL2 event filter (installed with an SDL window, which the Metal build never
creates), so index 0 kept the switched-off pad's old instance id forever.
Each poll now drains SDL's joystick/controller events, closes a removed
controller by its handle, and on a device event (or every second while a
port is free) rescans and opens what is new: the same pad gets its port
back by GUID, motors off, no stale rumble; ports 1-3 report
CELL_PAD_STATUS_ASSIGN_CHANGES. Polls are serialised (SetActDirect too).

The in-game menu's Controls tab gains a rebind table (keyboard, mouse,
controller per PS3 button; applies live, saved to the launcher's
input.toml), "Restore defaults", a live input mode (PS3_INPUT_MODE) and a
mouse camera on/off switch.

Toolkit side: infamous2-lle/patches/pending/pad-hotplug-live-remap.patch,
with tests test_pad_hotplug.c (faked SDL behaving like sdl2-compat) and
writer round-trips in test_pad_input_map.c. README/ROADMAP updated.

fix(gfx): honour the RSX depth-bounds test; depth-copy cache crash

and every light and occlusion volume with NV4097 0x0380/0x0384/0x0388;
the engine ignored it. Metal's setDepthTestMinBound traps on the M4, so
the fragment program reads the 24-bit depth copy on a free texture unit
and discards outside the bounds (PS3RECOMP_ENG_DEPTH_BOUNDS=0 = old,
live toggle). The mask program already fades itself to its cascade's
slice, so the reachable dusk scenes look the same; the doubled shadows of
Erik's daylight yard were not reproduced headless (ROADMAP, open).

Also: the Metal depth-as-colour copy cache returned a released handle
once its slot was reused (crop pair at 0x0F770000) and the 2D view of
the resulting 3D texture aborted the game (2 of 2 dusk walks on the
current fold; 0 of 2 with the fix).

5db31a44f56e52416b5e160a839ba0cd6585b459.message:
fix(toolkit): flip status race lost the flip handler's deferred put; SPU fault diagnostics

A late ppu_gcm_pump delivery of an older flip set the status to DONE over a
newer request's WAITING, so cellGcmTickFlip never completed the new flip and
the game's flip handler never wrote the put it had deferred: the GPU-SSAO
hang with ref stuck at get == put. Flip requests and ticks carry a sequence
number now; the pump marks DONE only when no newer request is pending.
Six GPU-SSAO runs without a flip hang, walk 26-27 fps.

Diagnostics for the remaining rare SPU fault: a per-SPU interrupt event ring
dumped on faults, and a host backtrace (with the image base for atos) on
unresolved SPU branches.

6c640f2ad9734c11b1b2e73762c59af732180e90.message:
fix(toolkit): the stuck-get watchdog no longer overrides a self-JUMP park

The FIFO walker stops at a JUMP to its own address while inFAMOUS 2 links
its command blocks: it moves put to the ring start first and only then
rewrites the park as a JUMP to the new commands. The park has its own
time-based grace (GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS) for exactly that, but the generic
stuck-get watchdog counts drain passes: a park stops every pass at the same
get, so after 8 passes -- a few milliseconds -- it resynced to put before
the patch landed and dropped the frame's commands. The game then stopped
presenting for good: m2 on the daytime pier at ~40 s of gameplay
('stuck-get' at a 0x2055C940 self-jump, no 'jump-park' before it), and
about one New Marais run in five. Parks are now exempt from the pass
counter, as semaphore-acquire waits already were.

Not the cause of the cityfalls cutscene stall: most stalled runs there show
no stuck-get at all. Roadmap updated; validation runs queued.

slow frame skipped the flip's completion and the handler never wrote its
deferred FIFO put; the pending flip is now left to the tick, and the status

f1 (it arrived as garbage) and applied at present as out = in^gamma, like
RPCS3, so the game's brightness setting reaches the screen
(PS3_DISPLAY_GAMMA overrides).

RSX CPU: texture units decoded once per draw and program-only unit masks
cached in the program memo; the fetch plan finds the per-vertex span once
per draw, and not at all for a consecutive range. Drawstats reports the
per-frame texture re-hash; unresolved SPU branches print a host backtrace.

options, play_dump, and the known problems (dark facades on Metal, the rare

The title asks the RSX for sRGB-to-linear decoding when it samples its
colour textures (TEXTURE_ADDRESS bits 20..23) and for linear-to-sRGB on
the framebuffer write (SET_SHADER_PACKER); the fork's draw engine honoured
neither, which is why the picture came out dark and muddy, with characters
nearly black against the sky. PR #304 went in earlier; this ports #305:
per-unit gamma masks from format, remap, filter and address state, a
_rsx_gamma_input helper applied after TEX/TXP/TXB/TXL, and the masks in
the pipeline key. A first A/B with #304 alone already shows the docks
cutscene lit like the original; #305 is being validated.

SPU_INTERP_ENTRY_LOG=1 lists every distinct (image, pc) the interpreter is
entered at, so a job module whose lift misses a region can be re-lifted
with all its entries in one pass. Credits: #304 and #305 by tekulvw.

cascade's taps, median |tap - ref| 18844 D24 steps), so 1/3/4 change

8834f6f63080f04a680409d01917741a403d0158.message:
fix(toolkit): biased unsigned-remap textures expand on every fetch

SET_TEXTURE_ADDRESS bit 12 (CELL_GCM_TEXTURE_UNSIGNED_REMAP_BIASED) asks
the sampler to return every fetch of that unit re-centred to -1..1, not
only the TEX ops that carry EXP_TEX. The first version of the expansion
gated on EXP_TEX and never fired: inFAMOUS 2's deferred composite and its
sun pass read the normals G-buffer (0xE3C000, addr 0x00031303) with plain
TEX. Follow RPCS3's _process_texel: (round(x*255)-128)/127 on the biased
lanes (16-bit formats on 32767), after gamma and not on gamma lanes; an
EXP_TEX fetch takes x*2-1 and bypasses gamma. rsx_texture_expand_mask
marks 16-bit channels in bit 4; rsx_fp_texture_expand_units counts every
TEX/TXP/TXB/TXL on a biased unit.

Also: PS3RECOMP_ENG_MEMDUMP accepts "<n>s" (seconds after the first
frame) in place of a world frame, since frame counts drift with load
times; PS3RECOMP_ENG_SIGNLOG=1 lists units with signed or biased reads;
PS3RECOMP_ENG_TEXSTATE=1 prints the texture registers of full-screen
draws per fragment program; PS3RECOMP_METAL_PASS_LOG_FLUSH=1 logs the
slice a mid-frame submit_and_wait ends (the G-buffer pass lives there).

99/99.

fix(res-scale): faces and fps at 1080p+ (framebuffer fetch for decals)

Toolkit (infamous2-lle/patches/pending/res-scale-fixes.patch, against the
fork as cloned for this branch):
- rsx_draw_engine.c / rsx_fp_decompiler.c / rsx_shader_msl.cpp: the

  otherwise, or if the variant fails to build, the copy as before.

  GPU per frame on the dusk walk: 1.5x 19.1 -> 9.0 ms, 2x 32.1 -> 13.0 ms

- rsx_metal_backend.m: SSAO upsample at the scaled size (ssao_up4s_fs, live
  knob PS3_RES_SSAO_FULL); async presents record their GPU time in

92481e18247b384b30e2afb368b1582574f2fac6.message:
feat(port): decrypt the EBOOT and firmware without RPCS3 (tools/decrypt_self.py)

tools/decrypt_self.py turns a retail SELF into the ELF `rpcs3 --decrypt`
writes, byte for byte in layout (ELF header, program headers after it,
each segment at its p_offset, section headers at e_shoff, nothing else):
the NPDRM EBOOT.BIN with the player's .rap (rap_to_rif from rap2rifkey.py)
and the firmware .sprx (APP, key revision 0x1C). Based on
sp00nznet/twistedmetal's tools/decrypt_self.py (MIT). No key is in the
repository: they come from the player's key file (--keys / PS3_KEYS,
scetool format or name=hex lines), the RAP key also from PS3_RAP_KEY and
checked against its SHA-256. --selftest round-trips a synthetic SELF
(APP with a compressed segment, NPDRM local licence) with made-up keys.

rebuild.py: --decrypt-with auto|python|rpcs3 (auto: python when a key file
is given, RPCS3 stays the default and the fallback), --keys, --firmware DIR
(a dev_flash, its sys/external or any folder with the three .sprx). The
python path needs no RPCS3 and does not touch RPCS3's exdata; the checks
read the EBOOT's and the modules' key revision from their clear headers and
fail early on a key the file lacks. The decrypted modules are checked
against the hashes of the tested firmware 4.93 build, like the EBOOT.
install.json's dev_flash follows --firmware when it is a dev_flash tree.

rap2rifkey.py imports pycryptodome lazily so rebuild.py can parse a key
file before the venv exists.

987f6aa142846f102238414b086d933c34136cc0.message:
fix(toolkit): _bx2 fetches always expand; stencil in the depth snapshot; on-demand frame dump

The fragment decompiler expanded a texture read to x*2-1 only when the
unit's SET_TEXTURE_ADDRESS asked for UNSIGNED_REMAP_BIASED. The _bx2
modifier (EXP_TEX, OPDEST bit 21) belongs to the instruction and expands
every lane whatever the texture's remap says. 213 of inFAMOUS 2's ~615
fragment programs read with TEX_bx2: every tangent-space normal map came
in unsigned (flat, wrong shading on all normal-mapped materials) and the
prop occlusion volumes' 8x8x8 cone LUT, whose values sit symmetrically
round 128, gave cone directions in one octant only, so the whole box
counted as occluded: solid black cubes round cafe tables and crates.
rsx_fp_texture_bx2_units names the units; the biased-remap rule stays
for plain fetches.

The depth-as-A8R8G8B8 snapshot now carries the stencil in its B lane
(a X32_Stencil8 view of the depth target): the deferred composite reads
its material flags there (bit 7 ambient scale, bit 5 no-SSAO) and the
occlusion volumes exclude characters through bit 6.

Tools: PS3RECOMP_METAL_DUMP_TRIGGER=<file> dumps every render target and
the next frame's pass log when the file appears (infamous2-lle
tools/play_dump.sh: play in a window, press Enter at the bad frame);
PS3RECOMP_METAL_SURF_DUMP_AT=<sec>; the right stick in PAD_SCRIPT
(0x100000 up, 0x200000 down, 0x400000 left, 0x800000 right); a log line
for every texture bind that fails; DUMPTEX reads R16/R8 textures; dumped

9be4e99f1ef1bf49c214c0025967f4d391e716a6.message:
fix(port): block on RSX semaphore acquires so the composite sees the SPU light

Each frame inFAMOUS 2's FIFO copies the normals and depth targets into XDR
(0x07000B80 / 0x07384B80), writes label 134, and acquires label 137, which
the SPU light task writes once it has replaced those copies with the light
buffers (32x40 tiles around each light, zero elsewhere). With the toolkit
default the walker falls through the acquire, so the deferred composite's
textures were hashed and uploaded while XDR still held the normals and
depth: glossy props (Cole's Amp, the boat hull, bins, the winch) blew out
white because the depth copy's high byte drove the env-cube specular, the
lighting came out in normal colours with per-target MRT masks, and the
tiles the SPU had already written showed as screen-aligned rectangles.

run.sh now exports GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1 and GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS=200 (both
overridable), the bounded blocking acquire. The bound relies on
ps3_ms_now() counting on macOS (CLOCK_MONOTONIC, toolkit commit 48f8156);
no acquire timed out from boot to the pier and the frame count over 250 s
is within noise. ROADMAP: root cause, dump recipe, what is left to check.

9cf4a3ada29582d2497dfb02f8cf3331d40f2583.message:
fix(toolkit): fragment programs honour perspective_corr on texcoord reads SRC2 bit 31 (perspective_corr) multiplies a TC0..TC9 read by 1/w on the RSX, and the decompiler ignored it. New Marais's water writes uv*w into TC2 from the vertex program and samples its screen copy (VRAM 0x00E3C000) through TC2 with the bit set; read raw, uv*w lands far outside the copy and the river came out black. The read is now tcN * _rsx_inv_w(position) (RPCS3's * gl_FragCoord.w): glslang paths define RSX_FRAGCOORD_W_IS_RCP, since SPIR-V FragCoord.w and Metal's [[position]].w are already 1/w; under FXC the helper divides. 163 New Marais pixel shaders use the bit; others are byte-identical. Tests in test_fp_decompiler and test_shader_msl. Also two off-by-default diagnostics: RSX_FP_NAN_COLOR=1 (FP outputs that would be NaN magenta, Inf cyan) and PS3RECOMP_ENG_FPK_PIPE=

(the FP constants each draw through pipeline p receives).

fix(toolkit): deliver GCM callbacks at sys_timer_usleep; light pass on the GPU by default (walk ~15 fps)

inFAMOUS 2 defers its FIFO put to its flip handler and then waits for the
ref register with usleep only. The runtime ran GCM callbacks only at HLE
imports, so the title depended on another thread's HLE calls; once the
light job finished at once (GPU light pass), ~1 run in 3 hung with get ==
put at a JUMP. ppu_gcm_pump now also runs at sys_timer_usleep/sleep: six
runs out of six clean.

atomics, label 135 and yield bookkeeping kept, no tile DMA); both copies
keep their write-back (the SSAO job reads the depth one); the SPU
runtime overhead cuts of ba8cd16 are back (+8%); a stuck-ref diagnostic
and per-job SPU DMA logs. run.sh enables the GPU light pass. New Marais
walk 14.3-15.0 fps, dock 16. SSAO job mapped (notes/ssao/).

b33bfc946e06eb3b3a9526f9a660526e3928aaaf.message:
fix(toolkit): SPU decrementer overflow; interrupt, atomic and label rate statistics

SPU_RdDec scaled elapsed nanoseconds by 79.8 MHz in 64 bits, which wraps
231 s after the context's base stamp; the SPURS kernel context never
rewrites its decrementer, so every timed loop on it saw the counter jump
forward by ~16 s of ticks at 231 s, 462 s, 693 s. Seconds and remainder are
scaled separately now.

Diagnostics for the cutscene stall, all off unless set: SPU_IRQSTAT (takes/s
per SPU with the last srr0 and events), SPU_ATOMICSTAT (GETLLARs per SPU
with the last line polled), RSX_LABELSTAT (back-end label writes per
window), and the SPU_STEPCAP dump now prints the loop's code words.

Roadmap: the stalled SPU runs the Edge geometry job (jobmod d0d15ec83992)
in lifted code, in a loop that leaves only on its time budget or when the
work drains, through the atomic output-ring allocation.

b3957499dbf4a2a915e919757c5b1cf4a93987dd.message:
fix(port): run the guest off the main thread when windowed on macOS

The Metal backend creates its window and pumps events with dispatch_sync onto
the main queue, and main() ran the guest on the main thread, which never
services that queue. The frame clock blocked in its first event pump, the FIFO
stopped draining, and the title spun on a fence: ./run.sh showed a grey
window that never drew (headless never pumps, so captures were unaffected).

Windowed, the guest now runs on its own thread with the 256 MB host stack
every guest thread gets, and the main thread turns the CFRunLoop. Headless
keeps the old layout. Verified: the window presents at ~29 fps through the
menu and the attract video.

fix(toolkit): one-channel texture crossbar, GPU write-back at NV3089 blits, bounded semaphore acquire

The main menu was checked against the original title screen and matches
(a black void, Cole from behind near silhouette, one bolt, sparks). What the
check turned up along the way, all in the fork's patch:

- rsx_texture_component_remap: X16, X32_FLOAT and DEPTH16/24 are one real
  channel uploaded as R16/R32F; present it on every lane as B8 already was.
  The 1024x8 X16 lighting ramp this title binds with crossbar 0xAAEE (R from B)
  read the empty B component. Unit test test_remap_one_channel_lanes.
- rsx_draw_engine_write_back(), called from nv3089_blit(): the game copies its
  normal and depth targets to main memory every frame for the SPUs' lighting,

  work and read the target (or the depth buffer, as Z24S8 bytes) back first.

  point (reusing it blacked out every cutscene). PS3RECOMP_ENG_WRITEBACK=0/1/2.
- cellGcmSys: GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1 with GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS=<ms> blocks the FIFO
  walker on an NV406E ACQUIRE for at most that long, and the stuck-get
  watchdog no longer resyncs while it waits. Off by default. GCM_SEMA_TRACE=<n>
  prints the semaphore methods with the label's value and the RSX label writes.
- Diagnostics: PS3RECOMP_ENG_TEXLOG=1 (textures created with handle, render
  target aliases per draw, every surface, write-backs), SPU_PUT_EA_AFTER /
  SPU_PUT_EA_MAX caps for SPU_PUT_EA.

ba8cd1605aacbb5d60c91aaed5e5c06986be9bb9.message:
perf(toolkit): cut SPU runtime overhead found by the first profile

A profile of the docks cutscene and pier put 23-31% of SPU time in runtime
helpers rather than the game's job code. The biggest pieces:

- spu_task_launch_check, run on every drain step, read five diagnostic
  flags atomically per call; with none set it now takes a short path that
  keeps only the end-of-job check.
- spu_check_stack_reset, also per step, read a thread-local (_tlv_get_addr
  on macOS) before comparing pc with its few entries; the compare is first.
- spu_overlay_note_get walked every registered overlay source on every DMA
  GET. A summary of the table (a bitset of the address sources' EAs, the
  union of the fixed-lift LS ranges, the 512-byte signature floor) skips GETs
  that cannot match anything; matches and their order are unchanged.
  Sources are only registered in constructors, before any SPU runs.
- cflts/cfltu: a NEON path (multiply by 2^scale, FCVTZS/FCVTZU) for lanes
  with an ordinary exponent; exponent-0 lanes forced to 0, any exponent-255
  lane takes the exact path. tests/test_spu_cflt_fast.c: 102.4 M conversions
  over all 256 scales and edge values, 0 mismatches.
- spu_ls_read128/spu_ls_write128 were left out of line in every lifted SPU
  file; they are always_inline now, with the watch hook kept out of line
  (both its call sites are behind the debug flag).

Before/after fps and SPU split pending the next profile run.

run.sh execs the game as caffeinate's child, so kill -9 on caffeinate left

bb5033a8456e084e59134b6e2bf4685e8260feea.message: docs(roadmap): cutscene stall diagnosis -- interpreted job after a stall-and-notify resume

bb8235ef1a2ba90b7bdb84fa6fe87e6d40fd8295.message:
perf(toolkit): row copy for unscaled 2D blits; pacing, QoS, extra-SPU and usleep-spin knobs

New Marais profile (tools/profile_run.sh newmarais, samples at 250/400 s):
the 5 SPU threads are the title's own lifted SPURS kernel at ~96% busy
(~55% lifted job code, ~35% lifter runtime), the RSX thread spends
~50 ms of CPU per frame, a quarter of it in nv3089_blit copying the
1280x720 G-buffer surfaces to XDR pixel by pixel through vm_read32 /
vm_write32 for the SPU lighting. In the walking phase nobody is
saturated (SPUs 68%, RSX 55%, main thread 52% in the usleep(10)
light-task wait, the kicker thread 98% in usleep): the pipeline is
latency-bound there.

- cellGcmSys.c: unscaled NV3089 blits copy a row at a time with memmove
  and per-128-byte-line reservation bookkeeping (NV3089_ROWCOPY, default
  1; =0 restores the per-pixel copy the PPU_WWATCH/PPU_WVAL diagnostics
  see). The blit disappears from the RSX profile; fps unchanged at the
  dock, where the RSX is not the limit. cellGcm_drain_sema_blocked()
  reports a drain parked on a semaphore acquire.
- main.cpp: GCM_FLIP_IMMEDIATE=1 completes the flip at present time
  instead of on the 16 ms tick; GCM_SEMA_FASTPOLL=1 polls the parked
  drain every 1 ms instead of 4; PS3_HOT_QOS=1 raises the frame clock
  (and, in lv2_register.c, the SPU threads) to above-normal priority /
  QOS_CLASS_USER_INTERACTIVE. Interleaved A/B (base/exp/base/exp, 480 s):
  dock 12-13 fps and walk 7-8 fps on both sides, no proven gain; all off.
- lv2_register.c: SPURS_EXTRA_SPUS=<n> creates the CellSpursKernelGroup
  with n more threads cloned from the title's last one (r3 = spu num),
  keeps the workload max-contention bytes raised, and mirrors the
  signal-notification writes to the clones. Parked: libsre caps each
  workload's readyCount at its nSpus, so the clones never get work.
- sys_timer.c: PS3_USLEEP_SPIN_US=<n> makes POSIX guest sleeps of n us or
  less spin with sched_yield instead of nanosleep (macOS nanosleep(3 us)
  takes >= 50 us; the Windows branch always spun below 1 ms). 1

c721a5be3c7b7e884dece1b502a210588107c9f9.message:
fix(gfx): depth-clamp the sun-shadow casters; prune one-frame vertex-cache keys

inFAMOUS 2 draws every sun-shadow caster (zeta 0x0F2F0000) with
NV4097_SET_ZMIN_MAX_CONTROL = 0x10 (cellGcmSetZMinMaxControl(FALSE, TRUE,
FALSE)): no near/far clipping, depth clamped, so a caster between the sun
and a cascade's near plane is pancaked to depth 0. The draw engine ignored
the register and always clipped, so such casters vanished from that
cascade -- first from the near cascade, whose depth range is the
tightest: building shadows seen from afar and gone up close. The engine
now passes the clamp to a new optional backend call, set_depth_clamp, and
Metal sets setDepthClipMode per draw (as RPCS3: clamp when the clamp bit
is set or clipping is off). PS3RECOMP_ENG_DEPTH_CLAMP=0 = old (live
toggle after PS3T_ENG_POLY_OFFSET). Headless next to the dock warehouse:
0.19% of the near cascade is pancaked casters with the clamp, none
without; no fps cost.

Vertex cache: Erik's session log shows the table starting over (every
persistent buffer dropped) twice in a dense street at ~20 fps, with
36574/46205 keys drawn in the last 60 frames, mostly one-frame keys. The
prune now also drops keys without a persistent buffer not drawn in the
last 2 frames (PS3RECOMP_ENG_VCACHE_PRUNE=1 = v0.2.13's prune).

Diagnostics: PS3RECOMP_ENG_CLAMP_CULL_FLIP (live), ZMIN_MAX_CONTROL /
cull / viewport sign in PS3RECOMP_ENG_POLY_OFFSET_LOG,

c8e3a00a2cd22f26905fc9a66e70e6cf6965d4a7.message:
fix(toolkit): Y16_X16 crossbar rule; FP debug output; gameplay-relative pad script

Y16_X16 (and HILO8) textures encode their crossbar in 16-bit blocks and
present the two channels interleaved R-G-R-G, or R-R-R-G when CONTROL1's
high word (the remap override) is set (RPCS3 decoded_remap). inFAMOUS 2's
water reads its 64x64 wave map through .yw with the override set; through
the plain ARGB table .w was the resource's empty alpha, 1.0, so every wave
normal was tilted by a whole unit. The engine now passes CONTROL1's bit 16
to the texture cache key and the backend.

Diagnostics: RSX_FP_DEBUG=<fp hash>:<n>:<reg[.swz]> returns the register
after the n-th emitted instruction as colour target 0 (an intermediate of a
long shader, on screen); PS3RECOMP_ENG_WORLD_MARK=<path> (+ _AFTER=<sec>)
marks the first gameplay frame and PAD_SCRIPT times written w<sec> count
from it, so a scripted walk lands on the same spot regardless of loading
time; the triggered pass log skips empty flush slices.

Tests: test_texture_layout (Y16_X16 cases), test_fp_decompiler 60/60.

d72f62b64c2c0e1140b9f845919f6032a1dfc889.message:
feat: lift New Marais's relocatable SPU job code (spu_lifter --relocatable)

New Marais's SPU jobs are ~30 position-independent blobs the SPURS kernel
streams from the EBOOT (0x8E8C00-0x928150) to a different local-store
address on every run, so no fixed-address lift matched and they all ran
on the SPU interpreter.

Toolkit (patch):
- spu_lifter.py --relocatable: lift at LS 0; every LS address the code
  derives from its own position (link values, tail-branch pcs, drain
  return pcs, lqr/stqr, fallthrough and stub pcs) adds
  spu_context.code_base. Nested calls save and restore it; bra/brasl stay
  absolute and dispatch by address.
- runtime: spu_overlay_register_region_reloc(); a GET from the region's EA
  makes it resident at whatever LS address it targets. Dispatch (the lookup,
  the indirect branch, the fast path, the musttail path and the drain loop)
  resolves pc - lsa and sets code_base. Relocatable images answer only for
  their own id, never a wildcard. Resident code slots go from 4 to 16
  (SPU_RESIDENT_CODE_SLOTS), since a job batch stages eight or nine modules.

Port:
- tools/lift_relocmods.py finds the blobs by their shared header, lifts all
  30 and writes spu/relocmods_register.c. PS3_RELOCMODS=0 turns them off.

Measured in New Marais (same scripted route, a second game instance
running in both runs):

  interpreted SPU instructions over 8 min   14.8 G -> 2.4 G
  audio blocks with sound                   ~35%   -> 64-86%
  frame rate                                11-16  -> 10-16 (unchanged)

Rendering checked: Amp swing and running through the bayou draw correctly.
What stays interpreted: libsre's taskset-policy body at image 0x2A180
(LS 0xA00) and the register-save stub at LS 0x3FEC0.

v0.2.12 aligned the map (crop) and compares in the RSX's strict order,
a caster that also receives met its own depth and failed on alternate
texels: sawtooth acne bands on walls, trims and foliage.

the offset to a new optional backend call, set_depth_bias; Metal sets
it on the encoder per draw, outside the pipeline key.
PS3RECOMP_ENG_POLY_OFFSET=0 restores the old draw (live toggle after
PS3T_ENG_ZTEX_CROP); N > 1 multiplies the constant term (diagnostic);
PS3RECOMP_ENG_POLY_OFFSET_LOG=1 lists depth targets with their offset
and the programs that compare against a depth map.

Checked headless on the dusk save with live A/B in one run: acne on
the pier wall and trims goes with the offset and returns without it;
fps unchanged within noise. Still open (ROADMAP): blue blotches on the
shadow side of the dock posts/boat (unchanged by the offset) and the

dc68c6f98b8f8c9e7fa5a0ea8576378f6a86832e.message:
fix(gfx): sun shadows inverted and 1.25x misplaced (pier at dusk)

Two toolkit bugs in every sun-shadow lookup, found at the start of the
dusk save (Cole on the pier) by recomputing the cascade mask on the CPU
from OCCDUMP data and reading the GPU's own values with FP_PATCH:

- The RSX depth compare is "stored texel OP reference" (RPCS3 flips the
  operator for its API samplers); the shadow helper compared the other
  way, so with the game's zfunc GREATER lit and shadowed were swapped:
  dark planks with bright streaks where shadows should be.
  PS3RECOMP_ENG_SHADOW_CMP=0 = old (live toggle).
- The 1024x1024 cascades live in a 1280-wide depth buffer at 0x0F2F0000
  and depth-format textures sampled the copy of the whole buffer, so
  every lookup landed 1.25x too far along x: no shadow under Cole,
  detached shadows of far casters, cascades 2/3 nearly shadowless. The
  copy is now the texture's top-left corner, as the colour-format copy
  was. PS3RECOMP_ENG_ZTEX_CROP=0 = old (live toggle).

After both, all three cascades match the game's math (mean |diff| 0.04 /
0.09 / 0.09) and the pier is sunlit with Cole's shadow at his feet.
Toolkit patch: infamous2-lle/patches/pending/pier-lighting.patch.

e347d14ea79fb2381d51b4036b93aa1771bfe9d3.message:
feat(diag): live A/B toggle file (PS3_TOGGLE_FILE) and tools/ab_live.sh

PS3_TOGGLE_FILE=<file> names a text file, one NAME=value per line, that the
frame clock re-reads every 250 ms when its mtime/size/inode changes. It
switches performance and debug knobs while the game runs, so an fps A/B
compares the same scene at the same moment inside one run. The idea comes from
gow3_pc's GOW3_TOGGLE_FILE; no code was taken from it.

Toolkit side (patches/pending/live-toggles.patch, fold into the toolkit
patch): include/ps3emu/ps3_toggles.h holds header-only state (weak, as in
ps3_ftrace.h, so the self-contained test compiles keep linking).
libs/misc/ps3_toggles.c holds the poll. Watchers rewrite the module-local ints
the hot paths always read, so without the variable behaviour and cost are as
before. Live: VCACHE (off drops the persistent buffers, on starts empty),
TEXHASH_FULL, SKIP_FP, SPU_FASTJOB, SPU_STUB_MICRO, SPU_STACK_HINT,
PS3_SPU_DRAIN_INLINE (new), PS3_DISPLAY_GAMMA, PS3_SHARPEN, PS3_AA, PS3_ANISO
(part of the sampler key) and PS3RECOMP_METAL_FPS. Each change logs
"[toggle] NAME old -> new" and leaves a PS3_FT_TOGGLE mark. PS3_FTRACE_KINDS
filters span kinds.

The same patch carries two texture re-hash fixes: textures under 64 bytes
are hashed bytewise, where they used to be never re-hashed, and the full hash
is due by age (last_full_frame, staggered per slot), where an alternate-frame
texture could miss its (frame + slot) & 7 turn forever.

Port side: main.cpp polls from frame_clock. tools/ab_live.sh flips one knob
every PERIOD s in a profile_run.sh run, and ftrace_report.py --phases splits
the frames by value. First result: VCACHE on 28.7 ms vs off 32.4 ms median
frame in New Marais (-11.5%).

prefetch (jbi_intro_001#31.xpps) and the world switch that releases update
group 0 -- the stalled run never reloads #31 and polls the asset registry
forever. Audio, Edge job chain, FIOS wake-ups, event queues and fd races

ebd556e414a014f04698bed083b68b941e218ea5.message:
perf(toolkit): sparse per-frame texture re-hash; inline gate for the SPU stack-reset check (walk 28 fps)

Every cached texture was hashed in full every frame (~950, 88 MB, 2.5 ms of
the RSX thread) for 4 that changed: a sparse check runs every frame and the
full hash every eighth, staggered by slot (PS3RECOMP_ENG_TEXHASH_FULL=1 =
old). spu_check_stack_reset, the hottest SPU leaf (~6%), is now gated by an
inline hint table so the call only happens at a registered entry.
Frame 36.2 -> 35.5 ms, SPUs 32.4 -> 30.6 ms busy.

ffad410dfe081831e8b81413e682bf92ad1f024b.message:
fix(net): answer the PSN terms check offline; Quit game in the menu

The endless "Please wait..." box at dusk came back: after the PSN connect
dialog ends cancelled, inFAMOUS 2 still asks sceNpEulaCheckEulaStatus
(NID 0x59D1629A), which was unresolved, so its callback never came and the
game's online state machine waited in state 14 with its spinner up. The
toolkit now implements cellSysutilNpEula (CheckEulaStatus, Abort,
ShowCurrentEula, after RPCS3): the answer arrives through the callback on
the next sysutil poll, SCE_NP_EULA_ERROR offline (the game gives up
quietly: state 24, spinner closed), already-accepted with PS3_NET_ONLINE=1.
The NP manager's ticket/region/network-time imports answer OFFLINE instead
of a silent CELL_OK.

F1 > Quit game asks for confirmation and quits; Cmd+Q quits on the first
press (it did nothing before). Both send REQUEST_EXITGAME, then end the
process with status 0 after PS3_QUIT_GRACE_MS (3 s), never mid-save.
PS3_QUIT=1 is a new live toggle.

Toolkit side: infamous2-lle/patches/pending/eula-quit.patch.

# inFAMOUS 2 — static recompilation for PC (macOS) 🌐 **English** · [Português (BR)](README.pt-BR.md) A native port of **inFAMOUS 2** (PS3, digital release `NPUA80638`) to **macOS/arm64**, built with static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C/C++ and compiled into a native executable, with graphics on Metal. It is not an emulator. **It boots, shows its menus and cutscenes, and New Marais is playable**, at ~38-40 fps on Apple silicon in headless runs (the game has no 30 fps cap in gameplay). Get the app from the [**v0.2.12 alpha release**](https://github.com/erikomis/infamous2-recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.12) and it rebuilds the game from your own copy ([how](#download-and-play)); from v0.2.7 on, the app updates itself. | | | | --- | --- | | [](docs/screenshots/01-boot-sucker-punch-logo.jpg)
Boot: the studio logos | [](docs/screenshots/02-main-menu.jpg)
3D main menu | | [](docs/screenshots/03-intro-comic.jpg)
Comic-book intro (Bink video) | [](docs/screenshots/04-cutscene-sunset-docks.jpg)
Arriving in New Marais (in-engine cutscene) | | [](docs/screenshots/05-cutscene-kuo.jpg)
Kuo on the pier (in-engine cutscene) | [](docs/screenshots/06-pier-gameplay.jpg)
Gameplay: the pier by day | | [](docs/screenshots/07-street-amp.jpg)
The streets of New Marais, Amp in hand | [](docs/screenshots/08-street-corner.jpg)
Late afternoon in the city | | [](docs/screenshots/09-dusk-neon-taxi.jpg)
Neon at dusk | | Frames from the port itself running on an Apple-silicon Mac (M4 Pro), built from the player's own copy, at the game's 1280×720; subtitles are in Brazilian Portuguese, the port's default dub. inFAMOUS 2 © Sony Interactive Entertainment, developed by Sucker Punch Productions; shown only to document the port. Built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) and, above all, on [NoahBPeterson](https://github.com/NoahBPeterson/ps3recomp)'s **inFAMOUS 1 fork**, which brought the firmware LLE and the fixes that got the first game running on the Mac. See [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md). > [!WARNING] > **Alpha, not tested from start to finish yet.** The game runs from boot to > the first missions in New Marais, only on Apple silicon macOS. Nobody has > gone past 1% of the story yet, so later missions may break. What is missing > is in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). > **This repository contains no game data, no firmware, no Sony keys and > nothing translated from them.** Everyone generates all of that locally from > their own legitimate copy. A fan project, not affiliated with Sony > Interactive Entertainment or Sucker Punch Productions. ## Status | | | | --- | --- | | Boot, firmware LLE, SPURS, Wwise audio (SPU jobs) | ✅ | | Health warning, studio logos, Bink videos, loading screens | ✅ | | 3D main menu, pause menu, options | ✅ | | New game → comic-book intro → in-engine cutscenes | ✅ | | Empire City prologue (the Beast, the freighter) | ✅ | | New Marais: first missions, played in a window with a DualSense | ✅ | | Performance | ✅ ~38-40 fps on the headless New Marais walk on Apple silicon. The game has no 30 fps cap in gameplay; menus and the comics stay at 30, as on the console. A long windowed session is still to confirm it | | Internal resolution 1080p / 1440p / 4K | ✅ since v0.2.9; 1080p runs at ~37 fps headless since the framebuffer-fetch fix (v0.2.11); 4K is too heavy for now | | Ultrawide 21:9 and 32:9 (wider view, HUD kept 16:9 in the centre) | ✅ since v0.2.10, checked headless | | Controller (DualSense tested; DualShock 4 and Xbox through SDL), rumble, reconnect without a restart | ✅ | | Keyboard and mouse (mouse camera, remappable, also live in the in-game menu) | 🧪 mapped, little tested in a window | | Button prompts that follow the controller (Xbox A/B/X/Y, keyboard keys) | 🧪 since v0.2.6, checked headless, waiting for a windowed test | | In-game menu (F1 / Cmd+, / L3+R3): image, audio, controls, game languages, performance HUD | ✅ since v0.2.4 (live changes) | | Quit game (F1 > Quit game, Cmd+Q, closing the window) | ✅ since v0.2.10, checked headless; a save being written finishes first | | Texture packs and more image effects (clarity, curves, colour presets) | 🧪 since v0.2.8, waiting for a windowed test | | Saves and trophies (in `~/Library/Application Support`), saves manager in the app | ✅ | | Brazilian Portuguese dub and subtitles (default), other languages your copy ships, DLC | ✅ | | The app: install, rebuild, play, settings, controls, saves, debug mode | ✅ [v0.2.12 alpha](https://github.com/erikomis/infamous2-recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.12) | | The app updates itself | 🧪 since v0.2.7 (v0.2.8 to v0.2.12 were offered through it), waiting for Erik's confirmation | | Add to Steam (Big Picture with the controller) | 🧪 since v0.2.7, waiting for a test with Steam | | Whole game | ❓ nobody has gone past 1% yet | | Linux and Windows | ⏳ planned | Details and next steps in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). ## Download and play You need an Apple-silicon Mac and your own copy of inFAMOUS 2 (the PSN release `NPUA80638`, for example installed in [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net) with its `.rap` licence). 1. Download `infamous2-recomp_0.2.12_aarch64.dmg` from the [v0.2.12 release](https://github.com/erikomis/infamous2-recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.12) (every release so far is a pre-release; the [releases page](https://github.com/erikomis/infamous2-recomp/releases) lists any newer one) and drag the app to Applications. It is not notarized: the first time, right-click > Open (or System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway). 2. The app lists what your Mac still needs (Xcode Command Line Tools, a few Homebrew packages) and installs it with your OK. 3. Pick your game folder; the `.rap` is found on its own. Decryption uses RPCS3 if you have it, or your own key file and the PS3 firmware (a `dev_flash` folder or Sony's `PS3UPDAT.PUP`). No keys ship with the app. 4. **Install** (the first rebuild takes a few minutes), then **Play**. From v0.2.7 on, the app updates itself: the Updates card on Home offers **Download and install**, then **Restart to finish** (signed and checked; "Check for updates automatically" can be turned off). After an update it offers **Rebuild the game**. On v0.2.6 or older, install the new app by hand once. The release ships no game files: the app recompiles the game on your Mac. ## The app [`launcher/`](launcher/README.md) is a desktop app (Tauri) that does all of this without a terminal, in the game's own look: Home (your copy's art, PLAY, quick settings, last save, status), Graphics, Performance, Game, Controls and Advanced. - **Install / rebuild** with a progress bar: checks and installs the tools, finds your copy and its `.rap`, decrypts with RPCS3 or without it. - **Graphics:** window, fullscreen or borderless, screen, vsync, gamma, anisotropic filtering, FXAA or SMAA, sharpening (CAS), vibrance, contrast, MetalFX upscaling, fps counter, and ready-made profiles (Performance / Balanced / Quality). macOS Game Mode turns on in fullscreen. - **Controls:** remap keyboard, mouse and controller, mouse camera, vibration; **audio** volume and output; **game language** (the ones your copy ships), with the voice and the subtitles/menus each in its own language if you like (e.g. English voice, Portuguese subtitles). - **Saves:** list, back up, restore, import/export with RPCS3, `.zip`. - **Trophies:** the game's trophies with your unlocks (names and icons from your copy), and a "Trophy unlocked" notice in the game. - **Community patches** from your own RPCS3 patch file: skip the intro, a wider field of view. - **Debug mode** (Advanced > Debug mode): play normally while the game logs what goes wrong (missing functions, shader/texture failures, GPU stalls, SPU faults, audio falling behind, files it cannot open, frame-rate drops) and keeps a timed index of the session; press **F12** in the game (or **Capture this frame** in the app) when something looks wrong. Afterwards **Analyse** runs `infamous2-lle/tools/log_triage.py` on the session and lists the top issues (also in `triage.md` in the session folder, for a developer or an agent to go through), and **Create .zip** packs it all for an issue. Details in [launcher/README.md](launcher/README.md#debug-mode-report-a-problem). Plus a **game log viewer** that follows the log live. - **Updates card:** downloads and installs a newer app version (signed, verified, one click and a restart), and offers a rebuild when the installed game is older than the app's sources. - **Your copy's icon** in the Dock for the app and the game (read from your install, never shipped). - **Play shortcut** (Home > Status): a "Play inFAMOUS 2" icon on the Desktop that opens the app and starts the game at once with your settings. - **Add to Steam** (Home > Status, optional): inFAMOUS 2 as a non-Steam game with cover art made from your copy, to start from Big Picture with the controller; **Remove from Steam** takes it out again. **In the game,** F1 (fn+F1), Cmd+, or L3+R3 opens the **in-game menu**: image (gamma, sharpening, FXAA/SMAA, vibrance, contrast, clarity, curves, colour presets, MetalFX, vsync, display mode, internal resolution, aspect ratio), audio volume, controls (live remapping of keyboard, mouse and controller, "play with" controller / keyboard and mouse / both, vibration, mouse), the game's voice and text languages, a performance HUD (fps, frame time, CPU/GPU) and **Quit game**. # inFamous PC

> **Official repo: [github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn).**
> Only download the Setup from the [Releases page](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn/releases) here.
> Forks are not supported, and bugs from forks won't be fixed.

An unofficial native Windows port of **inFamous** (PlayStation 3, 2009, European
release `BCES00220`). The game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code is statically
recompiled to x86-64 C/C++ with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp),
so it runs as a normal Windows program rather than under an emulator.

**This repository contains no game code or data.** You build the game yourself,
on your own PC, from your own copy of the game.

## Easy install

Download **inFamous Setup.exe** from the latest release, run it, choose your
`.iso` (an encrypted image works with its `.dkey` next to it) or your game
folder (the one with `PS3_GAME` in it), pick an install location and press
**Install**.

Setup checks for Python and the C++ build tools and offers to install them,
copies the game out of the disc image, regenerates the recompiled code from your
copy, builds it and adds an inFamous shortcut. Running Setup again on the same
folder updates or repairs the install and only redoes what changed.

## Updating

When a new version is published here, players update in place instead of reinstalling:
**Update now** in Setup (it finds the existing install), the **Update inFamous** shortcut in
the Start menu, or `Update inFamous.cmd` in the install folder. The updater compares every file
with this repository, downloads only what changed, regenerates the game code only if the
port's patches changed, and recompiles only the affected parts. Installs made with an older
Setup need one run of the new Setup on the same folder first.

## Requirements

- Your own inFamous disc dump, European release (`BCES00220`).
- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with Direct3D 12 support.
- A CPU with SSE4.1 (2008 or newer). On CPUs without AVX2 (Intel before 2013, Pentium/Celeron
  without AVX, AMD before 2015) Setup builds a slower compatibility version automatically.
  On PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the game uses fewer threads and less CPU (tested down to 4 threads).
- [Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) with "Add python.exe to
  PATH" ticked.
- [Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/)
  with the **Desktop development with C++** workload and the **C++ Clang
  Compiler for Windows** component.
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), only if your `PS3_GAME\USRDIR` has `EBOOT.BIN`
  but no decrypted `EBOOT.elf`. Setup uses it to decrypt the executable.
- About 10 GB of free disk space and 16 GB of RAM.

## Building manually

```bat
cd installer
cargo build --release
target\release\infamous-installer --game "D:\Dumps\inFamous"
```

`infamous-installer doctor` checks the requirements only. Finished steps are
skipped when you run it again, so an interrupted install continues where it
stopped. See [installer/README.md](installer/README.md) for every step and the
maintainer commands.

## Playing

Run **inFamous** (the shortcut Setup made). It opens a small options window first
(vsync, frame cap, resolution, language and more, saved to `settings.ini`);
**Play** starts the game. The same settings are in the game's pause menu under
**Settings**. Controllers work as on the console, and keyboard and mouse are supported.

**F10** opens the in-game trainer: God Mode, Infinite Energy, Refill Health,
Max Health x2/x5/x10, Add XP, Karma +/-, Kill Enemies / Civilians, Super Speed
and Player Model (play as Zeke, Trish, Kessler, Alden or John). Set `TRAINER=0`
to turn it off.

## DLSS and FSR (optional)

The game can use NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA or AMD FSR for upscaling, and AMD FSR frame generation.
They are not included in the download because NVIDIA and AMD distribute their SDKs themselves,
but both are free and take a few minutes to add.

- **DLSS** needs an NVIDIA RTX graphics card.
- **FSR** works on any modern GPU (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel). FSR 4 needs a Radeon RX 9000 card;
  other cards get FSR 3.1 automatically.

**1. Download the SDK(s) you want.** You need the **source code**, not a Windows or Linux demo.
On the page, click the green **Code** button, then **Download ZIP**. If you go through the
Releases page instead, pick **Source code (zip)**, not the files with "demo" or "samples" in the name.

| For | Download | Rename the extracted folder to |
|---|---|---|
| DLSS / DLAA | [github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS) | `dlss-sdk` |
| FSR and frame generation | [github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK) | `fsr-sdk` |

**2. Put the folder(s) in your inFamous install folder**, next to `infamous-recomp` and
`ps3recomp`:

```
inFamous\
  dlss-sdk\        <- contains include\ and lib\
  fsr-sdk\         <- contains Kits\
  infamous-recomp\
  ps3recomp\
  ...
```

Make sure you don't end up with a folder inside a folder (`dlss-sdk\DLSS-main\include`).
`include` (DLSS) or `Kits` (FSR) must be directly inside.

**3. Rebuild the game once.** Open a Command Prompt in the install folder and run:

```bat
type nul > .installer\update.pending
"Update inFamous.cmd"
```

This rebuilds the game with the SDK(s), which takes a while. Any later update also picks them up
automatically, so you only do this once.

**4. Turn it on in game:** pause, then **Settings**, then **Upscaling** (DLAA, DLSS Quality /
Balanced / Performance, FSR Native AA / Quality / Balanced / Performance) and **Frame
Generation**. The same options are in the launcher's options window. Upscaling and frame
generation apply after a restart.

If the **Upscaling** row is missing, the build didn't find the SDK: check the folder names and
layout from step 2, then repeat step 3.

## How it works

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `ps3recomp` | The recompiler toolkit and runtime: PPU and SPU lifters, HLE system libraries, RSX on Direct3D 12, audio and input |
| `infamous-recomp` | The inFamous-specific parts: program entry, game stubs and fixes, asset tools |
| `installer` | Setup and the command-line installer: reads the disc, regenerates the code from your game, applies `installer/patches`, builds |
| `installer/infamous.toml` | Everything about the game and the port: pipeline steps, generated files, build and launch settings |
| `installer/generated.lock` | Hashes of each generated file before and after the port's patches |

## Credits

- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet and
  contributors (see [ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md](ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md)).
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), used to decrypt the game executable.
- Sucker Punch Productions, for the game.
- [Lorenzo Aiello](https://github.com/aiellolorenzo23) and [ibrahimpuri](https://github.com/ibrahimpuri), for their support.

# Naruto: Ultimate Ninja Storm — port experimental para PC

Recompilação experimental para **Windows x64/D3D12**, usando ps3recomp.
Aberto a contribuições; campanha completa e estabilidade geral continuam em desenvolvimento.

## Instalar no Windows

Baixe o [Setup experimental 0.1.0](https://github.com/OPaiva-1721/naruto-storm-recomp/releases/tag/v0.1.0)
e confira o SHA-256 que acompanha o arquivo. O Setup recompila **sua própria cópia
PS3 BLES00371 01.00** localmente; não baixa nem inclui o jogo ou firmware.

Requer Python 3.12+, Git/CMake/Ninja, Visual Studio Build Tools com C++/Clang,
FFmpeg 8.1 compartilhado e dev_flash próprios. Reserve 12 GiB livres além do dump.
Escolha a pasta contendo PS3_GAME e um destino novo; após concluir, use Jogar.cmd.

- [Guia do instalador e requisitos](docs/INSTALL.md)
- [Validação e limites conhecidos](docs/INSTALL_VALIDATION.md)
- [Build manual](docs/PC_SETUP.md)
- [Estado do port](docs/STATUS_PC.md)
