# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

Every row is exercised by CI on every push, and **all three are green on
`master`** — the PPU boot scaffold ratchet that had been red since before v0.11.0
([#139](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/issues/139)) is at zero on all
four toolchains. The rows below describe what those jobs actually do, not what a
green tick would imply: building the runtime and passing the suites is not the
same as running a game, and only one row claims that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter + 8 test suites | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | null (headless software) |
| Runs a recompiled game | **yes** | **no** | no |

The gap on macOS is the PPU boot scaffold — `ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp`
and the HLE dispatch are still Win32-only (thread creation, VirtualAlloc, SEH,
stack walking), and they are compiled per-game rather than into the library.
So macOS builds the runtime, renders through Metal and passes the full test
suite, but cannot yet load and run a title. `ps3recomp_host` drives
cellGcm → RSX → Metal end to end without a game, which is what makes further
graphics work possible there.

Linux builds and passes the same suites under both GCC and Clang, and runs
`ps3recomp_host` end to end, on every push. Its backend is the null backend's
headless software path: a host-memory framebuffer with a CPU triangle filler,
enough to prove the guest's command stream produced the pixels it asked for on
a runner with no display and no GPU. It is not a renderer — no depth, no
blending, no textures — so Linux is still one real backend, plus the same PPU
boot scaffold macOS needs, away from running a title.

### What each platform needs next

Both non-Windows platforms are blocked on the *same* two things, in this order.

**1. The PPU boot scaffold, on POSIX.** This is the shared blocker and the only
one that gates "runs a recompiled game" on both. `ppu_loader.cpp`,
`boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled *per game* rather than into
the library, and were Win32-only — thread creation, `VirtualAlloc`, SEH, stack
walking. v0.10.0 took it to zero errors on POSIX and put it under CI so it
cannot rot again, and ported the guest-pointer trap, thread-locals and host
backtraces. What is left is running it: load a lifted image on POSIX and reach
the guest's first instruction, then `main`. Until that works, neither platform
can run a title no matter how good its renderer is.

**2. One real backend each.** The RSX abstraction landed in v0.10.0 (#101, #102,
#103) — texture conversion, the `TEXTURE_CONTROL1` crossbar, texture layout and
a neutral draw record all live outside the D3D12 file now, so a backend no
longer has to reimplement them to draw anything.

- **macOS** has the furthest to go that is *interesting* rather than
  mechanical: [@slushiimusic](https://github.com/slushiimusic)'s Metal backend
  (#96) does clear, flip, guest vertex fetch, a pipeline-state cache and blend
  translation. Reaching D3D12 parity means the guest's own fragment programs
  through the decompiler, then textures. `ps3recomp_host` already drives
  cellGcm → RSX → Metal with no lifted game, so each step is testable before a
  title exists to run.
- **Linux** has no renderer at all — the headless backend is a CPU triangle
  filler for CI, deliberately. Vulkan is the obvious target, and it starts from
  the same neutral draw record Metal reads.

**Deliberately not claimed:** the table above says "no" for running a game on
macOS and Linux, and it will keep saying "no" until a title actually boots to
gameplay on one of them. Building the runtime, passing the suites and rendering
through `ps3recomp_host` are all real, and none of them is that.

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Auto-generate HLE stubs from RPCS3 modules
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   ├── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   │   └── atomic.h          # PS3 atomic operations (lwarx/stwcx)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       ├── sys_prx.h         # PRX module loading
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations (from RPCS3's module system)
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse, cellGem
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
├── patches/                  # Patches for upstream tools
│   └── xenonrecomp-ppu.patch # XenonRecomp adaptations for PPU (Cell != Xenon)
│
└── docs/                     # Documentation (incl. ARCHITECTURE, RUNTIME, SPU_LIFTER, RSX_GRAPHICS, ...)
    ├── ARCHITECTURE.md        # Cell processor and recomp pipeline deep-dive
    ├── GETTING_STARTED.md     # How to recompile your first PS3 game
    ├── MODULE_STATUS.md       # Implementation status of all HLE modules
    ├── MODULES_REFERENCE.md   # Detailed per-module documentation
    ├── RUNTIME.md             # Runtime reference: VM, PPU/SPU contexts, types
    ├── SYSCALLS.md            # All LV2 kernel syscall implementations
    ├── NID_SYSTEM.md          # PS3 NID linking system explained
    ├── TOOLS.md               # Recompiler pipeline tools reference
    ├── BUILDING.md            # Build system, compilers, platform notes
    ├── GAME_PORTING_GUIDE.md  # Step-by-step game porting walkthrough
    └── PLATFORM_ABSTRACTION.md # Win32/POSIX cross-platform details
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

We're building HLE implementations based on RPCS3's module system. **97 modules complete, 1 partial (media decode)** — 219 files and ~76,000 lines under `libs/`.

| Category | Modules | Status |
|----------|---------|--------|
| **Kernel Threading** | sys_ppu_thread, sys_mutex, sys_cond, sys_semaphore, sys_rwlock | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Events** | sys_event (queues, ports, flags), sys_timer | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Memory** | sys_memory, sys_mmapper (containers, shared mem) | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Filesystem** | sys_fs (path mapping, real I/O) | ✅ Complete |
| **Filesystem** | cellFs (real file I/O, dir ops, stat, path translation) | ✅ Complete |
| **Save System** | cellSaveData (callback-driven, PARAM.SFO), cellGame | ✅ Complete |
| **Input** | cellPad (XInput/SDL2), cellKb, cellMouse | ✅ Complete |
| **Audio** | cellAudio (WASAPI/SDL2, mixing thread, multi-port) | ✅ Complete |
| **Video Output** | cellVideoOut (resolution config, 720p default) | ✅ Complete |
| **Codecs** | cellPngDec, cellJpgDec, cellGifDec (stb_image) | ✅ Complete |
| **Font** | cellFont (stb_truetype backend + fallback metrics) | ✅ Complete |
| **Network** | sys_net (BSD sockets), cellNet, cellNetCtl, cellHttpUtil, cellSsl, sceNp*, sceNpTrophy | ✅ Complete |
| **Hardware** | cellUsbd (USB), cellCamera (PS Eye), cellGem (PS Move) — stub, no devices | ✅ Complete |
| **Sync** | cellSync (atomic spinlocks, LF queue), cellSync2 (OS-backed) | ✅ Complete |
| **System** | cellRtc, cellMsgDialog, cellOskDialog, cellUserInfo, cellGameExec | ✅ Complete |
| **Localization** | cellL10n (UTF-8/16/32/UCS-2, ISO-8859-1, generic converter) | ✅ Complete |
| **Resolution** | cellResc (display modes, scaling, interlace, aspect ratio) | ✅ Complete |
| **Fibers** | cellFiber (PPU fibers via Windows Fibers/ucontext) | ✅ Complete |
| **AV Config** | cellAvconfExt (audio output info, gamma, sound availability) | ✅ Complete |
| **Input Util** | cellKey2char (HID scancode → Unicode, US-101 layout) | ✅ Complete |
| **Graphics** | cellGcmSys (cmd buffer, IO mapping, tile/zcull, flip handlers, timestamps, FIFO walker + ring recycle), RSX command processor (NV47xx parsing, state tracking, backend callbacks), **live D3D12 backend** (executes the title's real NV4097 vertex/fragment p

# Project Pyrrhus (work in progress) **Killzone 2: Unofficial PC Port (static recompilation)** [![CI](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) ![Status: partly playable](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-partly%20playable-orange) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/undecuple/project-pyrrhus?include_prereleases&label=release)](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/releases) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/total)](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/releases) ![Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20x64-0078D6) ![Direct3D 12](https://img.shields.io/badge/graphics-Direct3D%2012-555) **[Status](#status)** · **[Features](docs/FEATURES.md)** · **[Screenshots](docs/SCREENSHOTS.md)** · **[Requirements](docs/requirements.md)** · **[Getting it](#getting-it)** · **[Building](docs/BUILDING.md)** · **[How it works](#how-it-works-briefly)** · **[Known issues](docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md)** · **[Accessibility](docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md)** · **[Release criteria](docs/RELEASE-CRITERIA.md)** · **[AI use](#how-ai-was-used)** · **[Contributing](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)** · **[Related project](#related-project)** *Pyrrhus* is the Helghast capital where most of Killzone 2 is fought; Project Pyrrhus is a fan project, not official and not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Guerrilla Games. **What this is:** a static recompilation. It runs the game's own code, with the PPU and SPU programs recompiled ahead of time to native x64. It is **not an emulator** (no CPU emulator runs at play time) and **not a rewrite** (the game's logic is not reimplemented). Around that code, the PS3's system libraries and hardware behaviour are reimplemented on PC APIs. An unofficial port of **Killzone 2** (PS3, 2009) to Windows x64, built on your PC from your own copy of the game. The game's PowerPC (PPU) and Cell SPU code is translated to C++ ahead of time with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) (the build pins ps3recomp v0.18.0 plus this project's own patch set in `port/patches/`) and compiled into a native Windows program, so no CPU emulator runs at play time. The PS3 system libraries are reimplemented on PC APIs. The hardware around the code is still provided by a runtime layer, much as an emulator provides it: the game's GPU command stream is meant to be replayed on Direct3D 12, and SPU scheduling, DMA and the PS3's memory layout are reproduced. It is tested under Proton on Linux. > **Status: early, partly playable.** The game's code is translated, and the Windows program builds and starts. The > intro movie plays, the menus run with sound, and the first level loads and draws, but > **at about 23 frames per second** in one 330 s scripted run after a logging fix (the PS3 runs it at 30; earlier > runs gave 13-17, and a hand-played run is not measured yet). Sound is > stereo only. A DualShock 4, including motion, was hand-tested on > 2026-10-22. What works today and what does not: the dated table under [Status](#status). This port currently supports Direct3D 12 only. For a Vulkan version of a Killzone 2 port, please use [Tokisaki Port](https://github.com/YYOzcan/tokisaki-port), which is developed separately by its own author. **You need your own copy of the game.** This repository contains only the port: source code, patches to the recompiler, tools and documentation. It contains no game code, data, assets, keys or firmware, and it never will. Killzone 2 is © Sony Interactive Entertainment; this project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony or Guerrilla Games. ## Status


The port on 2026-10-28: the first level in play. More, by milestone: screenshots.

As of 2026-10-27, on Windows x64, tested under Proton on Linux; the installer and first-run build also ran on Windows 10 in a virtual machine (no play there). | | | |---|---| | Code translation | the game's PowerPC code is translated (about 54,000 functions for the 1.29 update) on ps3recomp v0.18.0 with this project's patches, and the Windows program builds | | Boot and menus | starts, brings up the game's job system, file system and graphics, shows the front end and menus (played by hand with a pad on 2026-10-22, with the selection highlight, Mission Select pictures and pause menu drawn since that day), and starts the first level (Corinth River). The main menu has an Exit to desktop entry and a Keyboard page that saves key choices to `keybinds.ini`; both were checked in scripted runs only, not by hand | | First level | loads and runs without a stall; the briefing cutscene plays with its subtitles | | Picture | the first level is drawn lit and in proportion (since 2026-10-19). Since 2026-10-20 the lighting reads the scene the right way up: a faint mirrored copy of the scene, with a second upside-down head, is gone, and the compared frames match RPCS3. Moving images looked doubled, because the game's motion blur is tuned for 30 frames per second; motion blur is now off by default until the port runs near full speed, with a switch to turn it back on | | Speed | 23.3 frames per second in one 330 s scripted run of the first level with motion blur off, after the session-log buffering fix (13-17 before it), against the PS3's 30; not yet measured by hand. Since 2026-10-20 the translated SPU code is built for SSE4.1 and FMA (about 3x), so the port needs a CPU with AVX and FMA3 (from about 2013); the port checks at startup for AVX and FMA3 and says so if they are missing. Most of each frame was the game's SPU post-processing; its jobs now also spread over all SPU threads. Shaders are still compiled the first time they are needed, which pauses the first minute of a level; a pipeline list kept by each session cut frames over 100 ms in that minute from 18-20 to 2 in scripted runs, and it is not shipped with the port yet | | SPU programs | the game's SPU programs and job modules are translated and run, including the post-processing chain | | Update 1.29 | the build targets the 1.29 update; its added archive and patch files are mapped and read; the effect of the patches on the game data is not checked yet | | Saves | the game's save format is mapped; the port writes its own saves, including checkpoint saves in the first level; loading a checkpoint back is not checked yet. Saves copied over from RPCS3 are copied unchanged, with no promise that they load | | Input | pads go through SDL3 (PlayStation and Xbox pads; SDL3.dll ships with the port, XInput is the fallback without it); a DualShock 4 was played by hand on 2026-10-22, including its motion sensor; Xbox and DualSense pads are not yet tried by hand; a pad layout setting (Original by default, Modern selectable) writes the chosen layout into the game's profile, and the game's buttons follow it in play (Modern: crouch on Circle, use on Square, zoom and flashlight on L1); on-screen button prompts can show PlayStation 4/5, Xbox or keyboard symbols (set in keybinds.ini), in menus and in the level | | Audio, video, online | the intro movie plays with pictures and sound through FFmpeg's LGPL decoders, loaded from separate DLLs (the other 27 movies are not yet tried); the movies' 5.1 tracks decode, but all sound is mixed down to stereo for now (no surround output yet); menu and game sound play; online not started | | Installer and portable zip | the first-run checks, generators and packaging (including SDL3.dll and the movie decoders) exist and are tested without the game; the installer compiles; setup can reuse an existing RPCS3 install (tested with stand-in folders only); on 2026-10-27 install, first-run build and uninstall worked in a Windows 10 virtual machine without a GPU, and the game started but exited with a message there (no GPU, no play); nothing is released | Feature by feature, the PS3 game against the port: [FEATURES.md](docs/FEATURES.md) (generated from the repository's own records). What is broken or unfinished today: [docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md](docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md). Controls, button prompts, display modes and subtitles: [docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md](docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md). ## What goes online Nothing unless you ask. The port does not start any connection of its own. - **Version check, off by default.** The installer's "Check now" button and the portable zip's first run ask GitHub once, when you choose to, whether a newer release exists. With "Check for new versions" ticked, the launcher asks at most once a day. Each check is one anonymous request for this project's list of releases, with nothing about you, your computer or your game. - **Updating, only when you say yes.** When a check finds a newer release, the launcher asks first. Only after a yes does it download that release's setup and its published checksum from this project's GitHub releases, check the file against the checksum, and start it for your install folder. - **Project website** (`site/`): viewing it loads the Rajdhani font from Google Fonts, which sees your visit. The repository, installer and game do not. Online multiplayer, if it comes, will only use a self-hosted server you choose. ## Getting it **Pre-release [v0.1.2](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/releases/tag/v0.1.2):** a Windows installer (recommended) and a portable zip, on the [releases page](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus/releases) with a `.sha256` file for each and `SHA256SUMS`. They check your own disc dump (a folder or a decrypted ISO file), the 1.29 update and the decrypted EBOOT ([what each must contain](docs/GETTING-FILES.md)), then translate and build the game's code on your own machine with a bundled compiler. No game code, assets or keys are ever shipped or downloaded. Do not install into a OneDrive folder (a precaution from a problem reported on Project Helghast: OneDrive would sync the build's thousands of files while they are written), and keep your game files on this device (in OneDrive: "Always keep on this device"); the setup refuses both. You can also build the port yourself (below). It is partly playable: the first level can be played with a pad (a scripted run gives about 23 frames per second, the PS3 30; hand play is not measured), and the rest of the campaign has not been tried. What changed in each version: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). A first release that calls itself playable waits for the conditions in [docs/RELEASE-CRITERIA.md](docs/RELEASE-CRITERIA.md). Until then every release is a pre-release. There is no date for it. ## Requirements Your own Killzone 2 disc (US, BCUS98116) dumped as a folder, the 1.29 update, and the decrypted EBOOT from your own copy; a Direct3D 12 GPU. Hardware figures come once the game runs. Details: [docs/requirements.md](docs/requirements.md); what each folder must hold and what the first-run check prints: [docs/GETTING-FILES.md](docs/GETTING-FILES.md). ## Building The port is built with a Nix flake and the patched [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) it pins (release v0.18.0 plus this project's patch set; `tools/ps3recomp-patched.sh` applies it); the tested route is Linux with a Windows cross build run under Proton. The steps, the files you need and the macOS and Windows notes: [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md). Forking or reusing this project (names, addresses, versions, what to change): [docs/FORKING.md](docs/FORKING.md). ## How it works, briefly - **PPU:** the game's PowerPC functions are lifted to C++ by ps3recomp's lifter and compiled with MinGW-w64. - **SPU:** the embedded SPU programs are lifted the same way; SPURS runs on host threads. - **Graphics:** the game's RSX command stream is replayed on Direct3D 12, as in Project Helghast (in progress; the first level is drawn, and speed is the open problem). - **Data:** the game reads its own archive in place through its file system library; the 1.29 update's added archive and patch files are layered over the disc data as on the PS3 (in progress). General fixes found here are offered to ps3recomp upstream. ## How AI was used This project is developed by one person with AI coding agents. The agents did most of the work of reading the game's binary and the reference material, writing and testing patches, tools and documentation, and running the builds, inside a sandbox with no network access and with the maintainer reviewing and merging what they produced. The maintainer sets the goals, decides what is published, and is responsible for it. Findings are dated and marked as verified, assumed or open; an `ASSUMPTION:` in the code or the docs is not fact. If you find a statement here that was not verified, please open an issue. ## Roadmap A playable first level first (frame rate, shader pauses on a first play, hand play), then the rest of the campaign, sound and the local-build installer; later PC display options, keyboard and mouse, and a stand-in for the campaign's motion-control sections. Gameplay changes stay optional. No dates are given: see the [release criteria](docs/RELEASE-CRITERIA.md). Item by item, with what is done and what is planned: [ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md). ## Related project **[Project Helghast](https://github.com/undecuple/project-helghast)**: Killzone 3 (PS3) ported to PC the same way. Project Pyrrhus uses its method and reuses its general runtime work (ps3recomp fixes, renderer, SPU job system), adapted to Killzone 2. Most patches in `port/patches/` come from there; the rest are Killzone 2's own. Its builds are pre-releases on its [releases page](https://github.com/undecuple/project-helghast/releases), as this project's are. ## Contributing Pull requests and feature requests are welcome. Details: [CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). In short: - Open an issue first for big work, so effort is not wasted. - There is no promise of review time, or that a change will be merged. - Never post game files, keys or decrypted binaries, in issues, pull requests or logs. - Contributions must be MIT-compatible; no code from GPL projects such as RPCS3. - If an AI tool helped write a pull request, say so in it. AI coding agents: read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) first (the same rules, written for agents). Security problems: [SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md). ## Licence The port's own code, tools and documentation: [MIT](LICENSE). The licence covers nothing of the game itself. **Reusing this work, including by AI systems and automated tools:** the MIT licence applies to every use, including crawling, indexing, training and code generation. Copies or substantial portions must keep the copyright and permission notice, and we ask that derived work credits "Project Pyrrhus by undecuple" with a link to this repository. Details: [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md#reuse-and-attribution-including-ai-and-automated-use).

# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível e à primeira luta contra um chefe, mas ainda lento (~18-23 fps no nível, 13-21 na luta). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot à primeira luta contra um chefe:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~50-55 fps; o primeiro nível a ~22-27 fps, conforme a cena (era ~9); a luta contra o chefe a 13-21. Atrasando um thread de cada vez e medindo quanto o quadro atrasa junto, o limite hoje é o thread que executa os comandos de vídeo (o RSX do RPCS3) e o thread principal do jogo, não as SPUs nem a placa de vídeo. Partes pesadas das SPUs já rodam como código nativo, cada uma conferida contra o original: a geometria por draw (índices, skinning, normais e tangentes) e o pós-processamento que suaviza as bordas da imagem. O foco agora é deixar o jogo mais leve para processadores comuns: o uso total de CPU já caiu ~10% (de 7,2 para 6,4 núcleos no menu) sem perder fps, e o próximo passo é a espera pelas consultas de oclusão (ZCULL) no thread do RSX. Esses números são de um Ryzen 5 5600G com uma RX 7600; num Ryzen 7 9800X3D com uma RX 9070 XT (RSX do RPCS3, Vulkan), o jogo chega a 60 fps fora das lutas e cai para cerca da metade nelas. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); e o jogo às vezes trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`). - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md).

## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), abra o launcher, `launcher\AscensionLauncher.exe`:

JOGAR abre o jogo dentro da própria janela do launcher. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). 1438133055.readme_excerpt:
# GT5 Native Recomp

[![Source checks](https://github.com/MauricioRSJ98/gt5-native-recomp/actions/workflows/source-checks.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/MauricioRSJ98/gt5-native-recomp/actions/workflows/source-checks.yml)

Experimental native recompilation research for **Gran Turismo 5, PS3, BCUS98114 v2.17**, targeting **Windows x86-64 and Vulkan**.

**Pre-alpha / boot bring-up. The game does not render a frame yet and is not playable.** This repository publishes the integration code, runtime patches, generation tools and address-only analysis metadata so other developers can help.

[Português brasileiro](README.pt-BR.md) · [Roadmap](https://github.com/MauricioRSJ98/gt5-native-recomp/issues/1) · [Build and regeneration](docs/BUILDING.md) · [Current status](docs/STATUS.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Credits and tools](docs/CREDITS.md)

## What this project does

The intended execution path recompiles PPU and SPU instructions ahead of time into native code. A native compatibility runtime implements the necessary PS3 services and consumes RSX commands through Vulkan. Missing CPU code stops execution for investigation and another AOT generation pass. The integrated executable excludes the SPU instruction interpreter; DirectX 12 is disabled.

The immediate goal is to reach the first real game frame, then a menu and eventually a drivable race, even at very low performance. These are separate milestones; no gameplay or performance claim is made.

## Latest local checkpoint — 29 October 2026

| Area | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| PPU | 43,525 generated native entry addresses, including internal CFG entries |
| SPU | Six embedded ELF images plus 16 captured raw images compiled/registered; raw images contain 6,723 generated entries |
| Vulkan | GTX 1050 Ti initialization; guest shader translation through glslang/SPIR-V enabled |
| Files | Reads from the original disc ISO and installed update files |
| Startup | Display buffers configured; audio initialization/port/thread and XInput controller initialization reached |
| Graphics | **No observed guest draw or game flip/frame** |
| Current blockers | Uncompiled PPU targets and incomplete USB HLE services |

Compilation counts are **not completion percentages or proofs of correctness**. Some entries are basic-block wrappers; SPU code/data boundaries and indirect transfers still need review. See [the checkpoint and its limitations](docs/STATUS.md).

## Help wanted

Useful contributions include:

- PPU/SPU lifting, control-flow recovery and ABI review.
- SPURS scheduling, synchronization and correctly routed SPU-to-PPU events.
- RSX command consumption, shader translation and Vulkan rendering.
- USB/controller compatibility services and clean Windows builds.
- Reproducing a documented blocker using your own local game data.

Start with the [pinned roadmap](https://github.com/MauricioRSJ98/gt5-native-recomp/issues/1), [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [issues labeled `help wanted`](https://github.com/MauricioRSJ98/gt5-native-recomp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20is%3Aopen%20label%3A%22help%20wanted%22). Small, evidenced changes are especially helpful. Report what changed and the next observed blocker; avoid repeated unchanged boot runs. Use [Discussions](https://github.com/MauricioRSJ98/gt5-native-recomp/discussions) for questions and planning.

## Source and local data

The repository contains **no game executable, disc image, update package, captured SPU binary, generated game instruction bodies, firmware, SDK, keys, or playable download**. Contributors must supply their own local inputs. `private/`, `game/`, `game-data/`, `tools/` and `third_party/` are excluded from Git.

The local checkpoint was built with private generated artifacts. A clean public clone must regenerate them; the clean-clone workflow is not yet validated end to end. The public repository is a research starting point, not a one-click game release. [Build details](docs/BUILDING.md) distinguish established local results from remaining reproduction work.

## Foundations and disclosure

- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp): main PPU/SPU lifting and compatibility-runtime foundation.
- [GT5 Prologue Recompiled](https://github.com/sp00nznet/GT5P): loader and startup/presentation integration reference. Prologue addresses are not treated as GT5 addresses.
- [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): behavior and file-format reference, including SPURS/user-event routing; its CPU emulation engine is not incorporated into this executable.
- [ShadowOfTheColossus-PC](https://github.com/Oussama268/ShadowOfTheColossus-PC/releases/tag/v0.60.6-opt11): architectural inspiration. Its different console/CPU/GPU path is not a drop-in GT5 implementation.
- [Ghidra](https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra): targeted static analysis via PyGhidra.
- [REA](https://github.com/morluto/rea): installed/evaluated analysis tooling; its Ghidra/PS3 integration is **not operational in this workflow**. Analysis that worked used Ghidra directly.

Development is AI-assisted with **OpenAI Codex, GPT-6.1 Sol, medium reasoning**, as specified by the maintainer. AI assistance covers code, analysis and documentation; it does not replace review or execution evidence. This is an independent community project, without endorsement from OpenAI, Sony, Polyphony Digital or the projects referenced above.

Full versions, roles, licenses and limitations: [CREDITS](docs/CREDITS.md) and [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

cdb581579fd7ba76d429fab741828ce9e04161d6.message:
Low-CPU update: fewer threads on weaker PCs, support for CPUs without AVX2

- SPURS: on PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the lanes/kernels spin less, wake the
  main thread sooner and run on fewer threads (4-thread PCs: ~10 fps -> ~29 fps,
  8 threads: ~38 -> ~50 fps). Big PCs keep the old behaviour.
- Vertex workers spin far less after each job, fewer workers on small CPUs.
- The once-per-second thread scan only walks the game's own threads.
- No exclusive core reservations on PCs with fewer than 20 CPU threads;
  P-core pinning only on hybrid CPUs with at least 8 P-core threads.
- CPUs without AVX2/FMA/BMI2 (pre-2013 Intel, AVX-less Pentium/Celeron, AMD before
  2015): Setup/the updater detect this and build an SSE4.1 compatibility version
  automatically (same results, slower). The game also checks the CPU at startup and
  shows a clear message instead of crashing.

# inFamous PC

> **Official repo: [github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn).**
> Only download the Setup from the [Releases page](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn/releases) here.
> Forks are not supported, and bugs from forks won't be fixed.

An unofficial native Windows port of **inFamous** (PlayStation 3, 2009, European
release `BCES00220`). The game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code is statically
recompiled to x86-64 C/C++ with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp),
so it runs as a normal Windows program rather than under an emulator.

**This repository contains no game code or data.** You build the game yourself,
on your own PC, from your own copy of the game.

## Easy install

Download **inFamous Setup.exe** from the latest release, run it, choose your
`.iso` (an encrypted image works with its `.dkey` next to it) or your game
folder (the one with `PS3_GAME` in it), pick an install location and press
**Install**.

Setup checks for Python and the C++ build tools and offers to install them,
copies the game out of the disc image, regenerates the recompiled code from your
copy, builds it and adds an inFamous shortcut. Running Setup again on the same
folder updates or repairs the install and only redoes what changed.

## Updating

When a new version is published here, players update in place instead of reinstalling:
**Update now** in Setup (it finds the existing install), the **Update inFamous** shortcut in
the Start menu, or `Update inFamous.cmd` in the install folder. The updater compares every file
with this repository, downloads only what changed, regenerates the game code only if the
port's patches changed, and recompiles only the affected parts. Installs made with an older
Setup need one run of the new Setup on the same folder first.

## Requirements

- Your own inFamous disc dump, European release (`BCES00220`).
- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with Direct3D 12 support.
- A CPU with SSE4.1 (2008 or newer). On CPUs without AVX2 (Intel before 2013, Pentium/Celeron
  without AVX, AMD before 2015) Setup builds a slower compatibility version automatically.
  On PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the game uses fewer threads and less CPU (tested down to 4 threads).
- [Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) with "Add python.exe to
  PATH" ticked.
- [Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/)
  with the **Desktop development with C++** workload and the **C++ Clang
  Compiler for Windows** component.
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), only if your `PS3_GAME\USRDIR` has `EBOOT.BIN`
  but no decrypted `EBOOT.elf`. Setup uses it to decrypt the executable.
- About 10 GB of free disk space and 16 GB of RAM.

## Building manually

```bat
cd installer
cargo build --release
target\release\infamous-installer --game "D:\Dumps\inFamous"
```

`infamous-installer doctor` checks the requirements only. Finished steps are
skipped when you run it again, so an interrupted install continues where it
stopped. See [installer/README.md](installer/README.md) for every step and the
maintainer commands.

## Playing

Run **inFamous** (the shortcut Setup made). It opens a small options window first
(vsync, frame cap, resolution, language and more, saved to `settings.ini`);
**Play** starts the game. The same settings are in the game's pause menu under
**Settings**. Controllers work as on the console, and keyboard and mouse are supported.

**F10** opens the in-game trainer: God Mode, Infinite Energy, Refill Health,
Max Health x2/x5/x10, Add XP, Karma +/-, Kill Enemies / Civilians, Super Speed
and Player Model (play as Zeke, Trish, Kessler, Alden or John). Set `TRAINER=0`
to turn it off.

## DLSS and FSR (optional)

The game can use NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA or AMD FSR for upscaling, and AMD FSR frame generation.
They are not included in the download because NVIDIA and AMD distribute their SDKs themselves,
but both are free and take a few minutes to add.

- **DLSS** needs an NVIDIA RTX graphics card.
- **FSR** works on any modern GPU (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel). FSR 4 needs a Radeon RX 9000 card;
  other cards get FSR 3.1 automatically.

**1. Download the SDK(s) you want.** You need the **source code**, not a Windows or Linux demo.
On the page, click the green **Code** button, then **Download ZIP**. If you go through the
Releases page instead, pick **Source code (zip)**, not the files with "demo" or "samples" in the name.

| For | Download | Rename the extracted folder to |
|---|---|---|
| DLSS / DLAA | [github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS) | `dlss-sdk` |
| FSR and frame generation | [github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK) | `fsr-sdk` |

**2. Put the folder(s) in your inFamous install folder**, next to `infamous-recomp` and
`ps3recomp`:

```
inFamous\
  dlss-sdk\        <- contains include\ and lib\
  fsr-sdk\         <- contains Kits\
  infamous-recomp\
  ps3recomp\
  ...
```

Make sure you don't end up with a folder inside a folder (`dlss-sdk\DLSS-main\include`).
`include` (DLSS) or `Kits` (FSR) must be directly inside.

**3. Rebuild the game once.** Open a Command Prompt in the install folder and run:

```bat
type nul > .installer\update.pending
"Update inFamous.cmd"
```

This rebuilds the game with the SDK(s), which takes a while. Any later update also picks them up
automatically, so you only do this once.

**4. Turn it on in game:** pause, then **Settings**, then **Upscaling** (DLAA, DLSS Quality /
Balanced / Performance, FSR Native AA / Quality / Balanced / Performance) and **Frame
Generation**. The same options are in the launcher's options window. Upscaling and frame
generation apply after a restart.

If the **Upscaling** row is missing, the build didn't find the SDK: check the folder names and
layout from step 2, then repeat step 3.

## How it works

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `ps3recomp` | The recompiler toolkit and runtime: PPU and SPU lifters, HLE system libraries, RSX on Direct3D 12, audio and input |
| `infamous-recomp` | The inFamous-specific parts: program entry, game stubs and fixes, asset tools |
| `installer` | Setup and the command-line installer: reads the disc, regenerates the code from your game, applies `installer/patches`, builds |
| `installer/infamous.toml` | Everything about the game and the port: pipeline steps, generated files, build and launch settings |
| `installer/generated.lock` | Hashes of each generated file before and after the port's patches |

## Credits

- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet and
  contributors (see [ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md](ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md)).
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), used to decrypt the game executable.
- Sucker Punch Productions, for the game.
- [Lorenzo Aiello](https://github.com/aiellolorenzo23) and [ibrahimpuri](https://github.com/ibrahimpuri), for their support.

spu_interp: SPU_INTERP_STATS also lists where the interpreter is entered

Entries are credited to the image that owns the resident code region, so
the list names the lift that is missing them. Entries spread over a code
body mean its lift isn't dispatched at all; a few hot ones inside an
otherwise lifted body are resume points (return addresses after an SPU
interrupt) or function starts the lifter didn't find. In God of War HD the
remaining interpreted SPU time comes from four of them (0xA68 in the
Wws_Job policy module, 0x5318 and 0x87E8 in the mixer job).

CPU reports say what each thread is. PS3_USLEEP_MIN_US=<n> (default off)
blocks sleeps shorter than n us on a timer; measured as a regression for Buzz

06aa9375568380b75c2a35b9bd91959aa321310b.message:
sceNp: tickets, account region and network time answer OFFLINE

sceNpManagerRequestTicket2, GetTicket, GetTicketParam,
GetAccountRegion and GetNetworkTime were not implemented, so their
imports answered CELL_OK with nothing written. A title that asked for a
ticket waited for a GOT_TICKET manager event that never came, and one
that read the region or the time used whatever was in its buffer.

Implement them with RPCS3's argument checks and offline answers: without
a psnr server the NP manager is OFFLINE and so are these
(SCE_NP_ERROR_OFFLINE), and there is never a ticket, so GetTicket
reports a size of 0 and GetTicketParam INVALID_STATE. Signed in to a
psnr server, which issues no tickets, a request is answered at once with
a GOT_TICKET event carrying an error instead of a ticket size; the
region is the fake account's (US, English) and the network time is the
host clock as a CellRtcTick.

06b2292def31186d507aa8cfd38ed487ec220a9c.message:
.github/workflows: pin the five third-party actions to commit SHAs

release.yml fires on `push: tags: ['v*']` with `permissions: contents:
write`, so every action it invokes runs holding a token that can write to
this repo and attach release assets. Referenced by floating major tag, any
of those five actions could be retargeted upstream -- a tag is mutable, and
whoever controls it controls what executes inside that job. Pinning to a
commit SHA makes the referenced code immutable.

Each SHA is the commit the action's current major tag points at, so this
changes no behaviour: the same code runs, it just can no longer be swapped
out from under us. The readable version stays in a trailing comment because
a bare SHA tells a later reader nothing about how stale the pin is.

Only `uses:` lines and their comments change -- 13 references across all
five workflows, no other workflow edits.

(cherry picked from commit 903d023f4a88ace083b0d9843fd3cf71a40f6572)

0d6154fe3185a83a7bf774b16c90eb9de6138252.message:
SPURS job pool: optional bounded polling before idle lanes sleep

A job chain separated by SYNCs reaches the pool as many short stages.
Buzz! Quiz World's studio runs ~165 stages of ~14 image 40/41 jobs per
frame, so all four lanes go idle at every stage boundary; sleeping on the
condition variable there cost an OS wake-up per lane per stage, and the
lanes sat ~14-25 us between jobs (66 % busy inside pool groups).

SPURS_POOL_SPIN_US=n makes an idle lane poll the queue head for up to n us
(a lock-free hint; work is still claimed under the pool lock) before it
sleeps. It stays off by default, and is ignored below 12 logical
processors, where polling lanes would compete with the guest PPU, RSX and
audio threads.

Vulkan, EU 1.00, Ryzen 9 7900, n=1000 vs 0: main menu 27.3/27.5 ->
30.0/31.6 FPS (200 us: 27.9/28.9, 3000 us: 30.3); solo round 31.9 ->
36.3 FPS, p90 36.4 -> 32.0 ms.

118b6281a756697391f178e523a409e0b1f60ce1.message:
cellGcmSys: GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS sets how long a FIFO park may stand

When the drain stops on a self-jump park and `put` has moved, it waits
GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS (50 ms) for the title to patch the park and then follows
`put`. That suits a title that leaves a park standing when it switches
segments. It does not suit one that appends commands right after the
park, moves `put` there and patches the park last: if the patch comes
after the grace, the drain skips the commands in between.

God of War HD does the latter, and while it loads its menu the two stores
have been more than 50 ms apart: the drain jumped from 0x57C40 to put
0x5AA2C, dropped ~11 KB of commands with a fence among them, and the boot
stopped (once in about 45 runs). The RSX itself would wait.

GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS=<ms> now sets the grace; the default is unchanged.

147e59a79e63cefcf0c2f53fc7314d83f54167e2.message:
rsx_d3d12: pass the FP depth-export bits of SHADER_CONTROL

Draws recorded only the 32-bit-exports bit of SET_SHADER_CONTROL, so a
fragment program that replaces the fragment depth (bits 1-3) was
translated without SV_Depth. God of War HD's resolve pass writes the
scene depth it reads from the 2x-AA depth surface into the resolved
one this way; without it the pass wrote the quad's own depth (0), and
every depth-tested pass after it failed everywhere: the stencil
shadows, the fog, rain, the waterfall mist and the glows.

The draw now records the export bits (32-bit exports and depth export)
as fp_ctrl, part of the pipeline key, and hands them to the
decompiler, which already emits SV_Depth from r1.z.

1530be7cfd1295f9db57e380a3dc2314770a82c1.message:
ppu_lifter: per-function copy of the memory model; PPU_FAST_FP

A guest store goes through vm_base + ea, a byte pointer the compiler
cannot tell apart from the memory-model globals, so the inline load and
store paths reloaded vm_base, ppu_vm_size, ppu_hle_inject_base and the
two enable flags after every store. Each lifted function now copies them
into a local at entry (PPU_MM_SNAP) and its accesses use the copy. They
are all set before guest code runs. The SPU reservation bitmap and the
store watches can change while a function runs, so those are still read
from the globals. Code outside lifted functions keeps vm_read*_inl and
vm_write*_inl, which now take a fresh copy per access.

PPU_FAST_FP, off unless the build defines it, drops the NaN checks in
ppu_fp_bin and ppu_fmadd_core. The host's NaN differs from the PPC one
only in its sign and in which of two NaN operands propagates.

God of War HD, func_001BEFA4, built with FMA3: 6,195 instructions before,
5,855 with the copy, 4,553 with PPU_FAST_FP as well (branches 1,342,
1,063, 583).

test_ppu_lift.py: the conformance driver defines PPU_NO_INLINE_LOADS. Its
vm_read*/vm_write* are its own functions, and its statements do not run
inside a lifted function.

170be32ac21c17795a97d244d8fa559ed47e21f0.message:
ftrace: a span for each HLE import call

PS3_FTRACE recorded syscalls and timer sleeps but not HLE imports, so a
guest thread blocked or busy inside an import (a file read, a SPURS
wait, a lock taken hundreds of thousands of times) showed up nowhere.
ps3_hle_call's exit guard now closes a PS3_FT_HLE span (who = thread,
a = NID, b = guest lr) for calls at least PS3_FTRACE_MIN_US long. With
the trace off it costs one load per call.

This is what found God of War HD's 360 ms frame: 320,355 lwmutex
lock/unlock pairs in it (PS3_FTRACE_MIN_US=0), against 71 in a normal
frame.

1891b8fe718534bef9d143c7b665beb762adbc07.message:
gcm: count the drain's own ring recycle as the JUMP to begin

Once a title has been seen to overrun its ring, the drain recycles the
ring itself when current nears end. A title whose callback also
recycles (cellGcm_fifo_recycle) can be in that callback at the same
moment: it writes its JUMP and put, and only then marks itself waiting,
so a pass that read the mark clear still teleports get to begin. The
callback then waits for a backward JUMP that never comes, because get
is already at begin == put, and gives up after 2 s of no progress.

God of War HD stopped for 2-4 s this way at random points in about
half of the gameplay runs. Counting the teleport as the backward JUMP
ends the callback's wait at once.

1be9e80d533ae0ff253fa169f5d2f5f783a1364d.message:
rsx_shader_msl: compile a vertex program's position invariant

Titles draw the same geometry twice with two different vertex programs,
the second pass testing EQUAL against the depth the first one wrote. The
RSX runs the position arithmetic instruction by instruction, so both
programs land on the same depth. The Metal compiler optimises each
program on its own (it may fuse a multiply and an add into one FMA in one
of them and not in the other), the two depths can then differ in the last
bit, and the EQUAL pass leaves holes.

Resistance: Fall of Man's foliage writes depth through an alpha-tested
program, then colour through one that also lights it, with
SET_DEPTH_FUNC EQUAL.

The translator now marks a vertex program's position [[position,
invariant]], and the Metal backend compiles guest programs with
MTLCompileOptions.preserveInvariance (macOS 11 and later), so programs
that compute the position the same way get the same bits.
PS3RECOMP_MSL_INVARIANT=0 leaves the position as it was.

test_shader_msl checks the vertex program's MSL for
"[[position, invariant]]" (and for "[[position" under
PS3RECOMP_MSL_INVARIANT=0).

1c7c1d914374d59451f5b73421119af501606cfb.message:
rsx engine: a scissored CLEAR_SURFACE clears only the scissor

RSX clears what the surface clip and the scissor let through. The engine
cleared every colour and depth target whole, whatever the scissor said.

Resistance: Fall of Man's co-op split screen renders both views into one
2x1 antialiased 1280x720 scene target: the scissor on the left half, a
colour and depth clear and player 1's view, then the scissor on the right
half, a clear and player 2's view. The second clear wiped player 1's view,
and the left half of the screen was black under the HUD.

sink_clear now asks eng_clear_rect what the clear may write: the clip
from the origin, then the scissor (eng_scissor_rect, the draw path's
scissor code moved into a function). Only a scissor narrower than the
clip makes a clear partial; a clip smaller than the target alone stays a
whole clear, as before. A partial clear goes to two new optional backend
hooks, clear_color_rect and clear_depth_stencil_rect. A backend without
them, or PS3RECOMP_ENG_RECT_CLEAR=0, clears whole as before. A depth clear
that covers everything the zeta was ever bound with (ext_w/ext_h) stays
whole, and a partial depth clear keeps had_write.

The Metal backend records a rectangle clear as a clear record with the
rectangle in its scissor and encodes it as a pass of its own: the
attachment is loaded and a full-target triangle under that scissor writes
the colour, or the depth and stencil with the test always passing. Such a
record is never folded into a pass's load action.

New test_clear_rect in test_rsx_draw_engine (the co-op frame, whole and
empty scissors, a zeta only bound at a small clip, a backend without the
hooks), and test_metal_rect_clears.m (tools/test_metal_rect_clears.py) on
the GPU: a rectangle clear of the right half keeps the left half, for
colour, depth and stencil, and a whole clear after one covers the target.

21c14a650a346b18a4f79c82689ad5c060c34693.message:
rsx_d3d12: guest depth/stencil state and samplers in the guest-FP pipelines

Every guest-FP pipeline had a fixed LESS_EQUAL depth test with writes,
no stencil, and four static samplers (s0 point/clamp for the dbgfont
atlas, s1-s3 linear/wrap), whatever the title set. In God of War HD:

- Its stencil shadow volumes marked nothing, and the shadow pass, a
  full-screen reverse-subtract quad meant only for the marked pixels,
  darkened the whole frame (0.16 -> 0.012 on a lit pixel).
- Depth state ignored: rain and blood particles were rejected.
- Unit 0 was point-sampled and clamped. The soldiers wrap their texture
  atlas (v up to ~2), sampled the transparent bottom row and drew
  nothing over an untextured base; Kratos' tattoo and skirt came out
  white; textures shimmered.

Depth test/write/func and front/back stencil (func, ops, masks) are
packed per draw into a PSO key (rsx_zs_key); the stencil reference is
set per draw. The cull key now always carries the front face, which
two-sided stencil needs with culling off. Samplers are four descriptor
tables built from each unit's TEXTURE_ADDRESS/FILTER/CONTROL0/BORDER
(one cached descriptor per distinct state); units without guest state
keep the old two defaults.

23540a1007e37f28c404c3adfa8ea2d22e188194.message:
rsx_d3d12: cache converted vertices within a draw

Indexed lists (shared vertices), strips and fans (each vertex in up to
three triangles) and indexed quads expand one guest vertex into several
output vertices, and each one was fetched again: 16 attributes, each with
its own address resolve and conversion, for every reference. God of War
HD's gameplay frames expand ~370k vertices through these paths and the
fetch was a third of the frame.

A direct-mapped cache on the low index bits (8192 entries, 2 MB) keeps
the converted 256-byte vertex; a hit is a memcpy. It is dropped at every
draw, since attribute state and the guest arrays may change between
draws. Measured in GoW HD gameplay: vertex time per 20 frames 0.80 s ->
0.29 s, ~9.0 -> ~12.1 fps. VTX_CACHE_CHECK=1 refetches on every lookup
and counts differences: 0 in 312M lookups. VTX_NOCACHE=1 disables it.

27745b54d1b60e5232e48a1234a182fc6f52e113.message:
ppu_lifter: inline guest stores, the store side of the inline loads

Every lifted store called vm_write8/16/32/64 out of line. In God of War
HD gameplay those calls were about a fifth of the main thread.

The generated header now has vm_write*_inl beside vm_read*_inl. A store
is done in place when vm_inl_ok accepts the address, no store diagnostic
is armed (vm_inline_st_ok: PPU_WVAL, PPU_WWATCH, PT), the barrier watch
and the null-page sweep are idle, and no SPU holds a reservation on the
line (g_spu_coh_bits). Anything else goes to the out-of-line store as
before. PPU_NO_INLINE_STORES keeps the calls, and the runtime's own files
keep them through PPU_NO_INLINE_LOADS.

Re-lift to pick it up. God of War HD: the main thread runs about 14.8 ms
a frame instead of 16.2 with the HLE lookup cache, vm_write32 is gone
from its profile and vm_write64 is 1.2%. The executable grows from 57 to
87 MB.

279bd0049a1cf1abb66b1cb69e65fd4d8dd8006f.message:
rsx vertex fetch: frequency 1 under a modulo divider bit is one element per draw

NV4097_SET_FREQUENCY_DIVIDER_OPERATION's bit makes an attribute's element
vertex % frequency. At frequency 1 that is element 0 for every vertex; the
fetch read frequency 0 and 1 as an ordinary per-vertex array whatever the
bit. rsx_vertex_freq_plain() names the ordinary case (frequency 0, or 1 with
division); rsx_vertex_element_index, the compact fetch's shared span and the
legacy rsx_fetch_attrib use it.

29154bc66a6956228da34bcac3de4ea7fa4c2080.message:
ppu: test the SPU reserved-line bitmap inline on guest stores

Every guest store called spu_coh_is_reserved, and in God of War HD
gameplay that call was 9.5% of the main PPU thread's samples. Most of it
was not the call: spu_coh_reserve stored s_coh_armed = 1 and or-ed the
line's bit into the bitmap on every GETLLAR, the same values each time.
The SPURS kernel reserves the same few lines over and over, so those
cache lines kept moving to the SPU threads' cores, and each PPU store
missed on them.

- spu_coh_reserve writes the bit, and the published pointer, only when
  they change.
- spu_coh_bitmap.h publishes the bitmap as g_spu_coh_bits, NULL until
  the first reservation, and spu_coh_line_reserved tests it inline.
  VM_WRITE_COH in ppu_loader.cpp and ppu_memory.h, and
  vm_block_reserved, use it. s_coh_armed goes away.
- g_spu_coh_bits is one merged definition per program (selectany /
  weak), so the loader fixtures, which link ppu_loader.cpp without
  spu_coherency.c, still link and see no reserved lines.

2d4f931ab8b5f1b648b5045c5c9e0a3e16041a91.message:
Merge PR #572: halt and iret longjmp without unwinding on 64-bit Windows (@MaChInEgUn3)

Two conflicts, and the second one is the interesting one: #434 (earlier in
this wave) reached for a different tool for the same problem.

spu_drain.c, the iret frame's setjmp. #434 introduced SPU_SETJMP/SPU_LONGJMP,
which pick setjmp/longjmp or _setjmp/_longjmp per platform. #572 adds
spu_jmp_no_unwind(), which zeroes the jump buffer's Frame under _WIN64 +
_MSC_VER so longjmp restores registers directly instead of walking
RtlUnwindEx per host frame, and is a no-op everywhere else.

They are not alternatives. On MSVC setjmp already *is* _setjmp, so the macro
alone does not stop the unwinding -- the Frame store is what does. Both are
kept: the macro for the platform spelling, then #572's registration before
the call. #572's other call site (the halt env in spu_channels.c) merged
cleanly, so keeping this one means the two jump sites behave the same way,
which is what the PR is for.

spu_channels.c, the SPU_ARGWATCH probe: the getenv was already hoisted on the
branch, so #572's version of that hunk is the same change under a different
variable name. HEAD's code stays; #572's comment comes with it, because it
carries the measurement that justifies the hoist (~3% of a SPURS workload's
SPU time) and HEAD's did not.

3099075391d4105873242cd4c3f3555ed43fe397.message:
ppu_lifter: --insn-patches lifts patched instructions as run-time switches

A patch that changes an instruction word in .text does nothing to a
lifted title, which never executes the guest's code words. Making it a
second lift means a second build of the whole title for one changed
word, and a port that wants it optional ships two.

--insn-patches FILE takes {"patches": [{addr, orig, new, guard}, ...]}.
Each patched instruction is lifted in both forms and emitted as

    if (guard) { <new> } else { <orig> }  /* insn patch 0x...: orig -> new */

guard being an int the port defines and sets before the guest runs; each
function that uses a guard declares it extern "C". The original's branch
label and the code around it are unchanged. The lift stops when the
input does not hold orig at addr (a patch set for one build of a title
never lands on another), when a patch is at an address no lifted
function covers, or when new is a branch, sc or CR op (it would need
labels and call targets the function was not lifted with). The patches
reach the parallel workers too; a mismatch there raises instead of
exiting, so the pool does not hang on a dead worker.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) caps its campaign's frame rate in
code. The port lifts the cap's instructions this way and turns 60 fps on
or off from its settings, with one build.

New tools/test_ppu_lifter_insn_patches.py: a patched branch and a
patched li lift in both forms behind their guards, with the guard
declarations and the branch label in place; a wrong orig stops the lift
serially and with two workers; a patch at an address no function covers
stops it. docs/TOOLS.md describes the file with a generic example.

g_files[fd] directly, and #430 replaced that with one snapshot per handler

adds #456's direction tracking: g_fd_dir[i] = 0 on allocate and on close,

3b3fdfaa7b6ecaaee70d18b5948da69de5eefe59.message:
sys_timer: one host clock for mftb, system time and timers (mach_absolute_time on macOS)

On POSIX hosts the PPU timebase (every lifted mftb), the
sys_time_get_system_time HLE and the lv2 timers' expiration times each
called clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) and scaled it themselves. On macOS
that call is not a plain counter read: it goes through
_mach_boottime_usec and gettimeofday every time, and the mftb site is
hot in game loops that poll the time.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) reads the timebase in a loop on its
main thread; in a profile of the campaign that mftb site was about 14%
of the main thread's time.

host_monotonic_ns() is now the one source: mach_absolute_time scaled by
mach_timebase_info on macOS (split so the multiply cannot overflow),
clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) elsewhere. ppu_timebase_now,
sys_time_get_system_time and timer_now_us derive from it, so guest code
that mixes mftb, the system time and timer events reads one clock.
Windows is unchanged (QueryPerformanceCounter).

New tests/test_host_monotonic_clock.c (tools/test_host_monotonic_clock.py,
skipped on Windows): the clock is monotonic over a million reads, runs at
CLOCK_MONOTONIC's rate over a 200 ms sleep (to within 1 ms), and a
timebase or timer-clock reading falls between two host_monotonic_ns
readings. It prints the cost of a read: 11.6 ns against 18.7 ns for
clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) on an M-series Mac.

a condition variable and paid an OS wake-up for every publication (Buzz's
studio: ~50 JTS waits per frame on the geometry chain). SPURS_JTS_SPIN_US=n
polls the slot and the chain's published PC with atomic loads for up to n
us first; the caller re-reads the slot as before. Off by default, ignored
below 12 logical processors like SPURS_POOL_SPIN_US, which now counts
processors portably (sysconf off Windows).

main menu 30.68/30.38 -> 31.23/31.39 FPS (frames over 40 ms 19-20 % ->
14 %); solo round 36.49 -> 37.94 FPS, p90 32.1 -> 31.0 ms.

3e9311c6287b1220d57e99b3a2a7d3e45a1cf7db.message:
cellGcmSys: forget a park once the walker has left it

The walker gives a self-JUMP park GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS with the same put to
be patched, then resyncs to put. Its record of the park (address, put,
start time) was only cleared by that resync. A park the walker left any
other way -- the title patched it into a JUMP elsewhere, or wrote
commands over it -- kept its start time, so when the walker next stopped
at the same address with the same put, the new park was taken for the
old one. Its grace had run out long before, the resync fired at once,
and the commands the title was about to link in were dropped with the
fences and labels in them. A title that reuses its command blocks
meets its parks again at the same address, frame after frame.

Clear the record as soon as the walker reads anything other than that
park's own self-JUMP: a new park always starts a fresh grace. The three
variables move from the JUMP branch to file scope for that, under the
same names.

41bae9560bd0def7d49aa3675e89fa388e27f74e.message:
rsx_d3d12: stage guest textures in a shared upload ring; LRU slots

Each texture slot had its own committed upload buffer, created with the
texture whenever the slot took a new size or format. In God of War HD's
texture bursts, when new effects first appear, creating resources was
most of the cost: one report interval had 50 new textures, 67 ms of
CreateCommittedResource (41 ms of it for the upload buffers) against
18 ms of decoding.

- Uploads are staged in one persistently mapped upload buffer, 32 MB per
  frame in flight, reset where that frame index's command allocator is
  reset (its copies have finished by then). A texture that does not fit
  in what is left uses the slot's own upload buffer, created on demand.
- A new texture takes an empty slot, else the least recently used one.
  Taking the first slot not used this frame evicted textures the next
  frame needed again: up to 22 a report interval in those bursts.
- 192 slots instead of 96; the game used up to 66.
- A frame with no free slot returned slot -1 and indexed vp_tex with it;
  it now returns -1 to the caller (untextured), as the lookup failure
  path does.

God of War HD: the drain stalls of 67-75 ms in the bursts at 131 and
135-136 s are now under 40 ms. The rendering check passes.

45c634575e648b55b2da417f0a17fff1d65aaf92.message:
Merge PR #421: opt-in per-thread MFC engine lookup cache (@tekulvw)

Conflict with #243 (@Kurtisone, wave 2) at the top of mfc_for(). Both PRs
make the same function cheaper, from different ends, and both are kept.

#243's fix is the SPU_PCSAMPLE hoist: the old guard only latched `started`
when the variable was actually set, so with SPU_PCSAMPLE unset every MFC
channel access paid a getenv -- a tenth of the samples in a Twisted Metal
profile. It sets `checked` either way. #421 adds the generation-checked
per-thread cache in front, which returns before the claim lock on a hit.

#421 was written against master, so its hunk carries the pre-#243 `started`
form. Taking it as written would have reverted #243 while keeping its test
-- and #243 ships test_spu_mfc_env_once.c precisely to catch that, so this
one would have failed loudly rather than silently. Resolved anyway as
#421's cache check first, then #243's once-only latch, then the lock.

Composition is fine in that order: the first call misses the cache, falls
through and starts the sampler thread, and later calls that hit the cache
return before a getenv they no longer need to reach.

There is only one mfc_for() in the file -- the Win32 primitives it uses are
shimmed on POSIX by win32_compat.h -- so there is no second copy needing
the same resolution.

4609b3f0bf7db6fdf3a9c36a5037b0be230b8d7c.message:
spu: halt and iret longjmps without unwinding on 64-bit Windows

On 64-bit Windows longjmp unwinds every host frame between it and its
setjmp: RtlUnwindEx, with a function-table lookup and a virtual unwind per
frame. The SPU runtime longjmps on every halt back to spu_run_with_halt (a
SPURS policy module's run ends that way) and on every iret back to the
drain loop that took the interrupt.

spu_jmp_no_unwind() zeroes the jmp_buf's Frame right after setjmp returns
0, which makes longjmp restore the registers directly. These jumps only
cross C frames of the runtime and of lifted code, which have no destructors
or __finally blocks. SPU_LONGJMP_UNWIND=1 keeps the unwinding jump. No
change on other platforms.

498476267cb8405597ffecc6e9bde9dfed65cd92.message:
RSX vertex remap: direct table for a compact index range

rsx_vertex_remap_build hashed every reference of every rebuilt draw
(6.7 % of the Vulkan RSX thread in Buzz! Quiz World's studio). Indexed
draws reference one base_index and a narrow vertex range, so when the
range is at most 4x the reference count (+4096, and below 4M) a
generation-stamped table indexed by vertex_id replaces the hash. First-use
order, the unique prefix and the occurrence map are identical to the hash
path, which still handles everything else.

A randomized check against naive first-use deduplication (20000 cases,
both paths, up to 65536 references) passes. Vulkan menu EXE A/B: FIFO
drain 20.06/19.82 -> 19.30/19.08 ms, 36.0/36.5 -> 36.3/36.7 FPS.

vp_upload_tex_slot wrote an SRV for each uploaded texture at heap slot

window at DRAW_SRV_BASE. Since VP_TEX_SLOTS went to 96 they cover heap
slots 1..96, over the offscreen-RT SRVs and the windows of the first
draws of the frame, so a texture uploaded late in the pre-pass (a new
or animated one) replaced a descriptor an earlier draw had already

4f693f4e5756394bf3c337566fc0f860391ffc31.message:
rsx_d3d12: D3D12_VSYNC=0 allows tearing, or a window still waits for DWM

D3D12_VSYNC=0 presented with a sync interval of 0, but a windowed
flip-model swap chain is still composed by DWM at the display's rate
unless it allows tearing. God of War HD's main menu stayed at exactly 60
fps with the switch on.

With D3D12_VSYNC=0 the swap chain is now created with

once the first access has read their switches); otherwise the generic path

tools/host_window: say when the window is off screen, show the newest frame on return

macOS shows nothing of a window that is not on screen: another app or
Space in front (a full-screen window has a Space of its own, so bringing
any other app to the front hides it), minimized, or fully covered.
Presents go on and are dropped unseen, so the display rate reads 0 while
the guest's goes on, which in a log looks like a frozen picture.

In the Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) port, a full-screen run with
another app brought to the front reads exactly like that in its log:
display=0 while the guest rate goes on, as if the picture had frozen.

The window delegate now follows the occlusion state: leaving the screen
logs once ("window off screen ..."), coming back logs how long it was
away and presents at once, so the newest frame the game published
meanwhile goes up without waiting for the next one. [RSX FPS] lines end
in hidden=1 while the window is off screen.

New tools/host_window/test_host_window_offscreen.m (macos.yml), with a
bare CAMetalLayer and no window: on screen a frame goes up and the rate
line is plain; off screen is logged once and the rate line says
hidden=1; two frames published while away, and coming back logs the
time away and shows the newer of them; a repeated on-screen change says
nothing.
