33e3c759e06cebca48146e82414cd1d678a50359.message:
Online build: decrypt the 01.60 EBOOT without RPCS3; build_online.sh resumes

The 01.60 update's EBOOT.BIN is an NPDRM SELF with a free licence, so
tools/decrypt_self.py decrypts it with the NPDRM key and NP_klic_free /
NP_klic_key: tools/fetch_keys.py --npdrm takes them from RPCS3's
key_vault.cpp and key_vault.h at the pinned commit (each checked by its
SHA-256). The result has the SHA-256 tools/r2_layout.py knows for 01.60
(697bd1df...). RPCS3 stays the fallback.

With no step named, tools/build_online.sh now continues where it stopped,
as tools/install.sh does: download, extract and stage are skipped once the
update's files are staged (the extracted folders are then removed),
analyse, lift and spu when they finished with the same inputs (stamps in
out/install_v160/). It checks the free space, runs one at a time, and
ends a failure with an ERROR: line.

3a092867ec85a5452a8fbb84deccf2168c4843f4.message:
Continue Game: read the save back at boot

Saves were written at every checkpoint but never read back:
cellSaveDataUserListAutoLoad was not registered, and the generic fallback
that answered it ran only funcFixed, so GAME.SAV was never loaded, the
Campaign menu offered only New Game and Cinematics, and every session
started over. It now runs the whole fixed-load path, as UserListAutoSave
does (RES_SAVEDATA_LOAD, =0 restores the fallback): Continue Game, Load
Level and the last checkpoint come back.

README, ROADMAP (both languages): the fix and the switch.

3d34bfadaed707c022c9dff73fdc0fc96d229775.message:
Aim flash, area-load stalls, memory growth, audio clipping

- Toolkit patch:
  - Aiming: a CPU-path NV3089 half-size scene copy into memory that also
    holds a swizzled Z16 shadow map is remembered and wins over the zeta at
    that address, instead of the depth being stored over it and decoded as
    colour (PS3RECOMP_ENG_GUEST_OVER).
  - PS3_SHADER_ASYNC_SYNC_HIT defaults to 1: only pipelines whose functions
    are in memory build on the RSX thread; disk-cache hits still ran the
    Metal compile there, 20-60 ms each and up to 127 in a row, stalling for
    3 s and tripping the game's "GPU sit and spin timeout".
  - The frame-clock thread drains an autorelease pool every iteration
    (PS3_RSX_AUTORELEASE); each render target created there kept a texture
    descriptor alive, ~0.2 MB/s.
  - Metal shader function table of 65536 (PS3RECOMP_METAL_MAX_FUNCS).
  - Stereo output with a peak limiter (PS3_AUDIO_OUT_STEREO,
    PS3_AUDIO_LIMITER): the game was mixing 5.1 that was folded down past
    full scale. The volume gain runs before the limiter and clip.
  - NV3089 colour copies recorded on the GPU, growing destinations only
    these blits write (PS3RECOMP_ENG_BLIT_GPU_COLOR).
  - A cheaper SPU interpreter loop (PS3_SPU_INTERP_FAST).
  - Copy rects rounded edge by edge at non-integer scales
    (PS3RECOMP_METAL_COPY_EDGES); per-frame dumps for diagnosis
    (PS3RECOMP_METAL_FRAME_DUMP_ALL); more [tele] fields (drain, gpu, cpu,
    footprint, thermal).
  - Off by default while being tested: relocatable SPU lifts
    (PS3_RELOCMODS) and ports of ps3recomp #670, #693, #635, #666, #659.
- port/main.cpp: the audio defaults and the autorelease pool.
- tools/export_toolkit_patch.sh: never export *.orig/*.rej/*.bak or the
  port's lift_r2_* tools.
- README, ROADMAP (both languages): the fixes since 2026-10-31 and the
  thermal throttling left.

- Toolkit patch: the game exits by itself when its window closes or on
  SIGTERM (PS3_CLEAN_EXIT): SDL's own signal handlers, which only post an
  unread SDL_QUIT, are kept out, a save in progress is waited for, and the
  FIFO keeps draining after the window is gone (it used to spin on its fence
  and take a SIGKILL). PS3_EXIT_REQUEST_MS sends the game the system's
  exit-game request first. cellFs, cellGame and the trophy store use the
  HDD mounts (PS3_HDD0_ROOT/PS3_HDD1_ROOT) instead of a cwd-relative
  gamedata/ folder (PS3_CELLFS_HOST_ROOTS, PS3_TROPHY_HDD0). The Metal
  backend submits a full record stream and carries on instead of dropping
  every draw past 8192 records (PS3RECOMP_METAL_REC_FLUSH; the Moonpool
  area reached ~9300 draws a frame). Volume textures in texel coordinates
  divide z by the depth too (PS3RECOMP_FP_UNNORM_VOL_Z). Quieter SPU
  channel-block log.

MetalFX frame generation (PS3_FRAMEGEN=1), opt-in

One generated frame between every two the game renders, from the inFAMOUS 2
port's toolkit work, fitted to this fork: MTLFXFrameInterpolator (macOS 26,
weak-linked), motion vectors from the depth buffer and the camera, the HUD
put back untouched, a pacer that shows the real frame half an interval later.

Resistance 2's camera is taken from the vertex constants (c[8..11], the
frame's most common world view-projection, so shadow cascades and the
first-person weapon's own projection do not count); the depth is copied
where the scene is composited (fragment program 23c9cdc5b534e1c9) and
stretched to the display; depth under 0.2 (the weapon) moves with the camera.

Headless self-test, walking and turning in the first level: 34-41 dB against
24-28 for a 50/50 blend and 27-33 with zero motion, motion scale 1 best, a
static camera exactly zero motion, ~2 ms GPU per generated frame.
tools/framegen_score.py scores a PS3_FRAMEGEN_TEST dump.

allowed online too (the game keeps its 30 fps).

1438770078.readme_excerpt: # Resistance 2 — static recompilation for PC (macOS) 🌐 **English** · [Português (BR)](README.pt-BR.md) A native port of **Resistance 2** (PS3, disc `BCUS98120`) to **macOS/arm64**, built with static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C/C++ and compiled into a native executable, with graphics on Metal. It is not an emulator. **The campaign is playable.** It runs from the boot through the menus into the campaign: Iceland, then the Bay Area, at close to the game's own 30 fps on an Apple-silicon Mac (heavy fights still dip below it), with a controller or keyboard and mouse. Online play through the PS Rewired community servers works from the launcher with the game's 01.60 update (sign-in, lobby and a match were played on 2026-11-12). See [Status](#status). Built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), with the toolkit, the layout and the tools of the author's [Resistance: Fall of Man port](https://github.com/erikomis/resistance-recomp). See [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md). > [!WARNING] > **Work in progress.** The campaign has been played into the Bay Area, > not to the end, and some heavy scenes run below 30 fps. The launcher > ([releases](https://github.com/erikomis/resistance2-recomp/releases)) > builds the game on your Mac from your own disc; nothing is downloaded from > the game. Apple-silicon macOS only. > What is missing is in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). > **This repository contains no game data, no firmware, no Sony keys and > nothing translated from them.** Everyone generates all of that locally from > their own legitimate copy. A fan project, not affiliated with Sony > Interactive Entertainment or Insomniac Games. ## Status As of 2026-10-30: boot → intro movies → menus → New Game → the first level (`iceland`) played through by hand, with combat, dialogue and checkpoints, into the second level (`bay area`). Normal gameplay runs at **28–30 fps** (was 14.5 on 2026-10-29); heavy combat can still drop lower (see known issues). Sessions of 70+ minutes without a hang. Since 2026-10-29: - **Neon surfaces and a world that stopped drawing:** the Metal backend kept at most 4096 pipeline states, and Resistance 2 keeps creating them as a level goes on (4600+ in a 15-minute session). Once the table was full, every new pipeline failed and its draws were dropped for the rest of the session, which left flat neon colours and missing geometry minutes into a level, worse when aiming. The pipeline tables are now 65536 entries (`PS3RECOMP_METAL_MAX_PIPES`, `PS3RECOMP_ENG_MAX_PIPELINES`). - **Frame rate, 14.5 → ~28 fps:** the RSX thread was CPU-bound (~68 ms a frame; the GPU worked ~8 ms). Shadow maps and NV3089 depth downsamples stay on the GPU instead of being read back every frame (`PS3RECOMP_ENG_ZETA16_GPU`); attribute-major vertex fetch (upstream #458, `PS3RECOMP_ENG_FETCH_MANY`); a vertex cache that no longer starts over and hashes resident geometry sparsely (`PS3RECOMP_ENG_VCACHE_KEEP2`, `PS3RECOMP_ENG_VCACHE_SPARSE`); faster swizzled texture decode (upstream #578). - **Shader hitches:** 99% of a pipeline build was HLSL→MSL translation, so translations are cached on disk across sessions and builds (`PS3_SHADER_CACHE`), new pipelines build in the background, four at a time (`PS3_SHADER_ASYNC`, `PS3_SHADER_ASYNC_JOBS`), and one whose translation is already cached builds at once (`PS3_SHADER_ASYNC_SYNC_HIT`), which removes the brief flash when aiming. - **Saves:** the game saves every checkpoint through `cellSaveDataUserListAutoSave`, and the menu through `UserListSave` / `UserListLoad`; none was registered, so the unresolved-NID default returned OK without writing anything. They now run the game's callbacks, and saves go to the HDD folder the game lists them from. - **HDD install:** `cellGameDataCheckCreate2` reported the game-data folder as already installed, so the game never copied its caches and streamed dialogue to the HDD and every dialogue line failed to open. It now reports a new install until the files exist; the game copies ~354 MB on first boot (`PS3_GAMEDATA_ISNEW=0/1` forces it). - **Linear textures with mips** keep the base pitch on every level (`PS3RECOMP_TEX_LN_PITCH`); a recursion guard that halted an SPU job now unwinds and resumes it. - **Pause menu background and CPU-side copies:** the Metal backend never implemented writing guest bytes into a colour target, so an NV3089 copy the CPU path performs into memory the GPU holds as a surface was lost. At pause the game copies the scene into the depth buffer's memory and blurs it back every frame; the menu showed depth read as colour (neon blobs) or a flat cream background. Those writes now reach the GPU target (`PS3RECOMP_ENG_GUEST_WRITE`), and the GPU depth downsample is back on (`PS3RECOMP_ENG_BLIT_GPU`). - **Heavy combat:** SPU-built geometry lands at new addresses every frame and each piece is drawn about twice; the second draw now reuses the vertices decoded for the first (`PS3RECOMP_ENG_VCACHE_FRAMEREUSE`), which cut frames over 100 ms from 9 to 5 a minute in a probe. - **Shaders sampling a volume texture in texel coordinates** were cut to two components and failed to compile (2400 failures in one session's Moonpool area, every such draw dropped); they are scaled as volumes under `PS3RECOMP_FP_UNNORM_VOL=1` (on in `play.sh`, being confirmed in play). Since 2026-10-31: - **Continue Game and Load Level:** saves were written but never read back. `cellSaveDataUserListAutoLoad` was not registered, and the fallback that answered it ran only the first callback, so `GAME.SAV` was never loaded, the Campaign menu offered only New Game and Cinematics, and every session started over. It now runs the whole fixed-load path (`RES_SAVEDATA_LOAD`, `=0` restores the old fallback): the menu offers Continue Game, New Game, Load Level and Cinematics, and Continue lands at the last checkpoint. - **Aiming:** for a few frames after pressing aim, the sky and far background turned white with magenta and green noise bands. The aim transition copies the scene at half size through the CPU-path NV3089 into memory that also holds a swizzled Z16 shadow map; no surface had that pitch, so the texture bind took the shadow map as the newest content, stored the depth over the copy and decoded it as colour. A CPU copy over a target of another layout is now remembered and wins (`PS3RECOMP_ENG_GUEST_OVER`). In probes, 14 of 15 aims flashed before and 0 of 10 after. - **3-second stalls entering new areas** ("GPU sit and spin timeout"): pipelines whose MSL translation was on disk were built on the RSX thread, and their Metal compiles cost 20-60 ms each, up to 127 in a row. Only pipelines whose functions are already in memory build at once now (`PS3_SHADER_ASYNC_SYNC_HIT=1`). - **Memory growth:** the frame-clock thread never drained an autorelease pool, so every render target it created kept a texture descriptor alive (~0.2 MB/s, about 2 GB over 3 hours). Each iteration now runs in a pool (`PS3_RSX_AUTORELEASE`). - **Shader function table:** the Metal backend's 4096 compiled functions filled after about 3 hours, the same failure as the pipeline table; it is 65536 now (`PS3RECOMP_METAL_MAX_FUNCS`). - **Audio clipping:** the runtime offered 5.1, so the game mixed six channels that were then folded to stereo at up to 2.4x full scale. It is offered stereo now, as RPCS3 does, with a peak limiter for what still peaks (`PS3_AUDIO_OUT_STEREO`, `PS3_AUDIO_LIMITER`): 3568 clipped samples in a 365-second probe became 0. - **Scene copies on the GPU:** NV3089 colour copies are recorded on the GPU instead of read back (`PS3RECOMP_ENG_BLIT_GPU_COLOR`); readbacks dropped from 372 to 93 per 120 frames. - **SPU interpreter:** the dispatch loop no longer writes a shared global and looks up the lifted-code registry on every step (`PS3_SPU_INTERP_FAST`): its own overhead fell from 35-39% to 8-11% of the threads that run it. - **Ported from ps3recomp v0.19, off by default while being tested:** the per-source precision modifiers in fragment programs (#670, `PS3RECOMP_FP_SRC_PREC`), the depth clamp (#693, `PS3RECOMP_ENG_DEPTH_CLAMP`), DDX/DDY lowering (#635), the lock-line sleep (#666, `SPU_LOCKLINE_SLEEP`), `SPURS_IDLE_MAX` (#659). - **Green or wrong-coloured surfaces at the start of a level:** draws are skipped while their pipeline builds in the background. Every cached shader is now compiled once in the background as soon as the game opens (`PS3_SHADER_PREWARM`), so the system's shader cache has it, and pipelines whose translations are on disk build at once again, within a budget of compile time (`PS3_SHADER_SYNC_BUDGET_MS`, 8 ms per 100 ms) so a burst cannot stall the game. Loading the second level with a warm cache: draws skipped 117,000 → 2,000, same frame rate, no stall. - **Relocatable SPU lifts** (`tools/lift_r2_relocmods.py`, on; `PS3_RELOCMODS=0` turns them off): the 142 position-independent SPU modules the jobs load anywhere in local store were interpreted. Lifted, the interpreted steps fall by 80-95%. On a cool machine frame rate and CPU are unchanged at the 30 fps cap; the interpreter's load grows four-fold when the host is hot, which is where the lifts save the most. - **Second level (bay area): hitches, strange colours, water that seemed to follow the camera.** Post-process and water programs sample render targets in texel coordinates, and the scale (1/width, 1/height) was baked into the shader text; in the bay area those targets change size with the view, so every size was a new shader and a new pipeline (37,000 pipelines and 4,300 Metal functions in a 21-minute session, 254,000 draws skipped while their pipelines built). The scale now travels in the constant buffer (`PS3RECOMP_FP_UNNORM_UNIFORM`). Walking the flooded corridor for four minutes: functions 594 → 205, draws skipped 11,000 → 0, passes of 100 ms or more 6 → 1, seconds under 25 fps 42 → 0. What it took, with the cause of each: - **SPURS r4 layout:** the Wws_Job policy module takes the canonical r4 layout (word 1 = the job list). Putting the list in word 0 made it read the list as an audit buffer, write `FFFFFFFF` over it and exit without running a job: the "render db spu timeout in WaitTillReady" freeze ~90 s in. The port no longer sets `SPURS_PM_R4_WORD0`. - **`ESRCH` for exited threads:** the save system waits for its "Check Thread" to go away by polling `sys_ppu_thread_get_priority` until it gets `ESRCH`; the runtime answered OK for exited threads and "New Game" hung. - **Raw-SPU programs lifted:** the Bink decoder and the two programs the levels run every frame are raw SPU bytes (a `DEADDEAD` header, not ELFs) that `igInitRawSpu` streams into LS `0x200`. The image scanner never saw them and they ran in the interpreter (movies at ~3 fps). `tools/prepare_r2_rawspu.py` lifts all three; they register as resident code regions by source address. The Wws_Job policy module (also raw bytes) is lifted by `tools/prepare_r2_job_pm.py`. - **LFQueue lost wake-up:** an intermittent hang loading the level, between the PPU's push on a lock-free queue and the zlib task's `WAIT_SIGNAL`. The task now registers as parked before it re-checks the queue, with fences on both sides. - **Per-instance workload IDs:** the game runs two SPURS instances; the runtime numbered workloads with one global counter of 16, so the 17th ("triangulate") got no ID and the job API asserted. `cellSpurs.c`'s workload tables are now per instance. - **29 lifted job modules:** the WWS job modules (`0xC0DEC0DE` headers in the EBOOT, loaded at LS `0x4000`) are lifted by `tools/regen_r2_jobmods.sh` and registered by signature. - **Stale overlay retirement:** the job manager also loads bodies that are not among those 29 at `0x4000`; the runtime kept the previous module "resident" and ran its lifted code over the new bytes (garbage geometry in play). An overlay is now retired when its header in LS is overwritten (A/B switches: `SPU_OVL_SIG_OFF=1`, `SPU_OVL_SIG_ONLY=`). - **lwcond events on by default:** real `sys_lwcond` notifications (`PS3_LWCOND_EVENTS=1`, now the default in `port/main.cpp`) cut the pause after the Insomniac movie from ~5 s to ~1 s. - **The RSX FIFO race (5 s stalls, exploded geometry, neon colours):** the game links a side buffer whose JUMP back sits at `put`, and reuses that memory for vertex data right after moving `put` on. The emulated GPU woke every 1 ms and read the vertex data where the JUMP had been ("FIFO JUMP to unmapped IO", the game's 5-second "GPU sit and spin timeout", state lost in the resync). The frame clock now wakes every 50 µs (`port/main.cpp`; `PS3_FRAMECLOCK_US` still sets it), and the FIFO reader re-reads `put` every 8 words and after each JUMP/CALL/RET. A 440-second run: no bad jumps. - **Split / duplicated left half:** the scene renders into a 2560×704 (2×1 AA) target and the final pass reads 1280×704 of it with unnormalised coordinates, but the draw engine handed over the whole target. It now copies a sub-rectangle of the declared size on the GPU. With these fixes the light border around the play image is gone too. - **NV0039 memory-to-memory copies:** the copy engine is implemented on subchannel 1, where libgcm binds it; its methods used to land in the 3D engine as state. - **SPU PUT order:** SPU PUT, PUTLLC and PUTLLUC write their first 128 bytes last, so a reader polling a header never sees it before the payload (a port of upstream ps3recomp [#632](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/632)). - **Input at the first screen:** the front end's input dispatcher read port 0 as disabled before a local player existed, so X did nothing at the auto-save notice. A narrowly scoped hook in the lifted dispatcher (`tools/apply_r2_frontend_patch.py`, applied at configure time; switch: `RES_FRONTEND_PORT0=0`) keeps port 0's events flowing. It injects nothing. Known issues, being worked on: - **Heavy combat** can still drop below 30 fps: SPU-built geometry at new addresses every frame misses the vertex cache (same-frame reuse above halves the decode; more to do). - **Thermal throttling:** the game uses about 3.5 CPU cores at 30 fps; once macOS reports thermal pressure, frame rate can fall to 11-19 fps for tens of seconds. The relocatable SPU lifts above cut the interpreter's share of that load; their effect on a hot machine is not measured yet. - **Effects** to confirm in play after the fixes above: black squares where a steam/water effect should be, odd electric sparks, a water-like distortion that follows the camera in some places (Moonpool area). - The fog reads a little darker than on a PS3. ## How it works Same pipeline as the Resistance: Fall of Man port: 1. **Decrypt** your disc's `EBOOT.BIN` with RPCS3 into `game/BCUS98120/EBOOT.elf`. 2. **Analyse and lift** it with the toolkit's `ppu_loader.py` and `ppu_lifter.py`: about 41,500 PowerPC functions become C++ in `recompiled/BCUS98120/` (24 translation units). 3. **SPU code:** the SPU ELFs embedded in the EBOOT are found and lifted by the build (`PORT_SPU_INPUTS`). Resistance 2 also keeps SPU code as raw bytes, which no scanner finds: the Wws_Job policy module (EBOOT VA `0x00CF9680`, LS `0xA00`), the three raw-SPU programs (the Bink decoder at `0x00EB6580` and two level programs at `0x00E9B400` and `0x00EA2580`, LS `0x200`), the raw-SPU loader `igInitRawSpu` (`0x00ED2330`, LS `0x10`) and the 29 WWS job modules. The `tools/prepare_r2_*.py` scripts and `tools/regen_r2_jobmods.sh` cut each one out of your EBOOT, check its fingerprint against the tested executable and lift it. 4. **Build** with CMake/Ninja against the patched toolkit: the runtime (LV2 syscalls, HLE firmware libraries, SPURS, the Metal RSX backend, FFmpeg for video) plus the lifted code, into `build/BCUS98120/

1438789976.readme_excerpt:
# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível e à primeira luta contra um chefe, mas ainda lento (~18-23 fps no nível, 13-21 na luta). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot à primeira luta contra um chefe:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~50-55 fps; o primeiro nível a ~22-27 fps, conforme a cena (era ~9); a luta contra o chefe a 13-21. Atrasando um thread de cada vez e medindo quanto o quadro atrasa junto, o limite hoje é o thread que executa os comandos de vídeo (o RSX do RPCS3) e o thread principal do jogo, não as SPUs nem a placa de vídeo. Partes pesadas das SPUs já rodam como código nativo, cada uma conferida contra o original: a geometria por draw (índices, skinning, normais e tangentes) e o pós-processamento que suaviza as bordas da imagem. O foco agora é deixar o jogo mais leve para processadores comuns: o uso total de CPU já caiu ~10% (de 7,2 para 6,4 núcleos no menu) sem perder fps, e o próximo passo é a espera pelas consultas de oclusão (ZCULL) no thread do RSX. Esses números são de um Ryzen 5 5600G com uma RX 7600; num Ryzen 7 9800X3D com uma RX 9070 XT (RSX do RPCS3, Vulkan), o jogo chega a 60 fps fora das lutas e cai para cerca da metade nelas. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); e o jogo às vezes trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`). - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md).

## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), instale o launcher pelo `AscensionLauncher__x64-setup.exe` das [releases](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/releases) e, na primeira vez, aponte a pasta `ascension` em **Avançado › Pasta do jogo**. Ele se atualiza sozinho quando sai uma versão nova.

JOGAR abre o jogo; o launcher se esconde até ele fechar. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível e à primeira luta contra um chefe, mas ainda lento (~18-23 fps no nível, 13-21 na luta). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot à primeira luta contra um chefe:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~50-55 fps; o primeiro nível a ~22-27 fps, conforme a cena (era ~9); a luta contra o chefe a 13-21. Atrasando um thread de cada vez e medindo quanto o quadro atrasa junto, o limite hoje é o thread que executa os comandos de vídeo (o RSX do RPCS3) e o thread principal do jogo, não as SPUs nem a placa de vídeo. Partes pesadas das SPUs já rodam como código nativo, cada uma conferida contra o original: a geometria por draw (índices, skinning, normais e tangentes) e o pós-processamento que suaviza as bordas da imagem. O foco agora é deixar o jogo mais leve para processadores comuns: o uso total de CPU já caiu ~10% (de 7,2 para 6,4 núcleos no menu) sem perder fps, e o próximo passo é a espera pelas consultas de oclusão (ZCULL) no thread do RSX. Esses números são de um Ryzen 5 5600G com uma RX 7600; num Ryzen 7 9800X3D com uma RX 9070 XT (RSX do RPCS3, Vulkan), o jogo chega a 60 fps fora das lutas e cai para cerca da metade nelas. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); e o jogo às vezes trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`). - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md).

## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), instale o launcher pelo `AscensionLauncher__x64-setup.exe` das [releases](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/releases) e, na primeira vez, aponte a pasta `ascension` em **Avançado › Pasta do jogo**. Ele se atualiza sozinho quando sai uma versão nova.

JOGAR abre o jogo; o launcher se esconde até ele fechar. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

# Digger HD, recompiled for Mac, iPad and Apple TV

A native port of the PlayStation 3 game **Digger HD** (PSN, `NPEB00121`) made by
statically recompiling the game's own code with
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). The PowerPC and SPU code
of the original is translated to C++ and compiled for Apple silicon, so the
game plays as it does on the console; only the platform layer -- graphics
(Metal), audio, input, saves -- is new.

**This repository contains no part of the game.** You build it from the
package you own, on your own Mac.

![From your package to three builds](docs/images/pipeline.svg)

| | Mac | iPad / iPhone | Apple TV 4K |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plays | yes | yes | yes |
| Frame rate | display rate (any window size) | 60 | 60 |
| Input | controllers, keyboard | controllers, keyboard, touch | controllers, Siri Remote |
| Picture | MetalFX upscale to the window | MetalFX to the screen | 720p, scaled by the box |

## Build it from your own copy

You need:

- your own Digger HD package (`.pkg`, PSN release `NPEB00121`, version 01.00);
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net) with the PS3 firmware installed in it -- it
  decrypts the game, and the game's audio decoders come from that firmware;
- a Mac with Apple silicon, Xcode, CMake, Ninja and Python 3 with the packages
  in `vendor/ps3recomp/tools/requirements.txt` plus Pillow;
- for iPad and Apple TV: a paid Apple developer account, a provisioning profile
  whose App ID has the *Extended Virtual Addressing* capability (and, for iPad,
  *Increased Memory Limit*), and SDL2, glslang and SPIRV-Cross built for the
  device (see [Devices](#ipad-iphone-and-apple-tv)).

Then either open the builder app (`builder/`, build it with
`xcodegen generate && xcodebuild`), drop the package on it, tick the targets
and press **Build** -- or run the same pipeline from a terminal:

```bash
git clone <this repository> && cd <it>
git clone --branch v0.18.0 https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp vendor/ps3recomp
python tools/build_from_pkg.py "Digger HD.pkg" --mac --install-ios <UDID> --install-tvos <UDID>
```

`tools/build_from_pkg.py` unpacks the package, checks it is the tested release
(`EBOOT.elf` SHA-256 `90a74374149fe4ef...`), decrypts it with RPCS3, lifts the
PPU code and the SPU programs, applies `patches/` to ps3recomp, makes the icons
from the package's own art (or a cover image you pass), and builds
`work/out/Digger HD.app` plus the iPad and Apple TV apps, signing and installing
them. Machine-specific paths (Xcode, libraries, profiles, signing identity) can
go in an uncommitted `config.local.json`; see the top of the script.

## Legal

- No game data, no decrypted or recompiled game code, no console keys and no
  firmware are in this repository or its history. The pipeline reads them from
  the package and the RPCS3 installation on your own machine, and what it
  produces stays there; do not redistribute the builds.
- Decryption is done by RPCS3, a separate program; this project ships no
  decryption keys.
- Digger HD and its art are the property of their owners. PlayStation, PS3 and
  PSN are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This project is not
  affiliated with or endorsed by either.
- The code here is under the MIT licence (see `LICENSE`). ps3recomp, which it
  builds on, is MIT as well.

## How it works

ps3recomp lifts the game's `EBOOT.elf` -- 22,709 PowerPC functions -- into
C++, and the SPU programs it runs (the SPURS job-queue policy module, the
firmware MP3 decoder that the game's MultiStream audio loads at run time) into
C. Its runtime answers the console's system calls and libraries (GCM and the
RSX command stream, SPURS, cellAudio, cellPad, savedata) on the host. This port
adds the Apple platform layer and fixes found on the way; every change to
ps3recomp is a patch in `patches/`, described below.

### Getting an Apple TV to 60 fps

The Apple TV 4K's A15 started at 23 fps in a level. Measured on the device with
an on-device autoplay and an in-app profiler (Instruments could not reach the
box), the fixes were, in order:

![Apple TV frame rate, fix by fix](docs/images/appletv-fps.svg)

- **720-line drawable.** Drawing the TV's 3840x2160 ourselves -- MetalFX into
  it and a present pass over it -- cost the GPU about 13 times the work of the
  game's own passes. The box scales a 720p frame to the TV in its display
  hardware, as a TV scaled the PS3's.
- **Vblank from the display.** The frame clock ticked every whole 16 ms, which
  is 62.5 Hz; on a 60 Hz screen one frame in 25 was thrown away. A
  `CADisplayLink` drives it now.
- **SPU threads on the fast cores.** At default QoS the thread running the
  game's SPU tasks sat on an efficiency core at a third of the speed; it and
  the RSX and main threads now run at user-interactive QoS (only those).
- **Mailbox present.** The RSX thread waited for a drawable before it could
  drain the next frame's commands -- a third of every frame. It now copies the
  finished frame into one of three textures and moves on; a present thread
  shows the newest one, and the game is held at most one frame ahead of the
  screen.

Along the way: an idle SPURS policy module spinning a core at 100% now backs
off; DXT textures are decoded on upload for GPUs without BC sampling (the
A15); translated shaders and built pipelines are cached.

### Controls

Game controllers (Xbox, DualShock 4, DualSense, Switch Pro, DualShock 3) work
through SDL, mapped by button position. Without one, the keyboard drives port 0
while the game window is active:

| Key | PS3 button | In Digger HD |
|---|---|---|
| Arrows / WASD | D-pad | move |
| Space | cross | fire, confirm |
| Return / P | START | start, pause |
| Escape / Delete | circle | back |
| Q / E | square / triangle | menu options |
| Tab | SELECT | |
| 1 2 3 4 | L1 R1 L2 R2 | |

Cmd+Q quits. The window can be any shape or full screen (green button); the
picture keeps its proportions. At its own size the frame is shown texel for
texel; enlarged, it is scaled with Apple's MetalFX spatial upscaler
(`PS3_UPSCALE=off` falls back to a Mitchell bicubic). FXAA and CAS sharpening
are available but off (`PS3_AA=fxaa`, `PS3_SHARPEN=0.3`): at 1:1 they added
about 19% local contrast to the PS3's picture.

### Tests

`tools/playtest.py` plays the game unattended: it starts it silently with a
fresh save directory, presses through the title and menu with `PAD_SCRIPT`,
plays a level with random moves, and fails on a frame stall, a FIFO error, a
crash or a screen that does not arrive. Screens are recognised from the frames
the renderer dumps, against reference thumbnails in `tests/refs/` (cut from the
user's own game by `playtest.py --calibrate`; not committed). Each run writes
`tests/runs/<time>/` with the log, frames, a `report.json`, and on failure a
`sample` of every thread.

```bash
python tools/playtest.py --play-seconds 150 --seed 1
```

On a device, `PAD_AUTOPLAY=1` plays the same route on the device itself,
recognising the screens against `tools/make_autoplay_refs.py` output, in a fresh
save directory. `PS3_PERF_UDP=<ip>:<port>` sends frame-rate, per-thread CPU and
sleep lines over UDP, `PS3_PROFILE=<thread>|*` adds a sampling profile, and a
watchdog sends every thread's stack when presents stop.

### Patches to ps3recomp

`patches/` holds fixes applied on top of the pinned tag:

| Patch | Fix |
|---|---|
| `0001-hle-fast-path-fills-the-toc-slot.patch` | The HLE fast path (`sys_lwmutex_lock`/`unlock`) returned before the caller's TOC was written to `0x28(r1)`, so the caller reloaded `r2 = 0` and every global read went through a null base during static init. |
| `0002-spu-pipeline-accepts-staged-targets.patch` | The SPU pipeline rejected a program with a direct branch past its own image. The job-queue policy module calls code it stages above itself at `0x1620`; the lifter already emits an indirect-dispatch stub for it. |
| `0003-apple-input-window-present-and-ios-layer.patch` | The keyboard pad fallback existed only on Windows; the Metal event pump now records keys for the game window and `cellPad` maps them (Space is cross). `PAD_SCRIPT=<file>` drives port 0 from timed presses for unattended tests. The drawable follows the window's real pixels and the present pass fits the frame: wider windows get side bars; narrower ones lose up to 6.25% per side of the playfield's decorative border while the top band (HUD) is narrowed instead of cut, then black bars; MetalFX spatial upscaling when enlarged (Mitchell bicubic without it), exact texels at 1:1, sRGB colour space declared. On iOS the backend renders into a `CAMetalLayer` the app hands it (`rsx_metal_backend_set_ios_layer`) instead of running headless, the FPS log works there too, and the runtime links UIKit instead of AppKit. GPUs without BC sampling (the A15 of an Apple TV 4K) get DXT textures as RGBA8, decoded on upload. The layer is opaque with no background. `PS3RECOMP_METAL_FPS=1` also logs GPU time per second, mid-frame flushes and their waits, passes, draws, the largest target and the present buffers' GPU time. |
| `0004-gcm-flip-pacing-and-ring-callback.patch` | `cellGcmSetPrepareFlip` completed the flip at call time, so a title pacing itself on `cellGcmGetFlipStatus` never waited: Digger HD queued about 130 frames per presented one. It now queues the flip in the command buffer like `_cellGcmSetFlipCommand`. The buffer-full callback is rewritten after the SDK's: it flushes, writes the JUMP to `begin` and returns at once, and while the RSX still reads the previous lap it lowers `ctx->end` to the RSX's position instead of waiting for it to finish the lap. Waiting deadlocked with Digger HD, whose ring holds self-JUMP holes that only get filled once the title runs on; the old 2 s timeout then let the title overwrite unread commands. Wrap JUMPs are counted as laps the RSX owes, so the title is never allowed onto commands it has not read. |
| `0005-rsx-vp-arl-writes-dst-tmp-register.patch` | ARL loaded every address register named by `addr_reg_sel`, which only selects the register an indexed constant read uses; the register written is the temp destination field (RPCS3's GetDST). Digger HD loads its material colour indices into A1 and reads `c[128 + A1.x]`, so every enemy took slot 128's white. |
| `0006-rsx-linear-textures-pitch-every-mip.patch` | A linear (LN) texture keeps the pitch register's row spacing on every mip level and a linear compressed one honours it at all (RPCS3 `get_subresources_layout_impl`). The minified 1920x128 DXT1 sky strip read sheared levels and drew as horizontal bands. |
| `0007-audio-posix-mixer-paced-to-device.patch` | The macOS/Linux mixing thread mixed on a fixed 2-5 ms sleep, about 200 blocks/s against the PS3's 187.5, so SDL's queue grew without limit and the read index outran the guest's writes. It now paces to the device queue like the Windows thread, and gains its AUDIO_WAV / AUDIO_PEAK / AUDIO_RATE probes. |
| `0008-sysutil-bgm-status-sdk-values.patch` | The BGM playback constants were swapped (STOP 0, PLAY 1; the SDK and RPCS3 have PLAY 0, STOP 1), so the status query reported the user's XMB music as playing and Digger HD muted its own music. The status struct is also 0x20 bytes, not 0x28: the query overran the caller's buffer by eight. |
| `0009-spu-overlay-verified-by-signature.patch` | `spu_overlay_register_verified_sig`: a verified streamed overlay recognised by the first 16 bytes of the GET that loads it, for code copied to a buffer allocated at run time (the firmware MP3 decoder). |
| `0010-diag-spu-unpark-record.patch` | Diagnostic: with `GCM_RECDBG`, SPU stores over a self-JUMP park in the RSX ring are recorded and listed when a park stands for a second. |
| `0011-ios-mach-vm-region-declared.patch` | The iOS SDK refuses `<mach/mach_vm.h>`; `mach_vm_region` is declared by hand there (it is in libsystem_kernel on both). |
| `0012-tvos-no-sbrk.patch` | tvOS has no `sbrk`; the guest pointer trap's program-break check is skipped there. |
| `0013-spurs-idle-backoff-and-thread-names.patch` | An idle SPURS policy module (a job manager with an empty queue) calls `cellSpursModulePoll` in a tight loop and held a host core at 100%; after 32 polls with no data DMA in between it now sleeps 20-250 us. On the Apple TV this took the title screen from 33 to 41 fps at 4K. Threads made through `CreateThread` are named after their entry function on Apple hosts. |
| `0014-apple-tv-pacing-spu-qos-shader-cache.patch` | Apple hosts name runtime threads (`ps3_thread_name`) and run the threads that execute SPU code at user-interactive QoS (`ps3_thread_hot`; on an A15 an SPU job had sat on an efficiency core). `PS3RECOMP_METAL_FPS=1` also logs requested vs actual guest sleeps. An optional hand-off (`PS3_USLEEP_HANDOFF=1`) wakes the RSX thread from short guest sleeps; off by default. |

Apply with `git -C vendor/ps3recomp apply ../../patches/*.patch`.

### Status

Open issues:

- Two rare stalls not caught yet: one in a level on an Apple TV, one during
  start-up on an iPad. The watchdog and `PS3_STACKS_AT=<s>` are there to catch
  them.
- The intro movies flicker.
- `cellGame` boots the title as a disc game (`BLES00000`) instead of the
  installed PSN title `NPEB00121`, so saves are filed under the former.
- Unresolved imports: `_sys_spu_printf_initialize` (`0x45FE2FCE`),
  `cellSpursTaskAttributeSetExitCodeContainer` (`0xA121A224`).

### Running a development build

```bash
R=$PWD/run   # run/hdd0/game/NPEB00121 holds the unpacked, decrypted game
PS3_TITLE="Digger HD" PS3_HDD0_ROOT=$R/hdd0 PS3_HDD1_ROOT=$R/hdd1 \
PS3_DEV_FLASH=$R/dev_flash PS3_VFS_ROOT=$R/hdd0/game/NPEB00121 \
./build/DiggerHDRecomp $R/hdd0/game/NPEB00121/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf
```

## iPad, iPhone and Apple TV

`port/ios/ios_app.m` is the UIKit host: a full-screen view whose
`CAMetalLayer` the backend draws into, the game on a thread with the guest's
256 MB stack, game controllers through SDL, a hardware keyboard (same keys as
the Mac) and on-screen controls that hide while a controller or keyboard is
connected. Saves, the hdd1 cache and `log.txt` go to the app's Documents.

Needs SDL2, glslang and SPIRV-Cross built for iOS as static libraries
(SDL2 2.32.10, glslang 16.6.0, SPIRV-Cross vulkan-sdk-1.4.363.0, each with
`-DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=iOS -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64
-DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=17.0`, static only; glslang with
`-DENABLE_OPT=OFF`), and an App ID with the extended virtual addressing and
increased memory limit capabilities (the guest address space is a 4 GB
reservation).

```bash
I=<prefix of the iOS libraries>
PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR=$I/lib/pkgconfig cmake -S port -B build-ios -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=iOS -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=17.0 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_PACKAGE=BOTH -DCMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_LIBRARY=BOTH \
  -DCMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_INCLUDE=BOTH -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=$I \
  -DCMAKE_IGNORE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/homebrew -DSDL2_DIR=$I/lib/cmake/SDL2 \
  -Dglslang_DIR=$I/lib/cmake/glslang \
  -DPS3RECOMP_DIR=$PWD/vendor/ps3recomp -DRECOMP_DIR=$PWD/recompiled \
  -DPython3_EXECUTABLE=<venv python> \
  "-DPORT_SPU_INPUTS=$PWD/game/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf;$PWD/spu-inputs/jobqueue_pm.elf"
ninja -C build-ios
PROFILE=<profile> SIGN_ID=<identity sha1> \
  tools/ios_bundle.sh build-ios/DiggerHD.app <out dir> [device id]
```

Apple TV: the same with `-DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=tvOS` and the libraries built
for tvOS; `port/ios/Info-tvOS.plist` is used. There are no on-screen
controls (the Siri Remote is a controller, and the root view controller is a
`GCEventViewController` so Menu reaches the game), the writable files live in
Caches, and the saves are mirrored into the user defaults because tvOS may
empty Caches.

How the Apple TV reaches 60 fps is described [above](#getting-an-apple-tv-to-60-fps).

Translated shaders are cached (`PS3_SHADER_CACHE`); a cache made by
a Mac playtest (`run/shader-cache`) is bundled and compiled ahead at start,
and built pipelines go into a Metal binary archive beside it
(`pipelines.binarchive`), so a fresh install compiles them once. The apps
declare themselves games (Game Mode on iPad).

Icons come from the game's own art (`tools/make_icons.py`: a cover image when
one is given, else the package's ICON0 and PIC1; never committed): one
1024x1024 icon for iPad, a two-layer parallax icon and top shelf image

# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível e à primeira luta contra um chefe, mas ainda lento (~18-23 fps no nível, 13-21 na luta). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot à primeira luta contra um chefe:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~50-55 fps; o primeiro nível a ~22-27 fps, conforme a cena (era ~9); a luta contra o chefe a 13-21. Atrasando um thread de cada vez e medindo quanto o quadro atrasa junto, o limite hoje é o thread que executa os comandos de vídeo (o RSX do RPCS3) e o thread principal do jogo, não as SPUs nem a placa de vídeo. Partes pesadas das SPUs já rodam como código nativo, cada uma conferida contra o original: a geometria por draw (índices, skinning, normais e tangentes) e o pós-processamento que suaviza as bordas da imagem. O foco agora é deixar o jogo mais leve para processadores comuns: o uso total de CPU já caiu ~10% (de 7,2 para 6,4 núcleos no menu) sem perder fps, e o próximo passo é a espera pelas consultas de oclusão (ZCULL) no thread do RSX. Esses números são de um Ryzen 5 5600G com uma RX 7600; num Ryzen 7 9800X3D com uma RX 9070 XT (RSX do RPCS3, Vulkan), o jogo chega a 60 fps fora das lutas e cai para cerca da metade nelas. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); e o jogo às vezes trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`). - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md).

## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), instale o launcher pelo `AscensionLauncher__x64-setup.exe` das [releases](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/releases) e, na primeira vez, aponte a pasta `ascension` em **Avançado › Pasta do jogo**. Ele se atualiza sozinho quando sai uma versão nova.

JOGAR abre o jogo; o launcher se esconde até ele fechar. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

**720p~4K 지원. 30 FPS 제한을 유지하며 제한 해제는 수정 중으로 사용할 수 없습니다.**

**[런처 다운로드 / Download launcher / ランチャー](https://github.com/saintiron82/macross30-releases/releases/download/v0.3.9/Macross30-launcher-0.3.9.zip)**

게임 / Game **0.3.10** · 런처 / Launcher **0.3.9**

**[English installation and usage guide](README.en.md)** · [Release notes](https://github.com/saintiron82/macross30-releases/releases/tag/v0.3.11) · [Discord](https://discord.gg/WqaaJ6hTmY)

ZIP 압축 해제 → `Macross30Launcher.exe` 실행 → 플레이 언어 선택 → **플레이/업데이트** → 첫 설치 시 본인 정품에서 직접 덤프한 지원 일본판 ISO 선택.

암호화된 ISO는 해당 이미지에 맞는 복호화 키가 필요합니다. 런처의 **ISO 설정**에서 직접 준비한 `.dkey` 또는 `.key` 파일을 선택하세요.

한국어·영어·러시아어 v6-r2·스페인어 v3를 지원하며 일본어는 원본 데이터를 사용합니다. 러시아어·스페인어·영어 보정팩은 영어 기반팩을 함께 사용합니다. 번역·표시 검수는 계속 진행 중입니다. 모든 언어에서 실행·렌더링·진행 문제가 있을 수 있으며 제보를 받습니다. 런처가 사전 빌드 Windows 실행 파일과 선택한 언어팩을 설치합니다. 원본 EBOOT와 게임 데이터는 사용자 ISO에서 로컬로 준비합니다.

Windows 10/11 x64, D3D12 GPU, AVX2/SSE4.1 CPU가 필요합니다. 테스트 배포이며 원작과 다른 그래픽, 이벤트 미발생·오작동, 미션 진행 정지와 실행·조작·저장·오디오·번역 문제를 제보받습니다.

**본인 소유 정품에서 직접 덤프한 ISO만 사용하세요.** 비공식·비상업 팬 프로젝트이며 관련 권리자의 승인이나 제휴를 받은 프로젝트가 아닙니다. 원본 소유가 모든 복제·변경·배포를 자동 허용하는 것은 아닙니다. 관련 법과 이용 조건을 준수하세요. **권리자 요청이나 프로젝트 사정에 따라 사전 예고 없이 언제든 배포가 중단될 수 있습니다.**

## Source and attribution

The v0.3.9 tag preserves the frozen language-loader, launcher, installer and tooling source changes with hashes in release-baselines/0.3.9; retained renderer/link inputs remain identified by the 0.3.8 baseline. Precompiled game assets retain previously verified link inputs; this is not a claim of a fully self-hosted game build from this snapshot. Based on ps3recomp; its MIT license is retained at `vendor/ps3recomp-master/LICENSE`. Bundled third-party notices also apply. The English guide describes the current installation flow.


## 기존 런처 0.3.0 사용자

1. 런처 하단 **런처 업데이트**를 누르고 교체를 승인하세요.
2. 다시 열린 런처에서 기존 플레이 언어를 선택하고 **업데이트/플레이**를 눌러 게임 수정 파일도 적용하세요.
3. 자동 업데이트에 실패하면 최신 런처 ZIP을 받아 런처를 종료한 뒤 기존 런처 파일을 교체하세요.

기존 게임 설치 폴더와 저장 파일은 삭제하지 마세요. 원본 데이터 복구가 필요하면 기존에 사용하던 본인 소유 ISO를 지정하세요.


런처 0.3.2부터 실행 시 새 런처를 자동으로 다운로드·교체·재시작합니다. 게임 실행 중에는 런처를 유지하고 버튼에 실행 중으로 표시합니다. 기존 0.3.0/0.3.1은 런처 업데이트를 한 번 눌러 최신 버전으로 교체하세요. 게임은 0.3.10, 런처는 0.3.9, 한글·영어 기반팩은 0.3.8입니다. 러시아어 텍스트팩은 0.3.11(v6-r2), 영어·스페인어 텍스트팩은 0.3.10입니다.


게임 종료 후 런처의 **로그 → 마지막 플레이 로그 보내기**에서 내용을 확인하고 전송할 수 있습니다. 로그인 없이 운영진 전용 Discord 채널로 보내며 세이브는 선택 첨부입니다. ZIP은 로컬 bug-reports에 남습니다.

## ISO가 암호화되어 있다고 표시되는 경우

런처 0.3.7의 **ISO 설정**에서 ISO 식별 해시(SHA-1)를 확인하고 해당 이미지에 맞게 준비한 `.dkey` 또는 `.key` 파일을 선택하세요. 키 없음·파일 형식 오류·키 불일치를 구분해서 안내합니다. 키가 맞으면 원본을 보존하며 별도 ISO를 준비하므로 ISO 크기만큼의 추가 공간이 필요합니다. 이미 복호화된 ISO는 별도 디스크 키가 필요하지 않습니다.

## 0.3.9 업데이트 안내

인증서 오류(`CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED`)로 구버전 런처의 자동 업데이트가 막히면 위의 새 런처 ZIP을 직접 받아 교체하세요. 기존 설치 폴더와 세이브는 유지합니다. 실행 전 옵션은 다음 게임 실행부터 적용하며 실행 중에는 **게임 옵션 열기**를 사용합니다. HD는 기존 미리보기용 텍스처를 전투에서 사용하므로 기체별 색상 차이가 있을 수 있습니다.

## 0.3.10 시작 화면 핫픽스

0.3.9 이후 영어 등에서 검은 로딩 화면이 계속되면 기존 런처의 **플레이/업데이트**로 0.3.10을 받으세요. 긴 언어팩 경로가 잘려 설치 데이터를 인식하지 못하던 문제를 수정했습니다. 런처 0.3.9 표시는 정상입니다. 세이브와 설정은 유지합니다. 수정 소스와 해시는 `v0.3.10` 태그의 `release-baselines/0.3.10`에 보존합니다.

## 러시아어 v6-r2 표시 개선 (0.3.11)

러시아어 이용자는 기존 런처에서 **Русский → 플레이/업데이트**로 적용하세요. 격납고·파일럿 정보·옵션 문구 30곳을 줄였습니다. 게임/런처 재설치는 필요하지 않으며 폰트·자막·세이브는 유지합니다. 기존 영어 이미지와 잔존 일본어 값은 이번 변경에 포함하지 않습니다. 수정 규칙·도구·해시는 `v0.3.11` 태그와 `release-baselines/0.3.11`에 보존합니다.

103253636c9a94af96bf493694b178de0c0224f1.message:
Level scripts at the game's 30 updates a second (last level platform, triggers, smooth motion) (#56)

* Level scripts: OnUpdate 30 times per second of game time

The main loop (func_0021AB28) calls the level scripts' Lua OnUpdate once per
frame, and the scripts count in those calls. On the PS3 a frame is at least
one 1/30 s tick, so that was 30 a second; with the port's game clock at 60 or
144 Hz it ran 2 to 5 times as often. In 11.SDDockingBay the platform to the
main station moves 0.34 per call over 502.3 (about 49 s on the PS3): at
144 Hz it took about 12 s, the story events timed in seconds fell behind and
the section never ended.

A native func_00069A3C lets the two OnUpdate calls of the main loop through
once per 1/30 s of game time (script_rate.h); every other call is unchanged.
KZ_SCRIPT_EVERY_FRAME=1 restores the old behaviour, KZ_SCRIPT_LOG=1 logs the
rate. Host test: tools/tests/test_script_rate.sh.

* Level scripts: never drop script messages on a frame without OnUpdate

The main loop empties the script message queue (object +0xB4, ready
messages at +0x8/+0x10) right after OnUpdate, every frame (0x21AEC0 to
0x21BB98). With OnUpdate at 30 a second, area triggers, finished dialogue
and delayed messages that arrived on a frame without it were lost: in the
last level enemies did not come and a gate never opened.

A frame with messages waiting now calls OnUpdate even inside a 1/30 s step;
the call is taken from the following steps (at most 8 ahead, then
forgiven), so the rate stays 30 a second and no message is dropped. The
host test checks that no message is lost and the rate holds.

* Level scripts: slide objects the scripts move step by step

With OnUpdate at 30 a second, an object a script moves in OnUpdate jumped
once per 1/30 s and stood still in between. The 11.SDDockingBay platform
moved in visible jerks at 144 fps, and the 3D sound of the characters riding
it heard their speed swing 30 times a second: a Doppler warble that made
the voices sound robotic.

A native func_00069A3C-side hook of the obj

Patches 2053 to 2055: AMD black blocks, focus loss and the flip cap on Windows (#17, #18) (#35)

* Patch 2053: a barrier between the present's clear of the bars and the frame's blit

When the frame has bars, the window's present cleared the swapchain image
and blitted the frame into it with no barrier between the two transfer
writes, so the clear could land over the frame. The Khronos validation
layer's synchronization check reports it on an NVIDIA card in a 1280x800
window (SYNC-HAZARD-WRITE-AFTER-WRITE) and is clean with the patch. It fits
issue #17 on a Radeon 8060S: black blocks in every mode with bars, none in
fullscreen 1920x1080. The order is in rsx_present_steps.h, checked by the
new host test test_present_steps. Not yet confirmed on an AMD card.

* Patch 2054: a minimized window pauses the presents instead of going headless

A fullscreen window minimizes on Windows when it loses the focus; its
surface then has no area, and the present treated the failed swapchain
creation as fatal and dropped the window for good (issue #17's log: "window
has no drawable area", then "continuing headless"). The old swapchain is
kept and presents wait until the window has an area again. Not yet tried on
Windows.

* Patch 2055: PS3_GCM_MAX_QUEUED_FLIPS waits on Windows too

The cap's wait was 1000 rounds of Sleep(0) on Windows, over within
microseconds, so the cap held nothing: under FIFO the menus ran 430 to 650
flips ahead of the screen in the tester's logs (issue #18, Radeon 8060S)
and in the Windows build under Wine at 144 Hz. The wait is now bounded by
time (100 ms) with a real sleep, in gcm_flip_wait.h; the Windows build
under Wine stays at 0 to 2 ahead. test_gcm_flip_wait runs on Linux and in
tools/wine-host-tests.sh.

* docs/dev/patch-numbers.md: patches 2053 to 2055

* Patch 2054: also a window with no area at start waits for one

The window could also have no area when the swapchain was first made (once
under Wine in exclusive fullscreen), and that still dropped the window. The
first present that finds an area now

(ENHANCEMENT: the game only has 1280x720). mlaa_ref_cli and mlaa_vk_test

scale, or the PC page's default fill to a window of any other size, the

motion blur (Level 8 at scale 2: only 'GPU MLAA ... not run' in the log).

Patch 2080 runs the pass at the drawn size with the game's rules
(rsx_mlaa_size.h, per-workgroup scratch buffers instead of shared memory
sized for 1280-pixel lines), runs the glow and motion blur over the scaled
frame, and scales their 640x360 sources down instead of reading the

level load no longer sends the presses into another screen, and the script

perf: route rebase, interleaved A/B bench and PSGL verify harness (#53)

* Routes: KZ_ROUTE_REBASE writes a replay out as a route of this build

A route recorded by playing does not replay exactly: the game reacts to
resources that finish loading on other threads, which land on other frames
in the live recording than in a replay (docs/rotas.md of the private tree:
Level 7's facial animation load, then the blink timer's draws from the
random generator). Replays agree with each other, so a loose replay written
out as a route is one that later replays on the same build follow.

KZ_ROUTE_REBASE=<file> next to KZ_ROUTE_PLAY writes the frame clock values,
the pad reads as the game got them, the mouse and the position and random
generators where the replay compares them. The route file writer moves to
route_rebase.h and is shared with recording, so the two cannot drift; the
host test checks its lines against what load() reads.

Checked in the game (2026-11-09, headless, 144 Hz, loose, the recording's
kz1hd_pc.ini): the testkit Level 1 and 7 routes rebased, then replayed
twice each: 0 position differences, no random-generator difference and no
desync to the end (15305 and 14961 frames); before, 10340 and 8258 frames
off the recorded position.

* tools/perf/ab.sh: alternating A/B runs on a recorded route

Runs two builds (or one build with A_ENV/B_ENV) alternately on a route,
each run under a benchmark lock shared by every game run on the machine
(BENCH_LOCK), and reports per run the frame rate, 1 % and 0.1 % lows, p50
and p99, the main PPU thread's CPU time per frame (perf.cpp's window),
loadavg and the other busy processes, then the paired difference B - A
with a 95 % interval. route_play.sh is one headless replay; it refuses the
player's work/vfs.

docs/dev/perf-bench.md says why routes need their own kz1hd_pc.ini (the
mouse look is replayed through mouse_invert and the sensitivities) and a
rebase, and how to run and read an A/B.

A/A check (2026-11-09, the same binary both sides, 4 pairs, rebased
Level 7): fps -0.30 %

8506323ffe19c10b7bde9d428a2524c19b7ecbf2.message:
jm_post glow on the GPU, and the stencil it was missing (#63)

* Vulkan: a depth target read as A8R8G8B8 carries its stencil (patch 2076)

The renderer's depth-to-colour pack (rsx_vk_depth_pack.comp) wrote the
stencil byte of the Z24S8 word as 0. Killzone HD's glow source pass multiplies
its glow texture by that byte (.z of the depth target read as A8R8G8B8), and
its glow sprites write stencil 255 (ALWAYS, ref 255, REPLACE on depth pass),
so the glow source was black on both post paths. The D32S8 target's stencil
aspect is now copied after the depth floats and packed into the byte.

Host test test_depth_pack_stencil.py parses the pack's SPIR-V push-constant
block and checks the backend's copy, sizing and push; it fails on the tree
without the patch.

* jm_post glow on the GPU: C reference, glow source counter, GPU pass (patches 2077, 2078)

The glow chain (Modulate 1.0, Downsample, 7 blur pairs, Modulate 1.5, 4 blur
pairs, two Upsamples and a saturating add) decoded from the lifted SPU
modules: port/kz1hd/native/glow_ref.c equals the lifted code on every pixel,
stage by stage and over the whole chain (tools/mb_harness/check_glow.py).

Patch 2077 makes NV0039_STATS count the lit pixels of the glow source (IO
0x10000) and dump it when lit. Patch 2078 adds rsx_vk_glow.comp: after the
MLAA and before the motion blur, or over a temporal upscaler's output, with
size-0 indirect dispatches when the source has no colour or the strength is
0; strength in 1/256 through rsx_vulkan_set_glow_strength (256, the default,
is the game's, bit for bit), KZ_GLOW=<percent> for tests. jm.c turns it on
(PS3RECOMP_GLOW_GPU=0x10000) on the default path. regress_glow.sh checks GPU
= C at strengths 256, 128 and 0; check_dump.sh checks frames dumped in the
game. Host test test_glow_ref.sh. Notes in docs/dev/wws-jm-post.md, "The
glow".

* Docs: where the game draws its glow, and the GPU glow checked in the game

Aspect ratios: 4:3 and 16:10 fill the window, a forced aspect setting (#61)

* Windows: per-monitor DPI awareness, real pixels at display scaling above 100 %

Without it Windows gave the program a scaled desktop (1920x1200 at 150 % became
a 1280x800 swapchain, stretched; issue #18). main sets SDL2's
SDL_WINDOWS_DPI_AWARENESS=permonitorv2 before the window opens unless the
environment already has a value (win_dpi.h). Host test on Linux and a Wine
test that checks the process is per-monitor v2 aware once SDL's video starts.

* Patch 2068: fill for frames taller than 16:9, and a forced display aspect

PS3RECOMP_VK_SCALE_FIT=fill widened only: a 4:3 or 16:10 window got the
fitted 16:9 frame with bars. Fill now scales both axes either way.
PS3RECOMP_VK_ASPECT=W:H renders and shows the picture in the largest box
of that aspect in the window, with bars. Host test for the arithmetic
(rsx_fit_scale.h).

* HUD below 16:9: the 2D layer narrows, the HUD's sides at the window's edges

On a window narrower than 16:9 (4:3, 16:10) the 2D layer's ortho narrows
around the middle as it widens on an ultrawide one, so the 1280x720 layout
keeps its shape, and the HUD's sides go to the window's edges whatever the
HUD position (the game's own 4:3 mode does not move its HUD: the HUD module
never reads the aspect setting). Math in hud_layout.h, with a host test.

* Windows narrower than 16:9: the game's own 4:3 FOV rule, and an aspect setting

Below 16:9 the cameras now take the window's aspect too (before: 16:9 with
bars). The world's cameras follow the game's own 4:3 mode (func_00211540:
vertical FOV = 100 / aspect, 75 vertical and 91.3 horizontal at 4:3; the
weapon's FOV comes from the same aspect), so 16:9 and wider are unchanged;
FOV_NARROW_HOR=1 keeps the 16:9 vertical FOV instead (fov.h, fov_narrow).
New setting aspect = auto | 4:3 | 16:10 | 16:9 | 21:9 | 32:9 (PC menu row
"Aspect Ratio (on restart)", PS3RECOMP_VK_ASPECT, patch 2068). Host tests
for the FOV rule and the setting.

9ade5b3895b39a0e3db4729e81cda4798b982b41.message:
perf: sleeping frame clock, SPURS without idle probes, reservation fix (#758) (#58)

* tools/perf: whole-process CPU per frame, by thread group

route_play.sh samples every thread's CPU time once a second during the
replay; ab_report.py prints the CPU ms per frame of all threads and of the
main PPU thread, the RSX thread, SPURS/SPU and the rest, and the paired
difference of the whole process. For changes that aim at lower CPU use,
not only frame rate.

* Frame clock: sleep until the next tick instead of spinning (KZ_FRAME_WAIT_SPIN=1 restores)

The game's main loop starts each frame in func_0021C0F8, which reads the
millisecond timer in a loop until a whole tick has passed. At the default
60 Hz clock and 60 fps limit that loop was 66.6 % of the main thread's CPU
time (KZ_PROF_STACK, Level 7, the player standing still) and the main
thread ~99 % busy. The native wrapper now sleeps, in steps of at most 1 ms,
while more than 2 ms are left until the next tick (frame_wait.h: the
deadline from the clock's last tick and the tick factor at 0x21C0F0; the
game/host time rate learned for PS3_TIMEBASE_SCALE); the lifted loop then
spins the rest and takes the tick exactly as before. Replays are unchanged
(they take the recorded ticks without waiting). Host test test_frame_wait:
no sleep reaches the next tick at 30, 60 and 144 Hz with game time at 1x to
3x host time.

Checked (2026-11-10, headless, the player standing still 30 s, 3
alternating pairs per level, the same executable): main thread at 60 Hz
98.6 -> 43.7 % (Level 7), 99.0 -> 49.0 % (Level 1); whole process 148.6 ->
92.2 % and 160.7 -> 110.0 % of a core; other threads unchanged. Presents at
60 Hz unchanged (60.0 fps, p50 13.95 ms, p99 20.95 ms, max 20.98 ms both
ways); at 144 Hz 143.9 fps both ways in Level 7. Rebased Level 1 and 7
replays: 0 position differences.

* tools/perf/ab_report.py: whole-process CPU up to the last full sample

The last per-second sample can catch the process exiting with only the main
thread left, which dropped the other threads from a run's

Draw engine: a converted-vertex cache (ps3recomp patches 2062, 2063) (#52)

* Draw engine: a converted-vertex cache (ps3recomp patches 2062, 2063)

Patch 2062 is the engine side of ps3recomp pull request #718 by n0madic (MIT):
a draw whose index bytes, layout, attribute state and vertex bytes hash the
same as a stored one draws that stored copy instead of fetching, converting
and staging its vertices again. Added here: PS3RECOMP_ENG_VCACHE_VERIFY=1,
which converts every hit anyway and checks the copy byte for byte, and
tools/test_rsx_vertex_cache.py, which runs the cache's C tests in the
upstream suite. Patch 2063 is the Vulkan half, ours: chunks as coherent
host-visible vertex and index buffers, a cached draw that binds them, and a
submission serial so a block is rewritten only after the GPU is done with it.
PS3RECOMP_ENG_VCACHE=0 turns it off.

Patch 1020: an unreserved SPU PUT checks for reservations again after its copy

The DMA fast path (patch 1010) copied a PUT whose span had no reserved line and
stopped there, so a GETLLAR landing during the copy kept a valid reservation
with a stale snapshot and no SPU_EVENT_LR until the 10 ms poll. The patch adds
the full path's check after the copy and a fence on both sides of the race (the
full path missed without it, now that patch 0002 drops marks).
tools/tests/test_spu_put_recheck.sh races the two for 200000 rounds: 89864
stale reservations on the fast path and 158 on the full path before, 0 after.
