1439286882.readme_excerpt: # Project Vekta (work in progress) **Killzone HD: unofficial PC port (static recompilation)** ![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue) ![Status: playable, testing](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-playable%2C%20testing-orange) ![Linux x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Linux%20x64-333) ![Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20x64%20(cross--built)-0078D6) ![Vulkan](https://img.shields.io/badge/graphics-Vulkan-A41E22) **[Status](#status)** · **[Features](docs/FEATURES.md)** · **[Screenshots](docs/SCREENSHOTS.md)** · **[Requirements](docs/requirements.md)** · **[Getting your files](docs/GETTING-FILES.md)** · **[Building](docs/BUILDING.md)** · **[How it works](docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md)** · **[Known issues](docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md)** · **[Roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md)** · **[Glossary](docs/GLOSSARY.md)** · **[AI use](#how-ai-was-used)** · **[Contributing](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)** · **[Forking](docs/FORKING.md)** *Vekta* is the ISA colony world where the first Killzone is fought. Project Vekta is a fan project, not official and not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Guerrilla Games. **What this is:** a static recompilation of **Killzone HD**, the PS3 remaster of the first Killzone (title NPUA80856, the package on the Killzone Trilogy disc). The game's PowerPC (PPU) and Cell SPU code is translated to C++ ahead of time with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) (pinned at v0.19.0, plus this project's patches in `port/patches/`) and compiled into a native Linux or Windows x64 program. It is **not an emulator** (no CPU emulator runs at play time) and **not a rewrite** (the game's logic is the game's own code). Around that code, the PS3's system libraries and hardware behaviour are reimplemented on PC APIs, and the game's graphics commands are replayed on Vulkan. **You need your own copy of the game.** This repository contains only the port: source code, patches to the recompiler, tools and documentation. It contains no game code, data, assets, keys or firmware, and it never will. Each player translates and builds the game's code on their own machine, from their own files. ## Status As of 2026-10-30, on Linux x64 with an NVIDIA RTX 3070 Ti, the maintainer's machine: | | | |---|---| | Code translation | the whole EBOOT is translated (about 23,400 PPU functions) plus the SPU programs, job modules and the firmware pieces the game loads; this repository's scripts rebuild it byte for byte from the player's files | | Boot, menus, movies | work: intro movies, front end, options, pause menu, saves and Continue | | Campaign | Level 1 played by hand from start to end; all 11 levels load and reach gameplay; parts of the campaign played by hand on 2026-10-20; levels 2 to 11 not yet each played to their end | | Frame rate | a steady 60 frames per second by default (the game logic runs at 60 Hz instead of the PS3's 30); an optional 144 Hz mode reaches about 131 to 134 frames per second in Level 1 and Level 7 | | Sound | stereo, 5.1 and 7.1 output (the game's own mixer fills the extra channels); music through the firmware's MP3 decoder | | Windows | the Windows exe is cross-built on Linux and runs under Wine, Proton and on a real Windows; the full campaign on Windows is not checked yet, and speed under Wine and Proton is lower (about 100 frames per second in Level 7) | | Distribution | you build the port from your own files: on Windows the setup program or folder builds it on your PC (since 0.2.0); on Linux from source, or (since 0.3.0) a Linux folder with its own toolchain (no compiler or packages needed) | What works and what does not, item by item: [docs/FEATURES.md](docs/FEATURES.md). Open problems: [docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md](docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md). ## PC features All optional, set in a **PC** page inside the game's own Options and Pause menus and kept in `kz1hd_pc.ini`: - display mode (window, borderless, fullscreen), output resolution, internal resolution scale, V-Sync (on, off, adaptive), VRR, frame-rate limit (30, 60, 144), NVIDIA Reflex - AMD FSR 1 upscaling and RCAS sharpening, anisotropic filtering (the game's own or 2x to 16x) - temporal upscaling on Linux and Windows: AMD FSR 3.1 in every build, and NVIDIA DLSS (Super Resolution and DLAA) when you choose to download it at install ([docs/dev/upscalers.md](docs/dev/upscalers.md)) - any aspect ratio (Hor+ for 21:9, 32:9 and wider, the game's own 4:3 view for 4:3 and 16:10, a forced ratio if you want one, with the menus and movies kept 16:9), field of view for the world and, apart, the first-person weapon (70 to 120 degrees at 16:9), HUD size and position - presets: Original (PS3), Performance, Balanced, Quality - keyboard and mouse (direct mouse look, mouse in menus, remappable keys), Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo and generic controllers through SDL, with button prompts that follow the device in use - stereo, 5.1 or 7.1 sound; game language; skip the opening movie; local trophies from the game's own trophy set ## What goes online Nothing, unless you choose it. The port and its scripts make no network connection of their own. The downloads are the ones you start: cloning this repository with its ps3recomp submodule, your system's packages, the build tools' Python packages, and these, only when you choose them: - **NVIDIA DLSS**: only if you accept NVIDIA's DLSS SDK licence when `tools/install.sh` or `run.cmd` asks, or tick the Windows setup's DLSS box (unticked by default), or pass `--dlss accept`, the build downloads the DLSS SDK's files from NVIDIA's repository on GitHub (`raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/DLSS`, pinned to v310.9.16 and checked by SHA-256) into `work/toolchain-cache/dlss-sdk/`. The question first downloads the licence's text from there, for you to read. Declined, nothing is downloaded and the build has no DLSS. ## Where your data goes Everything stays in the folder the game runs from, `work/vfs/` (made by `tools/setup-vfs.sh`): the PC settings in `kz1hd_pc.ini`, the key map in `kz1hd_keys.ini`, saves under `gamedata/dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata/`, and the local trophy log in `gamedata/trophies/`. The log of a run goes to `work/play.log`. Nothing is written outside the repository's `work/` folder, and nothing is written into your game files. The Windows setup program is the one exception: unless you pick its "Portable" option, the settings and saves go to `%APPDATA%\Project Vekta` instead. ## Getting it Latest release: [v0.4.0](https://github.com/gustavomorinaga/project-vekta/releases/tag/v0.4.0), a pre-release. Each release carries the Windows setup program and the same folder as a zip, a Linux folder with its own toolchain, and a source archive (this tree with ps3recomp at its pinned commit), each checked by SHA-256; either way the port is built on your machine from your own game ([docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md)). You need: - the Killzone HD package from your own **Killzone Trilogy** disc, installed, plus its decrypted EBOOT and data archive, and the decrypted `libsre` from your own PS3 firmware: what each must be, and how the scripts check them, is in [docs/GETTING-FILES.md](docs/GETTING-FILES.md); - Linux x64 with clang, CMake, Ninja, Python 3, SDL2, zlib, glslang and the Vulkan headers; for the Windows exe, the MinGW-w64 sysroot as well; - a CPU with AVX2 (x86-64-v3) and a Vulkan GPU ([docs/requirements.md](docs/requirements.md)). The short way, from a release's archive or a clone: one command asks where your files are, checks them, and builds with one progress bar; it remembers the paths, so afterwards `tools/play.sh` is all you need. ```sh tools/install.sh tools/play.sh ``` Step by step (what `tools/install.sh` runs): ```sh git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/gustavomorinaga/project-vekta cd project-vekta tools/ps3recomp-patched.sh # ps3recomp v0.19.0 with port/patches applied, in work/ tools/lift.sh # translates your EBOOT, SPU code and firmware pieces, in work/lift tools/setup-vfs.sh # the folder the game runs from, in work/vfs tools/build.sh # work/build/KZ1HD tools/play.sh # plays in a window ``` ## How it works, briefly - **PPU:** the game's PowerPC functions are lifted to C++ by ps3recomp's lifter and compiled with clang; a few hot functions are reimplemented natively (`port/kz1hd/native_ppu/`). - **SPU:** the SPU programs and the WWS job modules are lifted the same way; SPURS runs on host threads; some SPU jobs run as native C (`port/kz1hd/native/`). - **Graphics:** the game's RSX command stream is replayed on Vulkan, with PC options (scaling, FSR 1, widescreen) applied around it. - **Data:** the game reads its own archive through its own file system code; movies are decoded with FFmpeg. More: [docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md](docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md). General fixes are offered to ps3recomp upstream. ## How AI was used This project is developed by one person with AI coding agents (Claude Code). The agents did most of the work of reading the game's binary and reference material, writing and testing patches, tools and documentation, and running the builds, with the maintainer setting the goals, playing and checking the game, reviewing what they produced and deciding what is published. Findings are dated; an `ASSUMPTION:` in the code or the docs is not fact. If you find a statement here that was not verified, please open an issue. ## Related projects - [Project Helghast](https://github.com/undecuple/project-helghast) (Killzone 3) and [Project Pyrrhus](https://github.com/undecuple/project-pyrrhus) (Killzone 2), by undecuple: the same approach for the rest of the trilogy, and the model for this repository's layout. Credits: [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md). - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), the recompiler this port is built on. ## Official channels Project Vekta is made by **Gustavo Morinaga**: GitHub [@gustavomorinaga](https://github.com/gustavomorinaga), and the project site . Code and, when there are any, builds come only from this repository. We never ask anyone to paste a command they were sent into a terminal or PowerShell. Anyone else offering builds, "fixes" or donations in this project's name is not us. ## Contributing Tests on other hardware, reports with logs, and fixes are welcome: [CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). The rules for everyone, people and AI coding agents alike, are in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Security problems and rights holders' reports go privately through the Security tab ([SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md)). ## Repository layout | Path | What it holds | |---|---| | `port/kz1hd/` | the program: boot, game clock, window, HLE overrides, the PC menu, native SPU and PPU code | | `port/patches/` | numbered patches to ps3recomp and `series`, the order they apply in | | `third_party/ps3recomp/` | the recompiler, a pinned submodule (never edited in place) | | `tools/` | patch, lift, build, run and check scripts; data and profiling tools | | `re/` | tables the tools read; numbers only | | `docs/` | the public documentation; `docs/dev/` holds engineering notes | | `site/`, `assets/` | the project page and its images | ## Licence The port is MIT ([LICENSE](LICENSE)): that licence covers the port only, its code, patches, tools and documentation. Third-party parts and credits are in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md). Killzone and Killzone HD are (c) Sony Interactive Entertainment; nothing of the game is licensed or included here.

023877b7e07f4e5b159f6c5fe2ff35a809474e26.message:
port: under 16 logical CPUs the main thread's busy waits sleep 1 ms every 256 turns

The main thread waits on the WWS job lists in busy loops (func_00445048/
00445320/00445720, PAUSE). On a 6-core/12-thread i5-11400F that spin shared a
core with the EDGE SPU threads that limit the frame. With fewer than 16
logical CPUs the default is now GOWA_PPU_PAUSE=3 (1 ms sleep every 256 turns
in the same wait); 16+ keep the plain spin. A/B inside one run (GOWA_PRIO_AB,
chapter 16, 25 s phases): i5-11400F against the plain spin +2.6% and +0.3%
(13 of 18 pairs up), against yielding (mode 2) +2.0%, process CPU per frame
-7%; i5-10300H against mode 2: same FPS, CPU -2%. New A/B mode Y (3 x 1).

0348189deb3670e2a009b57c5d8b1e142dbf5707.message:
FP: modificadores de precisão do RSX e DP3 em cadeia (mãos amarelas, brilho estourado)

O decompilador ignorava a precisão do RSX: a do destino (OPDEST bits 22-23: fp16, fixo12 [-2, 2],
fixo9 [-1, 1]) e o modificador de cada fonte (SRC1 bits 19-27; saturado [0, 1] antes do abs, os
outros depois do abs e antes do neg). Em ponto fixo não existe NaN -- o hardware dá 0 --, então um
NaN nascido num termo de luz (o especular do metal das manoplas do Kratos) morre ali e a cor sai
certa; aqui ele chegava à saída, onde a guarda de NaN zerava aquele canal (azul -> amarelo). Regras
como no hardware (as do RPCS3, testadas em console): COL0/COL1/SSA e temporário fp16 lido como fp16
ficam sem; o destino não limita NRM/MIN/MAX/COS/SIN/RFL/FRC/LIT/LIF/LG2, um MOV fp16 de temporário
fp16 nem fp16 num registrador de 32 bits. GOWA_FP_PREC=0 desliga.

DP3 em precisão total como x*x' + (y*y' + z*z') com mad, a ordem do RSX (RPCS3 PR #19293: a cor
do céu do GoW3/Ascension na torre de Delfos). GOWA_FP_DP3=0 volta ao dot().

Henry (RX 9060 XT): fase 1 com imagem igual, fps igual (40,3-41), 0 pso-fail; 228 shaders de pixel
da fase 1 usam os modificadores. Falta a NVIDIA (o amarelo só aparece nela): A/B do usuário.

every 200 ms, only for a start less than 64 KB behind; GOWA_PARK_REWIND=0
turns it off. Holds with the bad word at the walker also print the jump
history (and the SPU PUT ring with GOWA_PUTRING).

# God of War: Ascension — Native PC Port (PS3 Static Recompilation) + Launcher

**God of War Ascension running natively on Windows PC, with no emulator.** By **Musthaq Ahamed S** ([@musthaq-ai](https://github.com/musthaq-ai)).

The PS3 game's code is statically recompiled to x86-64 C/C++ and rendered with Direct3D 12. This project packages it with a one-click **PC launcher** (720p, 60 FPS, max-performance mode, frame generation, Fast AA) and a **portable package** tool, so you can build once and play on any Windows PC.

> **Fan project, non-commercial, not affiliated with Sony.** *God of War* is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment. **This repository contains no game files, no game code and no PS3 firmware.** You need **your own copy** of God of War: Ascension (**BCUS98232**, USA). Your PC builds the game part from your copy.

![Chapter 16](docs/imagens/cap16_9800x3d.png)

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Level 1](docs/imagens/fase1_dodge.png) | ![Level 1, the Fury](docs/imagens/fase1_furia.png) |

## Features

- **Native PC executable** (static recompilation of the PS3 PPU and SPU code, built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp)); RSX graphics on **Direct3D 12**.
- **Launcher** (`GoW Ascension.cmd`):
  - 720p internal resolution (1440p option for dedicated GPUs), 60 FPS cap
  - **Max performance while playing**: Windows "Best performance" power mode + high process priority, restored when the game closes
  - Runs on the **high-performance GPU** on dual-GPU (NVIDIA Optimus) laptops
  - **Frame generation** (about 2x shown frames on 120/144 Hz screens)
  - **Fast AA** option (skips the PS3 SPU MLAA pass for more FPS)
  - Fullscreen, VSync / VRR, performance overlay (F10), sound toggle
  - Smart **thread pinning**: off on Intel hybrid P+E CPUs
  - Warnings for low free RAM (8 GB laptops), other apps using the NVIDIA card's VRAM, and running on battery
  - After you quit: average FPS, 1% low and peak RAM
- **Portable copy** (`MAKE-PORTABLE.cmd`): copies the built game to a folder or drive (with live progress) so it runs on another PC without building there. It bundles the Visual C++ runtime.

## Requirements

- Windows 10/11 64-bit, a CPU with **AVX2** (Intel 4th gen+, AMD Ryzen), a **DirectX 12** GPU
- Your copy of **God of War: Ascension BCUS98232** (a folder containing `PS3_GAME`), about 35 GB
- To build (once): [Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/) and **Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools** (C++). Clang comes either from the VS "C++ Clang tools" or from a standalone [LLVM](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/releases); this fork accepts either.

```
winget install Python.Python.3.12
winget install Microsoft.VisualStudio.2022.BuildTools --override "--quiet --wait --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Workload.VCTools --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Llvm.Clang --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.CMake.Project --includeRecommended"
```

## How to play

1. **Download** this repository (Code → Download ZIP, or `git clone`). Put it in a folder **without spaces** in the path, e.g. `C:\gowa`.
2. **Build:** double-click **`BUILD.cmd`** and choose your game folder (the one with `PS3_GAME`). The script then:
   - downloads the free official **update 1.04** and the **PS3 firmware** from Sony's servers (or use your own: `-Update`, `-Firmware`)
   - decrypts the executable, translates the game code and compiles it

   It takes about 5–15 minutes. If it stops, run it again and it resumes.
3. **Play:** double-click **`GoW Ascension.cmd`**, then press **PLAY**. Click "Desktop shortcut" in the launcher if you want one.

### Another PC (e.g. a gaming laptop)

Run **`MAKE-PORTABLE.cmd`** and choose a folder or drive. It must be **exFAT or NTFS**, because one game file is 9.3 GB. Copy the resulting `GoWAscension` folder to the other PC and run `GoW Ascension.cmd` there. Nothing needs installing.

### Tips for more FPS

- The game is mostly **CPU-bound**. Play plugged in, and close browsers, Discord and overlays.
- NVIDIA laptops: in NVIDIA Control Panel, set *Power management mode = Prefer maximum performance* for `gowa.exe`. If the laptop has a MUX switch, choose *dGPU / Discrete only* mode.
- On a 120/144 Hz screen, enable **Frame generation**. Try **Fast AA** together with **1440p** on a dedicated GPU.
- Don't raise the 60 FPS cap: above 60, the game logic speeds up.

## Controls and keys

Xbox / PlayStation controllers work. **F10** shows the performance overlay, **F11** or **Alt+Enter** switches fullscreen, and **Esc** returns to windowed mode. Saves are in `saves\` and the log is in `out\jogo.log`.

## How it works

The PS3 has a PowerPC CPU (PPU), six vector co-processors (SPUs) and the RSX GPU. The PPU executable is translated function by function into C++. The SPU programs (SPURS jobs, EDGE geometry, policy modules) become C, with hot loops turned into AVX2/AVX-512 kernels. The official firmware's libsre runs as LLE, and RSX commands are drawn with D3D12, with the shaders converted to HLSL. Build details: [docs/COMO_GERAR.md](docs/COMO_GERAR.md).

## Author

**Musthaq Ahamed S** ([@musthaq-ai](https://github.com/musthaq-ai)): the PC launcher, portable package, build tooling and this distribution.

Based on the MIT-licensed native port by otavix010 and contributors, and on the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) toolkit (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)).

## License

Copyright (c) 2026 Musthaq Ahamed S. MIT License for the code and tools in this repository (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)). It does **not** cover God of War: Ascension, its code or data, the PS3 firmware, or anything generated from them. None of these are included here.

1439498844.readme_excerpt:
# LittleBigRecomp

A static recompilation of **LittleBigPlanet** (PS3, BCES00141, disc v02.00) to a
native macOS arm64 executable. The game's PowerPC code is lifted to C++ ahead of
time, and so is every SPU program it runs (FMOD, Bink, the WWS physics/job
manager policy module and its 43 job modules, a voice-codec job). Everything is
linked against the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) runtime,
a git submodule in `ps3recomp/` tracking the `lbp` branch of
[benjidotsh/ps3recomp](https://github.com/benjidotsh/ps3recomp) (upstream
`0fe7dbf`, MIT, plus the fixes this port needed). Clone with
`git clone --recursive`, or run `git submodule update --init`. Rendering goes through Metal.

No game code, assets, keys or game-derived output are in this repository.

## Status

Boots on an Apple-silicon Mac through the first-boot save creation, the
"Important Information" notice, the logos and intro movie (Bink, decoded by the
recompiled SPU code), and loads **the first level, the Introduction**, where the
game is live: it renders the level and answers the pad (START opens the
in-level pause menu).

Known limits: an occasional frame flashes a bright wedge, and depth/stencil
clears ignore the scissor. In-level the game holds
its 30 fps target. FMOD's runtime-relocated DSP plugins run through the SPU
interpreter.

## Building

Needs Xcode clang, CMake, Ninja, Python 3.10+ with `pip install -r ps3recomp/requirements.txt`,
and SDL2 (`brew install sdl2`).

1. Extract the disc ISO and put the decrypted EBOOT in place:

   ```sh
   python3 tools/extract_iso.py "/path/to/LittleBigPlanet.iso" disc
   mkdir -p game && cp /path/to/decrypted/EBOOT.elf game/EBOOT.elf
   ```

   Use a fresh extraction: a pre-extracted copy this port was first tried on
   had 73 corrupt files (among them `output/blurayguids.map`, which breaks
   resource loading).

2. Lift and build:

   ```sh
   PYTHON=/path/to/python3 tools/relift.sh      # PPU + SPU lift, NID table
   cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja && cmake --build build
   ```

3. Run:

   ```sh
   ./run.sh
   ```

   Guest writes (HDD install data, cache, saves) go to `hdd/`; the disc copy
   stays read-only. `PAD_FILE=<file>` drives the pad from a file (write a
   button mask such as `0x4000` for CROSS, `0x0008` for START);
   `tools/autorun.sh <seconds> <log>` runs headless-style and skips the
   intro movie.

## Debugging aids added by this port

- `FN_PROBE=<addr,...>` logs entry/return of guest functions;
  `FN_PROBE_REGS=1` adds all GPRs. `FN_TRACE_AT=<s>` / `FN_TRACE_EXIT=1` write
  each thread's last 64K function entries. `FN_DUMP_AT=<fn>[:n]` /
  `FN_DUMP_SEC=<s>` dump guest memory for `tools/memrd.py`.
- `SPURS_KTRACE=1`, `SPU_TAGSTUCK=1`, `SPU_SNTRACE=1`, `RSX_TEX_LOG/RSX_TEX_DUMP`,
  `RSX_ZSAMPLE_LOG`, `PS3RECOMP_METAL_FRAME_DUMP=dir/f%05u.ppm` (every 120th
  present; `PS3RECOMP_METAL_FRAME_DUMP_FROM=<n>` and `_EVERY=<n>` pick the
  first one kept and the stride, e.g. `_EVERY=1` for consecutive frames).
- `AUDIO_WAV=<file>` writes the final mix as raw f32le stereo 48 kHz;
  `AUDIO_UNDERRUN=1` logs each time the host audio queue ran dry.
- `tools/ppcdis.py`, `tools/fnstrings.py`, `tools/peek.sh` (tile frame dumps).

1439619315.readme_excerpt:
# Demon's Souls Switch port

Experimental Nintendo Switch startup prototype for Demon's Souls US v1.00
(BLUS30443), built around a checked, segmented-memory backend and a bounded
slice of locally translated PowerPC code.

**This is not a playable port. Graphics, audio, menus, and gameplay are not
implemented.** Version 0.27.0 completes thirteen static constructors and all
eight narrow/wide C++ stream initializers, then stops before constructor
fourteen. The latest checkpoint was installed and read back on hardware;
execution of v0.27 on hardware is still pending in the recorded evidence.

## Repository layout

- [`switch-port/`](switch-port/README.md): Switch loader, memory and native
  service backends, entry generator, host tests, and local packaging tools.
- [`switch-probe/`](switch-probe/README.md): earlier memory and launch diagnostics.
- [`analysis/SWITCH_WIDE_STREAMS_STATUS.md`](analysis/SWITCH_WIDE_STREAMS_STATUS.md):
  latest checkpoint, test results, and hardware-validation status.
- [`analysis/PORT_STATUS.md`](analysis/PORT_STATUS.md): broader development status.
- [`analysis/CONTINUATION_STATE.md`](analysis/CONTINUATION_STATE.md): handoff notes
  and next-constructor investigation.
- `tools/`: input auditing and Linux reference-build helpers.

Game executables, game assets, firmware, keys, generated game translations,
compiled binaries, and local installation archives are excluded. Build and
packaging instructions in the detailed development notes refer to artifacts
you generate locally.

## Prepare the local inputs

Clone this repository and run the following from its root. The directory
layout matters because the existing scripts resolve paths relative to it.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/JonathanDC64/DemonsSoulsRecomp.git upstream/DemonsSoulsRecomp
git -C upstream/DemonsSoulsRecomp checkout e99b4f02cd60139c6f795b1209e8c8ba35207376
git clone https://github.com/JonathanDC64/ps3recomp.git upstream/DemonsSoulsRecomp/ps3recomp
git -C upstream/DemonsSoulsRecomp/ps3recomp checkout bae620c0cfa040d5dbc4b3e0bcb5b025576ef5a4
```

Supply your own US v1.00 game executable at
`upstream/DemonsSoulsRecomp/work/game/EBOOT.ELF`, then follow the pinned
upstream repository's input preparation and PowerPC lifting instructions.
The Switch entry generator expects `work/loader/EBOOT.functions.json`,
`work/recomp/ppu_recomp.h`, and the corresponding `ppu_recomp_*.cpp` chunks.
Its hash checks reject mismatched executables or translated function bodies.

The expected EBOOT.ELF SHA-256 is:

```text
90eaa5e9e48b4874292badc311ccea253e6a622ff188bfbdbe76e6f6821269d8
```

The optional Linux reference build also uses
[`analysis/source-preparation.patch`](analysis/source-preparation.patch).
Apply it to the pinned upstream checkout before using `tools/build-headless.sh`.
That helper expects the local CMake and Ninja paths described in its source;
it is separate from the Switch build.

## Validate and build

Host checks require Python 3, Bash, Clang/Clang++, OpenSSL development headers,
and the prepared local inputs. Run from this repository's root:

```sh
python3 switch-port/tools/generate_reference.py
bash switch-port/tests/run_host_tests.sh
bash switch-port/tests/run_heap_tests.sh
bash switch-port/tests/run_entry_tests.sh --explore-wide-streams
```

The detailed [port README](switch-port/README.md) documents the remaining
regression and fault-injection modes. These tests execute startup code;
they do not establish graphics or gameplay support.

The Switch build requires devkitA64 and libnx from devkitPro:

```sh
make -C switch-port DEVKITPRO=/path/to/devkitpro
python3 switch-port/tools/prepare_sd.py
```

Packaging creates a local SD-card archive containing your supplied executable
and the compiled loader. Keep that archive and all generated translations
local. The generated SD-card instructions describe how to run the checkpoint
and collect `loader.log`.

## Credits and licensing

The upstream reference is
[JonathanDC64/DemonsSoulsRecomp](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/DemonsSoulsRecomp),
with its pinned [ps3recomp fork](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/ps3recomp).
See [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for attribution and the
upstream license. No new license grant is specified for the original
Switch-port code in this repository.

1439639917.readme_excerpt:
# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível e à primeira luta contra um chefe, mas ainda lento (~18-23 fps no nível, 13-21 na luta). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot à primeira luta contra um chefe:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~50-55 fps; o primeiro nível a ~22-27 fps, conforme a cena (era ~9); a luta contra o chefe a 13-21. Atrasando um thread de cada vez e medindo quanto o quadro atrasa junto, o limite hoje é o thread que executa os comandos de vídeo (o RSX do RPCS3) e o thread principal do jogo, não as SPUs nem a placa de vídeo. Partes pesadas das SPUs já rodam como código nativo, cada uma conferida contra o original: a geometria por draw (índices, skinning, normais e tangentes) e o pós-processamento que suaviza as bordas da imagem. O foco agora é deixar o jogo mais leve para processadores comuns: o uso total de CPU já caiu ~10% (de 7,2 para 6,4 núcleos no menu) sem perder fps, e o próximo passo é a espera pelas consultas de oclusão (ZCULL) no thread do RSX. Esses números são de um Ryzen 5 5600G com uma RX 7600; num Ryzen 7 9800X3D com uma RX 9070 XT (RSX do RPCS3, Vulkan), o jogo chega a 60 fps fora das lutas e cai para cerca da metade nelas. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); e o jogo às vezes trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`). - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md).

## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), instale o launcher pelo `AscensionLauncher__x64-setup.exe` das [releases](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/releases) e, na primeira vez, aponte a pasta `ascension` em **Avançado › Pasta do jogo**. Ele se atualiza sozinho quando sai uma versão nova.

JOGAR abre o jogo; o launcher se esconde até ele fechar. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

like "Lair" or "Female" instead of area names) or stayed blank.

A post_lift hook in func_001C0540 now draws any request still queued
before the thread sleeps, and the thread's wait gets a 20 ms timeout as a
safety net for the producer's own window.

# Tokyo Jungle Recompiled **Tokyo Jungle (PS3, 2012) as a native Windows program. No emulator.** [**Download BUILD.bat**](../../releases/latest) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Português](#português) · [Controls](#controls) · [How it works](#how-it-works) ![Tokyo Jungle running natively, the title screen](assets/title-screen.gif)
Tokyo Jungle was a digital-only PS3 exclusive whose studios are gone, and the PS3 store is closing. This project turns the game's own PS3 code into a Windows program with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). **No game data is included:** you build it from your own copy, and this fork makes that a double-click. ## Quick start You need Windows 10/11 (64-bit), about 10 GB free, and **your own copy** of Tokyo Jungle (NA, `NPUA80523`) with its license file. 1. Make a new folder and put these three things in it: ``` 📁 My Tokyo Jungle ├── BUILD.bat ← from the Releases page ├── 📁 NPUA80523 ← your extracted game (any name) │ ├── PARAM.SFO │ └── 📁 USRDIR (EBOOT.BIN, data\ ...) └── UP9000-NPUA80523_00-TOKYOJUNGLE00001.rap ← your license ``` 2. Double-click **`BUILD.bat`** and wait. The first build takes **30–60 minutes**. 3. Open **`TokyoJungle.exe`**, pick the resolution and window mode, and play. That's it. If something goes wrong, the full log is in `build.log` in the same folder. **With [RecompLauncher](https://recomplauncher.com):** install Tokyo Jungle Recompiled there and pick your game folder (put the `.rap` inside it). The launcher runs the same build on its setup screen, shows the resolution and window settings on the game's page, and Play starts the game directly.
What BUILD.bat does 1. Installs anything missing with `winget`: Git, Python 3.11, CMake, Ninja, LLVM, Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools (C++) and FFmpeg. The Visual Studio installer may ask for administrator permission. 2. Downloads ps3recomp at the commit this port was made for and applies the port's patches. 3. Decrypts `EBOOT.BIN` and `tj.edat` with **your** `.rap` through RPCS3. An existing RPCS3 install is used if found; otherwise the portable build is downloaded from the [official RPCS3 releases](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3-binaries-win) and checked by SHA-256. The decrypted EBOOT must match the tested one byte for byte ([hashes](docs/GAME_INPUT_HASHES.md)). 4. Recompiles the PS3 code (PPU) and the 18 SPU programs to C, then compiles everything. 5. Leaves `TokyoJungle.exe` (launcher) and `engine\` (the game) in your folder. The `.build` folder it creates is only needed to rebuild; you can delete it. Your extracted game folder is left as it was, except `USRDIR\data\tj.edat`, which is replaced by its decrypted contents (the original is kept as `tj.edat.original`).
## The launcher `TokyoJungle.exe` opens a small window before the game: | Option | Choices | |---|---| | **Resolution** | 1280×720 (the PS3's, lighter) · 2560×1440 (2K, sharper; on a 1080p screen it acts as supersampling) | | **Display** | Window · Full screen (any monitor) | | **Don't ask again** | Starts straight away next time. Hold **Shift** while opening it to see the window again. | Command line (handy for Steam shortcuts): `-play` uses the saved choice, `-2k` forces 2560×1440, `-fullscreen` forces full screen. ![Grass at the PS3's 720p (left) and in 2K mode (right)](assets/grass-720p-vs-2k.png) *Left: the PS3's 720p. Right: 2K mode.* ## Status: playable - **Survival mode works start to finish.** A full **102-year run** (about 2 hours) was played with no crash or freeze. - **60 FPS**, including big fights. - **Movies, player and animal models, menus, sound and PC controls** work in builds made with `BUILD.bat`. - **Still to check:** Story mode, save and reload across sessions, local 2-player, and Steam Deck / Proton. ![The game's Stats screen after the run: Max years survived 102](assets/stats-102-years.jpg) ## Controls Keyboard, mouse buttons and Xbox-style controllers all work. Press **F1** in game (or **Back + Start** on a controller) to change any key or button; changes save to `engine\controls.ini` and apply right away. Menus show your PC keys instead of PS3 buttons. | Action | Keyboard | Controller | |--------|----------|------------| | Move | W A S D | Left stick | | Dodge | Arrow keys | Right stick | | Jump | Space or Z | A | | Eat / mark / carry | F | B | | Claw attack | E | X | | Pack: fight / decoy | V | Y | | Creep / Bite | Left Ctrl / Left Shift | LB / RB | | Roar | Caps Lock | Right stick click | | Pack commands | 1 | LT | | Pause, map / Info | Enter / Backspace | Start / Back | | Items, menus | Numpad 8 / 2 / 4 / 6 | D-pad | The first connected controller is player 1, whatever slot Windows gives it (with Steam open, the real pad often isn't in the first slot). To quit, close the window; a save in progress finishes first. ![The in-game Controls screen](assets/controls-screen.jpg) ## Troubleshooting | Problem | What to do | |---|---| | `BUILD.bat` stops with an error | Read the last lines of `build.log`. Run `BUILD.bat` again after fixing it; finished steps are skipped. | | "nenhuma pasta com USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN" | The game folder must sit **directly** in the same folder as `BUILD.bat`. | | "o RPCS3 nao descriptografou o EBOOT" | The `.rap` isn't this game's license (`UP9000-NPUA80523_00-TOKYOJUNGLE00001`). | | "EBOOT descriptografado diferente do esperado" | A different game version; only the NA release (`NPUA80523`, v1.00) is supported. | | Movies are skipped | `engine\ffmpeg.exe` is missing; run `BUILD.bat` again. | | The controller does nothing | Click the game window once (input only goes to the focused window). | | Anything else | Logs of the last session are in `logs\stdout.log` and `logs\stderr.log`. | To rebuild from scratch, run `BUILD.bat -Rebuild`. ## Português **Tokyo Jungle do PS3 rodando nativo no Windows, sem emulador.** O jogo não vem incluído: você compila a partir da sua própria cópia. 1. Numa pasta nova, coloque o **`BUILD.bat`** (da página de [Releases](../../releases/latest)), a **pasta do jogo extraída** (com `PARAM.SFO` e `USRDIR` dentro) e o arquivo de licença **`UP9000-NPUA80523_00-TOKYOJUNGLE00001.rap`**. 2. Dê dois cliques no `BUILD.bat` e espere (30 a 60 minutos na primeira vez). Ele instala sozinho o que faltar e grava tudo em `build.log`. 3. Abra o **`TokyoJungle.exe`**, escolha a resolução (1280×720 ou 2560×1440) e janela ou tela cheia, e jogue. Pra mudar a escolha depois, segure **Shift** ao abrir. **F1** muda os controles. Se der algum problema, veja o `build.log` (no build) ou a pasta `logs` (no jogo). ## How it works ``` EBOOT.BIN ──RPCS3 + your .rap──► EBOOT.ELF │ ├── PPU code ──ppu_lifter──► C++ (≈7,900 functions) ┐ └── 18 SPU programs ──spu_lifter──► C ├─► clang-cl ─► tokyojungle.exe ps3recomp runtime (HLE OS, RSX → D3D12, audio, input) ┘ ``` The game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code is translated to C/C++ and compiled into a native x86-64 program; the PS3's operating system, graphics, sound and input are reimplemented by the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) runtime. More in [docs/ABOUT.md](docs/ABOUT.md).
What this fork adds to the build Building from the original instructions failed on a clean machine, because the port was made with newer ps3recomp tools and steps than the README listed. This fork scripts all of it: - `patches/ps3recomp/tj-build-fixes.patch`: ps3recomp fixes from after the pinned commit — the find_functions call-target pass; the SPU lifter's `bi $rN` classification, non-r0 link returns and `orbi`/`xorhi`/`xorbi` decoding (without it the player model renders as a spike); `find_spu_functions --raw` — plus the first connected XInput pad as player 1, full screen on any monitor, the real-hardware save-data callback error (new saves unlock the first Survival animals) and audio that reopens the Windows output when the device resets or changes and plays on 5.1/7.1 outputs (`TJ_AUDIO_CHANNELS=3..8` forces a channel count); and a GPU command reader that skips commands at an unmapped address instead of freezing the game (`TJ_TEST_GPU_HANG=1` forces one ~40 s in, to check). - `src/tj_font_queue.cpp` (hook added by `scripts/post_lift.py`): the game's text thread could miss a request and leave old words on map labels; it now draws any request still queued. - `scripts/tj_extract_spu_images.py`: the 18 SPU programs are inside `EBOOT.ELF`; they are cut out by fingerprint (no run-time capture needed). `scripts/tj_lift_spu.py` lifts them. - `scripts/tj_split_fixups.py`: the parts of `gen_stubs.py` that still matter, for the lifter's split output. - `scripts/fix_import_slots.py`: takes import names the NID database lacks from `src/main.cpp` (without `cellSailPlayerInitialize2` the movies show a white screen). - `src/recomp_bridge.h`: room for all 554 HLE handlers (the limit was 512). - `tools/launcher/launcher.c`: the launcher; `scripts/tj_build_all.ps1`: the build.
Manual build (for developers) The steps `BUILD.bat` runs, by hand. You need CMake, Ninja, LLVM (clang-cl), Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools and Python 3.10+, plus the decrypted `EBOOT.ELF` and `PARAM.SFO` of your copy. ```bash git clone https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp.git git clone tokyojungle cd ps3recomp && git checkout d7fff845aca42b5083791801a01d150f5f0ec18c git apply ../tokyojungle/patches/ps3recomp/ps3recomp-tokyojungle-2026-10-17.patch git apply ../tokyojungle/patches/ps3recomp/tj-build-fixes.patch cd ../tokyojungle pip install -r requirements.txt cp /path/to/EBOOT.ELF /path/to/PARAM.SFO input/ python scripts/analyze.py python scripts/fix_import_slots.py python scripts/tj_split_fixups.py python scripts/tj_extract_spu_images.py python scripts/tj_lift_spu.py python -I scripts/fuse_spu_loops.py --apply cmake -B build-clang -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl cmake --build build-clang ``` Run it with `scripts\launch_tokyojungle.ps1 -Run -Recommended -GameData ` (add `-RenderScale 2 -DisplayVBlank -PresentPhase` for 2K). Movies need `ffmpeg.exe` next to `tokyojungle.exe` or on `PATH`, and the decrypted `tj.edat` in place of the encrypted one. Tested game files (SHA-256 and the Redump disc they came from): [docs/GAME_INPUT_HASHES.md](docs/GAME_INPUT_HASHES.md). More: [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md) (play-test log), [docs/HISTORY-2026-09.md](docs/HISTORY-2026-09.md).
| Region | ID | Format | Supported | |--------|----|--------|-----------| | NA (Digital) | NPUA80523 | PSN | **Yes (tested)** | | JP (Disc) | BCAS20219 | Blu-ray | No | | EU (Digital) | NPEA00421 | PSN | No | ## Credits and legal - **Original port and ps3recomp:** [sp00nznet](https://github.com/sp00nznet). - **Renderer, 60 FPS and 2K, pacing, stability and controls** (August–October 2026), play-tested by [LasVola](https://github.com/LasVola). - **Automatic build, launcher and build fixes:** [Silvio Diaz](https://github.com/SilvioDiaz). - Movies are decoded with [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org); decryption uses [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net). Neither is included in this repository. The code here is MIT licensed ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). **No game data is included, and none must be shared:** every player builds from their own legally owned copy. Don't upload the built `engine` folder, `EBOOT.ELF` or anything in `generated/`; they are made from the game. **Tokyo Jungle** is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This project turns the game's own PS3 code into a Windows program with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). **No game data is included:** you build it from your own copy, and this fork makes that a double-click. ## Quick start You need Windows 10/11 (64-bit), about 10 GB free, and **your own copy** of Tokyo Jungle (NA, `NPUA80523`) with its license file. 1. Make a new folder and put these three things in it: ``` 📁 My Tokyo Jungle ├── BUILD.bat ← from the Releases page ├── 📁 NPUA80523 ← your extracted game (any name) │ ├── PARAM.SFO │ └── 📁 USRDIR (EBOOT.BIN, data\ ...) └── UP9000-NPUA80523_00-TOKYOJUNGLE00001.rap ← your license ``` 2. Double-click **`BUILD.bat`** and wait. The first build takes **30–60 minutes**. 3. Open **`TokyoJungle.exe`**, pick the resolution and window mode, and play. That's it. If something goes wrong, the full log is in `build.log` in the same folder.
What BUILD.bat does 1. Installs anything missing with `winget`: Git, Python 3.11, CMake, Ninja, LLVM, Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools (C++) and FFmpeg. The Visual Studio installer may ask for administrator permission. 2. Downloads ps3recomp at the commit this port was made for and applies the port's patches. 3. Decrypts `EBOOT.BIN` and `tj.edat` with **your** `.rap` through RPCS3. An existing RPCS3 install is used if found; otherwise the portable build is downloaded from the [official RPCS3 releases](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3-binaries-win) and checked by SHA-256. The decrypted EBOOT must match the tested one byte for byte ([hashes](docs/GAME_INPUT_HASHES.md)). 4. Recompiles the PS3 code (PPU) and the 18 SPU programs to C, then compiles everything. 5. Leaves `TokyoJungle.exe` (launcher) and `engine\` (the game) in your folder. The `.build` folder it creates is only needed to rebuild; you can delete it. Your extracted game folder is left as it was, except `USRDIR\data\tj.edat`, which is replaced by its decrypted contents (the original is kept as `tj.edat.original`).
## The launcher `TokyoJungle.exe` opens a small window before the game: | Option | Choices | |---|---| | **Resolution** | 1280×720 (the PS3's, lighter) · 2560×1440 (2K, sharper; on a 1080p screen it acts as supersampling) | | **Display** | Window · Full screen (any monitor) | | **Don't ask again** | Starts straight away next time. Hold **Shift** while opening it to see the window again. | Command line (handy for Steam shortcuts): `-play` uses the saved choice, `-2k` forces 2560×1440, `-fullscreen` forces full screen. ![Grass at the PS3's 720p (left) and in 2K mode (right)](assets/grass-720p-vs-2k.png) *Left: the PS3's 720p. Right: 2K mode.* ## Status: playable - **Survival mode works start to finish.** A full **102-year run** (about 2 hours) was played with no crash or freeze. - **60 FPS**, including big fights. - **Movies, player and animal models, menus, sound and PC controls** work in builds made with `BUILD.bat`. - **Still to check:** Story mode, save and reload across sessions, local 2-player, and Steam Deck / Proton. ![The game's Stats screen after the run: Max years survived 102](assets/stats-102-years.jpg) ## Controls Keyboard, mouse buttons and Xbox-style controllers all work. Press **F1** in game (or **Back + Start** on a controller) to change any key or button; changes save to `engine\controls.ini` and apply right away. Menus show your PC keys instead of PS3 buttons. | Action | Keyboard | Controller | |--------|----------|------------| | Move | W A S D | Left stick | | Dodge | Arrow keys | Right stick | | Jump | Space or Z | A | | Eat / mark / carry | F | B | | Claw attack | E | X | | Pack: fight / decoy | V | Y | | Creep / Bite | Left Ctrl / Left Shift | LB / RB | | Roar | Caps Lock | Right stick click | | Pack commands | 1 | LT | | Pause, map / Info | Enter / Backspace | Start / Back | | Items, menus | Numpad 8 / 2 / 4 / 6 | D-pad | The first connected controller is player 1, whatever slot Windows gives it (with Steam open, the real pad often isn't in the first slot). To quit, close the window; a save in progress finishes first. ![The in-game Controls screen](assets/controls-screen.jpg) ## Troubleshooting | Problem | What to do | |---|---| | `BUILD.bat` stops with an error | Read the last lines of `build.log`. Run `BUILD.bat` again after fixing it; finished steps are skipped. | | "nenhuma pasta com USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN" | The game folder must sit **directly** in the same folder as `BUILD.bat`. | | "o RPCS3 nao descriptografou o EBOOT" | The `.rap` isn't this game's license (`UP9000-NPUA80523_00-TOKYOJUNGLE00001`). | | "EBOOT descriptografado diferente do esperado" | A different game version; only the NA release (`NPUA80523`, v1.00) is supported. | | Movies are skipped | `engine\ffmpeg.exe` is missing; run `BUILD.bat` again. | | The controller does nothing | Click the game window once (input only goes to the focused window). | | Anything else | Logs of the last session are in `logs\stdout.log` and `logs\stderr.log`. | To rebuild from scratch, run `BUILD.bat -Rebuild`. ## Português **Tokyo Jungle do PS3 rodando nativo no Windows, sem emulador.** O jogo não vem incluído: você compila a partir da sua própria cópia. 1. Numa pasta nova, coloque o **`BUILD.bat`** (da página de [Releases](../../releases/latest)), a **pasta do jogo extraída** (com `PARAM.SFO` e `USRDIR` dentro) e o arquivo de licença **`UP9000-NPUA80523_00-TOKYOJUNGLE00001.rap`**. 2. Dê dois cliques no `BUILD.bat` e espere (30 a 60 minutos na primeira vez). Ele instala sozinho o que faltar e grava tudo em `build.log`. 3. Abra o **`TokyoJungle.exe`**, escolha a resolução (1280×720 ou 2560×1440) e janela ou tela cheia, e jogue. Pra mudar a escolha depois, segure **Shift** ao abrir. **F1** muda os controles. Se der algum problema, veja o `build.log` (no build) ou a pasta `logs` (no jogo). ## How it works ``` EBOOT.BIN ──RPCS3 + your .rap──► EBOOT.ELF │ ├── PPU code ──ppu_lifter──► C++ (≈7,900 functions) ┐ └── 18 SPU programs ──spu_lifter──► C ├─► clang-cl ─► tokyojungle.exe ps3recomp runtime (HLE OS, RSX → D3D12, audio, input) ┘ ``` The game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code is translated to C/C++ and compiled into a native x86-64 program; the PS3's operating system, graphics, sound and input are reimplemented by the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) runtime. More in [docs/ABOUT.md](docs/ABOUT.md).
What this fork adds to the build Building from the original instructions failed on a clean machine, because the port was made with newer ps3recomp tools and steps than the README listed. This fork scripts all of it: - `patches/ps3recomp/tj-build-fixes.patch`: ps3recomp fixes from after the pinned commit — the find_functions call-target pass; the SPU lifter's `bi $rN` classification, non-r0 link returns and `orbi`/`xorhi`/`xorbi` decoding (without it the player model renders as a spike); `find_spu_functions --raw` — plus the first connected XInput pad as player 1 and full screen on any monitor. - `scripts/tj_extract_spu_images.py`: the 18 SPU programs are inside `EBOOT.ELF`; they are cut out by fingerprint (no run-time capture needed). `scripts/tj_lift_spu.py` lifts them. - `scripts/tj_split_fixups.py`: the parts of `gen_stubs.py` that still matter, for the lifter's split output. - `scripts/fix_import_slots.py`: takes import names the NID database lacks from `src/main.cpp` (without `cellSailPlayerInitialize2` the movies show a white screen). - `src/recomp_bridge.h`: room for all 554 HLE handlers (the limit was 512). - `tools/launcher/launcher.c`: the launcher; `scripts/tj_build_all.ps1`: the build.
Manual build (for developers) The steps `BUILD.bat` runs, by hand. You need CMake, Ninja, LLVM (clang-cl), Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools and Python 3.10+, plus the decrypted `EBOOT.ELF` and `PARAM.SFO` of your copy. ```bash git clone https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp.git git clone tokyojungle cd ps3recomp && git checkout d7fff845aca42b5083791801a01d150f5f0ec18c git apply ../tokyojungle/patches/ps3recomp/ps3recomp-tokyojungle-2026-10-17.patch git apply ../tokyojungle/patches/ps3recomp/tj-build-fixes.patch cd ../tokyojungle pip install -r requirements.txt cp /path/to/EBOOT.ELF /path/to/PARAM.SFO input/ python scripts/analyze.py python scripts/fix_import_slots.py python scripts/tj_split_fixups.py python scripts/tj_extract_spu_images.py python scripts/tj_lift_spu.py python -I scripts/fuse_spu_loops.py --apply cmake -B build-clang -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl cmake --build build-clang ``` Run it with `scripts\launch_tokyojungle.ps1 -Run -Recommended -GameData ` (add `-RenderScale 2 -DisplayVBlank -PresentPhase` for 2K). Movies need `ffmpeg.exe` next to `tokyojungle.exe` or on `PATH`, and the decrypted `tj.edat` in place of the encrypted one. Tested game files (SHA-256 and the Redump disc they came from): [docs/GAME_INPUT_HASHES.md](docs/GAME_INPUT_HASHES.md). More: [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md) (play-test log), [docs/HISTORY-2026-09.md](docs/HISTORY-2026-09.md).
| Region | ID | Format | Supported | |--------|----|--------|-----------| | NA (Digital) | NPUA80523 | PSN | **Yes (tested)** | | JP (Disc) | BCAS20219 | Blu-ray | No | | EU (Digital) | NPEA00421 | PSN | No | ## Credits and legal - **Original port and ps3recomp:** [sp00nznet](https://github.com/sp00nznet). - **Renderer, 60 FPS and 2K, pacing, stability and controls** (August–October 2026), play-tested by [LasVola](https://github.com/LasVola). - **Automatic build, launcher and build fixes:** [Silvio Diaz](https://github.com/SilvioDiaz). - Movies are decoded with [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org); decryption uses [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net). Neither is included in this repository. 00478cb0ec475f0344a8204fa262e0d94da033d6.message:
M6: the SPU reservation test retired from the release's lifted stores

Every lifted store tested its line for an SPU reservation; R8 priced that at
0.4 ms of the game thread a frame and kept it while lifted SPU code took
reservations. None does now: FMOD's SPU code is out of the lift (M5), every
other SPU workload is native with its reachable fallbacks native too, and the
census shows no SPU reservation or line watch in any run.

- ps3recomp patch 0155: the lifter's header takes PPU_STORES_NO_SPU_COH (every
  store keeps its range test, loses the reservation test), and the runtime's
  spu_coh_forbid makes any later SPU reservation or line watch fatal, naming
  why -- never a store that silently misses one.
- The store mode mov-nospu is the native release's default on Windows x86-64
  (port/CMakeLists.txt); main.cpp calls spu_coh_forbid at start. The
  comparison build keeps the old stores (-DDOTHEROES_PPU_STORES=mov) for the
  check modes and the lifted fallbacks' switches.
- The native solver's lock moves off the runtime's lock-line lock onto a host
  compare-and-swap; it still breaks PPU reservations on its line. The PPU's
  own lwarx/stwcx. semantics are unchanged.
- The memory test checks the stores at a line's end for their bytes in this
  mode; the install test compares with the new lift (gen15, which differs from
  gen14 only in its header).

Validation (rel47): the memory test (668 checks), the 11 drives, the menu's
quit, the movie, seven save flows, the reference scenes (5/5 within): no
crash, trap or fatal diagnostic, no reservation in any census. The water's
check mode stops at once with the diagnostic, as intended. A fresh
installation, update, relift and a river fight from it pass. Against rel46:
the game thread 0.47 ms less a frame; uncapped, the river fight 235.1-237.7
fps (from 210.0-213.7) and the fields 277.2-281.6 (from 246.6-247.6); p99 and
p99.9 lower; the 144 fps cap held. docs/OPENAL_MIGRATION_PLAN.md section 10.5.

00f5358b387798876285f947de8482938e4180e5.message:
Solver: native iterate behind DOTHEROES_NATIVE_SOLVER=4 (off)

Command 4, a round of the solver's iterations, done natively: cells claimed
under the round's ticket lock and masks as the lifted tasks do, each cell's
bodies copied in and written back whole, contacts in the packets the SPU
task's local store allows (normal rows, then friction rows with limits from
the contact's impulse), each row in the lifted task's order of operations
with the runtime's exact SPU single-precision helpers. The ten rounds, the
PPU's side and each task's completion are unchanged. Experimental, off by
default, separate from native collision.

For checking it: DOTHEROES_SOLVER_SERIAL=1 runs the lifted iterate tasks
one at a time (cells in index order); DOTHEROES_SOLVER_SNAP_ROUNDS and
_SHARED capture every round, and steps with a body in two cells' lists;
DOTHEROES_NATIVE_SOLVER_CHECK compares each round with the native model
run on its inputs; DOTHEROES_SOLVER_BENCH times it per round (compute
only). tests/solver_iterate_layout.py checks the structures on captures,
bullet_solver_snapcheck gains an iterate mode, solver_bench.py an iterate
table, solver_ab.py a per-run frame table with a no-physics control.

  R5G6B5_UNORM_PACK16, the guest's own 16 bits, as RPCS3 keeps it; the old

  shadow map sat 10 steps of 2^-24 deeper than RPCS3's; now equal.
  DOTHEROES_PPFX_BIAS_NV=0: not halved.

Audio M5: FMOD excluded from the lift; OpenAL Soft the only audio path

The lifter's new exclusion (ps3recomp patches 0146-0148, generic): every
function starting in a range of config/excluded_code.json is lifted as a trap
that reports the address and ends the game, and the runtime treats any other
address in the range the same way. FMOD Ex's PPU code (2,853 functions:
its library and its classes' out-of-line methods) is excluded; its 41 static
constructors and destructors, reached only through the C runtime's tables,
are lifted as a plain return. Its 21 SPU programs are no longer lifted.

Removed with it: the 28 FMOD API hooks, the flashMP3 patch and its guard,
the DOTHEROES_NATIVE_AUDIO switch (=0 is ignored with a message), and the
silent fallback without OpenAL Soft (the build now stops instead). The
setup's lift passes the exclusion and leaves the images out; the
configuration is part of the lift's fingerprint. cellAudio and SDL2's audio
stay for the movies until FFmpeg replaces Bink (M8). The executable: 131.7 MB
to 120.4 MB.

Validation (rel41), every run without a crash or a trap: the memory test
(695/695); the 11 validation drives; Vulkan validation (0 messages); the
damage run; quitting through the game's menu; the water check (2,483/2,483
equal) and the waver check (1,170/1,177, the known mid-ripple class); the

16d9cc122ff8a730986d28395c6f1ac1e89fb9d4.message:
r1_replay --chain: R2's executor, a whole chain frame after frame; r2_compare.py

The executor runs chain.json on images of its own, one per captured
resource. External inputs are seeded where they arrive -- at the frame's
start, or mid-frame where asp hands the scene target back; history would be
seeded once and carried; everything else starts as 0xA5 poison (again each
frame with --poison-each-frame). Each image's layout, last write and reads
since are tracked, and every access gets exactly the barrier its hazard
needs (read after write, write after read, write after write, a layout
change). The feedback pass reads a copy made into a separate image just
before it. Correctness runs read each pass's output back right after it,
before anything can overwrite it; timing runs (--reps) time each segment
between seeds after a full barrier, copies and barriers included, without
readbacks, then run the chain once more and keep its outputs for checking.

r2_compare.py compares every output with its reference at the format's own
precision (r1_compare.py's measures), records both hashes, and can prune
the native outputs that are bit-exact.

1a91b992c2b9b6acbc5d8b97f81857a2963d2185.message:
Title-screen freezes fixed: SDL's controllers polled on a thread of their own

After a device arrives or leaves anywhere on the system, SDL2's Windows driver
re-enumerates every input device under its joystick lock (312 ms here), and
the game's pad read and the window's event pump waited on it: the game froze.
ps3recomp patch 0150 reports an SDL update of 50 ms or more with its time;
patch 0151 moves every SDL joystick and controller call to a "pad" thread
that publishes each port's state every 4 ms. The game's pad reads copy the
latest state, the window's pump no longer updates joysticks, and rumble goes
through the thread (renewed only while the game still reads its pad).
PAD_SDL_THREAD=0 restores the old way.

Reproduced with tools/sdl_device_poke.py (SDL's own device-change message,
six times on the title screen): before, six 312 ms freezes (the longest
frame 335 ms); with the thread, the same six enumerations and no frame over
25 ms (the longest 17.7 ms, as with no pokes); PAD_SDL_THREAD=0 on the same
build froze again (334 ms). The drives that read the attached controller and
the seven save flows pass; an A/B against the build without it shows no cost.
Validated apart from M6's measurements. docs/PC_EXPERIENCE.md section 7b.

5ef863d46b4112ef254b422551e2fa50968942d2.message:
M6: the main thread's short sleeps wait on the GCM delivery; SPURS threads start lazily

The main thread paces itself with two loops: it waits for a flag its vblank
handler sets (usleep(300) between the looks), then for the previous frame's
flip (cellGcmGetFlipStatus, usleep(200)). The runtime spun every sleep under a
millisecond to its deadline, so the main thread took a whole core at every
frame cap. ps3recomp patches 0152 and 0154: such a sleep waits on the GCM
delivery event and a high-resolution timer; a vblank or a flip's completion
runs the pump at once and the rest of the requested time is still spun, so a
sleep never ends early and the game sees its handler's change no later than
before. PS3_FLIP_WAIT=spin restores the spin. Patch 0153: a SPURS instance's
threads start with its first workload, task or job chain; the physics
set-up's two instances, which the native physics never schedules on, now run
no thread (PS3_SPURS_EAGER=1 as before). The test stop prints the waits'
report (dev_state.cpp).

Measured, the same binary against itself at 30, 60, 120 and 144 fps and
uncapped, two scenes, two rounds: the main thread at 16-20%, 28-38%, 54-65%
and 64-76% of a core where it took 25-26% and 99%; the process at 60 fps
0.86-0.91 cores where it took 1.50-1.53; p99, p99.9 and the worst frame lower
at every cap (the river fight at 120: p99 8.69 against 9.33 ms). Uncapped the
frame rates overlap. The flip's completion to the next frame at 60 fps:
105-125 us on average against 154-169 us. The validation set (memory test,
11 drives, the menu's quit, the movie, seven save flows): no crash, trap or

stay equal. docs/OPENAL_MIGRATION_PLAN.md section 10.4.

tools/edit_import.py: import edited characters saved on a real PS3

A real PS3 keeps an edit save's DATA.EDT encrypted (listed in its PARAM.PFD);
this port's save data keeps files as they are. The tool decrypts once, as
the PS3's save system would for the game (the method of Apollo Save Tool's
pfd_util.c, bucanero/apollo-ps3, GPL-3.0), and installs the save folder in
the port's format, never over an existing one.

No secret is in the repository: the PS3's syscon manager key comes from a
local copy of Apollo's source into build/ext; the game's secure file ID is
captured from the game (ps3recomp 0127, PS3_SAVEDATA_SECURE_ID_LOG=1 on an
editor save) or searched for in the decrypted EBOOT, and is checked against
the file's HMAC-SHA1 in the PARAM.PFD before anything is decrypted.

decrypted (each now starts with the game's own EDTFILE1.9 header, as the
port's own edit saves do) into build/play-route's saves.

game's other threads as isolate does, but lets the main thread use either of
its logical processors (CPU sets, no hard affinity), so an interrupt or
another process on one does not hold it. In the placement A/B isolate kept
the main thread's headroom at 72 fps but missed the period by a millisecond
in ~0.3% of ordinary frames, against ~0.07% unpinned.

PS3_FTRACE kind 18 now carries the logical processor in a (| 0x100): the
walker's spans, and the vblank clock's thread every 16th tick (who 4), so a
trace shows which of them shared the main thread's core.

63cb998f253a1681cbf79245c155e58600090a2f.message:
CPU placement, experimental: DOTHEROES_CPU_PLACE=normal|percore|isolate

For the placement A/B. normal (the default) leaves every thread to Windows;
percore holds the process to one logical processor of each core (the
affinity the store-check A/B set from outside); isolate puts the PPU main
thread alone on one logical processor and keeps every other thread of the
process off both of that core's (CPU sets: the process default without the
core, the main thread's own set and affinity the one processor). The
topology is read from the system; isolate's core is DOTHEROES_CPU_CORE or
the last of the highest efficiency and scheduling class, not core 0's. The
topology is logged at start in every mode.

With ps3recomp 0093: the frame trace's kind 26 says per frame where the main
thread ran and how busy its core's other logical processor was.

Save-data screen: the picture composed in cached memory (no freeze)

The owner's M4 play session (rel35, fullscreen 1920x1080) found the save
and load lists very slow: each move of the cursor took effect late and the
game froze 0.4-1.1 s at a time while a list was open (the session's two

there against 15 ms in cached memory. It ran under the present mutex, so the
game's next flip waited for it. Now it is composed in a cached buffer and
copied in one pass: 15 ms, the same picture byte for byte.

Behaviour fix: FIFO subchannel 1 no longer feeds the 3D engine (GCM_SUBCH1_2D=1 by default)

Subchannel 1 is libgcm's memory-to-memory object here. PPFX's one report
copy after each area load (0x006A1D1C, from 0x007C2F94) puts its FORMAT
method there, method 0x0324 with 0x101; the walker routed subchannel 1 to
the 3D engine, which took it as the colour mask: PPFX's next 46 draws, one
frame after every load, wrote green and blue only. On a PS3 the 3D engine
never sees it. The copy itself (16 bytes of a report into main memory) was
not carried out before and is not now; it goes to the 2D path's unhandled
methods. GCM_SUBCH1_2D=0 restores the old routing. R3 had read the tint as
state PPFX inherits from other code (docs/NATIVE_R3B.md section 1).

Behaviour fix: FIFO subchannel 1 no longer feeds the 3D engine (GCM_SUBCH1_2D=1 by default)

Subchannel 1 is libgcm's memory-to-memory object here. PPFX's one report
copy after each area load (0x006A1D1C, from 0x007C2F94) puts its FORMAT
method there, method 0x0324 with 0x101; the walker routed subchannel 1 to
the 3D engine, which took it as the colour mask: PPFX's next 46 draws, one
frame after every load, wrote green and blue only. On a PS3 the 3D engine
never sees it. The copy itself (16 bytes of a report into main memory) was
not carried out before and is not now; it goes to the 2D path's unhandled
methods. GCM_SUBCH1_2D=0 restores the old routing. R3 had read the tint as
state PPFX inherits from other code (docs/NATIVE_R3B.md section 1).

Native PPFX records: an explicit description instead of the RSX-shaped block; asp's state API observed; per-image barriers; every comparison accounted for

Records now carry what PPFX's calls meant -- the surface, viewport,
scissor, both programs with their CgBinary parameters, textures and
samplers, vertex inputs, render state -- in libgcm's own vocabulary
(ppfx_native.h State). The native renderer derives its pipelines,
samplers, vertex fetch and constants from those fields; the 754-word
register block and the scratch register file are gone. Where a toolkit
helper takes a hardware word (the fragment translator's control word,
the remap crossbar) it is made at the call from the record's fields. The
register file is read in one place only, the bridge's development
cross-check, which decodes the engine's state into the same explicit form.

What PPFX's draws take from asp, the engine: the observers now include
asp's state API (colour mask setter, sampler bind, state-store
re-emission, pass apply, its other setters). The recorder follows asp's
colour mask from its setter's booleans and a unit's address mode from
asp's state store once a bind or re-emission has put it there
(docs/NATIVE_R3B.md section 1). River run: 0 cross-check differences.

The native renderer tracks each image's layout, last write and reads and
gives each access the barrier its hazard needs (R2's r2_access);
DOTHEROES_PPFX_BARRIERS=full keeps R3's way. Each batch timestamps its
operations: GPU time by draws, copies, readbacks.

Comparisons: every one asked for ends as equal, differ, skipped (no engine
copy, no readback, extent, not drawn) or unfinished; finals and the frames
after a structure change get reserved buffers and wait for one rather than
skip. A test's stop (dev_state) now runs the renderer's drain and the last
report first.

Geometry cache without resets; a command-ring freeze fixed

Resident geometry (patch 0041): the cache filled and flushed itself every
~25 s of play, rebuilding the whole scene. The new keys came from
post-processing quads drawn out of a streaming vertex ring
(tests/geom_newkeys.py), not from UI or particles. Now an entry is
admitted on its second sighting through a fixed 4096-key filter, no
placeholder is kept for unwatchable draws, and when space runs out the
least recently drawn entries go (never the scene in view) and their GPU
blocks are reused instead of everything being flushed.

Five-minute soaks of walking, menu, map, guard and sword
(tests/scripts/soak_timing.drive, DUMP=0): ~1,200-1,450 entries / 73-76
MB, levelling off after the first minute, 86-88% of draws resident, no
evictions or resets needed; 59.5-60 fps, p99 21-22 ms. Forced small
(1,100 entries / 128 MB) it evicts old entries and keeps 88% of draws
resident. Check mode: no missed write in nine runs.

The check-mode soaks also froze the game (patch 0043): after a flip the
runtime wraps the title's 2 MB command ring, and the title's next ~0.9 MB
frame could then write over commands the walker had not read; decoding
them, the walker ran past the flip the title was waiting for. The new lap
now ends at the walker until it gets there. 9 check-mode runs clean (was
5 freezes in ~12); at full speed the limit never engages and frame times
are unchanged. Traced with the runtime's new flip and walker recorders,
GCM_FLIP_RING=1 (patch 0042). The vblank thread is as in the last commit.

b230bb1ca4e72ae135d54c8ae9dcc5268a4d2659.message:
CPU placement, experimental: DOTHEROES_CPU_PLACE=normal|percore|isolate

For the placement A/B. normal (the default) leaves every thread to Windows;
percore holds the process to one logical processor of each core (the
affinity the store-check A/B set from outside); isolate puts the PPU main
thread alone on one logical processor and keeps every other thread of the
process off both of that core's (CPU sets: the process default without the
core, the main thread's own set and affinity the one processor). The
topology is read from the system; isolate's core is DOTHEROES_CPU_CORE or
the last of the highest efficiency and scheduling class, not core 0's. The
topology is logged at start in every mode.

With ps3recomp 0093: the frame trace's kind 26 says per frame where the main
thread ran and how busy its core's other logical processor was.

CPU placement: a reserve mode; the trace says where the walker and vblank ran

DOTHEROES_CPU_PLACE=reserve keeps the PPU main thread's core free of the
game's other threads as isolate does, but lets the main thread use either of
its logical processors (CPU sets, no hard affinity), so an interrupt or
another process on one does not hold it. In the placement A/B isolate kept

R4: a texture in guest memory taken by the walker, at the record's place in the stream

transfer into a 1280x720 surface (local 0x05530000 / 0x058F0000) that PPFX

The RSX walker's time split: active work, each wait, what delays a frame

trace (kind 18, runtime patch 0058: a guest frame's present begun there, the
window pump, the sleep). tests/walker_breakdown.py reads it per guest frame:

then to the frame shown (its first present), the walker thread's time in
both split into active drain work, the GPU waits inside it (flush, batch in

waited in. The game's frame end waits for the vblank (lr 0x29C20) and for
