0377fec2ed185a48b1b6790e073dc0df2f81e702.message:
Skip the title's frame-pacer pad: it copied every hitch onto later frames

With every draw dropped the race still missed vblanks. The render thread
pads each frame with a sleep up to the slowest of its last four frames once
one passes a vblank (func_007AF300; the sleep returns to 0x00B24AF4). On a
console frame times vary by microseconds; here SPU spin waits and the odd
preemption made it fire constantly and turn one slow frame into a run of
them. The render thread's own CPU never exceeded 15 ms a frame.

Sleeps from that call site are now skipped by default (frame_pacer_sleep_lr
in config/targets.json; GT5P_PACER_PAD=1 keeps the padding). Frame test:
55 -> ~58 FPS, ~14% -> 7-9% of frames over 20 ms, p99 ~43 -> ~30 ms; no draws
59.3 FPS, 1.6% late. Game speed unchanged (0.99), rolling start still 30.

Diagnostics: PS3_USLEEP_LONG, PS3_USLEEP_SKIP_LR, timeline events C (render
thread CPU vs wall per frame) and Q (spin-wait sleeps), scripts/diag/
rtsplit.py. Phase 106.

Phase 72: pit crew animate; SPU skinning never ran

The geometry job picks its skinning routine into r0 and calls it with

clears as the hardware does, and to a loop entry only reachable through an
absolute address table, which lift_spu_jobs.py now seeds.

241f795b094a9e898efe743e18dcef8676f2835f.message:
Cache repeated vertex streams across frames (Phase 57)

Plan step 4a. Half of a Car Dealer frame's indexed draws read the same
vertex bytes as the frame before (static meshes); the other half is the
SPU's output ring, new every frame. Vertex attributes are grouped into
streams, and a stream seen two frames running is copied once into a
persistent area of the raw vertex buffer. Draws compare their bytes
against its mirror, once a frame for streams stable over eight frames.
Two-stream layouts no longer fall back to the CPU.

Uploads 21 -> 12.5 ms a frame; 17.4 -> about 19.6 fps. RSX_VTX_GPU=check
reports 0 differing fetches. RSX_VTXCACHE=0 turns it off; RSX_XFSTAT=1
measures frame-to-frame repetition.

249b62e029be207b046d3704e28400e2315db323.message:
Unblock SPURS dispatch, yield guest spin waits, keep frame buffers in VRAM

Three measured limits on race frame rate:

- One-SPU SPURS workloads ran inline on the kernel thread, so the render
  list waited up to 8 ms to be dispatched while a 13-15 ms one-SPU pass
  ran. They now use their lane pool like the others.
- The render thread waited for its SPU job list in a bare guest spin,
  holding one of the two guest CPUs while Main Thread (host IDLE
  priority) starved. A new post-lift step, scripts/spin_patch.py, makes
  the listed waits pause, yield, then sleep briefly.
- Per-frame vertex, index and constant buffers were read from system
  memory by every draw. A copy list now fills video-memory mirrors with
  what each frame wrote, before its draws.

In a fixed High Speed Ring timeline window at 1080p/2x, the mean frame
went from 25.8 to 17.5 ms, and introduction GPU time from 12-15 to 6-10
ms. The introduction still locks to 30 FPS. Each change has a rollback
switch (Phase 101).

deb6fa5303e6655610fc1596e4f0dfee8646779c.message:
Rebuild the SPU lanes and fetch vertices on the GPU (Phase 56)

SPU lanes: a per-workload pool of lane threads woken by events, the
SPURS kernel woken by kicks instead of a 1 ms poll, lanes that never get
work pruned, finished lanes leave at once, 1 ms stagger, high-resolution
usleep. Title-only on the Car Dealer page: 23.4 to 29.3 fps.

GPU vertex fetch (RSX_VTX_GPU): indexed uploads copy raw guest vertex
bytes and a shader variant decodes them from SV_VertexID; sparse calls
stay on the CPU, regions are reused only when every byte matches. With
drawing: 15.7 to 17.2 fps. Two faults found on the way: a triangle list
split across records joined the wrong vertices (the leftover indices are
now carried), and stale record flags replayed quads as GPU-fetch draws.

PS3_TIMELINE records a run's frame-pacing events; scratch/tl.py reads
them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

dfcd46e99008f3a237869e874dc9b240b9279343.message:
Inline guest memory access by default; chain SPU job bodies

Out-of-line vm_read*/vm_write* calls were about 65% of the race render
thread's CPU. GT5P_VM_INLINE is now on by default: render thread 14.1 ->
5.8 ms a frame (-DGT5P_VM_INLINE=OFF builds the old way, VM_INLINE=0 at
run time sends accesses out of line).

The render thread then waited each frame for the race's one-SPU workloads
5/6 (job body 0x0133A700), 14-17 ms a pass: every lifted block returned to
the dispatcher, because lift_spu_jobs.py only chained forward transfers in
job images, never in job bodies. Bodies are chained too now
(SPU_CHAIN_BODIES=0 skips; --chain updates generated/): passes ~6 ms.

Frame test 57.7-58.1 -> 58.9-59.0 FPS, 7-9% -> 3% of frames over 20 ms.
Game speed unchanged, rolling start still 30. GT5P_SAMPLE_WID profiles one
SPURS workload across pool lanes; the sampler takes up to 16 threads.
Phase 107.

SPU runtime fast paths: render lanes 1.15x, Ferrari median 25 fps (Phase 62)

  they can apply; SPU_ARGWATCH read once instead of a getenv per lane run

1.15-1.16x less lane CPU per pass. Ferrari 25.1 fps median over 6 runs
(23.3 before), Acura 29.6; no stalls. Also GCM_PARK_TIMEOUT_MS for a park

1440438589.readme_excerpt: # Project Tourline Prologue **Gran Turismo 5 Prologue: unofficial PC port (static recompilation)** [![No game files](https://github.com/mathewdouglas/Tourline-Prologue/actions/workflows/no-game-files.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mathewdouglas/Tourline-Prologue/actions/workflows/no-game-files.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) ![Status: partly playable](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-partly%20playable-orange) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/mathewdouglas/Tourline-Prologue?label=release)](https://github.com/mathewdouglas/Tourline-Prologue/releases) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/mathewdouglas/Tourline-Prologue/total)](https://github.com/mathewdouglas/Tourline-Prologue/releases) ![Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20x64-0078D6) ![Direct3D 12](https://img.shields.io/badge/graphics-Direct3D%2012-555) **[Release notes](docs/release-v0.2.5.md)** · **[Getting started](#getting-started)** · **[Known problems](#known-problems)** · **[Player setup](docs/player-setup.md)** · **[Shader preparation](docs/shader-precompile.md)** · **[Progress](docs/progress.md)** · **[Roadmap](ROADMAP.md)** · **[Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)** · **[AI use](docs/AI.md)** An unofficial port of **Gran Turismo 5 Prologue** (PS3, US disc BCUS98158) to Windows x64. It is a static recompilation: the game's own code, translated ahead of time to native x64, then run with a Direct3D 12 renderer. No emulator runs while you play. The player build is **Tourline Prologue**. The window title is Project Tourline Prologue. > **Status: early, partly playable.** The supported disc build boots to the menu, the dealerships draw, and a race loads and drives. The current download is [v0.2.5](https://github.com/mathewdouglas/Tourline-Prologue/releases/tag/v0.2.5). The investigation, with dates and measurements, is in [docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md). This tree is a fork of [sp00nznet/GT5P](https://github.com/sp00nznet/GT5P), built with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). ### What you need - **Your own US disc copy** of Gran Turismo 5 Prologue, **BCUS98158 version 03.00**, extracted as a folder or as its `PS3_GAME` directory. An ISO is not accepted. - **Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit**, and a GPU with Direct3D 12. - **A decrypted `EMAIN.ELF` from that disc**, or an installed copy of RPCS3 that the launcher can use to decrypt a private copy. RPCS3, firmware and keys are not included, and the original dump is left unchanged. This project ships none of the game. Player notes in the download: [launcher/START-HERE.txt](launcher/START-HERE.txt). ## Getting started 1. Download the Windows ZIP from [v0.2.5](https://github.com/mathewdouglas/Tourline-Prologue/releases/tag/v0.2.5) on the [releases page](https://github.com/mathewdouglas/Tourline-Prologue/releases). 2. Extract the entire ZIP to a normal folder. Do not run it from inside the ZIP. 3. Run **tourline-prologue.exe**. Choose where to keep saves, settings and shaders (the default folder, or an empty folder on another drive). Then select your extracted disc folder. 4. If `EMAIN.ELF` is not already available, choose your installed RPCS3 when asked, or choose a decrypted `EMAIN.ELF` made from your own `EMAIN.SELF`. 5. Use **tourline-prologue.exe** for every later launch. Setup is remembered. Press **F1** for settings. The first preset is 720p with 2x MSAA. The file `runtime/gt5p.exe` is the engine. It is not the icon you double-click. Optional shader preparation, after setup and with the game closed: run **Prepare shaders.cmd**. It reads the game folder you already selected. No separate asset copy, Python install or compiler install is required. It can take several minutes and uses extra disk space. Cancelling keeps finished work; run the same command again to resume. Later launches use a preparation only after it verifies. `tourline-prologue.exe --no-prepared` returns to the ordinary cache and does not delete either cache. To move saves and shaders, close the game and run **Change storage.cmd**. To point at a different dump, run `tourline-prologue.exe --setup`. For an update, close the game and extract the new ZIP into its own folder. Your selected storage stays where it is. More detail: [launcher/START-HERE.txt](launcher/START-HERE.txt), [docs/player-setup.md](docs/player-setup.md), [docs/release-v0.2.5.md](docs/release-v0.2.5.md). Changes per version: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## Known problems - Shader preparation is optional and partial. The starter covers observed menu, High Speed Ring, Daytona and Fuji Speedway F pipelines at the supported settings. At 720p and 1080p 16:9 it also writes menu and race shader packs. Other cars, cameras, track sections and settings still compile on demand. One High Speed Ring comparison had fewer long frames with those packs. That is not a guarantee that stutter is gone. - A locked 60 frames per second is not guaranteed. The first visit to a new effect can pause the picture while shaders compile. - Post-race replay has been reported with several overlaid copies of the scene, and replay controls have been reported missing. Those reports are still open. - Returning to the main menu after a race has once shown the menu scene's glowing paper windows and lanterns as flat bright yellow. It did not happen again on a repeat of the same steps. A render-target slot reused after the race is suspected; the report is open. - The keyboard is used when no controller is connected. Some assignment-page text still names PlayStation buttons. - Only the US disc build BCUS98158 v03.00 is supported. The measurement record is [docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md). For a bug report, enable **F1 → DEBUG → Debug export** before the fault, then use **F3 → Export debug report** (or **F8** while F3 is open) and attach the ZIP from `logs/debug/`. ## Building from source The supported way to play is the release ZIP above. A source build targets the same disc executable, BCUS98158 v03.00. You need your own dump, Windows 10/11 x64, Visual Studio 2022 (C++ workload), LLVM 18+ (`clang-cl`), CMake 3.20+, Ninja and Python 3.10+. `python scripts/setup_runtime.py` prepares the pinned ps3recomp checkout. Per-build addresses live in [config/targets.json](config/targets.json). The integration notes are [docs/ps3recomp-upgrade.md](docs/ps3recomp-upgrade.md). Packaging the player ZIP is [docs/player-setup.md](docs/player-setup.md). From a dump of your own disc: ```bash python scripts/setup_runtime.py T=../ps3recomp-gt5p-v018/tools rpcs3 --decrypt /PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EMAIN.SELF # writes EMAIN.elf beside it cp /PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EMAIN.elf input/EMAIN.ELF mkdir -p input/pkg && cp -r /PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO /PS3_GAME/USRDIR input/pkg/ echo BCUS98158 > input/target python scripts/jumptables.py --write python $T/find_functions.py input/EMAIN.ELF --json --seed-json config/extra_seeds_bcus98158.json --output analysis/functions.json python -c "import json; f=json.load(open('analysis/functions.json')); json.dump([x for x in f if int(x['start'],16) < 0xE3EC24], open('analysis/functions_code.json','w'))" PYTHONPATH=$T python scripts/gen_hle_stubs.py input/EMAIN.ELF analysis/hle_stubs.json python $T/ppu_lifter.py input/EMAIN.ELF --functions analysis/functions_code.json --output generated --code-end 0xE3EC24 --header-name ppu_recomp.h --source-name ppu_recomp.c --hle-stubs analysis/hle_stubs.json python scripts/setjmp_patch.py python scripts/spin_patch.py python scripts/ui_mask_patch.py python $T/gen_hle_nids.py --all --out src/gen/ppu_hle_nids.cpp scripts/build.cmd -DGT5P_TARGET=BCUS98158 ``` Generated sources stay in gitignored `generated/`. 1440626866.readme_excerpt:
# sys3xx-recomp

Native Windows ports of **Namco System 357 / 369** arcade games (the PS3-based boards), made by
static recompilation: the game's PPU and SPU code is lifted to C/C++ and built against the
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/soyjxck/ps3recomp) runtime, plus a layer for what the arcade
board adds around the PS3 (I/O board, USB key, operator settings, the TeknoParrot dump layout).

No game data is included or downloaded. You need your own dump of each game.

## Games

| Game | id | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Tekken 6 | `t6` | Playable: attract, movies, coin-up, fights at ~61 fps, sound, 4:3, config tool |
| Tekken 6: Bloodline Rebellion | `t6br` | Playable: attract, movies, fights at 52-61 fps, sound, motion blur, 4:3, config tool |
| Tekken Tag Tournament 2 / Unlimited | | Not started |
| Dragon Ball Zenkai Battle Royale | | Not started |
| Razing Storm, Deadstorm Pirates Special, Dark Escape 4D, Sailor Zombie | | Not started (light-gun I/O) |
| Taiko no Tatsujin (all colours), Wadaiko Master | | Not started (drum I/O) |

Per-game details, decisions and known issues: `games/<id>/NOTES.md` and `games/<id>/README.txt`.

## Layout

```
ps3recomp/        the PS3 runtime (vendored copy, see Credits): recompilers, lv2, SPURS, RSX, codecs
core/             the arcade layer, shared by every game: launcher, I/O board (USIO/cellUsbd),
                  movies (cellPamf/cellDmux), settings, main loop, profiler
config/           config.exe (resolution, 4:3, controls, controllers)
games/<id>/       one profile per game:
  game_profile.h    exe, title, SELF, boot args, USB serial, 4:3 addresses, runtime switches
  game.env          what the scripts need: code end, lift hooks, SPU job source, bench input
  patches.cpp       native replacements for a few lifted functions (USB key checks)
  local.env         (yours, not committed) GAME_DUMP=<folder that holds dev_hdd0>
tools/            per-game scripts: lift, lift_spu, build, run, fightbench, package
work/<id>/        (generated) extracted ELF, lifted code, build, logs
```

## Building a game

Windows, with clang-cl + [xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin) (no Visual Studio), CMake,
Ninja, Python 3, and the FFmpeg shared build (for movies). Paths are set in `tools/build.sh`.

```
git clone --recursive <this repo>
python -m venv .venv
echo GAME_DUMP="D:/dumps/Tekken6" > games/t6/local.env    # the folder with dev_hdd0

tools/lift.sh t6         # PPU -> work/t6/recompiled   (extracts the ELF from the dump first)
tools/lift_spu.sh t6     # SPU thread images + SPURS jobs -> work/t6/spu
tools/build.sh t6        # -> work/t6/build/t6.exe + config.exe
tools/run.sh t6 60       # dev run, log in work/t6/out/run/latest.log
tools/package.sh t6      # -> dist/t6/: t6.exe, config.exe, FFmpeg DLLs, README
```

The packaged `<id>.exe` needs no arguments: it finds the dump (a `game` folder next to it, or
`[Paths] Game=` in `<id>.ini`), extracts the ELF into `cache/`, and starts.

## Adding a game

Copy a profile (`games/t6br/` is the most complete), then fill it in as you go:
the SELF name and boot args (from the TeknoParrot profile or the game's argument table), the
code end and any USB-key hooks (`game.env`, `patches.cpp`), the SPURS job binaries
(`SPU_JOBS`), and runtime switches the game needs (`GAME_ENV_DEFAULTS`). The notes of the two
Tekken 6 ports record how each of those was found.

## Credits and license

`ps3recomp/` is a copy of [ps3recomp](https://github.com/soyjxck/ps3recomp) by Ned Heller
(sp00nznet), soyjxck and its other contributors, taken at upstream commit `018024d`, plus the
changes this project needed (SPURS job-chain parking and queues, GPU-side NV3089 blits, the
cellVdec lock, the SPURS watchdog). It stays under its own MIT license, `ps3recomp/LICENSE`.

The I/O board details and several library function names come from
[RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (GPLv2). Everything else in this repository is
released under the GNU General Public License v2, see `LICENSE`.

1440788630.readme_excerpt:
# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível e à primeira luta contra um chefe, mas ainda lento (~18-23 fps no nível, 13-21 na luta). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot à primeira luta contra um chefe:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~50-55 fps; o primeiro nível a ~22-27 fps, conforme a cena (era ~9); a luta contra o chefe a 13-21. Atrasando um thread de cada vez e medindo quanto o quadro atrasa junto, o limite hoje é o thread que executa os comandos de vídeo (o RSX do RPCS3) e o thread principal do jogo, não as SPUs nem a placa de vídeo. Partes pesadas das SPUs já rodam como código nativo, cada uma conferida contra o original: a geometria por draw (índices, skinning, normais e tangentes) e o pós-processamento que suaviza as bordas da imagem. O foco agora é deixar o jogo mais leve para processadores comuns: o uso total de CPU já caiu ~10% (de 7,2 para 6,4 núcleos no menu) sem perder fps, e o próximo passo é a espera pelas consultas de oclusão (ZCULL) no thread do RSX. Esses números são de um Ryzen 5 5600G com uma RX 7600; num Ryzen 7 9800X3D com uma RX 9070 XT (RSX do RPCS3, Vulkan), o jogo chega a 60 fps fora das lutas e cai para cerca da metade nelas. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); e o jogo às vezes trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`). - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md).

## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), instale o launcher pelo `AscensionLauncher__x64-setup.exe` das [releases](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/releases) e, na primeira vez, aponte a pasta `ascension` em **Avançado › Pasta do jogo**. Ele se atualiza sozinho quando sai uma versão nova.

JOGAR abre o jogo; o launcher se esconde até ele fechar. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

> **Goal:** Turn the legendary PS3 racing sim into a true native PC port — higher performance potential, full moddability, and long-term preservation.

![GT6PP bring-up status](docs/progress.svg)

*Source: `docs/progress.svg`*

---

## Why this exists

Gran Turismo 6 is one of the best racing games ever made. RPCS3 already runs it well, but **static recompilation** is a different approach:

| | RPCS3 (emulator) | GT6PP (static recomp) |
|---|---|---|
| **How it runs** | Interprets/JITs PowerPC + SPU at runtime | Translates the game to C++ **ahead of time** |
| **Performance** | Good, but always pays emulation tax | Native code — no translation overhead |
| **Modding** | Limited | Full source-level access once lifted |
| **Requirements** | High-end PC recommended | Potentially much lighter once polished |
| **Approach** | One binary, many games | Deep per-game port |

This project uses [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) to lift GT6's PPU/SPU code into native C++ and link it against a clean-room HLE runtime + D3D12 backend.

**You must own the game.** This repo contains **zero** game data, keys, or generated binaries.

## Architecture

GT6PP is a **static recompilation**, not an emulator:

1. **Lift** - `ps3recomp` translates GT6's PPU (PowerPC) code into C++ (`gt6/generated/`).
2. **HLE runtime** - PS3 OS services (threads, lwcond, file I/O, RSX) are reimplemented as native C++ in `third_party/ps3recomp` and `gt6/src/`.
3. **PFS cache** - GT6's proprietary file system is served from a host cache seeded from your own `GT.VOL`.
4. **RSX -> D3D12** - the PS3 graphics command stream is replayed through a D3D12 backend.

Key entry points:
- `gt6/src/main.cpp` - host entry, window, D3D12 setup
- `gt6/src/stubs.cpp` - HLE overrides, boot tracing, project pump
- `gt6/generated/ppu_recomp_*.cpp` - lifted game code (regenerated by relift)

## Quick start

### Requirements
- Your own **Gran Turismo 6** disc (USA `BCUS98296` v1.00 recommended)
- Windows 10/11 x64
- CMake, Ninja, [LLVM-MinGW](https://github.com/mstorsjo/llvm-mingw)
- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) cloned into `third_party/ps3recomp`

### Build
```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\build-gt6.ps1
```

### Run
1. Place your disc files under `PS3-Version/Gran Turismo 6 (USA) (En,Ja,Fr)/PS3_GAME/`
2. Extract `GT.VOL` to `work/gt6_vol/` (use the included tools)
3. Launch:

```powershell
$env:GCM_GUEST_FB="0,1280,720,6144"
$env:PPU_STUCKMAX="1000000"
gt6\build\gt6.exe work\bin\EMAIN.elf
```

Console = log. Separate window = game framebuffer.

1494c0aa6bc7e624fa6651ce0e2c438127534416.message:
Faster frame chain for 100+ fps: core pinning, PPU SIMD flags, cheaper SPU-line stores

- The game pins itself to the CPU's biggest L3 on multi-CCD CPUs (the
  V-Cache die on X3D parts): the HighGraphics <-> SPU dispatcher hand-offs
  stop crossing dies. Busy Valley spot at 100 fps: 77 -> ~90 fps.
  DES_AFFINITY=0 = off.
- Lifted PPU code built with SSE4.1 (+ AVX2/FMA with DS_AVX2), no stack
  cookies, -ffp-contract=off (results unchanged: VMX fast-vs-scalar test
  0 mismatches in 16 M ops). ~+4%.
- PPU stores to SPU-reserved lines visit only SPUs that may hold the line
  (held-line table) and no longer break other PPU threads' reservations
  there; SPU writes still do. Store path 16.9% -> 7.6% of HighGraphics.
  Two review rounds; runtime coherency unit test 195/195.
- Guest function-pointer calls take a fast path with a per-thread lookup
  cache when no debug switch is set.
Details and measurements: docs/NOTES.md fixes 65-68.

5be2eb389d35b50ea9cdb2baa01fd2dc98b9f96b.message:
Latria 4-2 53.5 -> 55.7 fps on a 5800X: the SPU dispatcher's no-op PUTLLC skips the lock-line lock

The command dispatcher pops each of ~1.8M commands a second with GETLLAR
of the queue's control line and a PUTLLC of the same, unchanged bytes.
That PUTLLC now goes through spu_wrch_light: with the data unchanged it
cannot change memory, so it succeeds iff memory still equals the
snapshot, ends PPU reservations first, consumes the reservation, runs
the commit hooks, and takes the lock and notifies only when another
holder or a watch could be on the line. Diagnostics, the barrier sync
watch, SPU_LOCKGUARD and SPU_COH_STATS keep the exact path;
DES_DISPQ_LIGHT=0 turns it off.

Fix flashing and wrong pictures at 2x and above (fix 104)

The scaled present (2x and up, or a resized / fullscreen window) draws the game's picture into the
window through a descriptor table taken from the per-frame SRV ring. After Present the render
thread only waits for the frame's own work, so the next frame's draws could overwrite that table
while the present was still queued on the GPU: it then shrank whatever texture a later draw had
put there. A test counter (LD_PRES_HAZARD=1) caught 8+ such overwrites in 80 s on the title.

The scaled present now has four descriptor tables of its own after the ring, used in turn
(LD_PRES_OWN=0 = the old behaviour). 1x was never affected (a plain copy).

Latria 4-2 52.3 -> 58.5 fps on a 5800X: the SPU dispatcher's per-command chain runs as one native loop

Each command HighGraphics posts to the SPU command dispatcher ran through
~15 small lifted functions (bookkeeping, GETLLAR, PUTLLC, the entry GET,
the cursor PUT, the jump table, and commands 7 / 8), each hop a lifted call
or tail call with the drain loop's bookkeeping around it. des_dispq_native
is those functions' own bodies copied statement for statement by a
generator, with only the transfers between them turned into gotos; every
channel and MFC operation is still spu_wrch / spu_rdch. It hands back
exactly where the lifted code transfers (every 256 commands, 3C90's rare
branches, the empty-queue wait, other handlers) and runs only while the
tail-call path would be taken anyway. DES_DISPQ_NATIVE=0 = lifted chain.

d7912b3cc41b5629a0745521d74d1c184a0713eb.message:
Pacing: guest clock locked to the display by the swap chain's vblank times (NOTES fix 133)

The vblank lock (fix 53) fitted the display grid from a thread woken by WaitForVBlank. Its
wake times are late by a varying amount (and the call spins on Windows 11 26300), so the fit
put a 60.002 Hz display at 60.004-60.030 Hz, the guest clock wandered, frames queued up to 3
deep and every change of depth was an 8.3 ms slip between game time and screen time
(PresentMon: present-to-display latency 16 -> 49 ms in tick-sized steps).

After each Present the fit now takes IDXGISwapChain::GetFrameStatistics (SyncRefreshCount,
SyncQPCTime) as its sample; the WaitForVBlank thread parks while they come and takes over
again without them. New series on DISJOINT or a sample that does not match the refreshes
counted; tearing (VRR) presents keep the old source. LD_VBLANK_STATS=0 = the old source.

User's walk with PresentMon: slips 16 in 158 s -> 8 in 191 s, queue-depth changes 26 -> 3.3
a minute, "felt better for sure". Test kit 1-1: 14 / 2 -> 3 / 2 / 1 dropped frames. Latria

1440988244.readme_excerpt:
# Demon's Souls — native PC port (ps3recomp)

A native Windows build of **Demon's Souls** (PS3, USA, **BLUS-30443**). The game's PPU and SPU code is statically
recompiled to C/C++ with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) and runs as a normal x64 program
on a PS3 runtime and a Direct3D 12 renderer. It is not an emulator.

> **No game files are included.** This repo holds only tools, patches and build scripts. SETUP builds the game
> on your PC from **your own disc image**.

**Community Discord:** [discord.gg/gTvrZZ75G](https://discord.gg/gTvrZZ75G) for questions, setup help and
screenshots. Bug reports with a REPORT.bat zip are best as a GitHub issue. Thanks to MrSuS60 for having me in their Discord, and a special thanks to zackage7 who has been an immense help in testing and polishing.

## Status

- **The whole game is playable**, with sound, music and movies, on keyboard + mouse or an Xbox controller.
- **60 fps** is recommended (50 on a 100 Hz screen). 30, uncapped and any custom rate work too. Above 60 fps
  there are still known bugs, such as the sound drifting out of sync.
- **No online play yet.** Multiplayer comes once the game is optimised.
- **Performance:** mostly smooth on high-end PCs; work on lower-end PCs and the Steam Deck is ongoing. The full
  development log is [docs/NOTES.md](docs/NOTES.md).

Hit a stutter or crash? Press **F8** when it happens and run `REPORT.bat` afterwards
([details](#reporting-stutters-and-crashes)).

## What you need

- **Windows 10/11 x64** with a **Direct3D 12** GPU. AVX2 is used if your CPU has it (Haswell / Ryzen or newer).
- About **14 GB** free disk space.
- **Your disc image** of Demon's Souls USA (BLUS-30443): a `.iso`, a Redump `.zip`, or a dumped folder with
  `PS3_GAME` in it. An encrypted image also needs its **disc key**: the `.dkey` file from the dump, or the
  "Disc Key" line on [Redump's page for this disc](http://redump.org/disc/16199/).
- **Nothing else.** SETUP downloads what is missing into `deps\`, with no installer or admin rights: portable
  Python and Git, the PS3 keys for `EBOOT.BIN` (from [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net)'s public source, kept in
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%`), and a portable LLVM compiler with Microsoft's SDK via
  [xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin). All downloads are checksum-verified. An existing Python 3.10+,
  Git, or Visual Studio 2022 (*Desktop development with C++*) + LLVM 17+ is used instead.
- A plain folder path: no `[ ]` or `&`.

**Linux / Steam Deck** and **macOS (Apple silicon):** see their install guides below
([Linux](#linux--steam-deck), [macOS](#macos-apple-silicon)).

## Build it (one time)

1. Download the newest **[release](https://github.com/timboat/demons-souls-recomp/releases/latest)** ZIP (or
   `git clone`) and unpack it, e.g. to `C:\Games\DemonsSouls`.
2. Start **`DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe`**, press **PLAY**, and answer **Yes** to run `SETUP.bat`.
3. Give it your disc image: drag it into the window and press Enter. If it needs the disc key, SETUP opens
   Redump's page; copy the "Disc Key" line and paste it with **Ctrl+V**. **Enter** takes the suggested
   answer to every other question.
4. Wait for **All done**, then press **PLAY**.

| step | what SETUP does | time* |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | extracts and decrypts the game files into `game/` | 2–5 min |
| 2 | decrypts `EBOOT.BIN` → `EBOOT.elf` and checks it is the tested version | seconds |
| 3 | fetches ps3recomp at the tested commit and applies this port's runtime patch | < 1 min |
| 4 | recompiles ~94,000 PPU functions + 12 SPU programs into `port/` | 2–4 min |
| 5 | applies this port's edits to the recompiled code | seconds |
| 6 | compiles `DemonsSoulsRecomp.exe` and the launcher | 10–30 min |

\* on a fast 16-core PC. The compiler's full output goes to `logs\build_last.txt`. If something fails, fix
what it says and run SETUP.bat again: finished steps are skipped.

### Linux / Steam Deck

The Windows build runs through Proton (Steam's compatibility layer), built on your PC from your disc image.
It plays on Ubuntu 24.04 and the Steam Deck; the Deck is not smooth yet and loads are slow. You need a
Vulkan GPU driver, about **25 GB** free, and an internet connection for the first run.

1. Download `DemonsSoulsRecomp-Setup-x86_64.AppImage`: GitHub → **Actions** → *Linux AppImage* → the newest
   run → **Artifacts** (a zip with the AppImage inside). Make it executable (`chmod +x`, or right-click →
   Properties → Permissions → *Is executable*). On a Steam Deck, do this in desktop mode.
2. Run it. It asks for your disc image (a file picker, or drag the file in), then the disc key if needed,
   and runs the same six steps as SETUP.bat into `~/DemonsSoulsRecomp` (`DS_HOME=/other/folder` puts it
   elsewhere, e.g. on an SD card). It asks before each download, including Microsoft's SDK license. The
   first build takes 10–30 minutes on a desktop and 1–2 hours on a Steam Deck.
3. It offers to start the game; the first start sets up Proton (a few hundred MB). To play later, run the
   AppImage again (it updates and rebuilds what changed) or `~/DemonsSoulsRecomp/linux/play.sh`.

Settings are the same switches as on Windows, e.g. `DES_FPS=60 ./DemonsSoulsRecomp-Setup-x86_64.AppImage play`
(a Steam Deck defaults to 30 fps). **Steam Deck game mode:** add `~/DemonsSoulsRecomp/linux/play.sh` as a
non-Steam game, with *Start in* set to `~/DemonsSoulsRecomp` and no forced Proton version. **From a git
checkout** instead: install Python 3.10+, git, and clang + lld 17 or newer, then run
`sh linux/setup.sh /path/to/image.iso` and `sh linux/play.sh`. Troubleshooting: [docs/LINUX.md](docs/LINUX.md).

### macOS (Apple silicon)

A native arm64 build on Metal (by erikomis). **It is playable, but very behind on updates:** most of the
Windows and Linux features are missing. The Mac version will be worked on once Windows and Linux are finished.
You need about **14 GB** free.

1. Install Apple's command-line tools (`xcode-select --install`), then with [Homebrew](https://brew.sh):
   `brew install cmake ninja sdl2 glslang spirv-cross ffmpeg python@3.12` (FFmpeg is for the movies).
2. Get this repo (`git clone`, or the release ZIP) and, in its folder, run
   `DES_ISO="/path/to/Demon's Souls (USA).iso" mac/install.sh`. A Redump image also needs
   `DES_KEY=<32 hex digits or the .dkey file>`. It extracts the game, decrypts the EBOOT, recompiles and
   builds; after a failure or a quit, run it again and it continues where it stopped.
3. Play with `mac/play.sh`. There is no on-screen keyboard yet: `DES_NAME=<name> mac/play.sh` names your
   character. `DES_FPS=30` gives the console's 30 fps (60 is the default).

`mac/launcher/` has a desktop app that does all of this without a terminal (see its README). Controls,
settings and what is still missing: [docs/MACOS.md](docs/MACOS.md).

## Updating

Press **Check for updates** in the launcher. It downloads the newest release (no Git needed), rebuilds what
changed and reopens. Your game files, saves and settings are kept. Tick **Keep my build after updates** (or
`set DES_NO_REBUILD=1`) to play your current build and rebuild later with `BUILD.bat`.

**Copies from before v2026.11.03.7**, once: unpack the newest release ZIP over your folder, replacing files,
then press Play.

## Play

Start **`DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe`** and press **PLAY**. It holds every option (frame rate, resolution, mods,
fullscreen, movies, god mode, recording, keys by letter, CPU pinning) and saves them in `launcher.ini`.
*Extra settings* takes any `NAME=value` switch from this page or from an issue. `--play` starts the game
straight away, for a shortcut. Without the launcher, set the switches before running `PLAY.bat`.

| launcher option | switch | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| *Frame rate* | `DES_FPS=30\|50\|60\|unlimited\|31-240` | Auto = an even rate for your screen: 60 on 60 / 120 / 240 Hz, 50 on 100 Hz, 72 on 144 Hz, 55 on 165 Hz, 75 on 75 Hz. Game speed is right at any rate. A rate that divides your refresh rate is perfectly even; others turn vsync off. |
| *My screen has G-Sync / FreeSync* | `DES_VRR=1` | lets a variable-refresh monitor follow the frames (vsync-off frames may tear, so the monitor shows each when it is ready); Auto is then 60 at any refresh rate. Leave it off on other screens: the picture would tear. |
| *Resolution* | `DES_RES_SCALE=1.25\|1.5\|2\|3\|4` | renders above 1280x720: 1.25 = 1600x900, 1.5 = 1920x1080 (a 1080p screen), 2 = 2560x1440; *Sharper shadows* = `LD_RES_SCALE_SHADOW=1` |
| *Game* | `DES_GAME=game_remaster` / `game_mod`, `DES_BOSS_RUSH=1` | the PC Remaster mod, your imported models (see below), or [boss rush mode](#boss-rush-mode) |
| *Dump textures* | `LD_TEX_DUMP=1` | saves every texture drawn, for texture packs |
| *Skip the intro* | `DES_SKIP_INTRO=1` | starts at PRESS START; story movies still play |
| *Keep my build after updates* | `DES_NO_REBUILD=1` | plays your current build instead of rebuilding |

Other switches: `DES_MOVIES=0` skips movies, `DES_CUT_BLEND=0` restores the original 30 fps cutscene camera,
`DES_FULLSCREEN=1` starts fullscreen.

### Controls

An Xbox (XInput) controller works when plugged in. A DualShock / DualSense needs Steam Input or DS4Windows.
Keyboard + mouse work alongside a controller; whichever you touch last takes over.

| key | action |
|---|---|
| WASD | move |
| mouse (or IJKL) | camera (click into the game to capture the mouse) |
| left mouse / Shift | attack (R1) / strong attack (R2) |
| right mouse / Ctrl | block (L1) / parry (L2) |
| Space | roll / dash / back (Circle) |
| E | interact / confirm (Cross) |
| F / R | two-hand (Triangle) / use item (Square) |
| Tab / middle mouse | lock on (R3) |
| arrows | d-pad (switch items) |
| Enter / Backspace | Start / Select |
| Esc or F1 | release the mouse (close the game with the X or Alt+F4) |
| Alt+Enter / F11 | borderless fullscreen |
| F9 | god mode (no death, HP/MP/stamina stay full) |

- **Menus:** the mouse is a pointer. Hover selects, left click confirms, right click goes back, the wheel
  scrolls, and side buttons or PageUp / PageDown are L1 / R1. `DES_POINT=0` turns pointing off;
  `PAD_MENU_MOUSE=0` turns the mouse off in menus.
- **Button icons** show keys or PS3 buttons depending on what you used last (`LD_TEX_KBM=0` = always PS3,
  `1` = always keyboard).
- **Mouse look** follows the game's invert options. `PAD_MOUSE_LOOK_SENS=0.0012` sets the sensitivity;
  `PAD_MOUSE_LOOK=0` restores the old stick-style mouse.
- **Keys go by position**, so AZERTY uses ZQSD. `PAD_KEYS_BY_LETTER=1` = by letter.
- **Change any key** in the launcher: **Controls**, click a slot, press the key or mouse button (right-click clears
  it). The button prompts and the title's *PRESS ENTER KEY* follow your keys.

Saves go to `gamedata/`, and logs to `logs/`; they grow ~600 MB an hour, and the previous run is kept.

### Boss rush mode

*Game: Boss rush* in the launcher (or `DES_BOSS_RUSH=1 linux/play.sh`; not on macOS yet). Make a new character:
you skip the tutorial and start in the Nexus in soul form, with 7,000 souls and every trader there. Boldwin also
sells every weapon and shield, every armour piece and ring, every upgrade material, Turpentine and Firebombs,
priced by tier: the best weapons 40,000-75,000, top armour sets 30,000-50,000, rings 5,000-50,000, and items normal
shops sell at their usual price, so a run's boss souls buy a build but not everything.
- **Pick a boss:** each world's archstone offers that world's next unbeaten boss and puts you at its fog gate.
- **After a kill:** the boss's archstone offers the next boss (*Fight the Tower Knight?*) or *Return to the Nexus?*
- **Dying:** you go back to the same boss's fog in body form.
- **The Nexial Binding** takes you back to the Nexus and keeps your souls (its description says so too).
- **The run** ends when King Allant dies; his fight and the ending are the game's own.
- **The timer** at the bottom of the screen appears once you are in the game. It starts at the first fog and pauses
  on loading screens, cutscenes and the title screen (and while the game is closed). Splits and the final time go to
  `bossrush\splits.txt` and `bossrush\results.txt`.
- **Boss rush souls** in the launcher (2x by default; `DES_BR_SOULS=2`, 3, 5 or 10): every enemy and boss gives that many times its
  souls. The timer shows *Souls x2* and so on when it is not 1x, so runs and videos say which they used.

It has its own saves in `bossrush\`, so your normal saves are never used. Play makes `game_bossrush\` from your
game files the first time, in seconds and with no extra disk space (again when you change the souls setting).

## Reporting stutters and crashes

Every run records frame timing (about 25 MB an hour, no visible cost; the last 10 sessions stay in `perf\`).

1. **Press F8** right after a stutter or slowdown. Each press marks that moment.
2. After quitting or a crash, press **Report a problem** in the launcher (or run **`REPORT.bat`**). It packs
   the session into one zip and opens GitHub's *New issue* page.
3. Pick the *Stutter / slowdown* or *Crash / bug* template, drag the zip in, and say where you were.

The zip holds a frame-pacing summary (`report.txt`), the recording (`perf.txt`), your system info
(`system.txt`) and the end of the game log (`log_tail.txt`). Your Windows user name is removed. Untick
*Record frame timing* (or `set DES_RECORD=0`) to play without recording.

## Mods (optional)

**PC Remaster mod** by fromsoftserve (Nexus Mods, Demon's Souls mod 106): download its zip, then run the line
below. It makes `game_remaster/` from hard links, so it uses no extra space and `game/` is unchanged.

```bat
.venv\Scripts\python tools\install_remaster.py "path\to\the mod.zip" --apply
```

**Texture packs:**
1. Tick *Dump textures* and play; textures land in `textures\dump\` as `<KEY>_<w>x<h>_<format>.png`.
2. Put an edited or larger file whose name starts with the same KEY in `textures\replace\`. `.dds` (DXT, BC7,
   BC4, RGBA) loads faster than PNG.

Details are in `textures\README.txt`.

**Models:**
- Export armour, weapons, characters or map pieces to glTF, edit them in Blender, and import them back.
- Import writes `game_mod\` from hard links; play it with *Game: My models*, and delete the folder to undo.
- Edit the `_l` low-detail copy too. Rules are in `models\README.txt`.

```
.venv\Scripts\python tools\flver_tool.py export game\PS3_GAME\USRDIR\PARTS\bd_f_5010.partsbnd.dcx
.venv\Scripts\python tools\flver_tool.py import models\BD_F_5010\edited.glb game\PS3_GAME\USRDIR\PARTS\bd_f_5010.partsbnd.dcx
```

Packs and models are the game's art; share them only where that is allowed.

## Repo layout

```
SETUP.bat / BUILD.bat        one-time setup / rebuild
DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe      the settings window (source in project/launcher/)
PLAY.bat / REPORT.bat        start the game / pack a bug report
setup/                       setup pipeline, toolchain finder, Linux cross toolchain
project/                     CMake project
patches/                     ps3recomp-local.patch (runtime, on ps3recomp @ 4e8f3ca) and lifted-code.patch (game code)
tools/                       disc extraction, SPU lifting, perf report, mod installer, model tool
docs/NOTES.md                development log: every fix, why, and how it was measured
linux/, mac/                 Linux / Steam Deck kit and macOS build (docs/LINUX.md, docs/MACOS.md)
```

Everything SETUP produces (`game/`, `port/`, `deps/`, `.venv/`, saves, logs) is git-ignored.
**Never commit or share those**: they are the game.

## Troubleshooting

- **"could not get the keys … using RPCS3 instead":**
  - The key download failed, so SETUP falls back to RPCS3; you can also run SETUP again later.
  - If RPCS3 then fails ("did not write EBOOT.elf"), close any open RPCS3 window and retry. Or decrypt
    `game\PS3_GAME\USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN` by hand with RPCS3's *Utilities → Decrypt PS3 Binaries*; install the
    firmware first if it asks.
  - In Windows Sandbox or a VM, RPCS3 can crash. Decrypt on another PC, copy `EBOOT.elf` into that folder,
    and rerun SETUP.
- **"EBOOT.BIN is not the tested one":** only the USA disc (BLUS-30443) is supported.
- **Build tools not found:** rerun SETUP or BUILD and allow the portable compiler download. Or install VS 2022
  Build Tools with C++ and LLVM (`winget install LLVM.LLVM`), or set `LLVM_DIR`.

1f3ef381a5862e8763a32748391814d080add700.message:
Vulkan: RGBA8 targets read as Y16_X16 converted on the GPU

SEGA Rally samples two 912x912 RGBA8 shadow targets as Y16_X16 ~3 times a
frame; each was a readback, a CPU decode and an upload. A new optional backend
hook, color_as_format, converts them in command order (rsx_vk_rgba8_y16x16.comp),
once per colour write. Race: no texture decoded per frame; 21 -> ~23 fps on
the dev box.

Vulkan: batch draws by default; fps, GPU-wait and texture-cache counters

A race ran at ~9 fps (5 on the Phoenix iGPU test box): the backend waited for
the GPU after every draw. VK_DRAW_BATCH=1 (now set by build_linux.sh and run.sh)
doubles that. PS3_FPS, VK_WAIT_STATS and ENG_TEX_STATS show where the rest goes.

445a390e44417adb5e957dc46b5bd611d10d29c0.message:
Vulkan: submit full batches and the present without waiting for the GPU

Three submission slots, each with its own command buffer, fence, part of the
batching rings and descriptor pool. A batch that fills up, and the batch before
a present, are submitted without a wait and recording goes on in the next slot;
a slot is reused after its fence signals. Every other submission still waits
for all slots. ZPASS counts are resolved per finished slot (the query pool is a
ring by sequence number), so reports no longer wait for a waiting flush.

Race: ~22.5 -> 30 fps (the game's cap) on the dev box, ~14.5 -> ~22.5 on the
Phoenix iGPU test box, which is now CPU-bound in the FIFO walker.

69844800402be27c2da619395ce08b58e4cdfb8b.message:
Audio without pops on slower CPUs, asynchronous present, vertex cache

Audio (#14): a 15-minute recording of the speaker output on the Ryzen
7840HS test box had ~490 pops a minute, all on 256-sample block
boundaries. Two causes, both in the mix rather than the device:

- The Linux mix thread mixed whenever SDL's queue had room, and SDL
  drains a device period (four blocks) at a time, so the game saw its
  block notifications in bursts and its MultiStream writer fell a lap
  behind its 8-block ring. The mixer now takes one block every 5.33 ms
  on the clock, steers the period by 2% towards PS3_AUDIO_BUF_MS, and
  rebases instead of bursting after a stall. A block the writer has not
  yet filled gets up to PS3_AUDIO_LATE_MS (default 4) to arrive.
- With even pacing, 20-35% of blocks were still empty during races:
  MultiStream's ATRAC decoder took 11-14 ms of host time per job on Zen
  4, against ~10.6 ms of real time per job. Its float ops were emulated
  bit-exactly (widened to double, SPU truncation, per-lane fixups; ~30
  instructions an op). The audio program and its run-time overlays now
  use the host's float ops (PORT_SPU_AUDIO_FAST_FLOAT, SPU_FLOAT_FAST in
  spu_helpers.h): 7.5 -> 3.6 ms per job on the dev box, and 0 late
  blocks on the test box. Output compared against the exact path: the
  aligned windows agree to ~97 dB.

Performance (#11): the Vulkan present waited for the GPU twice a frame
(the frame copy, then the window blit), so the FIFO walker sat idle
while the GPU drew. The window blit is now recorded into the present's
own submission and nothing waits; the readback completes at the next
present (VK_PRESENT_SYNC=1 restores the old behaviour). Race 42.5 -> 46
fps on the dev box; test box 15-minute median 35.8 -> 39.8. The converted-vertex
cache (ENG_VTX_CACHE, 0 mismatches in check mode) and building the whole
program for x86-64-v3 (inline FMA for the AltiVec helpers) add a little
more.

Diagnostics: AUDIO_RATE reports late-writer waits; SPU_MBOX_IDLE=1
reports how long each SPU waits for work

91d8669ce602b737d9dad575dd114188c236fa7f.message:
SPU groups: stop host threads before a group is reused or freed

sys_spu_thread_group_terminate only marked the group stopped and
group_destroy then freed the threads' contexts and local stores while their
host threads still ran on them. SEGA Rally destroys and recreates its SPU
groups at every track change, so its job workers kept polling in freed memory:
heap corruption (malloc aborts, a NULL ctx->ls in spu_indirect_branch, crashes
inside the Vulkan driver) a few track changes in. Terminate now stops the
threads (stop_request, honoured at the next channel read) and waits; destroy
frees only what no host thread still uses; group_start never re-initialises a
running context; a finishing thread no longer touches its context after
reporting it is done. 15 min of attract demo (16 track changes): no crash.

1440990932.readme_excerpt:
# SEGA Rally Online Arcade Recompiled (PS3)

Work in progress: static recompilation of **SEGA Rally Online Arcade** (PlayStation 3 PSN, SEGA 2011; NPUB30375,
content ID `UP0177-NPUB30375_00-SEGARALLYARCADE1`, update 1.01) to native PC, using
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp).

This is the PS3 release, not the Xbox 360 XBLA one, so it does not use the ReXGlue SDK like the After Burner
Climax and OutRun recomps. ps3recomp is much younger than ReXGlue: so far it boots titles to gameplay on
Windows only (Linux/macOS compile the per-game boot code but have not run a title from the upstream tree).

**No game data is included.** You need your own PSN package (`.pkg`) and license (`.RAP`).

Progress and known problems are tracked in the [issues](https://github.com/BitJager-dev/segarally-online-arcade-recomp/issues).

## Status
| Step | State |
|---|---|
| Extract the PKG (base + 1.01 update) | done: `tools/ps3_pkg_extract.py` |
| Decrypt `EBOOT.BIN` (retail NPDRM SELF, key rev 0x10 in 1.01) | done: `tools/ps3_unself.py` -> `game/EBOOT.elf` (PPC64, entry 0x5D26F0) |
| Analysis, function finding, PPU lift (`tools/recomp_pipeline.sh`) | done: 25,339 functions, 1,215 HLE handlers |
| Game project (CMake from ps3recomp's template), Linux build + test boot | builds (container); plays the intro movie, the menus and a full race with its replay (Vulkan, game shaders) |
| SPU programs | 6 of 6 lifted, plus the code the audio program loads at run time (below) |
| Audio | plays: the MultiStream SPU program, the ATRAC decoder it loads from `/dev_flash` (`flashATRAC.pic`) and three of the game's SPU images it swaps in are lifted at the addresses they run at (`tools/lift_spu_overlays.py`) |

## Building (Linux)
`tools/build_linux.sh` configures and builds `out/linux/segarally_online_arcade`, stages the game data as
`run/dev_hdd0/game/NPUB30375` (base + 1.01; `PS3_HDD0_ROOT`), and boots it for 60 s into `logs/boot.log`.
Needs clang, ninja, SDL2; install `vulkan-headers` for the Vulkan renderer (otherwise the headless null
renderer). `JOBS=` sets parallel compiles (default 6: each lifted file is ~600k lines).

Requirements to run: an x86-64 CPU with AVX2 (Intel Haswell / AMD Zen or later; the SPU code is built for
x86-64-v3, `PORT_SPU_X86_LEVEL`: with SSE4.2 only the audio mixer cannot keep up and the sound breaks up), a
Vulkan GPU, and your firmware's `/dev_flash` (below) for sound.

## Building in a container
`tools/docker_build.sh` builds in `docker/Dockerfile` (Arch, the same clang, glslang, SPIRV-Tools and SDL2 as the
CachyOS host) into `out/linux-docker`, then runs the test boot on the host, which has the GPU, display and controller.
The `xbla` folder is mounted at its own path and the container runs as you. `--no-run` builds only; `--shell` opens a
shell in the build environment. The image is rebuilt when the Dockerfile or ps3recomp's Python requirements change.

## Getting the ELF
`tools/setup_ps3.sh` does everything: it decrypts the 1.01 `EBOOT.BIN` with your `.RAP` (no RPCS3 needed; the
keys are read from RPCS3's open-source `key_vault.cpp`/`.h`, downloaded to `../deps/rpcs3src`, never stored here),
sets up ps3recomp's Python environment and runs `tools/recomp_pipeline.sh`. Log: `setup_ps3.log`.

Firmware: `tools/ps3_pup_devflash.py PS3UPDAT.PUP ../deps/ps3fw/root --keys ../deps/rpcs3src` installs `/dev_flash`
(same RPCS3 key source as the EBOOT); `build_linux.sh` uses it when present, and the build lifts the audio
decoder from it (without it there is no sound).

`USRDIR/KEY.EDAT` is NPDRM-encrypted data the game reads at runtime; the port's `cellFs`/EDAT layer has to
decrypt it with the same license.

## Layout
| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `tools/ps3_pkg_extract.py` | Retail PS3 PKG extractor (AES-128-CTR; the package key is read from RPCS3's `key_vault.h`; system `cryptography` module) |
| `tools/ps3_unself.py` | NPDRM SELF -> ELF with the title's RAP (port of RPCS3's `unself.cpp`; keys loaded from RPCS3's source at run time) |
| `tools/ps3_pup_devflash.py` | `/dev_flash` from an official `PS3UPDAT.PUP` (port of RPCS3's firmware installer) |
| `tools/setup_ps3.sh` | One-shot setup: decrypt, Python environment, pipeline |
| `tools/recomp_pipeline.sh` | ps3recomp phases 3-5: ELF/imports, functions, SPU images, PPU lift |
| `tools/lift_spu_overlays.py` | Lifts the code the MultiStream audio program loads at run time, at the addresses it runs at (run by CMake) |
| `patches/` | ps3recomp fixes for this title (against ps3recomp `4e8f3ca`), applied by `build_linux.sh`: lifting SPU programs with data in their code and calls into run-time code (`--runtime-code`, `spu_lifter --external-calls`), lifted run-time overlays checked against local store (`spu_overlay_register_static`), real-time audio mixing on Linux (one block every 5.33 ms on the clock, a few ms of patience for a late writer, `PS3_AUDIO_BUF_MS`), native float ops for the audio SPU program's ATRAC decoder (`PORT_SPU_AUDIO_FAST_FLOAT`, twice as fast; the exact SPU rounding left a Ryzen 7840HS decoding ~80% of real time), a present that no longer waits for the GPU (the walker records the next frame meanwhile; `VK_PRESENT_SYNC=1` for the old wait), a converted-vertex cache (`ENG_VTX_CACHE`), blocked event waits deliver GCM callbacks (Linux), SPU group thread slots, answers for a stopped audio SPU, Vulkan 3D textures, ZPASS pixel counts (occlusion queries), a window swapchain on Wayland drivers that list over 64 surface formats (RADV), a flip-time ring wrap that no longer overwrites commands the GPU has not read, flips that complete one at a time after the GPU has run past them (the main loop no longer needs `EVT_RECV_KICK`), cellVoice notify queues (its thread blocks instead of spinning), SPU job workers that back off while they poll an unchanged line (`SPU_POLL_SPIN`), `sys_mempool_*`, `cellUsbdRegisterExtraLdd2`, `UTF8stoUCS2s` and the sceNp custom-menu calls (registered in `stubs.cpp`, since the NID generator only picks up cell*/sce*/sys* names) |
| `tools/docker_build.sh`, `docker/Dockerfile` | Container build environment |
| `game/` | Your decrypted `EBOOT.elf` (not in git) |
| `analysis/`, `generated/` | Pipeline output (not in git). The HLE NID table is generated by CMake in the build tree, so new handlers in ps3recomp are picked up on the next build |

Expected next to this folder: `../deps/ps3recomp` (toolkit checkout), `../deps/ps3-venv` (its Python deps),
`../deps/segarally_ps3/{pkg,game,update}` (your package and its extracted files).

## Disclaimer
Unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by SEGA or Sony. Contains no game data.

01a14065d9fd886e51d5aac6ecf9692415877914.message:
rsx: the pipeline index, pipelines a title asks for, built ahead

A first start still waits on the graphics driver for each new pipeline,
7-20 ms where the driver has not seen the shaders. The pipeline library
and its manifest only know what this PC's game drew before.

The pipeline index is a list a title keeps of the pipelines its players'
games asked for: each one's two guest programs as code fingerprints, and
the draw state vp_get_fp_pso keys a pipeline by. A fingerprint cannot be
turned back into a program, so the list holds nothing of the game's.

- Recording: every pipeline a draw asks for is a row. Rows the cache has
  not seen go to pso_index_seen.tsv in the shader cache, off the render
  thread.
- Building: rsx_shader_precompile_index takes a list. After the queued
  programs, the decompile thread finds each row's programs by their
  fingerprints (rsx_d3d12_program_hash64), makes their texts as a draw
  does (each once) and queues them for the cache. The backend builds the
  rows the library lacks once the manifest's startup build is done, on as
  many threads, below normal priority, in the list's order.
- A build through the whole list writes the list's hash to
  pso_index.built, so a later start skips the list
  (rsx_shader_precompile_index_built). A new library removes it.
- vp_get_fp_pso's description block is vp_fp_desc, shared by both, so a
  pipeline built ahead has the name a draw looks up.
- cellGame_get_app_ver: PARAM.SFO's APP_VER, for the game version a list
  is kept for.

PS3_PSO_INDEX=0 turns recording and building off.

Demon's Souls, a scripted Tutorial route from a first start: 161
pipelines compiled in play without a list; with the 161 rows that run
recorded, all 161 found and built (134 ms with the driver's cache warm)
and loaded, and 6 compiled (pipelines the first walk did not meet).

08cff3eb84efc2fd3c22811bb5632c00f0d5f0e6.message:
platform: plat.h's threads and events, and the SPU job pool on every platform

The async SPU job pool was Windows-only. Off Windows every async job
created a detached pthread with a 256 MB stack and let it exit:
Demon's Souls runs about 650 of them a second, so Linux and macOS paid a
thread start, a cold stack and cold caches per job.

runtime/platform/plat.h is the start of the platform module: detached
threads with a stack reservation, the stack guarantee, the calling
thread's stack range, an auto-reset event with a timed wait, and a small
mutex. On Windows each call is the Win32 call it stands for, inline;
off Windows it is pthreads directly (plat_posix.c), not the Win32 shim.

The pool moves to runtime/spu/spu_async_pool.c, written once on plat.h,
with the same rules: no queue and no cap, idle workers exit after 5 s or
at once beyond 64 idle, image 22 gets its own thread, SPU_ASYNC_POOL=0
makes a thread per job. On Windows the worker and the dispatch make the
same Win32 calls in the same order; the job now runs through one
function call instead of being inlined into the worker. Linux and macOS
also run the stack-range forget calls after each job now, as Windows did.

0947a82e8010c7a9a975cc0022fdf78e1faaef69.message:
video: HDR output (RSX_HDR) and the game's own highlights

RSX_HDR=1 (default 0, live): while the window's display has HDR on in
Windows, the swap chain is FP16 scRGB and the blit maps the game's
picture into it: gamma 2.2 (RSX_HDR_GAMMA=1: the sRGB curve), white at
Windows' SDR white level (RSX_HDR_WHITE), brighter values rolled off
towards the display's peak (RSX_HDR_PEAK). The display is asked again
when the window is activated, the display setup changes or the window
moves. A swap chain that refuses scRGB stays RGBA8. Off Windows
(vkd3d) the display always reads as SDR.

RSX_HDR_SCENE_FP=<fp>[:<limit>] names the program that clamps the
finished scene. While HDR is on:
- the scene target the display copy samples, and the targets it is
  copied into after that program, are FP16 (written back to guest
  memory in the title's format);
- that program clamps at its limit instead of 1;
- draws into other targets read them clamped to 1, as their 8-bit
  format held them (Demon's Souls' display copy looks the scene up in a
  table whose sampler wraps: 1.3 read 0.3);
- the blit adds what the scene target holds above 1.
Each variant's compile is logged once.

rsx_d3d12_hdr() gives the menus the paper white, and
rsx_d3d12_back_buffer_format() follows the swap chain. RSX_HDR_SNAP=
<file> writes the swap chain buffer once, raw, for checks.

With HDR off nothing changes: the swap chain stays RGBA8, and every
pipeline key and shader is as before.

18075dc500c3ec4f69217ed177fa375608e86d77.message:
spu: the ring post's prologue stores in straight line

The native ring post (ring_post_run, image 2's 0x4808-0x4818) writes the
13 quadwords 0x3C90's prologue stores into the SPU frame, then the segment
quadword. It did so in a loop over k_post_slot / k_post_reg through
spu_ls_write128, which reloaded ctx->ls and tested the LS-probe flag for
each one, every command: 3.9% of image 2 in an instruction profile of the
deep Palace, the largest single piece of ring_loop.

Now they are 14 straight stores (ls_put128): the same bytes, in the same
order, at the same addresses. Both callers run the post only while
g_spu_ls_dbg is 0 (spu_hook_ring_post's entry test, ring_loop's
loop_yield), and sp has passed the frame checks, so every slot is in local
store and no probe has to see the stores.

SPU_POST_FAST (live): 1 (default) the straight stores; 0 the table loop as
before; 2 the straight stores, then every slot checked against the table
loop's bytes (no check covered these slots: SPU_NATIVE_POST=2 checks the
recorded path, SPU_NATIVE_LOOP=2 leaves the frame out).

Deep Palace, DES_FPS=unlocked, vsync off, knobab plain windows, on master
+ #157 + #158 + #159, session locked: SPU_POST_FAST=0 is 3.91% slower
(193.42 vs 201.28 fps, 4 boots, 12 pairs, p < 0.001), so about +4.1%.
soak.sh with SPU_POST_FAST=2: kept flipping for 6 minutes (43,007 flips by
361 s), 1,073,741,824 posts checked, 0 differ. regress.sh: 4 of 4 shots ok.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

1be0a91618a66be172d2dcf001f30794f2e1d806.message:
ppu: a run of frame saves shares one stack test

The lifter writes a store with base r1 as vm_write*_stk, which tests the
address against the stack limit, stores, and keeps a slow path behind
the test. A function's prologue is a run of such stores (Demon's Souls'
func_00CFEC70 saves 17 registers in a row), and each one reloads the
limit, r1 and vm_base, because the store before it, made through
vm_base, may alias any of them. That is about ten instructions a store.

ppu_lifter.py now writes a run of three or more of them (one store of a
GPR per line, nothing between them) under one test: vm_stk_run gives
the host address of the run's lowest byte when every byte it stores
would take vm_write*_stk's direct store, and the stores then go through
that pointer (vm_stk_put*, big-endian, as the direct store); otherwise
the run's lines run as before. In Demon's Souls' lift: 47,482 runs in
94,017 functions. With each run put back as its else block, every
function is the same as the lift before.

vm_stk_run reads its own limit, the third word on the armed flag's line
(game_module.c's copy too): the stack limit, or 0 while PPU_STK_RUN=0
(live), which sends every run through vm_write*_stk one by one. It reads
the limit once for the run where each store read it before. A first SPU
reservation of a stack line between the run's test and its stores is
missed, as a store that read the limit just before it already could.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

gpu: the Vulkan backend for the portable renderer's GPU layer

The GPU layer's second backend, beside D3D12's, built with

Windows and Linux; nothing changes with the HAL off).

- gpu_vk.c: the instance and device (Vulkan 1.3 with dynamic
  rendering, synchronization2, timeline semaphores and partially
  bound descriptors), adapter choice (WARP means a CPU device such as
  lavapipe), caps, handle tables, recorders, the timeline as every
  fence, submits, the fault report. RSX_VK_VALIDATION=1 turns the
  validation layer on; RSX_VK_MASK turns caps off to run fallbacks.
- gpu_vk_mem.c: buffers, host import, heaps and placed textures,
  D3D12's copyable footprints, first layouts, frees after a fence.
- gpu_vk_desc.c: views, samplers, table pools (one set per table),
  the memo, set 0's cache, empty entries (null descriptors, or 1x1
  textures without them).
- gpu_vk_pipe.c: layouts, pipelines (a fixed table: gpu_pipeline.v is
  its index + 1), the pipeline cache file.
- gpu_vk_swap.c: swap chains, presents (FIFO and IMMEDIATE, switched
  per present with swapchain_maintenance1), present_wait statistics,
  colour spaces and HDR metadata.
- gpu_vk_cmd.h: every command static inline onto the VkCommandBuffer
  through volk's device table; lazy passes; one bind of every set per
  draw.
- third_party/volk at the Vulkan SDK 1.4.363.0 pin, and the pinned
  Vulkan-Headers from cmake/gpu_deps.cmake.
- test_gpu_vk: test_gpu_d3d12's cases on Vulkan with the validation
  layer on (any message fails it), each fallback checked by its cap,
  the footprints against D3D12's, and the test's own HLSL compiled
  with glslangValidator (test_gpu_vk_spv.h says how).

Contract changes (gpu.h, gpu_cmd_ops.h; D3D12's numbers kept):
- swap_image_count and swap_image(d, sc, index): every swap chain
  image by index, valid until the next resize or destroy, for making
  the views up front (C1's gap). Vulkan may make more images than

1e8156fd4f0c576d31ea2b65954728d739e1aa23.message:
rsx: RSX_VP_BUFFERS=0 makes no vertex-program buffers

The D3D12 backend makes its four per-frame vertex-program buffers at
start: the vertex buffer (768 MB at the default size), the per-draw vertex
and fragment constants (264 and 80 MB) and the vertex fetch ring (128 MB),
1.2 GB of upload memory in all. A process that runs no game and draws only
its overlay never uses them. Demon's Souls' setup screens are one, and the
compile they run beside them is short of exactly that memory.

RSX_VP_BUFFERS=0 skips the four and says so. Only a frame with guest draws
uses them, and render_frame's vertex-program pass now checks for the
vertex buffer and the vertex constants, so a game started with the knob,
or one whose allocation failed, skips that pass instead of faulting.

253d83c5c244dcb67a0f021bca6a40dc7c64180a.message:
spu: image 2's empty ring waits on put alone before the lifted wait (SPU_RING_WAIT)

When the ring is empty, the fetch now reads only the producer's put word,
with a pause between reads that doubles up to SPU_RING_WAIT (default 16),
for up to 64 reads, and takes the command as soon as put moves. Then the
lifted wait runs as before. The lifted wait is a GETLLAR, the lock-line
event read and a GETLLAR again, back to back, each a copy or compare of
the control line, so every poll takes the line from HighGraphics, which
holds the frame in the deep Palace. The run's deferred state PUT goes out
before the wait, as on every way out of the loop. SPU_RING_WAIT=0 gives
the empty ring to the lifted code at once.

In the deep Palace, uncapped, in-boot A/Bs (4 boots, 12 pairs each): the
wait at 64 against none +0.7% (p 0.009, every boot), +1.8% on a build
where image 2 is faster (p < 0.001); 16 against 64 +1.1% (p 0.11) and
+1.4% (p 0.008), every boot in both batches; 64 against 256 +1.2%; 4 even
with 64. So the default is 16.

test_spu_ring_lazy varies the knob, moves put during some waits (at the
same read in both runs) and checks that the state is PUT before each wait.

  the last acquire gave (s_rc_image) and the slot the per-frame resources

2c05c6be3b5edf79f97d947d33c05a7588635068.message:
audio: one clock-paced mixer loop on every platform

Off Windows the mixer mixed a block, then slept 5 ms (2 ms with under
four blocks queued). A block is 5.33 ms of sound, so it made about 196
blocks a second for the device's 187.5, and SDL's queue has no bound: the
sound fell behind the picture by about 49 ms more every second (Demon's
Souls on Linux: 20-30 s after a few minutes, port issue #138).

The Windows loop's schedule now runs everywhere (audio_mix_loop): a block
every 5.33 ms by a monotonic clock, slip a block when the device has no
room, gain one when it is nearly empty. The clock and the wait are one
small function each per platform (mix_clock_ns, mix_wait_until). SDL's
room and starving checks follow the device's chunk (have.samples), the
same numbers as before at 256 frames; the device's spec is logged at open,
and AUDIO_RATE=1 works off Windows, with SDL's queue.

Measured: Linux (WSL, PulseAudio) 187.5-187.7 blocks/s with 11-16 ms
queued for 75 s of play, where the old loop's queue grew 49 ms a second;
Windows 187.5 blocks/s, nothing dropped.

30a2484c5aeb5d0e395bead5f9d9a90cc02f7e60.message:
rsxcore: the clamp in the vertex shader and D32S8 depth (step V5)

Two forms for GPUs that lack a feature, picked when the device is made
(rc_forms_pick). With neither knob set, on a device with geometry shaders
and D24S8, every changed line does what it did.

RSX_CLAMP_FORM=gs|vs (default gs where the device has GPU_CAP_GS): the
sprite-edge clamp without a geometry shader. Kind 4 of rsxc_shader.c
(rsxc_vs_inject_uvclamp; kinds 4 and 5 of rsxc_shader_hlsl, from kinds 0
and 2) renames the program's main and adds an entry point that runs the
program on all three corners of its triangle and hands the pixel shader
uvclamp_gs's bounds from every corner. The pixel shader is kind 3's, as
before. The frame's pre-pass writes a table of each clamp draw's corners
(uvc_table: three vertex numbers a triangle, in the order the input
assembler gives a geometry shader, after the frame's data in vp_vb or
vf_buf), and the draw loop draws it as a list of 3n vertices with t20 on
that ring. A program's kind 4 is made at its first clamp draw from a copy
of its bytes (VPVSEntry.vs4). vp_vb is a raw buffer too in that form.

RSX_DEPTH_FORMAT=d24s8|d32s8 (default d24s8 where the device has
GPU_CAP_D24S8): the depth buffer, the zeta surfaces, their depth read as a
texture and every pipeline's depth format are D32S8. No shader changes:
rsx_d2c rounds the sampled float to 24 bits, and nothing writes depth back
to guest memory.

With either form the pipelines are ones the d3d12 route never makes, so
none goes into pso_manifest.bin (that route's file too); the pipeline
library keeps them. copy_manifest.txt says what changed.

the HUD. RSX_AA=2 now runs SMAA 1x there instead, from the reference

3cd463b960a5cbf768cbc2c6bf3a11930d7d56f4.message:
spu: the stripe lock takes one line's stripe in line (SPU_LL_ONE_LINE)

Every guest store into a reserved line takes and releases that line's
stripe (spu_lockline_lock_ea, spu_lockline_unlock_ea). In Demon's Souls the
HighGraphics ring's producer makes about 5 million of those stores a second,
and almost all of them stay inside one 128-byte line. Yet each one paid for
the general case:

- spu_ll_set's walk over the lines a range touches, which clang vectorizes,
  so both functions saved five xmm registers on entry (Win64 makes xmm6-15
  callee-saved) and restored them on the way out;
- spu_ll_acquire's frame for the lock statistics (a stack cookie, the
  pushes), with the statistics off.

That was most of the lock's time outside its two locked instructions.

Now a range in one line takes its stripe in line: a lock bts, and the
lock inc to release it. The rest (a stripe that is held, ranges over several
lines, SPU_LOCKLINE_STATS) goes to out-of-line functions with the old code,
so their frames are paid only there. Both paths take the same stripes in
the same order, so SPU_LL_ONE_LINE (live; 0 sends everything through the
out-of-line paths, for A/B) can change between a lock and its unlock.

requests to the sign-in server's address and psnr's connection go over

the roots built in (Let's Encrypt's ISRG Root X1 and X2, Root YE and YR)
or to PS3_NET_CA_FILE's, and carry the server's name (PS3_NET_SIGNIN's
host, or PS3_NET_TLS=<name>). TLS 1.2 at least. A connection that can't
be made secure isn't made: the reason is logged, and the sign-in leaves
one notice for the host to show. psnr's relay streams and P2P traffic
are unchanged.

libs/network/ps3_tls.c wraps mbedTLS 3.6 (previous commit) with its
default configuration. That configuration has no threading, so every
call into it is made under one lock; sockets are non-blocking while TLS
runs on them and the waits (poll) happen outside the lock.

3dad7c22a19862061252ae772e511fb6ea4c8e78.message:
input: RPCS3's squircling for host sticks (PAD_STICK_SQUIRCLE)

RPCS3 turns a modern pad's stick into the PS3's bytes in two steps: the
radial deadzone, then squircling, which stretches the round range toward
the DualShock 3's square one (full diagonal 0.80 a side with a factor of
8000, instead of 0.71 on the circle). We had the deadzone only. Every pad
in RPCS3 but the DualShock 3 is squircled, so this was the one place where
the stick a game reads here differed from RPCS3's.

pad_stick_to_u8 takes the factor (/1000, 0 off). The DualSense and
DualShock 4 over HID, XInput and SDL pads all read PAD_STICK_SQUIRCLE,
default 8000 (the factor in RPCS3's older profiles; 4000 in newer ones).
Without squircling, a push past the circle now keeps its length, as RPCS3
keeps it, instead of being pulled onto the circle. The direction never
changes either way.

401745ab779c2240e43b13968caf313dba90f317.message:
cellAudio: libmixer's notify key when cellSurMixerStart beats its mixer thread

libmixer (a static library, so the title's own code) registers its surround
mixer with cellAudioSetNotifyEventQueue from cellSurMixerStart. The key it
passes is the one its mixer thread, _cellsurMixerMain, stores just before it
creates its queue. On a PS3 that thread (priority 400) runs before its
creator reaches Start. Here both run at once, and Start can read the key
before the thread has stored it, so it passes 0. Nothing is ever notified
then: the mixer never mixes, and the whole session has no sound.

In Demon's Souls about one start in two had no sound at all. Its sound
streams never play out, so after a trip from Boletarian Palace back to the
Nexus no new stream can start: no music, and NPC lines skip by at once
(docs/116 in the port).

With key 0 while _cellsurMixerMain is alive, register the key that thread
uses (0x8000CAFE02460300). The notify looks the queue up by key at each
block, so the key can be registered before the queue exists. A runtime
helper, ppu_thread_named, answers whether the thread is there. RPCS3
handles the same race in its cellAudio.

46d8358c31d37d6dff2e3b4aae286a308b1fd8ba.message:
spu: give MFC slots back when a job's context ends; 64 slots

The MFC engine table had 8 slots, and only a raw SPU thread gave its slot
back. Every SPURS job and async-worker job runs on a stack-local context,
and each one that did a DMA kept a slot after it returned. Demon's Souls
filled the table within seconds ("[SPU] more than 8 contexts hold an MFC
engine at once" in nearly every log), and from then on every new context
shared one fallback engine, unlocked, and took the claim lock exclusively
on every channel access, since its thread's cached slot never matched.

The job paths (spu_run_lifted_job_abi, spu_run_lifted_job_img,
spu_run_spurs_job) now release their context's slot next to its
lock-line unregister, and spu_async_run_one gives back any slot on the
worker's stack after a job, as it does for the lock-line set, logging
what it finds (at most 16 lines). spu_mfc_release skips the lock when the
context holds no slot. The table has 64 slots; a lookup scans it only
when its thread's cached slot misses.

46e46ec1bbf913d54d14d82f7d51941bfe9a1336.message:
spu: a cheaper DMA fast path and ring fetch for image 2

Demon's Souls' image 2 (the HighGraphics ring consumer) sets the frame in
the deep Palace now: 20 ns added per ring command cost 15% of the frame
rate. About half its time was small runtime helpers, most of it call
overhead, a lookup or a stall per DMA rather than work.

- mfc_for's slot check is inline; the search and the claim stay out of line.
- spu_wrch runs mfc_fast_xfer itself for a plain GET or PUT, with the rest
  of mfc_submit behind a call.
- mfc_repeat_check keeps its count in the MFC engine (one per context, as
  the per-thread count was) instead of three TLS variables.
- Whole-quadword transfers up to 256 bytes are copied inline, not through
  memcpy.
- The PUT path's per-line coherence check is inline, the same two loads
  ppu_loader.cpp already inlines.
- The ring fetch works its registers out in locals and only stores them.
  Stored a word at a time and read back whole, they could not be forwarded
  from the store buffer.
- No /GS cookie checks on the hot path. A u128 argument, a result through a
  pointer or a byte array on the stack each gave a function one:
  - the LS write probe gets the stored bytes, not the quadword, which takes
    the check out of every lifted region that inlines spu_ls_write128;
  - mfc_fast_xfer returns its result;
  - the hooks write channels through spu_wrch_word;
  - the overlay dump is out of line behind a gate in spu_overlay_note_get.

The registers, local store and channel accesses are the same as before.

VBLANK_MHZ=960000, RSX_PRESENT=0), exeab, 3 rounds of 2 windows:
