4b1d3e1748f08923071e87c8aee910666eca54d9.message:
d3d12: GPU vertex fetch for strips that reach up to 64 vertices an index

A strip range whose indices reach more than 4 vertices an index (plus
256) took the CPU path, on the rule that copying the guest's vertex
bytes over [lo, hi] would cost more than converting the vertices. The
CPU path writes 256 bytes a vertex and converts every attribute; the
copy is the guest's own bytes, tens a vertex, and the next ranges of the
same mesh usually reuse it. Demon's Souls draws its level meshes as
256-index ranges of one BEGIN/END, and in the deep Palace the rule left
64,500 vertices a frame (17 MB into the upload heap) to the CPU. At 64,
10,800 are left (no limit at all: 10,000).

VF_SPARSE (live, default 64): how many vertices an index may reach.

Deep Palace, unlocked, vsync off, presenting, 3 boots, 9 plain-window
pairs: VF_SPARSE=4 (the old rule) is 2.22% slower (180.8 vs 176.8 fps,
p < 0.001). Window captures at 64 and at 4 differ by the noise floor
(0.1-0.2% of pixels, as two windows at the same setting). regress.sh ok.

4c79b2876f29fba4a050a8a529086755ce80e319.message:
ppu_fs: an AIO read keeps the fd's position and cannot interleave

cellFsAioRead did a bare seek + fread on the fd's shared FILE*. Its own
comment says AIO reads are absolute and leave the fd's position alone,
but they moved it: the next cellFsRead went on from where the AIO read
stopped. And titles submit AIO reads from several threads on one fd, so
another thread's seek could land between the seek and the read and hand
back someone else's bytes. The request id counter was a plain static,
so two submits at once could get the same id.

The read now holds the stream's lock (_lock_file / flockfile, the lock
stdio's own calls take) across the seek, the read and the seek back to
the saved position, and the id counter is atomic. Upstream made the same
change in 7208d22b.

tools/test_ppu_fs_aio.py (next commit) runs the real handler on the host.
On master the plain read after an AIO read gets the wrong bytes, and 1356
of 8000 AIO reads racing from 4 threads get another read's bytes (Windows;
699 and 4 repeated ids under WSL Ubuntu 24.04). With this change all of
it passes on both. Demon's Souls imports cellFsAioRead but made no AIO
read in a boot and 1-1 load with PS3_FSLOG=1; Scott Pilgrim loads
everything through it.

4e7e0ff06e9abf6d92635181e8c22d28db2cfb78.message:
rsx_d3d12: present at display clears while the flips are outside the stream

Once the title's first flip in the command stream has reached the walker,
only such flips end a frame: display clears and the ticker no longer
present. A flip the PPU makes directly (an immediate cellGcmSetFlipCommand,
_cellGcmSetFlipCommandWithWaitLabel, or a flip with no room in its buffer)
never reaches d3d12_fifo_flip, so if the title's flips all go that way,
nothing presents again: the picture stops while the game, its sound and the
overlay go on (the symptom of DemonsSoulsRecomp#205).

d3d12_fifo_flip notes the flip request count. From three flip requests
past it, display clears end the frame again, as before present-at-flip,
until a flip in the stream arrives. Both changes of state are logged (at
most 10 lines each). In Demon's Souls every flip is in the stream, so
nothing changes in normal play.

4fc6cd17edd10214bd1bba6df557bcb2af5d32f4.message:
spu: the scan block's check mode puts the state back and counts only calls that skip

Two faults in SPU_NATIVE_SCAN=2, the scan block's check against the SPU
interpreter (#170). Neither touches modes 0, 1 or 3.

A mismatch turned the block off for the session but left that call's state
as the block had left it: its registers and step count, and its done flag
as the return. So a wrong result went on into the lifted code. The check
now saves the registers and the step count before the block runs; on a
mismatch it puts them back (and local store from the interpreter's copy,
taken before the block ran; the loop stores nothing) and returns 0, so the
lifted loop runs those entries.

Every SPU_NATIVE_SCAN_EVERY-th call was checked, but a call whose first
entry goes to a handler skips nothing, so the check compared nothing and
the tick was used up: fewer calls were compared than the knob said. Now
only calls that skip an entry count, and a check that found nothing to
compare is tried again at the next call.

5aae820640cd66d6e8c3f9ff3528e82713e216e6.message:
spu: 64 lock-line reserver slots; walks stop at the slots in use

The table of SPU contexts that reserve a lock line had 8 slots. A context
left out gets no lock-line wake: its GETLLAR idle wait sleeps the full
2 ms, and an Lr event wait its 10 ms re-poll. About 19 Demon's Souls
contexts reserve lines (one per SPURS and async-worker thread, plus the
long-lived ones), so "[spu-coh] more than 8 reserving SPU contexts" was
in nearly every log. In 90 s at the Palace, 16.7 million GETLLARs came
from contexts outside the table, most polling image 7's line 0x477FD980.

The table has 64 slots. s_coh_used marks the slots claimed so far, and
every walk stops there. A notify tests the hints four at a time with
SSE2 on x86-64 and visits only the slots whose hint is its line, so it
costs fewer instructions over 19 used slots than the old loop over 8.
spu_coh_notify_write_except (DMA PUTs) uses the hints too: both of its
callers hold the line's stripe, which is what makes the hints enough.

test_spu_coherency gets a case with 20 more contexts: one line shared by
all, one line each, unregister, and reuse of a freed slot. It fails on
the 8-slot table and passes with gcc and clang.

5eacbb48797eb17498a0fe32c4eb3b03733dfb11.message:
codec: movies off Windows through FFmpeg

cellSail's movie player (sail_movie.cpp) decoded MPEG-2 with Media
Foundation, so off Windows sail_movie_open returned NULL and every movie
ended at once. Only the decoder was Windows-specific; the demuxer, the
LPCM, the frame queue and the clock were not.

They are now shared, and the decoder is per platform: Media Foundation
on Windows as before, and elsewhere FFmpeg's libavcodec through the
run-time loader cellVdec already uses (ffmpeg_runtime.h,
PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG_RUNTIME). A PES payload ends anywhere in a picture, so
libavcodec's MPEG-2 parser gathers whole pictures before they are
decoded; the loader's table gains av_parser_init/parse2/close for it.
Pictures from either decoder go through one 4:2:0 converter (NV12 from
Media Foundation, planar from FFmpeg).

Without FFmpeg (a build without the option, the library not found or of
another major version, PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG=0) a movie with video does not
open and ends at once, as before. Portable calls replace the remaining
Windows ones in the shared part: steady_clock for the performance
counter, __builtin_bswap32 for _byteswap_ulong; the seek is the one
per-platform helper (_fseeki64 / fseeko).

On Windows the order is unchanged: convert, unlock the decoder's
buffer, then wait for room in the queue. A picture that cannot be read
is now opaque black rather than the recycled buffer's old frame.

5f90df91ace569dbcd609e540a3b3fb44dc8e4ca.message:
timer: usleep of a few microseconds stays a yield in a poll streak

After 64 back-to-back short usleeps a thread sleeps on the
high-resolution timer (~0.5 ms granularity), so an idle poller such as
Demon's Souls' HighGraphics (usleep(30) loops) does not pin a core.
Havok's job queue also polls in a streak, with usleep(1), while it
waits for its SPU jobs and the main thread waits for the physics step.
On the timer each poll came back up to 0.5 ms late, and the step took
that many times longer.

Sleeps of at most USLEEP_YIELD_US microseconds (default 10; 0 = the
old behaviour) now keep the precise spin in a streak too. In Demon's
Souls only the Havok thread sleeps that briefly; every other poller asks
for 30 us or more and still goes to the timer.

Demon's Souls, ten replayed breakable breaks (above 30 fps, physics
capped at 30 Hz), worst step frame per break: 12-54 ms before, 12-22 ms
after; step frames over 16 ms: 56 and 50 before, 9 and 7 after.

6223ef7303637af4624a2b6944282911f4f81594.message:
spu: room for 256 tasksets, and a stop inside a call ends the program

Demon's Souls issue #202: after some play, entering 2-1 slowed the game
to 12-40 fps with the sound behind it and the CPU at 100%. Two faults
made it:

- The taskset tables (s_ts_run, s_ts_life) held 32 taskset addresses.
  An entry is never cleared, and an address neither table has room for
  is not tracked: shutdown does not stop that taskset's waiting tasks,
  and join does not wait for them. Demon's Souls uses some 30-35
  addresses in a session that reaches 2-1, so the tasks of the later
  tasksets stayed parked after their shutdown, on memory the game then
  reused. Both tables now hold 256, the scans stop at the first unused
  entry (so a bigger table costs the lock-line check nothing), and a
  full table says so, once.

- A `stop` the SPU does not resume from ends its lifted function with a
  plain return and the pc where the function began. Inside a call, the
  call's drain then found a lifted entry at that pc and resumed it: the
  same stop again, for good, one host thread at 100% each. That is what
  the stale tasks above ran into (image 1's inflater, `stop 0` at 0x4690,
  its bad-data exit, on whatever the reused memory held); the reporter's
  log shows the resume at 0x04690 again and again. On hardware the SPU
  stops there. Now, when one resume ran one function that stopped and
  left the pc where the resume put it, spu_drain_call ends the program
  through spu_halt, as a task's EXIT does, and says so (8 times at most).

Tested: Demon's Souls, the reporter's save at the 2-1 entrance with the
reporter's settings (120 fps, render scale 200%, VSync off), split host
with the patched runtime on the same game module: the 33rd taskset
address now has its 5 waiting tasks stopped at shutdown (it had none
before), about 5 fewer threads alive, the same frame rate (median 120,
p10 120 over two minutes). The spin itself never happened on this PC,
before or after.

cellHttp: read chunked answers (Transfer-Encoding: chunked)

cellHttp read a body by its Content-Length, or to the end of the

and a title that makes its requests one at a time sent nothing more. Demon's

chunk. A Content-Length beside it does not count (RFC 9112 6.3). A malformed
or cut framing fails the body; a size never takes the body past 4 GiB.

65c48762932575f56c6894c957110ea29be7af59.message:
timer: a usleep of a few microseconds waits in place

A usleep of at most USLEEP_YIELD_US (10 us) is a yield, not idling.
Until now it spun on SwitchToThread to its deadline, and SwitchToThread
hands the core to any thread that is ready on it. The poller then waits
for that thread's whole quantum. Demon's Souls' Havok thread polls its
job queue lock with usleep(1) while it posts jobs to the SPU tasks, and
about 1 in 40 of those calls took 0.05-1.7 ms (console trace, after a
breakable broke). The four SPU tasks spent 60-85% of the physics step
waiting for jobs.

Such a sleep now spins on the CPU's pause instruction to the same
deadline, as RPCS3 does (tpause or mwaitx for short sleeps). Off
Windows it did nanosleep, which adds the timer slack (50 us by default)
to every call; it spins the same way there too. USLEEP_SHORT_SWITCH=1
restores the old behaviour.

6797dfeac7da63ac2206a8b48a255c219132c835.message:
rsx_d3d12: draw a full batch at a flip with no display draw

A flip whose batch has no display draw keeps the batch for the composite
that ends it. If the batch is full (the 16384-record draw table, the VP
vertex buffer or the legacy one), that composite is refused too, and
render_frame, the only place that empties the batch and grows the vertex
buffer, never runs again: the picture stops for good while the game, its
sound and the overlay go on (the symptom of DemonsSoulsRecomp#205).

flip_without_display() draws such a batch at the flip without a present,
as the ticker draws offscreen-only work, so the next frame starts empty,
and logs it (at most 20 lines). It also logs 300 flips in a row that have
draws but no display draw. d3d12_fifo_flip and d3d12_present both call it.
Batches that are not full keep accumulating as before.

6920e816f33fabfd6cd4a7acad367ca2001966a8.message:
runtime: image 2's table compare-and-copy loop runs natively

Demon's Souls' HighGraphics ring consumer (SPURS image 2) spends about 13%
of its lifted statements in the loop at LS 0x8E18-0x8F60 (region 0x8CB8,
reached by ring commands 31-34): 32 passes over two pairs of 2 KB tables,
each pass comparing and copying eight quadwords and shifting two masks.

spu_hook_state_diff (spu_diff_hook.c, for --native-block
0x8E18-0x8F60=spu_hook_state_diff) runs every pass but the last with plain
16-byte compares and copies, keeping only what the next pass reads, then
runs the last pass and the four instructions after the loop as lifted, so
every register and local-store byte leaves as the lifted loop leaves it.
It declines (the lifted loop runs) whenever the lifted loop would leave its
region at the next back edge, a local-store probe is on, or the counter is
not below 32.

SPU_NATIVE_DIFF (live): 1 (default) native; 0 the lifted loop; 2 checks:
every SPU_NATIVE_DIFF_EVERY-th time (64) the loop also runs in the SPU
interpreter on a copy of the context and local store, and every register
and the whole local store are compared ([spu-diff] lines); a mismatch turns
the block off for the session. Deep Palace: 131,072 checks in the level and
32,768 at load, 0 mismatches.

Deep Palace, uncapped, not presenting, an in-boot knob A/B in plain
windows (no profile session: it loads the FIFO thread, which then holds
the frame and hides image 2's share): native 161.2 fps, lifted
(SPU_NATIVE_DIFF=0) 158.4, +1.8%, faster in all 5 boots (15 pairs, p <
0.001). Regress at 30 and 240 fps passes.

6f78678b3bd885c0d64cc4d7c34a3d4140514b1f.message:
gpu: a D3D12 device and textures over the caller's objects (step V4)

The port's menu renderer on the GPU layer (render_gpu.cpp) has to run
beside today's: on the D3D12 device and queue the host already made, and
drawing into the swap chain's own buffers. gpu.h gets two calls for that,
in a step V4 block at its end, with the D3D12 backend's code in one at
the end of gpu_d3d12.c:

- gpu_d3d12_create_on(device, queue, desc): a gpu_device over an
  ID3D12Device and ID3D12CommandQueue the caller made. It AddRefs both
  (gpu_destroy releases them) and makes its own fence, recorders and
  descriptor heaps, as gpu_d3d12_create does; its submits go to that
  queue, in order with the caller's own work there. The adapter is found
  by the device's LUID, so gpu_adapter and the caps read as for a device
  of its own.
- gpu_d3d12_texture_on(d, resource, out): a gpu_texture over a resource
  the caller made (a swap chain buffer), AddRef'd and released when the
  handle is destroyed, its description read from the resource (size,
  layers, mips, format, samples, and its target flags as use).

Both take native objects as void*, so gpu.h still needs no D3D12 header.
They are D3D12 calls like gpu_d3d12_create, not device functions: the
null and Vulkan backends and the contract are unchanged.

The port's ui_render_compare uses both: one of its renderers runs on a
gpu_d3d12_create_on device with the back buffers named by
gpu_d3d12_texture_on, and its pictures match today's renderer byte for
byte on every page, on the GPU and on WARP. test_gpu_contract,
test_gpu_null and test_gpu_d3d12 (WARP) pass; test_gpu_vk passes with

  that setup does not clear), a Vulkan start writes renderer_starting
  there and removes it at its first present (rsx_out_route_presented,
  from rsxc_vk.c). A start that finds it uses d3d12; any start not on

860f69920d8203570b16cbda0405a0c1284eccaf.message:
spu: image 2's ring fetch skips a GET the last one covered; its state PUT every 16th command

Image 2 is the consumer of the HighGraphics command ring. For every
16-byte command its fetch GETs the 128-byte block around get, and after
it PUTs its state (get) back, where the producer reads it before each
command it writes. Both are transfers of lines the producer is writing
at the same moment.

GET: a block holds eight commands and was copied up to eight times. A
command is now skipped when the last GET already covered it: the same
block and LS buffer, get the command after the last one taken, get + 16
at or before the put read ahead of that GET (the commands before it were
in memory then, and the producer does not write them again until get is
past them), and the command's quadword in LS still as the GET left it.
SPU_RING_GET_SKIP (live): 1 (default), 0 GETs every command, 2 prints
the share skipped (74% in the deep Palace).

PUT: inside the loop the state PUT waits up to 16 commands; what reaches
memory is the newest state, as from a slower consumer. Every way out of
the loop PUTs first, so the producer sees get before image 2 waits for a
command or runs lifted code, and a full ring still drains.
SPU_RING_PUT_EVERY=<n> (live, default 16); 1 every command.

Deep Palace, unlocked, vsync off, presenting, with the GPU write-back
and the 64-vertex fetch rule in (image 2 then holds the frame):
SPU_RING_GET_SKIP=0 is 5.0% slower (186.8 vs 177.5 fps, 3 boots, 9
pairs, p < 0.001). PUT every n against every command (2 boots, 6 pairs
each): 2 +4.5%, 4 +5.1%, 8 +6.1%, 16 +8.2%, 32 +7.1%, 64 +8.5%, no
limit +7.3%. A 6-minute soak at DES_FPS=120 kept flipping. regress.sh ok.

9182696b3e817b245a2f31e533b73c6b3bedd595.message:
ppu_loader: a thread's TLS block is the TLS image, not image + 0x7000

Each sys_ppu_thread_create'd thread takes a TLS block from the 1 MB
window above the main one, and when every block is in use a new thread
shares the main block. A block was memsz + 0x7000 rounded to a page, so
for Demon's Souls' 0x434-byte image it was 0x8000 and the window held 31.
The 0x7000 is the ABI's r13 bias, not storage: the game addresses TLS as
r13 - 0x7000 + off, and every offset in the lift is 0 to 0x430.

Freeing blocks at thread exit (b1e26833) fixed the churn, but threads
alive at once still count: the Tutorial -> Nexus -> Palace run peaks at
26 besides the main thread, five short of the limit, and online play
starts more. A thread past the limit shares more than thread-locals. The
game takes r13 as a thread's identity (its recursive locks compare the
owner word with it), so two threads on the main block would pass each
other's lock.

A block is now the image rounded up to a page, 0x1000 here, and the
window holds 255. r13 points into a later block, which nothing reads
through it. Upstream made the same change to its bump allocator in
088befac; this applies it to the free list. The boot line says how many
blocks fit.

98b38f8937c035544f4c380a44b3fb770b004ca6.message:
ppu_fs: cellFsFtruncate on its own files (every call was EBADF)

registered cellFsFtruncate. The call went to libs/filesystem/cellFs.c,
whose own table never holds those descriptors, so every call returned
EBADF. Demon's Souls makes it (func_00C30C28) for each file it writes to
its HDD cache (/dev_hdd1/cache), to set the file's final size. On the error
it records an I/O error in its file object and reports it. Issue #205's log
has 93 of these calls, and a Tutorial load has about 175.

ppu_fs now cuts or zero-extends the open host file (_chsize_s, or
ftruncate off Windows) and leaves its position where it was. A descriptor
ppu_fs doesn't hold gets EBADF; a host failure gets EIO and one log line.
The game's other cellFs imports that ppu_fs doesn't handle take paths, not
descriptors.

Tested with a Tutorial load from the regression save: no failures, and the
157 cache files whose size the game set all have that size. The game's use
of its cache looks the same as before (FS_TIME=1: 4 files read back, 203
written, with and without this change).

99598029cd86b9c579736b1ed5387719e0bc2124.message:
gpu_vk: a window with no RGBA8 images gets a BGRA8 swap chain, the frame blitted in

The core's swap chain is RGBA8 (gpu.h's contract, D3D12's back buffers). On
Linux the surfaces of X11 and Wayland on Mesa (lavapipe's included) and of
NVIDIA's driver offer BGRA8 only, so the Vulkan route could not start there:
"[VK] the window takes no swap chain of format 28".

Such a swap chain is now BGRA8, and its images, as the core sees them, are
RGBA8 textures of the backend's. The present's own submit, which every
present makes already, blits the acquired one into the chain's image (a
blit swaps the channels' order) and waits for the acquire there, so the
core's submits no longer wait for it. One recorder and one fence an image.
It says so once:
  [VK] the window takes no RGBA8 images: its swap chain is BGRA8, each frame copied in
A window that has RGBA8 is as before.

Cost: one copy of the window's image a frame, on those systems only. The
other way would be the core drawing into BGRA8 itself, which touches the
blit's, the output filter's and the capture's pipelines and gpu.h.

9f2ccef0bb566a8998307dbcbb26345936242b00.message:
cellSysutil: cellSysCacheMount clears the cache it says it cleared

cellSysCacheMount answered CELL_SYSCACHE_RET_OK_CLEARED (0) but left the
host files of /dev_hdd1 in place. The PS3 clears the system cache at a
mount whose id is empty or names another cache, and the title then trusts
every file it finds there. Demon's Souls mounts with an empty id and copies
the files it loads into the cache, writing each copy in pieces. A session
closed during a copy left it short, and every later session read it back
as good data: the decompressor waited for blocks that never came and the
first trip from the Nexus to Boletarian Palace 1-1 never finished loading
(DemonsSoulsRecomp issue #171).

The mount now empties the cache directory through a hook that the
filesystem layer (runtime/ppu/ppu_fs.cpp) sets at startup. Nothing here
records a cache id or a session that ended cleanly, so every mount clears,
which is what the return value already said. Only a /dev_hdd1/cache path is
touched, and a file still open elsewhere is left in place. Without the
filesystem layer the hook stays NULL and nothing changes.

Tested: the trip on a cache whose copy of the 3.2 MB file was cut to half
hung with the old runtime (the load stopped after m02_9999.tpf.dcx, as in
the issue's reports) and arrives with this one: 734 entries cleared at

a018e5d9dbd47c93a2ef9c21406db6866a53feef.message:
gpu: one present and loss contract; Vulkan's loss, present modes and pipeline cache file (step VC2)

gpu.h states what gpu_swap_present, the fence waits and gpu_lost return
(its step VC2 block): a present gives GPU_PRESENTED or a GPU_PRESENT_*
code (lost, surface lost, failed), a fence wait passes once the device is
lost, and gpu_lost keeps the API's own code from the first loss on. The
D3D12 and null backends return the codes; nothing else changes there.

Vulkan:
- DEVICE_LOST from any call is the loss the core reports as it does a
  removed D3D12 device (the line, rc_be_lost_text, the stop). OUT_OF_DATE
  and SUBOPTIMAL remake the swap chain; SURFACE_LOST remakes the surface
  and its swap chain, and when that fails the core says so and stops
  presenting, as for a loss (rc_be_surface_lost). A loss noted by hand
  (RSX_LOSE_DEVICE_AT_FRAME) asks the driver for no fault report.
- RSX_VSYNC=1 presents FIFO, 0 IMMEDIATE, else FIFO with the line the
  d3d12 route prints; never MAILBOX. With swapchain_maintenance1 the mode
  switches per present, else by a new swap chain. RSX_VSYNC=2-4 hold each
  frame that many refreshes with present_wait (the present gate); without
  present_wait they are FIFO, one refresh, as before.
- The core draws into no image when the acquire gave none (a minimized
  window or a lost surface): rsxc_state.inc's s_rc_have_image.
- The pipeline library is the device's VkPipelineCache, in
  <cache>/gpu/vulkan/<vendor>_<device>_<driver>_<uuid>.vkpc: loaded at the
  start, saved where pipelines.lib is saved. Its header (magic, version,
  length, the driver, the data's length and sum) and Vulkan's own are
  checked; a file that fails is ignored and the next save replaces it.
  The route writes no .dxbc, pso_library.bin or pso_manifest.bin.
  PS3_PSO_LOG=1 prints the pipelines made, the cache's hits and the time
  in the driver when the device goes.

The core's edits, each for Vulkan (copy_manifest.txt's step VC2 block):
swap_present reads the code (rsxc_hdr.inc), rc_acquire keeps whether an
image

a65a0bc7a34518e66d9575be8ba2f8a7efa50c81.message:
gcm: a context seen past its end keeps its flips in the FIFO near the end

Demon's Souls' command buffer runs on past its end, so since c01c7f7 its
flips go into the FIFO as markers, and the walker presents at each one.
But its current is not always past end at a flip. When it fell in the
ring's last 4 KB, gcm_flip_into_fifo refused, as it does for a title
that wraps its ring itself, and the flip took the immediate path. With no
flip in the stream, the walker put that frame and the next into one
present: twice the draws, and a frame on screen for two refreshes.

At 138 fps that was about one flip in 2,000, a 15 ms hitch every 10-30 s.
GCM_RATES showed it as a second with one more flip request than flip
words.

Once a context has flipped past its end, the 4 KB reserve and the
guest-side wrap no longer apply to it. libgcm writes its 8-byte flip
command there as well. A title that never runs past end is unchanged.

Demon's Souls at 144 fps with G-Sync / FreeSync (138 fps), a first start,
the same 30 s walk:
- seconds with a flip off the FIFO: 3 -> 0 (in 78 s);
- presents with twice the draws: 2 -> 0;
- frames over twice the period: 2 -> 0, worst 15.7 -> 11.5 ms.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

a7e5022f3a56aeed5b8d703c268d20bd6c0b0aa8.message:
ppu: a run of stores through one other base register shares one test too

A run of three or more stores of GPRs through one base register other
than r1 (a structure filled in) now goes under one test as the frame
saves do: vm_st_run gives the host address of the run's lowest byte when
every byte it stores would take vm_write*_inl's direct store (below the
store limit at both ends, no line of it reserved), and the stores then
go through that pointer; otherwise the run's lines run as before. Such a
run spans at most 256 bytes, so the test reads three reservation bits at
most. In Demon's Souls' lift: 31,953 such runs beside the 47,482 frame
save runs. With each run put back as its else block, every function is
the same as master's lift.

The run stores are vm_run_put* now (were vm_stk_put*), as both kinds use
them. vm_st_run reads its own switch, the fourth word on the armed flag's
line (game_module.c's copy too): 1 while the store limit is on, 0 while
PPU_ST_RUN=0 (live), which sends every such run store by store. The
run reads the reservation bits once where each store read its own; the
bits are sticky, so only a line's first reservation can fall between the
test and the stores, as it already could between one store's test and
its store, and the PUTLLC's compare still sees the changed line.

afa453eda0523498456cc19b251a6ba7ebdcdceb.message:
rsx, vblank: a vblank clock on the display's vblanks, and frames held n refreshes

A title's frames judder when its rate does not divide the display's: 60 fps
on a 144 Hz display shows frames for 2, 3, 2, 2, 3 refreshes however evenly
they come. At a rate that divides it (72 at 144 Hz), the vblank timer still
drifts against the display, and its wake-up jitter puts runs of frames on
either side of a refresh: 6% of them held 3 refreshes or 1.

- rsx_d3d12_display_timing / rsx_d3d12_display_refresh_mhz: the window's
  display's refresh period and one vblank's time, from the swap chain's
  frame statistics (read after a present, at most every 100 ms), checked
  against the display mode; else DWM's timing; else the mode. Any thread.
- ps3_vblank_lock_display(n): the clock thread ticks every n refreshes, each
  tick on the nearest of the display's vblanks; 0 goes back to the timer.
- RSX_VSYNC=2..4 presents with that sync interval, so a late frame moves the
  frames after it a refresh instead of being shown n + 1 and the next n - 1.
  Repaints over a held frame stay at 1.

b3a9b8e4dd054aeb8a86539670b0e8914151981a.message:
rsxcore: the FP constant memo copies nothing for a program without constants

The memo hit called memcpy for 0 bytes too. VCRUNTIME's short copy is an
AVX-512 masked load and store over 64 bytes, and a masked access that
reaches a page nothing has touched takes a microcode assist every time.
Two hot programs at the Tutorial have no constants, and their entries' k
start within 64 bytes of a page whose neighbour entry is unused, so every
draw with them paid the assist: about 6% of the FIFO thread, and -1.3% fps
against today's renderer at m08. Which entries end a page depends on where
s_fpkm lands in the binary, which is why the replay and today's renderer
did not show it.

The hit now skips the copy when n is 0, and a new entry writes its k whole
once, so a short copy's tail always finds its page. The bytes written to
the ring are the same.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

spu: build the local-store debug probes only on request

spu_ls_read128 and spu_ls_write128 test g_spu_ls_dbg at every access
and call the probes (SPU_LS_WATCH, SPU_LS_LOWREAD, SPU_SMC_WATCH,

instructions: 0x4498 8,314 -> 6,143, 0x7140 7,051 -> 4,803, 0x59C0

PS3RECOMP_SPU_LS_PROBES, off by default; a game that compiles its lifted
SPU sources itself defines it for them too). Without it g_spu_ls_dbg is
0, so the native ring and diff hooks stay on, and setting one of the
probe variables prints a notice once (from the channel diagnostics'

b4200f008d66a8abe078db9a31f8ae61bdb66f41.message:
network: sign in to a server that has a sign-in (PS3_NET_SIGNIN)

A Demon's Souls Recomp server knows a player by a key, not only by a name.
With PS3_NET_SIGNIN=<host>[:port] and PS3_NET_KEY_FILE set
(libs/network/ps3_net_signin.c, include/ps3emu/ps3_net_signin.h):

- The first sign-in makes an Ed25519 key and writes it to the key file, which
  is never written over afterwards. The name is np_psnr_online_id().
- The runtime asks for a challenge, signs it, and gets a session back. A key
  the server has not seen first does the proof of work the server asks for
  (SHA-256, include/ps3emu/sha256.h), within a limit.
- cellHttp adds X-DSS-Session to the title's requests to that server's
  address only. psnr's HELLO carries the session too; when psnr says it has
  ended, np_psnr signs in once more. psnr's new refusals map to Matching2's
  FORBIDDEN where a title asks to join.
- The session is renewed before it ends; a failure waits a minute before the
  next try. A server that does not answer, or has no sign-in, leaves the
  title's requests as they were.
- A refusal's message (a ban, maintenance, an old build) is kept for the host
  to show: ps3_net_signin_notice(). A refused co-op adds its own, unless the
  sign-in itself failed, whose message then stays.

PS3_NET_CLIENT_VERSION and PS3_NET_NETWORK_VERSION tell the server which
build asks. docs/ONLINE.md, "Sign-in".

Tests: test_net_signin (SHA-256 and RFC 8032 vectors, parsing, and a loopback
server that checks the challenge, the signature and the work: new and known
keys, a ban, maintenance, a server with no sign-in, the header to that server
only, a damaged key file left alone) and test_np_psnr_notice. The network
tests that include cellHttp or np_psnr now build the sign-in with them.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

babf03cbf5f839cdfbedb5c837420c58729b0a86.message:
gpu: the portable renderer's GPU layer contract, behind PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL

The first piece of the portable renderer: the contract its RSX core and its
D3D12, Vulkan and null backends will share. Today's renderer
(rsx_d3d12_backend.c) is untouched and nothing uses the contract yet.

- libs/video/gpu/gpu.h: plain C99 that C++ includes too. Small handles with a
  generation count; native-valued hot handles (gpu_pipeline, gpu_table); a
  64-bit fence timeline and buffer addresses (gpu_addr). The numbers are
  D3D12's (DXGI formats, resource states, Shader4ComponentMapping, blend,
  compare, filter), and the sampler, footprint, box, rect and viewport
  structures are D3D12's field for field, so code copied from today's
  renderer needs no translation. Descriptions for every object, feature bits
  read once, and the device's function table (an X-macro, with
  gpu_<name>() wrappers).
- gpu_cmd_ops.h: the 35 commands a recorder takes, as one X-macro, the
  recorder's table, and GPU_CMD_CHECK, which fails to compile unless a
  command header defines every command with the list's parameters.
- gpu_vt_cmd.h: the commands through the recorder's table, for code
  compiled once for every backend.
- CMakeLists.txt: option PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL (off). On, it defines
  PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL=1 publicly, adds the gpu folder to the include path,
  declares the pinned dependencies (cmake/gpu_deps.cmake: Vulkan-Headers,
  volk, SPIRV-Headers, SPIRV-Tools, glslang, SPIRV-Cross at Vulkan SDK
  1.4.363.0, by commit; none fetched until a later sub-option asks) and
  builds the contract test.
- libs/video/tests/test_gpu_contract.c/.cpp: one program, C and C++ halves.
  D3D12's numbers and structure layouts against the SDK on Windows and the
  documented values everywhere; GPU_CMD_CHECK on gpu_vt_cmd.h in both
  languages; commands and device calls through the tables; every type's
  size the same in C and C++.

Checked: with the option off, every source's compile command is the same as
on master; with it on, the runtime's objects are byte for byte

bae620c0cfa040d5dbc4b3e0bcb5b025576ef5a4.message:
runtime: split build, the lifted code as a DLL beside a host exe (PS3RECOMP_GAME_SPLIT)

PS3RECOMP_GAME_SPLIT=ON builds the runtime for a host exe that loads the
lifted code (PPU chunks, SPU images, a lifted system PRX and their glue) from
a DLL. The ABI is include/ps3emu/game_module.h. The lifted sources compile
exactly as they do for a single exe. runtime/ppu/game_module.c supplies what
they need from outside the DLL:

- a jump thunk for each runtime function they call by name, through a slot
  the host fills at load (about the cost of an import-table call);
- the globals their inline fast paths read: the guest-memory limits, the SPU
  coherency bitmap, the SPU dispatch flags;
- the two trampoline thread-locals. Windows cannot share a thread-local
  across modules, so they live in the DLL, and the host reaches the current
  thread's copy through a pointer it caches per thread.

runtime/ppu/game_host.c loads the DLL once vm_base is set, before anything
reads the function table. It checks the ABI and the struct sizes, then wires
the module up. The split runtime force-includes ps3emu/game_split.h, which
points the shared names at the DLL's copies. Where the runtime compares a
function pointer with spu_indirect_branch, it also accepts the module's
thunk for it.

The option is off by default. In a default build, every changed source
preprocesses to the same text as before.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

D3D12: say when the graphics device is lost

When the driver resets the GPU (a TDR: the GPU has not finished its work
in about 2 s) or the GPU goes away, nothing can be drawn again, while the
game runs on: the picture stays on its last frame. Nothing said so.
Present's result was never looked at, and every fence of a lost device
reads as done at once (UINT64_MAX), so no wait timed out either.
Demon's Souls issue #205's second report is this: a 3 s stall, then the
game at its frame cap with a frozen picture, 508 "could not make a
texture for the menu" lines (the overlay shares the device), and no
screenshot in the report (its read-back failed). ps3recomp#132's
fallback never ran there.

check_device() asks GetDeviceRemovedReason when Present fails, when the
frame fence reads UINT64_MAX, and when a fence wait times out. The first
time it is not S_OK it logs the reason once ("[D3D12] the graphics device
was lost ..."), runs dred_report (D3D12_DRED=1) and keeps the reason for
rsx_d3d12_device_lost(), which the host's report and dialog read. In
normal play this adds a comparison per frame and one per present.

Test: a scratch switch that calls ID3D12Device5::RemoveDevice at frame
900, in Demon's Souls with presents off (a locked session). The fence
path caught it in the same frame: "the graphics device was lost (seen at
frame fence): ... DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED, 0x887A0005", and the game ran
on. The present path was not run (it needs an unlocked session).

c106bfb0800924425f3b6c0bb95bb802cc044df0.message:
sysPrxForUser: a spinlock is a 4-byte exchange on LP64 hosts too

spin_word() handed _InterlockedExchange a volatile long*, and the POSIX
shim in win32_compat.h sizes the exchange by the pointer type. long is
8 bytes on Linux and macOS, so sys_spinlock_initialize, lock, trylock and
unlock each wrote the guest word after the lock as well (zero on
initialize and unlock, the low half of the 1 on lock), and a lock 4 bytes
past an 8-byte boundary was a misaligned 8-byte RMW. LONG is 32-bit
everywhere, as it is on Windows, where nothing changes.

Upstream fixed the same lines in 67e18b9e; its test
(tools/test_spinlock_word_width.py, the next commit) fails on the fork's
master under WSL Ubuntu 24.04 g++ ("initialize: modified byte outside
four-byte lock at +4") and passes with this change. Demon's Souls does
not import the spinlock family, so the game run cannot exercise it;
Virtua Fighter 5 does.

cabb152dc9d4c48b370458495afa858216205092.message:
rsx: a frame's missing pipelines built on worker threads

On a first start the pipelines are built as the game first draws with
them, one after another in render_frame's draw pre-pass. A miss costs
about 2 ms on a PC whose driver has seen the shaders, 7-20 ms where it has
not, and a camera turn brings tens at once: 32 in one Demon's Souls
Tutorial frame took 55 ms in a row, a 73 ms frame. At 138 fps on a G-Sync
display that is a visible stutter every few seconds of a first walk.

PSO_THREADS=<n> (live; default half the processors less one, at most 7;
0 = the old way): in the pre-pass a miss puts its key in the cache as
pending and its description in the frame's batch, and psj_finish builds
the batch on n workers and the render thread together before the draw
loop, then fills the pipelines into the entries and the draws that asked.
The frames are the same: every pipeline exists before anything is
recorded either way. The decompile and the shader cache stay on the render
thread.

The manifest's files (pso_blobs/, pso_manifest.bin) are written on a
thread of their own from copies, so neither the render thread nor the
workers touch a file, and the manifest has its own lock instead of the
library's. Records still queued at shutdown are written there.

A native block (--native-block ADDR-END=SYMBOL) may leave a register as

own live registers) and returns (under the SPU ABI). With exit:0xSTART
it also prints which registers a loop body writes that are live at the

cdfa47eaf053524307431a04c7d90b9ca39eb33a.message:
CMake: a Windows build downloads the pinned FFmpeg for its movies

When PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG_RUNTIME is off, a Windows configure now downloads
the ffmpeg-win64 zip that ffmpeg-archive.yml makes (FFmpeg's MPEG-2
decoder and parser as DLLs, with the headers), checks its SHA-256,
unpacks it to <build>/ffmpeg-win64 and turns the run-time FFmpeg on. A
game build copies <build>/ffmpeg-win64/bin/*.dll beside its executable,
and the movies decode through FFmpeg instead of Windows' own decoder,
which needs the Microsoft Store's MPEG-2 Video Extension.

The download is once per build directory (a stamp holds its SHA-256) and
again when the pin changes. A changed CMakeLists.txt makes the next build
configure again, so a pull and a build are enough to get it. With no
network, or a file that does not match, the configure warns and goes on
without FFmpeg, as before. PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG_DOWNLOAD=OFF never downloads;
PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG_URL with PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG_SHA256 takes another copy.

The pin is empty in this commit, so nothing is downloaded yet: it is set
once the first ffmpeg-win64 release exists. docs/BUILDING.md and the
README say what a Windows build gets (and the README no longer says
cellAtrac decodes through FFmpeg: it uses third_party/at3_standalone).

d0a6149036515692ca27da18eb3d1f032efbda20.message:
gpu: the null backend, which records and checks for headless CI

gpu_null*.c/h: gpu.h's device functions and gpu_cmd_ops.h's commands with
no GPU under them, for CI on every system (plain C99, no system or GPU
headers). Buffers are CPU memory: maps, copies between buffers and host
imports move real bytes. Textures hold nothing, so their readbacks and
occlusion results are zeroes. The GPU is instant: fences complete at
submit and waits never block. Each command is static inline in
gpu_null_cmd.h, one call into the recorder, and so are the per-draw device
calls (GPU_FAST_FUNCS), so the core's frame file builds against it as
against D3D12.

Every command and the device calls around it are checked against the
contract, as they are recorded and as they run at submit, in submission
order: stale and freed handles; frees before the fence of the work using
them; barriers against each subresource's tracked state, with D3D12's
promotion from COMMON and decay; states a use does not allow; draws
missing a layout, pipeline, pass or bound slot; binds without their
GPU_USE bit or outside their buffer; cb_align and the copies' alignments;
boxes and footprints out of bounds; query reset, begin and end order;
table entries written while unfinished work reads them; fences never
reached, and slots or readbacks used before their fence was seen; recorders
used after their end; swap chain images used without an acquire. Failures
are counted by kind (gpu_null_errors), and the first of each kind is
printed with the command and its arguments.

gpu_null_stream_hash is FNV-1a 64 over the operation stream: every command
in submission order and the device calls that change what a GPU would see,
handles as creation numbers and pipelines by their contents, so a run
hashes the same on every system and compiler. GPU_NULL_DUMP=<file> writes
the stream as text. gpu_null.h has the encoding.

test_gpu_null (built on demand; ctest -R gpu_null) records three frames of
the guest pipelines' commands on two recorders and a swap chain with no
failure and th

d2a0678866dd35405d5503d062336d65a00dd58d.message:
SPU ring loop: write the registers and the frame once per run of commands

Image 2's native ring loop (spu_ring_hook.c, SPU_NATIVE_LOOP=1) left every
register, the frame and the context fields as the lifted path leaves them at
each command's end, and the next command wrote nearly all of them again
before anything read them. ring_lazy runs the same commands with the same
local-store stores, transfers and latches, keeps r80, the last command and
the last fetch's reads in locals, and writes the post's registers and frame
(and, when the run ends at 0x4730, the fetch's registers) once at the end.
The tag waits of a deferred PUT and a skipped GET are left out: no transfer
came since the last wait, so they would read what it read.

SPU_RING_LAZY (live): 1 (default), 0 the per-command path, for A/B.

test_spu_ring_lazy.c runs both on random rings (all native commands, some
the loop leaves to the lifted code, failed no-op commits, the PUT interval,
one-call transfers, the GET skip and the line read varied) and compares the
registers, context, local store, guest memory, transfers and the GET memo.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

d9df3cc861ba77a67554edf5599e3c952920f931.message:
spu: the MFC engine lookup tries the context's own slot first

mfc_for finds a context's MFC engine on every MFC channel access. It
remembered the last slot in a thread-local, and on Windows a thread-local
is three dependent loads before the slot's owner can be compared with
ctx. Demon's Souls' image 2 asks two or three times a ring command.

The context now keeps its slot as well (spu_context.mfc_slot1, the index
plus 1, 0 for none, at the end of the struct), and mfc_for tries it
first: a range check, then the slot's owner against ctx. A slot has one
owner, so a stale or never-set value can only miss, and a miss goes to
the thread's slot and the search as before; both record the slot in the
context too.

SPU_MFC_HINT=0 (live, read with the channel diagnostics) goes straight
to the thread's slot, for A/B.

de6a31ffdbbae35cd1d8f37e9d40a86736a723bb.message:
spu: the ring loop's word and halfword inserts as stores

Image 2's native commands 7, 8 and 12 (ring_loop) did each of their six
sub-quadword stores as the lifted instructions do: load the quadword, make
a cwd / cwx / chd mask, shufb, store the 16 bytes back. A shufb by such a
mask, stored where its quadword came from, changes one word (or halfword):
the value's preferred word lands where the address points and the other
bytes are stored as they were. So each is now that word's or halfword's
store (ls_put_word / ls_put_half). For command 12 the mask positions and
the store addresses differ by 0x370 each, so the low four bits agree.
Command 8's insert was the hottest spot of ring_loop in an instruction
profile after the post's stores went straight.

SPU_LOOP_INSERTS=0 (live) runs the load, shuffle and store as before.
SPU_NATIVE_LOOP=2's check (the native commands predicted on a copy of
local store, compared after the lifted run) covers the new stores.

Deep Palace, DES_FPS=unlocked, vsync off, knobab plain windows, on master
+ #157-#160, session locked: SPU_LOOP_INSERTS=0 is 0.61% slower (210.00 vs
211.28 fps, 4 boots, 12 pairs, p 0.025). A small gain, kept because the
change is simple and checked. soak.sh with SPU_NATIVE_LOOP=2: kept
flipping for 6 minutes, 4,194,304 commands compared, 0 mismatches.
regress.sh: 4 of 4 shots ok.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

dec4ea8b463d8e1c5f055deadbc1fc2ff9f6155c.message:
ppu: the function table keeps address and function on one line

ppu_lookup, which every indirect call to a lifted function makes, read
the guest address from one array and the host function from another:
two cache lines for each slot it probed. In a profile of Demon's Souls'
HighGraphics the stall on those loads was about 1% of the thread. A slot
now holds both (16 bytes, four to a line).

The home slot is now the top PPU_HASH_BITS bits of a * 2654435761
(Fibonacci hashing). The low bits used before are 0 in their two lowest
places for every 4-byte aligned address, so only one slot in four could
be a home: Demon's Souls' 94,017 functions took 1.96 probes a lookup on
average, 1.28 now (the longest chain is 16 either way). Registration
and lookup take the home from ppu_fn_home; the profiler's inverse map
reads the slots as before.

def094193858066a599e624e228598011ba7bcb6.message:
rsx: the vertex-program memo keeps 32 programs per start, most recent first

vp_get_vs_mode runs for every draw. Its memo kept two programs per
program start; past that it sized the program, hashed it a byte at a
time (FNV-1a, about 4 cycles a byte, and the hash stays: the pipeline
library keys on it) and scanned the cache. In Demon's Souls' deep
Palace one start cycles through up to 32 programs. A count of the
lookups by how far back their program was last used at its start:
81.4% the last one, 89.4% within 2, 96.5% within 8, all within 32. So
two ways missed 10.6% of the lookups, each miss hashing about 850
bytes: 2.7% of the FIFO thread. (Eight ways were tried on 10-24 and
did not show; they would still miss 3.5%.)

The memo now keeps RSX_VP_MEMO programs per start (2 to 32, default
32) in most-recently-used order: a hit moves to the front, a new entry
takes the last one's place and its copy buffer. The copy compare after
a store write then meets the likely programs first. RSX_VP_MEMO=2
(live) is the memo as it was: two ways, least recently used out. A
pass-0 entry is now rejected on its version before the other checks.

e5d7a65fbf6603cfe3b4b81556a084266b199c86.message:
gpu: the Vulkan backend's gaps the core's replays found (step VC1)

The core's first replays on Vulkan, with the validation layer and its
synchronization validation, reported three kinds of message; the backend
now does what D3D12 does in each case, and two contract points are
written down in gpu.h.

- Table slots: set layouts of up to 16 entries are one layout
  (GPU_VK_TABLE_MIN), so a slot of up to 16 binds any table of up to 16.
  The core's blit binds the blit pool's 2-entry tables through a
  1-texture slot, which D3D12 allows and Vulkan's set layouts did not
  (VUID-vkCmdBindDescriptorSets-pDescriptorSets-00358).
- Vertex attributes: shader_create reads a SPIR-V module's Input and
  Output Locations, and a pipeline gets only the attributes its vertex
  shader reads (WARNING-Shader-OutputNotConsumed).
- Pixel shader outputs with no target (a depth-only pass's colour, slots
  past nrt): the pipeline is made with a copy of the module in which those
  outputs are Private variables, as D3D12 drops them
  (Undefined-Value-ShaderOutputNotConsumed-DynamicRendering). The copy is
  made from the words kept for pixel shaders with outputs and destroyed
  once the pipeline exists.
- Swap chains: GPU_SUBMIT_PRESENT_SIGNAL signalled the image's done
  semaphore in the first such submit only, so a present waited for none of
  the frame's later submits (the core says PRESENT_SIGNAL on every
  submit). The present's own empty submit now signals it, after them all.
- Textures with memory of their own start zeroed, as D3D12's committed
  resources: cleared in the init command buffer before their first layout
  (not BC formats; placed textures are what their heap held, on both).

ecf42d73afd978813c3670c1088f0dd96f35c715.message:
spu, lift: the SSE paths build on arm64 through sse2neon

The SIMD paths are written with SSE intrinsics behind x86 guards, each
with a scalar loop beside it, so an arm64 build compiled but took every
loop: spu_shufb as a byte loop (about 11% of an FMOD mixer task), the
quadword byte shifts at ~70 instructions each, the scan and diff blocks
on lane loops, and the PPU lift's vperm/vsldoi/vmaxfp/vminfp/vrsqrtefp/
lvlx/lvrx as loops.

third_party/sse2neon is sse2neon v1.9.1 (MIT, pinned by commit, blobs in
its README), unmodified. include/ps3emu/ps3_sse.h includes it on arm64
under GCC or Clang and defines PS3_SSE2NEON; on x86 it defines nothing.
These guards now also take PS3_SSE2NEON, and keep including their own
x86 header on x86:

f0703ff284d1a613abe281ca3f8209027405d4ee.message:
spu: the native ring loop runs commands 10-13, 17 and 18 too (loop v2)

SPU_NATIVE_LOOP ran commands 7 and 8 of image 2's ring without leaving
the fetch block: four in five commands in Boletarian Palace. It now also
runs 12, which stores a 16-byte record into the state block, and the GET
commands 10, 11, 13, 17 and 18, which GET 16 to 128 bytes from an EA in
the command into the state block through the GET-and-wait helper at
0xC4D8 (10 then sets a dirty quadword as 8 does). Together that is
nineteen commands in twenty.

The GET is the call bracket and 0xC4D8's main case as the lifted code
runs them: the link and the back chain on the stack, the latches, the GET
on tag 0 and its wait, r0 read back. Every case the lifted path would take
differently is left to it before the command's first side effect: an LSA
or EA that is not 16-byte aligned (0xC4D8 halts on it), a GET that runs
off local store, or one that fills the ring's quadwords or the frame. The
GET's tag write and wait go through spu_wrch_word, as every hook's do
since #90, so no u128 copy brings a /GS check. The check mode
(SPU_NATIVE_LOOP=2) covers the new commands, with the GET's guest bytes
copied into its prediction.

SPU_NATIVE_LOOP_V2 (live, default 1) set to 0 leaves the new commands to
the lifted code, as before, so one exe compares the two.

fps with SPU_NATIVE_LOOP_V2=0, 168.15 fps with the default: +2.3%,

f59a0387809b6b62df0683fe28fdef19cb39b80b.message:
d3d12: colour write-back from the GPU straight into guest memory

The write-back stored 13.1 MB a frame in the deep Palace (three 1280x720
A8R8G8B8 targets and a dozen smaller) on the RSX thread: a read of each
byte from the readback buffer and a write into guest memory, about
31 GB/s each way. It is bound by that traffic: a faster loop or streamed
stores do not help (streamed: -2.5%), and a worker thread moves the
traffic without removing it (no change).

Now the GPU stores it. The boot reserves RSX local memory
[0xC0000000, 0xD0000000) as an allocation of its own inside the 4 GB
guest space (VirtualAlloc2 placeholders; the addresses do not change).
The backend commits that range, opens a heap on it
(OpenExistingHeapFromAddress) and places one buffer over it. Each linear
A8R8G8B8 target in local memory is drawn into the guest's byte order (the
write-back's downscale pass with an .argb shader) and copied into place;
the store only takes its checksum. Other formats, swizzled and
main-memory targets, offsets the copy cannot address (512-byte offsets,
256-byte pitches), and machines where the heap cannot be made store on
the CPU as before.

RSX_WB_GPU (live): 1 (default) as above, 0 every target on the CPU,
2 also makes the CPU store into a scratch copy and compares it with what
the GPU stored. Deep Palace, mode 2: 19,456 targets compared, 0 differ.

Deep Palace, unlocked, vsync off, presenting, 3 boots, 9 plain-window
pairs: RSX_WB_GPU=0 is 1.26% slower (180.0 vs 177.7 fps, p 0.008).
render_frame 1.57 -> 1.28 ms, its store 0.41 -> 0.06 ms. regress.sh ok.

f6216f8e84d368f1ec55e7236a40689cb4d7cc51.message:
ppu lifter: stack stores skip the SPU reservation test

Two thirds of Demon's Souls' lifted guest stores have base r1: the frame
saves, the spills, the back chain. Each one tested the store limit, the SPU
armed flag and the reservation bitmap. The lifter now writes them as
vm_write*_stk (ps3emu/ppu_lift.h), which stores an address in the stack
region (0xD0000000 up) straight away while it is below the stack limit, and
otherwise takes the inline path as before. The rewrite happens as each
function is written out, so the frame analyses still see the plain stores.

The limit is the word after the armed flag on its line, so a game module
carries it with no new export (game_module.c names it). The runtime keeps it
(spu_coh_stk_eval): it follows the store limit, so it is 0 until the limits
are decided and while any store diagnostic is on, and it goes to 0 for good
once an SPU reserves a line in the stack region (logged once); those stores
then take the full path. A store that read the limit just before that first
stack reservation can miss its one event, as any store can at the first
GETLLAR.

tools/test_ppu_stack_stores.py: the lifter writes the r1 stores, and only
those, as vm_write*_stk; the header stores straight only inside the limit,
big-endian, and calls the accessor otherwise, with the limit on and off and
with PPU_VM_NO_INLINE.

The gain needs the main thread's stack in the stack region
(PS3_MAIN_STACK_LV2=1, which the port now sets by default): without it the
main thread's r1 is 0x0FEFxxxx, its stores fail the stack test and take
the inline path after it, and on Demon's Souls' break replay the change
lost 3.4% fps after the breaks. A title that leaves the knob off should
measure before taking this.

Measured with the knob on both sides (the port's PR build, one host, the
game DLL with and without this commit, every run locked):
- the break replay (ABBAAB): after the breaks 257.1 -> 271.9 fps (+5.8%),
  the Havok step 5.35 -> 5.13 ms (-4.2%), before the breaks 266.0 -> 278.8
  (+4.8%), the Havok thread's cycle

fa697149615a0c3c32edacf18d707ec32a25b1bb.message:
runtime: guest memory off Windows is one 4 GB-aligned mapping

The boot harness backed the guest's address space with calloc(0xE0000000).
malloc aligns that to 16 bytes, so every vm_commit (mprotect from vm_base +
the guest address) was handed an address off a page boundary and failed:
every sys_memory_allocate returned ENOMEM, Dantelion's heaps came back null,
and Demon's Souls panicked in DLStdAllocator before its first thread. The
base was also not 4 GB aligned, which the host-pointer-to-guest-address
truncation vm.h describes depends on.

Map the same space Windows reserves (VM_SIZE, the 4 GB guest space and its
guard) read/write with MAP_NORESERVE, so the kernel backs a page when it is
first touched as the Windows handler commits one, on a 4 GB boundary by
mapping 4 GB more and unmapping both ends. ppu_vm_size is 0 as on Windows:
the whole 32-bit space is backed.

On Linux (WSL, Ubuntu 24.04) Demon's Souls now boots to its level.

rsxcore: a frame waits for its slot's use before it, as today's does

With RSX_PRESENT=0 nothing is presented, so the swap chain's buffer index
never moves and every frame uses one slot. Today's move_to_next_frame then
signals the slot's fence value again, which render_frame's opening
wait_for_gpu has already reached, so it doesn't wait: the GPU runs the frame
while the next batch records. The new path signalled a fresh value and
waited for it, a full drain every frame. That was about 0.2 ms a frame of
extra waiting on capset0 (+5% to +9% in halgate --time at RSX_PRESENT=0,
the only mode a locked PC can time). With presenting, the slots alternate
and both behaved alike.

move_to_next_frame now waits for the new slot's point from before this
frame, then stores this frame's. frame_cmd_begin waits for the slot's point
before its recorder is reset. After the opening drain that is a fence read,
and it keeps a repaint, which opens a slot right after a present, from
resetting a recorder still in flight. The slot points are cleared before
init's first frame_cmd_begin, so a device made again starts from zero.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   └── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse
│   ├── hardware/             # cellGem, cellCamera, cellUsbd
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
└── docs/                     # See the Documentation table below
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

HLE implementations of the PS3 system libraries, written for this project. RPCS3 is a behavioural reference, not a code source. **About 93 modules complete and 5 partial** (media decode, SPURS), in roughly 260 files and 100,000 lines under `libs/`.

| **Kernel Memory** | sys_memory, sys_mmapper (containers, shared mem) | ✅ Complete |
| **Kernel Filesystem** | sys_fs (path mapping, real I/O) | ✅ Complete |
| **Filesystem** | cellFs (real file I/O, dir ops, stat, path translation) | ✅ Complete |

| **Audio** | cellAudio (WASAPI/SDL2, mixing thread, multi-port) | ✅ Complete |
| **Video Output** | cellVideoOut (resolution config, 720p default) | ✅ Complete |
| **Codecs** | cellPngDec, cellJpgDec, cellGifDec (stb_image) | ✅ Complete |
| **Font** | cellFont (stb_truetype backend + fallback metrics) | ✅ Complete |
| **Network** | sys_net (BSD sockets, P2P), cellNet, cellNetCtl, cellHttpUtil, cellSsl, sceNp*, sceNpTrophy, sceNpMatching2 + Score over [psnr](docs/ONLINE.md) | ✅ Complete |
| **Hardware** | cellUsbd (USB), cellCamera (PS Eye), cellGem (PS Move) — stub, no devices | ✅ Complete |
| **Sync** | cellSync (atomic spinlocks, LF queue), cellSync2 (OS-backed) | ✅ Complete |

| **Fibers** | cellFiber (PPU fibers via Windows Fibers/ucontext) | ✅ Complete |
| **AV Config** | cellAvconfExt (audio output info, gamma, sound availability) | ✅ Complete |
| **Input Util** | cellKey2char (HID scancode → Unicode, US-101 layout) | ✅ Complete |
| **Graphics** | cellGcmSys (cmd buffer, IO mapping, tile/zcull, flip handlers, timestamps, FIFO walker + ring recycle), RSX command processor (NV47xx parsing, state tracking, backend callbacks), **live D3D12 backend** (executes the title's real NV4097 vertex/fragment programs — indexed draws, per-draw VP constants + textures, render-to-texture, MRT, FP predication), null backend (Win32 window) | ✅ Complete |

1441287685.readme_excerpt:
# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. É irmão do [Sparta](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ghost-of-sparta-pc) e do [Olympus](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-chains-of-olympus-pc), que fazem o mesmo com os God of War de PSP. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível e à primeira luta contra um chefe, mas ainda lento (~18-23 fps no nível, 13-21 na luta). Só Windows por enquanto (o suporte ao macOS está pausado). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Outubro de 2026, no Windows: - **Do boot à primeira luta contra um chefe:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~50-55 fps; o primeiro nível a ~22-27 fps, conforme a cena (era ~9); a luta contra o chefe a 13-21. Atrasando um thread de cada vez e medindo quanto o quadro atrasa junto, o limite hoje é o thread que executa os comandos de vídeo (o RSX do RPCS3) e o thread principal do jogo, não as SPUs nem a placa de vídeo. Partes pesadas das SPUs já rodam como código nativo, cada uma conferida contra o original: a geometria por draw (índices, skinning, normais e tangentes) e o pós-processamento que suaviza as bordas da imagem. O foco agora é deixar o jogo mais leve para processadores comuns: o uso total de CPU já caiu ~10% (de 7,2 para 6,4 núcleos no menu) sem perder fps, e o próximo passo é a espera pelas consultas de oclusão (ZCULL) no thread do RSX. Esses números são de um Ryzen 5 5600G com uma RX 7600; num Ryzen 7 9800X3D com uma RX 9070 XT (RSX do RPCS3, Vulkan), o jogo chega a 60 fps fora das lutas e cai para cerca da metade nelas. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); e o jogo às vezes trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`). - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md).

## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), instale o launcher pelo `AscensionLauncher__x64-setup.exe` das [releases](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/releases) e, na primeira vez, aponte a pasta `ascension` em **Avançado › Pasta do jogo**. Ele se atualiza sozinho quando sai uma versão nova.

JOGAR abre o jogo; o launcher se esconde até ele fechar. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.
