# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**What stops macOS and Linux running a title is the PPU boot scaffold.**
`ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled per game,
not into the library. They compile on POSIX with zero errors (a CI ratchet
keeps it that way) and the frame clock runs there, but no title has yet been
booted to gameplay from this tree on either OS.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   └── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse
│   ├── hardware/             # cellGem, cellCamera, cellUsbd
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
└── docs/                     # See the Documentation table below
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

HLE implementations of the PS3 system libraries, written for this project. RPCS3 is a behavioural reference, not a code source. Most modules are complete. The ones still marked Partial are the media decoders (cellVdec, cellAdec, cellDmux, cellAtrac, cellAdecAtrac3p) and cellSpurs. [docs/MODULE_STATUS.md](docs/MODULE_STATUS.md) has one row per module and is the source for the counts.

| **Codecs** | cellPngDec, cellJpgDec, cellGifDec (stb_image) | ✅ Complete |

# Resistance: Fall of Man: native PC port

A static recompilation of the PS3 game *Resistance: Fall of Man* into a native Windows program. Nothing is emulated: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C/C++ and compiled for your PC. It renders through its own Direct3D 12 renderer, with NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA and AMD FSR 3.1.

> **No game files and no translated game code are distributed, in this repository or in the installer.** You need your own copy of the game. Setup decrypts its program on your PC, translates it into C/C++ and builds the game there; the generated code and the built game never leave your PC, and no prebuilt game program is released. The repository holds the port's own code plus the small references it needs to find its place in the game's program: function addresses, patch values and short context lines from the generated code (`tools/hooks/`).

## Highlights

- **60 fps and higher** (30 to 165, *Just under refresh* for G-Sync / FreeSync, or unlimited). Game speed is correct at every frame rate.
- **NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA, AMD FSR 3.1 and Intel XeSS**, NVIDIA Reflex, render resolutions up to 4K, and a *1080p → DLSS 4K* preset for RTX 40 / 50 cards.
- **Native PC controls:** raw mouse look (not stick emulation), rebindable keys, and separate melee and interact keys. Xbox and PlayStation controllers work and can be swapped at any time.
- **Button prompts follow your device:** your keyboard keys, or Xbox buttons when an Xbox controller is in use.
- **In-game PC menu** (F10, or hold Esc / Start): Resume, PC Options, and **Quit to Desktop** with a confirmation. No Alt+F4 needed.
- **Ultrawide (Hor+)**, field of view slider, performance overlay (F3), screenshots (F12), mods folder, and saves in *Saved Games*.
- **Launcher** that detects your hardware and picks recommended settings.
- **Performance work:** the renderer was profiled down to about 5 µs of CPU per draw (see *Performance*).

## What you need

- A PC running Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit).
- A CPU with AVX2 (Intel 4th generation or newer, or any AMD Ryzen).
- A DirectX 12 GPU. It has been tested on AMD (RX 6700 XT) and NVIDIA (RTX 5070) cards. DLSS needs a GeForce RTX card; every other GPU uses FSR 3.1 or Intel XeSS (XeSS runs on any DirectX 12 GPU with Shader Model 6.4).
- Your own dump of **Resistance: Fall of Man, US disc (BCUS98107), version 1.00**: the folder that contains `PS3_GAME`, the same kind of folder RPCS3 uses. Other regions and patched versions are not supported yet.
- About 25 GB of free disk space: 16 GB for the game files, the rest for the build tools and the build.
- An internet connection for setup.

## Install

**Quick install (recommended):**

1. Download the release zip from the Releases page and unzip all of it to a folder with no spaces in the path, for example `C:\Games\ResistancePort`.
2. Run **`Setup.exe`** in that folder. (It is not code-signed: if Windows says *"Windows protected your PC"*, click **More info → Run anyway**.)
3. Pick your game: **ISO...** or **Folder...**. Setup checks the copy at once and says what to do if it can't be used (see *If your game copy is not accepted* below).
4. Click **Install** and wait. Setup installs the missing build tools (one administrator prompt), copies your game files, builds the game with as many parallel jobs as your RAM allows, adds Start-menu and desktop shortcuts and starts the launcher. It shows the progress and the time left. If it stops (error, sleep, power cut), run `Setup.exe` again and click **Resume**.

The release contains no game code: the game is always built from your own copy. Requirements, disk space, build times, uninstalling and troubleshooting (SmartScreen, antivirus, low RAM, no winget): [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md).

### Manual install (advanced)

**With the Inno installer** (if a `-Setup-<version>.exe` is on the Releases page): download `ResistancePort-Setup-<version>.exe` from the Releases page and run it. It installs the port (default `C:\Games\ResistancePort`), adds Start-menu and desktop shortcuts, and asks for your game. It lists the copies it finds on the PC (common folders and RPCS3's game list); you can also type or paste a path, or use the **ISO...** / **Folder...** buttons. It checks the copy before going on and says what is wrong and what to do if it can't be used (see *If your game copy is not accepted* below). At the end it runs `Setup.bat` for you (step 2 below). The installer contains only the port; the game files always come from your own copy. Use a decrypted ISO or a game folder (the same kind RPCS3 uses). Tick **Portable mode** to keep settings and saves only in the install folder.

**By hand:**

1. Download this repository (**Code → Download ZIP**) and unzip it to a path without spaces, for example `C:\Games\ResistancePort`.
2. Double-click **`Setup.bat`**. It:
   - installs the free build tools if they're missing (Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, LLVM, CMake, Ninja, Python) using `winget`;
   - looks for your game (an ISO or a game folder), checks it, then copies it into the port folder (or moves a folder, if it's on the same drive);
   - decrypts the game's two program files using the application keys from RPCS3's public source code;
   - downloads the DLSS SDK and FFmpeg;
   - generates the game code from your copy and builds the game.

   The first run takes a while: installing the tools, plus a 20 to 60 minute build.
3. Play with **`Launcher.exe`**. On the first start it detects your hardware and picks recommended settings; everything is adjustable there.

Run Setup again only after downloading a newer version of the port.

**Choosing the game in Setup.bat:** it lists the copies it found, numbered. Type a number, or type or paste the path of the ISO or game folder (you can also drag it into the window). **B** opens a file picker (Windows only). `Setup.bat -Game "<path>"` skips the question. The path can be an ISO, the game folder, or a file inside it. An ISO is opened by Windows, copied from and closed again; if Windows can't open it, Setup reads it directly.

### If your game copy is not accepted

The installer and Setup check the copy before copying anything. The supported version is **Resistance: Fall of Man (US disc, BCUS98107)**, about 16.5 GB.

| Message | What to do |
|---|---|
| compressed archive (.zip, .7z, .rar) | Extract it first, then pick the ISO or folder inside. |
| PlayStation Store package (.pkg) / game update folder | Pick the disc copy. Game updates are not needed. |
| not <game> / from another region | Use the supported disc version listed above. |
| PlayStation Store version | Only the disc version is supported. |
| encrypted disc image / PARAM.SFO is not valid | Decrypt the ISO first (for example PS3Dec with the disc key from the `.dkey` file), or use a game folder from a PS3 or RPCS3. |
| program file was decrypted or replaced (plain ELF) | Use the original, unmodified files. Setup decrypts them itself. |
| files are missing / smaller than expected | The copy is incomplete. Copy or dump it again. |
| different from the known file (warning) | The copy may be modified. You can continue; Setup stops later if the decrypted program is not the supported version. |
| not enough free space | Free up space, or install on another drive. |

The checks run on your PC only. Nothing is uploaded.

**Updates:** the launcher checks this repository's Releases page once at start and says when a newer version is out (it only opens the download page; nothing is downloaded or replaced). Turn it off with Launcher → Advanced → *Check for updates* → Off, or the environment variable `PORT_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`. The installed version is in the `VERSION` file.

**Settings and controls** (`settings.ini`, `settings.bat`, `controls.txt`, `mouselook.cfg`) are also kept in `%USERPROFILE%\Saved Games\Resistance Fall of Man\config`. Missing files are restored from there when the launcher or game starts, so they survive reinstalling or updating the port. To keep everything in the port folder only, create an empty file named `portable.txt` next to `Launcher.exe` (the installer's *Portable mode* does this).

**No console window:** the launcher starts the game without a console. Everything the console used to show is written to `logs\run.log`.

**First launch:** the game shows its one-time "initial setup" screens. Shaders are compiled before the game starts, with a **Compiling shaders N / M** progress panel (see *Shader precompile*), so levels don't sit black while they compile. The shader cache is kept, including a backup that survives updates and reinstalls.

## Controls

Keyboard and mouse, Xbox controllers, PlayStation pads (DualShock 4, DualSense, DualShock 3 with its driver) and Switch Pro / Joy-Con all work, and you can switch between them at any time. Controllers are read through SDL3 (built in, no extra DLL), so **DS4Windows and Steam Input are no longer needed** (they still work; a virtual Xbox pad they add next to the real controller is ignored as a duplicate). If SDL3 can't start, the port falls back to XInput (`logs\run.log`: `[cellPad] controllers: SDL3` or `SDL3 could not start`).

- **Button prompts follow the last device you used.** On keyboard and mouse the game shows your key bindings. On an Xbox / XInput controller it shows Xbox buttons that match the real mapping: Cross = **A**, Circle = **B**, Square = **X**, Triangle = **Y**, L1/R1 = **LB/RB**, L2/R2 = **LT/RT**, L3/R3 = **LS/RS**, Select = **View**, Start = **Menu**. The Xbox glyphs are drawn by the port (coloured circles with letters); no Microsoft artwork is used. A PlayStation controller (by its SDL3 type, or with XInput by its USB / Bluetooth ID) keeps the PlayStation symbols. Switch controllers are read by button position (bottom = Cross) and show PlayStation symbols; with *Nintendo button layout = Nintendo style* A (right) confirms and B cancels, and the prompts show the Xbox-style letters. `RFOM_PAD_GLYPHS=auto|xbox|ps` overrides the choice (default `auto`; use it under Steam Input if the real controller type isn't reported).
- **Controller hot-plug:** controllers are polled every few milliseconds, so plugging one in or pulling it out works at any time without a restart. The log shows `[cellPad] controller N connected` / `disconnected`.
- **Mouse look is native.** Raw mouse movement (Windows raw input) turns the player's camera directly, 1:1 on foot; it is not converted into an analog stick. Scoped weapons scale it by their zoom.
- Melee and interact are split onto separate keys (on the PS3 they shared a button).
- Bindings are edited in the launcher (Controls page) or by hand in `controls.txt` (`KEY = ACTION`, one per line; the header of the file lists every key and action name).

Mouse and controller options in `controls.txt`:

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `mouse_look` | `direct` | `direct`: raw mouse deltas turn the camera. `stick`: the old analog-stick emulation. |
| `mouse_sensitivity` | `2.00` | Overall mouse speed (also multiplied by the game's own Look Sensitivity). |
| `mouse_degrees_per_count` | `0.050` | Degrees turned per mouse count in direct mode, before `mouse_sensitivity`. |
| `mouse_invert_y` | `0` | `1` inverts vertical look. |
| `mouse_deadzone`, `mouse_smoothing` | `0.28`, `0.03` | Only for `mouse_look = stick`. |
| `mouse_release_key` | `F8` | Frees / recaptures the mouse cursor. |
| `pad_interact` | `NONE` | A controller button that only uses things (doors, switches, vehicles); the Action button then only melees. `NONE` = as on PS3. |

More input options (launcher → Controls page, written to `settings.bat`; log line at start: `[controls] PC options: vertical mouse x.., stick deadzone .., curve .., zoom hold|toggle (game)`):

| Launcher setting | Choices (default) | Environment variable | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vertical sensitivity | 50%, 75%, **Same as horizontal**, 125%, 150%, 200% | `PAD_MOUSE_SENS_Y=0.1..4` | Up/down mouse speed relative to left/right (direct and stick mouse look). |
| Zoomed sensitivity | 50%, 75%, **Same**, 125%, 150% | `RFOM_ADS_SENS=0.1..3` | Extra mouse multiplier while zoomed or scoped, on top of the automatic zoom matching (`RFOM_ZOOM_SENS`). |
| Zoom | **Toggle** (PS3), Hold | `PAD_AIM_HOLD=1` | Hold: zoomed only while the zoom key / R3 is held. The game's zoom is a toggle, so the port presses zoom again when you let go (keyboard, mouse and the first controller). |
| Stick deadzone | **Default** (24%, per axis, as on PS3), 5-30% | `PAD_DEADZONE=0..0.9` | A radial deadzone for both controller sticks, rescaled so the full range stays usable. Raise it if the view drifts. |
| Stick response curve | **Linear**, Fast, Precise, Very precise | `PAD_CURVE=0.5..3` (exponent; 1 = linear) | Above 1: small movements are slower for fine aiming; below 1: quicker. A curve other than 1 also switches the sticks to a radial 24% deadzone when none is chosen. |

"Restore default controls" also resets these.

**Controllers (SDL3), gyro and light bar** (launcher → Controls page, and in game *More PC Options*; written to `settings.bat`). Rumble works on every pad that has it, DualSense included. **Gyro aiming** (DualShock 4, DualSense, Switch Pro, Joy-Con; off by default) turns the camera directly like the mouse (smooth, not limited by the stick; with `mouse_look = stick` it drives the right stick instead). Leave the controller still for about a second after it connects so its resting drift is calibrated.

| Launcher setting | Choices (default) | Environment variable | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Controller support | **SDL3**, XInput | `PAD_BACKEND=sdl3\|xinput` | XInput = the old path (Xbox pads and wrappers only, up to four, no gyro / light bar). `sdl2` is accepted and uses SDL3. Restart to change. |
| Gyro aiming | **Off**, On, While zoomed | `PAD_GYRO=0\|1\|aim` | `aim`: only while zoomed in / scoped. |
| Gyro sensitivity | **2x**, 0.5x-6x | `PAD_GYRO_SENS=0.05..20` | View degrees per controller degree. |
| Gyro vertical | **Normal**, Inverted | `PAD_GYRO_INVERT_Y=1` | On top of the game's own invert setting. |
| Gyro turning axis | **Controller**, Player | `PAD_GYRO_SPACE=local\|player` | Player: yaw follows gravity, so it works with the controller flat or upright. |
| Gyro calibration | **On connect**, Off | `PAD_GYRO_CALIBRATE=0` | Off: no 1 s still-calibration. |
| Light bar | **Player colour** (blue), Off | `PAD_LIGHTBAR=0` | DualShock 4 / DualSense light bar. |
| Nintendo button layout | **By position**, Nintendo style | `PAD_NINTENDO_SWAP=1` | Switch controllers: A confirms, B cancels. |
| (none) | **Automatic** (the first connected) | `PAD_P1_CONTROLLER=1..8` | Which controller (SDL3: in connection order) is the player's while it is connected; otherwise the first connected one is used. |
| (none) | **On** | `PAD_DEDUP=0` | Keep virtual duplicates (Steam Input / DS4Windows / ViGEm) as separate controllers. |
| (none) | **360** | `PAD_GYRO_STICK_DPS=deg/s` | Gyro speed equal to a full right stick (only when gyro drives the stick). |

### Keys that always work

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Alt + Enter** | Switch between borderless fullscreen and a window. |
| **F8** | Free / capture the mouse cursor (changeable with `mouse_release_key`). |
| **F10**, or hold **Esc** for 1 s, or hold **Start / Menu** for 1.5 s | **PC menu**: Resume / PC Options / Quit to Desktop (see *Window, focus and quitting*). It always opens on Resume (the mouse takes over the highlight only once moved). The game is paused and muted while it is up, and its SPU threads idle instead of spinning. |
| **F12** or **PrtScn** | Screenshot: a PNG in the `screenshots` folder (`RFOM_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_mmm.png`); a "Screenshot saved" toast shows briefly. |
| **F3** | Performance overlay (see *Performance overlay*). |
| **Alt + F4** / the window's close button | Also quits cleanly (waits for a save in progress). |

## Launcher settings

`Launcher.exe` writes `settings.ini` (its own choices) and `settings.bat` (the environment variables the game reads); **Play** runs `run.bat`, which loads `settings.bat`. On the first start (no `settings.ini` yet) the launcher detects your hardware and fills in the recommended settings. Each list tags the value recommended for your PC with a small "recommended" label. áudio: prioridade alta para a SPU que mixa o som; marca só para medir (sem espera)

A espera pelo jogo (98835b5) piorou muito com o processador apertado (691 buracos contra 38 em 80 s):
o escritor do GoW anda com o índice de leitura e nunca escreve o bloco que está sendo lido. Medido
com a marca: o jogo escreve 6 a 7 blocos adiantado, por PUT de DMA de uma SPU (o workload de áudio
da SPURS), então o silêncio vem dessa SPU sem CPU por mais de ~37 ms. Agora a SPU que roda o
workload que escreve nos anéis do cellAudio fica em THREAD_PRIORITY_HIGHEST enquanto ele roda
(GOWA_AUDIO_SPU_PRIO=0 desliga). A marca continua, só para o log: blocos atrasados e o
adiantamento do jogo (média, mínimo e histograma) na linha [audio].

98835b5cddcbed057bfb9029b9df4b6014b76bb6.message:
áudio: espera pelo jogo, thread com MMCSS e log de saúde do som (reports 285, 286, 259, 299, 346)

O relógio do dispositivo guiava a leitura do anel do jogo sem saber se o jogo já tinha escrito o
próximo bloco: num PC em que a tarefa de áudio do jogo (um job de SPU) atrasa, o bloco era lido
antes e tocava como silêncio, um engasgo em qualquer tamanho de buffer. Agora cada bloco consumido
guarda uma marca (um NaN) na última amostra; com o próximo bloco ainda marcado e mais de dois
blocos na fila do dispositivo, a leitura espera o jogo (é aí que o buffer de 100 ms passa a dar
tempo a ele), e um bloco lido ainda marcado conta como atrasado e toca silêncio sem a marca chegar
à mistura. GOWA_AUDIO_ESPERA=0 volta ao comportamento antigo.
A thread de mixagem entra no MMCSS "Pro Audio" com prioridade time-critical (o Xeon do 285 tem
todos os núcleos ocupados pelas SPUs). No log do jogo: [audio] a cada 10 s quando houve atraso ou
dispositivo vazio (senão a cada 60 s), e uma linha quando o jogo para de escrever o som por 3 s.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

SPU: corrida que apagava a reserva nova sem evento (trava do kick perdido)

O avisador de escrita (spu_coh_notify_write[_except]) verificava resv_valid
e resv_ea, marcava o LR e depois zerava resv_valid com um store comum. Com a
thread interrompida entre a marca e o store, a SPU consumia o LR, reservava a
linha do SPURS e dormia; o store atrasado apagava essa reserva nova sem evento
e a SPU nunca mais acordava (as SPUs se perdem uma a uma em sessões longas:
o jogo fica mais lento e o som degrada com o tempo).
Agora resv_valid guarda (linha | 1) e o avisador o zera com CAS condicionado
à mesma linha, marcando o LR só depois. As quatro escritas de event_status
que restavam (tag e stall-and-notify) passam a ser OR atômico.
Henry, série de 240 s: antes 1 trava a cada 4-12 rodadas; com a correção
22/22 limpas (gow-edge 0a02a86).

# God of War: Ascension — port nativo para PC

> **Projeto de fãs, sem fins lucrativos, sem relação com a Sony.** *God of War* é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. Este repositório **não contém o jogo** nem o firmware: você precisa da **sua própria cópia** do jogo (BCUS98232). O **update 1.04** e o **firmware oficial do PS3** são **gratuitos**, baixados direto da Sony (links em [Como jogar](#como-jogar)).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Para jogar, baixe o [Otavix Launcher](https://github.com/otavix010/otavix-launcher/releases/latest).** Ele baixa este port, gera o jogo no seu PC e o mantém atualizado sozinho. O port recebe **cerca de 6 atualizações por dia**, feitas a partir dos reports e pedidos dos jogadores: para relatar um problema ou pedir algo, use **"Reportar problema"** na página do jogo no launcher. O relatório já vai com o log, as configurações e as fotos, e é por ele que as correções saem mais rápido.
>
> **To play, download the [Otavix Launcher](https://github.com/otavix010/otavix-launcher/releases/latest).** It downloads this port, makes the game on your PC and keeps it updated by itself. The port gets **about 6 updates a day**, driven by players' reports and requests: to report a problem or ask for something, use **"Report a problem"** on the game's page in the launcher. The report carries the log, the settings and the screenshots, and that is how fixes come out fastest.

![Capítulo 16 a 66 FPS num Ryzen 7 9800X3D](docs/imagens/cap16_9800x3d.png)

[English summary below](#english-summary)

## O que é

Um port **nativo** do *God of War: Ascension* (PS3, 2013) para Windows. Não é um emulador: o código do jogo é **traduzido para C/C++ e compilado** para x86-64 (recompilação estática), em cima do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) do sp00nznet.

Como o código do jogo não pode ser distribuído, **o seu PC gera e compila a parte do jogo a partir da sua cópia**. Um comando só faz tudo.

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Fase 1, luta com a Fúria](docs/imagens/fase1_dodge.png) | ![Fase 1, close da Fúria](docs/imagens/fase1_furia.png) |

## Como jogar

### Recomendado: pelo Otavix Launcher

O [Otavix Launcher](https://github.com/otavix010/otavix-launcher/releases/latest) junta tudo num lugar só: baixa este port, confere se o Python e as ferramentas do Visual Studio estão instalados, pede só a pasta do disco (o update 1.04 e o firmware o gerador baixa da Sony; quem já tiver os arquivos, inclusive o PS3UPDAT.PUP, pode escolhê-los), gera o jogo para a sua CPU e abre com as opções de vídeo e os saves. Quando sai uma versão nova, ele avisa e atualiza. É o jeito mais simples; o caminho à mão vem a seguir.

### À mão

**1. O que você precisa ter:** só a sua cópia do jogo. O update 1.04 e o firmware do PS3 são gratuitos, e o gerador baixa os dois sozinho dos servidores oficiais da Sony (o RPCS3 não é mais necessário).

| O quê | Onde conseguir |
|---|---|
| **O jogo**: a cópia do disco do *God of War: Ascension* **BCUS98232** (EUA) | A sua cópia, numa pasta que contenha `PS3_GAME`, ou ainda compactada (`.7z`, `.zip`, `.rar` ou `.iso` decriptada): o gerador extrai uma vez (uns 35 GB livres). |
| **O update 1.04** (grátis, ~235 MB) | **Baixado sozinho pelo gerador.** Se preferir baixar você mesmo: **[o update 1.04 no servidor da Sony](http://b0.ww.np.dl.playstation.net/tppkg/np/BCUS98232/BCUS98232_T76/5525fbb7b6b5456d/UP9000-BCUS98232_00-GOWABDPATCH00001-A0104-V0100-PE.pkg)** (o arquivo `.pkg`; SHA-1 do arquivo `5a94c17aa07cb5181a505d3429c88ea3d9f4e4d0`). Tem que ser a **1.04**: as versões 1.05 em diante não servem. Se você já instalou a 1.04 no RPCS3, serve também a pasta `RPCS3\dev_hdd0\game\BCUS98232`. |
| **O firmware oficial do PS3** (grátis, ~200 MB) | **Baixado sozinho pelo gerador**, do servidor de atualização do PS3. Se preferir baixar você mesmo: na [página oficial da PlayStation](https://www.playstation.com/pt-br/support/hardware/ps3/system-software/), botão **"Baixar atualização do PS3"** (o arquivo `PS3UPDAT.PUP`, que o gerador aceita direto). Também serve a pasta do RPCS3 com o firmware instalado. |

**2. Instale as ferramentas (uma vez só)**, num terminal:
```
winget install Python.Python.3.12
winget install Microsoft.VisualStudio.2022.BuildTools --override "--quiet --wait --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Workload.VCTools --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Llvm.Clang --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.CMake.Project --includeRecommended"
```

**3. Baixe este repositório** (botão *Code > Download ZIP*, ou `git clone`) e extraia numa pasta **sem espaços no caminho**, por exemplo `C:\gow-ascension-pc`.

**4. Clique duas vezes em `gerar.cmd`** e escolha a pasta do disco. Ele faz o resto sozinho:
- confere as ferramentas e baixa o FFmpeg;
- baixa o update 1.04 e o firmware oficiais (ou usa os seus: `-Update` e `-Firmware`);
- prepara os arquivos do jogo, sem copiar os 34 GB do disco;
- decripta o executável;
- traduz e compila, escolhendo a build certa para a sua CPU.

Num Ryzen 7 9800X3D (8 núcleos) leva ~5 minutos; num PC de 4 núcleos, bem mais. Se parar no meio, rode de novo: ele continua de onde parou.

Versão nova do port: baixe por cima e rode `gerar.cmd -RefazerDe 4` num terminal. Ele refaz só a tradução e a compilação, sem repetir o disco, o update e o firmware.

**5. Jogue com `jogar.cmd`.** O log fica em `out\jogo.log` e os saves em `saves\`.

Opções (defina antes de abrir o `jogar.cmd`; pelo launcher, elas ficam nas configurações do jogo):
- `GOWA_FLIP_HZ`: limitador, padrão 60. Acima de 60 o jogo **acelera** (parte da lógica avança por quadro); `0` = sem limite, com teto de 240.
- `GOWA_RES_SCALE`: resolução interna, 1 = 720p, 2 = 1440p, 3 = 4K.
- `GOWA_VRR`: VRR (G-SYNC / FreeSync), padrão 1: cada quadro vai para a tela assim que fica pronto, sem esperar a atualização dela. Num monitor sem VRR a imagem pode rasgar em movimento; `0` volta ao vsync (cada quadro espera a tela).
- `GOWA_OSD=1`: medidor de desempenho na tela (FPS, ms por quadro, uso e temperatura da CPU e da GPU, VRAM e RAM; a temperatura da CPU some quando o Windows só tem a zona térmica da ACPI, que em muitos desktops fica parada). Vem desligado; **F10** liga e desliga durante o jogo (`GOWA_OSD_TECLA=0` desativa a tecla).
- **Tela cheia sem bordas:** **F11** ou **Alt+Enter** (também o botão maximizar, ou Win+Cima) cobrem o monitor mantendo 16:9, com faixas pretas em telas de outro formato; F11, Alt+Enter ou **Esc** voltam para a janela. `GOWA_TELA_CHEIA=1` já abre assim.
- `GOWA_AUDIO_MUTE=1`: sem som.

O jogo grava um resumo de desempenho em `desempenho.json`, ao lado do exe (ou em `GOWA_PERF_JSON`): CPU, GPU e FPS médio, p1 e mínimo do tempo jogando. Não é enviado a lugar nenhum; o launcher só manda, e só com a sua autorização.

Detalhes de cada etapa, e como fazer à mão: [docs/COMO_GERAR.md](docs/COMO_GERAR.md).

## Como funciona

O PS3 tem um processador central (PPU, PowerPC), seis co-processadores vetoriais (SPUs) e uma GPU (RSX):

- **PPU**: o executável do jogo é traduzido para C++ função por função pelo tradutor do ps3recomp, com os remendos do port aplicados por scripts.
- **SPU**: os programas das SPUs (jobs do SPURS, o EDGE de geometria, as tarefas de malha, o gerenciador de políticas) também viram C. Os laços mais pesados podem virar **núcleos vetoriais** gerados por scripts (AVX-512 ou AVX2), conferidos bit a bit. O código que o jogo carrega nas SPUs em tempo de execução e que não foi traduzido roda num interpretador.
- **SPURS**: a biblioteca de agendamento das SPUs (libsre) roda o código do firmware oficial (LLE).
- **RSX**: os comandos da GPU são desenhados em **Direct3D 12**, com os shaders do RSX convertidos para HLSL.
- **Áudio**: WASAPI, até 8 canais. Vídeos (MPEG-2) com FFmpeg.

## Estado atual

- Abre, passa pelos vídeos e menus, carrega saves e roda a **fase 1** e o **Capítulo 16** (a parte mais pesada que testamos) com imagem correta.
- **60 FPS travados** nas duas cenas num Ryzen 7 9800X3D, com o limitador ligado (padrão).
- O jogo inteiro, do começo ao fim, **ainda não foi verificado**.
- Só a versão **BCUS98232 (EUA) 1.04**: o `gerar.ps1` confere o executável e recusa outras.

## Desempenho medido

**Capítulo 16** (a cena mais pesada) e **fase 1**, em FPS de jogo, **sem o limitador de 60** (é como dá para comparar máquinas). **O hardware muda tudo**: o gargalo é a CPU, e CPUs com AVX-512 rodam bem mais rápido.

| PC | CPU | GPU | Build | Cap. 16 | Fase 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Principal | Ryzen 7 9800X3D (8/16, AVX-512) | RTX 5080 | AVX-512 | **~68** | **~84** |
| PC teste 2 | Core i5-11400F (6/12, AVX-512) | RX 9060 XT | AVX-512 (Rocket Lake) | **~32** (1ª execução) | — |
| Notebook | Core i5-10300H (4/8, sem AVX-512, ~2,8 GHz sustentado) | GTX 1650 | sem AVX-512 | **~8** | — |

> **A build que o `gerar.cmd` produz agora tem o mesmo desempenho da nossa.** Os passes de desempenho que aplicamos ao longo do desenvolvimento entram na geração (`scripts/otimizar.py`). No notebook, no cap. 16, a build gerada empatou com a nossa (antes da automação, ela dava 3,9 FPS). Depois disso, com a fixação de threads desligada em CPUs com menos de 12 processadores lógicos, ela chegou a **~8 FPS** (média de 200 s de fase, rodadas intercaladas). O PGO fica de fora; o que ainda difere está no fim de [docs/COMO_GERAR.md](docs/COMO_GERAR.md).

![Capítulo 16 no notebook com a build sem AVX-512](docs/imagens/cap16_notebook_portatil.png)

O que medimos num PC fraco (4 núcleos, sem AVX-512), o que ajudou, o que não ajudou e como medir: [docs/DESEMPENHO_PC_FRACO.md](docs/DESEMPENHO_PC_FRACO.md).

## Requisitos

- **Windows 10/11 64 bits** e GPU com **Direct3D 12**.
- **CPU com AVX2** (Intel Haswell em diante, AMD Zen em diante). **Com AVX-512** (Ryzen 7000/9000, Intel 11ª geração desktop) é muito mais rápido; o `gerar.ps1` escolhe sozinho.
- 16 GB de RAM. Espaço: ~3 GB para a geração e a build (o disco do jogo não é copiado).

## Problemas conhecidos

- **Engasgo na primeira entrada de cada área**: os pipelines de shader são compilados na hora e ficam em cache; da segunda vez some.
- **Sem o limitador de 60** o jogo **acelera**, porque parte da lógica avança por quadro.
- **Trava do leitor da GPU em PC lento**: corrigida. O leitor executava blocos de comandos que a PPU ainda escrevia; na variante rara, ele saía de passo com o bloco (ficava no meio dos dados de um comando) e agora volta ao início do trecho. No notebook: antes, 4 travas em 9 rodadas; depois, 17 rodadas sem nenhuma. Se a imagem congelar, relate com o `out\jogo.log` (procure `[park-settle]`).
- Travas raras de carregamento ainda em investigação.
- PC fraco (4 núcleos, sem AVX-512) roda, mas abaixo de 10 FPS nas partes pesadas.

## Licença e créditos

- **Nosso código e ferramentas: [MIT](LICENSE).** O RPCS3 (GPL-2.0) foi usado como referência de comportamento; o código foi revisado linha a linha contra o do RPCS3 e nenhum trecho foi copiado. A única coincidência literal são duas tabelas de valores medidos do hardware, herdadas do ps3recomp.
- **[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp)**, de Ned Heller (sp00nznet), MIT: o tradutor, o runtime e o motor de desenho em que o port se apoia. Ele vem dentro deste repositório, em `ps3recomp/`: o primeiro commit importa a v0.15.0 sem mudanças, e as nossas alterações vêm em commits separados logo depois.
- **`scripts/gpl/unself.py` e `scripts/gpl/pup_libsre.py` são GPL-2.0** (`scripts/gpl/COPYING`): o decriptador de SELF, que segue o `unself.cpp` do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3), e o que tira o `libsre.sprx` do `PS3UPDAT.PUP`, que segue o instalador de firmware do RPCS3. Os dois rodam como programas separados.
- **Chaves**: nenhuma chave foi criada por nós. As de decriptação de executáveis são lidas do código-fonte do RPCS3: o `gerar.ps1` baixa dois arquivos dele (`key_vault.cpp/.h`, numa versão fixa) para `dl\rpcs3_chaves`, ou usa os que você indicar com `-ChavesRpcs3`. A KLIC do jogo sai da sua própria cópia. O `ps3recomp` embutido traz, como o original, chaves públicas de formatos do PS3.
- **[FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org)** (LGPL), baixado pelo `gerar.ps1` dos builds do BtbN, para os vídeos.
- God of War e God of War: Ascension são marcas da Sony Interactive Entertainment. Este projeto não é afiliado nem endossado pela Sony.

## English summary

A **native PC port** of *God of War: Ascension* (PS3), made by **static recompilation**: the game's PPU and SPU code is translated to C/C++ and compiled for x86-64 on top of [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). The GPU command stream is rendered with Direct3D 12, and SPURS runs the official libsre module (LLE).

**Easiest: the [Otavix Launcher](https://github.com/otavix010/otavix-launcher/releases/latest)**, which downloads this port, asks for your folders, generates the game for your CPU and starts it. **Bring your own disc**: no game code or data and no firmware here. You need your own copy of the game (BCUS98232). Update 1.04 and the official PS3 firmware are free from Sony, and `gerar.cmd` downloads both from Sony's servers by itself (or use your own: [update 1.04 .pkg](http://b0.ww.np.dl.playstation.net/tppkg/np/BCUS98232/BCUS98232_T76/5525fbb7b6b5456d/UP9000-BCUS98232_00-GOWABDPATCH00001-A0104-V0100-PE.pkg) (must be exactly 1.04), and `PS3UPDAT.PUP` from [PlayStation's PS3 system software page](https://www.playstation.com/en-us/support/hardware/ps3/system-software/); RPCS3 is no longer needed). Install Python and the Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools with Clang (commands above), download this repository to a path without spaces, double-click **`gerar.cmd`** (it asks for the disc folder, then downloads the update and firmware, decrypts your copy, translates and builds; ~4 minutes on an 8-core Ryzen 7 9800X3D), then play with **`jogar.cmd`**.

Status: boots, menus, chapter 1 and chapter 16 play with correct image, 60 FPS locked on a Ryzen 7 9800X3D; the full game is not verified yet. Performance is CPU-bound and much better with AVX-512: ~68 FPS uncapped in chapter 16 on a 9800X3D, ~32 on an i5-11400F, ~8 on a 4-core laptop without AVX-512. The build `gerar.cmd` produces includes the same performance passes as ours (`scripts/otimizar.py`); only PGO is left out. Thread pinning is now off on CPUs with fewer than 12 logical processors (+4% on the laptop), and the GPU command reader no longer hangs on slow PCs.

License: our code is MIT; ps3recomp is MIT (Ned Heller); `scripts/gpl/unself.py` and `scripts/gpl/pup_libsre.py` are GPL-2.0 (they follow RPCS3's unself.cpp and firmware installer). Decryption keys are read from RPCS3's source (downloaded at a pinned commit). *God of War* is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment; this is a non-commercial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony.

6820c2bc54ebcd8f2258b5fc82dd5d054d274bda.message:
v18: hold the game-data check until file streaming settles (patch 6004 + host)

The v0.15 port's boot fix, missing in v18. J-Stars re-binds every CPK right after a successful cellGameDataCheck;
here the check is instant, so the re-bind lands mid-way through the boot-logo stream. CRI then falls back to a
loose-file open of game/logo/logo_US_v.pak that fails, and the boot either stays on "Now loading" or the skipped
block corrupts memory (null-page writes, stuck at flip 81).

Host: cellGameDataCheck override waits at least JSTARS_DATACHECK_MS (default 1000), then until no cellFsRead for
750 ms, at most 15 s. Patch 6004: cellFsRead records the time of the last read.

Attract-demo boots on the same warm cache: before, 4 of 6 runs failed this way; after, 3 of 3 reached the demo
fights (no failed logo open, no null-page writes).

a86cf1f54ad16e43931561c9fbb82dfd8d76b9ca.message:
Frame pacing: draw list of 8192, LATE_FLIP in the frame clock (patches 2913 and 6011, main.cpp)

A 2 against 2 fight with the town in view has 4,200 to 7,000 draws a frame; the
draw list held 4096, so every such frame was cut in two batches and the second
waited for the GPU. Flips also completed only on a 60 Hz tick and the game waits
for a vblank after each flip, so a frame a little over 33.3 ms cost 50 ms.
Patch 2913 raises the list to 8192; patch 6011 adds cellGcm_flip_ready() and the
frame clock in main.cpp completes a late flip at once, brings the next vblank
2.5 ms later and holds an early flip to 33.3 ms (LATE_FLIP=0 turns it off).

cebe4f52bfcc26947af28b4029ad40890a639553.message:
Toolkit patch 3004: cellAudio re-opens the default render device after a lost device or a default-device change

The WASAPI backend opened the endpoint once. When the device went away
(AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED and similar), the mix thread paced on the
clock with no output until exit. Patch 3004 re-opens the current default
endpoint on its own thread (retries 0.5-2 s), follows a default-device
switch, and retries when no device exists at start. The decision logic
has a host test (libs/audio/tests/test_audio_device_recover.c).

cec60694aac421a0d5398b6c4da15cd10bf2167f.message:
CI: make the host tests run on Windows

The runner starts Python tests with -X utf8 (-I ignores PYTHONUTF8, so printing accented or Japanese paths failed under cp1252). test_rpcs3_locate drops LOCALAPPDATA/APPDATA in the Wine-path case, portable_selftest compares paths with the platform's separators, support_bundle_test closes its zip files before the temp folder is deleted, and lan_discover_test compiles with the .NET Framework csc.exe on Windows instead of needing Mono. test_release_tag.py is posix-only: release.yml runs the tag step on ubuntu-latest and the test fakes gh with a script Windows cannot start.

v18: sound (patch 1003 JOBCRT Ver14 context pad, patch 3001 AUDIO_NBLOCK, host CRI_LEAD)

v18 was 100% silent: J-Stars' SPU jobs use a "JOBCRT Ver14" crt, and v0.18.0 fills the
job context's low 28 bits only for Ver13, so CRI's decoder jobs stopped before main.
Patch 1003 gives Ver14 jobs their descriptor's LS address there (SPURS_CTX_PAD=0 = off).
Patch 3001 adds the opt-in AUDIO_NBLOCK ring size; the host sets AUDIO_NBLOCK=16 and
CRI_LEAD=12 and raises CRI's lead in a cellAudioGetPortConfig override, as the v0.15
port does (there by an edit of the lifted driver).

Tested (US disc, title and menus, 240 s): before 100.0% silent in every window; after
0.0% silent once the sound starts; SPURS_CTX_PAD=0 silent again (48 of 48 windows).

1446337291.readme_excerpt:
J-Stars Victory VS-EX, Fan Revival

J-Stars Victory VS+ running natively on Windows: the game's own code, recompiled to x64 on your PC from your own copy.

Download · Installing · Features · Troubleshooting · Report an issue · Building · Contributing

--- J-Stars Victory VS-EX is an unofficial fan port of J-Stars Victory VS+ (PS3) to Windows x64. **Bring your own game:** this repository holds no game code, no game assets and no firmware (no ISO, EBOOT, recompiled game code, captures or screenshots). You need your own copy of the game (US BLUS31519 or EU BLES02136) and its decrypted EBOOT, from your own copy, see RPCS3 and its documentation. Please do not post game files in issues or pull requests. --- ## Status > **Pre-release (0.3.0), work in progress.** The default build is the v19 tree, built on ps3recomp v0.19.0 (installer switch `--tree current`). | What | Result | Measured on | |---|---|---| | Lift, build, boot, opening movie, menus, fights with sound | Works | One Windows machine, CI-built setup program | | Frame rate, default tree | About 30 frames per second in the demo and in Free Battle | One Windows machine | | Frame rate, its earlier v18 build (toolkit v0.18.0) | 16 to 22 frames per second | One Windows machine | | Frame rate, earlier v15 tree (`--tree legacy`) | About 29 frames per second in fights | One Windows machine | | Install with the setup program and the portable zip, menus, fights, online matches | Played | Play testers' own Windows 11 PCs, AMD and NVIDIA graphics | | EU disc, first-start window, long runs | Not re-checked on the default tree | Not measured | | Older CPU without AVX2 | Not tried; it will most likely not run | Not measured | | Linux and Steam Deck (Proton) | Not supported; an earlier v18 build reached fights under Proton in tests | Coming soon | The default tree has had fewer tests than the v15 tree and has known problems: see [KNOWN_ISSUES.md](KNOWN_ISSUES.md) and [issue #9](https://github.com/Tsamiuy/jsp-vs-ex/issues/9). Play testers' reports are in KNOWN_ISSUES.md. A dated table, refreshed 2026-10-30 and mostly for the v15 tree, is in [docs/notes/STATUS.md](docs/notes/STATUS.md). --- ## Download and play **What you need** | Need | Detail | |---|---| | Windows | Windows 10 or 11, x64. No admin rights. | | Your game | The disc folder (the one with `PS3_GAME`) of the US or EU disc. | | The decrypted EBOOT | `EBOOT.elf`, from your own copy. | | CPU | AVX2 and FMA (Intel Haswell, 2013, or newer; AMD Excavator or Zen). | | Disk space | At least 4 GB free for the build, then about 2.5 GB for the game data. | | Graphics | A Windows driver with Direct3D 12. | Linux and Steam Deck (Proton) are not supported yet. Every detail is in [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md). **Steps** 1. Download `jsp-setup.exe` from the [0.3.0 pre-release](https://github.com/Tsamiuy/jsp-vs-ex/releases/tag/v0.3.0). A portable zip (`jsp-0.3.0-portable.zip`) is there too. You now have the file. 2. Run `jsp-setup.exe`. The setup wizard opens. Windows may warn that the file is not code-signed. To check the download first, compare its SHA-256 with the release page: `SHA256SUMS.txt` for 0.3.0 and earlier, `SHA256SUMS` from the next release ([how](docs/INSTALL.md#check-your-download)). 3. Point the wizard at your disc folder and at `EBOOT.elf`. It checks both and names the problem if one is wrong. 4. Let setup finish. It builds the game on your PC, which takes a while. You see the finish page. 5. Open **JSP Fan Revival** from the Start menu. The launcher opens. 6. Start the game. The first start installs the game data, then the opening movie plays and the menus open. You can also build `jsp-setup.exe` yourself: [installer/README.md, "Building the installer"](installer/README.md#building-the-installer-windows). **If setup stops** Setup checks your inputs before the long build and refuses with a code: - `D1` to `D3`: the folder is not the disc folder, or the game is not US or EU. Other regions are refused. - `E1` to `E3`: the file is not a decrypted `EBOOT.elf`, or it is from the other region or another build. The game update 1.02 and digital editions are refused. - `P1`, `P2`: the install or disc path has characters that break the build. - `S1`: a folder is not writable, or there is too little free space. The full list is in [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md#what-setup-refuses). If the build itself stops, click **Build again** in the Start menu to resume it. --- ## What goes online and where your data goes Nothing goes online unless you turn Online Battle on. There is no update check, no crash report and no telemetry. The support bundle is a file on your Desktop that you attach yourself. Saves stay in `%APPDATA%\JSP Fan Revival\hdd0` (a portable install: `hdd0` in the install folder). Details: [installer/README.md](installer/README.md). --- ## What makes it different | | | |---|---| | Native x64 code, not an emulator: the game's own code translated ahead of time with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) | [docs/LAYOUT.md](docs/LAYOUT.md) | | Built on your PC from your own copy; nothing from the game is shipped | [installer/README.md](installer/README.md) | | Higher resolutions, a resizable window and borderless fullscreen | [Features: Display](docs/FEATURES.md#resolution) | | Keyboard, mouse or controller, with a launcher to rebind keys | [Features: Input](docs/FEATURES.md#input-modes) | | Training Mode in Free Battle | [Features: Training](docs/FEATURES.md#training-mode) | | The game's own Online Battle over a self-hosted re-psn server (experimental, opt-in, newer tree) | [docs/ONLINE.md](docs/ONLINE.md) (quick start) | | Coming soon: online matches with rollback netcode, spectating and lobbies | [Roadmap, section 4](docs/ROADMAP.md) | | Coming soon: more match options and Training options | [Roadmap, section 3](docs/ROADMAP.md) | --- ## Settings and controllers - **Controllers:** keyboard, keyboard and mouse, or a controller that Windows reads through XInput (Xbox-style pads). Buttons can be remapped in the settings window. - **DualSense and DualSense Edge:** read directly over USB or Bluetooth. This is marked "in progress", because the button tests are pending. It has no rumble or lightbar. - **Other pads:** a pad that only works through DirectInput is not handled by the code. Use the keyboard. - **Player 2:** the keyboard or a second controller. - **Display:** the picture is 16:9 today. The window, a resolution scale and borderless fullscreen (F11) are in the settings window. - **Wide monitors:** fullscreen stretches the picture to a monitor of another shape. Wide screens without stretching are planned. See [Features: Input](docs/FEATURES.md#input-modes), [DualSense](docs/FEATURES.md#dualsense) and [Features: Wide screens](docs/FEATURES.md#wide-screens). Saves, updating and uninstalling: [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md#saves). --- ## Known issues Heavy fights can drop to about 20 frames per second. The Training freeze after Return to character select and two online freezes are open. The default build needs a CPU with AVX2. The full list, with the build each affects and a workaround where there is one, is in [KNOWN_ISSUES.md](KNOWN_ISSUES.md). Status is tracked in [issue #9](https://github.com/Tsamiuy/jsp-vs-ex/issues/9). --- ## Troubleshooting and reporting bugs | You see | Do this | Log | |---|---|---| | Setup stops | Read the code in the message, see "If setup stops". Then click **Build again** in the Start menu. | `logs\firstrun-.log` | | A black screen | Click **Build again**. If that does not help, make a support bundle. | `game\run\launcher_log.txt` | | A pad does nothing | Use the keyboard, or an XInput pad. | `game\run\launcher_log.txt` | | Windows or an antivirus warns | The files are not code-signed; check the SHA-256 sums. | None | More symptoms and the log places: [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). To report a bug, click **Make a support bundle (JSP Fan Revival)** in the Start menu (portable zip: double-click `support-bundle.cmd`). It writes `jsp-support-.zip` on the Desktop. It holds logs and settings as text, never the EBOOT, disc files or saves, and it sends nothing anywhere. Attach it to a [new issue](https://github.com/Tsamiuy/jsp-vs-ex/issues/new/choose) and say which graphics card and CPU you have. The forms are: bug report, performance report, play-test report, feature request, and feedback or question. Never attach game files. --- ## Building Players build the game with the installer. For a hand build, the checks and the tree layout, see [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md), [docs/LAYOUT.md](docs/LAYOUT.md) and [installer/README.md](installer/README.md). --- ## How it works The installer lifts the game's PowerPC and SPU code from your `EBOOT.elf` to C. It compiles that with a bundled compiler and links it against the ps3recomp runtime. The runtime provides the PS3 system libraries and draws through Direct3D 12. Details: [installer/README.md](installer/README.md) and [docs/LAYOUT.md](docs/LAYOUT.md). --- ## Roadmap Close the open problems of the v19 tree ([issue #9](https://github.com/Tsamiuy/jsp-vs-ex/issues/9)), then online rollback, more match options and Linux through Proton. See [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md). --- ## Contributing Pull requests are welcome: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Only `main` is used. Rules for AI coding agents are in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Community: [Discord](https://discord.gg/h3j2wFwqvn). --- ## How AI was used Developed with AI agent assistance under the maintainers' direction. --- ## Licence and disclaimer The port's own code, tools and documentation are MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Security problems: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Unofficial fan project. Not affiliated with, authorized or endorsed by the game's publisher, developer or rights holders. Trademarks belong to their owners. **You need your own copy of the game.** --- ## Related projects and credits Third-party software and licences: [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md). People: [CONTRIBUTORS.md](CONTRIBUTORS.md).

every ~0.8 ms and burned half a core doing nothing, taking CPU from the game's

1446434740.readme_excerpt:
# Demon's Souls — native PC port (ps3recomp)

A native Windows build of **Demon's Souls** (PS3, USA, **BLUS-30443**), made by statically
recompiling the game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code to C/C++ with
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), plus a PS3 runtime and a Direct3D 12 renderer.
It is not an emulator: the game's code runs as a normal x64 program.

> **No game files are included.** This repo holds only the tools, patches and build scripts. You
> need your own copy of the game, dumped from your own disc. The setup reads your disc image and
> builds everything on your PC.

## Status

**The entire game seems playable.** It runs with sound and music at 60 fps (or 50 on a 100 Hz
screen, 30, uncapped, or any frame rate you pick), with keyboard + mouse or an Xbox controller. The game's movies play (title screen, intro,
story and endings; `set DES_MOVIES=0` skips them). The in-engine cutscenes are smooth at 60 fps and above too:
their camera is blended between its 30 fps keys (`set DES_CUT_BLEND=0` for the original nearest-key camera).

**Above 60 fps there are known bugs**, such as the sound drifting out of sync with the picture and the
character's run speed being off. 60 fps (or 50 on a 100 Hz screen) is the recommended setting; higher frame
rates are still being worked on.

**There is no online play yet.** Multiplayer will be added once the game is optimised.

**Performance:** on high-end hardware the game is mostly smooth. Optimisations for lower-end PCs
(fewer cores, older CPUs, Steam Deck) are happening now.

I'm currently playing through the whole game to find and fix any spots that still run slower
than they should (stutters, frame drops in heavy scenes). Boletarian Palace, the heaviest area
tested so far, is already smooth on a fast PC. Expect more performance fixes as the playthrough goes on; see
[docs/NOTES.md](docs/NOTES.md) for the full development log (50 fixes and counting).

If you hit a stutter or a crash, please report it: see
[Reporting stutters and crashes](#reporting-stutters-and-crashes). Every run is recorded, so all it
takes is pressing **F8** when it happens and running `REPORT.bat` afterwards.

## What you need

- **Windows 10/11 x64** and a **Direct3D 12** GPU. AVX2 (Intel Haswell / AMD Ryzen or newer) is used
  when your CPU has it; on older CPUs BUILD.bat builds without it (a couple of fps slower in the
  heaviest areas).
- About **14 GB** free disk space (8 GB game files + build + tools).
- **Your disc image** of Demon's Souls USA (BLUS-30443): a `.iso` (a Redump `.zip` works as is), or a
  dumped disc folder with `PS3_GAME` in it. A Redump-style encrypted image also needs its
  **disc key** (the `.dkey` file that comes with the dump). No `.dkey`? The key is public: it is the
  "Disc Key" line on [Redump's page for this disc](http://redump.org/disc/16199/) (Demon's Souls, USA, BLUS-30443, version
  01.00). SETUP opens that page for you when it needs the key.
- **Nothing else to install.** SETUP downloads what it needs into the folder (`deps\`), with no
  installer and no administrator rights: a portable **Python** and **Git** when you have none,
  **[RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net)** (used once to decrypt the game's `EBOOT.BIN`), and, without Visual
  Studio, a portable compiler (**LLVM** + Microsoft's C runtime and Windows SDK, about 1.3 GB, fetched
  by [xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin); Microsoft's license applies). The Python, Git, LLVM,
  RPCS3 and xwin downloads are checked against pinned or published checksums. Already have Python 3.10+, Git, RPCS3
  (`SETUP.bat --rpcs3 path\to\rpcs3.exe`) or **Visual Studio 2022** with *Desktop development with
  C++* + **LLVM** 17 or newer? Then those are used instead. RPCS3 needs the Microsoft Visual C++
  runtime, which most PCs already have; SETUP offers Microsoft's installer if yours does not. (Installed
  Visual Studio later and want it used? Delete `deps\.portable_compiler`.) Keep the folder's path plain:
  no `[ ]` or `&` in it (the build tools cannot handle them; SETUP says so).

**Linux / Steam Deck:** a setup + play kit (an AppImage) builds the same port from your own disc
image on Linux and runs it through Proton. See [docs/LINUX.md](docs/LINUX.md).
**It works on Linux:** set up and played on Ubuntu 24.04 (Intel i7-4770K + NVIDIA GTX 980). On that
4-core CPU it is still choppier than on Windows (Linux performance work is under way). A Steam Deck is
not confirmed yet; please report how it goes.

## Build it (one time)

The setup below has been tested on a clean Windows install (Windows Sandbox: no
Python, Git, Visual Studio, RPCS3 or Visual C++ runtime) and on a normal gaming PC.

1. Download the newest release: **[Releases](https://github.com/timboat/demons-souls-recomp/releases/latest)** → `DemonsSoulsRecomp-<version>.zip` (or the
   green **Code** button → *Download ZIP*, or `git clone`), and unpack it somewhere with enough
   space, for example `C:\Games\DemonsSouls`. Keep the path plain (no `[ ]` or `&`). There is no
   ready-to-play download: the game is built on your PC from your own disc.
2. Double-click **`DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe`** (it is in the release ZIP) and press **PLAY**. It sees
   that the game is not built yet and offers to run `SETUP.bat`: answer **Yes**. (Or drag your disc
   image onto `SETUP.bat`, or double-click `SETUP.bat`; same thing.)
3. Answer SETUP's questions. Pressing **Enter** takes the suggested answer, which is right almost always:
   - **your disc image**: drag the `.iso` / `.zip` / disc folder into the window (or paste its path) and
     press Enter;
   - **the disc key**, only for an encrypted image without a `.dkey` file: SETUP opens
     [Redump's page](http://redump.org/disc/16199/) in your browser; copy the long code on its
     "Disc Key" line and paste it with **Ctrl+V**;
   - whether it may **download** RPCS3, a portable Python / Git and the portable compiler (say yes);
   - the **Microsoft Visual C++ runtime** for RPCS3, if your PC has none: Windows asks you to allow
     Microsoft's installer;
   - **xwin** asks you to accept Microsoft's license for the C runtime / Windows SDK it downloads.
4. Wait for **All done**, then press **PLAY** in the launcher.

SETUP.bat then:

| step | what happens | time* |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | extracts all game files from the image (and decrypts them) into `game/` | 2–5 min |
| 2 | decrypts `EBOOT.BIN` → `EBOOT.elf` with RPCS3 and checks it is the tested version | < 1 min |
| 3 | downloads ps3recomp at the tested commit and applies this port's runtime patch | < 1 min |
| 4 | recompiles the game: ~94,000 PPU functions + 12 SPU programs → C/C++ in `port/` | 2–4 min |
| 5 | applies this port's edits to the recompiled code (`patches/lifted-code.patch`) | seconds |
| 6 | compiles everything with clang-cl into `port/build_opt/DemonsSoulsRecomp.exe` (plus `DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe`, next to `PLAY.bat`) | 10–30 min |

\* on a fast 16-core PC; the first compile is the long part. The compile shows one progress line
(`compiling 47/322 (15%)`); the compiler's full output goes to `logs\build_last.txt`. If anything fails, fix
what it says and run SETUP.bat again: finished steps are skipped.

## Updating

Press **Check for updates** in the launcher: it asks GitHub, lists what is new and, if you say yes,
downloads it, puts it in the folder and rebuilds the game; the launcher then opens again. **No Git
needed:** a copy from a release ZIP (or the Code ZIP) gets the newest release (checked against the
checksum GitHub publishes for it; your game files, build, saves and settings are not touched), a
`git clone` gets `git pull`. The launcher's status line shows which release you have.
Copies from before release v2026.11.03.7 need this once by hand: download the newest
[release](https://github.com/timboat/demons-souls-recomp/releases/latest) ZIP and copy everything inside its folder over your old folder,
replacing files (`game/`, `port/`, `deps/` and your saves are not in the ZIP, so they stay), then
press Play (or run **`BUILD.bat`**). It re-applies
the patches that changed since your last setup and recompiles only the files they touch. If it
says so, run `SETUP.bat` instead: that also works, keeps the game files and skips what is done.
If you forget, Play notices that the folder was updated but not rebuilt and runs BUILD.bat first
(an old build with new files can stay on a black screen).
Setups made before 2026-11-03 could not take updates (the patches were applied once and never
again); the first `BUILD.bat` or `SETUP.bat` with this version brings them up to date.

## Play

Double-click **`DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe`** (SETUP.bat / BUILD.bat build it next to `PLAY.bat`) and
press **PLAY**. The logos and first load take about a minute.

The launcher is one window for every option below: frame rate (Auto, 30, 50, 60, unlimited or any
number, with a line saying how it will look on your screen), internal resolution, Normal / PC Remaster
mod / your imported models, fullscreen, movies, god mode, frame-timing recording, texture dumping,
keys by letter and CPU core pinning. It remembers them in `launcher.ini`. Its buttons: **Check for
updates** (shows what is new on GitHub; on yes `git pull` + `BUILD.bat`, then it opens again), **Report a problem** (`REPORT.bat`), **Controls** and
**Folders** (saves, logs, recordings, texture and model folders). If the game crashes it offers to
make the report. *Extra settings* takes any `NAME=value` switch from this README or from an issue
(e.g. `LD_PSO_ASYNC=0`). `DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe --play` starts the game straight away with the
saved settings, for a desktop shortcut.

The launcher runs `PLAY.bat` with your choices. `PLAY.bat` on its own starts the game at 60 fps (50 fps
automatically on a ~100 Hz monitor, every frame shown exactly 2 refreshes), and the `set X=...` switches
in this README work in front of it too. The separate `PLAY_30FPS.bat`, `PLAY_REMASTER.bat` etc. are gone:
those are all launcher options now.

| launcher option | what it does |
|---|---|
| *Frame rate*: Auto / 30 / 50 / 60 / Unlimited / Custom... | Auto = 60, or 50 on a ~100 Hz screen; 30 = the original; Unlimited = up to 240 fps, no vsync, game speed stays correct; Custom = **any frame rate you type in** (31–240) |
| *Game*: Normal / PC Remaster mod / My models | your game as on the disc, with the *PC Remaster* mod installed, or with your imported models (see below) |
| *Dump textures* | saves every texture the game draws, for texture packs (see below) |

Without the launcher (Linux, or `PLAY.bat` by hand) the same choices are switches: `DES_FPS=30|50|60|unlimited|31-240`,
`DES_GAME=game_remaster` (PC Remaster) or `DES_GAME=game_mod` (your models), `LD_TEX_DUMP=1` (dump textures).
In the launcher, any other folder made by `tools\flver_tool.py import --mod <folder>` goes in *Extra settings*
as `DES_GAME=<folder>`.

**Custom frame rate.** In the launcher pick *Custom...* and type a
number, e.g. 45, 72, 120 or 144. The game
runs at real speed at any of them. If your monitor's refresh rate is a whole multiple of the number
(72 or 144 on a 144 Hz screen, 40 or 120 on 120 Hz), every frame is shown for the same number of
refreshes and motion is perfectly even. Otherwise vsync is turned off, which looks fine on a
G-Sync / FreeSync screen but can tear on others. The launcher says which one you got. You can also
`set DES_FPS=<number>` before running `PLAY.bat`.

**Higher resolution.** *Resolution* in the launcher, or `set DES_RES_SCALE=2` (up to 4) before running
`PLAY.bat`, renders the game at
2x its 1280x720 (2560x1440), much sharper, at no cost on the CPU side; a mid-range GPU handles 2x easily.
The window and borderless fullscreen show the picture at the window's own size, at the game's 16:9
with black bars on other screens (`set LD_SWAP_RESIZE=0` = the old stretched picture).
*Sharper shadows too* (`set LD_RES_SCALE_SHADOW=1`) also renders the 2048x2048 shadow map at the
higher resolution.

**Controls.** An Xbox (XInput) controller works when plugged in (A = Cross, B = Circle, X = Square,
Y = Triangle, LB/RB = L1/R1, LT/RT = L2/R2, Back = Select). A DualShock/DualSense needs Steam Input or
DS4Windows. Keyboard + mouse work too, also with a controller connected (the mouse takes over the
camera once you press a key or mouse button, and the controller takes it back when you use it):

| | |
|---|---|
| WASD | move |
| mouse (or IJKL) | camera (click into the game to capture the mouse) |
| left mouse | attack (R1) |
| Shift | strong attack (R2) |
| right mouse | block (L1) |
| Ctrl | parry (L2) |
| Space | roll / dash / back (Circle) |
| E | interact / confirm (Cross) |
| F | two-hand (Triangle) |
| R | use item (Square) |
| Tab / middle mouse | lock on (R3) |
| arrows | d-pad (switch items) |
| Enter / Backspace | Start / Select |
| Esc or F1 | release the mouse (F1 also captures it again; leaving the window or using a controller also releases it). Esc no longer closes the game: use the X or Alt+F4 |
| Alt+Enter / F11 | borderless fullscreen on/off (`set DES_FULLSCREEN=1` starts in it) |
| F9 | god mode on/off (no death, HP/MP/stamina stay full) |

**In menus** (title screen, Start menu, inventory, shops, level-up, ...) the mouse works as menu controls: **left
click = confirm**, **right click = back**, the **wheel** moves the cursor up and down, and the mouse's side buttons
or **PageUp / PageDown** are L1 / R1. A click in a menu needs no capturing click first. Outside menus the mouse
buttons attack and block as before. `set PAD_MENU_MOUSE=0` turns this off. (Pointing at an item is not supported
yet but is currently being worked on.)

**Button icons follow what you play with:** while the keyboard / mouse is what you used last, the game's button
icons (key guides, "Pick up" prompts, the HUD's equipment boxes, the Start menu tabs) show the keys and mouse
buttons instead of the PS3 buttons; touch the controller and they are PS3 buttons again. BUILD.bat draws them
once from your own copy of the game into `textures\kbm` (the letters are the game's own font). `set LD_TEX_KBM=0`
always shows the PS3 buttons, `set LD_TEX_KBM=1` always the keyboard ones. The title screen says "PRESS ENTER
BUTTON" instead of "PRESS START BUTTON" the same way.

The mouse turns the camera directly (no stick dead zone or speed limit) and follows the game's invert-camera
options. `set PAD_MOUSE_LOOK_SENS=0.0012` sets the sensitivity (radians per mouse count), `set PAD_MOUSE_LOOK=0`
goes back to the old stick-style mouse.

Keys go by position, not by letter: on an AZERTY or QWERTZ keyboard you move with the keys where
WASD would be (ZQSD on AZERTY), and the others follow the same way. `set PAD_KEYS_BY_LETTER=1` = by letter.

At *Create Profile* a text box opens for the character name. Saves go to `gamedata/`. Each run
writes logs to `logs/` (they grow by ~600 MB an hour; the previous run is kept as `*_prev.txt`).

## Reporting stutters and crashes

The game records frame timing while you play (*Record frame timing (F8)* in the launcher, on by default) (about 25 MB an hour, no visible cost; the newest
10 sessions are kept in `perf\`). The window title shows `[RECORDING - F8 = stutter, N marked]`.

1. **Press F8** in the game right after you see a stutter, hitch or slowdown. Each press puts a mark
   in the recording at that moment, so the exact frames can be found later. Press it as often as you
   like.
2. **After you quit** (or right after a crash), press **Report a problem** in the launcher (or
   double-click **`REPORT.bat`**). It packs the last
   session into one zip, shows it in Explorer and opens the GitHub *New issue* page.
3. **Open an issue** with the *Stutter / slowdown* or *Crash / bug* template, **drag the zip into
   it**, and say where you were in the game and what you saw at each F8 press.

What the zip contains (nothing else, and your Windows user name is removed from all of it):

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `report.txt` | the summary from `tools/perf_report.py`: frame pacing, every hitch with its likely cause (a slow game step, shader compile, slow file read, the renderer, the GPU), and what happened just before each F8 mark |
| `perf.txt` | the recording itself, so we can dig into the exact frames (trimmed to the minutes around your F8 marks if the session is too long for GitHub's 25 MB limit) |
| `system.txt` | Windows version, CPU, R

0097bed08208ab6863c40ead94e454bd382d5dc8.message:
Fix the GT5 race freeze: lock-line waiters stop starving an idle-priority holder

Phase 32's 1-4 s freeze was priority inversion on the runtime's lock-line
spinlock: an IDLE-priority PPU thread was preempted inside a coherent store
while ~18 higher-priority threads spun with SwitchToThread, which never
yields to lower priority. Waiters now Sleep(1) after 1 ms
(SPU_LOCKLINE_SLEEP_US, 0 = old spin); the lock records its holder for
[lockline] reports and the stall dump. HSR: 0 freezes in 6 races vs 3 in 5;
rollback reproduces. Synthetic test: 2559 ms -> 15 ms.

Skip the title's frame-pacer pad: it copied every hitch onto later frames

With every draw dropped the race still missed vblanks. The render thread
pads each frame with a sleep up to the slowest of its last four frames once
one passes a vblank (func_007AF300; the sleep returns to 0x00B24AF4). On a
console frame times vary by microseconds; here SPU spin waits and the odd
preemption made it fire constantly and turn one slow frame into a run of
them. The render thread's own CPU never exceeded 15 ms a frame.

Sleeps from that call site are now skipped by default (frame_pacer_sleep_lr
in config/targets.json; GT5P_PACER_PAD=1 keeps the padding). Frame test:
55 -> ~58 FPS, ~14% -> 7-9% of frames over 20 ms, p99 ~43 -> ~30 ms; no draws
59.3 FPS, 1.6% late. Game speed unchanged (0.99), rolling start still 30.

Diagnostics: PS3_USLEEP_LONG, PS3_USLEEP_SKIP_LR, timeline events C (render
thread CPU vs wall per frame) and Q (spin-wait sleeps), scripts/diag/
rtsplit.py. Phase 106.

Restore menu and race sound: SPU arithmetic in the audio DSP

The game-audio port's PCM turned to NaN in DSP image j9804ABA8. Two SPU
differences: 0 x extended-range estimate (from sqrt(0)) is 0 on the SPU
but NaN on the host, and SPU single precision truncates, while round to

GT5P_AUDIO_EXTENDED_ZERO, default ON); spu_native_patch.py wraps the five
measured coefficient-constructor calls in a round-toward-zero MXCSR scope
(GT5P_AUDIO_ROUND_ZERO=0 off). Live, scrubbing off: menu 77 s and HSR
race 145 s with no NaN/Inf; movie clean.

  priority) starved. A new post-lift step, scripts/spin_patch.py, makes
  the listed waits pause, yield, then sleep briefly.

  memory by every draw. A copy list now fills video-memory mirrors with
  what each frame wrote, before its draws.

went from 25.8 to 17.5 ms, and introduction GPU time from 12-15 to 6-10
ms. The introduction still locks to 30 FPS. Each change has a rollback
switch (Phase 101).

GT5 Phase 12: menu at full speed; milestone-driven GT5 tests

The FIFO walker dropped GT5's SPU display lists: a list parked at its write
head counted as "the same ring" as put because GT5 maps its main memory to
IO contiguously, so the walker resynced to put, lost the frame's user
command, and the render thread waited 5 s for every frame. Parks now count
as the PPU's ring only within 64 KB of where put has been
(GCM_PARK_PUTWIN). The menu holds 30 fps and draws its 3D background.

(GCM_USER_QUEUE); GCM_FLIPSUM / GCM_FTRACE_SLOW diagnostics; named and
file milestones in cellPad (SaveData, LoadData, MusicDecode,

c7034171f004431d548818b74ed0648a388802a0.message:
Fix shader-cache eviction that could drop the page to 8 fps (Phase 59)

A user run fell to 8 fps with shaders compiling. The pipeline cache
grows past 700 entries on one Car Dealer page; the old 1,024-entry cache
evicted by shifting entries and releasing a pipeline a frame in flight
might hold, so a longer session rebuilt pipelines in a cycle. It is now
8,192 entries behind a hash index, never moved, and emptied whole at a
frame start if it ever fills. The vertex-shader cache (indexed by slot
everywhere) no longer evicts at all. Car Dealer page median 30.6 fps.
