ecbd99f23f4662f69a1fd0f343dcb37c79fd8925.message:
GT5 Phase 11: doubled SPURS job completions fixed (heap corruption)

GT5's sound engine asks each DSP module for its state size through a
one-job SPURS chain and reads the answer from the completion event. The
module jobs signal for themselves, but the chain walker also sent stand-in
completions with data3 = 0 (per job, at END, at walker exit), which the
engine consumed as the answers to its next queries. Modules got 16-byte
state buffers and their SPU jobs wrote 16-35 KB of state over the menu's
heap objects.

SPURS_SYNTH_SKIP_SENT (default on): no stand-in when the job, pass or chain
signalled for itself. The menu's null calls are gone; a render SPU job still
waits on an RSX label (0.4 fps), which is next.

f3f50277a104c339749cda1f171d05a077f2056e.message:
GT5 Phase 9: memory accounting and pager faults; install runs to its end

GT5's pager budgets physical pages from the free memory lv2 reports and
trades its 1 MB reservations for 64 KB pages as faults arrive. The fixed
192 MB answer and silently committed faults left its heap unable to grow:
the install spun in page compaction, or deadlocked on a C library lock
leaked by atexit's error path.

ps3recomp patch: PS3_USER_MEM_ACCOUNT (syscall 352 reports total minus
base minus allocations; legacy mmapper unmap returns real ids, free drops
blocks), PS3_PAGE_FAULT=2 (faults reach the pager with flat blocks, a
mapped block's first touch excepted), PS3_PAGE_FAULT_LOG, memtrace lines.
GT5 defaults to accounting, PAGE_FAULT=2 and the lv2 area layout. The
install now matches RPCS3 for 746 of 747 file steps.

1446476478.readme_excerpt: # Project Tourline 5 **Gran Turismo 5: unofficial PC port (static recompilation)** [![No game files](https://github.com/mathewdouglas/Project-Tourline-5/actions/workflows/no-game-files.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mathewdouglas/Project-Tourline-5/actions/workflows/no-game-files.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) ![Status: early](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-early-orange) ![Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20x64-0078D6) ![Direct3D 12](https://img.shields.io/badge/graphics-Direct3D%2012-555) **[Getting started](#getting-started)** · **[Known problems](#known-problems)** · **[Progress](docs/progress-gt5.md)** An unofficial port of **Gran Turismo 5** (PS3, US disc BCUS98114, update 01.04) to Windows x64. It is a static recompilation: the game's own code, translated ahead of time to native x64, then run with a Direct3D 12 renderer. No emulator runs while you play. > **Status: early.** The game boots to the main menu with sound, and Arcade races run at around 55 FPS at High Speed Ring. Player builds are on the [Releases](https://github.com/mathewdouglas/Project-Tourline-5/releases) page; what changed in each is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). The investigation, with dates and measurements, is in [docs/progress-gt5.md](docs/progress-gt5.md). This tree continues [Tourline Prologue](https://github.com/mathewdouglas/Tourline-Prologue). Both are built with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), from the [sp00nznet/GT5P](https://github.com/sp00nznet/GT5P) port of Gran Turismo 5 Prologue. ### What you need - **Your own US disc copy** of Gran Turismo 5, **BCUS98114** (disc version 02.00), extracted to a folder: the one containing `PS3_GAME`, with `PS3_GAME\INSDIR` and the full `USRDIR\GT.VOL`. ISO files must be extracted first. The port runs the **01.04 update** executable from that disc's own `INSDIR/DATA000.PKG`, which is what a console and RPCS3 install before the first boot, so no update download is needed. - **Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit**, a GPU with Direct3D 12, and an internet connection during setup (for RPCS3; see below). - Nothing else. Setup fetches the official RPCS3 build on its own, uses it only to unpack the update on your disc, and deletes it. No game files, firmware or keys are included, and your disc folder is never modified. ## Getting started ### With the player download 1. Download the latest player ZIP from [Releases](https://github.com/mathewdouglas/Project-Tourline-5/releases) and extract it anywhere, keeping the folder together. 2. Run **tourline5.exe**. Keep the default storage folder (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\ProjectTourline5`) or choose an empty folder, including one on an external SSD. Saves, settings and shaders live there. 3. Select your extracted GT5 disc folder (the one containing `PS3_GAME`). 4. Choose **Prepare from my disc (recommended)**. That is all. Setup downloads RPCS3 (37 MB, the pinned official build), installs the 01.04 update from your disc with it, decrypts the executable and copies the verified files into storage. An RPCS3 window opens and closes on its own: leave it alone. It takes under a minute, then RPCS3 is deleted again. 5. The game starts. Later launches go straight in; setup is remembered. To use your own RPCS3 instead of the download, choose **Prepare from my disc with my installed RPCS3**; setup presses its Install button and closes it for you. Importing an existing 01.04 installation also works. ### With RecompLauncher Import the player folder, open **Easy Setup**, drop your extracted disc folder into the disc input, leave the other inputs empty, and press Play. Preparation runs the same steps as above, unattended. [RecompLauncher integration](docs/recomplauncher.md) has the details. ### Afterwards **Change storage.cmd** moves storage to another folder, copying and verifying it and keeping the original as a backup. **Change game files.cmd** selects the game files again. [Setup, storage and game-file selection](docs/setup.md) describes the full flow and its switches. Source builds put the same launcher in `build\tourline5.exe`, also opened by **Setup and play.cmd**. ### Developer layout The direct developer layout is also still supported: 1. Put the extracted disc where the port reads it: `input/pkg/PARAM.SFO` and `input/pkg/USRDIR/`, including `GT.VOL`. The port maps `/dev_bdvd/PS3_GAME/` to `input/pkg/`. 2. Decrypt the installed update executable, `dev_hdd0/game/BCUS98114/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN`, to `input/EMAIN.ELF`. RPCS3's **Utilities → Decrypt PS3 Binaries** writes an ELF beside that file. Write `BCUS98114-v104` as the only line of `input/target`. 3. Copy a finished install to `gamedata/dev_hdd0/game/BCUS98114`. That folder is `dev_hdd0/game/BCUS98114` from RPCS3, after the game's own install has finished. The port maps `/dev_hdd0/` to `gamedata/dev_hdd0/`. 4. Run **build\\gt5.exe**. It finds this repository by looking upward from its own folder for `input\EMAIN.ELF`. A first boot with only the update package's `PDIPFS` files, and with `GT.VOL` in place, runs the game's own install. That install copies the rest of the files out of `GT.VOL`. The screen order measured against RPCS3 is the warning, the install, the logo, adjust display, system files, the logo, the opening movie, then the menu. The keyboard is used when no controller is connected: arrows, Z Cross, X Circle, A Square, S Triangle, Q/W L1/R1, 1/2 L2/R2, Enter Start, Tab Select. **F1** opens settings. They are saved in `gt5p_settings.toml` in the selected storage (the repository root for direct developer launches). **F3** opens the profiler. F1 **Controls** has trigger dead-zone and response-curve options. **Feedback** offers optional SDL vibration, Xbox trigger rumble and fixed DualSense trigger resistance; these default off. The shared improvements adopted from Tourline Prologue, their rollback switches and remaining GT5 prerequisites are recorded in [the port review](docs/prologue-sync-review.md). `scripts\get_sdl2.ps1` fetches SDL2 for more controllers. `scripts\get_ffmpeg.ps1` fetches FFmpeg for the opening movie. Without FFmpeg the movie stays black. The build copies both beside the executable. Keep `shadercache/`. It belongs to this machine. **DXC** is the default shader compiler (player builds include it; source builds run `scripts/get_dxc.py` and rebuild). FXC stays available under F1 > Shaders. [Setup, cache separation and validation](docs/dxc.md). F1 > Shaders > **Draw while compiling** (on by default) draws a stand-in while a new shader compiles, instead of leaving the detail out. ## Known problems - A locked 60 frames per second is not reached. Warm High Speed Ring races run at about 55 frames per second at 720p, Eiger Nordwand in rain at about 47 to 50, and runs vary. The first visit to a menu, track or effect still has some hitches while shaders compile; later visits use the shader cache. - One-frame flashes (a purple road, grass on the road, noise in the mirror) were reported while thousands of shaders compiled. Copies that changed a texture the frame still being drawn had bound are now ordered with that frame. The flashes were not reproduced in the shorter local checks. - A split-second blue flicker of the road, about 18 seconds into a race and during the rolling start, was reported. Burst captures after that report did not show it again. - Online services are not part of this port. - Only the US disc build BCUS98114, update 01.04, is the current target. The measurement record is [docs/progress-gt5.md](docs/progress-gt5.md); release notes are in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) still describes the Prologue disc build. ## Building from source The supported game is the 01.04 update executable above. A source build needs your own dump, Windows 10/11 x64, Visual Studio 2022 (C++ workload), LLVM 18+ (`clang-cl`), CMake 3.20+, Ninja and Python 3.10+. Run `.venv\Scripts\python scripts/setup_runtime.py` first. It prepares the pinned runtime and this branch's GT5 compatibility patch in `../ps3recomp-tourline5`, without changing another project's runtime. `--check` verifies it. `scripts\build.cmd` uses that checkout unless `PS3RECOMP_DIR` is set. Per-build addresses live in [config/targets.json](config/targets.json). The 01.04 key is `BCUS98114-v104`. `code_end` is `0x011752A4`. The HLE and SPU lift scripts use the same runtime, including `PS3RECOMP_DIR` overrides. Use that toolkit for all lifter commands and the build. From your own disc and the decrypted 01.04 executable: ```bash echo BCUS98114-v104 > input/target python scripts/jumptables.py --write python scripts/code_labels.py --write T=${PS3RECOMP_DIR:-../ps3recomp-tourline5}/tools python $T/find_functions.py input/EMAIN.ELF --json --seed-json config/extra_seeds_bcus98114_v104.json --output analysis/functions.json python -c "import json; f=json.load(open('analysis/functions.json')); json.dump([x for x in f if int(x['start'],16) < 0x11752A4], open('analysis/functions_code.json','w'))" python scripts/gen_hle_stubs.py input/EMAIN.ELF analysis/hle_stubs.json python $T/ppu_lifter.py input/EMAIN.ELF --functions analysis/functions_code.json --output generated --code-end 0x11752A4 --header-name ppu_recomp.h --source-name ppu_recomp.c --hle-stubs analysis/hle_stubs.json python scripts/setjmp_patch.py python $T/gen_hle_nids.py --all --out src/gen/ppu_hle_nids.cpp scripts/build.cmd -DGT5P_TARGET=BCUS98114-v104 ``` `code_labels.py --write` is required. It seeds the computed-goto labels in the title's script VM. Without those labels the boot stops on a null object after the warning screen. Generated sources stay in gitignored `generated/`. The committed SPU registry is `src/gen/spu_workloads_bcus98114_v104.c`. Captured SPU images are produced locally with `SPU_DUMP_MISS` and `python scripts/lift_spu_jobs.py`. After every SPU lift, run `python scripts/spu_native_patch.py`, then `python scripts/spu_regpromo.py`, then `python scripts/spu_region.py`. The job bodies come from the executable (`wws_job_bodies` in [config/targets.json](config/targets.json)). Re-run the lifts when ps3recomp's lifters change. Then run `build\gt5.exe`. | Target | What it is | |--------|------------| | BCUS98114-v104 | US disc, update 01.04. This is the executable the port runs. | | BCUS98114 | US disc, version 01.00. A different executable. Kept, and not what a console runs after the update installs. | ## AI, licence, disclaimer Project Tourline 5 is developed with AI coding agents. The maintainer reviews their work before merging it. Numbers in [docs/progress-gt5.md](docs/progress-gt5.md) are what that phase measured. The port's own code, tools and documentation are [MIT](LICENSE). The licence covers nothing of the game itself. **Gran Turismo** is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This is a fan project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Sony Interactive Entertainment or Polyphony Digital. **You need your own copy of the game.** This repository contains the port: source, tools and documentation. It contains no game code, data, assets, keys or firmware. `scripts/check_no_game_files.py` refuses those files on every push. Gran Turismo 5 is © Sony Interactive Entertainment.

# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. > [!WARNING] > **Um experimento: ainda não dá para jogar do começo ao fim.** O jogo chega ao primeiro nível e à primeira luta contra um chefe, mas ainda lento (~18-23 fps no nível, 13-21 na luta). Feito para Windows; no macOS (Apple Silicon) ele voltou a rodar, por enquanto só para testes. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Novembro de 2026, no Windows (e no Mac, em testes): - **Do boot à primeira luta contra um chefe:** telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Desempenho:** menu principal a ~50-55 fps; o primeiro nível a ~22-27 fps, conforme a cena (era ~9); a luta contra o chefe a 13-21. Na mesma cena do primeiro nível, o RPCS3 faz 35-40 fps: é a distância que queremos vencer. Em novembro o quadro do primeiro nível foi medido parte por parte: dos ~50 ms, ~21 ms são as listas de geometria das SPUs (o EDGE), ~9-12 ms o jogo espera o thread do RSX entre as duas passadas dessa geometria, e o resto são os jobs de renderização no começo e no fim do quadro. Já entraram como padrão o thread do RSX dormir quando a fila de comandos está vazia, em vez de girar (~8% a menos no tempo do quadro num PC de 4 núcleos), e as SPUs escolherem sozinhas o próximo trabalho (~1,6% a menos no mesmo PC). Os próximos passos: ver exatamente o que o RSX faz naquela espera e levar o módulo de geometria das SPUs para código nativo. Partes pesadas das SPUs já rodam como código nativo, cada uma conferida contra o original: a geometria por draw (índices, skinning, normais e tangentes) e o pós-processamento que suaviza as bordas da imagem. Esses números são de um Ryzen 5 5600G com uma RX 7600; num Ryzen 7 9800X3D com uma RX 9070 XT (RSX do RPCS3, Vulkan), o jogo chega a 60 fps fora das lutas e cai para cerca da metade nelas. - **Travamento corrigido:** o jogo às vezes congelava no nível com as listas de geometria das SPUs esperando para sempre. A causa era uma escrita do processador principal que se perdia no meio de uma operação atômica de uma SPU; corrigida, a reprodução passou de 3 travamentos em 5 rodadas para nenhum em 4. - **Multijogador (em desenvolvimento):** com um servidor próprio do projeto (ainda privado), o jogo já entra no multijogador, chega ao lobby do guerreiro e guarda o perfil do jogador na conta. A partida online ainda não funciona. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); o jogo às vezes ainda trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`; conferindo se a correção acima também resolve este); e a fila de comandos de vídeo às vezes chega corrompida (`FIFO error: possible desync`), mais vezes no Mac: o thread do RSX agora se recupera em vez de travar o jogo, mas a causa ainda está aberta. - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas e mods; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado a partir do seu disco americano. As mudanças de novembro estão no branch [`ascension-perf`](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/tree/ascension-perf) até serem medidas no Windows. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md).

## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), instale o launcher pelo `AscensionLauncher__x64-setup.exe` das [releases](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/releases) e, na primeira vez, aponte a pasta `ascension` em **Avançado › Pasta do jogo**. Ele se atualiza sozinho quando sai uma versão nova.

JOGAR abre o jogo; o launcher se esconde até ele fechar. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Mods:** liga, desliga e ordena. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Criar mod PT-BR** monta o português do Brasil a partir da imagem do seu disco americano. Os mods incluídos são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

cdb581579fd7ba76d429fab741828ce9e04161d6.message:
Low-CPU update: fewer threads on weaker PCs, support for CPUs without AVX2

- SPURS: on PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the lanes/kernels spin less, wake the
  main thread sooner and run on fewer threads (4-thread PCs: ~10 fps -> ~29 fps,
  8 threads: ~38 -> ~50 fps). Big PCs keep the old behaviour.
- Vertex workers spin far less after each job, fewer workers on small CPUs.
- The once-per-second thread scan only walks the game's own threads.
- No exclusive core reservations on PCs with fewer than 20 CPU threads;
  P-core pinning only on hybrid CPUs with at least 8 P-core threads.
- CPUs without AVX2/FMA/BMI2 (pre-2013 Intel, AVX-less Pentium/Celeron, AMD before
  2015): Setup/the updater detect this and build an SSE4.1 compatibility version
  automatically (same results, slower). The game also checks the CPU at startup and
  shows a clear message instead of crashing.

# inFamous PC

> **Official repo: [github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn).**
> Only download the Setup from the [Releases page](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn/releases) here.
> Forks are not supported, and bugs from forks won't be fixed.

An unofficial native Windows port of **inFamous** (PlayStation 3, 2009, European
release `BCES00220`). The game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code is statically
recompiled to x86-64 C/C++ with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp),
so it runs as a normal Windows program rather than under an emulator.

**This repository contains no game code or data.** You build the game yourself,
on your own PC, from your own copy of the game.

## Easy install

Download **inFamous Setup.exe** from the latest release, run it, choose your
`.iso` (an encrypted image works with its `.dkey` next to it) or your game
folder (the one with `PS3_GAME` in it), pick an install location and press
**Install**.

Setup checks for Python and the C++ build tools and offers to install them,
copies the game out of the disc image, regenerates the recompiled code from your
copy, builds it and adds an inFamous shortcut. Running Setup again on the same
folder updates or repairs the install and only redoes what changed.

## Updating

When a new version is published here, players update in place instead of reinstalling:
**Update now** in Setup (it finds the existing install), the **Update inFamous** shortcut in
the Start menu, or `Update inFamous.cmd` in the install folder. The updater compares every file
with this repository, downloads only what changed, regenerates the game code only if the
port's patches changed, and recompiles only the affected parts. Installs made with an older
Setup need one run of the new Setup on the same folder first.

## Requirements

- Your own inFamous disc dump, European release (`BCES00220`).
- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with Direct3D 12 support.
- A CPU with SSE4.1 (2008 or newer). On CPUs without AVX2 (Intel before 2013, Pentium/Celeron
  without AVX, AMD before 2015) Setup builds a slower compatibility version automatically.
  On PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the game uses fewer threads and less CPU (tested down to 4 threads).
- [Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) with "Add python.exe to
  PATH" ticked.
- [Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/)
  with the **Desktop development with C++** workload and the **C++ Clang
  Compiler for Windows** component.
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), only if your `PS3_GAME\USRDIR` has `EBOOT.BIN`
  but no decrypted `EBOOT.elf`. Setup uses it to decrypt the executable.
- About 10 GB of free disk space and 16 GB of RAM.

## Building manually

```bat
cd installer
cargo build --release
target\release\infamous-installer --game "D:\Dumps\inFamous"
```

`infamous-installer doctor` checks the requirements only. Finished steps are
skipped when you run it again, so an interrupted install continues where it
stopped. See [installer/README.md](installer/README.md) for every step and the
maintainer commands.

## Playing

Run **inFamous** (the shortcut Setup made). It opens a small options window first
(vsync, frame cap, resolution, language and more, saved to `settings.ini`);
**Play** starts the game. The same settings are in the game's pause menu under
**Settings**. Controllers work as on the console, and keyboard and mouse are supported.

**F10** opens the in-game trainer: God Mode, Infinite Energy, Refill Health,
Max Health x2/x5/x10, Add XP, Karma +/-, Kill Enemies / Civilians, Super Speed
and Player Model (play as Zeke, Trish, Kessler, Alden or John). Set `TRAINER=0`
to turn it off.

## DLSS and FSR (optional)

The game can use NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA or AMD FSR for upscaling, and AMD FSR frame generation.
They are not included in the download because NVIDIA and AMD distribute their SDKs themselves,
but both are free and take a few minutes to add.

- **DLSS** needs an NVIDIA RTX graphics card.
- **FSR** works on any modern GPU (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel). FSR 4 needs a Radeon RX 9000 card;
  other cards get FSR 3.1 automatically.

**1. Download the SDK(s) you want.** You need the **source code**, not a Windows or Linux demo.
On the page, click the green **Code** button, then **Download ZIP**. If you go through the
Releases page instead, pick **Source code (zip)**, not the files with "demo" or "samples" in the name.

| For | Download | Rename the extracted folder to |
|---|---|---|
| DLSS / DLAA | [github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS) | `dlss-sdk` |
| FSR and frame generation | [github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK) | `fsr-sdk` |

**2. Put the folder(s) in your inFamous install folder**, next to `infamous-recomp` and
`ps3recomp`:

```
inFamous\
  dlss-sdk\        <- contains include\ and lib\
  fsr-sdk\         <- contains Kits\
  infamous-recomp\
  ps3recomp\
  ...
```

Make sure you don't end up with a folder inside a folder (`dlss-sdk\DLSS-main\include`).
`include` (DLSS) or `Kits` (FSR) must be directly inside.

**3. Rebuild the game once.** Open a Command Prompt in the install folder and run:

```bat
type nul > .installer\update.pending
"Update inFamous.cmd"
```

This rebuilds the game with the SDK(s), which takes a while. Any later update also picks them up
automatically, so you only do this once.

**4. Turn it on in game:** pause, then **Settings**, then **Upscaling** (DLAA, DLSS Quality /
Balanced / Performance, FSR Native AA / Quality / Balanced / Performance) and **Frame
Generation**. The same options are in the launcher's options window. Upscaling and frame
generation apply after a restart.

If the **Upscaling** row is missing, the build didn't find the SDK: check the folder names and
layout from step 2, then repeat step 3.

## How it works

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `ps3recomp` | The recompiler toolkit and runtime: PPU and SPU lifters, HLE system libraries, RSX on Direct3D 12, audio and input |
| `infamous-recomp` | The inFamous-specific parts: program entry, game stubs and fixes, asset tools |
| `installer` | Setup and the command-line installer: reads the disc, regenerates the code from your game, applies `installer/patches`, builds |
| `installer/infamous.toml` | Everything about the game and the port: pipeline steps, generated files, build and launch settings |
| `installer/generated.lock` | Hashes of each generated file before and after the port's patches |

## Credits

- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet and
  contributors (see [ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md](ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md)).
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), used to decrypt the game executable.
- Sucker Punch Productions, for the game.
- [Lorenzo Aiello](https://github.com/aiellolorenzo23) and [ibrahimpuri](https://github.com/ibrahimpuri), for their support.

06caadeb929bd996a69f14d5c13bc2faace29054.message:
Smoother new areas, texture heaps, and the Storm King arena's missing geometry

- New shaders compile on worker threads instead of freezing the game (the
  slowest took ~300 ms each); a model whose shader is not ready yet is drawn
  a few frames late, screen-critical passes still wait. LD_PSO_ASYNC=0 = old.
- A direct flip wakes the presenting thread at once (was up to 4 ms late).
- Guest textures are placed in 64 MB heaps instead of one driver
  allocation each (arrival texture creation 126 -> 11 ms).
- The shader disk cache is read into memory during the logos (cold
  per-file reads froze the first gameplay frame for ~0.6 s).
- A draw kept at most 256 packets (65,536 indices) and dropped the rest:
  the Storm King arena lost whole meshes. Now 16,384 packets.
- perf_report.py understands the new pipeline / texture timing lines.
Details and measurements: docs/NOTES.md fixes 62-64.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

0816da134edec71a2468b3732fdae0a055d15299.message:
Sound thread no longer drops voices; SPU float zeros in the vector path

- synth2 (the SPU sound synthesizer) sat at 90-100% of a core once
  voices started and was dropping work: effects came out quieter or
  missing. Its voice-clear loop (112 bytes, one byte per pass, ~30% of
  the thread) now does its stores directly and ends in the exact same
  state. synth2 92% -> 62%; standing-still audio is bit-identical.
- AVX2 SPU fa/fm/fma: SPU zeros and underflow handled in the vector
  path like the NEON path (0 mismatches vs the exact reference on
  20M random vectors; 5x faster on denormal-range data).
- PLAY.bat records late-step stack samples (main + HighGraphics) so a
  freeze in a recording says what the game was doing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

0a96a611057b4c568ab490a88c5aea43c40443e8.message:
Make AVX2 optional: build without it on CPUs that lack it

with a "needs AVX2" message on older CPUs. BUILD.bat now checks the CPU
(IsProcessorFeaturePresent) and passes DS_AVX2=ON/OFF to CMake; without
AVX2 the SPU float ops use their exact scalar paths (~2 fps slower in the
heaviest area). "set DS_AVX2=0" builds a copy for an older PC. PLAY.bat
only asks for AVX2 when the build used it (port/build_opt/no_avx2.txt).

124c0b431a7be2f6a577be48b441abb47b748fc8.message:
Pointing in menus: the item under the mouse arrow is selected, a click confirms it

In a menu the mouse is released and the Windows arrow shows. Every menu
item is a shape the dialog draw loop draws with its world matrix, so its
screen rectangle is known each frame; the focused dialog's own step
functions then move the selection to the item under the arrow, with the
game's sound, help text and highlight. A left click confirms on the

The remo cutscene camera sampler (func_005F71D0) picked the nearest of the
track's keys, which are baked one per 1/30 s. At 30 fps the cut time lands on
keys; at 60 every other frame is half way, so the camera moved 30 times a
second while the characters moved 60: the picture moved in pairs (the
tutorial's opening walk through the black void, the Nexus intro, ...).

the other Euler set at a flip); holds, shot changes inside a track (> 2 m,
> 0.5 rad, scale > 0.25) and unset keys keep the nearest key, as lifted.
DES_CUT_BLEND=0 restores the original. Analysis credit: JonathanDC64/
DemonsSoulsRecomp (MIT), docs/40 and docs/62.

59 paired seconds -> 0; Nexus intro 56 of 64 -> 0; game time 1.000, no long

The game's sub-millisecond usleeps were busy-waited: the streaming thread polls
every ~0.8 ms and burned half a core doing nothing, taking CPU from the game's
real threads on 4-6 core PCs. Waits of 200 us and longer now sleep on a
per-thread high-resolution timer (Windows 10 1803+); shorter ones still spin.

sampled a coprocessor (SPU) thread, and could deadlock on a lock the paused
thread held. It now copies the stack, resumes the thread and unwinds the copy.

Every PPU store to an SPU-reserved line walked the WAIT_SIGNAL watch list
(6 nodes on parked tasks' stacks, a cache miss each) -- 1.75M stores/s
from HighGraphics into the SPU command-queue line. A 64-bit mask of the
watched lines, on its own cache line and kept under the lock-line lock,
lets spu_coh_wake_watches return at once for unwatched lines.

Frames over 25 ms 42 -> 25 on average. NOTES fix 90.

1447361124.readme_excerpt:
# Demon's Souls — native PC port (ps3recomp)

A native Windows build of **Demon's Souls** (PS3, USA, **BLUS-30443**), made by statically
recompiling the game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code to C/C++ with
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), plus a PS3 runtime and a Direct3D 12 renderer.
It is not an emulator: the game's code runs as a normal x64 program.

> **No game files are included.** This repo holds only the tools, patches and build scripts. You
> need your own copy of the game, dumped from your own disc. The setup reads your disc image and
> builds everything on your PC.

## Status

**The entire game seems playable.** It runs with sound and music at 60 fps (or 50 on a 100 Hz
screen, 30, uncapped, or any frame rate you pick), with keyboard + mouse or an Xbox controller. The game's movies play (title screen, intro,
story and endings; `set DES_MOVIES=0` skips them). The in-engine cutscenes are smooth at 60 fps and above too:
their camera is blended between its 30 fps keys (`set DES_CUT_BLEND=0` for the original nearest-key camera).

**Above 60 fps there are known bugs**, such as the sound drifting out of sync with the picture and the
character's run speed being off. 60 fps (or 50 on a 100 Hz screen) is the recommended setting; higher frame
rates are still being worked on.

**There is no online play yet.** Multiplayer will be added once the game is optimised.

**Performance:** on high-end hardware the game is mostly smooth. Optimisations for lower-end PCs
(fewer cores, older CPUs, Steam Deck) are happening now.

I'm currently playing through the whole game to find and fix any spots that still run slower
than they should (stutters, frame drops in heavy scenes). Boletarian Palace, the heaviest area
tested so far, is already smooth on a fast PC. Expect more performance fixes as the playthrough goes on; see
[docs/NOTES.md](docs/NOTES.md) for the full development log (50 fixes and counting).

If you hit a stutter or a crash, please report it: see
[Reporting stutters and crashes](#reporting-stutters-and-crashes). Every run is recorded, so all it
takes is pressing **F8** when it happens and running `REPORT.bat` afterwards.

## What you need

- **Windows 10/11 x64** and a **Direct3D 12** GPU. AVX2 (Intel Haswell / AMD Ryzen or newer) is used
  when your CPU has it; on older CPUs BUILD.bat builds without it (a couple of fps slower in the
  heaviest areas).
- About **14 GB** free disk space (8 GB game files + build + tools).
- **Your disc image** of Demon's Souls USA (BLUS-30443): a `.iso` (a Redump `.zip` works as is), or a
  dumped disc folder with `PS3_GAME` in it. A Redump-style encrypted image also needs its
  **disc key** (the `.dkey` file that comes with the dump). No `.dkey`? The key is public: it is the
  "Disc Key" line on [Redump's page for this disc](http://redump.org/disc/16199/) (Demon's Souls, USA, BLUS-30443, version
  01.00). SETUP opens that page for you when it needs the key.
- **Nothing else to install.** SETUP downloads what it needs into the folder (`deps\`), with no
  installer and no administrator rights: a portable **Python** and **Git** when you have none,
  **[RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net)** (used once to decrypt the game's `EBOOT.BIN`), and, without Visual
  Studio, a portable compiler (**LLVM** + Microsoft's C runtime and Windows SDK, about 1.3 GB, fetched
  by [xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin); Microsoft's license applies). The Python, Git, LLVM,
  RPCS3 and xwin downloads are checked against pinned or published checksums. Already have Python 3.10+, Git, RPCS3
  (`SETUP.bat --rpcs3 path\to\rpcs3.exe`) or **Visual Studio 2022** with *Desktop development with
  C++* + **LLVM** 17 or newer? Then those are used instead. RPCS3 needs the Microsoft Visual C++
  runtime, which most PCs already have; SETUP offers Microsoft's installer if yours does not. (Installed
  Visual Studio later and want it used? Delete `deps\.portable_compiler`.) Keep the folder's path plain:
  no `[ ]` or `&` in it (the build tools cannot handle them; SETUP says so).

**Linux / Steam Deck:** a setup + play kit (an AppImage) builds the same port from your own disc
image on Linux and runs it through Proton. See [docs/LINUX.md](docs/LINUX.md).
**It works on Linux:** set up and played on Ubuntu 24.04 (Intel i7-4770K + NVIDIA GTX 980). On that
4-core CPU it is still choppier than on Windows (Linux performance work is under way). A Steam Deck is
not confirmed yet; please report how it goes.

## Build it (one time)

The setup below has been tested on a clean Windows install (Windows Sandbox: no
Python, Git, Visual Studio, RPCS3 or Visual C++ runtime) and on a normal gaming PC.

1. Download the newest release: **[Releases](https://github.com/timboat/demons-souls-recomp/releases/latest)** → `DemonsSoulsRecomp-<version>.zip` (or the
   green **Code** button → *Download ZIP*, or `git clone`), and unpack it somewhere with enough
   space, for example `C:\Games\DemonsSouls`. Keep the path plain (no `[ ]` or `&`). There is no
   ready-to-play download: the game is built on your PC from your own disc.
2. Double-click **`DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe`** (it is in the release ZIP) and press **PLAY**. It sees
   that the game is not built yet and offers to run `SETUP.bat`: answer **Yes**. (Or drag your disc
   image onto `SETUP.bat`, or double-click `SETUP.bat`; same thing.)
3. Answer SETUP's questions. Pressing **Enter** takes the suggested answer, which is right almost always:
   - **your disc image**: drag the `.iso` / `.zip` / disc folder into the window (or paste its path) and
     press Enter;
   - **the disc key**, only for an encrypted image without a `.dkey` file: SETUP opens
     [Redump's page](http://redump.org/disc/16199/) in your browser; copy the long code on its
     "Disc Key" line and paste it with **Ctrl+V**;
   - whether it may **download** RPCS3, a portable Python / Git and the portable compiler (say yes);
   - the **Microsoft Visual C++ runtime** for RPCS3, if your PC has none: Windows asks you to allow
     Microsoft's installer;
   - **xwin** asks you to accept Microsoft's license for the C runtime / Windows SDK it downloads.
4. Wait for **All done**, then press **PLAY** in the launcher.

SETUP.bat then:

| step | what happens | time* |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | extracts all game files from the image (and decrypts them) into `game/` | 2–5 min |
| 2 | decrypts `EBOOT.BIN` → `EBOOT.elf` with RPCS3 and checks it is the tested version | < 1 min |
| 3 | downloads ps3recomp at the tested commit and applies this port's runtime patch | < 1 min |
| 4 | recompiles the game: ~94,000 PPU functions + 12 SPU programs → C/C++ in `port/` | 2–4 min |
| 5 | applies this port's edits to the recompiled code (`patches/lifted-code.patch`) | seconds |
| 6 | compiles everything with clang-cl into `port/build_opt/DemonsSoulsRecomp.exe` (plus `DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe`, next to `PLAY.bat`) | 10–30 min |

\* on a fast 16-core PC; the first compile is the long part. The compile shows one progress line
(`compiling 47/322 (15%)`); the compiler's full output goes to `logs\build_last.txt`. If anything fails, fix
what it says and run SETUP.bat again: finished steps are skipped.

## Updating

Press **Check for updates** in the launcher: it asks GitHub, lists what is new and, if you say yes,
downloads it, puts it in the folder and rebuilds the game; the launcher then opens again. **No Git
needed:** a copy from a release ZIP (or the Code ZIP) gets the newest release (checked against the
checksum GitHub publishes for it; your game files, build, saves and settings are not touched), a
`git clone` gets `git pull`. The launcher's status line shows which release you have.
Copies from before release v2026.11.03.7 need this once by hand: download the newest
[release](https://github.com/timboat/demons-souls-recomp/releases/latest) ZIP and copy everything inside its folder over your old folder,
replacing files (`game/`, `port/`, `deps/` and your saves are not in the ZIP, so they stay), then
press Play (or run **`BUILD.bat`**). It re-applies
the patches that changed since your last setup and recompiles only the files they touch. If it
says so, run `SETUP.bat` instead: that also works, keeps the game files and skips what is done.
If you forget, Play notices that the folder was updated but not rebuilt and runs BUILD.bat first
(an old build with new files can stay on a black screen).
Setups made before 2026-11-03 could not take updates (the patches were applied once and never
again); the first `BUILD.bat` or `SETUP.bat` with this version brings them up to date.

## Play

Double-click **`DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe`** (SETUP.bat / BUILD.bat build it next to `PLAY.bat`) and
press **PLAY**. The logos and first load take about a minute.

The launcher is one window for every option below: frame rate (Auto, 30, 50, 60, unlimited or any
number, with a line saying how it will look on your screen), internal resolution, Normal / PC Remaster
mod / your imported models, fullscreen, movies, god mode, frame-timing recording, texture dumping,
keys by letter and CPU core pinning. It remembers them in `launcher.ini`. Its buttons: **Check for
updates** (shows what is new on GitHub; on yes `git pull` + `BUILD.bat`, then it opens again), **Report a problem** (`REPORT.bat`), **Controls** and
**Folders** (saves, logs, recordings, texture and model folders). If the game crashes it offers to
make the report. *Extra settings* takes any `NAME=value` switch from this README or from an issue
(e.g. `LD_PSO_ASYNC=0`). `DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe --play` starts the game straight away with the
saved settings, for a desktop shortcut.

The launcher runs `PLAY.bat` with your choices. `PLAY.bat` on its own starts the game at 60 fps (50 fps
automatically on a ~100 Hz monitor, every frame shown exactly 2 refreshes), and the `set X=...` switches
in this README work in front of it too. The separate `PLAY_30FPS.bat`, `PLAY_REMASTER.bat` etc. are gone:
those are all launcher options now.

| launcher option | what it does |
|---|---|
| *Frame rate*: Auto / 30 / 50 / 60 / Unlimited / Custom... | Auto = 60, or 50 on a ~100 Hz screen; 30 = the original; Unlimited = up to 240 fps, no vsync, game speed stays correct; Custom = **any frame rate you type in** (31–240) |
| *Game*: Normal / PC Remaster mod / My models | your game as on the disc, with the *PC Remaster* mod installed, or with your imported models (see below) |
| *Dump textures* | saves every texture the game draws, for texture packs (see below) |

Without the launcher (Linux, or `PLAY.bat` by hand) the same choices are switches: `DES_FPS=30|50|60|unlimited|31-240`,
`DES_GAME=game_remaster` (PC Remaster) or `DES_GAME=game_mod` (your models), `LD_TEX_DUMP=1` (dump textures).
In the launcher, any other folder made by `tools\flver_tool.py import --mod <folder>` goes in *Extra settings*
as `DES_GAME=<folder>`.

**Custom frame rate.** In the launcher pick *Custom...* and type a
number, e.g. 45, 72, 120 or 144. The game
runs at real speed at any of them. If your monitor's refresh rate is a whole multiple of the number
(72 or 144 on a 144 Hz screen, 40 or 120 on 120 Hz), every frame is shown for the same number of
refreshes and motion is perfectly even. Otherwise vsync is turned off, which looks fine on a
G-Sync / FreeSync screen but can tear on others. The launcher says which one you got. You can also
`set DES_FPS=<number>` before running `PLAY.bat`.

**Higher resolution.** *Resolution* in the launcher, or `set DES_RES_SCALE=2` (up to 4) before running
`PLAY.bat`, renders the game at
2x its 1280x720 (2560x1440), much sharper, at no cost on the CPU side; a mid-range GPU handles 2x easily.
The window and borderless fullscreen show the picture at the window's own size, at the game's 16:9
with black bars on other screens (`set LD_SWAP_RESIZE=0` = the old stretched picture).
*Sharper shadows too* (`set LD_RES_SCALE_SHADOW=1`) also renders the 2048x2048 shadow map at the
higher resolution.

**Controls.** An Xbox (XInput) controller works when plugged in (A = Cross, B = Circle, X = Square,
Y = Triangle, LB/RB = L1/R1, LT/RT = L2/R2, Back = Select). A DualShock/DualSense needs Steam Input or
DS4Windows. Keyboard + mouse work too, also with a controller connected (the mouse takes over the
camera once you press a key or mouse button, and the controller takes it back when you use it):

| | |
|---|---|
| WASD | move |
| mouse (or IJKL) | camera (click into the game to capture the mouse) |
| left mouse | attack (R1) |
| Shift | strong attack (R2) |
| right mouse | block (L1) |
| Ctrl | parry (L2) |
| Space | roll / dash / back (Circle) |
| E | interact / confirm (Cross) |
| F | two-hand (Triangle) |
| R | use item (Square) |
| Tab / middle mouse | lock on (R3) |
| arrows | d-pad (switch items) |
| Enter / Backspace | Start / Select |
| Esc or F1 | release the mouse (F1 also captures it again; leaving the window or using a controller also releases it). Esc no longer closes the game: use the X or Alt+F4 |

| F9 | god mode on/off (no death, HP/MP/stamina stay full) |

**In menus** (title screen, Start menu, inventory, shops, level-up, ...) the mouse is a pointer: the Windows arrow
appears, **moving it over an item selects it** (with the game's own cursor sound and help text), **left click on an
item confirms it** (on another item it selects it first, on empty space it does nothing), **right click = back**,
the **wheel** moves the cursor up and down, and the mouse's side buttons or **PageUp / PageDown** are L1 / R1. Keys
and the controller take over as soon as you use them; the mouse only takes over again once it moves. When the menu
closes the mouse goes back to the camera. Pointing works in the title, profile select, Start menu tabs, inventory,

Options rows still use keys / wheel (a click there confirms as before). `set DES_POINT=0` turns pointing off (the
mouse then only clicks / scrolls in menus), `set PAD_MENU_MOUSE=0` turns the mouse in menus off altogether. Outside
menus the mouse buttons attack and block as before.

**Button icons follow what you play with:** while the keyboard / mouse is what you used last, the game's button
icons (key guides, "Pick up" prompts, the HUD's equipment boxes, the Start menu tabs) show the keys and mouse

options. `set PAD_MOUSE_LOOK_SENS=0.0012` sets the sensitivity (radians per mouse count), `set PAD_MOUSE_LOOK=0`

Keys go by position, not by letter: on an AZERTY or QWERTZ keyboard you move with the keys where
WASD would be (ZQSD on AZERTY), and the others follow the same way. `set PAD_KEYS_BY_LETTER=1` = by letter.

At *Create Profile* a text box opens for the character name. Saves go to `gamedata/`. Each run

Linux: the runtime patch failed to apply (mixed line endings)

endings, and patches/ps3recomp-local.patch has LF context. Git for
Windows (core.autocrlf=true) matches them; stock git on Linux compares
byte for byte, so linux/setup.sh stopped at step 3 ("patch failed:

fixes a Windows git set to autocrlf=false). No git config change
needed in existing setups.

runs step 3 on a fresh clone, then updates from the last three

The remo cutscene camera sampler (func_005F71D0) picked the nearest of the
track's keys, which are baked one per 1/30 s. At 30 fps the cut time lands on
keys; at 60 every other frame is half way, so the camera moved 30 times a
second while the characters moved 60: the picture moved in pairs (the
tutorial's opening walk through the black void, the Nexus intro, ...).

Port patch in ppu_recomp_040.cpp: once a call, keys one frame apart are blended
by the fraction the game already computes (rotation the short way round, or to
the other Euler set at a flip); holds, shot changes inside a track (> 2 m,
> 0.5 rad, scale > 0.25) and unset keys keep the nearest key, as lifted.
DES_CUT_BLEND=0 restores the original. Analysis credit: JonathanDC64/
DemonsSoulsRecomp (MIT), docs/40 and docs/62.

Measured (frame-pair analysis of captures, 60 fps mode): tutorial opening 19 of
59 paired seconds -> 0; Nexus intro 56 of 64 -> 0; game time 1.000, no long
frames. NOTES fix 80.

1447381086.readme_excerpt:
# Demon's Souls — native PC port (ps3recomp)

A native Windows build of **Demon's Souls** (PS3, USA, **BLUS-30443**), made by statically
recompiling the game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code to C/C++ with
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), plus a PS3 runtime and a Direct3D 12 renderer.
It is not an emulator: the game's code runs as a normal x64 program.

> **No game files are included.** This repo holds only the tools, patches and build scripts. You
> need your own copy of the game, dumped from your own disc. The setup reads your disc image and
> builds everything on your PC.

**Community Discord:** [discord.gg/gTvrZZ75G](https://discord.gg/gTvrZZ75G) (questions, help with setup,
bug reports and screenshots). Bug reports with a REPORT.bat zip are still best as a GitHub issue.

## Status

**The entire game seems playable.** It runs with sound and music at 60 fps (or 50 on a 100 Hz
screen, 30, uncapped, or any frame rate you pick), with keyboard + mouse or an Xbox controller. The game's movies play (title screen, intro,
story and endings; `set DES_MOVIES=0` skips them). The in-engine cutscenes are smooth at 60 fps and above too:
their camera is blended between its 30 fps keys (`set DES_CUT_BLEND=0` for the original nearest-key camera).

**Above 60 fps there are known bugs**, such as the sound drifting out of sync with the picture and the
character's run speed being off. 60 fps (or 50 on a 100 Hz screen) is the recommended setting; higher frame
rates are still being worked on.

**There is no online play yet.** Multiplayer will be added once the game is optimised.

**Performance:** on high-end hardware the game is mostly smooth. Optimisations for lower-end PCs
(fewer cores, older CPUs, Steam Deck) are happening now.

I'm currently playing through the whole game to find and fix any spots that still run slower
than they should (stutters, frame drops in heavy scenes). Boletarian Palace, the heaviest area
tested so far, is already smooth on a fast PC. Expect more performance fixes as the playthrough goes on; see
[docs/NOTES.md](docs/NOTES.md) for the full development log (50 fixes and counting).

If you hit a stutter or a crash, please report it: see
[Reporting stutters and crashes](#reporting-stutters-and-crashes). Every run is recorded, so all it
takes is pressing **F8** when it happens and running `REPORT.bat` afterwards.

## What you need

- **Windows 10/11 x64** and a **Direct3D 12** GPU. AVX2 (Intel Haswell / AMD Ryzen or newer) is used
  when your CPU has it; on older CPUs BUILD.bat builds without it (a couple of fps slower in the
  heaviest areas).
- About **14 GB** free disk space (8 GB game files + build + tools).
- **Your disc image** of Demon's Souls USA (BLUS-30443): a `.iso` (a Redump `.zip` works as is), or a
  dumped disc folder with `PS3_GAME` in it. A Redump-style encrypted image also needs its
  **disc key** (the `.dkey` file that comes with the dump). No `.dkey`? The key is public: it is the
  "Disc Key" line on [Redump's page for this disc](http://redump.org/disc/16199/) (Demon's Souls, USA, BLUS-30443, version
  01.00). SETUP opens that page for you when it needs the key.
- **Nothing else to install.** SETUP downloads what it needs into the folder (`deps\`), with no
  installer and no administrator rights: a portable **Python** and **Git** when you have none,
  **[RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net)** (used once to decrypt the game's `EBOOT.BIN`), and, without Visual
  Studio, a portable compiler (**LLVM** + Microsoft's C runtime and Windows SDK, about 1.3 GB, fetched
  by [xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin); Microsoft's license applies). The Python, Git, LLVM,
  RPCS3 and xwin downloads are checked against pinned or published checksums. Already have Python 3.10+, Git, RPCS3
  (`SETUP.bat --rpcs3 path\to\rpcs3.exe`) or **Visual Studio 2022** with *Desktop development with
  C++* + **LLVM** 17 or newer? Then those are used instead. RPCS3 needs the Microsoft Visual C++
  runtime, which most PCs already have; SETUP offers Microsoft's installer if yours does not. (Installed
  Visual Studio later and want it used? Delete `deps\.portable_compiler`.) Keep the folder's path plain:
  no `[ ]` or `&` in it (the build tools cannot handle them; SETUP says so).

**Linux / Steam Deck:** a setup + play kit (an AppImage) builds the same port from your own disc
image on Linux and runs it through Proton. See [docs/LINUX.md](docs/LINUX.md).
**It works on Linux:** set up and played on Ubuntu 24.04 (Intel i7-4770K + NVIDIA GTX 980). On that
4-core CPU it is still choppier than on Windows (Linux performance work is under way). A Steam Deck is
not confirmed yet; please report how it goes.

## Build it (one time)

The setup below has been tested on a clean Windows install (Windows Sandbox: no
Python, Git, Visual Studio, RPCS3 or Visual C++ runtime) and on a normal gaming PC.

1. Download the newest release: **[Releases](https://github.com/timboat/demons-souls-recomp/releases/latest)** → `DemonsSoulsRecomp-<version>.zip` (or the
   green **Code** button → *Download ZIP*, or `git clone`), and unpack it somewhere with enough
   space, for example `C:\Games\DemonsSouls`. Keep the path plain (no `[ ]` or `&`). There is no
   ready-to-play download: the game is built on your PC from your own disc.
2. Double-click **`DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe`** (it is in the release ZIP) and press **PLAY**. It sees
   that the game is not built yet and offers to run `SETUP.bat`: answer **Yes**. (Or drag your disc
   image onto `SETUP.bat`, or double-click `SETUP.bat`; same thing.)
3. Answer SETUP's questions. Pressing **Enter** takes the suggested answer, which is right almost always:
   - **your disc image**: drag the `.iso` / `.zip` / disc folder into the window (or paste its path) and
     press Enter;
   - **the disc key**, only for an encrypted image without a `.dkey` file: SETUP opens
     [Redump's page](http://redump.org/disc/16199/) in your browser; copy the long code on its
     "Disc Key" line and paste it with **Ctrl+V**;
   - whether it may **download** RPCS3, a portable Python / Git and the portable compiler (say yes);
   - the **Microsoft Visual C++ runtime** for RPCS3, if your PC has none: Windows asks you to allow
     Microsoft's installer;
   - **xwin** asks you to accept Microsoft's license for the C runtime / Windows SDK it downloads.
4. Wait for **All done**, then press **PLAY** in the launcher.

SETUP.bat then:

| step | what happens | time* |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | extracts all game files from the image (and decrypts them) into `game/` | 2–5 min |
| 2 | decrypts `EBOOT.BIN` → `EBOOT.elf` with RPCS3 and checks it is the tested version | < 1 min |
| 3 | downloads ps3recomp at the tested commit and applies this port's runtime patch | < 1 min |
| 4 | recompiles the game: ~94,000 PPU functions + 12 SPU programs → C/C++ in `port/` | 2–4 min |
| 5 | applies this port's edits to the recompiled code (`patches/lifted-code.patch`) | seconds |
| 6 | compiles everything with clang-cl into `port/build_opt/DemonsSoulsRecomp.exe` (plus `DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe`, next to `PLAY.bat`) | 10–30 min |

\* on a fast 16-core PC; the first compile is the long part. The compile shows one progress line
(`compiling 47/322 (15%)`); the compiler's full output goes to `logs\build_last.txt`. If anything fails, fix
what it says and run SETUP.bat again: finished steps are skipped.

## Updating

Press **Check for updates** in the launcher: it asks GitHub, lists what is new and, if you say yes,
downloads it, puts it in the folder and rebuilds the game; the launcher then opens again. **No Git
needed:** a copy from a release ZIP (or the Code ZIP) gets the newest release (checked against the
checksum GitHub publishes for it; your game files, build, saves and settings are not touched), a
`git clone` gets `git pull`. The launcher's status line shows which release you have.
Copies from before release v2026.11.03.7 need this once by hand: download the newest
[release](https://github.com/timboat/demons-souls-recomp/releases/latest) ZIP and copy everything inside its folder over your old folder,
replacing files (`game/`, `port/`, `deps/` and your saves are not in the ZIP, so they stay), then
press Play (or run **`BUILD.bat`**). It re-applies
the patches that changed since your last setup and recompiles only the files they touch. If it
says so, run `SETUP.bat` instead: that also works, keeps the game files and skips what is done.
If you forget, Play notices that the folder was updated but not rebuilt and runs BUILD.bat first
(an old build with new files can stay on a black screen).
Setups made before 2026-11-03 could not take updates (the patches were applied once and never
again); the first `BUILD.bat` or `SETUP.bat` with this version brings them up to date.

## Play

Double-click **`DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe`** (SETUP.bat / BUILD.bat build it next to `PLAY.bat`) and
press **PLAY**. The logos and first load take about a minute.

The launcher is one window for every option below: frame rate (Auto, 30, 50, 60, unlimited or any
number, with a line saying how it will look on your screen), internal resolution, Normal / PC Remaster
mod / your imported models, fullscreen, movies, god mode, frame-timing recording, texture dumping,
keys by letter and CPU core pinning. It remembers them in `launcher.ini`. Its buttons: **Check for
updates** (shows what is new on GitHub; on yes `git pull` + `BUILD.bat`, then it opens again), **Report a problem** (`REPORT.bat`), **Controls** and
**Folders** (saves, logs, recordings, texture and model folders). If the game crashes it offers to
make the report. *Extra settings* takes any `NAME=value` switch from this README or from an issue
(e.g. `LD_PSO_ASYNC=0`). `DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe --play` starts the game straight away with the
saved settings, for a desktop shortcut.

The launcher runs `PLAY.bat` with your choices. `PLAY.bat` on its own starts the game at 60 fps (50 fps
automatically on a ~100 Hz monitor, every frame shown exactly 2 refreshes), and the `set X=...` switches
in this README work in front of it too. The separate `PLAY_30FPS.bat`, `PLAY_REMASTER.bat` etc. are gone:
those are all launcher options now.

| launcher option | what it does |
|---|---|
| *Frame rate*: Auto / 30 / 50 / 60 / Unlimited / Custom... | Auto = 60, or 50 on a ~100 Hz screen; 30 = the original; Unlimited = up to 240 fps, no vsync, game speed stays correct; Custom = **any frame rate you type in** (31–240) |
| *Game*: Normal / PC Remaster mod / My models | your game as on the disc, with the *PC Remaster* mod installed, or with your imported models (see below) |
| *Dump textures* | saves every texture the game draws, for texture packs (see below) |

Without the launcher (Linux, or `PLAY.bat` by hand) the same choices are switches: `DES_FPS=30|50|60|unlimited|31-240`,
`DES_GAME=game_remaster` (PC Remaster) or `DES_GAME=game_mod` (your models), `LD_TEX_DUMP=1` (dump textures).
In the launcher, any other folder made by `tools\flver_tool.py import --mod <folder>` goes in *Extra settings*
as `DES_GAME=<folder>`.

**Custom frame rate.** In the launcher pick *Custom...* and type a
number, e.g. 45, 72, 120 or 144. The game
runs at real speed at any of them. If your monitor's refresh rate is a whole multiple of the number
(72 or 144 on a 144 Hz screen, 40 or 120 on 120 Hz), every frame is shown for the same number of
refreshes and motion is perfectly even. Otherwise vsync is turned off, which looks fine on a
G-Sync / FreeSync screen but can tear on others. The launcher says which one you got. You can also
`set DES_FPS=<number>` before running `PLAY.bat`.

**Higher resolution.** *Resolution* in the launcher, or `set DES_RES_SCALE=2` (up to 4) before running
`PLAY.bat`, renders the game at
2x its 1280x720 (2560x1440), much sharper, at no cost on the CPU side; a mid-range GPU handles 2x easily.
The window and borderless fullscreen show the picture at the window's own size, at the game's 16:9
with black bars on other screens (`set LD_SWAP_RESIZE=0` = the old stretched picture).
*Sharper shadows too* (`set LD_RES_SCALE_SHADOW=1`) also renders the 2048x2048 shadow map at the
higher resolution.

**Controls.** An Xbox (XInput) controller works when plugged in (A = Cross, B = Circle, X = Square,
Y = Triangle, LB/RB = L1/R1, LT/RT = L2/R2, Back = Select). A DualShock/DualSense needs Steam Input or
DS4Windows. Keyboard + mouse work too, also with a controller connected (the mouse takes over the
camera once you press a key or mouse button, and the controller takes it back when you use it):

| | |
|---|---|
| WASD | move |
| mouse (or IJKL) | camera (click into the game to capture the mouse) |
| left mouse | attack (R1) |
| Shift | strong attack (R2) |
| right mouse | block (L1) |
| Ctrl | parry (L2) |
| Space | roll / dash / back (Circle) |
| E | interact / confirm (Cross) |
| F | two-hand (Triangle) |
| R | use item (Square) |
| Tab / middle mouse | lock on (R3) |
| arrows | d-pad (switch items) |
| Enter / Backspace | Start / Select |
| Esc or F1 | release the mouse (F1 also captures it again; leaving the window or using a controller also releases it). Esc no longer closes the game: use the X or Alt+F4 |
| Alt+Enter / F11 | borderless fullscreen on/off (`set DES_FULLSCREEN=1` starts in it) |
| F9 | god mode on/off (no death, HP/MP/stamina stay full) |

**In menus** (title screen, Start menu, inventory, shops, level-up, ...) the mouse is a pointer: the Windows arrow
appears, **moving it over an item selects it** (with the game's own cursor sound and help text), **left click on an
item confirms it** (on another item it selects it first, on empty space it does nothing), **right click = back**,
the **wheel** moves the cursor up and down, and the mouse's side buttons or **PageUp / PageDown** are L1 / R1. Keys
and the controller take over as soon as you use them; the mouse only takes over again once it moves. When the menu
closes the mouse goes back to the camera. Pointing works in the title, profile select, Start menu tabs, inventory,
equipment, item commands, shops, talk choices, level-up, the archstone list, the System menu and yes / no boxes; the
Options rows still use keys / wheel (a click there confirms as before). `set DES_POINT=0` turns pointing off (the
mouse then only clicks / scrolls in menus), `set PAD_MENU_MOUSE=0` turns the mouse in menus off altogether. Outside
menus the mouse buttons attack and block as before.

**Button icons follow what you play with:** while the keyboard / mouse is what you used last, the game's button
icons (key guides, "Pick up" prompts, the HUD's equipment boxes, the Start menu tabs) show the keys and mouse
buttons instead of the PS3 buttons; touch the controller and they are PS3 buttons again. BUILD.bat draws them
once from your own copy of the game into `textures\kbm` (the letters are the game's own font). `set LD_TEX_KBM=0`
always shows the PS3 buttons, `set LD_TEX_KBM=1` always the keyboard ones. The title screen says "PRESS ENTER
BUTTON" instead of "PRESS START BUTTON" the same way.

The mouse turns the camera directly (no stick dead zone or speed limit) and follows the game's invert-camera
options. `set PAD_MOUSE_LOOK_SENS=0.0012` sets the sensitivity (radians per mouse count), `set PAD_MOUSE_LOOK=0`
goes back to the old stick-style mouse.

Keys go by position, not by letter: on an AZERTY or QWERTZ keyboard you move with the keys where
WASD would be (ZQSD on AZERTY), and the others follow the same way. `set PAD_KEYS_BY_LETTER=1` = by letter.

At *Create Profile* a text box opens for the character name. Saves go to `gamedata/`. Each run
writes logs to `logs/` (they grow by ~600 MB an hour; the previous run is kept as `*_prev.txt`).

Limit score boards and rank from a sorted list

The memory store had no bound on boards or players, so any client could
grow it without limit, and every rank sorted the whole board, up to 100
times per request under the store lock.

Cap the memory store at 1000 boards per title and 10000 players per
board; a Put past either returns ErrFull, which the handler answers as
ERROR 6 and logs at debug. Keep each board as a slice ordered by score
and time, so ranks are a binary search and reads are slices. Refuse
GET_RANKING_BY_ID counts over 100 before reading the ids.

reply (ports, relay flag, player count, name, version), only when
-discover is on and only to private, carrier-grade NAT, link-local or
loopback senders. It passes through the existing UDP rate limiter; a
public source is counted as discover_refused in udp_drops. Off by
default, in which case behaviour is unchanged.

749b2301785a651e481c3466f2c8687c5f92f45e.message:
Bound client writes with a deadline

client.send wrote to a client's socket under the recipient's sendMu with
no write deadline. A member who stopped reading let its socket buffers
fill, and every other member whose request pushed to it blocked in flush
holding that lock, so their own requests went unanswered and they stayed
in the room as ghosts. Each write now has a 10 second deadline
(writeTimeout, a var for tests); a failed or timed out write closes the
connection as before.

room's external blob, so a few rooms with large data made the reply
exceed maxPayload. writePacket refused it and the server closed the
searcher's connection, so every later search dropped the player too.

caller pages on with start = count. An entry that cannot fit even alone
is sent with an empty external blob so paging always moves on.

Refuse joins whose room state would not fit one reply

is not added. A member who asks again gets the same error instead of a

Add install scripts for Linux and Windows

scripts/install.sh (POSIX sh) installs the server for the current user on
Linux amd64 or arm64: it picks the newest non-draft release or a pinned
one, downloads the archive and SHA256SUMS from the GitHub release only,
stops on a checksum mismatch or a missing line before writing anything,

no profile edits, refuses root unless asked; --dry-run, --appimage.
macOS and other systems are refused with a clear message.

%LOCALAPPDATA%\re-psn\bin, with Get-FileHash, TLS 1.2, no administrator
rights, and a user PATH change only with -AddToPath.

scripts/test-install.sh and scripts/test-install.ps1 run them against a
fake release with stub downloads; no network.

Refuse a second HELLO and hold names by the full address

A connection that already completed HELLO could send another one and
change its title, name and UDP token while keeping its rooms, so other
members saw a new name and one connection could mint many score
identities. A second HELLO now gets error 1 and changes nothing.

Names were held against c.ip, which is all zero for IPv6, so every IPv6
player counted as one address and any of them could take another's name.
Identity now compares the real remote address (c.addr), and a player with
no IPv4 address is never treated as on the same network as another
(udp.go endpoint, relay.go relayStream). c.ip stays for HELLO_ACK and UDP.
