# re-psn
![re-psn: matchmaking rooms and leaderboards for recompiled PS3 games; self-hosted, with NAT traversal, an optional relay and a desktop app](docs/img/banner.png) **Run your own matchmaking and leaderboard server for statically recompiled PS3 games: one small binary, no accounts, no cloud.** [![CI](https://github.com/undecuple/re-psn/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/undecuple/re-psn/actions/workflows/ci.yml) ![version v0.6.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/pre--release-v0.6.0-997e95?labelColor=2b2733&style=flat-square) ![status: alpha](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-alpha-a86438?labelColor=45403d&style=flat-square) ![licence: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-MIT-a7d8b0?labelColor=2b2733&style=flat-square) [![Ask DeepWiki](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepWiki-Ask-007ac0)](https://deepwiki.com/undecuple/re-psn) **[Download](https://github.com/undecuple/re-psn/releases)** · [Quick start](#quick-start-host-a-server) · [Features](docs/features.md) · [Install](#install) · [Configuration](#configuration) · [Documentation](#more) · [Website](https://undecuple.github.io/re-psn/) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/undecuple/re-psn/issues/new/choose)
> [!IMPORTANT] > **Bring your own game.** This repository has no game code, assets, keys, firmware or BIOS, and you need none from it. Play > only games you own. re-psn is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment. | | | |---|---| | **1** static server binary | the server uses only Go's standard library; the optional desktop app uses third-party modules ([app/README.md](app/README.md)) | | **1** port | TCP and UDP 36100 for players ([ports](docs/running.md#ports)) | | **1** C file | the client: no third-party libraries and no threads ([client/psnr.c](client/psnr.c)) | | **Linux and Windows** | amd64 and arm64 on Linux, amd64 on Windows ([releases](https://github.com/undecuple/re-psn/releases)) | | **1** desktop app | a terminal UI to watch a server's rooms and leaderboards; release archives from v0.5.0, or build it from source ([app/README.md](app/README.md)) | ## Quick start: host a server The steps for hosting a server. A game still has to be recompiled to use the [client](client/psnr.c); no shipped game is claimed to work yet; see the [features list](docs/features.md) for what is tested. **Linux** 1. Download the archive for your CPU from the [releases page](https://github.com/undecuple/re-psn/releases) and check it: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing`. 2. Unpack it and run `./re-psn`. It listens on TCP and UDP 36100. 3. Give your players your address and port 36100 (they must not use `127.0.0.1`). *Caveat: the newest release is a pre-release; behind a router you must forward TCP and UDP 36100 ([ways to connect](docs/connecting.md)).* **Windows** 1. Download the `.zip` from the releases page and compare `Get-FileHash` with the line in `SHA256SUMS`. 2. Unzip it and run `re-psn.exe`. 3. Allow TCP and UDP 36100 in the firewall, then give your players your address and port. *Caveat: the release's Windows binary is cross-built and has not been run by us; the server's tests do run on Windows in CI.* More ways to install (container, install script, from source) are under [Install](#install); the [wiki](https://github.com/undecuple/re-psn/wiki) has short guides for players and hosts. --- ## What makes it different | Claim | Proof | |---|---| | Nothing to sign up for: no accounts or passwords, and nothing is stored on disk except the log file if you set one | [Security and privacy](#security-and-privacy) | | The server uses only Go's standard library | [go.mod](go.mod) has no `require` line, and CI enforces it ([ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml)) | | Players behind routers get connected, with an optional relay | tested in Docker by the [NAT lab](lab/README.md) | | The client is one C file | [client/psnr.c](client/psnr.c), tested against the server by `client/test_psnr.c` | | Hardened and checked | fuzz tests, race detector, vulnerability and secret scans in [CI](.github/workflows/ci.yml) | | A lobby you can read: games by name, verified player counts and player-reported latency | in v0.5.0: [features list](docs/features.md), [`/api/stats`](docs/api.md#http) | | Every feature says how far it got | [features list](docs/features.md) with status and evidence | --- ## Coming soon Not built yet. Each is in the [features list](docs/features.md) and the [roadmap](ROADMAP.md) with its status: friends, presence and invites, private rooms, an opt-in SQLite store, connection checks, a graphical desktop client, a metrics endpoint, signed releases. --- ## Contents - [Quick start: host a server](#quick-start-host-a-server) - [What makes it different](#what-makes-it-different) - [Coming soon](#coming-soon) - [About this project](#about-this-project) - [Overview](#overview) - [Example](#example) - [Features](#features) - [Desktop app](#desktop-app) - [For recomp developers](#for-recomp-developers) - [Install](#install) - [Configuration](#configuration) - [Security and privacy](#security-and-privacy) - [More](#more) - [Website](#website) - [Credits](#credits), [Licence](#licence), [How AI was used](#how-ai-was-used) --- ## About this project re-psn began as a fork of [psnr](https://github.com/sp00nznet/psnr) by sp00nz, who wrote the original server, the C client and the protocol. [LICENSE](LICENSE) keeps upstream's MIT licence and copyright line, and [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md) credits the upstream work. re-psn adds hardened CI and fuzz tests, invite-only rooms, limits, logging, reverse proxy support, a UDP source check, container files and release tooling. The [features list](docs/features.md) and [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) have the details. v0.5.0 added a lobby view with game names, verified player counts and player-reported latency. It also added `-relay-force` for testing the relay from one network, LAN discovery (`-discover`), the server half of opt-in peer keys, and archives of the desktop app. --- ## Overview A recompiled PS3 game that wants to play online needs someone to answer its matchmaking and leaderboard calls. re-psn is that someone, for a group running its own server: a LAN, a VPN, or friends connecting to one person's machine. The server keeps rooms and leaderboards and tells each player where the others are. The game traffic itself goes directly between players, and through the server only when two players cannot reach each other and the host has turned the relay on.
The message flow of a session, as a diagram ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant A as player A (title + client/psnr.c) participant S as re-psn server participant B as player B (title + client/psnr.c) A->>S: TCP 36100: HELLO (title, name, P2P port) S-->>A: HELLO_ACK (user id, address seen, token, flags) A->>S: UDP 36100 from the P2P socket: PROBE (token) S-->>A: PROBE_REPLY (public address and port) A->>S: CREATE_ROOM S-->>A: ROOM_JOINED B->>S: HELLO, PROBE, SEARCH_ROOMS, JOIN_ROOM S-->>B: ROOM_JOINED with A's address and P2P port S-->>A: MEMBER_JOINED with B's address and P2P port A->>B: PUNCH, then game traffic, peer to peer B->>A: PUNCH, then game traffic, peer to peer Note over A,B: if nothing direct gets through and the server runs with -relay,
datagrams and streams go through the server instead ```
### A session, step by step 1. **The host starts re-psn**, listening on TCP and UDP 36100 (and, with `-http 127.0.0.1:36101`, a status page there). 2. **A game connects** through the C client (`client/psnr.c`): it sends HELLO with the game's ID, the player's name and P2P port. HELLO_ACK returns a user id, the address the server sees, a token and flags (relay on, invite-only rooms). 3. **A UDP PROBE** from the game's P2P socket tells the server its public address and port (accepted only from the TCP address). 4. **Rooms:** one player creates a room, others search and join, or join with a code. Each member entry carries the address and P2P port that work from where the receiving player is. 5. **Direct:** both sides send PUNCH packets to open their routers, then play peer to peer. 6. **Relay, if needed:** when nothing direct gets through and the server runs with `-relay`, traffic goes through the server. Without it, players need port forwarding or a shared VPN. Leaderboards use the same TCP connection. More in [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) (the parts, the relay) and [docs/api.md](docs/api.md) (every message). ### Using it from a game Games are recompiled with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), whose NP modules talk to re-psn through the C client. That side is upstream's work and not part of this repository. It needs a ps3recomp build with [ps3recomp#200](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/pull/200) (merged into ps3recomp on 2026-10-07). There, `PS3_NET_ONLINE=1` and `PSNR_SERVER=host[:port]` point a game at the server (its `docs/ONLINE.md` lists the rest). With it, upstream has played Simpsons Arcade online, two players from lobby to Stage 1 in sync, on one machine and later across two with either player behind a NAT. --- ## Example Two test players meet in a room and connect directly, and the C client's test leaves a score; all captured from real local runs.
The transcripts: the server, two players, the status page and the C client test Two test players meet in a room and connect directly. They are `lab/natcheck.c`, the NAT lab's player, which does what the runtime does for a game (HELLO, probe, room, punch, ping, a stream) without one. Built from a fresh clone with the commands shown. Captured from a local run on loopback with an early build (the `version=` field shows 0.2.0; the current release is 0.6.0): start the server with the defaults. ```text $ ./re-psn time=2026-11-06T01:44:42.396Z level=INFO msg=storage backend=memory time=2026-11-06T01:44:42.396Z level=INFO msg=started version=0.2.0 clients=[::]:36100 udp=[::]:36100 relay=false ``` The status page is off by default. The rest comes from a second run of the same build, started as `./re-psn -v -http 127.0.0.1:36101` (debug log, status page on). Captured from a local run on loopback: build the test player, and let alice host a room in one terminal. ```text $ gcc -std=gnu11 -o natcheck client/psnr.c lab/natcheck.c $ ./natcheck 127.0.0.1 alice host 3658 alice: P2P socket seen at 127.0.0.1:3658 alice: the other player is at 127.0.0.1:3659 PASS alice: "PONG bob" direct PASS alice: stream direct, got "ACK from bob" ``` Captured from a local run on loopback: in a second terminal, while alice waits, the status page shows her room; then bob joins. ```text $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:36101/api/stats {"uptime":"2s","clients":1,"connections_total":1,"rooms":[{"id":1,"title":"NPWR00001_00","members":["alice"],"max":2,"age":"1s"}],"unlisted_rooms":0,"boards":[]} $ ./natcheck 127.0.0.1 bob join 3659 bob: P2P socket seen at 127.0.0.1:3659 bob: the other player is at 127.0.0.1:3658 PASS bob: "PONG alice" direct PASS bob: stream direct, got "SETUP from alice" ``` Captured from a local run on loopback: the C client's own test (`client/test_psnr.c`: HELLO, a room joined by a second client, a room message, a score), then the leaderboard it left on the status page. ```text $ gcc -std=gnu11 -o test_psnr client/psnr.c client/test_psnr.c $ ./test_psnr 127.0.0.1 36100 test_psnr: all passed $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:36101/api/stats {"uptime":"6s","clients":0,"connections_total":4,"rooms":[],"unlisted_rooms":0,"boards":[{"title":"NPWR00001_00","board":1,"entries":1,"leader":"alice","best":100}]} ```
With `-http 127.0.0.1:36101`, http://127.0.0.1:36101/ shows a terminal-style status page. Overview shows both tables; Rooms and Leaderboards open either table separately. Below, alice is hosting a room and leads the leaderboard with 100. The screenshot uses the old image's 1000 px width, with enough height to show both tables, and comes from a real loopback server and protocol clients ([tools/art/capture-status.sh](tools/art/capture-status.sh) can capture another). System/Light/Dark, text size, spacing and custom colours are [browser-local appearance settings](docs/running.md#status-page-appearance). Routers and the relay are tested in Docker by the [NAT lab](lab/README.md). ![Terminal-style server status in dark mode: alice's room and her leaderboard score of 100, shown together in Overview](docs/status.png) --- ## Features Available on `main` today; [docs/features.md](docs/features.md) has every feature with its status, evidence and notes. - **Rooms:** create, search, join and leave, room and member data, owner handoff, and invite-only rooms with an 8-character code. - **Leaderboards:** each player's best score, higher- or lower-is-better, ranked by range or by name; kept in memory for now. - **NAT traversal:** address probes and hole punching, an optional relay, and a UDP source address check. - **Hosting:** limits, log levels, a status page with an optional token, reverse proxy support, `RE_PSN_*` settings, Docker and Podman files, and deployment examples. - **Lobby view (v0.5.0):** the status page and `/api/stats` name known games, count verified players and show the round trip each player reports, labelled as reported and unverified. - **Peer keys (v0.5.0, server side only):** an opt-in way for the server to give each pair of players in a room a shared key for tagging their direct packets. No client uses it yet, and it gives no confidentiality ([docs/api.md](docs/api.md#peer-keys)). - **C client:** one file, no third-party libraries, no threads. - **Checks:** fuzz tests; CI with the race detector, vulnerability and secret scans, the NAT lab and code scanning. Partial, unverified and planned work (release archives and the AppImage, the nginx and HAProxy examples, storage backends, the desktop apps and more) is in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) too. --- ## Desktop app [app/](app/README.md) holds the start of the desktop app, a separate Go module. It has a Go client for the protocol, tested against the real server; a settings file reader; `re-psn-app check HOST:PORT`, which connects, says HELLO and reports what the server answered; and a terminal UI (`re-psn-app` with no arguments). The UI asks on first start whether this machine plays, hosts or both. It then shows the server's rooms and one leaderboard at a time over the game protocol, and edits the settings. The theme is dark or light, in the website's colours. The server's version, uptime and connection counts are not available over the protocol, so the UI says so. An explicitly configured [HTTP status source](app/README.md#optional-native-http-status) adds uptime, connection totals, public-room members and board summaries natively, with the existing token rules and no browser. It falls back to the game protocol when HTTP is unavailable; the server version remains unshared. From v0.5.0 a release carries the app as `re-psn-app-vX.Y.Z--` archives (see [Release archives](#release-archives)); you can also build it from source (see [app/README.md](app/README.md)). On Linux desktops, starting without a terminal can open a supported terminal; the Windows build uses its console. See the [desktop startup instructions](app/README.md#starting-from-the-desktop) and the limits of local testing. The terminal UI uses [Bubble Tea](https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea) and [Lip Gloss](https://github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss) (MIT); the server module stays standard-library only. The app module needs Go 1.26 or newer; the server and the C client keep their own requirements. --- ## For recomp developers Start with [Integrating re-psn into a recompiled game](docs/integrating.md): existing ps3recomp bridge setup, direct C/C++ integration, callback ownership, peer/relay transport and failure handling. The [minimal C example](client/examples/minimal.c) is compiled and exercised against a loopback server by the required native-client check. Source-level runtime findings are pinned; synthetic checks do not certify a title's gameplay or NAT behavior. --- ## Install **Recommended:** download an official [release archive or AppImage](#release

Smoother new areas, texture heaps, and the Storm King arena's missing geometry

  slowest took ~300 ms each); a model whose shader is not ready yet is drawn
  a few frames late, screen-critical passes still wait. LD_PSO_ASYNC=0 = old.

- Guest textures are placed in 64 MB heaps instead of one driver
  allocation each (arrival texture creation 126 -> 11 ms).
- The shader disk cache is read into memory during the logos (cold
  per-file reads froze the first gameplay frame for ~0.6 s).
- A draw kept at most 256 packets (65,536 indices) and dropped the rest:
  the Storm King arena lost whole meshes. Now 16,384 packets.

0816da134edec71a2468b3732fdae0a055d15299.message:
Sound thread no longer drops voices; SPU float zeros in the vector path

- synth2 (the SPU sound synthesizer) sat at 90-100% of a core once
  voices started and was dropping work: effects came out quieter or
  missing. Its voice-clear loop (112 bytes, one byte per pass, ~30% of
  the thread) now does its stores directly and ends in the exact same
  state. synth2 92% -> 62%; standing-still audio is bit-identical.
- AVX2 SPU fa/fm/fma: SPU zeros and underflow handled in the vector
  path like the NEON path (0 mismatches vs the exact reference on
  20M random vectors; 5x faster on denormal-range data).
- PLAY.bat records late-step stack samples (main + HighGraphics) so a
  freeze in a recording says what the game was doing.

0a96a611057b4c568ab490a88c5aea43c40443e8.message:

with a "needs AVX2" message on older CPUs. BUILD.bat now checks the CPU
(IsProcessorFeaturePresent) and passes DS_AVX2=ON/OFF to CMake; without
AVX2 the SPU float ops use their exact scalar paths (~2 fps slower in the
heaviest area). "set DS_AVX2=0" builds a copy for an older PC. PLAY.bat
only asks for AVX2 when the build used it (port/build_opt/no_avx2.txt).

1494c0aa6bc7e624fa6651ce0e2c438127534416.message:
Faster frame chain for 100+ fps: core pinning, PPU SIMD flags, cheaper SPU-line stores

- The game pins itself to the CPU's biggest L3 on multi-CCD CPUs (the
  V-Cache die on X3D parts): the HighGraphics <-> SPU dispatcher hand-offs
  stop crossing dies. Busy Valley spot at 100 fps: 77 -> ~90 fps.
  DES_AFFINITY=0 = off.
- Lifted PPU code built with SSE4.1 (+ AVX2/FMA with DS_AVX2), no stack
  cookies, -ffp-contract=off (results unchanged: VMX fast-vs-scalar test
  0 mismatches in 16 M ops). ~+4%.
- PPU stores to SPU-reserved lines visit only SPUs that may hold the line
  (held-line table) and no longer break other PPU threads' reservations
  there; SPU writes still do. Store path 16.9% -> 7.6% of HighGraphics.
  Two review rounds; runtime coherency unit test 195/195.
- Guest function-pointer calls take a fast path with a per-thread lookup
  cache when no debug switch is set.
Details and measurements: docs/NOTES.md fixes 65-68.

The remo cutscene camera sampler (func_005F71D0) picked the nearest of the
track's keys, which are baked one per 1/30 s. At 30 fps the cut time lands on
keys; at 60 every other frame is half way, so the camera moved 30 times a
second while the characters moved 60: the picture moved in pairs (the
tutorial's opening walk through the black void, the Nexus intro, ...).

by the fraction the game already computes (rotation the short way round, or to
the other Euler set at a flip); holds, shot changes inside a track (> 2 m,
> 0.5 rad, scale > 0.25) and unset keys keep the nearest key, as lifted.
DES_CUT_BLEND=0 restores the original. Analysis credit: JonathanDC64/
DemonsSoulsRecomp (MIT), docs/40 and docs/62.

59 paired seconds -> 0; Nexus intro 56 of 64 -> 0; game time 1.000, no long

d9c1d0219027de3ab6e86de25e59cdcf1aeda614.message:
Short sleeps no longer spin; crash-proof stutter recorder

The game's sub-millisecond usleeps were busy-waited: the streaming thread polls
every ~0.8 ms and burned half a core doing nothing, taking CPU from the game's
real threads on 4-6 core PCs. Waits of 200 us and longer now sleep on a
per-thread high-resolution timer (Windows 10 1803+); shorter ones still spin.
On a 2-core test the worst frames drop from ~90-105 ms to ~55 ms.
PS3_USLEEP_SPIN_US=1000 restores the old timing.

The stack sampler behind the stutter recorder could crash the game when it
sampled a coprocessor (SPU) thread, and could deadlock on a lock the paused
thread held. It now copies the stack, resumes the thread and unwinds the copy.

docs/NOTES.md fix 75 (also the profile of the heavy Palace spot on slower CPUs).

e67ddeff01ed39f1b74626ee5964f0de6ba7cc2f.message:
Latria 4-2 54.2 -> 55.2 fps on a 5800X: coherent stores skip the watch list

Every PPU store to an SPU-reserved line walked the WAIT_SIGNAL watch list
(6 nodes on parked tasks' stacks, a cache miss each) -- 1.75M stores/s
from HighGraphics into the SPU command-queue line. A 64-bit mask of the
watched lines, on its own cache line and kept under the lock-line lock,
lets spu_coh_wake_watches return at once for unwatched lines.

Frames over 25 ms 42 -> 25 on average. NOTES fix 90.

1447392537.readme_excerpt:
# Demon's Souls — native PC port (ps3recomp)

A native Windows build of **Demon's Souls** (PS3, USA, **BLUS-30443**), made by statically
recompiling the game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code to C/C++ with
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), plus a PS3 runtime and a Direct3D 12 renderer.
It is not an emulator: the game's code runs as a normal x64 program.

> **No game files are included.** This repo holds only the tools, patches and build scripts. You
> need your own copy of the game, dumped from your own disc. The setup reads your disc image and
> builds everything on your PC.

## Status

**The entire game seems playable.** It runs with sound and music at 60 fps (or 50 on a 100 Hz
screen, 30, uncapped, or any frame rate you pick), with keyboard + mouse or an Xbox controller. The game's movies play (title screen, intro,
story and endings; `set DES_MOVIES=0` skips them). The in-engine cutscenes are smooth at 60 fps and above too:
their camera is blended between its 30 fps keys (`set DES_CUT_BLEND=0` for the original nearest-key camera).

**Above 60 fps there are known bugs**, such as the sound drifting out of sync with the picture and the
character's run speed being off. 60 fps (or 50 on a 100 Hz screen) is the recommended setting; higher frame
rates are still being worked on.

**There is no online play yet.** Multiplayer will be added once the game is optimised.

**Performance:** on high-end hardware the game is mostly smooth. Optimisations for lower-end PCs
(fewer cores, older CPUs, Steam Deck) are happening now.

I'm currently playing through the whole game to find and fix any spots that still run slower
than they should (stutters, frame drops in heavy scenes). Boletarian Palace, the heaviest area
tested so far, is already smooth on a fast PC. Expect more performance fixes as the playthrough goes on; see
[docs/NOTES.md](docs/NOTES.md) for the full development log (50 fixes and counting).

If you hit a stutter or a crash, please report it: see
[Reporting stutters and crashes](#reporting-stutters-and-crashes). Every run is recorded, so all it
takes is pressing **F8** when it happens and running `REPORT.bat` afterwards.

## What you need

- **Windows 10/11 x64** and a **Direct3D 12** GPU. AVX2 (Intel Haswell / AMD Ryzen or newer) is used
  when your CPU has it; on older CPUs BUILD.bat builds without it (a couple of fps slower in the
  heaviest areas).
- About **14 GB** free disk space (8 GB game files + build + tools).
- **Your disc image** of Demon's Souls USA (BLUS-30443): a `.iso` (a Redump `.zip` works as is), or a
  dumped disc folder with `PS3_GAME` in it. A Redump-style encrypted image also needs its
  **disc key** (the `.dkey` file that comes with the dump). No `.dkey`? The key is public: it is the
  "Disc Key" line on [Redump's page for this disc](http://redump.org/disc/16199/) (Demon's Souls, USA, BLUS-30443, version
  01.00). SETUP opens that page for you when it needs the key.
- **Nothing else to install.** SETUP downloads what it needs into the folder (`deps\`), with no
  installer and no administrator rights: a portable **Python** and **Git** when you have none,
  **[RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net)** (used once to decrypt the game's `EBOOT.BIN`), and, without Visual
  Studio, a portable compiler (**LLVM** + Microsoft's C runtime and Windows SDK, about 1.3 GB, fetched
  by [xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin); Microsoft's license applies). The Python, Git, LLVM,
  RPCS3 and xwin downloads are checked against pinned or published checksums. Already have Python 3.10+, Git, RPCS3
  (`SETUP.bat --rpcs3 path\to\rpcs3.exe`) or **Visual Studio 2022** with *Desktop development with
  C++* + **LLVM** 17 or newer? Then those are used instead. RPCS3 needs the Microsoft Visual C++
  runtime, which most PCs already have; SETUP offers Microsoft's installer if yours does not. (Installed
  Visual Studio later and want it used? Delete `deps\.portable_compiler`.) Keep the folder's path plain:
  no `[ ]` or `&` in it (the build tools cannot handle them; SETUP says so).

**Linux / Steam Deck:** a setup + play kit (an AppImage) builds the same port from your own disc
image on Linux and runs it through Proton. See [docs/LINUX.md](docs/LINUX.md).
**It works on Linux:** set up and played on Ubuntu 24.04 (Intel i7-4770K + NVIDIA GTX 980). On that
4-core CPU it is still choppier than on Windows (Linux performance work is under way). A Steam Deck is
not confirmed yet; please report how it goes.

## Build it (one time)

The setup below has been tested on a clean Windows install (Windows Sandbox: no
Python, Git, Visual Studio, RPCS3 or Visual C++ runtime) and on a normal gaming PC.

1. Download the newest release: **[Releases](https://github.com/timboat/demons-souls-recomp/releases/latest)** → `DemonsSoulsRecomp-<version>.zip` (or the
   green **Code** button → *Download ZIP*, or `git clone`), and unpack it somewhere with enough
   space, for example `C:\Games\DemonsSouls`. Keep the path plain (no `[ ]` or `&`). There is no
   ready-to-play download: the game is built on your PC from your own disc.
2. Double-click **`DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe`** (it is in the release ZIP) and press **PLAY**. It sees
   that the game is not built yet and offers to run `SETUP.bat`: answer **Yes**. (Or drag your disc
   image onto `SETUP.bat`, or double-click `SETUP.bat`; same thing.)
3. Answer SETUP's questions. Pressing **Enter** takes the suggested answer, which is right almost always:
   - **your disc image**: drag the `.iso` / `.zip` / disc folder into the window (or paste its path) and
     press Enter;
   - **the disc key**, only for an encrypted image without a `.dkey` file: SETUP opens
     [Redump's page](http://redump.org/disc/16199/) in your browser; copy the long code on its
     "Disc Key" line and paste it with **Ctrl+V**;
   - whether it may **download** RPCS3, a portable Python / Git and the portable compiler (say yes);
   - the **Microsoft Visual C++ runtime** for RPCS3, if your PC has none: Windows asks you to allow
     Microsoft's installer;
   - **xwin** asks you to accept Microsoft's license for the C runtime / Windows SDK it downloads.
4. Wait for **All done**, then press **PLAY** in the launcher.

SETUP.bat then:

| step | what happens | time* |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | extracts all game files from the image (and decrypts them) into `game/` | 2–5 min |
| 2 | decrypts `EBOOT.BIN` → `EBOOT.elf` with RPCS3 and checks it is the tested version | < 1 min |
| 3 | downloads ps3recomp at the tested commit and applies this port's runtime patch | < 1 min |
| 4 | recompiles the game: ~94,000 PPU functions + 12 SPU programs → C/C++ in `port/` | 2–4 min |
| 5 | applies this port's edits to the recompiled code (`patches/lifted-code.patch`) | seconds |
| 6 | compiles everything with clang-cl into `port/build_opt/DemonsSoulsRecomp.exe` (plus `DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe`, next to `PLAY.bat`) | 10–30 min |

\* on a fast 16-core PC; the first compile is the long part. The compile shows one progress line
(`compiling 47/322 (15%)`); the compiler's full output goes to `logs\build_last.txt`. If anything fails, fix
what it says and run SETUP.bat again: finished steps are skipped.

## Updating

Press **Check for updates** in the launcher: it asks GitHub, lists what is new and, if you say yes,
downloads it, puts it in the folder and rebuilds the game; the launcher then opens again. **No Git
needed:** a copy from a release ZIP (or the Code ZIP) gets the newest release (checked against the
checksum GitHub publishes for it; your game files, build, saves and settings are not touched), a
`git clone` gets `git pull`. The launcher's status line shows which release you have.
Copies from before release v2026.11.03.7 need this once by hand: download the newest
[release](https://github.com/timboat/demons-souls-recomp/releases/latest) ZIP and copy everything inside its folder over your old folder,
replacing files (`game/`, `port/`, `deps/` and your saves are not in the ZIP, so they stay), then
press Play (or run **`BUILD.bat`**). It re-applies
the patches that changed since your last setup and recompiles only the files they touch. If it
says so, run `SETUP.bat` instead: that also works, keeps the game files and skips what is done.
If you forget, Play notices that the folder was updated but not rebuilt and runs BUILD.bat first
(an old build with new files can stay on a black screen).
Setups made before 2026-11-03 could not take updates (the patches were applied once and never
again); the first `BUILD.bat` or `SETUP.bat` with this version brings them up to date.

## Play

Double-click **`DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe`** (SETUP.bat / BUILD.bat build it next to `PLAY.bat`) and
press **PLAY**. The logos and first load take about a minute.

The launcher is one window for every option below: frame rate (Auto, 30, 50, 60, unlimited or any
number, with a line saying how it will look on your screen), internal resolution, Normal / PC Remaster
mod / your imported models, fullscreen, movies, god mode, frame-timing recording, texture dumping,
keys by letter and CPU core pinning. It remembers them in `launcher.ini`. Its buttons: **Check for
updates** (shows what is new on GitHub; on yes `git pull` + `BUILD.bat`, then it opens again), **Report a problem** (`REPORT.bat`), **Controls** and
**Folders** (saves, logs, recordings, texture and model folders). If the game crashes it offers to
make the report. *Extra settings* takes any `NAME=value` switch from this README or from an issue
(e.g. `LD_PSO_ASYNC=0`). `DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe --play` starts the game straight away with the
saved settings, for a desktop shortcut.

The launcher runs `PLAY.bat` with your choices. `PLAY.bat` on its own starts the game at 60 fps (50 fps
automatically on a ~100 Hz monitor, every frame shown exactly 2 refreshes), and the `set X=...` switches
in this README work in front of it too. The separate `PLAY_30FPS.bat`, `PLAY_REMASTER.bat` etc. are gone:
those are all launcher options now.

| launcher option | what it does |
|---|---|
| *Frame rate*: Auto / 30 / 50 / 60 / Unlimited / Custom... | Auto = 60, or 50 on a ~100 Hz screen; 30 = the original; Unlimited = up to 240 fps, no vsync, game speed stays correct; Custom = **any frame rate you type in** (31–240) |
| *Game*: Normal / PC Remaster mod / My models | your game as on the disc, with the *PC Remaster* mod installed, or with your imported models (see below) |
| *Dump textures* | saves every texture the game draws, for texture packs (see below) |

Without the launcher (Linux, or `PLAY.bat` by hand) the same choices are switches: `DES_FPS=30|50|60|unlimited|31-240`,
`DES_GAME=game_remaster` (PC Remaster) or `DES_GAME=game_mod` (your models), `LD_TEX_DUMP=1` (dump textures).
In the launcher, any other folder made by `tools\flver_tool.py import --mod <folder>` goes in *Extra settings*
as `DES_GAME=<folder>`.

**Custom frame rate.** In the launcher pick *Custom...* and type a
number, e.g. 45, 72, 120 or 144. The game
runs at real speed at any of them. If your monitor's refresh rate is a whole multiple of the number
(72 or 144 on a 144 Hz screen, 40 or 120 on 120 Hz), every frame is shown for the same number of
refreshes and motion is perfectly even. Otherwise vsync is turned off, which looks fine on a
G-Sync / FreeSync screen but can tear on others. The launcher says which one you got. You can also
`set DES_FPS=<number>` before running `PLAY.bat`.

**Higher resolution.** *Resolution* in the launcher, or `set DES_RES_SCALE=2` (up to 4) before running
`PLAY.bat`, renders the game at
2x its 1280x720 (2560x1440), much sharper, at no cost on the CPU side; a mid-range GPU handles 2x easily.
The window and borderless fullscreen show the picture at the window's own size, at the game's 16:9
with black bars on other screens (`set LD_SWAP_RESIZE=0` = the old stretched picture).
*Sharper shadows too* (`set LD_RES_SCALE_SHADOW=1`) also renders the 2048x2048 shadow map at the
higher resolution.

**Controls.** An Xbox (XInput) controller works when plugged in (A = Cross, B = Circle, X = Square,
Y = Triangle, LB/RB = L1/R1, LT/RT = L2/R2, Back = Select). A DualShock/DualSense needs Steam Input or
DS4Windows. Keyboard + mouse work too, also with a controller connected (the mouse takes over the
camera once you press a key or mouse button, and the controller takes it back when you use it):

| | |
|---|---|
| WASD | move |
| mouse (or IJKL) | camera (click into the game to capture the mouse) |
| left mouse | attack (R1) |
| Shift | strong attack (R2) |
| right mouse | block (L1) |
| Ctrl | parry (L2) |
| Space | roll / dash / back (Circle) |
| E | interact / confirm (Cross) |
| F | two-hand (Triangle) |
| R | use item (Square) |
| Tab / middle mouse | lock on (R3) |
| arrows | d-pad (switch items) |
| Enter / Backspace | Start / Select |
| Esc or F1 | release the mouse (F1 also captures it again; leaving the window or using a controller also releases it). Esc no longer closes the game: use the X or Alt+F4 |
| Alt+Enter / F11 | borderless fullscreen on/off (`set DES_FULLSCREEN=1` starts in it) |
| F9 | god mode on/off (no death, HP/MP/stamina stay full) |

**In menus** (title screen, Start menu, inventory, shops, level-up, ...) the mouse is a pointer: the Windows arrow
appears, **moving it over an item selects it** (with the game's own cursor sound and help text), **left click on an
item confirms it** (on another item it selects it first, on empty space it does nothing), **right click = back**,
the **wheel** moves the cursor up and down, and the mouse's side buttons or **PageUp / PageDown** are L1 / R1. Keys
and the controller take over as soon as you use them; the mouse only takes over again once it moves. When the menu
closes the mouse goes back to the camera. Pointing works in the title, profile select, Start menu tabs, inventory,
equipment, item commands, shops, talk choices, level-up, the archstone list, the System menu and yes / no boxes; the
Options rows still use keys / wheel (a click there confirms as before). `set DES_POINT=0` turns pointing off (the
mouse then only clicks / scrolls in menus), `set PAD_MENU_MOUSE=0` turns the mouse in menus off altogether. Outside
menus the mouse buttons attack and block as before.

**Button icons follow what you play with:** while the keyboard / mouse is what you used last, the game's button
icons (key guides, "Pick up" prompts, the HUD's equipment boxes, the Start menu tabs) show the keys and mouse
buttons instead of the PS3 buttons; touch the controller and they are PS3 buttons again. BUILD.bat draws them
once from your own copy of the game into `textures\kbm` (the letters are the game's own font). `set LD_TEX_KBM=0`
always shows the PS3 buttons, `set LD_TEX_KBM=1` always the keyboard ones. The title screen says "PRESS ENTER
BUTTON" instead of "PRESS START BUTTON" the same way.

The mouse turns the camera directly (no stick dead zone or speed limit) and follows the game's invert-camera
options. `set PAD_MOUSE_LOOK_SENS=0.0012` sets the sensitivity (radians per mouse count), `set PAD_MOUSE_LOOK=0`
goes back to the old stick-style mouse.

Keys go by position, not by letter: on an AZERTY or QWERTZ keyboard you move with the keys where
WASD would be (ZQSD on AZERTY), and the others follow the same way. `set PAD_KEYS_BY_LETTER=1` = by letter.

At *Create Profile* a text box opens for the character name. Saves go to `gamedata/`. Each run
writes logs to `logs/` (they grow by ~600 MB an hour; the previous run is kept as `*_prev.txt`).

## Reporting stutters and crashes

The game records frame timing while you play (*Record frame timing (F8)* in the launcher, on by default) (about 25 MB an hour, no visible cost; the newest
10 sessions are kept in `perf\`). The window title shows `[RECORDING - F8 = stutter, N marked]`.

1. **Press F8** in the game right after you see a stutter, hitch or slowdown. Each press puts a mark

Launcher: a headless --prepare and --play for RecompLauncher

- --prepare --game <copy> [--update <pkg>] [--pack <pack>]: Install the
  game without a window. The copy is checked without mounting it (an .iso's
  ISO 9660 PS3_DISC.SFB, a folder's PARAM.SFO and PS3_DISC.SFB, BLUS31029
  only); the update and the data pack as given, else as the Install card
  remembered them; the key file only from the Install card or
  <data>/keys/self_keys.txt (existence only, never an argument); a
  placeholder left in an argument counts as not given. Then the Command Line
  Tools (their installer is opened and it stops), Homebrew's formulas (only
  looked at), the copy remembered as the disc and the files as the Install
  card's, and the window's own install job with the sources in
  Contents/Resources/port. A disc folder links no image (Play passes it as
  PES_MOUNT). progress <0..1> <text> lines from the window's steps and
  weights (never going back), the scripts' output as plain lines, one run at
  a time (prepare.lock), exit 0 only when the build is there, then Play uses
  the installed port; 40-46 for the copy and its files, what the player has
  to do, the connection, the build, already running, not built, the
  launcher itself. The Option File and the active profile are left alone.
- --play under RECOMPLAUNCHER=1: no window; the copy given with --game is
  remembered, the window's Play runs and the launcher's process becomes
  tools/run.sh, which execs the game, so the game's exit code and Stop are
  its own. Without the variable --play opens the window as before; --game
  is remembered first.
- "Already running" is a command line with BLUS31029/PES2013Recomp, not the
  name alone.
- Shared with the window: install_job/spawn_install (start_install),
  finish_install (install_finished), stage_in (bundled_stage),

# PES 2013 — static recompilation for PC (macOS) 🌐 **English** · [Português (BR)](README.pt-BR.md) A native port of **Pro Evolution Soccer 2013** (PS3, US disc `BLUS31029`, updated to 01.04) to **macOS/arm64**, built with static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C/C++ and compiled into a native executable, with graphics on Metal. It is not an emulator. **It boots, shows its menus in Portuguese and plays full matches**, at a steady 60 fps in gameplay (headless measurement on Apple silicon, the game's 1280×720), with Data Pack 6 and an Option File loaded. A friendly has been played to the end in a window. | | | | --- | --- | | [](docs/screenshots/01-gameplay-camera.jpg)

Goal kick, shadows on the grass | [](docs/screenshots/04-match-card.jpg)
Match card | Frames from the port itself (the RSX frame dump of a headless run) on an Apple-silicon Mac, built from the player's own copy, at the game's 1280×720. PES 2013 © Konami Digital Entertainment; club names and kits come from the player's own Option File. Shown only to document the port. Built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) and on the toolkit fixes made for the inFAMOUS, Resistance and Deadpool ports. See [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md). > [!WARNING] > **Alpha.** Runs only on Apple-silicon macOS. Master League, Become a Legend, > online modes and long sessions have not been tested yet. Pass settings as `VAR=value` after it. | Setting | What it does | | --- | --- | | `PS3_LANG=PT` | Console language (default `PT`; `pt-br` or `17` for Brazil). The first-run setup still asks for the game language | | `PS3_ANISO=16` | Anisotropic filtering (default 16; `0` = the game's own) | | `PS3_AA=fxaa`, `PS3_SHARPEN=0..1`, `PS3_DISPLAY_GAMMA` | Anti-aliasing, sharpening, gamma at present | | `AUDIO_ELASTIC=1` | A 43 ms audio queue that waits for a late block (default; `0` = 21 ms) | | `PS3_AUDIO_VOLUME=0..100`, `PS3_AUDIO_MUTE=1`, `PS3_AUDIO_DEVICE=` | Host audio level, mute, output device | | `PS3_WINDOW_MODE=windowed\|borderless\|fullscreen`, `PS3_WINDOW_SIZE=WxH`, `PS3_DISPLAY=`, `PS3_VSYNC=0` | The window (Cmd+F toggles fullscreen) | | `PS3_UPSCALE=metalfx` | MetalFX spatial upscaling to the window's pixel size | | `PS3_VIBRANCE`, `PS3_CONTRAST`, `PS3_VIGNETTE`, `PS3_GRAIN`, `PS3_LUT=`, `PS3_LUT_STRENGTH`, `PS3_LUT_PRESET=warm\|cool\|film\|vivid` | Picture filters (all off by default) | | `PS3_MODS_DIR=`, `PS3_MODS=`, `PS3_MODS_DUMP=` | Texture packs (`<16-hex key>.png`, first pack wins) and a texture dump to start one | | `PS3RECOMP_METAL_FPS=1` | Frame-rate counter | | `RSX_PACE_LOG=5`, `AUDIO_RATE=1` | Every 5 s: fps, frame-time percentiles, audio gaps (what to send with a report) | | `PS3_VERBOSE=1` | The full runtime log (very large) | Keyboard: Enter is START, Space is CROSS. A DualSense, DualShock 4 or Xbox controller works through SDL. ## Season 2026 profile A test profile (a copy; the owner's saves are not touched) built with the `tools/*_2026.py` scripts from public sources (CBF match sheets, ESPN rosters, Wikipedia/Wikimedia crests, community kit and face packs): - Série A and B 2026 with 20 clubs each (the stock Option File has 18 Série B slots; `port/pes_leagues.cpp` reads a 20-club layout). - Club names in every game language; 2026 squads (names, shirt names, numbers) for the 40 Brazilian clubs and 49 Libertadores and Sudamericana clubs; the Libertadores list and the South American league replaced in place. - 2026 home and away kits for the 40 clubs and crests for the clubs that were missing or sat in another club's slot, as texture packs. - No player wears another player's face any more: 14 players got their own face back, the rest a fictional one; 63 more wear their real 2026 face from PES 2013 PC face packs, as a texture pack (`faces-2026`). - Positions, abilities, foot, height, age and nationality written for every renamed player, calibrated to PES 2013's scale: from eFootball's 2026 cards (pesdb.net) where collected, a position template elsewhere. - The stadium creator's 20 stadiums carry 2026 names (only the names). HD textures: a texture pack image may be larger than the texture it replaces (the crest pack is 256x256 over 128x128), so kits, crests, faces and pitch textures can go in at higher resolution from their sources. Faces from PES 2013 PC packs (same texture layout, 1024 or 2048) go in at 512x1024 or 1024x2048, two to four times the PS3's 256x512. ## The app [`launcher/`](launcher/README.md) is a desktop app (Tauri) that runs `tools/run.sh` with your settings: Home, Graphics, Controls (labelled with the football actions), Game, **Option File** (save profiles: the default `rpcs3/` tree, copies, profiles installed from a PS3 save folder or a .zip) and Advanced (rebuild, game log, debug mode). A control whose feature the build does not have yet says so instead of doing nothing. ```sh cd launcher && npm install && npm run tauri build ``` ## Fixes made here Most of the work is in the toolkit, shared with the other ports. Highlights: - **Players invisible in the gameplay camera:** the far players' kits are baked into small main-memory render targets; the pixels stayed on the GPU, and the draw engine's surface table (64) filled up before kick-off and dropped draws silently. Write-back of small main-memory targets, and a 512-entry table. - **Neon skin and black faces:** NV308A inline uploads stopped at 256 of 1792 words, cutting every fragment program after 1 KB. - **Striped kits:** linear mipmapped textures lost their pitch below level 0. - **T-pose:** SPURS `JOBLIST` was not implemented, so animation never ran. - **Exit after the title screen:** a vblank callback delivered inside another guest callback restarted at the top of the same stack. - **Random freeze in a match:** the FIFO overrun fallback recycled the game's ring on a reading taken mid-update; now it needs 250 ms of no progress. - **Performance (2026-11-05):** shadow depth converted on the GPU instead of two full GPU waits per frame; vertex constants staged by the rows a program reads; per-program memo; buffer pool; state bound only when it changes; thread QoS so the game stays on performance cores. From about 18 fps before this work to 60. ## Layout | Folder | What it is | | ------ | ---------- | | `port/` | The CMake project: `main.cpp` (frame clock, vblank, QoS), `stubs.cpp`, `config.toml` | | `tools/` | Build, run, lift, save installer, Option File and roster tools | | [`launcher/`](launcher/README.md) | The desktop app | | `docs/` | Inventory, compatibility, work list (pt-BR), Brazil 2026 data, screenshots | | `patches/` | The toolkit changes this port needs, applied by `tools/setup_toolkit.sh` | ## License Code in this repository: MIT ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). # Resistance 2 — native PC port/recomp (work in progress)

A static recompilation of the PS3 game *Resistance 2* into a native Windows program. No emulation of the CPU: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C/C++ and compiled for your PC. Graphics go through RPCS3's Vulkan renderer, with NVIDIA DLSS / AMD FSR upscaling, 60 fps, keyboard and mouse controls, and higher resolutions.

> ⚠️ **Not Perfect.** I have only tested it **on my PC** (Ryzen 5 5600X, GeForce RTX 5070, 32 GB RAM, Windows 11, 1080p screen) and haven't beaten the game. The campaign has been played through the opening Iceland levels; past that it's untested, so things could go wrong. Some crashes or freezes may happen.

> **No game files and no translated game code are distributed, in this repository or in the installer.** You need your own copy of the game. Setup decrypts its program on your PC, translates it into C/C++ and builds the game there; the generated code and the built game never leave your PC, and no prebuilt game program is released. The repository holds the port's own code plus the small references it needs to find its place in the game's program: function addresses, patch values and short context lines from the generated code (`tools/hooks/` and `project/r2_patches.cpp`).

## What you need

- A PC running Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit).
- A CPU with AVX2: Intel 4th gen or newer, or any AMD Ryzen. Older CPUs without AVX2 won't run it.
- A Vulkan 1.3 GPU. DLSS needs a GeForce RTX card; everything else (including FSR) works on AMD, NVIDIA and Intel. Only tested on NVIDIA so far.
- Your own dump of **Resistance 2, EU disc (BCES00226), version 1.00**. This is the folder that contains `PS3_GAME`, the same kind of folder RPCS3 uses. Other regions and patched versions are not supported yet.
- About 35 GB of free disk space: ~22 GB for the game files and the rest for the build tools and the build.
- An internet connection for the setup.

## Install

**Quick install (recommended):**

1. Download the release zip from the Releases page and unzip all of it to a folder with no spaces in the path, for example `C:\Games\Resistance2Port`.
2. Run **`Setup.exe`** in that folder. (It is not code-signed: if Windows says *"Windows protected your PC"*, click **More info → Run anyway**.)
3. Pick your game: **ISO...** or **Folder...**. Setup checks the copy at once and says what to do if it can't be used (see *If your game copy is not accepted* below).
4. Click **Install** and wait. Setup installs the missing build tools (one administrator prompt), copies your game files, builds the game with as many parallel jobs as your RAM allows, adds Start-menu and desktop shortcuts and starts the launcher. It shows the progress and the time left. If it stops (error, sleep, power cut), run `Setup.exe` again and click **Resume**.

The release contains no game code: the game is always built from your own copy. Requirements, disk space, build times, uninstalling and troubleshooting (SmartScreen, antivirus, low RAM, no winget): [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md).

### Manual install (advanced)

**With the Inno installer** (if a `-Setup-<version>.exe` is on the Releases page): download `Resistance2Port-Setup-<version>.exe` from the Releases page and run it. It installs the port (default `C:\Games\Resistance2Port`), adds Start-menu and desktop shortcuts, and asks for your game. It lists the copies it finds on the PC (common folders and RPCS3's game list); you can also type or paste a path, or use the **ISO...** / **Folder...** buttons. It checks the copy before going on and says what is wrong and what to do if it can't be used (see *If your game copy is not accepted* below). At the end it opens **Setup**, the window with the progress bar, with your game already filled in: click **Install** there (step 2 below). The installer contains only the port; the game files always come from your own copy. Use a decrypted ISO or a game folder (the same kind RPCS3 uses). Tick **Portable mode** to keep settings only in the install folder.

**By hand:**

1. Download this repository: click on Code at the top, then Download ZIP, then unzip it somewhere with no spaces in the path, for example `C:\Games\Resistance2Port`.
2. Double-click **`Setup.bat`**. It will:
   - install the free build tools if they're missing (Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, LLVM, CMake, Ninja, Python, Git), using `winget`;
   - look for your game (an ISO or a game folder), check it, then copy it into the port folder (or move a folder, if it's on the same drive);
   - decrypt the game's program file, using the application keys from RPCS3's public source code;
   - download RPCS3's source at a fixed version and apply this port's renderer patch (`ps3recomp/patches/r2-rpcs3.patch`);
   - generate the game code from your copy and build the game.

   The first run takes a while: tool installs plus a 20–60 minute build. At the end, Setup offers to put a "Resistance 2" shortcut to the launcher on your desktop.
3. Play with **`Launcher.exe`**. It has the settings (display mode, resolution, frame rate, VSync, anti-aliasing, upscaling, texture filtering, sharpening) and the key bindings.

You only need to run Setup again after downloading a newer version of the port; otherwise just use the launcher.

**Choosing the game in Setup.bat:** it lists the copies it found, numbered. Type a number, or type or paste the path of the ISO or game folder (you can also drag it into the window). **B** opens a file picker (Windows only). `Setup.bat -Game "<path>"` skips the question. The path can be an ISO, the game folder, or a file inside it. An ISO is opened by Windows, copied from and closed again; if Windows can't open it, Setup reads it directly.

### If your game copy is not accepted

The installer and Setup check the copy before copying anything. The supported version is **Resistance 2 (EU disc, BCES00226)**, about 23.3 GB.

| Message | What to do |
|---|---|
| compressed archive (.zip, .7z, .rar) | Extract it first, then pick the ISO or folder inside. |
| PlayStation Store package (.pkg) / game update folder | Pick the disc copy. Game updates are not needed. |
| not <game> / from another region | Use the supported disc version listed above. |
| PlayStation Store version | Only the disc version is supported. |
| encrypted disc image / PARAM.SFO is not valid | Decrypt the ISO first (for example PS3Dec with the disc key from the `.dkey` file), or use a game folder from a PS3 or RPCS3. |
| program file was decrypted or replaced (plain ELF) | Use the original, unmodified files. Setup decrypts them itself. |
| files are missing / smaller than expected | The copy is incomplete. Copy or dump it again. |
| different from the known file (warning) | The copy may be modified. You can continue; Setup stops later if the decrypted program is not the supported version. |
| not enough free space | Free up space, or install on another drive. |

The checks run on your PC only. Nothing is uploaded.

**Updates:** the launcher checks this repository's Releases page once at start and says when a newer version is out (it only opens the download page; nothing is downloaded or replaced). Turn it off with the launcher's *Check for updates* option (Advanced page) or the environment variable `PORT_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`. The installed version is in the `VERSION` file.

**Settings and controls** (`settings.ini`, `settings.bat`, `controls.txt`, `mouselook.cfg`) are also kept in `%USERPROFILE%\Saved Games\Resistance 2\config`. Missing files are restored from there when the launcher or game starts, so they survive reinstalling or updating the port. To keep everything in the port folder only, create an empty file named `portable.txt` next to `Launcher.exe` (the installer's *Portable mode* does this). Saves are still kept in the port folder (`gamedata`); the uninstaller asks before deleting it, and its default is to keep it.

**No console window:** the launcher starts the game without a console. The game's output goes to `logs\run.log`.

**First launch:** the game shows its own one-time setup screens and an autosave notice. Before the game starts, the launcher prepares the shader cache from your game files (a progress panel; **Skip for now** or Esc skips it), and the game then compiles every known shader behind a **Compiling shaders N / M** panel (see *Shader precompile*), so levels play without shader stutter from the first visit. Shaders are cached for later starts.

## Controls

Keyboard and mouse are supported out of the box (WASD, mouse look, Mouse1 fire, Mouse2 aim, R reload, G grenade, E use, V/Mouse4 melee, Q / wheel switch weapon, T flashlight, M map, Esc pause). Controllers work too. All keyboard and mouse bindings can be changed in the launcher.

**Button prompts follow the device you used last.** Touch the keyboard or mouse and the on-screen prompts (hints, menu legends, tutorial text) show your keys; press a button or move a stick on a controller and they switch to that controller's buttons. Switching is instant and works mid-game. With an Xbox / XInput controller (or any non-PlayStation pad) the prompts show Xbox buttons, drawn by the port as simple coloured letters (no copied artwork):

| PS3 | Xbox | PS3 | Xbox |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cross | A | L1 / R1 | LB / RB |
| Circle | B | L2 / R2 | LT / RT |
| Square | X | L3 / R3 | LS / RS (stick click) |
| Triangle | Y | Select / Start | View / Menu |
| D-pad | D-pad | Left / right stick | Left / right stick |

With the XInput backend (`PAD_BACKEND=xinput`), a Sony DualShock 3/4 or DualSense that is plugged in (detected by its USB/Bluetooth ID, used through DS4Windows / Steam Input as XInput) keeps the PlayStation symbols; with SDL3 (default) the prompts follow the controller type, see *Controllers (SDL3)* below. The launcher's **Controller button prompts** option forces Xbox or PlayStation. Prompts name the game's default button layout; if you remap buttons in the game's own options, the prompts still name the default ones.

**Mouse look is direct:** raw mouse counts turn the camera's yaw and pitch each frame (× the launcher's sensitivity × the game's own Look Sensitivity), not an emulated right stick — no acceleration, dead zone or speed cap. While aiming down sights the turn rate is scaled by the scope zoom so the same mouse movement covers the same part of the screen (`R2_ZOOM_SENS`: 1 = default, 0 = no scaling, up to 2). The game's aim assist only acts on stick input, so it doesn't pull against the mouse, and while the mouse is in use the right stick's turn rate is ignored so the two never add up. Mouse counts made while the camera isn't yours (menus, pause, cutscenes, scripted sequences) are dropped, so the view doesn't jump afterwards. The launcher's **Mouse aiming = Classic** switches back to stick emulation. The game has no mouse pointer in its menus; they are driven by the keyboard (arrows / Enter / Esc) or a controller. F8 frees the cursor.

**Controllers (SDL3).** The port reads controllers through SDL3 (built in, no extra DLL): Xbox, DualShock 4, DualSense, DualShock 3 (with its Windows driver), Switch Pro and Joy-Con work directly. **DS4Windows and Steam Input are no longer needed** (they still work; if they expose a virtual Xbox pad next to the real controller, the port ignores the duplicate so it doesn't become a ghost player 2). Controllers can be plugged in and out at any time, no restart, up to 8. Rumble works on every pad that has it (DualSense included), and a DualShock 4 / DualSense light bar shows the player's colour (player 1 blue, player 2 red). If SDL3 can't start, the port falls back to XInput automatically (`logs\run.log` shows `[cellPad] controllers: SDL3` or `SDL3 could not start`).

**Button prompts by controller type:** with *Controller button prompts = Auto*, a PlayStation pad (DualShock 3/4, DualSense) shows PlayStation symbols and an Xbox or other pad shows Xbox letters. Switch controllers are read by button position (the bottom button is Cross); with *Nintendo button layout = Nintendo style* A (right) confirms and B cancels as on a Switch, and the prompts show the Xbox-style letters. Under Steam Input the real controller type is used when SDL reports it; otherwise set the prompts by hand.

**Gyro aiming** (DualShock 4, DualSense, Switch Pro, Joy-Con; off by default): turning the controller turns the view, added directly to the camera like the mouse (smooth, not limited by the stick). *While aiming* only uses it with the Aim button (L1 / LB) held. Leave the controller still for about a second after it connects so the resting drift is calibrated. In split-screen co-op each player's gyro moves only their own view (as a right-stick input, like the second player's mouse).

| Option (launcher Controls page / in game *More PC Options*) | Values | Variable |
|---|---|---|
| Controller support | **SDL3**, XInput | `PAD_BACKEND=sdl3\|xinput` (restart). `sdl2` is accepted and uses SDL3 |
| Gyro aiming | **Off**, On, While aiming | `PAD_GYRO=0\|1\|aim` |
| Gyro sensitivity | **2x**, 0.5x-6x | `PAD_GYRO_SENS=<0.05..20>` (view degrees per controller degree) |
| Gyro vertical | **Normal**, Inverted | `PAD_GYRO_INVERT_Y=1` (on top of the game's own invert setting) |
| Gyro turning axis | **Controller**, Player | `PAD_GYRO_SPACE=local\|player` (player = yaw around gravity, works flat or upright) |
| Gyro calibration | **On connect**, Off | `PAD_GYRO_CALIBRATE=0` turns off the 1 s still-calibration |
| Light bar | **Player colour**, Off | `PAD_LIGHTBAR=0` |
| Nintendo button layout | **By position**, Nintendo style | `PAD_NINTENDO_SWAP=1` |
| (no launcher option) | **On** | `PAD_DEDUP=0` keeps virtual duplicates (Steam Input / DS4Windows / ViGEm) as separate controllers |
| (no launcher option) | **360** | `PAD_GYRO_STICK_DPS=<deg/s>`: gyro speed that equals a full right stick (co-op / classic mouse aiming, where gyro drives the stick) |

With `PAD_BACKEND=xinput` the old behaviour returns: XInput only (up to four), PlayStation pads through DS4Windows / Steam Input, no gyro or light bar.

## Local co-op

Two players on one PC, split-screen, as on PS3. No PSN account is needed: the port provides a second local user.

**Starting it:** plug in two controllers (or one, with *Player 2 uses keyboard and mouse*). Main menu → **Co-op** → the offline / split-screen co-op staging screen (the online options need PSN and don't work). On the staging screen player 2 presses **START** (or Enter / Esc on the keyboard for a keyboard player 2) to join: on PS3 this opens the "select a user" box; the port answers it at once with a local user named **Player 2**, and player 2 shows as logged in. Start the mission and the screen splits.

Only the offline, split-screen part of co-op works: everything that needs PSN (online co-op, competitive, the lobby browser) stays unavailable.

**Who is who:**

- Player 1 = the keyboard and mouse plus the first controller found (as in single player).
- Player 2 = the next controller. A controller keeps its player while it stays plugged in. A controller plugged in later takes the lowest free player; when one is unplugged, its player has no input until it is plugged back.
- With two local players the direct mouse look is off. The mouse then moves the keyboard player's view like a right stick (it would otherwise turn both heroes).

**Options** (launcher, Controls page; or `settings.bat`):

| Option | Values | Variable |
|---|---|---|
| Local co-op (split-screen) | **On**, Off | `PAD_COOP=0`: the game sees only player 1. Extra controllers (or duplicate virtual pads from Steam Input / DS4Windows) can't join |
| Player 1 controller | **Automatic**, Controller 1-8 | `PAD_P1_CONTROLLER=<1..8>`: the controller that is player 1 (SDL3: in the order they were connected; XInput: 1-4, Windows' XInput order) |
| Player 2 controller | **Automatic**, Controller 1-8 | `PAD_P2_CONTROLLER=<1..8>`: the controller that is player 2 (numbered as above) |
| Player 2 uses keyboard and mouse | **Off**, On | `PAD_P2_KEYBOARD=1`: player 1 = the first controller only, player 2 = keyboard and mouse |
| (no launcher option) | **2** | `PS3_LOCAL_USERS=<1..4>`: local users the game sees. `1` = player 2 can't sign in. `PS3_USER2_NAME=<name>` renames player 2 |

1447847437.readme_excerpt:
# God of War: Ascension — native macOS port (Apple Silicon)

**[Leia em português](README.pt-BR.md)**

God of War: Ascension (PS3, BCES-01741, Europe) **statically recompiled to native arm64 code** and
running on macOS. No emulator and no Wine: the PPU code is translated to C and compiled for the
Apple CPU, the SPU programs (including the EDGE geometry jobs) are translated per image, and the RSX
GPU is reimplemented on Vulkan through MoltenVK (Metal).

**Status: playable from start to the areas tested, natively on macOS, with correct graphics and no
shader-compilation stutter.** Played for long sessions on an M4 Max.

> This repository contains **no game data**. You need your own legally obtained copy of the game
> (disc image) and must decrypt your own `EBOOT.BIN`. Everything derived from the game (the
> recompiled code, shader caches, saves) is generated locally and is git-ignored.

## Test machine

| | |
|---|---|
| Computer | MacBook Pro 14" (Mac16,6) |
| Chip | Apple M4 Max — 14-core CPU (10 performance + 4 efficiency), 32-core GPU |
| Memory | 36 GB unified |
| OS | macOS 27.0.1 |
| Graphics stack | MoltenVK 1.4.2 + Vulkan loader 1.4.363, SDL2 (sdl2-compat 2.32), glslang 16.6 |
| Display | 3024×1964 Retina; game renders at 1280×720, upscaled (Catmull-Rom + adaptive sharpening) |

All numbers below were measured on this machine, on mains power.

## Performance

Frame rate by scene with build v20 (2026-11-08): the game's own frame counter over a fixed ~75 s
window of each scene, measured headless from a save.

| Scene | fps (v20) | Earlier |
|---|---|---|
| Main menu | 60 (locked; not re-measured) | 60 (locked); ~74 uncapped |
| Opening of the first level | **~69** | 46–54 |
| Megaera fight | **~60** (59.9 in A/B; 61.1 in its steady part; 59.7 over 10 minutes) | ~41 |
| Bridge / prison area | **~63** | 42–44 |
| Rooftop fight (heaviest scene measured) | **~33** | 22–27 |
| Harem illusion scene | ~30 (earlier build; not re-measured) | ~3.6 before translating the EDGE code fragments it uses |

- Values above 60 are real: the port does not cap the frame rate at 60 in these scenes.
- The harem scene needs someone to play up to it: a headless run resumes at the save's last
  checkpoint, which is the bridge.

Captures from those runs. The game has no on-screen counter: the number is drawn on the frame from
the game's own frame counter, averaged over the 10 s around it (`scripts/print_fps.py`).

| Opening of the first level | Megaera fight |
|---|---|
| ![Opening of the first level, 68.6 fps](docs/img/fps-level-opening.jpg) | ![Megaera fight, 60.8 fps](docs/img/fps-megaera.jpg) |
| **Bridge / prison area** | **Rooftop fight** |
| ![Bridge / prison area, 64.3 fps](docs/img/fps-bridge.jpg) | ![Rooftop fight, 33.3 fps](docs/img/fps-rooftop.jpg) |

How the Megaera scene got from unplayable to ~60 fps:

| Step | fps |
|---|---|
| First boot to the level (SPU code interpreted) | 3.5 |
| EDGE code fragments translated (443 placements) | 20 |
| SPU float in NEON under FPCR round-to-zero + flush-to-zero | 33 |
| EDGE native kernels via SIMDe where they beat the translated code | 35 |
| NEON helpers for SPU operations, 3-instruction float range check | ~41 |
| Main-thread park spin capped to the next vblank tick | 43.7 |
| Extra SPURS lanes for the job lists the main thread waits on | 50.8 |
| New textures no longer wait for the GPU; larger draw batches; dense SPU coherence table | ~52 |
| Live-reservation mirror, lock-line backoff, adaptive texture hash | ~56 |
| SPU lock-line lock striped by line | 57.6 |
| Relocatable SPU code copies recognized by content (out of the interpreter); thread-locals cached per SPU context | ~60 |

Shader compilation (the stutter on entering a new area or doing something for the first time):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Pipelines a long session creates | ~8,200 (table full after ~13 min → broken image) | ~900–1,450 |
| Worst stall when a new pipeline appears | 98 ms + 190 ms on the draw | 0.4 ms (compiled on worker threads) |
| Precompiling the known pipelines at boot | 7.2 s | 0.12 s on the game thread; the rest in the background |
| Same shader pair in many pipelines | recompiled by Metal each time | one shared module (8.8 → 0.4 ms) |

The game is CPU-bound (SPU work), not GPU-bound. In the Megaera fight the median frame is under
16.7 ms; the ~14% of frames that run past 20 ms are bound by the EDGE geometry jobs, which the game
confines to four SPUs.

## What was built or fixed for macOS

See **[docs/CHANGES.md](docs/CHANGES.md)** for the full list. In short:

- **arm64 correctness:**
  - torn 16-byte SPU writes, which caused rare hangs where the FIFO walker read data as commands;
  - memory ordering on the FIFO and on SPU DMA;
  - SPU reservation race;
  - `_setjmp`, TLS and the clock.
- **Performance:**
  - translated EDGE code fragments (1,720 placements);
  - NEON SPU helpers and the native SPU float path on arm64;
  - SPURS kernel latency;
  - per-region choice between native and translated EDGE code.
- **Graphics (RSX → Vulkan/MoltenVK):**
  - depth bounds test emulated (Metal has none);
  - shadow cascades and comparison direction;
  - polygon offset (no more shadow acne);
  - 3D textures (colour-grading LUT);
  - blend constants;
  - fragment-program precision and R/H register aliasing;
  - 3,072-entry texture cache.
- **Shader stutter:**
  - canonical pipeline keys;
  - on-disk pipeline catalog;
  - shared shader modules;
  - asynchronous pipeline compilation;
  - SPIR-V disk cache.
- **Mac integration:**
  - window on the main thread;
  - DualSense and keyboard through SDL;
  - full screen with HiDPI upscaler;
  - `.app` bundle with icon.
- **Tooling:**
  - on-demand capture of every render pass (colour, depth, stencil, per-draw state);
  - SPU interpreter-miss logging;
  - quick headless benchmark from a save.

## Repository layout

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `ps3recomp/` | [sp00nznet/ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) v0.17.0 + the GoW:A patch + all macOS/arm64 changes (MIT) |
| `gowa-port/` | [MaChInEgUn3/God-of-War-Ascension-Recompiled](https://github.com/MaChInEgUn3/God-of-War-Ascension-Recompiled) + macOS changes (MIT) |
| `scripts/` | test, benchmark and analysis scripts |
| `app/` | builds `God of War Ascension.app` (icon generated from your own disc's artwork) |
| `data/` | addresses only: SPU images in the EU EBOOT and the EDGE code-fragment placements to translate from your EBOOT |
| `jogar.sh` | launcher (window, controller, save, caches) |
| `docs/` | build guide, change list, technical notes |

## Building and playing

See **[docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md)**. Summary: Homebrew dependencies → mount your ISO →
decrypt your EBOOT → translate PPU and SPU code → CMake/Ninja → `./jogar.sh` or
`app/fazer_app.sh`.

Controls: DualSense/controller via SDL, or keyboard (arrows, Z=✕ X=○ A=□ S=△, Q/W=L1/R1,
1/2=L2/R2, Enter/Esc=START, Tab=SELECT). ⌘Q quits.

## Known issues

- Character "replicas" drawn on some walls; water reflection not right yet.
- The depth-of-field background can look blocky.
- New areas can still drop fps until their EDGE code fragments are translated (see
  `docs/BUILDING.md`, "fps drop in a new area"). Shader compilation never freezes the game, but an
  object may appear a few frames late the first time.

## Contributing

Forks and pull requests are welcome — especially for the open graphics issues, performance (the SPU
side is the bottleneck), and other PS3 titles on the same base. The technique notes in
[docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md](docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md) explain how each problem was found.

## Credits and license

- **ps3recomp** by Ned Heller / sp00nznet — MIT.
- **God of War: Ascension Recompiled** by MaChInEgUn3 and contributors — MIT. The base of this
  port: game patch, job-module extraction, EDGE native kernels.
- Reference ports for Windows: arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc and otavix010/gow-ascension-pc (fragment
  program and SPU fixes ported from the latter).
- macOS port: Pedro Henrique ([@Pedrohds1](https://github.com/Pedrohds1)), developed with Claude
  (Anthropic).

Our own files are MIT ([LICENSE](LICENSE)); `ps3recomp/` and `gowa-port/` keep their own licenses.
God of War is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This project is not affiliated with or
endorsed by Sony; it contains no copyrighted game code or assets.

1447959106.readme_excerpt:
# inFamous PC (US Release - BCUS98119)

> **Dedicated US Recompilation Project (`BCUS98119`)**  
> Maintained separately for the North American / US release.  
> Based on upstream recompiler foundation from [sp00nznet/ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) and [whompay/inFAMOUSreborn](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn).

An unofficial native Windows port of **inFamous** (PlayStation 3, 2009, North American / US
release `BCUS98119`). The game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code is statically
recompiled to x86-64 C/C++ with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp),
running natively on Windows Direct3D 12 rather than under an emulator.

**This repository contains no game code or data.** You build the game yourself,
on your own PC, from your own copy of the game.

## US Release Architecture & Optimizations

This dedicated US release tree integrates key structural rebases and optimizations:

* **PPU Address Translation & Rebase:** Uses custom US PPU patches in `installer/regions/BCUS98119/` and dynamic guest address translation via `infamous-recomp/infamous_region.h` to cleanly align US functions, TOC offsets, and static BSS globals.
* **US HUD Prompt & Font Glyphs:** Maps US-specific `core.xpp` texture object IDs for on-screen controller and keyboard/mouse prompts using `make_kbm_prompts.py` and `make_kbm_icons.py`.
* **Rooftop & Elevation Stutter Fix:**
  - **Asymmetric Adaptive LOD:** Fast reduction (EMA tau=6 frames / 0.4s) and gradual recovery (EMA tau=30 frames / 3.5s) with `ADAPT_LOD=1` and `ADAPT_LOD_MIN=0.85` prevents draw-call explosions (25k+ draws/frame) when overlooking Empire City.
  - **Synchronized PPU Dynamic Actor Scaling:** Multiplies the EBOOT `.data` LOD table (`0x0078AD30`) by `g_v237_lodf` in `rsx_d3d12_backend.c`, ensuring cars, pedestrians, and dynamic props scale down symmetrically with SPU geometry jobs.
* **Dual-CCD & Multi-Core Affinity Shielding:** Multi-CCD processors (such as AMD Ryzen 9 7950X / 9950X) are protected from high-latency Infinity Fabric stalls (`[TASKWAIT]`) by keeping critical SPU worker threads pinned to CCD 0 (`SPURS_PCORE_WIDS=0,1,2,6`, `V221A_PLACE=0`).

## Requirements

- Your own inFamous US disc dump: `BCUS98119`.
- Decrypted `EBOOT.elf` (SHA-256: `4f2db3fb7c76fbb4f80cbc8445cf0ea1570a664996a7787e690efcc1a39befb4`).
- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with Direct3D 12 support.
- A modern multi-core CPU. Multi-CCD AMD Ryzen and Intel hybrid CPUs are natively supported.
- [Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) with "Add python.exe to PATH" ticked.
- [Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/)
  with the **Desktop development with C++** workload and the **C++ Clang
  Compiler for Windows** component.
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), only if your `PS3_GAME\USRDIR` has `EBOOT.BIN`
  but no decrypted `EBOOT.elf`. Setup uses it to decrypt the executable.
- About 10 GB of free disk space and 16 GB of RAM.

## Quick Launch

To play:
1. Double click **`Play inFamous.cmd`** in the root directory.
2. If diagnosing GPU device lost or investigating rendering hangs, run **`play-dred.cmd`** (writes extended D3D12 breadcrumbs to `play-dred.err.log`).

## Easy install

Download or run the installer targeting your `BCUS98119` folder (the one containing `PS3_GAME`), pick an install location, and press **Install**.

## Updating

When updates are published to this repository, run `Update inFamous.cmd` in the root folder. The updater compares files, pulls updates, and recompiles only what changed.

## Building manually

```bat
cd installer
cargo build --release
target\release\infamous-installer --game "D:\Dumps\inFamous [BCUS98119]"
```

`infamous-installer doctor` checks the requirements only. Finished steps are
skipped when you run it again, so an interrupted install continues where it
stopped. See [installer/README.md](installer/README.md) for every step and the
maintainer commands.

## Playing

Run **inFamous** (the shortcut Setup made). It opens a small options window first
(vsync, frame cap, resolution, language and more, saved to `settings.ini`);
**Play** starts the game. The same settings are in the game's pause menu under
**Settings**. Controllers work as on the console, and keyboard and mouse are supported.

### Controls and button prompts

Xbox pads (and Steam Input's virtual pads) work through XInput; DualShock 4, DualSense, Switch Pro, Joy-Con,
Steam Controller and most other pads work through SDL3, with the community mappings in
`sdl3/gamecontrollerdb.txt` for pads SDL does not know by itself. **Button Prompts** (in the launcher and in the
Settings menu) is *Automatic* by default: the prompts follow the device you used last -- the game's own
PlayStation glyphs, Xbox, Nintendo or Steam Deck glyphs drawn in the same style, or the keyboard and mouse
keys -- and can be fixed to any one of them.

Keyboard and mouse defaults (every key can be changed in `controls.ini` next to `settings.ini`, one
`action=KEY` per line; run `Update inFamous.cmd` afterwards so the drawn key prompts follow):

| Action | Key | Action | Key |
|---|---|---|---|
| Move (run) / walk | W A S D / hold Shift | Camera | Mouse |
| Jump (Cross) | Space | Melee (Square) | F |
| Triangle | E | Circle | C |
| Aim (L1) | Right mouse | Fire (R1) | Left mouse |
| L2 / R2 | Q / R | L3 / R3 | V / Middle mouse |
| Precision (d-pad up) | Ctrl | Map (Select) | Tab |
| Pause (Start) | Esc | Free the mouse pointer | hold Alt |

Actions: `forward back left right jump melee triangle circle aim fire l2 r2 l3 r3 precision select start walk
free_mouse`. Keys: a letter or digit, `SPACE`, `ENTER`, `TAB`, `ESC`, `SHIFT`, `CTRL`, `ALT`, `BACKSPACE`,
`UP`/`DOWN`/`LEFT`/`RIGHT`, `F1`-`F12`, `LMB`/`RMB`/`MMB`/`MOUSE4`/`MOUSE5`, or `VK:<hex>`. In menus Enter
selects, Backspace goes back, and W/A/S/D or the arrow keys move the cursor.

**F10** opens the in-game trainer: God Mode, Infinite Energy, Refill Health,
Max Health x2/x5/x10, Add XP, Karma +/-, Kill Enemies / Civilians, Super Speed
and Player Model (play as Zeke, Trish, Kessler, Alden or John). Set `TRAINER=0`
to turn it off.

## DLSS and FSR (optional)

The game can use NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA or AMD FSR for upscaling, and AMD FSR frame generation.
They are not included in the download because NVIDIA and AMD distribute their SDKs themselves,
but both are free and take a few minutes to add.

- **DLSS** needs an NVIDIA RTX graphics card.
- **FSR** works on any modern GPU (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel). FSR 4 needs a Radeon RX 9000 card;
  other cards get FSR 3.1 automatically.

**1. Download the SDK(s) you want.** You need the **source code**, not a Windows or Linux demo.
On the page, click the green **Code** button, then **Download ZIP**. If you go through the
Releases page instead, pick **Source code (zip)**, not the files with "demo" or "samples" in the name.

| For | Download | Rename the extracted folder to |
|---|---|---|
| DLSS / DLAA | [github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS) | `dlss-sdk` |
| FSR and frame generation | [github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK) | `fsr-sdk` |

**2. Put the folder(s) in your inFamous install folder**, next to `infamous-recomp` and
`ps3recomp`:

```
inFamous\
  dlss-sdk\        <- contains include\ and lib\
  fsr-sdk\         <- contains Kits\
  infamous-recomp\
  ps3recomp\
  ...
```

Make sure you don't end up with a folder inside a folder (`dlss-sdk\DLSS-main\include`).
`include` (DLSS) or `Kits` (FSR) must be directly inside.

**3. Rebuild the game once.** Open a Command Prompt in the install folder and run:

```bat
type nul > .installer\update.pending
"Update inFamous.cmd"
```

This rebuilds the game with the SDK(s), which takes a while. Any later update also picks them up
automatically, so you only do this once.

**4. Turn it on in game:** pause, then **Settings**, then **Upscaling** (DLAA, DLSS Quality /
Balanced / Performance, FSR Native AA / Quality / Balanced / Performance) and **Frame
Generation**. The same options are in the launcher's options window. Upscaling and frame
generation apply after a restart.

If the **Upscaling** row is missing, the build didn't find the SDK: check the folder names and
layout from step 2, then repeat step 3.

## How it works

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `ps3recomp` | The recompiler toolkit and runtime: PPU and SPU lifters, HLE system libraries, RSX on Direct3D 12, audio and input |
| `infamous-recomp` | The inFamous-specific parts: program entry, game stubs and fixes, asset tools |
| `installer` | Setup and the command-line installer: reads the disc, regenerates the code from your game, applies `installer/patches`, builds |
| `installer/infamous.toml` | Everything about the game and the port: pipeline steps, generated files, build and launch settings |
| `installer/generated.lock` | Hashes of each generated file before and after the port's patches |
