09f87778b01ad499a92ed69f7eb1d4695feaee98.message:
fix(rsx): vertex programs run from their start slot; the pipeline key has it

Branch targets in RSX vertex microcode are absolute slots, and the draw
engine decompiled every program as if it started at slot 0. A branching
program loaded elsewhere never reached its output block and ran the
16,384-iteration loop bound per vertex: in-game frames took 0.4-3 s of
GPU and a cutscene looked frozen. rsx_draw_engine.c now hands the
decompiler the program's start slot (rsx_vp_set_branch_base), and since
the start slot changes the generated code, it is part of the pipeline
key too (the same bytes at two start slots used to share one pipeline;
tools/tests/vp_branch_base.c shows the HLSL differs). After the fix, 1
frame over 100 ms in 300 s instead of 116 of up to 3 s.

Diagnostics, all env-gated and off by default: RSX_GPU_SLOW_MS=<ms>
names Metal command buffers slower than that; GCM_SEMA_STATS=1 reports
semaphore acquires and their waits every 5 s (only the display labels
0x42/0x43 are acquired; GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1 deadlocks this title);
RSX_FP_SHADOW_ONE=1 makes every shadow-map comparison pass, to tell a
bad shadow map from bad shading; the per-draw pass dump also prints each
vertex stream's raw format word and its first elements.

test(tools): the vertex-program decompiler depends on the start slot

tools/tests/vp_branch_base.c compiles only the toolkit's VP decompiler
(no game code, no Metal) and feeds it the same four-instruction program
with an absolute BRI to slot 3 at two start slots: start 0 lowers the
target to relative 3, start 1 to relative 2, and going back to start 0
gives the first HLSL again; a program without branches is identical at
both. So the start slot is an input of shader generation and has to be
part of the pipeline key (fixed in the toolkit patch).

23a2da6a84464f74cf00079f4b3d1d35aff16ed8.message:
fix(port): closing the window or Ctrl+C quits the game cleanly

Closing the window only turned the video off: the vblank loop saw the
pump report it and went on with rsx_ok = 0, so the guest kept running
with no window and the process stayed behind until killed. SIGINT and
SIGTERM (Ctrl+C in the terminal, a plain kill, the launcher) killed it
mid-frame instead, a save being written included.

Both now go through the toolkit's ps3_host_quit, as Cmd+Q already did
and as the console's Quit Game does: REQUEST_EXITGAME to the title's
sysutil callbacks, then exit 0 after PS3_QUIT_GRACE_MS (default 3000),
never while a save is in flight. The signal handler only sets a flag
the vblank loop takes (a handler may not print or start threads); a
second signal ends the process at once with 128 + signal.

Measured, headless boot to the menus, SIGTERM at 40 s: "[quit]
requested", REQUEST_EXITGAME to 1 callback, process gone after 3 s
with status 0 (Afro Samurai does not exit on its own; the grace ends
it).

66997d3c41f8a432dbd11d5803c1a07e5cb023d3.message:
perf(spu): FMOD's codec and DSP plugins run lifted, not interpreted

In-game audio came out slow and smeared, hard to make out (user report,
windowed session). A sample of that session showed the FMOD mixer SPU
thread spending 84% of its time in the SPU interpreter, half of that in
lifted-code lookups: the mixer (spu_0001) DMAs each plugin's text straight
out of the EBOOT into its own local store (spu_0019 at EA 0x0089BA00 to
LS 0x25910, spu_0018 0x00897A00 to 0x34BA0, spu_0003 0x0087D680 to
0x2A650, the last one again on every use) and calls into it there.
lift_spu.sh lifts spu_0002..0019 at their link address, which never
matches, so every codec and effect call fell to the interpreter, too slow
for the mixer's 5.3 ms blocks once the GPU and PPU load a windowed run.

The plugin text in local store is the EBOOT's byte for byte (checked for
all three), i.e. position independent. tools/lift_fmod_plugins.sh lifts
the 18 plugins once with spu_lifter.py --reloc at their link address and
generates port/spu/fmodplug_register.c, which registers each with
spu_overlay_register_region_reloc (text EA, text size, canonical 0x80):
the GET that copies a plugin in makes its lift resident wherever it
landed. rebuild.sh's spu step runs it; CMake picks the TU up beside
jobmods_register.c. SPU_RELOC_OFF=1 leaves them to the interpreter (A/B).

Measured, headless New Game run to the village fight: the interpreter
drops from 979 of 1162 mixer-thread samples to none, the plugins show as
fmodplug_* frames with a handful of samples; recorded output has the same
level and the same transient counts per window as interpreter runs (19 at
100-120 s, 8 at 160-180 s), no unresolved calls.

66f9c2adac6115aa7df825408a7ccfbc73c6b211.message:
perf(rsx): less CPU per draw in the FIFO drain

A 10 s sample of a headless walk in the village had the frame-clock
thread draining the FIFO 58% of the time, and the slow frames (over
50 ms, 12% of them) spent ~41 ms there against ~17 ms in a 30 fps one.
Inside the drain: CPU vertex fetch 33%, the vertex dedupe 28%, texture
hashing 14%. Toolkit (patch), same results, three hot spots:

- rsx_vertex_remap_build: a draw whose references share one base
  index and span a small range (an indexed mesh) is deduplicated
  through a direct map, a sequential run is the identity outright;
  the hash stays for everything else. PS3RECOMP_VTX_REMAP_HASH=1 keeps
  the hash for every draw. New test test_vertex_remap (ctest

6f48120fd9b8a145d9062286cf9c2459ffa1e262.message:
fix(lift): jump-table case targets lifted as function entries

The lifter resolves a switch only over the cases inside the function it
lifted, and may cut a large function where another branch target begins.
Cases past the cut go through the indirect-call fallback, which needs a
lifted function at the case address; a case label is not one, so the
call was dropped ("[ppu] unresolved indirect call -> 0x...") and the
title ran on with garbage. The engine's message dispatcher
(func_001EA288, cmplwi r3,0x105E: 4191 cases, table at
[[r2-0x7EB0]-0x58E0]) lost case 0x1F079C that way, and New Game span for
ever on a NULL object in func_002BA670.

tools/augment_functions.py splits the function list at every target of
the tables in tools/jumptables.txt (or found by its scan for GCC PPC64
tables: lwz from the TOC, lwzx/add/mtctr, bounded by cmplwi) and writes
EBOOT.functions.aug.json, which rebuild.sh lift now feeds the lifter. A
case that falls through into the next stays correct: the lifter emits a
fall-through tail call. Relifted: no "unresolved indirect call" left in
four New Game runs (fx1-fx4).

7e40dbb89078e71bc0613656417cae6434574846.message:
fix(spurs): job chains run their JOBLISTs; one context pointer per input

The 3D scene in play was a mass of giant stretched triangles. The NTG
renderer laps its skinning job chain every frame as [JOB palette] ->
[JOBLIST of 5 vertex-skinning jobs] -> [JOB lap notify] -> END, and the
HLE chain walker treated JOBLIST (command 6) as a no-op. The skinning
jobs never ran, nothing was written into the RSX-visible ring where the
stride-24 character and prop vertices live, and ~100 colour draws a
frame read whatever another writer had left there (32-byte debug-point
records read at a 24-byte stride).

jc_execute now runs a JOBLIST's jobs in order, like JOB commands
(CellSpursJobList: numJobs, sizeOfJob, eaJobList; SPURS_JC_JOBLIST=0
skips it again). With it, SPU PUTs land in the ring at about 37 MB/s,
the first one at 0x11600380, the offset the shadow draws read.

Those skinning jobs carry two DMA inputs, and the older job context
(SPURS_JOB_CTX_V1, which this job's crt reads) is an array of LS
pointers, one per input buffer and then one per cache buffer; it held
the first input and then the cache buffers, so input 1 pointed at the
cache and the characters were skinned from the wrong data (shards in the
cutscenes). spurs_job.c now records where each input lands and fills the
array in that order.

Result, headless New Game run: Afro, the village and Ninja Ninja render
textured and lit at 240 and 270 s; a windowed session played without a
crash. Found with an independent analysis of the walker's command
handling; the old patches/ps3recomp-vp-start-cache-key.patch is folded
into the toolkit patch.

7ee1471e71af00c167e37e44f9f5b2b8ec70fdbc.message:
diag(port): AFRO_TEXT_RO=1 makes the guest text read-only

Lifted code never reads instructions, but switch tables live inline in
.text, and some read back zero mid-game ("unresolved indirect call" to a
table base) while PPU_WWATCH saw no guest store. With AFRO_TEXT_RO=1 the
text segment, from 0x10000 to its last whole 16 KB page (0x89C000), is
mprotect()ed read-only once the loader and the HLE setup are done, so a
host write (HLE memcpy, SPU DMA, file read) faults with the guest caller
and a host backtrace; AFRO_TEXT_RO_CONT=1 reports each writer once and
goes on. Off by default.

It caught the SPU skinning job PUTting its local store over the text
(next commit).

80fc7231aeaa514320319732f8c76261e14a45bf.message:
perf(spurs): run the skinning JOBLIST's jobs on four threads

The same 10 s sample had the job-chain thread 94% busy: the vertex-
skinning JOBLIST (job 8B2B4776E3A079D8) ran its jobs one after another
on the chain's host thread, and in the slow frames the render thread
sat in event_queue_receive waiting for the lap. On hardware jm2 spreads
a list over the instance's SPUs; the title creates its SPURS with 5.

Toolkit (patch): SPURS_JC_JOBLIST_PAR=<n> (2..8, off by default) runs
a JOBLIST on up to n host threads, the chain's own and n-1 helpers
taking the next job from a shared counter. Each thread is its own SPU
number (0..n-1; EDGE keys its output rings on it) and signals its own
jobs' completion (the job mailbox is thread-local). The chain moves on
only when every job of the list is done, as if a SYNC followed it. The
port sets 4.

Measured, identical headless New Game runs, warm shader cache,
t = 100-240 s (another session was compiling during both):
  serial    20.0 fps, p50 45.0 ms, p95 85.2, p99 153.7, 39.8% > 50 ms
  4 threads 25.9 fps, p50 33.9 ms, p95 54.2, p99  83.6,  8.0% > 50 ms
Snapshots of the walk show Afro skinned as in the serial run; no
unresolved calls. The one frame over 250 ms in the parallel run is
the 1.1 s load at 112.9 s; the serial run had five, four in play.

889f694f226745649077378bbbdadf53e2df21f4.message:
fix(gcm): 2D blit methods no longer clobber the 3D alpha-test registers

Grass and foliage cards still drew as dark rectangles after cfe7b35 (user
screenshot, village courtyard). A per-draw dump of the alpha registers
showed why: in the colour pass 0x0304/0x0308/0x030C read 8|4|C, 0x10004,
0x10004 -- alpha test off, a function that is no enum -- while the shadow
pass had the title's 1, GREATER, 0x7F. GCM_VAL_WATCH=10004 named the
writer: subchannel 5, methods 0x0308 and 0x030C. Those are the title's
NV3089 scaled-image blits (operation, clip point, clip size). The draw
engine strips the subchannel from every word it is handed, so they landed
in the NV4097 register file; the title sets its alpha test once and never
again, so every cut-out card after the first blit lost it.

Toolkit (patch): GCM_ENGINE_3D_SUBCH=1 mirrors into the draw engine only
the words the walker itself routes as 3D (subchannel 0, 1 unless
GCM_SUBCH1_2D, and the 0xE000+ driver methods). Off by default there,
since a title may bind NV4097 on another subchannel; the port sets it.

Measured, headless New Game run into the village: all 83 dumped draws
read alpha func 0x204 ref 0x7F with the enable the title set (was
garbage on 966 of 1178), no unresolved calls.

The patch also carries opt-in diagnostics added on the way: the alpha
and antialias registers on each RSX_ENGINE_PASS_DUMP_DRAWS line,
SPU_INTERP_DUMP=<dir>, AUDIO_CHRMS=1, AUDIO_RAW8=<file>, and an optional
PS3_AUDIO_DOWNMIX=itu stereo fold-down (default unchanged).

8b2a710c041e4dde56bef4b7644980b843a168d6.message:
fix(spurs): the skinning job chain runs after New Game

New Game froze on a black screen: the render thread waited for a
job-done event from the NTG SPU skinning chain, and nothing walked it.
Four causes, each behind a switch (the first three set in afro_defaults):

- The job binaries were never lifted: they are raw code+data blobs, not
  SPU ELFs, and the walker logged "dispatch MISS". tools/lift_jobs.sh
  lifts the ones a run dumps with SPU_DUMP_MISS=$PWD/cache/jobs (the
  17,552-byte skinning job 8B2B4776E3A079D8 and the 112-byte job beside
  it, 37DA975A7C220171) and registers them by fingerprint.
- SPURS_JG_WAIT_FOREVER=1: the chain is kicked at boot and sits on its
  guard until a game starts, minutes later; the 20 s give-up ended it.
  The walker now waits on a closed guard, keeps polling between jobs and
  waits on a transient END while the PPU appends the next frame's work,
  for as long as the chain runs.
- SPURS_JC_EVENT_FROM_JOB=1: the ring's last job sends the one event per
  lap the render thread waits for, on a queue of depth 1; a synthetic
  event per job filled it and the real one was dropped (rc=-1). Only
  jobs that write SPU_WrOutIntrMbox send-event post now.
- SPURS_JOB_CTX_V1=1: the skinning job reads numIoBuffer/numCacheBuffer
  at ctx+0x68/0x6A and the DMA tag at ctx+0x74 (an older context layout).
  Unset, it halted on its own guard every run, and a run whose garbage
  passed the guard PUT its whole local store to EA 0, over the PPU text
  and its switch tables from 0x10000. The context is 0x80 bytes now.

Also: an MFC PUT into the ELF's read-only segment (text + rodata) is
dropped, as it faults on hardware (ppu_loader records the segment,
spu_dma.h checks it).

New Game now reaches the 3D loading screen.

9e3be8b8c8fb795c954a06478c52e3b1c7c29acc.message:
fix(gcm): the title paces itself at 30 fps (prepare-flip, flip on vblank)

Gameplay ran about 1.5x real speed: ~45-48 frames a second where the
console and RPCS3 run 30. The title paces itself with libgcm's
prepare/flip-immediate scheme. Its render thread calls
cellGcmSetPrepareFlip and folds the RETURNED buffer id into a frame-ready
label (0x41) after the frame; its vblank handler flips that buffer with
cellGcmSetFlipImmediate on every 2nd vblank (interval word = 2), and its
flip handler then frees the per-buffer label (0x42/0x43) the RSX ACQUIREs
before it goes on.

The HLE broke every link of that: SetPrepareFlip completed the flip and
ran the flip handler at call time and returned 0 (so the ready label
always named buffer 0, the one on screen, and the vblank handler never
flipped); GetDisplayBufferByFlipIndex returned a host pointer instead of
the buffer id the flip handler indexes its labels with; the flip handler
ran inside SetFlipImmediate, before the vblank handler had recorded what
it flipped, so it freed the previous buffer's label; and ACQUIRE did not
block, so nothing held the render loop.

Toolkit (patch): GCM_PREPAREFLIP_FIFO=2 makes a prepare return the buffer
id without flipping and GetDisplayBufferByFlipIndex return the id (=1
queues the flip in the FIFO instead, kept as an option). Port defaults:
GCM_PREPAREFLIP_FIFO=2, GCM_FLIPCB_ONTICK=1 (handler at completion),
GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1 with a 250 ms bound. Unset/0 gives the old behaviour.

Measured, headless New Game runs to the combat tutorial: prepares 29.5-
30.1 a second over 260 s (was 45-48 in gameplay), ~230 blocking acquires
per 5 s and none timed out, no unresolved calls, scene renders as before.
The cellAudio mix rate was checked too: 187.5 blocks/s before and after,
so the odd in-game sound is expected to come from the speed-up; not yet
confirmed by ear.

aa2b0487c30ef96874eb5c5dae8e3854f5733474.message:
fix(fs): the Bink movies open (lv2 read/lseek on a cellFs descriptor)

The title opens each movie with cellFsOpen and hands the descriptor to
Bink (BINKFILEHANDLE), which seeks and reads it with the raw lv2 syscalls
818/802. Those keep their own descriptor table in sys_fs.c and knew
nothing of a cellFs fd, so every movie failed to open and the boot sat
on black frames after bng.bik.

Toolkit (patches/ps3recomp-ae92407b-afro.patch): sys_fs read, lseek and
fstat fall back to the cellFs table (ppu_fs_file_for_fd, weak, so the
runtime still links without ppu_fs.cpp). The fs-open trace also dumps the
guest stack, not only the host one.

Since then the boot plays bng.bik, two_headbands.bik and afro_credit.bik
and reaches the main menu over background_movie.bik.

c791826a1432eedb6dad25c6f7607bf06087cdad.message:
feat(tools): cut the skinning-chain jobs out of the EBOOT at rebuild time

not SPU ELFs, so a first build needed a run into New Game with
SPU_DUMP_MISS before tools/lift_jobs.sh had anything to lift.

tools/extract_jobs.py takes them from the decrypted EBOOT at their file
offsets (0x83C080 and 0x840580) and checks each slice's SHA-256 and the
toolkit fingerprint before writing anything; another executable revision
is refused, never guessed. lift_jobs.sh runs it first, and rebuild.sh spu
now lifts the jobs after the embedded SPU images. Checked byte for byte
against the runtime dumps. No game bytes are in the script, only offsets,

c81e249d2280feeafd40920e4018401fa8d4682c.message:
feat(rsx): supersampling, a Lanczos reduction of a picture larger than the window

With PS3_RES_SCALE above the window's size the picture reached the
drawable through the present's bilinear sample, which reads four source
pixels per output pixel: at 2x and more most of the extra pixels were
dropped and edges still shimmered. The Resistance port fixed this in its
window host today (its d1d93cc, acafe40, b87124d); here the window is the
backend's own, so the step goes into the engine's present.

eng_blit_to_display now reduces such a picture to its place in the window
with MPSImageLanczosScale before the present pass, which is then 1:1. The
filter clamps at the picture's edge (MPS's default reads black there and
darkens the outer row and column). The present's sharpening runs after the
reduction, on output pixels, which is the order the third of those commits
moved Resistance to. MetalPerformanceShaders is opened at run time, as
MetalFX is; if it is missing the old sample goes on, with one log line.

PS3_DOWNSCALE=0 turns it off. The in-game menu's internal resolution list
gains 5K (4x), which PS3_RES_SCALE already accepted.

Measured: test_metal_downscale.m (new): a one-pixel checkerboard three
times the drawable comes out between 110 and 145 on every pixel, white
stays >= 253 to the edge, a picture that fits is untouched, and with
PS3_DOWNSCALE=0 the same checkerboard comes out black and white. In a
1280x720 window (2560x1440 pixels) at 3x and 4x the log shows 3840x2160
and 5120x2880 reduced to 2560x1440 and the intro movie holds 59 fps (GPU
wait 4.1 ms at 4x). Not looked at in gameplay, where the 3D is what gains.

translation cache (rsx_shader_msl.cpp) is PS3RECOMP_MSL_CACHE. So every
run translated each guest shader again (glslang + spirv-cross, most of
a first use's cost) and cache/msl held four files from an old build.
run.sh now sets PS3RECOMP_MSL_CACHE=cache/msl; a file from another
translator build is a miss, never served.

tools/frametimes.py prints frame-time percentiles from a PS3_FTRACE
timeline: intervals between the title's flip requests (--kind flip) or
the host's presents (--kind present), with mean, p50/p95/p99/max and
the share over 1.5x and 2x a 30 fps frame.

Measured, two identical headless New Game runs, t = 100-240 s (loading,
the opening and the first walk), same cache dir: the cold run wrote 57
translations, the warm one none; worst frame 481 -> 261 ms, p50
36.9 -> 34.0 ms. The steady-state p95/p99 (67-71 / 109-122 ms) is not
the translator: the slow frames spend ~41 ms draining the FIFO against
~17 ms in a 30 fps frame (next on the roadmap).

cfe7b35d2aa9f20b8655f47958a5145a26bff436.message:
fix(rsx): alpha-to-coverage cuts out grass and foliage cards

Grass tufts and plant cards drew as dark rectangles (user screenshot: two
dark panels in a village corner, grass blades faintly visible inside).
The NTG renderer cuts those cards out with alpha-to-coverage: the scene
target is 2x antialiased (2560x720) and the title sets
SET_ANTI_ALIASING_CONTROL (0x1D7C) = 0xFFFF0011 -- MSAA on, alpha to
coverage on -- with alpha test off and a fragment program without KIL.
The draw engine never read 0x1D7C, so every texel of the card was drawn.

There is no multisampled target in the engine, so coverage collapses to
an alpha test at one half (the samples a 2x target would keep): when bit
0 and bit 4 are set and the title's own alpha test is off, the render
state gets alpha test GEQUAL 0.5 (ref encoded for the target's colour
format), which the pipeline key already carries. PS3RECOMP_ENG_A2C=0
ignores the register again.

Measured, headless New Game run: the register value is logged once;
grass tufts in the rocky cutscene at 185 s render as blades, no
rectangles. Found from a draw dump: the only opaque draw binding a
cut-out texture (DXT1 1024x256, 51% transparent texels) had no discard.

1448302505.readme_excerpt:
# Afro Samurai — static recompilation for PC (macOS) 🌐 **English** · [Português (BR)](README.pt-BR.md) A native port of **Afro Samurai** (PS3, disc `BLUS30264`, v01.00) to **macOS/arm64**, built with static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C/C++ and compiled into a native executable, with graphics on Metal. It is not an emulator. **It reaches gameplay, and the game renders correctly.** From the boot through the logo movies, the main menu and New Game (or Continue), the first level plays in a window with a controller: Afro, Ninja Ninja and the village are drawn textured and lit, and the opening cutscene and the combat tutorial run. It has been played in a window without a crash and runs at 30 frames a second like the PS3, and the in-game audio now sounds right. See [Status](#status). | | | | --- | --- | | [](docs/screenshots/03-gameplay-village.png)
Gameplay: Afro in the village | [](docs/screenshots/04-ninja-ninja.png)
Ninja Ninja | | [](docs/screenshots/01-main-menu.png)
The main menu | [](docs/screenshots/02-loading.png)
New Game: the loading screen | The code is at [github.com/erikomis/afro-samurai-recomp](https://github.com/erikomis/afro-samurai-recomp); problems and reports go to its [issues](https://github.com/erikomis/afro-samurai-recomp/issues). Built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), with the layout and the tools of the author's other ports ([inFAMOUS 2](https://github.com/erikomis/infamous2-recomp), [Resistance: Fall of Man](https://github.com/erikomis/resistance-recomp), [Resistance 2](https://github.com/erikomis/resistance2-recomp)). > [!WARNING] > **Early work in progress.** The first level is playable, but only its > start has been played, and the grass and foliage textures still await a > final visual check. There are no releases: you build the game yourself from your own > disc. Apple-silicon macOS only. What is missing is in > [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). > **This repository contains no game data, no firmware, no Sony keys and > nothing translated from them.** Everyone generates all of that locally from > their own legitimate copy. A fan project, not affiliated with Bandai Namco > Entertainment, Sony Interactive Entertainment or GONZO. ## Status As of 2026-11-07: boot → heaps and static constructors → SPURS and the game's threads → the save is loaded → audio up → the logo and credit movies (`bng.bik`, `two_headbands.bik`, `afro_credit.bik`) → the main menu over `background_movie.bik` → New Game or Continue → the 3D loading screen → the opening cutscene and the combat tutorial, rendered correctly, controlled with a pad (Xbox Series X and DualSense through SDL). RPCS3 running the same disc was the reference for what the scene should look like. Since then (2026-11-11), the audio and the textures: - **In-game audio (slow, smeared, unintelligible in windowed play), fixed.** A sample of the session showed the FMOD mixer SPU thread spending 84% of its time in the SPU interpreter: the mixer DMAs each of the 18 codec and DSP plugins (SPU images 2-19) from the EBOOT into a different local-store address than the one they were lifted at, so every call missed the lifted code and was interpreted, too slow for the mixer's 5.3 ms blocks. `tools/lift_fmod_plugins.sh` (run by `rebuild.sh spu`) now lifts them as relocatable overlays; the interpreter share dropped from 979 of 1162 mixer-thread samples to none, with the same output level. Confirmed by ear. `SPU_RELOC_OFF=1` goes back to the interpreter (for comparison). - **Alpha-to-coverage (grass and foliage cards drawn as dark rectangles).** The title cuts those cards out with alpha-to-coverage (`SET_ANTI_ALIASING_CONTROL`, `0x1D7C`), which the draw engine ignored. With no multisampled target it is now emulated as an alpha test at 0.5 (`PS3RECOMP_ENG_A2C=0` ignores the register again). - **2D blits wiping the 3D alpha-test state.** The title's NV3089 scaled-image blits (subchannel 5) landed in the 3D register file because the draw engine stripped the subchannel, so every cut-out card after the first blit lost its alpha test. Only 3D subchannels now reach the engine (`GCM_ENGINE_3D_SUBCH=1`, set by the port): all 83 dumped draws in the village read the title's alpha test (it was garbage on 966 of 1178). Later the same day, speed and housekeeping: - **Frame rate in play: 26.1 -> 28.9 fps.** Over the same 60 s of a headless walk in the village, p95 went from 64 to 42 ms, p99 from 83 to 57 ms, and frames over 50 ms from 12.4% to 2.0%. The vertex-skinning JOBLIST ran its jobs one after another on one host thread, 94% busy, and the render thread waited on it every frame; it now runs on four threads, as the SPURS job manager spreads a list over the SPUs (`SPURS_JC_JOBLIST_PAR=4`, set by the port). The FIFO drain also takes less CPU per draw (17.8 -> 14.3 ms a frame): a direct map for the vertex dedupe, a loop of its own for packed `CMP32` normals, and a four-lane texture hash. - **Shader translations kept across runs.** `run.sh` exported a variable nothing reads, so every run translated each shader again; it now sets `PS3RECOMP_MSL_CACHE=cache/msl` (worst frame in the first minutes of play 481 -> 261 ms). - **Quitting.** Closing the window used to leave the game running with no window; it, Ctrl+C and SIGTERM now quit the way Cmd+Q and the console's Quit Game do (REQUEST_EXITGAME, then exit 0 after `PS3_QUIT_GRACE_MS`, never while a save is being written). - **Long runs.** Ten minutes headless: memory steady at ~600 MB from the fourth minute on, no "unresolved indirect call". The two fixes that took the game from exploded geometry to a correct scene (2026-11-07): - **JOBLIST in the SPURS job chains.** The renderer laps its skinning chain every frame as [JOB palette] → [JOBLIST of 5 vertex-skinning jobs] → [JOB lap notify]. The HLE chain walker treated JOBLIST as a no-op, so the skinning jobs never ran and about 100 colour draws a frame read another writer's leftovers from the RSX-visible ring: giant stretched triangles. The walker now runs a JOBLIST's jobs (`SPURS_JC_JOBLIST=0` skips it). - **One job-context pointer per input.** Those skinning jobs take two DMA inputs, and the older job context they read lists one LS pointer per input and then per cache buffer; input 1 pointed at the cache, so the characters were skinned from the wrong data (shards in cutscenes). Earlier the same day, the vertex programs' start slot: branch targets in RSX vertex microcode are absolute, and decompiling every program as if it started at slot 0 left branching programs looping 16,384 times per vertex (0.4–3 s of GPU per frame). What it took, with the cause of each: - **Memory pools:** the game creates and destroys thousands of small `sys_mempool`s (about 3,800 in two minutes; 16-, 32- and 64-byte classes). `sysPrxForUser` now implements `try_allocate` / `allocate` / `free` / `destroy`, writes the counts big-endian, and hands out generation-tagged handles so a destroyed pool's handle is never reused by mistake (`SYS_MEMPOOL_LOG=1` traces it). - **The memory mapper:** the game places its own 1 MB heap pages with `sys_mmapper_map_memory` next to those 256 KB pools. The untracked cursor overlapped the two (a block array was `memset` over live list nodes), then ran out of address space and the game called `abort()`. The mapper now keeps a page-owner map with real map / unmap / free and a next-fit search per reservation (`PS3_MMAPPER_TRACK=1`, on by default). - **Six ascending reservations:** the game reserves 512 MB plus 5 × 256 MB of address space, and routes `free()` by which reservation range a pointer falls in, so they must come back in ascending order. Two came back `ENOMEM`. With `PS3_MAPPER_WIDE=1` (on by default) they ascend and may enclose the runtime's own windows, which the tracked mapper never hands out. - **FMOD's SPU plugins:** the FMOD Ex mixer task loads its DSP and codec plugins as overlays and branches into them (LS `0x25A18`). With no lifted code there the job ended (they are lifted now, see the audio fix above), and FMOD's event thread then waited for good on the mixer's event flag while holding the lwmutex the main thread needed. `SPU_INTERP_UNLIFTED` (on by default) interprets what has no lifted body, as the Deadpool port does. - **First save:** with no save yet, the game's stat callback answers `ERR_NODATA`; firmware turns that into `ERROR_CBRESULT`, which is how the game learns to create one. The toolkit answered `ERROR_NODATA`, and the game said its save data "appears to be damaged" and stopped. `SAVEDATA_CBRESULT_STRICT=1` (on by default) answers as firmware does; the game now writes and reads back `AFRO_0.SAV`. - **`cellKbRead`:** the game polls the keyboard every frame through `cellKbRead` (NID `0xFF0A21B7`, the SDK's name for `cellKbGetData`). It was unresolved, the generic path answered `CELL_OK` without writing anything, and the game read whatever the stack held as key events. - **SPURS lock-free queues:** `_cellSpursLFQueuePushBody` is implemented on the canonical 128-byte `CellSyncLFQueue` line the SPU consumer reads, and a task that parks in `WAIT_SIGNAL` while its queue already holds entries resumes instead of sleeping (both ported from the Resistance 2 tree; `SPURS_LFQ_NOWAKE=1` turns the second off). - **The movies (black screen at boot):** the game opens each movie with `cellFsOpen` and hands the descriptor to Bink, which seeks and reads it with the raw lv2 syscalls (818/802). Those keep their own descriptor table and knew nothing of a `cellFs` one, so every movie failed to open and the boot sat on black frames after `bng.bik`. lv2 read, lseek and fstat now fall back to the `cellFs` table. - **The skinning job chain (frozen after New Game):** the render thread waits for an event from the NTG SPU skinning chain, and nothing walked it. The job binaries are raw blobs, not SPU ELFs, so they were never lifted ("dispatch MISS"); `tools/lift_jobs.sh` lifts them. The chain is kicked at boot and sits on its guard until a game starts, and the walker's 20 s give-up ended it (`SPURS_JG_WAIT_FOREVER=1`). The ring's last job sends the one event per lap the render thread waits for, on a queue of depth 1, and a synthetic event per job filled it first (`SPURS_JC_EVENT_FROM_JOB=1`). And the job reads its buffer counts and DMA tag past the 48-byte job context (an older layout); unset, it halted on its own guard, or PUT its whole local store over the game's code at `0x10000` (`SPURS_JOB_CTX_V1=1`). A DMA PUT into the executable's read-only segment is now dropped, as it faults on hardware. - **Jump tables (New Game spinning on a NULL):** the lifter resolves a `switch` only over the cases inside the function it lifted, and cases past where it cut a large function went through the indirect-call fallback, which needs a lifted function at the case address. The engine's message dispatcher (`func_001EA288`, 4,191 cases) lost case `0x1F079C` that way. `tools/augment_functions.py` splits the function list at every case target of the tables in `tools/jumptables.txt` before lifting. Known issues, being worked on: - **The grass in the courtyard is not yet confirmed by eye.** The two texture fixes above were checked in headless runs (alpha registers read right on all 83 dumped draws; grass renders as blades in the cutscene), but the final look at the courtyard grass in a windowed session is pending. Other broken textures may remain and have not been reported yet: please open an [issue](https://github.com/erikomis/afro-samurai-recomp/issues) with a screenshot. - **Streamed textures** may be stale: the texture cache hashes the full texture only every 8 frames, which is suspected (not confirmed) for textures that stream in; `PS3RECOMP_ENG_TEXHASH_FULL=1` tests it. - **Only the start of the first level has been played**; the rest of the game is untested. - **Frame pacing** is not yet even: 2% of frames in play still take over 50 ms (the FIFO drain and the skinning jobs are the next costs). - **Keyboard and mouse** have not been tested; a controller works. - One headless run stalled once while loading the level (after `LoadRenderThreadProc` exited); not reproduced since, not investigated. ## How it works 1. **Decrypt** your disc's `EBOOT.BIN` (a disc SELF, `key_rev 0x0001`, type APP) into `game/EBOOT.elf` with `tools/decrypt_self.py` and your own key file. RPCS3 is not needed. 2. **Analyse and lift** it with the toolkit's `ppu_loader.py` and `ppu_lifter.py`: 12,869 functions in the OPD table, 32,951 emitted by the lifter, as C++ in `recompiled/BLUS30264/` (16 translation units). Before lifting, `tools/augment_functions.py` adds the case targets of the jump tables in `tools/jumptables.txt` to the function list. 3. **SPU code:** the 20 SPU ELFs embedded in the EBOOT are cut out by the toolkit's `extract_spu_images.py` and lifted by `tools/lift_spu.sh` into `port/spu/`: EDGE ZLIB inflate (`spu_0000`), the FMOD Ex SPURS mixer (`spu_0001`, lifted with every call's return as an entry, so the plugins return into lifted code) and 18 FMOD codec and DSP plugins (`spu_0002`–`spu_0019`). The SPURS job binaries of the skinning chain are not ELFs: `tools/extract_jobs.py` extracts them from the EBOOT and `tools/lift_jobs.sh` lifts them (the 17,552-byte skinning job `8B2B4776E3A079D8` and the 112-byte job beside it, `37DA975A7C220171`). 4. **Build** with CMake/Ninja against the toolkit: the runtime (LV2 syscalls, HLE firmware libraries, SPURS, the Metal RSX backend) plus the lifted code, into `build/BLUS30264/AfroSamuraiRecomp`. The game is Namco Bandai's own **NTG** engine (paths `nhi/ntg/...`), not Unreal Engine 3: scripts and configuration in `.ini` and `.ntg` files inside `ps3.psarc` (2.7 GB, all of the game's content), Bink movies, FMOD Ex audio, NavPower for AI navigation and EDGE 1.2.3.0. It has no PRX of its own and imports 156 firmware functions from 12 libraries; it saves through `cellSaveData` and keeps a cache in `/dev_hdd0/game/ntg_cache` and `/dev_hdd1`. The full inventory is in [`docs/game-manifest.md`](docs/game-manifest.md). The toolkit is upstream ps3recomp **v0.19.0** (`ae92407b`) plus this port's changes (the memory pools, the tracked mapper, the first-save answer, `cellKbRead`, the SPURS lock-free queue), which are generic and env-gated, kept as one patch: [`patches/ps3recomp-ae92407b-afro.patch`](patches/). `tools/setup_toolkit.sh` clones upstream, checks out `ae92407b` and applies it next to this repository (`../ps3recomp-afro`); `tools/export_toolkit_patch.sh` writes a changed checkout back into the patch. ## Building from source ### What you need - An Apple-silicon Mac (macOS with Metal). Each lifted chunk is tens of MB of C++ and clang takes 3–4 GB on one; `tools/build.sh` keeps the build to two compiles at a time and watches memory and disk. - Your own **Afro Samurai disc, `BLUS30264`**, dumped to an ISO. Put it (or a link to its folder) at `game_iso/`; it is mounted read-only and never written to. - Xcode Command Line Tools and Homebrew: ```sh brew install cmake ninja sdl2 glslang spirv-cross spirv-tools ffmpeg python@3.12 ``` ### Setting up ```sh git clone https://github.com/erikomis/afro-samurai-recomp.git cd afro-samurai-recomp tools/setup.sh # toolkit, Python venv, keys; no build tools/setup.sh --check # only validate ``` `tools/setup.sh` puts the ps3recomp toolkit at `../ps3recomp-afro` (`PS3RECOMP_DIR` changes it) with `tools/setup_toolkit.sh`, makes this repository's Python venv (`.venv`, from `python3.12`; `PYBIN` picks another) with the toolkit's `requirements.txt`, and writes the disc SELF key file with `tools/fetc

Entries are credited to the image that owns the resident code region, so

remaining interpreted SPU time comes from four of them (0xA68 in the

06aa9375568380b75c2a35b9bd91959aa321310b.message:
sceNp: tickets, account region and network time answer OFFLINE

sceNpManagerRequestTicket2, GetTicket, GetTicketParam,
GetAccountRegion and GetNetworkTime were not implemented, so their
imports answered CELL_OK with nothing written. A title that asked for a
ticket waited for a GOT_TICKET manager event that never came, and one
that read the region or the time used whatever was in its buffer.

Implement them with RPCS3's argument checks and offline answers: without
a psnr server the NP manager is OFFLINE and so are these
(SCE_NP_ERROR_OFFLINE), and there is never a ticket, so GetTicket
reports a size of 0 and GetTicketParam INVALID_STATE. Signed in to a
psnr server, which issues no tickets, a request is answered at once with
a GOT_TICKET event carrying an error instead of a ticket size; the
region is the fake account's (US, English) and the network time is the
host clock as a CellRtcTick.

.github/workflows: pin the five third-party actions to commit SHAs

release.yml fires on `push: tags: ['v*']` with `permissions: contents:
write`, so every action it invokes runs holding a token that can write to
this repo and attach release assets. Referenced by floating major tag, any
of those five actions could be retargeted upstream -- a tag is mutable, and
whoever controls it controls what executes inside that job. Pinning to a
commit SHA makes the referenced code immutable.

Each SHA is the commit the action's current major tag points at, so this
changes no behaviour: the same code runs, it just can no longer be swapped
out from under us. The readable version stays in a trailing comment because
a bare SHA tells a later reader nothing about how stale the pin is.

Only `uses:` lines and their comments change -- 13 references across all
five workflows, no other workflow edits.

(cherry picked from commit 903d023f4a88ace083b0d9843fd3cf71a40f6572)

0e8b9ef2ca28fae79e8e24d2dede074581350fb7.message:
rsx engine: a depth snapshot is the region the texture names

The engine's host depth target is at least canvas-sized
(eng_zdepth_get), but a depth texture covers only the top-left
width x height of it. eng_zdepth_snapshot resolved the whole target and
the Metal resolve sampled it with normalized coordinates, so a 128x160
shadow map in the corner of a 1280x720 target was stretched over the
whole canvas and the lookups landed outside the map.

eng_zdepth_snapshot takes the texture's size and asks the backend for
that region (clamped to the target); a cached snapshot is reused only at
the same size. The Metal resolve reads the depth 1:1 (src.read at the
fragment's pixel) instead of sampling it, so a smaller snapshot is the
top-left region. The Vulkan backend's copy already works this way.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) samples small shadow maps from
canvas-sized zetas. In the port, this together with #424 and the port's
other depth-texture changes removes the dark rectangles on the ground
under shadows; the effect was not isolated per change.

Tests: test_color_feedback_engine (a 128x160 texture over a 256x256 zeta
asks for a 128x160 snapshot), test_metal_depth_readback (a 2x2 snapshot
holds the top-left texels 1:1).

118b6281a756697391f178e523a409e0b1f60ce1.message:
cellGcmSys: GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS sets how long a FIFO park may stand

When the drain stops on a self-jump park and `put` has moved, it waits
GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS (50 ms) for the title to patch the park and then follows
`put`. That suits a title that leaves a park standing when it switches
segments. It does not suit one that appends commands right after the
park, moves `put` there and patches the park last: if the patch comes
after the grace, the drain skips the commands in between.

God of War HD does the latter, and while it loads its menu the two stores
have been more than 50 ms apart: the drain jumped from 0x57C40 to put
0x5AA2C, dropped ~11 KB of commands with a fence among them, and the boot
stopped (once in about 45 runs). The RSX itself would wait.

GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS=<ms> now sets the grace; the default is unchanged.

147e59a79e63cefcf0c2f53fc7314d83f54167e2.message:
rsx_d3d12: pass the FP depth-export bits of SHADER_CONTROL

Draws recorded only the 32-bit-exports bit of SET_SHADER_CONTROL, so a
fragment program that replaces the fragment depth (bits 1-3) was
translated without SV_Depth. God of War HD's resolve pass writes the
scene depth it reads from the 2x-AA depth surface into the resolved
one this way; without it the pass wrote the quad's own depth (0), and
every depth-tested pass after it failed everywhere: the stencil
shadows, the fog, rain, the waterfall mist and the glows.

The draw now records the export bits (32-bit exports and depth export)
as fp_ctrl, part of the pipeline key, and hands them to the
decompiler, which already emits SV_Depth from r1.z.

1530be7cfd1295f9db57e380a3dc2314770a82c1.message:
ppu_lifter: per-function copy of the memory model; PPU_FAST_FP

A guest store goes through vm_base + ea, a byte pointer the compiler
cannot tell apart from the memory-model globals, so the inline load and
store paths reloaded vm_base, ppu_vm_size, ppu_hle_inject_base and the
two enable flags after every store. Each lifted function now copies them
into a local at entry (PPU_MM_SNAP) and its accesses use the copy. They
are all set before guest code runs. The SPU reservation bitmap and the
store watches can change while a function runs, so those are still read
from the globals. Code outside lifted functions keeps vm_read*_inl and
vm_write*_inl, which now take a fresh copy per access.

PPU_FAST_FP, off unless the build defines it, drops the NaN checks in
ppu_fp_bin and ppu_fmadd_core. The host's NaN differs from the PPC one
only in its sign and in which of two NaN operands propagates.

God of War HD, func_001BEFA4, built with FMA3: 6,195 instructions before,
5,855 with the copy, 4,553 with PPU_FAST_FP as well (branches 1,342,
1,063, 583).

test_ppu_lift.py: the conformance driver defines PPU_NO_INLINE_LOADS. Its
vm_read*/vm_write* are its own functions, and its statements do not run
inside a lifted function.

159a47de817b1ef3206f4df7ddab80ceb0312801.message:
ps3_indirect_call: one thread-local lookup a call, not two

On macOS every access to a __thread variable is a call to tlv_get_addr, and
the fast path made two a call: the recursion depth before it and the
trampoline after it. Unreal's package loader is virtual calls through and
through, and in a load tlv_get_addr was up to a fifth of the game thread's
samples (5-20%, in-process sampler). Both variables are this file's
thread-locals, so they are one per-thread block at a fixed distance; the
fast path looks up the trampoline's address once and reaches the depth by
that distance (worked out at the first call). Same behaviour; the depth
test (tools/test_ppu_dispatch_depth.py) passes.

Measured on the Mac, Drakengard 3 start-up to the title, interleaved runs:
3.23 -> 3.14 s median (5 runs each). Where a thread-local is a load off a
register (Windows, Linux) it saves an instruction or two.

170be32ac21c17795a97d244d8fa559ed47e21f0.message:
ftrace: a span for each HLE import call

PS3_FTRACE recorded syscalls and timer sleeps but not HLE imports, so a
guest thread blocked or busy inside an import (a file read, a SPURS
wait, a lock taken hundreds of thousands of times) showed up nowhere.
ps3_hle_call's exit guard now closes a PS3_FT_HLE span (who = thread,
a = NID, b = guest lr) for calls at least PS3_FTRACE_MIN_US long. With
the trace off it costs one load per call.

This is what found God of War HD's 360 ms frame: 320,355 lwmutex
lock/unlock pairs in it (PS3_FTRACE_MIN_US=0), against 71 in a normal
frame.

180e324be8066b0566143dcfb403bdbbb1403a0b.message:
Draw engine: the guest pipeline list, and the caches rebuilt from it

A backend's caches hold what the decompilers made of a title's programs --
the D3D12 bytecode cache and its pipeline-state list -- so a change to a
decompiler leaves them stale, and only playing everything again refilled
them (the v0.17 merge left a release's cache matching 584 of 1,494
programs). The engine now also keeps what the title gave.

Every pipeline the engine translates is written once, by its key, as a line
of <dir>/guest_pipelines.txt: the two programs by hash (their bytes once each
in <dir>/guest_programs.bin), every input the decompilers take (shader
control, cube, volume, vertex-texture, shadow-compare, texel-addressed and
texel-op units), the vertex layout, the target format and count, the render
state field by field by name, and the hashes of the HLSL made of it then.
<dir> is PS3RECOMP_GUEST_DIR, else PS3RECOMP_DXBC_CACHE; PS3RECOMP_GUEST_LIST=0
records nothing.

RSX_GUEST_REBUILD=1 runs the list through the decompilers and the backend's
pipeline_create as they are now, on the build workers, when the engine
starts, and exits: the bytecode and the pipeline states are made again
without playing, and <dir>/guest_remap.txt lists each pipeline whose HLSL
changed (old and new hashes). RPCS3 keeps its shader cache the same way.

Drakengard 3, one level: 328 pipelines recorded (260 KB of lines, 575 KB of
programs); rebuilt into an empty cache in 11 s including the game's start,
328 built, the same 344 bytecode files byte for byte as play made, every
rebuilt pipeline state one that play had built.

1891b8fe718534bef9d143c7b665beb762adbc07.message:
gcm: count the drain's own ring recycle as the JUMP to begin

Once a title has been seen to overrun its ring, the drain recycles the
ring itself when current nears end. A title whose callback also
recycles (cellGcm_fifo_recycle) can be in that callback at the same
moment: it writes its JUMP and put, and only then marks itself waiting,
so a pass that read the mark clear still teleports get to begin. The
callback then waits for a backward JUMP that never comes, because get
is already at begin == put, and gives up after 2 s of no progress.

God of War HD stopped for 2-4 s this way at random points in about
half of the gameplay runs. Counting the teleport as the backward JUMP
ends the callback's wait at once.

1be9e80d533ae0ff253fa169f5d2f5f783a1364d.message:
rsx_shader_msl: compile a vertex program's position invariant

Titles draw the same geometry twice with two different vertex programs,
the second pass testing EQUAL against the depth the first one wrote. The
RSX runs the position arithmetic instruction by instruction, so both
programs land on the same depth. The Metal compiler optimises each
program on its own (it may fuse a multiply and an add into one FMA in one
of them and not in the other), the two depths can then differ in the last
bit, and the EQUAL pass leaves holes.

Resistance: Fall of Man's foliage writes depth through an alpha-tested
program, then colour through one that also lights it, with
SET_DEPTH_FUNC EQUAL.

The translator now marks a vertex program's position [[position,
invariant]], and the Metal backend compiles guest programs with
MTLCompileOptions.preserveInvariance (macOS 11 and later), so programs
that compute the position the same way get the same bits.
PS3RECOMP_MSL_INVARIANT=0 leaves the position as it was.

test_shader_msl checks the vertex program's MSL for
"[[position, invariant]]" (and for "[[position" under
PS3RECOMP_MSL_INVARIANT=0).

1c7c1d914374d59451f5b73421119af501606cfb.message:
rsx engine: a scissored CLEAR_SURFACE clears only the scissor

RSX clears what the surface clip and the scissor let through. The engine
cleared every colour and depth target whole, whatever the scissor said.

Resistance: Fall of Man's co-op split screen renders both views into one
2x1 antialiased 1280x720 scene target: the scissor on the left half, a
colour and depth clear and player 1's view, then the scissor on the right
half, a clear and player 2's view. The second clear wiped player 1's view,
and the left half of the screen was black under the HUD.

sink_clear now asks eng_clear_rect what the clear may write: the clip
from the origin, then the scissor (eng_scissor_rect, the draw path's
scissor code moved into a function). Only a scissor narrower than the
clip makes a clear partial; a clip smaller than the target alone stays a
whole clear, as before. A partial clear goes to two new optional backend
hooks, clear_color_rect and clear_depth_stencil_rect. A backend without
them, or PS3RECOMP_ENG_RECT_CLEAR=0, clears whole as before. A depth clear
that covers everything the zeta was ever bound with (ext_w/ext_h) stays
whole, and a partial depth clear keeps had_write.

The Metal backend records a rectangle clear as a clear record with the
rectangle in its scissor and encodes it as a pass of its own: the
attachment is loaded and a full-target triangle under that scissor writes
the colour, or the depth and stencil with the test always passing. Such a
record is never folded into a pass's load action.

New test_clear_rect in test_rsx_draw_engine (the co-op frame, whole and
empty scissors, a zeta only bound at a small clip, a backend without the
hooks), and test_metal_rect_clears.m (tools/test_metal_rect_clears.py) on
the GPU: a rectangle clear of the right half keeps the left half, for
colour, depth and stencil, and a whole clear after one covers the target.

1f23584802ab365a38eb51e5f103e786dda68cdf.message:
Metal: HDR (EDR) present and the highlight plane, as the D3D12 engine's

RSX_HDR=1 on a screen with EDR headroom puts the window's layer in EDR:
RGBA16Float, extended linear sRGB, wantsExtendedDynamicRangeContent. 1.0 is
the system's SDR white; the headroom (maximumExtendedDynamicRangeColorComponent
Value, which follows the brightness) is read on the main thread every half
second and after a settings change, and the layer is switched on the render
thread before it takes a drawable. Off -- or on a screen without headroom --
nothing changes.

The present into an EDR drawable is eng_present_hdr_fs, the MSL of
rsx_present_passes.h's ps_blit_area_hdr: each tap decoded to linear light (2.2
power, or the sRGB curve with RSX_HDR_GAMMA=srgb), the area average when
scaling down, scaled to the paper white, rolled off from max(white, peak/2) to
the peak. The video out's gamma and the sharpening (CAS, now a helper the SDR
present shares) go on each tap after the highlight test, which they would
fail. RSX_HDR_WHITE/RSX_HDR_PEAK are nits with 100 nits as 1.0 (what EDR 1.0
is in the display's reference modes); unset, the white is the system's and the
peak the headroom, which also caps a peak that is set.

The highlight plane: a pipeline whose HLSL names rsx_hdr_plane (the composite
override) gets a build with an RGBA16Float colour attachment 1. Metal binds
attachments per pass, and a pipeline without attachment 1 fails validation in
a pass that has it, so those draws get a pass of their own, the first since
the last present clearing the plane. The present reads it for the frame it
was drawn beside (the same surface and size): RSX_HDR_HIGHLIGHTS=0 turns it
off, RSX_HDR_DEBUG=1 shows it. A fragment function that writes color(1) with
no attachment 1 is accepted (API and GPU validation) and the output dropped, so
the override needs one build. PS3RECOMP_METAL_WINDOW_GRAB of an EDR window
writes the values to <prefix>.pfm and the share above white to the log.

21c14a650a346b18a4f79c82689ad5c060c34693.message:
rsx_d3d12: guest depth/stencil state and samplers in the guest-FP pipelines

Every guest-FP pipeline had a fixed LESS_EQUAL depth test with writes,
no stencil, and four static samplers (s0 point/clamp for the dbgfont
atlas, s1-s3 linear/wrap), whatever the title set. In God of War HD:

- Its stencil shadow volumes marked nothing, and the shadow pass, a
  full-screen reverse-subtract quad meant only for the marked pixels,
  darkened the whole frame (0.16 -> 0.012 on a lit pixel).
- Depth state ignored: rain and blood particles were rejected.
- Unit 0 was point-sampled and clamped. The soldiers wrap their texture
  atlas (v up to ~2), sampled the transparent bottom row and drew
  nothing over an untextured base; Kratos' tattoo and skirt came out
  white; textures shimmered.

Depth test/write/func and front/back stencil (func, ops, masks) are
packed per draw into a PSO key (rsx_zs_key); the stencil reference is
set per draw. The cull key now always carries the front face, which
two-sided stencil needs with culling off. Samplers are four descriptor
tables built from each unit's TEXTURE_ADDRESS/FILTER/CONTROL0/BORDER
(one cached descriptor per distinct state); units without guest state

23540a1007e37f28c404c3adfa8ea2d22e188194.message:
rsx_d3d12: cache converted vertices within a draw

Indexed lists (shared vertices), strips and fans (each vertex in up to
three triangles) and indexed quads expand one guest vertex into several
output vertices, and each one was fetched again: 16 attributes, each with
its own address resolve and conversion, for every reference. God of War
HD's gameplay frames expand ~370k vertices through these paths and the
fetch was a third of the frame.

A direct-mapped cache on the low index bits (8192 entries, 2 MB) keeps
the converted 256-byte vertex; a hit is a memcpy. It is dropped at every
draw, since attribute state and the guest arrays may change between
draws. Measured in GoW HD gameplay: vertex time per 20 frames 0.80 s ->
0.29 s, ~9.0 -> ~12.1 fps. VTX_CACHE_CHECK=1 refetches on every lookup
and counts differences: 0 in 312M lookups. VTX_NOCACHE=1 disables it.

26ca8af13554a947fac135b3303d58447a3c140e.message:
D3D12 engine: a pipeline-state list, built ahead at start-up

The bytecode cache saves the HLSL compile, but a pipeline state is the
driver's compile of that bytecode for one GPU -- milliseconds to tens of
them the first time a machine meets it -- and while the build runs the draw
that wanted it is skipped. The states themselves cannot be shipped; the list
of them can.

Every guest pipeline state the engine builds (the triangle, point and line
classes, the WPOS-undivided build, the snapshot-copy build, the multisampled
build) goes through eng_create_pso, which writes it once to
<PS3RECOMP_DXBC_CACHE>/pipelines.bin as a canonical record: the two programs
by their DXBC checksum and every value of the description, a sample count
above one recorded as one with a flag. At start-up, workers at the lowest
priority (two thirds of the cores, at most eight) build every state the list
names, in the order it was met, the multisampled form too when the player
has MSAA on, and a draw that first needs one gets it built. The programs come
from the bytecode cache's files, found by their checksum. A title ships the
list its own play-throughs recorded; a player's sessions add to it.

This is the approach of UnleashedRecomp's precompiled pipelines (recorded in
development, built behind the boot logos, the player's options masked out of
the record), DXVK's state cache and RPCS3's pipeline cache.

Drakengard 3, one level played twice from a complete bytecode cache: without
the list 319 states were built in play, 1,416 ms of driver compile, and 26
draws skipped in play; with it 337 states were built ahead in 0.1 s before
the title screen, the 313 asked for in play took 62 ms, and 5 draws were
skipped. With MSAA x4 the second session built 646 states ahead.

PS3RECOMP_PSO_LIST=0: no list. PS3RECOMP_PSO_PREWARM=0: recorded, not built
ahead. Neither runs with RSX_ASYNC_SHADERS=0 (the replays). A list from
another record layout is set aside as pipelines.bin.old.

27745b54d1b60e5232e48a1234a182fc6f52e113.message:
ppu_lifter: inline guest stores, the store side of the inline loads

Every lifted store called vm_write8/16/32/64 out of line. In God of War
HD gameplay those calls were about a fifth of the main thread.

The generated header now has vm_write*_inl beside vm_read*_inl. A store
is done in place when vm_inl_ok accepts the address, no store diagnostic
is armed (vm_inline_st_ok: PPU_WVAL, PPU_WWATCH, PT), the barrier watch
and the null-page sweep are idle, and no SPU holds a reservation on the
line (g_spu_coh_bits). Anything else goes to the out-of-line store as
before. PPU_NO_INLINE_STORES keeps the calls, and the runtime's own files
keep them through PPU_NO_INLINE_LOADS.

Re-lift to pick it up. God of War HD: the main thread runs about 14.8 ms
a frame instead of 16.2 with the HLE lookup cache, vm_write32 is gone
from its profile and vm_write64 is 1.2%. The executable grows from 57 to
87 MB.

279bd0049a1cf1abb66b1cb69e65fd4d8dd8006f.message:
rsx vertex fetch: frequency 1 under a modulo divider bit is one element per draw

NV4097_SET_FREQUENCY_DIVIDER_OPERATION's bit makes an attribute's element
vertex % frequency. At frequency 1 that is element 0 for every vertex; the
fetch read frequency 0 and 1 as an ordinary per-vertex array whatever the
bit. rsx_vertex_freq_plain() names the ordinary case (frequency 0, or 1 with
division); rsx_vertex_element_index, the compact fetch's shared span and the
legacy rsx_fetch_attrib use it.

29154bc66a6956228da34bcac3de4ea7fa4c2080.message:
ppu: test the SPU reserved-line bitmap inline on guest stores

Every guest store called spu_coh_is_reserved, and in God of War HD
gameplay that call was 9.5% of the main PPU thread's samples. Most of it
was not the call: spu_coh_reserve stored s_coh_armed = 1 and or-ed the
line's bit into the bitmap on every GETLLAR, the same values each time.
The SPURS kernel reserves the same few lines over and over, so those
cache lines kept moving to the SPU threads' cores, and each PPU store
missed on them.

- spu_coh_reserve writes the bit, and the published pointer, only when
  they change.
- spu_coh_bitmap.h publishes the bitmap as g_spu_coh_bits, NULL until
  the first reservation, and spu_coh_line_reserved tests it inline.
  VM_WRITE_COH in ppu_loader.cpp and ppu_memory.h, and
  vm_block_reserved, use it. s_coh_armed goes away.
- g_spu_coh_bits is one merged definition per program (selectany /
  weak), so the loader fixtures, which link ppu_loader.cpp without
  spu_coherency.c, still link and see no reserved lines.

2fa6555a304eb2f9323a3dc45eca0e57abd74b58.message:
HDR: the plane carries each pixel's HDR colour; 203-nit white, highlight hue, PQ roll-off

The highlight plane only said how many times brighter a pixel was, so bright
colours could only get brighter as the SDR picture had them (fire whitened)
and everything below the clip was the SDR picture at Windows' SDR white
(often 400-500 nits, leaving little room above it). On D3D12 and Vulkan the
plane is now R32G32 uint: the pixel's HDR colour as RGB9E5 beside the 8-bit
colour it wrote to the frame (rsx_draw_backend.hdr_plane_packed; the engine
puts RSX_HDR_PLANE_PACKED above the override's text). The HDR present
resolves each frame pixel against it before any scaling, mixes the plane's
hue with the frame pixel's colour at the HDR luminance (RSX_HDR_HUE, 0.5
unless set), and rolls the brightest channel off toward the peak on the PQ
curve above a third of the peak. The paper white is 203 nits unless set
(RSX_HDR_WHITE=windows: the system's SDR white). Metal keeps the RGBA16F
plane. RSX_HDR_DEBUG shows bands of brightness, purple where the HUD or
anything else was drawn over the plane's picture.

3099075391d4105873242cd4c3f3555ed43fe397.message:
ppu_lifter: --insn-patches lifts patched instructions as run-time switches

A patch that changes an instruction word in .text does nothing to a
lifted title, which never executes the guest's code words. Making it a
second lift means a second build of the whole title for one changed
word, and a port that wants it optional ships two.

--insn-patches FILE takes {"patches": [{addr, orig, new, guard}, ...]}.
Each patched instruction is lifted in both forms and emitted as

    if (guard) { <new> } else { <orig> }  /* insn patch 0x...: orig -> new */

guard being an int the port defines and sets before the guest runs; each
function that uses a guard declares it extern "C". The original's branch
label and the code around it are unchanged. The lift stops when the
input does not hold orig at addr (a patch set for one build of a title
never lands on another), when a patch is at an address no lifted
function covers, or when new is a branch, sc or CR op (it would need
labels and call targets the function was not lifted with). The patches
reach the parallel workers too; a mismatch there raises instead of
exiting, so the pool does not hang on a dead worker.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) caps its campaign's frame rate in
code. The port lifts the cap's instructions this way and turns 60 fps on
or off from its settings, with one build.

New tools/test_ppu_lifter_insn_patches.py: a patched branch and a
patched li lift in both forms behind their guards, with the guard
declarations and the branch label in place; a wrong orig stops the lift
serially and with two workers; a patch at an address no function covers
stops it. docs/TOOLS.md describes the file with a generic example.

Metal: a launch that loaded the pipeline archives and built nothing turns them off

A Drakengard 3 player on an M1 Pro with macOS 26.0 got a black screen with
the sound playing on every launch after the first. Their logs: every
pipeline the engine asked for stayed "compiling (draw skipped until it is)",
no build finished (no [pipe-slow] line either), and the warm-up never
reported. The first launch, with no archive yet, played; deleting the data
folder gave one more good launch. The builds hung in the archive's load or
lookup.

<archive dir>/launch is now written before the archives are loaded and
removed when the first pipeline is built (eng_pipeline_state, from the
archive or compiled). Found at the next launch, the archives are deleted
and <archive dir>/off records the macOS version: with it, pipelines are
compiled from the MSL cache as on a first launch, and the log says so. An
OS update removes off and tries the archives again. A player who meets the
hang sees one black launch, not every launch.

Checked on macOS 27.0.1 (no hang here): a normal launch leaves no marker
(190 of 190 pipelines from the archives); a marker left by hand gives
"archives dropped, and off on Version 27.0.1 (Build 26A434)" and the title
and menu render; the next launch keeps them off; an off file naming
another macOS is removed and the archives are used again.

Merge PR #456: cellFs repositions the stream on a read/write switch (@feanor-noldorin)

shape: #456 was written against master, where the fd handlers re-read
g_files[fd] directly, and #430 replaced that with one snapshot per handler
(fd_file()) behind g_fd_lock. Each resolution keeps #430's snapshot and
adds #456's direction tracking: g_fd_dir[i] = 0 on allocate and on close,
fs_set_dir() before the fread and the fwrite.

One fix beyond either PR, and it is the reason this one needed reading
rather than resolving mechanically. #456's fs_set_dir(int fd, uint8_t dir)
re-reads g_files[fd] to issue its FS_SEEK64 -- which is exactly the race
#430 exists to remove. A concurrent cellFsClose can null that slot between
the caller's fd_file() and the seek, and FS_SEEK64(nullptr, 0, SEEK_CUR)
is a crash, not an error return. Merged as written, #456 would have put
back the one window #430 closed, on the FIOS media threads that are the
reason #430 was written.

So fs_set_dir() takes the caller's FILE* snapshot: fs_set_dir(fd, f, dir).

g_fd_lock in cellFsClose. #456's own fixture does not touch fs_set_dir, so
the signature change is contained to this file.

3b3fdfaa7b6ecaaee70d18b5948da69de5eefe59.message:
sys_timer: one host clock for mftb, system time and timers (mach_absolute_time on macOS)

On POSIX hosts the PPU timebase (every lifted mftb), the
sys_time_get_system_time HLE and the lv2 timers' expiration times each
called clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) and scaled it themselves. On macOS
that call is not a plain counter read: it goes through
_mach_boottime_usec and gettimeofday every time, and the mftb site is
hot in game loops that poll the time.

Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) reads the timebase in a loop on its
main thread; in a profile of the campaign that mftb site was about 14%
of the main thread's time.

host_monotonic_ns() is now the one source: mach_absolute_time scaled by
mach_timebase_info on macOS (split so the multiply cannot overflow),
clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) elsewhere. ppu_timebase_now,
sys_time_get_system_time and timer_now_us derive from it, so guest code
that mixes mftb, the system time and timer events reads one clock.
Windows is unchanged (QueryPerformanceCounter).

New tests/test_host_monotonic_clock.c (tools/test_host_monotonic_clock.py,
skipped on Windows): the clock is monotonic over a million reads, runs at
CLOCK_MONOTONIC's rate over a 200 ms sleep (to within 1 ms), and a
timebase or timer-clock reading falls between two host_monotonic_ns
readings. It prints the cost of a read: 11.6 ns against 18.7 ns for
clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) on an M-series Mac.

3bf0233d06ff7d1d181a80754a0fbf7a16cfc253.message:
cellAudio: WASAPI keeps 60 ms queued, and the mixing thread runs ahead of the guest

On Windows the shared-mode stream asked for a 20 ms device buffer, and the
mixing thread ran at normal priority. A title that keeps every core busy
with PPU and SPU threads takes the CPU from the mixing thread often enough
for those 20 ms to run dry, and each time is an audible click or stutter.
Movie playback (Bink) was the worst case.

- The buffer is 60 ms by default; PS3_AUDIO_BUF_MS=<10..500> sets it.
- The mixing thread asks for THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL and joins the
  MMCSS "Pro Audio" task when the service is there. avrt.dll is loaded at
  run time, so nothing new is linked.
- AUDIO_RATE=1 also reports underruns: passes that found the device queue
  under half a block (it is about to play silence). The first 64 blocks are
  not counted, while the stream fills.

The guest still sees 256-sample blocks at 48 kHz paced by the device clock;
only how far ahead of the device the mixer may run changes (up to the buffer
size, so up to ~40 ms more output latency by default).

Seen with inFAMOUS 2 on a Ryzen 5 5600 (6 cores, all of them busy): with
the 20 ms buffer its Bink cutscenes stuttered audibly; with this change
they play cleanly. Only the Windows (WASAPI) path is touched.

3d7b7cf783b9cc0d6fd1695da34ac060d9d7498f.message:
Vulkan: HDR output and highlights (RSX_HDR), as the D3D12 engine

RSX_HDR=1 on the Vulkan engine: where the display under the window has HDR
on, the swap chain is scRGB (R16G16B16A16_SFLOAT, EXTENDED_SRGB_LINEAR) or,
where the driver offers no scRGB, HDR10 (10-bit, HDR10_ST2084; the present
pass then writes the BT.2020 primaries through the PQ curve, hdr2.x). The
instance enables VK_EXT_swapchain_colorspace where the loader has it. The
present runs kPresentHdrHLSL at the window's size into a target in the swap
chain's format -- decoded, area-averaged, the paper white, the highlights
rolled off toward the peak -- in place of the area pass, then the same blit.
Its constants are 8 floats at b1 (256 bytes a frame slot); t1 is the plane.

The highlight plane: a pipeline whose text names rsx_hdr_plane gets a build
with an FP16 second attachment (eng_pso_plane), used for a pass into one
target without MSAA while HDR is on, in a rendering instance of its own;
the present reads the plane for the frame it was drawn beside.
RSX_HDR_WHITE, RSX_HDR_PEAK, RSX_HDR_GAMMA, RSX_HDR_HIGHLIGHTS and
RSX_HDR_DEBUG as on D3D12; the settings page's reload and a poll every 60th
pump make a new swap chain when HDR is switched or the display's changes.

rsx_hdr_display.c: the display query (DXGI's colour space and peak,
DisplayConfig's SDR white level) and its staleness check, moved out of the
D3D12 engine so both Windows engines ask the same; a stub elsewhere, where a
backend decides from what its surface offers. kPresentHdrHLSL's constants
gain hdr2 (D3D12 passes zeros there).

Live, RTX 4090 on an HDR display: Vulkan picks scRGB FP16 at Windows' 480
nits white and the display's 1499 nit peak, makes the plane, and the debug
view marks the sword trails brightened and the HUD drawn over, as on D3D12;
D3D12 HDR unchanged. Replays (headless, never HDR) byte-identical to 0.4.1's
on both engines: 111 of 111 frames each.

3e9311c6287b1220d57e99b3a2a7d3e45a1cf7db.message:
cellGcmSys: forget a park once the walker has left it

The walker gives a self-JUMP park GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS with the same put to
be patched, then resyncs to put. Its record of the park (address, put,
start time) was only cleared by that resync. A park the walker left any
other way -- the title patched it into a JUMP elsewhere, or wrote
commands over it -- kept its start time, so when the walker next stopped
at the same address with the same put, the new park was taken for the
old one. Its grace had run out long before, the resync fired at once,
and the commands the title was about to link in were dropped with the
fences and labels in them. A title that reuses its command blocks
meets its parks again at the same address, frame after frame.

Clear the record as soon as the walker reads anything other than that
park's own self-JUMP: a new park always starts a fresh grace. The three
variables move from the JUMP branch to file scope for that, under the
same names.

41bae9560bd0def7d49aa3675e89fa388e27f74e.message:
rsx_d3d12: stage guest textures in a shared upload ring; LRU slots

Each texture slot had its own committed upload buffer, created with the
texture whenever the slot took a new size or format. In God of War HD's
texture bursts, when new effects first appear, creating resources was
most of the cost: one report interval had 50 new textures, 67 ms of
CreateCommittedResource (41 ms of it for the upload buffers) against
18 ms of decoding.

- Uploads are staged in one persistently mapped upload buffer, 32 MB per
  frame in flight, reset where that frame index's command allocator is
  reset (its copies have finished by then). A texture that does not fit
  in what is left uses the slot's own upload buffer, created on demand.
- A new texture takes an empty slot, else the least recently used one.
  Taking the first slot not used this frame evicted textures the next
  frame needed again: up to 22 a report interval in those bursts.
- 192 slots instead of 96; the game used up to 66.
- A frame with no free slot returned slot -1 and indexed vp_tex with it;
  it now returns -1 to the caller (untextured), as the lookup failure
  path does.

God of War HD: the drain stalls of 67-75 ms in the bursts at 131 and
135-136 s are now under 40 ms. The rendering check passes.

per-thread cache in front, which returns before the claim lock on a hit.

return before a getenv they no longer need to reach.

4609b3f0bf7db6fdf3a9c36a5037b0be230b8d7c.message:
spu: halt and iret longjmps without unwinding on 64-bit Windows

On 64-bit Windows longjmp unwinds every host frame between it and its
setjmp: RtlUnwindEx, with a function-table lookup and a virtual unwind per
frame. The SPU runtime longjmps on every halt back to spu_run_with_halt (a
SPURS policy module's run ends that way) and on every iret back to the
drain loop that took the interrupt.

spu_jmp_no_unwind() zeroes the jmp_buf's Frame right after setjmp returns
0, which makes longjmp restore the registers directly. These jumps only
cross C frames of the runtime and of lifted code, which have no destructors
or __finally blocks. SPU_LONGJMP_UNWIND=1 keeps the unwinding jump. No
change on other platforms.

48958fefdf401b95dc3c8ad1d1d15461db2eb89a.message:
ppu: a host thread gives its callback stack slot back when it exits

Slots were handed out by a counter and never returned, so once 64 host
threads had ever made a guest callback, every later thread shared the
last slot and the original bug came back. A movie player starts several
threads per movie, so a normal session gets there. Keep a 64-bit in-use
mask instead: a thread takes the lowest free slot on its first callback
and a thread_local owner releases it when the thread exits. Only more
than 64 live threads making callbacks at once share a slot now.

The test first runs 100 short-lived threads one after another, each
making a callback: they all get the first slot back, and the two
concurrent threads after them still get different stacks. Both checks
fail without the release.

4b8de9100d4cc959a5ccf37c51067d416691dc7a.message:
spu: lifted known-target branches tail-call their target (SPU_DIRECT)

A lifted cross-function branch with a known target (br, the conditional
branches, a fall-through into the next function) set the trampoline and
returned, and the drain loop then called the target: a host return, a
loop pass and an indirect call for every transfer. Most of those steps
have nothing for the drain to do. SPU_DIRECT tail-calls the target with
clang's musttail when that is so: the target is not LS 0, this is not
the run's first transfer, the target is not a registered stack-reset
entry (a 1024-byte hint table, set at registration), and no interrupt
is pending with interrupts enabled. Everything else takes the trampoline
as before, and so does every compiler without musttail.

The drain-step diagnostics (SPU_LOCKSTEP, SPU_TAILRET, SPU_PCHIST,
SPU_NO_LS0_END, SPU_EXITTRACE, SPU_STEPTRACE, SPU_JOBDRAIN,
SPURS_PM_FLOW) turn it off, and PS3_SPU_DIRECT=0 does too.

spu_drain_call now restores the enclosing drain's drain_ret_pc on the
way out instead of 0. The enclosing loop used to re-set it on its next
step; with direct tail calls the code after a nested call can run on for
a long time before it takes one.

In the inFAMOUS 2 port (about 18.8k such sites) the open-world walk went
from 34.5 to 36.3 fps (+5.4%), with SPU time per frame from 128 to 121 ms.

604bc92130d086c1c483ff97baf35614367ac26c.message:
rsx_shader_msl: cache HLSL -> MSL translations, in memory and optionally on disk

A guest pipeline's first use on Metal decompiles both programs,
translates each HLSL to MSL (glslang + spirv-cross), compiles the MSL
and builds the pipeline state, all on the RSX thread in the middle of a
frame. In inFAMOUS 2 the translation was 83% of that: 218 first uses
over two minutes of play cost 2.1 s, with single frames of up to
366 ms, against ~16% for newLibraryWithSource and under 1% for the
pipeline state, which Metal caches itself.

Keep the MSL the way rsx_shader_spirv.cpp keeps SPIR-V: in memory, and
with PS3RECOMP_MSL_CACHE=<dir> in one file per stage + HLSL text +
PS3RECOMP_MSL_FAST setting. The file header names the glslang and
spirv-cross versions and the translator's build, so a file any other
combination wrote is a miss, as is a damaged one; files are written
under a temporary name and renamed. Unset, nothing touches the disk.

macOS shows nothing of a window that is not on screen: another app or
Space in front (a full-screen window has a Space of its own, so bringing
any other app to the front hides it), minimized, or fully covered.
Presents go on and are dropped unseen, so the display rate reads 0 while
the guest's goes on, which in a log looks like a frozen picture.

In the Resistance: Fall of Man (BCUS98107) port, a full-screen run with
another app brought to the front reads exactly like that in its log:
display=0 while the guest rate goes on, as if the picture had frozen.

logs once ("window off screen ..."), coming back logs how long it was
away and presents at once, so the newest frame the game published
meanwhile goes up without waiting for the next one. [RSX FPS] lines end
in hidden=1 while the window is off screen.

bare CAMetalLayer and no window: on screen a frame goes up and the rate
line is plain; off screen is logged once and the rate line says
hidden=1; two frames published while away, and coming back logs the
time away and shows the newer of them; a repeated on-screen change says
nothing.

6404ecfe9252bc7bf633b1fa724bb88067bed5be.message:
cellSysutilNpEula: answer the PSN terms check through its callback

sceNpEulaCheckEulaStatus asks whether the player has accepted the
title's PSN terms of service, and the answer comes later, through the
callback the title passed, on one of its cellSysutilCheckCallback polls.
None of the three real exports was implemented (the module had only a
made-up cellSysutilNpEulaCheck), so the imports answered CELL_OK and the
callback never came. A title that waits for the answer behind a "Please
wait..." box waits there for the rest of the run; inFAMOUS 2 does it the
first time it tries to go online.

Implement CheckEulaStatus, Abort and ShowCurrentEula as RPCS3 does: one
request at a time (ALREADY_INITIALIZED otherwise), the callback queued
from the next sysutil poll, Abort turning a pending answer into ABORTED.
The answer depends on the connection. Offline, the default, the terms
cannot be fetched and the callback gets SCE_NP_EULA_ERROR, which is what
a console without a connection gets and what makes a title leave its
online features alone; RPCS3's ALREADY_ACCEPTED would send it on to ask
an offline NP manager for a ticket. With PS3_NET_ONLINE=1 or a psnr
server the answer is RPCS3's, ALREADY_ACCEPTED, version 1.
ShowCurrentEula has nothing to show and closes on the next poll.

cellNetCtl exports its PS3_NET_ONLINE check as ps3_netctl_online for
this.

6aaea446bc2f4e6d89378176b5155b10fb7474fd.message:
rsx engine: honour the polygon offset (SET_POLY_OFFSET_*)

The draw engine ignored SET_POLY_OFFSET_{POINT,LINE,FILL}_ENABLE,
SCALE_FACTOR and BIAS, so every draw was drawn without the offset a
title asked for. Shadow casters, decals and projected shadows are drawn
with an offset so they do not fight the depth they sit on.

Resistance: Fall of Man sets a polygon offset for its character shadow
maps, its terrain decals and its projected shadows; all of them were
drawn without it.

A new optional backend hook, set_depth_bias(slope, units, depth_bits),
is called before every draw like the stencil reference, with the enable
that matches what the primitive rasterises as (POINT, LINE or FILL) and
the zeta's depth bits (16 for Z16, 24 for Z24S8). Both terms are 0 while
the offset is off, and a NaN term reads 0. PS3RECOMP_ENG_POLY_OFFSET=0
draws without it, as before. The pass dump's draw log shows "po
factor/bias" for an offset draw.

The Metal backend keeps the offset in the draw record and sets
setDepthBias:slopeScale:clamp: per draw. Its depth targets are
Depth32Float, whose bias unit is 2^-24 over [0.5, 1), so Z24 units carry
over as they are and a Z16 unit is 256 of them.

New test_polygon_offset in test_rsx_draw_engine: 0/0 with the offset off
or only its values set, FILL's values against a Z24S8 and a Z16 zeta,
LINE applying to a line list and not to a triangle, a NaN factor, and
0/0 again once it is disabled.

New test_metal_poly_offset (a CMake target where the HLSL -> MSL
translation is built, run twice in macos.yml): a constant-depth triangle
at 0.75 drawn on the GPU through the engine and the Metal backend lands
at 0.75 + 2^-16 with BIAS 256 on Z24S8 and with BIAS 1 on Z16, a
SCALE_FACTOR alone does not move it, and with PS3RECOMP_ENG_POLY_OFFSET=0
nothing does.
