e4cc08a9a6ac2614ac9c0dd2e46d0ac466ee474c.message:
A processor without SSE4.1 gets a clear message, not a crash

Issues #349 and #350: a player's Pentium E5400 crashed with c000001d as the window opened. The runtime and the game module
are built with SSE4.1, and that CPU doesn't have it, so the first such instruction ended the program (pmovsxdq in
create_window, rsxc_d3d12.c). The crash dialog then asked them to report it, with nothing saying what was wrong.

des_cpu_check.cpp now asks the processor first, and says so if SSE4.1 is missing. It runs ahead of the C++ static
initializers, and is the one source here built without SSE4.1, so it can run on such a processor. The check comes
before setup too, so nobody spends time on a build that can't run.

AVX, LZCNT, AES and the like in the exe are in Microsoft's runtime and mbedTLS, which ask the CPU before using them. SSE4.1
is the only one the program assumes, so it is the only one checked.

The README now names the requirement. CI runs the check both ways (DES_TEST_OLD_CPU=1, and plainly) on both systems.

There is no processor without SSE4.1 here: the message was checked with DES_TEST_OLD_CPU=1, on the path it takes.

ebd14fd32eec85949fc5ead1ae6460611f8b026f.message:
Port: the viewport command waits for room in the render ring (des_viewport_room)

HighGraphics writes its commands to a 1 MB ring that SPU image 2 reads.
Every writer waits in usleep(30) until its command fits, except the
viewport command's (0x00D22670): with the ring full, or 16 bytes free, it
sleeps once and writes its 32 bytes anyway. On a PS3 image 2 frees the
room in time; here a busy PC can hold image 2's thread for milliseconds,
and the write took put onto get or 16 bytes past it. Every writer's check
then passed, HighGraphics wrote a lap over commands image 2 had not read,
and image 2 halted: the world stopped drawing (soaks at 120 fps on a busy
PC, 2 of 23; with image 2 held up on purpose, an overrun in 5 of 15).

An instruction hook after the sleep (0x00D229A4) sleeps on in the same
usleep(30) while the command does not fit, as the other writers do, and
logs each wait. DES_RINGFIX=0 turns it off. Needs a re-lift (only
ppu_recomp_029.cpp changes). docs/117.

ec1b9e91020e42ece19b1ee2f4fc576991c6c9c1.message:
des_prework: free the last shader pass's texts once it is done

run_passes resets the precompile module before each target's pass, but
not after the last one. So whenever the start's shader pass runs (after a
session that drew new fragment-program variants, or after an update), the
last target's work stays allocated for the rest of the session: every
decompiled HLSL text (3,654 on the US disc, 44 MB), the programs and the
pipeline index's rows.

It now resets after the last pass too. Nothing reads that state after it:
the rows were handed to the renderer during the pass
(rsx_out_pso_index_add, _ready), and run_pass leaves s_state at 3, so
des_prework_status no longer asks for the counts. reset() waits for the
compile threads first.

Found with a scratch walk of the process heap 30 s into the Tutorial

# Soulbrandt **Demon's Souls, running natively on PC.** [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt?filter=v%2A&sort=semver&display_name=tag&label=release&color=orange)](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases/latest) [![downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/latest/total?label=downloads&color=brightgreen)](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases/latest) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1565536292324769832?label=Discord&logo=discord&logoColor=white&color=5865F2)](https://discord.gg/BzmwDeca8s)
Soulbrandt is a PC port of *Demon's Souls* (PS3, 2009). The game's original code has been converted to run directly on Windows and Linux, with no emulator. You need your own copy of the game: the US version, **BLUS30443** (version 1.00). This project includes no game files. ## Status **0.1.0, the first release, is an alpha.** Download it from the [Releases](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases) page. The game plays from start to finish (a tester has beaten it), but not every part has been tried on every setting, so expect bugs. What [isn't supported yet](#not-supported-yet) is below; please [report](#problems) anything you find. Questions and help: [Discord](https://discord.gg/BzmwDeca8s). ## Highlights - Up to 240 fps or unlocked, with the game's timing fixed. Up to 4K, ultrawide, 16:10 and HDR. - Online play on this project's own server: messages, bloodstains, ghosts, co-op and invasions. - Roll in any direction while locked on, not only forward, back, left or right. - A stat respec in the Nexus (optional): get back the souls your levels cost and spend them again. - Keyboard and mouse, Xbox controllers, DualSense and DualShock 4. ## Features Press **F1** (or **L3 + R3** on a controller) at any time to open the menu. Most settings apply right away. Each setting has a short help text in the menu. **Picture** - Frame rates of 30 (the original), 60, 120, 144, 165 or 240 fps, a number of your own, or unlocked. The game's timing is fixed so it still plays the way it should. Above 60 fps is less tested. - Cutscenes play at 30 fps by default, as they judder above it. You can play them at your frame rate instead. - V-sync on or off, "Even frames" for smooth motion, and G-Sync / FreeSync. - Render resolution up to 300% (4K), ultrawide aspect ratios (21:9 and 32:9), and 16:10 for the Steam Deck's screen. - Anti-aliasing (FXAA or SMAA), anisotropic filtering up to 16x, texture filtering and a sharp scaling filter. - HDR on HDR displays (Windows), with settings for brightness, peak and shadows. - Turn off the game's depth of field and motion blur. - Window or fullscreen (Alt+Enter switches). - Two renderers (Settings > Display > Renderer): DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Windows starts on DirectX 12, Linux on Vulkan. **Controls** - Xbox controllers, DualSense and DualShock 4, over USB or Bluetooth, with vibration. Pick which controller the game uses when several are connected. - Keyboard and mouse, laid out like the Souls games on PC. To turn the camera with the mouse, turn on **Mouse look** in Settings > Controls. - Change which buttons and keys do what. - Mouse sensitivity, inverted axes, and switching lock-on targets with a flick of the mouse. - **Roll in any direction while locked on**: the roll goes where the stick points. It's on by default; turn off **Roll toward the stick** in Settings > Controls for the original's four directions. - The mouse in the game's own menus: point and click. Experimental, and off by default. **HUD** - Move, resize, hide or show each part of the HUD. - Change its size, and choose where it goes on wide screens. **Game** - Skip the logos and the opening movie, and go straight into your last save. - **Stat respec**: the Maiden in Black, or the statue in front of where you wake in the Nexus, puts your stats back to your class's and gives back the souls your levels cost, to spend again. Off by default: turn on **Stat respec in the Nexus** in Settings > Game. - Use several soul items at once, as Drop does. On by default: turn off **Use several souls at once** in Settings > Game for the original's one at a time. **Online** - On by default, on this project's own server: messages, bloodstains, ghosts, co-op and invasions. - Setup asks for your online name. You can change it, or turn online play off, in Settings > Network. - A matchmaking password, so you meet only your friends. - Show or hide other players' messages, bloodstains and ghosts. **The program** - A setup that builds the game from your copy, with an Original and an Enhanced preset (see [How to play](#how-to-play)). - Updates: the game checks for a new version at start and asks before changing anything. Your saves and settings are kept, and you can go back one version. - In the menu, the Large Sword of Moonlight is the cursor and a crystal lizard dances in the corner. Both can be turned off. - Trophies, with pop-ups. Setup can bring your trophies and save across from RPCS3. - **Report an issue** in the menu opens a GitHub issue with your PC's details filled in, and a zip to attach that includes your save, so the problem can be seen where it happened. It has no game files. If the game crashes or stops responding, a window offers to do the same. ## What you need - Your own copy of Demon's Souls for the PS3, US version (BLUS30443, version 1.00), as a folder with `PS3_GAME` in it. Setup cannot use ISO files yet. - RPCS3, the free PS3 emulator, with the PS3 system software installed (4.93, the version Sony offers now). Setup has it unlock the game's encrypted files. (Or decrypt the files yourself: see below.) - Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) with a graphics card that supports DirectX 12, or Linux (see [Linux](#linux)). - A processor with SSE4.1, which most have since about 2011. - An internet connection during setup. Setup downloads a compiler and Python (about 60 MB on Windows, about 130 MB on Linux). ## How to play These steps are for the release download. 1. Download the zip for Windows (`DemonsSoulsRecomp-X.Y.Z-windows.zip`) or the tarball for Linux (`DemonsSoulsRecomp-X.Y.Z-linux.tar.xz`), and unpack it into a folder of its own. 2. Start `Soulbrandt.exe` (on Linux, `Soulbrandt`). Setup opens. 3. Pick how setup gets your game's files: - **Import from RPCS3**: setup finds the game in RPCS3's list and has your RPCS3 unlock its files. It can bring your save, trophies and some settings across too. - **I have decrypted files**: your disc copy, plus the 28 files you decrypted yourself (`EBOOT.elf`, the `.sdat` files and `libsre.prx`). - **Show me how**: step by step, with free tools only. 4. Start the build. It runs on your PC and can take a while; setup shows an estimate first. You can stop it and carry on later. 5. Pick a preset: **Original** plays as on the PS3; **Enhanced** sets 60 fps, a resolution that fits your display, SMAA, 16x anisotropic filtering, fullscreen, and HDR when Windows has HDR on for your display. Then a few choices (HDR among them, on Windows) and your online name. You can change anything later in Settings. Then press **Play**. Windows may warn you the first time you start `Soulbrandt.exe` ("Windows protected your PC"), because the program isn't signed yet. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If setup says your `libsre.prx` came out different, your RPCS3 probably has PS3 system software 4.90. Install 4.93 in RPCS3 (*File > Install Firmware*) and try again. If RPCS3 is set to run as administrator, setup cannot start it: untick that in `rpcs3.exe`'s Properties. ### Linux CI builds the Linux program on every change, and each release includes a Linux download. It needs x86-64 Linux with glibc 2.35 or newer, a Vulkan driver, and `curl` and `tar`. Nothing else needs installing. The game renders on Vulkan, and setup prepares its shaders. If Vulkan can't start, the game falls back to its older renderer on vkd3d (DirectX 12 on Vulkan), which compiles shaders as it goes, with long pauses when a new area loads. Linux is newer and less tested than Windows. So far it has run in WSL (Ubuntu 24.04) and, on the older renderer, on one Steam Deck. The Vulkan renderer hasn't run on a real Linux graphics driver yet ([docs/106](docs/106-setup-on-linux.md)). macOS is not supported. On a Steam Deck, keys and the mouse stay out of the game while its controls are on, because Steam's desktop layout presses them too. To use a keyboard on a docked Deck, set `PAD_KEYBOARD_WITH_PAD=1`. ### Online play Online play is on by default and uses this project's own server. Setup asks for your online name; you can change it, or turn online play off, in Settings > Network. RPCS3 players use other servers, so you won't meet them. What the server keeps about you is in the [privacy note](PRIVACY.md). ### Not supported yet - Only the US version (BLUS30443) works. The European version is being looked at; other versions are not supported. - Setup can't read ISO files, and it needs RPCS3 to unlock the game's files (or files you decrypted yourself). - macOS isn't supported, and running the Windows download through CrossOver hasn't been tested all the way through. Linux is less tested than Windows, and the Steam Deck has had one test so far. - On-screen button prompts always show PlayStation buttons, even with a keyboard or an Xbox controller. ### Problems Use **Report an issue** in the menu (F1), or open an [issue](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/issues). For questions and help, join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/BzmwDeca8s). Report security problems privately, as [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) says. ## Building from source This is the technical part. The full notes are in [`docs/`](docs/). **Tools** | Windows | Linux | |---|---| | Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, LLVM (clang), CMake, Ninja, Python 3, Git Bash | clang or GCC, CMake, Ninja, Python 3, SDL2, Vulkan and FFmpeg development files, vkd3d ([details](docs/76-native-linux.md#building)) | On Windows, step 4 downloads FFmpeg's MPEG-2 video decoder for the game's movies (about 1 MB) and puts it beside `des_boot.exe`. If that download fails, the build says so and goes on, and the movies then need Microsoft's free [MPEG-2 Video Extension](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9n95q1zzpmh4) from the Microsoft Store; without either, they play their sound with no picture. (A paid app called "MPEG-2 Video Extensions", from another publisher, is a different thing; you don't need it.) **From your copy of the game** - The game disc's files (`PS3_GAME`) - [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), to decrypt the game's `EBOOT.BIN` - `libsre.prx` from your PS3 firmware, decrypted **Steps** 1. Get this repository, and its runtime inside it: ```sh git clone https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt.git cd Soulbrandt git clone https://github.com/JonathanDC64/ps3recomp.git ``` `ps3recomp.pin` names the ps3recomp commit this version of the port needs. `python tools/release/pin_ps3recomp.py local` checks your checkout against it. 2. In RPCS3, decrypt `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` (*Utilities > Decrypt PS3 Binaries*) to `work/game/EBOOT.ELF`. Copy `PS3_GAME/ICON0.PNG` next to it, for the program's icon. 3. Convert the game's main code: ```sh python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_loader.py work/game/EBOOT.ELF -o work/loader python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_lifter.py work/game/EBOOT.ELF \ --functions work/loader/EBOOT.functions.json --hle-stubs work/loader/EBOOT.imports.json \ --override-funcs "0x167AC88=ds_malloc,0x167AC58=ds_free,0x273D38=des_move_post,0x724E40=des_menu_tick" \ --insn-hooks @port/insn_hooks.txt --shadow-stack --chunk-lines 150000 --output work/recomp -j 16 python ps3recomp/tools/gen_hle_nids.py --all --out work/recomp/hle_nid_table.cpp python scripts/apply_boot_patches.py work/recomp ``` Then the SPU code with `python scripts/build_spu.py --eboot work/game/EBOOT.ELF` ([docs/09](docs/09-spu-spurs.md)), which first cuts the SPU programs out of the EBOOT, and libsre with `python scripts/build_libsre.py `. The lifter's flags above are also in `scripts/lift_ppu.json`, which setup reads; change both together. 4. Compile the runtime, then the game. On Windows: ```sh cmake -S ps3recomp -B ps3recomp/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \ -DPS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL=ON cmake -S port -B port/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl \ -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE= -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG= -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS_DEBUG= cmake --build ps3recomp/build --target ps3recomp_runtime rsx_shader_precompile cmake --build port/build --target des_boot --parallel 4 ``` `PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL=ON` builds the portable renderer: DirectX 12 through it, the default, and Vulkan beside it (Settings > Display > Renderer). Without it the game runs on the legacy renderer only. Its first configure downloads glslang and SPIRV-Tools at their pinned commits. On Linux, see [docs/76](docs/76-native-linux.md#building). 5. Copy `tools/des/local.env.example` to `tools/des/local.env`, set `PS3_VFS_ROOT` in it to the folder that holds `PS3_GAME`, and start the game with `tools/des/play.sh`. A direct start of `des_boot.exe` goes through setup instead, and keeps its saves in `port/build/gamedata`. Everything made from your copy of the game stays in `work/` and `gamedata/`, which git ignores. **Never share your build:** it contains code converted from your game. **For developers** - Each setting's help text ends with its name in brackets, such as `(DES_FPS)`. The same name works as an environment variable, which wins over the menu. - `-DDES_SPLIT=ON` also builds the game the way setup does: `des_host` plus the game as a separate library ([docs/57](docs/57-dll-split.md)). - `-DDES_DEV=ON` makes a developer build, with cheats and a Developer tab in Settings ([docs/55](docs/55-dev-cheats.md)). Never share one as a release. - The renderer is the portable one ([docs/120](docs/120-portable-renderer.md)): DirectX 12 by default, or Vulkan in Settings > Display > Renderer, then restart. If Vulkan fails to start, the game runs on DirectX 12 and says why. `RSX_BACKEND=legacy` runs the renderer from before it: retired, kept unchanged as a fallback, with no more fixes. A build has it when its ps3recomp is configured with `PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL=ON`, as in the steps above and in the released Windows build. ## Legal This project contains only its own code, scripts and documentation. It has no game code, no game files, no Sony firmware and no keys; you make those from your own copy ([docs/05](docs/05-legal.md)). *Demon's Souls* is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment, FromSoftware or Atlus. ## Credits - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet and its contributors: the recompiler and runtime this port is built on - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): a reference for how the PS3 behaves (no RPCS3 code is copied) - [RmlUi](https://github.com/mikke89/RmlUi) and [FreeType](https://freetype.org) for the menus, adapted from [Dusklight](https://github.com/TwilitRealm/dusklight)'s interface code - [SMAA](https://www.iryoku.com/smaa/) for the SMAA setting, [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org) for the movies, and [vkd3d](https://gitlab.winehq.org/wine/vkd3d) and [SDL](https://www.libsdl.org) for Linux Settings > About and [`port/ui/NOTICE.md`](port/ui/NOTICE.md) list the menus' parts with their licences. The download's `licenses` folder holds the licences of the libraries shipped beside the program. The source of its LGPL libraries, FFmpeg and vkd3d, is on [their own release](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases/tag/third-party-sources). ## License MIT, for this repository's own code, scripts and documentation ([`LICENSE`](LICENSE)). ps3recomp is MIT-licensed by its authors.

319519444f9760551d5c4ab12a287f533fb26326.message:
Time bomb: the bubble draws whole, without square holes

The time bomb's bubble arrives as an INLINE_ARRAY stream (vertices in the
command buffer), two layers of more than 64 KB each. The dispatcher
gathered inline streams in a fixed 64 KB buffer, and on overflow it emptied
the buffer and kept filling it, so each layer drew only the tail of its
stream. The quads it lost left blocky, staircase-shaped holes that moved as
the bubble grew. The buffer now grows as a stream needs it, up to 64 MB. A
stream past that is dropped whole and logged, instead of drawing its tail.

Also: the draw engine's DRAW_ARRAYS / DRAW_INDEX_ARRAY range lists grow
too, instead of silently dropping every range past the 256th in one
BEGIN_END group.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

3e435a2163ca782d7019e26714100d20d0f04f34.message:
Saving: stop handing a finished save thread's id to the next thread

A Crack in Time runs each save on a worker thread and polls the thread's
id with sys_ppu_thread_get_priority until it answers ESRCH. Save threads
are never joined, so their slots stay finished, and the runtime takes one
back only when no slot is free. After long play all 64 slots are in use,
and from then on find_free_slot reclaimed the lowest finished slot, often
the one of the autosave that had just ended. When the next thread was the
session's first movie, its "Bink Audio Thread" (alive until the game
quits) inherited the save thread's id and the poll kept answering OK. The
save manager stayed busy, autosaves stopped silently, and the Save menu
dimmed the screen and waited with the save icon flashing.

find_free_slot now hands out slots round-robin, so an id comes back only
after the other 63 have been used, whether the table is full or not.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

45f57afbfeea2cb4fda37e706e642131a4333f89.message:
Guest clocks count from the game's start, not the host's boot

Axiom City's cranes, the containers on them and the spinning platforms
moved only 8 times a second, and Ratchet stepped with a platform while
riding it; the ship's lift-off and landing were choppy the same way.

The game keeps a 32-bit float seconds clock off the timebase and animates
these from it. The runtime gave the guest absolute host time (QPC on
Windows, CLOCK_MONOTONIC elsewhere), which counts from the host's boot:
after ~15 days of uptime the clock read ~1.29 million seconds, where a
float only holds steps of 0.125 s. A PS3 counts from power-on, so the
game never sees values that large there. Measured: the crane's matrix
held for 7-8 frames and jumped, in step with the float clock at
0x00E20780 moving one 0.125 s step.

The guest clocks (the PPU timebase, sys_time_get_system_time, cellAudio
port timestamps, GCM timestamps) now subtract one shared origin, the host
clock at the guest's first read less 30 s, so they still share an epoch.
RACACIT_GUEST_CLOCK=host keeps absolute host time.

Runtime patch only: sys_timer.c/.h, ppu_sysprx.cpp, cellAudio.c,
cellGcmSys.c. Checked that the patch applies to a clean ps3recomp
checkout as setup_windows.sh applies it; in Axiom City the cranes and
containers now move every frame.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

1448530904.readme_excerpt:
Join the discord for updates!

## About RACiT is Recomped A Crack in Time. RACiT is a project to bring **Ratchet & Clank: A Crack in Time** (the greatest game ever made) to Windows and Android through static recompilation. It takes the original PS3 code and converts it to native C/C++, using ps3recomp. The Android target is ARM64. There is also a Linux build for debugging (Android and Linux builds not yet public) ## Features - Vulkan-based RSX renderer - DualSense (PS5 controller) speaker and trigger mod integrated - General controller support for most windows compatible controllers. - Mouse and keyboard controls (bindable in the launcher) - Added toggles for enhanced internal resolution and graphics settings ## What you'll need Game data isn't included. You'll need your own decrypted dump of the **North American disc version (`BCUS98124`)**, including: !!A LEGALLY DUMPED VERSION OF RATCHET AND CLANK FUTURE: A CRACK IN TIME (NO ASSESTS ARE OR WILL EVER BE INCLUDED WITH THIS PROJECT)!! - `EBOOT.ELF` - `USRDIR` - After downloading the launcher, extract and run the .exe, which will take you through the setup process, which is importing your .iso directly or directing the launcher to your PS3GAME folder. The game will also check for a decrypted EBOOT.elf, if your dumps .elf is showing as encrypted, the easier way to fix is with RPSC3. ## Current status This is a work in progress. RACiT is an unofficial project and is not affiliated with Sony, Insomniac Games, or the game's rights holders. Saves are currently not transferable between windows and android. Feature will be added in the future to sync saves between devices ## Thanks This version for the European disc (`BCES00511`) exists thanks to two projects: - [RACiT](https://github.com/HighDrexler/RACiT) by HighDrexler, the port this version is built on. - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet, the static recompilation toolkit behind it. Thank you for your work.

  tested with too"), the unlock's output checks and the stage take it
  unchanged, and the lift lifts it (its TOC comes from the file).

des_prework: one shader pass per target the runtime has, each with its stamp (step P3a)

With a runtime built with the portable renderer (PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL),
the shaders pass at a start and in setup runs once for each target the
runtime has, d3d12 first:

- d3d12 is today's pass, with today's stamp (precompile.stamp) and
  today's pipeline index work.
- dxbc (the new D3D12 path) and spv (Vulkan) each have their own stamp,
  <cache>/gpu/precompile_<target>.stamp: today's stamp text plus a line
  naming the target and what its files depend on (for spv, the compile
  service's tag: compiler versions, flags, text edits). A target whose
  stamp is up to date is skipped, and the log says so.

A skip stops the passes that are left. Setup's last line puts the
targets together: the worst result, and the counts and seconds summed.
The off-Windows "none" is gone with the option, since the spv target
needs no FXC.

Without the option nothing changes: des_prework.cpp preprocesses to the
same text and its object is identical.

10036dbff1459d1a3d5c4913a3047eff28f3aef7.message:
Setup: the first Python without curl or tar (Wine, CrossOver)

Setup's first step downloads Python with Windows' own curl.exe and unpacks it with its tar.exe, from System32. Wine
and CrossOver ship neither, so a Mac player on CrossOver stopped at "Setup could not start its first download", and the
log did not say why.

When curl or tar does not start, the host now does it itself. Machines that have curl and tar work as before.
- setup_http.cpp downloads with WinHTTP, which Windows and Wine both have. It does what the curl line does:
  - https only, TLS 1.2 or later;
  - redirects followed, but never from https to http;
  - a minute's timeouts;
  - a Range request carrying on from the .part file. A 200 answer starts the file over; a 206 for another range
    deletes it.
  Cancel closes its handles, which ends the call it is in.
- setup_unzip.cpp unpacks the zip:
  - stored and deflated entries, inflated by stb_image's zlib, which the UI already builds;
  - each file's CRC-32 checked;
  - zip64, encryption and several disks refused.
  The names go through the same check as tar's, and the archive's size and SHA-256 are checked first, as before.
- FIX lines (the reason under Details) now also go to the log, so a report has them.
- DES_SETUP_NO_SYSTEM_TOOLS=1 hides curl and tar, for tests.
- crc32.hpp is report.cpp's CRC-32, now shared with the zip reader, and its table is built once in a thread-safe way.
- docs/88 section 5 describes the fallback.

Off Windows nothing changes: setup_http.cpp has no download there, so a missing curl fails as before.

1375e434db45d5dde7c3a8d6b701386aada64b86.message:
ui: the menus' renderer on the GPU layer (step V4)

render_gpu.cpp is render_d3d12.cpp with each D3D12 call made through
ps3recomp's GPU layer (gpu.h) instead, so the menus can later draw on any
of its backends. It is a copy, not a rewrite: the same shaders, layers,
2x MSAA targets and resolves, filters (blur, drop shadow, colour
matrices, masks), clip mask on the shared stencil buffer, gradients,
blend factor, HDR pass, read_back and the two game models with depth,
and on D3D12 the same command for each call today's renderer makes.

- Shaders: the same HLSL, compiled once at start by the layer's compile
  service (gpu_sc_compile_layout, DXBC target) with today's FXC call, so
  the bytecode is the same.
- Pipelines, the binding layout, the texture table pool, samplers and the
  null table are made once at start (pipelines once per state, as
  today's PSO map); a draw takes no allocation, map lookup or getenv
  that today's does not.
- Textures sit in one 4096-entry table pool, one entry each, as today's
  descriptor heap; frames in flight have their own rings and recorder
  slots, and what RmlUi lets go of is freed when the GPU is past it.

Two ways in (renderer.hpp, under PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL only):
- ui::gpu::create(device, first_slot, back_buffers, images): on a
  gpu_device of the caller's, the back buffers given as its textures.
- ui::gpu::create_d3d12(device, queue, images): on the D3D12 device and
  queue d3d12::create takes, through gpu_d3d12_create_on and
  gpu_d3d12_texture_on (ps3recomp's step V4).

host.cpp's make_renderer takes DES_UI_RENDER=gpu for it in builds with
the route switch, and falls back to D3D12 if it cannot start; without
the variable nothing changes. host.hpp gets an init overload that takes
the renderer from the caller (for a test, and later for the core's own
device). CMake gives host.cpp and render_gpu.cpp the switch's define, and
render_gpu.cpp gpu.h's folder, inside the route switch's block.

With the switch off nothing changes: des_ui's objects built from this

1de3a23e3fb3df7c2ac173f6b7d8f0ab5bbe7a11.message:
Freestanding game module: no C++ exceptions (setup's link, #304)

Setup's link of des_game.dll stops with "undefined symbol:
__CxxFrameHandler3", referenced from the .xdata of ppu_recomp_005, _010
and more (issue #304).

The freestanding module is C++ compiled with /EHsc and linked with
/NODEFAULTLIB: no C runtime, so no C++ unwind handler. That held while no
module function had a local with a destructor. ps3recomp #212 (pinned by
#297) gave every lifted function that calls the guest setjmp a scope
object, ps3_sjlj_scope, whose destructor drops its slots. Under /EHsc
clang has to run that destructor when a call throws, so the 7 chunks with
a setjmp call get __CxxFrameHandler3 as an unwind handler. Every setup
since #297 lifts again and then fails at the link. The single-exe build
links the C runtime and was not affected.

The module never throws or catches, so it is now compiled with C++
exceptions off: /EHs-c- on Windows and -fno-exceptions on Linux, beside
/GR- and -fno-rtti and for the same reason. On Linux the missing names
are __gxx_personality_v0 and _Unwind_Resume, and -z defs fails that link
too. A host longjmp still unwinds through the module's frames by their
unwind tables. The guest-setjmp code does not need the destructor on that
path: the guest longjmp sets the slot list itself, and the thread proc
empties it after a thread exit.

Both game build descriptions gain the flag for the four C++ objects
(ppu, libsre, spu_workloads, des_game_module). The Windows one matches
CMake's commands again (game_build_desc.py --check --commands-only, as
CI's job does). With setup's commands and the pinned clang, the 8 chunks
with the guest setjmp or longjmp no longer need __CxxFrameHandler3
(llvm-nm), and a link of them with game_module and game_libc leaves only
the other chunks' functions and the port's own names undefined. With
master's flags the same link lacks __CxxFrameHandler3, as in the issue.
The Linux objects no longer need __gxx_personality_v0 or _Unwind_Resume.
In chunk 005 only the cleanup paths change: .

played up to again, both kinds of report now hold the save: Report an
issue (the menu) and the crash, hang and lost-graphics dialog's Report on

report::save_files takes each save folder in the game's save root, found
as cellSaveData.c finds it (PS3_SAVEDATA_ROOT, else
gamedata/dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata in the working folder; the
crash dialog's process has the game's environment and working folder).
Each goes in as save/<folder>/<file>. Two kinds of file stay out:

- the folder's two pictures (ICON0.PNG, PIC1.PNG), which are the game's

folder is read again, at most twice and half a second apart. The limits
are 8 MB a file and 32 MB in all; a Demon's Souls save is ten 256 KB
files. game.txt (and the crash issue's System block) gets one line: the
folder, how many files and KB, how many minutes before the report it was
saved, and whether the game was saving meanwhile.

The save holds the characters and their names, and the issue is public.
So the texts that said a report has no save data now say it holds the
save, with the characters' names: the menu's box, the crash dialog's
three, the README and docs/74. The port writes its own PARAM.SFO, so no
PSN account is in it.

28976ab4226b504ec3fd411369e1299fc5cbd7f7.message:
tests: ui_render_compare, the menus drawn by both renderers and compared

render_gpu.cpp's proof. On one D3D12 device (the PC's GPU, or WARP with
--warp) one stream of RmlUi calls feeds four renderers through a tee:
today's (d3d12::create), render_gpu.cpp over the same D3D12 objects
(gpu::create_d3d12, what DES_UI_RENDER=gpu runs), render_gpu.cpp on a
gpu_d3d12_create_on device with the back buffers named as its textures
(gpu::create), and today's once more as a control. After every frame
their pictures are read back and compared byte for byte, and at each
page's end their own read_backs too. Each renderer's command list calls
are counted per page (ui_render_compare_hooks.c patches the list's
vtable), and the counts must be the same.

Pages, 24 frames each by default: the six Settings tabs and the
pre-launch Settings, the five setup screens, a page of rounded clips and
overflow, a filters page (every filter, masks, gradients, so MSAA layers
and resolves) at 1280x720 and at an odd size, and on FP16 scRGB back
buffers the Interface tab, the filters and the clips. With PS3_VFS_ROOT
naming the game's folder, as for a run, also the sword cursor and the
lizard (the game's own textures, read where they are, nothing copied),
in SDR and HDR. The UI's settings and data go to a scratch folder
(--scratch), never the player's.

Some GPUs do not draw the same frame alike every time: on this PC's
NVIDIA GPU today's renderer's two models change by one step at a few
pixels between identical frames, and the control (today's renderer
twice) differs from itself there as much as render_gpu.cpp does. On the
test's still pages a difference only at such pixels is reported as the
GPU's; anywhere else, or on WARP, any byte fails.

Results: on WARP every page 0 differing bytes in every frame, SDR and
HDR, models too. On the GPU every page but the two model pages 0 bytes,
and the model pages differ only where every renderer's own picture,
the control's too, changed between frames. On every page each
renderer's call counts are the same. Exit

Build: DES_SPLIT stops at configure when an SPU native hook is not a host function

The SPU native hooks and blocks in scripts/build_spu.py are runtime
functions the lifted SPU code calls by name. In a split build each one
reaches the game module through PS3_GAME_HOST_FUNCS (ps3recomp's
ps3emu/game_module.h). A name missing there fails only the module's link,
and only a build with the lift links the module (setup's compile on the
player's PC), so #249's spu_hook_entry_scan got through CI.

Configure now reads every "ADDR=SYMBOL" and "ADDR-END=SYMBOL" in
build_spu.py and stops, naming them, when one is not an X(SYMBOL) in the
pinned game_module.h. CI's two build-description jobs configure the split
build, so the next hook that misses the list fails the port's pull request.

Checked with CI's configure (placeholder lift, DES_SPLIT=ON
DES_SPLIT_FREESTANDING=ON): it passes with ps3recomp 92bf11ea, and with the
header before it, it stops on spu_hook_entry_scan.

323bcf2464625a91ecbfab977bbc787395dc779b.message:
UI: the game gets its controls back a second after a menu closes

While a document is up, the game sees neutral pads (cellPad_set_host_hold),
and it got them back only once every key (virtual keys 1-0xFE, mouse
buttons too) and every pad button and stick was at rest. So the press that
closed the menu doesn't reach the game. But a key or pad that reads as
held for good, as a driver can leave one until a restart, kept the
controls from the game for the whole run.

Issue #298: a DualShock 3 on the BthPS3 drivers worked in the start
screen but not in the game. Some starts only; a restart of the PC
fixed it, and so did turning the start screen off. The game's own pad
read saw the pad connected ("keyboard input on port 0 (merged with the
pad)").

- The hold lets go once nothing is held, as before, or a second after
  the last document closed. Then the log names every key held and each
  pad's state ("[ui] the game gets its controls back a second after the
  menu closed, with this still held: ...").
- The menu's copy of pad_hid_sony.h's PadHidSonyState lacked the slot
  byte the runtime added for vibration (10 bytes, not 8). With two or
  more PlayStation pads, the poll wrote past the menu's array and the
  menu read the second pad from the wrong offsets, which could also
  keep the pads from reading as at rest. The copy has the field now, and
  a static_assert checks the size.
- docs/32 says so.

Setup gives the program its icon in Explorer: a render of Soulbrandt

The icon only showed while the program ran, as it was set on the window from the game's ICON0.PNG. A released exe cannot
hold a picture made from the game (docs/51), so setup makes it on the player's PC, at the end of a run:
  - The host draws the sword in software (--icon, souls_icon.cpp), the cursor's look filling the square, thickened at
    small sizes so that it still reads at 16 px. It writes 256 to 16 px frames.
  - If it cannot, the game's own icon (scripts/make_icon.py, the old work, unchanged).
  - A copy of the program gets it as icon resource 1, is started once (--program-check), and takes the program's place.
    A running exe can be renamed, so the old file goes to .update/ and the next start removes it.

It never fails setup, and only touches a player's install (setup/release-info.txt beside the exe). DES_SETUP_ICON=0
leaves the program as it is. Resource 1 also gives the window this icon once setup has run; rsx_window_icon.c's ICON0
path stays for before that.

Stamping the exe would conflict with code signing, if it is ever signed (docs/112 section 7).

A setup from a download ran with it to the level: the program had its icon resources, its .text unmoved.

495bfa2468aa30ee91e7d4fd8c5edeea2f9fe471.message:
tools/testkit: run_tests.sh, the tester kit (docs/128)

bash tools/testkit/run_tests.sh [game folder], from an install. For each
renderer (Linux: vulkan then legacy; Windows: d3d12 then vulkan;
DES_KIT_RENDERERS sets them) the game plays DES_ROUTE=look twice, with an
empty shader cache and then with the one the first run made. Each run plays
from a copy of the tester's save, muted, offline, at the original 30 fps,
with the tester's input left out, and ends itself (DES_KIT_MAX stops it).

It packs des_test_results_<date>.tar.gz: per run the log, shots, route.txt and
summary.json; results.txt (one line a run); system.txt (OS, CPU, RAM, session,
vulkaninfo where installed, each run's route and GPU lines). The shader caches
are deleted first. The home folder, user name and computer name are replaced
in every text file, and if any are left (in any case) nothing is packed.

bash 3.2 and later; no Python, jq or timeout. README.md is for testers.
.gitignore keeps the results folders out.

5e4ba3601888487575b8ee33150828f0ba0eae68.message:
Depth of field and bloom at render scales above 100%

Above 100% (RSX_SCALE), blurred areas showed offset copies and stripes
instead of a smooth blur. The depth of field's 640x360 buffers were scaled
with the scene, but its blur (16 taps, programs B41881 and B41C81) reads at
texture-space offsets one texel apart at the game's size. At 200% the taps
skipped every other texel, and the downsample into the buffer read a quarter
of what it read at 100%.

The game's start now sets RSX_SCALE_MIN=640 (run_defaults), unless the
environment has it. Targets of 640 px or less keep the game's size: in every
capture checked that is only the post chain (depth of field 640x360, bloom
320x180 and 160x90, exposure 64x64 and 16x16). The scene and the shadow
atlas still scale. RPCS3's "Minimum Scalable Dimension" is the same setting.

Checked on a Palace capture, with the composite showing only the blurred
buffer: smooth at 100%, copies and stripes at 200%, smooth again at 200%
with the threshold. The whole frame at 200% stays within 1/255 of 100% on
average. docs/37 has the write-up.

661efe0001e90f2c0a84561182a557867a349074.message:
tools/release: retry the source downloads, and take FFmpeg's from the fork when ffmpeg.org is down

release.yml's "Third-party sources" step downloads vkd3d's and FFmpeg's
source archives fresh every time, one try each. On 2026-11-04 ffmpeg.org
stopped answering, and the release dry run failed on it ("urlopen error
timed out"), so no release could be made until it came back.

Now each address gets three tries (10 s and 30 s apart), then the next
one. FFmpeg's second address is the fork's FFmpeg release
(ffmpeg-8.1.3-2), which attaches the source archive it was built from:
the same bytes (SHA-256 7138d28c..., checked against host.yml's pin).
The SHA-256 still decides, so a copy can't change what ships; the wrong
bytes from one address skip its other tries.

Checked with ffmpeg.org down: three timeouts there, then the fork's
copy, both archives in place, exit 0.

had it already, through clang's intrin.h). The lifter changed, so setup
lifts the game again on the first start after the update.

7c90c40e243e4a553e959d2a3774906f2ca0afaf.message:
port: the sun flare takes the probe's latest count above 30 fps (#290)

The flare's three readers (0x003E2D38, and in 0x003E5750 and 0x003E6368)
read report 1024 only once label 0x52 has reached the probe query's
counter, and otherwise keep the count they have. At 30 fps the RSX has
walked the last probe by the next frame's first check. Above 30 fps the
main thread runs 2-3 probes ahead of it, so the check fails every frame
and the count stays at whatever a rare pass took: the sun through walls,
or gone in the open. A trace at the reported Stonefang spot, uncapped
(about 315 fps), passed the check about once per camera sweep in 130 s.

des_sun_gate runs after each reader's load of the label (insn hooks at
0x003E2DF0, 0x003E6330, 0x003E6518) and raises it to at least the
counter, so the reader takes the latest stored count. With the fix the
held count followed the stored one within one check, at the same frame
rate. Only with DES_FPS; DES_SUNFIX=0 turns it off live. docs/28, "Sun
flare stuck above 30 fps".

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

7ef59983f9e18a6a30a170f4fbbf50dfb90ce379.message:
CI: cache the wrapper UI's FreeType, RmlUi and stb sources

port/ui/CMakeLists.txt clones FreeType, RmlUi and stb by commit, so not
shallow, in every configure of the port or the UI. On #320's run these
configures took 67-102 s each, most of it those clones:

- ci.yml, Linux: Wrapper UI, configure 91 s; Game build description,
  configure 95 s.
- ci.yml, Windows: Configure 67 s.
- host.yml, Windows: Configure des_host 71 s.
- host.yml, Linux: Configure des_host 102 s; the both-routes configure
  clones them again.

Each job now caches a copy of the three without .git, keyed on
port/ui/CMakeLists.txt (one per system), and hands it to the configure
through FetchContent's FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_<NAME>. On a miss, the
configure clones as before and the step after it keeps the copy, which
also serves a second configure in the same job.

tools/ci/fetch_src.py does both halves for every shell:
- "args" prints the -D lines when the copy is complete (its .complete
  file, written last), else nothing, so the configure clones.
- "keep" copies <build>/_deps/<name>-src. It never fails the job: a failed
  copy is removed, so no half copy is saved.

The game build descriptions name none of these sources, so their check
is unaffected.

ui: the menus on the renderer's own GPU device on the new path (overlay v2)

D3D12 device, queue and back buffer, and that route has none. With

to render_gpu.cpp on the core's own gpu_device:

  recorder and the swap image (a CoreFrame as the back buffer); the
  renderer records into it and the core submits it after the frame. A
  read back goes through the core's flush. Fences are gpu_signal's, taken
  in the next frame. Images RmlUi makes with no recorder of the core's
  (its update, or outside any frame) have their copies recorded first
  thing in the next recording. On Vulkan the shaders go through the
  compile service's spv target, the vertex inputs at the locations of
  their order; D32_S8 where the device has no D24S8 depth-stencil.
- des_ui.cpp: on the vulkan route, and on hal-d3d12 with
  DES_UI_RENDER=gpu, the overlay is v2 and the UI starts on create_core.
  On d3d12, and on hal-d3d12 without DES_UI_RENDER=gpu, nothing changes.

9c41cbadc4c000e6e1132849d5d2767928232295.message:
tools/des: halimg compares an HDR snapshot in 8-bit codes when its paper white is known

Under the vk rule an HDRP pair was held to 1e-3, with at most 0.01% of
the pixels allowed up to 8/255 (relative to the larger of 1 and the
value). That bound is in the snapshot's linear units, while the pixels
it is for, ones that sampled the next texel of an 8-bit texture, differ
by a step that grows with the paper white. At the settings a player
uses (RSX_HDR_WHITE=400, scale 300, AA 2, aniso 16) Vulkan's snapshots
of capsetu's courtyard and fog wall failed it with 19 and 119 pixels,
where the frames' own 8-bit shots pass: in codes those pixels are 1 to
5 apart, scattered one by one, nothing above 8.

- halimg.py --hdr-white <paper white, nits / 80> [--hdr-curve
  gamma|srgb]: under vk an HDRP pair is turned back into the codes the
  blit decoded (gamma 2.2, or the sRGB curve for RSX_HDR_GAMMA=1) and
  held to the 8-bit rule, heat map included. A NaN fails. Without it,
  and in the hdr mode, the rule is as it was.
- halgate.sh reads the paper white from A's "HDR snap" line and the
  curve from its "HDR: on" line.
- docs/120's G3 line says so.

The self-test gains the round trips (both curves), 120 pixels 4 codes
off (fails without the white, passes with it), 0.06% of pixels 2 codes
off and 0.02% 12 codes off (fail), the hdr mode and a NaN (fail).

cedeb063a02402a1fd11b6fbfd3d07bc18507ebd.message:
European disc: hook handlers read the instruction at the disc's own address

Six instruction-hook handlers decode the instruction their hook runs after,
to find the register to rescale: the camera eases and the bow zoom
(des_cam_rate, des_cam_step, des_cam_keep), the foot IK (des_ik_rate), the
locked-on twist (des_twist_rate), and the sound and fade rates (keep_rate,
des_fade_rate). They read it at the hook's key, which stays the US address,
so on the European disc they read an unrelated instruction. The camera,
noise and fade fixes did nothing there, and the IK and twist fixes could
rescale an unrelated register.

des_region_addr() gives the running disc's address for a key, and
hook_insn() reads the instruction there. Every hook's instruction is the
same on both discs, so nothing else changes.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

e13baf91ce5a8071202291fc8fd993117ded0ba5.message:
Physics cap: go by the last 8 frames, so 30 fps steps every frame

At 30 fps (Frame rate 30, DES_FPS=30) the game's step is the real frame
time, and frames come a little under and over 1/30 s by turns (44% under,
by at most 0.35 ms, in one run). des_phys_rate tested each frame on its
own: a frame under 1/30 skipped its step (the time it held was still short
of a step), and the next long frame stepped its own dt and dropped that
time. Replaying that run's 2,775 frames through the rule: 33% of the
steps skipped, the world 32% behind game time, and the cap on and off
1,802 times, which turned the in-between poses (DES_RAGINTERP,
DES_PARTINTERP) on and off from frame to frame. Ragdolls, debris and stuck
arrows jittered.

- The cap now goes on when the mean of the last 8 frames is under 0.85/n,
  and off when it is over 0.95/n. At 30 fps it stays off and every frame
  steps its own dt, as the game did. The same frames give 1 skipped step.

e4cc08a9a6ac2614ac9c0dd2e46d0ac466ee474c.message:
A processor without SSE4.1 gets a clear message, not a crash

Issues #349 and #350: a player's Pentium E5400 crashed with c000001d as the window opened. The runtime and the game module
are built with SSE4.1, and that CPU doesn't have it, so the first such instruction ended the program (pmovsxdq in
create_window, rsxc_d3d12.c). The crash dialog then asked them to report it, with nothing saying what was wrong.

des_cpu_check.cpp now asks the processor first, and says so if SSE4.1 is missing. It runs ahead of the C++ static
initializers, and is the one source here built without SSE4.1, so it can run on such a processor. The check comes
before setup too, so nobody spends time on a build that can't run.

AVX, LZCNT, AES and the like in the exe are in Microsoft's runtime and mbedTLS, which ask the CPU before using them. SSE4.1
is the only one the program assumes, so it is the only one checked.

The README now names the requirement. CI runs the check both ways (DES_TEST_OLD_CPU=1, and plainly) on both systems.

There is no processor without SSE4.1 here: the message was checked with DES_TEST_OLD_CPU=1, on the path it takes.

ebd14fd32eec85949fc5ead1ae6460611f8b026f.message:
Port: the viewport command waits for room in the render ring (des_viewport_room)

HighGraphics writes its commands to a 1 MB ring that SPU image 2 reads.
Every writer waits in usleep(30) until its command fits, except the
viewport command's (0x00D22670): with the ring full, or 16 bytes free, it
sleeps once and writes its 32 bytes anyway. On a PS3 image 2 frees the
room in time; here a busy PC can hold image 2's thread for milliseconds,
and the write took put onto get or 16 bytes past it. Every writer's check
then passed, HighGraphics wrote a lap over commands image 2 had not read,
and image 2 halted: the world stopped drawing (soaks at 120 fps on a busy
PC, 2 of 23; with image 2 held up on purpose, an overrun in 5 of 15).

An instruction hook after the sleep (0x00D229A4) sleeps on in the same
usleep(30) while the command does not fit, as the other writers do, and
logs each wait. DES_RINGFIX=0 turns it off. Needs a re-lift (only
ppu_recomp_029.cpp changes). docs/117.

ec1b9e91020e42ece19b1ee2f4fc576991c6c9c1.message:
des_prework: free the last shader pass's texts once it is done

run_passes resets the precompile module before each target's pass, but
not after the last one. So whenever the start's shader pass runs (after a
session that drew new fragment-program variants, or after an update), the
last target's work stays allocated for the rest of the session: every
decompiled HLSL text (3,654 on the US disc, 44 MB), the programs and the
pipeline index's rows.

It now resets after the last pass too. Nothing reads that state after it:
the rows were handed to the renderer during the pass
(rsx_out_pso_index_add, _ready), and run_pass leaves s_state at 3, so
des_prework_status no longer asks for the counts. reset() waits for the
compile threads first.

Found with a scratch walk of the process heap 30 s into the Tutorial
(d3d12, the regression save, DES_PRECOMPILE=force): busy blocks 113.5 MB ->
69.1 MB; text blocks 10,711 (44.0 MB) -> 2,481 (0.3 MB); the heap's
committed regions 81.9 -> 53.8 MB. A start whose passes are all up to date
queued nothing, so it changes nothing there.

1448540658.readme_excerpt:
# Soulbrandt **Demon's Souls, running natively on PC.** [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt?filter=v%2A&sort=semver&display_name=tag&label=release&color=orange)](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases/latest) [![downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/latest/total?label=downloads&color=brightgreen)](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases/latest) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1565536292324769832?label=Discord&logo=discord&logoColor=white&color=5865F2)](https://discord.gg/BzmwDeca8s)
Soulbrandt is a PC port of *Demon's Souls* (PS3, 2009). The game's original code has been converted to run directly on Windows and Linux, with no emulator. You need your own copy of the game: the US version, **BLUS30443** (version 1.00). This project includes no game files. ## Status **0.1.0, the first release, is an alpha.** Download it from the [Releases](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases) page. The game plays from start to finish (a tester has beaten it), but not every part has been tried on every setting, so expect bugs. What [isn't supported yet](#not-supported-yet) is below; please [report](#problems) anything you find. Questions and help: [Discord](https://discord.gg/BzmwDeca8s). ## Highlights - Up to 240 fps or unlocked, with the game's timing fixed. Up to 4K, ultrawide, 16:10 and HDR. - Online play on this project's own server: messages, bloodstains, ghosts, co-op and invasions. - Roll in any direction while locked on, not only forward, back, left or right. - A stat respec in the Nexus (optional): get back the souls your levels cost and spend them again. - Keyboard and mouse, Xbox controllers, DualSense and DualShock 4. ## Features Press **F1** (or **L3 + R3** on a controller) at any time to open the menu. Most settings apply right away. Each setting has a short help text in the menu. **Picture** - Frame rates of 30 (the original), 60, 120, 144, 165 or 240 fps, a number of your own, or unlocked. The game's timing is fixed so it still plays the way it should. Above 60 fps is less tested. - Cutscenes play at 30 fps by default, as they judder above it. You can play them at your frame rate instead. - V-sync on or off, "Even frames" for smooth motion, and G-Sync / FreeSync. - Render resolution up to 300% (4K), ultrawide aspect ratios (21:9 and 32:9), and 16:10 for the Steam Deck's screen. - Anti-aliasing (FXAA or SMAA), anisotropic filtering up to 16x, texture filtering and a sharp scaling filter. - HDR on HDR displays (Windows), with settings for brightness, peak and shadows. - Turn off the game's depth of field and motion blur. - Window or fullscreen (Alt+Enter switches). - Two renderers (Settings > Display > Renderer): DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Windows starts on DirectX 12, Linux on Vulkan. **Controls** - Xbox controllers, DualSense and DualShock 4, over USB or Bluetooth, with vibration. Pick which controller the game uses when several are connected. - Keyboard and mouse, laid out like the Souls games on PC. To turn the camera with the mouse, turn on **Mouse look** in Settings > Controls. - Change which buttons and keys do what. - Mouse sensitivity, inverted axes, and switching lock-on targets with a flick of the mouse. - **Roll in any direction while locked on**: the roll goes where the stick points. It's on by default; turn off **Roll toward the stick** in Settings > Controls for the original's four directions. - The mouse in the game's own menus: point and click. Experimental, and off by default. **HUD** - Move, resize, hide or show each part of the HUD. - Change its size, and choose where it goes on wide screens. **Game** - Skip the logos and the opening movie, and go straight into your last save. - **Stat respec**: the Maiden in Black, or the statue in front of where you wake in the Nexus, puts your stats back to your class's and gives back the souls your levels cost, to spend again. Off by default: turn on **Stat respec in the Nexus** in Settings > Game. - Use several soul items at once, as Drop does. On by default: turn off **Use several souls at once** in Settings > Game for the original's one at a time. **Online** - On by default, on this project's own server: messages, bloodstains, ghosts, co-op and invasions. - Setup asks for your online name. You can change it, or turn online play off, in Settings > Network. - A matchmaking password, so you meet only your friends. - Show or hide other players' messages, bloodstains and ghosts. **The program** - A setup that builds the game from your copy, with an Original and an Enhanced preset (see [How to play](#how-to-play)). - Updates: the game checks for a new version at start and asks before changing anything. Your saves and settings are kept, and you can go back one version. - In the menu, the Large Sword of Moonlight is the cursor and a crystal lizard dances in the corner. Both can be turned off. - Trophies, with pop-ups. Setup can bring your trophies and save across from RPCS3. - **Report an issue** in the menu opens a GitHub issue with your PC's details filled in, and a zip to attach that includes your save, so the problem can be seen where it happened. It has no game files. If the game crashes or stops responding, a window offers to do the same. ## What you need - Your own copy of Demon's Souls for the PS3, US version (BLUS30443, version 1.00), as a folder with `PS3_GAME` in it. Setup cannot use ISO files yet. - RPCS3, the free PS3 emulator, with the PS3 system software installed (4.93, the version Sony offers now). Setup has it unlock the game's encrypted files. (Or decrypt the files yourself: see below.) - Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) with a graphics card that supports DirectX 12, or Linux (see [Linux](#linux)). - A processor with SSE4.1, which most have since about 2011. - An internet connection during setup. Setup downloads a compiler and Python (about 60 MB on Windows, about 130 MB on Linux). ## How to play These steps are for the release download. 1. Download the zip for Windows (`DemonsSoulsRecomp-X.Y.Z-windows.zip`) or the tarball for Linux (`DemonsSoulsRecomp-X.Y.Z-linux.tar.xz`), and unpack it into a folder of its own. 2. Start `Soulbrandt.exe` (on Linux, `Soulbrandt`). Setup opens. 3. Pick how setup gets your game's files: - **Import from RPCS3**: setup finds the game in RPCS3's list and has your RPCS3 unlock its files. It can bring your save, trophies and some settings across too. - **I have decrypted files**: your disc copy, plus the 28 files you decrypted yourself (`EBOOT.elf`, the `.sdat` files and `libsre.prx`). - **Show me how**: step by step, with free tools only. 4. Start the build. It runs on your PC and can take a while; setup shows an estimate first. You can stop it and carry on later. Setup builds in AppData on Windows (`~/.local/share` on Linux) and needs about 4 GB free there; to build on another drive, press **Change** next to **Build folder** first. 5. Pick a preset: **Original** plays as on the PS3; **Enhanced** sets 60 fps, a resolution that fits your display, SMAA, 16x anisotropic filtering, fullscreen, and HDR when Windows has HDR on for your display. Then a few choices (HDR among them, on Windows) and your online name. You can change anything later in Settings. Then press **Play**. Windows may warn you the first time you start `Soulbrandt.exe` ("Windows protected your PC"), because the program isn't signed yet. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If setup says your `libsre.prx` came out different, your RPCS3 probably has PS3 system software 4.90. Install 4.93 in RPCS3 (*File > Install Firmware*) and try again. If RPCS3 is set to run as administrator, setup cannot start it: untick that in `rpcs3.exe`'s Properties. ### Linux CI builds the Linux program on every change, and each release includes a Linux download. It needs x86-64 Linux with glibc 2.35 or newer, a Vulkan driver, and `curl` and `tar`. Nothing else needs installing. The game renders on Vulkan, and setup prepares its shaders. If Vulkan can't start, the game falls back to its older renderer on vkd3d (DirectX 12 on Vulkan), which compiles shaders as it goes, with long pauses when a new area loads. Linux is newer and less tested than Windows. So far it has run in WSL (Ubuntu 24.04) and, on the older renderer, on one Steam Deck. The Vulkan renderer hasn't run on a real Linux graphics driver yet ([docs/106](docs/106-setup-on-linux.md)). macOS is not supported. On a Steam Deck, keys and the mouse stay out of the game while its controls are on, because Steam's desktop layout presses them too. To use a keyboard on a docked Deck, set `PAD_KEYBOARD_WITH_PAD=1`. ### Online play Online play is on by default and uses this project's own server. Setup asks for your online name; you can change it, or turn online play off, in Settings > Network. RPCS3 players use other servers, so you won't meet them. What the server keeps about you is in the [privacy note](PRIVACY.md). ### Not supported yet - Only the US version (BLUS30443) works. The European version is being looked at; other versions are not supported. - Setup can't read ISO files, and it needs RPCS3 to unlock the game's files (or files you decrypted yourself). - macOS isn't supported, and running the Windows download through CrossOver hasn't been tested all the way through. Linux is less tested than Windows, and the Steam Deck has had one test so far. - On-screen button prompts always show PlayStation buttons, even with a keyboard or an Xbox controller. ### Problems Use **Report an issue** in the menu (F1), or open an [issue](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/issues). For questions and help, join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/BzmwDeca8s). Report security problems privately, as [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) says. ## Building from source This is the technical part. The full notes are in [`docs/`](docs/). **Tools** | Windows | Linux | |---|---| | Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, LLVM (clang), CMake, Ninja, Python 3, Git Bash | clang or GCC, CMake, Ninja, Python 3, SDL2, Vulkan and FFmpeg development files, vkd3d ([details](docs/76-native-linux.md#building)) | On Windows, step 4 downloads FFmpeg's MPEG-2 video decoder for the game's movies (about 1 MB) and puts it beside `des_boot.exe`. If that download fails, the build says so and goes on, and the movies then need Microsoft's free [MPEG-2 Video Extension](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9n95q1zzpmh4) from the Microsoft Store; without either, they play their sound with no picture. (A paid app called "MPEG-2 Video Extensions", from another publisher, is a different thing; you don't need it.) **From your copy of the game** - The game disc's files (`PS3_GAME`) - [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), to decrypt the game's `EBOOT.BIN` - `libsre.prx` from your PS3 firmware, decrypted **Steps** 1. Get this repository, and its runtime inside it: ```sh git clone https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt.git cd Soulbrandt git clone https://github.com/JonathanDC64/ps3recomp.git ``` `ps3recomp.pin` names the ps3recomp commit this version of the port needs. `python tools/release/pin_ps3recomp.py local` checks your checkout against it. 2. In RPCS3, decrypt `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` (*Utilities > Decrypt PS3 Binaries*) to `work/game/EBOOT.ELF`. Copy `PS3_GAME/ICON0.PNG` next to it, for the program's icon. 3. Convert the game's main code: ```sh python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_loader.py work/game/EBOOT.ELF -o work/loader python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_lifter.py work/game/EBOOT.ELF \ --functions work/loader/EBOOT.functions.json --hle-stubs work/loader/EBOOT.imports.json \ --override-funcs "0x167AC88=ds_malloc,0x167AC58=ds_free,0x273D38=des_move_post,0x724E40=des_menu_tick" \ --insn-hooks @port/insn_hooks.txt --shadow-stack --chunk-lines 150000 --output work/recomp -j 16 python ps3recomp/tools/gen_hle_nids.py --all --out work/recomp/hle_nid_table.cpp python scripts/apply_boot_patches.py work/recomp ``` Then the SPU code with `python scripts/build_spu.py --eboot work/game/EBOOT.ELF` ([docs/09](docs/09-spu-spurs.md)), which first cuts the SPU programs out of the EBOOT, and libsre with `python scripts/build_libsre.py `. The lifter's flags above are also in `scripts/lift_ppu.json`, which setup reads; change both together. 4. Compile the runtime, then the game. On Windows: ```sh cmake -S ps3recomp -B ps3recomp/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \ -DPS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL=ON cmake -S port -B port/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl \ -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE= -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG= -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS_DEBUG= cmake --build ps3recomp/build --target ps3recomp_runtime rsx_shader_precompile cmake --build port/build --target des_boot --parallel 4 ``` `PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL=ON` builds the portable renderer: DirectX 12 through it, the default, and Vulkan beside it (Settings > Display > Renderer). Without it the game runs on the legacy renderer only. Its first configure downloads glslang and SPIRV-Tools at their pinned commits. On Linux, see [docs/76](docs/76-native-linux.md#building). 5. Copy `tools/des/local.env.example` to `tools/des/local.env`, set `PS3_VFS_ROOT` in it to the folder that holds `PS3_GAME`, and start the game with `tools/des/play.sh`. A direct start of `des_boot.exe` goes through setup instead, and keeps its saves in `port/build/gamedata`. Everything made from your copy of the game stays in `work/` and `gamedata/`, which git ignores. **Never share your build:** it contains code converted from your game. **For developers** - Each setting's help text ends with its name in brackets, such as `(DES_FPS)`. The same name works as an environment variable, which wins over the menu. - `-DDES_SPLIT=ON` also builds the game the way setup does: `des_host` plus the game as a separate library ([docs/57](docs/57-dll-split.md)). - `-DDES_DEV=ON` makes a developer build, with cheats and a Developer tab in Settings ([docs/55](docs/55-dev-cheats.md)). Never share one as a release. - The renderer is the portable one ([docs/120](docs/120-portable-renderer.md)): DirectX 12 by default, or Vulkan in Settings > Display > Renderer, then restart. If Vulkan fails to start, the game runs on DirectX 12 and says why. `RSX_BACKEND=legacy` runs the renderer from before it: retired, kept unchanged as a fallback, with no more fixes. A build has it when its ps3recomp is configured with `PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL=ON`, as in the steps above and in the released Windows build. ## Legal This project contains only its own code, scripts and documentation. 08cff3eb84efc2fd3c22811bb5632c00f0d5f0e6.message:
platform: plat.h's threads and events, and the SPU job pool on every platform

The async SPU job pool was Windows-only. Off Windows every async job
created a detached pthread with a 256 MB stack and let it exit:
Demon's Souls runs about 650 of them a second, so Linux and macOS paid a
thread start, a cold stack and cold caches per job.

runtime/platform/plat.h is the start of the platform module: detached
threads with a stack reservation, the stack guarantee, the calling
thread's stack range, an auto-reset event with a timed wait, and a small
mutex. On Windows each call is the Win32 call it stands for, inline;
off Windows it is pthreads directly (plat_posix.c), not the Win32 shim.

The pool moves to runtime/spu/spu_async_pool.c, written once on plat.h,
with the same rules: no queue and no cap, idle workers exit after 5 s or
at once beyond 64 idle, image 22 gets its own thread, SPU_ASYNC_POOL=0
makes a thread per job. On Windows the worker and the dispatch make the
same Win32 calls in the same order; the job now runs through one
function call instead of being inlined into the worker. Linux and macOS
also run the stack-range forget calls after each job now, as Windows did.

tests/plat_threads checks the events, the mutex, the stack range, 256 MB
reservations and the pool (8000 jobs from four threads on a handful of
workers, the idle exit, the idle limit, the own-thread rule, pool off).
It passes on Windows (clang-cl) and Linux (gcc, clang, and clang's
thread sanitizer). The game itself has not been run on this change yet.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

0bd6d3aff562164d9e64b70cb4d10714005adbdf.message:
rsxcore: the index buffer starts at 4M indices, so a heavy load frame stays on the fetch path

The RAM steps saved 986 MB at the regression save and 996 MB at 2-2, but
only 486 MB on the 1-2 bridge. The fetch path's index buffer (vp_ib) is
not in chunks: it starts at 1M indices and grows at a frame's end. The
bridge's load frame wanted up to 3.7M, so once the buffer was full the
fetch path refused the rest. Those draws went down the CPU path,
unindexed, and the vertex buffer made 9 chunks for them (576 MB), which
it keeps for the device's life.

vp_ib now starts at 4M indices (32 MB for both halves, 24 MB more than
before). VP_IB_INDICES sets the first size. legacy keeps 1M.

0d8517bcc0e314774220ffc78108825d5e39af12.message:
psnr: dial again when the connection is lost

The connection to psnr was made once a run (s_tried). When it was lost, as
when the server restarts for a deploy or the network drops, co-op and
invasions stayed off until the player restarted the game: the context
stayed "started" and every request failed with SERVER_NOT_AVAILABLE, and
no event told the title to start it again.

Now a connection that was up and is lost is dialled again on a thread of
its own: after 2 s, then 4, 8, 16 and 30, then every 60 s, until it
connects, psnr turns the sign-in or the name away, or the run is locked
offline. Dialling blocks (TCP, TLS, the HELLO: about 21 s with the network
gone), so it never runs on the title's thread. The title's context stays
started, and its requests go through again once the connection is back. A
"name taken" or "refused" answer is tried again: our own old connection
holds the name until the server notices it is gone, and maintenance ends.

PSNR_REDIAL=0 keeps one connection a run, as before. PSNR_REDIAL_MS sets
the first wait (the test uses 50 ms).

The dial (with the sign-in's one retry) moved into dial(), which the first
connection and the redial share. A lost connection also probes its P2P
address again on the next one. Its requests are taken all at once before
their handlers run, so a redial that connects meanwhile doesn't have its
own requests failed with them.

test_np_psnr_notice: a psnr that drops the connection right after its
welcome. With PSNR_REDIAL=0 it stays gone; with the redial it is back
after one try, and a context start finds it up.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

11420be13c03f99353b29820d40ff56ed731bf6d.message:
gpu_shader: the vertex fetch clamp (E3) only where robustness2 is missing

E3 clamps every vertex fetch load to t20 in the shader, so a read past its
end gives 0 as on D3D12. A device with robustBufferAccess2, which the
Vulkan backend turns on when it can, already gives that 0, so on such a
device the clamp is only extra ALU in every guest vertex shader.

The compile service now leaves E3 out unless the backend asks for it with
the new option GPU_SC_SPV_FETCH_CLAMP. The core sets it when the device has
no GPU_CAP_ROBUST2 (or RSX_VK_MASK masks it). The edit changes the text, so
the cache key records E3's version as 0 without it, and the two forms never
share a file. Setup's pass makes the form without the clamp.

Measured on the capset0 courtyard replay (RTX 5070 Ti, GPU timestamps, PC
unlocked so indicative): 850 -> 836 us of GPU time per recording, lower in
3 of 3 pairs. Images are byte-identical with and without the clamp.
test_gpu_vk's fetch-bounds check now runs both forms.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

13271a687011265eb2b4ddc8fc32a1bc8e218902.message:
spurs: LIBSRE_TRACE, a trace of the SPURS queue calls

LIBSRE_TRACE=<file> writes a record for each call of the LFQueue and
SpursQueue functions (initialize, attach, detach, the LFQueue push, the
SpursQueue pop) and of cellSyncLFQueueGetDirection, whether the loaded
libsre or the HLE serves it: the arguments, the return value, the time
the call took, the queue's 128-byte line as the call starts and the
words of it that changed by the end, and for a push or a pop the entry
and the buffer slot it matches. While such a call runs, the lv2 syscalls
and the other imports its thread makes are recorded with their results.
Every SPU PUTLLC or PUTLLUC that changes one of the queue lines is
recorded too, with the task's image and lr, and every 5 s each line's
SPU stores and failed PUTLLCs are counted. LIBSRE_TRACE_MAX caps the
records (default 2000000). The format is at the top of
libs/spurs/libsre_trace.c.

It is for writing our own version of these functions: the trace of the
loaded libsre is the behaviour to match, and the same trace of ours is
the comparison. Off, it costs one load and branch per HLE call and one
per syscall and SPU atomic store (two hooks, g_ppu_sc_watch in
ppu_loader.cpp and g_spu_line_store_watch in spu_channels.c, null
unless the trace is on).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

1364742b80d23676034e92e98942381fccb0e80e.message:
rsxcore: size the shared depth buffer to the targets bound with it, growing when a larger one shows up

The shared depth buffer (what the display buffers, offscreen targets drawn
without a guest depth surface and depth-only passes without one bind) was made
once at rt_host_dim(2048) square, the largest target a guest can declare: at
RSX_SCALE=300 6144x6144, a 180 MB block of commit and video memory, while the
largest target ever bound with it in Demon's Souls is the 1280x720 scene
(3840x2160 there). docs/124 "After #227".

It now starts at the display buffers' size, and depth_buffer_fit (rsxc_targets)
grows it after each frame's pre-pass, before the frame's first bind of it, to
cover the display and every offscreen target, so no pass is ever cropped (D3D12
clips to the smallest attachment, Vulkan's render area is the smallest's). The
old one goes into the grave. A growth is one depth texture's creation, no copy
(every bind of the buffer to other targets clears it; nothing samples it) and
no wait; it never shrinks, so it happens at most a few times a run and again
after an RSX_SCALE change, which starts it at the display size. The shadow
pass's own zeta (2048x2048, scaled with RSX_SCALE) is unchanged.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

18075dc500c3ec4f69217ed177fa375608e86d77.message:
spu: the ring post's prologue stores in straight line

The native ring post (ring_post_run, image 2's 0x4808-0x4818) writes the
13 quadwords 0x3C90's prologue stores into the SPU frame, then the segment
quadword. It did so in a loop over k_post_slot / k_post_reg through
spu_ls_write128, which reloaded ctx->ls and tested the LS-probe flag for
each one, every command: 3.9% of image 2 in an instruction profile of the
deep Palace, the largest single piece of ring_loop.

Now they are 14 straight stores (ls_put128): the same bytes, in the same
order, at the same addresses. Both callers run the post only while
g_spu_ls_dbg is 0 (spu_hook_ring_post's entry test, ring_loop's
loop_yield), and sp has passed the frame checks, so every slot is in local
store and no probe has to see the stores.

SPU_POST_FAST (live): 1 (default) the straight stores; 0 the table loop as
before; 2 the straight stores, then every slot checked against the table
loop's bytes (no check covered these slots: SPU_NATIVE_POST=2 checks the
recorded path, SPU_NATIVE_LOOP=2 leaves the frame out).

Deep Palace, DES_FPS=unlocked, vsync off, knobab plain windows, on master
+ #157 + #158 + #159, session locked: SPU_POST_FAST=0 is 3.91% slower
(193.42 vs 201.28 fps, 4 boots, 12 pairs, p < 0.001), so about +4.1%.
soak.sh with SPU_POST_FAST=2: kept flipping for 6 minutes (43,007 flips by
361 s), 1,073,741,824 posts checked, 0 differ. regress.sh: 4 of 4 shots ok.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

1be0a91618a66be172d2dcf001f30794f2e1d806.message:
ppu: a run of frame saves shares one stack test

The lifter writes a store with base r1 as vm_write*_stk, which tests the
address against the stack limit, stores, and keeps a slow path behind
the test. A function's prologue is a run of such stores (Demon's Souls'
func_00CFEC70 saves 17 registers in a row), and each one reloads the
limit, r1 and vm_base, because the store before it, made through
vm_base, may alias any of them. That is about ten instructions a store.

ppu_lifter.py now writes a run of three or more of them (one store of a
GPR per line, nothing between them) under one test: vm_stk_run gives
the host address of the run's lowest byte when every byte it stores
would take vm_write*_stk's direct store, and the stores then go through
that pointer (vm_stk_put*, big-endian, as the direct store); otherwise
the run's lines run as before. In Demon's Souls' lift: 47,482 runs in
94,017 functions. With each run put back as its else block, every
function is the same as the lift before.

vm_stk_run reads its own limit, the third word on the armed flag's line
(game_module.c's copy too): the stack limit, or 0 while PPU_STK_RUN=0
(live), which sends every run through vm_write*_stk one by one. It reads
the limit once for the run where each store read it before. A first SPU
reservation of a stack line between the run's test and its stores is
missed, as a store that read the limit just before it already could.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

video: give border-addressed samplers the guest's border colour

TEXTURE_BORDER_COLOR was tracked but never reached a sampler: every border
address mode read transparent black. Demon's Souls samples its shadow atlas
with a border address mode and a white border (0xFFFFFFFF), so a lookup past
the atlas's edge should read depth 1.0 (lit), not 0 (shadowed).

The draw record now carries each unit's border colour, and the sampler key
holds it as a third word per unit when an axis uses the border (0 otherwise,
so other units share tables as before). It is decoded as ARGB8, as RPCS3
does. The HAL path sets gpu_sampler_desc.border the same way. On D3D12 that
is the sampler's BorderColor; Vulkan takes the nearest of its three fixed
colours by RPCS3's rule, which is exact for the colours the game uses, and
the static samplers now share that rule.

No visible change in the captures checked: a Palace passage replays the same
with and without it, so the lookups there stay inside the atlas.
