1e58d25421fa0fa5cdc0faae34975053122d1621.message:
gpu: the Vulkan backend for the portable renderer's GPU layer

The GPU layer's second backend, beside D3D12's, built with
PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL and PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL_VULKAN (on by default on
Windows and Linux; nothing changes with the HAL off).

- gpu_vk.c: the instance and device (Vulkan 1.3 with dynamic
  rendering, synchronization2, timeline semaphores and partially
  bound descriptors), adapter choice (WARP means a CPU device such as
  lavapipe), caps, handle tables, recorders, the timeline as every
  fence, submits, the fault report. RSX_VK_VALIDATION=1 turns the
  validation layer on; RSX_VK_MASK turns caps off to run fallbacks.
- gpu_vk_mem.c: buffers, host import, heaps and placed textures,
  D3D12's copyable footprints, first layouts, frees after a fence.
- gpu_vk_desc.c: views, samplers, table pools (one set per table),
  the memo, set 0's cache, empty entries (null descriptors, or 1x1
  textures without them).
- gpu_vk_pipe.c: layouts, pipelines (a fixed table: gpu_pipeline.v is
  its index + 1), the pipeline cache file.
- gpu_vk_swap.c: swap chains, presents (FIFO and IMMEDIATE, switched
  per present with swapchain_maintenance1), present_wait statistics,
  colour spaces and HDR metadata.
- gpu_vk_cmd.h: every command static inline onto the VkCommandBuffer
  through volk's device table; lazy passes; one bind of every set per
  draw.
- third_party/volk at the Vulkan SDK 1.4.363.0 pin, and the pinned
  Vulkan-Headers from cmake/gpu_deps.cmake.
- test_gpu_vk: test_gpu_d3d12's cases on Vulkan with the validation
  layer on (any message fails it), each fallback checked by its cap,
  the footprints against D3D12's, and the test's own HLSL compiled
  with glslangValidator (test_gpu_vk_spv.h says how).

Contract changes (gpu.h, gpu_cmd_ops.h; D3D12's numbers kept):
- swap_image_count and swap_image(d, sc, index): every swap chain
  image by index, valid until the next resize or destroy, for making
  the views up front (C1's gap). Vulkan may make more images than
  asked, so per-image arrays take swap_image_count.

253d83c5c244dcb67a0f021bca6a40dc7c64180a.message:
spu: image 2's empty ring waits on put alone before the lifted wait (SPU_RING_WAIT)

When the ring is empty, the fetch now reads only the producer's put word,
with a pause between reads that doubles up to SPU_RING_WAIT (default 16),
for up to 64 reads, and takes the command as soon as put moves. Then the
lifted wait runs as before. The lifted wait is a GETLLAR, the lock-line
event read and a GETLLAR again, back to back, each a copy or compare of
the control line, so every poll takes the line from HighGraphics, which
holds the frame in the deep Palace. The run's deferred state PUT goes out
before the wait, as on every way out of the loop. SPU_RING_WAIT=0 gives
the empty ring to the lifted code at once.

In the deep Palace, uncapped, in-boot A/Bs (4 boots, 12 pairs each): the
wait at 64 against none +0.7% (p 0.009, every boot), +1.8% on a build
where image 2 is faster (p < 0.001); 16 against 64 +1.1% (p 0.11) and
+1.4% (p 0.008), every boot in both batches; 64 against 256 +1.2%; 4 even
with 64. So the default is 16.

test_spu_ring_lazy varies the knob, moves put during some waits (at the
same read in both runs) and checks that the state is PUT before each wait.

2b3d6ae98c69d5537d3f828d1b146ddca795b86e.message:
rsxcore: the core on Vulkan, RSX_BACKEND=vulkan (step VC1)

rsxc_vk.c is the core's third instance, on gpu_vk*.c, in builds with
PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL_VULKAN (Windows for now). rsx_out.c routes
RSX_BACKEND=vulkan to it and prints "[rsx_out] route vulkan (the new path
on its Vulkan backend)"; a build without it runs d3d12 as for any other
name. It is for developers' A/Bs: not in Settings, and the menu does not
draw on it yet (no D3D12 device, queue or back buffer for the overlay).

Its hooks: shaders are the compile service's spv target, with the
post-pass options the device has (no denorm or signed-zero preserve where
the device lacks them); no pipeline library and none of today's cache
files (rc_be_cache_files 0, as on null: pso_manifest.bin's records are
D3D12 pipeline descriptions); device lost through gpu_vk_lost_note, and
RSX_VK_BREADCRUMBS for the hint.

Two things the core needed for it, the same on D3D12 and null:
- Shaders by layout: sc_compile takes the layout a shader is for
  (sc_shader_for; sc_shader is the guest's), since SPIR-V's bindings follow
  the layout. The blits, AA, SMAA and the write-back downscale fill their
  gpu_layout_desc before they compile; the layouts are made where they
  were. rc_be_sc_compile takes it; dxbc and null do not use it.
- The frame slot and the swap image: a Vulkan swap chain may have more
  images than FRAME_COUNT and hands them out in any order, so the image
  the last acquire gave (s_rc_image) and the slot the per-frame resources
  use (s_d3d.frame_index) are two numbers, taken by rc_acquire through the

2f395ce2c876ef8896ed06cde5b816891606d775.message:
rsx: the 2D engine's inline writes sync only where they land on a copied page

Every 2D-engine method was a sync point (g_rsx_sync_hook): it finished the
queued vertex copies on the FIFO thread and ended the copy table's
stretch. Demon's Souls patches fragment program constants with inline
transfers (NV308A), one method per 4-byte word: about 9,200 sync calls a
frame on the 1-2 bridge, 3,200 at the 2-2 Patches area. The 120 a frame
that found copies queued cost the FIFO thread about 1 ms a frame there,
and every one cut the stretch the copy table reuses copies in.

A 2D write is no fence for the RSX's vertex reads: on the PS3 the 3D pipe
may still be reading earlier draws' vertices when it lands, so a title
can't rely on one to reuse vertex memory. What the write must not do is
change bytes a queued copy has yet to read, or that a later draw would
take from the table. So:

- g_rsx_sync_write_hook (new, rsx_commands.c) is called before an inline
  COLOR word's write, with its address. With it set, the 2D methods that
  write no memory (the surface and transfer setup) don't sync at all, and
  the scaled blit's trigger and unhandled methods sync as before.
- The backend tags each 64 KB guest page a span copy reads with the
  stretch (vf_copy). The write hook syncs and ends the stretch only if the
  word lands on a page of this stretch, or while a CPU-path vertex job is
  queued, whose reads aren't tracked.
- VF_SYNC_2D (live, default 1); 0 syncs at every inline word, as before.

The portable renderer's core gets the same change (rsxc_state.inc,
rsxc_vertex.inc).

On Demon's Souls (#213 in, knobab.sh, one exe, B = VF_SYNC_2D=0, 3 boots
each, ABBAAB), on top of the first commit:

- 1-2 bridge, render scale 300: 195.2 -> 201.8 fps (+3.4%, 9 of 9 pairs);
- 2-2 Patches area, scale 100: 237.1 -> 245.4 fps (+3.5%, 9 of 9 pairs);
- with the second commit's page lookup in too, the same A/B: bridge
  206.5 -> 209.2 fps (+1.3%, 9 of 9 pairs), Patches 258.1 -> 266.3 fps
  (+3.2%, 9 of 9 pairs). The page lookup leaves fewer copi

30a2484c5aeb5d0e395bead5f9d9a90cc02f7e60.message:
rsxcore: the clamp in the vertex shader and D32S8 depth (step V5)

Two forms for GPUs that lack a feature, picked when the device is made
(rc_forms_pick). With neither knob set, on a device with geometry shaders
and D24S8, every changed line does what it did.

RSX_CLAMP_FORM=gs|vs (default gs where the device has GPU_CAP_GS): the
sprite-edge clamp without a geometry shader. Kind 4 of rsxc_shader.c
(rsxc_vs_inject_uvclamp; kinds 4 and 5 of rsxc_shader_hlsl, from kinds 0
and 2) renames the program's main and adds an entry point that runs the
program on all three corners of its triangle and hands the pixel shader
uvclamp_gs's bounds from every corner. The pixel shader is kind 3's, as
before. The frame's pre-pass writes a table of each clamp draw's corners
(uvc_table: three vertex numbers a triangle, in the order the input
assembler gives a geometry shader, after the frame's data in vp_vb or
vf_buf), and the draw loop draws it as a list of 3n vertices with t20 on
that ring. A program's kind 4 is made at its first clamp draw from a copy
of its bytes (VPVSEntry.vs4). vp_vb is a raw buffer too in that form.

RSX_DEPTH_FORMAT=d24s8|d32s8 (default d24s8 where the device has
GPU_CAP_D24S8): the depth buffer, the zeta surfaces, their depth read as a
texture and every pipeline's depth format are D32S8. No shader changes:
rsx_d2c rounds the sampled float to 24 bits, and nothing writes depth back
to guest memory.

With either form the pipelines are ones the d3d12 route never makes, so
none goes into pso_manifest.bin (that route's file too); the pipeline
library keeps them. copy_manifest.txt says what changed.

3cd463b960a5cbf768cbc2c6bf3a11930d7d56f4.message:
spu: the stripe lock takes one line's stripe in line (SPU_LL_ONE_LINE)

Every guest store into a reserved line takes and releases that line's
stripe (spu_lockline_lock_ea, spu_lockline_unlock_ea). In Demon's Souls the
HighGraphics ring's producer makes about 5 million of those stores a second,
and almost all of them stay inside one 128-byte line. Yet each one paid for
the general case:

- spu_ll_set's walk over the lines a range touches, which clang vectorizes,
  so both functions saved five xmm registers on entry (Win64 makes xmm6-15
  callee-saved) and restored them on the way out;
- spu_ll_acquire's frame for the lock statistics (a stack cookie, the
  pushes), with the statistics off.

That was most of the lock's time outside its two locked instructions.

Now a range in one line takes its stripe in line: a lock bts, and the
lock inc to release it. The rest (a stripe that is held, ranges over several
lines, SPU_LOCKLINE_STATS) goes to out-of-line functions with the old code,
so their frames are paid only there. Both paths take the same stripes in
the same order, so SPU_LL_ONE_LINE (live; 0 sends everything through the
out-of-line paths, for A/B) can change between a lock and its unlock.

4ae6477e29bc1a3ffa90dbf1dc31a322e79b326b.message:
rsx: a fetch span that a copy of the same stretch holds points into it

The GPU fetch path copies each new descriptor's spans of guest vertex
bytes into the fetch ring. A mesh drawn in several passes (depth, shadow
cascades, the main pass) was copied once per pass: on Demon's Souls' 1-2
bridge the copies came to 114 MB a frame, most of them bytes already
copied earlier in the same stretch of the stream, and they were a third
of the FIFO thread, which is what holds the frame rate there.

A table of the stretch's copies (256 sets of 4, by guest start) now
answers a new descriptor's span that starts where a copy starts and ends
inside it, and the descriptor points at that copy instead of copying the
bytes again. A stretch ends at each point where the title can see the RSX
move on (g_rsx_sync_hook: labels, semaphores, reports, the reference, the
2D engine, the end of a drain pass) and at each frame's ring reset.
Within a stretch the title can't know the RSX has read a range, so it
can't have rewritten it either; the copy queue already relies on that
rule, since its copies run some time before the next sync point.

- A copy grows its entry with what later draws of its descriptor append
  to it.
- A descriptor that points at a copy takes all of it, so the next pass's
  draws that continue the first find their ranges there, with no new
  descriptor. It can't append to that copy (its own header follows it).
- The continue path tries every span when one gives another place for an
  array, since a whole copy can overlap the descriptor's other spans, and
  a span inside an earlier span of the same descriptor takes that one's
  place. Each array's x is taken from its span's place.
- The sync hook is now set with or without vertex workers, so the same
  draws give the same descriptors either way (test_rsx_synth's second
  process runs VP_FETCH_THREADS=0). With nothing queued, vpj_sync returns
  at once.
- VF_ONCE (live, default 1); 0 copies per descriptor, as before.
  VF_ONCE_CHECK=1 (debug, slow) compares each reused range

256) took the CPU path, on the rule that copying the guest's vertex
bytes over [lo, hi] would cost more than converting the vertices. The
CPU path writes 256 bytes a vertex and converts every attribute; the
copy is the guest's own bytes, tens a vertex, and the next ranges of the
same mesh usually reuse it. Demon's Souls draws its level meshes as
256-index ranges of one BEGIN/END, and in the deep Palace the rule left
64,500 vertices a frame (17 MB into the upload heap) to the CPU. At 64,
10,800 are left (no limit at all: 10,000).

4fc6cd17edd10214bd1bba6df557bcb2af5d32f4.message:
spu: the scan block's check mode puts the state back and counts only calls that skip

Two faults in SPU_NATIVE_SCAN=2, the scan block's check against the SPU
interpreter (#170). Neither touches modes 0, 1 or 3.

A mismatch turned the block off for the session but left that call's state
as the block had left it: its registers and step count, and its done flag
as the return. So a wrong result went on into the lifted code. The check
now saves the registers and the step count before the block runs; on a
mismatch it puts them back (and local store from the interpreter's copy,
taken before the block ran; the loop stores nothing) and returns 0, so the
lifted loop runs those entries.

Every SPU_NATIVE_SCAN_EVERY-th call was checked, but a call whose first
entry goes to a handler skips nothing, so the check compared nothing and
the tick was used up: fewer calls were compared than the knob said. Now
only calls that skip an entry count, and a check that found nothing to
compare is tried again at the next call.

5e1c9b1c7496fa1b34e362d92c106d97ff0fe0de.message:
rsx_d3d12: SMAA's edge pass binds no table holding its own target

SMAA's three passes read their textures through two 3-entry windows of
the SRV heap. The edge pass's window (SMAA_SRV_SLOT + 0..2) held the
edges target it draws into, at + 2, so a texture of the bound table was
in RENDER_TARGET at the draw. D3D12 allows a descriptor of a resource in
another state only while the shader doesn't read it, and drivers that
check descriptors at bind (as Vulkan's do) can object; the portable
renderer's null backend reported it once a frame.

The edges, AreaTex and SearchTex move up one (+ 3..5, the weight pass's
window); + 2 keeps the heap's null view. The weights, in the edge and
blend passes' window, are made readable before the edge pass too (they
are made as a target; from the second run on the blend pass leaves them
readable, so there is no barrier then). Each pass reads the same
textures at the same registers, so the picture is the same.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

63cca9d973b7890e02b0b7a5165349f087aabbf7.message:
rsxcore: DRAWPRINT's vertex hash reads only what the draw's chunk holds

drawprint_write hashed vertex_count vertices from the draw's vp_vb offset.
A GPU-fetch draw keeps its vertices in vf_buf, and its offset is just the
vp_vb cursor, so a 39,723-vertex fetch draw read about 10 MB from a 4 MB
chunk. Legacy's one 768 MB buffer kept the same read in bounds. With the
chunks, the replay crashed (an access violation in drawprint_write) when
nothing was mapped after the chunk: two of the big set's scale-150 replays,
only sometimes.

The hash now stops at the end of the draw's chunk (or the big buffer), and
skips a chunk that isn't made. Only RSX_DRAWPRINT runs this code; the
images were never affected. The vertex hashes that differed from legacy's
on big draws came from the same read.

713fad7009af40a419bb6c47256e21e90d7a9edd.message:
cellSaveData: put each save file on the disk before it replaces the old one

A whole-file write went to a temp file that was closed and renamed over
the old one, with its data still in the system's cache. After a crash,
a hang or a power cut the file system can keep the rename and the new
size but not the data, so the save reads back as zeros or garbage. A
Demon's Souls tester's PC hung at a warp, where the game autosaves, then
stopped with a blue screen, and afterwards the save no longer loaded
(their files are not checked yet).

The temp file is now flushed to the disk (_commit / fsync) before the
rename, and the rename is written through (MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH; the
folder is synced on POSIX). PARAM.SFO is written the same way, and an
append to PARAM.PFD is synced. A failed sync fails the write and keeps
the old file, as a failed write already did.

Tested with Demon's Souls: autosaves of the character slot and the
system file at Stonefang, then a boot from the files written (both load,
the level comes up and autosaves again). No leftover temp files.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

71df9a6f7b9434fe17ddaae964f7ee77a6f2d1f9.message:
rsx: copy-once finds a span that starts inside a copy too

The copy table found a copy only by the guest address a span starts at.
A quarter of the bytes it still copied on Demon's Souls' 1-2 bridge lay
wholly inside a copy of the same stretch that started earlier: a draw
taking a later part of a vertex buffer an earlier draw had copied whole.

Each entry is now also listed by the 64 KB guest pages it covers (the
first 16), in 512 sets of 8, so a span that starts inside a copy finds it
there and points into it at the right offset. A page slot can name an

7ac7715fbeac38cc51b9a75d5705b63d43485303.message:
rsxcore: the GPU write-back off Windows too

Off Windows every render target went back to guest memory on the CPU. On a Steam
Deck that is 2.15 ms of each 25 ms frame on the RSX thread, which is the thread
that holds the frame there. Windows has had the GPU do it for a long time, where
it is under 0.1 ms.

The Windows route needs a heap on RSX local memory as an allocation of its own.
Off Windows the guest's space is one anonymous mapping, which
VK_EXT_external_memory_host can import as it is, so each target gets a buffer
over its own pages, made once and kept. Not one over all 256 MB: amdgpu checks an
imported buffer's pages one by one at every submit (amdgpu_cs_parser_bos), and
they stay resident. Without the extension (vkd3d, null), or past 32 spans, a
target stores on the CPU as before.

rsx_out: a Vulkan start that fails runs today's renderer, and says why (step V6)

- A start that fails at a step the core sees falls back in the same
  process. The core names its steps (rsxc_init.inc's start_step: loader,
  instance, adapter, features, device, window, swap chain, targets,
  shaders, rings), and on a failure undoes what it made (rc_abort_init:
  the hooks set to NULL, the device and all on it, the window and its
  class, which today's renderer registers under the same name). The
  switch then hands today's renderer the overlay and the game's tag it was
  given before the start, and starts it. A failure to make the frame's
  buffers fails the start only on Vulkan (rc_be_start_strict); hal-d3d12
  and null go on without them, as today's renderer does.
- A start that never finished: with RSX_STATE_DIR set (a host's folder
  that setup does not clear), a Vulkan start writes renderer_starting
  there and removes it at its first present (rsx_out_route_presented,
  from rsxc_vk.c). A start that finds it uses d3d12; any start not on
  Vulkan removes it, so the next one tries Vulkan again. No RSX_STATE_DIR
  (test runs): no mark.
- rsx_out_renderer_info(&why): the route that runs and why it is d3d12
  when another was asked for, without picking a route (NULL before one is
  picked: a crash dialog's process). The log says it too:
    [rsx_out] route d3d12 (Vulkan failed to start: no Vulkan 1.3 driver (loader); this start uses D3D12)
    [rsx_out] route d3d12 (RSX_BACKEND=vulkan, but the last start on Vulkan did not finish, ...)
- RSX_FAIL_START_AT=<step> fails the start there on purpose, for tests.

rc_backend_shutdown's device release moves into rc_release_device, which
the abort shares; shutdown does what it did. With PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL off
every object is identical; with it on and route d3d12, today's renderer
runs as before (the switch adds a delete of a mark left in RSX_STATE_DIR,

rsx: the Vulkan route starts with a minimized window, and the core takes the swap chain's images again after the backend makes it again

A process started minimized (STARTUPINFO's SW_SHOWMINNOACTIVE, a "Run:
Minimized" shortcut) shows the core's window minimized: its surface is
0x0, so the swap chain could not be made, the start failed at "swap chain"
and the route fell back to D3D12. And the backend makes its swap chain
again by itself (out of date, a restore after a minimize) and frees the
old images with their views, while the core kept the image handles and
views it took at init and in its own resize.

- gpu_vk_swap.c: a minimized window is not a failure. chain_make returns 1
  then and drops the old swap chain too (its images and semaphores went
  with chain_drop, so no acquire is made on it); swap_create and
  swap_resize take it, and the first acquire after the window shows makes
  the images. chain_again does not idle the GPU while there is nothing to
  drop (each acquire while minimized).
- The core (rsxc_state.inc, rsxc_hdr.inc): rc_acquire's image that is not
  the core's at its index means the swap chain was made again
  (swap_follow): the images and their views are taken again, and the
  window's size is its last WM_SIZE's. swap_buffers_get takes a swap chain
  with no images yet; init takes the images before its first acquire
  (rsxc_init.inc).
- gpu.h: swap_acquire, swap_image_count and swap_image say so.

D3D12 routes: the images change only in swap_resize, which takes them
itself, so swap_follow never acts there.

spu: image 2's table-diff block runs its passes in SSE registers

The native block for image 2's compare-and-copy loop (spu_diff_hook.c)
ran each of its up to 31 fast passes through two 128-byte arrays on the
stack: memcpy in, memcmp per quadword with a branch, memcpy out, and
ctx->ls read again before each of the eight stores, since a byte store
may change it. In a profile of Demon's Souls' deep Palace the block was
2.3% of image 2.

diff_pass_sse keeps the sixteen quadwords in SSE registers (all loads
before the stores, the stores in the lifted order, as before), takes
each change bit from a byte compare's mask without a branch, and gets
the local store's address once from the caller. The masks, A, B and the
counter come out as diff_pass_fast leaves them. SPU_NATIVE_DIFF=3
(live) runs diff_pass_fast instead, for A/B; the check mode
(SPU_NATIVE_DIFF=2) checks the SSE passes against the interpreter. A
build for something other than x86-64 keeps diff_pass_fast.

rsxcore: the vertex fetch ring in chunks, a full chunk goes on in the next

docs/124 step 1. vf_buf was one upload buffer, and a draw that did not fit
took the CPU path (256 bytes a vertex in vp_vb) until vf_grow made it bigger
at the frame's end: the first frame after loading a heavy area pushed about a
million vertices into vp_vb, which is why vp_vb is sized so big. vf_buf is now
an rc_arena (s_vf): VP_FETCH_RING_MB is a chunk's half (default 32, rounded
down to a power of two, 4..1024), two chunks to start, up to 1024 MB a half
in all. A descriptor that does not fit the chunk the frame writes in goes to
the next one (rc_arena_fit, made then if the spare is used up); only a
descriptor bigger than a chunk still takes the CPU path.

A descriptor and every span it points at lie in one chunk. fdesc and s_fx keep
virtual offsets; the records' x are from the chunk's start. An append to the
last span stays inside its chunk, else the range takes a new descriptor, and
VF_ONCE reuses only a copy in the new descriptor's chunk. render_frame keeps
the chunk bound at t20 as a virtual range: a fetch draw outside it binds its
own chunk, and the push constant is the offset in that chunk. The chunk the
frame writes in is kept (s_vf_lo, s_vf_end, s_vf_wp), so a draw's upload and
a draw in render_frame never divide. rc_arena_frame_end replaces vf_grow,
which goes with ring-retire slot 2.

uvc_table (rsxc_fp.inc) and render_frame's uvc_vf_va still use chunk 0 by its
old names (s_rc_vf_buf, vf_mapped, s_vf_cap, s_vf_short), so a clamp table
for a fetch draw is only made while the frame stays in chunk 0.

860f69920d8203570b16cbda0405a0c1284eccaf.message:
spu: image 2's ring fetch skips a GET the last one covered; its state PUT every 16th command

Image 2 is the consumer of the HighGraphics command ring. For every
16-byte command its fetch GETs the 128-byte block around get, and after
it PUTs its state (get) back, where the producer reads it before each
command it writes. Both are transfers of lines the producer is writing
at the same moment.

GET: a block holds eight commands and was copied up to eight times. A
command is now skipped when the last GET already covered it: the same
block and LS buffer, get the command after the last one taken, get + 16
at or before the put read ahead of that GET (the commands before it were
in memory then, and the producer does not write them again until get is
past them), and the command's quadword in LS still as the GET left it.
SPU_RING_GET_SKIP (live): 1 (default), 0 GETs every command, 2 prints
the share skipped (74% in the deep Palace).

PUT: inside the loop the state PUT waits up to 16 commands; what reaches
memory is the newest state, as from a slower consumer. Every way out of
the loop PUTs first, so the producer sees get before image 2 waits for a
command or runs lifted code, and a full ring still drains.
SPU_RING_PUT_EVERY=<n> (live, default 16); 1 every command.

Deep Palace, unlocked, vsync off, presenting, with the GPU write-back
and the 64-vertex fetch rule in (image 2 then holds the frame):
SPU_RING_GET_SKIP=0 is 5.0% slower (186.8 vs 177.5 fps, 3 boots, 9

gpu: E3's t20 bounds in words, so the Vulkan route reads all of the fetch ring

E3 keeps the vertex fetch's loads inside t20 with GetDimensions. glslang
lowers a ByteAddressBuffer's GetDimensions to OpArrayLength, the length in
uints, where D3D12's is in bytes; E3 took it as bytes, so every load past a
quarter of t20's range read 0. vf_buf is 64 MB a parity half, bound from its
half to the buffer's end: a Demon's Souls Palace frame's fetch draws past
32 MB (parity 0) or 16 MB (parity 1) lost their vertices, so the Vulkan
route drew no far geometry from the second frame on, a different cut on
each parity.

E3 version 2 compares in words. test_gpu_sc_spv: the golden for version 2,
and its check for left-over loads takes the new helpers.

93fe1c3e34ecc1e2920bf4da453d60c0bbfe95b8.message:
cellAudio: follow Windows' default output device

The WASAPI stream opened on the device that was the default at start and
stayed there. When another device became the default (headphones or a
headset plugged in or connected, a choice in Windows' sound settings),
the game kept playing to the old one, and the player heard nothing until
a restart (Demon's Souls, issue #296). A device that went away
(AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED) was never reopened either: the mixer
paced on its clock for the rest of the run.

- An IMMNotificationClient flags a change of the default render device
  (role eConsole). The mixing thread then reopens the stream on the new
  default, unless that is the device already playing.
- A failed call on the stream closes it. The mixer tries the default
  device on its next block, then about once a second while there is
  none, and paces on its clock meanwhile. One log line per outage.
- The log says what kind of device plays ("headphones", "speakers",
  "display audio"), not its name, which can carry the player's.

RPCS3's cellAudio also reopens its backend when the default device
changes, and retries while the backend isn't working. This is our own
code for our WASAPI backend. Off Windows, SDL plays to the system's
default device, and SDL or the sound server moves it.

9513615c3e20dc2a64acf37e06ae5a5f48150f16.message:
gpu: the D3D12 pipeline library's file is mapped, not read into memory

D3D12 keeps reading the bytes a pipeline library is made from for as long
as the library lives (CreatePipelineLibrary does not copy them). The new
path read pipelines.lib into a malloc'd buffer, so the whole file stayed in
the process's private memory: 24.7 MB with the game's cache today, and it
grows with the pipelines a cache holds. Now the file is mapped read-only.
Its pages are the file's: they don't count as private memory or commit, and
under memory pressure Windows drops them instead of writing them to the
page file (docs/124, step 5).

- plat.h: plat_file_map_read / plat_file_unmap, a whole file mapped
  read-only. Windows: CreateFileMapping and MapViewOfFile, inline; the file
  and section handles are closed once the view is mapped. Linux and macOS:
  mmap in plat_posix.c, the descriptor closed the same way.
- Only the view holds the file, so the library's save still replaces it:
  it writes a temporary and renames it over the mapped file, which NTFS
  and FAT allow (they refuse a delete or a truncation of a mapped file, not
  a rename over it), and the library goes on reading the old file's bytes.
  Checked on Windows 11 with both the POSIX and the classic rename forms.
- gpu_d3d12_pipe.c: pipeline_cache_load maps the file; the mapping is
  dropped where the buffer was freed (a refused file, a replaced library,
  gpu_destroy after the library is released), so the library never
  outlives it.
- gpu.h: pipeline_cache_save's contract says the file is replaced, never
  written into, since the loaded one may still be in use.

Vulkan is unchanged: VkPipelineCache copies its initial data, and the file's
buffer is freed right after vkCreatePipelineCache already. The legacy
renderer (pso_library.bin) is frozen and unchanged.

Checked: the game at the regression save, the same cache (5,857 pipelines,
25,254 KB library): before, a 24.7 MB private allocation (committed, and in
RAM in full unless trimmed); after, none, and pipelines.lib is a 24.

rsx_shader_precompile: one target a pass, through a sink (step P3a)

Setup's shader pass now makes its texts and fills its cache through a
sink: the calls it makes, as a table. Built with PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL there
are three targets:

  service's dxbc target. FXC with today's call, so the same .dxbc names

later). Those sinks hand no rows over, report the index as not built,
and an index-only pass has nothing to do for them. A full pass still
makes the rows' texts.

rsx_shader_precompile_sink_of, _use and _current pick a target, and
_reset readies the next pass in the same process. The call sites read
as before: one block renames each of today's calls to the sink's.

The threads, locks and counters go through a small rsx_pc_sync.h. On
Windows each name is the Win32 call itself, as a macro; elsewhere it is
pthreads and __atomic. With the option the pass builds off Windows too,
for spv, and keeps to 63 compile threads, so one wait covers every

CI: sccache for the configurations a pull request runs

992d082bc7af4d2400b6132c540795b4e1ec1c22.message:
rsx: a batch's occlusion counts are stored when the next batch needs them

A batch with counted draws (Demon's Souls's sun probe, on every frame with
the sky in view) waited for the GPU right after its submit, to store the
counts. That held the FIFO drain on the vblank ticker for the GPU's whole
frame, so the walk of the next batch could not run beside the GPU's work,
as it does for batches with no queries since the write-back store moved to
the next frame's start (RSX_WRITE_COLOR_DEFER). In the 2-2 Patches area at
render scale 300 that wait was 3.55 ms of an 8.85 ms frame.

The counts are now stored when the stream reaches the next batch's first
ZPASS GET_REPORT, after a GPU wait there, or at the next batch's start
(after the wait it makes anyway) if none comes before it. The next batch's
other ZPASS events queue behind the pending batch's meanwhile: zq_finish
takes how many events are the batch's and the counting state at its end,
and moves the rest up. Demon's Souls turns counting off at the start of
each frame and probes near its end (record 2439 of about 2,900), so a store
at the next ZPASS method of any kind waited at the frame's start and saved
only 0.3 ms; at the GET_REPORT, the GPU is done with the last frame.

The game reads report 1024 after a semaphore released right after the
probe's GET_REPORT. Both stores land before that semaphore, so it reads the
previous probe's count as before. RSX_ZPASS_DEFER=0 restores the wait after
submit.

The portable renderer's core gets the same change (rsxc_zpass.inc,
rsxc_frame.inc). test_rsx_synth's goldens change with it, as the change
means them to: the zpass scene's last frame no longer waits after its
submit, so the null backend's stream has one fence signal fewer from
there on. In the first pass the hashes of zpass and the two scenes after
it move, and in the second pass all of them; every other check passes.

Measured with knobab.sh (one exe, the knob switched inside each boot,
3 boots, ABBAAB windows; uncapped, RSX_PRESENT=0, SMAA, HDR, 16x AF):
- 2-2 Patches,

99598029cd86b9c579736b1ed5387719e0bc2124.message:
gpu_vk: a window with no RGBA8 images gets a BGRA8 swap chain, the frame blitted in

The core's swap chain is RGBA8 (gpu.h's contract, D3D12's back buffers). On
Linux the surfaces of X11 and Wayland on Mesa (lavapipe's included) and of
NVIDIA's driver offer BGRA8 only, so the Vulkan route could not start there:
"[VK] the window takes no swap chain of format 28".

Such a swap chain is now BGRA8, and its images, as the core sees them, are
RGBA8 textures of the backend's. The present's own submit, which every
present makes already, blits the acquired one into the chain's image (a
blit swaps the channels' order) and waits for the acquire there, so the
core's submits no longer wait for it. One recorder and one fence an image.
It says so once:
  [VK] the window takes no RGBA8 images: its swap chain is BGRA8, each frame copied in
A window that has RGBA8 is as before.

Cost: one copy of the window's image a frame, on those systems only. The
other way would be the core drawing into BGRA8 itself, which touches the
blit's, the output filter's and the capture's pipelines and gpu.h.

9c435d2bcddb67ca0fbbaa94fee1b096e1304ae3.message:
rsxcore: the vertex buffer in chunks of 64 MB, made as frames need them

vp_vb was one upload heap sized for the worst frame: the port starts it at
1.5M vertices (VP_VB_VERTS), 768 MB in RAM whatever a frame uses, while
steady frames write 5k-55k vertices (docs/124). It is now an rc_arena of
VP_VB_CHUNK vertices a parity half (default 131,072: 64 MB a chunk), one
made at start and one more at a frame's end when the frame got past half of
the last. A draw's vertices never cross a chunk's end (vb_room); a draw
bigger than a chunk goes to the arena's big buffer, made for it. The draw's
vb_byte_offset is its virtual offset; render_frame binds the chunk that
holds it when it is not the bound one (a compare per draw), and draws from
the offset inside it. Strip and list merges stay inside one chunk. The
kind-4 clamp's table goes in the chunk of the draw it numbers.

rc_arena also gets the big buffer, chunk arithmetic by shift for a power of
two, and the helpers the binds use. VP_VB_VERTS is today's renderer's only;
VP_VB_MAX_VERTS still caps the vertices in all (default 2M). The log says
each chunk made in a frame's middle, each new peak, and the biggest draw
from 16,384 vertices on.

gpu: one present and loss contract; Vulkan's loss, present modes and pipeline cache file (step VC2)

gpu.h states what gpu_swap_present, the fence waits and gpu_lost return
(its step VC2 block): a present gives GPU_PRESENTED or a GPU_PRESENT_*
code (lost, surface lost, failed), a fence wait passes once the device is
lost, and gpu_lost keeps the API's own code from the first loss on. The
D3D12 and null backends return the codes; nothing else changes there.

Vulkan:
- DEVICE_LOST from any call is the loss the core reports as it does a
  removed D3D12 device (the line, rc_be_lost_text, the stop). OUT_OF_DATE
  and SUBOPTIMAL remake the swap chain; SURFACE_LOST remakes the surface
  and its swap chain, and when that fails the core says so and stops
  presenting, as for a loss (rc_be_surface_lost). A loss noted by hand
  (RSX_LOSE_DEVICE_AT_FRAME) asks the driver for no fault report.
- RSX_VSYNC=1 presents FIFO, 0 IMMEDIATE, else FIFO with the line the
  d3d12 route prints; never MAILBOX. With swapchain_maintenance1 the mode
  switches per present, else by a new swap chain. RSX_VSYNC=2-4 hold each
  frame that many refreshes with present_wait (the present gate); without
  present_wait they are FIFO, one refresh, as before.
- The core draws into no image when the acquire gave none (a minimized
  window or a lost surface): rsxc_state.inc's s_rc_have_image.
- The pipeline library is the device's VkPipelineCache, in
  <cache>/gpu/vulkan/<vendor>_<device>_<driver>_<uuid>.vkpc: loaded at the
  start, saved where pipelines.lib is saved. Its header (magic, version,
  length, the driver, the data's length and sum) and Vulkan's own are
  checked; a file that fails is ignored and the next save replaces it.
  The route writes no .dxbc, pso_library.bin or pso_manifest.bin.
  PS3_PSO_LOG=1 prints the pipelines made, the cache's hits and the time
  in the driver when the device goes.

swap_present reads the code (rsxc_hdr.inc), rc_acquire keeps whether an
image

a7e5022f3a56aeed5b8d703c268d20bd6c0b0aa8.message:
ppu: a run of stores through one other base register shares one test too

A run of three or more stores of GPRs through one base register other
than r1 (a structure filled in) now goes under one test as the frame
saves do: vm_st_run gives the host address of the run's lowest byte when
every byte it stores would take vm_write*_inl's direct store (below the
store limit at both ends, no line of it reserved), and the stores then
go through that pointer; otherwise the run's lines run as before. Such a
run spans at most 256 bytes, so the test reads three reservation bits at
most. In Demon's Souls' lift: 31,953 such runs beside the 47,482 frame
save runs. With each run put back as its else block, every function is
the same as master's lift.

The run stores are vm_run_put* now (were vm_stk_put*), as both kinds use
them. vm_st_run reads its own switch, the fourth word on the armed flag's
line (game_module.c's copy too): 1 while the store limit is on, 0 while
PPU_ST_RUN=0 (live), which sends every such run store by store. The
run reads the reservation bits once where each store read its own; the
bits are sticky, so only a line's first reservation can fall between the
test and the stores, as it already could between one store's test and
its store, and the PUTLLC's compare still sees the changed line.

aafc5cf47666c949a25beecd0d8b38a573ff23a6.message:
ppu, cellAudio: a title's urgent threads and the mixer ahead of the rest on every host

Players on handhelds hear the sound stutter in Demon's Souls when the
CPU is busy ("the audio lags a lot when hitting enemies"). Its libmixer
threads (_cellsurMixerMain 400, _sys_mixerSurBusReq 402,
_sys_MixerChStripMain 404) write each 5.3 ms block when cellAudio's
notify wakes them. They ran at normal host priority beside every busy
guest thread, so under load they woke more than a block late and the
slot played as silence.

Guest threads the title ranks ahead of its default 1001 (priority
below 1000, was below 256) now get one step up: above normal on
Windows, nice -5 elsewhere. Off Windows the new thread raises itself,
since Linux's nice is per thread id and macOS's QoS is for the calling
thread only. On Linux SDL_LinuxSetThreadPriority tries setpriority and
then RealtimeKit over D-Bus (what PipeWire uses), since a game may not
lower its own nice. PPU_RAISE_BELOW=<prio> moves the line (256 for the
old one, 0 for none).

Off Windows the cellAudio mixer thread had no priority call at all (on
Windows it has MMCSS Pro Audio). It now asks SDL for TIME_CRITICAL:
on Linux the best nice level RealtimeKit grants, not a real-time class.

Measured with AUDIO_GAPS on the 1-2 dragon bridge, game held to 2 CPUs,
4-minute runs: 216 and 317 gaps at normal priority; 15 with the three
libmixer threads above normal; 39 with only the thread that takes the
notify raised (the other two do part of the work).

Same build, the new line against PPU_RAISE_BELOW=256 (the old one),
2.5-minute runs, gaps: 24 against 91 on 2 CPUs (one run each); 12
against 51 on 4 CPUs (two runs each). On 8 CPUs gaps are rare either
way (11 against 4 in two runs each, within the noise of a busy PC).

Not tested on Linux or macOS hardware. Under WSL as an unprivileged
user with no RealtimeKit both calls fail cleanly, log one line, and the
threads stay at nice 0.

b0788fd8d79fa84d2d9fdd2bf4dd2c98783fa01c.message:
spurs: mark a new task running before it becomes ready

cellSpursCreateTask made the task ready (spurs_taskset_add_task) and marked it
running only afterwards. A task of the same taskset exiting on another thread
in that gap saw it ready and not running, and started it. CreateTask then
started it again, so one id had two runs.

The first run to exit frees the id. The second then clears the id's bits under
whichever task took it next. In Demon's Souls, HighGraphics gave the freed id
to its second task, and that task's SPU child took the same id, because the
stray exit had cleared it. The child's pending bit was set while the id still
read as running, so nothing started it, and its parent's exit wiped it.
HighGraphics then waited forever for the child's report: the picture froze and
the music played on.

The frozen game shows this: no task bits set, HighGraphics asleep on an empty
queue, task 1's slot holding the child's image with no dispatch of it, and the
image started twice with one id, once by HighGraphics and once by a worker.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

b33c751d758c0d137bed881c14ad70ac49be2e6c.message:
rsx: RSX_SUBMIT_SPLIT, a batch submitted in parts so the GPU starts while the rest records

A batch's GPU work starts only at its one submit, after the whole batch is
recorded, and the next batch opens with wait_for_gpu. On Vulkan that wait is
about 12% of the render thread (the 11-02 profiles: wait_for_gpu ->
vkb_fence_wait -> the driver's WaitForMultipleObjects); on D3D12 it barely
shows. With RSX_SUBMIT_SPLIT=<records> (default 0, off) a batch goes to the
GPU in parts: a part ends before the first draw once it has that many
records and that many are still to come, so the GPU works on it while the
rest is recorded. The same commands in the same order; only where the
submits fall moves, and that by the records, not by time.

- gpu.h: cmd_split, submit what a recorder has so far and go on recording
  in it (nothing bound after it, as after cmd_begin).
  - D3D12: Close, ExecuteCommandLists, the list's Reset on the same
    allocator (its Reset waits for the slot's next cmd_begin).
  - Vulkan: the next part in another buffer of the slot's pool, up to 8
    a recording; no opening barrier (a part follows the one before on the
    queue as it would in one buffer).
  - Null: cmd_end, submit, and the slot open again; queries' states stay.
- The core: the VP pass's batch-wide binds move into vp_pass_binds, called
  at the pass's start (the same calls in the same order) and after each
  split, which binds the draw's targets again as the AA pass's return does.
  The first batch that splits says so once.

Checked on capset0 (courtyard, fogwall), 4 frames, split off against 64,

b3a9b8e4dd054aeb8a86539670b0e8914151981a.message:
rsxcore: the FP constant memo copies nothing for a program without constants

The memo hit called memcpy for 0 bytes too. VCRUNTIME's short copy is an
AVX-512 masked load and store over 64 bytes, and a masked access that
reaches a page nothing has touched takes a microcode assist every time.
Two hot programs at the Tutorial have no constants, and their entries' k
start within 64 bytes of a page whose neighbour entry is unused, so every
draw with them paid the assist: about 6% of the FIFO thread, and -1.3% fps
against today's renderer at m08. Which entries end a page depends on where
s_fpkm lands in the binary, which is why the replay and today's renderer
did not show it.

The hit now skips the copy when n is 0, and a new entry writes its k whole
once, so a short copy's tail always finds its page. The bytes written to
the ring are the same.

A permanent form of the timing patch used for the Vulkan study (docs/120's
speed work): the GPU's time, not the CPU's or the wall clock's, on both
backends at the same calls. Off by default; with it off no stamps are
written.

- gpu_times.h (backend-internal): the knob, and the sums.
  - RSX_GPU_TIMES=1 stamps each recording's start (cmd_begin) and end
    (cmd_end).
  - 2 also stamps each pass_begin, and every 600 frame-sized recordings
    prints the steps between stamps:
    [gpu-times] 600 recordings: 599.9 us a recording; steps (us): 0:1.8 ...
- D3D12: a timestamp heap of 512 stamps a slot, resolved at cmd_end into a
  readback buffer, and read when the slot is begun again or at wait_idle.
  The frequency comes from the queue.
- Vulkan: a timestamp pool a slot, reset at cmd_begin, read the same way.
  The tick is timestampPeriod, and the stamp is masked to the queue's
  timestampValidBits. None is made when the queue keeps no timestamps.
- gpu.h: gpu_gpu_ns(d, &n), the GPU's nanoseconds in the recordings read so
  far. The null backend has none and returns 0.
- rsx_replay: with RSX_REPLAY_TIMES=1, the times line adds
  ", gpu X ms a frame (N recordings)". It waits for the GPU before frame
  1's clock starts and after the last frame.
- The core, every 600 batches: "[gpu-times] N frames: gpu X ms a frame",
  by the title's flips that drew, or per batch when there are none (a

b8263848271814189c2449aea7423829acefd598.message:
video: clip depth as the RSX does, from SET_ZMIN_MAX_CONTROL

The guest pipelines always clamped depth: their description is zeroed, so
DepthClipEnable was FALSE. The RSX clips by default (SET_ZMIN_MAX_CONTROL
resets to 1: clip on, clamp off), and Demon's Souls never writes the
register. A shadow map therefore kept casters outside the light's depth
range, squashed onto its near or far plane. Things on the floor above, or
behind the light, threw hard shadows where nothing stands: a dark slab on the
Boletarian Palace stairs, and shadows that jump when the player enters the
1-1 lever room (issue #286).

The RSX state now tracks the register (reset value 1, as RPCS3 has it), and
rsx_cull_key carries "depth is clamped" as bit 3: set when the clamp bits are
on or the clip bits are off, which is when RPCS3 turns on depth clamp. Both
today's renderer and the HAL path (pd->depth_clip) clip unless that bit is
set. Default draws keep their key values, so pipeline-index rows still match;
their pipeline descriptions change, and setup's pipeline pass rebuilds them
for a new build.

The field goes at the end of rsx_state, because captures hold the struct as
it is (section RSXS). A replay reads an older capture's shorter copy over the
reset state, instead of skipping it as "captured by another build", which
started those replays from the wrong state.

Checked: a capture in a Palace passage replays the same on d3d12 and
hal-d3d12 (0 differing pixels) and within 1/255 on Vulkan; the user saw the
stairs slab and the lever-room shadows gone in a live run; regress.sh ok.

bbfad9428f3e63718add611ddbf4ebfb343fe29f.message:
sys_event: a queue's lock is made once and kept; a queue goes live when set up

A tester's game crashed at start on Vulkan (DemonsSoulsRecomp #311):
access violation writing 0x24 in EnterCriticalSection, called from
cellAudio's mixing thread through sys_event_queue_push_by_id.

The mixer finds the game's notify queue by its key every audio period,
without the table lock. Demon's Souls sets that key before it creates the
queue. sys_event_queue_create marked the slot active, with the key, then
logged a line, and only then made the queue's lock. A mixer period in
that window entered a zeroed CRITICAL_SECTION (its null DebugInfo is the
0x24). sys_event_queue_destroy had the mirror race: it deleted the lock
before clearing active.

Now:
- Each slot's lock and condition variable are made the first time the
  slot is used, and never deleted or cleared (q_lock_make). Create clears
  only the fields before the lock.
- A queue goes live (active, a release store) only after it is set up,
  under its own lock. Destroy clears active under that lock.
- event_queue_push checks active again under the lock.
- The lock-free lookups (sys_event_find_queue_by_key and the check in
  sys_event_queue_push_by_id) read active with acquire.

test_event_queue_life makes and destroys 20,000 queues with one key while
two threads find it by key and push to it, then checks a live queue's
pushes and a destroyed one's refusal.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

cellAudio: a 1024-frame SDL buffer, and gains spread over four mixes

A Demon's Souls player on CachyOS (PipeWire, 240 fps) hears crackle.
SDL hands the device's buffer size to PulseAudio as the stream's whole
target latency (tlength) and to PipeWire as the node's latency. We
asked for one block, 256 frames, so the sound server held 5.3 ms of
sound: any late write on a busy desktop ran it dry.

- The device opens with 1024 frames (21.3 ms), SDL's usual size for
  games. AUDIO_SDL_FRAMES=<n> sets it (256 is the size before).
- The queue keeps up to two of the device's takes and two blocks more
  (2560 frames). WSLg's PulseAudio took twice within a few ms every few
  seconds, and one take plus three blocks then ran dry.
- Starving is now the lowest queue level over two takes, under half a
  take, decided once per two takes. Read at one moment against a whole
  take (as before), nearly every take looked starving once a take is
  larger than a block.
- A gain (the sound card running ahead of our clock) moves the clock a
  quarter block on each of the next four mixes, on every backend. A
  whole block at once mixed two blocks back to back, and the title,
  which writes one block per notify, had no time for the second, so it
  played as silence.
- The "SDL audio:" device line goes to stderr: stdout reaches des.log
  only when its buffer fills, so a report made mid-session missed it.

A standalone test of this pacing against SDL 2.32's PulseAudio backend
(WSLg, two CPUs, four busy threads beside it, 30 s): with 256 frames
the stream took 162-166 blocks a second of 187.5 (the server ran short
12-14% of the time); with 1024 frames 181-186, and the queue was never
empty. Idle, both kept up. PULSE_LATENCY_MSEC=40 with the old pacing
kept the rate up but let the queue run empty 34 times in 30 s.

On Windows (WASAPI) gains are rare: 0 to 2 in a 2.5-minute run of the
game on the 1-2 dragon bridge, so the spread changes little there. Gaps
stayed at their level: 1 and 4 on 8 CPUs, 16 in 2 minutes on 2 CPUs.

c6f0be313531f82bb8634f66d557a760ce2490a1.message:
rsxcore: make the draw records when the backend starts, not in each backend's static data

s_d3d. rsxc_state.inc is in each backend's copy of the core (d3d12, vulkan,

only the running route's is used. It is a pointer now:

  succeeded, as a "rings" start step: a failed allocation fails the start
  like the others (start_step + rc_abort_init), so the route falls back.
  It comes after init_d3d12 so that RSX_FAIL_START_AT=rings still fails at
  the rings it always did.
- They are kept through a shutdown for a start after it, and zeroed then,
  as the array was by the memset of s_d3d. rc_abort_init frees them.

The records are written and read on the per-draw path. With
-fno-strict-aliasing a store through a heap pointer may be to any global,
so the record blocks of d3d12_draw_arrays and d3d12_draw_indexed read
s_d3d.current_rsx_state again after every field they wrote (where the
array let the compiler see it was not that field); they read it once now
(st; the calls in the blocks leave it as it was: vp_get_vs restores it).

record blocks take the record's address once.

cb767e37b5859b2ed715a6e3d57c95ce1b462484.message:
gpu: Vulkan's set 0 for t20 going back and forth (step V5v)

The clamp's vertex-shader form (RSX_CLAMP_FORM=vs, the pick on a device
without geometry shaders) binds t20 to the vertex ring and back to the fetch
ring around each of its non-fetch draws. On Vulkan a raw buffer's offset is
its set 0's, so each switch looked set 0 up again in the device's cache,
under its lock, twice a draw.

- The recorder keeps the last two sets 0 it found (key and set), newest
  first; binds_slow takes one from there before it asks the cache. Sets and
  buffer handles live as long as the device, so an entry never goes stale.
- The device counts the cache's lookups (n_set0_gets, a test hook).
- A raw range cut at maxStorageBufferRange says so once: the fetch's loads
  (E3) read 0 past the cut, so a corner table there would lose its corners.

The rest of what V5 listed for Vulkan was there already: every buffer is a
storage buffer too; a raw range runs from its address to the buffer's end
(the whole ring half the table sits in); E4 takes any one-uint member name
(uvc_tab); E1 puts UVBOUND0-7 at 13-20 and nointerpolation is Flat; the
format table maps R32G8X24_TYPELESS and D32_FLOAT_S8X24_UINT to
D32_SFLOAT_S8_UINT, R32_FLOAT_X8X24 to its depth aspect and X32_G8X24 to its
stencil aspect. No pipeline of the core sets a depth bias, so nothing scales
on a float depth format.

d0a6149036515692ca27da18eb3d1f032efbda20.message:
gpu: the null backend, which records and checks for headless CI

gpu_null*.c/h: gpu.h's device functions and gpu_cmd_ops.h's commands with
no GPU under them, for CI on every system (plain C99, no system or GPU
headers). Buffers are CPU memory: maps, copies between buffers and host
imports move real bytes. Textures hold nothing, so their readbacks and
occlusion results are zeroes. The GPU is instant: fences complete at
submit and waits never block. Each command is static inline in
gpu_null_cmd.h, one call into the recorder, and so are the per-draw device
calls (GPU_FAST_FUNCS), so the core's frame file builds against it as
against D3D12.

Every command and the device calls around it are checked against the
contract, as they are recorded and as they run at submit, in submission
order: stale and freed handles; frees before the fence of the work using
them; barriers against each subresource's tracked state, with D3D12's
promotion from COMMON and decay; states a use does not allow; draws
missing a layout, pipeline, pass or bound slot; binds without their
GPU_USE bit or outside their buffer; cb_align and the copies' alignments;
boxes and footprints out of bounds; query reset, begin and end order;
table entries written while unfinished work reads them; fences never
reached, and slots or readbacks used before their fence was seen; recorders
used after their end; swap chain images used without an acquire. Failures
are counted by kind (gpu_null_errors), and the first of each kind is
printed with the command and its arguments.

gpu_null_stream_hash is FNV-1a 64 over the operation stream: every command
in submission order and the device calls that change what a GPU would see,
handles as creation numbers and pipelines by their contents, so a run
hashes the same on every system and compiler. GPU_NULL_DUMP=<file> writes
the stream as text. gpu_null.h has the encoding.

test_gpu_null (built on demand; ctest -R gpu_null) records three frames of
the guest pipelines' commands on two recorders and a swap chain with no
failure and th

d2a0678866dd35405d5503d062336d65a00dd58d.message:
SPU ring loop: write the registers and the frame once per run of commands

Image 2's native ring loop (spu_ring_hook.c, SPU_NATIVE_LOOP=1) left every
register, the frame and the context fields as the lifted path leaves them at
each command's end, and the next command wrote nearly all of them again
before anything read them. ring_lazy runs the same commands with the same
local-store stores, transfers and latches, keeps r80, the last command and
the last fetch's reads in locals, and writes the post's registers and frame
(and, when the run ends at 0x4730, the fetch's registers) once at the end.
The tag waits of a deferred PUT and a skipped GET are left out: no transfer
came since the last wait, so they would read what it read.

SPU_RING_LAZY (live): 1 (default), 0 the per-command path, for A/B.

test_spu_ring_lazy.c runs both on random rings (all native commands, some
the loop leaves to the lifted code, failed no-op commits, the PUT interval,
one-call transfers, the GET skip and the line read varied) and compares the
registers, context, local store, guest memory, transfers and the GET memo.

d740ce6847f68e1ebca83d41cd2902ffe5c682b0.message:
rsx_d3d12: the FP constant memo copies nothing for a program without constants

fpk_extract_at's memo hit copied the program's constants with
memcpy(out, m->k, 16 * n), n = 0 for most programs. The CRT's copy for 64
bytes or less is an AVX-512 masked load and store over 64 bytes, even for
0 bytes, and a masked access that reaches a page nothing has touched
takes a microcode assist on every call (fault suppression; it never
really reads the page, so the page never gets mapped). An entry whose k
starts within 64 bytes of a page's end, with an unused neighbour, pays
that each draw.

Which entries end a page depends on where s_fpkm lands in the binary.
In today's build none of the hot ones do, so this costs nothing now. In
the portable renderer's copy of this code two did, and it cost the FIFO
thread about 6% at the Tutorial (-1.26% fps, 12 rounds; with this fix
+0.30%, no change). Any change that moves the array could bring that
here.

The hit skips the copy when n is 0, and a new entry clears its k array
once, so a short copy's tail always lands on a touched page. The bytes
written to the constant ring are the same.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

d791b6ace351edc0697b9066e6d4ac62c7e38aa2.message:
rsxcore: no new sampler while a split part runs (RSX_SUBMIT_SPLIT)

With RSX_SUBMIT_SPLIT on, a batch's first parts are on the GPU while the rest
is recorded, and vp_sampler_table can make a new sampler in that time. That is
legal Vulkan, but lavapipe faults on it: llvmpipe_register_sampler (Mesa 25.2.8)
reallocs every texture's sample_functions array with no lock against the
rasterizer threads that read those arrays. The arrays are all one size, so a
freed one goes straight to the next texture, and a late read or write through
the old pointer gives a texture another texture's sample function. Those
functions have the texture's size compiled in, so the read runs off the end of
the memory: SIGSEGV in generated shader code, in 3 of 8 split runs and 0 without
the split. One core shows a sample function for a 256x1024 BC1 texture reading
from 60 KB of memory, on two threads at once.

Without the split the GPU is idle while a batch is recorded, so this never
overlaps. Now a sampler table new to the session waits for the parts first. It
is rare (128 tables at most) and only happens with the split on; the wait is the
same one this function already makes when it reuses a table.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

spu: the MFC engine lookup tries the context's own slot first

mfc_for finds a context's MFC engine on every MFC channel access. It
remembered the last slot in a thread-local, and on Windows a thread-local
is three dependent loads before the slot's owner can be compared with
ctx. Demon's Souls' image 2 asks two or three times a ring command.

plus 1, 0 for none, at the end of the struct), and mfc_for tries it
first: a range check, then the slot's owner against ctx. A slot has one
owner, so a stale or never-set value can only miss, and a miss goes to
the thread's slot and the search as before; both record the slot in the
context too.

de2096dee4bef7c8714100be7f416e333f1e79b0.message:
spu: the striped lock-line lock and its lock-free reads off Windows too

Off MSVC the lock-line lock was one global spinlock, with no pause and no
yield, and the lock-free reads always answered "take the lock". So every SPU
atomic on Linux queued on one cache line, a polling SPU wrote that line on
each read, and spu_llar_noop_commit gave up after its eight tries on every
fetch. Windows has had 64 stripes as sequence locks for a long time.

The Windows lock now builds everywhere. Only what differs by compiler goes
through macros: taking and giving a stripe, reading its odd bit, pause, yield
and the bit scan. Off MSVC the take and give are seq_cst, as the interlocked
calls are: spu_coh_notify_write and spu_lockline_read_ok rely on a full fence
between taking a stripe and reading a reservation. The read side already used
portable atomics. SPU_LOCKLINE_STATS stays a Windows tool.

Windows doesn't change: spu_coherency.c compiles to a byte-identical object
before and after, with the runtime's own flags and /Brepro.

The peer and coherency tests pass on Linux with clang and gcc, unoptimized
and at -O2, 36 runs at -O2 on 16, 8 and 2 threads. ThreadSanitizer finds no
new kind of problem: its new reports are the sequence lock's copy overlapping
a writer, which the second read of the stripe word throws away, and the
reservation fields the same lock-free path writes on Windows.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

de6a31ffdbbae35cd1d8f37e9d40a86736a723bb.message:
spu: the ring loop's word and halfword inserts as stores

Image 2's native commands 7, 8 and 12 (ring_loop) did each of their six
sub-quadword stores as the lifted instructions do: load the quadword, make
a cwd / cwx / chd mask, shufb, store the 16 bytes back. A shufb by such a
mask, stored where its quadword came from, changes one word (or halfword):
the value's preferred word lands where the address points and the other
bytes are stored as they were. So each is now that word's or halfword's
store (ls_put_word / ls_put_half). For command 12 the mask positions and
the store addresses differ by 0x370 each, so the low four bits agree.
Command 8's insert was the hottest spot of ring_loop in an instruction
profile after the post's stores went straight.

SPU_LOOP_INSERTS=0 (live) runs the load, shuffle and store as before.
SPU_NATIVE_LOOP=2's check (the native commands predicted on a copy of
local store, compared after the lifted run) covers the new stores.

Deep Palace, DES_FPS=unlocked, vsync off, knobab plain windows, on master
+ #157-#160, session locked: SPU_LOOP_INSERTS=0 is 0.61% slower (210.00 vs
211.28 fps, 4 boots, 12 pairs, p 0.025). A small gain, kept because the
change is simple and checked. soak.sh with SPU_NATIVE_LOOP=2: kept
flipping for 6 minutes, 4,194,304 commands compared, 0 mismatches.
regress.sh: 4 of 4 shots ok.

def094193858066a599e624e228598011ba7bcb6.message:
rsx: the vertex-program memo keeps 32 programs per start, most recent first

vp_get_vs_mode runs for every draw. Its memo kept two programs per
program start; past that it sized the program, hashed it a byte at a
time (FNV-1a, about 4 cycles a byte, and the hash stays: the pipeline
library keys on it) and scanned the cache. In Demon's Souls' deep
Palace one start cycles through up to 32 programs. A count of the
lookups by how far back their program was last used at its start:
81.4% the last one, 89.4% within 2, 96.5% within 8, all within 32. So
two ways missed 10.6% of the lookups, each miss hashing about 850
bytes: 2.7% of the FIFO thread. (Eight ways were tried on 10-24 and
did not show; they would still miss 3.5%.)

The memo now keeps RSX_VP_MEMO programs per start (2 to 32, default
32) in most-recently-used order: a hit moves to the front, a new entry
takes the last one's place and its copy buffer. The copy compare after
a store write then meets the likely programs first. RSX_VP_MEMO=2
(live) is the memo as it was: two ways, least recently used out. A
pass-0 entry is now rejected on its version before the other checks.

e5d7a65fbf6603cfe3b4b81556a084266b199c86.message:
gpu: the Vulkan backend's gaps the core's replays found (step VC1)

The core's first replays on Vulkan, with the validation layer and its
synchronization validation, reported three kinds of message; the backend
now does what D3D12 does in each case, and two contract points are
written down in gpu.h.

- Table slots: set layouts of up to 16 entries are one layout
  (GPU_VK_TABLE_MIN), so a slot of up to 16 binds any table of up to 16.
  The core's blit binds the blit pool's 2-entry tables through a
  1-texture slot, which D3D12 allows and Vulkan's set layouts did not
  (VUID-vkCmdBindDescriptorSets-pDescriptorSets-00358).
- Vertex attributes: shader_create reads a SPIR-V module's Input and
  Output Locations, and a pipeline gets only the attributes its vertex
  shader reads (WARNING-Shader-OutputNotConsumed).
- Pixel shader outputs with no target (a depth-only pass's colour, slots
  past nrt): the pipeline is made with a copy of the module in which those
  outputs are Private variables, as D3D12 drops them
  (Undefined-Value-ShaderOutputNotConsumed-DynamicRendering). The copy is
  made from the words kept for pixel shaders with outputs and destroyed
  once the pipeline exists.
- Swap chains: GPU_SUBMIT_PRESENT_SIGNAL signalled the image's done
  semaphore in the first such submit only, so a present waited for none of
  the frame's later submits (the core says PRESENT_SIGNAL on every
  submit). The present's own empty submit now signals it, after them all.
- Textures with memory of their own start zeroed, as D3D12's committed
  resources: cleared in the init command buffer before their first layout
  (not BC formats; placed textures are what their heap held, on both).

ecf42d73afd978813c3670c1088f0dd96f35c715.message:
spu, lift: the SSE paths build on arm64 through sse2neon

The SIMD paths are written with SSE intrinsics behind x86 guards, each
with a scalar loop beside it, so an arm64 build compiled but took every
loop: spu_shufb as a byte loop (about 11% of an FMOD mixer task), the
quadword byte shifts at ~70 instructions each, the scan and diff blocks
on lane loops, and the PPU lift's vperm/vsldoi/vmaxfp/vminfp/vrsqrtefp/
lvlx/lvrx as loops.

third_party/sse2neon is sse2neon v1.9.1 (MIT, pinned by commit, blobs in
its README), unmodified. include/ps3emu/ps3_sse.h includes it on arm64
under GCC or Clang and defines PS3_SSE2NEON; on x86 it defines nothing.
These guards now also take PS3_SSE2NEON, and keep including their own
x86 header on x86:

- spu_helpers.h: shufb, the quadword byte shifts/rotates, cbd/chd/cwd/cdd;
- spu_scan_hook.c: scan_run_sse;
- spu_diff_hook.c: diff_pass_sse;
- the PPU lifter's preamble: the VMX helpers.

Kept on the loop on arm64, with a note why: spu_coh_hint_match (its
loads are atomic in C; a movemask is several NEON instructions for a few
groups of four) and mfc_copy (the 8-byte copies are one ldp/stp pair).
rsx_d3d12_backend.c's vf_strip_native_w is not touched: it is frozen and
not built on Apple.

sse2neon's precision options stay at 0: on AArch64 div and sqrt are
then the exact vdivq_f32/vsqrtq_f32, and vmaxfp/vminfp handle NaNs and
equal operands themselves.

Windows objects with the default options: all 302 identical to
fork/master's (COFF timestamp ignored).

ed411b5e5da6d39b033c30985861dd6e53f9e4fc.message:
rsx: the GPU vertex fetch ring grows when a frame needs more

The GPU fetch path copies a strip's guest vertex bytes into vf_buf, a
ring of VP_FETCH_RING_MB (64 MB) per frame half. A strip that does not
fit takes the CPU path instead, which converts every vertex to 256
bytes. The ring never grew.

On Demon's Souls' dragon bridge in 1-2 a frame asks for up to ~120 MB
of ring. There, 41 million strip uploads fell to the CPU path for lack
of room against 29 million that fit, the CPU path wrote ~2 million
vertices a frame (vp_vb grew to its 1 GB cap), and the FIFO thread held
the frame rate at ~77 fps: 87% busy in upload_strip_vp_indexed,
rsx_fetch_vertex_arrays and memcpy (issue #288).

The ring now grows at the frame's end like vp_vb and vp_ib: a frame
counts the bytes it found no room for (s_vf_short), and vf_grow doubles
the ring until it holds that frame with an eighth to spare, up to
1024 MB a half. The old ring goes with the deferred releases (today's
renderer) or with its frame's fence (rc_ring_retire, the core). On the
bridge the ring grows once, to 128 MB a half, and the frame rate is
144, the display's cap.

The portable core gets the same change (rsxc_state, rsxc_vertex,
rsxc_writeback, rsxc_frame, rsxc_init), and its kind-4 corner table,
which also writes the ring, counts its shortfall too.

f0ec8cbb2b45ac512d2847d88fc09f3e617bd725.message:
gpu_vk: fewer driver calls a frame on the Vulkan route

The Vulkan route was 18% slower than D3D12 in the Tutorial and 8% at the
Palace (the night of 10-31), with the render thread busy on both. Most of
the extra CPU time was calls the D3D12 drivers would have dropped or merged:

- Barriers are held and sent as one vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 just before the
  next command that does work (a draw's pass, a copy, a query, the end).
  One that touches what a held one does sends those first, so the order is
  the same. 73 calls a frame become 31.5.
- The attachment-order barrier between passes is sent only when one of
  the pass's targets was an attachment since the last barrier that orders
  it, not before every pass.
- Descriptor sets are bound only when they change, in runs.
- Repeated state is not sent again: the pipeline, viewport, scissor,
  topology, depth writes, vertex and index buffers and push constants.
  Replay CPU against D3D12 went from +14.3% to +8.3%.
- A whole-target clear made before its pass opens becomes the pass's load
  op, the drivers' fast clear (the better path on AMD and tile-based
  GPUs); a read-only depth's clear stays inside the rendering.
- A typeless colour image names the formats its views may take (its D3D12
  family), so a driver need not drop its compression.

Images are unchanged: the capture gates pass with the validation layer
(synchronization validation on) quiet.

f3c1c274f4c9ff7d5ce636c0ea3526b99996117f.message:
ppu: a guest longjmp lands in the frame of its setjmp

The lifted longjmp restored the guest registers from the buffer, then
returned to its own C caller. The function that called setjmp is a host
frame further up the stack, so execution went on after the throw with
the stack pointer and registers of the setjmp, in the wrong function.

Demon's Souls hits this when a script errors. Lua 5.0 raises an error
with longjmp (luaD_throw) back to the protected call that catches it
(luaD_rawrunprotected). In the Penetrator fight in 1-3, the boss
script 502000_battle errors at line 86 ("attempt to compare nil with
number"). That is the game's own bug: a PS3 catches it and the fight
goes on. Here the throw came back into luaV_execute, which then read a
NULL savedpc. The game's abort path then ended the process with
sys_process_exit(1), so the window closed with no crash report.

The lifter now finds the SDK's setjmp and longjmp by their first five
instructions (find_guest_setjmp). Each call of setjmp becomes
PS3_GUEST_SETJMP: a host setjmp in the caller's frame, beside the guest
call, recorded in a slot on a per-thread list (g_ps3_sjlj_top). The
function's scope object drops its slots when it returns. The guest
longjmp, after its own register restore, ends in ps3_guest_longjmp. That
takes the newest slot with the same buffer and stack pointer and host-
longjmps to it. With no such slot it returns as before, and says so once
on stderr. The thread proc empties the list before each run of a guest
thread's entry (ps3_sjlj_thread_reset). sys_ppu_thread_exit's own longjmp
out of the lifted frames can leave their slots behind, and an interrupt
handler runs its entry again on the same host thread.

The host setjmp and longjmp are the C library's. The Windows one unwinds
through the lifted frames by their unwind tables, as the runtime's thread
exit already does. __builtin_setjmp fails fast under clang-cl on Windows
x64. A freestanding game module gets _setjmp and longjmp from the host
as jump thunks (PS3_GAME_HOST_CRT_FUNCS, PS3_GAME

f59a0387809b6b62df0683fe28fdef19cb39b80b.message:
d3d12: colour write-back from the GPU straight into guest memory

The write-back stored 13.1 MB a frame in the deep Palace (three 1280x720
A8R8G8B8 targets and a dozen smaller) on the RSX thread: a read of each
byte from the readback buffer and a write into guest memory, about
31 GB/s each way. It is bound by that traffic: a faster loop or streamed
stores do not help (streamed: -2.5%), and a worker thread moves the
traffic without removing it (no change).

Now the GPU stores it. The boot reserves RSX local memory
[0xC0000000, 0xD0000000) as an allocation of its own inside the 4 GB
guest space (VirtualAlloc2 placeholders; the addresses do not change).
The backend commits that range, opens a heap on it
(OpenExistingHeapFromAddress) and places one buffer over it. Each linear
A8R8G8B8 target in local memory is drawn into the guest's byte order (the
write-back's downscale pass with an .argb shader) and copied into place;
the store only takes its checksum. Other formats, swizzled and
main-memory targets, offsets the copy cannot address (512-byte offsets,
256-byte pitches), and machines where the heap cannot be made store on
the CPU as before.

RSX_WB_GPU (live): 1 (default) as above, 0 every target on the CPU,
2 also makes the CPU store into a scratch copy and compares it with what
the GPU stored. Deep Palace, mode 2: 19,456 targets compared, 0 differ.

Deep Palace, unlocked, vsync off, presenting, 3 boots, 9 plain-window
pairs: RSX_WB_GPU=0 is 1.26% slower (180.0 vs 177.7 fps, p 0.008).
render_frame 1.57 -> 1.28 ms, its store 0.41 -> 0.06 ms. regress.sh ok.

fb753cf3d581815c239705d5889ab006faba0df9.message:
RSX_CORE: the RSX thread alone on a core (Linux)

On a Steam Deck the RSX thread holds the frame, and two guest threads spin in
sys_timer_usleep beside it. With that thread alone on one CPU of a core and
every other thread off the core, its second hardware thread included, the
Deck ran 4.1% and 7.8% faster (kit 3, two rounds, taskset from outside).

plat_core_reserve (plat.h, Linux) picks the core by the system's own figures
(cpufreq's max, then ACPI CPPC's highest_perf), not the first core when others
tie, since CPU 0 takes most interrupts. It moves every other thread off the
core. A thread starts on its starter's CPUs, so the ones the RSX thread starts
later (vertex workers, the driver's) would share its CPU: plat_core_keep moves
them, every 64 flips, reading the thread list only when the count of threads
changed or every 16th call.

RSX_CORE=1 turns it on, auto only with SMT and at least 4 cores, 0 or unset
leaves things as they are (the default). Elsewhere than Linux it does nothing.
test_plat_core checks it on the machine it runs on.

fe930bb8705eebebcfe48987993b2827f5359053.message:
rsxcore: a frame waits for its slot's use before it, as today's does

With RSX_PRESENT=0 nothing is presented, so the swap chain's buffer index
never moves and every frame uses one slot. Today's move_to_next_frame then
signals the slot's fence value again, which render_frame's opening
wait_for_gpu has already reached, so it doesn't wait: the GPU runs the frame
while the next batch records. The new path signalled a fresh value and
waited for it, a full drain every frame. That was about 0.2 ms a frame of
extra waiting on capset0 (+5% to +9% in halgate --time at RSX_PRESENT=0,
the only mode a locked PC can time). With presenting, the slots alternate
and both behaved alike.

move_to_next_frame now waits for the new slot's point from before this
frame, then stores this frame's. frame_cmd_begin waits for the slot's point
before its recorder is reset. After the opening drain that is a fence read,
and it keeps a repaint, which opens a slot right after a present, from
resetting a recorder still in flight. The slot points are cleared before
init's first frame_cmd_begin, so a device made again starts from zero.
