# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**The POSIX boot path runs in CI, but not yet with a retail title in this
tree.** `ps3recomp_boot_smoke` loads a synthetic PPU ELF through
`ppu_loader.cpp`, the HLE dispatch, guest threads, the frame clock and the
renderer. CI also builds and boots that ELF through `templates/project` on
macOS and Linux. That proves the per-game scaffold runs on both hosts; it is
not a compatibility claim for a retail game.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch

│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

HLE implementations of the PS3 system libraries, written for this project. RPCS3 is a behavioural reference, not a code source. Most modules are complete. The ones still marked Partial are the media decoders (cellVdec, cellAdec, cellDmux, cellAtrac, cellAdecAtrac3p) and cellSpurs. [docs/MODULE_STATUS.md](docs/MODULE_STATUS.md) has one row per module and is the source for the counts.

# Red Dead Redemption — Recompiled (PS3 → PC)

*[English below](#english)*

Recompilação estática **pessoal e experimental** de *Red Dead Redemption — Game of the Year Edition* (PS3, EUA; diretório de dados `BLUS30418`) para Windows x64, construída sobre o toolkit [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp).

> **Este repositório não contém o jogo.** Não há aqui executável, ELF, código traduzido do jogo, programas SPU, firmware, chaves, dados do disco, quadros crus nem logs (só as quatro capturas abaixo, da saída do port). Para compilar é preciso ter a sua própria cópia do jogo e produzir localmente os arquivos de entrada. Ver [docs/LEGAL.md](docs/LEGAL.md).

## Estado

> **Pesquisa, longe de ser jogável.** O jogo inicia, passa pelos menus e chega à **primeira cutscene 3D** (cerca de 2 minutos depois do boot), que roda a **4–6 FPS**. A tela título roda a 5–7 FPS.
>
> - **Áudio:** funcionando: música, ambiente e os vídeos da abertura (sete correções do runtime, a maioria genérica; ver [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md)).
> - **Desempenho:** limitado pela CPU. Um experimento com o PR sp00nznet/ps3recomp#632 (float do SPU nativo) levou a tela título a 29–44 FPS; ainda não está no build.
> - **Imagem:** a cena é desenhada com defeitos (cintilação, elementos sumindo, trechos escuros). O backend Vulkan do toolkit já compila no Windows, mas no RDR ainda desenha bem pior que o Direct3D 12.
> - **Entrada:** só XInput; a navegação até a cena é feita por roteiro de botões (`PAD_SCRIPT`).
> - **Estabilidade:** o PC hospedeiro já congelou em boots longos; por isso o jogo só deve rodar por `scripts\boot_seguro.ps1`.
>
> Detalhes, números e próximos passos: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).

## O que tem aqui

| Caminho | Conteúdo |
| :--- | :--- |
| `port/` | Projeto CMake do executável (derivado do `templates/project` do ps3recomp), `main.cpp`, `stubs.cpp`, `src/fs_area.c` e `src/audio_float/` |
| `patches/` | Mudanças no ps3recomp: `ps3recomp-v0.19.0-upstream-prs.patch` (12 PRs abertos do toolkit), `ps3recomp-v0.19.0-rdr.patch` (runtime e bibliotecas HLE) e `ps3recomp-v0.18.0-ppu_lifter.patch` (tabelas de salto do lifter) |
| `scripts/` | Preparação, build, boot protegido e atalhos (PowerShell), com caminhos relativos a `RDR_ROOT` |
| `launcher/` | Janela tkinter: confere a instalação, roda e para o jogo sempre pelo boot protegido |
| `analysis/` | Ferramentas de diagnóstico e análise, experimentos e scripts históricos das tentativas |
| `spu/` | `images.json`: identificadores (hash, tamanho) dos programas SPU, jobs e plugins DSP traduzidos — sem código |
| `docs/` | [BUILDING](docs/BUILDING.md), [STATUS](docs/STATUS.md), [DEBUGGING](docs/DEBUGGING.md), [RELATED_PROJECTS](docs/RELATED_PROJECTS.md), [LEGAL](docs/LEGAL.md); visão geral em [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) |
| `.github/workflows/` | CI `no-game-files`: falha se algo do jogo for rastreado ou se um arquivo passar de 2 MB |
| `local/` | **Ignorada pelo git.** ELF, lift, SPU traduzido, VFS, build, logs — tudo que vem do jogo |

## Capturas

Saída do próprio port (`LD_FRAME_DUMP`, 1280×720), boot `seg182` de 2026-11-08 (cópias NV0039 ligadas, hoje no build), sem retoque.

| | |
| :---: | :---: |
| ![Tela título](docs/screenshots/title-screen.jpg) | ![Tela de carga](docs/screenshots/loading.jpg) |
| Tela título (~8 FPS) | Carga da primeira missão |
| ![Abertura: barco ao longe](docs/screenshots/cutscene-boat.jpg) | ![Abertura: o cais](docs/screenshots/cutscene-dock.jpg) |
| Primeira cutscene: barco ao longe (~6 FPS) | O plano seguinte, no cais: escuro e com defeitos |

## Início rápido

1. Tenha a sua cópia do jogo e gere você mesmo o ELF decriptado e a árvore de dados (este repositório não explica nem automatiza isso).
2. Clone o ps3recomp na tag `v0.19.0` em `local\ps3recomp` e rode `scripts\prepare_toolkit.ps1` (aplica os 12 PRs em `local\ps3recomp-rdr`).
3. Traduza o ELF com o `ppu_lifter.py` da v0.18.0 mais `patches/ps3recomp-v0.18.0-ppu_lifter.patch`; para ter música, traduza também o `flashMP3.pic` do seu firmware com `analysis\tools\lift_mp3.py`.
4. `scripts\prepare_overlay.ps1` → aplica o patch do RDR em cópias, em `local\overlay`.
5. `scripts\build.ps1` → `local\build\MyGameRecomp.exe`.
6. `scripts\boot_seguro.ps1 -Tag teste -Segundos 330`, ou o launcher: `scripts\launch.ps1`.

Passo a passo completo em [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md).

## English

A **personal, experimental** static recompilation of *Red Dead Redemption — Game of the Year Edition* (PS3, US; data directory `BLUS30418`) to Windows x64, built on the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) toolkit.

> **This repository does not contain the game.** No executable, ELF, lifted game code, SPU programs, firmware, keys, disc data, raw frames or logs (only the four screenshots of the port's output shown here). You need your own copy of the game and must produce the inputs locally. See [docs/LEGAL.md](docs/LEGAL.md).

### Status

> **Research, far from playable.** The game boots, goes through the menus and reaches the **first 3D cutscene** (about 2 minutes after boot), which runs at **4–6 FPS**. The title screen runs at 5–7 FPS.
>
> - **Audio:** working: music, ambience and the intro videos (seven runtime fixes, most of them generic; see [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md)).
> - **Performance:** CPU-bound. An experiment with PR sp00nznet/ps3recomp#632 (native SPU float) took the title screen to 29–44 FPS; it is not in the build yet.
> - **Picture:** the scene renders with defects (flicker, disappearing elements, dark areas). The toolkit's Vulkan backend now builds on Windows, but on RDR it still draws far worse than Direct3D 12.
> - **Input:** XInput only; menus are driven by a scripted button sequence (`PAD_SCRIPT`).
> - **Stability:** the host PC has frozen during long boots, so only run the game through `scripts\boot_seguro.ps1`.
>
> Details and next steps: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) (Portuguese, with an English summary).

### Screenshots

The port's own output (`LD_FRAME_DUMP`, 1280×720), boot `seg182` from 2026-11-08 (NV0039 copies on, now in the build), untouched: title screen (~8 FPS), first-mission loading screen, and the first cutscene — the boat in the distance (~6 FPS), then the next shot on the dock, dark and with rendering defects. Images are in the table above.

### Quick start

1. Own the game and produce the decrypted ELF and the data tree yourself (this repository neither explains nor automates that).
2. Clone ps3recomp at tag `v0.19.0` into `local\ps3recomp` and run `scripts\prepare_toolkit.ps1` (applies the 12 PRs into `local\ps3recomp-rdr`).

03b0b8e7aca435f5ccbccb23b3f3200569288b25.message:
add native Edge vertex decompression and compression kernels

The Edge Geometry job (image 209) still spent ~20% of the SPU time in two
lifted loops after skinning and culling went native: 0x4448, which
decompresses the special vertex format (u16 positions with an offset and a
scale, 24-bit unit vectors), and the format-1 case of the compression
function 0x9780 (0x99E8 and its loop 0x9C20: three floats and two X11Y11Z10
words per vertex). Both are now native, bit-exact against the lifted code
in the offline harness, including the pipelined loops' stray stores (the
two zero quads past the decompressed vectors, the trailing pattern of the
compression's last step).

0x99E8 is a chunk inside 0x9780, so lift_spu.py learns NATIVE_ENTRIES
pairs (entry, continuation): the hook transfers to 0x98B0 instead of
returning, and compare mode runs the lifted chunk up to that point. The
hook insertion now leaves unchanged files alone, so a re-run does not
force the other SPU modules to rebuild.

Both kernels are opt-in: PS3RECOMP_NATIVE_EDGE_DEC and
PS3RECOMP_NATIVE_EDGE_ENC (1 on, 2 compare with the lifted code), until a
compare run in the game shows no difference.

run the scene walker natively; add Edge geometry kernels, off for now

Job bc11 (overlay 217) walks each view's scene tree, culls boxes against
height, size, distance and a visibility BSP, and writes the bucketed draw
list. Its worker (LS 0x4358) now runs in C with host floats in round-to-zero
and FTZ/DAZ, falling back to the SPU on exponent-255 inputs, overflow, or an
op the model lacks. In the city compare mode matched 408k jobs (10.9 us vs
54 us); 71% of jobs run natively, and with the camera turning heavy_bench
holds 69-82 fps where it held 62-66.

The Edge geometry kernels (skinning 0xD0A8, cull transform 0xA3C8, triangle
cull 0xA798) are wired but off: in-game compare found 143 cull differences in
4M calls and skinning rejecting every real input.

07681e3afb29bee9309798f40159b05b94670bf5.message:
export fragment depth; mailbox present; capture stacks on a hang

- Fragment programs with SHADER_CONTROL's depth-export bits write r1.z as
  SV_Depth. The game fills its 512x288 particle depth buffer with such a
  pass; without it the buffer kept its clear value and most particles were
  depth-tested and soft-tested against a flat 0.5, dropped or cut along
  straight lines.
- Vulkan presents with mailbox by default (PS3RECOMP_VK_PRESENT): FIFO
  blocked every present while the window was hidden and slowed the whole
  title to ~1 fps on another workspace.
- Closing the window exits the process instead of leaving it running
  headless.
- play.sh saves every thread's stack (eu-stack) after 30 s without a frame.
- PS3RECOMP_ENG_DRAWTRACE_PX names the draws that change one pixel.
- stwcx/stdcx read the reservation address through a volatile access, as
  the restrict-qualified lifted code writes it.

Suite 8/8.

queue pulled draws and pull vertices by default

A pulled draw waited for the recording thread to drain and recorded
itself, serialising both threads. Queued like other draws, vertex pulling
holds 55-59 fps while turning in the city, where the CPU fetch drops to

0efb21d615df2cd9fe0a3bd592a2d3e086f2faf4.message:
keep depth snapshots in VRAM, add a GPU profiler

A depth or stencil snapshot bounced through a host-visible buffer created on
every call: the bytes crossed the bus twice and each call allocated memory.
At 2x in New Marais six of them took ~8.4 ms of GPU time a frame against
2.9 ms for every draw. One device-local scratch buffer, grown as needed and
fenced between uses, replaces them: New Marais runs ~93 fps at 1x, 2x and
3x (native 4K), from 86 and 70.

PS3RECOMP_VK_GPUPROF=1 times every render pass and every other engine
operation with bottom-of-pipe timestamps and prints the totals by pass size
and by caller every 300 batches.

311738687884ac51d539c50914925a461d2a8f17.message:
keep a frame in flight on the GPU

A present submitted the frame and waited for the GPU to finish it, so GPU
time added to every frame: 21-33% of the RSX thread at 1x, 46% at 2x. Now
the next frame records into a second set of everything a batch holds
(command buffers and fence, window blit, rings, dead buffers, descriptor
pools, ZPASS queries, deferred readbacks) while the GPU renders the first.

ZPASS reports recorded before a clear in their batch carry the count of
the batches before, known once those complete. The small-target writeback
(the luminance the CPU reads for auto-exposure) is recorded before the
present and delivered when its batch completes, instead of forcing a wait
after every present. The parked frame is polled and completed as soon as
the GPU is done with it.

2x (2560x1440) pier walk: ~63 -> ~114 fps; RSX time at present 0-4%.
PS3RECOMP_VK_PIPELINE=0 restores the wait.

add adjustable FOV through a wrap of CView::SetFov

The camera's tangents (+0x2A8/+0x2AC) are computed only in SetFov
(func_0043E370), and everything that frames the world -- the projection
built by vf27, the frustum the culling jobs get, the screen<->world
helpers -- reads them. Poking +0x2A4 does nothing (the early return keeps
the old tangents) and scaling +0x29C feeds back through the FOV_TO blend
and the LOD factor, so the wrap runs the lifted body with a remapped f1
and puts the game's FOV and aspect back afterwards.

PS3RECOMP_FOV_SCALE (1 = the lifted code untouched) is the player's
option, live from the F1 menu ([video] fov, 0..30 %). PS3RECOMP_ASPECT
forces the aspect tan_x is taken with while the render target stays
720p: it exists to measure what a Hor+ frustum costs the CPU before the
ultrawide backend work. Only CView and CViewReflection are touched, and
each view remembers which settings computed its tangents so a change is
applied once even when the game keeps calling with the same FOV.

65c75cd2eded770ceaf70e177d51f31b3cdfd18f.message:
add a native kernel for the Edge index decompression (0xC7B8)

0xC7B8 decodes the compressed triangle lists (flags, 2-bit triangle codes
and bit-packed, delta-coded vertex numbers) in place, once per segment
before the cull. With the vertex kernels native it is the largest piece of
the geometry job still lifted (0.64% of the samples, 2.7% of the module).

The kernel runs the job's four loops on host-order copies and stores each
buffer exactly as the job leaves it, including the blocks unpacked past N0,
the list past the flags and the triangles of the last group past T. Loop 2
does eight entries per flag byte with one shuffle, loop 4 two triangles per
two-source permute, the same idea as the job's tables; scalar versions were
slower than the lift, which already does eight triangles at a time.

It falls back, before writing anything, where the job's pipelined in-place
loops could read their own stores, and on shapes no real segment has. The
offline harness compares the whole LS against the lifted code: 0
differences on 22000 random and malformed streams, 1.7-2.9x faster.

Opt-in with PS3RECOMP_NATIVE_EDGE_IDX (1 on, 2 compare) until a compare
run in the game shows no difference. lift_spu.py gets the native entry, so
the module needs a relift of its hooks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fd2845fbc6cc09a3dd3e18598c384b9c7b976532.message:
let the vertex decompression run on the job's own table layout

In the game's first compare run 0x4448 matched on millions of calls, but
18% of them still fell back to the lifted code. The job lays the uniform
tables out back to back, 16 bytes times the count rounded up to 8 apart
(0x7198), so with a count of 0 or 7 mod 8 the two zero quads past the
normals are the first two tangents, and the overlap guard refused that.

The two loops that write those spans run one after the other (0x4A30, then
0x4D18), so the guard now tags each written span with its loop and lets
spans of different loops overlap; the kernel writes them in the job's
order. Spans of one loop still may not overlap: the zero quads past the
normals landing on the positions is order-sensitive inside 0x4A30 and still
falls back.

The stats line also names why each fallback happened, so the next run says
whether anything but this layout is left.

00316e84d6112f9d6ff2efe39a0012a88330e908.message:
rsx-vtx: per-draw data paths -- pair memo, fast consecutive fetch, lazy first-sight hash, constant window reuse, texture bind memo

Profile basis: rsx5-prof-b3 (city dock, RSX thread 88.5% busy). 90% of the
draws there are index+vertex cache hits (vk_eng_draw_vbuf_ib 19.6% incl.), so
the vertex conversion itself is 5.0%; the larger cost on the hits is finding
the cache entries again (plan init 1.1%, plan prepare 1.8%, eng_vc_probe 4.7%,
key mixing) and copying constants into the write-combined uniform arena
(MoveSmall4 in vk_eng_draw_ex_body 3.2%). Every change has a switch; =0 is the
old path.

- PS3RECOMP_ENG_PAIR_MEMO (default 1): an index-cache hit remembers the
  vertex-cache entry it drew from and a hash of every register the search
  reads (layout, VERTEX_DATA_BASE_OFFSET, divider op, element base, run lo/span,
  each slot's VTXFMT / VTXBUF_OFFSET / current value). Same hash, no IO remap
  since (g_gcm_xlate_gen, new in cellGcmSys), entry still at its slot with its
  key, spans still write-protected with the same stamp -> the entry is taken
  without plan init, span mapping, key build, table probe and span merge. Only
  with rsx_wtrack mode 1 and no test reader; anything else goes the whole way
  (which records the pair again). A pair hit leaves fetch_plan unprepared
  (dc.plan_stale); the one later reader (sink_end's non-indexed refetch)
  prepares it.
- PS3RECOMP_ENG_FETCH_FAST (default 1): rsx_vertex_fetch_all_ex -- for a
  consecutive run (ranged remap / index-cache hit) each ordinary attribute whose
  stable span covers the run is read straight down the span: no per-vertex
  element index, range test or resolver; SNORM16 and CMP32 divide four lanes at
  once (SSE2 divps = the scalar divss per lane), UNORM8 reads a table built with
  the same division. Bit-identical: tests/test_vertex_fetch.c now also runs
  every 16-bit pattern (HALF/SNORM16/SINT16), every byte (UNORM8/UINT8) and
  64K random CMP32/FLOAT words, sizes 1-4, three strides, plus the random plans
  through the fast path: 0 failures.

0059f21685ca9d310f6e0cef3f9b0a9032f87b3f.message:
gcm/dispatch: whole FIFO headers to the draw engine in one call (GCM_FIFO_BURST)

The walker translated, read (out-of-line vm_read32 with its diagnostics gates)
and routed every data word on its own -- gcm_rsx_process_fifo_unlocked was
13% of the RSX thread's own samples, rsx_dispatch_method another 5-6%, in the
burning-city view on the pier (combat run, 262-270 s).

- cellGcmSys: a header whose words all go to the draw engine and nothing else
  (3D subchannel, lean state, no live engine, no per-word FIFO or guest memory
  diagnostic, none of SET_REFERENCE / GET_REPORT / the 0x1D6C-74 semaphore
  writes in its range, all words in one 1 MB IO page) is handed over whole:
  rsx_draw_engine_burst -> rsx_dispatch_burst. GCM_FIFO_BURST=0 = per word.
- rsx_dispatch_burst: exactly the rsx_dispatch_method calls of the per-word
  walk; runs inside the transform-constant window (usually right behind the
  VP_UPLOAD_CONST_ID word of the same header) and the program-upload window
  in tight loops, plain registers just stored (a method table built from the
  same ranges rsx_dispatch_method special-cases), the rest through it.
- eng_vtex_mask: the three fields it needs read from the registers instead of
  two full vertex-texture decodes (memset + 11 fields per unit) per draw.

Class V/E-neutral: the same register file, constants and program words.

04121bd2f98e2f49be61d40d7f23b0af6a7901c1.message:
jobrec: natives of a job's main function can be replay-checked; SPU_INTERP_REGTRACE

A native that replaces a job's main (it reads the inputs from guest memory and PUTs through
the MFC engine) cannot leave the local store as the lifted code does and issues none of its
channel operations. For such natives the job replay now:
- spu_native_dead_ls(lo,hi): skips the local-store ranges the native declares dead after it
  (stack frames below its caller, scratch, output buffers) in the end-of-job compare;
- spu_native_replay_begin(ctx): primes guest memory from the recording (every recorded GET's
  bytes at its EA, each GETLLAR's line, PUT targets committed), under a lock, zeroed after;
- spu_native_replay_end(ctx, ran): replaces the recorded operations from the native's entry up to
  the wrapper's 32-byte record PUT by checks of its results: every recorded PUT against guest
  memory (a 4096-byte command block through its first JUMP/RETURN word, the RSX never reads past
  it), every recorded atomic store against its guest line; the stream positions then continue.
No effect on jobs without such a native: ck-rec2 721, ck-rec3 272, spu3-p2 760 recordings pass.

SPU_INTERP_REGTRACE=<file>: the SPU interpreter (job replay with PS3_JOBREPLAY_INTERP=1) writes
"pc opcode rt-register" per instruction, to derive a job's arithmetic.

08b6db7e297ba2641b148dde65ef59cdc08070fe.message:
fp decompiler: DDX/DDY -- the Beast's shredded fragments in the prologue fight

The RSX screen-space derivatives were "unhandled FP opcode" comments, so their
destination kept whatever the register held (0 at the start). inFAMOUS 2's
Beast (the opening fight) is drawn whole into the scene, then its meshes are
drawn again into a 320x180 distortion map with FP d8160c63900ef8ce, which the
final composite uses to offset its scene reads. That program soft-tests each
fragment against the 512x288 depth copy -- which already holds the Beast --
with a slope allowance of |DDX z| + |DDY z| (r1.x, r2.x): discard where
copy + allowance <= z. With the allowance 0 the Beast's own surface z-fought
with its depth copy, the distortion map became a torn, quantised mask with
large offsets, and the composite drew the Beast as jagged horizontal
fragments (found with a RenderDoc capture of the fight: scene target correct,
distortion map 6449 torn, composite 23150 torn).

DDX/DDY now emit ddx()/ddy() (RPCS3: dFdx/dFdy), per RSX pixel under
PS3_RES_SCALE, DDY along the RSX window y (fp_alpha.y = -1 when SHADER_WINDOW
puts the origin at the bottom, as WPOS). Of the 1499 programs a scripted run
to the fight builds, these were the only unhandled opcodes. Unit test added.

0ae9f581f643402160aa64d9ec1e49dda158b649.message:
vulkan: depth_snapshot hands out a new texture per request

The engine owns what depth_snapshot returns: eng_zdepth_snapshot and the
crop release the copy they held once a newer one arrives, and the GPU
light path (eng_gpu_light_blit) releases its previous depth input without
comparing handles. Metal makes a new texture per request, which is what
that code is written against.

This backend kept ONE snapshot per depth target and refilled it, so the
light path released the very handle it had just been given: the light
pass then found a freed slot -- or, once reused, an unrelated texture --
and the next request "refilled" whatever now lived there. A crop of
another size likewise freed the full-size copy the engine still held. A
refill also overwrote depth that a caller was still to read; on Metal a
snapshot stays as it was when it was taken.

Now each request allocates its R32_SFLOAT texture and copies into it in
the same submission as the layout move; nothing links snapshots to their
depth target any more (the engine releases them, the table at shutdown).
The copy itself is vk_eng_copy_depth, for the RGBA8 decode to reuse.

0c0f5c735ae0c1b9e6eb195013902d54361a6e13.message:
perf: texture-pack images decoded once, off the RSX thread

A pack replacement's PNG was decoded on the RSX thread every time its texture
was created: 15-65 ms each (pf-sl-A: one 65.6 ms frame on the first fire after
the load, 4 images = 117 ms in the load frame, and again after each eviction).
Each pack entry now keeps its decoded image (512 MB budget; fire-smoke-hd is

0f360c95842df6dc7f674d79d2dbe556ccdf578c.message:
platform: PS3_CPU_PLACE / PS3_HIGHQOS -- host thread placement on hybrid CPUs (off by default)

Measured first (2026-11-08, ETW CPU sampling through the VS standard collector,
docks walk 262-270 s): left to Windows, the five SPURS worker threads ran ~40%
of their time on the E-cores, the RSX thread 21%, the main PPU thread 14%,
while the two guest pollers that spin in sub-ms usleep (the SPU light and Edge
geometry task kickers, ~90% of a core between them) sat on the P-cores.

runtime/platform/host_place.c places each host thread by role at its entry
(main PPU thread in ppu_run, SPU threads in spu_exec_thread_proc, guest PPU
threads in ppu_host_thread_proc, the FIFO-draining thread at its first
cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo) with Windows CPU Sets:
  p     main/RSX/SPU on the performance cores, the rest free
  pe    as p, everything else (process default) on the efficiency cores
  ded   main and RSX a P-core each (both hyperthreads), SPU the other P-cores,
        everything else the E-cores; dedx: SPU also on the E-cores
PS3_HIGHQOS=1 turns process power throttling (EcoQoS) off.

Result (combat.ps1, ded vs baseline): whole gameplay 262-378 s 81.5 vs 82.6 fps
-- no gain; the RSX thread's drain per frame was ~4% cheaper on its own core.
The E-core share was not what limited the frame. Kept as an A/B switch, off.

1a1169750328fb86e744131208d0ca8767e7c309.message:
vulkan: shader + pipeline disk cache

Every run translated each guest shader HLSL -> SPIR-V through glslang and
had the driver build every pipeline from nothing: the long black screen at
a level load and the hitch when an effect first appears. Both now persist
in one directory.

- <key>.spv: glslang's output, key = 128-bit FNV-1a (two seeds) of
  VK_SC_VERSION, a translator fingerprint, the PS3RECOMP_FRAGCOORD_W knob,
  the stage and the whole HLSL text. A hit skips glslang. A file is used
  only if it is whole words, has the SPIR-V magic, its instructions tile it
  exactly and end on OpFunctionEnd, and every OpEntryPoint/OpFunctionCall
  target is defined (catches a file cut between glslang's main and @main).
  The fingerprint is the SPIR-V of two canary shaders, translated once per
  run, so a glslang update or a translator option change invalidates every
  key by itself. Used by the engine (vk_eng_translate) and the older guest
  path (vk_guest_module).
- pipelines.bin: a VkPipelineCache passed to every vkCreateGraphicsPipelines
  (engine variants, guest, fallback, full-screen passes), behind our own
  header (magic, size, hash); the driver header (vendor, device, UUID) is
  checked before the driver sees it, and creation is retried empty if the
  driver refuses the data. Saved at shutdown, every 64 new pipelines (at
  most every 2 s) and 2 s after the last new one at a present, since the
  game is usually killed; an unchanged blob is not rewritten.
- All writes go to <name>.<pid>.tmp and are renamed over the target
  (MoveFileExA REPLACE_EXISTING / rename), so a kill never leaves a torn file.
- PS3RECOMP_VK_SHADER_CACHE=<dir> (default %LOCALAPPDATA%\ps3recomp\
  shader_cache\<title>, XDG/HOME cache off Windows), =0 off (behaviour as
  before); PS3RECOMP_VK_SHADER_CACHE_STATS=1 prints the stats line at every
  save (default: at most once per 64 shaders+pipelines, and at shutdown).
- PS3_FT_COMPILE spans: who 1/2 shader (b = from disk), 3 pipeline
  (b = call site), 5 pipeline-cache save.

Measured on the 1024

1acf75d441c7b21eed6b6bef23055a6724c941c6.message:
perf17: the SPU PUT "RSX memory?" test inline against the IO mappings' interval, no call per PUT (PS3RECOMP_SPU_PUT_INLINE)

critic2's freeze fix (5c5c5c3) asked cellGcmSys for every SPU PUT > 4 bytes and every
128-byte line commit whether it touches IO-mapped memory: an indirect call to
gcm_spu_put_is_rsx, a loop over the 16 mapping slots. cellGcmSys now keeps the
mappings' union in g_spu_put_rsx_lo/hi (runtime/spu/spu_channels.c) after every change
to s_io_mappings (init, auto-map, MapMainMemory, MapEaIoAddress, the iomap syscall,
unmaps, terminate), and spu_dma.h spu_put_is_rsx tests it inline: two compares when
the mappings are one interval (inFAMOUS 2: cellGcmInit's single 0x40500000 + 0x7900000
mapping), else the bounding box first and the old hook inside it. Same answers as the
hook (a reader racing a map/unmap call may mix old and new bounds for one PUT, which
only picks that PUT's copy order, as a stale hook answer did); the top-down copy itself
(gm_copy_to_desc) is unchanged, so runtime/memory/tests/test_gm_copy_order.c still
holds.

PS3RECOMP_SPU_PUT_INLINE=0 = the hook for every PUT, as m17; PS3RECOMP_SPU_PUT_DESC=0 =
ascending copies, as before critic2 (unchanged). A stderr line "[cellGcmSys] SPU PUT RSX
range lo-hi exact|box" shows the interval at each change (first 16).

Measured: in m17's dock ETW profile the hook was 62 of 69,577 samples (~0.06 ms of SPU
time per frame), and m17 with PUT_DESC=0 was within noise of PUT_DESC=1 (124.1 vs 124.9
fps, 3 + 1 clean runs): the freeze fix never cost real fps. This removes that small
cost; its fps effect is below the run noise (+-3%).

What the m16 -> m17 dock regression actually was (inf2-perf, 2026-11-11, ETW + census):
not this test. m17's PGO profile (inf2-r6next) names static functions by full source
path and was trained from wt\next + work\port-cpuint; m17 was built from wt\m17 +
work\port-m17, so every static function (the SPU channel/DMA inlines, the draw
engine's helpers) compiled without profile, and spu_wrch lost its own (critic2 changed
its CFG)

2f51546f839f90a26faa852557d1d18072c254ac.message:
critic: SPU bit-exactness -- spec float ops flush a folded denormal; csflt/cuflt never constant-folded with round-to-nearest

Found by the critic's SPU review (standalone probes, no game run):
- spu-cg's speculative fa/fs/fm/fma output step only turned -0 into +0, on the
  ground that FTZ never yields a denormal. True for an executed op, but with a
  constant second operand that the lift makes visible (il/ilhu in the same run
  after dead-store removal) clang folds x + -0, x * 1.0, x * -1.0 to x / -x and
  a denormal input passes through: spec 0x000003F0 / 0x800003F0 where the
  per-op form gives +0. 19 spec fm sites in the cpuint lift have such a +-1.0
  operand. Now the full exponent-0 flush (spu__xflush, two more operations).
  -DSPU_SPEC_OUT_OLD=1 = the old form.
- spu__xi_csflt / spu__xi_cuflt (spu_helpers_x86int.h, the forms in use) had no
  barrier, so a constant input was converted at compile time with
  round-to-nearest instead of the RZ MXCSR (cuflt 0xFFFFFFFB,155 -> 0x4F800000
  instead of 0x4F7FFFFF). Latent: 0 constant sites in today's lift. Now opaque.
Probes (work\critic\spu spec_fold_probe.c, fold_probe.c) built against these
headers: spec = per-op lean form, constant = runtime = scalar reference.
Needs the jobreplay gate (721/272/760 + rn fail) before merging.

30659a5bc025638412c29e987dc51a2561f57e9c.message:
vulkan: vertex/index caches, ranged VS constants, descriptor reuse, state filter, minimize -- skyline 38 -> 51 fps

The Empire City skyline at the end of the boat cutscene (5-8k draws a frame)
was RSX-thread bound at ~38 fps: ~24 ms of sink_end per frame.

- vbuf_create / vbuf_release / draw_vbuf / draw_vbuf_ib: the engine's vertex
  and index caches were off on this backend (Metal had them). Persistent
  buffers are sub-allocated from 64 MB host-coherent chunks in size classes
  (no per-entry allocation: NVIDIA's 4096 limit); released blocks are freed
  with the batch's dead objects. fetch+decode 6.1 -> ~1 ms, remap 1.7 -> 0.4.
- bind_vs_constants_range: only the rows the program reads, the viewport
  tail and the PS block are written into the draw's uniform window (52 MB of
  constant copies a frame before).
- The constant blocks are dynamic UBOs, so a descriptor set is just the
  textures and samplers: sets are reused within a batch (87% of draws),
  PS3RECOMP_VK_DSET_REUSE=0 = a set per draw.
- Redundant pipeline/viewport/scissor/stencil/bias/vertex/index binds inside
  one open pass are skipped (PS3RECOMP_VK_STATE_FILTER=0 records all).
- Engine: the age-due full texture re-hashes are budgeted per frame
  (PS3RECOMP_ENG_TEXHASH_BUDGET_MB, default 12): a camera cut put 50-73 MB of
  hashing in one frame.
- A minimized window (no drawable area) pauses presenting and is rebuilt on
  restore; it used to drop the window for good (black screen after a
  minimize).

107 -> 123 fps, boat cutscene 60. Pictures unchanged, no Vulkan errors.

36cb41467272c05b0e4aebc23de58e53531aff33.message:
rsx-par: the RSX frame on two threads (PS3RECOMP_RSX_SPLIT, default 1; 0 = one thread, as before)

The thread that drains the FIFO keeps the walk and runs the register
dispatcher on an instance of its own; the draw engine (sink_end and everything
under it, the Vulkan recording included) runs on a new exec thread, rsx_exec,
on the engine's instance, fed through a 16 MB single-producer ring
(libs/video/rsx_split.c). At the dock the walk + dispatch were ~20% of the RSX
thread (rsx5 profile b3), so the engine thread no longer pays them.

- State: the walker's instance tracks the 64-byte blocks of regs/vp/constants
  it writes (rsx_dispatch.dirty, marked per burst range / per word / per upload
  run); before every event the changed blocks go into the ring (a block whose
  bytes the engine already holds is not sent). Events = the dispatcher's sink
  calls (clear, begin, arrays, index, inline, end, flip) with current_primitive,
  in_begin_end, pair_packets, vp_gen and the texture/misc generation counters
  (now per instance: rsx->tgen/mgen; the exec thread writes the globals the
  engine reads before each sink call). Inline arrays travel in the event and
  land in g.rsx.inline_data. The two upload windows' own registers are not
  followed (nothing but the dispatcher reads them).
- Guest-visible effects of the walk itself (NV406E semaphore release, back-end
  labels, SET_REFERENCE fences, reports, user commands, flip requests, FIFO
  flip words, the 2D / memory-copy subchannels) are queued actions run on the
  exec thread in FIFO order behind the draws before them (gcm_split_run).
- The walker waits for the exec thread before a semaphore acquire reads its
  label (only up to the last queued action) and for everything at the end of
  a drain, so GET, the fence publication, the ring recycle, the present and
  the window pump see a quiet engine as before. A drain that catches up while
  the title moved put walks on (up to ~4 ms) instead of stopping cold.
- Only when the walker's fast conditions hold (lean state, no FIFO dia

4dcdbb5d55ffd9c79445919bb49d429e7143fa3d.message:
spu-cg: lifted SPU codegen -- dead register stores, speculative float runs, cold fix-ups out of line, vector csflt/cuflt

What the x86 of long lifted SPU functions spent its time on (job 201's hot leaf 0x9D98,
llvm-mca over the fall-through path): one ctx->gpr store per SPU instruction (LLVM's DSE gives
up on these functions), a movemask + branch after every checked float op (blocks of a few
instructions, so the scheduler cannot shorten live ranges), cflts's four scalar exact lanes
inlined into the hot code, and an out-of-line spu_img_restore call after every SPU call.

Lift (tools/spu_lifter.py, cg_rewrite; default on, =0 = the old form, off with --trace or
register locals):
- SPU_LIFT_DSE: in a straight run of register statements, a register write the same run
  writes again goes to a C local instead of ctx->gpr. Nothing can read ctx->gpr inside such a
  run, so the register file at every label, branch, call, return and runtime call is the old
  one. (--no-dse)
- SPU_LIFT_SPEC_FLOAT: a stretch of such a run with no LS store and >= 2 checked float ops
  (fa fs fm fma fms fnms cflts cfltu) runs first with the checks deferred (spu_*_spec: no
  branch per op, one unsigned max into an accumulator, one test at the end). If any op would
  have taken its exact path, nothing has been stored for the registers it read and then
  overwrote, and the stretch runs again in the ordinary per-op form -- same bits either way
  (each _spec result is the per-op fast result; the verdict is the per-op test). Per-site
  counter: a site that took its exact path PS3_SPU_SPEC times (default 64, 0 = never
  speculate, run time) stops speculating. Knobs: SPU_LIFT_SPEC_MIN (2), SPU_LIFT_SPEC_MAX
  (256 statements), SPU_LIFT_SPEC_SAVE=slot (old values in volatile stack slots instead of
  new values committed after the test), SPU_LIFT_SPEC_VOLX=1 (exact pass rereads via volatile
  loads) -- both measured worse. (--no-spec-float)

Helpers (runtime/spu/spu_helpers.h, lifted AVX2 TUs; -D...=0 = the old form):
- SPU_CG_COLD: the vector RZ fix-ups

6678667bd7c842797465c1ff2fbadd01acc200af.message:
rsx_wtrack: page-protection write tracking for the texture, vertex and index caches (PS3RECOMP_WTRACK)

Every cached texture (sparse every frame + budgeted full hashes), every
resident vertex range and every resident index list was re-hashed each frame
to learn that nobody had written it: eng_hash_span + the two texture hashes +
eng_vc_probe were ~16% of the RSX thread in the burning-city view (combat run
262-270 s), nearly all of it cache misses on bytes that had not changed.

Now the pages under an entry are made read-only when it is hashed (an idea
from RPCS3's texture cache, written fresh here). A write faults once: a
vectored handler (first in the chain, ahead of the VM's commit-on-access one)
makes the page writable again and bumps its version. An entry whose pages are
all still protected with the version sum it saw is unchanged -- no byte read.
Protocol (rsx_wtrack.h): arm = protect, then read versions, then hash; fault =
unprotect, then bump, then clear the flag; so every unprotect is followed by a
bump and a write after the protect can never be missed. Kernel writes (fread
into guest memory: cellFs.c, ppu_fs.cpp read + aio) do not fault -- they would
fail with ERROR_NOACCESS -- so they are bracketed through g_vm_host_io_hook
(ppu_loader.cpp): pages unprotected and pinned before, bumped after. Pages
that fault three times with <= 4 frames between rest 240 frames (dynamic and
double-buffered data stays on the hash path, as before). A span that cannot be
armed falls back to the old logic; a dirty texture that could be armed gets the
full hash (exact, no sparse shortcut).

PS3RECOMP_WTRACK=0 off, 1 on (default), 2 shadow: track AND hash, report every
"clean" entry whose bytes changed. PS3RECOMP_WTRACK_STATS=1: faults, protect
calls, rested pages, kernel writes, shadow misses / passes every 600 frames.

Gate (rsx-s1, WTRACK=2, whole combat run incl. streaming loads): 0 missed
writes in 15.3 M shadow checks; 0 Vulkan errors. Steady gameplay costs ~40-90
write faults and ~45 protect calls a frame. Drawstats (rs

70e1fabc83dc0667cfb5f6caebb4edfc891cc03a.message:
video: shadow casters keep their polygon offset -- the Kuo dock-cutscene face/clothes stripes (PS3RECOMP_VK_BIAS_RESET, PS3RECOMP_ENG_SOFT_BIAS)

The cause (first difference against RPCS3): the character shadow map (zeta 0x0F2F0000, read by the
bit-7 receivers' mask FP 25f427a67ef667f7, whose own reference bias is 0) is drawn with the casters'
polygon offset on (POLY_OFFSET_FILL, slope 1, 2000 units; the guest registers say so, POLY_OFFSET_LOG).
RPCS3 draws those no-cull character casters with depth bias 1000 (its NVIDIA D24 half of 2000) /
slope 1.0; the port drew them with 0 / 0: the Vulkan state filter (744f6df) skipped vkCmdSetDepthBias
when the factors repeated, but a pipeline without polygon offset (the second-depth world casters,
cull FRONT, between the characters) declares depth bias static, and binding it invalidates the dynamic
value. Only the pass's first offset draw got its bias; the characters met their own depth in the map:
at Cole's forehead the four PCF taps 0.18557 0.18214 0.18391 0.18032 against reference 0.18076 ->
0.497 (acne), where slope 1 adds ~0.0034 (one texel of slope) to every tap.

- PS3RECOMP_VK_BIAS_RESET (live, default 1; 0 = as before): binding a static-bias pipeline clears the
  filter's "bias set" flag, so the next offset draw sets its bias again.
- PS3RECOMP_ENG_SOFT_BIAS (live, default 1; 0 = as before): with the Lighting page's soft shadows
  (s > 0) a positive caster slope offset is multiplied by R = s + 1, the tent's radius in texels (the
  game sizes its offset for the RSX's 2x2 filter; Softer left faint bands on lit faces).

7b5d44c338c77b422ebbe6cc6f2bb91f8c7bc5a9.message:
spu_coherency: full fences on the PPU-reservation Dekker pair

A PPU line reservation (lwarx + ppu_resv_line_note) and an SPU write to
the same line form a Dekker pair: the PPU publishes "I hold the line" and
then reads other words of it; the writer (PUTLLC/PUTLLUC/PUT) stores into
the line and then reads the reservation records to break them. Both
halves used release stores (a plain mov on x86), so each side's load
could pass its own buffered store: the SPU found no reservation to break
and the PPU read the line from before the SPU's commit -- and the
store-conditional succeeded on stale reads.

inFAMOUS 2 deadlocked there on every full-speed boot: libsre's
_cellSpursSendSignal read the fios decompression task's `waiting` bit as
0 just as the task set it, committed `signalled` without sending the
workload signal, and the task slept forever with waiting=signalled=1
(taskset 0x47E7E380, wid 3). fios never got its block, and the title
never left the loading emblem. Slowing presentation (per-frame dumps)
hid it some of the time.

Publish the PPU record SEQ_CST and fence after it; fence in
ppu_resv_clear before the records are read. Full-speed boots to the 3D
title: 0/8 before, 4/4 after.

7d04b0285f6721d32c33120a6530824f7c5ad949.message:
rsx-par2: fix the boot hang under PS3RECOMP_VK_BT (vk_tq_sync waited for r == w) + PS3_STALL_MS sees the RSX threads

The cycle (cv-B1-fight, 1 boot in ~6, right after START when the first
texture-pack images are applied):
- the texture-pack preload thread decodes pack images through
  g.be->image_load; under PS3RECOMP_VK_BT that thunk drained the recording ring
  (vk_tq_sync) from the preload thread.
- vk_tq_sync waited for the worker's position to EQUAL the published one it
  read. Only the producer can rely on that; here rsx_exec kept recording, the
  worker went past that value and the preload thread spun for ever -- holding
  its claim on the pack entry (st 1).
- rsx_exec then wanted that same entry (eng_mod_take: usleep loop while st 1),
  the walker waited in rsx_split_sync for rsx_exec, the SET_REFERENCE 0x683 it
  had queued never ran, and the main thread waited for ref 0x683 for ever.
  Evidence: "[mods] N pack image(s) decoded ahead" (printed when the preload
  thread finishes) is in every healthy probe log (27 images) and missing in
  cv-B1-fight; the game kept ~3 cores busy in the hang (the spinning thread).

Fix:
- vk_tq_sync waits until the worker is AT OR PAST the position (r >= w): r and
  w only grow, so this is right for any caller (same result for the producer).
- PS3RECOMP_VK_BT's image_load / image_save go straight to the backend from
  any thread: file + PNG code, no backend state, no drain, no touch of the
  producer's bind memory.

Diagnosis for next time (PS3_STALL_MS / PS3RECOMP_LIMITS=1): a [stall-rsx] line
after every [stall] line -- the split ring (owner, wl, pub, w, r, rc,
label_pos, sleep/wait flags), the recording ring (w, r, wlocal, sleep, direct,
presents), and for the walker, rsx_exec and rsx_vk_record: the wait each one
marks (rsx_diag_wait: split ring, vk_tq_sync, present wait, full ring, idle,
eng_mod_take) with its age, host RIP and up to 8 return addresses in the exe
(exe+offset, map with the PDB). Targets are suspended only for the register
read and an 8 KB stack copy.

8fe6309cab7114a223a1f8c94e1012efe434ebb5.message:
vulkan: FUNC_ADD_SIGNED blending (0xF006) -- the Beast's heat distortion

The second half of the prologue Beast bug (after DDX/DDY). inFAMOUS 2 builds
its heat distortion in a 320x180 A8R8G8B8 map cleared to 0x80 (no offset): the
Beast's meshes, fire and explosions draw into it with FP d8160c63900ef8ce and
friends under NV4097_SET_BLEND_EQUATION 0xF006 (FUNC_ADD_SIGNED, both halves)
and ONE/ONE, writing each offset as x for x >= 0 and 1 + x for x < 0 (cc
select + 1.0), and the final composite reads the map back unsigned around 0.5
(uv + map * 0.0398). That only adds up if the blend takes the SOURCE as a
two's-complement byte: dst + signed(src). Drawn as FUNC_ADD (no signed blend
in Vulkan; RPCS3 does the same and logs it), every negative offset saturated
the map at 1.0, i.e. a +0.5 shift: with DDX/DDY fixed the Beast was still
striped by 25-px shifts wherever the noise went negative.

Vulkan clamps a UNORM source to [0,1] before blending, so such a draw is split:
the positive half as written (max(s, 0), FUNC_ADD with the guest factors),
then the same draw again with the negative half (max(-s, 0)), REVERSE_SUBTRACT,
dst factor ONE and only the signed lanes written (s = the byte the RSX would
store, read as two's complement; the program's single-float4 return is
wrapped, _rsx_sblend). Exact unless a lane saturates half-way. The distortion
map in a RenderDoc capture of the fight goes from a torn mask of full-scale
offsets to a faint, smooth silhouette; the Beast is solid with glowing cracks,
as on the PS3 (reference: YouTube PS3 walkthroughs of the prologue).

PS3RECOMP_VK_SIGNED_BLEND: 1 (default) splits the ONE/ONE case only; 2 also
the SRC_ALPHA/ONE (alpha ZERO/ONE) particles the game blends signed -- not
checked against hardware yet, so not default; 0 = FUNC_ADD everywhere (old).
Factors that read the split source itself keep FUNC_ADD and are logged, as is
any other blend equation the backend does not map.

962eed58388b6542a20599d465bb5baf56d691c0.message:
vulkan: cut the 1080p GPU waste -- depth read in place, decals through input attachments

Both behind switches read at the engine's init ([res] in rsx_vulkan_backend.c):
- PS3RECOMP_VK_ZDIRECT (default on; 0 = the copies): engine depth targets are
  sampleable with depth- and stencil-aspect views. The depth-as-RGBA8 decode
  reads them in its one pass (kVkDepthRgba8DFS / DnFS) and the R32F depth
  snapshot is a pass reading the depth view (kVkDepthR32FS), instead of
  depth -> buffer -> R32F image (+ stencil -> buffer -> R8) every time. Same
  values. The decode/snapshot set ring grows 16 -> 64.
- PS3RECOMP_VK_FBF=input|copy (default input): the engine's framebuffer fetch
  (decals reading the G-buffer they draw into) through input attachments.
  Engine render passes declare their colour attachments as input attachments
  with a by-region self-dependency; the SubpassInput programs get
  [[vk::binding(K, 1)]] (set 1, bindings K and 16+K: glslang shifts it); a
  per-target-set descriptor set (vk_fbfin_set, keyed by handle + serial) and a
  by-region barrier before each such draw replace the full-target copies and
  the render pass break of every decal. copy = the previous copies.
City test, 1080p + play.ps1 extras, one exe A/B: GPU busy 12.0 -> 5.4 ms/frame,
dock view 65.5 -> 102.5 fps; 720p picture check vs the golden passes.

spu: DMA path and call drain without their per-call overhead (PS3_SPU_DMA_FAST, PS3_SPU_DRAIN_FAST)

- PS3_SPU_DMA_FAST (default 1): mfc_do_transfer_raw / mfc_submit_body carry ~50
  environment-gated probes (a static load and branch each, on every one of ~2.5 M
  transfers a second, in a 0x268-byte frame with a stack cookie). With none of those
  variables set, mfc_do_transfer_lean / mfc_submit_lean do what is left, in the same
  order: the malformed / size / LS / committed-EA checks, the copy, the overlay note and
  LS watch for a GET, the reserved-line copy-and-notify, PUT hook and sync watch for a
  PUT, the same tag bookkeeping, the always-on policy trace and batch probe. Any of the
  variables set selects the full functions (the list is every getenv in them).
- PS3_SPU_DRAIN_FAST (default 1): spu_drain_call's front takes the case the callee has
  already returned (pc == return_pc, nothing or the depth-0 dispatcher pending) with the
  same steps -- depth guard, transfer cleared, drain_ret_pc cleared -- without the full
  drain's jmp_buf frame, eight saved registers and stack cookie. The depth guard's fast
  part is inlined (same ring, same limit, same trip).

230/272 fail. Replay time vs both off: 204 -5%, 210 -3.5%, others -0..-12%.

b34b05156121cad4bff24c7ab0a869623498c3bc.message:
spu: exact native single precision on x86 (MXCSR round-toward-zero + FTZ + DAZ) -- skyline 48 -> 56 fps

Every SPU run executes with MXCSR at round toward zero, flush-to-zero and
denormals-are-zero -- the SPU's own single-precision rules -- and the lean
fa/fs/fm/fma/fms/fnms are the host's native ops plus one range check and the
+0 rule (~7 operations instead of ~35). Lanes whose result reaches FLT_MAX or
Inf/NaN (the SPU's extended range) are redone on the exact integer path.
The mode is set on entry to spu_run_with_halt and restored on exit (runs can
happen on PPU threads); double precision (round to nearest on the SPU) and the
double compares switch back to the default MXCSR around themselves. An empty
asm on one operand keeps clang from folding a constant op in round-to-nearest.
Same mechanism as upstream PR #632 (x86, open) and RPCS3's SPU threads.
SPU_FLOAT_RZ=0 = the exact emulation in the default MXCSR (A/B).

Also fixes the default-mode lean fa/fs: TwoSum's s - x overflowed next to
FLT_MAX (x + -FLT_MAX rounded away from zero), leaving e NaN and the result
one ulp too large (0x7BAC9CC0 + 0xFF7FFFFF = FF7EA6C6, exact FF7EA6C5); a NaN
or Inf e now takes the exact path. Same fix in the NEON form (not run here).

Gates (PLAN.md "speed WITH precision"):
- tests/test_spu_float_rz_x86.c: 3M vectors x 33 float ops (random words plus
  zeros, denormals, extended range, overflow, cancellation; double precision,
  conversions, estimates, compares) -- both forms equal the integer
  definition, every other helper equal in both modes: 0 mismatches.
- -DSPU_FLOAT_RZ_CHECK in-game build: 7,247,757,312 vector ops checked against
  the integer path over the scripted suite, 0 lanes differ.
- Picture suite: characters, skyline, gameplay as the golden set.
- title_batch 6/6.
Suite (same build, SPU_FLOAT_RZ=0 -> on): title 86 -> 104, boat cutscene
58.6 -> 73.1, skyline 48.2 -> 56.3, docks 70 -> 86, gameplay 122 -> 137 fps.

   a frame is drawn, post-processed and submitted but not presented; presenting
   resumes with the first frame after it comes back on.

(the writer's longest disk write), acq / qp (longest acquire / present, timed on
the thread that makes them), tqw (the RSX thread waiting for the recording
worker), slow (longest texture create/upload/release or completed-batch free),

bfe27bed501400063cd04864cd68a7f44b5346d7.message:
vulkan: image quality -- SMAA/FXAA, CAS sharpening, FSR 1 upscale, 16x anisotropic filtering (vk_postfx.c)

A new module, libs/video/vk_postfx.{c,h}, with five marked [postfx] hooks in
rsx_vulkan_backend.c (device feature, init, shutdown, the present, the
sampler). At present, before the blit into the window, the 1280x720 frame
goes through:
  AA       SMAA 1x (SMAA.hlsl as GLSL 4, high preset, luma edges) or
           FXAA 3.11 (quality 29)
  upscale  window larger than the frame (fullscreen 1080p): FSR 1 EASU to
           the window's size + RCAS, instead of the bilinear stretch
  sharpen  window = frame: AMD CAS (gamma-2 input, per the CAS docs)
and the engine's samplers get anisotropic filtering where the guest
minifies linearly through mipmaps (point/LUT/unmipped samplers untouched;
the level is part of the sampler key, cache 64 -> 256 for live changes).
The shader libraries are the vendored third_party sources compiled with
glslang at run time; only the wrappers are ours.

Settings (env at start; vk_postfx_set*() live, for the overlay menu):

value (checked equal to the ulong original on 44M inputs). Every pass is
recorded, submitted and waited for at once, like everything else in this
backend, so the call order is the stream order and one UBO and descriptor
set per pass suffices. Outputs are COLOR objects so surface_view and

c3169b44126b5c176ed11205395558e52914af7d.message:
gcm/draw engine: RSX-thread CPU -- skip the dead copies into the GPU-light inputs, separable NV309E swizzle, no getenv per drain

From an ETW profile of the docks walk (VS standard collector, 1 kHz with stacks,
line-resolved through the PDB): the RSX/frame-clock thread was 85% busy and the
frame's bottleneck there; ~9-11% of it was nv3089_blit memmoving the normals and
depth targets into the light job's two main-memory buffers.

* PS3RECOMP_ENG_GPU_LIGHT_SKIPCOPY (default 1): with both GPU passes on
  (PS3RECOMP_ENG_GPU_LIGHT + _GPU_SSAO) eng_gpu_light_blit already skips the
  source's write-back, so the blit copied the same stale VRAM bytes into
  buffers no SPU job reads any more and whose texture units the engine binds
  to the GPU outputs. rsx_draw_engine_gpu_light_dst_dead() says so after the
  write-back call (only when that call took the light path) and the guest
  copy is skipped. =0 keeps the copy.
* NV309E_FAST (default 1): swz(x,y) = swz(x,0) | swz(0,y) (the x and y bits
  never share a position): a per-blit x table and one OR per pixel instead of
  a bit loop per pixel. Same words to the same places; =2 also runs the loop
  and logs any differing offset; =0 the old loop.
* GCM_RATE / GCM_CTXDBG / GCM_DRAINDBG / GCM_SCANREF / CELLMARK_BLINKDBG are
  read once instead of a getenv per drain (0.9% of the RSX thread).

Measured with the rest of the perf work (PGO + the frame-clock kick, private
build): combat.ps1 262-378 s 82.6 -> 88.5 fps, docks 262-270 (city view)

rsx_shader_spirv: rsx_glsl_to_spirv for the Vulkan backend's own passes

The Vulkan backend's full-screen passes (GPU light, SSAO, depth decode)
are written in GLSL, not run through the decompilers, so they need a
GLSL front end next to the HLSL one: same glslang driver, Vulkan 1.0

preamble, and no legalisation passes, so the NoContraction decorations

sys_timer: PS3_USLEEP_WAIT=spin|pause|sleep[:<us>] -- how a sub-ms usleep waits (A/B, default spin)

The main PPU thread waits for SPU jobs and the GCM ref with usleep(1)/usleep(5)
polls (func_0038B43C, func_0038AA14, func_0013ACE8); on Windows each turn of
the spin is a SwitchToThread syscall plus a QPC read. In the docks-walk profile
(ETW, pf-prof1) those waits were ~33% of the main thread, a third of it kernel
entry/exit, and the two guest task kickers spin on usleep(100..900) for ~0.9
of a core.

  spin   (default) the existing yield-spin to the QPC deadline
  pause  PAUSE-spin to the deadline, SwitchToThread only every ~64 us
  sleep  once a thread has polled from one guest call site (same lr, calls
         < 30 us apart) for <us> (default 200), each further usleep sleeps on
         a per-thread CREATE_WAITABLE_TIMER_HIGH_RESOLUTION timer (~0.5 ms
         granularity on this machine: 100 us -> 530 us, measured) -- a real
         wait that may see the condition up to ~0.5 ms late.

Timing only; the guest sees the same values.

dbaf4517fd323bfe03c5ebd7c8ee588c2bb247cc.message:
ppu-xfn: real tail calls (PPU_XTAIL) + inlined leaves (PPU_XINLINE), lift-time switches

PPU_XTAIL=1: a direct tail jump (b/bc to another function, a body running off its end,
a jump-table arm outside the function) is emitted as a clang musttail call (one jmp)
instead of the trampoline + return + the caller's drain loop. Drain elision then follows
the tail-call graph (least fixed point): 26307 of 32426 functions never return with the
trampoline set (21640 before); static drains 36740 -> 25860. A function the elision
takes as clean that still has a trampoline stops the lift. PPU_XTAIL_VERIFY=1 keeps each
dropped drain as a test that reports and runs a pending trampoline.

PPU_XINLINE=1: a bl to a small frameless leaf (no call/syscall/HLE/indirect jump, no LR,
no r1, no write to r2/r13, no non-volatile register, no hook/native/patch, <= 48
statements, <= 160 with at most 3 bl sites: PPU_XINLINE_MAX / PPU_XINLINE_FEW) is lifted
in place of the call, before the callee-save and register-locals passes: labels renamed
per site, return -> goto end of site, a tail jump -> call + drain + goto. Leaves made by
the mid-function passes are learned afterwards and their callers lifted again (3641).
8505 call sites in 4211 functions; register-locals pass keeps 0 functions plain.

All off (unset/0) = the old lift, byte for byte.

dfee0febb0a5ec5267dece6439d14d98d2f1287f.message:
rsx-par: the Vulkan backend's draw work on the recording worker (PS3RECOMP_VK_BT, default 1; 0 = as before)

vk_threaded_rec.h moved the driver's vkCmd* cost to the worker; the backend's
own per-draw work (vk_eng_draw_ex_body and the binds: arenas, descriptor set,
framebuffer, pass logic, state filter -- ~21% of the RSX thread at the city
dock, rsx5 profile b3) stayed on the engine's thread. Now the engine calls the
backend through thunks (libs/video/vk_threaded_be.h):

- binds, sets, clears, the three draws and the releases are TQ_BCALL records
  in the same ring (arguments and pointed-to bytes copied); the worker runs
  the backend's own function in ring order. bind_vs_constants_range's rows go
  into a worker-side buffer (the backend keeps that pointer until the draw).
- every call that returns something or reads a pointer in place (creates,
  uploads, snapshots, light/SSAO passes, pipelines, readback, present,
  submit_and_wait, image load/save) drains the ring and runs on the calling
  thread, as before: the backend's state is touched by one thread at a time.
- vbuf_create runs on the engine thread without a drain (its handle/block
  lists now take a recursive lock: create, release, free; a create that opens
  a new chunk drains first); surface_view is answered from a memo checked
  against per-slot release counters (s_eobj_sg) and dropped on every release
  the engine makes; vbuf_prefetch is a no-op.
- the ring is drained at the end of every FIFO drain (g_rsx_drain_end_hook)
  and after the engine's present, so the frame loop finds the worker idle
  whenever it touches the backend directly.
- with the switch on, the worker by default chases the producer
  (PS3RECOMP_VK_TQ_WAKE_KB default 0 instead of 64) and is not pinned to the
  E-cores (PS3RECOMP_VK_THREADED=2 still pins it): it now does real work.

e20c89db05f20f6234996bf9cbd9c5aa62c7c053.message:
vulkan: frames in flight, GPU-local depth bounce, GPU timestamp profiler -- gameplay 48 -> 86 fps

Frames in flight (PS3RECOMP_VK_FIF, default 2; 1 = old): the windowed present
submitted the frame's batch and waited for it, so the RSX thread idled while the GPU
drew and the GPU idled while the next frame was recorded (~8 ms recording + ~10 ms
waiting, in series; the guest main thread then waited on the RSX thread). Two slots:
command buffer, fence, acquire semaphore, arenas, per-draw descriptor pool, dead lists,
the passes' UBOs and descriptor sets and the timestamp pool are per slot; the active
slot's stay where the code already used them and the other's are parked. Objects freed
while the other slot's frame may use them go to the active slot's dead list.

Depth decodes bounced depth and stencil through the host-visible staging arena (two
PCIe crossings, ~1.2 ms each, twice a frame); now a device-local bounce arena.

PS3RECOMP_VK_GPU_PROF=1: timestamps around every pass, gap, backend pass and the
present blit, per-interval command counts, a per-frame report every 5 s
(_DUMP=1: one raw frame). PS3RECOMP_VK_BARRIER_MODE: measurement only.

ppu-vmx: VMX float ops test only operands that may be denormal, integer AltiVec on SSE, single FP in float registers, one-instruction fctiw

Lift-time switches (tools/ppu_vmx_flow.py, called from ppu_fastpath; all =0 = the lift
as before, byte for byte):

  ops, word compares, splats/shifts/merges of clean words, splat immediates without
  denormal lanes, logic ops that keep whole clean lanes. Each float op gets a mask of the
  operands that still need the denormal test (vmx_*_k in ppu_vmx_sse.h); the result test

  hot path 599 -> 441 instructions. PPU_VMX_CLEAN_VERIFY=1 = the check build.

e3ef8005de896bf2ed0a056788ed096a1f0662ac.message:
vulkan: batch the draw engine's work instead of waiting on every operation

The backend submitted and waited on every operation, so each draw cost a
full CPU -> GPU -> CPU round trip; the inFAMOUS 2 title spent ~265 ms of
each ~340 ms frame in RSX drains, mostly blocked on fences (2.8 fps).

PS3RECOMP_VK_BATCH (default on; =0 restores the synchronous path):
- draws, clears, target/texture creation, texture uploads, colour and
  depth snapshots and the depth-as-RGBA8 pass record into the one open
  command buffer; it is submitted at a present, a readback, the engine's
  submit_and_wait hook, a full arena or descriptor pool;
- per-batch linear arenas for vertices, indices, constants (the VS file
  and the bound PS bytes, from a CPU shadow) and transfer staging; one
  descriptor set per draw from a pool reset at each flush;
- consecutive draws into the same framebuffer continue one render pass
  (barriers once per run; a draw sampling one of the pass's own targets
  starts a new pass behind a barrier, as every draw did before);
- images and framebuffers destroyed mid-batch are retired with it;
- the frame rides in the window present's own submit; the full-frame CPU
  readback is skipped unless PS3RECOMP_VK_DUMP / PS3RECOMP_VK_READBACK;
- PS3RECOMP_VK_BATCH_STATS=1 reports flushes per source line; fence waits
  are PS3_FTRACE GPU_WAIT spans (kind 12).

inFAMOUS 2 3D title: 2.8 -> 7-9 fps; RSX drains 75% -> 20% of wall time,
the remaining wait is on the guest's own semaphores. Boots to the title
3/3 batched, 1/1 with PS3RECOMP_VK_BATCH=0.

ppu_lifter: register locals (PPU_NV_LOCALS), memory-gate snapshot (PPU_MM), drain elision (PPU_DRAIN_ELIDE), SO-zero compares (PPU_SO_ZERO)

Lift-time switches, all off by default (the default lift is byte for byte the old one):

- PPU_NV_LOCALS=1 (or --nonvolatile-locals): every guest register a lifted
  function names is a C local; writes back only what changed and what the
  other side of a call / syscall / tail jump / return may read, from a
  whole-program liveness solve. tools/ppu_nv_dirty.py is soyjxck/ps3recomp's
  (MIT, f1fdcf4977), vendored unmodified; its frame-entry and access-run
  rewrites stay off (they need that fork's ppu_vm_fast.h). Indirect-call
  targets are the --functions entries with an OPD. inFAMOUS 2: 31952 of 32426
  functions rewritten, 0 bailed; write-backs 0.95 M of 8.3 M.
- PPU_MM=1: each lifted function snapshots the memory-model gates (vm_base,
  vm_inline_ok, the range, the gcm ref-poll word, the coherence pointers) in a

eb5dbee9b9ce4276f23db04671951b73c9f1c27e.message:
critic2: SPU PUTs into RSX memory are written top-down, so the FIFO walker never decodes a half-written command segment (the m16 Kuo-cutscene freeze)

The freeze (m16-N1-city at 61 s; q-face-trim1 at 26 s, same signature):
- the walker decoded words that were not commands (colour target format 3
  4880x4115, then a CALL/JUMP to unmapped IO), resynced to put and skipped
  everything up to it (it rescues fences only). The skipped range held the
  frame's release of label 0x86 (labels 0x86/0x87 stayed 0x1E53 while
  0x88/0x89 reached 0x1E54), so the SPU Light Task Kicker (func_00350C2C) and
  the main thread (func_00350CE0, called from 0x1EF29C) both wait for
  [0xA93900+0x318] for good: usleep(10) at 1EF2A0, usleep(900) at 350C88.
- q-face-trim1's [FIFOSTEP] trace: the walker chases Edge-shaped segments
  (0x1740/0x1680/0x1714/0x181C/0x1808/0x1824, 0x1D6C/0x1D74 pairs, 0x0100
  runs) appended at the ring write head behind self-JUMP parks (0x14BC0,
  0x14E90, 0x14F00), and after the last park decodes a non-command word.
- On Cell an SPU DMA lands in whole 128-byte lines; gm_copy_to writes
  ascending doublewords. A reader that waits on the park word and reads upward
  can see the head new and the rest of the segment old. m15 woke on 0.5-1 ms
  timer ticks and almost never caught a copy in flight (1 such resync in all
  recordings, cpuf-B3 on 11-09, which skipped no label); m16's
  PS3RECOMP_GCM_SPIN_US=300 polls the park and put every ~0.1 us, and in the
  Kuo close-up the walker waits on Edge's write head: 2 freezes in 2 m16 runs
  that played the cutscene, 0 in the 16 pre-m16 kuo* runs.

Fix: PUT copies and 128-byte line commits (PUTLLC / PUTLLUC) into IO-mapped
memory are written top-down with release stores (gm_copy_to_desc): a reader
that sees any new word sees every word above it. Other PUTs unchanged.
PS3RECOMP_SPU_PUT_DESC=0 = ascending, as before.
runtime/memory/tests/test_gm_copy_order.c (two threads, 200k 384-byte
segments, the reader waiting on the first word): ascending 640 half-written
reads, top-down

f065c64257256135be0048aa5fa3606ae0f5e5dc.message:
perf: texture cache 4096 + no mid-frame GPU waits from a full frame; per-frame hitch attribution

Sami's 55 s slideshow (4-5 fps, ~12k draws, "looking at the city from above"):
the draw engine's texture cache was a 1024-entry LRU, smaller than what that
view binds in one frame, so every bind missed and every frame re-hashed,
decoded, uploaded and re-created every texture; the Vulkan backend then
flushed and waited on the GPU whenever >256 released images piled up or the
staging/vertex/uniform arenas filled.

- engine texture cache 1024 -> 4096 (PS3RECOMP_ENG_TEXCACHE=1024 = old), index
  updated in place instead of rebuilt per miss (backward-shift delete)
- texture-pack key reuses the caller's content hash (one full hash per upload)
- Vulkan object table 2048 -> 8192, allocation from a rotating cursor
- dead-image list 256 -> 1024 (PS3RECOMP_VK_DEAD_IMG=256 = old), FIF swap
  copies only the used entries
- staging / vertex / index / uniform / GPU-bounce arenas double after a
  mid-frame overflow, with caps and a fallback (PS3RECOMP_VK_ARENA_GROW=0 = old)
- textures <= 1 MB suballocated from 16 MB blocks, power-of-two classes
  (PS3RECOMP_VK_TEXSUB_MB=0 = old): 4096 textures stay under NVIDIA Windows'
  4096-allocation limit and skip a kernel allocation each
- PS3RECOMP_PLAYLOG HITCH lines carry what the RSX thread spent the frame on
  (drain, sema, flush@line, fif, tex new+reup/evict MB ms, hash, mod, texc,
  pipe, spv, alloc); PS3RECOMP_PLAYLOG_HITCH_MS sets the threshold

Cache size, arena growth and texture suballocation ideas from
ThiagoFraga761/infamous2-pc 0.2.0 (MIT: TEXCACHE 4096, ring doubling,
PS3RECOMP_VK_TEXSUB_MB); own code.

hitchcatch: stacks of every guest PPU/SPU thread during a frozen frame (PS3RECOMP_HITCHCATCH)

On whenever PS3RECOMP_PLAYLOG is set (PS3RECOMP_HITCHCATCH=0 turns it off). A watchdog
thread (below normal) reads the play log's frame clock; once a frame passes 40 ms it samples
every 1 ms, until the frame ends, every registered thread: the guest PPU threads (with the
HLE call in flight), the SPU workers (with the job module resident in their context:
resident_ovl, image_id, pc, policy_mode) and the presenting thread. A frame that ends over
80 ms is appended to hitches.tsv beside playlog.tsv (frame start/end on the play log clock,
raw module+RVA call trees); shorter ones are dropped. PS3RECOMP_HITCHCATCH_MS=start,keep,
_MAX (hitches per session, 200), _MB (sample buffer, 16), _PERIOD_US, _DEPTH, _FILE.
tools/hitch_stacks.py (project repo) names the stacks against the exe's PDB.

While a thread is stopped only SuspendThread, GetThreadContext, a copy of the top 128 KB of
its stack (never below the TEB's StackLimit: no guard page) and four ints of its SPU
context run: no lock, no allocation, no loader/heap call. The unwind (RtlLookupFunctionEntry
/ RtlVirtualUnwind, SEH-guarded, bounded) runs on the copy after ResumeThread. A thread
whose QueryThreadCycleTime did not move since the last pass is not suspended (its stack is
the recorded one); the suspend's own cost on a sleeping thread is measured at start (CAL
line) so it is not taken for a run. Buffers are allocated once, when the play log opens.

Normal frames: one store on the presenting thread, the watchdog wakes ~30 times a second.
Hooks: sys_ppu_thread.c (each guest thread), ppu_loader.cpp (main + the HLE table),
lv2_register.c (SPU workers), rsx_vulkan_backend.c (session + frame clock).
