# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

Every row is exercised by CI on every push, and **all three are green on
`master`** — the PPU boot scaffold ratchet that had been red since before v0.11.0
([#139](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp/issues/139)) is at zero on all
four toolchains. The rows below describe what those jobs actually do, not what a
green tick would imply: building the runtime and passing the suites is not the
same as running a game, and only one row claims that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter + 8 test suites | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | null (headless software); Vulkan (opt-in) |
| Runs a recompiled game | **yes** | **no** | no |

The gap on macOS is the PPU boot scaffold — `ppu_loader.cpp`, `boot_main.cpp`
and the HLE dispatch are still Win32-only (thread creation, VirtualAlloc, SEH,
stack walking), and they are compiled per-game rather than into the library.
So macOS builds the runtime, renders through Metal and passes the full test
suite, but cannot yet load and run a title. `ps3recomp_host` drives
cellGcm → RSX → Metal end to end without a game, which is what makes further
graphics work possible there.

Linux builds and passes the same suites under both GCC and Clang, and runs
`ps3recomp_host` end to end, on every push. Its backend is the null backend's
headless software path: a host-memory framebuffer with a CPU triangle filler,
enough to prove the guest's command stream produced the pixels it asked for on
a runner with no display and no GPU. It is not a renderer — no depth, no
blending, no textures — so Linux is still one real backend, plus the same PPU
boot scaffold macOS needs, away from running a title.

### What each platform needs next

Both non-Windows platforms are blocked on the *same* two things, in this order.

**1. The PPU boot scaffold, on POSIX.** This is the shared blocker and the only
one that gates "runs a recompiled game" on both. `ppu_loader.cpp`,
`boot_main.cpp` and the HLE dispatch are compiled *per game* rather than into
the library, and were Win32-only — thread creation, `VirtualAlloc`, SEH, stack
walking. v0.10.0 took it to zero errors on POSIX and put it under CI so it
cannot rot again, and ported the guest-pointer trap, thread-locals and host
backtraces. What is left is running it: load a lifted image on POSIX and reach
the guest's first instruction, then `main`. Until that works, neither platform
can run a title no matter how good its renderer is.

**2. One real backend each.** The RSX abstraction landed in v0.10.0 (#101, #102,
#103) — texture conversion, the `TEXTURE_CONTROL1` crossbar, texture layout and
a neutral draw record all live outside the D3D12 file now, so a backend no
longer has to reimplement them to draw anything.

- **macOS** has the furthest to go that is *interesting* rather than
  mechanical: [@slushiimusic](https://github.com/slushiimusic)'s Metal backend
  (#96) does clear, flip, guest vertex fetch, a pipeline-state cache and blend
  translation. Reaching D3D12 parity means the guest's own fragment programs
  through the decompiler, then textures. `ps3recomp_host` already drives
  cellGcm → RSX → Metal with no lifted game, so each step is testable before a
  title exists to run.
- **Linux** has an opt-in Vulkan backend (`-DPS3RECOMP_RSX_VULKAN=ON`). With
  guest programs on (glslang at build time, `PS3RECOMP_VK_GUEST_PROGRAMS=1`) it
  runs on the shared register-file draw engine, the path Metal takes, and every
  `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on it -- including render-to-texture, MRT and
  depth textures; without them it draws the null backend's fixed-function
  contract. It has not run a recompiled title yet. The default is still the
  headless backend, a CPU triangle filler for CI, deliberately.

**Deliberately not claimed:** the table above says "no" for running a game on
macOS and Linux, and it will keep saying "no" until a title actually boots to
gameplay on one of them. Building the runtime, passing the suites and rendering
through `ps3recomp_host` are all real, and none of them is that.

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

Download > **Setup.exe** from the [latest release](../../releases/latest), run it and press **Install**: it builds the > game from your copy once (20–60 minutes), then **Play**. Details: [What you need](#-what-you-need) · > [Install](#-install). On **Linux**: [Linux (experimental)](#-linux-experimental). ## 🆕 What's new **v0.5.3** - 🎥 **Field of view slider:** F2 → Display → Camera → *Field of view*, 70–130% of the game's. [More](#-trophies-in-playnite-and-recomplauncher) - ✨ **Glow at high resolutions fixed:** no more blocky or doubled glow around lightning and lamps above 720p ([#12](../../issues/12)). - 🎥 **No more stutter at cutscene cuts and loading:** the graphics card's drawing programs are made in the background and prepared ahead at the title screen. - 🗺️ **Minimap icons and world objects:** the map's icons show again, and objects no longer pop in and out as the camera turns ([#7](../../issues/7)). - 🎮 **The right button pictures:** the game shows Xbox or keyboard prompts when you play with those ([#10](../../issues/10)). - 💾 **The "save game error" of the digital (PSN) version is fixed.** - 📦 **One repository:** the engine and the port base are folders of this repository now, so Setup downloads one thing instead of three. Every version and its changes: [Releases](../../releases). ## 🚀 Performance: native vs RPCS3 ![The same spot from the same save: this port at 99 fps (left), RPCS3 at 43 fps (right)](docs/same-spot.jpg) | Same PC, same save, same spot | RPCS3 0.0.42 | **This port** | |---|:-:|:-:| | 🏙️ City: the dock right after loading (720p) | 43 fps (39–46) | **99 fps** | | 🎥 Camera turned to three more views (720p) | not measured | **104 / 132 / 139 fps** | | 🖥️ The same four views at **native 1080p** with every picture extra on | | **99 / 103 / 133 / 140 fps** | | 🔧 Developer build (profile-guided optimisation and hand-written SPU code, not in the Setup build), the same four views at 1080p with every extra | | 116 / 126 / 161 / 166 fps | This port: measured on 10 Nov 2026 with the build Setup makes today. RPCS3: measured on 9 Nov 2026. Both on an i5-13600K, RTX 2070 Super and 32 GB RAM, Windows 11. The PC was a normal desktop with a browser open in the background. RPCS3 ran with its default settings: LLVM recompilers, Vulkan, 100% resolution (720p). Here the CPU sets the pace, so native 1080p with every extra runs as fast as 720p. Story videos and cutscenes run at 30 fps in both, as on the PS3. "Picture extras" means soft shadows, full-resolution ambient occlusion, smooth light gradients and full-resolution effects. **v0.5.2 is faster again.** The build Setup makes now has native versions of the game's heaviest SPU jobs. In the same kind of player build on the test PC: **+14% to +26%** across the city, the dock, the opening fight and the cathedral spire, and **+13% to +19%** with the game held to 4 cores (in that fight, frames slower than 60 fps went from 770 to 121). Setup's *Optimise for this PC* adds about **5–11%** more. F2 → Graphics → *Internal resolution*: 720p / **1080p** / 1440p / 4K. Players play at 1440p too, and native 4K runs at about 66 fps on the test PC's RTX 2070 Super. The game's glow and background blur keep the PS3's look at every resolution (F2 → Effects → *Glow and blur*). ![720p upscaled (left) vs native 1080p (right)](docs/feat-1080p.jpg) ### 🎮 Full controller support **Plug in any controller and play.** - Xbox, DualShock 4, DualSense, Switch Pro, 8BitDo and every pad in the community [SDL_GameControllerDB](https://github.com/mdqinc/SDL_GameControllerDB) work out of the box. - Turn it on before or during the game: it's picked up while you play. - Buttons work by position, as on a PlayStation pad (bottom = ✕, right = ○). - The game's button pictures follow what you play with: PlayStation, Xbox, or keyboard and mouse (F2 → Controls says which one it shows). - **Remap any button in the game:** F2 → Controls → *Buttons and keys* lists every PS3 control, each with two keys, a mouse button and a controller button. Click a cell (✕ on a controller) and press the new one; right-click (□) clears it. An input that is already used asks first: *Swap* or *Cancel*. A change applies at once and is saved in `input.toml`. *Reset to defaults* puts everything back. ### 🖱️ Direct mouse aiming The mouse turns the camera **directly**, by how far you move it, as in a PC game. Before, the mouse moved a pretend stick, and the game's stick speed limit made quick turns and aiming feel slow. - F2 → Controls → *Mouse camera*: **Direct** (the default) or *Like a stick* - *Mouse sensitivity*, and a separate *Aiming sensitivity* for while you aim - in menus, the map and cutscenes the mouse still works like a stick; a controller plays as before ### 💡 Enhanced lighting Soft sun shadows instead of stair-stepped ones, contact shadows (ambient occlusion) at full resolution instead of half, and smooth light gradients without banding. Every option is in F2 → Lighting, and **F3** flips between your picture and the original PS3 look. The fine stripes on faces and clothes in the Kuo cutscene at the dock are fixed: the game's shadow offset now reaches the graphics card, as on the PS3. ![The original PS3 look (left) vs the new lighting (right)](docs/feat-lighting.jpg) ### 🔥 HD fire, smoke and effects The PS3 drew every fire, smoke, spark and explosion into a tiny 512×288 image and stretched it over the screen, which gave blocky edges and blobby flames. Here they're drawn at full resolution (F2 → Effects). The port also keeps the glow around lightning, lamps and fire as the PS3 made it at any resolution (F2 → Effects → *Glow and blur*), and it loads **texture packs** (PNG/DDS), so the community can make HD versions of any texture. Packs are made from your own game's textures, so none are included. ![Fire and smoke: as the PS3 drew them (top), at full resolution (middle), plus an HD texture pack (bottom)](docs/feat-effects.jpg) ### 🧪 In-game cheats menu F2 → Cheats: - **Invincibility**, **infinite energy**, **max battery** - **super jump** (2× to 10×) - **karma rank**: pick any of the game's seven ranks (Hero to Infamous) and karma is set inside it when you close the menu, through the game's own karma setter - **karma lock** (blue/red only), a karma multiplier, **XP for karma**, *Add karma* / *Add XP* buttons - **unlock all powers**: every power in the game is Cole's at once (rockets, Kinetic Pulse, the Ionic powers, every upgrade, hero and evil together), through the game's own power code, and the story can't take them back while it's on; *karma powers of both sides* alone lets hero and evil karma powers work together. The game saves the powers: try it in a New Save Data slot - **infinite ionic charges**: Cole always has 3, the game's most, and they refill the moment one is used - **one-hit kills**, enemy speed, enemies hold fire - **longer glide**: Cole sinks more slowly while gliding (R1, the Static Thrusters), so a glide lasts up to 3× as long and goes further - L_'s patches, re-made for the port: **black lightning** (electric arcs drawn with the game's evil-lightning shader), **Static Thrusters flight** (while gliding, Cross climbs, Circle dives, neither hovers; needs the Improved Static Thrusters upgrade) and a faster glide - **saved spots**: *Save this spot* remembers where Cole stands, which way he faces and the camera; *Go to saved spot* (or **F7**, menu open or closed) puts him back there, through the game's own placing code (two places in New Marais come with it) Cheats can be remembered between sessions, with a short reminder at start. ![The Cheats page](docs/feat-cheats.jpg) ### 🧩 Mods The community's inFAMOUS 2 mods work as they are: the ones made for tiffsomniac's **inFAMOUS Mod Manager** (whole files, texture patches, xpps patches, and mods with options). - **F2 → Mods → Add a mod from a zip**: the zips in your Downloads folder, checked first (only mod files are taken out, never a program), installed into the **`mods`** folder next to the game; or unzip a mod there yourself (`mods\\mod.json`) - **no Unlocker** and nothing to install: your game files are never changed, the port hands the game the mod's files in their place - **F2 → Mods**: every mod with its preview picture and what it changes, turn each on or off, pick its options; the page shows at once what the next start will use, and **Restart to apply** restarts the game to its title screen (Continue there to go on from your last save) - options that all change the same texture (a T-shirt in seven designs) are one at a time, as radio buttons; options that change different things (a skin for the sword, the amp and the outfit) are check boxes - two mods that change the same file: **Use this one instead** picks the one that wins (the page says first what the other loses), else the first by folder name - a texture patch made for another version of the game is never written beside its texture: the mod is left out and the page says which option to untick (for example *"15 textures were made for another version of cole_gold_amp.xpps: untick Solid Gold Amp"*) How it works and the mod format: [`engine/docs/MODS.md`](engine/docs/MODS.md). ### 💾 Save manager The PS3's own "choose a save" screen, which the port didn't have before: - every save with its picture, mission, completion and date - **New Save Data**, so you never overwrite by accident - overwrite and delete, each asking first - real Yes/No answers to the game's questions, like "save before loading?" ![The Load Game screen](docs/feat-saves.jpg) ### 🏆 Trophies, in Playnite and RecompLauncher The game's 52 trophies unlock as on a PS3, the platinum with the last of the others, with a notice in your language. The port keeps them in `game\gamedata\trophies\NPWR01730.json` and also writes them the way RPCS3 does, in `game\gamedata\dev_hdd0\home\00000001\trophy\NPWR01730_00\` (the names, the icons and `TROPUSR.DAT` with the unlock times), so trophy trackers made for RPCS3 can read them. **Playnite** ([Playnite Achievements](https://github.com/justin-delano/PlayniteAchievements) or [SuccessStory](https://github.com/Lacro59/playnite-successstory-plugin)). Both look for an emulator with RPCS3 in its name, so the port gets one: 1. Library → Configure Emulators → Add: name it `RPCS3 inFAMOUS 2 port`, installation folder `\game\gamedata`, and one custom profile whose executable is `\Play inFAMOUS 2.cmd`. 2. Add the game by hand: installation folder `\game\disc\PS3_GAME` (the plugins find the game's `TROPHY.TRP` there), and a play action of the Emulator type with that emulator and profile. 3. Playnite Achievements: turn on its RPCS3 source. SuccessStory: Settings → RPCS3 → turn it on and add `\game\gamedata\dev_hdd0\home\00000001` as a home user folder. 4. Start the game once (the folder is made then), then refresh the game's achievements. Already set up for RPCS3? Add `PS3_TROPHY_RPCS3_DIR=` to `settings.ini` and the port also copies its unlocks into RPCS3's own trophy folder for the game. It never locks anything or moves a date later there, and it keeps a copy of RPCS3's file once (`TROPUSR.DAT.port-backup`). With Playnite Achievements, the game's Manage Achievements → Override

cdb581579fd7ba76d429fab741828ce9e04161d6.message:
Low-CPU update: fewer threads on weaker PCs, support for CPUs without AVX2

- SPURS: on PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the lanes/kernels spin less, wake the
  main thread sooner and run on fewer threads (4-thread PCs: ~10 fps -> ~29 fps,
  8 threads: ~38 -> ~50 fps). Big PCs keep the old behaviour.
- Vertex workers spin far less after each job, fewer workers on small CPUs.
- The once-per-second thread scan only walks the game's own threads.
- No exclusive core reservations on PCs with fewer than 20 CPU threads;
  P-core pinning only on hybrid CPUs with at least 8 P-core threads.
- CPUs without AVX2/FMA/BMI2 (pre-2013 Intel, AVX-less Pentium/Celeron, AMD before
  2015): Setup/the updater detect this and build an SSE4.1 compatibility version
  automatically (same results, slower). The game also checks the CPU at startup and
  shows a clear message instead of crashing.

1451404951.readme_excerpt:
# inFamous PC

> **Official repo: [github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn).**
> Only download the Setup from the [Releases page](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn/releases) here.
> Forks are not supported, and bugs from forks won't be fixed.

An unofficial native Windows port of **inFamous** (PlayStation 3, 2009, European
release `BCES00220`). The game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code is statically
recompiled to x86-64 C/C++ with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp),
so it runs as a normal Windows program rather than under an emulator.

**This repository contains no game code or data.** You build the game yourself,
on your own PC, from your own copy of the game.

## Easy install

Download **inFamous Setup.exe** from the latest release, run it, choose your
`.iso` (an encrypted image works with its `.dkey` next to it) or your game
folder (the one with `PS3_GAME` in it), pick an install location and press
**Install**.

Setup checks for Python and the C++ build tools and offers to install them,
copies the game out of the disc image, regenerates the recompiled code from your
copy, builds it and adds an inFamous shortcut. Running Setup again on the same
folder updates or repairs the install and only redoes what changed.

## Updating

When a new version is published here, players update in place instead of reinstalling:
**Update now** in Setup (it finds the existing install), the **Update inFamous** shortcut in
the Start menu, or `Update inFamous.cmd` in the install folder. The updater compares every file
with this repository, downloads only what changed, regenerates the game code only if the
port's patches changed, and recompiles only the affected parts. Installs made with an older
Setup need one run of the new Setup on the same folder first.

## Requirements

- Your own inFamous disc dump, European release (`BCES00220`).
- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with Direct3D 12 support.
- A CPU with SSE4.1 (2008 or newer). On CPUs without AVX2 (Intel before 2013, Pentium/Celeron
  without AVX, AMD before 2015) Setup builds a slower compatibility version automatically.
  On PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the game uses fewer threads and less CPU (tested down to 4 threads).
- [Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) with "Add python.exe to
  PATH" ticked.
- [Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/)
  with the **Desktop development with C++** workload and the **C++ Clang
  Compiler for Windows** component.
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), only if your `PS3_GAME\USRDIR` has `EBOOT.BIN`
  but no decrypted `EBOOT.elf`. Setup uses it to decrypt the executable.
- About 10 GB of free disk space and 16 GB of RAM.

## Building manually

```bat
cd installer
cargo build --release
target\release\infamous-installer --game "D:\Dumps\inFamous"
```

`infamous-installer doctor` checks the requirements only. Finished steps are
skipped when you run it again, so an interrupted install continues where it
stopped. See [installer/README.md](installer/README.md) for every step and the
maintainer commands.

## Playing

Run **inFamous** (the shortcut Setup made). It opens a small options window first
(vsync, frame cap, resolution, language and more, saved to `settings.ini`);
**Play** starts the game. The same settings are in the game's pause menu under
**Settings**. Controllers work as on the console, and keyboard and mouse are supported.

**F10** opens the in-game trainer: God Mode, Infinite Energy, Refill Health,
Max Health x2/x5/x10, Add XP, Karma +/-, Kill Enemies / Civilians, Super Speed
and Player Model (play as Zeke, Trish, Kessler, Alden or John). Set `TRAINER=0`
to turn it off.

## DLSS and FSR (optional)

The game can use NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA or AMD FSR for upscaling, and AMD FSR frame generation.
They are not included in the download because NVIDIA and AMD distribute their SDKs themselves,
but both are free and take a few minutes to add.

- **DLSS** needs an NVIDIA RTX graphics card.
- **FSR** works on any modern GPU (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel). FSR 4 needs a Radeon RX 9000 card;
  other cards get FSR 3.1 automatically.

**1. Download the SDK(s) you want.** You need the **source code**, not a Windows or Linux demo.
On the page, click the green **Code** button, then **Download ZIP**. If you go through the
Releases page instead, pick **Source code (zip)**, not the files with "demo" or "samples" in the name.

| For | Download | Rename the extracted folder to |
|---|---|---|
| DLSS / DLAA | [github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS) | `dlss-sdk` |
| FSR and frame generation | [github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK) | `fsr-sdk` |

**2. Put the folder(s) in your inFamous install folder**, next to `infamous-recomp` and
`ps3recomp`:

```
inFamous\
  dlss-sdk\        <- contains include\ and lib\
  fsr-sdk\         <- contains Kits\
  infamous-recomp\
  ps3recomp\
  ...
```

Make sure you don't end up with a folder inside a folder (`dlss-sdk\DLSS-main\include`).
`include` (DLSS) or `Kits` (FSR) must be directly inside.

**3. Rebuild the game once.** Open a Command Prompt in the install folder and run:

```bat
type nul > .installer\update.pending
"Update inFamous.cmd"
```

This rebuilds the game with the SDK(s), which takes a while. Any later update also picks them up
automatically, so you only do this once.

**4. Turn it on in game:** pause, then **Settings**, then **Upscaling** (DLAA, DLSS Quality /
Balanced / Performance, FSR Native AA / Quality / Balanced / Performance) and **Frame
Generation**. The same options are in the launcher's options window. Upscaling and frame
generation apply after a restart.

If the **Upscaling** row is missing, the build didn't find the SDK: check the folder names and
layout from step 2, then repeat step 3.

## How it works

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `ps3recomp` | The recompiler toolkit and runtime: PPU and SPU lifters, HLE system libraries, RSX on Direct3D 12, audio and input |
| `infamous-recomp` | The inFamous-specific parts: program entry, game stubs and fixes, asset tools |
| `installer` | Setup and the command-line installer: reads the disc, regenerates the code from your game, applies `installer/patches`, builds |
| `installer/infamous.toml` | Everything about the game and the port: pipeline steps, generated files, build and launch settings |
| `installer/generated.lock` | Hashes of each generated file before and after the port's patches |

## Credits

- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet and
  contributors (see [ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md](ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md)).
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), used to decrypt the game executable.
- Sucker Punch Productions, for the game.
- [Lorenzo Aiello](https://github.com/aiellolorenzo23) and [ibrahimpuri](https://github.com/ibrahimpuri), for their support.

03b0b8e7aca435f5ccbccb23b3f3200569288b25.message:
add native Edge vertex decompression and compression kernels

The Edge Geometry job (image 209) still spent ~20% of the SPU time in two
lifted loops after skinning and culling went native: 0x4448, which
decompresses the special vertex format (u16 positions with an offset and a
scale, 24-bit unit vectors), and the format-1 case of the compression
function 0x9780 (0x99E8 and its loop 0x9C20: three floats and two X11Y11Z10
words per vertex). Both are now native, bit-exact against the lifted code
in the offline harness, including the pipelined loops' stray stores (the
two zero quads past the decompressed vectors, the trailing pattern of the
compression's last step).

0x99E8 is a chunk inside 0x9780, so lift_spu.py learns NATIVE_ENTRIES
pairs (entry, continuation): the hook transfers to 0x98B0 instead of

311738687884ac51d539c50914925a461d2a8f17.message:
keep a frame in flight on the GPU

A present submitted the frame and waited for the GPU to finish it, so GPU
time added to every frame: 21-33% of the RSX thread at 1x, 46% at 2x. Now
the next frame records into a second set of everything a batch holds
(command buffers and fence, window blit, rings, dead buffers, descriptor
pools, ZPASS queries, deferred readbacks) while the GPU renders the first.

the batches before, known once those complete. The small-target writeback
(the luminance the CPU reads for auto-exposure) is recorded before the
present and delivered when its batch completes, instead of forcing a wait
after every present. The parked frame is polled and completed as soon as
the GPU is done with it.

65c75cd2eded770ceaf70e177d51f31b3cdfd18f.message:
add a native kernel for the Edge index decompression (0xC7B8)

0xC7B8 decodes the compressed triangle lists (flags, 2-bit triangle codes
and bit-packed, delta-coded vertex numbers) in place, once per segment
before the cull. With the vertex kernels native it is the largest piece of
the geometry job still lifted (0.64% of the samples, 2.7% of the module).

The kernel runs the job's four loops on host-order copies and stores each
buffer exactly as the job leaves it, including the blocks unpacked past N0,
the list past the flags and the triangles of the last group past T. Loop 2
does eight entries per flag byte with one shuffle, loop 4 two triangles per
two-source permute, the same idea as the job's tables; scalar versions were
slower than the lift, which already does eight triangles at a time.

It falls back, before writing anything, where the job's pipelined in-place
loops could read their own stores, and on shapes no real segment has. The
offline harness compares the whole LS against the lifted code: 0
differences on 22000 random and malformed streams, 1.7-2.9x faster.

Opt-in with PS3RECOMP_NATIVE_EDGE_IDX (1 on, 2 compare) until a compare
run in the game shows no difference. lift_spu.py gets the native entry, so
the module needs a relift of its hooks.

fd2845fbc6cc09a3dd3e18598c384b9c7b976532.message:
let the vertex decompression run on the job's own table layout

In the game's first compare run 0x4448 matched on millions of calls, but
18% of them still fell back to the lifted code. The job lays the uniform
tables out back to back, 16 bytes times the count rounded up to 8 apart
(0x7198), so with a count of 0 or 7 mod 8 the two zero quads past the
normals are the first two tangents, and the overlap guard refused that.

The two loops that write those spans run one after the other (0x4A30, then
0x4D18), so the guard now tags each written span with its loop and lets
spans of different loops overlap; the kernel writes them in the job's
order. Spans of one loop still may not overlap: the zero quads past the
normals landing on the positions is order-sensitive inside 0x4A30 and still
falls back.

The stats line also names why each fallback happened, so the next run says
whether anything but this layout is left.

Veja o [Status](#status). **inFAMOUS 2** (PS3, BCUS98125, versão 01.00) rodando nativo no Linux, sem emulador. O código do jogo, PowerPC (PPU) e SPU, é traduzido para C antes da compilação por recompilação estática com o [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). O sistema do PS3 é reimplementado, e a GPU (RSX) roda os shaders do próprio jogo traduzidos para Vulkan. > **Nenhum arquivo do jogo vem com este projeto, e não há binários para > baixar.** Para jogar, você precisa da sua própria cópia, tirada do seu PS3. O > build transforma o **seu** executável em código na **sua** máquina, e esse > código não pode ser distribuído. | | | |---|---| | ![Cole no píer de Empire City](docs/screenshots/01-pier.jpg) | ![Cutscene de abertura](docs/screenshots/02-cutscene.jpg) | | ![Passarela no pântano de New Marais](docs/screenshots/03-new-marais.jpg) | ![Ruas de New Marais](docs/screenshots/04-cidade.jpg) | ![Empire City vista do píer](docs/screenshots/05-empire-city.jpg) Capturas direto da GPU no Linux, com uma Radeon RX 9070 XT, em 1280×720. As de Empire City foram renderizadas em 2× (2560×1440) e reduzidas. ## Novidades da v0.1.0 (a v0.2.0 está no [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md)) O histórico completo está no [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). - **+19% na área mais pesada.** A thread do RSX ficou mais barata por draw: a FIFO é percorrida em lote, e o estado de render, a superfície, os programas e as texturas são reaproveitados enquanto não mudam. Medido na mesma cena: de 90,6 para 107,7 fps sem limite. - **Edge nativo.** A descompressão e a compressão de vértices do Edge, que rodavam como código SPU traduzido, agora são C escrito à mão. Em ~2,5 milhões de chamadas comparadas no jogo não houve nenhuma diferença, e cada chamada ficou ~4× mais rápida (1,15 µs contra 4,9 µs). - **Sem as travadas de segundos.** Em 06/11, depois de um update do driver, havia frames de 2,7 s e 1% low de 0,7 fps. Os pipelines já vistos são recriados em segundo plano na partida, e os novos são montados fora do frame. O `play.sh` também usa um cache de shaders do driver só para o jogo. Na sessão de 07/11, com limite de 60: 59–60 fps, p99 médio de 21 ms e nenhuma travada. - **Limite de FPS no menu**, com 60 como padrão. Com `PS3_MAIN_WAITS=1` (opcional), a thread principal espera de verdade em vez de girar: com o limite de 60, ela cai de 99% para 46% de CPU. - **Imagem:** - anti-aliasing FXAA ou SMAA 1x; - FSR 1 para ampliar até a janela; - média por área para reduzir de 4K/5K; - nitidez ajustável; - escala 4× (5K, supersampling). - **Campo de visão ajustável** no menu, do FOV do jogo até +30%, ao vivo. - **Teclado e mouse (fase 1):** WASD e o mouse viram os analógicos, junto com o controle. Sensibilidade, inversão do eixo e teclas no menu e no `settings.ini`. - **Ultrawide experimental:** F1 > Vídeo > Ultrawide desenha o mundo no formato do monitor (Hor+) e põe o HUD, os menus e os vídeos em 16:9 no centro. Na área pesada a 3440×1440 custa ~7% (108 → 101 fps). Veja [docs/OPCOES.md](docs/OPCOES.md#2-ultrawide-e-fov). - **Caixa-preta das travas:** a cada parada, o estado do runtime (fences, job chains, SPURS, eventos) vai para `work/runs/freezes/`, e cada frame lento gera uma linha `[vk hitch]` com a causa. - **Saves gravados por inteiro ou nada:** um crash no meio do save mantém o save anterior. - **Esc** abre o menu, como o F1, e o motor pequeno da vibração voltou a funcionar (ficava em 0,4% da força). a caixa-preta grava o estado quando acontece | | Imagem | 🔧 Correta na maior parte; falhas pontuais ainda aparecem | | Linux | ✅ Testado no Fedora 44 | | Windows e macOS | ❌ Jogo não suportado: o toolkit compila e linka (CI), mas o jogo nunca foi rodado lá | ### Desempenho Ryzen 7 9800X3D + Radeon RX 9070 XT, Fedora 44, render em 1280×720: | Cena | Condição | Resultado | Medido em | |---|---|---|---| | Área pesada da cidade, na praça onde o save atual começa (~9 mil draws por frame) | bench automático, parado, sem limite | **107,7 fps** (90,6 com as otimizações da v0.1.0 para o RSX desligadas) | 07/11/2026 | | Sessão de jogo normal | limite de 60 (padrão) | 59–60 fps, p99 médio de 21 ms, nenhuma travada | 07/11/2026 | | Píer de Empire City (tutorial, andando) | sem limite | ~120–130 fps | out/2026 | | Pântano de New Marais | sem limite | ~100 fps | out/2026 | | Menu 3D | sem limite | ~115 fps | out/2026 | - As cenas de outubro foram medidas antes das otimizações de 07/11 e não foram medidas de novo. - Na área pesada, as quatro threads quentes (principal do PPU, RSX, gravação Vulkan e SPUs) ficam todas em 85–91%: nenhuma otimização isolada sobe muito mais o teto. - Quem limita é a CPU, não a GPU. Em outubro, o pântano de New Marais rodou em 4K no mesmo fps que em 720p. - Os detalhes de onde vai o tempo de cada frame estão em [docs/NOTES.md](docs/NOTES.md). ### PS3 × este port | | PS3 | Este port | |---|---|---| | Resolução | 1280×720 | 720p, 1440p, 4K ou 5K, com FSR 1 ou redução por área até a janela | | Taxa de quadros | alvo de 30 fps | 60 com o limite padrão; ~100–130 sem limite | | Anti-aliasing | — | FXAA ou SMAA 1x | | Campo de visão | fixo | até +30% | | Monitor ultrawide | — | barras pretas, esticado ou Hor+ experimental | | Controles | DualShock 3 | controle via SDL2, teclado e mouse | | Execução | Cell (PPU + SPUs) e RSX | código traduzido para x86-64, GPU em Vulkan | ## Requisitos **Arquivos do jogo.** Tudo vem do **seu** PS3, e nada disso está no repositório. O passo a passo está em [docs/ARQUIVOS_NECESSARIOS.md](docs/ARQUIVOS_NECESSARIOS.md). - **O disco:** inFAMOUS 2, **BCUS98125 (EUA), versão 01.00**, em dump do seu disco, com `disc/PS3_GAME/` na raiz do repositório. - **O executável:** `disc/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf`, o `EBOOT.BIN` do disco descriptografado (por exemplo no RPCS3). O `scripts/lift.sh` confere o SHA-256. - **O firmware:** o PUP oficial do PS3 instalado no RPCS3 (`dev_flash`). **PC:** - Linux x86-64 (testado no Fedora 44). - CPU com AVX2. O código SPU é compilado com AVX-512 por padrão; para CPU sem ele, `PORT_SPU_MARCH=x86-64-v3`. - 8 núcleos com SMT para a afinidade de threads (`PS3_HOT_PIN`); com menos, o jogo roda, só que sem esse ganho. - GPU com Vulkan e uma fila gráfica que também faz compute. - ~14 GB de RAM livres e ~3 GB de disco para compilar, além do jogo. - Pacotes no Fedora (adapte para a sua distro): `gcc gcc-c++ clang cmake ninja-build python3 SDL2-devel vulkan-headers vulkan-loader-devel glslang-devel libpng-devel`. O libpng só desenha a arte do disco no menu; sem ele, o fundo é liso. ## Como compilar Não há binários para baixar: o código traduzido é o do jogo e só pode existir na sua máquina. ```sh scripts/setup.sh # ps3recomp no commit base + o patch deste port, Dear ImGui, venv Python scripts/lift.sh # traduz o PPU e os SPUs do SEU EBOOT.elf scripts/build.sh # compila em work/port/build-vk ``` - A tradução leva alguns minutos. A primeira compilação é demorada, porque o código traduzido do PPU é grande. - O `build.sh` roda num escopo de memória de 14 GB do systemd, para não derrubar o desktop. - `JOBS=` muda o paralelismo. `PORT_PPU_GCC=1` compila o PPU com GCC. - `PS3RECOMP_DIR=` usa um ps3recomp que já está em outro lugar. - Para contribuir: `scripts/install-hooks.sh` instala os hooks que rodam o `scripts/check_clean.sh` antes de cada commit e push. O mapa do repositório está em [docs/ESTRUTURA.md](docs/ESTRUTURA.md). ## Como jogar ```sh work/play.sh # janela + controle + som, com o menu principal work/play.sh --play # direto no jogo, sem o menu do port work/play.sh --title # direto na tela de jogo novo do inFAMOUS 2 ``` O controle precisa estar ligado antes de abrir. Cada sessão grava um log em `work/runs/play-.log`. ### Menu principal Ao abrir, aparece o menu do port, sobre a arte do próprio disco (`PIC1.PNG`). Ele funciona com controle, teclado ou mouse: | Item | O que faz | |---|---| | **Continuar** | entra no save mais recente (mostra nome, progresso e data) | | **Novo jogo** | abre a tela de jogo novo do próprio inFAMOUS 2 | | **Carregar jogo** | lista os seus saves; escolha um | | **Opções** | as abas abaixo | | **Sair** | fecha | O inFAMOUS 2 não tem menu principal: com save, ele entra direto no autosave; sem save, mostra só "Começar um jogo novo". O menu do port faz esse papel. Antes de **Novo jogo** ou de carregar um save que não é o autosave, os saves são copiados para `user/backups`, porque o próximo autosave do jogo grava por cima do slot de autosave, como no console. Dentro do jogo: **Start → Dados salvos**. ### Opções (F1 no jogo) **F1**, **Esc** ou **Select+Start** segurados abrem as opções no meio do jogo. Tudo fica gravado em `user/settings.ini`. | Aba | Opções | |---|---| | **Vídeo** | Resolução (720p, 1440p, 4K, 5K com supersampling) · Anti-aliasing (desligado, FXAA, SMAA 1x) · Ampliar para a janela (bilinear, FSR 1) · Reduzir para a janela (bilinear, média por área) · Nitidez (automática, ou de 0 a 1) · Tela cheia · VSync · Esticar a imagem (sem barras) · Campo de visão (do jogo até +30%) · Monitor (com mais de um) | | **Idioma** | Dublagem e legendas/textos, separados (dá para misturar) | | **Desempenho** | Predefinição (Desempenho 720p, Equilibrado 1440p, Qualidade 4K) · Limite de FPS (sem limite, 30, 40, 60, 80, 120, 240, taxa do monitor) · Contador de FPS na tela · Thread de gravação Vulkan | | **Mods** | Partículas em resolução cheia · Filtro anisotrópico (do jogo, 2x a 16x) · Mods instalados ([docs/MODS.md](docs/MODS.md)) | | **Controle e saves** | Controle detectado e teste de botões · Abrir a pasta dos saves · Fazer backup dos saves · Abrir a pasta dos logs | | **Teclado e mouse** | Jogar com teclado e mouse · Sensibilidade do mouse (0,10–5,00) · Inverter o eixo vertical · Início do giro (0–60%) · Lista de teclas | - Resolução, monitor, idioma e a thread de gravação valem a partir da próxima vez que o jogo abrir. O resto muda na hora. - Uma variável de ambiente ganha do arquivo, e o campo dela fica cinza no menu (`PS3RECOMP_RES_SCALE=2 work/play.sh`). A lista completa está em [docs/OPCOES.md](docs/OPCOES.md). ### Controles **Controle** (Xbox, DualShock 4, DualSense): como no PS3. **Select+Start** segurados abrem o menu do port. **Teclado e mouse**, junto com o controle. O mouse é capturado no primeiro clique ou tecla; Alt+Tab e F1 o soltam. | Tecla | Botão do PS3 | |---|---| | **W A S D** | analógico esquerdo (andar) | | **Mouse**, ou **I J K L** | analógico direito (câmera) | | **Botão esquerdo** / **direito** | R1 (atirar) / L1 (mirar) | | **Espaço** | Xis | | **Shift esquerdo** ou **Backspace** | Bola | | **F** ou **botão lateral 4** | Quadrado | | **E** ou **botão lateral 5** | Triângulo | | **Q** / **R** | R2 / L2 | | **Ctrl esquerdo** / **V** ou **botão do meio** | L3 / R3 | | **Enter** ou **P** / **Tab** | Start / Select | | **Setas** ou **1 2 3 4** | direcional | Para trocar teclas: `[keyboard] map` no `user/settings.ini`, no formato `Tecla=BOTÃO` (por exemplo `F=SQUARE Q=NONE`). As ações `WALK` (andar devagar) e a roda do mouse (`WheelUp`, `WheelDown`) existem, mas não têm tecla no mapa padrão. **Teclas do port:** | Tecla | O que faz | |---|---| | **F1** ou **Esc** | abre e fecha o menu | | **F11** ou **Alt+Enter** | tela cheia / janela | ## Idioma O disco traz voz e texto de todas as regiões (`brazilian.psarc`, `brazilian_text.psarc`, `latino.psarc`…), e o jogo escolhe pelo idioma do console: - O jogo foi feito antes de o PS3 ter "Português (Brasil)" (número 17), então trata esse número como desconhecido e cai no inglês. - O caminho para o PT-BR é o idioma "Português" (7), que a lista da região norte-americana liga aos arquivos `brazilian`. - O port escolhe esse número sozinho a partir do idioma das legendas, e serve os arquivos de voz e de texto que você escolheu na aba Idioma. ## Saves e dados - Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata/`. .env NATIVE=1 (ASCENSION_NATIVE, off by default) adds -march=native to the
lifted SPU and PPU sources, so on a Zen 4/5 or recent Intel host clang uses
AVX-512 there. The exe then needs a CPU like the one that built it.

A/B on a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, ps3kit develop 5c65f747, 60 fps limit, the same
save and route, loading screens left out:

  NATIVE=1:   57.9 fps avg, 22% of seconds under 58, SPU busy 46.7%

Frames keep going until a heap overflow: SPURS_READY_LEVEL, patch 0018

SPURS_READY_LEVEL=1 is now on by default: without it RsxSync's round-2 job
waited for a kick that never came and the render thread spun on frame slot
0x99AAC8. With it and the park hold, every run gets past frame 2 (21-28
frame reports in 60 s).

All runs now stop at frame ~12 in the same place: func_0037D548 copies
past the end of a block in the heap at 0x14FB8F68 and zeroes the next free
node's header, and the first-fit walk func_00397318 loops on it. STATUS
records how the guard caught it and what to look at next. Patch 0018 caps
[null-read] per reading function and adds the reader's registers, which is
what named the heap.

Past the loading screen to the save prompt: patches 0019-0020

The loading screen waited on a particle job whose last task creates the
next phase from the SPU. Three SPURS taskset gaps on the fork kept that
from happening (tasks started twice, Taskset2 made as a 0x1900-byte
taskset without event flags, SPU-created tasks never started); with them
fixed the game shows its first-use save prompt, writes BCES01741-SYSDATA
and goes on to a black screen, which is next. STATUS has the chain and the
diagnostics that found it; gamedata/ (the emulated HDD) and the old lift
are ignored.

# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.pt-BR.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. > [!WARNING] > **Ainda experimental, mas já dá para zerar.** O [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor) jogou do começo ao fim no PC dele (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT). Em processadores comuns o jogo ainda é lento (~24 fps no primeiro nível num Ryzen 7 5700G, 13-21 na luta contra o chefe), e ainda pode travar. Feito para Windows; no macOS (Apple Silicon) ele voltou a rodar, por enquanto só para testes. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Novembro de 2026, no Windows (e no Mac, em testes): - **O jogo inteiro, do boot ao fim:** o iSamigor zerou o jogo. Nos nossos testes: telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Dois renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente, e o *live draw* próprio do projeto (D3D12). - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas, melhorias e o **online** com a sua conta do site; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado no [site](https://gow-ascension.com.br/pt-br) a partir dos seus discos. As mudanças de novembro estão no branch [`ascension-perf`](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/tree/ascension-perf) até serem medidas no Windows. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.pt-BR.md](docs/MILESTONES.pt-BR.md) (em inglês: [MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md)). ### Desempenho O objetivo é rodar bem em processadores comuns, não só nos fortes. Primeiro nível, num Ryzen 7 5700G (cada número medido no Windows, na mesma cena): | Onde | Começo de novembro | Hoje (5 de novembro) | RPCS3 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Primeiro nível, PC inteiro (8 núcleos, 16 threads) | ~21-23 fps | **~24 fps** | 35-40 fps | | Primeiro nível, só 4 núcleos (8 threads) | ~14-15 fps | **~17-18 fps** | | | Menu principal | ~50-55 fps | ~50-55 fps | | | Luta contra o chefe | 13-21 fps | ainda não medida de novo | | Num Ryzen 7 9800X3D com uma RX 9070 XT (RSX do RPCS3, Vulkan), o jogo chega a 60 fps fora das lutas e cai para cerca da metade nelas. **O que rendeu em novembro** (cada mudança medida sozinha, com o jogo alternando entre ligado e desligado na mesma rodada, num PC de 4 núcleos): - O código do processador principal compilado com perfil de uso real do jogo (PGO): ~6 ms a menos por quadro (~10%). Estendido ao código das SPUs e ao runtime: ~1 ms a mais. - O thread principal do jogo com prioridade acima do normal: -2,7 ms por quadro. - Os jobs do fim do quadro espalhados por até 4-5 SPUs: -2,1 ms por quadro. - O thread do RSX dormindo quando a fila de comandos está vazia, em vez de girar: ~8% a menos; as SPUs escolhendo sozinhas o próximo trabalho: ~1,6% a menos. - Mais partes do módulo de geometria das SPUs (o EDGE) em código nativo, conferidas contra o original: o job mais pesado dele ficou 28% mais rápido. **Para onde vai o quadro agora:** o RSX saiu do caminho crítico nos dois PCs de teste (a espera dele entre as duas passadas da geometria caiu de 9-12 ms para ~0,1 ms). Hoje o quadro é ~55% o EDGE (o módulo 218 das SPUs), mais os jobs de renderização no começo e no fim. Dentro do EDGE, o maior desperdício achado são as interrupções do gerenciador de jobs no meio de cada job: custam tanto quanto o código do próprio job. **Próximos passos:** diminuir essas interrupções, deixar mais leve a cópia de dados das SPUs (DMA em lista), refazer o PGO com o código novo e, depois, o culling do EDGE em código nativo (o banco de teste dele já reproduz as 412 chamadas gravadas do nível). ### Estabilidade - **Corrigido:** o travamento no nível com as listas de geometria esperando para sempre (uma escrita do processador principal se perdia no meio de uma operação atômica de uma SPU: de 3 travamentos em 5 rodadas para nenhum em 4). - **Corrigido:** o travamento com `CopyLocalMemory offset error` (um contador do Edge Zlib e a troca da tabela de streaming de texturas sem proteção): nenhum em 40 rodadas no nível. - **Protegido:** comandos de vídeo corrompidos (`FIFO error: possible desync`) não derrubam mais o thread do RSX, e um draw pedindo uma quantidade absurda de vértices é descartado em vez de travar o jogo. A causa da corrupção ainda está aberta. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); o jogo às vezes trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`); e houve um crash silencioso ~70-105 s depois de entrar no nível em duas rodadas. ### Multijogador online (em desenvolvimento) Os servidores originais do jogo ainda funcionam para quem joga no PS3, mas o jogo recompilado não entra na PSN. Por isso o projeto tem o próprio servidor (em Rust, ainda privado), no ar em [gow-ascension.com.br](https://gow-ascension.com.br) com o cadastro fechado por enquanto; o runtime manda para ele os nomes que o jogo procura. O servidor nunca se passa pela Sony: ele responde só o que o jogo espera, lido no código traduzido ou nas capturas do próprio jogo falando com ele. A partida usa o netcode do próprio jogo (uma malha P2P por UDP); como dois jogadores em casa quase nunca se alcançam direto (cada um atrás do seu roteador), os pacotes passam por um relay do servidor, e o jogo nem percebe. | Passo | Estado | | --- | --- | | Entrar online, Online Pass | ok | | Configuração do online (o jogo lê a nossa) | ok | | Termos de uso, perfil do multijogador guardado na conta | ok | | Tutorial pulado, lobby do guerreiro | ok | | Partida rápida: localização do jogador | ok | | Partida rápida: escolha do servidor de matchmaking | ok | | Conexão com o matchmaking (sessão SSL 3.0) | ok | | Dois jogadores casados numa partida, um deles host | ok (dois jogos no mesmo PC) | | A rede da partida pelo relay do servidor | ok (dois jogos no mesmo PC) | | Launcher: entrar na conta e jogar online | ok | | Partida entre dois PCs pela internet | **em andamento** | | A partida inteira, do lobby ao fim | falta | ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph PC["PC do jogador"] L["Launcher
conta e online"] G["Jogo recompilado
(runtime ps3kit)"] L -- "endereço, configuração e perfil" --> G end subgraph SRV["Servidor do projeto (Rust)"] API["Contas e API"] CFG["Configuração do online"] TUS["Perfil do multijogador
por conta"] GEO["Localização"] SAM["Matchmaking
(SSL 3.0)"] REL["Signaling e relay
(UDP)"] DB[("PostgreSQL")] TUS --> DB API --> DB end WEB["Site do projeto
perfil, ranking, painel"] G2["Jogo de outro jogador"] L -- "login por código" --> API L -- "configuração, perfil" --> CFG L -- "perfil" --> TUS G -- "TCP" --> GEO G -- "TCP + SSL" --> SAM G <-- "partida (UDP)" --> REL REL <-- "partida (UDP)" --> G2 WEB -- "HTTP" --> API ``` No ar no servidor e no site: as contas, o perfil do multijogador guardado por conta, o perfil público com nível e conquistas, o ranking (vazio até haver partidas), um painel administrativo e o login do launcher por código. Planejado: os troféus do jogo assinados e conferidos pelo servidor. **"Jogar offline" vai continuar sempre funcionando**: a campanha nunca vai pedir conta. ## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), instale o launcher pelo `AscensionLauncher__x64-setup.exe` das [releases](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/releases) e, na primeira vez, aponte a pasta `ascension` em **Avançado › Pasta do jogo**. Ele se atualiza sozinho quando sai uma versão nova.

JOGAR abre o jogo; o launcher se esconde até ele fechar. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Melhorias:** liga e desliga. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Abrir a pasta de melhorias** é onde entram as outras, como o **português do Brasil**, que a [página do site](https://gow-ascension.com.br/pt-br) monta no seu navegador a partir das imagens dos seus discos (nada é enviado). As melhorias incluídas são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo. - **Online:** entra na sua conta do site por um código (como numa TV) e liga o online; os troféus do jogo ficam na mesma aba.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

1451938638.readme_excerpt:
# inFAMOUS 2 Recomp

Experimental Windows port of the PlayStation 3 BCUS98125 release, built with a pinned [PS3Recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) revision and a local patch series.

**Status (November 2026): not playable.** Local native runs have reached the campaign dock sequence and produced partial 3D backbuffer images. Controllable character movement, correct rendering, reliable audio, and acceptable performance have not been established. See [observed status](docs/public-status.md) for the evidence and its limits.

The original maintainer has stepped away from active development and published this snapshot so others can continue the work. The technical handoff records the current state, reproducible checks, open questions, and next investigation. There is no planned release date or promise of ongoing maintainer support.

This is an independent research project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Sucker Punch Productions.

## Continue the work

Start with the [technical handoff](docs/MASTER-HANDOFF-AND-REPLICATION-GUIDE.md), then read [getting started](docs/getting-started.md), [the patch stack](docs/patches.md), and [regression testing](docs/regression-testing.md). The handoff identifies the current unknowns and the next bounded investigation.

The repository includes handwritten integration code, build and diagnostic scripts, synthetic tests, and ordered patches for PS3Recomp. The pinned third-party SDK is fetched separately. The game executable, generated translations of game code, assets, firmware, keys, saves, dumps, and a runnable game binary are not distributed.

## Test without the game

On Windows with Python, CMake, Ninja, clang-cl, and the Windows SDK:

```powershell
./scripts/setup.ps1 -CheckOnly
./scripts/setup.ps1
./scripts/build.ps1 -Target tests
./scripts/test.ps1 -Regression -IncludeGpu
```

The WARP fixtures require a suitable graphics environment. Record pass, failure, and skip counts; a skipped fixture is not a pass. The full port also requires the contributor's own legitimately obtained local game files and generated code. See [building](docs/building.md).

## Publication and licensing

Before sharing changes, run the [publication checks](CONTRIBUTING.md). Keep proprietary material and personal paths out of commits and history. Patch files contain context from the MIT-licensed PS3Recomp project; preserve its notices and the other exceptions in [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Original contributions are licensed under [GPL-3.0-only](LICENSE), subject to the documented third-party terms.

No repository check can guarantee that a rights holder will not file a complaint. Share only material you have the right to publish.

4e324ad9f5ff0fa8d99e936e5a97ceecbe430968.message:
Game update 2.17 runs (US BCUS98114): two lifter fixes, 2.17's SPU jobs

2.17 was built with a newer compiler than the disc, and the lift did
not know two of its patterns (tools/ppu_lifter.py, in ps3recomp.patch):

- Switch tables whose base is built from immediates (lis/addi) are
  decoded; only TOC-loaded bases were accepted, so every such bctr
  lifted to an unresolved indirect call and the game stayed on a black
  screen from its static constructors on.
- The raw-index search for the table bound only looks before the lwzx:
  with `lwzx r0, r9, r0` it took the later `add r0,r0,r9` as the index,
  missed the bound compare and cut func_00B7288C's 310-case table at
  256.
- Two vectors in tools/test_ppu_jumptables.py.

On the US 01.00 EBOOT the lifter's jump-table discovery is byte for
byte as before (92 dispatchers, 459 targets); on 2.17 it goes from 80
dispatchers to 358.

version_addrs.py: the computed goto is matched by opcodes only (2.17
reads its field off r31, with no TOC reload before it), its labels are
read from the code that stores them when no data table holds them, and
duplicate targets are dropped. US 01.00 output is unchanged.

spu_jobs_from_eboot.py: the four SPU jobs US 2.17 changed or added
(CB9BD024 replaces D58063CD; 0B07CA3D, 18DE3719, CF635263 are new); the
summary counts the jobs only updates have.

setup.ps1 and version_addrs.py name US 2.17's EBOOT.elf; README, STATUS
and CHANGELOG updated.

Tested on BCUS98114 with updates 1.01-2.17: menus, GT Mode, a full
16-car Arcade race at 59.4 fps median, no missed SPU job and no
unresolved indirect call. Ryzen 7 9850X3D, Radeon RX 9070 XT,
Windows 11.

9f73bed81cb35438704c5dd9ca2e70b1ed67a186.message:
DLC works offline with your own licence keys (runtime only; no keys in the repo)

The runtime part of #24, as asked in its review: no installer, no key
material in the repository.

Runtime (ps3recomp.patch):
- PS3_EDAT_STRICT=1: an EDAT opens the way the PS3 kernel serves it, as
  stored for a plain open and as plaintext for an open with the 8-byte
  NPDRM argument (GT5 passes [0, 2]). GT5's buildIndex reads each
  voucher's NPD header with a plain open and checks its content id;
  decrypted on every open, all vouchers failed and nothing was granted.
- sceNpManagerGetEntitlementById answers "not owned", as PSN does for an
  account without the purchase; unimplemented, it returned success with
  nothing written. GT5's DLCUtil unlocks the 2011 packs by entitlement or
  voucher and the 2012 packs by voucher only, so the DLC comes from the
  vouchers, each of which decrypts only with its licence key.
- PS3_NP_SIGNED_IN=1: the NP manager reports signed in with the local
  profile and no network, for the Downloadable Content screen.
- Licence keys from dev_hdd0/home/00000001/exdata/<content id>.rifkey,
  and the decrypted cache in dev_hdd0/edat_cache: GT5 opens every file
  in USRDIR/vou, so neither may sit beside the vouchers.

play.bat: PS3_EDAT_STRICT on; PS3_NP_SIGNED_IN only when a voucher is
installed (checked at every start), so players without DLC stay offline
and the game doesn't try for tickets.

README: a DLC section (vouchers from RPCS3 or a PS3, a key per content
id in exdata). STATUS and CHANGELOG.

e67ff9e9a0c9ff2a0d620b5e9a9c7904461d0ad0.message:
Fix noisy distant road and track textures (Tsukuba)

Many track textures have only their top two or three mip levels written; the rest of the chain held zeros on a fresh boot and leftover data from earlier scenes otherwise, which showed as blocky black-and-white or grass-green noise on the road at Tsukuba. Each DXT level is now checked against the one above it (mean colour of each 4x4 block), and from the first empty or mismatched level the chain is rebuilt from the last good one (decode, box filter, re-encode). LD_MIP_REBUILD=0 turns it off; LD_MIP_FOLLOW_MAX sets the threshold (default 12); LD_MIP_DUMP=<dir> saves mipped DXT textures for offline checks.

💬 Discord · Install · Launcher · Updating · Version history · Changelog · Status · FAQ · Modding · Contributing · License

# GT5 Recomp An unofficial PC port of **Gran Turismo 5** (PS3) made by static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated into C++ that is compiled for Windows x64, and the PS3's graphics, sound, input and system calls are reimplemented on Windows (Direct3D 12 for the RSX). A native [Linux build](#linux) (Vulkan) is new and early. It is built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) and borrows from the [GT5 Prologue port](https://github.com/sp00nznet/GT5P), both by Ned Heller (sp00nznet). > **Game version required:** your own **Gran Turismo 5** Blu-ray disc, using the disc's own > executable (version **01.00**, with **no game update** installed): > > - **Europe, BCES00569**: tested. This is the copy the port was built from. > - **North America, BCUS98114**: works; players have raced on it (thanks!). The lift finds the few addresses > that differ between releases in your own executable. > > See [Which copy of GT5](#which-copy-of-gt5) for how to check your files. ## 📑 Contents | 🚀 Getting started | 📈 How it's going | 🛠️ Setting up by hand | 📚 About the project | |---|---|---|---| | [Install](#install) | [Current state](#current-state) | [Requirements](#requirements) | [What this repository contains](#repo-contents) | | [The launcher](#launcher) | [Try it, tell me how it went](#feedback) | [Which copy of GT5](#which-copy-of-gt5) | [Fork it, mod it](#modding) | | [Updating](#updating) | [FAQ](#faq) | [Setup](#setup) | [Credits](#credits) | | [Controls](#controls) | | [Switches](#switches) | [License](#license) | | [Linux](#linux) | | | | **More pages:** [Version history](VERSIONS.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Status board](STATUS.md) · [Modding guide](MODDING.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [License](LICENSE) ## ⬇️ Install **The easy way, on Windows 10 or 11:** 1. Download **[GT5-Installer.bat](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/releases/latest/download/GT5-Installer.bat)** and double-click it. If Windows warns about a downloaded file, choose **Run** (or **More info**, then **Run anyway**). 2. In its window, pick two things and press **Install**: - **your GT5 game**: the folder of your disc dump (the one with `PS3_GAME` in it) or an `.iso`; - **PS3UPDAT.PUP**, Sony's free PS3 system software (the window has a button that opens Sony's page). That's all. It installs whatever's missing (Git, Python, Microsoft's C++ build tools), downloads this code, unlocks your game's executable and the system software with RPCS3 (used only as a tool for that: the game itself runs natively as `gt5.exe`, not in an emulator), builds the game (about an hour the first time) and puts **Gran Turismo 5 (PC)** on your desktop, which opens the [launcher](#launcher). Nothing from the game is ever uploaded or shared. Rather do it by hand? See [Setup](#setup). On Linux? See [Linux](#linux). ## 🎛️ The launcher

**Gran Turismo 5 (PC)** on your desktop (or `GT5Launcher.exe` in your `gt5-recomp` folder) opens the launcher: every setting in one window, then **Play**. No more editing `play.bat`. - **Display:** 1080p or 720p, **Speed** (30 fps draws every other frame; it only helps when the graphics card is the limit, the window title then shows both numbers, e.g. `FPS: 15 (game 30)`), screen shape (ultrawide), **borderless full screen**, maximized or a window size, watch mode, SPU threads. - **Controls:** steering wheel on/off, wheel rotation, force feedback strength and direction, pad in the background, mouse clipping. - **Game:** the game's language (as far as your disc has it), your mods from `GT5\mods`, the launcher's own language (English or 中文). - **Updates:** shows your version and the newest one with what's new, and **Update now** does the whole update for you and opens the launcher again. - **Help:** **Save logs for a report** puts your logs on the desktop as `.txt` files GitHub accepts, plus the logs folder, the problem form and this FAQ. It's built on your PC from [`launcher/GT5Launcher.cs`](launcher/GT5Launcher.cs) with the C# compiler that comes with Windows, every time the game is built, so it updates with the game; its picture is the logo from your own disc. Settings are saved in `GT5\settings.bat`, which `play.bat` reads, so `play.bat` still works and starts the game the same way. (`GT5Launcher.exe --play` starts the game straight away.) ## 🔄 Updating Every change to the port comes out as a numbered version (v0.1.0, v0.1.1, ...) on the [Releases page](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/releases), with what changed. To hear about new ones, click **Watch** at the top of this page, then **Custom** and tick **Releases**. ### The easy way - **The launcher** checks for a new version when it opens: its **Updates** page shows what's new, and **Update now** does everything below and opens the launcher again. - Or **double-click `Update.bat`** in your `gt5-recomp` folder. Both run `update.ps1`, so everything below applies. (No launcher or `Update.bat` yet? Your next update brings them: run the command below once.) ### Are you out of date? Close the game, open PowerShell in your `gt5-recomp` folder and run: ``` powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -List ``` It lists every version and marks the one you have (`<- installed`) and the newest (`[newest]`). If they're different, you're out of date. ### Update to the newest version ``` powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 ``` That one command does everything: 1. It downloads the new version. 2. It swaps the old ps3recomp patch for the new one. 3. It re-generates the game code only if that version needs it (about 10 minutes). 4. It rebuilds only what changed. Kept as they are: - your saves (`GT5\gamedata`), a game update's data (`GT5\hdd0`) and game files (`GT5\input`, `GT5\vfs`, `GT5\dev_flash`); - the shader cache; - edits you made to files such as `play.bat`. The previous `gt5.exe` is kept as `GT5\build\gt5.previous.exe`. If one of your edits clashes with a change in the new version, the new version's file is used and your edit is saved in `backups\` so you can copy it back. **If you're several versions behind,** run the same command. It goes straight to the newest version; there's no need to step through the ones in between. ### Installed before update.ps1 existed? If your folder has no `update.ps1` (you set up before v0.1.0), get it first, then update: ``` git pull powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 ``` If `git pull` says your local changes would be overwritten (usually `play.bat`), run `git stash`, then `git pull`, then `git stash pop`, then the update. Your first update re-generates the game code once (about 10 minutes), because older installs have no record of what their code was made from. ### Downloaded the ZIP instead of cloning? A ZIP download can't update itself. Clone the repository fresh as in [Setup](#setup), step 1. Then move these folders over from your old copy and run `update.ps1`: - your game files: `GT5\input`, `GT5\vfs`, `GT5\dev_flash`; - your saves: `GT5\gamedata` (and `GT5\hdd0`, if you set up a game update). ### Go back to an older version If a new version gives you trouble, switch back to the one that worked (see `-List` for the names): ``` powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -Version v0.1.0 ``` To play the previous build right away instead, copy `GT5\build\gt5.previous.exe` over `GT5\build\gt5.exe` (the last update kept it). Please also [report what went wrong](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml). ### Other options | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `update.ps1 -Dev` | The newest changes, before they're released. | | `update.ps1 -NoBuild` | Switch versions without building; build later with `GT5\scripts\build.cmd gt5`. | | `update.ps1 -Force` | Re-generate and rebuild everything, even when nothing changed. | ## 🎮 Controls A DualSense, DualShock 4 or XInput pad works. Without one, the keyboard: Z = Cross, X = Circle, A = Square, S = Triangle, arrow keys = D-pad, Enter = Start, Tab = Select. A steering wheel works too, with force feedback (new and untested on real wheels): see the [FAQ](#faq). ## 📋 Current state

**Playable.** Races run at 45 to 58 fps on the tested rig, and most of the game's modes work. The full board (tested rig, what works, what's being worked on, known issues, recent changes) is in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md); updates are also posted in [Announcements](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/discussions/categories/announcements). Everything done on the port since the first day, with dates, is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## 🏁 Try it, then tell me how it went If you own the game, please set it up and play. 10036dbff1459d1a3d5c4913a3047eff28f3aef7.message:
Setup: the first Python without curl or tar (Wine, CrossOver)

Setup's first step downloads Python with Windows' own curl.exe and unpacks it with its tar.exe, from System32. Wine
and CrossOver ship neither, so a Mac player on CrossOver stopped at "Setup could not start its first download", and the
log did not say why.

When curl or tar does not start, the host now does it itself. Machines that have curl and tar work as before.
- setup_http.cpp downloads with WinHTTP, which Windows and Wine both have. It does what the curl line does:
  - https only, TLS 1.2 or later;
  - redirects followed, but never from https to http;
  - a minute's timeouts;
  - a Range request carrying on from the .part file. A 200 answer starts the file over; a 206 for another range
    deletes it.
  Cancel closes its handles, which ends the call it is in.
- setup_unzip.cpp unpacks the zip:
  - stored and deflated entries, inflated by stb_image's zlib, which the UI already builds;
  - each file's CRC-32 checked;
  - zip64, encryption and several disks refused.
  The names go through the same check as tar's, and the archive's size and SHA-256 are checked first, as before.
- FIX lines (the reason under Details) now also go to the log, so a report has them.
- DES_SETUP_NO_SYSTEM_TOOLS=1 hides curl and tar, for tests.
- crc32.hpp is report.cpp's CRC-32, now shared with the zip reader, and its table is built once in a thread-safe way.
- docs/88 section 5 describes the fallback.

Off Windows nothing changes: setup_http.cpp has no download there, so a missing curl fails as before.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

Setup: read a disc RPCS3 keeps on its hard disk, and let no leftover entry hide a copy

always read, for every disc. Two others failed, for every disc:

- A disc game kept in dev_hdd0/game/<TITLE_ID>: PS3_GAME's files in that
  folder, with no PS3_GAME folder inside it (RPCS3's "Disc game located in
  dev_hdd0/game"; games.yml has it with "/./" only after its first boot).
  The check stopped at "no PS3_GAME folder", or RPCS3's library looked empty.
- An entry stays in games.yml after its game has gone. The first listed disc
  won even with no game in its folder, so a leftover entry for another disc
  hid the copy the player has.

Setup now takes a library entry whose copy is there first. A disc kept in
dev_hdd0/game is read through a link in setup's own folder
(<data>/setup/disc-view/<TITLE_ID>/PS3_GAME: a junction on Windows, a
symbolic link elsewhere), so nothing is written in RPCS3's folders. A library
folder with no game in it now names that folder and what was looked for. The
command-line check names the disc it matched, not always the US one.

Issue #453.

17c28aac99235d025c5c8ac77573dd75f4a4815c.message:
Run defaults: Havok's threads at normal priority (PPU_RAISE_BELOW=0)

ps3recomp raises a title's threads below guest priority 1000 to above
normal, for audio and I/O pollers that sleep between blocks. In this game
those are Havok's: hkSpuUtil Helper (80), Havok PPU Thread (100) and
SPURuntimeService (200). The Havok PPU Thread polls the job queue's lock
with usleep(1), which waits in place (docs/77). Raised, on 2-4 CPUs it
likely keeps the SPU tasks of its own step off the cores: in a console
trace the long frames are the main thread waiting 34-42 ms for the step
while that thread makes no call for about 40 ms.

Held to 2 CPUs at 60 fps (PS3_AFFINITY=5, with ps3recomp #261), two
rounds, 9 roll-breaks each:
- raised (the runtime's 1000): 3.1% and 2.9% of frames over 25 ms away
  from breaks, jitter 2.8 ms, 68 and 88 frames over 25 ms after breaks;
- none raised (0): 0.5% and 0.6%, jitter 1.1 ms, 8 and 11;
- Havok PPU + helper raised (150): 2.1%, 84; helper only (90): as 0.
Audio gaps (AUDIO_GAPS=1) were fewer with 0: 1 and 4 against 5 and 12.
libmixer's threads still go up by name (PPU_MIXER_RAISE), and the
runtime's line stays at 1000 for other titles.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

1de3a23e3fb3df7c2ac173f6b7d8f0ab5bbe7a11.message:
Freestanding game module: no C++ exceptions (setup's link, #304)

Setup's link of des_game.dll stops with "undefined symbol:
__CxxFrameHandler3", referenced from the .xdata of ppu_recomp_005, _010
and more (issue #304).

The freestanding module is C++ compiled with /EHsc and linked with
/NODEFAULTLIB: no C runtime, so no C++ unwind handler. That held while no
module function had a local with a destructor. ps3recomp #212 (pinned by
#297) gave every lifted function that calls the guest setjmp a scope
object, ps3_sjlj_scope, whose destructor drops its slots. Under /EHsc
clang has to run that destructor when a call throws, so the 7 chunks with
a setjmp call get __CxxFrameHandler3 as an unwind handler. Every setup
since #297 lifts again and then fails at the link. The single-exe build
links the C runtime and was not affected.

The module never throws or catches, so it is now compiled with C++
exceptions off: /EHs-c- on Windows and -fno-exceptions on Linux, beside
/GR- and -fno-rtti and for the same reason. On Linux the missing names
are __gxx_personality_v0 and _Unwind_Resume, and -z defs fails that link
too. A host longjmp still unwinds through the module's frames by their
unwind tables. The guest-setjmp code does not need the destructor on that
path: the guest longjmp sets the slot list itself, and the thread proc
empties it after a thread exit.

Both game build descriptions gain the flag for the four C++ objects
(ppu, libsre, spu_workloads, des_game_module). The Windows one matches
CMake's commands again (game_build_desc.py --check --commands-only, as
CI's job does). With setup's commands and the pinned clang, the 8 chunks
with the guest setjmp or longjmp no longer need __CxxFrameHandler3
(llvm-nm), and a link of them with game_module and game_libc leaves only
the other chunks' functions and the port's own names undefined. With
master's flags the same link lacks __CxxFrameHandler3, as in the issue.
The Linux objects no longer need __gxx_personality_v0 or _Unwind_Resume.
In chunk 005 only the cleanup paths change: .
