27d85b1d73fe516de055145649639c3558825baf.message:
Problem reports: put the player's save in the zip

So that a reported problem can be loaded where it happened, instead of
played up to again, both kinds of report now hold the save: Report an
issue (the menu) and the crash, hang and lost-graphics dialog's Report on
GitHub.

report::save_files takes each save folder in the game's save root, found
as cellSaveData.c finds it (PS3_SAVEDATA_ROOT, else
gamedata/dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata in the working folder; the
crash dialog's process has the game's environment and working folder).
Each goes in as save/<folder>/<file>. Two kinds of file stay out:

- the folder's two pictures (ICON0.PNG, PIC1.PNG), which are the game's
  art;
- a file the runtime is still writing (.<name>.tmp).

If a file changed or was being written while the folder was read, the
folder is read again, at most twice and half a second apart. The limits
are 8 MB a file and 32 MB in all; a Demon's Souls save is ten 256 KB
files. game.txt (and the crash issue's System block) gets one line: the
folder, how many files and KB, how many minutes before the report it was
saved, and whether the game was saving meanwhile.

The save holds the characters and their names, and the issue is public.
So the texts that said a report has no save data now say it holds the
save, with the characters' names: the menu's box, the crash dialog's
three, the README and docs/74. The port writes its own PARAM.SFO, so no
PSN account is in it.

UI: the game gets its controls back a second after a menu closes

While a document is up, the game sees neutral pads (cellPad_set_host_hold),
and it got them back only once every key (virtual keys 1-0xFE, mouse
buttons too) and every pad button and stick was at rest. So the press that
closed the menu doesn't reach the game. But a key or pad that reads as
held for good, as a driver can leave one until a restart, kept the
controls from the game for the whole run.

Issue #298: a DualShock 3 on the BthPS3 drivers worked in the start
screen but not in the game. Some starts only; a restart of the PC
fixed it, and so did turning the start screen off. The game's own pad
read saw the pad connected ("keyboard input on port 0 (merged with the
pad)").

  the last document closed. Then the log names every key held and each
  pad's state ("[ui] the game gets its controls back a second after the
  menu closed, with this still held: ...").
- The menu's copy of pad_hid_sony.h's PadHidSonyState lacked the slot
  byte the runtime added for vibration (10 bytes, not 8). With two or
  more PlayStation pads, the poll wrote past the menu's array and the
  menu read the second pad from the wrong offsets, which could also
  keep the pads from reading as at rest. The copy has the field now, and
  a static_assert checks the size.

3dfb4ee2d121c86a58f93ffe972471477843b0bf.message:
The Linux download gets the Vulkan renderer and setup's shader step

Issue #351, the first Steam Deck report: long freezes when a new scene loads. The Linux download was still the legacy
renderer on vkd3d alone, which compiles each shader as the game first draws it. A level load needs 18 vertex and 27 pixel
programs: 8.2 s through the shipped vkd3d on the development PC, about 19 s scaled to the Deck, and the tester's notices read
16-23 s. docs/120 said Vulkan was Linux's default, which is true of the option but not of what shipped: host.yml built that
version only as a check, on a second build, and never uploaded it.

host.yml now builds the runtime with PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL from the start, as on Windows, and the second build goes. So Linux
starts on Vulkan, and setup's shader step has its spv target (it was Pass::Off before). A Vulkan start that fails falls back
to the legacy renderer in the same process, and the next start after one that crashed uses it too.

The licences of what the renderer compiles in (glslang, SPIRV-Tools, SPIRV-Headers, volk, the Vulkan headers) go along, as
in the Windows job. README and docs/76 and 120 say what ships.

port: the game ending itself with an error shows the crash dialog

The game's fatal paths end in sys_process_exit with a non-zero code: abort()
and Lua's exit(1) on an error with no protected call. Neither is a fault, so
the crash report's filter and abort handler never ran and the window just
closed, with nothing for the player to report.

des_guest_exit.cpp takes the runtime's new hook. Several threads can get there
within a millisecond of each other, since exit() frees objects under threads
still playing. Each records what it knows, the first waits a moment and writes
the one report, and the others stay until the process ends.

The report says when it was Lua running out of memory and carries each
thread's HOST-bt line. There is no Settings row.

674155d64ca01e566600e8447f6097b531e24f3b.message:
port: enemies no longer T-pose for a frame above 30 fps

Havok's sample-and-combine fills a bone whose animation weight is under
the skeleton's reference-pose threshold (0.05) with the reference pose, a
T-pose. When an enemy starts a new move, the new clip can fade in from 0
with nothing under it, growing about as t^2. At 30 fps one frame of the
fade is under the threshold; above 30 fps several are, near weight 0, so
the enemy is drawn in the T-pose for 20-30 ms.

des_refpose_rate runs after each load of the threshold: the SPU sample
job's copy (0x01005978) and the four PPU sample paths. It scales the
threshold by (30 dt)^2, so a fade stays under it for about one frame at
any frame rate. Nothing changes at 30 fps or below. DES_TPOSEFIX=0 turns
it off live. Region rows for the European, Japanese and Asian discs.

Tutorial route, unlocked: with the fix off, a fade-in in view drew 5-6
frames at 72-100% reference pose; with it on, one frame at 26%.

Pantheon: take real characters' records, and send our own even when one fails

Players reached the Pantheon but saw no statues. The live server had 0
records on all five boards. Each player's own game refused its record
before sending it, and it did so without an error.

The record checks came from two records of one new character. Records
dumped from 20 saved characters (the game's own record builder, run on
each save) failed them 18 times, and 138 of 147 records rebuilt from save
slots failed too.

Widened, here and in the server's table (DemonsSoulsServer desrecord.go)
with the same rows:
- +0xAC: 0 to 100 (0 after the first area)
- +0xAE: 0 to 9999, and +0xB0..+0xCC eight counts, 0 to 999,999,999
  (it was "padding")
- +0xD4..+0xDC: signed, from -65536 (0xFFFF0000 unset; +0xD8 can be set)
- colours: 0 to 4 (up to 1.875 seen)
- list entries: kind 1 to 3, and any last word (list B's holds a stack
  leftover)
- list B: its order and count aren't checked (two entries, a count of 1)

All 20 dumped and 147 rebuilt records now pass both tables.

Going up, a record that fails is logged and sent all the same. The server
checks it with the same rows and logs the field it refuses, so a limit
still too tight shows in the server's log. This needs ps3recomp's
fix/score-refused-game-data (#286): without it, the game takes the
refusal for a lost connection and skips its later boards. A received
record that fails is still refused.

6927ea3b096b2f11f363722791c5f4fbffebbe4e.message:
Setup: when Python can't check a server's certificate, Windows' own curl downloads (#493)

#493: setup stopped at the compiler's download with "CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED:
unable to get local issuer certificate", and the update check said there was no
connection to GitHub. On the same PC Windows' curl had just downloaded Python.

On Windows, Python checks a server's certificate against the roots it copies from
Windows' store. Windows adds a root there only when its own check first needs one
(from Windows Update), so a PC where nothing Windows runs has needed that root yet
fails Python's check and passes Windows'. A TLS-scanning antivirus or proxy that
Windows trusts can look the same.

Now, when Python's check refuses the certificate, on Windows only:
- a tool's download (fetch.py) goes through Windows' own curl.exe, from the System
  folder, with the host's own options (setup_python.cpp): https only, -C - to carry
  on from the .part file, and a start over once when the server ignores the range.
  The size and SHA-256 checks are unchanged. Setup's log gets a note saying so.
- the update check (update.read_feed, with its ETag) and the release's small files
  (update._small) get the same: a GET through curl.
Any other failure, and any failure off Windows, is reported as before.

Setup: have RPCS3 open the update's package, remove the key

Setup's rule is no keys and no decryptor (docs/51, docs/90), and #442 broke
it with a PS3 package key and an AES routine in game_update.py. No release
has them. The player's RPCS3, which setup already runs to decrypt the game's
files, now installs the package in a folder of setup's own
(rpcs3.install_package). Without an RPCS3 that setup can start, the player
is told to install the package in RPCS3 and choose its folder.

RPCS3 decrypts the 14 .sdat files as it installs them and keeps their names,
so a folder it installed failed the table's sums and was refused. They equal
the table's decrypted files, so either form is now good, and they aren't
decrypted again.

The journal also wrapped UpdateError, so a sentence meant for the player
became a failed step.

no crash report in the Penetrator fight (1-3). The boss script errors at
line 86 ("attempt to compare nil with number"), the game's own bug, which
a PS3 catches. Here the throw came back into the interpreter, which read
a NULL pointer, and the game ended itself.

The game module ABI goes from 3 to 4: the host hands the module the C
library's _setjmp and longjmp, and the module hands the host its setjmp
list. Both game build descriptions say 4, and the Linux one lists
game_libc/setjmp.h, which the lifted chunks now include (the Windows one
had it already, through clang's intrin.h). The lifter changed, so setup
lifts the game again on the first start after the update.

7c90c40e243e4a553e959d2a3774906f2ca0afaf.message:
port: the sun flare takes the probe's latest count above 30 fps (#290)

The flare's three readers (0x003E2D38, and in 0x003E5750 and 0x003E6368)
read report 1024 only once label 0x52 has reached the probe query's
counter, and otherwise keep the count they have. At 30 fps the RSX has
walked the last probe by the next frame's first check. Above 30 fps the
main thread runs 2-3 probes ahead of it, so the check fails every frame
and the count stays at whatever a rare pass took: the sun through walls,
or gone in the open. A trace at the reported Stonefang spot, uncapped
(about 315 fps), passed the check about once per camera sweep in 130 s.

des_sun_gate runs after each reader's load of the label (insn hooks at
0x003E2DF0, 0x003E6330, 0x003E6518) and raises it to at least the
counter, so the reader takes the latest stored count. With the fix the
held count followed the stored one within one check, at the same frame
rate. Only with DES_FPS; DES_SUNFIX=0 turns it off live. docs/28, "Sun
flare stuck above 30 fps".

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

81cb29d1690c7f23f73eef635c8ce6bc018e86da.message:
port: Lua takes room in the port's heap when its own heap is full

Each of the game's Lua states gets its memory through a small-block pool,
and the pool gets pages and every block over 128 bytes from a heap object.
Two heap classes stand behind the game's Lua states, and each hands
everything to one fixed arena of its own:
- 0x01852D20 serves the two script systems' states, in 2.375 MB;
- 0x01852EC0 serves a third, small state, in 9 MB.

When an arena can't give a block, luaM_realloc throws LUA_ERRMEM. Nothing
catches it on a character's script, so Lua calls exit(1) and the window
closes. The early collection (des_luagc.cpp) keeps the scripts well below
the limit above 30 fps. This change is the safety net under it.

Every method of the two classes that hands out or takes back a block is
wrapped (all calls to them go through their vtables). The classes are one
template over a different arena: the same methods at the same vtable
offsets, forwarding to the same functions.
- When an arena can't give an allocation, it comes from the port's own
  guest heap instead.
- Free, realloc, a block's size and "is this block yours" send those blocks
  back there. Every other block goes to the game's own method unchanged.
- Until an arena can't give a block, nothing changes.
- The pool finds a block's page by its address range, not by alignment, so
  pages from the port's heap work the same way.
- Lua 5.0 can't safely collect inside the allocator, so the net doesn't
  collect: it only gives room.

Which heaps a Lua state can get: the game's lua_open takes the heap, and a
state's threads share its pool. Only the state's constructor calls lua_open,
and the constructor is called from six places.
- Four are the script systems, and they read one global heap pointer.
- Two are "new state on this heap" methods, each reached only through its
  class's vtable. One is in the code with the second TOC and reaches the
  constructor through a TOC stub.
- Both methods are wrapped as well. Each writes a line to the log if a state
  ever lands

8fb4175e5f8f6062c0d63ae3dd90706b0a91c36d.message:
tools: DES_MEMSTAT, how full the game's own heaps get (docs/59 T1)

The game makes 13 heaps of fixed sizes at boot and never asks for more;
a full one ends in its error report. Mods with bigger files need more of
some of them. DES_MEMSTAT=1 shows which, and how close each comes:

- A thread reads each heap's arena every millisecond. It only reads (no
  lock taken, nothing in the game called), so the game runs as without
  it. Each class keeps its arena in a global of its own; the ten
  DLStaticHeap-like arenas keep their free bytes at +0x3C and their block
  list's ends at +0x04/+0x18, HAVOK's, MO's and TEMP's the same fields
  8 bytes lower (+0x34, +0x28/+0x2C).
- The log gets each heap's size, a line as its peak use passes another
  tenth from half full up, and a table (size, in use now, at most, share)
  every DES_MEMSTAT_EVERY seconds and on every game error.
  DES_MEMSTAT=2 adds each arena's first words.
- With DES_MEMSTAT off, a game error still prints one table: each heap's
  use at that moment (no peaks: no thread ran). A full heap ends in the
  game's error report, so a player's report zip then shows which one.
- A 14th row, LOCAL, is the game's heap over the RSX's local (video)
  memory, 248 MB. Its arena is in a static object: the base its heap
  object points at (0x01AD6358) + 0x18, as the class's methods take it.
- The addresses are in the region tables: European +0x280, Japanese and
  Asian +0x30, read from the game's own address table that the heap
  methods use (r30 = [r2 + slot], then [r30 + offset]).
- des_heap.cpp: ds_heap_usage, the port's own guest heap now and at most.

Off by default (apart from that one table). First numbers (1-2 bridge, 240 s): the file-loading heap
CORERES peaks at 92% of its 12.25 MB without mods and at 12.24 MB with a
large set of texture and model mods.

927ea39a8c365776ca4fd372fa5bd05edaee829d.message:
Mods: a mods folder, Settings > Mods, and offline play with gameplay mods

Each folder in <data folder>/mods is a mod. Settings > Mods lists them,
one row each, off until turned on (DES_MODS in settings.ini). At start
the mods that are on become PS3_VFS_MODS, which the runtime reads in
place of the game's files (ps3recomp: vfs mod folders). Nothing in the
game's own files changes.

- A mod's files are found flat, in wrapper folders, or in
  (PS3_GAME/)USRDIR, up to five folders deep. Folders named Original,
  Backup, Vanilla, Uninstall or Unmodded (the game's own files, shipped
  to undo a mod) are passed over. Notes and pictures beside the files
  are left out. A mod with an EBOOT.BIN, two versions of itself or no
  game files can't be used, and its row says why.
- Order: folder names A to Z; the first mod with a file gives it. A
  "Same files" row lists files that mods that are on share.
- Look or gameplay: textures, models, text, sound, effects, menus and
  lighting are look-only; parameters, map layouts and collision,
  characters, objects, scripts and unknown files are gameplay.
- A gameplay mod keeps the session offline: apply_network sets no
  network knobs, the runtime's network is locked off, and when Online is
  on a notice says why ("Playing offline: gameplay mods are on"). The
  Network and Mods tabs say so too.
- Problem reports get a "Mods:" line.
- settings.ini lines can be up to 8 KB (was 512 bytes), for long mod
  lists.
- mods_check (CI, Windows and Linux): the rules, finding a mod's files,
  the unusable cases, order, shared files and PS3_VFS_MODS.
- docs/143: how it works and what is planned.

Tested live with test mods and with published mods of each layout
(flat, a wrapper folder, a version folder with a backup copy beside
it): the runtime gave the mods' files and the level loaded; a gameplay
mod kept the session offline with the notice; a look-only mod left
online alone; toggling a row saved DES_MODS.

9c41cbadc4c000e6e1132849d5d2767928232295.message:
tools/des: halimg compares an HDR snapshot in 8-bit codes when its paper white is known

Under the vk rule an HDRP pair was held to 1e-3, with at most 0.01% of
the pixels allowed up to 8/255 (relative to the larger of 1 and the
value). That bound is in the snapshot's linear units, while the pixels
it is for, ones that sampled the next texel of an 8-bit texture, differ
by a step that grows with the paper white. At the settings a player
uses (RSX_HDR_WHITE=400, scale 300, AA 2, aniso 16) Vulkan's snapshots
of capsetu's courtyard and fog wall failed it with 19 and 119 pixels,
where the frames' own 8-bit shots pass: in codes those pixels are 1 to
5 apart, scattered one by one, nothing above 8.

- halimg.py --hdr-white <paper white, nits / 80> [--hdr-curve
  gamma|srgb]: under vk an HDRP pair is turned back into the codes the
  blit decoded (gamma 2.2, or the sRGB curve for RSX_HDR_GAMMA=1) and
  held to the 8-bit rule, heat map included. A NaN fails. Without it,
  and in the hdr mode, the rule is as it was.
- halgate.sh reads the paper white from A's "HDR snap" line and the
  curve from its "HDR: on" line.
- docs/120's G3 line says so.

The self-test gains the round trips (both curves), 120 pixels 4 codes
off (fails without the white, passes with it), 0.06% of pixels 2 codes
off and 0.02% 12 codes off (fail), the hdr mode and a NaN (fail).

af3fb1da919858470cb1ca109eebda71388404e6.message:
tools/region: data through the code's own address tables, and no guesses on the 1.04 discs

region_table.py find gave a confident wrong answer for data on the
Japanese and Asian 1.04 discs: +0x80 for the heap globals at 0x01AD6498..
0x01AD6AF0 ("data, 26 references"), where the game has them at +0x30. It
counted TOC slots holding a base below the address, read at the same slot
offset on the other disc. Two things break that on the 1.04 discs:
- their TOC starts 0x18 higher and many slots moved, so the same offset
  is another slot (kContextAspect's one exact vote pointed 0x60 off);
- their data moved in pieces (the 0x50 bytes below 0x01AD62C8 shrank, and
  some objects were reordered), so a base below can have moved by another
  amount than the address.

Changes:
- New way, find_table: code that loads the address from a TOC slot, or
  loads an address table's base and then the table's word at a fixed
  offset (lwz rX,d(r2); lwz rY,k(rX)), is matched on the other disc, and
  that disc's own slot gives the answer. This is how the heap classes
  reach their arenas.
- SlotMap: whether TOC slots keep their offsets is found from a sample of
  matched loads (yes on the European disc, no on the 1.04 discs); where
  they don't, find_data maps each slot through code that loads it, and
  the anchors (find_between) are not used.
- The ways that read the other disc (find_table, find_content) win; the
  ones that assume (find_data, find_between) only answer when those two
  don't, and a disagreement is noted. On a disc whose data moved in
  pieces, a base below is only a hint ("perhaps ..."), never an answer.

verify against each table (the tables as on master plus the DES_MEMSTAT
rows):
- European: 270 agree, 0 differ, 25 unchecked -> 285 / 0 / 10.
- Japanese and Asian (1.04 EBOOTs, the tables checked with the same code):
  before, the arena rows came out +0x80 (wrong) and kContextAspect's
  agreeing row would have been reported as differing; after, 280 agree,
  0 differ, 15 unchecked.
The 13 unit tests pass; check passes.

bfe7b859ab551ac790675ea6efbccdae65973cee.message:
European disc: Japanese, Chinese (Traditional) and Korean in Settings > Game > Language

The European disc carries the text and fonts for these three (Japanese
in the root of msg/ and font/, Chinese and Korean in their own folders),
but its program never picks them: on a PS3 set to one of them it shows
English.

The program keeps its language as one index (0 Japanese, 1 Asian
English, 2 Korean, 3 Chinese, 4 US English, 5-9 the European five) and
fills it at first use, only ever with 5-9. The text, the fonts and the
menus' language folder all follow it. For these three the port sets it
(0, 3 or 2) before the game runs.

Two other switches on the index are pointed at a Western case for 0-3,
so only the text changes:
- the balance file stays GameParamNA (0-3 would load the Japanese and
  Asian discs' GameParam), so weapons, enemies, saves and online stay
  the European disc's;
- the server info's tags stay UK English's (the Asian ones were the
  Japanese world on the original servers).

These are writes to guest memory before the game runs: no hook and no
new lift. Three new lines in regions/BLES00932.inc; region_table.py
verify matches the index word, and the two jump tables were checked by
hand.

The PC's language picks Japanese or Korean on such a PC, and Chinese
only on a Traditional Chinese one (Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau).
PS3_SYS_LANG given at start still wins, with the original behaviour.
Trophy names stay English for all three: the European trophy set has
no names in them.

European disc: hook handlers read the instruction at the disc's own address

Six instruction-hook handlers decode the instruction their hook runs after,
to find the register to rescale: the camera eases and the bow zoom
(des_cam_rate, des_cam_step, des_cam_keep), the foot IK (des_ik_rate), the
locked-on twist (des_twist_rate), and the sound and fade rates (keep_rate,

so on the European disc they read an unrelated instruction. The camera,
noise and fade fixes did nothing there, and the IK and twist fixes could
rescale an unrelated register.

des_region_addr() gives the running disc's address for a key, and
hook_insn() reads the instruction there. Every hook's instruction is the
same on both discs, so nothing else changes.

e13baf91ce5a8071202291fc8fd993117ded0ba5.message:
Physics cap: go by the last 8 frames, so 30 fps steps every frame

At 30 fps (Frame rate 30, DES_FPS=30) the game's step is the real frame
time, and frames come a little under and over 1/30 s by turns (44% under,
by at most 0.35 ms, in one run). des_phys_rate tested each frame on its
own: a frame under 1/30 skipped its step (the time it held was still short
of a step), and the next long frame stepped its own dt and dropped that
time. Replaying that run's 2,775 frames through the rule: 33% of the
steps skipped, the world 32% behind game time, and the cap on and off
1,802 times, which turned the in-between poses (DES_RAGINTERP,
DES_PARTINTERP) on and off from frame to frame. Ragdolls, debris and stuck
arrows jittered.

- The cap now goes on when the mean of the last 8 frames is under 0.85/n,
  and off when it is over 0.95/n. At 30 fps it stays off and every frame
  steps its own dt, as the game did. The same frames give 1 skipped step.
- Under the cap, a frame of 1/n or longer still steps its own dt, but it
  keeps the time the short frames before it held.
- des_phys_kf acts only under the cap. The ride test runs under the cap.
- Above about 35 fps nothing changes: replayed fast stretches skip the
  same steps as before.

docs/71 has a section on it.

e4cc08a9a6ac2614ac9c0dd2e46d0ac466ee474c.message:
A processor without SSE4.1 gets a clear message, not a crash

Issues #349 and #350: a player's Pentium E5400 crashed with c000001d as the window opened. The runtime and the game module
are built with SSE4.1, and that CPU doesn't have it, so the first such instruction ended the program (pmovsxdq in
create_window, rsxc_d3d12.c). The crash dialog then asked them to report it, with nothing saying what was wrong.

des_cpu_check.cpp now asks the processor first, and says so if SSE4.1 is missing. It runs ahead of the C++ static
initializers, and is the one source here built without SSE4.1, so it can run on such a processor. The check comes
before setup too, so nobody spends time on a build that can't run.

AVX, LZCNT, AES and the like in the exe are in Microsoft's runtime and mbedTLS, which ask the CPU before using them. SSE4.1
is the only one the program assumes, so it is the only one checked.

The README now names the requirement. CI runs the check both ways (DES_TEST_OLD_CPU=1, and plainly) on both systems.

There is no processor without SSE4.1 here: the message was checked with DES_TEST_OLD_CPU=1, on the path it takes.

ec1b9e91020e42ece19b1ee2f4fc576991c6c9c1.message:
des_prework: free the last shader pass's texts once it is done

run_passes resets the precompile module before each target's pass, but
not after the last one. So whenever the start's shader pass runs (after a
session that drew new fragment-program variants, or after an update), the
last target's work stays allocated for the rest of the session: every
decompiled HLSL text (3,654 on the US disc, 44 MB), the programs and the
pipeline index's rows.

It now resets after the last pass too. Nothing reads that state after it:
the rows were handed to the renderer during the pass
(rsx_out_pso_index_add, _ready), and run_pass leaves s_state at 3, so
des_prework_status no longer asks for the counts. reset() waits for the
compile threads first.

Found with a scratch walk of the process heap 30 s into the Tutorial
(d3d12, the regression save, DES_PRECOMPILE=force): busy blocks 113.5 MB ->
69.1 MB; text blocks 10,711 (44.0 MB) -> 2,481 (0.3 MB); the heap's

f586581cba40c3ac525015aab8e7d754cb432b59.message:
Physics cap: stuck arrows follow the pose, ragdolls blend by the leftover

Above 30 fps, arrows stuck in the player still hopped back at every physics
step (up to 3-4 cm at a run), and ragdolls and debris moved on unevenly at
each step. Both treated the frames since a step as one step's time, but at
144 fps a step of 1/30 s comes every 4 or 5 frames (28 or 35 ms).

- Stuck arrows (DES_PARTINTERP): a keyframed part is drawn from the pose the
  game drives it to every frame. des_kf_target, a new hook after 0x00011768
  in the stub to Havok's hard keyframe, keeps each body's last two poses,
  with the frame time of the pass that set them (from des_phys_kf: the
  passes run before des_phys_rate, so the game clock is a frame late).
  des_body_sample carries the last pose on by the game's own look-ahead, and
  des_body_sampled, a new hook after 0x011B1D6C past the sampler's call,
  writes it over the sampled transform. That is where the world would have
  the part if it stepped every frame. Without fresh poses it carries the
  last step on as before.
- Ragdolls, debris and a dead character's parts (DES_RAGINTERP): the blend
  is the cap's leftover (the game time the world has not stepped yet) over
  the step length, for a body that got the world's last step, instead of
  the game time since the body's step changed.
- The two hooks' European addresses are in BLES00932.inc. They need a
  re-lift, which setup does.

Measured with a scratch trace on the deep Palace save under the 1-1
archers, old and new from the same frames: how far an arrow's part moves
against the player from one frame to the next, 95th percentile.
- 144 fps: 32.7 mm before, 7.5 mm after (no cap: 6.2-7.1 mm).
- 60 fps: 54.6 mm before, 19.5 mm after (no cap: 17.8 mm).
- Ragdolls at 144 fps (26 bodies): the 95th percentile of the unevenness
  went from 1.26 mm to 0.75 mm.
See docs/71, "Steps of 4 or 5 frames".

trail check flags four lines. They match words ("world time", "Havok time",
"report", "fps") from learnings about measuring the cap's clock agains

fd0a6cb56aff00de1ea6c82edea55797ee267c7a.message:
port: collect Lua early above 30 fps, the game ran out of script memory

The game's Lua has its automatic collector off and collects from two
countdowns in game time, every 1.0 s and 0.5 s. Scripts make garbage per
frame, so at high frame rates there is several times more of it between two
collections. The two Lua states share a small heap. When an allocation fails,
luaD_throw(LUA_ERRMEM) finds no protected call on a character's script and
Lua calls exit(1): the window closes, in the middle of play.

Once a frame, above 30 fps, expire a countdown early when its state has made
64 KB since its last collection. The game then collects at its usual place
in the frame. It counts the guest's own bytes, so it doesn't depend on the PC.

DES_LUAGC=0 keeps the game's countdowns only. DES_LUAGC_LOG=1 prints each
state's memory once a second. DES_LUAGC_HOLD=1 is a test knob: the countdowns
never reach zero, which with DES_LUAGC=0 is the crash on demand.

1451952339.readme_excerpt:
# Soulbrandt **Demon's Souls, running natively on PC.** [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt?filter=v%2A&sort=semver&display_name=tag&label=release&color=orange)](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases/latest) [![downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/latest/total?label=downloads&color=brightgreen)](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases/latest) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1565536292324769832?label=Discord&logo=discord&logoColor=white&color=5865F2)](https://discord.gg/BzmwDeca8s)
Soulbrandt is a PC port of *Demon's Souls* (PS3, 2009). The game's original code has been converted to run directly on Windows and Linux, with no emulator. You need your own copy of the game: the US version, **BLUS30443**, or the European version, **BLES00932** (both version 1.00, on disc or from the PlayStation Store), or the Japanese or Asian disc, **BCJS30022** or **BCAS20071**, with its 1.04 update. This project includes no game files. ## Status **0.1.2, the current release, is an alpha.** Download it from the [Releases](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases) page. The game plays from start to finish (a tester has beaten it), but not every part has been tried on every setting, so expect bugs. What [isn't supported yet](#not-supported-yet) is below; please [report](#problems) anything you find. Questions and help: [Discord](https://discord.gg/BzmwDeca8s). ## Highlights - Up to 240 fps or unlocked, with the game's timing fixed. Up to 4K, ultrawide, 16:10 and HDR. - The US, European, Japanese and Asian versions, each with its languages, plus Japanese on the US disc and Japanese, Chinese and Korean on the European disc. - Online play on this project's own server: messages, bloodstains, ghosts, co-op, invasions and the Pantheon. - Roll in any direction while locked on, not only forward, back, left or right. - A stat respec in the Nexus (optional): get back the souls your levels cost and spend them again. - Keyboard and mouse, Xbox controllers, DualSense and DualShock 4. ## Features Press **F1** (or **L3 + R3** on a controller) at any time to open the menu. Most settings apply right away. Each setting has a short help text in the menu. **Picture** - Frame rates of 30 (the original), 60, 120, 144, 165 or 240 fps, a number of your own, or unlocked. The game's timing is fixed so it still plays the way it should. Above 60 fps is less tested. - Cutscenes play at 30 fps by default, as they judder above it. You can play them at your frame rate instead. - V-sync on or off, "Even frames" for smooth motion, and G-Sync / FreeSync. - Render resolution up to 300% (4K), ultrawide aspect ratios (21:9 and 32:9), and 16:10 for the Steam Deck's screen. - Anti-aliasing (FXAA or SMAA), anisotropic filtering up to 16x, texture filtering and a sharp scaling filter. - HDR on HDR displays (Windows), with settings for brightness, peak and shadows. - Turn off the game's depth of field and motion blur. - Window, borderless fullscreen, or exclusive fullscreen on Windows (Settings > Display > Display mode). Alt+Enter switches. - Two renderers (Settings > Display > Renderer): DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Windows starts on DirectX 12, except with a GeForce GTX 10 series card or older, which starts on Vulkan. Linux starts on Vulkan. **Controls** - Xbox controllers, DualSense and DualShock 4, over USB or Bluetooth, with vibration. Pick which controller the game uses when several are connected. - Keyboard and mouse, laid out like the Souls games on PC. To turn the camera with the mouse, turn on **Mouse look** in Settings > Controls. - Change which buttons and keys do what. - The game's button prompts show the buttons of the controller you're using, or your keys (Settings > Game > Button icons). - A deadzone for each stick, set as how far you tilt it, with a live picture of the stick (Settings > Controls). - Mouse sensitivity, inverted axes, and switching lock-on targets with a flick of the mouse. - **Roll in any direction while locked on**: the roll goes where the stick points. It's on by default; turn off **Roll toward the stick** in Settings > Controls for the original's four directions. - The mouse in the game's own menus: point and click. Experimental, and off by default. **HUD** - Move, resize, hide or show each part of the HUD. - Change its size, and choose where it goes on wide screens. **Game** - Skip the logos and the opening movie, and go straight into your last save. - **Stat respec**: the Maiden in Black, or the statue in front of where you wake in the Nexus, puts your stats back to your class's and gives back the souls your levels cost, to spend again. Off by default: turn on **Stat respec in the Nexus** in Settings > Game. - Use several soul items at once, as Drop does. On by default: turn off **Use several souls at once** in Settings > Game for the original's one at a time. - **Change Appearance** at the statue in front of where you wake in the Nexus: the game's own Edit Appearance, with your character. Off by default: turn on **Change appearance in the Nexus** in Settings > Game. - Choose the language in Settings > Game > Language. The European disc has English, French, German, Spanish and Italian, plus Japanese, Chinese (Traditional) and Korean; the US disc has English and Japanese; the Asian disc has English, Chinese (Traditional) and Korean. It starts in your PC's language when it can. A change needs a restart. **Online** - On by default, on this project's own server: messages, bloodstains, ghosts, co-op and invasions. - Players of every supported version play together. - The Pantheon in the Nexus: its statues show the characters of the players at the top of each board. - Setup asks for your online name. You can change it, or turn online play off, in Settings > Network. - A matchmaking password, so you meet only your friends. - Show or hide other players' messages, bloodstains and ghosts. **Mods** - Put mods in the mods folder (Mods in the menu or on the start screen, then Open the mods folder) and turn each one on or off there. Mods for the PS3 game or RPCS3 that replace the game's files work, and the game's own files are never changed. - A mod that changes how the game plays keeps you offline, so you never meet players without it. Mods that only change the look or sound keep online play. - When two mods change the same thing, the one higher in the list wins; the arrows on each mod move it. The list is kept in `mods\load_order.txt`, which mod managers can use too (docs/143). **The program** - A setup that builds the game from your copy, with an Original and an Enhanced preset (see [How to play](#how-to-play)). - Updates: the game checks for a new version at start and asks before changing anything. Your saves and settings are kept, and you can go back one version. - In the menu, the Large Sword of Moonlight is the cursor and a crystal lizard dances in the corner. Both can be turned off. - Trophies, with pop-ups and a tune from the game. Setup can bring your trophies and save across from RPCS3. - A Discord status: your profile shows that you're playing, the area you're in and whether you're online (Settings > Network). - **Report an issue** in the menu opens a GitHub issue with your PC's details filled in, and a zip to attach that includes your save, so the problem can be seen where it happened. It has no game files. If the game crashes or stops responding, a window offers to do the same. ## What you need - Your own copy of Demon's Souls for the PS3, as a folder with `PS3_GAME` in it: the US (BLUS30443) or European (BLES00932) disc, version 1.00, or the Japanese (BCJS30022) or Asian (BCAS20071) disc with its 1.04 update, as a folder or a `.pkg` file that setup has RPCS3 install. The US and European PlayStation Store versions (NPUB30910, NPEB01202) work once installed in RPCS3. Setup cannot use ISO files yet. - RPCS3, the free PS3 emulator. Setup has it unlock the game's encrypted files. You don't need the PS3 system software. (Or decrypt the files yourself: see below.) - Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) with a graphics card that supports DirectX 12, or Linux (see [Linux](#linux)). - A processor with SSE4.1, which most have since about 2011. - An internet connection during setup. Setup downloads a compiler and Python (about 60 MB on Windows, about 130 MB on Linux). ## How to play These steps are for the release download. 1. Download the zip for Windows (`DemonsSoulsRecomp-X.Y.Z-windows.zip`) or the tarball for Linux (`DemonsSoulsRecomp-X.Y.Z-linux.tar.xz`), and unpack it into a folder of its own. 2. Start `Soulbrandt.exe` (on Linux, `Soulbrandt`). Setup opens. 3. Pick how setup gets your game's files: - **Import from RPCS3**: setup finds the game in RPCS3's list and has your RPCS3 unlock its files. It can bring your save, trophies and some settings across too. If RPCS3 has several copies, setup lets you pick one. - **I have decrypted files**: your disc copy, plus the 27 files you decrypted yourself (`EBOOT.elf` and the `.sdat` files). - **Show me how**: step by step, with free tools only. 4. Start the build. It runs on your PC and can take a while; setup shows an estimate first. You can stop it and carry on later. Setup builds in AppData on Windows (`~/.local/share` on Linux) and needs about 4 GB free there; to build on another drive, press **Change** next to **Build folder** first. 5. Pick a preset: **Original** plays as on the PS3; **Enhanced** sets 60 fps, a resolution that fits your display, SMAA, 16x anisotropic filtering, fullscreen, and HDR when Windows has HDR on for your display. Then a few choices (HDR among them, on Windows) and your online name. You can change anything later in Settings. Then press **Play**. **A portable install:** put an empty file named `portable.txt` next to `Soulbrandt.exe` before its first start. Your settings, logs and setup's build then stay inside the program's folder, as your saves already do, and you can move or rename that folder. Windows may warn you the first time you start `Soulbrandt.exe` ("Windows protected your PC"), because the program isn't signed yet. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If RPCS3 is set to run as administrator, setup cannot start it: untick that in `rpcs3.exe`'s Properties. ### Linux CI builds the Linux program on every change, and each release includes a Linux download. It needs x86-64 Linux with glibc 2.35 or newer, a Vulkan driver, and `curl` and `tar`. Nothing else needs installing. The game renders on Vulkan, and setup prepares its shaders. If Vulkan can't start, the game falls back to its older renderer on vkd3d (DirectX 12 on Vulkan), which compiles shaders as it goes, with long pauses when a new area loads. Linux is newer and less tested than Windows. Players run it on desktop Linux and on the Steam Deck, on Vulkan ([docs/106](docs/106-setup-on-linux.md)). macOS is not supported. On a Steam Deck, keys and the mouse stay out of the game while its controls are on, because Steam's desktop layout presses them too. To use a keyboard on a docked Deck, set `PAD_KEYBOARD_WITH_PAD=1`. On a Steam Deck the game runs best with **Manual GPU Clock Control** at **800 MHz** and the **Thermal Power (TDP) Limit** at **15 W** (Quick Access menu > Performance). ### Online play Online play is on by default and uses this project's own server. Setup asks for your online name; you can change it, or turn online play off, in Settings > Network. Players of every supported version meet on the same server. RPCS3 players use other servers, so you won't meet them. What the server keeps about you is in the [privacy note](PRIVACY.md). ### Not supported yet - The Japanese and Asian discs without their 1.04 update, the Japanese PlayStation Store version (NPJA00102) and the US demo don't work. - Setup can't read ISO files, and it needs RPCS3 to unlock the game's files (or files you decrypted yourself). - macOS isn't supported, and running the Windows download through CrossOver hasn't been tested all the way through. Linux and the Steam Deck are less tested than Windows. ### Problems Use **Report an issue** in the menu (F1), or open an [issue](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/issues). For questions and help, join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/BzmwDeca8s). Report security problems privately, as [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) says. ## Building from source This is the technical part. The full notes are in [`docs/`](docs/). **Tools** | Windows | Linux | |---|---| | Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, LLVM (clang), CMake, Ninja, Python 3, Git Bash | clang or GCC, CMake, Ninja, Python 3, SDL2, Vulkan and FFmpeg development files, vkd3d ([details](docs/76-native-linux.md#building)) | On Windows, step 4 downloads FFmpeg's MPEG-2 video decoder for the game's movies (about 1 MB) and puts it beside `des_boot.exe`. If that download fails, the build says so and goes on, and the movies then need Microsoft's free [MPEG-2 Video Extension](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9n95q1zzpmh4) from the Microsoft Store; without either, they play their sound with no picture. (A paid app called "MPEG-2 Video Extensions", from another publisher, is a different thing; you don't need it.) **From your copy of the game** - The game disc's files (`PS3_GAME`) - RPCS3, to decrypt the game's `EBOOT.BIN` - Optional: `libsre.prx` from your PS3 firmware, decrypted. The game doesn't need it; it is only for the `LIBSRE_OWN=0` fallback ([docs/88](docs/88-setup-screens.md)). **Steps** 1. Get this repository, and its runtime inside it: ```sh git clone https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt.git cd Soulbrandt git clone https://github.com/JonathanDC64/ps3recomp.git ``` `ps3recomp.pin` names the ps3recomp commit this version of the port needs. `python tools/release/pin_ps3recomp.py local` checks your checkout against it. 2. In RPCS3, decrypt `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` (*Utilities > Decrypt PS3 Binaries*) to `work/game/EBOOT.ELF`. Copy `PS3_GAME/ICON0.PNG` next to it, for the program's icon. 3. Convert the game's main code: ```sh python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_loader.py work/game/EBOOT.ELF -o work/loader python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_lifter.py work/game/EBOOT.ELF \ --functions work/loader/EBOOT.functions.json --hle-stubs work/loader/EBOOT.imports.json \ --override-funcs "0x167AC88=ds_malloc,0x167AC58=ds_free,0x273D38=des_move_post,0x724E40=des_menu_tick" \ --insn-hooks @port/insn_hooks.txt --shadow-stack --chunk-lines 150000 --output work/recomp -j 16 python ps3recomp/tools/gen_hle_nids.py --all --out work/recomp/hle_nid_table.cpp python scripts/apply_boot_patches.py work/recomp ``` Then the SPU code with `python scripts/build_spu.py --eboot work/game/EBOOT.ELF` ([docs/09](docs/09-spu-spurs.md)), which first cuts the SPU programs out of the EBOOT, and, if you have `libsre.prx`, libsre with `python scripts/build_libsre.py `. The lifter's flags above are also in `scripts/lift_ppu.json`, which setup reads; change both together. 4. Compile the runtime, then the game. On Windows: ```sh cmake -S ps3recomp -B ps3recomp/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \ -DPS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL=ON cmake -S port -B port/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl \ -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE= -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG= -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS_DEBUG= cmake --build ps3recomp/build --target ps3recomp_runtime rsx_shader_precompile cmake --build port/build --target des_boot --parallel 4 ``` `PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL=ON` builds the portable renderer: DirectX 12 through it, the default, and Vulkan beside it (Settings > Display > Renderer). Without it the game runs on the legacy renderer only. Its first configure downloads glslang and SPIRV-Tools at their pinned commits. On Linux, see [docs/76](docs/76-native-linux.md#building). 5. Copy `tools/des/local.env.example` to `tools/des/local.env`, set `PS3_VFS_ROOT` in it to the folder that holds `PS3_GAME`, and start the game with `tools/des/play.sh`. A direct start of `des_boot.exe` goes through setup instead, and keeps its saves in `port/build/gamedata`. Everything made from your copy of the game stays in `work/` and `gamedata/`, which git

Low-CPU update: fewer threads on weaker PCs, support for CPUs without AVX2

- SPURS: on PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the lanes/kernels spin less, wake the
  main thread sooner and run on fewer threads (4-thread PCs: ~10 fps -> ~29 fps,
  8 threads: ~38 -> ~50 fps). Big PCs keep the old behaviour.
- Vertex workers spin far less after each job, fewer workers on small CPUs.
- The once-per-second thread scan only walks the game's own threads.
- No exclusive core reservations on PCs with fewer than 20 CPU threads;
  P-core pinning only on hybrid CPUs with at least 8 P-core threads.
- CPUs without AVX2/FMA/BMI2 (pre-2013 Intel, AVX-less Pentium/Celeron, AMD before
  2015): Setup/the updater detect this and build an SSE4.1 compatibility version
  automatically (same results, slower). The game also checks the CPU at startup and
  shows a clear message instead of crashing.

1451958063.readme_excerpt:
# inFamous PC

> **Official repo: [github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn).**
> Only download the Setup from the [Releases page](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn/releases) here.
> Forks are not supported, and bugs from forks won't be fixed.

An unofficial native Windows port of **inFamous** (PlayStation 3, 2009, European
release `BCES00220`). The game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code is statically
recompiled to x86-64 C/C++ with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp),
so it runs as a normal Windows program rather than under an emulator.

**This repository contains no game code or data.** You build the game yourself,
on your own PC, from your own copy of the game.

## Easy install

Download **inFamous Setup.exe** from the latest release, run it, choose your
`.iso` (an encrypted image works with its `.dkey` next to it) or your game
folder (the one with `PS3_GAME` in it), pick an install location and press
**Install**.

Setup checks for Python and the C++ build tools and offers to install them,
copies the game out of the disc image, regenerates the recompiled code from your
copy, builds it and adds an inFamous shortcut. Running Setup again on the same
folder updates or repairs the install and only redoes what changed.

## Updating

When a new version is published here, players update in place instead of reinstalling:
**Update now** in Setup (it finds the existing install), the **Update inFamous** shortcut in
the Start menu, or `Update inFamous.cmd` in the install folder. The updater compares every file
with this repository, downloads only what changed, regenerates the game code only if the
port's patches changed, and recompiles only the affected parts. Installs made with an older
Setup need one run of the new Setup on the same folder first.

## Requirements

- Your own inFamous disc dump, European release (`BCES00220`).
- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with Direct3D 12 support.
- A CPU with SSE4.1 (2008 or newer). On CPUs without AVX2 (Intel before 2013, Pentium/Celeron
  without AVX, AMD before 2015) Setup builds a slower compatibility version automatically.
  On PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the game uses fewer threads and less CPU (tested down to 4 threads).
- [Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) with "Add python.exe to
  PATH" ticked.
- [Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/)
  with the **Desktop development with C++** workload and the **C++ Clang
  Compiler for Windows** component.
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), only if your `PS3_GAME\USRDIR` has `EBOOT.BIN`
  but no decrypted `EBOOT.elf`. Setup uses it to decrypt the executable.
- About 10 GB of free disk space and 16 GB of RAM.

## Building manually

```bat
cd installer
cargo build --release
target\release\infamous-installer --game "D:\Dumps\inFamous"
```

`infamous-installer doctor` checks the requirements only. Finished steps are
skipped when you run it again, so an interrupted install continues where it
stopped. See [installer/README.md](installer/README.md) for every step and the
maintainer commands.

## Playing

Run **inFamous** (the shortcut Setup made). It opens a small options window first
(vsync, frame cap, resolution, language and more, saved to `settings.ini`);
**Play** starts the game. The same settings are in the game's pause menu under
**Settings**. Controllers work as on the console, and keyboard and mouse are supported.

**F10** opens the in-game trainer: God Mode, Infinite Energy, Refill Health,
Max Health x2/x5/x10, Add XP, Karma +/-, Kill Enemies / Civilians, Super Speed
and Player Model (play as Zeke, Trish, Kessler, Alden or John). Set `TRAINER=0`
to turn it off.

## DLSS and FSR (optional)

The game can use NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA or AMD FSR for upscaling, and AMD FSR frame generation.
They are not included in the download because NVIDIA and AMD distribute their SDKs themselves,
but both are free and take a few minutes to add.

- **DLSS** needs an NVIDIA RTX graphics card.
- **FSR** works on any modern GPU (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel). FSR 4 needs a Radeon RX 9000 card;
  other cards get FSR 3.1 automatically.

**1. Download the SDK(s) you want.** You need the **source code**, not a Windows or Linux demo.
On the page, click the green **Code** button, then **Download ZIP**. If you go through the
Releases page instead, pick **Source code (zip)**, not the files with "demo" or "samples" in the name.

| For | Download | Rename the extracted folder to |
|---|---|---|
| DLSS / DLAA | [github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS) | `dlss-sdk` |
| FSR and frame generation | [github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK) | `fsr-sdk` |

**2. Put the folder(s) in your inFamous install folder**, next to `infamous-recomp` and
`ps3recomp`:

```
inFamous\
  dlss-sdk\        <- contains include\ and lib\
  fsr-sdk\         <- contains Kits\
  infamous-recomp\
  ps3recomp\
  ...
```

Make sure you don't end up with a folder inside a folder (`dlss-sdk\DLSS-main\include`).
`include` (DLSS) or `Kits` (FSR) must be directly inside.

**3. Rebuild the game once.** Open a Command Prompt in the install folder and run:

```bat
type nul > .installer\update.pending
"Update inFamous.cmd"
```

This rebuilds the game with the SDK(s), which takes a while. Any later update also picks them up
automatically, so you only do this once.

**4. Turn it on in game:** pause, then **Settings**, then **Upscaling** (DLAA, DLSS Quality /
Balanced / Performance, FSR Native AA / Quality / Balanced / Performance) and **Frame
Generation**. The same options are in the launcher's options window. Upscaling and frame
generation apply after a restart.

If the **Upscaling** row is missing, the build didn't find the SDK: check the folder names and
layout from step 2, then repeat step 3.

## How it works

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `ps3recomp` | The recompiler toolkit and runtime: PPU and SPU lifters, HLE system libraries, RSX on Direct3D 12, audio and input |
| `infamous-recomp` | The inFamous-specific parts: program entry, game stubs and fixes, asset tools |
| `installer` | Setup and the command-line installer: reads the disc, regenerates the code from your game, applies `installer/patches`, builds |
| `installer/infamous.toml` | Everything about the game and the port: pipeline steps, generated files, build and launch settings |
| `installer/generated.lock` | Hashes of each generated file before and after the port's patches |

## Credits

- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet and
  contributors (see [ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md](ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md)).
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), used to decrypt the game executable.
- Sucker Punch Productions, for the game.
- [Lorenzo Aiello](https://github.com/aiellolorenzo23) and [ibrahimpuri](https://github.com/ibrahimpuri), for their support.

1452045567.readme_excerpt: # God of War: Ascension (PS3) Native PC Port An x86-64 static recompilation port of God of War: Ascension for Windows. The project translates the original PlayStation 3 binary and embedded SPU workloads into native C and C++ using the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) toolchain. ## How it works Traditional emulators interpret or JIT-compile machine code at runtime. This port uses static recompilation, converting the game ahead of time so it compiles into a normal 64-bit Windows executable: The game binary (`EBOOT.ELF`) is split and translated into eight C++ translation units (`src/gen/ppu_recomp_*.cpp`). Syscalls and OS library calls resolve through high-level emulation (HLE) shims in `src/compat/`. Embedded SPU binaries, including Sony's WWS Job System Policy Module and Edge Geometry code, are lifted into C and execute across host worker threads. The RSX (NV4097) graphics pipeline renders through a Direct3D 12 backend. It reads command packets directly from the GCM ring buffer, handles descriptor binding and pipeline states, and presents through a standard DXGI swapchain. Game data streams through an asynchronous Virtual File System (VFS) mapped to local disk instead of the PS3 Blu-ray drive. The Win32 window message loop runs on its own thread, isolated from the 60 Hz RSX presentation ticker so the window stays responsive even during long file loads. Controller input maps through XInput with keyboard fallbacks. ## Status [View detailed tables and classification methodology](docs/status.md) Firmware coverage measures imported PS3 OS functions against working high-level emulation handlers and offline-safe stubs. Hardware metrics are parsed directly from live runtime execution logs. Speed remains at 0% (not reached) until in-game level gameplay begins. Regenerate the dashboard and status documents with: ```bash python tools/gen_status.py ``` ## Current status | Component | Status | Details | |---|---|---| | PPU code lifting | Working | 19,570 functions across 8 translation units; 17 concurrent guest threads | | SPU / SPURS workloads | Working | 5 lifted SPU images; WWS job policy module running with zero interpreter fallbacks | | VFS streaming | Working | Asynchronous disk streaming reaches ~23 MB/s across 22 archive descriptors | | RSX presentation | Working | Direct3D 12 swapchain presents live-draw frames with active FIFO command processing | | RSX FIFO processing | Working | GCM offset tables mapped, JUMP/CALL validation in place | | FIOS synchronization | Working | Real Win32 event wait queues with FIFO condition variable ordering | | Audio engine | Partial | CellAudio initialized with WASAPI output backend and stubs | | In-game gameplay | Not reached | Boot progression advances through intro loops and title presentation | Technical notes and bring-up logs live in [docs/](file:///C:/IfItWorksItWorks/Project/gowassension/docs/) and [.planning/](file:///C:/IfItWorksItWorks/Project/gowassension/.planning/). ## Requirements - Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) - Visual Studio 2022 (MSVC v143 or `clang-cl`) with C++20 support - CMake 3.24 or newer - Ninja - Python 3.10 or newer - A legally dumped copy of God of War: Ascension (PS3) ## Building from source ### 1. Clone with submodules ```bash git clone --recursive https://github.com/YJuDeAd/gow-ascension-pc-port cd gowassension ``` If you cloned without `--recursive`, initialize them now: ```bash git submodule update --init --recursive ``` ### 2. Add your game files Copy your decrypted game files into the `vfs` folder: ```text vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.ELF vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN vfs/PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO ``` Game assets and executables are not included in this repository. ### 3. Apply upstream runtime patches Apply the required compatibility fixes to the local `ps3recomp` tree: ```powershell git -C ps3recomp apply ../patches/ps3recomp_current.patch ``` ### 4. Compile Build the `ps3recomp` runtime library first, then build the main executable: ```powershell # Build ps3recomp runtime cmake -S ps3recomp -B ps3recomp/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build ps3recomp/build # Build the game executable cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build ``` The output binary is written to `build/gow_ascension.exe`. ## Running Launch the port with the PowerShell runner: ```powershell # Run with Direct3D 12 graphics enabled .\tools\run_port.ps1 -LiveDraw # Interactive mode (no automatic timeout) .\tools\run_port.ps1 -Interactive # Custom resolution .\tools\run_port.ps1 -LiveDraw -Width 1920 -Height 1080 -TimeoutSeconds 30 ``` Default settings can also be edited in `config.toml`: ```toml [video] width = 1280 height = 720 vsync = "on" live_draw = true [input] auto_pad_start = false deadzone = 7849 ``` ## Repository layout ```text gowassension/ ├── .planning/ Roadmaps, phase specs, and verification records ├── analysis/ Function maps, symbol tables, and SPU/PPU triage data ├── docs/ Architecture notes and bring-up progress logs ├── patches/ Patches for the upstream ps3recomp runtime ├── ps3recomp/ Upstream runtime and lifter tools (submodule) ├── src/ │ ├── main.cpp Window setup, thread orchestration, main loop │ ├── boot_main.cpp Alternative boot harness │ ├── hle_extra.cpp Additional HLE handlers │ ├── compat/ Game-specific HLE overrides (GCM, FIOS, SPURS, sync) │ └── gen/ Machine-generated PPU and SPU code ├── tools/ Automation scripts for lifting, testing, and triage ├── twistedmetal/ Reference PS3 port implementation (submodule) ├── vfs/ Virtual file system root for game data └── CMakeLists.txt Root build configuration ``` ## Contributing Pull requests and issues are welcome. A few rules keep the codebase maintainable: - Keep `ps3recomp/` and `twistedmetal/` as read-only upstream references. All game-specific overrides, patches, and shims belong in `src/compat/` or `patches/`. - Never hand-edit files in `src/gen/`. Those are generated by the lifters. If a lifted function needs different behavior, change the lifter script or override the symbol in `src/compat/`. - Automation scripts in `tools/` should be cross-platform Python (`.py`) or PowerShell (`.ps1`). - Compile generated code in Release mode (`-O2` / `/O2`) without full debug PDBs to avoid consuming tens of gigabytes of disk space. ### Where to help right now - Implementing real Win32 condition variables in `src/compat/ascension_hle.cpp` for `sys_lwcond`. The existing stub drops signals, leaving media worker threads stuck. - Translating NV4097 microcode into HLSL to draw the first 3D passes once scenes finish loading. - Optimizing SPU-assisted skinning and vertex buffer decompression in Edge Geometry. - Building a real audio output backend for CellAudio callbacks. ## Acknowledgments Portions of runtime research and compatibility patches are adapted from [gow-ascension-pc](https://github.com/arnaldo-lima/gow-ascension-pc) by Arnaldo Lima & contributors under the MIT License (see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](file:///C:/IfItWorksItWorks/Project/gowassension/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)). ## Legal This is an independent preservation and research project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Santa Monica Studio. This repository does not contain any copyrighted game assets, proprietary Sony code, encryption keys, or disc images. You must provide your own legally obtained copy of the game.

1452109945.readme_excerpt:
# inFAMOUS 2 Recomp

Experimental Windows port of the PlayStation 3 BCUS98125 release, built with a pinned [PS3Recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) revision and a local patch series.

**Status (November 2026): not playable.** Local native runs have reached the campaign dock sequence and produced partial 3D backbuffer images. Controllable character movement, correct rendering, reliable audio, and acceptable performance have not been established. See [observed status](docs/public-status.md) for the evidence and its limits.

The original maintainer has stepped away from active development and published this snapshot so others can continue the work. The technical handoff records the current state, reproducible checks, open questions, and next investigation. There is no planned release date or promise of ongoing maintainer support.

This is an independent research project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Sucker Punch Productions.

## Continue the work

Start with the [technical handoff](docs/MASTER-HANDOFF-AND-REPLICATION-GUIDE.md), then read [getting started](docs/getting-started.md), [the patch stack](docs/patches.md), and [regression testing](docs/regression-testing.md). The handoff identifies the current unknowns and the next bounded investigation.

The repository includes handwritten integration code, build and diagnostic scripts, synthetic tests, and ordered patches for PS3Recomp. The pinned third-party SDK is fetched separately. The game executable, generated translations of game code, assets, firmware, keys, saves, dumps, and a runnable game binary are not distributed.

## Test without the game

On Windows with Python, CMake, Ninja, clang-cl, and the Windows SDK:

```powershell
./scripts/setup.ps1 -CheckOnly
./scripts/setup.ps1
./scripts/build.ps1 -Target tests
./scripts/test.ps1 -Regression -IncludeGpu
```

The WARP fixtures require a suitable graphics environment. Record pass, failure, and skip counts; a skipped fixture is not a pass. The full port also requires the contributor's own legitimately obtained local game files and generated code. See [building](docs/building.md).

## Publication and licensing

Before sharing changes, run the [publication checks](CONTRIBUTING.md). Keep proprietary material and personal paths out of commits and history. Patch files contain context from the MIT-licensed PS3Recomp project; preserve its notices and the other exceptions in [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Original contributions are licensed under [GPL-3.0-only](LICENSE), subject to the documented third-party terms.

No repository check can guarantee that a rights holder will not file a complaint. Share only material you have the right to publish.
