1453020357.readme_excerpt:
# Civilization Revolution: PC port

Play **Sid Meier's Civilization Revolution** (PS3, 2008) on Windows as a normal PC
program, made **from your own copy of the game**. It is not an emulator: the
game's PS3 program is translated into PC code, on your computer, during setup.

> ### ⚠️ Please read first: this download does NOT contain the game
> - The download (and this whole repository) contains **no game code, no graphics,
>   no sounds, no music, no videos and no keys**. It is about 40 KB of scripts and
>   this project's own source code.
> - **You need your own copy** of the PS3 game: the **European disc, BLES00238**.
>   Other versions (for example the North American BLUS30130) do not work.
> - Everything that comes from the game is made **on your PC, from your copy**, while
>   Setup runs. Nothing from the game is ever downloaded from here.
> - This is a fan project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Firaxis Games,
>   2K, Take-Two Interactive or Sony.

## What works today
- **The whole game, start to finish:** full matches play without problems,
  including long ones.
- **High frame rate:** on the developer's PC (AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D, NVIDIA
  GeForce RTX 4060 Ti) the game usually runs **well above 60 FPS, typically
  70 to 180 FPS**.
- **Saving:** the game's own menus to **save, load and delete** games work.
  Saves are kept in a folder you can back up.
- **Playtime counter:** the game window's title bar shows your **total
  playtime** and the time of the **current session**.
- **Controllers:** Xbox-compatible controllers work directly; PlayStation
  controllers work through a tool that makes them look like an Xbox controller
  (for example DS4Windows, or Steam).
- **Videos, music and sound** from your disc, controller vibration (can be
  switched off), fullscreen (Alt+Enter).

---

## Contact
Questions, problems or ideas? You can reach me in two ways:
- **GitHub:** open an [issue](https://github.com/CapTiveEel20/civrev-port/issues).
  This is the best place for bug reports: attach `setup.log` (Setup problems) or
  `civrev-port\run.err.log` (game problems).
- **Discord:** my username is **captiveeel20**. Send me a friend request or a
  message.

Please don't send or ask for game files, `EBOOT` files or ISOs: I can't share them.

---

## Contents
1. [How it works (in 30 seconds)](#how-it-works-in-30-seconds)
2. [What you need](#what-you-need)
3. [Step 1: prepare your game files](#step-1-prepare-your-game-files)
4. [Step 2: install](#step-2-install)
5. [Playing](#playing)
6. [Known problems](#known-problems)
7. [Help and common questions](#help-and-common-questions)
8. [Uninstalling](#uninstalling)
9. [For developers](#for-developers)
10. [Legal and credits](#legal-and-credits)

---

## How it works (in 30 seconds)
1. You download a small zip (about 40 KB) from [Releases](https://github.com/CapTiveEel20/civrev-port/releases).
2. You run **Setup.bat** and give it two files from **your** game: the disc (`.iso`)
   and the decrypted game program (`EBOOT.elf`).
3. Setup copies your disc, translates the game program into PC code and builds
   the game. **About 10 minutes on a fast PC**, longer on slower ones (plus
   10 to 30 minutes the first time, if it has to install the free build tools).
4. You play from the desktop shortcut.

---

## What you need

| What | Details |
|---|---|
| **Your game** | Sid Meier's Civilization Revolution for PS3, **European disc BLES00238**, as a decrypted `.iso` file or as the disc folder (see Step 1). |
| **The decrypted game program** | `EBOOT.elf`, made from your disc with the free RPCS3 emulator (see Step 1). Only the disc's own program, not one from a game update. |
| **Windows** | Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit (tested on Windows 11). |
| **Graphics card** | One that supports DirectX 12. |
| **Processor** | Any 64-bit processor with SSE4.1 (practically every PC processor since about 2011). |
| **Disk space** | About **10 GB** free where you put the game, plus about **8 GB on C:** if Setup has to install the build tools. |
| **Internet** | Only during Setup. |
| **Build tools** | Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools (Microsoft's free C++ compiler) and Python. **You don't need to install them yourself:** if they are missing, Setup offers to install them for you. |
| **Controller** | An Xbox-compatible controller, or a PlayStation controller through DS4Windows or Steam. |

---

## Step 1: prepare your game files

You need two things from **your own** game disc.

### 1a. Your disc as an `.iso` or a folder
- **Either** a decrypted `.iso` file of your disc: if you double-click it,
  Windows opens it and you see a `PS3_GAME` folder,
- **or** the disc folder: the folder that contains `PS3_GAME` and `PS3_DISC.SFB`
  (the "folder" format RPCS3 uses).

To make one from your disc, see RPCS3's guide: <https://rpcs3.net/quickstart>.

### 1b. The decrypted game program (`EBOOT.elf`)
The game program on the disc (`EBOOT.BIN`) is encrypted. RPCS3, a free PS3
emulator, can decrypt it. You only need RPCS3 for this one step.

1. Download and install RPCS3: <https://rpcs3.net/download>. If RPCS3 asks you
   to install the PS3 firmware first, follow its instructions.
2. Copy `EBOOT.BIN` from your disc to an ordinary folder, for example your
   Desktop. It is inside `PS3_GAME\USRDIR\` (with an `.iso`, double-click it
   first to open it).
3. In RPCS3: **Utilities → Decrypt PS3 Binaries**, then choose that `EBOOT.BIN`.
4. RPCS3 writes **`EBOOT.elf`** next to it. That's the file Setup needs.

Setup checks this file. It tells you if it is still encrypted or from a different
version of the game.

---

## Step 2: install
1. Go to [Releases](https://github.com/CapTiveEel20/civrev-port/releases) and
   download **`CivRevPC-<version>.zip`** (for example `CivRevPC-1.1.zip`,
   under "Assets").
2. Right-click the zip → **Extract All…** and choose a folder with enough free
   space, for example `C:\Games`. Don't run anything from inside the zip.
3. Open the extracted `CivRevPC` folder and double-click **`Setup.bat`**.
   If Windows warns you about a downloaded file, choose **Run**
   (or **More info → Run anyway**).
4. Answer Setup's questions:
   - **"Install them now?"**: shown only if the build tools are missing.
     Answer **Y**. Windows asks once *"Do you want to allow this app to make
     changes to your device?"*: answer **Yes**. An installer window shows its
     progress.
   - **Your disc**: choose your `.iso`. To use a disc folder instead, press
     **Cancel** and then choose the folder.
   - **Your `EBOOT.elf`**: choose the file from Step 1b.
5. **Wait.** Setup shows one progress line per step, for example
   `Compiling: 120 of 450 files (26%)`. Leave the window open until it says
   **DONE**. The steps are:
   1. Check tools
   2. Copy your game disc (about 5 GB)
   3. Check your EBOOT
   4. Tidy the multiplayer menu art
   5. Download and build the ps3recomp runtime
   6. Generate code from your EBOOT (a few minutes)
   7. Compile the game (the longest step: 5 to 30+ minutes depending on your processor)
   8. Build the launcher
6. At the end Setup asks two things:
   - **Create a desktop shortcut?** Yes is recommended.
   - **Delete the build leftovers (about 1.1 GB)?** The game works either way.
     Answer **No** if you want a later update to install faster.

**If something goes wrong**, Setup stops and says why in plain words. Fix the
problem and double-click `Setup.bat` again: finished steps are skipped.
Everything Setup did is written to `setup.log` in the same folder. That file
contains thousands of "warning" lines from the compiler: **those are normal
and harmless**.

### Updating from an older version (for example 1.0 → 1.1)
1. Download the new `CivRevPC-<version>.zip` and extract it **into the same
   place as before**, so its `CivRevPC` folder lands on top of your existing
   one. When Windows asks, choose **Replace the files in the destination**.
2. Double-click **`Setup.bat`** again. It notices the new version, downloads
   the new ps3recomp runtime and rebuilds the game. Your disc copy is kept, so
   it doesn't ask for your files again. Expect about as long as the
   "Compile the game" step took the first time.
3. **Your saves are kept** (`civrev-port\gamedata\` is not touched).

---

## Playing
Start the game with the **Civilization Revolution** desktop shortcut, or with
`civrev-port\CivRev.exe` in the game folder.

- Play with a **controller** (see [What works today](#what-works-today)).
- **Alt+Enter** switches fullscreen. **Esc** closes the game.
- **Your saves** are in `civrev-port\gamedata\`. Back this folder up and never delete it.
- **Settings** are in `civrev-port\CivRev.ini` (created on the first start; open it
  with Notepad). For example: `vibration=on` or `vibration=off` for controller vibration.
- **Turning controller vibration off (or back on):** vibration is on by default. The
  kit includes a step-by-step guide next to `Setup.bat`:
  *Controller vibration - how to turn it on or off.txt*.

---

## Known problems
Version 1.1 has so far been tested on one PC (the developer's).
- Some 3D models are not drawn perfectly yet.
- **See-through shallow water after loading a second save:** if you load a
  saved game, then go back to the menu and load another one without closing
  the game, shallow water can turn transparent. Close and restart the game
  before loading the other save.
- Short stutters can happen the first time some effects appear (the game
  prepares them on the fly; the PS3 did this too).
- **Online multiplayer does not work:** the game's online service was shut
  down in 2014.

Found a problem? Please open an [issue](https://github.com/CapTiveEel20/civrev-port/issues)
and attach `setup.log` (Setup problems) or `civrev-port\run.err.log` (game
problems). Note: these logs contain folder paths, which can include your
Windows user name.

---

## Help and common questions

**Why doesn't the download just include the game, ready to play?**
A ready-made program would contain the game's code, which belongs to its
publisher. This way the download contains nothing from the game, and the game's
code is only ever made on your PC, from your own copy.

**Setup says "This EBOOT is still encrypted".**
You chose `EBOOT.BIN`. Decrypt it with RPCS3 first (Step 1b) and choose the
`EBOOT.elf` it makes.

**Setup says the EBOOT is "a different version of the game".**
Use the `EBOOT.BIN` from the disc itself. The one RPCS3 keeps after installing
a game update (in its `dev_hdd0\game\` folder) is a different version.

**Setup says the disc is a different one (for example "BLUS30130").**
Only the European disc BLES00238 is supported.

**Setup says something is "Missing".**
It lists exactly what: build tools, free disk space, or 64-bit Windows. If you
said No to installing the tools, run `Setup.bat` again and answer Y, or install
them by hand as described in the message.

**The game crashed.**
The launcher shows a message. Please report it with `civrev-port\run.err.log`
(see [Known problems](#known-problems)).

**Can I share the game folder with a friend?**
No. After Setup, the folder contains your copy of the game and a program made
from the game's code. Point your friend to this page instead.

---

## Uninstalling
1. Copy `civrev-port\gamedata\` somewhere safe if you want to keep your saves.
2. Delete the `CivRevPC` folder and the desktop shortcut.
3. If Setup installed Visual Studio Build Tools or Python and you don't need
   them anymore, remove them in **Windows Settings → Apps**.

---

## For developers
<details>
<summary>Building without the kit, repository layout, making a kit</summary>

The game's PS3 program is statically recompiled with
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp): its PowerPC and SPU code
is translated to C++ and linked with a runtime that stands in for the PS3's
system (graphics → Direct3D 12, audio → WASAPI, controller → XInput).
The kit uses the fork [CapTiveEel20/ps3recomp](https://github.com/CapTiveEel20/ps3recomp)
at the commit in `setup/ps3recomp.lock`. The project layout follows
[sp00nznet/tornado](https://github.com/sp00nznet/tornado).

**Requirements:** Visual Studio 2022 with *C++ Clang Compiler for Windows* and
*C++ CMake tools for Windows*; a ps3recomp checkout with its Python `.venv` and
`build-release\ps3recomp_runtime.lib` (Release, clang-cl); your decrypted `EBOOT.elf`.

**Folder layout** (side by side, by default):
```
ps3recomp\          ps3recomp checkout
civrev-gamefiles\   your game files; keep them outside every repo
  EBOOT.elf           decrypted game program
  vfs\PS3_GAME\       the disc's PS3_GAME folder (the game's "/dev_bdvd")
civrev-port\        this repository
```
Other locations: `tools\relift.ps1 -PS3Recomp <path> -Elf <path>`, and
`-DPS3RECOMP_DIR=<path>` (or the `PS3RECOMP_DIR` environment variable) for CMake.

**Build and run:**
```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\relift.ps1   # generate code from your EBOOT.elf
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File build.ps1          # compile build\civrev.exe
```
`run.bat` starts `build\civrev.exe` with `PS3_VFS_ROOT=..\civrev-gamefiles\vfs`
and writes `run.log` / `run.err.log`.

**Making the player kit:** `tools\make_kit.ps1 -Version <n>` packs
`dist\CivRevPC-<n>.zip` from an allowlist of files (it refuses uncommitted
changes). Tests: `setup\tests\*.tests.ps1`.

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `CMakeLists.txt`, `build.ps1` | Build configuration (clang-cl + Ninja) |
| `run.bat` | Starts the game with the folder layout above |
| `setup/` | The player kit: `Setup.bat`, `setup.ps1`, `kitlib.ps1`, `README-PLAYERS.txt`, tests |
| `launcher/` | Source of `CivRev.exe`, the game launcher |
| `tools/relift.ps1` | Runs the ps3recomp pipeline on your EBOOT (loader, PPU lifter, HLE table, SPU lifter) |
| `tools/fix_import_stub_toc.py`, `tools/fix_inline_opd_funcs.py` | Fixes applied during code generation |
| `tools/patch_menu_assets.py` | Tidies one image in the multiplayer menu of your disc copy |
| `tools/make_kit.ps1` | Packs the player kit |
| `tools/import_coverage.py` | Checks the game's firmware imports against ps3recomp's handlers |
| `src/port/civrev_hle.cpp` | Civ Rev-specific overrides of PS3 system functions |
| `src/compat/` | POSIX header shims for Windows |

</details>

---

Frames keep going until a heap overflow: SPURS_READY_LEVEL, patch 0018

SPURS_READY_LEVEL=1 is now on by default: without it RsxSync's round-2 job
waited for a kick that never came and the render thread spun on frame slot
0x99AAC8. With it and the park hold, every run gets past frame 2 (21-28
frame reports in 60 s).

All runs now stop at frame ~12 in the same place: func_0037D548 copies
past the end of a block in the heap at 0x14FB8F68 and zeroes the next free
node's header, and the first-fit walk func_00397318 loops on it. STATUS
records how the guard caught it and what to look at next. Patch 0018 caps
[null-read] per reading function and adds the reader's registers, which is
what named the heap.

The loading screen waited on a particle job whose last task creates the
next phase from the SPU. Three SPURS taskset gaps on the fork kept that
from happening (tasks started twice, Taskset2 made as a 0x1900-byte
taskset without event flags, SPU-created tasks never started); with them
fixed the game shows its first-use save prompt, writes BCES01741-SYSDATA
and goes on to a black screen, which is next. STATUS has the chain and the
diagnostics that found it; gamedata/ (the emulated HDD) and the old lift
are ignored.

1453196731.readme_excerpt:
# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.pt-BR.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. > [!WARNING] > **Ainda experimental, mas já dá para zerar.** O [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor) jogou do começo ao fim no PC dele (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT). Em processadores comuns o jogo ainda é lento (~20 fps na luta contra o chefe num Ryzen 7 5700G), e ainda pode travar. Feito para Windows; no macOS (Apple Silicon) ele voltou a rodar, por enquanto só para testes. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Novembro de 2026, no Windows (e no Mac, em testes): - **O jogo inteiro, do boot ao fim:** o iSamigor zerou o jogo. Nos nossos testes: telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente; o renderizador Vulkan próprio do projeto, onde está o trabalho de desempenho; e o *live draw* (D3D12). - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas, melhorias e o **online** com a sua conta do site; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado no [site](https://gow-ascension.com.br/pt-br) a partir dos seus discos. Atualizado em 10 de novembro. As mudanças de novembro estão no branch [`ascension-perf`](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/tree/ascension-perf) até serem medidas no Windows. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.pt-BR.md](docs/MILESTONES.pt-BR.md) (em inglês: [MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md)). ### Desempenho O objetivo é rodar bem em processadores comuns, não só nos fortes. Desde 6 de novembro o caminho é **sair do modelo do PS3**: em vez de emular cada vez melhor as SPUs e o RSX, o trabalho deles vira código nativo do PC e da placa de vídeo, com a meta de não sobrar nenhuma emulação de SPU. > [!NOTE] > **Um erro de medida corrigido (9 de novembro):** o contador de fps do nosso renderizador Vulkan contava cada quadro duas vezes (o mesmo quadro era apresentado de novo ~1 ms depois, sem nada desenhado). Os números desse renderizador publicados antes valem a metade. Os de baixo já são quadros reais. A luta contra o chefe logo depois da cinemática de abertura, a cena mais pesada que medimos, num Ryzen 7 5700G (Windows, renderizador Vulkan do projeto, mediana de várias janelas de 5 s): | Quando | fps na luta | Thread de vídeo, por draw | | --- | --- | --- | | 9 de novembro, à noite | ~15-17 | ~17,5 µs | | 10 de novembro, de manhã | ~18 | ~16,0 µs | | 10 de novembro, à tarde | **~20** | **~15,0 µs** | **O que entrou de 6 a 10 de novembro** (cada parte medida e com a imagem conferida antes de virar padrão): - **Renderizador Vulkan próprio** (no ps3kit), onde está o trabalho de desempenho: o anti-aliasing que o jogo fazia nas SPUs (o MLAA delas não roda mais) agora é feito na placa de vídeo (SMAA, FXAA ou MLAA), filtro anisotrópico, vértices convertidos em lotes e um contador de fps compacto nas cores do jogo. - **60 fps:** o limite de 30 do jogo destravado, com o jogo andando na velocidade certa, e um limite de 60. Os carregamentos, que tinham ficado lentos com o destrave, voltaram a ~4,5 s. - **SPUs em código nativo:** três módulos de geometria do EDGE (218, 202 e 210) rodam inteiros como código nativo, cada um conferido contra o original em centenas de jobs gravados do próprio jogo (resultado idêntico). - **Thread de vídeo mais leve:** cópias 2D divididas entre 3 threads (4 → 1,7 ms por quadro); constantes dos shaders copiadas só quando mudam; os comandos de vídeo comuns despachados em bloco (-1,5 µs por draw); e as texturas: o jogo move ~150 texturas por segundo dentro da memória de vídeo, e agora uma textura movida fica com a imagem que já estava na placa em vez de ser decodificada e enviada de novo (texturas de 1,56 para 1,00 µs por draw). - **macOS:** voltou a compilar e a abrir o jogo (Vulkan sobre MoltenVK), ~24 fps no primeiro nível num Mac com Apple Silicon; ainda trava em parte das aberturas. **Para onde vai o quadro agora:** na luta, quem segura o quadro é o thread que executa os comandos de vídeo, e o maior custo dele é copiar os vértices que os jobs do EDGE acabaram de escrever (~5 dos ~15 µs de cada draw, perto de 50 MB por quadro). **Próximos passos:** levar essa geometria para a placa de vídeo (as posições calculadas na GPU, sem a cópia no processador), que deve ser o primeiro salto grande (estimativa de ~28-32 fps, ainda a medir); depois o resto do EDGE na GPU e os outros módulos das SPUs em código nativo. ### Estabilidade - **Corrigido:** num PC lento, o thread de vídeo desistia de uma espera depois de 2 s e perdia os comandos do quadro; o jogo ficava parado no carregamento do nível. - **Corrigido:** o travamento no nível com as listas de geometria esperando para sempre (uma escrita do processador principal se perdia no meio de uma operação atômica de uma SPU: de 3 travamentos em 5 rodadas para nenhum em 4). - **Corrigido:** o travamento com `CopyLocalMemory offset error` (um contador do Edge Zlib e a troca da tabela de streaming de texturas sem proteção): nenhum em 40 rodadas no nível. - **Protegido:** comandos de vídeo corrompidos (`FIFO error: possible desync`) não derrubam mais o thread do RSX, e um draw pedindo uma quantidade absurda de vértices é descartado em vez de travar o jogo. A causa da corrupção ainda está aberta. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); o jogo às vezes trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`); e houve um crash silencioso ~70-105 s depois de entrar no nível em duas rodadas. ### Multijogador online (em desenvolvimento) Os servidores originais do jogo ainda funcionam para quem joga no PS3, mas o jogo recompilado não entra na PSN. Por isso o projeto tem o próprio servidor (em Rust, ainda privado), no ar em [gow-ascension.com.br](https://gow-ascension.com.br) com o cadastro fechado por enquanto; o runtime manda para ele os nomes que o jogo procura. O servidor nunca se passa pela Sony: ele responde só o que o jogo espera, lido no código traduzido ou nas capturas do próprio jogo falando com ele. A partida usa o netcode do próprio jogo (uma malha P2P por UDP); como dois jogadores em casa quase nunca se alcançam direto (cada um atrás do seu roteador), os pacotes passam por um relay do servidor, e o jogo nem percebe. | Passo | Estado | | --- | --- | | Entrar online, Online Pass | ok | | Configuração do online (o jogo lê a nossa) | ok | | Termos de uso, perfil do multijogador guardado na conta | ok | | Tutorial pulado, lobby do guerreiro | ok | | Partida rápida: localização do jogador | ok | | Partida rápida: escolha do servidor de matchmaking | ok | | Conexão com o matchmaking (sessão SSL 3.0) | ok | | Dois jogadores casados numa partida, um deles host | ok (dois jogos no mesmo PC) | | A rede da partida pelo relay do servidor | ok (dois jogos no mesmo PC) | | Launcher: entrar na conta e jogar online | ok | | Partida entre dois PCs pela internet | **em andamento** | | A partida inteira, do lobby ao fim | falta | ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph PC["PC do jogador"] L["Launcher
conta e online"] G["Jogo recompilado
(runtime ps3kit)"] L -- "endereço, configuração e perfil" --> G end subgraph SRV["Servidor do projeto (Rust)"] API["Contas e API"] CFG["Configuração do online"] TUS["Perfil do multijogador
por conta"] GEO["Localização"] SAM["Matchmaking
(SSL 3.0)"] REL["Signaling e relay
(UDP)"] DB[("PostgreSQL")] TUS --> DB API --> DB end WEB["Site do projeto
perfil, ranking, painel"] G2["Jogo de outro jogador"] L -- "login por código" --> API L -- "configuração, perfil" --> CFG L -- "perfil" --> TUS G -- "TCP" --> GEO G -- "TCP + SSL" --> SAM G <-- "partida (UDP)" --> REL REL <-- "partida (UDP)" --> G2 WEB -- "HTTP" --> API ``` No ar no servidor e no site: as contas, o perfil do multijogador guardado por conta, o perfil público com nível e conquistas, o ranking (vazio até haver partidas), um painel administrativo e o login do launcher por código. Planejado: os troféus do jogo assinados e conferidos pelo servidor. **"Jogar offline" vai continuar sempre funcionando**: a campanha nunca vai pedir conta. ## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), instale o launcher pelo `AscensionLauncher__x64-setup.exe` das [releases](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/releases) e, na primeira vez, aponte a pasta `ascension` em **Avançado › Pasta do jogo**. Ele se atualiza sozinho quando sai uma versão nova.

JOGAR abre o jogo; o launcher se esconde até ele fechar. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Melhorias:** liga e desliga. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Abrir a pasta de melhorias** é onde entram as outras, como o **português do Brasil**, que a [página do site](https://gow-ascension.com.br/pt-br) monta no seu navegador a partir das imagens dos seus discos (nada é enviado). As melhorias incluídas são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo. - **Online:** entra na sua conta do site por um código (como numa TV) e liga o online; os troféus do jogo ficam na mesma aba.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

cellPad (in the toolkit patch), from the Resistance 2 toolkit:

main.cpp: the light bar defaults to an electric blue, 1e78ff
(setenv(..., 0): the environment and the launcher win).

Toolkit: DualSense adaptive triggers, on the trigger that fires bolts

cellPad (in the toolkit patch), from the inFAMOUS 2 toolkit's version: the
DS5 trigger effect blocks through SDL_GameControllerSendEffect (47-byte
state, enable bits 0x04|0x08, right block at 10, left at 21), sent only on

of the map in the game's menu moves the feel on the next poll.
PS3_PAD_ADAPTIVE=0 turns it off.

42f0e5c598368f2f44a424206d37fa43bf87413f.message:
Supersampling: clamp the Lanczos edge; bilinear if it gives up

- MPSImageLanczosScale's default edge mode (zero) reads black past the
  picture's edge, so the outer row and column came out darker: a solid
  white 192x108 -> 64x36 gave 224 at the border. edgeMode =
  MPSImageEdgeModeClamp: 255 everywhere.
- When the reduction gives up mid-run, the larger picture left to the
  present pass is sampled bilinear (before: point, as only the upscale
  option set it).
- test_metal_downscale: the solid white frame must stay >= 254 at every
  pixel, edges included (fails with 224 before the fix); the checkerboard
  still gives 127..127.

Found by the Resistance port's audit of this code.

49277bef35d355ee572ab6d7e70b414a6a7c48d2.message:
Toolkit: lean SPU lifts and parallel shader builds, from the inFAMOUS 2 port

- SPU lifter (spu_context.h, spu_helpers.h, spu_lifter.py): lean shufb and
  local-store access, bit-exact. test_spu_shufb_lean (20M vectors) and
  test_spu_ls_lean (11M loads, 11M stores) pass with 0 mismatches and fail
  with their planted bugs. SPU_LIFT_LEAN_SHUFB=0 / SPU_LIFT_LEAN_LS=0 keep
  the old form. rebuild.py relifts by itself (its spu, jobs and firmware
  keys include the patch); the PPU lift is unchanged.
- rsx_metal_backend.m (+ ps3_ftrace.h, ps3_toggles.h): a frame's pipeline
  misses build on a worker pool and every encode waits for the pipelines it
  uses, so no draw is skipped (PS3_SHADER_PARALLEL=0 inline). The MSL
  translator is untouched, so shader caches stay valid.

Checked with rebuild.py from the player's copy into a clean folder: every
step passed, recompiled/ and lle/ came out the same, spu/ and lle_spu/
relifted. Headless with the scripted pad it plays the intro; side by side
with the build before it (same load) both reached the same scenes at the
same moments, ~equal fps per phase, no abort; 175 pipelines built on 3
workers, 0 draws dropped.

rsx_metal_backend.m: when PS3_RES_SCALE makes the display buffer larger
than the window's backing pixels (fitted to its aspect), the drawable takes
the window's size and each frame is reduced into it with
MPSImageLanczosScale (into a private ShaderWrite texture, then the present

new is linked; a failure says why once and falls back to the old path.

creates (shadows and reflections included), viewports and scissors with
them.

1453368252.readme_excerpt:
# inFAMOUS 1 — static recompilation for PC (macOS) 🌐 **English** · [Português (BR)](README.pt-BR.md) A native port of **inFAMOUS** (PS3, digital release `NPUA80480`) to **macOS/arm64**, built with static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C/C++ and compiled into a native executable, with graphics on Metal. It is not an emulator. **It boots, plays the studio logos and videos, reaches the 3D title screen, and gets through the opening explosion to Cole in the tutorial** ("Use the right stick to look up at the chopper"), at ~44 fps on Apple silicon in headless runs. It is built from your own copy ([how](#building-from-source)). | | | | --- | --- | | [](docs/screenshots/01-boot-sucker-punch-logo.jpg)
Boot: the studio logo | [](docs/screenshots/02-title-screen.jpg)
3D title screen | | [](docs/screenshots/03-intro-cutscene.jpg)
The blast (in-engine cutscene) | [](docs/screenshots/04-cole-after-the-blast.jpg)
Cole after the blast | | [](docs/screenshots/05-crater.jpg)
The crater | [](docs/screenshots/06-tutorial.jpg)
Gameplay: the first tutorial | Frames from the port itself running on an Apple-silicon Mac (M4 Pro), built from the player's own copy, at the game's 1280×720, captured headless with `tools/capture.sh`. inFAMOUS © Sony Interactive Entertainment, developed by Sucker Punch Productions; shown only to document the port. > [!WARNING] > **Early alpha.** The game runs from boot to the prologue tutorial, only on > Apple silicon macOS. The full campaign and long sessions have not been > validated. What is missing is in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). > **This repository contains no game data, no firmware, no Sony keys and > nothing translated from them.** Everyone generates all of that locally from > their own legitimate copy. A fan project, not affiliated with Sony > Interactive Entertainment or Sucker Punch Productions. Built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) and, above all, on [NoahBPeterson](https://github.com/NoahBPeterson/ps3recomp)'s **inFAMOUS 1 fork**, which brought the firmware LLE and the fixes that got the game running on the Mac; the launcher and the shared runtime come from the [inFAMOUS 2 port](https://github.com/erikomis/infamous2-recomp). See [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md). ## Status | | | | --- | --- | | Boot, firmware LLE, SPURS, SPU job modules | ✅ | | Studio logos, Bink videos, loading screens | ✅ | | 3D title screen ("Press the Start Button") | ✅ | | New game → opening explosion → Cole in the tutorial | ✅ | | Performance | ✅ ~44 fps in the menu and cutscenes, headless, on Apple silicon (the console aimed at 30). Gameplay fps still to measure with `tools/profile_run.sh` | | Anisotropic filtering up to 16× | ✅ checked on this game | | Internal resolution, MetalFX, FXAA/SMAA, sharpening, colour | 🧪 through the shared runtime and the launcher, options mapped; no visual A/B per combination yet | | Controller, keyboard and mouse, rumble | 🧪 adapted in the launcher, bindings tested; not every device combination | | DualSense adaptive triggers, light bar, player lights, gyro aim | 🧪 unit-tested; not tried on a controller yet (quit Steam first) | | In-game menu (F1 / Cmd+, / L3+R3) | 🧪 shared runtime, not checked on this game yet | | Saves and trophies, saves manager in the app | ✅ local saves `BCUS98119_INFAMOUS_*` recognised, saves from inFAMOUS 2 rejected | | The app: play, settings, controls, saves, logs | ✅ macOS bundle built, 72 tests pass, window starts the game | | Rebuild from your copy in one command (`rebuild.py`) | ✅ checked from a clean install: lifts identical to the tested build, boots to the tutorial | | The app: install / rebuild wizard | 🧪 turned on again, on top of the ported `rebuild.py`; not clicked through in the app yet | | The app updates itself | ⏳ disabled in this distribution | | GPU lighting and SSAO (the inFAMOUS 2 speed-up) | ⏳ needs this game's own work, see the roadmap | | Ultrawide with fixed camera and HUD | ⏳ pending, option hidden | | Whole game | ❓ not played past the tutorial yet | | Linux and Windows | ⏳ planned | Details and next steps in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). The list of features brought over from the inFAMOUS 2 port, with what was checked, is in [PORT_FEATURES.md](PORT_FEATURES.md). ## Download and play There is no release yet. You need an Apple-silicon Mac and your own copy of inFAMOUS (the PSN release `NPUA80480`, for example installed in [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net) with its `.rap` licence). 1. Build the game from your copy with one command, see [Building from source](#building-from-source). 2. Open **Jogar inFAMOUS.command** to play straight away, or **Launcher inFAMOUS.command** for the app (graphics, controls, audio, mods and saves) and use its Play button. ## The app [`launcher/`](launcher/README.md) is a desktop app (Tauri), adapted from the inFAMOUS 2 one, with its own settings folder (`infamous1-recomp`) apart from the second game's. English and Portuguese. - **Graphics:** window, fullscreen or borderless, screen, vsync, gamma, anisotropic filtering (up to 16×), FXAA or SMAA, sharpening, MetalFX upscaling, internal resolution, colour adjustments. - **Controls:** keyboard, mouse and controller, mouse camera, vibration, DualSense adaptive triggers; **audio** volume and output. - **Saves:** list, back up, restore, import/export with RPCS3, `.zip`. It accepts `BCUS98119` / `NPUA80480` and rejects `BCUS98125` (inFAMOUS 2). - **Trophies, logs and reports**, all local; nothing is uploaded. - **Texture packs** and the shader cache manager. - **Steam shortcut** (optional, only when asked in the interface). The **install/rebuild** screen runs `infamous1-lle/tools/rebuild.py` (checked from the command line; the screen itself not yet clicked through). Not enabled for this game yet: GPU lighting and SSAO, removal of the inFAMOUS 2 shader passes by hash, ultrawide camera/HUD fix and the self-update. See [launcher/README.md](launcher/README.md). ## Known problems - The full campaign and long sessions are not validated. - Lighting and SSAO still run on the original SPU jobs, which costs fps; the job that does the lighting is being identified (candidate: image 209). - Ultrawide aspect ratios stretch the HUD: the camera patch is limited to the inFAMOUS 2 EBOOT hash. - The first time the game shows a new effect, its shader is translated on the render thread, which can stall for a moment; the cache makes it happen once. - Windows and Linux are not supported yet. ## Work in progress What is being worked on now (details in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md)): - **Playing the whole story**, past the tutorial, and fixing what turns up. - **GPU lighting and SSAO** for this game: find the lighting job, map its buffers and signals, compare with the Metal shaders of inFAMOUS 2. - **Fixes for the original game's problems** (fps drops, aliasing, pop-in, camera, climbing, combat, AI, checkpoints, textures): the ones about image and speed come from the runtime's levers, the ones about game logic need patches in the translated code. - **A release** of the app, and a click-through of its install screen. - **Windows and Linux:** planned. ## Building from source ### What you need - An Apple Silicon Mac (tested on an M4 Pro, macOS 27). - A legitimate copy of inFAMOUS installed in [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), its license (`.rap`) and the PS3 firmware installed there. - Xcode Command Line Tools and Homebrew: ```sh brew install cmake ninja sdl2 glslang spirv-cross spirv-tools python@3.12 python3.12 -m venv .venv ``` ### Building ```sh git clone https://github.com/erikomis/infamous1-recomp.git cd infamous1-recomp tools/setup_toolkit.sh # toolkit in ./ps3recomp-fork .venv/bin/pip install -r ps3recomp-fork/requirements.txt ``` `setup_toolkit.sh` clones NoahBPeterson's fork at `770660a` and applies `infamous1-lle/patches/ps3recomp-fork-770660a-with-upstream-prs.patch` (the inFAMOUS 2 port's toolkit patch plus this port's memory-window fix). Then one command does the rest (decrypt, translate, compile), from your copy and its licence: ```sh python3 infamous1-lle/tools/rebuild.py --game "/dev_hdd0/game/NPUA80480" --rap ``` `--dry-run` lists the steps and checks every prerequisite first. By default the EBOOT and the firmware are decrypted with RPCS3; without RPCS3, pass your own key file (scetool format) with `--keys KEYFILE`, and the firmware as Sony's `PS3UPDAT.PUP` with `--firmware PS3UPDAT.PUP`. No keys ship with this repository. The output goes to `--out` (default `~/Library/Application Support/infamous1-recomp/install`); `--toolkit DIR` uses a patched checkout you already have. The manual recipe is in [`infamous1-lle/README.md`](infamous1-lle/README.md#rebuilding). On an M4 Pro, from a clean install (2026-11-11), translating took about 40 s and compiling about 2 minutes. The result was checked against the tested build: the firmware, PPU and SPU lifts came out byte for byte the same, and the binary boots to the tutorial. CI (`.github/workflows/`) builds the launcher for macOS, Windows and Linux and checks the Python and shell tools on every change; no game data is involved. ## Playing from the terminal ```sh cd infamous1-lle ./run.sh ``` `run.sh` sets the memory window (`PS3_MEM_ALLOC_SIZE=0x30000000`) and the HDD boot path (`/dev_hdd0/game/NPUA80480/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN`) the game needs. A controller (DualSense tested) works out of the box; keyboard and mouse add on top of it, with the same layout as the inFAMOUS 2 port. On a DualSense the triggers get a feel (`PS3_PAD_ADAPTIVE=0`, or the launcher's Controls switch, turns it off). The trigger you fire bolts with, the one the controls map binds to R1 (the right one when R1 is on neither, as in the default map, where the triggers are L2/R2), clicks like a gun's: it reads as pressed at the click, about half way (`PS3_PAD_FIRE_AT=<10-90>`), and buzzes with the motors while you fire. The other trigger, aiming with L1 bound to it, has a light resistance. Both are set free when the game closes. The game logs `adaptive triggers on (fires with the right trigger at 50%)`. The rest of the DualSense (and a DualShock 4's light bar and gyro): the player lights show the port; the light bar is Cole's electric blue (`PS3_PAD_LIGHT=|off`) and glows red while the game runs the motors (`PS3_PAD_LIGHT_HIT=0` keeps it steady); gyro aim (`PS3_PAD_GYRO=`, off by default) turns the camera while you hold aim, L1 or whatever the map binds to it (`PS3_PAD_GYRO_MODE=always` without holding). All of it is in the launcher's Controls. **Quit Steam first:** with Steam Input on it takes over the DualSense and the triggers and the light bar stay off (rumble still works); the game logs a line when Steam is running. **Heartbeat at low health** (any controller with rumble): below 35% of Cole's health the controller beats like a heart, 70 to 140 beats a minute as it runs out, and the light bar pulses red with it; it stops when he recovers or dies, and in menus and loading screens (`PS3_HEARTBEAT=0` or the launcher's switch turns it off, `PS3_HEARTBEAT_AT=<5-90>` moves the threshold). The game's own picture goes black and white at about the same point. How Cole's health was found: [`infamous1-lle/notes/health/`](infamous1-lle/notes/health/README.md). | Key | PS3 | | --- | --- | | W A S D | left stick | | I J K L or mouse | right stick (camera) | | Arrow keys | D-pad | | Space | ✕ | | Q / E / R | ○ / □ / △ | | U / O | L1 / R1 | | Y / P | L2 / R2 | | G / H | L3 / R3 | | Return / Tab | START / SELECT | On the title screen **START** (`0x0008`) moves on; ✕ does not. Useful variables, shared with the other ports of this toolkit: | Variable | What it does | | --- | --- | | `PS3_ANISO=2\|4\|8\|16` | anisotropic filtering (only mipmapped textures). Default off | | `PS3_AA=fxaa` / `smaa` | anti-aliasing on the 1280×720 image | | `PS3_RES_SCALE=1.5\|2\|3` | internal resolution (1080p / 1440p / 4K): every colour and depth target, shadows and reflections included. Above the window's pixels it is supersampled: each frame is reduced into the window with a Lanczos filter, every pixel counted (`PS3_DOWNSCALE=0`: the old shrink) | | `PS3_UPSCALE=metalfx` | MetalFX spatial upscaling to the window | | `PS3_SHARPEN=<0..1>` | contrast-adaptive sharpening | | `PS3_WINDOW_MODE=windowed\|fullscreen\|borderless` | how the game opens | | `PS3_MEM_ALLOC_SIZE=` | the allocator window, 16 MB to 3 GB (default 256 MB; `run.sh` uses 768 MB) | | `PS3_ASPECT=21:9` | ultrawide; **pending for this game**, the HUD is not fixed | For headless tests: `tools/capture.sh ` saves a PNG of the frame every 10 s, `PAD_SCRIPT="145:0x0008"` presses START at 145 s, and `tools/play_prologue.sh` runs the title-to-tutorial path in one command. `tools/profile_run.sh` reports fps per period and the hottest code. ## Fixes made here - **Memory window (`sys_memory`):** the toolkit's allocator ended 256 MB after its base, so the boot's scan of the streaming cache ran out of memory and the audio/streaming init never finished. The end of the window is now `PS3_MEM_ALLOC_SIZE`. This is what got the game past the boot. - **Boot from HDD (`cellGame`):** `runtime_overrides/cellGame.c` reads `CATEGORY` from `PARAM.SFO` (`HG` here) and reports an HDD boot instead of a disc one. - **Recursive cleanup:** `func_00105550` did a recursive clean-up over the install while `cellFsUnlink` / `cellFsRmdir` were no-ops, reopening `sounds/music` tens of thousands of times; found with the file-system trace. - **SPU returns:** fixes for SPU returns in the translated job modules (`relift_spu_returns.py`). - **Game patches** (`game_patches.cpp`) are filtered by the program header hash (`PPU-`), so an inFAMOUS 2 patch never applies to this EBOOT. ## Layout | Folder | What it is | | ------ | ---------- | | [`infamous1-lle/`](infamous1-lle) | **Current port.** inFAMOUS 1 fork + firmware LLE: `main.cpp`, `stubs.cpp`, `run.sh`, runtime overrides, SPU/PPU tools. | | `infamous1/` | Local game files (`vfs/`), never published. | | [`launcher/`](launcher/README.md) | The desktop app (Tauri): play, settings, saves. | | `tools/` | `setup_toolkit.sh` clones the fork at the commit in use and applies the patch; job-module lifting scripts. | | `docs/screenshots/` | The gallery at the top of this page. | | [`NOTES.md`](NOTES.md) | Working notes and evidence, in Portuguese. | | [`PORT_FEATURES.md`](PORT_FEATURES.md) | What came from the inFAMOUS 2 port and what was checked. | ## License Code in this repository: MIT ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). # shaderscan

Offline RSX shader-cache seeding for statically recompiled PS3 games.

shaderscan finds the RSX vertex and fragment programs in **your own** game files and writes them into the shader
cache of the renderer your port uses. The game then compiles them in its normal start-up preload ("Compile shaders
before playing"), so shaders no longer have to be discovered, and stutter, during a playthrough.

It is a command-line tool (`shaderscan.exe`, Windows x64, no installer, no runtime DLLs). The Resistance ports'
Setup downloads a pinned release build into `tools\shaderscan.exe`, and their launchers run it before Play.

- [Supported games and back ends](#supported-games-and-back-ends)
- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Command line](#command-line)
- [Launcher contract](#launcher-contract)
- [Results](#results)
- [Building](#building)
- [Extending it](#extending-it): C/C++ API, front ends, back ends, runtime harvest
- [Legal note and licence](#legal-note-and-licence)
- [Credits](#credits)

## Supported games and back ends

| Game | Port | Back end | Cache written |
|---|---|---|---|
| Resistance 3 (BCES01905 and others) | Resistance3Port (not released yet) | `rpcs3` | `<port>\shadercache\rpcs3\shaders_cache` (RPCS3's Vulkan cache: `raw\*.fp`, `raw\*.vp`, `pipelines\vulkan\v1.95\*.bin`) |
| Resistance 2 | Resistance2Port (not released yet) | `rpcs3` | same |
| Resistance: Fall of Man | Resistance-Fall-of-Man-Recomp (not released yet) | `r1d3d12` | `<port>\shadercache` (`<key>.hlsl` + `<key>.dxbc`, the port's own D3D12 renderer) |

The core knows nothing about a particular game or renderer. Engine knowledge lives in small **front ends**
(`insomniac`, plus the engine-agnostic `signature` research aid). Renderer knowledge (how a program becomes a cache
entry) lives in **back ends**: `rpcs3` (any port rendering through RPCS3's Vulkan backend) and `r1d3d12`.
`--backend auto` (the default) picks `r1d3d12` for Resistance: Fall of Man and `rpcs3` otherwise.

```
game files ──► front end (per engine) ──► program_set (dedupe by RPCS3 ucode hash)
                                              │
            state profile (embedded + learned from an existing cache)
                                              │
                                              ▼
                     back end ──► the renderer's on-disk cache (atomic writes, stamp last)
```

## How it works

1. **Inputs.** It reads the decrypted `EBOOT.elf` (default `<game>\game\EBOOT.elf`), loose files and PSARC
   archives under `--game` (zlib members are inflated with miniz). By default only the members a front end asks for
   (`wants_file`) are read. `--deep` reads every member: slow, and mainly useful while writing a new front end.
2. **Front end.** `scan()` gets one file image and adds each program it finds to a `program_set`, together with the
   register state it knows: FP texcoord mask, centroid mask, shader control bits, VP output mask.
3. **Analysis and hashing** (`rsx_program.cpp`) mirror RPCS3's `ProgramStateCache.cpp`:
   - FP: `analyse_fragment_program` (start offset, length including embedded constants, texture and BX2 masks), then
     `get_fragment_program_ucode_hash`.
   - VP: `analyse_vertex_program` (the branch walk builds the instruction mask and jump table; unreached slots are
     zeroed), then `get_vertex_program_ucode_hash`.

   Programs are deduplicated by these hashes, so the `raw\` file names are exactly the ones RPCS3 would produce.
4. **States.** A pipeline entry also needs the fragment and vertex state RPCS3 keys on (control bits, texture
   dimensions, MRT count, ...) plus the Vulkan pipeline properties (raster, depth/stencil, blend, render pass). These
   are not in the program, so they come from a **profile**:
   - **embedded** profiles (`profiles\*.inc`) are statistics over the emulator state (template lines only; no game
     data);
   - **learned**: when `--out` (or `--learn <dir>`) already holds a recorded cache with at least 100 pipelines, its
     state templates and VP↔FP pairings are learned and merged in front of the embedded ones. Entries written by
     earlier shaderscan runs (listed in `shaderscan_manifest.txt`) are never learned from.

   Each fragment program gets up to `--variants` state templates × `--td` texture-dimension combinations ×
   `--props` pipeline states. Every vertex program and output mask is emitted at least once.
5. **Write** (`rpcs3`). It writes `raw\<hash>.fp` (exact guest ucode), `raw\<hash>.vp` (RSXVertexProgram data) and
   a 672-byte `pipeline_data` record per entry. The file name is built from the same four hashes RPCS3 uses (ucode
   hashes, `hash_struct(vk::pipeline_props)`, `hash_array(state params)`). Modification times are placed after every
   recorded pipeline, so the preload order still follows real first use.

### What a generated entry buys you (`rpcs3`)

RPCS3's pipeline key includes state that only exists at run time (which VP is paired with which FP, render pass,
blend state ...). Offline, shaderscan therefore warms three things:

| Level | What is reused at run time | Needs exact state? |
|---|---|---|
| Shader modules (GLSL/SPIR-V decompile + compile of each VP/FP) | Every program it found | VP: output mask only. FP: control bits, texture dims |
| GPL library parts (`R2_VK_GPL`): vertex-input, pre-raster, fragment-shader, fragment-output | Parts whose key matches | Partially |
| Whole pipelines (exact `.bin` name) | Only with a recorded pairing | Yes |

The exact-name rate is low without a recorded cache. The point is to remove the expensive shader-module compiles
and as many GPL parts as possible before the first frame.

### r1d3d12 back end (Resistance: Fall of Man)

R1 has its own D3D12 renderer: RSX ucode → HLSL (`rsx_fp_decompiler.c` / `rsx_vp_decompiler.c`) → `D3DCompile`
(system `d3dcompiler_47`, flags 0, `ps_5_0` / `vs_5_0`) → `shadercache\<key>.dxbc` plus `<key>.hlsl`. The key is
FNV-1a 64 over `"rfom-shc-v1"`, target, entry `"main"` and the HLSL; there is no driver or version check, the key is
the validation.

- **Where the programs live:** only in `game\EBOOT.elf` (329 FP + 171 VP unique). There is no `shaders.dat` and no
  runtime assembly. The `insomniac` front end's EBOOT header scan covers it.
- **Translator:** the port's own translator sources, vendored under `third_party\rfom_translators` (MIT), so the
  generated HLSL is the game's byte for byte. `src\r1d3d12\r1_glue.c` holds verbatim copies of the renderer's text
  steps: FP state wrapper, VP and `SV_VertexID` (gf) forms, the motion-vector VS/PS, and the key.
- **Variants:** fragment state (shadow compare, expand, unnormalised dims, clamp/mirror, exp32) comes from draw
  state. It is learned from the recorded `.hlsl` files (`--learn`), the embedded `profiles\r1_profile.inc`, and a
  generic top-K (`--variants`, default 4). The VS gets plain, gf, and the MV forms when `RSX_FSR` > 0.
- **Environment:** `RSX_RES_SCALE`, `RSX_FSR`, `RSX_FSR_REACTIVE` are read like the runtime sees them (`run.bat` /
  `settings.bat` `set` lines, then the process environment) and fingerprinted in the stamp, so changing the scale
  makes `--check` ask for a rescan.
- **Verify:** `--verify <shadercache>` re-derives every key from its `.hlsl` and recompiles it, comparing the DXBC.
- **Not covered:** `pso_manifest_*2.bin` (the game's list of PSOs to build at start-up) needs the root signature,
  blend, raster and render-target state of real draws, so it is left to the game. The first draw of a new state
  still builds a PSO, but no longer compiles shaders.

## Command line

```
shaderscan --game <port or USRDIR dir> --out <shader cache dir> [options]
  --backend <name>     auto (default) | rpcs3 (RPCS3 Vulkan ...\shadercache\rpcs3\shaders_cache)
                       | r1d3d12 (Fall of Man D3D12 <port>\shadercache)
  --eboot <file>       decrypted EBOOT.elf (default <game>\game\EBOOT.elf)
  --frontend <name>    insomniac (default) | signature | none
  --discovery <mode>   how level containers are searched: both (default: byte-scan + index tables,
                       deduplicated) | tables (index tables; byte-scan only where unusable) | scan
  --profile <name>     embedded state profile: r3 | r2 | generic | auto (default, from PARAM.SFO)
                       | none (r1d3d12: learned states only)
  --learn <dir|->      shaders_cache to learn state templates from (default: --out; '-' = embedded only)
  --variants <K>       state templates per fragment program (default 6; r1d3d12: 4)
  --props <N>          pipeline states per fragment variant (default 1)
  --td <M>             texture-dimension combinations per variant (default 2)
  --cache-version <v>  pipeline directory version (default v1.95)
  --deep               scan every archived file, not only shader containers
  --dry-run            count only
  --clean              remove entries written by earlier runs
  --progress           machine-readable progress on stdout (@progress/@done/@error lines)
  --check              exit 0 if the cache is already seeded by this version, 1 otherwise
  --verify <dir>       load a cache like the renderer does and re-derive every key; exit 0 when consistent
  --emit-profile <f> <symbol>   write the back end's profile learned from --learn as a C include
  -q                   quiet
  --version            print the release, the cache stamp version and the built-in back ends
```

All arguments are Unicode (`wmain`); paths with spaces and non-ASCII characters work.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | done (`--check`: the cache is already seeded by this version; `--verify`: consistent) |
| `1` | failed; an `@error` line (with `--progress`) or a `shaderscan: ` line explains why (`--check`: a run is needed) |
| `2` | usage error |
| `3` | no supported programs found. The stamp is still written, so a launcher does not retry on every start |

### Progress output

With `--progress`, stdout gets one flushed line per event, at most about 20 per second (always the first and last
step of a phase):

```
@progress <phase> <done> <total>      phase = scan | write | clean
@done <entries_written> <entries_total>
@error <text>
```

Without `--progress`, human-readable progress goes to stderr as `[<phase>] <done>/<total>`.

### Versions and stamps

`shaderscan.stamp` in the output dir records `SHADERSCAN_VERSION` (currently **1**), the back end, and for
`r1d3d12` the game root and environment fingerprint. `--check` exits 1 when that does not match, which makes a
launcher rescan. `SHADERSCAN_VERSION` is only raised when the output changes; release numbers (`v1.0.0`, ...) can
change without it, so updating the exe does not force a rescan. `shaderscan --version` prints both.

## Launcher contract

This is the contract used by the Resistance launchers (R1, R2, R3). Any launcher can use it.

```
shaderscan.exe --check --out "<root>\shadercache\rpcs3\shaders_cache"          # exit 1 = run needed
shaderscan.exe --game "<root>" --out "<root>\shadercache\rpcs3\shaders_cache" --progress
```

(R1: `--out "<root>\shadercache"`; `--backend auto` recognises the game.)

- The exe is looked up as `<root>\shaderscan.exe`, then `<root>\tools\shaderscan.exe`. No exe = no hook; the game
  works without it.
- On **Play**, before the game starts, the launcher runs `--check`; exit 1 means a scan is needed (first launch, a
  new `SHADERSCAN_VERSION`, or after "Rebuild shader cache", which deletes `shaderscan.stamp`). If `--check` exits
  with anything other than 0 or 1, or takes more than 10 s, the launcher skips the scan for this launch.
- cwd = `<root>`, no console window, stdout and stderr on one pipe, below-normal priority. Nothing else is passed:
  the defaults (`--frontend auto`, `--profile auto`, EBOOT at `<root>\game\EBOOT.elf`, learn from `--out`) do the
  right thing for each port.
- The launcher shows the `@progress` lines in a progress panel with a Cancel / Skip button. It also accepts the
  stderr `[<phase>] <done>/<total>` format.
- Exit codes: `0` starts the game; `1` / `2` show the `@error` text and start the game (retried on the next Play);
  `3` starts the game silently (stamp written, not retried).

**Crash safety.** A launcher may `TerminateProcess` the tool at any time:
- Every file is written to `<out>\shaderscan.tmp\` and renamed into place. That dir is outside `pipelines\`, because
  RPCS3 counts every file in the pipelines dir and deletes wrong-sized ones.
- Each manifest line (`shaderscan_manifest.txt`) is flushed before its file appears.
- The stamp (`shaderscan.stamp`) is written last.

A rerun skips existing entries and finishes the job. Deleting the stamp forces a rescan, which only adds what is
missing. `--clean` removes only what the manifest lists, never entries the game recorded.

### Verify mode

`--verify <dir>` (`rpcs3`) mirrors `rsx::shaders_cache::load()` / `unpack()`, read-only:
- the record size must be 672;
- the raw VP must be at least 16 bytes and the raw FP non-empty;
- the VP instruction mask must not reach past the data;
- the FP must analyse from offset 0 with exactly the file's length;
- the jump table must be sorted and terminated.

It then **re-derives the file name** from the raw programs and the record. Run on a cache RPCS3 itself wrote, it is
a check of shaderscan's hashing. Run on generated output, it shows RPCS3 will accept and correctly key every entry.
`r1d3d12` re-derives every `.hlsl` key and recompiles each one, comparing against its `.dxbc`.

## Results

Measured on the Resistance ports with the user's own data. The recorded caches are the ones the games wrote while
playing the opening levels; they are only read.

| | R3 | R2 |
|---|---|---|
| Programs found (FP / VP) | 746 / 209 | 358 / 191 |
| Recorded raw FP reproduced (same hash, equal under RPCS3's compare) | **144 / 144** | **164 / 164** genuine |
| Recorded raw VP reproduced (byte-identical) | **70 / 70** | **94 / 94** |
| Entries written (defaults, embedded profile only) | 6324 | 2382 |
| Run time (scan + write) | ≈ 5 s | ≈ 1.6 s |
| `--verify` on generated cache | OK, 0 disagreements | OK, 0 disagreements |
| `--verify` on the game's own recorded cache | 1505/1505 keys re-derived | 2035/2035 keys re-derived (1656/1656 after the torn entries were purged) |
| Recorded pipelines whose VP module is warmed | 1505/1505 | 2035/2035 |
| ... whose FP module is warmed | 970/1505 | 1305/2035 |
| ... whose GPL pre-raster / fragment-output part is warmed | 594 / 692 | 931 / 1054 |
| Launcher mode (learning from the recorded cache): exact recorded pipelines reproduced | 149 | 90 |

R2's recorded cache once held 221 extra fragment programs that were torn reads of ring-buffer copies (a FIFO bug
since fixed in the port), not real programs; every genuine recorded FP is reproduced. Byte differences in recorded
`.fp` files are expected: the engine patches FP constants at run time, and RPCS3's `fragment_program_compare` skips
constant slots.

**Variants trade-off** (R3, embedded profile). More templates per program give more exact fragment states, at the
cost of more entries to compile in the preload:

| `--variants` / `--td` | entries | recorded pipelines with a generated FP state |
|---|---|---|
| 6 / 2 (default) | 6.3 k | 970 / 1505 |
| 12 / 2 | 12.3 k | 1289 / 1505 |
| 24 / 4 | 24.1 k | 1362 / 1505 (saturates) |

**r1d3d12** (R1, keys normalised to a 3× scale):

| mode | PS | VS | entries |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--verify` recorded cache | 190 keys, 0 disagree | 313 keys, 0 disagree | DXBC byte-identical |
| learned (`--learn` recorded cache) | 172/172 | 313/313 | 2058 |
| fresh install, embedded profile | 190/190 | 313/313 | 2058 |
| hold-out (learn half, test other half) | 66/91 (73 %); 73/91 with `--variants 8` | 160/160 | 2141 |

## Building

Requirements: Windows x64, Visual Studio 2022 C++ build tools (MSVC v143 and the Windows SDK), CMake ≥ 3.20 and
Ninja (both ship with Visual Studio). clang-cl (LLVM) is used when it is installed; release builds use it.

```
build.bat
```

or by hand, from a "x64 Native Tools" prompt:

```
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl
cmake --build build
```

The result is `build\shaderscan.exe`, a single exe with the C runtime linked statically.

Fix the frozen intro logo: the game's event reset can deadlock

The title's event (vtable 0x1201500) reset, fn 0xFF5B40, takes the guard
lock and then waits on the event lock while holding it; a job batch that
finishes late needs the guard to Set the event, so both threads stop. On
slow frames the main thread resets a still-reset batch event and freezes,
leaving AsyncVidRender on the last movie picture. Native replacement
backs off holding nothing; identical when the event is already set.

1453849559.readme_excerpt:
MotorStorm Apocalypse — native PC port (Linux, Vulkan)

MotorStorm Apocalypse PC port · native on Linux · PS3 static recompilation · Vulkan

**MotorStorm Apocalypse** (PS3, BCES-00484, version 01.00) running natively on Linux, without an emulator. The game's code, PowerPC (PPU) and SPU, is translated to C before compilation by static recompilation with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). The PS3 system is reimplemented, and the GPU (RSX) runs the game's own shaders translated to Vulkan. > **No game files come with this project.** To play you need your own copy of > the game, dumped from your own disc. The build turns **your** executable into > code on **your** machine, and that code must not be distributed.

1440p, native MLAA anti-aliasing, 60 fps simulation (shown here scaled to 1280×720).

## Status | Area | State | |---|---| | Lift (PPU + SPU) and link | ✅ 76,362 PPU functions plus the SPU job and task images (ps3recomp v0.18.0) | | Boot, videos, menus | ✅ Boots to the main menu, navigable with a pad (intro movies decode and play) | | Races, single player | 🔧 Races run start to finish with correct lighting, shadows and anti-aliasing; every track is being checked. ~60 fps at 720p and 1440p on a Ryzen 9 5950X (median frame 16.7 ms); dips in physics-heavy moments are being worked on | | Split-screen (2–4 players) | 🔧 Races start and render correctly; 4 players run at ~34 fps (limited by the GPU command thread) | | Audio, saves, controllers | 🔧 Saves and controllers work; race audio plays (the firmware's MP3 decoder is lifted from your own firmware) | | Port menu, options, up to 4K, 60 fps | ✅ Start screen, in-game menu (F1), resolution scale 1–3 (720p / 1440p / 4K), 60 fps simulation (or 30 as on the PS3), performance HUD (F10) | | Online play | ❌ Not planned (the servers are gone) | | Windows | ❌ Not yet: the Vulkan backend is Linux-only | Plan and progress: [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md). Technical notes: [docs/NOTES.md](docs/NOTES.md). ## What you need **Game and firmware** (all from your own hardware and discs — see [docs/REQUIRED_FILES.md](docs/REQUIRED_FILES.md) for the details): - A disc dump of **MotorStorm Apocalypse, BCES-00484 (Europe), version 01.00**. No other region or version is supported: the port's addresses are those of this executable. Game updates (1.01, 1.02) are not used. - [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), only to decrypt the game's executable and to install the official PS3 system software (firmware). RPCS3 is not used to run the game. - The official PS3 firmware file (`PS3UPDAT.PUP`) from Sony's site, installed in RPCS3. The port reads fonts and system files from it, and lifts its MP3 decoder for the race music. **PC:** - Linux x86-64. Developed on Pop!_OS 24.04 (Ubuntu 24.04 base). - A CPU with AVX2 (AVX-512 is used when present). A fast 8-core or larger CPU is needed for 60 fps; the reference machine is a Ryzen 9 5950X. - A Vulkan GPU and driver. - A game controller (Xbox, PlayStation or any SDL-supported pad). On Linux there is no keyboard control. - About 30 GB of disk space (the game itself is ~19 GB) and **at least 16 GB of RAM** to compile; the translated PPU code is very large. **Packages** (Ubuntu / Debian / Pop!_OS names): ```sh sudo apt install git build-essential cmake ninja-build clang python3 python3-venv \ libsdl2-dev libvulkan-dev glslang-dev glslang-tools libpng-dev libfreetype-dev \ zlib1g-dev libavcodec-dev libavformat-dev libavutil-dev libswresample-dev ``` GCC 13 and clang 18 are what the port is built with; the lifted PPU code is compiled with clang (`clang++` must be on `PATH`), the rest with the system compiler. FFmpeg is loaded at run time for the intro videos. ## Installing ### 1. Get the code ```sh git clone https://github.com/millennium-h4x0r/motorstorm-apocalypse-pc.git motorstorm_apoca cd motorstorm_apoca scripts/install-hooks.sh # optional: blocks commits of game files ``` ### 2. Dump the game Dump your disc with your own PS3 (for example with a backup manager on a console that can run one) or with a compatible Blu-ray drive. You need the whole `PS3_GAME/` folder: `PARAM.SFO`, the icons, and `USRDIR/` with `EBOOT.BIN`, `ms3.psarc`, `budgets/` and `ui/`. ### 3. Install the firmware in RPCS3 Install RPCS3 (Flatpak or native), then *File → Install Firmware* and pick `PS3UPDAT.PUP`. The port finds it on its own in either place (`~/.var/app/net.rpcs3.RPCS3/config/rpcs3/dev_flash` or `~/.config/rpcs3/dev_flash`). Elsewhere, point `PS3_DEV_FLASH` at the `dev_flash` folder. ### 4. Decrypt the executable `USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` is encrypted. In RPCS3: *Utilities → Decrypt PS3 Binaries*, select `EBOOT.BIN`. Keep the result as `EBOOT.elf`. It must be: ``` sha256 387c9fb795e1709bd2cf1a1145c0548a0fc911a295aa860a27b41441a15418ff size 21318304 bytes ``` ```sh sha256sum EBOOT.elf ``` ### 5. Put the game files in `disc/` `disc/` is ignored by git. Copy the dump there, or link to it so the 19 GB are not copied (adjust `SRC`): ```sh SRC=/path/to/your/dump/PS3_GAME mkdir -p disc/PS3_GAME/USRDIR for f in "$SRC"/*; do [ "$(basename "$f")" = USRDIR ] || ln -s "$f" disc/PS3_GAME/; done for f in "$SRC"/USRDIR/*; do [ "$(basename "$f")" = EBOOT.BIN ] || ln -s "$f" disc/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/; done cp /path/to/EBOOT.elf disc/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/ ``` The result: ``` disc/PS3_GAME/ ├── PARAM.SFO, ICON0.PNG, PIC0.PNG, PIC1.PNG, SND0.AT3, ... └── USRDIR/ ├── EBOOT.elf # the decrypted executable (a real file, not a link) ├── ms3.psarc ├── budgets/ └── ui/ ``` ### 6. Build ```sh scripts/setup.sh # fetches ps3recomp at the pinned commit, applies this port's patch, Python venv scripts/lift.sh # translates the PPU and SPU code of YOUR EBOOT.elf (checks its hash) scripts/build.sh # compiles into work/port/build-vk ``` `lift.sh` takes about 12 minutes. `build.sh` runs up to 8 jobs in parallel (fewer on a machine with fewer CPU threads or less free memory: about 3 GB a job), inside a memory cap of 85% of the free memory. With 4 jobs a fresh build took about 35 minutes on a Ryzen 9 5950X; with more cores and memory, `JOBS=16` or more is faster. `JOBS=` and `PORT_BUILD_MEM=` (with a unit, e.g. `24G`) override it. A build that hits the cap is stopped rather than freezing the machine; run it again with fewer jobs and it carries on where it stopped. Optional: `work/pgo/ppu.profdata` and `work/pgo/spu.profdata`, when present, are used for profile-guided optimisation. They are not shipped; the port runs without them, somewhat slower. ### 7. Play ```sh work/play.sh # start screen, then the game work/play.sh --play # straight into the game ``` Connect the controller before starting. Each run's log goes to `work/runs/play-.log`. Saves and settings stay in the repository folder (`hdd0/`, `user/`), all git-ignored. ## Settings and keys The start screen and the in-game menu (**F1**) write `user/settings.ini`; the file can also be edited by hand (a variable set in the environment wins over it): | Setting | Values | |---|---| | `scale` | 1 = 720p, 2 = 1440p, 3 = 4K (the window opens at that size) | | `fullscreen`, `vsync`, `stretch`, `display` | full screen; vsync; stretch instead of black bars; which monitor | | `frame_rate` | 60, or 30 as on the PS3 | | `fps_limit` | 0 = none | | `fps_counter` | performance HUD: 0 off, 1 detailed, 2 compact | | `fullres_particles`, `aniso` | particles at full resolution; anisotropic filtering 2–16 | | Key | | |---|---| | F1 | port menu | | F10 | performance HUD: detailed / compact / off | | F11 or Alt+Enter | full screen and back | | Esc | quit | On a scaled Wayland desktop (125%, 150%, ...) the window is sized in real pixels, so 1440p is 2560×1440 screen pixels. `PS3RECOMP_VK_X11=1` uses Xwayland instead of native Wayland. ## Troubleshooting - **`lift.sh` warns about the sha256:** the executable is not the BCES-00484 01.00 one, or it was not decrypted. Only that version works. - **No sound in races / missing fonts:** the firmware is not installed in RPCS3, or `PS3_DEV_FLASH` does not point at its `dev_flash`. - **The build is killed:** the memory cap was hit; lower `JOBS` or raise `PORT_BUILD_MEM` (with a unit, e.g. `24G`). - **No controller:** connect it before starting; SDL picks controllers up at launch. - **Bugs:** include the `work/runs/play-.log` of the run. Do not attach game files or anything under `work/src/` or `work/port/spu/` — that is the game's code. ## Contributing See [docs/GITHUB_SETUP.md](docs/GITHUB_SETUP.md). Changes to ps3recomp go in `work/patches/ps3recomp.patch` (`scripts/make_patch.sh`). The tests are in `work/tests/` (`work/tests/run_all.sh`). ## Credits See [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md). ## License MIT for the code in this repository; see [LICENSE](LICENSE). MotorStorm Apocalypse and its content belong to their owners (Evolution Studios / Sony Interactive Entertainment). This is a research and preservation project; it contains no game code or assets.

1453927105.readme_excerpt:
# Asura's Wrath — static recompilation for PC (macOS)

🌐 **English** · [Português (BR)](README.pt-BR.md)

A native port of **Asura's Wrath** (PS3, disc `BLUS30721`, v01.02) to
**macOS/arm64**, built with static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU
code is translated to C/C++ and compiled into a native executable, with
graphics on Metal. It is not an emulator.

**The path to the game's true ending is included**: the port fetches and
installs the add-on content alongside the game — the *Episode Pack Part IV:
Nirvana* (episodes 19-22), which is where the story actually ends. See
[docs/DLC.md](docs/DLC.md) (in Portuguese). Whether those episodes load
and play has not been tried yet.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Game | Asura's Wrath — Capcom / CyberConnect2, 2012 |
| Engine | Unreal Engine 3 (PS3 cook) — CC2's "BCGAME" build |
| Disc | BLUS30721 (USA, EnJaFrDeEsIt), version 01.02 |
| Target | Apple-silicon macOS, Metal graphics |

> [!WARNING]
> **Early alpha, not playable to the end.** In headless probes (no window) the
> game reaches the title screen, creates or loads a save, enters NEW GAME,
> plays the opening of Episode 1 and gets to the first QTEs with no error in
> the log (reported by the developer). **Audio does not work**, and playing
> through a window, the QTEs' response and the rest of the episode have not
> been verified. There are no releases: you build the game yourself from your
> own disc. What is missing is in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).

> **This repository contains no game data, no DLC, no firmware, no Sony keys
> and nothing translated from them.** Everyone generates all of that locally
> from their own legitimate copy (and fetches their own add-on content; the
> URLs in `fetch_dlc.sh` are Sony's public CDN for this title ID, and the
> packages stay encrypted with the buyer's licence). A fan project, not
> affiliated with Capcom, CyberConnect2 or Sony Interactive Entertainment.

## Building

Prerequisites: the disc (ISO) in `~/Downloads` (or adjust the `game_iso`
symlink), Xcode CLT, CMake + Ninja, and the shared Python venv.

```sh
tools/rebuild.sh            # stage → decrypt → analyse → lift → spu → dlc → build
tools/rebuild.sh dlc        # just the DLC (fetch + extract + link into the VFS)
tools/run.sh                # run the game (mounts the ISO read-only)
```

## Status

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Disc inventory, EBOOT decrypted, PPU and SPU lifted, builds with Metal | ✅ |
| Boot, first-run install, legal screens and loading videos | ✅ |
| Title screen, save, NEW GAME | ✅ in headless probes |
| Opening of Episode 1, pause menu, first QTEs | 🧪 reached in a 470 s headless probe; the rest of the episode not checked |
| Playing in a window | 🧪 not verified after the latest fixes |
| Audio | ❌ does not work yet |
| Add-on episodes (Part IV: Nirvana) | 🧪 fetched and linked into the VFS; never loaded |

## Layout

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [`port/`](port/) | The game-specific code: boot, stubs, SPURS queues, CMake |
| [`patches/`](patches/) | The ps3recomp toolkit patches ([notes](patches/README.md), in Portuguese) |
| [`tools/`](tools/) | Rebuild, decrypt, DLC, run and probe scripts |
| [`docs/`](docs/) | DLC notes and the game manifest (Portuguese) |

Built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), with the layout
and the tools of the author's other ports ([Resistance: Fall of Man](https://github.com/erikomis/resistance-recomp),
[inFAMOUS 2](https://github.com/erikomis/infamous2-recomp), among others). See
[CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md). The technical diary is in Portuguese
([ROADMAP.pt-BR.md](ROADMAP.pt-BR.md)); the roadmap has an English summary.

## License

The port's own code is MIT ([LICENSE](LICENSE)); ps3recomp keeps its own
licence. Asura's Wrath belongs to Capcom and CyberConnect2; no part of the
game is included.

03eadcc6908a107bf74accf613dd03dcd87b3435.message:
cellAdec: decode AC3 through the run-time FFmpeg loader

cellAdec only produced silence, 1024 stereo samples an access unit, whatever the codec. A title that sizes its PCM ring from bsiInfo+0x14 (channels x 4 bytes a sample) then took the wrong number of samples for an AC3 5.1 movie track: 341 sample frames per 1536-sample AC3 frame.

AC3 (codecType 2) now decodes through the loader cellVdec already uses (ps3_ffmpeg_get, no new FFmpeg symbols) into interleaved big-endian float in the decoder's channel order, one 1536-sample frame per access unit, its size in the PcmItem and in bsiInfo+0x14. StartSeq flushes the decoder and Close frees it. The AU bytes and info are copied before AUDONE, which hands the AU buffer back to the title. Without a decoder (no FFmpeg build, PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG=0, a damaged AU) AC3 gives silence of the real frame size, 1536 samples in the channels the frame header names; other codecs keep the old 1024-sample stereo silence. The PCM block moves from the 16 KB per-handle scratch to its own 64 KB per handle in the HLE inject window.

test_adec_ac3 (libs/codec/tests, streams made by the ffmpeg program at test time) checks the silence sizes with and without the library, and that every access unit of a 5.1 stream equals FFmpeg's own decode sample for sample; two swapped channels and one dropped AU must be caught.

cellGame: report 40 GiB - 256 KiB free above 4 GiB, so hddFreeSizeKB * 1024 cannot wrap

Games turn hddFreeSizeKB into bytes as hddFreeSizeKB * 1024 in 32 bits.
With 4 GiB or more free that wraps, and what is left is whatever the host
disk's free space happens to be modulo 4 GiB: a few MB on some disks, so the
install check fails with "not enough space" at random. inFAMOUS 2 refused
to boot that way with 41.7 GB free. RPCS3 reports 40 GiB - 256 KiB in every
one of these calls for the same reason (its x1024 is 0xFFFC0000, nearly
4 GiB after the wrap).

cellGameBootCheck, cellGameDataCheck and the cellGameDataCheckCreate(2)
status callback's get block now report the measured value below 4 GiB,
where it cannot wrap and a nearly full disk still reads as one, and
RPCS3's figure above.
PS3_GAME_FREE_SPACE_RAW=1 reports the measured value always, as before.

test_game_space: the 12 GiB case now expects 40 GiB - 256 KiB (and checks
the wrapped byte count), plus 4 GiB - 4 KiB reported as is, exactly 4 GiB
replaced, and the raw switch. It needed a ppu_vfs_root stub to link again,
and macos.yml now runs it with the other self-contained sysutil tests.

0b874166c7bb5caa389d351863a417367ffb4362.message:
perf(spu): NEON fi and cflts on ARM64

On ARM64 spu_fi (the frest/frsqest interpolation step) and spu_cflts fell
through to the per-lane scalar references. Those loops are too large to
inline, so every use in lifted float code became an out-of-line call with the
vector registers spilled around it. This adds NEON forms beside the AVX2 ones
from #500; the other estimate and conversion helpers keep their references.

- fi: the reference's fixed-point arithmetic in 32-bit lanes; the 33-bit
  magnitude 2^32 + (base << 19) - step * y is split on the borrow of the low
  word.
- cflts, scales 0..127: multiply by 2^scale (exact, or an overflow that
  FCVTZS saturates like the SPU), FCVTZS, and exponent-0 / exponent-255 lanes
  patched to 0 / the saturated bound. Other scales use the reference.

test_spu_fi_cflts_neon compares both with the references over 5.6M vectors
(every exponent, fi's borrow edge, all cflts scales) in the default FPCR and
under round-toward-zero plus flush-to-zero, the mode SPU_FLOAT_RZ runs lifted
