1454369706.readme_excerpt:
# ps3recomp

### *Because the Cell processor deserves a second life*

> Static recompilation runtime libraries for PlayStation 3 titles.
> Turn PS3 binaries into native executables. No emulator required.

**[Join the sp00nznet recomp Discord](https://discord.gg/CRpzGWZFcu)** — the
community hub for sp00nznet's recomp projects, where ps3recomp development
happens in the open. Good place to ask questions, show a port you are working
on, or find out what people are stuck on before you duplicate the effort.

---

## What Is This?

**ps3recomp** is an open-source toolkit that provides the runtime libraries, system stubs, and analysis tools needed to **statically recompile PlayStation 3 games into native PC executables**.

Instead of interpreting or dynamically recompiling PowerPC/SPU instructions at runtime (what emulators like RPCS3 do brilliantly), we take the opposite approach: **translate everything ahead of time** into C/C++ that compiles with your favorite compiler on any modern platform.

This is the same philosophy behind:
- [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp) (N64 -> native)
- [UnleashedRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) (PS2 -> native)
- [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) (Original Xbox -> native)
- [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) (Xbox 360 -> native)
- [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) (PS5 -> native)

...but for the PS3's glorious, terrifying **Cell Broadband Engine**.

## Why PS3?

The PlayStation 3 has over **3,000 titles** and some of the most beloved games ever made. RPCS3 has done heroic work making ~70% of the library playable through emulation, but static recompilation offers something different:

- **Native performance** — no runtime translation overhead
- **Lower hardware requirements** — runs on mid-range PCs
- **Moddability** — recompiled C/C++ is infinitely more hackable than PPC binaries
- **Preservation** — native ports survive long after emulators stop being maintained
- **Portability** — the output is C/C++, so it can target any platform a compiler does (see [platform support](#platform-support) for where the runtime actually stands today)

## Platform support

CI builds and tests every row on every pull request: Windows (clang-cl), macOS
arm64, Linux (GCC and Clang), and Linux with the Vulkan backend on lavapipe
under the validation layer. A green check means the runtime built and the tests
passed. It does not mean a game ran; the last row is the only one that claims
that.

| | Windows | macOS (arm64) | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime library builds | yes | yes | yes |
| Lifter test suites + C unit tests | yes | yes | yes |
| Render backend | D3D12 | Metal | Vulkan (opt-in); null (headless, CI) |
| Runs a recompiled game, in this tree | **yes** | **no** | **no** |

**The POSIX boot path runs in CI, but not yet with a retail title in this
tree.** `ps3recomp_boot_smoke` loads a synthetic PPU ELF through
`ppu_loader.cpp`, the HLE dispatch, guest threads, the frame clock and the
renderer. CI also builds and boots that ELF through `templates/project` on
macOS and Linux. That proves the per-game scaffold runs on both hosts; it is
not a compatibility claim for a retail game.

**The renderers are further along than that.** `ps3recomp_host` drives cellGcm
→ RSX → backend end to end with no game. With guest programs on, Metal and
Vulkan both run the title's own shaders on the shared register-file draw
engine. Every `ps3recomp_host` scene passes on both, including render-to-texture,
MRT, depth textures, cube maps and stencil. Linux's default stays the headless
null backend, a CPU triangle filler that CI draws with.

**Downstream, people are already past this.** Twisted Metal's menus run on
Linux/Vulkan, inFamous on macOS, and Killzone 3 under Proton (see
[In the community](#in-the-community)). Those ports carry patches that are
still on their way upstream, which is why the table still says "no".

## The Challenge

The PS3's Cell processor is a beast unlike anything else:

| Component | What It Is | Why It's Hard |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **PPU** | PowerPC 64-bit main CPU | Custom ISA extensions, VMX/AltiVec SIMD |
| **6x SPU** | 128-bit SIMD vector processors | Proprietary ISA, 256KB local store, explicit DMA |
| **Memory** | 256MB XDR RAM | 128-byte alignment requirements, split bus |
| **LV2 Kernel** | Proprietary OS layer | ~300+ system calls, complex threading model |
| **PRX Modules** | Dynamic libraries | 100+ system libraries with intricate interdependencies |

We don't shy away from hard problems. We just break them into smaller ones.

## Architecture

```
ps3recomp/
├── tools/                    # Binary analysis & recompilation pipeline
│   ├── elf_parser.py         # Parse PS3 ELF/SELF/PRX binaries
│   ├── ppu_disasm.py         # PowerPC disassembler with PS3 extensions
│   ├── ppu_lifter.py         # PPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── spu_disasm.py         # SPU instruction set disassembler
│   ├── spu_lifter.py         # SPU assembly -> C code lifter
│   ├── extract_spu_images.py # Extract embedded SPU images from PRX/ELF
│   ├── find_spu_functions.py # SPU function boundary detection
│   ├── wrap_spu_elf.py       # Wrap a raw SPU blob as a loadable ELF
│   ├── prx_analyzer.py       # Analyze PRX imports/exports and NIDs
│   ├── nid_database.py       # Function Name ID (NID) resolver
│   ├── find_functions.py     # Function boundary detection
│   └── generate_stubs.py     # Generate HLE stub skeletons from a NID list
│
├── runtime/                  # Core runtime for recompiled executables
│   ├── ppu/                  # PPU execution context
│   │   ├── ppu_context.h     # Register file, CR, LR, CTR, FPSCR
│   │   ├── ppu_memory.h      # Memory access macros (loads, stores, byte-swap)
│   │   └── ppu_ops.h         # Instruction operation macros
│   ├── spu/                  # SPU execution context
│   │   ├── spu_context.h     # 128×128-bit register file, 256KB local store, image_id
│   │   ├── spu_channels.c    # Channel ops + per-image function-table dispatch
│   │   ├── spu_helpers.h     # SPU intrinsics (incl. float conversions)
│   │   ├── spu_dma.h         # DMA (MFC) transfer engine
│   │   └── tests/            # Self-contained SPU runtime tests
│   ├── memory/               # Memory subsystem
│   │   └── vm.h              # Virtual memory manager (256MB address space)
│   └── syscalls/             # LV2 kernel system call implementations
│       ├── sys_ppu_thread.h  # Thread creation/management
│       ├── sys_mutex.h       # Mutex/cond synchronization
│       ├── sys_memory.h      # Memory allocation/mapping
│       ├── sys_fs.h          # Filesystem operations
│       └── lv2_syscall_table.h # Full syscall dispatch table
│
├── libs/                     # HLE library implementations
│   ├── audio/                # cellAudio, cellAdec, libmixer, libsnd3, libsynth2
│   ├── video/                # cellGcmSys, cellResc, cellVideoOut, cellVpost, cellVdec
│   ├── input/                # cellPad, cellKb, cellMouse
│   ├── hardware/             # cellGem, cellCamera, cellUsbd
│   ├── network/              # cellNetCtl, cellHttp, cellHttps, cellSsl, sceNp*
│   ├── filesystem/           # cellFs, cellGame, cellSaveData, cellStorage
│   ├── system/               # cellSysutil, cellSysmodule, cellRtc, sysPrxForUser
│   ├── spurs/                # cellSpurs, cellFiber, cellSpursJq, cellDaisy (SPU task management)
│   ├── sync/                 # cellSync, cellSync2 (cross-PPU/SPU synchronization)
│   ├── codec/                # cellJpgDec, cellPngDec, cellGifDec, cellPamf, cellDmux, cellAdecAtrac3p, cellAdecCelp8, cellVdecDivx
│   ├── font/                 # cellFont, cellFontFT, cellFreeType, cellL10n
│   └── misc/                 # cellScreenshot, cellSubdisplay, cellImeJp, cellVideoExport, cellMusicExport, cellGameRecording, etc.
│
├── include/ps3emu/           # Public API headers
│   ├── ps3types.h            # Fundamental PS3 types (u8-u128, s8-s64, be_t<>)
│   ├── endian.h              # Big-endian <-> little-endian conversion
│   ├── nid.h                 # NID hashing and lookup
│   ├── module.h              # Module registration framework
│   └── error_codes.h         # PS3 system error codes (CELL_OK, CELL_E*)
│
├── templates/project/        # Starter template for new game ports
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Build system
│   ├── main.cpp              # Application entry point
│   ├── stubs.cpp             # Game-specific function overrides
│   └── config.toml           # Recompiler configuration
│
├── config/                   # Reference configurations
│   └── example.toml          # Example recompilation config
│
└── docs/                     # See the Documentation table below
```

## How It Works

The pipeline follows the same proven approach as our [burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3) project, adapted for the Cell architecture:

```
   PS3 Game Disc / PKG
         │
         ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  SELF/EBOOT  │  Encrypted PS3 executable
   │  Decryption  │  (requires keys / fSELF)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  ELF Parser  │  Extract sections, segments, relocations
   │  + PRX Scan  │  Identify imported NIDs & library deps
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Disasm  │  Disassemble PowerPC 64-bit + VMX
   │  + Analysis  │  Function boundaries, jump tables, ABI
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  PPU Lifter  │  PowerPC → C code generation
   │  + SPU Lift  │  SPU programs → C code generation
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Link with   │  ps3recomp runtime + HLE libs
   │  Runtime     │  Provides all PS3 OS services
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │  Compile &   │  MSVC / GCC / Clang
   │  Ship!       │  Native x86-64 executable
   └─────────────┘
```

## SPU Strategy

The SPU is the elephant in the room. Each SPU has its own instruction set, its own 256KB memory, and communicates with the PPU via DMA and mailbox channels. Our approach:

1. **SPU programs are self-contained** — they live in ELF segments loaded to local store (`extract_spu_images.py` pulls them out of PRX/ELF)
2. **Recompile each SPU program separately** — dedicated `spu_disasm.py` + `spu_lifter.py` handle the SPU ISA
3. **SPU local store becomes an array** — 256KB per "virtual SPU"
4. **DMA operations become memcpy** — via the MFC engine (`spu_dma.h`)
5. **Channels become cross-thread message queues** — preserving ordering guarantees
6. **Per-image function-table dispatch** — `image_id` lets multiple SPU programs (e.g. a SPURS kernel, a policy module, and a job) coexist at overlapping local-store addresses

This mirrors how RPCS3 handles SPU but at compile time rather than runtime. The
disassembler, lifter, and runtime are functional and covered by self-contained
tests (`runtime/spu/tests/`: sum, shufb, DMA, brsl-return).

## Module Status

HLE implementations of the PS3 system libraries, written for this project. RPCS3 is a behavioural reference, not a code source. Most modules are complete. The ones still marked Partial are the media decoders (cellVdec, cellAdec, cellDmux, cellAtrac, cellAdecAtrac3p) and cellSpurs. [docs/MODULE_STATUS.md](docs/MODULE_STATUS.md) has one row per module and is the source for the counts.

7d0ae6b7cbc8e1c6836e78ea15b32f3f355ebef5.message:
main.cpp: LBP2_RSX_POLL_US sets the RSX thread's sleep between FIFO passes

The frame clock slept a fixed 4 ms between passes, so every park on an
unready semaphore acquire or an empty FIFO cost up to 4 ms. The option
(50..4000 us, default 4000 = unchanged) shortens that; the window pump
and the pre-flip present keep their ~4 ms cadence. In a level, 250 us:
7.8-7.9 -> 8.2 fps without draw batching, 12.3 -> 12.7-13.0 with it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

91c4a8f9d3904518d4ba4133bc311f6258770cd6.message:
CMake: also -mfma for the lifted SPU code when the host has FMA

LBP2_SPU_FMA (default: host has FMA3) adds -mfma next to -mavx2, so the
runtime's SPU_FLOAT_RZ forms of fma/fms/fnms become one fused op.
-ffp-contract=off still applies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

956ea969314fdc44ffa3a2213ddae4c0c5598807.message:
CMake: build the lifted SPU code with -mavx2 when the host has AVX2

LBP2_SPU_AVX2 (default: ON when the compiler takes -mavx2 and the
configuring machine has AVX2) adds -mavx2 to the lifted SPU sources only.
That selects the runtime's AVX2 form of the exact SPU float ops (four
lanes as one f64x4 instead of two SSE halves) and VEX code. The runtime's
float tests built with -mavx2 -ffp-contract=off pass bit-identical, and
-ffp-contract=off still applies, so nothing is contracted into fma.

Wws_Job/MAIN, the job list the main thread's barrier waits on, went from
~52 to ~45 ms per frame; the level from 7.6 to 7.8-7.9 flips/s. The
binary then needs AVX2: -DLBP2_SPU_AVX2=OFF builds one that runs anywhere.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

it a level runs at 12.3-13.0 fps instead of ~7.9, and the frames match.

# ps3recomp-lbp2

Work in progress: a static recompilation of **LittleBigPlanet 2** (BCUS98245, USA) with
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), built against the
[`lbp2-fixes` branch of the zeropaulsy fork](https://github.com/zeropaulsy/ps3recomp/tree/lbp2-fixes).

**This repository contains no game code or data.** The lifted C/C++ (generated from the
game's executable), the SPU images and job modules, the disc contents, keys and saves are all
excluded (`.gitignore` is a whitelist). You need your own copy of the game, and you have to
decrypt and lift it yourself.

## Status

- Boots through all 73 init steps, plays the intro movie and runs the opening credits level
  indefinitely (6-minute runs).
- The Vulkan build renders that level correctly with the game's own shaders. Known problems:
  white patches during the level intro (~110 s), the final image is shrunk to 0.875 of the
  frame, and it runs at ~7 frames/s (~11.5 headless with `LBP2_NO_RASTER=1`).
- No audio by design in these scripts (see "Running").

## What is here

| Path | What |
|------|------|
| `project/` | The game project: `CMakeLists.txt`, `main.cpp`, `stubs.cpp`, and `lbp2_local.cpp` (game-specific shims: offline `cellNetCtlGetState`, a UDP loopback for the game's party code, init-step logging, `LBP2_NO_RASTER`, `LBP2_CRASH_BT`) |
| `env.sh` | Workspace paths and the runtime settings LBP2 needs; sourced by the scripts |
| `run.sh` | Silent launcher: `./run.sh <seconds> [label]`, log in `runs/` |
| `run_frames.sh` | Same, saving a Vulkan frame every 5 s: `./run_frames.sh <seconds> <label> <new-dir>` |
| `patch_stubs.py` | Post-lift fix for import stubs (see below) |
| `gdb/` | `run_gdb.sh <seconds> <absolute script> <label>` and the probe scripts used during bring-up |
| `tools/` | Small ELF helpers: `ppc_view.py ADDR:N`, `callers.py ADDR`, `tocref.py`, `opd.py`, `str.py` (need `capstone`) |

## Building

1. **Get the runtime.** Clone the fork's branch into this checkout (it is ignored by git):
   ```
   git clone -b lbp2-fixes https://github.com/zeropaulsy/ps3recomp.git ps3recomp
   ```
2. **Decrypt the game's `EBOOT.BIN`** to an ELF with your own tools and keys, and put its path
   in `local.env`: `LBP2_ELF=/path/to/lbp2.elf`.
3. **Extract the disc** into `game/` by its Joliet names (the ISO9660 tree is upper-case and
   truncates long names), so that `game/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/...` exists. `data.sdat` must also be
   decrypted to `game/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/data.sdat.dec` for the SPU job modules.
4. **Lift the PPU code** into `recompiled/`:
   ```
   python3 ps3recomp/tools/ppu_loader.py "$LBP2_ELF" -o out/
   python3 ps3recomp/tools/ppu_lifter.py "$LBP2_ELF" --functions out/lbp2.functions.json \
       --hle-stubs out/lbp2.imports.json --output recompiled/
   python3 patch_stubs.py
   ```
   `patch_stubs.py` makes every import stub save r2 the way the real stub does (the runtime's
   fast HLE path returns before restoring it, and LBP2 uses three TOCs). Run it after every lift.
5. **Lift the SPU code** into `spu/`: the embedded SPU images (`extract_spu_images.py`,
   `spu_lifter.py`, `build_spu_workloads.py`), the raw `Wws_Job` policy module (ELF offset
   0xC26F80, 12160 bytes; not an ELF, so it is wrapped at LS 0xA00 and lifted with
   `--extra-funcs pm_wwsjob=0xA2C`), and the 100 job modules from `data.sdat.dec`
   (`extract_jobmods.py --usrdir game/PS3_GAME/USRDIR --sdat data.sdat.dec`, then
   `lift_jobmods.py --jobmods spu/jobmods --out spu --register spu/jobmods_register.c
   --symbol-prefix lbp2`). This step is not scripted yet; the commands are what the bring-up
   used and may need adjusting.
6. **Configure and build** (the lifted files are large: keep the job count low, about 1.5 GB
   of RAM per job):
   ```
   cmake -S project -B build -G Ninja
   ninja -C build -j3
   ```
   Add `-DPS3RECOMP_RSX_VULKAN=ON` (in a second build directory, e.g. `build-vk`) for real
   pixels; it needs glslang. The default build uses the headless null renderer.
   `-DPS3RECOMP_DIR=`, `-DRECOMP_DIR=` and `-DSPU_DIR=` point elsewhere if your layout differs.
   The lifted SPU code is built with `-mavx2` (and `-mfma` if present) when the configuring
   machine has AVX2 (faster SPU float ops); the binary then needs the same CPU features.
   `-DLBP2_SPU_AVX2=OFF` builds one without them, `-DLBP2_SPU_FMA=OFF` drops only `-mfma`.

## Running

Always through `run.sh` or `gdb/run_gdb.sh`. Both force SDL's dummy audio driver, make the
PulseAudio/PipeWire/JACK servers unreachable, and kill the game if it opens an audio device.
Any new launcher should do the same.

```
./run.sh 200 test                                            # headless, 200 s
BIN=$PWD/build-vk/lbp2_recomp ./run_frames.sh 200 vk frames-1 # Vulkan, a frame every 5 s
```

Progress shows in the log as `[lbp2-local] t=Ns flips=N` and `init at: step N`.

### Runtime settings

`env.sh` sets these by default (set one before calling to change it, or
`LBP2_NO_DEFAULT_ENV=1` to skip them all):

| Variable | Why |
|----------|-----|
| `PAD_SCRIPT=25:0x4000,30:0x4000,35:0x4000` | Presses Cross for the game's two boot prompts |
| `SPU_INTERP_UNLIFTED=1` | Interprets SPU code loaded at run time (the FMOD mixer's DSP plugins) |
| `SPU_DMA_REPEAT_EXEMPT=8` | SPU image 8 waits on a control block between frames; the repeat watchdog must not halt it |
| `SPU_WWS_PM_IMAGE=1` | The `Wws_Job` policy module is image 1 here, so job modules dispatch to lifted code |
| `GCM_USER_QUEUE=1` | Delivers every GCM user command; the game releases a job-list gate per command |
| `GCM_FIFO_SEGMENT=0x8000` | 32 KB command-ring segments, as the SDK's default context; avoids a deadlock with the next setting |
| `GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE=1`, `GCM_SEMA_ACQUIRE_MS=2000` | The RSX waits for labels the SPU jobs write; without it frames show 128x128 blocks of older frames |
| `CELL_FIBER_RUN_RETURNS=1` | `cellFiberPpuRunFibers` returns when nothing is runnable; the game signals its fibers after it returns |
| `PS3RECOMP_VK_GUEST_PROGRAMS=1` | Vulkan build: use the game's shaders |
| `SPU_MFC_LOOKUP_CACHE=1` | Per-thread cache of the SPU MFC engine lookup; about 19% faster in levels |
| `VK_DRAW_BATCH=1` | Vulkan build: records draws, uploads and clears into one GPU submission instead of waiting for the GPU after each draw; about 7.9 -> 12.3 fps in levels |

Useful extras: `LBP2_NO_RASTER=1` (headless build without the software rasterizer, much
faster), `GCM_SEMA_STATS=1`, `VK_BLACK_STATS=1`, `RSX_PRESENT_LOG=1`, `LBP2_CRASH_BT=1`.
`LBP2_RSX_POLL_US=<50..4000>` (default 4000) sets how long the RSX thread sleeps between FIFO
passes; 250 gave a few percent more fps in levels.

## Credits

ps3recomp by sp00nznet and contributors. LittleBigPlanet is a trademark of Sony Interactive
Entertainment; this project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony or Media Molecule.

# inFAMOUS 2 Reborn

A native Windows PC port of **inFamous 2** (PS3) made by static recompilation. The game's PPU
and SPU code is translated to C/C++ and compiled for x86-64, with a D3D12 renderer standing in
for the RSX.

**This repository contains no game code or game data.** The installer regenerates everything
from your own legally dumped copy of the game, then compiles it on your PC.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), a D3D12-capable GPU
- Your own dump of **inFamous 2, European/Australian release `BCES01143`**: a disc image
  (`.iso`, Redump images with their `.dkey` next to them) or a decrypted game folder
- About 25 GB of free space for the install; 16 GB of RAM recommended
- Python 3.10+ and Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools with the C++ and Clang tools. The setup
  program installs both through winget if they are missing.

## Install

1. Download **`inFamous 2 Setup.exe`** from the
   [Releases](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUS2reborn/releases) page.
2. Run it and pick your disc image or game folder.
3. Choose an install folder and let it work. The first install takes a while: the game code is
   lifted and compiled on your machine.
4. Start the game with **`inFamous 2.exe`** in the install folder. Its options window has
   V-Sync, shadows, mipmaps and button prompts.

To update, use **Update now** in the setup program or `Update inFamous 2.cmd` in your install
folder. Only changed files are downloaded and only the affected steps are redone.

## Controls

Xbox/XInput controllers work out of the box. Keyboard and mouse are supported too: bindings and
mouse sensitivity live in `infamous2-recomp\kbm.ini` (changes apply while the game runs). On-screen
prompts switch between keycaps and controller buttons depending on what you last used.

## Status

The game boots, plays its cutscenes and runs in the open world. Performance depends mostly on
CPU single-thread speed; busy scenes currently run around 20–27 FPS on the development PC.
Lighting is rendered exactly (no stale-frame halos). Expect bugs. Please report them with
`infamous2-recomp\play.err.log` attached.

## Repository layout

| Folder | What |
|---|---|
| `infamous2-recomp/` | The port: build files, entry point, input bindings, pipeline tools and the hand-written SPU registrations |
| `ps3recomp/` | The recompilation toolkit and the PS3 runtime (PPU/SPU lifters, HLE firmware libraries, D3D12 RSX backend) |
| `installer/` | The installer, setup program and launcher (Rust), the pipeline manifest `infamous2.toml`, and the patch set that turns the regenerated code into the port's maintained version |

See `installer/README.md` for how the setup is built and `infamous2-recomp/README.md` for the
port's technical notes and runtime switches.

## Credits and license

Built on the [ps3recomp](ps3recomp/README.md) toolkit (MIT; see `ps3recomp/LICENSE` and
`ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md`). Third-party components keep their own licenses under
`ps3recomp/third_party/`.

inFamous 2 is © Sony Interactive Entertainment, developed by Sucker Punch Productions. This is
an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony or Sucker Punch. You need to
own the game to use it.

Low-CPU update: fewer threads on weaker PCs, support for CPUs without AVX2

- SPURS: on PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the lanes/kernels spin less, wake the
  main thread sooner and run on fewer threads (4-thread PCs: ~10 fps -> ~29 fps,
  8 threads: ~38 -> ~50 fps). Big PCs keep the old behaviour.
- Vertex workers spin far less after each job, fewer workers on small CPUs.
- The once-per-second thread scan only walks the game's own threads.
- No exclusive core reservations on PCs with fewer than 20 CPU threads;
  P-core pinning only on hybrid CPUs with at least 8 P-core threads.
- CPUs without AVX2/FMA/BMI2 (pre-2013 Intel, AVX-less Pentium/Celeron, AMD before
  2015): Setup/the updater detect this and build an SSE4.1 compatibility version
  automatically (same results, slower). The game also checks the CPU at startup and
  shows a clear message instead of crashing.

1454455680.readme_excerpt:
# inFamous PC

> **Official repo: [github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn).**
> Only download the Setup from the [Releases page](https://github.com/whompay/inFAMOUSreborn/releases) here.
> Forks are not supported, and bugs from forks won't be fixed.

An unofficial native Windows port of **inFamous** (PlayStation 3, 2009, European
release `BCES00220`). The game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code is statically
recompiled to x86-64 C/C++ with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp),
so it runs as a normal Windows program rather than under an emulator.

**This repository contains no game code or data.** You build the game yourself,
on your own PC, from your own copy of the game.

## Easy install

Download **inFamous Setup.exe** from the latest release, run it, choose your
`.iso` (an encrypted image works with its `.dkey` next to it) or your game
folder (the one with `PS3_GAME` in it), pick an install location and press
**Install**.

Setup checks for Python and the C++ build tools and offers to install them,
copies the game out of the disc image, regenerates the recompiled code from your
copy, builds it and adds an inFamous shortcut. Running Setup again on the same
folder updates or repairs the install and only redoes what changed.

## Updating

When a new version is published here, players update in place instead of reinstalling:
**Update now** in Setup (it finds the existing install), the **Update inFamous** shortcut in
the Start menu, or `Update inFamous.cmd` in the install folder. The updater compares every file
with this repository, downloads only what changed, regenerates the game code only if the
port's patches changed, and recompiles only the affected parts. Installs made with an older
Setup need one run of the new Setup on the same folder first.

## Requirements

- Your own inFamous disc dump, European release (`BCES00220`).
- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with Direct3D 12 support.
- A CPU with SSE4.1 (2008 or newer). On CPUs without AVX2 (Intel before 2013, Pentium/Celeron
  without AVX, AMD before 2015) Setup builds a slower compatibility version automatically.
  On PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the game uses fewer threads and less CPU (tested down to 4 threads).
- [Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) with "Add python.exe to
  PATH" ticked.
- [Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/)
  with the **Desktop development with C++** workload and the **C++ Clang
  Compiler for Windows** component.
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), only if your `PS3_GAME\USRDIR` has `EBOOT.BIN`
  but no decrypted `EBOOT.elf`. Setup uses it to decrypt the executable.
- About 10 GB of free disk space and 16 GB of RAM.

## Building manually

```bat
cd installer
cargo build --release
target\release\infamous-installer --game "D:\Dumps\inFamous"
```

`infamous-installer doctor` checks the requirements only. Finished steps are
skipped when you run it again, so an interrupted install continues where it
stopped. See [installer/README.md](installer/README.md) for every step and the
maintainer commands.

## Playing

Run **inFamous** (the shortcut Setup made). It opens a small options window first
(vsync, frame cap, resolution, language and more, saved to `settings.ini`);
**Play** starts the game. The same settings are in the game's pause menu under
**Settings**. Controllers work as on the console, and keyboard and mouse are supported.

**F10** opens the in-game trainer: God Mode, Infinite Energy, Refill Health,
Max Health x2/x5/x10, Add XP, Karma +/-, Kill Enemies / Civilians, Super Speed
and Player Model (play as Zeke, Trish, Kessler, Alden or John). Set `TRAINER=0`
to turn it off.

## DLSS and FSR (optional)

The game can use NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA or AMD FSR for upscaling, and AMD FSR frame generation.
They are not included in the download because NVIDIA and AMD distribute their SDKs themselves,
but both are free and take a few minutes to add.

- **DLSS** needs an NVIDIA RTX graphics card.
- **FSR** works on any modern GPU (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel). FSR 4 needs a Radeon RX 9000 card;
  other cards get FSR 3.1 automatically.

**1. Download the SDK(s) you want.** You need the **source code**, not a Windows or Linux demo.
On the page, click the green **Code** button, then **Download ZIP**. If you go through the
Releases page instead, pick **Source code (zip)**, not the files with "demo" or "samples" in the name.

| For | Download | Rename the extracted folder to |
|---|---|---|
| DLSS / DLAA | [github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS) | `dlss-sdk` |
| FSR and frame generation | [github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK) | `fsr-sdk` |

**2. Put the folder(s) in your inFamous install folder**, next to `infamous-recomp` and
`ps3recomp`:

```
inFamous\
  dlss-sdk\        <- contains include\ and lib\
  fsr-sdk\         <- contains Kits\
  infamous-recomp\
  ps3recomp\
  ...
```

Make sure you don't end up with a folder inside a folder (`dlss-sdk\DLSS-main\include`).
`include` (DLSS) or `Kits` (FSR) must be directly inside.

**3. Rebuild the game once.** Open a Command Prompt in the install folder and run:

```bat
type nul > .installer\update.pending
"Update inFamous.cmd"
```

This rebuilds the game with the SDK(s), which takes a while. Any later update also picks them up
automatically, so you only do this once.

**4. Turn it on in game:** pause, then **Settings**, then **Upscaling** (DLAA, DLSS Quality /
Balanced / Performance, FSR Native AA / Quality / Balanced / Performance) and **Frame
Generation**. The same options are in the launcher's options window. Upscaling and frame
generation apply after a restart.

If the **Upscaling** row is missing, the build didn't find the SDK: check the folder names and
layout from step 2, then repeat step 3.

## How it works

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `ps3recomp` | The recompiler toolkit and runtime: PPU and SPU lifters, HLE system libraries, RSX on Direct3D 12, audio and input |
| `infamous-recomp` | The inFamous-specific parts: program entry, game stubs and fixes, asset tools |
| `installer` | Setup and the command-line installer: reads the disc, regenerates the code from your game, applies `installer/patches`, builds |
| `installer/infamous.toml` | Everything about the game and the port: pipeline steps, generated files, build and launch settings |
| `installer/generated.lock` | Hashes of each generated file before and after the port's patches |

## Credits

- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet and
  contributors (see [ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md](ps3recomp/CONTRIBUTORS.md)).
- [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net), used to decrypt the game executable.
- Sucker Punch Productions, for the game.
- [Lorenzo Aiello](https://github.com/aiellolorenzo23) and [ibrahimpuri](https://github.com/ibrahimpuri), for their support.

1454506174.description: This is a native PS5 build of the PS3 game Soulcalibur II HD Online, made with static recompilation. It runs as an ordinary PS5 homebrew app on a jailbroken console, at 60 fps with full audio. It’s based on the PC recompilation by n0madic and the ps3recomp toolchain, carried over to the PS5’s FreeBSD-based system and Vulkan graphics.
1454506174.readme_excerpt:
Soulcalibur II HD Online for PS5 (homebrew port)

This is a native PS5 build of the PS3 game Soulcalibur II HD Online, made with static recompilation. It runs as an ordinary PS5 homebrew app on a jailbroken console, at 60 fps with full audio. It’s based on the PC recompilation by n0madic and the ps3recomp toolchain, carried over to the PS5’s FreeBSD-based system and Vulkan graphics.

How it’s a port, not emulation

An emulator like RPCS3 runs the original PS3 program as-is. It reads the game’s PowerPC machine code while the game is playing and translates or interprets it on the fly, pretending to be a PS3 the whole time.

This build works differently:

The game’s code was translated before it ever runs. The PS3 executable’s PowerPC code was converted ahead of time into C code. That code was then compiled with a normal compiler into x86-64 code for the PS5’s AMD CPU. What runs on your PS5 is a native program; no PowerPC code is decoded during play.
The Cell co-processor (SPU) programs got the same treatment. The game uses them for sound mixing and other jobs, and they were translated into native code as well.
The PS3’s system libraries are rewritten, not emulated. When the game calls PS3 system functions for audio output, file access, controllers, threads and so on, those calls go straight to new implementations built on the PS5’s own system. There’s no PS3 operating system or firmware underneath, and no PS3 BIOS is needed.
Graphics are translated to Vulkan. The game still builds PS3-style graphics command lists. A renderer reads those lists and draws them with Vulkan on the PS5’s GPU, using shaders converted from the PS3 originals. This is the one part that works like a compatibility layer, closer to how Proton translates DirectX on Linux than to emulating a CPU.

The game logic is the original game’s, translated into native code, and everything it talks to has been rebuilt around it for the PS5. This is also why it can run at full speed where emulating the Cell processor would be far heavier.

What it needs

You must supply your own copy of the game. The build contains none of the game’s data, and it’s for personal use only.

Extract the PPSA77069 contents to your /data directory

copy game files into /data/sc2hd/ on the PS5
  - your game package  UP0700-NPUB31366_00-SC2HDONLINEGAME1*.pkg (Rename it to game.pkg)
  - the 01.01 update package (UP0700-NPUB31366_00-SC2HDONLINEGAME1-A0101-V0100-PE.pkg), if you have it
  - the license (UP0700-NPUB31366_00-SC2HDONLINEGAME1.rap)
The title installs and decrypts them into /data/sc2hd/hdd0 (once; several
minutes), then starts the game.

Status

Story and arcade modes, versus and character select all play at full speed with correct audio and graphics. Online mode isn’t available yet, same as in the PC port.

1454584210.description: Resistance 3 (PS3, BCUS98176) statically recompiled to native macOS/arm64 with ps3recomp. No game data included.

112912d74e759a64accea97524c8267ed1ac995a.message:
Gameplay at ~29 fps under thermal throttling

- tools/rebuild.sh lifts igPm's job loop too (lift_r3_igjobs.py --loop).
  Interpreted, it cleared each job's bss one quadword at a time: 97% of the
  SPU code still interpreted in gameplay, ~20 M steps/s.
- Toolkit patch: a thread that only polls the timebase (2000 reads in a row
  with no guest work between them) sleeps 10 us per further read. The main
  thread spins up to 1 ms on every SPU job wait, which held a core at 100%
  and heated the Mac into throttling. PS3_TB_POLL_SLEEP_US / _CALLS /
  _GAP_NS tune it, 0 turns it off.
- Toolkit patch: SPU_INTERP_PCS=<image> adds the hottest interpreted
  instructions to SPU_INTERP_STATS.

Gameplay in the Haven cellar averaged 28.9 fps over 146 s with the Mac at
thermal state 2 the whole time; it was 18-20 fps in that state before.

- ROADMAP (both languages): a short status at the top, a table of how far
  the game has been played (install, menus, new game, the Haven cellar and
  streets with the Stalker fight, pause, checkpoint reloads; later
  chapters not yet), the day-by-day fixes moved under "Fixes so far, in

2f3ec1cfe13a2572e7b121fad72ce5970e236bf2.message:
Collision: serve the SPU thread local-store window

- CollBroad leaves its candidate list in its own local store and CollNarrow
  GETs it through the SPU thread LS window (EA 0xF0000000 + n*0x100000,
  0xF0007410 here). The MFC read that EA as plain guest memory, so every
  ground probe tested 0 triangles and the player fell through the world.
  spu_ls_window_copy (spurs_policy.c) now serves it from lane n's context;
  probes return 4-18 hits and the camera stays at floor height.
- SPU fast dispatch looks code up with spu_lifted_lookup, so jobs that
  overwrite a policy module run their resident code (regression test
  tools/test_spu_dispatch_residency.py).
- R3_COLL_SNAPSHOT_LR=other: snapshot the first non-CollBroad GET of the
  collision request block, for offline replays of CollNarrow.
- README and ROADMAP: first level playable, campaign not validated yet.

30f153535a95cb50e055110d1e59e21ac63d2d03.message:
Launcher 0.1.1

- The sound output is a list of the Mac's outputs (PS3_AUDIO_DEVICE).
- Sets up the port as of this commit: Haven playable at 30 fps, pause menu,
  collision, checkpoint reloads, pipelines prewarmed between sessions.

3896d42e497da8049540a19c783f944929ef96c0.message:
Port upstream ps3recomp PRs that apply to R3

872b5d6424a940e236e4ca0b6ba830583d735eb8.message:
Revert upstream #757: it invalidated every cached vertex shader

8e234c4505608f67937d16acbc06a24fd5fa6280.message:
RSX thread 45 -> 18 ms a frame in combat: no more depth round trips

  views and returned none when full; in Haven combat (shadow-map

b244c73ad97520f6424829480772f78db6483219.message:
No more 6-24 s reload stalls; recorded pipelines prewarmed at boot

- Toolkit patch, cellGcmSys.c: the FIFO walker, a frame or more behind,
  jumped into chained per-frame lists the game had already reclaimed and
  derailed; its resync then swept memory for fences and never wrote the
  label the game's end-of-frame routine polls (func_0073439C: 2 x 2.5 s
  timeout), hence the 6 s stalls at reloads, and a garbage loop cost four
  5 s circling passes. A shadow fetch follows put from the watcher thread
  and copies each list entered by a JUMP (up to 256 KB) so the walker reads
  the copy (GCM_SHADOW_FETCH); a resync replays the semaphore/label,
  reference, report and flip writes on the real path (GCM_RESYNC_REPLAY);
  the pass budget is counted in words (GCM_FIFO_BUDGET_WORDS);
  GCM_BAD_DMA=resync is available.
- Toolkit patch, rsx_metal_backend.m: every pipeline built is recorded to
  pipelines.rec in the shader cache and rebuilt at boot on utility threads
  into a backend table keyed by what the Metal pipeline is made of
  (PS3_PIPELINE_RECORD, PS3_PIPELINE_PREWARM, PS3_PIPELINE_PREWARM_JOBS).
  Second session: 617 recorded pipelines prewarmed, 1878 requests served
  ready, in-game builds 663 -> 124. MTLBinaryArchive persistence is in
  (PS3_PIPELINE_ARCHIVE) but off: some saves failed whole.
- Toolkit patch, ppu_fs.cpp: PS3_FS_TIMING=<s> times file calls (the
  reload stalls turned out not to be I/O).
- port/main.cpp: PS3_PIPELINE_ARCHIVE=0 by default.
- ROADMAP (both languages).

9-minute run in the Haven fight: no derail, resync or freeze; median
30.0 fps, worst frame 85 ms. 15-minute soak: memory flat at 3.4-3.9 GB.

c53ed64f700d15b83dad4580a1b40c0ca5d1e32f.message:
Shader builds made at once all count against the compile budget

ea6fb342cc89031b7645c8bbf44cd288d41eb277.message:
Gameplay hang: FIFO detour return, bounded engine stores

- Toolkit patch, cellGcmSys.c: R3 runs its level-start NV0039 texture moves
  by detouring an idle RSX through a one-off list (JUMP written at get, a
  JUMP back at the list's end) and frees that list right after setting put
  back. The walker reached the JUMP back too late, read the freed bytes as
  commands, swept the NV4097 register file and bound garbage targets. It
  now remembers the detour's way back and takes it when the word changed
  under it (GCM_DETOUR_RETURN=0 disables). A tripwire logs "FIFO desync

  value (GCM_BAD_DMA=skip also drops the block).

  leaves RSX memory is refused (PS3RECOMP_ENG_STORE_BOUNDS=0 restores):

  game's .bss and corrupted a 64-entry object table, and ~50 s later the
  main thread called through a zeroed vtable and spun forever.

f27aaa3dfbe233f7a0a89ef5a84a54ead9256f9e.message:
igPm jobs over the policy module: reload it, keep interpreting

The loading movie's igBink jobs (queues 3 and 4) are loaded at LS 0x100 and
reach past 0x18000, over igPm itself.

- Toolkit patch:
  - A policy module whose entry bytes no longer match its image is reloaded
    before it is entered again, as the SPURS kernel does when it dispatches
    one. igPm reads constants back from its own image (lqr 0xC00..0xC20); run
    over Bink's code it built a wrong stage 2 and its lane served nothing.
    Only the entry is compared, so wwsjob's state inside its image stays.
  - spu_lifted_lookup applies the same "LS still holds the module" check as
    the dispatcher: the interpreter stopped at every one of igPm's lifted
    entries inside Bink's code and bounced off the dispatcher (two cores at
    100% for under 1 M steps/s); Bink now interprets at ~80 M steps/s.
  - SPURS_PM_DUMP=<s>: pc, status, link register, events and reservation of
    every policy-module context every <s> seconds.
- port/patches.cpp: RES_PEEK_FROM and RES_PEEK_MAX for the memory watcher.

Bink runs but its jobs have not completed within 90 s, so the movie still
stalls; next is lifting the ig job modules (igBink and the rest).

- port/main.cpp: PS3RECOMP_ENG_TEXCACHE_SLOTS=4096 by default. Haven's
  streets use more than 1024 textures, so the engine evicted and
  re-uploaded ~9,500 every 120 frames (~500 MB, frames of 300-800 ms, 6 fps

  background into vertical garbage. Both are gone at 4096.
- Toolkit patch: lines, line strips and line loops are rebuilt into an
  indexed line list bounded by the restart cuts, like triangles
  (PS3RECOMP_ENG_LINE_REBUILD, on). The power lines are indexed line
  strips; passed through as one host strip, each wire joined the next
  across the sky.
- tools/play.sh: the RES_DEBUG summary greps the log as text (-a); the log's
  "(R)" made grep call it binary and the summary came out empty.

fed0f610294f2beb8969dd05478300c45b481340.message:

1454584210.readme_excerpt: # Resistance 3 — static recompilation for PC (macOS) 🌐 **English** · [Português (BR)](README.pt-BR.md) A native port of **Resistance 3** (PS3, disc `BCUS98176`; the European disc is `BCES01118`) to **macOS/arm64**, built with static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C/C++ and compiled into a native executable, with graphics on Metal. It is not an emulator. The third port in the series, after the author's [Resistance: Fall of Man](https://github.com/erikomis/resistance-recomp) and [Resistance 2](https://github.com/erikomis/resistance2-recomp) ports, on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Resistance 3 is the same Insomniac engine three years on, so this port starts from the Resistance 2 port's toolkit patch, scripts, runner and launcher. See [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md). > [!WARNING] > **Playable at the start of the campaign; not validated past it.** Install, > menus, a new game, the Haven cellar and the Haven streets (including the > Stalker fight) play at the game's 30 fps; later chapters have not been > played yet. How far it has been played and what comes next are in > [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). > > **This repository contains no game data, no firmware, no Sony keys and > nothing translated from them.** Everyone generates all of that locally from > their own legitimate copy. A fan project, not affiliated with Sony > Interactive Entertainment or Insomniac Games. ## Status As of 2026-11-13: the 01.00 disc is lifted and built. HDD installation, movies, menus, New Game / Continue, the Haven cellar and the Haven streets work, with collision, the pause menu and checkpoint reloads; the Haven combat holds 30 fps (median 30.0 fps, worst frame ~60 ms), SPU code runs almost entirely lifted, and pipelines are recorded and prewarmed from a binary archive so later sessions do not stall on shaders. The campaign past Haven has not been played yet. Details in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). - The toolkit: ps3recomp v0.17.0 (`a6d76c8`) plus `patches/ps3recomp-a6d76c8-resistance3.patch`, the Resistance 2 patch with Resistance 3 installation, SPURS and SPU adaptations. - `tools/r3_survey.py`, new: identifies the EBOOT by RPCS3's PPU hash (01.00 disc or 01.05 update, USA or Europe), and lists what the earlier ports had to find by hand: the embedded SPU ELFs, the WWS job modules, the relocatable SPU blobs, the Insomniac pieces named in strings (`igInitRawSpu`, `Wws_Job`, Bink), any second executable, and the words the community FPS/FOV patches change. Checked against the Resistance 2 EBOOT (it finds the 3 SPU ELFs, 29 job modules and 142 relocatable blobs that port documents, and RPCS3's hash for it). - The community patches RPCS3 ships for this game ("Unlock FPS" by Whatcookie and boma, "Extended FOV" by illusion) are wired in (`RES_UNLOCK_FPS`, `RES_FOV`), to be generated from the EBOOT. ## How it works The same pipeline as the earlier ports: 1. The disc's `EBOOT.BIN` (a SELF) is decrypted to an ELF (`tools/decrypt_self.py`, keys from RPCS3's public source; RPCS3 itself as the fallback). 2. The toolkit's `ppu_loader.py` finds the functions and imports, and `ppu_lifter.py` translates every PowerPC function to C++. 3. The SPU programs are lifted to C: the SPU ELFs the build finds by itself, the WWS job modules (`tools/regen_r3_jobmods.sh`), and the raw SPU code the survey points at (port-specific `tools/prepare_r3_*.py`, written as they are found). 4. CMake builds that with the toolkit's runtime (HLE firmware libraries, lv2 syscalls, SPURS, the RSX→Metal backend) and `port/` (the runner, the patches) into `build/BCUS98176/ResistanceRecomp`. ## Building from source ### What you need - An Apple-silicon Mac (macOS with Metal). - Your own **Resistance 3 disc** (`BCUS98176`), dumped to an image and mounted, or extracted to `game/BCUS98176/` (the folder that holds `PS3_GAME/`). For the European disc set `RES_TITLE_ID=BCES01118`. - The Xcode Command Line Tools. Everything else (CMake, Ninja, Python, SDL2, glslang, SPIRV-Cross, SPIRV-Tools, FFmpeg) is installed without Homebrew by `tools/install.sh` (`tools/bootstrap_deps.sh`), or from Homebrew: ```sh brew install cmake ninja sdl2 glslang spirv-cross spirv-tools ffmpeg python@3.12 ``` ### Building ```sh git clone https://github.com/erikomis/resistance3-recomp.git cd resistance3-recomp tools/install.sh # deps, toolkit, venv, decrypt, survey, analyse, lift, spu, build ``` or, with the tools already installed, `tools/rebuild.sh`, whose steps run alone by name too (`tools/rebuild.sh survey`, `tools/rebuild.sh lift build`): | Step | What it does | | --- | --- | | `toolkit` | `tools/setup_toolkit.sh`: clones ps3recomp to `./ps3recomp`, checks out `a6d76c8`, applies the patch | | `decrypt` | `EBOOT.BIN` → `game//EBOOT.elf` (and `PARAM.SFO` beside it); `RES_EBOOT_BIN=<path>` decrypts another one, e.g. the 01.05 update's | | `survey` | `tools/r3_survey.py` → `out/survey/<title>.txt` and `.json` | | `analyse` | `ppu_loader.py` → `analysis/<title>/` | | `lift` | `ppu_lifter.py` → `recompiled/<title>/` (24 chunks; `JOBS` limits parallelism), with `port/patches/eboot_<version>.insn.json` when it exists | | `spu` | `tools/regen_r3_jobmods.sh` and every `tools/prepare_r3_*.py` → `port/spu/` | | `build` | CMake + Ninja → `build/<title>/ResistanceRecomp` and `build/<title>/Resistance` | The disc is found through `PS3_VFS_ROOT`, `game/<title>/PS3_GAME`, or a volume under `/Volumes` whose `PARAM.SFO` names the title (`tools/env.sh`). ### The 01.05 update RPCS3's community patches exist for both 01.00 (the disc) and 01.05 (the last update). To port the update's executable, install the update in RPCS3 and point the decrypt step at its EBOOT: ```sh rm -f game/BCUS98176/EBOOT.elf RES_EBOOT_BIN=~/Library/Application\ Support/rpcs3/dev_hdd0/game/BCUS98176/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN \ tools/rebuild.sh decrypt survey analyse lift spu build ``` ### The FPS and FOV patches Once the EBOOT is decrypted: ```sh tools/r3_survey.py game/BCUS98176/EBOOT.elf --write-insn port/patches tools/rebuild.sh lift build ``` writes `port/patches/eboot_<version>.insn.json` (the code words, lifted in both forms) and `eboot_<version>.words.h` (the original words `port/patches.cpp` checks, and the data words it writes). Then `RES_UNLOCK_FPS=1` and `RES_FOV=0.7` work with `tools/play.sh`. ## Playing The launcher in [`launcher/`](launcher/README.md) installs, rebuilds and plays without a terminal (it is the Resistance 2 port's, renamed). From a terminal, with the disc mounted and a controller connected: ```sh tools/play.sh ``` Saves, the HDD folders and the log (`last.log`) live in `~/Library/Application Support/resistance-recomp-3/` (`RES_DATA`). ### Environment | Variable | Effect | | --- | --- | | `RES_TITLE_ID` | `BCUS98176` (default) or `BCES01118` | | `PS3_VFS_ROOT` | the folder holding `PS3_GAME/` | | `RES_EBOOT_BIN` | the `EBOOT.BIN` the decrypt step reads | | `RES_DATA` | saves, HDD folders and the log | | `RES_DEBUG=1` | bring-up diagnostics (interpreted SPU code, SPURS policy modules, hot firmware calls, where SPU code is loaded from) and, on exit, `logs/summary-<time>.txt` with the lines that matter | | `RES_UNLOCK_FPS=1` | "Unlock FPS"; the frame rate follows the vblank rate (`PS3_VBLANK_HZ`, default 62.5; patch.yml advises against more than 60–75) | | `RES_FOV=<f>` | "Extended FOV" (RPCS3's value is 0.7) | | `RES_HTTP_POLL_COMPAT=0` | `cellHttpClientPollConnections` back to the toolkit default (carried from Resistance 2, where the default made the HTTP thread spin) | | `PS3_GAMEDATA_MARKERS` | the files whose presence means the first boot's HDD install is done (`:`-separated, relative to the game-data folder); the default is Resistance 2's pair | The runner keeps Resistance 2's defaults (SPURS kernel-style scheduling, `sys_lwcond` events, a 50 µs RSX wake-up, stereo with a limiter); each has a switch to turn it off for comparison, documented in `port/main.cpp` and `tools/play.sh`. ## Updating the toolkit patch Change the toolkit in `./ps3recomp`, then: ```sh tools/export_toolkit_patch.sh ``` regenerates `patches/ps3recomp-a6d76c8-resistance3.patch` from it (never exporting game-derived files) and checks it applies to a clean `a6d76c8`. ## Layout | Path | What | | --- | --- | | `port/` | the runner (`main.cpp`), patches and hooks (`patches.cpp`, `stubs.cpp`), `CMakeLists.txt` | | `port/patches/` | generated FPS/FOV patch words (`tools/r3_survey.py --write-insn`) | | `patches/` | the toolkit patch | | `tools/` | install, rebuild, play, survey, SPU and toolkit scripts | | `launcher/` | the desktop app (Tauri) | | `game/`, `analysis/`, `recompiled/`, `build/`, `out/`, `ps3recomp/` | generated locally, never committed | ## License MIT; see [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md).

1454599891.description: A native Windows port of God of War: Ascension (PS3) by static recompilation on ps3recomp. No game files included.

001fe21beabd2b1bbc7bb22e560216af53a92839.message:
Ultrawide: the title's cameras at the screen's width (display.ultrawide)

Widens the aspect and the half-widths of the perspective and orthographic cameras by the same factor, so the vertical view stays and more shows at the sides. The camera controller keeps 16:9. Off by default.

0059cc2162832efe2f9690e1b156784452625783.message:
launcher: show progress while preparing the game, fetch RPCS3 in pieces

Download with WinHTTP instead of URLDownloadToFile. Four connections take
2 MB pieces, so a slow route only costs its own piece. A connection that
goes quiet or falls far behind the rest is dropped and its piece resumes
where it stopped; 30 s with no data at all ends the download. Every piece
is asked for at the release address, since the links it redirects to run
out within minutes.

The System tab shows each stage with a bar, speed, time left, reconnects,
how long no data has come, and a Stop button.

Also find the .rap beside the game when there is no rpcs3.exe, unpack with
a relative path because tar takes no non-ASCII path, and name the missing
VC++ Redistributable instead of failing without a reason.

00a5f5578e2f0071d755cee186db8b4f1965ce33.message:
GOWA_WWS_WATCH/TRACE: the job lists of workloads 2-17

The watch read only RenderJobs, MeshProc, EDGE and RsxSync. It now covers
General6, BatchJobList and RenJobSet too, so a PS3_FTRACE trace shows who
publishes General6's jobs (the main thread, in three bursts a cycle).

00dc77f3df8234903171f96e89409230df18d074.message:
EDGE: skinned jobs on the SPU again by default (no more trails in the prison)

The game draws its skinned meshes twice, a depth pass and a lit pass that
tests EQUAL against it, and never clears the scene's colour. The skinned path
(GOWA_EDGE_SKIN) skins a job in the vertex pass on the GPU, a job it does not
take on the SPU, and takes a mesh's two jobs each on its own: in the prison of
the damned (profile 3's opening) ~45% stay on the SPU. The GPU rounds to
nearest and the SPU toward zero, so where a mesh was split the depths differed
in the last bit, the lit pass left holes, and the frames before showed through
them: Kratos and the walls in trails.

GOWA_EDGE_SKIN now defaults to 0. The prison with FSR 3.1, frame generation
and VSync: no trails. The fight with the same settings, one run each: 27.94
flips/s off against 28.30 on, the later windows 27.05 against 28.30 (the ~4%
the path gave). The note has the search and a failed try at an exact pass.

0190a52f2362f6217fca389c4bf8a09a9c0b499f.message:
Launcher: Graphics card, discrete or integrated

A row in the Graphics tab, with the names of the two GPUs, on a PC that
has two. It asks Windows what the renderer asks, so the name shown is
the GPU the game runs on, and the Ready check follows the choice.

01f84209d18918b0b212275548327ad43a72223b.message: Notes: where shader compiling spends its time

02f34608fb753f134c5602c2f02e89ee4383f851.message:
Make frame generation's cap follow the display

With no Frame rate cap the game is held at half the refresh rate instead of a fixed 30: 60 at 120 Hz. Past 60 flips, the most a PS3 flips, it takes the next even division, so frames keep an even pace: 36 at 144 Hz. graphics.frame_generation_refresh gives the rate by hand.

03f66f8e9fc26570ba24af8607ebe1ba76c21f52.message:
EDGE: leave out what skipped lighting left without a reader

With the lighting stage skipped, the binormals (0xA880's loop) and the
packing of ids 27-30 had no reader: the stage was their only reader, and
the GPU pass writes over the packed bytes. A hook at 0xA928 leaves the
loop out for the lit layout, and the output piece packs bytes 0-23 of a
vertex. If the stage runs on the SPU after all, the binormals run first.
GOWA_EDGE_GPU_LEAN=0 keeps both.

Replay with every skipped stage run late: 10 corpora, 0 differences.
Gate, four runs a side: 22.48 -> 22.96 flips/s.

0760d3b170113fa9cb75ebda3508027e82235744.message: package: read the status of the first changed file right

096408e5e84399f07f7e549c12f408e32954f20b.message:
Runtime: SPU overlay GETs skip the signature scan for data

ps3recomp 07c2a2b9 and its parent d71918df.

0a015a7124800aeda8fed7ebe9a47eb207271048.message:
EDGE vertex transform (0xF538) as native code

The 4x4 transform of a vertex stream, eight vertices a pass in AVX2 with
the SPU's exact float forms, the loop's two-deep order kept (each pass's
loads before the previous pass's stores, pass 0's initial registers
stored too). The last pass runs with the runtime's SPU forms and leaves
every register as the lifted loop does: the job's later code spills some
of them, and the strict replay saw those bytes differ.

The call-by-call check can compare all 128 registers (all_regs); the
transform uses it. 358 replay calls identical, strict replay 0 differ.
Replay: -1.5 to -2% per job. On by default (GOWA_EDGE_NATIVE bit 1024).

0aae8f99e41bb485db6dc05d60efb728238a9f3a.message:
GOWA_MAIN_SLOW: probe of the main thread's own work; it sets ~30% of it

Runtime d0b71071 (g_ppu_icall_hook). At each indirect call the main thread
spins for <percent> of the time since the previous one, waits left out.
+25%: 16.34 -> 15.98 flips/s, +100% (~12 ms a frame): 15.44, so about a
third of its own work is on the frame's path. Plan 2.8: the main thread's
PPU code is not the first lever; EDGE is.

0cd1fdaeabdf33907c07d75bec477c131e5eae79.message:
Rename what a player sees to Ascension-R

The exe, the launcher and game windows, the issue URL and the settings
file. ascension-r.ini starts as a copy of gowa.ini, which is left as it
is. The target and the internal gowa_ names stay, so the objects are not
rebuilt.

0d513a7c89f8cd48ceda897bdbe1ff75a0322bbc.message:
Lift the EDGE code pieces Tisiphone's brothel illusion streams

The room the player recorded fell to 3.5 frames a second: its EDGE jobs
fetch 20 code pieces the list did not have, and the SPU interpreter ran
them at 10-20 M steps a second. Found by replaying the player's recording
with SPU_INTERP_BYSIG and SPU_DMA_RANGE_UNIQ; listed and lifted, the room
runs at 25-27 flips/s in the same replay. The note has the measurements,
and the replay fix in the runtime is in the submodule.

0d5196cd3277a483637486ae770a71ab20933a99.message: ps3recomp: the fs test fixtures link again

0d92c52afe59fad29640849b0b34d582b13cd79f.message:
EDGE job: the hook at the job's entry, and the replay's state mode

The first step of the C job (docs/notes/2026-11-04-edge-host-reference.md):
- gowa_edge_job_ad98 hooks the job module's entry, behind GOWA_EDGE_JOB=1 (off by default).
- It reads the job's input set: the own buffer set, the DMA list's 22 slots, the pieces,
  skinning, the descriptor and the segment header's counts.
- It counts the kinds it sees (GOWA_EDGE_NATIVE_STATS=1) and declines every job, so the
  lifted job runs.
- The 120 gate jobs replay with 0 differences with it on, every input set read.

The fork gains the replay's state compare mode, for a job done another way than its lifted
code.

0d958e1709610e871183750a2941a7a7fbcc14ee.message:
SPU float option; jobcap builds leave the lifted PPU code alone

- PORT_SPU_FLOAT_APPROX (gowa.py build --spu-approx): the lifted SPU code
  with SPU_FLOAT_APPROX, which keeps the host's -0 where the SPU has +0.
  Off by default: the lifted SPU code stays bit-exact.
- PS3_SPU_JOBCAP now reaches only the runtime library and the lifted SPU
  code. On the lifted PPU code's command line it changed nothing in that
  code but rebuilt all of it at every switch of --jobcap (446 steps, about
  16 minutes); a switch is now the runtime and the SPU code.
- gowa.py build -D VAR=VALUE passes another CMake cache setting.
- Runtime update: leaner SPU single-precision forms (bit-identical;
  General6 jobs -20%, EDGE -14% on the replay), SPU_FLOAT_APPROX, and the
  replay's classes of differing output words.

0dc2cfbadde878eb3b8196ccafa41fd3f93f79ad.message:
Rendering accuracy step 3: runtime update, progress

Runtime update to fork 531d2252: fragment programs read their constants
from b1 again and are read to their end, each draw's b1 slot sized to its
program; a new texture takes over an idle one's resource; no shader blob
is shared between threads; the shader caches replace their least
recently used entries; audio ring and texture upload diagnostics;
SPURS_BOOST_WID.

In a minute of the first level no program is compiled and no draw is
skipped, the red bands are gone, and the heap corruption that ended 8 of
15 runs (d3dcompiler_47 blobs shared by the shader workers and the drain
thread) did not come back in 8. Level: 11.4-11.9 flips/s, against
10.4-10.6 after step 2.

102b78860eedba5476f62faa5d7e9554f16644c9.message:
EDGE skinning in the vertex pass the SPU's way, bit for bit; the path on again

The game draws a skinned mesh twice, a depth pass and a lit pass that tests
EQUAL against it, and either job may be skinned in the vertex pass or on the
SPU. With the GPU's rounding the depths differed in the last bit and the lit
pass left holes (the trails in the prison of the damned), so the skinned path
had been turned off this morning.

The pass now works the rows and the position out with the SPU's fm and fma
done in 32-bit integer operations: mantissas multiplied exactly, a 64-bit
window with a sticky bit, the result cut toward zero, denormals as zero, a
zero +0. The same code in C (tests/native/skin_fma_test.c) matches the x86
FMA under the SPU's MXCSR over 160 million operations. In the shader as
loops: written out, FXC took ten minutes over it.

GOWA_EDGE_SKIN is on by default again. With FSR 3.1, frame generation and
VSync: the prison has no trails; the fight, ABBA, 29.52/29.92 flips/s on
against 27.36/27.91 off (~+7%, at the 30 cap). Fork 7099ab74 compiles the
pass in the background and keeps it in the shader cache.

10336b43925c1cd9fb48b7489cd438222bd8d9b8.message:
Add a Cheats tab: infinite health and one hit kill

Both hook the title's damage: func_00087440 takes all of it, and func_00156680 and func_00154460 know the attacker. A creature's controller tells Kratos, enemies and the level's props apart, and the props stay out of one hit kill because a script may need them alive. Both are off by default. Tried in one scripted fight: Kratos stays at 100, and each parasite falls to one hit instead of three.

104ed02dc25b695ffdc321bbef249dd9ddeb1c52.message:

29f6a5d82a698e88948bd26bd5ab94ea161b555c.message:
RPCS3 against the port at the job level: the SPURS contention is lost

scripts/guestscope.py reads the title's SPURS instance and its Wws ticket
rows from outside a process, RPCS3 or the port alike, and reports SPUs per
workload, jobs per list and EDGE jobs per contention level.

Both run the same jobs a frame. RPCS3's EDGE phase is 27.6 ms of its frame,
the port's 52.8: about the whole difference. The causes, measured:
- the title's maximum contention (5-8 SPUs a workload) is the ninth argument
  of _cellSpursWorkloadAttributeInitialize, on the stack; the HLE writes 1;
- the port's kernel picks round robin, takes one from the ready count at each
  pick and never makes a polling policy module yield; RPCS3's keeps EDGE
  (priority 3) on four SPUs 86% of its time;
- an EDGE job takes ~1.4 times as long at any contention, a Batch job ~8.

With only the maxima raised, General6 and RenderJobs run on 4 SPUs
(39.6 -> 11.1 and 26.4 -> 7.7 ms a frame) but starve EDGE, and the frame
rate stays. The note gives the order of work; the plan gets section 2.10
and two 2026-10-28 conclusions are marked overturned.

EDGE: the second fixed-point decoder as native code, the first paired

304A0 (piece 0x758590) is the decoder that also reads four table entries
by decoded indices and rebuilds two third coordinates as

30310 now does two iterations with each 256-bit op where every store of
the call misses every quadword its fetches read, checked once a call; the
one-vertex form runs elsewhere. 14.2 -> 12.3 ns an iteration. Bit 16.

outputs forced onto the records and the table; 21 mutants are caught.

564751bee846a79aba720809bbc4a02d804ad85e.message:
Rendering accuracy: what is wrong, why, and the plan

Measured against RPCS3 (a screenshot of the main menu, and its settings
for this title read, not changed: Write Color Buffers on, Disable MLAA
and Disable Mesh Trimming on), with whole-frame captures and one switch
per run:

- The main menu's flicker is the title's MLAA path: its SPUs smooth a
  copy of the frame that is stale here, and draws read that copy when
  no GPU snapshot of it is found. MLAA off: the change from frame to
  frame drops from 6.5 to 1.4 and grows with the lag, as a slow scene's
  does. Depth of field, the texture cache, render target feedback: no
  effect.
- The opening cinematic's blocks are of two kinds: stale rectangles
  with MLAA on (the same copy, read with no or a mismatched snapshot),
  and a band across a frieze with MLAA on or off that starts in the
  screen-space shadow mask, made within the frame by 358 passes with
  depth bounds and stencil tests.
- Some textures decode wrongly (rainbow stripes, a blue patch), with
  MLAA off and the texture cache off; the suspects are the component
  remaps and the swizzled float formats the cinematic samples.
- The picture is ~19% darker than RPCS3's, shadows -36%, highlights -6%.
  Not a setting (the system save is RPCS3's), not the sRGB pairing (every

5b170052182bf91bd9f7d81cc5652cd07eebaf86.message:
EDGE: e77C8's jobs start with no memo state (the Grotto freeze)

The EDGE native code keeps a job's state per thread, the memo of kept
results. e6D98's entry empties it and the hooks in e6D98's functions
fill it, while the hooks on the position-independent pieces read it,
and both EDGE modules call those pieces. Nothing emptied it for the
other build, jobmod_9b03908f93a9_e77C8, which the Grotto runs: a job of
it started with what the last e6D98 job on its thread had left. With a
kept result's state, the vertex piece's hook gave that result up and ran
the calls it had left out, e6D98's functions by name, on this job's
local store, leaving r0 as the last of them had it; the piece returned
there, into an epilogue that took r81-r83 from the piece's frame. That
is issue #7's register dump: the object pointer in r81 was the piece's
pattern, and the job branched to nowhere.

e77C8's entry (0xB7C8) now empties the state as e6D98's does, and
edge_memo_revoke never runs e6D98's calls in a job of another module.
On the reporter's save and replayed session: before, 12,652 of 1.57 M
calls into the memo from those hooks found another job's state, and that
run froze; after, 0 of 3.1 M, and no freeze in three runs. The Megaera
fight: the memo's hits as before.

EDGE: keep job results across frames

meshes every frame, in the depth pass and the lit pass. The end of 0x9990

job whose stage runs on the SPU after all gets its arrays made late.
GOWA_EDGE_MEMO=0 turns it off, =2 checks every hit against the stages.

Check in the game: 4.5 M hits at the gate and in the fight, no list and no
vertex different. Replay of ten corpora: 0 differences, with results on too.

7e3c5e2f8f3623ac7d5c258abc39fb652559c0c0.message:
Notes: EDGE job inputs, slot by slot

Mapped from the 120 gate jobs and 160 consecutive jobs, with a replay that logged every
local-store load and store of the job module and the pieces by function.
- How inputs arrive: two buffer sets, the next job's set fetched while a job runs. The job
  module keeps the previous job's set at 0x10918; laid out from that, all 120 gate jobs'
  pieces match the executable.
- The DMA list has 22 fixed slots (light set, three pieces, index and vertex streams, skinning
  palette and weights, segment header, formats, view block, matrix), each with its readers.
- The descriptor's words: ring base, hole EA, matrix count, frame counter, attribute slot
  list, fragment program and constants block EAs and sizes, screen size.
- The light set's header and arrays, and which lights each lighting routine takes.
- The vertex formats: the output types are the RSX's, the input adds fixed point and 3-byte
  unit vectors. The slot list picks the emitted attributes; that gives the hole's vertex
  arrays in 278 of 280 jobs.
- The segment header slot vs. the context copy: the job fills in the hole size, the format
  numbers and the vertex count rounded up to 8.

This replaces the earlier element table, which was read by position and with the capture
header taken as 48 bytes (it is 56).

a3d62d58979eb695e290a3fbcc122c607aaeefb2.message:
SPU code generation: the level's profile and the design

Profile of the six SPU workers on the first level by workload and operation, and x86 instruction counts of the hottest lifted functions under four codegen variants. Every float operation is compiled in both its round-toward-zero and its exact form and chosen at run time; choosing at compile time halves the float-heavy code bit for bit, approximate float halves it again, while SPU registers in locals done plainly makes it larger. Steps in order: compile-time float form, job modules with --merge-chunks, an approximate float option, LS accesses without the diagnostic gate, cheaper transfers, then registers in locals where barriers sit in loops.

a97617bd6eef7845d393ee3e7f0f6541e389e68e.message:
EDGE lighting loops: a fast pass with one range test a call

The two lighting loops (0x7BB4, 0x7ED8) tested every op's result for the
native range (and, compare, movemask, branch, then +0), which made the
native loops barely faster than the lifted ones. Now a call runs fast
first with no test per op: under round-toward-zero an exact result beyond
FLT_MAX sets MXCSR's overflow flag, and operands with the SPU's exponent
255 are looked for in what the ops read (the constants and carried values
once, the loaded quadwords each iteration). Either one redoes the call
with the exact forms from the same start; the stores of the fast pass go
only to output arrays apart from everything read. A zero's sign never
changes a non-zero result of these ops, so +0 is applied where values
leave (stores, registers).

GOWA_EDGE_EXACT=1 forces the redo (to test the exact pass). Strict replay
0 differ both ways. Replay, the lit jobs: 100.3 -> 88.0 us (-12%).

aa60d2e2d2c0c5c7a190030a4b1290cef3ad6bd6.message:
EDGE's vertex unpacking (piece 0x75BD10) as native code

The lit jobs' vertex stream is 18-byte records: x y z, then a 48-bit code. The code holds two
unit vectors (attributes 3 and 4), each as two 10-bit components and a 4-bit pattern index.
The third component is a square root by frsqest and fi. The pattern, one of 12 the piece
writes to its frame, gives that component's place and sign and a handedness w. An index
past 11 reads the caller's stack; those pairs are done with the piece's own operations.

The format was mapped with a bit-exact model of the probed calls. The routine also leaves what
the piece leaves: the list and table entries, the frame's patterns, two zero quadwords past
two arrays, r1 and r3.

Checked identical in 188,416 calls in the game and by strict replay. The lit jobs: -6% in
replay. Gate, ABBA: 17.95 -> 17.91 flips/s, within the spread.

EDGE: the skinning loop as native AVX2 code, 15.88 -> 16.06 flips/s

(e8f44fbc6dbf): matrix-palette skinning, two vertices an iteration, now in
one 256-bit register so each blend or transform is one op for both. The
float ops are native under the SPU code's MXCSR with the +0 rule, checked

range, and the last one, run in the lifted loop from the registers as it

loop's invariant registers (masks, 1.0, 1/255) are the ones it was written
for.

Notes: design for a C implementation of the whole EDGE job

  with their arguments.
- Where the time goes, measured in the game at the gate. A position-only job is 35.8 us
  (natives 8, the job manager 10.5, glue ~17); a lit job is 113 us (natives 57, the job
  manager 12, glue ~42).

  hole's NOP data, which are stale local store.
- The state a job reads that is not its input.
- What the strict replay compares.

The design: one core on a local-store image in the job's own layout, calling the existing
natives. It is used in the SPU job, in the replay (a new compare mode), and later as step 3's
oracle. It is built bottom-up, glue function by function, with the rare kinds and ring wraps

d720ed90130e132ffa89afaba2c633dd5481d0f6.message:
EDGE: skinned jobs from kept inputs, skinning in the vertex pass (GOWA_EDGE_SKIN)

A skinned job's vertexes, weights and indexes are the same every frame; only the
palette changes. So its key leaves the palette and the matrix out, and a hit skips
the decoding, 0xE550 and the packing: the job hands the palette to the vertex pass
with its record, and the pass works out position, normal and tangent before it
lights them. A position job gets a record too.

Revoking a hit puts the kept arrays back and runs 0xE550 after all. A job that
goes on to 0xF538 stays on the SPU: no skinned job at the gate or in the fight does.

GOWA_EDGE_SKIN=2 compares every job with spu_edge_gpuskin.c's CPU version. In the
fight, 565 million vertexes: positions bit for bit, tangents at most a unit off,
98.4% of the normals within 2 units of 32767.

Two runs a side, one executable name: gate 28.84 -> 29.98 flips/s, at the game's 30
in half of its windows; warm fight 26.16 -> 27.39. Job outputs identical on the
replay lists, where it is off. The gate's picture right with every draw on the
CPU fallback and with 925 refills of the resident part.

Also: a result the output stage cannot leave out of the ring now goes out whole.
Before, the packing could still leave all but 16 bytes out.

e7312e3b7ac6b13b11b598da328c11e14ce7499d.message:
Re-kick a stranded EDGE job list: the menu-start freeze

About one run in fifteen froze right after the opening movie, the RSX
standing at the first hole of one EDGE job list for good. The main thread
kicks an EDGE list when the MeshProc batch counter (0xA0B724) reaches 0,
and re-arms that counter for the next frame's list right after. When the
re-arm came before the kicked list's policy module had read its first
wait, the module saw the new count and went idle; the next zero kicked
the next list, and nothing kicked the first again.

wws_rekick, the park stall hook (GCM_PARK_STALL_MS=100 by default),
signals an EDGE list whose next entry is a wait already met, on a
workload nothing runs or has asked for. Interleaved A/B on one binary:
2 of 22 runs froze without it, none of 22 with it. The level's speed is
unchanged (19.65 -> 20.27 flips/s, two runs each, within the spread).

The park dump now covers every workload, marks a list a main-thread wait
would still wait for, and shows the job descriptors, the batch counters,
the MLAA block and barriers, and the guest threads. SPU_SIG_RING_DUMP_S
prints it at a set time, for a stall without a park.

A rarer stall during the opening movie (3 of the first 43 runs with the
fix, none in the 74 after) is open; the note has what is known.

  leave the last pass that copies, and those after it, to the lifted loop.

  registers and the whole local store: 378 calls of 0xE550 and 1719 of
  0x88B0 in replay, 90,114 and 413,696 in the game, 0 differences; 1720
  replayed jobs, 0 differences.

f9259bac0437b9b8879b3fb9aeb1fb21bbb2b7f1.message:
EDGE natives: order the MXCSR flag reads against the fast ops

The compiler takes the float ops for pure and moved some of them across a
plain _mm_getcsr: in the game the vertex pass (0xD250) stored FLT_MAX
where the SPU saturates to 0x7FFFFFFF in 6923 calls, its overflow flag
read before the op ran. The flags now go through volatile asm (ldmxcsr,
stmxcsr with a memory clobber), ordered by the values they carry: the
pass's register inputs come out of an empty asm after the clear, its
results go into one before the read.

The transform and the vertex pass read the flags once a call when their
output is apart from their input, and redo the whole call exact when they
show; in place, once a pass as before.

GOWA_EDGE_VERIFY=1 also checks each fast call of the two lighting loops
against the exact pass from the same start.

Checked in the game: the transform 1.13M calls, culling 414K, point lights
352K, the lighting loops' self-check, all identical; strict replay 0
differences both ways. Gate, ABBA: 15.34 -> 15.94 flips/s (+3.9%) over
main.

fef5ac98bd8fcf77b8dccb95efebd527f3ba0a55.message:
EDGE's index decompression (0xE4D0 -> 0xDCC0) as native code

Every EDGE job decompresses its triangle indices in place. The format, mapped stage by stage
from snapshots at each loop head and checked with a model of the whole local store:
- an 8-byte header (reuse count, delta bias, bitmask bytes, bits a reuse);
- a bitmask, 2-bit triangle codes, then k-bit reuse values.

The stages:
- the reuses are eight interleaved running sums of the k-bit deltas;
- the bitmask picks a reuse or the next new vertex for each slot of the vertex sequence;
- each triangle code is a fresh triangle of three sequence values, or a turn on one edge of
  the triangle before, reversed, with the next value.

The scratch past the indices goes out by DMA, so the routine makes it byte for byte, along
with c + 0x50/0x58, the frame and r3.

Bit reader, a pshufb expand a mask byte at a time, and one pshufb a triangle:
9,154 -> 4,737 cycles a call. Checked identical in 561,152 calls in the game and by strict
replay. Gate, ABBA: 18.14 -> 18.71 flips/s.
