with os.path.relpath, which raises across drives: on a player's PC the Kit is
beside the exe and GOWA_WORK in the data folder, so the Kit on E: with the data
on C: stopped at 'path is on mount C:, start on mount E:'. shown() falls back to
the path as it is; test_kit_paths checks it and that no message takes a work
folder relative to the root.

1454599891.readme_excerpt:
# Ascension-R

[![CI](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
![Platform: Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20x64-lightgrey.svg)
![Status: alpha](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-alpha-orange.svg)

A native Windows port of **God of War: Ascension** (PS3), made by static recompilation with
[ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). The game's PPU and SPU code is translated to x86-64 ahead of time and the RSX
is drawn with Direct3D 12, so no emulator runs while you play.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This repository holds no game files. You build the port from your own copy of the game. See [Legal](#legal).

## Contents

- [Status](#status)
- [Features](#features)
- [Download](#download)
- [What you need](#what-you-need)
- [Building from source](#building-from-source)
- [Playing](#playing)
- [Reporting a problem](#reporting-a-problem)
- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Project layout](#project-layout)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [Legal](#legal)
- [Credits](#credits)
- [License](#license)

## Status

It boots, plays the cinematics and goes through the menus into the levels. It has not been played from start to finish, so expect
problems further in.

- **Game:** God of War: Ascension, digital US release, NPUA80918, version 1.12: the game and its updates 1.04 to 1.12.
- **Platform:** Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. Tested on Windows 11.
- **Speed:** above 30 frames a second in the two scenes measured, a fight of the first level and the gate, on a Ryzen 5 4600H with
  a GTX 1650 Ti and the Smooth preset.
- **Online:** not supported. The port is single player.
- **Downloads:** the Kit, on the [releases page](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/releases). It holds none of the game's code
  and builds it on your PC from your copy.

## Features

- **Launcher:** a ready check, three presets (Smooth, Balanced, Faithful) and every setting below. It finds the game's folder by
  itself.
- **Picture:** internal resolution from 1x to 4x or native, AMD FSR 1 and FSR 3.1 scaling, FSR 3.1 frame generation, SMAA 1x and
  anisotropic filtering.
- **Display:** windowed or borderless, ultrawide, VSync, a frame rate cap, and frame rate and load on screen.
- **Shaders:** a compressed cache, pipelines built before the title, and vertex shaders that can be compiled before you play.
- **Game patches:** switch off MLAA, depth of field, motion blur, mesh trimming or dynamic shadows.
- **Cheats:** damage to and from Kratos, max red orbs, infinite magic and items, infinite rage and double jumps.
- **Controls:** a controller or keyboard and mouse. Xbox and other XInput pads, and through SDL3 the DualShock 4, the
  DualSense, Switch controllers and many others; stick dead zone, confirm button, vibration and controller API settings.
- **Saves:** backups kept before the game writes over a save.
- **Problem reports:** one button makes a zip of the logs, with your paths hidden.

[docs/FEATURES.md](docs/FEATURES.md) describes each one and its setting.

## Download

The [releases page](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/releases) has the Kit: a zip of the program without the game's code.
Its launcher finds your copy of the game, decrypts it with RPCS3 and builds the game's code on your PC, once, in about ten minutes.
There is nothing else to install: the Kit brings its own Python and LLVM. Each release's notes have the steps.

Your copy needs all nine of the game's updates, 1.04 to 1.12, installed in RPCS3 in that order. Each brings its own files:
1.12's is the EBOOT alone, and the archives come with the ones before it. With 1.12 alone the game stops on its first
loading screen.

## What you need

To build it from source:

- Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit.
- A CPU with AVX2 and FMA, and a GPU with Direct3D 12.
- The game, installed in RPCS3 with its license, and its updates 1.04 to 1.12, installed in that order.
- Python 3.10 or later, Git, CMake, Ninja, Visual Studio with "C++ Clang Compiler for Windows", a Windows SDK, and about 20 GB free.
- For the game's movies: an LGPL shared build of FFmpeg with its headers, unpacked under `..\ffmpeg`, for example
  `win64-lgpl-shared` from [BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds](https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/releases).
- Optional, for AMD FSR 3.1: [FSR SDK 2.4.0](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK), unpacked under
  `..\fsr-sdk`.

## Building from source

```
git clone --recursive https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R
cd Ascension-R
python -m venv ..\.venv
..\.venv\Scripts\pip install -r ps3recomp\requirements.txt

# 1. Decrypt USRDIR\GOWA.SELF to GOWA.elf with RPCS3 (Utilities > Decrypt PS3 Binaries).
# 2. Point the project at the installed game. It is only read.
..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py setup --game-dir <RPCS3>\dev_hdd0\game\NPUA80918
..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py doctor
..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py analyze
..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py lift
..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py build
..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py run
```

`doctor` lists anything that is missing. The lift and the first build take about 13 minutes on a Ryzen 5 4600H. `run` starts the
game straight away, with its log in `logs\`.

## Playing

Open `build\Ascension-R.exe`. The launcher checks the game's folder and your setup, and **Play** starts the game.

Shaders are built the first time they are needed, so expect stutter at first. **Precompile shaders**, in the launcher's sidebar,
compiles the vertex shaders ahead of time.

A build from source keeps its settings, logs and shader caches in `build\`, and its saves in `gamedata\`.

## Reporting a problem

**Report a problem**, in the launcher's sidebar, makes a zip in `logs\` beside the settings file, for you to attach to an
[issue](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/issues/new?template=problem.yml). The launcher offers it by itself after a session
that crashed, lost the graphics device, froze or stopped with no reason in its log. `Ascension-R --report [--with-saves]` makes one
without the window.

The zip holds the logs and pad recordings of the last three sessions the game ran in, your settings, the build, your hardware and
driver versions, and Windows' records of crashes and hangs of this exe in the last two weeks. Folder paths and your Windows account
and PC names are hidden. The game sends nothing by itself and no game file goes in. Saves go in only if you tick the box, without
the game's images and sounds.

If no new frame comes for 15 seconds, the log gets what each thread was doing, and again at 60 (`GOWA_FREEZE_WATCH=<seconds>`,
`0` = off).

## How it works

1. `gowa.py lift` translates the PPU code of `GOWA.elf` to C++, and `build` does the same to C for the SPU programs and job modules.
   Both are compiled for x86-64 with clang-cl.
2. The [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) runtime stands in for the PS3: its system calls and libraries, SPURS, the
   file system, audio, pads and save data.
3. The game's RSX commands are drawn with Direct3D 12. Its shaders are translated to HLSL and compiled with DXC.
4. Movies are decoded with FFmpeg.
5. SPU code that was not translated ahead of time runs in an interpreter. The session records it, and the next `lift` adds it.

More detail: [what the game is made of](docs/ANALYSIS.md), [what has been measured](docs/PERF.md), and the
[development notes](docs/notes), one per session.

## Project layout

```
port/          the port: entry point, launcher, game-specific code
native/        hand-written routines for the SPU code that costs the most
scripts/       gowa.py, the pipeline (doctor, setup, analyze, lift, build, run, symbolize), and the bench
tools/         which of the game's imports the runtime answers, shader cache checks, RenderDoc helpers
tests/         tests for the launcher's game search, shader compile guards and native routines
docs/          analysis, measurements, features and development notes
packaging/     text files that go beside the program in a package
third_party/   zlib
ps3recomp/     the toolkit and runtime, as a submodule (fork rigaz29/ps3recomp, branch gowa)
```

## Contributing

Anyone can help: by playing and reporting, or with changes to the port or to the runtime under it.
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) says where help is most useful, where a change goes, and what must never be committed.

## Legal

No game files are in this repository, and none will be. You need your own copy of the game and its license, and you decrypt it
yourself.

What you build from your copy contains code translated from the game. Keep it on your machine: do not commit it or share it.

God of War is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by it.

## Credits

Built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet. The other code and libraries the port uses, among them
FFmpeg, AMD FSR, SMAA, zlib and Zstandard, are listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

## License

The code in this repository is under the MIT License, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). It does not cover the game or anything made from it.

1454621779.readme_excerpt: # God of War: Ascension (PS3) Native PC Port An x86-64 static recompilation port of **God of War: Ascension – Asian Release (`BCAS-25016`, v1.00)** for Windows. The project translates the original PlayStation 3 binary and embedded SPU workloads into native C and C++ using the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) toolchain. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Primary Target:** Asian Release (`BCAS-25016`, v1.00). > **Reference Implementation:** `arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc` (European Release `BCES-01741`). > Per `ANTIGRAVITY.md`, regional separation is strictly enforced: shared runtime components (`ps3recomp/runtime/`, `ps3recomp/libs/`) remain architecture-agnostic, while region-specific PPU lifted code, memory presets, and compatibility overrides live strictly in `src/compat/` and `src/targets/bcas25016/`. PPU function addresses, TOC pointers (`r2`), and descriptor offsets from `BCES-01741` are never blindly copied. ## Architectural Highlights ### Regional Target & Separation - **Target Identification:** `BCAS-25016` v1.00 (validated against decrypted `EBOOT.BIN` SHA-256 hash, segment boundaries, and verified SPU module fingerprints). - **Separation of Concerns:** Shared runtime synchronization (LV2, SPURS kernel/policy, WWS Job PM mechanics, `CellFs`/`FIOS`, audio/video decoders) lives in `ps3recomp/`, while region-specific lifted translation units and symbol maps live in `src/`. ### Dual-Renderer Roadmap (Direct3D 12 + RPCS3 RSX) - **Direct3D 12 (`--renderer=d3d12`):** Native D3D12 command processor reading command packets from the GCM ring buffer with DXGI presentation. - **RPCS3 RSX (`--renderer=rpcs3-rsx`):** Follows the reference `ps3kit` modular RSX pattern (`RSX_VULKAN=1` via `ps3rsx_link()`), sharing unified virtual memory mappings (`0xC0000000` RSX local memory and `cellGcmMapMainMemory` IO ranges). Gated behind `-DGOW_ENABLE_RPCS3_RSX=ON/OFF` to keep core builds MIT-clean (GPL-2.0 when linked). ## How it works Traditional emulators interpret or JIT-compile machine code at runtime. This port uses static recompilation, converting the game ahead of time so it compiles into a normal 64-bit Windows executable: The game binary (`EBOOT.ELF`) is split and translated into eight C++ translation units (`src/gen/ppu_recomp_*.cpp`). Syscalls and OS library calls resolve through high-level emulation (HLE) shims in `src/compat/`. Embedded SPU binaries, including Sony's WWS Job System Policy Module and Edge Geometry code, are lifted into C and execute across host worker threads. The RSX (NV4097) graphics pipeline renders through a Direct3D 12 backend. It reads command packets directly from the GCM ring buffer, handles descriptor binding and pipeline states, and presents through a standard DXGI swapchain. Game data streams through an asynchronous Virtual File System (VFS) mapped to local disk instead of the PS3 Blu-ray drive. The Win32 window message loop runs on its own thread, isolated from the 60 Hz RSX presentation ticker so the window stays responsive even during long file loads. Controller input maps through XInput with keyboard fallbacks. ## Status [View detailed tables and classification methodology](docs/status.md) Firmware coverage measures imported PS3 OS functions against working high-level emulation handlers and offline-safe stubs. Hardware metrics are parsed directly from live runtime execution logs. Speed remains at 0% (not reached) until in-game level gameplay begins. Regenerate the dashboard and status documents with: ```bash python tools/gen_status.py ``` ## Current status | Component | Status | Details | |---|---|---| | PPU code lifting | Working | 19,570 functions across 8 translation units; 17 concurrent guest threads | | SPU / SPURS workloads | Working | 5 lifted SPU images; WWS job policy module running with zero interpreter fallbacks | | VFS streaming | Working | Asynchronous disk streaming reaches ~23 MB/s across 22 archive descriptors | | RSX presentation | Working | Direct3D 12 swapchain presents live-draw frames with active FIFO command processing | | RSX FIFO processing | Working | GCM offset tables mapped, JUMP/CALL validation in place | | FIOS synchronization | Working | Real Win32 event wait queues with FIFO condition variable ordering | | Audio engine | Partial | CellAudio initialized with WASAPI output backend and stubs | | In-game gameplay | Not reached | Boot progression advances through intro loops and title presentation | Technical notes and bring-up logs live in [docs/](file:///C:/IfItWorksItWorks/Project/gowassension/docs/) and [.planning/](file:///C:/IfItWorksItWorks/Project/gowassension/.planning/). ## Requirements - Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) - Visual Studio 2022 (MSVC v143 or `clang-cl`) with C++20 support - CMake 3.24 or newer - Ninja - Python 3.10 or newer - A legally dumped copy of God of War: Ascension (PS3) ## Building from source ### 1. Clone with submodules ```bash git clone --recursive https://github.com/YJuDeAd/gow-ascension-pc-port cd gowassension ``` If you cloned without `--recursive`, initialize them now: ```bash git submodule update --init --recursive ``` ### 2. Add your game files Copy your decrypted game files into the `vfs` folder: ```text vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.ELF vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN vfs/PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO ``` Game assets and executables are not included in this repository. ### 3. Apply upstream runtime patches Apply the required compatibility fixes to the local `ps3recomp` tree: ```powershell git -C ps3recomp apply ../patches/ps3recomp_current.patch ``` ### 4. Compile Build the `ps3recomp` runtime library first, then build the main executable: ```powershell # Build ps3recomp runtime cmake -S ps3recomp -B ps3recomp/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build ps3recomp/build # Build the game executable cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build ``` The output binary is written to `build/gow_ascension.exe`. ## Running Launch the port with the PowerShell runner: ```powershell # Run with Direct3D 12 graphics enabled .\tools\run_port.ps1 -LiveDraw # Interactive mode (no automatic timeout) .\tools\run_port.ps1 -Interactive # Custom resolution .\tools\run_port.ps1 -LiveDraw -Width 1920 -Height 1080 -TimeoutSeconds 30 ``` Default settings can also be edited in `config.toml`: ```toml [video] width = 1280 height = 720 vsync = "on" live_draw = true [input] auto_pad_start = false deadzone = 7849 ``` ## Repository layout ```text gowassension/ ├── .planning/ Roadmaps, phase specs, and verification records ├── analysis/ Function maps, symbol tables, and SPU/PPU triage data ├── docs/ Architecture notes and bring-up progress logs ├── patches/ Patches for the upstream ps3recomp runtime ├── ps3recomp/ Upstream runtime and lifter tools (submodule) ├── src/ │ ├── main.cpp Window setup, thread orchestration, main loop │ ├── boot_main.cpp Alternative boot harness │ ├── hle_extra.cpp Additional HLE handlers │ ├── compat/ Game-specific HLE overrides (GCM, FIOS, SPURS, sync) │ └── gen/ Machine-generated PPU and SPU code ├── tools/ Automation scripts for lifting, testing, and triage ├── twistedmetal/ Reference PS3 port implementation (submodule) ├── vfs/ Virtual file system root for game data └── CMakeLists.txt Root build configuration ``` ## Contributing Pull requests and issues are welcome. A few rules keep the codebase maintainable: - Keep `ps3recomp/` and `twistedmetal/` as read-only upstream references. All game-specific overrides, patches, and shims belong in `src/compat/` or `patches/`. - Never hand-edit files in `src/gen/`. Those are generated by the lifters. If a lifted function needs different behavior, change the lifter script or override the symbol in `src/compat/`. - Automation scripts in `tools/` should be cross-platform Python (`.py`) or PowerShell (`.ps1`). - Compile generated code in Release mode (`-O2` / `/O2`) without full debug PDBs to avoid consuming tens of gigabytes of disk space. ### Where to help right now - Implementing real Win32 condition variables in `src/compat/ascension_hle.cpp` for `sys_lwcond`. The existing stub drops signals, leaving media worker threads stuck. - Translating NV4097 microcode into HLSL to draw the first 3D passes once scenes finish loading. - Optimizing SPU-assisted skinning and vertex buffer decompression in Edge Geometry. - Building a real audio output backend for CellAudio callbacks. ## Acknowledgments Portions of runtime research and compatibility patches are adapted from [gow-ascension-pc](https://github.com/arnaldo-lima/gow-ascension-pc) by Arnaldo Lima & contributors under the MIT License (see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](file:///C:/IfItWorksItWorks/Project/gowassension/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)). ## Legal This is an independent preservation and research project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Santa Monica Studio. This repository does not contain any copyrighted game assets, proprietary Sony code, encryption keys, or disc images. You must provide your own legally obtained copy of the game.

1455348776.readme_excerpt:
# [AS] DiRT 3 — native PS3 port for iOS

A native iOS build of **DiRT 3** (PS3, EU disc
`BLES01548`, version 01.01). The game's PPU and SPU code is recompiled ahead of
time with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) and rendered with
Metal. The project began from the MotorStorm port
(<https://github.com/nossramo/motorstorm-ps3>), which remains the reference for
the shared runtime; everything MotorStorm-specific has been removed here.

This project does not include the game, firmware or generated game code. Use
your own legally obtained copy.

## Status

New port, set up on 12 Nov 2026 from the WRC 5 port's iOS shell and runtime
(which includes the fixes found there: real lwcond waits, SPU event-queue
binding, SPURS LF queue / Task2 / urgent commands, cellFsSt*, callback TLS).
Nothing has been verified on a device yet. The game is known to run in RPCS3
on macOS and iOS, so RPCS3 is the reference when the port diverges. The app
writes a session log you can pull from the device (see *Diagnostics*).

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `DIRT3/` | Xcode project, single iOS target/scheme `DIRT3` (UIKit host, touch/Xbox controls, diagnostics) |
| `port/` | Game runner `main.cpp`, CMake build, `ios/dirt3-runtime-options.json` launch environment, dependency pins |
| `port/recompiled/`, `port/spu/` | Lifted DiRT 3 PPU/SPU code — generated, not in Git |
| `vendor/ps3recomp/` | Runtime checkout — restored, not in Git |
| `patches/ps3recomp-local.patch` | All local runtime changes on top of the pinned ps3recomp commit |
| `game/` | Your DiRT 3 files — not in Git |
| `scripts/build-dirt3-ios.sh` | One-command IPA build |
| `tools/` | Runtime bootstrap, lifting, iOS dependency and Xcode build helpers, diagnostics collector |

## Game files

Place the extracted disc in `game/` so these exist:

```
game/PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO              (TITLE_ID BLES01548)
game/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN
game/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf       (decrypted executable, see below)
game/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/install.nfs, ps3_000.nfs, shaders.nfs.sdat, video/
```

`EBOOT.BIN` on the disc is encrypted. Decrypt it with RPCS3: *Utilities ›
Decrypt PS3 Binaries*, pick `game/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN`; it writes
`EBOOT.elf` beside it. A disc copy keeps the folders read-only, so make
`USRDIR` writable first (`chmod u+w game/PS3_GAME/USRDIR`).

`PS3_UPDATE/` (firmware updater) is not needed. The game data is about 6.7 GB.

## Build the IPA

Requirements: macOS with Xcode (iOS SDK and Metal toolchain), `python3`,
`cmake`, `ninja` (Homebrew).

```sh
python3 tools/bootstrap_runtime.py      # once: vendor/ps3recomp at the pinned commit + local patch
sh tools/analyze_dirt3.sh                # once: lift EBOOT.elf into port/recompiled and port/spu (slow)
./scripts/build-dirt3-ios.sh             # builds iOS deps on first run, then the app and the IPA
```

Result: `output/DIRT3-AnubisSoft.ipa` (unsigned). A full first build takes
roughly an hour; later builds only recompile what changed. Logs go to `logs/`.

To sign during the build instead, open `DIRT3/DIRT3.xcodeproj`, set your team on
the `DIRT3` target, and run the script with `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=YES`.

## Install and run

1. Sideload `DIRT3-AnubisSoft.ipa` with SideStore, AltStore or LiveContainer
   (they re-sign it).
2. Copy the repo's `game` folder into the app's Documents so that
   `Documents/game/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf` exists. Use the Files app
   (*On My iPhone › [AS] DiRT 3*) or Finder's file sharing; for LiveContainer,
   the app's Documents live under LiveContainer's data folder.
3. Launch **[AS] DiRT 3**. The app checks that every file in `PS3_GAME` is
   present with the right size; if not, it offers a folder picker.

Controls: on-screen Xbox-style layout (toggle at the top centre; "3D" shows
analog sticks and L3/R3), or any MFi/Xbox/PlayStation controller.

## Diagnostics

Each launch writes `Documents/logs/performance/session-*/` (`native.log`,
samples, metadata). With the phone connected:

```sh
python3 tools/collect_ios_diagnostics.py --device <UDID> --out logs/device-run-1
```

For an app running inside LiveContainer, pass
`--bundle-id <LiveContainer bundle id> --container-path Documents/Data/Application/<UUID>`.

Launch options live in `port/ios/dirt3-runtime-options.json`. The current
profile keeps two low-cost boot traces (`PS3_SPU_PCWATCH`, thread-local, and
`PS3_EVT_RECV_TRACE`, capped at 60 lines); `SPU_POLLTRACE` was dropped because
its shared counters sit on the hottest SPU channel paths. Remove the rest once
the game boots.

## Changing the runtime

Edit `vendor/ps3recomp`, then run `python3 tools/export_runtime_patch.py` to
update `patches/ps3recomp-local.patch`.

123bf526d26913cdae31ec5b6bc54dbac29646eb.message:
The launcher updates the port from its GitHub releases (Windows)

When the launcher opens it reads the repository's release list -- not
GitHub's "latest release", which leaves pre-releases out, and every
release so far is one -- on a thread nothing waits for, and offers the
newest release above its own version that has a Windows zip with a
SHA-256 digest: "Update to ..." in the footer opens an Update panel with
the release's notes, Install Update and Release Page.

Install Update (src/install/update.cpp): the zip is downloaded into
.update/ beside the program (WinHTTP), checked against the size and digest
GitHub lists, unpacked (install/zip.h, CRC-checked; the '\' names of
PowerShell's Compress-Archive taken), and each file swapped in: the old one
renamed to <name>.old, which Windows allows for the running program and its
DLLs, the new one moved into its place. A failed swap puts back every file
swapped so far; a failed try leaves nothing. game/, gamedata/ and an
existing dod3.ini are never written. The launcher then starts the new
dod3.exe and closes; the new one's first start removes the .old files and
says what it was updated from. The approach follows King Kong
Recompiled's updater (MIT).

Settings > System > Check for Updates (DOD3_UPDATE_CHECK = 0 turns it
off). The Mac's app is replaced another way: compiled out there for now.

Checked: a build acting as 0.4.0 (DOD3_UPDATE_AS) found 0.4.1 on GitHub,
downloaded it, matched its digest and installed it -- the folder then
equal to the 0.4.1 zip file for file but for dod3.ini, which kept the
player's line -- and started 0.4.1. From a local release
(DOD3_UPDATE_API, DOD3_UPDATE_ZIP): the new build cleaned up after itself
and said "Updated from"; a wrong digest installed nothing; a file held
open mid-swap put every file back (1,736 files unchanged).

2e87a0061f01bcc59898b233381bd923b15c3441.message:
Loads: the package loader's reads natively; DOD3_LOAD_LOG; DOD3_PROF on macOS

What a load waits on, measured on the Mac (start-up, New Game -> prologue):
the game thread, running Unreal's package loader. Reads take ~85 us and the
I/O and inflate threads are idle over 80% of a load; the loader is millions
of tiny reads, each a virtual call to FArchiveAsync::Serialize and the
guest's memcpy, both lifted with a page-table test on every load and store.

src/patches/archive_native.cpp, through the function registry (no re-lift):
- FArchiveAsync::Serialize (func_00141420): bytes already in the precache
  buffer, with the read done, are one memcpy; anything else (outside the
  buffer, a read in flight, pages a diagnostic watches, overlap) runs the
  lifted body. Over 99.9% of reads take the native path.
- FLinkerLoad::Serialize (func_0014A32C), which only forwards to the
  archive: straight to the native one.
- FLinkerLoad::operator<<(FName&) (thunk func_0014A62C): index and number
  in one step; an index outside the name map is the lifted one's to report.
DOD3_ARCHIVE_NATIVE=0 turns them off. 1.01 only (eboot.h).

Measured, interleaved runs, with ps3recomp 9b62c14 (one TLS lookup a
virtual call):
- start-up to the title's loading frame: 3.18 -> 2.95 s (fastest of 6
  each; medians 3.32 -> 3.00)
- New Game load span: 1.85-1.91 -> 1.56-1.60 s (3 runs each); its
  blocking frame 406-412 -> 311-312 ms; the 48-package load 27-29 -> 24
  frames
Chapter 0 plays as before (live run, frame grabs).

Tools for the next ones:
- DOD3_LOAD_LOG=1 (patches/load_idle.cpp): the start-up's steps timed from
  the process's launch, each load's span, frames and longest frame, the
  native/lifted read counts, and every frame over 100 ms (handed to the
  profiler's slow-frame report on both platforms).
- DOD3_PROF on macOS (src/os/macos/prof_mac.cpp): the Windows profiler's
  switches and report (DOD3_PROF_TREE, _CALLERS, _REPORT), from inside the
  process: thread_suspend and a frame-pointer walk, names fr

Crash report for an end that raises no exception; the log flushed first

abort(), std::terminate, the C runtime's invalid-argument and pure-call
checks end the process in a fast fail the exception filter never sees: the
game closed with no [crash] line, and a log on disk lost its last 200 ms of
buffered lines with it -- the shape of issue 3's log, which stops mid-boot.
Each now writes "[crash] <what> on thread <name>" with the stack and flushes
both streams before the process goes; the exception filter flushes stdout
too now, not only stderr. One abort() the port has is the lifted libsre
LFQueue push path's assertion trap (src/kernel/spurs_lfqueue.cpp), which
the zlib tasks use while the boot loads its packages.

527495dd5dcdb40857935efe907df16842d910a9.message:
The lifted libsre built with PPU_INLINE_VM too

It includes the game's ppu_recomp.h. Since the ps3recomp v0.18 lifter,
code lifted without PPU_INLINE_VM opens each function with a copy of the
memory model (PPU_MM_SNAP) that only a header from a v0.18 lift defines;
libsre is lifted at build time, the game's header comes from an older
lift, and the build failed. With PPU_INLINE_VM, libsre takes the game's
inline fast path, which falls back to the full accessors wherever they
matter (an SPU's reserved line, the raw SPU window, the diagnostics).

The setup's moves wait out a scanner holding a new file

right after thousands of files are written, a scanner (Windows Defender,

back, the update's and DLC's files, the executable) now tries again for up
to five seconds before it fails.

ps3recomp at 26ca8af: the D3D12 engine records each pipeline state it
builds in cache/dxbc/pipelines.bin and builds the listed ones on
low-priority threads at start-up, so the draw that first needs one no longer
waits a frame or more for the driver's compile (one level, played twice:
1,416 ms of pipeline builds in play without the list, 62 ms with it; 26
draws skipped in play, then 5). And the PPU store-conditional fails, as on
the Cell, when an SPU rewrote its line while it waited for the lock-line
lock: the game's PhysX task queues let about 2,000 such stores through in
four minutes of a battle on four host threads.

tools/shader_cache.py: `build` compiles shader dumps into the bytecode cache
exactly as the engine does (byte for byte the same files), `list` counts,
checks against a cache and merges pipeline lists. The upstream merge changed
the shader text, so the 0.4.0 cache holds only 584 of the 1,494 programs a
sweep of every chapter met; the next release's cache is to be rebuilt this
way, with the list its play-throughs record.

da6a1a510cf4d30c0393f7f16a17add079c3a177.message:
Aspect Ratio: the HUD fitted into the view; 16:10; movies and the title as on that screen

In a view boxed to another shape the HUD's canvas is the view's: moved to
its corner and as big as it is. The HUD lays itself out on 1280x720 whatever
the canvas, so at 21:9 it ran off the bottom of the view. Now
Sqex03GameHUD.DrawHUD hands its canvas to the port (bridge 17) and
src/patches/hud_aspect.cpp makes the canvas's top transform a scale and a
move that put the 16:9 HUD in the middle of the view, as big as fits; the
canvas reports 1280x720 meanwhile, as the HUD's native code places some
things by its size. The markers placed on the view (enemy gauges, lock-on,
talk icons) are mapped back through it in hooks on UCanvas::execProject and
ASqex03GameHUD::CalcTransformPosition, so they stay on their targets. The
30 full-screen layers of the HUD's scripts -- fades, dimming, filters, the
dying overlay, the screen-split effect -- are marked by the script patch and
cover the whole view. A narrower view's room above and below the HUD is
clipped (through the depth, the 2D canvas having no depth test): the HUD
keeps a bar parked above itself there.

The HUD's begin also tells the present the view's shape each frame, and the
setting the screen's (ps3recomp: rsx_present_set_screen_aspect), so that
the title, menus and movies are 16:9 in the middle of that screen: a 16:9
window set to 21:9 shows what a 21:9 screen would.

16:10 is a choice of the setting (and auto takes a window narrower than
16:9): the view keeps its FOV and is taller. The fit only runs when the
setting has boxed the view, so 16:9 is as it was.

1.00 keeps the HUD as it was (the hooks' addresses are 1.01's) and gets the
present's half. Replay regression: 110 of 110 frames identical.

df1c0b49f15cc73df2c64de6f90f3c5a69969912.message:
The setup takes the US PSN release's game package in place of the disc

Drakengard 3 was also sold on PSN in the US (NPUB31251). Its game package,
UP0082-NPUB31251_00-DOD3MAINGAME0000 (1.00), holds the disc's files but for
four: an executable of its own build, COALESCED_INT.BIN as an .EDAT, both
under the buyer's licence, a PARAM.SFO of its own, and a PS3TOC.TXT whose
one line names that .EDAT. The port runs the disc release's 1.01 executable
and reads the config from its update, so neither locked file is wanted.

The setup now takes the package in the disc's slot, checked by the SHA-1 its
footer carries, and unpacks it as the disc is laid out (PS3_GAME/...),
leaving out its EBOOT.BIN and the .EDAT; the file list's line goes back to
the disc's, which makes the list the disc's own (checked by its hash). The
update is the disc release's for either: the PSN release's own 1.01 update
and the European release (NPEB01407, a build of its own) are refused with
what to add instead. An installed game is now told by its PARAM.SFO and
PS3TOC.TXT, not by EBOOT.BIN, which a 1.01 build never reads there.

pkg_extract takes an optional layout naming where each entry goes (or that
it is left out). The setup's pages, README.md, docs/PLAYING.md and
docs/BUILDING.md name the PSN package beside the disc.

Tested: an install from the package with the update and a DLC pack has
8,791 files identical to a disc install's, the others as above; a new game
from it reaches the chapter 1 battle at 60 fps, the settings pages in place
and the config read from the update. The disc installed over it, and the
package over that, each swap the game and keep the update and the DLC.

Motion Blur and Post-Processing set Off stay off (#12)

# Drakengard 3 Recompiled **A native port of the PlayStation 3 game Drakengard 3.** [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/soyjxck/dod3-recomp?include_prereleases&label=release)](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/total?label=downloads)](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/soyjxck/dod3-recomp?style=flat)](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/stargazers) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/soyjxck/dod3-recomp?label=last%20commit)](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/commits/main) [![Open issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/soyjxck/dod3-recomp?label=issues)](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/issues) [![Support on Ko-fi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ko--fi-support-FF5E5B?logo=kofi&logoColor=white)](https://ko-fi.com/soyjack) ![Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-x64-0078D6) ![Linux x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/Linux-x64-FCC624?logo=linux&logoColor=black) ![macOS arm64](https://img.shields.io/badge/macOS-arm64-000000?logo=apple&logoColor=white) ![Direct3D 12](https://img.shields.io/badge/Direct3D-12-5E5E5E) ![Vulkan](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vulkan-AC162C?logo=vulkan&logoColor=white) ![Metal](https://img.shields.io/badge/Metal-147EFB) ### [Download](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) · [Installing](#installing) · [Playing guide](docs/PLAYING.md) [Report an issue](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/issues) · [Build from source](#building) · [Technical notes](docs/TECHNICAL.md) · [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/soyjack)
## Contents - [About](#about) - [Installing](#installing) - [Building](#building) - [Status](#status) - [How it fits together](#how-it-fits-together) - [Legal](#legal) - [Credits](#credits) ## About A native PC port of **Drakengard 3** (Drag-On Dragoon 3, PlayStation 3, BLUS31197) for Windows, macOS and Linux, made by static recompilation of the game's code on the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) toolkit. The game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C++ ahead of time and built into a normal executable, with the PS3's system libraries replaced by native implementations and the RSX graphics by Direct3D 12, Metal or Vulkan. There is no emulation at run time. ![The start of the game, running natively on Windows](docs/images/opening.jpg) **Nothing of the game is in this repository.** You need your own copy of Drakengard 3: the US disc and the game's 1.01 update, plus whatever DLC you own. The installer takes them from there. If this helped you, consider [buying me a coffee](https://ko-fi.com/soyjack) ## Installing What you need: - A PC with Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), a GPU with Direct3D 12 and a CPU with AVX2 (Intel Haswell / AMD Zen or newer), or a Mac with Apple silicon on macOS 13 or newer. About 16 GB of free disk space, 10 GB more for the Japanese voice pack and about 3 GB for the Spanish translation. - Your copy of the game, US release, as either: - the disc (BLUS31197), dumped to a folder or a **decrypted** `.iso` ([PS3 Disc Dumper](https://github.com/13xforever/ps3-disc-dumper) writes one; an image from an ordinary disc tool is still encrypted and is refused), or - the PSN release (NPUB31251): the game's package as a PlayStation 3 downloads it (`UP0082-NPUB31251_00-DOD3MAINGAME0000`, 15.6 GB). No licence files are needed. Other regions, the European PSN release among them, are refused. - The 1.01 update, as the package a PlayStation 3 downloads: `UP0082-BLUS31197_00-DOD3PATCH0000000-A0101-V0101-PE.pkg`. This is the disc release's update; the PSN release takes it too. - Optionally, the DLC packages you own (`UP0082-NPUB31251_00-...`). No licence files are needed. - Optionally, mods: the Spanish fan translation and the DLC Undub (Japanese voices for the DLC chapters), which the launcher installs on its Mods page; see [docs/PLAYING.md](docs/PLAYING.md#mods). Windows: 1. Download `dod3-recomp--win64.zip` from the [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) and unzip it anywhere (not inside Program Files). 2. Run `dod3.exe`. SmartScreen may warn the first time, as the program is not signed: "More info", then "Run anyway". 3. In the setup that opens, add your files (the disc image or folder, or the PSN game package; the update package; any DLC packages) with Add Files / Add Folder, in any order, then Install. The game's files are copied into the `game` folder next to `dod3.exe` (a few minutes). 4. Play. From then on `dod3.exe` opens the launcher: Play, and the game's mods, DLC and settings. macOS: 1. Download `dod3-recomp--macos-arm64.zip` from the [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases), unzip it and move "Drakengard 3 Recompiled.app" to Applications. 2. The app is not notarised, so macOS refuses it the first time. On macOS 15 and later: open it once, then allow it in System Settings > Privacy & Security ("Open Anyway"). On macOS 13 and 14: Control-click the app, choose Open, then Open again. 3. The setup opens as on Windows. The game's files go into `~/Library/Application Support/Drakengard 3 Recompiled`. Linux (x86-64; the Steam Deck included), experimental: 1. Download `dod3-recomp--linux-x86_64.tar.gz` from the [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) and unpack it anywhere you can write to. It needs a Vulkan 1.3 driver (Mesa's RADV, ANV, or NVIDIA's), SDL2 (`sdl2` or `sdl2-compat`; SteamOS has it) and glibc 2.38 or newer. 2. Run `dod3` in the folder. The setup opens as on Windows, and the game's files are copied into the `game` folder beside it. Add Files uses the desktop's picker (kdialog or zenity); without either, `./dod3 --install ` in a terminal does the same. 3. On a Steam Deck: install from Desktop Mode, then add `dod3` to Steam as a non-Steam game to play it in Game Mode. `dod3.log` beside it says what happened if it does not start. Settings (resolution, display mode, frame-rate cap, anti-aliasing, field of view, draw distance, skipping the intro, the keyboard's keys) are in the launcher's Settings, in the game's own Settings menu (Graphics Settings, System Settings, Advanced Graphics and Picture Settings), or in `dod3.ini`. [docs/PLAYING.md](docs/PLAYING.md) has the controls, the saves, the Japanese voices, and what to do if something goes wrong. ## Building The port is built in three steps: the game's PPU code is lifted to C++, its SPU programs are lifted, and the whole is compiled with CMake. Lifting needs the game's executable, so you need your own copy of the game first. 1. **Toolchain.** Windows: Visual Studio 2022 or newer (the Build Tools are enough, with "Desktop development with C++" and the Windows SDK), LLVM with clang-cl, CMake 3.20 or later, Ninja, Python 3.11 or later, Git for Windows, and vcpkg with `zlib:x64-windows` and `sdl2:x64-windows` (`VCPKG_ROOT`, or `C:\vcpkg`). macOS: Xcode's command-line tools and, from Homebrew, `cmake ninja python zlib sdl2 glslang spirv-cross`. Linux: Clang, CMake, Ninja, Python and the SDL2, zlib, Vulkan and glslang development files (Ubuntu 24.04 package names, and the Steam Deck's distrobox, in [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md#prerequisites)). All three also need a decrypted `libsre.prx` from the PS3 firmware ([docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md#the-games-files)). 2. **The sources.** ```sh git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp cd dod3-recomp python3 -m venv .venv # py -3 -m venv .venv on Windows .venv/bin/pip install -r ps3recomp/tools/requirements.txt -r tools/requirements.txt ``` 3. **The game's files.** Any built `dod3` (a release's, or one from another machine) installs the game into the repository root, which decrypts the update's executable to `elf/EBOOT_101.ELF` and lays out `game/disc`: ```sh DOD3_INSTALL_BASE=. path/to/dod3 --install [DLC .pkg ...] ``` 4. **Lift the PPU code** (a few minutes; about 550 MB of C++ in `recompiled_101/`): ```sh .venv/bin/python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_loader.py elf/EBOOT_101.ELF -o out/v101/ .venv/bin/python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_lifter.py elf/EBOOT_101.ELF \ --functions out/v101/EBOOT_101.functions.json \ --hle-stubs out/v101/EBOOT_101.imports.json \ --code-end 0x157fc00 \ --nonvolatile-locals \ --hook 0x000C1E50 --hook 0x00EE7728 --hook 0x00272E58 \ -o recompiled_101/ ``` 5. **Lift the SPU programs** into `spu/`, with the native fast paths hooked in: ```sh tools/lift_spu.sh ``` 6. **Compile.** Windows, from a plain command prompt (the script finds Visual Studio, LLVM, CMake and vcpkg): ```bat tools\build_win.bat ``` macOS: ```sh cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build ``` A clean build takes about 15 minutes, nearly all of it the lifted code. 7. **Run** the game installed in the repository root: ```sh DOD3_INSTALL_BASE=. build/dod3 ``` [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md) has the CMake options, the developer run form, packaging a release and regenerating the committed tables; [docs/TECHNICAL.md](docs/TECHNICAL.md) how the port works; [docs/DEBUGGING.md](docs/DEBUGGING.md) the switches, profiling and the regression tests; [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) the layout of the tree and the conventions. ## Status | | | |---|---| | Windows 10/11, Direct3D 12 | Playable. 60 fps at 4K on an RTX 4090 / i9-13900K (chapter 1 through the heavy destruction scene, open areas, the village); 120 fps holds at lower resolutions | | Windows, Vulkan | Experimental (`RSX_BACKEND = vulkan`) | | Linux, Vulkan | Experimental. Tested on a Steam Deck (SteamOS, Desktop Mode): the chapter 1 battle at 55-65 fps uncapped, the heaviest moments in the 40s; Gaming Mode not yet tried | | macOS 13+, Apple silicon, Metal | Playable. 60 fps at 1080p in battle on an M1 Pro | | Game version | The 1.01 update (required) | | DLC | All 20 packs, including the Japanese voice pack | What the port adds over the original: any internal resolution (supersampling included), windowed, borderless or full-screen display, wider screens (16:10, 21:9, 32:9), a frame-rate cap of your choice (60 and 120 tested) or one that follows the scene, with the frames shown at even intervals, FXAA or MSAA, anisotropic filtering, a wider field of view, sharper shadows, a longer draw distance for scenery and for trees, HDR (Windows and macOS: the light the game clips at white goes up to your display's peak), a depth of field and bloom drawn smoothly at high resolutions, depth of field and the blood on the screen each on or off, skipping the intro logos and movie, pausing or muting when the window is in the background, keyboard and mouse, trophies (a pop-up as you earn one, and their list in the launcher), cheats, and the button prompts of the pad you hold -- set in the launcher, or in a Graphics Settings, a System Settings, an Advanced Graphics and a Picture Settings page added to the game's own Settings menu. The launcher also installs your DLC and two fan-made mods (the Spanish translation, with the added pages in Spanish, and the DLC Undub), and on Windows updates the port from its releases. Known issues: the game has been tested on few machines, and at 16:10, 21:9 and 32:9 some of the HUD is still out of place. ## How it fits together ``` elf/EBOOT_101.ELF --ppu_loader/ppu_lifter--> recompiled_101/*.cpp (the game's PPU code as C++) SPU programs --tools/lift_spu.sh------> spu/ (SPURS tasks, jobs, the audio DSP) src/ ---------------------------> the port: the runner, native fast paths, the settings menu, the installer ps3recomp/ ---------------------------> runtime, HLE libraries, the RSX draw engine and its backends ``` The executable `dod3` installs the game from your files (a Dear ImGui setup, `src/install/` and `src/ui/`), then opens a launcher for its mods, DLC and settings, and runs it. ## Legal This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Square Enix, Access Games or Sony Interactive Entertainment. 123bf526d26913cdae31ec5b6bc54dbac29646eb.message:
The launcher updates the port from its GitHub releases (Windows)

When the launcher opens it reads the repository's release list -- not
GitHub's "latest release", which leaves pre-releases out, and every
release so far is one -- on a thread nothing waits for, and offers the
newest release above its own version that has a Windows zip with a
SHA-256 digest: "Update to ..." in the footer opens an Update panel with
the release's notes, Install Update and Release Page.

Install Update (src/install/update.cpp): the zip is downloaded into
.update/ beside the program (WinHTTP), checked against the size and digest
GitHub lists, unpacked (install/zip.h, CRC-checked; the '\' names of
PowerShell's Compress-Archive taken), and each file swapped in: the old one
renamed to <name>.old, which Windows allows for the running program and its
DLLs, the new one moved into its place. A failed swap puts back every file
swapped so far; a failed try leaves nothing. game/, gamedata/ and an
existing dod3.ini are never written. The launcher then starts the new
dod3.exe and closes; the new one's first start removes the .old files and
says what it was updated from. The approach follows King Kong
Recompiled's updater (MIT).

Settings > System > Check for Updates (DOD3_UPDATE_CHECK = 0 turns it
off). The Mac's app is replaced another way: compiled out there for now.

Checked: a build acting as 0.4.0 (DOD3_UPDATE_AS) found 0.4.1 on GitHub,
downloaded it, matched its digest and installed it -- the folder then
equal to the 0.4.1 zip file for file but for dod3.ini, which kept the
player's line -- and started 0.4.1. From a local release
(DOD3_UPDATE_API, DOD3_UPDATE_ZIP): the new build cleaned up after itself
and said "Updated from"; a wrong digest installed nothing; a file held
open mid-swap put every file back (1,736 files unchanged).

2e87a0061f01bcc59898b233381bd923b15c3441.message:
Loads: the package loader's reads natively; DOD3_LOAD_LOG; DOD3_PROF on macOS

What a load waits on, measured on the Mac (start-up, New Game -> prologue):
the game thread, running Unreal's package loader. Reads take ~85 us and the
I/O and inflate threads are idle over 80% of a load; the loader is millions
of tiny reads, each a virtual call to FArchiveAsync::Serialize and the
guest's memcpy, both lifted with a page-table test on every load and store.

src/patches/archive_native.cpp, through the function registry (no re-lift):
- FArchiveAsync::Serialize (func_00141420): bytes already in the precache
  buffer, with the read done, are one memcpy; anything else (outside the
  buffer, a read in flight, pages a diagnostic watches, overlap) runs the
  lifted body. Over 99.9% of reads take the native path.
- FLinkerLoad::Serialize (func_0014A32C), which only forwards to the
  archive: straight to the native one.
- FLinkerLoad::operator<<(FName&) (thunk func_0014A62C): index and number
  in one step; an index outside the name map is the lifted one's to report.
DOD3_ARCHIVE_NATIVE=0 turns them off. 1.01 only (eboot.h).

Measured, interleaved runs, with ps3recomp 9b62c14 (one TLS lookup a
virtual call):
- start-up to the title's loading frame: 3.18 -> 2.95 s (fastest of 6
  each; medians 3.32 -> 3.00)
- New Game load span: 1.85-1.91 -> 1.56-1.60 s (3 runs each); its
  blocking frame 406-412 -> 311-312 ms; the 48-package load 27-29 -> 24
  frames
Chapter 0 plays as before (live run, frame grabs).

Tools for the next ones:
- DOD3_LOAD_LOG=1 (patches/load_idle.cpp): the start-up's steps timed from
  the process's launch, each load's span, frames and longest frame, the
  native/lifted read counts, and every frame over 100 ms (handed to the
  profiler's slow-frame report on both platforms).
- DOD3_PROF on macOS (src/os/macos/prof_mac.cpp): the Windows profiler's
  switches and report (DOD3_PROF_TREE, _CALLERS, _REPORT), from inside the
  process: thread_suspend and a frame-pointer walk, names fr

pipeline states for the player's driver on low-priority threads at

package; package_win.sh refuses a package that has it.

cache/dxbc; the player guide says the shaders come compiled and that an
update should leave the old cache behind.

The setup's moves wait out a scanner holding a new file

right after thousands of files are written, a scanner (Windows Defender,

low-priority threads at start-up, so the draw that first needs one no longer
waits a frame or more for the driver's compile (one level, played twice:
1,416 ms of pipeline builds in play without the list, 62 ms with it; 26
draws skipped in play, then 5). And the PPU store-conditional fails, as on
the Cell, when an SPU rewrote its line while it waited for the lock-line
lock: the game's PhysX task queues let about 2,000 such stores through in
four minutes of a battle on four host threads.

tools/shader_cache.py: `build` compiles shader dumps into the bytecode cache
exactly as the engine does (byte for byte the same files), `list` counts,
checks against a cache and merges pipeline lists. The upstream merge changed
the shader text, so the 0.4.0 cache holds only 584 of the 1,494 programs a
sweep of every chapter met; the next release's cache is to be rebuilt this
way, with the list its play-throughs record.

da6a1a510cf4d30c0393f7f16a17add079c3a177.message:
Aspect Ratio: the HUD fitted into the view; 16:10; movies and the title as on that screen

In a view boxed to another shape the HUD's canvas is the view's: moved to
its corner and as big as it is. The HUD lays itself out on 1280x720 whatever
the canvas, so at 21:9 it ran off the bottom of the view. Now
Sqex03GameHUD.DrawHUD hands its canvas to the port (bridge 17) and
src/patches/hud_aspect.cpp makes the canvas's top transform a scale and a
move that put the 16:9 HUD in the middle of the view, as big as fits; the
canvas reports 1280x720 meanwhile, as the HUD's native code places some
things by its size. The markers placed on the view (enemy gauges, lock-on,
talk icons) are mapped back through it in hooks on UCanvas::execProject and
ASqex03GameHUD::CalcTransformPosition, so they stay on their targets. The
30 full-screen layers of the HUD's scripts -- fades, dimming, filters, the
dying overlay, the screen-split effect -- are marked by the script patch and
cover the whole view. A narrower view's room above and below the HUD is
clipped (through the depth, the 2D canvas having no depth test): the HUD
keeps a bar parked above itself there.

The HUD's begin also tells the present the view's shape each frame, and the
setting the screen's (ps3recomp: rsx_present_set_screen_aspect), so that
the title, menus and movies are 16:9 in the middle of that screen: a 16:9
window set to 21:9 shows what a 21:9 screen would.

16:10 is a choice of the setting (and auto takes a window narrower than
16:9): the view keeps its FOV and is taller. The fit only runs when the
setting has boxed the view, so 16:9 is as it was.

1.00 keeps the HUD as it was (the hooks' addresses are 1.01's) and gets the
present's half. Replay regression: 110 of 110 frames identical.

df1c0b49f15cc73df2c64de6f90f3c5a69969912.message:
The setup takes the US PSN release's game package in place of the disc

Drakengard 3 was also sold on PSN in the US (NPUB31251). Its game package,
UP0082-NPUB31251_00-DOD3MAINGAME0000 (1.00), holds the disc's files but for
four: an executable of its own build, COALESCED_INT.BIN as an .EDAT, both
under the buyer's licence, a PARAM.SFO of its own, and a PS3TOC.TXT whose
one line names that .EDAT. The port runs the disc release's 1.01 executable
and reads the config from its update, so neither locked file is wanted.

The setup now takes the package in the disc's slot, checked by the SHA-1 its
footer carries, and unpacks it as the disc is laid out (PS3_GAME/...),
leaving out its EBOOT.BIN and the .EDAT; the file list's line goes back to
the disc's, which makes the list the disc's own (checked by its hash). The
update is the disc release's for either: the PSN release's own 1.01 update
and the European release (NPEB01407, a build of its own) are refused with
what to add instead. An installed game is now told by its PARAM.SFO and
PS3TOC.TXT, not by EBOOT.BIN, which a 1.01 build never reads there.

pkg_extract takes an optional layout naming where each entry goes (or that
it is left out). The setup's pages, README.md, docs/PLAYING.md and
docs/BUILDING.md name the PSN package beside the disc.

Tested: an install from the package with the update and a DLC pack has
8,791 files identical to a disc install's, the others as above; a new game
from it reaches the chapter 1 battle at 60 fps, the settings pages in place
and the config read from the update. The disc installed over it, and the
package over that, each swap the game and keep the update and the DLC.

# Drakengard 3 Recompiled **A native port of the PlayStation 3 game Drakengard 3.** [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/soyjxck/dod3-recomp?include_prereleases&label=release)](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/total?label=downloads)](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/soyjxck/dod3-recomp?style=flat)](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/stargazers) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/soyjxck/dod3-recomp?label=last%20commit)](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/commits/main) [![Open issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/soyjxck/dod3-recomp?label=issues)](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/issues) [![Support on Ko-fi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ko--fi-support-FF5E5B?logo=kofi&logoColor=white)](https://ko-fi.com/soyjack) ![Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-x64-0078D6) ![Linux x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/Linux-x64-FCC624?logo=linux&logoColor=black) ![macOS arm64](https://img.shields.io/badge/macOS-arm64-000000?logo=apple&logoColor=white) ![Direct3D 12](https://img.shields.io/badge/Direct3D-12-5E5E5E) ![Vulkan](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vulkan-AC162C?logo=vulkan&logoColor=white) ![Metal](https://img.shields.io/badge/Metal-147EFB) ### [Download](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) · [Installing](#installing) · [Playing guide](docs/PLAYING.md) [Report an issue](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/issues) · [Build from source](#building) · [Technical notes](docs/TECHNICAL.md) · [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/soyjack)
## Contents - [About](#about) - [Installing](#installing) - [Building](#building) - [Status](#status) - [How it fits together](#how-it-fits-together) - [Legal](#legal) - [Credits](#credits) ## About A native PC port of **Drakengard 3** (Drag-On Dragoon 3, PlayStation 3, BLUS31197) for Windows, macOS and Linux, made by static recompilation of the game's code on the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) toolkit. The game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C++ ahead of time and built into a normal executable, with the PS3's system libraries replaced by native implementations and the RSX graphics by Direct3D 12, Metal or Vulkan. There is no emulation at run time. ![The start of the game, running natively on Windows](docs/images/opening.jpg) **Nothing of the game is in this repository.** You need your own copy of Drakengard 3: the US disc and the game's 1.01 update, plus whatever DLC you own. The installer takes them from there. If this helped you, consider [buying me a coffee](https://ko-fi.com/soyjack) ## Installing What you need: - A PC with Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), a GPU with Direct3D 12 and a CPU with AVX2 (Intel Haswell / AMD Zen or newer), or a Mac with Apple silicon on macOS 13 or newer. About 16 GB of free disk space, 10 GB more for the Japanese voice pack and about 3 GB for the Spanish translation. - Your copy of the game, US release, as either: - the disc (BLUS31197), dumped to a folder or a **decrypted** `.iso` ([PS3 Disc Dumper](https://github.com/13xforever/ps3-disc-dumper) writes one; an image from an ordinary disc tool is still encrypted and is refused), or - the PSN release (NPUB31251): the game's package as a PlayStation 3 downloads it (`UP0082-NPUB31251_00-DOD3MAINGAME0000`, 15.6 GB). No licence files are needed. Other regions, the European PSN release among them, are refused. - The 1.01 update, as the package a PlayStation 3 downloads: `UP0082-BLUS31197_00-DOD3PATCH0000000-A0101-V0101-PE.pkg`. This is the disc release's update; the PSN release takes it too. - Optionally, the DLC packages you own (`UP0082-NPUB31251_00-...`). No licence files are needed. - Optionally, mods: the Spanish fan translation and the DLC Undub (Japanese voices for the DLC chapters), which the launcher installs on its Mods page; see [docs/PLAYING.md](docs/PLAYING.md#mods). Windows: 1. Download `dod3-recomp--win64.zip` from the [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) and unzip it anywhere (not inside Program Files). 2. Run `dod3.exe`. SmartScreen may warn the first time, as the program is not signed: "More info", then "Run anyway". 3. In the setup that opens, add your files (the disc image or folder, or the PSN game package; the update package; any DLC packages) with Add Files / Add Folder, in any order, then Install. The game's files are copied into the `game` folder next to `dod3.exe` (a few minutes). 4. Play. From then on `dod3.exe` opens the launcher: Play, and the game's mods, DLC and settings. macOS: 1. Download `dod3-recomp--macos-arm64.zip` from the [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases), unzip it and move "Drakengard 3 Recompiled.app" to Applications. 2. The app is not notarised, so macOS refuses it the first time. On macOS 15 and later: open it once, then allow it in System Settings > Privacy & Security ("Open Anyway"). On macOS 13 and 14: Control-click the app, choose Open, then Open again. 3. The setup opens as on Windows. The game's files go into `~/Library/Application Support/Drakengard 3 Recompiled`. Linux (x86-64; the Steam Deck included), experimental: 1. Download `dod3-recomp--linux-x86_64.tar.gz` from the [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) and unpack it anywhere you can write to. It needs a Vulkan 1.3 driver (Mesa's RADV, ANV, or NVIDIA's), SDL2 (`sdl2` or `sdl2-compat`; SteamOS has it) and glibc 2.38 or newer. 2. Run `dod3` in the folder. The setup opens as on Windows, and the game's files are copied into the `game` folder beside it. Add Files uses the desktop's picker (kdialog or zenity); without either, `./dod3 --install ` in a terminal does the same. 3. On a Steam Deck: install from Desktop Mode, then add `dod3` to Steam as a non-Steam game to play it in Game Mode. `dod3.log` beside it says what happened if it does not start. Settings (resolution, display mode, frame-rate cap, anti-aliasing, field of view, draw distance, skipping the intro, the keyboard's keys) are in the launcher's Settings, in the game's own Settings menu (Graphics Settings, System Settings, Advanced Graphics and Picture Settings), or in `dod3.ini`. [docs/PLAYING.md](docs/PLAYING.md) has the controls, the saves, the Japanese voices, and what to do if something goes wrong. ## Building The port is built in three steps: the game's PPU code is lifted to C++, its SPU programs are lifted, and the whole is compiled with CMake. Lifting needs the game's executable, so you need your own copy of the game first. 1. **Toolchain.** Windows: Visual Studio 2022 or newer (the Build Tools are enough, with "Desktop development with C++" and the Windows SDK), LLVM with clang-cl, CMake 3.20 or later, Ninja, Python 3.11 or later, Git for Windows, and vcpkg with `zlib:x64-windows` and `sdl2:x64-windows` (`VCPKG_ROOT`, or `C:\vcpkg`). macOS: Xcode's command-line tools and, from Homebrew, `cmake ninja python zlib sdl2 glslang spirv-cross`. Linux: Clang, CMake, Ninja, Python and the SDL2, zlib, Vulkan and glslang development files (Ubuntu 24.04 package names, and the Steam Deck's distrobox, in [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md#prerequisites)). All three also need a decrypted `libsre.prx` from the PS3 firmware ([docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md#the-games-files)). 2. **The sources.** ```sh git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp cd dod3-recomp python3 -m venv .venv # py -3 -m venv .venv on Windows .venv/bin/pip install -r ps3recomp/tools/requirements.txt -r tools/requirements.txt ``` 3. **The game's files.** Any built `dod3` (a release's, or one from another machine) installs the game into the repository root, which decrypts the update's executable to `elf/EBOOT_101.ELF` and lays out `game/disc`: ```sh DOD3_INSTALL_BASE=. path/to/dod3 --install [DLC .pkg ...] ``` 4. **Lift the PPU code** (a few minutes; about 550 MB of C++ in `recompiled_101/`): ```sh .venv/bin/python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_loader.py elf/EBOOT_101.ELF -o out/v101/ .venv/bin/python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_lifter.py elf/EBOOT_101.ELF \ --functions out/v101/EBOOT_101.functions.json \ --hle-stubs out/v101/EBOOT_101.imports.json \ --code-end 0x157fc00 \ --nonvolatile-locals \ --hook 0x000C1E50 --hook 0x00EE7728 --hook 0x00272E58 \ -o recompiled_101/ ``` 5. **Lift the SPU programs** into `spu/`, with the native fast paths hooked in: ```sh tools/lift_spu.sh ``` 6. **Compile.** Windows, from a plain command prompt (the script finds Visual Studio, LLVM, CMake and vcpkg): ```bat tools\build_win.bat ``` macOS: ```sh cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build ``` A clean build takes about 15 minutes, nearly all of it the lifted code. 7. **Run** the game installed in the repository root: ```sh DOD3_INSTALL_BASE=. build/dod3 ``` [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md) has the CMake options, the developer run form, packaging a release and regenerating the committed tables; [docs/TECHNICAL.md](docs/TECHNICAL.md) how the port works; [docs/DEBUGGING.md](docs/DEBUGGING.md) the switches, profiling and the regression tests; [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) the layout of the tree and the conventions. ## Status | | | |---|---| | Windows 10/11, Direct3D 12 | Playable. 60 fps at 4K on an RTX 4090 / i9-13900K (chapter 1 through the heavy destruction scene, open areas, the village); 120 fps holds at lower resolutions | | Windows, Vulkan | Experimental (`RSX_BACKEND = vulkan`) | | Linux, Vulkan | Experimental. Tested on a Steam Deck (SteamOS, Desktop Mode): the chapter 1 battle at 55-65 fps uncapped, the heaviest moments in the 40s; Gaming Mode not yet tried | | macOS 13+, Apple silicon, Metal | Playable. 60 fps at 1080p in battle on an M1 Pro | | Game version | The 1.01 update (required) | | DLC | All 20 packs, including the Japanese voice pack | What the port adds over the original: any internal resolution (supersampling included), windowed, borderless or full-screen display, wider screens (16:10, 21:9, 32:9), a frame-rate cap of your choice (60 and 120 tested) or one that follows the scene, with the frames shown at even intervals, FXAA or MSAA, anisotropic filtering, a wider field of view, sharper shadows, a longer draw distance for scenery and for trees, HDR (Windows and macOS: the light the game clips at white goes up to your display's peak), a depth of field and bloom drawn smoothly at high resolutions, depth of field and the blood on the screen each on or off, skipping the intro logos and movie, pausing or muting when the window is in the background, keyboard and mouse, trophies (a pop-up as you earn one, and their list in the launcher), cheats, and the button prompts of the pad you hold -- set in the launcher, or in a Graphics Settings, a System Settings, an Advanced Graphics and a Picture Settings page added to the game's own Settings menu. The launcher also installs your DLC and two fan-made mods (the Spanish translation, with the added pages in Spanish, and the DLC Undub), and on Windows updates the port from its releases. Known issues: the game has been tested on few machines, and at 16:10, 21:9 and 32:9 some of the HUD is still out of place. ## How it fits together ``` elf/EBOOT_101.ELF --ppu_loader/ppu_lifter--> recompiled_101/*.cpp (the game's PPU code as C++) SPU programs --tools/lift_spu.sh------> spu/ (SPURS tasks, jobs, the audio DSP) src/ ---------------------------> the port: the runner, native fast paths, the settings menu, the installer ps3recomp/ ---------------------------> runtime, HLE libraries, the RSX draw engine and its backends ``` The executable `dod3` installs the game from your files (a Dear ImGui setup, `src/install/` and `src/ui/`), then opens a launcher for its mods, DLC and settings, and runs it. ## Legal This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Square Enix, Access Games or Sony Interactive Entertainment. Drakengard 3 and all of its assets belong to their owners; none are included, and the port only runs from a copy of the game you own. The code in this repository is under the [MIT License](LICENSE). It builds on ps3recomp (MIT) and includes Dear ImGui (MIT) and the Inter typeface (SIL Open Font License 1.1); see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). ## Credits - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet: the recompiler, the runtime and the PS3 library implementations. This port's changes to it are in the [soyjxck/ps3recomp](https://github.com/soyjxck/ps3recomp) fork, the `ps3recomp/` submodule. - [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net): the reference for much of the PS3's behaviour, and the source of two techniques used here (write-watched texture memory, a guest clock that stops while the game is paused). - [XenonRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/XenonRecomp) and [Unleashed Recompiled](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp): the model for a recompiled port, and for its installer. - [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui) by Omar Cornut: the setup's and the launcher's user interface. - [Inter](https://github.com/rsms/inter) by Rasmus Andersson: their typeface. - The mods the launcher installs are their authors' work: the Spanish translation by Traducciones Vacuno ([TraduSquare](https://tradusquare.es)), the DLC Undub by Canzah and Slow.

1455582413.readme_excerpt:
God of War III — native Nintendo Switch port

**English** | [Español](README.es.md) A native Nintendo Switch port of the PS3 version of **God of War III** (BCUS-98111). It is not an emulator. The PPU (PowerPC) and SPU code in the game's `EBOOT.BIN` is statically recompiled to C/C++ with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), built for the Switch with devkitPro/libnx, and the game is drawn by a Vulkan backend running on NVK (Mesa). RSX shaders are translated to SPIR-V on the console. > [!NOTE] > This repository contains **no game data and no code derived from the game**. You need your own copy of the PS3 > disc and a decrypted `EBOOT.BIN`. ## Status > [!IMPORTANT] > **Paused until next week:** I ran out of tokens for the AI I use to develop this port; they renew next week and work > resumes then. The plan is in [PORT_STATUS.md](PORT_STATUS.md). **Latest (Nov 13):** from ~1.9 to **~3 FPS (overclocked)** with MLAA off, a cache for the color-grading LUT and a PPU wait backoff. The bottleneck is no longer the SPUs but the RSX thread, which submits and waits on a fence for every draw; draw batching is being tested. Estimated odds: 30 FPS without OC ~10 %, 15-20 FPS ~30-40 %. **Work in progress, not playable yet. Overall progress: ~25%.** ```text Material & analysis ██████████ 100 % Boot (boot → menu) ██████░░░░ 60 % Graphics (RSX → Vulkan) ███▌░░░░░░ 35 % Switch layer (Horizon) █████▌░░░░ 55 % Performance (30 FPS) █░░░░░░░░░ 10 % Full game ░░░░░░░░░░ 0 % Full translation ░░░░░░░░░░ 0 % ``` On the console, at stock clocks with no overclock, it boots, reads the PSARCs, runs SPURS and the SPU jobs, shows the studio logos and credits (~45 FPS), plays the intro video and draws the **brightness calibration screen** with the game's own shaders (32 of 32 pipelines OK). **Where it is stuck:** past the intro it runs at ~3 FPS (overclocked). The bottleneck is the RSX thread (Vulkan backend), which waits on the GPU for every draw; with draw batching it hung at flip 870 and the fix is untested. **Goals:** - **30 FPS without overclock.** This is the hardest one: the game leans heavily on all 6 SPUs, which run on 3 A57 cores on the Switch. The plan is to move MLAA from the SPUs to a shader AA pass, rewrite the hottest jobs with NEON, add dynamic resolution and cut post effects (DoF, motion blur). - **Full Spanish translation.** The US disc only ships `ENGLISH.PSARC`. It needs the language PSARC from a European or Latin American release (your own dump) or a text translation, plus fonts with á, ñ, ¿ and ¡. The detailed log is in [PORT_STATUS.md](PORT_STATUS.md) (newest first, in Spanish) and the phase plan is in [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md). ## Installing on the Switch There is no playable release yet. The NRO and instructions will be published once it reaches the menu. Current test setup: ```text /switch/gow3-nx/ gow3-nx.nro PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO USRDIR/ (the PSARCs, CINEMATICS/ and SOUNDS/ from your disc) ``` Run it in full application mode (hold **R** while opening an installed game, or use a forwarder). Applet mode (Album) does not give it enough memory. ## Layout | Path | What it is | |---|---| | `port/` | The port's own code: `main.cpp` (boot and title environment), extra HLE (`lfqueue.cpp`, `stubs.cpp`) and the game's CMake | | `nx/` | Horizon layer: 4 GB guest memory, exception bridge, POSIX compat, glslang shims | | `patches/` | Switch changes on top of ps3recomp `de4f090` (Vulkan/NVK, cellVdec without FFmpeg, SPU job queue, FS) | | `tools/lift_reloc_jobmods.py` | Lifts the 19 relocatable WWS SPU jobs | | `docs/ROADMAP.md` | Phase plan (Spanish) | ## Building (summary) 1. Install devkitPro (devkitA64 + libnx + switch-sdl2) and get the NVK SDK for Switch. 2. Clone ps3recomp at `de4f090` and apply `patches/ps3recomp-switch.patch`. 3. Decrypt your `EBOOT.BIN` (RPCS3: Utilities → Decrypt PS3 Binaries) and run the ps3recomp pipeline (output goes to `port/ppu/` and `port/spu/`, which are never committed). 4. Configure and build `port/` with the Switch toolchain. ## Credits - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) (MIT): lifters, runtime and HLE. - [gow2-recomp](https://github.com/andrebrumdev/gow2-recomp) and [Ascension-R](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R), references for the same Santa Monica Studio engine. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3), devkitPro, libnx, glslang and Mesa/NVK. God of War is a property of Sony Interactive Entertainment. Non-commercial project. ## Support If you like my work and want to support me:

Low-CPU update: fewer threads on weaker PCs, support for CPUs without AVX2

- SPURS: on PCs with 16 or fewer CPU threads the lanes/kernels spin less, wake the
  main thread sooner and run on fewer threads (4-thread PCs: ~10 fps -> ~29 fps,
  8 threads: ~38 -> ~50 fps). Big PCs keep the old behaviour.
- Vertex workers spin far less after each job, fewer workers on small CPUs.
- The once-per-second thread scan only walks the game's own threads.
- No exclusive core reservations on PCs with fewer than 20 CPU threads;
  P-core pinning only on hybrid CPUs with at least 8 P-core threads.
- CPUs without AVX2/FMA/BMI2 (pre-2013 Intel, AVX-less Pentium/Celeron, AMD before
  2015): Setup/the updater detect this and build an SSE4.1 compatibility version
  automatically (same results, slower). The game also checks the CPU at startup and
  shows a clear message instead of crashing.
