GT5 defragments its texture memory and moves textures with an NV0039 (memory to memory) copy on subchannel 1. The port never carried it out, so a moved texture showed whatever had been in its new place before: sponsor banners across the road at Chamonix, scrambled Eiger. cellGcmSys.c now recognises NV0039 on subchannel 1 (the libgcm transfer sequence) and does the copy.

💬 Discord · Install · Launcher · Updating · Version history · Changelog · Status · FAQ · Modding · Contributing · License

# GT5 Recomp An unofficial PC port of **Gran Turismo 5** (PS3) made by static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated into C++ that is compiled for Windows x64, and the PS3's graphics, sound, input and system calls are reimplemented on Windows (Direct3D 12 for the RSX). A native [Linux build](#linux) (Vulkan) is new and early. It is built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) and borrows from the [GT5 Prologue port](https://github.com/sp00nznet/GT5P), both by Ned Heller (sp00nznet). > **Game version required:** your own **Gran Turismo 5** Blu-ray disc, using the disc's own > executable (version **01.00**, with **no game update** installed): > > - **Europe, BCES00569**: tested. This is the copy the port was built from. > - **North America, BCUS98114**: works; players have raced on it (thanks!). The lift finds the few addresses > that differ between releases in your own executable. > > See [Which copy of GT5](#which-copy-of-gt5) for how to check your files. ## 📑 Contents | 🚀 Getting started | 📈 How it's going | 🛠️ Setting up by hand | 📚 About the project | |---|---|---|---| | [Install](#install) | [Current state](#current-state) | [Requirements](#requirements) | [What this repository contains](#repo-contents) | | [The launcher](#launcher) | [Try it, tell me how it went](#feedback) | [Which copy of GT5](#which-copy-of-gt5) | [Fork it, mod it](#modding) | | [Updating](#updating) | [FAQ](#faq) | [Setup](#setup) | [Credits](#credits) | | [Controls](#controls) | | [Switches](#switches) | [License](#license) | | [Linux](#linux) | | | | **More pages:** [Version history](VERSIONS.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Status board](STATUS.md) · [Modding guide](MODDING.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [License](LICENSE) ## ⬇️ Install **The easy way, on Windows 10 or 11:** 1. Download **[GT5-Installer.bat](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/releases/latest/download/GT5-Installer.bat)** and double-click it. If Windows warns about a downloaded file, choose **Run** (or **More info**, then **Run anyway**). 2. In its window, pick two things and press **Install**: - **your GT5 game**: the folder of your disc dump (the one with `PS3_GAME` in it) or an `.iso`; - **PS3UPDAT.PUP**, Sony's free PS3 system software (the window has a button that opens Sony's page). That's all. It installs whatever's missing (Git, Python, Microsoft's C++ build tools), downloads this code, unlocks your game's executable and the system software with RPCS3 (used only as a tool for that: the game itself runs natively as `gt5.exe`, not in an emulator), builds the game (about an hour the first time) and puts **Gran Turismo 5 (PC)** on your desktop, which opens the [launcher](#launcher). Nothing from the game is ever uploaded or shared. Rather do it by hand? See [Setup](#setup). On Linux? See [Linux](#linux). ## 🎛️ The launcher

**Gran Turismo 5 (PC)** on your desktop (or `GT5Launcher.exe` in your `gt5-recomp` folder) opens the launcher: every setting in one window, then **Play**. No more editing `play.bat`. - **Display:** 1080p or 720p, **Speed** (30 fps draws every other frame; it only helps when the graphics card is the limit, the window title then shows both numbers, e.g. `FPS: 15 (game 30)`), screen shape (ultrawide), **borderless full screen**, maximized or a window size, watch mode, SPU threads. - **Controls:** steering wheel on/off, wheel rotation, force feedback strength and direction, pad in the background, mouse clipping. - **Game:** the game's language (as far as your disc has it), your mods from `GT5\mods`, the launcher's own language (English or 中文). - **Updates:** shows your version and the newest one with what's new, and **Update now** does the whole update for you and opens the launcher again. - **Help:** **Save logs for a report** puts your logs on the desktop as `.txt` files GitHub accepts, plus the logs folder, the problem form and this FAQ. It's built on your PC from [`launcher/GT5Launcher.cs`](launcher/GT5Launcher.cs) with the C# compiler that comes with Windows, every time the game is built, so it updates with the game; its picture is the logo from your own disc. Settings are saved in `GT5\settings.bat`, which `play.bat` reads, so `play.bat` still works and starts the game the same way. (`GT5Launcher.exe --play` starts the game straight away.) ## 🔄 Updating Every change to the port comes out as a numbered version (v0.1.0, v0.1.1, ...) on the [Releases page](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/releases), with what changed. To hear about new ones, click **Watch** at the top of this page, then **Custom** and tick **Releases**. ### The easy way - **The launcher** checks for a new version when it opens: its **Updates** page shows what's new, and **Update now** does everything below and opens the launcher again. - Or **double-click `Update.bat`** in your `gt5-recomp` folder. Both run `update.ps1`, so everything below applies. (No launcher or `Update.bat` yet? Your next update brings them: run the command below once.) ### Are you out of date? Close the game, open PowerShell in your `gt5-recomp` folder and run: ``` powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -List ``` It lists every version and marks the one you have (`<- installed`) and the newest (`[newest]`). If they're different, you're out of date. ### Update to the newest version ``` powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 ``` That one command does everything: 1. It downloads the new version. 2. It swaps the old ps3recomp patch for the new one. 3. It re-generates the game code only if that version needs it (about 10 minutes). 4. It rebuilds only what changed. Kept as they are: - your saves (`GT5\hdd0`) and game files (`GT5\input`, `GT5\vfs`, `GT5\dev_flash`); - the shader cache; - edits you made to files such as `play.bat`. The previous `gt5.exe` is kept as `GT5\build\gt5.previous.exe`. If one of your edits clashes with a change in the new version, the new version's file is used and your edit is saved in `backups\` so you can copy it back. **If you're several versions behind,** run the same command. It goes straight to the newest version; there's no need to step through the ones in between. ### Installed before update.ps1 existed? If your folder has no `update.ps1` (you set up before v0.1.0), get it first, then update: ``` git pull powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 ``` If `git pull` says your local changes would be overwritten (usually `play.bat`), run `git stash`, then `git pull`, then `git stash pop`, then the update. Your first update re-generates the game code once (about 10 minutes), because older installs have no record of what their code was made from. ### Downloaded the ZIP instead of cloning? A ZIP download can't update itself. Clone the repository fresh as in [Setup](#setup), step 1. Then move these folders over from your old copy and run `update.ps1`: - your game files: `GT5\input`, `GT5\vfs`, `GT5\dev_flash`; - your saves: `GT5\hdd0`. ### Go back to an older version If a new version gives you trouble, switch back to the one that worked (see `-List` for the names): ``` powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -Version v0.1.0 ``` To play the previous build right away instead, copy `GT5\build\gt5.previous.exe` over `GT5\build\gt5.exe` (the last update kept it). Please also [report what went wrong](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml). ### Other options | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `update.ps1 -Dev` | The newest changes, before they're released. | | `update.ps1 -NoBuild` | Switch versions without building; build later with `GT5\scripts\build.cmd gt5`. | | `update.ps1 -Force` | Re-generate and rebuild everything, even when nothing changed. | ## 🎮 Controls A DualSense, DualShock 4 or XInput pad works. Without one, the keyboard: Z = Cross, X = Circle, A = Square, S = Triangle, arrow keys = D-pad, Enter = Start, Tab = Select. A steering wheel works too, with force feedback (new and untested on real wheels): see the [FAQ](#faq). ## 📋 Current state

**Playable.** Races run at 45 to 58 fps on the tested rig, and most of the game's modes work. The full board (tested rig, what works, what's being worked on, known issues, recent changes) is in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md); updates are also posted in [Announcements](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/discussions/categories/announcements). Everything done on the port since the first day, with dates, is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## 🏁 Try it, then tell me how it went If you own the game, please set it up and play. Every result helps decide what gets fixed next, whether it runs great, half works, or doesn't build at all. Laptops, integrated graphics and AMD cards especially: the port was tuned on one desktop with an NVIDIA card. | You want to... | Go here | |---|---| | Say how it went (takes two minutes, mostly quick picks) | [Tried it: here's how it went](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=1-tried-it.yml) | | Report something broken | [Something's broken](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml) | | Ask for a change | [Suggest a change](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=3-idea.yml) | | Post quick results, screenshots of it running, or ask for help | [Discussions](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/discussions/1) | | Chat, get help live, share results | **[The Workshop Discord](https://discord.gg/9cVPS7r5Ha)**: #gt5-help, #gt5-test-reports, #gt5-chat (I'm **mormonftp** there) | ## ❓ FAQ | Question | Short answer | |---|---| | Steering wheels? # inFAMOUS: ReCharged

inFAMOUS (2009), inFAMOUS 2 (2011) and inFAMOUS: Festival of Blood (2011), the PS3 games, recompiled to run
natively on the PS5, in one app with a launcher, by ChaosTheory1075.

> Built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) and erikomis'
> [infamous2-recomp](https://github.com/erikomis/infamous2-recomp), with frame generation from
> [MihawkGen](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_MihawkGen). All the credit goes to them.

An unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Sucker Punch
Productions. **No game files are included:** you need your own copies of the games for the PS3.

**Download:** the newest `inFAMOUS-ReCharged-*.zip` from
[Releases](https://github.com/ChaosTheory1075/infamous-ps5/releases).

## What's in it
- inFAMOUS, inFAMOUS 2 and Festival of Blood, recompiled to run natively on the PS5 (not emulated), in one app
  (PPSA95463): the launcher's HOME page picks the game
- About 30 FPS, as on the PS3: in play sessions on a PS5 the median was 29.9-30.0 FPS in all three games
- FSR 1 upscaling to 4K, SMAA anti-aliasing and 16x texture filtering, on by default
- FRAME GENERATION (on by default): an extra frame between each two for smoother motion (it does not make the
  game itself run faster)
- Installs each game from your own PS3 dumps: the launcher checks the edition, decrypts the game's program from
  your dump and copies the game files. Uninstalling keeps your saves
- inFAMOUS 2's four updates downloaded by the launcher from Sony's update server, or copied by hand
- Trophies: unlocked in the games, listed on the launcher's TROPHIES page
- An animated menu: lightning, sparks and arcs in each game's colours (bats for Festival of Blood); turn it off
  with SETTINGS > MENU EFFECTS
- A launcher with HOME, CONTENT, SAVES (back up your saves), TROPHIES, SETTINGS and CREDITS pages

## What you need
- A jailbroken PS5 that runs homebrew apps, with a payload loader on port 9021 (etaHEN or elfldr)
- Your **own** dumps of exactly these editions (other regions and editions are not accepted by the installer):

| Game | Edition | Files |
|---|---|---|
| inFAMOUS | USA disc **BCUS98119** (v1.00 or v2.00) or Europe disc **BCES00220** | a decrypted `.iso` or the disc's folder |
| inFAMOUS 2 | USA disc **BCUS98125** (v1.00 or v2.00) + its four updates **1.01, 1.02, 1.03, 1.04** | a decrypted `.iso` or the disc's folder, plus the four update `.pkg` files |
| Festival of Blood | USA PSN **NPUA80657** | the `.pkg` and its `.rap` licence file |

- inFAMOUS 2's updates: the launcher downloads the four official update packages (258 MB) from Sony's PS3
  update server for you (CONTENT page: X shows a notice, X again starts it; the PS5 needs internet; each file is
  checked against Sony's checksum). You can also copy them into `install/` by hand. All four are needed.
- An encrypted ISO (as dumped) is refused: decrypt it first (PS3Dec). No PS3 firmware file is needed.
- Free space: about 7.5 GB (inFAMOUS), 18 GB (inFAMOUS 2), 4.4 GB (Festival of Blood), plus the dumps until
  you delete them.

## Install
1. FTP the `PPSA95463` folder from the zip to `/data/homebrew/` on the PS5 (upgrading: copy it over the old
   one; installed games, saves and settings are kept).
2. Put your dumps (and the inFAMOUS 2 updates, if you have them) in `PPSA95463/install/`.
3. Open **inFAMOUS: ReCharged**. Pick a game and press X to install it; keep the app open until it is done.
4. When the game says PLAY, press X. You can then delete the dumps in `install/`.

Leave a game from the PS menu. `README.txt` in the download has the launcher's controls and folders.

## Known issues
- Festival of Blood: the light near green road flares flickers (a bug in the port; the PS3 shows it steady).
- A minor shadow glitch remains.
- inFAMOUS: painted road markings can sometimes show through walls.
- A short stutter the first time each effect appears (its shader is built once, then cached).
- No glare around lamps in inFAMOUS 2 and Festival of Blood; inFAMOUS: heat distortion is off.
- FRAME GENERATION: ghosting and uneven pacing when a game drops into the low 20s.
- Some Festival of Blood cutscenes play faster than on the PS3.
- DLC COSTUMES is on by default; turn it off in SETTINGS if you do not own them.

Report bugs in this repository's [Issues](https://github.com/ChaosTheory1075/infamous-ps5/issues): turn DIAGNOSTICS on for that game (SETTINGS), reproduce it once, and attach the game's log from
`PPSA95463/<if1|if2|fob>/logs/` (launcher and install problems: `PPSA95463/logs/launcher.log`).

## How it's put together
Each game is its own recompiled program: `eboot.bin` is the launcher, `if1.bin`, `if2.bin` and `fob.bin` are the
games, which the launcher starts in its place (`sceSystemServiceLoadExec`). The games are built with a fork of
ps3recomp (`toolkit/`: its base commit, our patch and our added files: the Vulkan RSX backend work, FSR 1, SMAA,
frame generation, SPU/PPU runtime changes) and erikomis' infamous2-recomp port templates, which our tools in
`tools/` edit.

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `tools/ps5/launcher/` | The launcher (`launcher.c`, texts in `launcher_text.inc`) and the installer (`installer.c`: decrypted ISO, disc folder, PSN package, update download) |
| `tools/ps5/` | PS5 glue: `ps5_app.c` (per-game defaults, settings, trophies), `ps5_shims.c`, the linker scripts, `ps5link.sh`, `build_if2.sh` (all three games), `ps5.cmake`, `ps5cc` |
| `tools/` | The edits to the port sources and the recompiled code (each an exact-text insertion that stops if its anchor is not found once), build and measurement scripts |
| `toolkit/` | Our changes to ps3recomp: `BASE_COMMIT.txt`, `ps3recomp-fork.patch`, `added/` |
| `work/` | Test-box measurement scripts (console environment, A/B runs, soak and boot tests) |
| `DONTFLIP.md` | Changes that broke something before: read before changing a default |

No recompiled game code is in this repository: it is generated from your own copy of each game's executable.

## Build from source
The build runs on Linux (Ubuntu 24.04), as root, with clang 18 and your own game files. The scripts read
`IF_ROOT` (this repository's folder, default `$HOME/inFamous`) and the other paths in `tools/local.env.example`.

1. The toolkit fork:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/NoahBPeterson/ps3recomp.git ps3recomp-fork
   cd ps3recomp-fork
   git checkout $(cat ../toolkit/BASE_COMMIT.txt)
   git apply ../toolkit/ps3recomp-fork.patch
   cp -r ../toolkit/added/. .
   ```
2. The port sources, from [infamous2-recomp](https://github.com/erikomis/infamous2-recomp) at `a69a052`, edited by
   `tools/if2_patch_rebuild.py` (all three games), then `tools/if1_patch_port.py` (inFAMOUS) or the edits in
   `tools/fob_build.sh` (Festival of Blood); `tools/if1_build.sh`, `tools/if2_build.sh` and `tools/fob_build.sh`
   run these steps and the lift from your own decrypted EBOOT.
3. After the lift: `tools/postlift.sh <if1|if2|fob>` (prints the commands; `GO=1` runs them).
4. The PS5 programs: `tools/ps5/build_if2.sh` (`GAME=if1|if2|fob`) and `tools/ps5/launcher/build_launcher.sh`,
   with the PS5 Payload SDK, Mesa RADV for the PS5 and the ps5-plume-triangle tooling (see
   [LICENSES/THIRD_PARTY.md](LICENSES/THIRD_PARTY.md) for each one's source).

- SPURS_MAXCONT=3=5,15=5,16=5,17=5 by default: the main menu's Wws job
  list (16 jobs a frame) and the EDGE lists ran on one SPU each, one after
  the other, and held the frame at ~14 fps.
- Lifted SPU code: -mfma -ffp-contract=off (ASCENSION_SPU_FMA) and
  SPU_ASSUME_SPU_FP. Without -ffp-contract=off clang fuses the helpers'
  scalar a*b+c and the menu text disappeared.
- patch 0033: SSE quadword byte ops, FMA, EXP_TEX in fragment programs (the
  menu's motion blur had full weight on every pixel), faster RSX copies and
  texture hashing, SPURS_WID_TIMELOG and other diagnostics.
- frame_timeline.py lays workload runs out per frame (SPURS_WID_TIMELOG);
  profile_threads.py and run.ps1 take profip; run.ps1 -CaptureAt;
  compare_menu.py puts a dumped frame next to the reference.

past the end of a block in the heap at 0x14FB8F68 and zeroes the next free
node's header, and the first-fit walk func_00397318 loops on it. STATUS
records how the guard caught it and what to look at next. Patch 0018 caps

# Ascension **God of War: Ascension (PS3), recompilado para rodar nativamente no PC.** [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimento-lightgrey)](docs/MILESTONES.pt-BR.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-ainda%20n%C3%A3o-lightgrey)](#onde-estamos) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11%20x64-0078D4)](#compilando) [![Licença](https://img.shields.io/badge/licen%C3%A7a-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Português (Brasil)** · [English](docs/README.en.md)
--- O Ascension traduz o código do jogo, do processador principal (PPU) e dos SPUs do PS3, para C++ e o compila para o seu PC, sobre o runtime do [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). Não é um emulador: é o próprio jogo, recompilado. > [!WARNING] > **Ainda experimental, mas já dá para zerar.** O [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor) jogou do começo ao fim no PC dele (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT). Em processadores comuns o jogo ainda é lento (~20 fps na luta contra o chefe num Ryzen 7 5700G), e ainda pode travar. Feito para Windows; no macOS (Apple Silicon) ele voltou a rodar, por enquanto só para testes. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Nenhum dado do jogo está incluído.** Você precisa da sua própria cópia, a **versão europeia `BCES-01741`** (1.00), tirada do seu disco. Ninguém aqui pode te dar o jogo ou chaves. Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Sony Interactive Entertainment ou a Santa Monica Studio. ## Onde estamos Novembro de 2026, no Windows (e no Mac, em testes): - **O jogo inteiro, do boot ao fim:** o iSamigor zerou o jogo. Nos nossos testes: telas de abertura, carregamento, menus de primeiro uso, cinemática de abertura (imagem e som sincronizados), menu principal, o primeiro nível com o Kratos acorrentado e a primeira luta contra um chefe. - **Renderizadores:** o RSX do [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) (Vulkan ou OpenGL), que desenha o jogo corretamente; o renderizador Vulkan próprio do projeto, onde está o trabalho de desempenho; e o *live draw* (D3D12). - **Launcher** em português, inglês e espanhol, com vídeo (incluindo desligar efeitos como desfoque de profundidade, motion blur e MLAA, ainda experimental), controles, idioma, legendas, melhorias e o **online** com a sua conta do site; **português do Brasil** com vozes e textos, montado no [site](https://gow-ascension.com.br/pt-br) a partir dos seus discos. Atualizado em 10 de novembro. As mudanças de novembro estão no branch [`ascension-perf`](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/tree/ascension-perf) até serem medidas no Windows. Ainda não há release. Os marcos estão em [docs/MILESTONES.pt-BR.md](docs/MILESTONES.pt-BR.md) (em inglês: [MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md)). ### Desempenho O objetivo é rodar bem em processadores comuns, não só nos fortes. Desde 6 de novembro o caminho é **sair do modelo do PS3**: em vez de emular cada vez melhor as SPUs e o RSX, o trabalho deles vira código nativo do PC e da placa de vídeo, com a meta de não sobrar nenhuma emulação de SPU. > [!NOTE] > **Um erro de medida corrigido (9 de novembro):** o contador de fps do nosso renderizador Vulkan contava cada quadro duas vezes (o mesmo quadro era apresentado de novo ~1 ms depois, sem nada desenhado). Os números desse renderizador publicados antes valem a metade. Os de baixo já são quadros reais. A luta contra o chefe logo depois da cinemática de abertura, a cena mais pesada que medimos, num Ryzen 7 5700G (Windows, renderizador Vulkan do projeto, mediana de várias janelas de 5 s): | Quando | fps na luta | Thread de vídeo, por draw | | --- | --- | --- | | 9 de novembro, à noite | ~15-17 | ~17,5 µs | | 10 de novembro, de manhã | ~18 | ~16,0 µs | | 10 de novembro, à tarde | **~20** | **~15,0 µs** | **O que entrou de 6 a 10 de novembro** (cada parte medida e com a imagem conferida antes de virar padrão): - **Renderizador Vulkan próprio** (no ps3kit), onde está o trabalho de desempenho: o anti-aliasing que o jogo fazia nas SPUs (o MLAA delas não roda mais) agora é feito na placa de vídeo (SMAA, FXAA ou MLAA), filtro anisotrópico, vértices convertidos em lotes e um contador de fps compacto nas cores do jogo. - **60 fps:** o limite de 30 do jogo destravado, com o jogo andando na velocidade certa, e um limite de 60. Os carregamentos, que tinham ficado lentos com o destrave, voltaram a ~4,5 s. - **SPUs em código nativo:** três módulos de geometria do EDGE (218, 202 e 210) rodam inteiros como código nativo, cada um conferido contra o original em centenas de jobs gravados do próprio jogo (resultado idêntico). - **Thread de vídeo mais leve:** cópias 2D divididas entre 3 threads (4 → 1,7 ms por quadro); constantes dos shaders copiadas só quando mudam; os comandos de vídeo comuns despachados em bloco (-1,5 µs por draw); e as texturas: o jogo move ~150 texturas por segundo dentro da memória de vídeo, e agora uma textura movida fica com a imagem que já estava na placa em vez de ser decodificada e enviada de novo (texturas de 1,56 para 1,00 µs por draw). - **macOS:** voltou a compilar e a abrir o jogo (Vulkan sobre MoltenVK), ~24 fps no primeiro nível num Mac com Apple Silicon; ainda trava em parte das aberturas. **Para onde vai o quadro agora:** na luta, quem segura o quadro é o thread que executa os comandos de vídeo, e o maior custo dele é copiar os vértices que os jobs do EDGE acabaram de escrever (~5 dos ~15 µs de cada draw, perto de 50 MB por quadro). **Próximos passos:** levar essa geometria para a placa de vídeo (as posições calculadas na GPU, sem a cópia no processador), que deve ser o primeiro salto grande (estimativa de ~28-32 fps, ainda a medir); depois o resto do EDGE na GPU e os outros módulos das SPUs em código nativo. ### Estabilidade - **Corrigido:** num PC lento, o thread de vídeo desistia de uma espera depois de 2 s e perdia os comandos do quadro; o jogo ficava parado no carregamento do nível. - **Corrigido:** o travamento no nível com as listas de geometria esperando para sempre (uma escrita do processador principal se perdia no meio de uma operação atômica de uma SPU: de 3 travamentos em 5 rodadas para nenhum em 4). - **Corrigido:** o travamento com `CopyLocalMemory offset error` (um contador do Edge Zlib e a troca da tabela de streaming de texturas sem proteção): nenhum em 40 rodadas no nível. - **Protegido:** comandos de vídeo corrompidos (`FIFO error: possible desync`) não derrubam mais o thread do RSX, e um draw pedindo uma quantidade absurda de vértices é descartado em vez de travar o jogo. A causa da corrupção ainda está aberta. - **Problemas conhecidos:** logo depois da luta das criaturas, perto do braço gigante, um objeto da área aparece desenhado várias vezes, cada cópia um pouco deslocada (some quando a câmera sai dali); o jogo às vezes trava com uma lista de jobs das SPUs que não termina (`BATCHJOB: Waiting for batch job list ...`); e houve um crash silencioso ~70-105 s depois de entrar no nível em duas rodadas. ### Multijogador online (em desenvolvimento) Os servidores originais do jogo ainda funcionam para quem joga no PS3, mas o jogo recompilado não entra na PSN. Por isso o projeto tem o próprio servidor (em Rust, ainda privado), no ar em [gow-ascension.com.br](https://gow-ascension.com.br) com o cadastro fechado por enquanto; o runtime manda para ele os nomes que o jogo procura. O servidor nunca se passa pela Sony: ele responde só o que o jogo espera, lido no código traduzido ou nas capturas do próprio jogo falando com ele. A partida usa o netcode do próprio jogo (uma malha P2P por UDP); como dois jogadores em casa quase nunca se alcançam direto (cada um atrás do seu roteador), os pacotes passam por um relay do servidor, e o jogo nem percebe. | Passo | Estado | | --- | --- | | Entrar online, Online Pass | ok | | Configuração do online (o jogo lê a nossa) | ok | | Termos de uso, perfil do multijogador guardado na conta | ok | | Tutorial pulado, lobby do guerreiro | ok | | Partida rápida: localização do jogador | ok | | Partida rápida: escolha do servidor de matchmaking | ok | | Conexão com o matchmaking (sessão SSL 3.0) | ok | | Dois jogadores casados numa partida, um deles host | ok (dois jogos no mesmo PC) | | A rede da partida pelo relay do servidor | ok (dois jogos no mesmo PC) | | Launcher: entrar na conta e jogar online | ok | | Partida entre dois PCs pela internet | **em andamento** | | A partida inteira, do lobby ao fim | falta | ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph PC["PC do jogador"] L["Launcher
conta e online"] G["Jogo recompilado
(runtime ps3kit)"] L -- "endereço, configuração e perfil" --> G end subgraph SRV["Servidor do projeto (Rust)"] API["Contas e API"] CFG["Configuração do online"] TUS["Perfil do multijogador
por conta"] GEO["Localização"] SAM["Matchmaking
(SSL 3.0)"] REL["Signaling e relay
(UDP)"] DB[("PostgreSQL")] TUS --> DB API --> DB end WEB["Site do projeto
perfil, ranking, painel"] G2["Jogo de outro jogador"] L -- "login por código" --> API L -- "configuração, perfil" --> CFG L -- "perfil" --> TUS G -- "TCP" --> GEO G -- "TCP + SSL" --> SAM G <-- "partida (UDP)" --> REL REL <-- "partida (UDP)" --> G2 WEB -- "HTTP" --> API ``` No ar no servidor e no site: as contas, o perfil do multijogador guardado por conta, o perfil público com nível e conquistas, o ranking (vazio até haver partidas), um painel administrativo e o login do launcher por código. Planejado: os troféus do jogo assinados e conferidos pelo servidor. **"Jogar offline" vai continuar sempre funcionando**: a campanha nunca vai pedir conta. ## Jogando Com o jogo compilado (abaixo), instale o launcher pelo `AscensionLauncher__x64-setup.exe` das [releases](https://github.com/arnaldolima1/gow-ascension-pc/releases) e, na primeira vez, aponte a pasta `ascension` em **Avançado › Pasta do jogo**. Ele se atualiza sozinho quando sai uma versão nova.

JOGAR abre o jogo; o launcher se esconde até ele fechar. - **Vídeo:** renderizador (RPCS3 Vulkan ou OpenGL, live draw), resolução interna e filtro anisotrópico (RPCS3), janela ou tela cheia (F11 ou Alt+Enter também alternam durante o jogo), tamanho da janela, proporção, escala da imagem, sincronização vertical, contador de FPS. - **Controles:** abas para teclado e mouse (duas teclas por comando, clique e aperte a nova) e para o controle (qual botão faz cada um, zona morta). Padrão: WASD anda, setas esquivam, Espaço/J/I/L ou o mouse nos botões, Shift defende, Esc ou Enter pausa. Teclado, mouse e controle funcionam juntos. - **Launcher** em vários idiomas; o automático segue o idioma do jogo. - **Jogo:** idioma (inglês, português, espanhol, francês, alemão, italiano, russo, polonês, turco) e legendas, que valem mesmo depois do primeiro uso; backup automático dos saves. - **Melhorias:** liga e desliga. Vem com **Pular intro** (direto ao carregamento, sem as telas de abertura); o botão **Abrir a pasta de melhorias** é onde entram as outras, como o **português do Brasil**, que a [página do site](https://gow-ascension.com.br/pt-br) monta no seu navegador a partir das imagens dos seus discos (nada é enviado). As melhorias incluídas são receitas: o launcher as aplica aos arquivos do seu disco, sem trazer nada do jogo. - **Online:** entra na sua conta do site por um código (como numa TV) e liga o online; os troféus do jogo ficam na mesma aba.

## Compilando ``` ascension-recomp/ ps3kit/ o runtime e o recompilador (fork do ps3recomp, com as mudanças deste projeto) ascension/ este repositório work/ o seu disco e o que sai dele (nunca vai para o git) ``` 1. **Disco:** extraia a sua imagem em `work/disc` e decripte `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` para `EBOOT.ELF` (com o RPCS3, ou `tools/decrypt_self.py` e o seu arquivo de chaves). 2. **Tradução:** gere o código C++ com o recompilador; os scripts de `scripts/` cobrem cada etapa (veja [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md)). 3. **Build:** Visual Studio 2022 (clang-cl), CMake e Ninja, com `.\scripts\windows\build.ps1`; o renderizador do RPCS3 se compila antes com `.\scripts\windows\build-gpu.ps1` (MSVC e Vulkan SDK). As configurações da máquina ficam num `.env` local. Um build do zero leva de 20 a 40 minutos e pede 16 GB de memória. Os saves ficam em `gamedata/dev_hdd0`. ## Créditos - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp), de sp00nznet e colaboradores: o recompilador, o runtime e as bibliotecas de sistema. - [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): o código do RSX usado como renderizador (GPL-2.0; um build com ele fica sob a GPL-2.0). - [iSamigor](https://github.com/iSamigor): testes num segundo PC (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RX 9070 XT) e correções no runtime. - `tools/decrypt_self.py`, do port do [Twisted Metal](https://github.com/sp00nznet/twistedmetal) (MIT). - O launcher segue o estilo do de [gow3_pc](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/gow3_pc); fonte Cinzel (SIL Open Font License). - God of War é marca registrada da Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## Licença MIT: veja [LICENSE](LICENSE). Vale só para o código deste repositório, não para o jogo.

062e18d27ab208d239c09fcbbf7f982749107b1a.message:
Linux: the port on Linux and the Steam Deck

dod3 builds and runs on Linux (x86-64), tested on a Steam Deck (SteamOS,
RADV): the game boots, plays the attract sequence's in-engine scenes and
the chapter 1 battle on the Vulkan draw engine, with the Deck's pad.

  - The renderer is ps3recomp's Vulkan draw engine in an SDL2 window

0f99dd18d9a7fd94f90d60779c0df3729f1b5565.message:
The mouse moves the dragon's shooting cursor (#22)

In the sky the dragon aims with a cursor on the screen, the lock-on's red
ring: holding Square sweeps it over enemies to lock them, and the release
fires a shot at each. The title moves it with the left stick
(ASqex03GamePawnPlayerDragon::UpdateShootingCursor, func_009D26F8, reached
by vtable) and springs it back to the top of the screen once the stick is
let go. The mouse look turns the view through the right stick's values, so
on the keyboard and mouse the cursor only ever answered to WASD and stayed
at the top however the mouse moved: nothing was locked, and the release
fired one shot -- the report in #22 (at 120 fps, but the frame rate was not
the cause: with a pad the lock-on locks and fires at 30 and 120 alike).

src/patches/dragon_cursor.cpp wraps the update: while the cursor is on
screen (IsEnableShootingCursor, func_0096B9A8) the mouse moves it, it stays
where the mouse leaves it (the spring back undone after the update), and a
move past the edge of its rectangle turns the view as before
(src/input/camera.cpp hands the mouse to the cursor meanwhile). A stick --
a pad's, or WASD -- takes it back as soon as it moves it. DOD3_MOUSE=0
leaves the mouse out; DOD3_CURSOR_LOG=1 says when the mouse takes the
cursor or gives it back. DOD3_MOUSE_TEST_FILE="dx dy" adds counts to the
mouse every frame, for tests without the window's focus.

Checked on Ch.2 Verse 6 Part 1 at 120 fps with a live read of the dragon's
m_xShooting: mouse counts move the cursor, it stays put, and the lock-on
locks a wyvern and fires; a pad with the mouse look on and the mouse still

123bf526d26913cdae31ec5b6bc54dbac29646eb.message:
The launcher updates the port from its GitHub releases (Windows)

When the launcher opens it reads the repository's release list -- not
GitHub's "latest release", which leaves pre-releases out, and every
release so far is one -- on a thread nothing waits for, and offers the
newest release above its own version that has a Windows zip with a
SHA-256 digest: "Update to ..." in the footer opens an Update panel with
the release's notes, Install Update and Release Page.

Install Update (src/install/update.cpp): the zip is downloaded into
.update/ beside the program (WinHTTP), checked against the size and digest
GitHub lists, unpacked (install/zip.h, CRC-checked; the '\' names of
PowerShell's Compress-Archive taken), and each file swapped in: the old one
renamed to <name>.old, which Windows allows for the running program and its
DLLs, the new one moved into its place. A failed swap puts back every file
swapped so far; a failed try leaves nothing. game/, gamedata/ and an
existing dod3.ini are never written. The launcher then starts the new
dod3.exe and closes; the new one's first start removes the .old files and
says what it was updated from. The approach follows King Kong
Recompiled's updater (MIT).

Settings > System > Check for Updates (DOD3_UPDATE_CHECK = 0 turns it
off). The Mac's app is replaced another way: compiled out there for now.

Checked: a build acting as 0.4.0 (DOD3_UPDATE_AS) found 0.4.1 on GitHub,
downloaded it, matched its digest and installed it -- the folder then
equal to the 0.4.1 zip file for file but for dod3.ini, which kept the
player's line -- and started 0.4.1. From a local release
(DOD3_UPDATE_API, DOD3_UPDATE_ZIP): the new build cleaned up after itself
and said "Updated from"; a wrong digest installed nothing; a file held
open mid-swap put every file back (1,736 files unchanged).

2e87a0061f01bcc59898b233381bd923b15c3441.message:
Loads: the package loader's reads natively; DOD3_LOAD_LOG; DOD3_PROF on macOS

What a load waits on, measured on the Mac (start-up, New Game -> prologue):
the game thread, running Unreal's package loader. Reads take ~85 us and the
I/O and inflate threads are idle over 80% of a load; the loader is millions
of tiny reads, each a virtual call to FArchiveAsync::Serialize and the
guest's memcpy, both lifted with a page-table test on every load and store.

src/patches/archive_native.cpp, through the function registry (no re-lift):
- FArchiveAsync::Serialize (func_00141420): bytes already in the precache
  buffer, with the read done, are one memcpy; anything else (outside the
  buffer, a read in flight, pages a diagnostic watches, overlap) runs the
  lifted body. Over 99.9% of reads take the native path.
- FLinkerLoad::Serialize (func_0014A32C), which only forwards to the
  archive: straight to the native one.
- FLinkerLoad::operator<<(FName&) (thunk func_0014A62C): index and number
  in one step; an index outside the name map is the lifted one's to report.
DOD3_ARCHIVE_NATIVE=0 turns them off. 1.01 only (eboot.h).

Measured, interleaved runs, with ps3recomp 9b62c14 (one TLS lookup a
virtual call):
- start-up to the title's loading frame: 3.18 -> 2.95 s (fastest of 6
  each; medians 3.32 -> 3.00)
- New Game load span: 1.85-1.91 -> 1.56-1.60 s (3 runs each); its
  blocking frame 406-412 -> 311-312 ms; the 48-package load 27-29 -> 24
  frames
Chapter 0 plays as before (live run, frame grabs).

Tools for the next ones:
- DOD3_LOAD_LOG=1 (patches/load_idle.cpp): the start-up's steps timed from
  the process's launch, each load's span, frames and longest frame, the
  native/lifted read counts, and every frame over 100 ms (handed to the
  profiler's slow-frame report on both platforms).
- DOD3_PROF on macOS (src/os/macos/prof_mac.cpp): the Windows profiler's

527495dd5dcdb40857935efe907df16842d910a9.message:
The lifted libsre built with PPU_INLINE_VM too

It includes the game's ppu_recomp.h. Since the ps3recomp v0.18 lifter,
code lifted without PPU_INLINE_VM opens each function with a copy of the
memory model (PPU_MM_SNAP) that only a header from a v0.18 lift defines;
libsre is lifted at build time, the game's header comes from an older
lift, and the build failed. With PPU_INLINE_VM, libsre takes the game's
inline fast path, which falls back to the full accessors wherever they
matter (an SPU's reserved line, the raw SPU window, the diagnostics).

and the old method processor only where it is still read, the draw
engine's cache indexes and single fragment-program pass, vertex cache
entries drawn in place once reused, the D3D12 encoder setting only what

usleepspin, pumpsleep, kickhr.

The setup's moves wait out a scanner holding a new file

Installing the disc over an install, the move of the fresh 15 GB copy into

right after thousands of files are written, a scanner (Windows Defender,
the search indexer) can still hold one open, and the folder cannot be

back, the update's and DLC's files, the executable) now tries again for up
to five seconds before it fails.

aa4936901a6a916cb952f6101283175d71d4e700.message:
Pipeline states built ahead at start-up; a tool for the shipped shader cache

ps3recomp at 26ca8af: the D3D12 engine records each pipeline state it
builds in cache/dxbc/pipelines.bin and builds the listed ones on
low-priority threads at start-up, so the draw that first needs one no longer
waits a frame or more for the driver's compile (one level, played twice:
1,416 ms of pipeline builds in play without the list, 62 ms with it; 26
draws skipped in play, then 5). And the PPU store-conditional fails, as on
the Cell, when an SPU rewrote its line while it waited for the lock-line
lock: the game's PhysX task queues let about 2,000 such stores through in
four minutes of a battle on four host threads.

tools/shader_cache.py: `build` compiles shader dumps into the bytecode cache
exactly as the engine does (byte for byte the same files), `list` counts,
checks against a cache and merges pipeline lists. The upstream merge changed
the shader text, so the 0.4.0 cache holds only 584 of the 1,494 programs a
sweep of every chapter met; the next release's cache is to be rebuilt this
way, with the list its play-throughs record.

(the lifter changed); the libsre module the build lifts is no longer in

  (tools/lift_native.py): the single-precision helpers round a NaN to

da6a1a510cf4d30c0393f7f16a17add079c3a177.message:
Aspect Ratio: the HUD fitted into the view; 16:10; movies and the title as on that screen

In a view boxed to another shape the HUD's canvas is the view's: moved to
its corner and as big as it is. The HUD lays itself out on 1280x720 whatever
the canvas, so at 21:9 it ran off the bottom of the view. Now
Sqex03GameHUD.DrawHUD hands its canvas to the port (bridge 17) and
src/patches/hud_aspect.cpp makes the canvas's top transform a scale and a
move that put the 16:9 HUD in the middle of the view, as big as fits; the
canvas reports 1280x720 meanwhile, as the HUD's native code places some
things by its size. The markers placed on the view (enemy gauges, lock-on,
talk icons) are mapped back through it in hooks on UCanvas::execProject and
ASqex03GameHUD::CalcTransformPosition, so they stay on their targets. The
30 full-screen layers of the HUD's scripts -- fades, dimming, filters, the
dying overlay, the screen-split effect -- are marked by the script patch and
cover the whole view. A narrower view's room above and below the HUD is
clipped (through the depth, the 2D canvas having no depth test): the HUD
keeps a bar parked above itself there.

The HUD's begin also tells the present the view's shape each frame, and the
setting the screen's (ps3recomp: rsx_present_set_screen_aspect), so that
the title, menus and movies are 16:9 in the middle of that screen: a 16:9
window set to 21:9 shows what a 21:9 screen would.

16:10 is a choice of the setting (and auto takes a window narrower than
16:9): the view keeps its FOV and is taller. The fit only runs when the
setting has boxed the view, so 16:9 is as it was.

1.00 keeps the HUD as it was (the hooks' addresses are 1.01's) and gets the
present's half. Replay regression: 110 of 110 frames identical.

df1c0b49f15cc73df2c64de6f90f3c5a69969912.message:
The setup takes the US PSN release's game package in place of the disc

Drakengard 3 was also sold on PSN in the US (NPUB31251). Its game package,
UP0082-NPUB31251_00-DOD3MAINGAME0000 (1.00), holds the disc's files but for
four: an executable of its own build, COALESCED_INT.BIN as an .EDAT, both
under the buyer's licence, a PARAM.SFO of its own, and a PS3TOC.TXT whose
one line names that .EDAT. The port runs the disc release's 1.01 executable
and reads the config from its update, so neither locked file is wanted.

The setup now takes the package in the disc's slot, checked by the SHA-1 its
footer carries, and unpacks it as the disc is laid out (PS3_GAME/...),
leaving out its EBOOT.BIN and the .EDAT; the file list's line goes back to
the disc's, which makes the list the disc's own (checked by its hash). The
update is the disc release's for either: the PSN release's own 1.01 update
and the European release (NPEB01407, a build of its own) are refused with
what to add instead. An installed game is now told by its PARAM.SFO and
PS3TOC.TXT, not by EBOOT.BIN, which a 1.01 build never reads there.

pkg_extract takes an optional layout naming where each entry goes (or that
it is left out). The setup's pages, README.md, docs/PLAYING.md and
docs/BUILDING.md name the PSN package beside the disc.

Tested: an install from the package with the update and a DLC pack has
8,791 files identical to a disc install's, the others as above; a new game
from it reaches the chapter 1 battle at 60 fps, the settings pages in place
and the config read from the update. The disc installed over it, and the
package over that, each swap the game and keep the update and the DLC.

# Drakengard 3 Recompiled **A native port of the PlayStation 3 game Drakengard 3.** [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/soyjxck/dod3-recomp?include_prereleases&label=release)](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/total?label=downloads)](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/soyjxck/dod3-recomp?style=flat)](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/stargazers) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/soyjxck/dod3-recomp?label=last%20commit)](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/commits/main) [![Open issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/soyjxck/dod3-recomp?label=issues)](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/issues) [![Support on Ko-fi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ko--fi-support-FF5E5B?logo=kofi&logoColor=white)](https://ko-fi.com/soyjack) ![Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-x64-0078D6) ![Linux x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/Linux-x64-FCC624?logo=linux&logoColor=black) ![macOS arm64](https://img.shields.io/badge/macOS-arm64-000000?logo=apple&logoColor=white) ![Direct3D 12](https://img.shields.io/badge/Direct3D-12-5E5E5E) ![Vulkan](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vulkan-AC162C?logo=vulkan&logoColor=white) ![Metal](https://img.shields.io/badge/Metal-147EFB) ### [Download](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) · [Installing](#installing) · [Playing guide](docs/PLAYING.md) [Report an issue](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/issues) · [Build from source](#building) · [Technical notes](docs/TECHNICAL.md) · [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/soyjack)
## Contents - [About](#about) - [Installing](#installing) - [Building](#building) - [Status](#status) - [How it fits together](#how-it-fits-together) - [Legal](#legal) - [Credits](#credits) ## About A native PC port of **Drakengard 3** (Drag-On Dragoon 3, PlayStation 3, BLUS31197) for Windows, macOS and Linux, made by static recompilation of the game's code on the [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) toolkit. The game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C++ ahead of time and built into a normal executable, with the PS3's system libraries replaced by native implementations and the RSX graphics by Direct3D 12, Metal or Vulkan. There is no emulation at run time. ![The start of the game, running natively on Windows](docs/images/opening.jpg) **Nothing of the game is in this repository.** You need your own copy of Drakengard 3: the US disc and the game's 1.01 update, plus whatever DLC you own. The installer takes them from there. If this helped you, consider [buying me a coffee](https://ko-fi.com/soyjack) ## Installing What you need: - A PC with Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), a GPU with Direct3D 12 and a CPU with AVX2 (Intel Haswell / AMD Zen or newer), or a Mac with Apple silicon on macOS 13 or newer. About 16 GB of free disk space, 10 GB more for the Japanese voice pack and about 3 GB for the Spanish translation. - Your copy of the game, US release, as either: - the disc (BLUS31197), dumped to a folder or a **decrypted** `.iso` ([PS3 Disc Dumper](https://github.com/13xforever/ps3-disc-dumper) writes one; an image from an ordinary disc tool is still encrypted and is refused), or - the PSN release (NPUB31251): the game's package as a PlayStation 3 downloads it (`UP0082-NPUB31251_00-DOD3MAINGAME0000`, 15.6 GB). No licence files are needed. Other regions, the European PSN release among them, are refused. - The 1.01 update, as the package a PlayStation 3 downloads: `UP0082-BLUS31197_00-DOD3PATCH0000000-A0101-V0101-PE.pkg`. This is the disc release's update; the PSN release takes it too. - Optionally, the DLC packages you own (`UP0082-NPUB31251_00-...`). No licence files are needed. - Optionally, mods: the Spanish fan translation and the DLC Undub (Japanese voices for the DLC chapters), which the launcher installs on its Mods page; see [docs/PLAYING.md](docs/PLAYING.md#mods). Windows: 1. Download `dod3-recomp--win64.zip` from the [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) and unzip it anywhere (not inside Program Files). 2. Run `dod3.exe`. SmartScreen may warn the first time, as the program is not signed: "More info", then "Run anyway". 3. In the setup that opens, add your files (the disc image or folder, or the PSN game package; the update package; any DLC packages) with Add Files / Add Folder, in any order, then Install. The game's files are copied into the `game` folder next to `dod3.exe` (a few minutes). 4. Play. From then on `dod3.exe` opens the launcher: Play, and the game's mods, DLC and settings. macOS: 1. Download `dod3-recomp--macos-arm64.zip` from the [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases), unzip it and move "Drakengard 3 Recompiled.app" to Applications. 2. The app is not notarised, so macOS refuses it the first time. On macOS 15 and later: open it once, then allow it in System Settings > Privacy & Security ("Open Anyway"). On macOS 13 and 14: Control-click the app, choose Open, then Open again. 3. The setup opens as on Windows. The game's files go into `~/Library/Application Support/Drakengard 3 Recompiled`. Linux (x86-64; the Steam Deck included), experimental: 1. Download `dod3-recomp--linux-x86_64.tar.gz` from the [releases](https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp/releases) and unpack it anywhere you can write to. It needs a Vulkan 1.3 driver (Mesa's RADV, ANV, or NVIDIA's), SDL2 (`sdl2` or `sdl2-compat`; SteamOS has it) and glibc 2.38 or newer. 2. Run `dod3` in the folder. The setup opens as on Windows, and the game's files are copied into the `game` folder beside it. Add Files uses the desktop's picker (kdialog or zenity); without either, `./dod3 --install ` in a terminal does the same. 3. On a Steam Deck: install from Desktop Mode, then add `dod3` to Steam as a non-Steam game to play it in Game Mode. `dod3.log` beside it says what happened if it does not start. Settings (resolution, display mode, frame-rate cap, anti-aliasing, field of view, draw distance, skipping the intro, the keyboard's keys) are in the launcher's Settings, in the game's own Settings menu (Graphics Settings, System Settings, Advanced Graphics and Picture Settings), or in `dod3.ini`. [docs/PLAYING.md](docs/PLAYING.md) has the controls, the saves, the Japanese voices, and what to do if something goes wrong. ## Building The port is built in three steps: the game's PPU code is lifted to C++, its SPU programs are lifted, and the whole is compiled with CMake. Lifting needs the game's executable, so you need your own copy of the game first. 1. **Toolchain.** Windows: Visual Studio 2022 or newer (the Build Tools are enough, with "Desktop development with C++" and the Windows SDK), LLVM with clang-cl, CMake 3.20 or later, Ninja, Python 3.11 or later, Git for Windows, and vcpkg with `zlib:x64-windows` and `sdl2:x64-windows` (`VCPKG_ROOT`, or `C:\vcpkg`). macOS: Xcode's command-line tools and, from Homebrew, `cmake ninja python zlib sdl2 glslang spirv-cross`. Linux: Clang, CMake, Ninja, Python and the SDL2, zlib, Vulkan and glslang development files (Ubuntu 24.04 package names, and the Steam Deck's distrobox, in [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md#prerequisites)). All three also need a decrypted `libsre.prx` from the PS3 firmware ([docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md#the-games-files)). 2. **The sources.** ```sh git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/soyjxck/dod3-recomp cd dod3-recomp python3 -m venv .venv # py -3 -m venv .venv on Windows .venv/bin/pip install -r ps3recomp/tools/requirements.txt -r tools/requirements.txt ``` 3. **The game's files.** Any built `dod3` (a release's, or one from another machine) installs the game into the repository root, which decrypts the update's executable to `elf/EBOOT_101.ELF` and lays out `game/disc`: ```sh DOD3_INSTALL_BASE=. path/to/dod3 --install [DLC .pkg ...] ``` 4. **Lift the PPU code** (a few minutes; about 550 MB of C++ in `recompiled_101/`): ```sh .venv/bin/python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_loader.py elf/EBOOT_101.ELF -o out/v101/ .venv/bin/python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_lifter.py elf/EBOOT_101.ELF \ --functions out/v101/EBOOT_101.functions.json \ --hle-stubs out/v101/EBOOT_101.imports.json \ --code-end 0x157fc00 \ --nonvolatile-locals \ --hook 0x000C1E50 --hook 0x00EE7728 --hook 0x00272E58 \ -o recompiled_101/ ``` 5. **Lift the SPU programs** into `spu/`, with the native fast paths hooked in: ```sh tools/lift_spu.sh ``` 6. **Compile.** Windows, from a plain command prompt (the script finds Visual Studio, LLVM, CMake and vcpkg): ```bat tools\build_win.bat ``` macOS: ```sh cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build ``` A clean build takes about 15 minutes, nearly all of it the lifted code. 7. **Run** the game installed in the repository root: ```sh DOD3_INSTALL_BASE=. build/dod3 ``` [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md) has the CMake options, the developer run form, packaging a release and regenerating the committed tables; [docs/TECHNICAL.md](docs/TECHNICAL.md) how the port works; [docs/DEBUGGING.md](docs/DEBUGGING.md) the switches, profiling and the regression tests; [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) the layout of the tree and the conventions. ## Status | | | |---|---| | Windows 10/11, Direct3D 12 | Playable. 60 fps at 4K on an RTX 4090 / i9-13900K (chapter 1 through the heavy destruction scene, open areas, the village); 120 fps holds at lower resolutions | | Windows, Vulkan | Experimental (`RSX_BACKEND = vulkan`) | | Linux, Vulkan | Experimental. Tested on a Steam Deck (SteamOS, Desktop Mode): the chapter 1 battle at 55-65 fps uncapped, the heaviest moments in the 40s; Gaming Mode not yet tried | | macOS 13+, Apple silicon, Metal | Playable. 60 fps at 1080p in battle on an M1 Pro | | Game version | The 1.01 update (required) | | DLC | All 20 packs, including the Japanese voice pack | What the port adds over the original: any internal resolution (supersampling included), windowed, borderless or full-screen display, wider screens (16:10, 21:9, 32:9), a frame-rate cap of your choice (60 and 120 tested) or one that follows the scene, with the frames shown at even intervals, FXAA or MSAA, anisotropic filtering, a wider field of view, sharper shadows, a longer draw distance for scenery and for trees, HDR (Windows and macOS: the light the game clips at white goes up to your display's peak), a depth of field and bloom drawn smoothly at high resolutions, depth of field and the blood on the screen each on or off, skipping the intro logos and movie, pausing or muting when the window is in the background, keyboard and mouse, trophies (a pop-up as you earn one, and their list in the launcher), cheats, and the button prompts of the pad you hold -- set in the launcher, or in a Graphics Settings, a System Settings, an Advanced Graphics and a Picture Settings page added to the game's own Settings menu. The launcher also installs your DLC and two fan-made mods (the Spanish translation, with the added pages in Spanish, and the DLC Undub), and on Windows updates the port from its releases. Known issues: the game has been tested on few machines, and at 16:10, 21:9 and 32:9 some of the HUD is still out of place. ## How it fits together ``` elf/EBOOT_101.ELF --ppu_loader/ppu_lifter--> recompiled_101/*.cpp (the game's PPU code as C++) SPU programs --tools/lift_spu.sh------> spu/ (SPURS tasks, jobs, the audio DSP) src/ ---------------------------> the port: the runner, native fast paths, the settings menu, the installer ps3recomp/ ---------------------------> runtime, HLE libraries, the RSX draw engine and its backends ``` The executable `dod3` installs the game from your files (a Dear ImGui setup, `src/install/` and `src/ui/`), then opens a launcher for its mods, DLC and settings, and runs it. ## Legal This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Square Enix, Access Games or Sony Interactive Entertainment. Drakengard 3 and all of its assets belong to their owners; none are included, and the port only runs from a copy of the game you own. The code in this repository is under the [MIT License](LICENSE). It builds on ps3recomp (MIT) and includes Dear ImGui (MIT) and the Inter typeface (SIL Open Font License 1.1); see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). ## Credits - [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet: the recompiler, the runtime and the PS3 library implementations. This port's changes to it are in the [soyjxck/ps3recomp](https://github.com/soyjxck/ps3recomp) fork, the `ps3recomp/` submodule. - [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net): the reference for much of the PS3's behaviour, and the source of two techniques used here (write-watched texture memory, a guest clock that stops while the game is paused). - [XenonRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/XenonRecomp) and [Unleashed Recompiled](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp): the model for a recompiled port, and for its installer. - [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui) by Omar Cornut: the setup's and the launcher's user interface. - [Inter](https://github.com/rsms/inter) by Rasmus Andersson: their typeface. - The mods the launcher installs are their authors' work: the Spanish translation by Traducciones Vacuno ([TraduSquare](https://tradusquare.es)), the DLC Undub by Canzah and Slow.

# Bleach: Soul Resurrección — PC Recomp

[![Support / Apoiar no Ko-fi](.github/assets/kofi-button.svg)](https://ko-fi.com/pxavier)

**[Português](#português) · [English](#english)**

---
## English

A static recompilation of **Bleach: Soul Resurrección** (PS3, BLUS30769) for Windows. The game's code is
translated from PowerPC/SPU to C++ and built as a native Windows program, rendering with DirectX 12 — it is
not an emulator.

> **This project does not contain the game.** No game code, files, images, sound, text or saves are distributed
> here or in the setup. You need your own, legally obtained copy of the game (BLUS30769, the US release without
> updates), for example a dump of your own disc made on your own PS3.

### Support my work

If you enjoy this project and would like to support my work on the recomp, you can contribute through
**[Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/pxavier)**. Your support helps me dedicate time to development, fixes and improvements.
Contributions are entirely optional, and the project remains free for everyone. Thank you!

### What the recomp offers

- Internal resolution from 720p up to 4K.
- 30, 60 or 120 FPS (the simulation runs at the chosen rate; game speed stays the original).
- Borderless fullscreen or windowed. The picture always keeps the chosen aspect ratio, with black bars when the screen has
  another shape.
- **Experimental** ultrawide (21:9 and 32:9): wider 3D view, with the HUD and menus filling the screen.
- Game text in English (original), Brazilian Portuguese, French or Spanish.
- Launcher in English, Portuguese, French and Spanish, with ready-made shortcuts for Steam/Playnite.

### Requirements

- Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit.
- A DirectX 12 graphics card.
- 8 GB of RAM recommended.
- 4 GB free while installing (afterwards the game takes about 0.4 GB).
- An internet connection while installing.
- Your dump of **Bleach: Soul Resurrección BLUS30769**: the `.iso` file or the folder with `PS3_GAME`.

### Installing

1. Download **`Bleach Soul Resurrección - Setup.exe`** from [Releases](../../releases).
2. Run it. The first page checks your PC and lists what will be downloaded.
3. Choose the install folder and your game (`.iso` or dump folder). The setup checks that it is BLUS30769.
4. PS3 firmware: keep **Download from Sony** (the setup downloads the official `PS3UPDAT.PUP` from Sony's PS3
   update server) or choose a `PS3UPDAT.PUP` you already have. Only the system fonts are used.
5. Click **Install**. The setup then:
   - decrypts **your** game's `EBOOT.BIN` with RPCS3;
   - extracts the firmware's fonts and font modules;
   - downloads the build tools from their official sites (Python, Capstone, CMake, Ninja and LLVM-MinGW, about
     245 MB, every file checked against its SHA-256);
   - **recompiles the game on your PC** (3 to 20 minutes depending on the CPU);
   - removes the tools and creates the shortcuts.

Downloads are kept in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\BleachSoulResurreccion\downloads`, so a reinstall or an update does not
download everything again.

#### Why does RPCS3 come with it?

[RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net) is the open-source PS3 emulator (GPL v2). The setup uses its program for only two
things: **decrypting your disc's EBOOT** and **reading Sony's firmware file**. The game does not run on RPCS3;
it runs as a native Windows program.

### Playing

Open the **Bleach Soul Resurrección** shortcut. In the launcher pick the resolution, FPS, display mode, aspect
ratio and the game text language, then click **Play**. The launcher remembers your dump; an `.iso` is mounted by Windows
automatically while the game runs.

- **Saves and settings:** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\BleachSoulResurreccion` (the uninstaller asks whether to remove them).
- **Shaders:** the first time each scene appears, the game prepares its shaders and may pause briefly; after
  that they are kept on disk.
- **Esc does not quit the game.** To quit, use the game's menu, the window's close button or Alt+F4.
- **Shortcuts without the launcher:** see the *Launch options* folder in the install folder (`--play`, `--fps`,
  `--display`, `--resolution`, `--aspect`, `--text`).

### Known issues

- Ultrawide (21:9 / 32:9) is still experimental: some screen may have elements out of place. If you find one, please
  open an issue with a screenshot. For the original experience, use 16:9.
- If the game closes with an error, the logs are in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\BleachSoulResurreccion\logs` (the install
  log is `logs\instalacao.log`). Please open an issue with them.

### For developers

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `ps3recomp/` | The [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) SDK (MIT) with this project's changes (runtime, HLE, D3D12 renderer). |
| `bleach-recomp/` | The recomp's own code (`main.cpp`, `native_*.h`, `CMakeLists.txt`), the manifests and `construir.py`, which generates and builds everything from the decrypted EBOOT. |
| `bleach-recomp/edicoes-recompilado.json` | The hand fixes to the generated code, stored as hashes of the original lines + the new lines (the game's code is not in it). |
| `launcher/` | Launcher and setup (C#, .NET Framework 4.8). `montar-instalador-ci.py` builds the complete installer with the tools prepared by `prepare-build.ps1`. |
| `traducao/` | Game text translations: only the translated strings and a hash of each original string. |

**Build the installer:** you can generate the complete **`Bleach Soul Resurrección - Setup.exe`** from this
public repository by following the [manual build instructions](docs/installer-verification.md#rebuild-locally-powershell-7-windows).
The steps prepare the required tools, compile the launcher and setup, and package the installer. Building the
installer does not require a game dump or PS3 firmware; those are supplied by the player when installing the game.

**Build the game manually** (with your decrypted EBOOT, the firmware modules, Python 3.11 + `capstone`,
LLVM-MinGW, CMake and Ninja):

```
python bleach-recomp/construir.py --elf EBOOT.elf --firmware <folder with libfont.prx, libfontFT.prx, libfreetype.prx, libresc.prx> --kit . --toolchain <llvm-mingw>\bin --cmake cmake.exe --ninja ninja.exe --trabalho build --saida bin
```

### Credits

- **ps3recomp** — sp00nznet and contributors (MIT).
- **RPCS3** — the RPCS3 team (GPL v2): EBOOT and firmware decryption, and a reference for PS3 behaviour.
- **FFmpeg** (GPL v3) — the game's videos. **LLVM-MinGW** (mstorsjo), **CMake**, **Ninja**, **Python**, **Capstone**.
- Recompilation, fixes, launcher and translations: this project.
- *Bleach* © Tite Kubo/Shueisha, TV Tokyo, dentsu, Pierrot. *Bleach: Soul Resurrección* (developed by Racjin)
  belongs to its respective owners. This is a non-commercial fan project, not affiliated with those rights
  holders. All trademarks belong to their owners.

---
## Português

Uma recompilação estática de **Bleach: Soul Resurrección** (PS3, BLUS30769) para Windows. O código do jogo é
traduzido de PowerPC/SPU para C++ e compilado como um programa nativo do Windows, com renderização em DirectX 12
— não é um emulador.

> **Este projeto não contém o jogo.** Nenhum código, arquivo, imagem, som, texto ou save do jogo é distribuído
> aqui ou no instalador. Você precisa da sua própria cópia original do jogo (BLUS30769, a versão americana sem
> atualização), obtida legalmente, por exemplo fazendo o dump do seu disco no seu PS3.

### Apoie meu trabalho

Se você gostou do projeto e deseja apoiar meu trabalho no recomp, pode contribuir pelo
**[Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/pxavier)**. Seu apoio me ajuda a dedicar tempo ao desenvolvimento, às correções e às melhorias.
As contribuições são totalmente opcionais, e o projeto continua gratuito para todos. Obrigado!

### O que o recomp oferece

- Resolução interna de 720p até 4K.
- 30, 60 ou 120 FPS (a simulação roda na taxa escolhida; a velocidade do jogo continua a original).
- Tela cheia sem borda ou janela. A imagem sempre mantém a proporção escolhida, com barras pretas quando a tela tem outro
  formato.
- Ultrawide **experimental** (21:9 e 32:9): visão 3D mais larga, com HUD e menus preenchendo a tela.
- Texto do jogo em inglês (original), português do Brasil, francês ou espanhol.
- Launcher em inglês, português, francês e espanhol, com atalhos prontos para Steam/Playnite.

### Requisitos

- Windows 10 ou 11, 64 bits.
- Placa de vídeo com DirectX 12.
- 8 GB de RAM recomendados.
- 4 GB livres durante a instalação (depois o jogo ocupa cerca de 0,4 GB).
- Internet durante a instalação.
- Seu dump do **Bleach: Soul Resurrección BLUS30769**: o arquivo `.iso` ou a pasta com `PS3_GAME`.

### Como instalar

1. Baixe **`Bleach Soul Resurrección - Setup.exe`** na página de [Releases](../../releases).
2. Abra o setup. A primeira tela verifica o seu PC e mostra o que vai ser baixado.
3. Escolha a pasta de instalação e o seu jogo (`.iso` ou a pasta do dump). O setup confere se é o BLUS30769.
4. Firmware do PS3: deixe **Baixar da Sony** (o setup baixa o `PS3UPDAT.PUP` oficial do servidor de
   atualizações da Sony) ou escolha um `PS3UPDAT.PUP` que você já tenha. Só as fontes do sistema são usadas.
5. Clique em **Instalar**. O setup então:
   - decifra o `EBOOT.BIN` do **seu** jogo com o RPCS3;
   - extrai as fontes e os módulos de fonte do firmware;
   - baixa as ferramentas de compilação dos sites oficiais (Python, Capstone, CMake, Ninja e LLVM-MinGW,
     cerca de 245 MB, cada arquivo conferido por SHA-256);
   - **recompila o jogo no seu PC** (de 3 a 20 minutos, conforme o processador);
   - apaga as ferramentas e cria os atalhos.

Os downloads ficam guardados em `%LOCALAPPDATA%\BleachSoulResurreccion\downloads`; uma reinstalação ou
atualização não baixa tudo de novo.

#### Por que o RPCS3 vem junto?

O [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net) é o emulador de PS3 de código aberto (GPL v2). O setup usa o programa dele só para
duas coisas: **decifrar o EBOOT do seu disco** e **ler o arquivo de firmware da Sony**. O jogo não roda no
RPCS3; ele roda como um programa nativo do Windows.

### Como jogar

Abra o atalho **Bleach Soul Resurrección**. No launcher escolha resolução, FPS, modo de tela, proporção e o idioma do
texto do jogo, e clique em **Jogar**. O launcher lembra o seu dump; se ele for um `.iso`, o Windows o monta sozinho
enquanto o jogo roda.

- **Saves e configurações:** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\BleachSoulResurreccion` (o desinstalador pergunta se deve apagá-los).
- **Shaders:** na primeira vez que cada cena aparece, o jogo prepara os shaders dela e pode dar uma pausa curta;
  depois eles ficam guardados no disco.
- **Esc não fecha o jogo.** Para sair, use o menu do jogo, o botão de fechar da janela ou Alt+F4.
- **Atalhos sem launcher:** veja a pasta *Opções de execução* na pasta de instalação (`--jogar`, `--fps`,
  `--tela`, `--resolucao`, `--proporcao`, `--texto`).

### Problemas conhecidos

- O ultrawide (21:9 / 32:9) ainda é experimental: alguma tela pode ter elementos fora do lugar. Se encontrar uma, abra
  uma *issue* com um print. Para a experiência original, use 16:9.
- Se o jogo fechar com erro, os logs ficam em `%LOCALAPPDATA%\BleachSoulResurreccion\logs` (e o da instalação em
  `logs\instalacao.log`). Abra uma *issue* com eles.

### Para desenvolvedores

| Pasta | Conteúdo |
|---|---|
| `ps3recomp/` | O SDK [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) (MIT) com as alterações deste projeto (runtime, HLE, renderizador D3D12). |
| `bleach-recomp/` | O código próprio do recomp (`main.cpp`, `native_*.h`, `CMakeLists.txt`), os manifestos e `construir.py`, que gera e compila tudo a partir do EBOOT decifrado. |
| `bleach-recomp/edicoes-recompilado.json` | As correções feitas à mão no código gerado, gravadas como *hash* das linhas originais + linhas novas (o código do jogo não está nele). |
| `launcher/` | Launcher e setup (C#, .NET Framework 4.8). `montar-instalador-ci.py` gera o instalador completo com as ferramentas preparadas por `prepare-build.ps1`. |
| `traducao/` | Traduções do texto do jogo: só os textos traduzidos e o *hash* do texto original. |

**Compilar o instalador:** você pode gerar o **`Bleach Soul Resurrección - Setup.exe`** completo a partir deste
repositório público seguindo o [passo a passo de compilação manual](docs/installer-verification.md#rebuild-locally-powershell-7-windows).
As etapas preparam as ferramentas necessárias, compilam o launcher e o setup e montam o instalador. Para gerar
o instalador, não é preciso ter o dump do jogo nem o firmware do PS3; o jogador fornece esses arquivos durante a instalação.

**Compilar o jogo manualmente** (com seu EBOOT decifrado, os módulos de firmware, Python 3.11 + `capstone`,
LLVM-MinGW, CMake e Ninja):

```
python bleach-recomp/construir.py --elf EBOOT.elf --firmware <pasta com libfont.prx, libfontFT.prx, libfreetype.prx, libresc.prx> --kit . --toolchain <llvm-mingw>\bin --cmake cmake.exe --ninja ninja.exe --trabalho build --saida bin
```

10036dbff1459d1a3d5c4913a3047eff28f3aef7.message:
Setup: the first Python without curl or tar (Wine, CrossOver)

Setup's first step downloads Python with Windows' own curl.exe and unpacks it with its tar.exe, from System32. Wine
and CrossOver ship neither, so a Mac player on CrossOver stopped at "Setup could not start its first download", and the
log did not say why.

When curl or tar does not start, the host now does it itself. Machines that have curl and tar work as before.
- setup_http.cpp downloads with WinHTTP, which Windows and Wine both have. It does what the curl line does:
  - https only, TLS 1.2 or later;
  - redirects followed, but never from https to http;
  - a minute's timeouts;
  - a Range request carrying on from the .part file. A 200 answer starts the file over; a 206 for another range
    deletes it.
  Cancel closes its handles, which ends the call it is in.
- setup_unzip.cpp unpacks the zip:
  - stored and deflated entries, inflated by stb_image's zlib, which the UI already builds;
  - each file's CRC-32 checked;
  - zip64, encryption and several disks refused.
  The names go through the same check as tar's, and the archive's size and SHA-256 are checked first, as before.
- FIX lines (the reason under Details) now also go to the log, so a report has them.
- DES_SETUP_NO_SYSTEM_TOOLS=1 hides curl and tar, for tests.
- crc32.hpp is report.cpp's CRC-32, now shared with the zip reader, and its table is built once in a thread-safe way.
- docs/88 section 5 describes the fallback.

Off Windows nothing changes: setup_http.cpp has no download there, so a missing curl fails as before.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

17c28aac99235d025c5c8ac77573dd75f4a4815c.message:
Run defaults: Havok's threads at normal priority (PPU_RAISE_BELOW=0)

ps3recomp raises a title's threads below guest priority 1000 to above
normal, for audio and I/O pollers that sleep between blocks. In this game
those are Havok's: hkSpuUtil Helper (80), Havok PPU Thread (100) and
SPURuntimeService (200). The Havok PPU Thread polls the job queue's lock
with usleep(1), which waits in place (docs/77). Raised, on 2-4 CPUs it
likely keeps the SPU tasks of its own step off the cores: in a console
trace the long frames are the main thread waiting 34-42 ms for the step
while that thread makes no call for about 40 ms.

Held to 2 CPUs at 60 fps (PS3_AFFINITY=5, with ps3recomp #261), two
rounds, 9 roll-breaks each:
- raised (the runtime's 1000): 3.1% and 2.9% of frames over 25 ms away
  from breaks, jitter 2.8 ms, 68 and 88 frames over 25 ms after breaks;
- none raised (0): 0.5% and 0.6%, jitter 1.1 ms, 8 and 11;
- Havok PPU + helper raised (150): 2.1%, 84; helper only (90): as 0.
Audio gaps (AUDIO_GAPS=1) were fewer with 0: 1 and 4 against 5 and 12.
libmixer's threads still go up by name (PPU_MIXER_RAISE), and the
runtime's line stays at 1000 for other titles.

27d85b1d73fe516de055145649639c3558825baf.message:
Problem reports: put the player's save in the zip

So that a reported problem can be loaded where it happened, instead of
played up to again, both kinds of report now hold the save: Report an
issue (the menu) and the crash, hang and lost-graphics dialog's Report on
GitHub.

report::save_files takes each save folder in the game's save root, found
as cellSaveData.c finds it (PS3_SAVEDATA_ROOT, else
gamedata/dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata in the working folder; the
crash dialog's process has the game's environment and working folder).
Each goes in as save/<folder>/<file>. Two kinds of file stay out:

- the folder's two pictures (ICON0.PNG, PIC1.PNG), which are the game's
  art;
- a file the runtime is still writing (.<name>.tmp).

If a file changed or was being written while the folder was read, the
folder is read again, at most twice and half a second apart. The limits
are 8 MB a file and 32 MB in all; a Demon's Souls save is ten 256 KB
files. game.txt (and the crash issue's System block) gets one line: the
folder, how many files and KB, how many minutes before the report it was
saved, and whether the game was saving meanwhile.

The save holds the characters and their names, and the issue is public.
So the texts that said a report has no save data now say it holds the
save, with the characters' names: the menu's box, the crash dialog's
three, the README and docs/74. The port writes its own PARAM.SFO, so no
PSN account is in it.

3dfb4ee2d121c86a58f93ffe972471477843b0bf.message:
The Linux download gets the Vulkan renderer and setup's shader step

Issue #351, the first Steam Deck report: long freezes when a new scene loads. The Linux download was still the legacy
renderer on vkd3d alone, which compiles each shader as the game first draws it. A level load needs 18 vertex and 27 pixel
programs: 8.2 s through the shipped vkd3d on the development PC, about 19 s scaled to the Deck, and the tester's notices read
16-23 s. docs/120 said Vulkan was Linux's default, which is true of the option but not of what shipped: host.yml built that
version only as a check, on a second build, and never uploaded it.

host.yml now builds the runtime with PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL from the start, as on Windows, and the second build goes. So Linux
starts on Vulkan, and setup's shader step has its spv target (it was Pass::Off before). A Vulkan start that fails falls back
to the legacy renderer in the same process, and the next start after one that crashed uses it too.

The licences of what the renderer compiles in (glslang, SPIRV-Tools, SPIRV-Headers, volk, the Vulkan headers) go along, as
in the Windows job. README and docs/76 and 120 say what ships.

port: enemies no longer T-pose for a frame above 30 fps

Havok's sample-and-combine fills a bone whose animation weight is under
the skeleton's reference-pose threshold (0.05) with the reference pose, a
T-pose. When an enemy starts a new move, the new clip can fade in from 0
with nothing under it, growing about as t^2. At 30 fps one frame of the
fade is under the threshold; above 30 fps several are, near weight 0, so
the enemy is drawn in the T-pose for 20-30 ms.

des_refpose_rate runs after each load of the threshold: the SPU sample
job's copy (0x01005978) and the four PPU sample paths. It scales the
threshold by (30 dt)^2, so a fade stays under it for about one frame at
any frame rate. Nothing changes at 30 fps or below. DES_TPOSEFIX=0 turns
it off live. Region rows for the European, Japanese and Asian discs.

Tutorial route, unlocked: with the fix off, a fade-in in view drew 5-6
frames at 72-100% reference pose; with it on, one frame at 26%.

6927ea3b096b2f11f363722791c5f4fbffebbe4e.message:
Setup: when Python can't check a server's certificate, Windows' own curl downloads (#493)

#493: setup stopped at the compiler's download with "CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED:
unable to get local issuer certificate", and the update check said there was no
connection to GitHub. On the same PC Windows' curl had just downloaded Python.

On Windows, Python checks a server's certificate against the roots it copies from
Windows' store. Windows adds a root there only when its own check first needs one
(from Windows Update), so a PC where nothing Windows runs has needed that root yet
fails Python's check and passes Windows'. A TLS-scanning antivirus or proxy that
Windows trusts can look the same.

Now, when Python's check refuses the certificate, on Windows only:
- a tool's download (fetch.py) goes through Windows' own curl.exe, from the System
  folder, with the host's own options (setup_python.cpp): https only, -C - to carry
  on from the .part file, and a start over once when the server ignores the range.
  The size and SHA-256 checks are unchanged. Setup's log gets a note saying so.
- the update check (update.read_feed, with its ETag) and the release's small files
  (update._small) get the same: a GET through curl.
Any other failure, and any failure off Windows, is reported as before.

Tested on Demon's Souls only. Not re-run: Virtua Fighter 5, The Simpsons Game, Tornado Outbreak, Tokyo Jungle, Midway Arcade Origins.

Setup: have RPCS3 open the update's package, remove the key

Setup's rule is no keys and no decryptor (docs/51, docs/90), and #442 broke
it with a PS3 package key and an AES routine in game_update.py. No release
has them. The player's RPCS3, which setup already runs to decrypt the game's
files, now installs the package in a folder of setup's own
(rpcs3.install_package). Without an RPCS3 that setup can start, the player
is told to install the package in RPCS3 and choose its folder.

RPCS3 decrypts the 14 .sdat files as it installs them and keeps their names,
so a folder it installed failed the table's sums and was refused. They equal
the table's decrypted files, so either form is now good, and they aren't
decrypted again.

The journal also wrapped UpdateError, so a sentence meant for the player
became a failed step.
