7ef59983f9e18a6a30a170f4fbbf50dfb90ce379.message:
CI: cache the wrapper UI's FreeType, RmlUi and stb sources

port/ui/CMakeLists.txt clones FreeType, RmlUi and stb by commit, so not
shallow, in every configure of the port or the UI. On #320's run these
configures took 67-102 s each, most of it those clones:

- ci.yml, Linux: Wrapper UI, configure 91 s; Game build description,
  configure 95 s.
- ci.yml, Windows: Configure 67 s.
- host.yml, Windows: Configure des_host 71 s.
- host.yml, Linux: Configure des_host 102 s; the both-routes configure
  clones them again.

Each job now caches a copy of the three without .git, keyed on
port/ui/CMakeLists.txt (one per system), and hands it to the configure
through FetchContent's FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_<NAME>. On a miss, the
configure clones as before and the step after it keeps the copy, which
also serves a second configure in the same job.

tools/ci/fetch_src.py does both halves for every shell:
- "args" prints the -D lines when the copy is complete (its .complete
  file, written last), else nothing, so the configure clones.
- "keep" copies <build>/_deps/<name>-src. It never fails the job: a failed
  copy is removed, so no half copy is saved.

The game build descriptions name none of these sources, so their check
is unaffected.

port: Lua takes room in the port's heap when its own heap is full

Each of the game's Lua states gets its memory through a small-block pool,
and the pool gets pages and every block over 128 bytes from a heap object.
Two heap classes stand behind the game's Lua states, and each hands
everything to one fixed arena of its own:
- 0x01852D20 serves the two script systems' states, in 2.375 MB;
- 0x01852EC0 serves a third, small state, in 9 MB.

When an arena can't give a block, luaM_realloc throws LUA_ERRMEM. Nothing
catches it on a character's script, so Lua calls exit(1) and the window
closes. The early collection (des_luagc.cpp) keeps the scripts well below
the limit above 30 fps. This change is the safety net under it.

Every method of the two classes that hands out or takes back a block is
wrapped (all calls to them go through their vtables). The classes are one
template over a different arena: the same methods at the same vtable
offsets, forwarding to the same functions.
- When an arena can't give an allocation, it comes from the port's own
  guest heap instead.
- Free, realloc, a block's size and "is this block yours" send those blocks
  back there. Every other block goes to the game's own method unchanged.
- Until an arena can't give a block, nothing changes.
- The pool finds a block's page by its address range, not by alignment, so
  pages from the port's heap work the same way.
- Lua 5.0 can't safely collect inside the allocator, so the net doesn't
  collect: it only gives room.

Which heaps a Lua state can get: the game's lua_open takes the heap, and a
state's threads share its pool. Only the state's constructor calls lua_open,
and the constructor is called from six places.
- Four are the script systems, and they read one global heap pointer.
- Two are "new state on this heap" methods, each reached only through its
  class's vtable. One is in the code with the second TOC and reaches the
  constructor through a TOC stub.
- Both methods are wrapped as well. Each writes a line to the log if a state
  ever lands

8fb4175e5f8f6062c0d63ae3dd90706b0a91c36d.message:
tools: DES_MEMSTAT, how full the game's own heaps get (docs/59 T1)

The game makes 13 heaps of fixed sizes at boot and never asks for more;
a full one ends in its error report. Mods with bigger files need more of
some of them. DES_MEMSTAT=1 shows which, and how close each comes:

- A thread reads each heap's arena every millisecond. It only reads (no
  lock taken, nothing in the game called), so the game runs as without
  it. Each class keeps its arena in a global of its own; the ten
  DLStaticHeap-like arenas keep their free bytes at +0x3C and their block
  list's ends at +0x04/+0x18, HAVOK's, MO's and TEMP's the same fields
  8 bytes lower (+0x34, +0x28/+0x2C).
- The log gets each heap's size, a line as its peak use passes another
  tenth from half full up, and a table (size, in use now, at most, share)
  every DES_MEMSTAT_EVERY seconds and on every game error.
  DES_MEMSTAT=2 adds each arena's first words.
- With DES_MEMSTAT off, a game error still prints one table: each heap's
  use at that moment (no peaks: no thread ran). A full heap ends in the
  game's error report, so a player's report zip then shows which one.
- A 14th row, LOCAL, is the game's heap over the RSX's local (video)
  memory, 248 MB. Its arena is in a static object: the base its heap
  object points at (0x01AD6358) + 0x18, as the class's methods take it.
- The addresses are in the region tables: European +0x280, Japanese and
  Asian +0x30, read from the game's own address table that the heap
  methods use (r30 = [r2 + slot], then [r30 + offset]).
- des_heap.cpp: ds_heap_usage, the port's own guest heap now and at most.

Off by default (apart from that one table). First numbers (1-2 bridge, 240 s): the file-loading heap
CORERES peaks at 92% of its 12.25 MB without mods and at 12.24 MB with a
large set of texture and model mods.

tools/des: halimg compares an HDR snapshot in 8-bit codes when its paper white is known

Under the vk rule an HDRP pair was held to 1e-3, with at most 0.01% of
the pixels allowed up to 8/255 (relative to the larger of 1 and the
value). That bound is in the snapshot's linear units, while the pixels
it is for, ones that sampled the next texel of an 8-bit texture, differ
by a step that grows with the paper white. At the settings a player
uses (RSX_HDR_WHITE=400, scale 300, AA 2, aniso 16) Vulkan's snapshots
of capsetu's courtyard and fog wall failed it with 19 and 119 pixels,
where the frames' own 8-bit shots pass: in codes those pixels are 1 to
5 apart, scattered one by one, nothing above 8.

- halimg.py --hdr-white <paper white, nits / 80> [--hdr-curve
  gamma|srgb]: under vk an HDRP pair is turned back into the codes the
  blit decoded (gamma 2.2, or the sRGB curve for RSX_HDR_GAMMA=1) and
  held to the 8-bit rule, heat map included. A NaN fails. Without it,
  and in the hdr mode, the rule is as it was.
- halgate.sh reads the paper white from A's "HDR snap" line and the
  curve from its "HDR: on" line.
- docs/120's G3 line says so.

The self-test gains the round trips (both curves), 120 pixels 4 codes
off (fails without the white, passes with it), 0.06% of pixels 2 codes
off and 0.02% 12 codes off (fail), the hdr mode and a NaN (fail).

af3fb1da919858470cb1ca109eebda71388404e6.message:
tools/region: data through the code's own address tables, and no guesses on the 1.04 discs

region_table.py find gave a confident wrong answer for data on the
Japanese and Asian 1.04 discs: +0x80 for the heap globals at 0x01AD6498..
0x01AD6AF0 ("data, 26 references"), where the game has them at +0x30. It
counted TOC slots holding a base below the address, read at the same slot
offset on the other disc. Two things break that on the 1.04 discs:
- their TOC starts 0x18 higher and many slots moved, so the same offset
  is another slot (kContextAspect's one exact vote pointed 0x60 off);
- their data moved in pieces (the 0x50 bytes below 0x01AD62C8 shrank, and
  some objects were reordered), so a base below can have moved by another
  amount than the address.

Changes:
- New way, find_table: code that loads the address from a TOC slot, or
  loads an address table's base and then the table's word at a fixed
  offset (lwz rX,d(r2); lwz rY,k(rX)), is matched on the other disc, and
  that disc's own slot gives the answer. This is how the heap classes
  reach their arenas.
- SlotMap: whether TOC slots keep their offsets is found from a sample of
  matched loads (yes on the European disc, no on the 1.04 discs); where
  they don't, find_data maps each slot through code that loads it, and
  the anchors (find_between) are not used.
- The ways that read the other disc (find_table, find_content) win; the
  ones that assume (find_data, find_between) only answer when those two
  don't, and a disagreement is noted. On a disc whose data moved in
  pieces, a base below is only a hint ("perhaps ..."), never an answer.

verify against each table (the tables as on master plus the DES_MEMSTAT
rows):
- European: 270 agree, 0 differ, 25 unchecked -> 285 / 0 / 10.
- Japanese and Asian (1.04 EBOOTs, the tables checked with the same code):
  before, the arena rows came out +0x80 (wrong) and kContextAspect's
  agreeing row would have been reported as differing; after, 280 agree,
  0 differ, 15 unchecked.
The 13 unit tests pass; check passes.

aspect: markers on a tall picture keep WorldToScreen's y (#472)

At 16:10 the lock-on reticle and the floating health bars sat 11% too far
from the middle, up and down.

WorldToScreen (0x0079EE00) builds its projection from the camera's own
FOV and shape (0x003DFF40 reads camera +0x50..+0x5C). On a tall picture

(cam_record_projection), so its y is 16:9's. In the taller picture a point
is (16/9) / A nearer the middle, and the taller canvas is (16/9) / A
taller: the two cancel. des_hud_w2s stretched y by the canvas's height on
top of that, as x is stretched at a wide shape.

  middle by A / (16/9). Before, it was left 11% out there too.

b82f2ba878889ea7919cbd87dca8cd6eb7c1c75f.message:
Pin: ps3recomp 079f5aad (#254 an empty SpursQueue poll takes no lock)

#254: with LIBSRE_OWN (the default since #390), a non-blocking
cellSpursQueuePopBody of an empty queue now reads the counts without
the lock-line stripe and returns AGAIN, as libsre's lwarx loop does.

HighGraphics' queue and its command ring share one of the 64 stripes.
Every poll took that stripe, so the ring's SPU reader fell off its
lock-free read and collided with HighGraphics' ring stores. On 2 CPUs
the game drew about a third fewer frames than on libsre (Linux) and
about 12% fewer draws (Windows). On all CPUs the two were even.

Counters, Windows on 2 CPUs, one boot a side: HighGraphics' contended
stripe takes per million, libsre 133, master 66,894, #254 205. One
Linux boot of #254 on 2 CPUs drew 2,207 frames in the window (master
averaged 1,479, libsre 2,272; one run on a PC in use, not a timing).

Six instruction-hook handlers decode the instruction their hook runs after,
to find the register to rescale: the camera eases and the bow zoom
(des_cam_rate, des_cam_step, des_cam_keep), the foot IK (des_ik_rate), the
locked-on twist (des_twist_rate), and the sound and fade rates (keep_rate,
des_fade_rate). They read it at the hook's key, which stays the US address,
so on the European disc they read an unrelated instruction. The camera,
noise and fade fixes did nothing there, and the IK and twist fixes could
rescale an unrelated register.

des_region_addr() gives the running disc's address for a key, and
hook_insn() reads the instruction there. Every hook's instruction is the
same on both discs, so nothing else changes.

e4cc08a9a6ac2614ac9c0dd2e46d0ac466ee474c.message:
A processor without SSE4.1 gets a clear message, not a crash

Issues #349 and #350: a player's Pentium E5400 crashed with c000001d as the window opened. The runtime and the game module
are built with SSE4.1, and that CPU doesn't have it, so the first such instruction ended the program (pmovsxdq in
create_window, rsxc_d3d12.c). The crash dialog then asked them to report it, with nothing saying what was wrong.

des_cpu_check.cpp now asks the processor first, and says so if SSE4.1 is missing. It runs ahead of the C++ static
initializers, and is the one source here built without SSE4.1, so it can run on such a processor. The check comes
before setup too, so nobody spends time on a build that can't run.

AVX, LZCNT, AES and the like in the exe are in Microsoft's runtime and mbedTLS, which ask the CPU before using them. SSE4.1
is the only one the program assumes, so it is the only one checked.

The README now names the requirement. CI runs the check both ways (DES_TEST_OLD_CPU=1, and plainly) on both systems.

There is no processor without SSE4.1 here: the message was checked with DES_TEST_OLD_CPU=1, on the path it takes.

settings: Vulkan is the Renderer's default on a GeForce GTX 1070

Two GTX 1070 owners (#205, and #372 on 0.1.0) had the GPU stop
responding on D3D12 again and again. Each time Windows reset the
driver in the middle of a frame (DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG), and the game
could draw no more. Both found that Settings > Display > Renderer:
Vulkan stops it. No other GPU has shown it.

- On Windows, when the GPU the renderer draws on is a GeForce GTX 1070
  (desktop or laptop, not the 1070 Ti), the Renderer's default is
  Vulkan (default_of). That GPU is DXGI's first hardware adapter in
  high-performance order, the one ps3recomp's adapter_pick takes.
- 0.1.0 wrote "RSX_BACKEND = d3d12" into every settings.ini, picked or
  not. So on that GPU a saved D3D12 becomes Vulkan once, and
  renderer_rule = 1 notes it. A D3D12 picked afterwards stays, and an
  RSX_BACKEND from the environment still wins.
- Other GPUs: nothing changes. Older cards are left out on purpose:
  how well they run Vulkan is not known.
- The row's help text says so. docs/111 section 9.

DES_RENDERER_GPU=<name> stands in for the GPU's name. settings_check
has six new cases: a saved D3D12 on a GTX 1070 and on a GTX 1070 laptop
switched, a 1070 Ti kept, D3D12 picked after the check kept, no
settings.ini, and the environment winning. All 15 cases pass, built
with and without the Renderer row (clang-cl). Four of the new cases
fail against master's settings.cpp.

ec1b9e91020e42ece19b1ee2f4fc576991c6c9c1.message:
des_prework: free the last shader pass's texts once it is done

run_passes resets the precompile module before each target's pass, but
not after the last one. So whenever the start's shader pass runs (after a
session that drew new fragment-program variants, or after an update), the
last target's work stays allocated for the rest of the session: every
decompiled HLSL text (3,654 on the US disc, 44 MB), the programs and the
pipeline index's rows.

It now resets after the last pass too. Nothing reads that state after it:
the rows were handed to the renderer during the pass
(rsx_out_pso_index_add, _ready), and run_pass leaves s_state at 3, so
des_prework_status no longer asks for the counts. reset() waits for the
compile threads first.

Found with a scratch walk of the process heap 30 s into the Tutorial
(d3d12, the regression save, DES_PRECOMPILE=force): busy blocks 113.5 MB ->
69.1 MB; text blocks 10,711 (44.0 MB) -> 2,481 (0.3 MB); the heap's
committed regions 81.9 -> 53.8 MB. A start whose passes are all up to date

f586581cba40c3ac525015aab8e7d754cb432b59.message:
Physics cap: stuck arrows follow the pose, ragdolls blend by the leftover

Above 30 fps, arrows stuck in the player still hopped back at every physics
step (up to 3-4 cm at a run), and ragdolls and debris moved on unevenly at
each step. Both treated the frames since a step as one step's time, but at
144 fps a step of 1/30 s comes every 4 or 5 frames (28 or 35 ms).

- Stuck arrows (DES_PARTINTERP): a keyframed part is drawn from the pose the
  game drives it to every frame. des_kf_target, a new hook after 0x00011768
  in the stub to Havok's hard keyframe, keeps each body's last two poses,
  with the frame time of the pass that set them (from des_phys_kf: the
  passes run before des_phys_rate, so the game clock is a frame late).
  des_body_sample carries the last pose on by the game's own look-ahead, and
  des_body_sampled, a new hook after 0x011B1D6C past the sampler's call,
  writes it over the sampled transform. That is where the world would have
  the part if it stepped every frame. Without fresh poses it carries the
  last step on as before.
- Ragdolls, debris and a dead character's parts (DES_RAGINTERP): the blend
  is the cap's leftover (the game time the world has not stepped yet) over
  the step length, for a body that got the world's last step, instead of
  the game time since the body's step changed.
- The two hooks' European addresses are in BLES00932.inc. They need a
  re-lift, which setup does.

Measured with a scratch trace on the deep Palace save under the 1-1
archers, old and new from the same frames: how far an arrow's part moves
against the player from one frame to the next, 95th percentile.
- 144 fps: 32.7 mm before, 7.5 mm after (no cap: 6.2-7.1 mm).
- 60 fps: 54.6 mm before, 19.5 mm after (no cap: 17.8 mm).
- Ragdolls at 144 fps (26 bodies): the 95th percentile of the unevenness
  went from 1.26 mm to 0.75 mm.
See docs/71, "Steps of 4 or 5 frames".

trail check flags four lines. They match words ("world time", "Havok time",
"report", "fps") from learnings about measuring the cap's clock agains

fd0a6cb56aff00de1ea6c82edea55797ee267c7a.message:
port: collect Lua early above 30 fps, the game ran out of script memory

The game's Lua has its automatic collector off and collects from two
countdowns in game time, every 1.0 s and 0.5 s. Scripts make garbage per
frame, so at high frame rates there is several times more of it between two
collections. The two Lua states share a small heap. When an allocation fails,
luaD_throw(LUA_ERRMEM) finds no protected call on a character's script and
Lua calls exit(1): the window closes, in the middle of play.

Once a frame, above 30 fps, expire a countdown early when its state has made
64 KB since its last collection. The game then collects at its usual place
in the frame. It counts the guest's own bytes, so it doesn't depend on the PC.

DES_LUAGC=0 keeps the game's countdowns only. DES_LUAGC_LOG=1 prints each
state's memory once a second. DES_LUAGC_HOLD=1 is a test knob: the countdowns
never reach zero, which with DES_LUAGC=0 is the crash on demand.

1456438467.readme_excerpt:
# Soulbrandt **Demon's Souls, running natively on PC.** [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt?filter=v%2A&sort=semver&display_name=tag&label=release&color=orange)](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases/latest) [![downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/latest/total?label=downloads&color=brightgreen)](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases/latest) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1565536292324769832?label=Discord&logo=discord&logoColor=white&color=5865F2)](https://discord.gg/BzmwDeca8s)
Soulbrandt is a PC port of *Demon's Souls* (PS3, 2009). The game's original code has been converted to run directly on Windows and Linux, with no emulator. You need your own copy of the game: the US version, **BLUS30443**, or the European version, **BLES00932** (both version 1.00, on disc or from the PlayStation Store), or the Japanese or Asian disc, **BCJS30022** or **BCAS20071**, with its 1.04 update. This project includes no game files. ## Status **0.1.2, the current release, is an alpha.** Download it from the [Releases](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/releases) page. The game plays from start to finish (a tester has beaten it), but not every part has been tried on every setting, so expect bugs. What [isn't supported yet](#not-supported-yet) is below; please [report](#problems) anything you find. Questions and help: [Discord](https://discord.gg/BzmwDeca8s). ## Highlights - Up to 240 fps or unlocked, with the game's timing fixed. Up to 4K, ultrawide, 16:10 and HDR. - The US, European, Japanese and Asian versions, each with its languages, plus Japanese on the US disc and Japanese, Chinese and Korean on the European disc. - Online play on this project's own server: messages, bloodstains, ghosts, co-op, invasions and the Pantheon. - Roll in any direction while locked on, not only forward, back, left or right. - A stat respec in the Nexus (optional): get back the souls your levels cost and spend them again. - Keyboard and mouse, Xbox controllers, DualSense and DualShock 4. ## Features Press **F1** (or **L3 + R3** on a controller) at any time to open the menu. Most settings apply right away. Each setting has a short help text in the menu. **Picture** - Frame rates of 30 (the original), 60, 120, 144, 165 or 240 fps, a number of your own, or unlocked. The game's timing is fixed so it still plays the way it should. Above 60 fps is less tested. - Cutscenes play at 30 fps by default, as they judder above it. You can play them at your frame rate instead. - V-sync on or off, "Even frames" for smooth motion, and G-Sync / FreeSync. - Render resolution up to 300% (4K), ultrawide aspect ratios (21:9 and 32:9), and 16:10 for the Steam Deck's screen. - Anti-aliasing (FXAA or SMAA), anisotropic filtering up to 16x, texture filtering and a sharp scaling filter. - HDR on HDR displays (Windows), with settings for brightness, peak and shadows. - Turn off the game's depth of field and motion blur. - Window, borderless fullscreen, or exclusive fullscreen on Windows (Settings > Display > Display mode). Alt+Enter switches. - Two renderers (Settings > Display > Renderer): DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Windows starts on DirectX 12, except with a GeForce GTX 10 series card or older, which starts on Vulkan. Linux starts on Vulkan. **Controls** - Xbox controllers, DualSense and DualShock 4, over USB or Bluetooth, with vibration. Pick which controller the game uses when several are connected. - Keyboard and mouse, laid out like the Souls games on PC. To turn the camera with the mouse, turn on **Mouse look** in Settings > Controls. - Change which buttons and keys do what. - The game's button prompts show the buttons of the controller you're using, or your keys (Settings > Game > Button icons). - A deadzone for each stick, set as how far you tilt it, with a live picture of the stick (Settings > Controls). - Mouse sensitivity, inverted axes, and switching lock-on targets with a flick of the mouse. - **Roll in any direction while locked on**: the roll goes where the stick points. It's on by default; turn off **Roll toward the stick** in Settings > Controls for the original's four directions. - The mouse in the game's own menus: point and click. Experimental, and off by default. **HUD** - Move, resize, hide or show each part of the HUD. - Change its size, and choose where it goes on wide screens. **Game** - Skip the logos and the opening movie, and go straight into your last save. - **Stat respec**: the Maiden in Black, or the statue in front of where you wake in the Nexus, puts your stats back to your class's and gives back the souls your levels cost, to spend again. Off by default: turn on **Stat respec in the Nexus** in Settings > Game. - Use several soul items at once, as Drop does. On by default: turn off **Use several souls at once** in Settings > Game for the original's one at a time. - **Change Appearance** at the statue in front of where you wake in the Nexus: the game's own Edit Appearance, with your character. Off by default: turn on **Change appearance in the Nexus** in Settings > Game. - Choose the language in Settings > Game > Language. The European disc has English, French, German, Spanish and Italian, plus Japanese, Chinese (Traditional) and Korean; the US disc has English and Japanese; the Asian disc has English, Chinese (Traditional) and Korean. It starts in your PC's language when it can. A change needs a restart. **Online** - On by default, on this project's own server: messages, bloodstains, ghosts, co-op and invasions. - Players of every supported version play together. - The Pantheon in the Nexus: its statues show the characters of the players at the top of each board. - Setup asks for your online name. You can change it, or turn online play off, in Settings > Network. - A matchmaking password, so you meet only your friends. - Show or hide other players' messages, bloodstains and ghosts. **Mods** - Put mods in the mods folder (Mods in the menu or on the start screen, then Open the mods folder) and turn each one on or off there. Mods for the PS3 game or RPCS3 that replace the game's files work, and the game's own files are never changed. - A mod that changes how the game plays keeps you offline, so you never meet players without it. Mods that only change the look or sound keep online play. - When two mods change the same thing, the one higher in the list wins; the arrows on each mod move it. The list is kept in `mods\load_order.txt`, which mod managers can use too (docs/143). **The program** - A setup that builds the game from your copy, with an Original and an Enhanced preset (see [How to play](#how-to-play)). - Updates: the game checks for a new version at start and asks before changing anything. Your saves and settings are kept, and you can go back one version. - In the menu, the Large Sword of Moonlight is the cursor and a crystal lizard dances in the corner. Both can be turned off. - Trophies, with pop-ups and a tune from the game. Setup can bring your trophies and save across from RPCS3. - A Discord status: your profile shows that you're playing, the area you're in and whether you're online (Settings > Network). - **Report an issue** in the menu opens a GitHub issue with your PC's details filled in, and a zip to attach that includes your save, so the problem can be seen where it happened. It has no game files. If the game crashes or stops responding, a window offers to do the same. ## What you need - Your own copy of Demon's Souls for the PS3, as a folder with `PS3_GAME` in it: the US (BLUS30443) or European (BLES00932) disc, version 1.00, or the Japanese (BCJS30022) or Asian (BCAS20071) disc with its 1.04 update, as a folder or a `.pkg` file that setup has RPCS3 install. The US and European PlayStation Store versions (NPUB30910, NPEB01202) work once installed in RPCS3. Setup cannot use ISO files yet. - RPCS3, the free PS3 emulator. Setup has it unlock the game's encrypted files. You don't need the PS3 system software. (Or decrypt the files yourself: see below.) - Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) with a graphics card that supports DirectX 12, or Linux (see [Linux](#linux)). - A processor with SSE4.1, which most have since about 2011. - An internet connection during setup. Setup downloads a compiler and Python (about 60 MB on Windows, about 130 MB on Linux). ## How to play These steps are for the release download. 1. Download the zip for Windows (`DemonsSoulsRecomp-X.Y.Z-windows.zip`) or the tarball for Linux (`DemonsSoulsRecomp-X.Y.Z-linux.tar.xz`), and unpack it into a folder of its own. 2. Start `Soulbrandt.exe` (on Linux, `Soulbrandt`). Setup opens. 3. Pick how setup gets your game's files: - **Import from RPCS3**: setup finds the game in RPCS3's list and has your RPCS3 unlock its files. It can bring your save, trophies and some settings across too. If RPCS3 has several copies, setup lets you pick one. - **I have decrypted files**: your disc copy, plus the 27 files you decrypted yourself (`EBOOT.elf` and the `.sdat` files). - **Show me how**: step by step, with free tools only. 4. Start the build. It runs on your PC and can take a while; setup shows an estimate first. You can stop it and carry on later. Setup builds in AppData on Windows (`~/.local/share` on Linux) and needs about 4 GB free there; to build on another drive, press **Change** next to **Build folder** first. 5. Pick a preset: **Original** plays as on the PS3; **Enhanced** sets 60 fps, a resolution that fits your display, SMAA, 16x anisotropic filtering, fullscreen, and HDR when Windows has HDR on for your display. Then a few choices (HDR among them, on Windows) and your online name. You can change anything later in Settings. Then press **Play**. **A portable install:** put an empty file named `portable.txt` next to `Soulbrandt.exe` before its first start. Your settings, logs and setup's build then stay inside the program's folder, as your saves already do, and you can move or rename that folder. Windows may warn you the first time you start `Soulbrandt.exe` ("Windows protected your PC"), because the program isn't signed yet. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If RPCS3 is set to run as administrator, setup cannot start it: untick that in `rpcs3.exe`'s Properties. ### Linux CI builds the Linux program on every change, and each release includes a Linux download. It needs x86-64 Linux with glibc 2.35 or newer, a Vulkan driver, and `curl` and `tar`. Nothing else needs installing. The game renders on Vulkan, and setup prepares its shaders. If Vulkan can't start, the game falls back to its older renderer on vkd3d (DirectX 12 on Vulkan), which compiles shaders as it goes, with long pauses when a new area loads. Linux is newer and less tested than Windows. Players run it on desktop Linux and on the Steam Deck, on Vulkan ([docs/106](docs/106-setup-on-linux.md)). macOS is not supported. On a Steam Deck, keys and the mouse stay out of the game while its controls are on, because Steam's desktop layout presses them too. To use a keyboard on a docked Deck, set `PAD_KEYBOARD_WITH_PAD=1`. On a Steam Deck the game runs best with **Manual GPU Clock Control** at **800 MHz** and the **Thermal Power (TDP) Limit** at **15 W** (Quick Access menu > Performance). ### Online play Online play is on by default and uses this project's own server. Setup asks for your online name; you can change it, or turn online play off, in Settings > Network. Players of every supported version meet on the same server. RPCS3 players use other servers, so you won't meet them. What the server keeps about you is in the [privacy note](PRIVACY.md). ### Not supported yet - The Japanese and Asian discs without their 1.04 update, the Japanese PlayStation Store version (NPJA00102) and the US demo don't work. - Setup can't read ISO files, and it needs RPCS3 to unlock the game's files (or files you decrypted yourself). - macOS isn't supported, and running the Windows download through CrossOver hasn't been tested all the way through. Linux and the Steam Deck are less tested than Windows. ### Problems Use **Report an issue** in the menu (F1), or open an [issue](https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt/issues). For questions and help, join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/BzmwDeca8s). Report security problems privately, as [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) says. ## Building from source This is the technical part. The full notes are in [`docs/`](docs/). **Tools** | Windows | Linux | |---|---| | Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, LLVM (clang), CMake, Ninja, Python 3, Git Bash | clang or GCC, CMake, Ninja, Python 3, SDL2, Vulkan and FFmpeg development files, vkd3d ([details](docs/76-native-linux.md#building)) | On Windows, step 4 downloads FFmpeg's MPEG-2 video decoder for the game's movies (about 1 MB) and puts it beside `des_boot.exe`. If that download fails, the build says so and goes on, and the movies then need Microsoft's free [MPEG-2 Video Extension](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9n95q1zzpmh4) from the Microsoft Store; without either, they play their sound with no picture. (A paid app called "MPEG-2 Video Extensions", from another publisher, is a different thing; you don't need it.) **From your copy of the game** - The game disc's files (`PS3_GAME`) - RPCS3, to decrypt the game's `EBOOT.BIN` - Optional: `libsre.prx` from your PS3 firmware, decrypted. The game doesn't need it; it is only for the `LIBSRE_OWN=0` fallback ([docs/88](docs/88-setup-screens.md)). **Steps** 1. Get this repository, and its runtime inside it: ```sh git clone https://github.com/JonathanDC64/Soulbrandt.git cd Soulbrandt git clone https://github.com/JonathanDC64/ps3recomp.git ``` `ps3recomp.pin` names the ps3recomp commit this version of the port needs. `python tools/release/pin_ps3recomp.py local` checks your checkout against it. 2. In RPCS3, decrypt `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` (*Utilities > Decrypt PS3 Binaries*) to `work/game/EBOOT.ELF`. Copy `PS3_GAME/ICON0.PNG` next to it, for the program's icon. 3. Convert the game's main code: ```sh python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_loader.py work/game/EBOOT.ELF -o work/loader python ps3recomp/tools/ppu_lifter.py work/game/EBOOT.ELF \ --functions work/loader/EBOOT.functions.json --hle-stubs work/loader/EBOOT.imports.json \ --override-funcs "0x167AC88=ds_malloc,0x167AC58=ds_free,0x273D38=des_move_post,0x724E40=des_menu_tick" \ --insn-hooks @port/insn_hooks.txt --shadow-stack --chunk-lines 150000 --output work/recomp -j 16 python ps3recomp/tools/gen_hle_nids.py --all --out work/recomp/hle_nid_table.cpp python scripts/apply_boot_patches.py work/recomp ``` Then the SPU code with `python scripts/build_spu.py --eboot work/game/EBOOT.ELF` ([docs/09](docs/09-spu-spurs.md)), which first cuts the SPU programs out of the EBOOT, and, if you have `libsre.prx`, libsre with `python scripts/build_libsre.py `. The lifter's flags above are also in `scripts/lift_ppu.json`, which setup reads; change both together. 4. Compile the runtime, then the game. On Windows: ```sh cmake -S ps3recomp -B ps3recomp/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \ -DPS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL=ON cmake -S port -B port/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl \ -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE= -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG= -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS_DEBUG= cmake --build ps3recomp/build --target ps3recomp_runtime rsx_shader_precompile cmake --build port/build --target des_boot --parallel 4 ``` `PS3RECOMP_RSX_HAL=ON` builds the portable renderer: DirectX 12 through it, the default, and Vulkan beside it (Settings > Display > Renderer). Without it the game runs on the legacy renderer only. Its first configure downloads glslang and SPIRV-Tools at their pinned commits. On Linux, see [docs/76](docs/76-native-linux.md#building). 5. Copy `tools/des/local.env.example` to `tools/des/local.env`, set `PS3_VFS_ROOT` in it to the folder that holds `PS3_GAME`, and start the game with `tools/des/play.sh`. A direct start of `des_boot.exe` goes through setup instead, and keeps its saves in `port/build/gamedata`. Everything made from your copy of the game stays in `work/` and `gamedata/`, which git

# GOWA_cMc_OmniPort Repositorio: **https://github.com/cMc292/GOWA_cMc_OmniPort** · Web: **https://cMc292.github.io/GOWA_cMc_OmniPort/** **God of War: Ascension [BCUS98232] — port nativo a Windows x64 por recompilación estática.** Adaptación a la **versión de disco US (`BCUS98232`) v1.12** por **cMc-OmniPort**, sobre [Ascension-R](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R) de **Ryan Bagas** y [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) de **Ned Heller (sp00nznet)** y colaboradores. [![Última release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/cMc292/GOWA_cMc_OmniPort?include_prereleases&label=release&color=B01B1B)](https://github.com/cMc292/GOWA_cMc_OmniPort/releases) [![Licencia: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/licencia-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) ![Plataforma: Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/plataforma-Windows%20x64-lightgrey.svg) ![Estado: alpha](https://img.shields.io/badge/estado-alpha-orange.svg) ![Base: Ascension-R v0.1.0-alpha.10](https://img.shields.io/badge/base-Ascension--R%20v0.1.0--alpha.10-informational.svg) > [!IMPORTANT] > **Este proyecto no contiene archivos del juego**: ni `PS3_GAME`, ni `*.psarc`, ni `EBOOT`, ni vídeos, ni trofeos. > Para jugar necesitas **tu propia copia** de *God of War: Ascension* `BCUS98232` v1.12 (disco + parches 1.04–1.12) > y su `GOWA.elf` descifrado. > > El **ejecutable del paquete sí contiene código traducido del juego**: es una obra derivada, la licencia MIT de este > repositorio **no** la cubre, y sigue perteneciendo a sus titulares. Léelo en el [aviso legal](#aviso-legal). ## Contenido - [Qué es](#qué-es) - [Estado](#estado) - [Novedades de la v0.1.0-alpha.10](#novedades-de-la-v010-alpha10) - [Capturas](#capturas) - [Características](#características) - [Descarga](#descarga) - [Requisitos](#requisitos) - [Instalación](#instalación) - [Apuntar el port a tu copia del juego](#apuntar-el-port-a-tu-copia-del-juego) - [Actualizar el port](#actualizar-el-port) - [Launcher y ajustes](#launcher-y-ajustes) - [Estructura del paquete](#estructura-del-paquete) - [Limitaciones conocidas](#limitaciones-conocidas) - [Cómo reportar un problema](#cómo-reportar-un-problema) - [Créditos](#créditos) - [Licencia](#licencia) - [Aviso legal](#aviso-legal) - [English summary](#english-summary) ## Qué es El código de la PS3 (`GOWA.SELF`: PPU y SPU) se traduce **antes de jugar** a x86-64 con [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) y el RSX se dibuja con **Direct3D 12**: mientras juegas no hay emulador. [Ascension-R](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R) hizo ese trabajo para la versión **digital US `NPUA80918` 1.12**; este proyecto lo adapta a la **versión de disco US `BCUS98232` 1.12**. El port a BCUS se apoya en un hecho comprobado: el `GOWA.elf` de `BCUS98232` 1.12 y el de `NPUA80918` 1.12 son **el mismo ejecutable** (mismo SHA-256), así que se puede reutilizar el lift del port original en vez de levantar el juego otra vez. Lo que cambia es el resto del pipeline: - vista fusionada **disco + parches 1.04–1.12** (los archivos son los de tu copia, enlazados: no se duplican); - identidad `BCUS98232` en la búsqueda del juego, el launcher y `game_files.inc`; - descifrado del `GOWA.SELF` de parche (NPDRM) mediante el **KLIC** del parche 1.12; - empaquetado **portable** con lanzadores nativos, FFmpeg, MinGit y Python embebido, y **modo de actualización** (`Update` / `Promote` / `Rollback`). Documentación del trabajo: [`docs/`](docs/). Historial de versiones: [`docs/CHANGELOG.md`](docs/CHANGELOG.md). ## Estado **alpha.** Arranca, reproduce las cinemáticas, pasa por los menús y entra en los niveles; **no** se ha jugado de principio a fin. Cada build del port pasa un *smoke test* de 180 s (entry OPD `0x8283F8`, backend Direct3D 12, `libavcodec` decodificando) y se prueba en sesiones manuales con el launcher. | | | |---|---| | Juego | *God of War: Ascension*, **disco US `BCUS98232` v1.12** (disco + parches 1.04–1.12) | | Base | Ascension-R **v0.1.0-alpha.10** (`62a7122`) + adaptación BCUS (`62dfaa1`) | | Plataforma | Windows 10/11, 64 bits | | Render | Direct3D 12 (RSX → D3D12) | | Online | **no soportado** (el port es de un jugador) | | Multijugador | no probado | | Estado | alpha, sin garantías | ## Novedades de la v0.1.0-alpha.10 - **Texturas rotas arregladas en su causa**: el recorte de mips del streaming de texturas del juego ya no se pasa del bloque (el que provocaba texturas rotas y caídas), y la copia de cada textura en la GPU se revalida antes y después de leerla (adiós a las «mitad viejas, mitad nuevas»). - **F9 relee todas las texturas** y el registro distingue con `[tex]` una copia rota del port de datos rotos del juego. - **Pantalla de precompilación con el estilo del launcher nuevo (F7)**: a resolución de ventana, arte opcional, Cinzel y textos en español. - **Navegación**: LOG y TROFEOS ya se abren con el ratón; la pestaña activa pliega a HOME. - Base **Ascension-R v0.1.0-alpha.10** (incluye los cambios de la alpha.9): sin el parón tras los logos, DXC en Linux y build del código del juego más rápido. Detalle: [release v0.1.0-alpha.10](https://github.com/cMc292/GOWA_cMc_OmniPort/releases/tag/v0.1.0-alpha.10-bcus) y [`docs/CHANGELOG.md`](docs/CHANGELOG.md). ## Capturas Launcher completo (10 páginas) y pantalla de precompilación. Las capturas de las páginas son de la `v0.1.0-alpha.8` (la interfaz es la misma); la de precompilación es de la `v0.1.0-alpha.10`. | | | |---|---| | **HOME**
| **GRÁFICOS**
| | **PANTALLA**
| **CONTROLES**
| | **PARCHES**
| **CHEATS**
| | **SISTEMA**
| **AVANZADO**
| | **LOG**
| **TROFEOS**
|

Precompilación (F7)

## Características ### El juego - **Recompilación estática**: PPU → C++, SPU → C, sin emulador en tiempo de ejecución. - **RSX → Direct3D 12**, con los shaders traducidos a HLSL y compilados con DXC. - **Cinemáticas y audio comprimido** con FFmpeg (LGPL, DLLs compartidas incluidas). - **SPURS y job modules** traducidos; lo que no se tradujo a tiempo corre en intérprete y se añade al siguiente lift. - **Texturas**: streaming del juego con el recorte de mips corregido, copia de texturas en la GPU revalidada antes/después de leer, y **F9** para releerlas todas (el log marca `[tex]`). ### Launcher La interfaz del port (estilo *SpartanPort*, con la paleta de *Ascension* y textos en español) tiene **diez páginas**: **HOME · GRÁFICOS · PANTALLA · CONTROLES · PARCHES · CHEATS · SISTEMA · AVANZADO · LOG · TROFEOS** - **HOME**: arte de fondo a sangre (tu imagen o el fondo procedural), wordmark, **PLAY**, presets *Suave / Equilibrado / Fieles*, chips de estado (copia del juego, `GOWA.elf`, GPU) y resumen de la sesión. - **GRÁFICOS**: resolución interna 1×–4× o nativa, escalado AMD FSR 1 y FSR 3.1, generación de fotogramas FSR 3.1, SMAA 1×, filtrado anisotrópico, caché de shaders comprimida. - **PANTALLA**: ventana o sin bordes, ultrapanorámica, VSync, límite de FPS, indicador de FPS y carga en pantalla. - **CONTROLES**: mando o teclado y ratón; XInput y, por SDL3, DualShock 4, DualSense, mandos de Switch y otros; zona muerta, botón de confirmar, vibración, API del mando. - **PARCHES**: MLAA, profundidad de campo, desenfoque de movimiento, recorte de mallas, sombras dinámicas. - **CHEATS**: daño recibido y hecho, orbes rojos, magia y objetos infinitos, furia infinita, doble salto. - **SISTEMA**: carpeta del juego, `GOWA.elf`, comprobar actualizaciones, informe de problemas, versión. - **AVANZADO**: ajustes finos y herramientas del paquete. - **LOG**: el registro de la última sesión, con scroll. **F9** relee todas las texturas del juego (útil si aparece una textura rara). - **Precompilación** con el estilo del launcher (F7): lectura de archivos, compilación de shaders y errores, en español. - **TROFEOS**: la lista completa leída del `TROPHY.TRP` del juego (icono, nombre, descripción y PLATINO/ORO/PLATA/BRONCE en el idioma del juego) y el progreso leído del `TROPUSR.DAT` de tus partidas (marca dorada y **CONSEGUIDO** en los conseguidos). Todos los ajustes viven en `_src\GOWA-cMc\build\gowa-cmc.ini` (los mismos de siempre) y la interfaz clásica sigue disponible con `[launcher] ui = classic`. ### Paquete portable - **Lanzadores nativos** `.exe` (sin consola al jugar): `Jugar`, `Launcher`, `Update`, `Promote`, `Rollback`. Todos calculan sus rutas desde su propia carpeta: **muévelo de disco o de PC** sin reinstalar. - **FFmpeg** LGPL compartido y **MinGit** + **Python 3.12** (con capstone) incluidos: no instalas nada para jugar. - **Modo de actualización** integrado (ver [Actualizar](#actualizar-el-port)). - `gamedata/` recibe las partidas; tu copia del juego **solo se lee**. ## Descarga La [página de releases](https://github.com/cMc292/GOWA_cMc_OmniPort/releases) tiene el paquete portable: | Archivo | Tamaño | Contenido | |---|---|---| | `GOWA_cMc_OmniPort-0.1.0-alpha.10-release.zip` | 177,5 MB (592 MB descomprimido) | lanzadores, `_src/GOWA-cMc` (fuente `bcus` + build), FFmpeg, `tools/` y documentación | No contiene archivos del juego. Los SHA-256 están en [SHA256SUMS.txt](SHA256SUMS.txt) y en las notas de cada release. ## Requisitos Para **jugar**: - Windows 10 u 11, 64 bits. - CPU con **AVX2** y **FMA**; GPU con **Direct3D 12**. - **Tu copia legítima** de *God of War: Ascension* `BCUS98232` **v1.12**: disco + parches **1.04–1.12** (instalados en ese orden y fusionados; ver abajo) y su `GOWA.elf` **descifrado**. - ~592 MB para el paquete y el espacio de tu copia del juego (la vista fusionada no duplica archivos). Para **actualizar o recompilar** (solo el modo `Update`): - Visual Studio 2022 **Build Tools** con «C++ Clang Compiler for Windows» (trae CMake y Ninja). - Nada más: Python y Git del paquete se usan solos. ## Instalación 1. Descarga el `.zip` del release y **descomprímelo entero** en una carpeta propia, por ejemplo `C:\GOWA-cMc`. > Evita corchetes (`[` `]`) en la ruta si vas a recompilar: rompen el `file(GLOB)` de CMake. 2. Abre **`Launcher GOWA-cMc.exe`** (o **`Jugar GOWA-cMc.exe`** para entrar directo al juego). 3. En **SISTEMA**, elige tu carpeta del juego con **Examinar** (o **Auto detectar**): la carpeta que contiene `PARAM.SFO` y `USRDIR`. 4. Si el chip de `GOWA.elf` está en rojo, descífralo una vez (ver la sección siguiente). 5. Pulsa **PLAY**. El primer arranque de cada versión compila los *vertex shaders* (uno o dos minutos, en una pantalla aparte); los *fragment shaders* se compilan la primera vez que se usan, así que habrá algo de tirones al principio. **Limpiar shaders**, en la barra lateral, fuerza a recompilarlos. Tus partidas, ajustes y cachés quedan en `_src\GOWA-cMc\gamedata` y `_src\GOWA-cMc\build` (paquete portable). ## Apuntar el port a tu copia del juego El port **solo lee** tu copia. Necesita dos cosas: 1. **La copia fusionada del disco y los parches.** La ruta que uses debe tener `PARAM.SFO` y `USRDIR` con los archivos del disco y de los parches 1.04–1.12. Con RPCS3, instala el juego y todos los parches en orden y usa `dev_hdd0\game\BCUS98232`; si prefieres no duplicar 36,8 GB, una vista con *hardlinks* al volcado y a la instalación de RPCS3 hace el mismo papel (es lo que usa el autor). 2. **El `GOWA.elf` descifrado** en `USRDIR\GOWA.elf`. Se saca **una vez** del `USRDIR\GOWA.SELF`: - RPCS3 → *Utilities* → *Decrypt PS3 Binaries* sobre `GOWA.SELF`. - El `SELF` de `BCUS98232` 1.12 está cifrado con **NPDRM de parche** y RPCS3 necesita licencia; en esta copia se descifró inyectando el **KLIC** del parche por *stdin* en `rpcs3.exe --decrypt` (documentado, con el detalle técnico, en [`CREDITOS.md`](CREDITOS.md) y en el informe del proyecto). Después, una vez: ``` cd _src\GOWA-cMc set GOWA_TITLE_ID=BCUS98232 ..\..\tools\python\python.exe scripts\gowa.py setup --game-dir "" ``` El `setup` crea los enlaces de `vfs\` y `gamedata\`, comprueba el `PARAM.SFO` y no copia nada del juego. También puedes apuntar la carpeta desde el launcher (página **SISTEMA**). ## Actualizar el port Cuando Ascension-R publique una release nueva: ``` Update-BCUS.exe trae la última release, la convierte a BCUS, compila en build.next y hace smoke test Promote-BCUS.exe activa build.next (la build anterior queda en build.prev) Rollback-BCUS.exe vuelve a build.prev (pide confirmación) ``` `Update-BCUS.exe` no toca la build que estás jugando: si algo falla, `bcus` no se mueve y sigues como estabas. Los informes quedan en `tools\bcus\reports\`. Los lanzadores `.cmd`/`.ps1` equivalentes están en `tools\bcus\`. Requisitos del modo actualización: Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools con «C++ Clang Compiler for Windows». Para jugar no hace falta nada de eso. Hay una tarea programada diaria (04:00) que solo actúa si hay release nueva. ## Launcher y ajustes - Ajustes: `_src\GOWA-cMc\build\gowa-cmc.ini` (mismas claves que Ascension-R). - Interfaz clásica: `[launcher] ui = classic` o variable `GOWA_UI_CLASSIC=1`; la nueva vuelve con `ui = new` / `GOWA_UI_NEW=1`. - Logo y fondo del launcher: `assets\launcher-logo.png` y `assets\launcher-bg.jpg` **opcionales**, junto al paquete. Sin ellos se usa el wordmark de texto y un fondo procedural. **No** se distribuyen con el paquete: si pones arte del juego, es tu copia local y no debe subirse al repositorio. - La barra inferior cambia de página; `LOG` muestra el registro de la última build y `TROFEOS` la lista del juego. ## Estructura del paquete ``` Jugar GOWA-cMc.exe arranca el juego (sin launcher, sin consola) Launcher GOWA-cMc.exe launcher: presets, gráficos, pantalla, controles, parches, cheats, trofeos Update-BCUS.exe trae la última release de Ascension-R, la convierte a BCUS y compila Promote-BCUS.exe activa la build nueva que dejó Update (guarda la anterior) Rollback-BCUS.exe vuelve a la build anterior _src/GOWA-cMc/ árbol git (rama bcus): fuentes, build/GOWA-cMc.exe, gowa-cmc.ini, gamedata/ _src/ffmpeg/ FFmpeg LGPL shared (cinemáticas y audio) tools/MinGit/ git portable (lo usa la actualización) tools/python/ Python 3.12 embebido con capstone (lo usa la actualización) tools/bcus/ scripts y estado del modo de actualización tools/launcher/ fuente del lanzador nativo (gowalaunch.c) y su build docs/ documentación gamedata/ partidas (vacío al publicar) ``` ## Limitaciones conocidas - **Alpha**: no se ha jugado de principio a fin; puede haber fallos más adelante. - Solo **`BCUS98232` 1.12** (disco US + parches 1.04–1.12). La versión digital `NPUA80918` es el proyecto original ([Ascension-R](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R)); no la sustituye. - **Online no soportado**; el multijugador no se ha probado. - El primer arranque de

4e324ad9f5ff0fa8d99e936e5a97ceecbe430968.message:
Game update 2.17 runs (US BCUS98114): two lifter fixes, 2.17's SPU jobs

2.17 was built with a newer compiler than the disc, and the lift did
not know two of its patterns (tools/ppu_lifter.py, in ps3recomp.patch):

- Switch tables whose base is built from immediates (lis/addi) are
  decoded; only TOC-loaded bases were accepted, so every such bctr
  lifted to an unresolved indirect call and the game stayed on a black
  screen from its static constructors on.
- The raw-index search for the table bound only looks before the lwzx:
  with `lwzx r0, r9, r0` it took the later `add r0,r0,r9` as the index,
  missed the bound compare and cut func_00B7288C's 310-case table at
  256.
- Two vectors in tools/test_ppu_jumptables.py.

On the US 01.00 EBOOT the lifter's jump-table discovery is byte for
byte as before (92 dispatchers, 459 targets); on 2.17 it goes from 80
dispatchers to 358.

version_addrs.py: the computed goto is matched by opcodes only (2.17
reads its field off r31, with no TOC reload before it), its labels are
read from the code that stores them when no data table holds them, and
duplicate targets are dropped. US 01.00 output is unchanged.

spu_jobs_from_eboot.py: the four SPU jobs US 2.17 changed or added
(CB9BD024 replaces D58063CD; 0B07CA3D, 18DE3719, CF635263 are new); the
summary counts the jobs only updates have.

setup.ps1 and version_addrs.py name US 2.17's EBOOT.elf; README, STATUS
and CHANGELOG updated.

Tested on BCUS98114 with updates 1.01-2.17: menus, GT Mode, a full
16-car Arcade race at 59.4 fps median, no missed SPU job and no
unresolved indirect call. Ryzen 7 9850X3D, Radeon RX 9070 XT,
Windows 11.

9f73bed81cb35438704c5dd9ca2e70b1ed67a186.message:
DLC works offline with your own licence keys (runtime only; no keys in the repo)

The runtime part of #24, as asked in its review: no installer, no key
material in the repository.

Runtime (ps3recomp.patch):
- PS3_EDAT_STRICT=1: an EDAT opens the way the PS3 kernel serves it, as
  stored for a plain open and as plaintext for an open with the 8-byte
  NPDRM argument (GT5 passes [0, 2]). GT5's buildIndex reads each
  voucher's NPD header with a plain open and checks its content id;
  decrypted on every open, all vouchers failed and nothing was granted.
- sceNpManagerGetEntitlementById answers "not owned", as PSN does for an
  account without the purchase; unimplemented, it returned success with
  nothing written. GT5's DLCUtil unlocks the 2011 packs by entitlement or
  voucher and the 2012 packs by voucher only, so the DLC comes from the
  vouchers, each of which decrypts only with its licence key.
- PS3_NP_SIGNED_IN=1: the NP manager reports signed in with the local
  profile and no network, for the Downloadable Content screen.
- Licence keys from dev_hdd0/home/00000001/exdata/<content id>.rifkey,
  and the decrypted cache in dev_hdd0/edat_cache: GT5 opens every file
  in USRDIR/vou, so neither may sit beside the vouchers.

play.bat: PS3_EDAT_STRICT on; PS3_NP_SIGNED_IN only when a voucher is
installed (checked at every start), so players without DLC stay offline
and the game doesn't try for tickets.

README: a DLC section (vouchers from RPCS3 or a PS3, a key per content
id in exdata). STATUS and CHANGELOG.

Fix noisy distant road and track textures (Tsukuba)

Many track textures have only their top two or three mip levels written; the rest of the chain held zeros on a fresh boot and leftover data from earlier scenes otherwise, which showed as blocky black-and-white or grass-green noise on the road at Tsukuba. Each DXT level is now checked against the one above it (mean colour of each 4x4 block), and from the first empty or mismatched level the chain is rebuilt from the last good one (decode, box filter, re-encode). LD_MIP_REBUILD=0 turns it off; LD_MIP_FOLLOW_MAX sets the threshold (default 12); LD_MIP_DUMP=<dir> saves mipped DXT textures for offline checks.

1456786459.readme_excerpt:
💬 Discord · Install · Launcher · Updating · Version history · Changelog · Status · FAQ · Modding · Contributing · License

# GT5 Recomp An unofficial PC port of **Gran Turismo 5** (PS3) made by static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated into C++ that is compiled for Windows x64, and the PS3's graphics, sound, input and system calls are reimplemented on Windows (Direct3D 12 for the RSX). A native [Linux build](#linux) (Vulkan) is new and early. It is built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) and borrows from the [GT5 Prologue port](https://github.com/sp00nznet/GT5P), both by Ned Heller (sp00nznet). > **Game version required:** your own **Gran Turismo 5** Blu-ray disc, using the disc's own > executable (version **01.00**, with **no game update** installed): > > - **Europe, BCES00569**: tested. This is the copy the port was built from. > - **North America, BCUS98114**: works; players have raced on it (thanks!). The lift finds the few addresses > that differ between releases in your own executable. > > See [Which copy of GT5](#which-copy-of-gt5) for how to check your files. ## 📑 Contents | 🚀 Getting started | 📈 How it's going | 🛠️ Setting up by hand | 📚 About the project | |---|---|---|---| | [Install](#install) | [Current state](#current-state) | [Requirements](#requirements) | [What this repository contains](#repo-contents) | | [The launcher](#launcher) | [Try it, tell me how it went](#feedback) | [Which copy of GT5](#which-copy-of-gt5) | [Fork it, mod it](#modding) | | [Updating](#updating) | [FAQ](#faq) | [Setup](#setup) | [Credits](#credits) | | [Controls](#controls) | | [Switches](#switches) | [License](#license) | | [Linux](#linux) | | | | **More pages:** [Version history](VERSIONS.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Status board](STATUS.md) · [Modding guide](MODDING.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [License](LICENSE) ## ⬇️ Install **The easy way, on Windows 10 or 11:** 1. Download **[GT5-Installer.bat](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/releases/latest/download/GT5-Installer.bat)** and double-click it. If Windows warns about a downloaded file, choose **Run** (or **More info**, then **Run anyway**). 2. In its window, pick two things and press **Install**: - **your GT5 game**: the folder of your disc dump (the one with `PS3_GAME` in it) or an `.iso`; - **PS3UPDAT.PUP**, Sony's free PS3 system software (the window has a button that opens Sony's page). That's all. It installs whatever's missing (Git, Python, Microsoft's C++ build tools), downloads this code, unlocks your game's executable and the system software with RPCS3 (used only as a tool for that: the game itself runs natively as `gt5.exe`, not in an emulator), builds the game (about an hour the first time) and puts **Gran Turismo 5 (PC)** on your desktop, which opens the [launcher](#launcher). Nothing from the game is ever uploaded or shared. Rather do it by hand? See [Setup](#setup). On Linux? See [Linux](#linux). ## 🎛️ The launcher

**Gran Turismo 5 (PC)** on your desktop (or `GT5Launcher.exe` in your `gt5-recomp` folder) opens the launcher: every setting in one window, then **Play**. No more editing `play.bat`. - **Display:** 1080p or 720p, **Speed** (30 fps draws every other frame; it only helps when the graphics card is the limit, the window title then shows both numbers, e.g. `FPS: 15 (game 30)`), screen shape (ultrawide), **borderless full screen**, maximized or a window size, watch mode, SPU threads. - **Controls:** steering wheel on/off, wheel rotation, force feedback strength and direction, pad in the background, mouse clipping. - **Game:** the game's language (as far as your disc has it), your mods from `GT5\mods`, the launcher's own language (English or 中文). - **Updates:** shows your version and the newest one with what's new, and **Update now** does the whole update for you and opens the launcher again. - **Help:** **Save logs for a report** puts your logs on the desktop as `.txt` files GitHub accepts, plus the logs folder, the problem form and this FAQ. It's built on your PC from [`launcher/GT5Launcher.cs`](launcher/GT5Launcher.cs) with the C# compiler that comes with Windows, every time the game is built, so it updates with the game; its picture is the logo from your own disc. Settings are saved in `GT5\settings.bat`, which `play.bat` reads, so `play.bat` still works and starts the game the same way. (`GT5Launcher.exe --play` starts the game straight away.) ## 🔄 Updating Every change to the port comes out as a numbered version (v0.1.0, v0.1.1, ...) on the [Releases page](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/releases), with what changed. To hear about new ones, click **Watch** at the top of this page, then **Custom** and tick **Releases**. ### The easy way - **The launcher** checks for a new version when it opens: its **Updates** page shows what's new, and **Update now** does everything below and opens the launcher again. - Or **double-click `Update.bat`** in your `gt5-recomp` folder. Both run `update.ps1`, so everything below applies. (No launcher or `Update.bat` yet? Your next update brings them: run the command below once.) ### Are you out of date? Close the game, open PowerShell in your `gt5-recomp` folder and run: ``` powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -List ``` It lists every version and marks the one you have (`<- installed`) and the newest (`[newest]`). If they're different, you're out of date. ### Update to the newest version ``` powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 ``` That one command does everything: 1. It downloads the new version. 2. It swaps the old ps3recomp patch for the new one. 3. It re-generates the game code only if that version needs it (about 10 minutes). 4. It rebuilds only what changed. Kept as they are: - your saves (`GT5\gamedata`), a game update's data (`GT5\hdd0`) and game files (`GT5\input`, `GT5\vfs`, `GT5\dev_flash`); - the shader cache; - edits you made to files such as `play.bat`. The previous `gt5.exe` is kept as `GT5\build\gt5.previous.exe`. If one of your edits clashes with a change in the new version, the new version's file is used and your edit is saved in `backups\` so you can copy it back. **If you're several versions behind,** run the same command. It goes straight to the newest version; there's no need to step through the ones in between. ### Installed before update.ps1 existed? If your folder has no `update.ps1` (you set up before v0.1.0), get it first, then update: ``` git pull powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 ``` If `git pull` says your local changes would be overwritten (usually `play.bat`), run `git stash`, then `git pull`, then `git stash pop`, then the update. Your first update re-generates the game code once (about 10 minutes), because older installs have no record of what their code was made from. ### Downloaded the ZIP instead of cloning? A ZIP download can't update itself. Clone the repository fresh as in [Setup](#setup), step 1. Then move these folders over from your old copy and run `update.ps1`: - your game files: `GT5\input`, `GT5\vfs`, `GT5\dev_flash`; - your saves: `GT5\gamedata` (and `GT5\hdd0`, if you set up a game update). ### Go back to an older version If a new version gives you trouble, switch back to the one that worked (see `-List` for the names): ``` powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -Version v0.1.0 ``` To play the previous build right away instead, copy `GT5\build\gt5.previous.exe` over `GT5\build\gt5.exe` (the last update kept it). Please also [report what went wrong](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml). ### Other options | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `update.ps1 -Dev` | The newest changes, before they're released. | | `update.ps1 -NoBuild` | Switch versions without building; build later with `GT5\scripts\build.cmd gt5`. | | `update.ps1 -Force` | Re-generate and rebuild everything, even when nothing changed. | ## 🎮 Controls A DualSense, DualShock 4 or XInput pad works. Without one, the keyboard: Z = Cross, X = Circle, A = Square, S = Triangle, arrow keys = D-pad, Enter = Start, Tab = Select. A steering wheel works too, with force feedback (new and untested on real wheels): see the [FAQ](#faq). ## 📋 Current state

**Playable.** Races run at 45 to 58 fps on the tested rig, and most of the game's modes work. The full board (tested rig, what works, what's being worked on, known issues, recent changes) is in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md); updates are also posted in [Announcements](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/discussions/categories/announcements). Everything done on the port since the first day, with dates, is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## 🏁 Try it, then tell me how it went If you own the game, please set it up and play. Every result helps decide what gets fixed next, whether it runs great, half works, or doesn't build at all. Laptops, integrated graphics and AMD cards especially: the port was tuned on one desktop with an NVIDIA card. | You want to... | Go here | |---|---| | Say how it went (takes two minutes, mostly quick picks) | [Tried it: here's how it went](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=1-tried-it.yml) | | Report something broken | [Something's broken](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml) | | Ask for a change | [Suggest a change](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=3-idea.yml) | | Post quick results, screenshots of it running, or ask for help | [Discussions](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/discussions/1) | | Chat, get help live, share results | **[The Workshop Discord](https://discord.gg/9cVPS7r5Ha)**: #gt5-help, #gt5-test-reports, #gt5-chat (I'm **mormonftp** there) | ## ❓ FAQ | Question | Short answer | |---|---| | Steering wheels? | 🧪 New, not yet tried on a real wheel: [wheel owners wanted](#faq) | | Force feedback? | 🧪 New, with wheel support, also untried on a real wheel | | Widescreen (16:9)? | ✅ Yes, GT5 is a 16:9 game | | Ultrawide (21:9, 32:9)? | ✅ New: a wider view, with the HUD kept 16:9 in the middle | | Which controllers? | ✅ DualSense, DualShock 4, Xbox pads, keyboard | | US copy (BCUS98114)? | ✅ Yes, players have raced on it | | Version 1.02, or a game update (2.xx)? | 🧪 New: game updates run: 2.17 (the last) tested on the US and European releases, 2.01 on the Asian one ([how to set one up](#game-updates)); 1.02 and 2.11 untried | | Settings without editing files? | ✅ New: the [launcher](#launcher) | | Full screen? | ✅ New: borderless full screen in the launcher (Alt+Enter is switched off since v0.1.17: it used to freeze the picture) | | Higher than 1080p (4K)? | ⚠️ The game's top mode is its 1080p one (races drawn at 1728x972), scaled up to your window; drawing above that isn't there yet | | Japanese or Asian release (BCJS, BCAS)? | ✅ Hong Kong / Asia (BCAS20108) runs, reported by a player, and its disc 01.00 and update 2.01 race in tests too; Japanese untried, please report | | Slow PC or laptop? | 🛠️ Laptops now use their dedicated graphics card. On most PCs the CPU sets the pace (the game's own threads), so the launcher's **Speed: 30 fps** rarely helps: it's for a graphics card at its limit. **On a laptop:** plug it in and set Windows' power mode to *Best performance* (and the maker's performance mode, e.g. in HP Command Center or Lenovo Vantage): a tester's i5-1135G7 ran into its power limit 88% of the time, which held its cores at 2.9 GHz instead of 4.2, while its graphics were only 30% busy. Speed-ups for 4-6 core CPUs are being worked on | | Linux? | 🧪 New and early: a [native Linux build](#linux). First test (no graphics card) reached the race start; races on a real GPU untested | | Steam Deck, Proton, Wine? | ❓ Not tried yet: the Linux build in a distrobox is the route to try ([Steam Deck](#steam-deck)). Reports welcome | | Android? | 🛠️ Being worked on | | Online? | ❌ No | | Is it legal? | ✅ No game files here: you build it from your own disc | | Ready-made download? | ❌ No, but [GT5-Installer.bat](#install) builds it for you | | Errors during setup? | 🛠️ Use [GT5-Installer.bat](#install), or run `setup.ps1` (see below) | | Black screen, `draws: 0`? | 🛠️ Fixed: update; if it's still black, `GT.VOL` may be missing or in pieces (see below) | **Q: Does it support steering wheels and force feedback?** **A: Yes, new in v0.1.2, but nobody has tried it on a real wheel yet.** On a PS3, GT5 talks to its Logitech wheels directly over USB, for both steering and force feedback. The port now plays that part: your PC wheel appears to the game as a **Logitech G27** (900°, three pedals, paddles and an H-shifter), and the game's force-feedback commands (the centring spring, the steering forces in a race) are played on your wheel through DirectInput, which Logitech, Thrustmaster, Fanatec and other wheels support. Plug the wheel in before you start the game; it's picked up by itself, and pads work as before. What has been checked, without a wheel: the game accepts the emulated G27, a race steers from it, and the force-feedback commands the game sends are decoded and logged. What hasn't: the feel on a real wheel, including which way the forces push. So **wheel owners are wanted**: please [tell us how it went](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=1-tried-it.yml) (or [report a problem](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml)), and attach `GT5\logs\play.err`: its `[wheel]` lines say which wheel was found, its axes, and what the game asked of it. If something is off, add a line to `play.bat` (next to the other `set` lines): | Problem | Fix | |---|---| | The forces push the wrong way (the wheel pulls away from the centre) | `set "PS3_WHEEL_FFB_INVERT=1"` | | Forces too strong or too weak | `set "PS3_WHEEL_FFB=60"` (percent, 0 = off) | | Steering too quick or too slow | set your wheel's rotation to 900° in its software (G HUB, ...), or tell the port what it i

1456888544.description: God of War: Ascension PC port: an unofficial, native Windows port of the PS3 game by static recompilation, no emulator. No game files included: you build it from your own copy.

first_sight.heading: Ascension-R: a God of War: Ascension

001fe21beabd2b1bbc7bb22e560216af53a92839.message:
Ultrawide: the title's cameras at the screen's width (display.ultrawide)

Widens the aspect and the half-widths of the perspective and orthographic cameras by the same factor, so the vertical view stays and more shows at the sides. The camera controller keeps 16:9. Off by default.

0059cc2162832efe2f9690e1b156784452625783.message:
launcher: show progress while preparing the game, fetch RPCS3 in pieces

Download with WinHTTP instead of URLDownloadToFile. Four connections take
2 MB pieces, so a slow route only costs its own piece. A connection that
goes quiet or falls far behind the rest is dropped and its piece resumes
where it stopped; 30 s with no data at all ends the download. Every piece
is asked for at the release address, since the links it redirects to run
out within minutes.

The System tab shows each stage with a bar, speed, time left, reconnects,
how long no data has come, and a Stop button.

Also find the .rap beside the game when there is no rpcs3.exe, unpack with
a relative path because tar takes no non-ASCII path, and name the missing
VC++ Redistributable instead of failing without a reason.

00a5f5578e2f0071d755cee186db8b4f1965ce33.message:
GOWA_WWS_WATCH/TRACE: the job lists of workloads 2-17

The watch read only RenderJobs, MeshProc, EDGE and RsxSync. It now covers
General6, BatchJobList and RenJobSet too, so a PS3_FTRACE trace shows who
publishes General6's jobs (the main thread, in three bursts a cycle).

00dc77f3df8234903171f96e89409230df18d074.message:
EDGE: skinned jobs on the SPU again by default (no more trails in the prison)

The game draws its skinned meshes twice, a depth pass and a lit pass that
tests EQUAL against it, and never clears the scene's colour. The skinned path
(GOWA_EDGE_SKIN) skins a job in the vertex pass on the GPU, a job it does not
take on the SPU, and takes a mesh's two jobs each on its own: in the prison of
the damned (profile 3's opening) ~45% stay on the SPU. The GPU rounds to
nearest and the SPU toward zero, so where a mesh was split the depths differed
in the last bit, the lit pass left holes, and the frames before showed through
them: Kratos and the walls in trails.

GOWA_EDGE_SKIN now defaults to 0. The prison with FSR 3.1, frame generation
and VSync: no trails. The fight with the same settings, one run each: 27.94
flips/s off against 28.30 on, the later windows 27.05 against 28.30 (the ~4%
the path gave). The note has the search and a failed try at an exact pass.

0190a52f2362f6217fca389c4bf8a09a9c0b499f.message:
Launcher: Graphics card, discrete or integrated

A row in the Graphics tab, with the names of the two GPUs, on a PC that
has two. It asks Windows what the renderer asks, so the name shown is
the GPU the game runs on, and the Ready check follows the choice.

01f84209d18918b0b212275548327ad43a72223b.message: Notes: where shader compiling spends its time

02f34608fb753f134c5602c2f02e89ee4383f851.message:
Make frame generation's cap follow the display

With no Frame rate cap the game is held at half the refresh rate instead of a fixed 30: 60 at 120 Hz. Past 60 flips, the most a PS3 flips, it takes the next even division, so frames keep an even pace: 36 at 144 Hz. graphics.frame_generation_refresh gives the rate by hand.

03f66f8e9fc26570ba24af8607ebe1ba76c21f52.message:
EDGE: leave out what skipped lighting left without a reader

With the lighting stage skipped, the binormals (0xA880's loop) and the
packing of ids 27-30 had no reader: the stage was their only reader, and
the GPU pass writes over the packed bytes. A hook at 0xA928 leaves the
loop out for the lit layout, and the output piece packs bytes 0-23 of a
vertex. If the stage runs on the SPU after all, the binormals run first.
GOWA_EDGE_GPU_LEAN=0 keeps both.

Replay with every skipped stage run late: 10 corpora, 0 differences.
Gate, four runs a side: 22.48 -> 22.96 flips/s.

0760d3b170113fa9cb75ebda3508027e82235744.message: package: read the status of the first changed file right

096408e5e84399f07f7e549c12f408e32954f20b.message:
Runtime: SPU overlay GETs skip the signature scan for data

ps3recomp 07c2a2b9 and its parent d71918df.

0a015a7124800aeda8fed7ebe9a47eb207271048.message:
EDGE vertex transform (0xF538) as native code

The 4x4 transform of a vertex stream, eight vertices a pass in AVX2 with
the SPU's exact float forms, the loop's two-deep order kept (each pass's
loads before the previous pass's stores, pass 0's initial registers
stored too). The last pass runs with the runtime's SPU forms and leaves
every register as the lifted loop does: the job's later code spills some
of them, and the strict replay saw those bytes differ.

The call-by-call check can compare all 128 registers (all_regs); the
transform uses it. 358 replay calls identical, strict replay 0 differ.
Replay: -1.5 to -2% per job. On by default (GOWA_EDGE_NATIVE bit 1024).

0aae8f99e41bb485db6dc05d60efb728238a9f3a.message:
GOWA_MAIN_SLOW: probe of the main thread's own work; it sets ~30% of it

Runtime d0b71071 (g_ppu_icall_hook). At each indirect call the main thread
spins for <percent> of the time since the previous one, waits left out.
+25%: 16.34 -> 15.98 flips/s, +100% (~12 ms a frame): 15.44, so about a
third of its own work is on the frame's path. Plan 2.8: the main thread's
PPU code is not the first lever; EDGE is.

0b04a1ea1798b32ad7eb5a208a7d649105d30a37.message:
The vertex pass's program no longer stops the frames (#12)

The fork lights the pass's draws on the CPU until its compute program is
compiled, and has DXC compile it under Wine, where D3DCompile is
vkd3d-shader's and did not finish it in a minute. Here, from an empty
shader cache, the frames went on through D3DCompile's 21 s, and DXC takes
0.7 s: docs/notes/2026-11-13-vertex-pass-compile.md.

0cd1fdaeabdf33907c07d75bec477c131e5eae79.message:
Rename what a player sees to Ascension-R

The exe, the launcher and game windows, the issue URL and the settings
file. ascension-r.ini starts as a copy of gowa.ini, which is left as it
is. The target and the internal gowa_ names stay, so the objects are not
rebuilt.

0d513a7c89f8cd48ceda897bdbe1ff75a0322bbc.message:
Lift the EDGE code pieces Tisiphone's brothel illusion streams

The room the player recorded fell to 3.5 frames a second: its EDGE jobs
fetch 20 code pieces the list did not have, and the SPU interpreter ran
them at 10-20 M steps a second. Found by replaying the player's recording
with SPU_INTERP_BYSIG and SPU_DMA_RANGE_UNIQ; listed and lifted, the room
runs at 25-27 flips/s in the same replay. The note has the measurements,
and the replay fix in the runtime is in the submodule.

0d5196cd3277a483637486ae770a71ab20933a99.message: ps3recomp: the fs test fixtures link again

0d92c52afe59fad29640849b0b34d582b13cd79f.message:
EDGE job: the hook at the job's entry, and the replay's state mode

The first step of the C job (docs/notes/2026-11-04-edge-host-reference.md):
- gowa_edge_job_ad98 hooks the job module's entry, behind GOWA_EDGE_JOB=1 (off by default).
- It reads the job's input set: the own buffer set, the DMA list's 22 slots, the pieces,
  skinning, the descriptor and the segment header's counts.
- It counts the kinds it sees (GOWA_EDGE_NATIVE_STATS=1) and declines every job, so the
  lifted job runs.
- The 120 gate jobs replay with 0 differences with it on, every input set read.

The fork gains the replay's state compare mode, for a job done another way than its lifted
code.

0f760b25f72bde7d73ae046dc44edbdb06d26b4f.message:
Launcher: the keyboard keys on a sheet in the new look

The window of Win32 controls is gone: the keyboard keys are a sheet over
the launcher with its widgets, the 24 bindings in two columns of sunk
boxes. A box clicked waits, gold, for a key or a mouse button pressed on
it; Backspace clears it and Esc gives up, as before. Esc otherwise is
Cancel, Enter is OK, and the window's close button closes the sheet
first. GOWA_LAUNCHER_SHOT draws it, with a binding waiting.

Driven in the window itself by posted clicks and keys, with a picture of
each step, it binds and clears, Cancel keeps nothing and the settings
file is unchanged after. Drawn at 100%, 125%, 150% and 200%. Left open
on the Play tab the launcher takes 5.1% of one core.

102b78860eedba5476f62faa5d7e9554f16644c9.message:
EDGE skinning in the vertex pass the SPU's way, bit for bit; the path on again

The game draws a skinned mesh twice, a depth pass and a lit pass that tests
EQUAL against it, and either job may be skinned in the vertex pass or on the
SPU. With the GPU's rounding the depths differed in the last bit and the lit
pass left holes (the trails in the prison of the damned), so the skinned path
had been turned off this morning.

The pass now works the rows and the position out with the SPU's fm and fma
done in 32-bit integer operations: mantissas multiplied exactly, a 64-bit
window with a sticky bit, the result cut toward zero, denormals as zero, a
zero +0. The same code in C (tests/native/skin_fma_test.c) matches the x86
FMA under the SPU's MXCSR over 160 million operations. In the shader as
loops: written out, FXC took ten minutes over it.

GOWA_EDGE_SKIN is on by default again. With FSR 3.1, frame generation and
VSync: the prison has no trails; the fight, ABBA, 29.52/29.92 flips/s on
against 27.36/27.91 off (~+7%, at the 30 cap). Fork 7099ab74 compiles the
pass in the background and keeps it in the shader cache.

10336b43925c1cd9fb48b7489cd438222bd8d9b8.message:
Add a Cheats tab: infinite health and one hit kill

Both hook the title's damage: func_00087440 takes all of it, and func_00156680 and func_00154460 know the attacker. A creature's controller tells Kratos, enemies and the level's props apart, and the props stay out of one hit kill because a script may need them alive. Both are off by default. Tried in one scripted fight: Kratos stays at 100, and each parasite falls to one hit instead of three.

104ed02dc25b695ffdc321bbef249dd9ddeb1c52.message:
Show where Kratos is in the stats panel

The panel's last line reads his creature's position through the title's two
globals that point at him, and shows dashes while he is not there. The runtime's
new panel is in the submodule.

1068a9603079573cd3f7715a37c88632c6db3bea.message:
Title patches can be on by default; MLAA, Motion Blur and Shadows are

A patch with "default": true in scripts/title_patches.json is on unless
switched off:
- gowa.py writes the default into the header;
- patches.cpp uses it as the setting's default;
- the launcher's checkboxes and its Defaults button follow it.

Disable MLAA, Disable Motion Blur and Disable Shadows have it. Disable Mesh
Trimming and Disable Depth of Field stay off.

Tested first against the settings before (MLAA and Mesh Trimming on), one
run each:
- the opening cinematic and the fight: 21.31 -> 30.10 flips/s;
- the gate, walking and jumping on for ~4 min: 17.61 -> 22.06.
No error, no hitch in play, and the screenshots are right. A boot with no
[patches] settings turns exactly those three on.

113c24ee28cc185b9960da917dbdef2c30ee69c2.message:
EDGE culling's vertex pass (0xD250) as native code, and a call-by-call check

- gowa.py: a native routine named ?name in spu_native_hooks.json takes the
  whole lifted function: nonzero returns from it.
- native/spu_edge_verify.h: GOWA_EDGE_VERIFY=1 runs the lifted function on

29f6a5d82a698e88948bd26bd5ab94ea161b555c.message:
RPCS3 against the port at the job level: the SPURS contention is lost

scripts/guestscope.py reads the title's SPURS instance and its Wws ticket
rows from outside a process, RPCS3 or the port alike, and reports SPUs per
workload, jobs per list and EDGE jobs per contention level.

Both run the same jobs a frame. RPCS3's EDGE phase is 27.6 ms of its frame,
the port's 52.8: about the whole difference. The causes, measured:
- the title's maximum contention (5-8 SPUs a workload) is the ninth argument
  of _cellSpursWorkloadAttributeInitialize, on the stack; the HLE writes 1;
- the port's kernel picks round robin, takes one from the ready count at each
  pick and never makes a polling policy module yield; RPCS3's keeps EDGE
  (priority 3) on four SPUs 86% of its time;
- an EDGE job takes ~1.4 times as long at any contention, a Batch job ~8.

With only the maxima raised, General6 and RenderJobs run on 4 SPUs
(39.6 -> 11.1 and 26.4 -> 7.7 ms a frame) but starve EDGE, and the frame
rate stays. The note gives the order of work; the plan gets section 2.10
and two 2026-10-28 conclusions are marked overturned.

304d1fe84e23b194331ed065e38a62bef031b1d4.message:
Each session started by hand keeps its log, and a crash its stack

Played from the launcher, the game's output went to its console and went
with it: a session that closed by itself left nothing to read. When stdout
is a console, not a file or pipe a script reads, stdout and stderr now go to
logs\session-<date>-<time>.log beside the settings file (the five newest
kept), and the console gives the path. How the session ended is at its end:
"[rsx] window closed", sys_process_exit, or "[crash]" with the exception
code, its address as module+offset and the crashed thread's stack, written
