38c9d6b8ae42e23835fa4ad673faa080239d3485.message:
EDGE: the second fixed-point decoder as native code, the first paired

304A0 (piece 0x758590) is the decoder that also reads four table entries
by decoded indices and rebuilds two third coordinates as
sqrt(1 - x^2 - y^2). It now runs natively statement for statement, its 13
local store accesses in the lifted order. Nearly all of its work comes in
pairs (two attributes, gathers that share their sources and shift counts,
two coordinate pairs, the two merges of a table entry); each pair is one
256-bit op, with frsqest and fi as 256-bit ports of the runtime's x86
forms. The loop: 83.2 -> 46.4 ns an iteration. GOWA_EDGE_NATIVE bit 8.

30310 now does two iterations with each 256-bit op where every store of
the call misses every quadword its fetches read, checked once a call; the
one-vertex form runs elsewhere. 14.2 -> 12.3 ns an iteration. Bit 16.

tests/native/test_edge_native.py covers both, 3000 cases each, with
outputs forced onto the records and the table; 21 mutants are caught.

each: 20.03 -> 20.17 flips/s.

The 16-byte header at c + 0x00 carries the hole size (it matched every hole written), the

3be8ed12c5fed312bea2093aca98a5ea47145f17.message:
EDGE natives: the fast pass with one range test for the transform, culling and point lights

spu_edge_simd.h gets the lighting loops' scheme as shared forms (ecf_*):
the ops native with nothing tested, then MXCSR's invalid and overflow
flags (an exact result beyond FLT_MAX leaves FLT_MAX and sets overflow
under round-toward-zero; a conversion out of range sets invalid) and the
exponent-255 lanes of what the ops read decide whether the work is redone
with the exact forms. +0 is applied where values leave.

The transform (0xF538), the vertex pass (0xD250) and the point lights
(0x6AC8) redo a pass from its inputs, still in registers, so input and
output may overlap; the cull masks (0xD618) go to a local array and are
redone as a whole. GOWA_EDGE_EXACT=1 forces the redo.

523875d077ae1036276ca4e261eb68041309a71c.message:
Guard the game's VRAM manager against negative block sizes

Issue #9: at the Delphi temple, on one PC and in every session, a block
of the game's VRAM pool got a negative size. The pool's allocator
(func_0039E3F8) then moves its top up instead of down, and the
defragmenter moves the block 16 MB at a time, over the textures after it
and, past local memory, over main memory. The game's own checks stop on a
trap there, which the lift leaves out.

Three hooks (port/vram_guard.cpp, scripts/ppu_hooks.json): a texture
whose size is negative or past 256 MB is logged with its first 0x50 bytes
and given an empty block, such an allocation from any caller is made 0,
and a MoveLocalMemory past local memory is made a move of nothing. A
replay of the temple with one allocation made negative on purpose printed
one line and nothing else. What gives a block such a size is not known
yet: the next report from that PC will say.

GAME_MODULE_ABI 3. tests/test_game_module_hooks.py checks that every hook
is in GAME_MODULE_FUNCS, which the Kit's DLL needs to link.

564751bee846a79aba720809bbc4a02d804ad85e.message:
Rendering accuracy: what is wrong, why, and the plan

Measured against RPCS3 (a screenshot of the main menu, and its settings
for this title read, not changed: Write Color Buffers on, Disable MLAA
and Disable Mesh Trimming on), with whole-frame captures and one switch
per run:

- The main menu's flicker is the title's MLAA path: its SPUs smooth a
  copy of the frame that is stale here, and draws read that copy when
  no GPU snapshot of it is found. MLAA off: the change from frame to
  frame drops from 6.5 to 1.4 and grows with the lag, as a slow scene's
  does. Depth of field, the texture cache, render target feedback: no
  effect.
- The opening cinematic's blocks are of two kinds: stale rectangles
  with MLAA on (the same copy, read with no or a mismatched snapshot),
  and a band across a frieze with MLAA on or off that starts in the
  screen-space shadow mask, made within the frame by 358 passes with
  depth bounds and stencil tests.
- Some textures decode wrongly (rainbow stripes, a blue patch), with
  MLAA off and the texture cache off; the suspects are the component
  remaps and the swizzled float formats the cinematic samples.
- The picture is ~19% darker than RPCS3's, shadows -36%, highlights -6%.
  Not a setting (the system save is RPCS3's), not the sRGB pairing (every
  target written with the encode is read with the decode). The suspect
  is the exposure: the luminance chain ends in a 1x1 target no draw
  reads, which our backend never writes back to guest memory.

5b170052182bf91bd9f7d81cc5652cd07eebaf86.message:
EDGE: e77C8's jobs start with no memo state (the Grotto freeze)

The EDGE native code keeps a job's state per thread, the memo of kept
results. e6D98's entry empties it and the hooks in e6D98's functions
fill it, while the hooks on the position-independent pieces read it,
and both EDGE modules call those pieces. Nothing emptied it for the
other build, jobmod_9b03908f93a9_e77C8, which the Grotto runs: a job of
it started with what the last e6D98 job on its thread had left. With a
kept result's state, the vertex piece's hook gave that result up and ran
the calls it had left out, e6D98's functions by name, on this job's
local store, leaving r0 as the last of them had it; the piece returned
there, into an epilogue that took r81-r83 from the piece's frame. That
is issue #7's register dump: the object pointer in r81 was the piece's
pattern, and the job branched to nowhere.

e77C8's entry (0xB7C8) now empties the state as e6D98's does, and
edge_memo_revoke never runs e6D98's calls in a job of another module.
On the reporter's save and replayed session: before, 12,652 of 1.57 M
calls into the memo from those hooks found another job's state, and that
run froze; after, 0 of 3.1 M, and no freeze in three runs. The Megaera
fight: the memo's hits as before.

6a07b4af6a6518528f80b9b94262dfc914044601.message:
Rendering note: the menu's flicker is the occlusion queries, not MLAA

The first version blamed the title's MLAA path, from eight captured
frames that happened to have no flicker in them. Counted instead in
screenshots once a second, VSync on (as the launcher runs it), frames
with objects missing and black in their place:

  default                                   15 of 30
  MLAA off                                  10 of 30
  GCM_REPORT_SPU_HOLD_MS=20                 10 of 30
  RSX_ZPASS=0 (every query "visible")        0 of 30

The title culls objects on its occlusion counts. The walker writes each
report when it reaches it, with the last count measured for that
address, and the GPU's count arrives a batch later: the culling jobs
read counts a frame or two old, or another object's, and drop objects
in view. The black is in the display before any post-processing.

The cinematic's band (in the screen-space shadow mask) and stale
rectangles were absent in the one run with the queries answered
visible; its default runs were stopped when the machine ran short of
memory, so that is still to confirm. Plan P1 is now answering the
queries right; MLAA moves under P3.

6bfc470ea60349a452b12241e4781c8822b52f5b.message:
EDGE: keep job results across frames

With culling on the RSX an unskinned job's indexes and vertexes depend only
on its inputs, and 95% of such jobs repeat one already done: the same
meshes every frame, in the depth pass and the lit pass. The end of 0x9990
hashes those inputs; a job seen twice keeps its index list and packed
records, and a later one leaves out the decoding, the transforms, the index
decompression and the packing. The glue around them runs as before. A lit
job whose stage runs on the SPU after all gets its arrays made late.
GOWA_EDGE_MEMO=0 turns it off, =2 checks every hit against the stages.

Check in the game: 4.5 M hits at the gate and in the fight, no list and no
vertex different. Replay of ten corpora: 0 differences, with results on too.
Gate, three runs a side: 23.63 -> 24.61 flips/s. With A and B, 22.89 ->
24.40, and the warm fight 21.17 -> 21.56.

EDGE: the normal loop as native AVX2 code; both EDGE loops 16.04 -> 16.26

native/spu_edge_normals.c runs the loop at LS 0xA950: eight elements an
iteration, each a cross product scaled by w, its squared length through
frsqest, fi and a Newton step, normalised above 1e-30. The vector part
puts two elements in a 256-bit register; the length and what follows is
one value an element, so the eight elements' values share one register and
frsqest/fi/Newton run once for all eight. Float ops are native with the
range check and +0 rule on every op, a half out of range done again by the
exact forms; the last iteration runs lifted.

GOWA_EDGE_NATIVE is now a mask: 1 skinning, 2 normals; unset both, 0 off.

7e3c5e2f8f3623ac7d5c258abc39fb652559c0c0.message:
Notes: EDGE job inputs, slot by slot

Mapped from the 120 gate jobs and 160 consecutive jobs, with a replay that logged every
local-store load and store of the job module and the pieces by function.
- How inputs arrive: two buffer sets, the next job's set fetched while a job runs. The job
  module keeps the previous job's set at 0x10918; laid out from that, all 120 gate jobs'
  pieces match the executable.
- The DMA list has 22 fixed slots (light set, three pieces, index and vertex streams, skinning
  palette and weights, segment header, formats, view block, matrix), each with its readers.
- The descriptor's words: ring base, hole EA, matrix count, frame counter, attribute slot
  list, fragment program and constants block EAs and sizes, screen size.
- The light set's header and arrays, and which lights each lighting routine takes.
- The vertex formats: the output types are the RSX's, the input adds fixed point and 3-byte
  unit vectors. The slot list picks the emitted attributes; that gives the hole's vertex
  arrays in 278 of 280 jobs.
- The segment header slot vs. the context copy: the job fills in the hole size, the format
  numbers and the vertex count rounded up to 8.

This replaces the earlier element table, which was read by position and with the capture
header taken as 48 bytes (it is 56).

EDGE fills of skinned meshes: the SPU's rounding

ek_fill works a skinned block's vertexes out on the backend's thread, for a
draw that does not take the resident part, and did it under the host's
rounding. The game's lit pass tests EQUAL against its depth pass, and the
two may come one from a fill and one from the vertex pass or the SPU, which
work the position out the SPU's way: the last bit differed and the lit pass
left speckled holes all over the mesh. It now sets the SPU's MXCSR for the
call, as er_fill does for unskinned blocks.

Found with VTX_RESIDENT_MB=8 on the Grotto replay (3,527 restarts: Kratos
speckled); the same run after it, 3,462 restarts, shows him as usual. The
note also has what issue #9's reports show of the Delphi temple's broken
textures, which this does not explain yet.

a3b80322e7678e195718718dea572a8295e2e767.message:
EDGE culling's triangle loop (0xD618) as native code

The cull masks eight triangles a pass in the SPU's exact forms (records
gathered with AVX2; degenerate after snapping, outside a plane, facing by
mode, Mesh Trimming), and the in-place writer statement for statement with
the runtime's SPU forms (its shuffle tables, the stores past the end into
the frame's scratch, the pipeline's fill passes), so the index buffer, the
frame and the scratch end the same byte for byte. The count field is the
halfword at ctx + 0x190.

The call-by-call check keeps one copy per level: the lifted culling's own
call of the vertex pass is checked inside it.

Checked identical on 82 replay calls and 520,193 in the game. Replay, the
lit jobs: -3.6%. Gate, ABBA: 14.56 -> 14.74 flips/s (within the spread).
On by default (GOWA_EDGE_NATIVE bit 512).

a97617bd6eef7845d393ee3e7f0f6541e389e68e.message:
EDGE lighting loops: a fast pass with one range test a call

The two lighting loops (0x7BB4, 0x7ED8) tested every op's result for the
native range (and, compare, movemask, branch, then +0), which made the
native loops barely faster than the lifted ones. Now a call runs fast
first with no test per op: under round-toward-zero an exact result beyond
FLT_MAX sets MXCSR's overflow flag, and operands with the SPU's exponent
255 are looked for in what the ops read (the constants and carried values
once, the loaded quadwords each iteration). Either one redoes the call
with the exact forms from the same start; the stores of the fast pass go
only to output arrays apart from everything read. A zero's sign never
changes a non-zero result of these ops, so +0 is applied where values
leave (stores, registers).

GOWA_EDGE_EXACT=1 forces the redo (to test the exact pass). Strict replay
0 differ both ways. Replay, the lit jobs: 100.3 -> 88.0 us (-12%).

aa60d2e2d2c0c5c7a190030a4b1290cef3ad6bd6.message:
EDGE's vertex unpacking (piece 0x75BD10) as native code

The lit jobs' vertex stream is 18-byte records: x y z, then a 48-bit code. The code holds two
unit vectors (attributes 3 and 4), each as two 10-bit components and a 4-bit pattern index.
The third component is a square root by frsqest and fi. The pattern, one of 12 the piece
writes to its frame, gives that component's place and sign and a handedness w. An index
past 11 reads the caller's stack; those pairs are done with the piece's own operations.

The format was mapped with a bit-exact model of the probed calls. The routine also leaves what
the piece leaves: the list and table entries, the frame's patterns, two zero quadwords past
two arrays, r1 and r3.

Checked identical in 188,416 calls in the game and by strict replay. The lit jobs: -6% in
replay. Gate, ABBA: 17.95 -> 17.91 flips/s, within the spread.

EDGE: the skinning loop as native AVX2 code, 15.88 -> 16.06 flips/s

(e8f44fbc6dbf): matrix-palette skinning, two vertices an iteration, now in
one 256-bit register so each blend or transform is one op for both. The
float ops are native under the SPU code's MXCSR with the +0 rule, checked
once an iteration before anything is stored; an iteration out of the single
range, and the last one, run in the lifted loop from the registers as it
has them, so the job's registers come out exact. It runs only when the
loop's invariant registers (masks, 1.0, 1/255) are the ones it was written
for.

d720ed90130e132ffa89afaba2c633dd5481d0f6.message:
EDGE: skinned jobs from kept inputs, skinning in the vertex pass (GOWA_EDGE_SKIN)

A skinned job's vertexes, weights and indexes are the same every frame; only the
palette changes. So its key leaves the palette and the matrix out, and a hit skips
the decoding, 0xE550 and the packing: the job hands the palette to the vertex pass
with its record, and the pass works out position, normal and tangent before it
lights them. A position job gets a record too.

Revoking a hit puts the kept arrays back and runs 0xE550 after all. A job that
goes on to 0xF538 stays on the SPU: no skinned job at the gate or in the fight does.

GOWA_EDGE_SKIN=2 compares every job with spu_edge_gpuskin.c's CPU version. In the
fight, 565 million vertexes: positions bit for bit, tangents at most a unit off,
98.4% of the normals within 2 units of 32767.

Two runs a side, one executable name: gate 28.84 -> 29.98 flips/s, at the game's 30
in half of its windows; warm fight 26.16 -> 27.39. Job outputs identical on the
replay lists, where it is off. The gate's picture right with every draw on the
CPU fallback and with 925 refills of the resident part.

Also: a result the output stage cannot leave out of the ring now goes out whole.
Before, the packing could still leave all but 16 bytes out.

dcbd347f9efb81e3e2f74ed8dc4c2e61ded8d5cb.message:
EDGE lighting on the GPU (phase 2b.1), on by default

The lighting stage's hook (0x73E0) takes a record of the job's lights from its arguments; the
output stage native publishes it after the vertex PUT, keyed by the vertexes' IO offset and
tagged with the first 16 bytes the job put there, and the D3D12 backend's vertex pass lights

GOWA_EDGE_GPU=2, the default in the game, skips the stage on the SPU. A skipped stage the
output stage cannot publish for runs there instead, and the index padding the stage writes is
written by the skip too (GOWA_EDGE_GPU_DEFER=1 runs every skipped stage late: the corpora
replay unchanged). 1 keeps the SPU's lighting and lets the backend compare (VTX_LIT_CHECK);
0 is off, and the default in a replay or a capture.

attributes at the gate, the same screenshots. The phase 2b plan note has the mapping, the

e7312e3b7ac6b13b11b598da328c11e14ce7499d.message:
Re-kick a stranded EDGE job list: the menu-start freeze

About one run in fifteen froze right after the opening movie, the RSX
standing at the first hole of one EDGE job list for good. The main thread
kicks an EDGE list when the MeshProc batch counter (0xA0B724) reaches 0,
and re-arms that counter for the next frame's list right after. When the
re-arm came before the kicked list's policy module had read its first
wait, the module saw the new count and went idle; the next zero kicked
the next list, and nothing kicked the first again.

wws_rekick, the park stall hook (GCM_PARK_STALL_MS=100 by default),
signals an EDGE list whose next entry is a wait already met, on a
workload nothing runs or has asked for. Interleaved A/B on one binary:
2 of 22 runs froze without it, none of 22 with it. The level's speed is
unchanged (19.65 -> 20.27 flips/s, two runs each, within the spread).

The park dump now covers every workload, marks a list a main-thread wait
would still wait for, and shows the job descriptors, the batch counters,
the MLAA block and barriers, and the guest threads. SPU_SIG_RING_DUMP_S
prints it at a set time, for a stall without a park.

A rarer stall during the opening movie (3 of the first 43 runs with the
fix, none in the 74 after) is open; the note has what is known.

Notes: docs/notes/2026-11-01-menu-freeze.md

ea6e9bbc981f58ae16494885c0dc26e50c22ad2d.message:
EDGE job: the skinning driver's loops and the context builder's table loops as native code

- native/spu_edge_skinmat.c (GOWA_EDGE_NATIVE bit 1048576, on by default):
  0xE550's matrix layout loop 0xE804 (word moves), and the skinned lit
  jobs' normal and tangent transform 0xF104. 0xF104 keeps its pipeline in
  eight 256-bit registers and makes one range test a pass, redoing a pass
  in the exact float forms when it fails. A first version with the
  pipeline in arrays saved nothing.
- native/spu_edge_ctx.c (bit 2097152, on by default): 0x88B0's two loops
  over the descriptor's tables, as byte moves. A pass sets only its own
  path's scratch registers, so the natives work out the passes left and
  leave the last pass that copies, and those after it, to the lifted loop.
- A GOWA_EDGE_VERIFY hook at each function's entry checks every call, all
  registers and the whole local store: 378 calls of 0xE550 and 1719 of
  0x88B0 in replay, 90,114 and 413,696 in the game, 0 differences; 1720
  replayed jobs, 0 differences.
- In the game 0xE550 went from 1.63% to 1.07% of the EDGE workers'
  samples, and 0x8930 from 1.20% to 1.00%. Gate, ABBA, steps 2-4 off
  against on: 18.84 -> 19.19 flips/s.
- Notes: the host reference's items 3.3 and 3.4, and the plan.

f9259bac0437b9b8879b3fb9aeb1fb21bbb2b7f1.message:
EDGE natives: order the MXCSR flag reads against the fast ops

The compiler takes the float ops for pure and moved some of them across a
plain _mm_getcsr: in the game the vertex pass (0xD250) stored FLT_MAX
where the SPU saturates to 0x7FFFFFFF in 6923 calls, its overflow flag
read before the op ran. The flags now go through volatile asm (ldmxcsr,
stmxcsr with a memory clobber), ordered by the values they carry: the
pass's register inputs come out of an empty asm after the clear, its
results go into one before the read.

The transform and the vertex pass read the flags once a call when their
output is apart from their input, and redo the whole call exact when they
show; in place, once a pass as before.

GOWA_EDGE_VERIFY=1 also checks each fast call of the two lighting loops
against the exact pass from the same start.

Checked in the game: the transform 1.13M calls, culling 414K, point lights
352K, the lighting loops' self-check, all identical; strict replay 0
differences both ways. Gate, ABBA: 15.34 -> 15.94 flips/s (+3.9%) over
main.

fef5ac98bd8fcf77b8dccb95efebd527f3ba0a55.message:
EDGE's index decompression (0xE4D0 -> 0xDCC0) as native code

Every EDGE job decompresses its triangle indices in place. The format, mapped stage by stage
from snapshots at each loop head and checked with a model of the whole local store:
- an 8-byte header (reuse count, delta bias, bitmask bytes, bits a reuse);
- a bitmask, 2-bit triangle codes, then k-bit reuse values.

The stages:
- the reuses are eight interleaved running sums of the k-bit deltas;
- the bitmask picks a reuse or the next new vertex for each slot of the vertex sequence;
- each triangle code is a fresh triangle of three sequence values, or a turn on one edge of
  the triangle before, reversed, with the next value.

The scratch past the indices goes out by DMA, so the routine makes it byte for byte, along
with c + 0x50/0x58, the frame and r3.

Bit reader, a pshufb expand a mask byte at a time, and one pshufb a triangle:
9,154 -> 4,737 cycles a call. Checked identical in 561,152 calls in the game and by strict
replay. Gate, ABBA: 18.14 -> 18.71 flips/s.

1456888544.readme_excerpt: # Ascension-R: a God of War: Ascension PC port [![CI](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) ![Platform: Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20x64-lightgrey.svg) ![Status: alpha](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-alpha-orange.svg) An unofficial, native PC port of **God of War: Ascension** (PS3) for Windows, made by static recompilation with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). The game's PPU and SPU code is translated to x86-64 ahead of time and the RSX is drawn with Direct3D 12, so no emulator runs while you play. Website: [rigaz29.github.io/Ascension-R](https://rigaz29.github.io/Ascension-R/) > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository holds no game files. You build the port from your own copy of the game. See [Legal](#legal). ## Contents - [Status](#status) - [Features](#features) - [Download](#download) - [What you need](#what-you-need) - [Building from source](#building-from-source) - [Playing](#playing) - [Reporting a problem](#reporting-a-problem) - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Project layout](#project-layout) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Legal](#legal) - [Credits](#credits) - [License](#license) ## Status It boots, plays the cinematics and goes through the menus into the levels. It has not been played from start to finish, so expect problems further in. - **Game:** God of War: Ascension, digital US release, NPUA80918, version 1.12: the game and its updates 1.04 to 1.12. - **Platform:** Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. Tested on Windows 11. - **Speed:** above 30 frames a second in the two scenes measured, a fight of the first level and the gate, on a Ryzen 5 4600H with a GTX 1650 Ti and the Smooth preset. - **Online:** not supported. The port is single player. - **Downloads:** the Kit, on the [releases page](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/releases). It holds none of the game's code and builds it on your PC from your copy. ## Features - **Launcher:** a ready check, three presets (Smooth, Balanced, Faithful) and every setting below. It finds the game's folder by itself, and says when a newer release is out, with a link to it. - **Picture:** internal resolution from 1x to 4x or native, AMD FSR 1 and FSR 3.1 scaling, FSR 3.1 frame generation, SMAA 1x and anisotropic filtering. - **Display:** windowed or borderless, ultrawide, VSync, a frame rate cap, and frame rate and load on screen. - **Shaders:** a compressed cache, pipelines built before the title, and every vertex shader built before the first start of each version, on an 8-bit screen with music of its own. - **Game patches:** switch off MLAA, depth of field, motion blur, mesh trimming or dynamic shadows. - **Cheats:** damage to and from Kratos, max red orbs, infinite magic and items, infinite rage and double jumps. - **Controls:** a controller or keyboard and mouse. Xbox and other XInput pads, and through SDL3 the DualShock 4, the DualSense, Switch controllers and many others; stick dead zone, confirm button, vibration and controller API settings. - **Saves:** backups kept before the game writes over a save. - **Problem reports:** one button makes a zip of the logs, with your paths hidden. [docs/FEATURES.md](docs/FEATURES.md) describes each one and its setting. ## Download The [releases page](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/releases) has the Kit: a zip of the program without the game's code. Its launcher finds your copy of the game, decrypts it with RPCS3 and builds the game's code on your PC, once, in about ten minutes. There is nothing else to install: the Kit brings its own Python and LLVM. Each release's notes have the steps. Your copy needs all nine of the game's updates, 1.04 to 1.12, installed in RPCS3 in that order. Each brings its own files: 1.12's is the EBOOT alone, and the archives come with the ones before it. With 1.12 alone the game stops on its first loading screen. ## What you need To build it from source: - Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. - A CPU with AVX2 and FMA, and a GPU with Direct3D 12. - The game, installed in RPCS3 with its license, and its updates 1.04 to 1.12, installed in that order. - Python 3.10 or later, Git, CMake, Ninja, Visual Studio with "C++ Clang Compiler for Windows", a Windows SDK, and about 20 GB free. - For the game's movies: an LGPL shared build of FFmpeg with its headers, unpacked under `..\ffmpeg`, for example `win64-lgpl-shared` from [BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds](https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/releases). - Optional, for AMD FSR 3.1: [FSR SDK 2.4.0](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK), unpacked under `..\fsr-sdk`. ## Building from source ``` git clone --recursive https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R cd Ascension-R python -m venv ..\.venv ..\.venv\Scripts\pip install -r ps3recomp\requirements.txt # 1. Decrypt USRDIR\GOWA.SELF to GOWA.elf with RPCS3 (Utilities > Decrypt PS3 Binaries). # 2. Point the project at the installed game. It is only read. ..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py setup --game-dir \dev_hdd0\game\NPUA80918 ..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py doctor ..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py analyze ..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py lift ..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py build ..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py run ``` `doctor` lists anything that is missing. The lift and the first build take about 13 minutes on a Ryzen 5 4600H. `run` starts the game straight away, with its log in `logs\`. ## Playing Open `build\Ascension-R.exe`. The launcher checks the game's folder and your setup, and **Play** starts the game. The first start of each version builds the game's vertex shaders before the game begins, on a screen of its own: a minute or two the first time, seconds after an update. Fragment shaders are built the first time they are needed, so expect some stutter at first. **Clear shaders**, in the launcher's sidebar, makes the next start build them again. A build from source keeps its settings, logs and shader caches in `build\`, and its saves in `gamedata\`. ## Reporting a problem **Report a problem**, in the launcher's sidebar, makes a zip in `logs\` beside the settings file, for you to attach to an [issue](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/issues/new?template=problem.yml). The launcher offers it by itself after a session that crashed, lost the graphics device, froze or stopped with no reason in its log. `Ascension-R --report [--with-saves]` makes one without the window. The zip holds the logs and pad recordings of the last three sessions the game ran in, your settings, the build, your hardware and driver versions, and Windows' records of crashes and hangs of this exe in the last two weeks. Folder paths and your Windows account and PC names are hidden. The game sends nothing by itself and no game file goes in. Saves go in only if you tick the box, without the game's images and sounds. If no new frame comes for 15 seconds, the log gets what each thread was doing, and again at 60 (`GOWA_FREEZE_WATCH=`, `0` = off). ## How it works 1. `gowa.py lift` translates the PPU code of `GOWA.elf` to C++, and `build` does the same to C for the SPU programs and job modules. Both are compiled for x86-64 with clang-cl. 2. The [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) runtime stands in for the PS3: its system calls and libraries, SPURS, the file system, audio, pads and save data. 3. The game's RSX commands are drawn with Direct3D 12. Its shaders are translated to HLSL and compiled with DXC. 4. Movies are decoded with FFmpeg. 5. SPU code that was not translated ahead of time runs in an interpreter. The session records it, and the next `lift` adds it. More detail: [what the game is made of](docs/ANALYSIS.md), [what has been measured](docs/PERF.md), and the [development notes](docs/notes), one per session. ## Project layout ``` port/ the port: entry point, launcher, game-specific code native/ hand-written routines for the SPU code that costs the most scripts/ gowa.py, the pipeline (doctor, setup, analyze, lift, build, run, symbolize), and the bench tools/ which of the game's imports the runtime answers, shader cache checks, RenderDoc helpers tests/ tests for the launcher's game search, shader compile guards and native routines docs/ analysis, measurements, features and development notes packaging/ text files that go beside the program in a package site/ the website, rigaz29.github.io/Ascension-R, published by .github/workflows/pages.yml third_party/ zlib ps3recomp/ the toolkit and runtime, as a submodule (fork rigaz29/ps3recomp, branch gowa) ``` ## Contributing Anyone can help: by playing and reporting, or with changes to the port or to the runtime under it. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) says where help is most useful, where a change goes, and what must never be committed. ## FAQ ### Is there an official PC version of God of War: Ascension? No. It came out on PlayStation 3 only. Ascension-R is an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony. ### How is this different from playing on RPCS3? RPCS3 emulates the PS3 and runs the game's code as it goes. Ascension-R translates that code to native x86-64 code ahead of time, on your PC, and draws with Direct3D 12, so no emulator runs while you play. RPCS3 is used only to decrypt your copy. ### Do I need to own the game? Yes. The download holds no code or assets of the game: its launcher builds the game's code from your own copy, with its license. ### Which copies of the game work? Only the digital US release NPUA80918 at version 1.12, with every update from 1.04 installed. European and disc releases are not supported yet ([#4](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/issues/4)). ### Does it run on Linux or the Steam Deck? One player plays it on Linux through Proton, in a Wine prefix made by Lutris ([#12](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/issues/12)). The Steam Deck has not been tried. ### Is it safe to run? The code is open source and built in the open. Each release lists the SHA-256 of its download and what the package was checked for, and the game's code is built on your own PC. The program is not signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn the first time. ## Legal No game files are in this repository, and none will be. You need your own copy of the game and its license, and you decrypt it yourself. What you build from your copy contains code translated from the game. Keep it on your machine: do not commit it or share it. God of War is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by it. ## Credits Built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet. The other code and libraries the port uses, among them FFmpeg, AMD FSR, SMAA, zlib and Zstandard, are listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). ## License The code in this repository is under the MIT License, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). It does not cover the game or anything made from it.

- Introduced a patch to filter legacy methods in the RSX state processing, improving performance in scenarios where the draw engine is active. This change was validated with performance metrics from Resistance 3, showing a notable increase in frame rates.
- Updated `cellGcmSys.c` to include a new function `gcm_legacy_method_has_effect` that identifies methods with outside effects, ensuring only relevant methods are processed when the draw engine is active.

73f19cb2dc2004922076c88477927f156bee4dcf.message:
gcm-rsx/0016: read swizzled shadow maps on the GPU; the lamp's light no longer vanishes near it

Close to a shadowed lamp Resistance 3 renders the lamp's shadow map into a swizzled power-of-two Z16 surface
(zeta pitch 64) and samples it as a swizzled DEPTH16 texture. The draw engine converted only linear reads of the
zeta's pitch and stored only pitched zetas to guest memory, so the light shader read other data at that address
and every shadowed light lit nothing: the lamp over the radio table in Home came and went with the view.
The engine records whether a zeta was written through a swizzled surface; a swizzled read of it goes to the
backend's depth_as_color like a linear one, and the guest-memory fallback stores it in Morton order. New unit test
(fails without the change); checked in play.

76ae439591eabb082f15ba03e4d620c062f5679a.message:
SPU: Update event_status atomically to prevent lost updates

This commit introduces atomic operations for updating the event_status in the SPU context. The event_status is modified by multiple threads, including the SPU's own thread and external threads (PPU stores and peer SPU operations). The previous implementation using plain read-modify-write operations could lead to lost updates, particularly in scenarios where one thread's update could overwrite another's.

Key changes include:
- Introduction of SPU_EVENT_SET and SPU_EVENT_CLEAR macros for atomic updates.
- Modifications in various SPU functions to utilize these macros instead of direct bitwise operations.
- Addition of tests to verify that event_status updates are correctly handled under concurrent conditions, ensuring that no bits are lost during updates.

This change addresses issues observed in Resistance 3 and ensures that the SPU's event handling remains robust and reliable.

Post effects can be turned off (--fx-off grain,motion-blur,dof|all)

Film grain, camera and object motion blur and depth of field each compare
their strength with a threshold loaded from code and return below it, the
game's own "off" path. Four profile instruction patches, guarded by
r3_fx_no_grain / r3_fx_no_motion_blur / r3_fx_no_dof, turn the `addi` that
forms the threshold's address into `lis r3,1`: the threshold is then the ELF
magic at 0x10000 (2.6e38), above any strength. The idea of the toggles is
the Windows port's (miroslavdanutalexandru-alt/Resistance3Port).

host/r3_fx.cpp sets the guards from R3_FX_OFF at start-up; the launcher
passes --fx-off (Makefile FX_OFF=). Checked in a scripted run to the Haven
fight while aiming: the scene through the scope is sharp, the sky has no
grain, the death fall is not smeared. The fps effect is within the fight's
noise at the 30 cap. Tests: test_r3_fx, launcher tests.

1456910623.readme_excerpt:
# Resistance 3 recompilation

A static recompilation of **Resistance 3** (PlayStation 3, EU release `BCES01118`) that runs natively on Apple Silicon
Macs with Metal. It is built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp): the game's PowerPC and Cell SPU
code is translated to C++ ahead of time and compiled into a native library, which a small host program loads together
with an HLE implementation of the PS3 system libraries (graphics, audio, input, file system, saves, trophies).

**You bring the game.** Nothing from the game, from Sony's firmware or from anyone's PS3 is in this repository or in the
release zip. On the first start the launcher takes *your* copy of the disc's `PS3_GAME` folder, translates its code and
compiles the result on *your* computer. The translated code never leaves it.

## Status

- **Tested on macOS only** (Apple Silicon, Metal). In principle the game can run anywhere
  [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) compiles, but no other platform has been tried. The patch set is
  already organized by platform (`patches/domains.txt`).
- **Single-player campaign only.** Co-op and multiplayer are not supported.
- Keyboard + mouse and game controllers are supported; the game is playable with either.
- Most testing has been in the opening chapters (Haven). Expect rough edges further in.
- Only the EU release (`BCES01118`, version 01.00) is supported.

## What you need

| | |
|---|---|
| Computer | Apple Silicon Mac with Metal, a current macOS |
| Python | 3.10 or newer (`brew install python`, or python.org). Only the standard library is used |
| Compiler | the Xcode command line tools (`xcode-select --install`): Apple's clang builds the game module. A portable compiler is not an option: zig was tried and its linker cannot link the module (see [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)) |
| Disk | about 6 GB besides the game: the build, the saves, and the caches the game writes while it runs |
| Game | your own **decrypted dump of the disc's `PS3_GAME` folder** (EU, `BCES01118`); it stays where it is and is not changed |

The launcher uses these parts of the dump: `PARAM.SFO`, `USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN`, `USRDIR/PACKED/GAME/*.PSARC`,
`USRDIR/PACKED/levels/`, `USRDIR/built/` (movies and the rest of the game data). The multiplayer levels are not needed.
Voice packs: English (`GLOBAL_SOUND_US.PSARC`) and Russian (`GLOBAL_SOUND_RU.PSARC`) are present in the tested copy.

## Quick start

```sh
unzip r3-0.1.0-macos-arm64.zip
cd r3
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine .      # only if macOS refuses to open the downloaded program

# first run: point it at the PS3_GAME folder of your dump (or the folder that holds it)
./r3.py --game "/path/to/PS3_GAME"

# every later run
./r3.py
```

The first run takes a few minutes (lifting the game's code, then compiling it into one library, `game.dylib`); later runs
start the game at once. Nothing is redone unless its inputs change.

1. **game**: decrypts the executable (`r3_host unself`, nothing is downloaded) and lays out the disc in the data directory
   as links to your files;
2. **lift**: translates the game's PPU code and its SPU programs to C/C++;
3. **compile**: builds that into `game.dylib` with all your cores;
4. **run**.

**First launch of the game.**

1. The first boot, and the first boot after changing the language, shows **"the game will need to install data"**.
   Press **Space** (Cross). Nothing else needs to be done.
2. **Press START** appears roughly 45-50 seconds after launch. Press **Enter**.
3. On a fresh install the game may also show brightness and screen calibration screens; confirm them with Space.
4. Expect stutter at first: every shader is translated to Metal the first time it is used. The result is cached in
   `cache/msl`, so later runs are smooth.

## Options

```
./r3.py [command] [--game PS3_GAME] [--fps] [--log] [--lang CODE] [--window WxH] [--fullscreen] [--sens DEG]
         [--unlock-fps] [--fx-off LIST]
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--game PS3_GAME` | the PS3_GAME folder of your dump; remembered, so only the first run needs it |
| `--fps` | print the presented frame rate in the terminal |
| `--log` | write the host's output to `logs/run-<time>.log` and `.log.err` in the data directory |
| `--lang CODE` | game language (voice pack and text): `en`, `ru`, ... Without it the macOS language is used, falling back to English |
| `--window WxH` | initial window size in points, e.g. `1600x900`; the window can be resized, the aspect ratio is kept |
| `--fullscreen` | start in full screen |
| `--sens DEG` | mouse speed in degrees per point |
| `--unlock-fps` | up to 60 fps in play and cutscenes (the game's own cap is 30); the main menu stays at 30 |
| `--fx-off LIST` | turn post effects off: a comma-separated list of `grain` (film grain), `motion-blur` (camera and objects), `dof` (depth of field), or `all` |
| `--data DIR` | where everything derived from the game lives (default `./data` next to `r3.py`, or `R3_HOME`) |
| `--yes` | answer yes: confirm `reset --all` |

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `run` (default) | build whatever is stale, then run |
| `build` | only build |
| `doctor` | check this machine and the installation, and say what is missing |
| `kill` | end a stuck host (it ignores a plain `kill`) |
| `clean-cache` | drop the game's disk cache (`--shaders` also the translated shaders) |
| `reset` | remove what is derived from the game (lift, module, disc layout); `--all` also the saves, caches, logs and `controls.txt` |

`./r3.py --help` lists the rest. Other environment variables go to the host, for example `PAD_KEYBOARD_LAYOUT=pad`.

## Where things are

Everything derived from the game is in the data directory (`./data` unless you moved it):

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `game.json` | which `PS3_GAME` folder was set up |
| `disc/PS3_GAME/` | the game as the host sees the disc: links to your files, plus the decrypted `EBOOT.elf` |
| `games/BCES01118-01.00/` | the decrypted executable, the lift, and `module/game.dylib` |
| `gamedata/dev_hdd0/` | **your saves and trophies**, and the game's HDD install |
| `cache/` | the game's disk cache (`BCES01118`) and the translated shaders (`msl`) |
| `controls.txt`, `logs/` | your key bindings, and the logs of `--log` runs |

Delete the data directory to start over (keep `gamedata/` if you want your saves). **Do not share the data directory or
the files in it:** they are derived from the game.

## Controls

### Keyboard and mouse

| Input | Action | PS3 button |
|---|---|---|
| `W` `A` `S` `D` | Move | Left stick |
| Mouse | Look | Right stick |
| Left mouse button | Fire | R1 |
| Right mouse button | Aim | L1 |
| Middle mouse button or `V` | Melee | R3 |
| `Space` | Jump | Cross |
| `C`, `Ctrl` or `Backspace` | Crouch; back in menus | Circle |
| `E` or `R` | Reload, use | Square |
| `G` | Grenade | L2 |
| `F` | Secondary fire | R2 |
| `Shift` | Sprint | L3 |
| Mouse wheel or `Q` | Weapons: tap = previous weapon, hold = weapon wheel (pick with `WASD`) | Triangle |
| Arrow keys or `1` `2` `3` `4` | D-pad | D-pad |
| `Tab` | Select | Select |
| `Enter` / `Esc` | Select / back in menus; start / pause elsewhere | Cross / Circle, Start |

- The mouse is captured while the window is in front and no menu is open. `Cmd+Tab` releases it.
- `Cmd+Q` or **Quit** in the app menu asks the game to quit (it exits after 3 seconds if the game does not). The window's
  close button quits at once.
- The window can be resized; the aspect ratio is kept.

### Tuning

- `--sens <degrees per point>` sets the mouse speed (the environment variable `PAD_MOUSE_SENS` does the same).
- The mouse is scaled by the field of view, so it covers the same part of the screen zoomed or not. `R3_ZOOM_SENS=0`
  turns that off.
- The mouse follows the game's **Options > Controls**: Camera Speed and Invert-X / Invert-Y. `R3_GAME_SETTINGS=0` turns
  that off.
- `controls.txt` (written in the data directory, with the defaults, on the first run) remaps the keys and
  mouse buttons: one line per action, e.g. `jump = Space` or `fire = MouseLeft`. `R3_CONTROLS=<path>` names another file.
  Mistakes are reported in the log with their line number.
- The game's button prompts (menus, HUD, hints) show the key or mouse button bound to each pad button in
  `controls.txt`. They are drawn at start-up, so a change to the file shows after a restart. If you play with a game
  controller, `R3_KEY_GLYPHS=0` brings back the PlayStation icons.
- `PAD_KEYBOARD_LAYOUT=pad` switches to a pad-shaped layout: arrows, `I` `J` `K` `L` for the camera, `Z` `X` `A` `S`
  for the face buttons.

### Game controllers

Controllers that SDL2 recognizes as game controllers (PS4/PS5, Xbox, and most others) are read by the toolkit's pad
layer and can be plugged in at any time. The keyboard and mouse path is the one tested most.


## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | What to do |
|---|---|
| Something does not work | `./r3.py doctor` lists what is missing |
| `no suitable compiler` | `xcode-select --install` |
| `... is not a supported game version` | only `BCES01118` 01.00 (EU) is supported |
| `r3_host is already running` | `./r3.py kill` |
| Textures or data stay broken from run to run | `./r3.py clean-cache`; the game rebuilds its disk cache |
| Stutter on the first run | Normal: shaders are being translated. See "First launch" |
| Start over | `./r3.py reset`, or delete the data directory (`gamedata/` holds your saves and trophies) |
| After an update of the launcher | run `./r3.py`; a changed host rebuilds the module by itself (host and module check each other's ABI) |

## How it works

- **Host** (`host/r3_host`): the ps3recomp runtime plus this port's sources in `host/`, with every dependency linked
  statically. It is the same for everyone and contains nothing from the game. It also decrypts the executable
  (`r3_host unself`).
- **Module** (`game.dylib`): the game's PPU and SPU code translated to C++ from *your* executable and compiled locally.
  The host loads it at start-up.
- **Launcher** (`r3.py`, `launcher/`): Python standard library only. It sets the game up, lifts, compiles and starts the
  host; every step is skipped while its inputs are unchanged.
- **Patches** (`patches/`): changes to the pinned ps3recomp revision that this game needs, grouped by subject (SPURS,
  SPU runtime, RSX/GCM, input, file system, ...). Each one names the symptom it fixes. Fixes that apply to other games
  are proposed upstream.

[docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) has the details, [docs/licensing.md](docs/licensing.md) the licenses, and
[CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) the patch workflow, the test suites and the debugging knobs.

## Building from source

You need git, cmake, ninja, Python 3.10+ and the Xcode command line tools (`brew install cmake ninja python`) and internet
access for the first build, which fetches the pinned toolkit and its dependencies (SDL2, glslang, SPIRV-Tools, SPIRV-Cross).

```sh
scripts/build_host.sh     # clones the pinned toolkit, applies patches/, builds the static dependencies and the host -> dist/host
scripts/package.sh        # dist/r3-<version>-macos-<arch>.zip
./r3.py --game "/path/to/PS3_GAME"   # in a checkout the launcher builds and runs the host from dist/ itself
```

In a checkout `./r3.py` rebuilds the host with `scripts/build_host.sh` when `host/`, `patches/` or the build scripts are
newer than it (`--no-host-build` skips that). `make` wraps the same steps and uses the checkout itself as the data
directory (`R3_HOME`), so `make run` keeps its saves in `gamedata/`; `make test` runs the unit tests.

## License

The code in this repository is free software under the **GNU GPL, version 2 or (at your option) any later version**
([LICENSE-GPL-2.0.txt](LICENSE-GPL-2.0.txt)). The prebuilt host also contains Apache-2.0 licensed parts, so as a whole it
is distributed under **GPL version 3 or later** ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). Parts derived from the MIT-licensed ps3recomp toolkit
(`host/main.cpp`, the patches) keep its notice: [LICENSE-MIT-ps3recomp.txt](LICENSE-MIT-ps3recomp.txt).

## Credits and disclaimer

- [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet: the recompilation toolkit and runtime this port is
  built on.
- [SDL2](https://libsdl.org), [glslang](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glslang),
  [SPIRV-Tools](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Tools) and
  [SPIRV-Cross](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Cross): window, input and shader translation.
- [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3): `r3_host unself` ports its executable decryption, and the key table is from
  its key vault.
- [envytools](https://github.com/envytools/envytools): the RSX memory-tiling address math.
- The launcher follows the one of the Soulcalibur II HD port.

Resistance 3 is a product of Insomniac Games and Sony Interactive Entertainment. This project is not affiliated with
or endorsed by either. It ships no game code or assets; you must own the game and supply your own copy.

1457091124.readme_excerpt:
# PS3 XMB background

The PlayStation 3 XMB wave background (firmware 4.93) as a KDE Plasma 6 wallpaper. The
console's own renderer is reimplemented in native code and runs the original shaders,
parameters and simulation from your firmware update. Nothing is redrawn by hand and no
recorded video is played back.

## Install

Download `ps3-xmb-installer.run` from the Releases page and run it:

```bash
sh ps3-xmb-installer.run
```

That's it. It needs KDE Plasma 6, `python3` and `openssl` (both preinstalled on most
desktops). The installer downloads Sony's free PS3 system software update (about 200 MB)
directly from Sony's update server, takes the renderer's shaders, parameters and textures
out of it into `~/.local/share/ps3-xmb` (every file checked by SHA-256), deletes the
download, installs the wallpaper and switches every screen to it. None of Sony's files are
part of this project. Already have `PS3UPDAT.PUP` (4.93)? `sh ps3-xmb-installer.run
PS3UPDAT.PUP` uses it instead. Set `PS3_XMB_KEEP_WALLPAPER=1` to install without switching.

### Windows 10/11

Download `PS3-XMB-Setup.exe` from the Releases page and run it (no administrator rights
needed). On first start the app asks to download Sony's PS3 system software (about 200 MB,
from Sony) and takes the renderer's data from it, then draws the background behind the
desktop icons across all monitors. It pauses while a fullscreen app or game is in front and
starts with Windows (tray icon: Pause, Start with Windows, Quit).

### From source

Install the build dependencies (Qt 6.9 or newer), then run `./install.sh` (same options):
- Arch: `sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel cmake ninja qt6-base qt6-declarative`
- Fedora: `sudo dnf install gcc-c++ cmake ninja-build qt6-qtbase-devel qt6-qtdeclarative-devel`
- Debian/Ubuntu: `sudo apt install build-essential cmake ninja-build qt6-base-dev qt6-declarative-dev libgl-dev libopengl-dev`

### Multiple screens

Screens using the wallpaper share one simulation and show one scene across the desktop. The
layout is physical: each screen keeps its real size (from its reported millimetres, 96 dpi if
unknown), and screens that touch in the display settings touch in the scene, aligned at the
nearer edge. The scene's axis runs along the line through the screen centres, snapped to
exactly horizontal or vertical within 20° (setting "Across screens": Automatic, Always level,
Exact angle). It follows layout changes live. Settings are shared by all screens
(`~/.config/ps3-xmb.conf`).

## Development

- `native/` — renderer (Qt/OpenGL), firmware import and shader translation tools, tests.

Firmware data and every file derived from it stay in `build/` (ignored). Do not commit them.

### Build and run

```bash
python3 native/tools/import_data.py /path/to/PS3UPDAT.PUP --output build/data
cmake -S native -B build/release -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build/release
build/release/moyou-preview --shaders build/data/shaders --reference build/data/reference \
  --cpu build/data/cpu --preset day
```

`moyou-preview --screens "x,y,w,h;…" --screen N` renders one screen of a multi-screen layout
(mm); `--output frame.png` renders offscreen.

### Verifying against the original programs

The native code was ported from translations of the firmware's own CPU and SPU programs and
is checked against them byte for byte. Those translations are firmware-derived and stay
local. To build with them, point CMake at them; this enables `MOYOU_VERIFY_NATIVE=1` (run the
original beside every native stage and report differences) and the `*=original` switches
(`MOYOU_PARTICLE_FRAME`, `MOYOU_PARTICLES`, `MOYOU_SURFACE`, `MOYOU_LIBM`).

```bash
W=$PWD/build/work
cmake -S native -B build/qt -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo \
  -DMOYOU_CPU_DIRECTORY=$W/cpu-particles -DMOYOU_SPU_DIRECTORY=$W/native-verified \
  -DMOYOU_RECOMPILER_DIRECTORY=$PWD/build/third_party/ps3recomp
cmake --build build/qt
native/check.sh
```

| Local path (`build/`) | Contents |
|---|---|
| `inputs/PS3-XMB-4.93.PUP` | Sony 4.93 update, sha256 `158471fd…cf365` |
| `third_party/ps3recomp` | ps3recomp at `4e8f3ca8` (MIT) |
| `work/reference` | `import_firmware.py` output |
| `work/native-verified` | `lift_simulation.py` output (SPU translations) |
| `work/cpu-particles` | `lift_rope.py` output (PPU translations, math image) |
| `work/native-shaders-hdr` | `translate_shaders.py` output |
| `work/decompiler` | Ghidra project used by `PrepareMoyou.java` / `ExportMoyou.java` |

## License

GPL-2.0-or-later (see `LICENSE`). Parts from other projects keep their notices:
`native/native/CellEstimate.h` (RPCS3, GPL-2.0-or-later), `native/native/SpuEstimate.h`
(after ps3recomp, MIT), `native/tools/sce.py` (format and public keys after RPCS3,
GPL-2.0-or-later). Firmware data
is not included and is not covered by this license; users supply their own update file.

4e324ad9f5ff0fa8d99e936e5a97ceecbe430968.message:
Game update 2.17 runs (US BCUS98114): two lifter fixes, 2.17's SPU jobs

2.17 was built with a newer compiler than the disc, and the lift did
not know two of its patterns (tools/ppu_lifter.py, in ps3recomp.patch):

- Switch tables whose base is built from immediates (lis/addi) are
  decoded; only TOC-loaded bases were accepted, so every such bctr
  lifted to an unresolved indirect call and the game stayed on a black
  screen from its static constructors on.
- The raw-index search for the table bound only looks before the lwzx:
  with `lwzx r0, r9, r0` it took the later `add r0,r0,r9` as the index,
  missed the bound compare and cut func_00B7288C's 310-case table at
  256.
- Two vectors in tools/test_ppu_jumptables.py.

On the US 01.00 EBOOT the lifter's jump-table discovery is byte for
byte as before (92 dispatchers, 459 targets); on 2.17 it goes from 80
dispatchers to 358.

version_addrs.py: the computed goto is matched by opcodes only (2.17
reads its field off r31, with no TOC reload before it), its labels are
read from the code that stores them when no data table holds them, and
duplicate targets are dropped. US 01.00 output is unchanged.

spu_jobs_from_eboot.py: the four SPU jobs US 2.17 changed or added
(CB9BD024 replaces D58063CD; 0B07CA3D, 18DE3719, CF635263 are new); the
summary counts the jobs only updates have.

setup.ps1 and version_addrs.py name US 2.17's EBOOT.elf; README, STATUS
and CHANGELOG updated.

Tested on BCUS98114 with updates 1.01-2.17: menus, GT Mode, a full
16-car Arcade race at 59.4 fps median, no missed SPU job and no
unresolved indirect call. Ryzen 7 9850X3D, Radeon RX 9070 XT,
Windows 11.

9ca7bb103ebd9a452ae9e641b15b72570ac0dead.message:
New shaders compile in parallel: first-visit stutter about 3x shorter

A shader missing from the cache took 25-35 ms to compile on the graphics
thread, one after another; a new car or track brings 100+ at once (a
12 s freeze at one race start from an empty cache). They now go to a pool
of up to 8 compile threads. The draw names a stand-in for its pipeline and
the walk carries on; the recording thread resolves the stand-in when it
reaches it, so the GPU sees the same commands in the same order.

Creating an RTV/DSV in a slot never used before no longer waits for the
recording ring (which waited for every shader still compiling).

Measured from an empty cache on the same route: 26.6 s of stutter instead
of 78.4 s, worst freeze 3.4 s instead of 12.2 s, no errors.
LD_ASYNC_SHADERS=0 restores compiling on the graphics thread.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

9f73bed81cb35438704c5dd9ca2e70b1ed67a186.message:
DLC works offline with your own licence keys (runtime only; no keys in the repo)

The runtime part of #24, as asked in its review: no installer, no key
material in the repository.

Runtime (ps3recomp.patch):
- PS3_EDAT_STRICT=1: an EDAT opens the way the PS3 kernel serves it, as
  stored for a plain open and as plaintext for an open with the 8-byte
  NPDRM argument (GT5 passes [0, 2]). GT5's buildIndex reads each
  voucher's NPD header with a plain open and checks its content id;
  decrypted on every open, all vouchers failed and nothing was granted.
- sceNpManagerGetEntitlementById answers "not owned", as PSN does for an
  account without the purchase; unimplemented, it returned success with
  nothing written. GT5's DLCUtil unlocks the 2011 packs by entitlement or
  voucher and the 2012 packs by voucher only, so the DLC comes from the
  vouchers, each of which decrypts only with its licence key.
- PS3_NP_SIGNED_IN=1: the NP manager reports signed in with the local
  profile and no network, for the Downloadable Content screen.
- Licence keys from dev_hdd0/home/00000001/exdata/<content id>.rifkey,
  and the decrypted cache in dev_hdd0/edat_cache: GT5 opens every file
  in USRDIR/vou, so neither may sit beside the vouchers.

play.bat: PS3_EDAT_STRICT on; PS3_NP_SIGNED_IN only when a voucher is
installed (checked at every start), so players without DLC stay offline
and the game doesn't try for tickets.

README: a DLC section (vouchers from RPCS3 or a PS3, a key per content
id in exdata). STATUS and CHANGELOG.

e67ff9e9a0c9ff2a0d620b5e9a9c7904461d0ad0.message:
Fix noisy distant road and track textures (Tsukuba)

Many track textures have only their top two or three mip levels written; the rest of the chain held zeros on a fresh boot and leftover data from earlier scenes otherwise, which showed as blocky black-and-white or grass-green noise on the road at Tsukuba. Each DXT level is now checked against the one above it (mean colour of each 4x4 block), and from the first empty or mismatched level the chain is rebuilt from the last good one (decode, box filter, re-encode). LD_MIP_REBUILD=0 turns it off; LD_MIP_FOLLOW_MAX sets the threshold (default 12); LD_MIP_DUMP=<dir> saves mipped DXT textures for offline checks.

💬 Discord · Install · Launcher · Updating · Version history · Changelog · Status · FAQ · Modding · Contributing · License

# GT5 Recomp An unofficial PC port of **Gran Turismo 5** (PS3) made by static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated into C++ that is compiled for Windows x64, and the PS3's graphics, sound, input and system calls are reimplemented on Windows (Direct3D 12 for the RSX). A native [Linux build](#linux) (Vulkan) is new and early. It is built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) and borrows from the [GT5 Prologue port](https://github.com/sp00nznet/GT5P), both by Ned Heller (sp00nznet). > **Game version required:** your own **Gran Turismo 5** Blu-ray disc, using the disc's own > executable (version **01.00**, with **no game update** installed): > > - **Europe, BCES00569**: tested. This is the copy the port was built from. > - **North America, BCUS98114**: works; players have raced on it (thanks!). The lift finds the few addresses > that differ between releases in your own executable. > > See [Which copy of GT5](#which-copy-of-gt5) for how to check your files. ## 📑 Contents | 🚀 Getting started | 📈 How it's going | 🛠️ Setting up by hand | 📚 About the project | |---|---|---|---| | [Install](#install) | [Current state](#current-state) | [Requirements](#requirements) | [What this repository contains](#repo-contents) | | [The launcher](#launcher) | [Try it, tell me how it went](#feedback) | [Which copy of GT5](#which-copy-of-gt5) | [Fork it, mod it](#modding) | | [Updating](#updating) | [FAQ](#faq) | [Setup](#setup) | [Credits](#credits) | | [Controls](#controls) | | [Switches](#switches) | [License](#license) | | [Linux](#linux) | | | | **More pages:** [Version history](VERSIONS.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Status board](STATUS.md) · [Modding guide](MODDING.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [License](LICENSE) ## ⬇️ Install **The easy way, on Windows 10 or 11:** 1. Download **[GT5-Installer.bat](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/releases/latest/download/GT5-Installer.bat)** and double-click it. If Windows warns about a downloaded file, choose **Run** (or **More info**, then **Run anyway**). 2. In its window, pick two things and press **Install**: - **your GT5 game**: the folder of your disc dump (the one with `PS3_GAME` in it) or an `.iso`; - **PS3UPDAT.PUP**, Sony's free PS3 system software (the window has a button that opens Sony's page). That's all. It installs whatever's missing (Git, Python, Microsoft's C++ build tools), downloads this code, unlocks your game's executable and the system software with RPCS3 (used only as a tool for that: the game itself runs natively as `gt5.exe`, not in an emulator), builds the game (about an hour the first time) and puts **Gran Turismo 5 (PC)** on your desktop, which opens the [launcher](#launcher). Nothing from the game is ever uploaded or shared. Rather do it by hand? See [Setup](#setup). On Linux? See [Linux](#linux). ## 🎛️ The launcher

**Gran Turismo 5 (PC)** on your desktop (or `GT5Launcher.exe` in your `gt5-recomp` folder) opens the launcher: every setting in one window, then **Play**. No more editing `play.bat`. - **Display:** 1080p or 720p, **Speed** (30 fps draws every other frame; it only helps when the graphics card is the limit, the window title then shows both numbers, e.g. `FPS: 15 (game 30)`), screen shape (ultrawide), **borderless full screen**, maximized or a window size, watch mode, SPU threads. - **Controls:** steering wheel on/off, wheel rotation, force feedback strength and direction, pad in the background, mouse clipping. - **Game:** the game's language (as far as your disc has it), your mods from `GT5\mods`, the launcher's own language (English or 中文). - **Updates:** shows your version and the newest one with what's new, and **Update now** does the whole update for you and opens the launcher again. - **Help:** **Save logs for a report** puts your logs on the desktop as `.txt` files GitHub accepts, plus the logs folder, the problem form and this FAQ. It's built on your PC from [`launcher/GT5Launcher.cs`](launcher/GT5Launcher.cs) with the C# compiler that comes with Windows, every time the game is built, so it updates with the game; its picture is the logo from your own disc. Settings are saved in `GT5\settings.bat`, which `play.bat` reads, so `play.bat` still works and starts the game the same way. (`GT5Launcher.exe --play` starts the game straight away.) ## 🔄 Updating Every change to the port comes out as a numbered version (v0.1.0, v0.1.1, ...) on the [Releases page](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/releases), with what changed. To hear about new ones, click **Watch** at the top of this page, then **Custom** and tick **Releases**. ### The easy way - **The launcher** checks for a new version when it opens: its **Updates** page shows what's new, and **Update now** does everything below and opens the launcher again. - Or **double-click `Update.bat`** in your `gt5-recomp` folder. Both run `update.ps1`, so everything below applies. (No launcher or `Update.bat` yet? Your next update brings them: run the command below once.) ### Are you out of date? Close the game, open PowerShell in your `gt5-recomp` folder and run: ``` powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -List ``` It lists every version and marks the one you have (`<- installed`) and the newest (`[newest]`). If they're different, you're out of date. ### Update to the newest version ``` powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 ``` That one command does everything: 1. It downloads the new version. 2. It swaps the old ps3recomp patch for the new one. 3. It re-generates the game code only if that version needs it (about 10 minutes). 4. It rebuilds only what changed. Kept as they are: - your saves (`GT5\gamedata`), a game update's data (`GT5\hdd0`) and game files (`GT5\input`, `GT5\vfs`, `GT5\dev_flash`); - the shader cache; - edits you made to files such as `play.bat`. The previous `gt5.exe` is kept as `GT5\build\gt5.previous.exe`. If one of your edits clashes with a change in the new version, the new version's file is used and your edit is saved in `backups\` so you can copy it back. **If you're several versions behind,** run the same command. It goes straight to the newest version; there's no need to step through the ones in between. ### Installed before update.ps1 existed? If your folder has no `update.ps1` (you set up before v0.1.0), get it first, then update: ``` git pull powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 ``` If `git pull` says your local changes would be overwritten (usually `play.bat`), run `git stash`, then `git pull`, then `git stash pop`, then the update. Your first update re-generates the game code once (about 10 minutes), because older installs have no record of what their code was made from. ### Downloaded the ZIP instead of cloning? A ZIP download can't update itself. Clone the repository fresh as in [Setup](#setup), step 1. Then move these folders over from your old copy and run `update.ps1`: - your game files: `GT5\input`, `GT5\vfs`, `GT5\dev_flash`; - your saves: `GT5\gamedata` (and `GT5\hdd0`, if you set up a game update). ### Go back to an older version If a new version gives you trouble, switch back to the one that worked (see `-List` for the names): ``` powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -Version v0.1.0 ``` To play the previous build right away instead, copy `GT5\build\gt5.previous.exe` over `GT5\build\gt5.exe` (the last update kept it). Please also [report what went wrong](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml). ### Other options | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `update.ps1 -Dev` | The newest changes, before they're released. | | `update.ps1 -NoBuild` | Switch versions without building; build later with `GT5\scripts\build.cmd gt5`. | | `update.ps1 -Force` | Re-generate and rebuild everything, even when nothing changed. | ## 🎮 Controls A DualSense, DualShock 4 or XInput pad works. Without one, the keyboard: Z = Cross, X = Circle, A = Square, S = Triangle, arrow keys = D-pad, Enter = Start, Tab = Select. A steering wheel works too, with force feedback (new and untested on real wheels): see the [FAQ](#faq). ## 📋 Current state

**Playable.** Races run at 45 to 58 fps on the tested rig, and most of the game's modes work. The full board (tested rig, what works, what's being worked on, known issues, recent changes) is in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md); updates are also posted in [Announcements](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/discussions/categories/announcements). Everything done on the port since the first day, with dates, is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## 🏁 Try it, then tell me how it went If you own the game, please set it up and play. Every result helps decide what gets fixed next, whether it runs great, half works, or doesn't build at all. Laptops, integrated graphics and AMD cards especially: the port was tuned on one desktop with an NVIDIA card. | You want to... | Go here | |---|---| | Say how it went (takes two minutes, mostly quick picks) | [Tried it: here's how it went](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=1-tried-it.yml) | | Report something broken | [Something's broken](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml) | | Ask for a change | [Suggest a change](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=3-idea.yml) | | Post quick results, screenshots of it running, or ask for help | [Discussions](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/discussions/1) | | Chat, get help live, share results | **[The Workshop Discord](https://discord.gg/9cVPS7r5Ha)**: #gt5-help, #gt5-test-reports, #gt5-chat (I'm **mormonftp** there) | ## ❓ FAQ | Question | Short answer | |---|---| | Steering wheels? | 🧪 New, not yet tried on a real wheel: [wheel owners wanted](#faq) | | Force feedback? | 🧪 New, with wheel support, also untried on a real wheel | | Widescreen (16:9)? | ✅ Yes, GT5 is a 16:9 game | | Ultrawide (21:9, 32:9)? | ✅ New: a wider view, with the HUD kept 16:9 in the middle | | Which controllers? | ✅ DualSense, DualShock 4, Xbox pads, keyboard | | US copy (BCUS98114)? | ✅ Yes, players have raced on it | | Version 1.02, or a game update (2.xx)? | 🧪 New: game updates run: 2.17 (the last) tested on the US and European releases, 2.01 on the Asian one, 2.11 with the Master Mod on the US one by a player ([how to set one up](#game-updates)); 1.02 untried | | Settings without editing files? | ✅ New: the [launcher](#launcher) | | Full screen? | ✅ New: borderless full screen in the launcher (Alt+Enter is switched off since v0.1.17: it used to freeze the picture) | | Higher than 1080p (4K)? | ⚠️ The game's top mode is its 1080p one (races drawn at 1728x972), scaled up to your window; drawing above that isn't there yet | | Japanese or Asian release (BCJS, BCAS)? | ✅ Hong Kong / Asia (BCAS20108) runs, reported by a player, and its disc 01.00 and update 2.01 race in tests too; Japanese untried, please report | | Slow PC or laptop? | 🛠️ Laptops now use their dedicated graphics card. On most PCs the CPU sets the pace (the game's own threads), so the launcher's **Speed: 30 fps** rarely helps: it's for a graphics card at its limit. **On a laptop:** plug it in and set Windows' power mode to *Best performance* (and the maker's performance mode, e.g. in HP Command Center or Lenovo Vantage): a tester's i5-1135G7 ran into its power limit 88% of the time, which held its cores at 2.9 GHz instead of 4.2, while its graphics were only 30% busy. Speed-ups for 4-6 core CPUs are being worked on | | Linux? | 🧪 New and early: a [native Linux build](#linux). First test (no graphics card) reached the race start; races on a real GPU untested | | Steam Deck, Proton, Wine? | ❓ Not tried yet: the Linux build in a distrobox is the route to try ([Steam Deck](#steam-deck)). Reports welcome | | Android? | 🛠️ Being worked on | | Online? | ❌ No | | Is it legal? | ✅ No game files here: you build it from your own disc | | Ready-made download? | ❌ No, but [GT5-Installer.bat](#install) builds it for you | | Errors during setup? | 🛠️ Use [GT5-Installer.bat](#install), or run `setup.ps1` (see below) | | Black screen, `draws: 0`? | 🛠️ Fixed: update; if it's still black, `GT.VOL` may be missing or in pieces (see below) | **Q: Does it support steering wheels and force feedback?** **A: Yes, new in v0.1.2, but nobody has tried it on a real wheel yet.** On a PS3, GT5 talks to its Logitech wheels directly over USB, for both steering and force feedback. The port now plays that part: your PC wheel appears to the game as a **Logitech G27** (900°, three pedals, paddles and an H-shifter), and the game's force-feedback commands (the centring spring, the steering forces in a race) are played on your wheel through DirectInput, which Logitech, Thrustmaster, Fanatec and other wheels support. Plug the wheel in before you start the game; it's picked up by itself, and pads work as before. What has been checked, without a wheel: the game accepts the emulated G27, a race steers from it, and the force-feedback commands the game sends are decoded and logged. What hasn't: the feel on a real wheel, including which way the forces push. So **wheel owners are wanted**: please [tell us how it went](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=1-tried-it.yml) (or [report a problem](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml)), and attach `GT5\logs\play.err`: its `[wheel]` lines say which wheel was found, its axes, and what the game asked of it. If something is off, add a line to `play.bat` (next to the other `set` lines): | Problem | Fix | |---|---| | The forces push the wrong way (the wheel pulls away from the centre) | `set "PS3_WHEEL_FFB_INVERT=1"` | | Forces too strong or too weak | `set "PS3_WHEEL_FFB=60"` (percent, 0 = off) | | Steering too quick or too slow | set your wheel's rotation to 900° in its softwa

001fe21beabd2b1bbc7bb22e560216af53a92839.message:
Ultrawide: the title's cameras at the screen's width (display.ultrawide)

Widens the aspect and the half-widths of the perspective and orthographic cameras by the same factor, so the vertical view stays and more shows at the sides. The camera controller keeps 16:9. Off by default.

0059cc2162832efe2f9690e1b156784452625783.message:
launcher: show progress while preparing the game, fetch RPCS3 in pieces

Download with WinHTTP instead of URLDownloadToFile. Four connections take
2 MB pieces, so a slow route only costs its own piece. A connection that
goes quiet or falls far behind the rest is dropped and its piece resumes
where it stopped; 30 s with no data at all ends the download. Every piece
is asked for at the release address, since the links it redirects to run
out within minutes.

The System tab shows each stage with a bar, speed, time left, reconnects,
how long no data has come, and a Stop button.

Also find the .rap beside the game when there is no rpcs3.exe, unpack with
a relative path because tar takes no non-ASCII path, and name the missing
VC++ Redistributable instead of failing without a reason.

00a5f5578e2f0071d755cee186db8b4f1965ce33.message:
GOWA_WWS_WATCH/TRACE: the job lists of workloads 2-17

The watch read only RenderJobs, MeshProc, EDGE and RsxSync. It now covers
General6, BatchJobList and RenJobSet too, so a PS3_FTRACE trace shows who
publishes General6's jobs (the main thread, in three bursts a cycle).

00dc77f3df8234903171f96e89409230df18d074.message:
EDGE: skinned jobs on the SPU again by default (no more trails in the prison)

The game draws its skinned meshes twice, a depth pass and a lit pass that
tests EQUAL against it, and never clears the scene's colour. The skinned path
(GOWA_EDGE_SKIN) skins a job in the vertex pass on the GPU, a job it does not
take on the SPU, and takes a mesh's two jobs each on its own: in the prison of
the damned (profile 3's opening) ~45% stay on the SPU. The GPU rounds to
nearest and the SPU toward zero, so where a mesh was split the depths differed
in the last bit, the lit pass left holes, and the frames before showed through
them: Kratos and the walls in trails.

GOWA_EDGE_SKIN now defaults to 0. The prison with FSR 3.1, frame generation
and VSync: no trails. The fight with the same settings, one run each: 27.94
flips/s off against 28.30 on, the later windows 27.05 against 28.30 (the ~4%
the path gave). The note has the search and a failed try at an exact pass.

0190a52f2362f6217fca389c4bf8a09a9c0b499f.message:
Launcher: Graphics card, discrete or integrated

A row in the Graphics tab, with the names of the two GPUs, on a PC that
has two. It asks Windows what the renderer asks, so the name shown is
the GPU the game runs on, and the Ready check follows the choice.

01f84209d18918b0b212275548327ad43a72223b.message: Notes: where shader compiling spends its time

02f34608fb753f134c5602c2f02e89ee4383f851.message:
Make frame generation's cap follow the display

With no Frame rate cap the game is held at half the refresh rate instead of a fixed 30: 60 at 120 Hz. Past 60 flips, the most a PS3 flips, it takes the next even division, so frames keep an even pace: 36 at 144 Hz. graphics.frame_generation_refresh gives the rate by hand.

03f66f8e9fc26570ba24af8607ebe1ba76c21f52.message:
EDGE: leave out what skipped lighting left without a reader

With the lighting stage skipped, the binormals (0xA880's loop) and the
packing of ids 27-30 had no reader: the stage was their only reader, and
the GPU pass writes over the packed bytes. A hook at 0xA928 leaves the
loop out for the lit layout, and the output piece packs bytes 0-23 of a
vertex. If the stage runs on the SPU after all, the binormals run first.
GOWA_EDGE_GPU_LEAN=0 keeps both.

Replay with every skipped stage run late: 10 corpora, 0 differences.
Gate, four runs a side: 22.48 -> 22.96 flips/s.

0760d3b170113fa9cb75ebda3508027e82235744.message: package: read the status of the first changed file right

096408e5e84399f07f7e549c12f408e32954f20b.message:
Runtime: SPU overlay GETs skip the signature scan for data

ps3recomp 07c2a2b9 and its parent d71918df.

0a015a7124800aeda8fed7ebe9a47eb207271048.message:
EDGE vertex transform (0xF538) as native code

The 4x4 transform of a vertex stream, eight vertices a pass in AVX2 with
the SPU's exact float forms, the loop's two-deep order kept (each pass's
loads before the previous pass's stores, pass 0's initial registers
stored too). The last pass runs with the runtime's SPU forms and leaves
every register as the lifted loop does: the job's later code spills some
of them, and the strict replay saw those bytes differ.

The call-by-call check can compare all 128 registers (all_regs); the
transform uses it. 358 replay calls identical, strict replay 0 differ.
Replay: -1.5 to -2% per job. On by default (GOWA_EDGE_NATIVE bit 1024).

0aae8f99e41bb485db6dc05d60efb728238a9f3a.message:
GOWA_MAIN_SLOW: probe of the main thread's own work; it sets ~30% of it

Runtime d0b71071 (g_ppu_icall_hook). At each indirect call the main thread
spins for <percent> of the time since the previous one, waits left out.
+25%: 16.34 -> 15.98 flips/s, +100% (~12 ms a frame): 15.44, so about a
third of its own work is on the frame's path. Plan 2.8: the main thread's
PPU code is not the first lever; EDGE is.

0b04a1ea1798b32ad7eb5a208a7d649105d30a37.message:
The vertex pass's program no longer stops the frames (#12)

The fork lights the pass's draws on the CPU until its compute program is
compiled, and has DXC compile it under Wine, where D3DCompile is
vkd3d-shader's and did not finish it in a minute. Here, from an empty
shader cache, the frames went on through D3DCompile's 21 s, and DXC takes
0.7 s: docs/notes/2026-11-13-vertex-pass-compile.md.

0cd1fdaeabdf33907c07d75bec477c131e5eae79.message:
Rename what a player sees to Ascension-R

The exe, the launcher and game windows, the issue URL and the settings
file. ascension-r.ini starts as a copy of gowa.ini, which is left as it
is. The target and the internal gowa_ names stay, so the objects are not
rebuilt.

0d513a7c89f8cd48ceda897bdbe1ff75a0322bbc.message:
Lift the EDGE code pieces Tisiphone's brothel illusion streams

The room the player recorded fell to 3.5 frames a second: its EDGE jobs
fetch 20 code pieces the list did not have, and the SPU interpreter ran
them at 10-20 M steps a second. Found by replaying the player's recording
with SPU_INTERP_BYSIG and SPU_DMA_RANGE_UNIQ; listed and lifted, the room
runs at 25-27 flips/s in the same replay. The note has the measurements,
and the replay fix in the runtime is in the submodule.
