102b78860eedba5476f62faa5d7e9554f16644c9.message:
EDGE skinning in the vertex pass the SPU's way, bit for bit; the path on again

The game draws a skinned mesh twice, a depth pass and a lit pass that tests
EQUAL against it, and either job may be skinned in the vertex pass or on the
SPU. With the GPU's rounding the depths differed in the last bit and the lit
pass left holes (the trails in the prison of the damned), so the skinned path
had been turned off this morning.

The pass now works the rows and the position out with the SPU's fm and fma
done in 32-bit integer operations: mantissas multiplied exactly, a 64-bit
window with a sticky bit, the result cut toward zero, denormals as zero, a
zero +0. The same code in C (tests/native/skin_fma_test.c) matches the x86
FMA under the SPU's MXCSR over 160 million operations. In the shader as
loops: written out, FXC took ten minutes over it.

GOWA_EDGE_SKIN is on by default again. With FSR 3.1, frame generation and
VSync: the prison has no trails; the fight, ABBA, 29.52/29.92 flips/s on
against 27.36/27.91 off (~+7%, at the 30 cap). Fork 7099ab74 compiles the

136e736ba67960fff02b96b179bfae304dd2bda5.message:
VRAM: a trim of a texture with only its smaller mips cuts nothing (#7, #9)

The streaming pass trims its oldest texture's block, cutting the mips above
the kept ones off the block's front (func_0039EA58). It also takes a texture
loaded with only its smaller mips, whose block is smaller than that cut: the
block's size went negative and its offset past its data, the pass took it
again every frame, and the moves after it wrecked local memory. Found with
probes on a replay of #7's save at the Sparta cinematic's level, where it
broke once in three or four runs.

gowa_vram_cut makes such a cut what the block holds in front of the kept
mips, nothing, and moves the texture's LRU stamp on so the pass takes
another. Leaving such textures out of the pass instead stopped the break but
left the pass short of memory: one run fell to 2 flips a second.
GAME_MODULE_ABI 5.

158f4994e3b81c062bc8ee80c924e9b6a4ac4e9b.message:
EDGE lighting's outer loop (0x79B0) as native code

The loop around the two native light loops: per pass eight vertices
gathered by index, light 0 begun, 0x7BB4's loop over the lights, the
weights' reciprocal and the light position, the normalized direction
and N.L of light 0, 0x7ED8's loop, then three quadwords a vertex stored
in the lifted order (with the fourth words the SPU's transpose leaves).
Mapped by running the lifted statements symbolically. The routine takes
every pass but the last, which stays lifted, so registers end as the
lifted loop leaves them; only r103 and r114 change from pass to pass.
Each pass runs fast and is redone exact before its stores when MXCSR's
flags or an exponent 255 show.

The two light loops are split into finish and begin so the outer pass
does not begin a light past the last one.

GOWA_EDGE_VERIFY=1 checks the whole stage (0x73E0) on a copy with the
routine against the stage without it: identical in 278,529 calls in the
game and in the replay; strict replay 0 differences both ways. Replay,
the lit jobs: -11%. Gate, ABBA: 16.01 -> 16.80 flips/s (+4.9%).

2127cf135e84d8137ac326923202880f5b855d08.message:
EDGE jobs: the runtime's work measured, three cuts

What the runtime does inside an EDGE job, counted per job (the fork's
SPU_JOB_TIME in a --jobcap build) and sampled: about a third of a job,
spread over a dozen mechanisms of 1-2 us each, none large.

The fork's three cuts:
- the dispatch cache now survives the ~2 KB position-independent pieces
  each EDGE job loads (residency per 4 KB page): misses 21 -> 6 a job,
  checked in shadow mode over a level run (1.28 billion hits, no
  mismatch);
- the job manager's interrupt handler entry (0xA2C) takes the fast
  branch path: full-path branches 8.7 -> 6.7 a job;
- the event acknowledge no longer takes the lock-line lock: lock
  acquisitions 4.4 -> 2.45 a job, waits 0.70 -> 0.38.

Level, ABBA, default builds, MLAA on: 20.75 -> 20.98 flips/s, both new
runs above both old ones.

Performance plan 2.15: the breakdown, the per-job counts, and why the
rest of the runtime's share is not worth chasing for the frame rate.

2870e97007bd7ac3fe0c46add6dbe2c485776f86.message:
EDGE: the fixed-point vertex decoder (piece 0x75EB40) as native code

The decoder loop at piece offset 0x310 turns two attributes of a 24-byte
record of packed bit fields into floats, pipelined three deep: fetch the
next record, decode the one before, convert and store what was decoded
before that. native/spu_edge_decode.c runs the same stages in the same
order, with what is fixed for the call (gather controls, shift counts)
prepared once, exact for any format: csflt as cvtdq2ps and cuflt as an
unsigned conversion with the same rounding, under the SPU code's MXCSR
(checked at entry); fa native with the range check and the +0 rule. The
last iteration runs lifted. GOWA_EDGE_NATIVE bit 4.

gowa.py lift now puts native hooks into the position-independent pieces
too (pic_<EA> entries in spu_native_hooks.json).

tests/native/test_edge_native.py runs the lifted loop, taken from its
lifted source, against the native one on random registers and local
store, a third of the cases with the outputs over the input: 3000 cases
identical, seven mutants caught. Replay: 0 differ, the 40 EDGE jobs
2064 -> 2045 us. The loop alone: 28.9 -> 13.9 ns an iteration. Level,
ABBA, two runs each: 19.42 -> 20.09 flips/s.

The profile behind the choice, and what is next, are in the performance
plan, 2.11.

28f612cbc6e4b0cb61d579cc08b3e3104f7e35f1.message:
EDGE job: the output stage as native code (off by default)

0x9080, the most valuable common block of the job's glue, behind GOWA_EDGE_OUT=1.
- It does the size, the index and vertex PUTs (0xAF38's pieces, with the lifted code's
  MachStat reads and interrupt toggles), the vertex packing through the piece at c+0x8C, the
  hole's set-up, and per pass the viewport, scissor, 0x1EFC block and draw commands, word by
  word at the same addresses.
- It calls, as the lifted code does: the ring allocation (0xC628), the method piece (0x5D68),
  the program binding (0x84C0) when there is one, and the hole's end (0xCC98).
- Its arithmetic is the lifted code's, op for op, on locals; it drops the register file, the
  per-label interrupt checks and the dispatcher round trips.

Checked:
- Replay state mode over the 120 gate and 160 consecutive jobs: 0 differences.
- In the game: 2.69M calls, none declined; 180 jobs captured with it on, replayed with the
  lifted code: 0 differences.
- Gate ABBA: 18.19 -> 18.70 flips/s.

GowARecomp.exe --precompile-shaders (precompile.cpp) reads the WAD and AS
files of the game's PSARC archives (zlib 1.3.1's inflate, third_party/zlib),
finds the vertex programs by the engine's header in front of each, and has
the runtime compile them into the shader cache (ps3recomp 206e06e). The
launcher's sidebar runs it after a Yes, shows its progress, and keeps Play
and Clear shaders waiting meanwhile.

3,455 programs, 88 s here (161 s with the archives read cold from the hard
disk), 3.1 MB more cache; a session of the first level then compiled 4
vertex shaders where it had compiled 212. Fragment programs are left out:
their text depends on the textures and state of their draws. The spike and
the numbers are in docs/notes/2026-11-08-shader-precompile-review.md.

RPCS3 against the port at the job level: the SPURS contention is lost

scripts/guestscope.py reads the title's SPURS instance and its Wws ticket
rows from outside a process, RPCS3 or the port alike, and reports SPUs per
workload, jobs per list and EDGE jobs per contention level.

Both run the same jobs a frame. RPCS3's EDGE phase is 27.6 ms of its frame,
the port's 52.8: about the whole difference. The causes, measured:
- the title's maximum contention (5-8 SPUs a workload) is the ninth argument
  of _cellSpursWorkloadAttributeInitialize, on the stack; the HLE writes 1;
- the port's kernel picks round robin, takes one from the ready count at each
  pick and never makes a polling policy module yield; RPCS3's keeps EDGE
  (priority 3) on four SPUs 86% of its time;
- an EDGE job takes ~1.4 times as long at any contention, a Batch job ~8.

With only the maxima raised, General6 and RenderJobs run on 4 SPUs
(39.6 -> 11.1 and 26.4 -> 7.7 ms a frame) but starve EDGE, and the frame
rate stays. The note gives the order of work; the plan gets section 2.10
and two 2026-10-28 conclusions are marked overturned.

Guard the game's VRAM manager against negative block sizes

Issue #9: at the Delphi temple, on one PC and in every session, a block
of the game's VRAM pool got a negative size. The pool's allocator
(func_0039E3F8) then moves its top up instead of down, and the
defragmenter moves the block 16 MB at a time, over the textures after it
and, past local memory, over main memory. The game's own checks stop on a
trap there, which the lift leaves out.

Three hooks (port/vram_guard.cpp, scripts/ppu_hooks.json): a texture
whose size is negative or past 256 MB is logged with its first 0x50 bytes
and given an empty block, such an allocation from any caller is made 0,
and a MoveLocalMemory past local memory is made a move of nothing. A
replay of the temple with one allocation made negative on purpose printed
one line and nothing else. What gives a block such a size is not known
yet: the next report from that PC will say.

GAME_MODULE_ABI 3. tests/test_game_module_hooks.py checks that every hook
is in GAME_MODULE_FUNCS, which the Kit's DLL needs to link.

attribute 1's x y z, 12 bytes a vertex. Two vertices go in each pass's three stores, which
leave one quadword past the end: 8 zero bytes, then the output's last 8. The rule came from

store in 12 of 12 calls.

564751bee846a79aba720809bbc4a02d804ad85e.message:
Rendering accuracy: what is wrong, why, and the plan

Measured against RPCS3 (a screenshot of the main menu, and its settings
for this title read, not changed: Write Color Buffers on, Disable MLAA
and Disable Mesh Trimming on), with whole-frame captures and one switch
per run:

- The main menu's flicker is the title's MLAA path: its SPUs smooth a
  copy of the frame that is stale here, and draws read that copy when
  no GPU snapshot of it is found. MLAA off: the change from frame to
  frame drops from 6.5 to 1.4 and grows with the lag, as a slow scene's
  does. Depth of field, the texture cache, render target feedback: no
  effect.
- The opening cinematic's blocks are of two kinds: stale rectangles
  with MLAA on (the same copy, read with no or a mismatched snapshot),
  and a band across a frieze with MLAA on or off that starts in the
  screen-space shadow mask, made within the frame by 358 passes with
  depth bounds and stencil tests.
- Some textures decode wrongly (rainbow stripes, a blue patch), with
  MLAA off and the texture cache off; the suspects are the component
  remaps and the swizzled float formats the cinematic samples.
- The picture is ~19% darker than RPCS3's, shadows -36%, highlights -6%.
  Not a setting (the system save is RPCS3's), not the sRGB pairing (every
  target written with the encode is read with the decode). The suspect
  is the exposure: the luminance chain ends in a 1x1 target no draw
  reads, which our backend never writes back to guest memory.

docs/notes/2026-11-01-rendering-accuracy.md: the evidence, how RPCS3
does surfaces and write-back (as a map), and the plan P1-P7.
scripts/rsxcap_check.py: pictures, flicker, sRGB pairing and texture
formats from captures, to measure each step the same way.

5b170052182bf91bd9f7d81cc5652cd07eebaf86.message:
EDGE: e77C8's jobs start with no memo state (the Grotto freeze)

The EDGE native code keeps a job's state per thread, the memo of kept
results. e6D98's entry empties it and the hooks in e6D98's functions
fill it, while the hooks on the position-independent pieces read it,
and both EDGE modules call those pieces. Nothing emptied it for the
other build, jobmod_9b03908f93a9_e77C8, which the Grotto runs: a job of
it started with what the last e6D98 job on its thread had left. With a
kept result's state, the vertex piece's hook gave that result up and ran
the calls it had left out, e6D98's functions by name, on this job's
local store, leaving r0 as the last of them had it; the piece returned
there, into an epilogue that took r81-r83 from the piece's frame. That
is issue #7's register dump: the object pointer in r81 was the piece's
pattern, and the job branched to nowhere.

e77C8's entry (0xB7C8) now empties the state as e6D98's does, and
edge_memo_revoke never runs e6D98's calls in a job of another module.
On the reporter's save and replayed session: before, 12,652 of 1.57 M
calls into the memo from those hooks found another job's state, and that
run froze; after, 0 of 3.1 M, and no freeze in three runs. The Megaera
fight: the memo's hits as before.

Rendering note: the menu's flicker is the occlusion queries, not MLAA

frames that happened to have no flicker in them. Counted instead in
screenshots once a second, VSync on (as the launcher runs it), frames
with objects missing and black in their place:

  MLAA off                                  10 of 30

6bfc470ea60349a452b12241e4781c8822b52f5b.message:
EDGE: keep job results across frames

With culling on the RSX an unskinned job's indexes and vertexes depend only
on its inputs, and 95% of such jobs repeat one already done: the same
meshes every frame, in the depth pass and the lit pass. The end of 0x9990
hashes those inputs; a job seen twice keeps its index list and packed
records, and a later one leaves out the decoding, the transforms, the index
decompression and the packing. The glue around them runs as before. A lit
job whose stage runs on the SPU after all gets its arrays made late.
GOWA_EDGE_MEMO=0 turns it off, =2 checks every hit against the stages.

Check in the game: 4.5 M hits at the gate and in the fight, no list and no
vertex different. Replay of ten corpora: 0 differences, with results on too.
Gate, three runs a side: 23.63 -> 24.61 flips/s. With A and B, 22.89 ->
24.40, and the warm fight 21.17 -> 21.56.

72ef5c370afa0788f9510726b4e30818ec187189.message:
EDGE: the normal loop as native AVX2 code; both EDGE loops 16.04 -> 16.26

native/spu_edge_normals.c runs the loop at LS 0xA950: eight elements an
iteration, each a cross product scaled by w, its squared length through
frsqest, fi and a Newton step, normalised above 1e-30. The vector part
puts two elements in a 256-bit register; the length and what follows is
one value an element, so the eight elements' values share one register and
frsqest/fi/Newton run once for all eight. Float ops are native with the
range check and +0 rule on every op, a half out of range done again by the
exact forms; the last iteration runs lifted.

GOWA_EDGE_NATIVE is now a mask: 1 skinning, 2 normals; unset both, 0 off.

Replay: 54.1 -> 52.0 us an EDGE job on top of the skinning loop, outputs
identical. Level: no op needed the exact forms; ABBA two runs each, both
loops on against off, 16.04 -> 16.26 flips/s.

7e3c5e2f8f3623ac7d5c258abc39fb652559c0c0.message:
Notes: EDGE job inputs, slot by slot

Mapped from the 120 gate jobs and 160 consecutive jobs, with a replay that logged every
local-store load and store of the job module and the pieces by function.
- How inputs arrive: two buffer sets, the next job's set fetched while a job runs. The job
  module keeps the previous job's set at 0x10918; laid out from that, all 120 gate jobs'
  pieces match the executable.
- The DMA list has 22 fixed slots (light set, three pieces, index and vertex streams, skinning
  palette and weights, segment header, formats, view block, matrix), each with its readers.
- The descriptor's words: ring base, hole EA, matrix count, frame counter, attribute slot
  list, fragment program and constants block EAs and sizes, screen size.
- The light set's header and arrays, and which lights each lighting routine takes.
- The vertex formats: the output types are the RSX's, the input adds fixed point and 3-byte
  unit vectors. The slot list picks the emitted attributes; that gives the hole's vertex
  arrays in 278 of 280 jobs.
- The segment header slot vs. the context copy: the job fills in the hole size, the format
  numbers and the vertex count rounded up to 8.

This replaces the earlier element table, which was read by position and with the capture
header taken as 48 bytes (it is 56).

EDGE fills of skinned meshes: the SPU's rounding

ek_fill works a skinned block's vertexes out on the backend's thread, for a
draw that does not take the resident part, and did it under the host's
rounding. The game's lit pass tests EQUAL against its depth pass, and the
two may come one from a fill and one from the vertex pass or the SPU, which
work the position out the SPU's way: the last bit differed and the lit pass
left speckled holes all over the mesh. It now sets the SPU's MXCSR for the
call, as er_fill does for unskinned blocks.

Found with VTX_RESIDENT_MB=8 on the Grotto replay (3,527 restarts: Kratos
speckled); the same run after it, 3,462 restarts, shows him as usual. The
note also has what issue #9's reports show of the Delphi temple's broken

a97617bd6eef7845d393ee3e7f0f6541e389e68e.message:
EDGE lighting loops: a fast pass with one range test a call

The two lighting loops (0x7BB4, 0x7ED8) tested every op's result for the
native range (and, compare, movemask, branch, then +0), which made the
native loops barely faster than the lifted ones. Now a call runs fast
first with no test per op: under round-toward-zero an exact result beyond
FLT_MAX sets MXCSR's overflow flag, and operands with the SPU's exponent
255 are looked for in what the ops read (the constants and carried values
once, the loaded quadwords each iteration). Either one redoes the call
with the exact forms from the same start; the stores of the fast pass go
only to output arrays apart from everything read. A zero's sign never
changes a non-zero result of these ops, so +0 is applied where values
leave (stores, registers).

GOWA_EDGE_EXACT=1 forces the redo (to test the exact pass). Strict replay
0 differ both ways. Replay, the lit jobs: 100.3 -> 88.0 us (-12%).

aa60d2e2d2c0c5c7a190030a4b1290cef3ad6bd6.message:
EDGE's vertex unpacking (piece 0x75BD10) as native code

The lit jobs' vertex stream is 18-byte records: x y z, then a 48-bit code. The code holds two
unit vectors (attributes 3 and 4), each as two 10-bit components and a 4-bit pattern index.
The third component is a square root by frsqest and fi. The pattern, one of 12 the piece
writes to its frame, gives that component's place and sign and a handedness w. An index
past 11 reads the caller's stack; those pairs are done with the piece's own operations.

The format was mapped with a bit-exact model of the probed calls. The routine also leaves what
the piece leaves: the list and table entries, the frame's patterns, two zero quadwords past
two arrays, r1 and r3.

Checked identical in 188,416 calls in the game and by strict replay. The lit jobs: -6% in
replay. Gate, ABBA: 17.95 -> 17.91 flips/s, within the spread.

(e8f44fbc6dbf): matrix-palette skinning, two vertices an iteration, now in
one 256-bit register so each blend or transform is one op for both. The
float ops are native under the SPU code's MXCSR with the +0 rule, checked
once an iteration before anything is stored; an iteration out of the single
range, and the last one, run in the lifted loop from the registers as it
has them, so the job's registers come out exact. It runs only when the
loop's invariant registers (masks, 1.0, 1/255) are the ones it was written
for.

  hole's NOP data, which are stale local store.

- What the strict replay compares.

d720ed90130e132ffa89afaba2c633dd5481d0f6.message:
EDGE: skinned jobs from kept inputs, skinning in the vertex pass (GOWA_EDGE_SKIN)

A skinned job's vertexes, weights and indexes are the same every frame; only the
palette changes. So its key leaves the palette and the matrix out, and a hit skips
the decoding, 0xE550 and the packing: the job hands the palette to the vertex pass
with its record, and the pass works out position, normal and tangent before it
lights them. A position job gets a record too.

Revoking a hit puts the kept arrays back and runs 0xE550 after all. A job that
goes on to 0xF538 stays on the SPU: no skinned job at the gate or in the fight does.

GOWA_EDGE_SKIN=2 compares every job with spu_edge_gpuskin.c's CPU version. In the
fight, 565 million vertexes: positions bit for bit, tangents at most a unit off,
98.4% of the normals within 2 units of 32767.

Two runs a side, one executable name: gate 28.84 -> 29.98 flips/s, at the game's 30
in half of its windows; warm fight 26.16 -> 27.39. Job outputs identical on the
replay lists, where it is off. The gate's picture right with every draw on the
CPU fallback and with 925 refills of the resident part.

e7312e3b7ac6b13b11b598da328c11e14ce7499d.message:
Re-kick a stranded EDGE job list: the menu-start freeze

About one run in fifteen froze right after the opening movie, the RSX
standing at the first hole of one EDGE job list for good. The main thread
kicks an EDGE list when the MeshProc batch counter (0xA0B724) reaches 0,
and re-arms that counter for the next frame's list right after. When the
re-arm came before the kicked list's policy module had read its first
wait, the module saw the new count and went idle; the next zero kicked
the next list, and nothing kicked the first again.

wws_rekick, the park stall hook (GCM_PARK_STALL_MS=100 by default),
signals an EDGE list whose next entry is a wait already met, on a
workload nothing runs or has asked for. Interleaved A/B on one binary:
2 of 22 runs froze without it, none of 22 with it. The level's speed is
unchanged (19.65 -> 20.27 flips/s, two runs each, within the spread).

The park dump now covers every workload, marks a list a main-thread wait
would still wait for, and shows the job descriptors, the batch counters,
the MLAA block and barriers, and the guest threads. SPU_SIG_RING_DUMP_S
prints it at a set time, for a stall without a park.

fix, none in the 74 after) is open; the note has what is known.

- native/spu_edge_skinmat.c (GOWA_EDGE_NATIVE bit 1048576, on by default):

  jobs' normal and tangent transform 0xF104. 0xF104 keeps its pipeline in

  pipeline in arrays saved nothing.

  path's scratch registers, so the natives work out the passes left and
  leave the last pass that copies, and those after it, to the lifted loop.
- A GOWA_EDGE_VERIFY hook at each function's entry checks every call, all
  registers and the whole local store: 378 calls of 0xE550 and 1719 of
  0x88B0 in replay, 90,114 and 413,696 in the game, 0 differences; 1720
  replayed jobs, 0 differences.

f9259bac0437b9b8879b3fb9aeb1fb21bbb2b7f1.message:
EDGE natives: order the MXCSR flag reads against the fast ops

The compiler takes the float ops for pure and moved some of them across a
plain _mm_getcsr: in the game the vertex pass (0xD250) stored FLT_MAX
where the SPU saturates to 0x7FFFFFFF in 6923 calls, its overflow flag
read before the op ran. The flags now go through volatile asm (ldmxcsr,
stmxcsr with a memory clobber), ordered by the values they carry: the
pass's register inputs come out of an empty asm after the clear, its
results go into one before the read.

The transform and the vertex pass read the flags once a call when their
output is apart from their input, and redo the whole call exact when they
show; in place, once a pass as before.

GOWA_EDGE_VERIFY=1 also checks each fast call of the two lighting loops
against the exact pass from the same start.

Checked in the game: the transform 1.13M calls, culling 414K, point lights
352K, the lighting loops' self-check, all identical; strict replay 0
differences both ways. Gate, ABBA: 15.34 -> 15.94 flips/s (+3.9%) over
main.

fef5ac98bd8fcf77b8dccb95efebd527f3ba0a55.message:
EDGE's index decompression (0xE4D0 -> 0xDCC0) as native code

Every EDGE job decompresses its triangle indices in place. The format, mapped stage by stage
from snapshots at each loop head and checked with a model of the whole local store:
- an 8-byte header (reuse count, delta bias, bitmask bytes, bits a reuse);
- a bitmask, 2-bit triangle codes, then k-bit reuse values.

The stages:
- the reuses are eight interleaved running sums of the k-bit deltas;
- the bitmask picks a reuse or the next new vertex for each slot of the vertex sequence;
- each triangle code is a fresh triangle of three sequence values, or a turn on one edge of
  the triangle before, reversed, with the next value.

The scratch past the indices goes out by DMA, so the routine makes it byte for byte, along
with c + 0x50/0x58, the frame and r3.

Bit reader, a pshufb expand a mask byte at a time, and one pshufb a triangle:
9,154 -> 4,737 cycles a call. Checked identical in 561,152 calls in the game and by strict
replay. Gate, ABBA: 18.14 -> 18.71 flips/s.

1457406567.readme_excerpt: # Ascension-R: a God of War: Ascension PC port [![CI](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) ![Platform: Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20x64-lightgrey.svg) ![Status: alpha](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-alpha-orange.svg) An unofficial, native PC port of **God of War: Ascension** (PS3) for Windows, made by static recompilation with [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp). The game's PPU and SPU code is translated to x86-64 ahead of time and the RSX is drawn with Direct3D 12, so no emulator runs while you play. Website: [rigaz29.github.io/Ascension-R](https://rigaz29.github.io/Ascension-R/) > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository holds no game files. You build the port from your own copy of the game. See [Legal](#legal). ## Contents - [Status](#status) - [Features](#features) - [Download](#download) - [What you need](#what-you-need) - [Building from source](#building-from-source) - [Playing](#playing) - [Reporting a problem](#reporting-a-problem) - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Project layout](#project-layout) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Legal](#legal) - [Credits](#credits) - [License](#license) ## Status It boots, plays the cinematics and goes through the menus into the levels. It has not been played from start to finish, so expect problems further in. - **Game:** God of War: Ascension, digital US release, NPUA80918, version 1.12: the game and its updates 1.04 to 1.12. - **Platform:** Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. Tested on Windows 11. - **Speed:** above 30 frames a second in the two scenes measured, a fight of the first level and the gate, on a Ryzen 5 4600H with a GTX 1650 Ti and the Smooth preset. - **Online:** not supported. The port is single player. - **Downloads:** the Kit, on the [releases page](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/releases). It holds none of the game's code and builds it on your PC from your copy. ## Features - **Launcher:** a ready check, three presets (Smooth, Balanced, Faithful) and every setting below. It finds the game's folder by itself, and says when a newer release is out, with a link to it. - **Picture:** internal resolution from 1x to 4x or native, AMD FSR 1 and FSR 3.1 scaling, FSR 3.1 frame generation, SMAA 1x and anisotropic filtering. - **Display:** windowed or borderless, ultrawide, VSync, a frame rate cap, and frame rate and load on screen. - **Shaders:** a compressed cache, pipelines built before the title, and every vertex shader built before the first start of each version, on an 8-bit screen with music of its own. - **Game patches:** switch off MLAA, depth of field, motion blur, mesh trimming or dynamic shadows. - **Cheats:** damage to and from Kratos, max red orbs, infinite magic and items, infinite rage and double jumps. - **Controls:** a controller or keyboard and mouse. Xbox and other XInput pads, and through SDL3 the DualShock 4, the DualSense, Switch controllers and many others; stick dead zone, confirm button, vibration and controller API settings. - **Saves:** backups kept before the game writes over a save. - **Problem reports:** one button makes a zip of the logs, with your paths hidden. [docs/FEATURES.md](docs/FEATURES.md) describes each one and its setting. ## Download The [releases page](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/releases) has the Kit: a zip of the program without the game's code. Its launcher finds your copy of the game, decrypts it with RPCS3 and builds the game's code on your PC, once, in about ten minutes. There is nothing else to install: the Kit brings its own Python and LLVM. Each release's notes have the steps. Your copy needs all nine of the game's updates, 1.04 to 1.12, installed in RPCS3 in that order. Each brings its own files: 1.12's is the EBOOT alone, and the archives come with the ones before it. With 1.12 alone the game stops on its first loading screen. ## What you need To build it from source: - Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. - A CPU with AVX2 and FMA, and a GPU with Direct3D 12. - The game, installed in RPCS3 with its license, and its updates 1.04 to 1.12, installed in that order. - Python 3.10 or later, Git, CMake, Ninja, Visual Studio with "C++ Clang Compiler for Windows", a Windows SDK, and about 20 GB free. - For the game's movies: an LGPL shared build of FFmpeg with its headers, unpacked under `..\ffmpeg`, for example `win64-lgpl-shared` from [BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds](https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/releases). - Optional, for AMD FSR 3.1: [FSR SDK 2.4.0](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK), unpacked under `..\fsr-sdk`. ## Building from source ``` git clone --recursive https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R cd Ascension-R python -m venv ..\.venv ..\.venv\Scripts\pip install -r ps3recomp\requirements.txt # 1. Decrypt USRDIR\GOWA.SELF to GOWA.elf with RPCS3 (Utilities > Decrypt PS3 Binaries). # 2. Point the project at the installed game. It is only read. ..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py setup --game-dir \dev_hdd0\game\NPUA80918 ..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py doctor ..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py analyze ..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py lift ..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py build ..\.venv\Scripts\python scripts\gowa.py run ``` `doctor` lists anything that is missing. The lift and the first build take about 13 minutes on a Ryzen 5 4600H. `run` starts the game straight away, with its log in `logs\`. ## Playing Open `build\Ascension-R.exe`. The launcher checks the game's folder and your setup, and **Play** starts the game. The first start of each version builds the game's vertex shaders before the game begins, on a screen of its own: a minute or two the first time, seconds after an update. Fragment shaders are built the first time they are needed, so expect some stutter at first. **Clear shaders**, in the launcher's sidebar, makes the next start build them again. A build from source keeps its settings, logs and shader caches in `build\`, and its saves in `gamedata\`. ## Reporting a problem **Report a problem**, in the launcher's sidebar, makes a zip in `logs\` beside the settings file, for you to attach to an [issue](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/issues/new?template=problem.yml). The launcher offers it by itself after a session that crashed, lost the graphics device, froze or stopped with no reason in its log. `Ascension-R --report [--with-saves]` makes one without the window. The zip holds the logs and pad recordings of the last three sessions the game ran in, your settings, the build, your hardware and driver versions, and Windows' records of crashes and hangs of this exe in the last two weeks. Folder paths and your Windows account and PC names are hidden. The game sends nothing by itself and no game file goes in. Saves go in only if you tick the box, without the game's images and sounds. If no new frame comes for 15 seconds, the log gets what each thread was doing, and again at 60 (`GOWA_FREEZE_WATCH=`, `0` = off). ## How it works 1. `gowa.py lift` translates the PPU code of `GOWA.elf` to C++, and `build` does the same to C for the SPU programs and job modules. Both are compiled for x86-64 with clang-cl. 2. The [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) runtime stands in for the PS3: its system calls and libraries, SPURS, the file system, audio, pads and save data. 3. The game's RSX commands are drawn with Direct3D 12. Its shaders are translated to HLSL and compiled with DXC. 4. Movies are decoded with FFmpeg. 5. SPU code that was not translated ahead of time runs in an interpreter. The session records it, and the next `lift` adds it. More detail: [what the game is made of](docs/ANALYSIS.md), [what has been measured](docs/PERF.md), and the [development notes](docs/notes), one per session. ## Project layout ``` port/ the port: entry point, launcher, game-specific code native/ hand-written routines for the SPU code that costs the most scripts/ gowa.py, the pipeline (doctor, setup, analyze, lift, build, run, symbolize), and the bench tools/ which of the game's imports the runtime answers, shader cache checks, RenderDoc helpers tests/ tests for the launcher's game search, shader compile guards and native routines docs/ analysis, measurements, features and development notes packaging/ text files that go beside the program in a package site/ the website, rigaz29.github.io/Ascension-R, published by .github/workflows/pages.yml third_party/ zlib ps3recomp/ the toolkit and runtime, as a submodule (fork rigaz29/ps3recomp, branch gowa) ``` ## Contributing Anyone can help: by playing and reporting, or with changes to the port or to the runtime under it. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) says where help is most useful, where a change goes, and what must never be committed. ## FAQ ### Is there an official PC version of God of War: Ascension? No. It came out on PlayStation 3 only. Ascension-R is an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony. ### How is this different from playing on RPCS3? RPCS3 emulates the PS3 and runs the game's code as it goes. Ascension-R translates that code to native x86-64 code ahead of time, on your PC, and draws with Direct3D 12, so no emulator runs while you play. RPCS3 is used only to decrypt your copy. ### Do I need to own the game? Yes. The download holds no code or assets of the game: its launcher builds the game's code from your own copy, with its license. ### Which copies of the game work? Only the digital US release NPUA80918 at version 1.12, with every update from 1.04 installed. European and disc releases are not supported yet ([#4](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/issues/4)). ### Does it run on Linux or the Steam Deck? One player plays it on Linux through Proton, in a Wine prefix made by Lutris ([#12](https://github.com/rigaz29/Ascension-R/issues/12)). The Steam Deck has not been tried. ### Is it safe to run? The code is open source and built in the open. Each release lists the SHA-256 of its download and what the package was checked for, and the game's code is built on your own PC. The program is not signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn the first time. ## Legal No game files are in this repository, and none will be. You need your own copy of the game and its license, and you decrypt it yourself. What you build from your copy contains code translated from the game. Keep it on your machine: do not commit it or share it. God of War is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by it. ## Credits Built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) by sp00nznet. The other code and libraries the port uses, among them FFmpeg, AMD FSR, SMAA, zlib and Zstandard, are listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). ## License The code in this repository is under the MIT License, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). It does not cover the game or anything made from it.

# KILLZONE MERCENARIES 2

## Branching to chronology

 - Easy to imagine some Helghast cruiser captain and his crew at the end of killzone 3, when Stahl shows his technologic adances like energy shielding and warp drive engine, sending these to attack Earth, understands their own futur might be on the edge.  
 - They might've secretly boarded their families and hijacked the destination, for exemple the furthest colony they heard about...  
 - Not ISA of course, Earth is huge they should be colons from a non ISA origin and their planet/star should have affected they evolution just like Helghan.  

## Character

I know it'd be weird but how about character customization like Vectan/Hybrid/Helghan.
Each with base particularity...
  
And your squad are specialists you recruit by doing something like missions, accessible by what origins you choose, ...
Each specialist has their skill tree.
  
Your alignment defines how the main player skill tree can evolve.
The Best weapons you can acquire also depends on your aliance.

## Generally

I like to see it as an **open-world, strategic, procedural, multi branch story, RPG**.  
The battelfield should be total chaos and feel like the war is all around with ever changing events...
 - sometimes troupers around one or two scorpion tanks...
 - sometimes ISA mechs battle Atac drones etc...
 - basically a feeling of overwhelming chaos

Try playing a coop conquest game of battelfield 2042 on ***orbital*** for a small exemple.

## Factions

The planet has 3 factions from the start:
 - New faction original from there
 - Helghast
 - ISA

So your cruiser crash lands on the colony, it makes your starting point, you base and the first "safe zone" on the map.  
First quests would be to secure, resupply your people and make contact with other present groups and get your first contracts.

As player choosing it's alignment, other factions should unveil for exemple:

### if your alignment is Halghast:

> VSA update with new VSA gears join and replace ISA

### ISA:

> Black Hand

### New faction

> Maybe increased threat from ISA/Helghasts

## alignment

You can accept attack missions from different contracts vendors in safe zones:
 - Capture some scientist or specialist will grant you rewards like:
   - Credits, if you bring the person to the faction camp, and a lot of alignment exp.
   - A new HUD/MENU fonctionnality OR in some case a new ally in your base you can take in your active squad, then less faction exp.
 - Attack enemy convoy
 - etc...

As you progress faction Exp milestones, you get more allied with that particular faction and main story unfolds as it closes for others.  
As each faction's goal is different the main story should be different too... That makes new game+ very attractive.  
Recruiting scientists should have an effect on menu/HUD by the tech they'll add.  
> Exemple, you get a contract to capture a helghast scientist, you recruit him, he adds a layer on your world map displaying in the "helghast orange/brownish" the "battle weather", icons like:
 - artillery strikes
 - huge armor column
 - snipers

## Map mechanics

The **map**  has basically 3 types of areas (some exist/accessible only ):
 - safe zones: a small percentage of the map
 - light intensity battlefield (most quests): a bigger part
 - high intesity/full chaos: about half size of the map

> Some place should be contextual to player alignment, for exemple:
> - Stahl arms factory
> - etc...

Map should be changing in the high intesity areas.
> for exemple: after a artillery on a zone there should be craters to hide in...  

Big cataclysmic events should happen like earthquakes, tornados, ice fall, thick fog.  
They should defines the strategy to adapt.  
Should you take on of your base's armored vehicle, a sniper in your team, shock troopers...  
That should be thought according to mission and **map battlefield weather**.

## Epic secondary/hidden bosses/objectives

Yes there should be **elite** activities on the high intesity map for highest level players.  
  
Also events are constantly happening, patrols attacking positions, fights, it's never quite.  
  
The teammates you recruit are just recruits at first, but they will tell you something they do care about, their NPC side quests.  
Doing these services will unlock more potential from them.  
  
Everything should have an experience gauge even weapons lvls will let you improve handling/precision/reloading then at milestones you can buy new sights/magazines/handles/...

## Exemple

> you picked a **hybrid** as your character, your alignement is **New faction**, your mission attack an **ISA base**.  

1. You take a helghast sniper/recon specialistand an engineer.  
2. Position your sniper/recon on a high place so your helghast helmet displays AR intels (the focal point aligns perfectly the display while it is a bit out of step on the sides).  
3. You approach the base which has **new faction** construction vehicles, your engineer hacks these causing a chaos. The sinper shoots their comms operator, causing the start of the battle...  
4. While you fight and reposition to keep the tactical advantage a helghast ATAC suddenly attacks the ISA base followed by helghast soldiers and a scorpion tank.  
5. OOPS! a **tornado** appears washing away the ATAC and now everyone tries to take cover...

# HOW ABOUT IT?

990607077.readme_excerpt:
# 🎮 Achievements Achievement notifications, an in-game overlay and playtime tracking for Windows, across supported launchers, emulators and native ports.

Windows · Download the latest release · Quick start · Supported platforms

Highlights · Install & Quick Start · Supported Platforms · Usage & Configuration · Troubleshooting · Development · Support & Credits

## Highlights - **One game library:** Dashboard search, platform filters, progress and custom collections. - **Achievement tracking:** live unlocks from compatible launchers, local saves, emulators and native ports. - **Your notification style:** animated presets, Native Windows notifications and optional Xbox Game Bar delivery. - **In-game overlay:** browse achievements and rarity with keyboard or controller navigation. - **Playtime tracking:** start/stop notifications and saved totals for each config. - **Screenshots & video clips:** capture unlocks on your selected monitor, with supported HDR handling. - **Customization:** themes, Achievements/SAN presets, sounds, positions, scale and timing. - **Backup & restore:** move configs, collections, preferences, artwork and progress to another profile or PC.
Full feature list and supported sources A desktop application built with Electron that monitors running games and displays achievement notifications for: - ✅ Achievement unlocks - ⏱️ Playtime tracking (Now Playing / You Played X minutes) - 📈 Progress updates - 🖼️ Game image overlays - 📊 Real-time achievement dashboard - Steam/Uplay/GOG/Epic emulators, Xbox PC, RetroAchievements, XLiveLessNess, MarkerPatch, MadnessPatch, FINAL FANTASY VII `achievement.dat` and official launcher schema support (auto-detected where possible) - PS4 Recomp trophy tracking for compatible Bloodborne, Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection, God of War III Remastered, MediEvil and CTR Nitro-Fueled ports ([setup and requirements](#ps4-recomp-support)) **Platform:** Windows (uses Task Scheduler + Windows paths). - **Achievement Tracking** - Detects running games using their process names - Sends notifications with custom HTML/CSS animation - Real-time progress monitoring and updates - Supports progress stats from Online-Fix `Stats.ini` and Tenoke `user_stats.ini` - Screenshots achievements when unlocked (optional) - Choose the monitor for animated notifications, screenshots and recordings in **Settings → Notifications → Notification Toggles**. If disconnected, the first available monitor is used until the selected monitor reconnects. - Records optional achievement clips with selectable 10–30 second duration, 30/60 FPS, and system audio - Optional GPU HDR-to-SDR conversion keeps recorded H.264/MP4 clips compatible with standard SDR players - **Smart Dashboard** - Grid view of all configured games - Real-time progress tracking per game - Multiple sorting options: - Alphabetical (A-Z / Z-A) - Progress (Low-High / High-Low) - Last Updated (Recent-Old / Old-Recent) - Quick game search and filtering - Platform filtering and multi-select actions for ignore/delete - Custom game collections shown as Dashboard cards, with Configs, Collections, or combined views; open a collection to view its games, add members with multi-select, and choose a color, icon, or custom image - Click-to-load configs - Play game launch button (requires executable and optional arguments) - Automatically refreshes when config or save files change - **Notification System** - Multiple notification types: - Achievement unlocks - Progress updates - Playtime tracking (Now Playing / Session Ended) - Animated presets, a native Windows preset, and native Xbox Game Bar notifications through the optional Game Bar Widget [Achievements Overlay by JokerVerse] - Game Bar delivery supports achievement unlock, rarity/platinum metadata, click navigation, and textual progress (`current / maximum • percentage`) - The Game Bar companion is optional; when it is not installed or connected, the Electron application remains independent and uses the configured fallback - Optional Trophy Mode classifies unlocks as Gold below 20% rarity, Silver from 20% to below 50%, and Bronze from 50% upward; completing every achievement keeps the dedicated Platinum notification profile - RPCS3, ShadPS4, KytyPS5 and PS4 Recomp notifications keep their platform preset, sound, position and timing regardless of Trophy Mode, retaining native trophy grades alongside available rarity percentages. Platinum keeps its dedicated notification profile. Xenia and other platforms follow the Trophy Mode preference. Emulator notification tests use demonstration percentages. - Trophy Mode shows the tier color around achievement icons in notifications, the main achievement table, and the overlay; Bronze/Silver/Gold notifications use the Rare profile - Customizable sounds and visual presets - Adjustable position, duration, and scaling (presets support up to 200%) - Non-intrusive overlay system - Optional click navigation to the matching achievement in the overlay or main application - Playtime header artwork cached locally for faster repeat notifications - Per-game progress mute (when a config is active) - **Playtime Tracker** - Detects when configured games start and stop via process monitoring - Stores total Playtime per config inside `%APPDATA%/Achievements/playtime-totals.json` - Shows Playtime totals in the Achievements panel - Triggers dedicated notifications rendered by `playtime.html` - **Customization** - Modern settings UI with tabs - Built-in GitHub release changelogs with cached offline fallback - Live application log viewer with source and severity filtering - Multiple visual themes/presets - Startup options (maximized/minimized) - UI scaling (75% to 200%) - Achievement duration slider (auto or custom) - Achievement sound volume (0% to 200%) - Show hidden descriptions (when available) - Close-to-tray option - Select which achievement schema languages are generated when the source supports localization - Optional controller support for the overlay (`Settings -> Advanced -> Rendering`) - Multi-language support for achievements - **Profile Backup & Restore** - Export the complete portable profile from **Settings -> Backup & Restore** - Stream backups through a TAR container compressed with Zstandard, without loading the full profile into memory - Restore configs, custom collections and their images, achievement cache, covers, images, presets, sounds, themes, playtime, preferences, account import metadata, and dashboard summary in one operation - Preview backup version and contents before replacing the current profile - Apply restore before watchers start, suppressing achievement notifications during migration - Rebase internal profile paths and refresh dashboard fingerprints when moving the profile to another Windows account or PC - Authentication token files are intentionally excluded; connected services can require sign-in again - Backup archives are not encrypted and may contain sensitive settings such as the Steam Web API key
## Install & Quick Start 1. Download the Windows installer from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/PSerban93/Achievements/releases/latest) and install Achievements. 2. Open the application, then follow the first-run steps below. Node.js and Git are only needed when [running from source](#development). ### Quick Start (Tutorial) 1. Open **Settings** and set Preset, and Scale. 2. Add your [**Watched Folders**](#auto-configuration) (recommended) so the app can detect saves/emulators. 3. Start a game once so its save folder appears; the watcher will auto-create a config when possible. 4. Let the game identify and auto-select the config, or Select the config manually, set your Language to view achievements, progress, and playtime. 5. Optional: mute progress notifications for that config using the checkbox under the config dropdown.
First-run folder selection and startup options - On first run (or after onboarding version changes), choose **Restore from Backup** or **Set Up as New Device** in the welcome dialog. Setting up a new device continues to folder selection before full auto-scan starts. - In folder selection, **Back** returns to the welcome dialog. - The app searches for known achievement/save signals (for example `achievements.json`, `achievements.ini`, `stats.bin`, emulator trophy/gpd files) and lists candidate folders. - **Start Auto-Config** keeps selected folders active and mutes unchecked discovered folders, then continues startup and background config generation. - **Skip and mute all** continues startup immediately and mutes discovered/default auto-config roots. - While onboarding is pending, folder watchers and boot auto-config scans are deferred by design to avoid unwanted automatic generation. - Onboarding completion state is saved in `%APPDATA%/Achievements/preferences.json` (`autoConfigOnboardingCompleted`, `autoConfigOnboardingVersion`, `autoConfigOnboardingCompletedAt`). - If the modal is not visible but startup is gated, use tray action **Resume Startup (Mute all)**.
Automatic configuration and default watched folders 1. Use **Watched Folders** (recommended) to scan your emulator/save directories. 2. The app will: - detect AppIDs and platform, - fetch game name + schema, - download achievement data and images when available, - generate configs automatically. 3. Default watched folders include: - %PUBLIC%\Documents\Steam\CODEX - %PUBLIC%\Documents\Steam\RUNE - %PUBLIC%\Documents\OnlineFix - %PUBLIC%\Documents\EMPRESS - %APPDATA%\Goldberg SteamEmu Saves - %APPDATA%\Goldberg UplayEmu Saves - %APPDATA%\R1 UplayEmu Saves - %APPDATA%\GSE Saves - %APPDATA%\NemirtingasEpicEmu - %APPDATA%\EMPRESS - %LOCALAPPDATA%\anadius\LSX emu\achievement_watcher - %APPDATA%\Steam\CODEX - %APPDATA%\SmartSteamEmu - %LOCALAPPDATA%\SKIDROW - %LOCALAPPDATA%\UniverseLAN **Note**: With a Steam API key, auto-configuration tries `GetSchemaForGame` first, then `GetGameAchievements`. Without a key, it tries Schema Parse → public Steam achievement JSON → SteamCommunity → SteamDB. SteamCommunity supplies achievement IDs, texts, color/gray icons and available translations directly, without a browser. Exophase can provide additional translations when needed. Unavailable translations fall back to English. Sources used when available: Steam Web API, Schema Parse, SteamCommunity, SteamDB, Exophase, GOG, Epic. `Goldberg UplayEmu Saves` and `R1 UplayEmu Saves` are explicitly routed through the Uplay-to-Steam mapping while keeping the original Uplay AppID and Uplay schema storage. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\UniverseLAN` is treated as a strict GOG root. Each immediate `` directory is mapped to a GOG config, and runtime progress is monitored from `\UniverseLANData\Achievements.ini`. Legacy game-local UniverseLAN installations continue to use `UniverseLAN.ini` discovery. RUNE Ubisoft Connect saves are supported as an opt-in watched folder. Add `%USERPROFILE%\Documents\RUNE\Ubisoft Connect` (or its `achievements` subfolder) manually in **Settings -> Folders**. The app reads `\achievements\\\achievements.cfg`, routes it through the existing Uplay schema/mapping flow, and ignores the sibling `savegames` tree. This path is intentionally not added to the default watched-folder list.
Rescan folders and manage the blacklist - **Folders -> Rescan** opens a selection modal containing active watched folders. Use **Select All** or **Deselect All**, then scan only the selected roots. - Ignored folders and ignored nested folders remain excluded even when their parent watched folder is selected. - Rescan does not clear the folder ignore list or the AppID blacklist. - Ignoring a configured game from the config/dashboard uses its AppID + platform identity, so another platform with the same AppID can remain active. - **Settings -> Advanced -> Add Blacklisted AppIDs** adds one or more AppIDs globally, including incorrectly detected UserIDs. Separate values with commas, spaces or new lines. - **Reset Blacklist** removes the saved global and platform-specific blacklist entries. It does not remove watched folders or rescan unrelated configs. - Automatic emulator generation records confirmed missing IDs separately for Steam, Uplay, GOG and Epic. Generic discovery skips only the blacklisted provider and continues with the remaining providers; a known source skips its own blacklisted ID directly. An identified game without achievements stops the current discovery and is blacklisted only on its platform. A global blacklist requires negative results from all applicable providers, without technical failures, ambiguity or a previously identified game. Automatic lookup reasons are removed with their blacklist entries; older entries without reasons are never used as proof for a global blacklist.
Video tutorials - [First Run](https://youtu.be/c1jDfynHd-U) + [Controller Support](https://youtu.be/fsqoKiMGLkw) - [Manual Config](https://youtu.be/abdVuDB80Ow) - [Auto Config](https://youtu.be/nOoiU5lPopM) - [Multi-Platform Support](https://youtu.be/KwRUo53VTho) - [Multi-Platform Support V2 + Overlay Controller Support](https://youtu.be/vDQ_4cNeIe8)

Open a setup guide below for its complete instructions and requirements. | Platform / integration | What to add or connect | Instructions | | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Steam emulators | Local Steam emulator saves, such as Goldberg/GSE, CODEX/RUNE, Online-Fix or Tenoke; detects Steam AppIDs and tracks their saved unlocks. | [Setup](#steam-emulators) · [Folde
